card.name: Elliot Shaw
card.occupation: bus accessibility route surveyor
card.personality: Practical and blunt, Elliot trusts his own feet over any official form. He is generous with directions but bristles when strangers treat him as a free tour guide. Careful to a fault, he double-checks slopes twice, yet he still laughs first at his own terrible jokes, which keeps him human.
card.background: Elliot once recommended a bus route from a spreadsheet alone, and a passenger met a steep ramp the data never mentioned. Since then he walks every route himself before signing it off. Today he is checking paths around this park for a new low-step bus stop, map in one hand, notebook in the other, hunting for a bridge approach the plan quietly ignores.
card.speechStyle: Short, plain sentences with dry asides. Counts things aloud when checking. Drops a deliberately bad joke, then rates it himself.
card.signature: "The map says flat. The map lies."
card.appearance: Angular jaw, short dark hair with a white front accent, rectangular glasses, blue open jacket over a dark shirt.

values: verified facts over paperwork
practical help without fuss
flaws: too blunt when correcting people
keeps testing things long after it is needed
boundaries: will not guess what he has not walked
refuses to be treated as an all-purpose guide
conversationalHabits: counts steps and slopes out loud
self-rates his own bad jokes
anchorLines: The map says flat. The map lies.
I don't sign off on paths I haven't walked.
That joke was a two out of ten. I'll allow it.

entries.summaryZh: 埃利奥特是公交无障碍路线调查员，曾被一张表格坑过，如今坚持用自己的双脚验证每条路。他直言、爱数台阶，还会自产自销冷笑话。公园地图上没标出的台阶，正好撞上他最较真的那根神经。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You stand at the park map board, tracing the dotted line toward the bridge with one finger. The paper is sun-faded and the paths look simpler than the park actually is.
beats.chinese: 你站在公园地图牌前，用手指描着通往桥的虚线。图纸已经晒得褪色，上面的路径看起来比公园实际的样子简单得多。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A man with a notebook under his arm stops beside you. He taps the same dotted line twice with his pencil.
beats.chinese: 一个胳膊下夹着本子的男人在你身边停下。他用铅笔在那条虚线上敲了两下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're looking at the bridge path too? Careful. That map says it's step-free. I counted eleven steps down there yesterday.
beats.chinese: 你也在看去桥的那条路？小心。这图上写着无台阶。我昨天在那边数了十一级。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I survey bus routes for wheelchair access. I don't trust maps I haven't argued with. Want to help me settle this?
beats.chinese: 我调查公交线路的无障碍情况。我不信我没吵过架的地图。想帮我弄清楚这事吗？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two ways to check. We walk the bridge path and count, or we follow that dotted line to the north gate and see where it actually goes.
beats.chinese: 有两种查法。我们走去桥的那条路数台阶，或者顺着虚线走到北门，看看它到底通到哪里。

choices.english: Let's walk the bridge path and count the steps.
choices.chinese: 我们去桥那条路数台阶吧。

choices.english: Let's follow the dotted line to the north gate.
choices.chinese: 我们顺着虚线走到北门吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You walk the gravel path together. The bridge appears ahead, and sure enough, a short flight of steps drops down to its deck.
beats.chinese: 你们一起走在碎石路上。桥出现在前方，果然，一小段台阶通向桥面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One, two, three... eleven. Eleven steps, no ramp, no rail on the left. The map calls this step-free. Unbelievable.
beats.chinese: 一，二，三……十一。十一级台阶，没有坡道，左边连扶手都没有。地图管这叫无台阶。难以置信。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He writes in a small notebook, pressing hard enough that you can see the numbers dent the next page.
beats.chinese: 他在一个小本子上写字，用力到你能看见数字压出了下一页的印子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Here's the thing. There's a side trail behind those bushes. It might loop around the steps, or it might be a dead end. I've been fooled before.
beats.chinese: 问题是，那丛灌木后面有条小径。它可能绕过台阶，也可能是条死路。我以前被坑过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So. Do we test the side trail, or do we go back and photograph every step for my report?
beats.chinese: 那么，我们去试那条小径，还是回去把每级台阶都拍下来写进报告？

choices.english: Let's test the side trail behind the bushes.
choices.chinese: 我们去试灌木后面的小径。

choices.english: Let's go back and photograph the steps for the report.
choices.chinese: 我们回去把台阶拍下来写报告。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You follow the dotted line along a hedge. It stops at a locked maintenance gate with a faded sign.
beats.chinese: 你们沿着树篱的虚线走。虚线在一扇上锁的维修门前停住了，门上的牌子已经褪色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There it is. The dotted line ends at a locked gate. Someone drew this map from a desk chair.
beats.chinese: 看到了吧。虚线的尽头是一扇锁着的门。有人是坐在办公椅上画的这张图。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He knocks twice on the gate, then crouches to look at the gap underneath it.
beats.chinese: 他敲了两下门，然后蹲下来看了看门下的缝隙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Gap's too narrow for wheels, so that's that. But look — there's a proper paved path running along the outside of this fence. It curves right around toward the road.
beats.chinese: 缝隙太窄，轮椅过不去，就这样吧。不过你看——围栏外面有一条正经的铺砌小路。它绕过去正好通向马路。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Your call. We take the paved path and trace it all the way round to see where it lets out, or we go back now and record this gate as a dead end.
beats.chinese: 你来定。我们走那条铺砌小路，一路绕过去看它通到哪儿，或者现在就回去，把这扇门记成死路。

choices.english: Let's take the paved path and trace it around.
choices.chinese: 我们走那条铺砌小路，绕过去看看。

choices.english: Let's go back and record the gate as a dead end.
choices.chinese: 我们回去把那扇门记成死路。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The side trail is narrow but solid. It curves behind the bushes and rises gently to meet the bridge deck with no steps at all.
beats.chinese: 小径很窄但很结实。它绕到灌木后面，缓缓上坡，一级台阶都没有就接上了桥面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, look at that. A way onto the bridge with no steps, hiding behind a bush. The map missed it, the council missed it, and a bush has been doing their job.
beats.chinese: 看啊。一条没有台阶的桥路，就藏在灌木后面。地图漏了它，市政漏了它，一丛灌木替他们干了活。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He walks it twice, once fast, once slow, counting under his breath both times. Then he kneels and presses his palm flat on the surface.
beats.chinese: 他走了两遍，一遍快，一遍慢，每次都小声数着什么。然后他跪下来，用手掌平按在路面上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Feels firm today, and the slope looks gentle. But I've been burned by 'looks gentle' before, so this goes in as a candidate approach only. Width, exact gradient, and park permission still need checking before anyone calls it accessible.
beats.chinese: 今天摸着很结实，坡度看着也平缓。但“看着平缓”坑过我，所以这条只作为候选路线记下。宽度、精确坡度和公园的许可都得查过，才能说它无障碍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Still — you counted with me, so I'll note a second witness. That's rare. Here's a joke for the road. Why don't steps ever win arguments? Because they always get stepped over. ...That was a three out of ten. Don't encourage me.
beats.chinese: 不过——你陪我一起数了，所以我会记上有一个证人。这可少见。送你一个路上讲的笑话。为什么台阶从来吵不赢架？因为它们总是被踩过去。……那个我自评三分。别鼓励我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You walk back to the steps. He photographs them from three angles, then lays a small level tool on the nosing of one step.
beats.chinese: 你们走回台阶。他从三个角度拍照，然后把一个小水平仪放在一级台阶的边缘上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eleven steps, no ramp, and the rise on this one is taller than the rest. That's the kind of detail a spreadsheet never shows. This goes straight to the council.
beats.chinese: 十一级台阶，没有坡道，而且这级比其他的高。这种细节表格永远不会显示。这要直接交给市政。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He marks the page with a red sticker and closes the notebook with a snap that sounds final.
beats.chinese: 他在那一页贴上红色标签，啪的一声合上本子，听着像是定了案。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The side trail behind the bushes might loop around, but I'm not writing maybes into a report. Photos first, trails later. That's the rule that keeps people safe.
beats.chinese: 灌木后面的小径也许能绕过去，但我不会把“也许”写进报告。先拍照，再探路。这是保证大家安全的规矩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You did the boring thing with me. Most people wander off at step three. I owe you a jar of jam if we ever meet where I'm not holding a clipboard.
beats.chinese: 你陪我做了这件无聊的事。大多数人数到第三级就溜了。要是哪天碰上我手里没拿记录板，我欠你一罐果酱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You follow the paved path as it curves along the outside of the fence. It is smooth and wide, and it lets out onto a quiet street with a bus stop sign.
beats.chinese: 你们沿着铺砌小路走，它顺着围栏外侧拐弯。路面平整宽阔，最后通到一条安静的街上，那里立着一个公交站牌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A bus stop. Right here, on the other side of that locked gate. Do you see what this means? The dotted line was half right. The route exists. The gate is the lie.
beats.chinese: 一个公交站。就在那扇锁着的门的另一边。你明白这意味着什么吗？虚线对了一半。路线是存在的。说谎的是那扇门。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He photographs the gate from the street side, then the bus stop, then the paved path, narrating the order to himself.
beats.chinese: 他从街这边拍下那扇门，再拍公交站，再拍那条铺砌小路，一边拍一边给自己报顺序。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Report writes itself now. Request a gate key for staff, or a pedestrian latch. Either way, this street becomes a real transfer point instead of a dotted lie.
beats.chinese: 报告现在自己会写了。要么给工作人员配一把门的钥匙，要么装一个行人闩。不管哪种，这条街都能变成真正的换乘点，而不是一条撒谎的虚线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good walking, by the way. You kept pace the whole way round without one complaint. That's rarer than you'd think. That's a four out of ten joke I just didn't tell. Saving it.
beats.chinese: 顺便说一句，你走得不错。你全程跟上了速度，一句怨言都没有。这比你想象的少见。我刚忍住了一个四分笑话。留着备用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You walk back the way you came. At the map board, he opens his own notebook and draws a firm X over his sketch of the dotted line.
beats.chinese: 你们原路返回。在地图牌前，他打开自己的本子，在临摹的虚线草图上画了一个重重的叉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Locked north gate. I'll keep this in my notes until the park team checks it. A dotted line shouldn't promise a way through that isn't there.
beats.chinese: 北门锁着。我先记在自己的本子里，等公园工作人员核实。地图上的虚线不能把不通的地方画成通路。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes out his phone and types a short note to the park office, reading it aloud as he taps.
beats.chinese: 他掏出手机给公园管理处写了条简短留言，一边打字一边念出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'North gate path ends at locked maintenance gate. Map shows it as through route. Please correct or unlock.' Short, factual, no drama. That's how you get things fixed.
beats.chinese: “北门小路止于上锁的维修门。地图显示为通路。请更正或开锁。”简短，就事论事，不带情绪。这样才能把事办成。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: We didn't find a shortcut today, but we closed a trap. That counts. And you got to watch me not tell a joke about gates. You're welcome.
beats.chinese: 今天我们没找到近路，但堵住了一个陷阱。这算数。而且你亲眼看到我没讲一个关于门的笑话。不用谢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: As you look over the walking route, Elliot recognises you and rests a finger beside the map, leaving the page clear.
beats.chinese: 你正看着散步路线，埃利奥特认出了你，把手指停在地图旁，没有挡住页面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you. I made plum jam and labelled it 'traffic jam'. Nobody at work laughed. A very difficult audience.
beats.chinese: 又见面了。我做了李子果酱，给它贴上‘交通堵塞’的标签——英语里都叫 jam。同事一个也没笑。这届观众可真难带。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Elliot taps the map's route key once, then gives his own joke a reluctant thumbs-down.
beats.chinese: 埃利奥特点了一下地图的路线图例，不情不愿地给自己的笑话比了个拇指向下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One out of ten. But the actual jam was good. I have independent reports on that.
beats.chinese: 十分里得一分吧。不过果酱确实不错。这可是有别人作证的。

card.name: Victor Lane
card.occupation: retired ferry dispatcher
card.personality: Victor is warm, chatty, and quick with a story, but he has learned to stop halfway and admit when he has stretched the truth. He loves precision—timetables, star charts, seam allowances—yet his memory embellishes freely. Outgoing with strangers, he still respects a closed door. He is proudest of fixing things: schedules, costumes, and lately, his own tall tales.
card.background: For thirty-one years Victor coordinated ferry departures, where one wrong minute meant a dock full of angry passengers. Retirement left his hands restless, so a costume shop taught him to mend, and now he repairs theatre costumes at his kitchen table. He studies the night sky with a secondhand telescope and is rewriting his most-repeated ferry anecdote into a version that honestly admits what he misremembered. Today he is testing a new walking route through the park against the old one he has used for years.
card.speechStyle: Rhythmic and dispatch-like: short counted phrases, then a longer roll. Says 'mark my words' and 'here's the honest bit'. Often pauses to correct himself mid-story, numbering details like departure times.
card.signature: One minute late is a story; two minutes late is a disaster.
card.appearance: Long narrow older face, long pale hair, small oval glasses, dark cardigan, arms folded.

values: honesty in storytelling
punctuality
flaws: embellishes memories
talks too long
boundaries: won't be rushed mid-story
won't pretend certainty he lacks
conversationalHabits: counts points on his fingers
stops to self-correct with 'here's the honest bit'
anchorLines: Two ways to go—old path or new path. I've walked one of them for years.
Here's the honest bit: I got half of that story wrong for twenty years.
Mark my words, a good route is like a good timetable—you test it twice.

entries.summaryZh: 维克多退休前调度轮渡，退休后缝戏服、学看星图，也爱讲故事。他最常讲的天鹅趣事其实掺了不少改编，如今想给故事贴上诚实的标签。你选哪条园路，会决定听到一个改写的旧故事，还是看到他准备尝试的新事情。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You stop at the park map to plan your walk. An old man stands beside you, tapping the frame with one finger, shifting his weight from foot to foot.
beats.chinese: 你在公园地图前停下，想规划散步路线。一位老人站在你旁边，用手指敲着图框，重心左右移动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two ways to go—old path or new path. I've walked one of them for years, and the other one just appeared on this map. Mark my words, this is a real decision.
beats.chinese: 两条路可走——旧路或新路。有一条我走了好多年，另一条是刚画上地图的。记住我的话，这可是个真正的决定。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls a folded paper from his coat pocket and smooths it against the map frame. It is a hand-drawn copy of the same map, with tiny notes in the margins.
beats.chinese: 他从外套口袋里掏出一张折起的纸，在地图框上抹平。那是同一张地图的手绘版，边上有许多小注。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I made my own copy. A dispatcher likes a second timetable. The old path runs by the water; the new one bends toward those benches inside the park.
beats.chinese: 我自己画了一份。做调度的总喜欢多备一张时刻表。旧路沿水边走，新路则拐向公园里面那几张长椅。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, stranger, you've got fresh eyes. Which way should we test first?
beats.chinese: 嗯，这位朋友，你眼睛是新的。我们先试哪条路？

choices.english: Let's take the old path by the water.
choices.chinese: 我们走水边的旧路吧。

choices.english: Let's try the new path toward the benches.
choices.chinese: 我们试试通向长椅的新路吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The old path it is. Good choice for a first test—this is the control route, as we used to say. Every ferry needs a baseline.
beats.chinese: 就走旧路。第一次测试选得好——这是基准路线，我们以前常这么说。每班渡轮都需要个基准。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You walk along the water together. Victor points at a bench with his walking stick as you pass it.
beats.chinese: 你们一起沿水边走。经过一条长椅时，维克多用手杖指了指它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That bench reminds me of a story I tell about my ferry days. I always say a swan blocked the gangway and made me miss a departure by one minute.
beats.chinese: 那张长椅让我想起轮渡时期常讲的一件事。我总说一只天鹅挡住跳板，让我晚了一分钟，错过开船。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stops walking and turns to face the bench, as if checking it against a memory.
beats.chinese: 他停下脚步，转身面对长椅，好像在把它和记忆核对。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Here's the honest bit: I got half of that story wrong for twenty years. It wasn't a swan. It was a delivery cart, and I was two minutes late, not one. I'm rewriting the whole tale this week.
beats.chinese: 说实话的部分来了：这个故事我讲错了二十年。不是天鹅，是一辆送货的车，而且我晚了不止一分钟，是两分钟。这周我正在重写整个故事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So—do I keep telling it with the swan, because it's funnier? Or tell it true? You decide while we walk.
beats.chinese: 那么——我是继续讲天鹅版，因为它更好笑？还是讲真话版？我们边走你边决定。

choices.english: Tell it true. The cart version sounds better anyway.
choices.chinese: 讲真话吧。送货车的版本其实更有意思。

choices.english: Keep the swan, but say you changed it. That's honest too.
choices.chinese: 保留天鹅，但说明你改过了。这也算诚实。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: New path it is. I'll mark the turn as we go. Otherwise I'll be telling everyone I discovered this route myself by next week.
beats.chinese: 那就走新路。我边走边记下转弯。不然过一星期，我怕是又要说这条路是自己发现的了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At a park bench, Victor opens his bag. A folded paper star wheel slips against a photo of a costume with a loose shoulder seam.
beats.chinese: 走到公园长椅边，维克多打开包。折好的纸星盘贴着一张戏服照片，照片上肩部的接缝松开了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two things I'm learning. How to use this star wheel, and how to offer help without announcing that I know best. The costume belongs to a theatre group.
beats.chinese: 两件我正在学的事：怎么用这个星盘，还有怎么提出帮忙，又不摆出自己最懂的架势。戏服是一家剧团的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He smooths both papers on his knees, keeping the photo in its sleeve. His finger stops over the loose seam, then moves to the wheel.
beats.chinese: 他在膝头铺平两张纸，照片还留在保护套里。他的手指停在松开的接缝上，随后移到星盘旁。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I mend costumes at home. They shared this photo asking about repairs, and I've been drafting an offer. The star wheel is a much quieter problem.
beats.chinese: 我在家里修补戏服。他们发了这张照片询问维修，我一直在拟一份帮忙的留言。比起来，星盘这个难题安静多了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Which shall I untangle first — the paper wheel, or that little note? I've got time for one before I carry on walking.
beats.chinese: 我先理清哪一个——纸星盘，还是那张小留言？继续散步前，我还有时间弄好一件。

choices.english: Look at the instructions on his paper star wheel together.
choices.chinese: 一起看看纸星盘上的使用说明。

choices.english: Help him keep the repair offer short and optional.
choices.chinese: 帮他把修补邀约写得简短，也给对方留下选择。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: True version it is. The delivery cart. You know, when I say it out loud, the cart is funnier—a man in a good coat, defeated by flour sacks.
beats.chinese: 就讲真话版。送货的车。你知道吗，大声说出来，那车反而更好笑——一个穿着体面外套的男人，败给了一袋袋面粉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You reach the end of the water path. Victor takes out his hand-drawn map and crosses out a small note with a pencil stub.
beats.chinese: 你们走到水路的尽头。维克多掏出手绘地图，用一小截铅笔划掉一条小注。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Note deleted: 'swan, one minute.' New note: 'cart, two minutes, and I was reading the wrong timetable.' That last part I only admitted last spring.
beats.chinese: 好了。注解删掉：'天鹅，一分钟'。新注解：'送货车，两分钟，而且我看错了时刻表'。最后那部分我是去年春天才承认的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the map carefully along its worn creases and pats it twice before pocketing it.
beats.chinese: 他沿着磨旧的折痕仔细把地图折好，拍了拍，才放回口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You helped me finish a job twenty years long. First honest telling happens this week, I promise you. Mark my words—the cart stays.
beats.chinese: 你帮我完成了一项二十年的工作。第一次诚实的讲述这周就会发生，我向你保证。记住我的话——送货车留下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Keep the swan, but say I changed it. Hmm. 'Once upon a time there was a swan, but the truth was a cart.' That's almost a poem, isn't it?
beats.chinese: 保留天鹅，但说明我改过了。嗯。'从前有一只天鹅，但真相是一辆车。'这几乎像一句诗了，对吧？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Victor walks a few steps in silence, mouthing the sentence to himself like he is testing the weight of it.
beats.chinese: 维克多默默走了几步，嘴里念着那句话，像在掂它的分量。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the honest version for a stage, maybe. I mend costumes for the theatre—people pay to watch a story they know isn't real. Nobody minds, as long as the curtain says so.
beats.chinese: 那也许是在舞台上的诚实版本。我给剧院缝戏服——人们花钱看一个他们明知不是真的故事。只要幕布上写明，没人介意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes out his hand-drawn map and writes a new line in the margin, reading it aloud as he writes.
beats.chinese: 他掏出手绘地图，在边上写下一行字，边写边念出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: New note: 'swan version allowed, only if labelled as a story.' My granddaughter will laugh. She's been calling me out on that swan since she was nine.
beats.chinese: 新注解：'天鹅版可以讲，但必须注明是故事'。我孙女会笑的。她从九岁起就揪着那只天鹅不放。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You've given me a third option I didn't see from the map. That's worth a walk any day.
beats.chinese: 你给了我一个从地图上看不出来的第三种选择。这值得走一趟。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You look at the printed instructions together. Victor finds the month ring, then turns the paper disc until two marked practice arrows meet.
beats.chinese: 你们一起看印好的说明。维克多找到月份环，转动纸盘，让两个练习箭头对齐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, it says this example is for practice. I was trying to make the diagram match the sky without even setting the date. Very professional of me.
beats.chinese: 啊，上面写了这只是练习示例。我连日期都没设，就想让图对上天空。真是太专业了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the wheel back and repeats the steps himself. This time he stops at the instruction about checking the place, date and time.
beats.chinese: 他把纸盘转回去，自己再做了一次。这回读到核对地点、日期和时间的提示，他停下来记住了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thirty-one years checking ferry times, and I forgot the clock on a paper sky. I'll try it properly another time. For now, I understand which ring moves.
beats.chinese: 查了三十一年轮渡时刻，我却忘了纸天空也要看时间。改天再正式试。至少现在我明白该转哪一圈了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the wheel along its existing creases and adds a small star beside the bench on his personal map.
beats.chinese: 他沿原有折痕收好星盘，在自己的地图上，给长椅旁画了一颗小星星。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. New path, one useful bench, one less muddle. I can tell that story exactly as it happened. No swans required.
beats.chinese: 好了，新路，一张有用的长椅，少了一件糊涂事。这个故事可以照实讲，一只天鹅都不用添。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Victor takes out a pencil and a spare card. He starts with a long account of his sewing experience, then pauses over the crowded first line.
beats.chinese: 维克多拿出铅笔和备用卡片，先写了一大段自己的缝补经历，又望着挤满的第一行停下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's a speech, isn't it? You said short and optional. Right. They asked about repairs, not the history of my kitchen table.
beats.chinese: 这成演讲了，对吧？你说要简短，也要留选择。好。他们问的是修补，不是我家厨房桌子的历史。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the card over and writes a new draft, leaving space beneath it for any details the group might ask for later.
beats.chinese: 他把卡片翻过来，重写一份草稿，下面留着空位，以后对方问起细节时再补。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I mend costumes and could look at that seam, if useful. No hurry — let me know. There. An offer, not a rescue mission.
beats.chinese: 我会修补戏服，如果需要，可以帮忙看看那条接缝。不急，方便时告诉我。好了，这是个邀约，不是什么救援行动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He places the unsent draft behind the photo in its sleeve. Then he puts both safely in his bag and checks the path ahead.
beats.chinese: 他把尚未发出的草稿放到照片后面的保护套里，一并收回包中，再看向前方的园路。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll read it once more at home before I decide to send it. A new path and a finished draft — plenty for one walk. Thanks for keeping me brief.
beats.chinese: 回家我会再看一遍，然后决定要不要发。走了新路，也写好了草稿，一趟散步够充实了。谢谢你让我少说两句。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: While you look over the map, Victor recognises you and pauses beside the table, keeping his hands clear of the marked paths.
beats.chinese: 你查看地图时，维克托认出了你，在桌旁停下，没有把手放到标出的路线上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hello again. I sewed a coat pocket shut by mistake. Told the costume shop it was a security feature.
beats.chinese: 又见面了。我不小心把一件大衣的口袋缝死了，还跟戏服店说那是防盗设计。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Victor starts to laugh, then raises one finger to interrupt his own story before looking back at the map.
beats.chinese: 维克托刚笑起来，又竖起一根手指打断自己的故事，然后才看回地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Here's the honest bit: I only thought of that line on the bus home. At the shop I just said sorry and unpicked it.
beats.chinese: 说实话吧：这话是坐公交回家时才想到的。在店里我只说了对不起，然后把线拆了。

card.name: Ted Callaghan
card.occupation: surtitle operator at a Melbourne theatre, running translated captions for opera and plays
hobbies: occasional shortwave listening on quiet nights
card.personality: Ted runs on booth timing: one correction, then the show moves. He'll say sorry in a single clean beat — but if you keep apologising back, he goes flat and starts watching the clock. Not anger. He just thinks a repeated apology muddies the cue. His warmth is practical: a posted card, a fixed hinge, a caption up half a second early so nobody stumbles. He'd rather show up than talk about showing up.
card.background: Twenty-odd years in the wings taught Ted that an audience forgives one slip and never forgives three. Now he sits in the surtitle booth — red light on, click, the line up in lights just before the singer needs it. Above his desk at home in Footscray hangs a shelf of masks: Venetian, Balinese, a lopsided one from a Bendigo fair. Since 2004 he's posted one hand-made card a month to Marianne, a chatty schoolteacher and his complete opposite. Neither ever explained the ritual. Neither stopped. On slow nights he still tunes a shortwave set, but the cards are the real habit.
card.speechStyle: Short, unhurried sentences with real pauses between them. Booth shorthand — 'stand by', 'that's cued' — slips in naturally. Rarely says a point twice.
card.signature: That's cued. Next.
card.appearance: Broad heavy jaw and cheeks, heavy brows, dark braids, blue work coat and shoulder strap.

values: one clean correction, then forward
keeping small promises exactly
flaws: impatient with repeated apologies — goes curt and checks the time
awkward receiving warm thanks face to face
boundaries: won't sit through long emotional debriefs
won't gossip about cast or crew
conversationalHabits: answers the actual question first, context only if asked
describes feelings through objects — the booth, the red light, the card on the kitchen table
anchorLines: Sorry. Said once, meant twice. Right — where were we?
If I miss a caption, I fix it and we move. Do the same and we'll get on fine.
Marianne rang for twenty minutes about her card. Mine said 'autumn'. Hers had a whole essay on the back.

entries.summaryZh: 墨尔本剧院字幕操作员泰德在公园里和一张塞不进口袋的手工小卡较劲。他话短、停顿自在，道歉只说一次，热心全藏在动作里。跟着他试折痕、挑开头，你会看到二十年寄卡习惯背后那个利落又固执的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the park's route map, a man beside you folds a small hand-painted card over and over, trying to slide it into his coat pocket. It sticks out by a finger's width every time.
beats.chinese: 在公园路线图旁，一个男人反复折一张手绘小卡，想塞进外套口袋，可每次都差一根手指的宽度。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Stand by... no. Still proud of it. Sorry — you're at the map. Go ahead.
beats.chinese: 预备……不行，还是鼓着。抱歉——你要看地图，请便。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He steps back from the map and holds the card up to the light, studying the crease like it owes him an answer.
beats.chinese: 他从地图前让开，把卡片举到光下，端详折痕，像等它给个说法。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Twenty years I've posted these to a friend. Still get the size wrong. One clean fold, that's all I want.
beats.chinese: 这些卡我寄给一位朋友二十年了，尺寸还是算不对。就想要一次干净的折痕。

choices.english: Ask if he'd like to try folding it a different direction.
choices.chinese: 问他能否换个方向折。

choices.english: Ask what he plans to write on the card.
choices.chinese: 问这张卡准备写什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the card sideways and makes a careful fold along its long edge.
beats.chinese: 他把卡片横过来，沿长边仔细折了一道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Flat... and there's the trouble.
beats.chinese: 好了。平整了……麻烦也来了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He opens it again. The crease runs straight through the little bridge he painted, cutting it in half.
beats.chinese: 他重新展开，折痕正好压过他画的小桥，把它切成两半。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Painted that this week. Bridge from the park here, actually. Now it's two bridges. That's cued — wrong cue.
beats.chinese: 这是我这周画的。画的就是这公园里的桥。现在成两座桥了。挂上了——挂错了。

choices.english: Suggest he keep the painting flat and just carry the card in his hand.
choices.chinese: 建议保留图案，把卡拿在手上。

choices.english: Ask whether he'd let the crease become part of the picture.
choices.chinese: 问他是否愿意让折痕成为图案的一部分。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the blank side toward you and taps it once with a finger.
beats.chinese: 他把空白的一面转向你，用手指敲了敲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nothing yet. Marianne and I post cards monthly. Never agreed on a rule. Hers run a whole essay. Mine say one line.
beats.chinese: 还没写。我和玛丽安每月互寄卡片，从没定过规矩。她的能写一整篇文章，我的只有一行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at the empty card, then at the bridge in the distance, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他看看空白的卡，又看看远处的桥，不慌不忙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Short's fine. I'm just picking an opening. Something that's actually today.
beats.chinese: 短没关系。我是在挑个开头。得是今天真发生的事。

choices.english: Suggest he open with the card refusing to fit in his pocket.
choices.chinese: 建议用卡片塞不进口袋这件小事开头。

choices.english: Say the blank card already looks good — no rush to pick an opening.
choices.chinese: 说空白卡现在也很好看，不必急着选开头。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He smooths the card flat on the map's ledge and holds it loosely in one hand.
beats.chinese: 他把卡片在地图台面上抚平，松松地拿在一只手里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Pocket's on holiday today. Card travels with me.
beats.chinese: 行。口袋今天放假，卡片跟我走。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks his hand in his pocket anyway, out of habit, and huffs a short laugh at himself.
beats.chinese: 他还是习惯性地把手插进口袋，然后自嘲地短笑一声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Problem's solved by not solving it. Next.
beats.chinese: 问题靠不解决解决了。下一个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He studies the painted bridge, then folds along the blank margin beside it — an uneven, deliberate crease.
beats.chinese: 他端详画好的桥，然后沿旁边空白的边缘折了一道不对称的、刻意的折痕。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The card folds shut, bridge intact, and slides into his pocket without a fight.
beats.chinese: 卡片折拢，桥完好无损，顺顺当当地滑进了口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Off-centre. Marianne will notice. She'll say it's my best one. Stand by — that's cued.
beats.chinese: 不对称。玛丽安会注意到的。她会说这是最好的一张。预备——挂上了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good accident. I'll keep it.
beats.chinese: 不错的意外，我留着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds the card out and tries the line quietly, testing it against the air.
beats.chinese: 他举起卡片，低声试了一句，像在试音。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'The card won't fit my pocket. The bridge still fits the park.' ...Hm. That's more me than hello.
beats.chinese: “卡片塞不进口袋，桥还留在公园里。”……嗯，这比问好更像我的近况。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the card once, blank side out, and puts it in his breast pocket with two fingers.
beats.chinese: 他把卡片折了一下，空白面朝外，用两根手指放进胸袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll write it proper at home. Line's cued. Thanks.
beats.chinese: 回家好好写。这句挂上了。谢谢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at the blank card a moment, then closes it without folding and slips it into his pocket, crease and all.
beats.chinese: 他看了空白卡一会儿，没有折就合上，连折痕一起放进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Blank's fine. Rest day's a rest day. I don't turn it into a task.
beats.chinese: 空白的也好。休息就是休息，我不把它变成任务。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives the map one last look, notes the bridge route with a nod, and straightens his coat.
beats.chinese: 他最后看了一眼地图，朝桥的方向点点头，理了理外套。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Bridge is worth the walk. Enjoy it. Right — off I go.
beats.chinese: 那座桥值得走一趟。玩得开心。好了——我走了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the route map. A bicycle bell rings somewhere behind you, and Ted, standing nearby, turns his head and steps aside before checking the path.
beats.chinese: 你回到路线图前。身后响起自行车铃，站在旁边的泰德侧身让开，然后才看清路况。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Bell's gone. Different path, already past. I always move before I look. Booth habit — you stand by, you don't ask questions.
beats.chinese: 铃声没了。另一条路，已经过去了。我总是先让再看清。机房习惯——预备就行，别多问。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He returns to the map and stands to one side, leaving the middle of the board clear for you.
beats.chinese: 他回到地图前，站到一侧，把图板中间留给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This month's card went out yesterday, by the way. Marianne rang about it. Twenty minutes. She always finds something to say about them.
beats.chinese: 对了，这个月的卡昨天寄出去了。玛丽安还打电话聊了二十分钟。她总能对那些卡说出点道道来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles into reading the map, unhurried, as if waiting for his own cue.
beats.chinese: 他不慌不忙地看起地图来，像在等自己的上场提示。

card.name: Jonah Petrov
card.occupation: bicycle wheel builder — I lace and true wheels by hand for a small shop in Brooklyn
card.personality: I'm quiet but not shy. I like saying yes to a spontaneous afternoon out — a friend texts, I go — but I need a whole evening alone afterward to feel like myself again. People read that as moodiness; it's just how my battery works. I have strong opinions about small things, like spoke tension and cheap glue sticks, and I'll state them gently but I won't budge. I'm patient with objects and less patient with vague plans.
card.background: I've been building wheels for about eleven years now. Started fixing my own commuter bike in a shared garage in Queens, then an old builder named Ray let me sweep his shop and taught me lacing on beat-up rims. There's something satisfying about a wheel that runs true — you can feel it under your hands before anyone rides it. I still live alone in a small apartment with a wall of half-finished collages and a list I wrote when I was twenty-six. Last month I crossed off four things I'd been carrying around for years: learning Italian, a motorcycle license, a tattoo, and 'run a marathon.' Didn't want any of them anymore. Felt lighter than finishing them would have.
card.speechStyle: Low volume, unhurried, complete sentences. Says 'hm, no' instead of a blunt no. Pauses before opinions, then commits to them fully. Asks short concrete questions.
card.signature: I'll come — I just might disappear after.
card.appearance: Smooth bald head, narrow angular face, raised wide jacket collar, dark utility clothing.

values: honesty about what you actually want
quiet craftsmanship
flaws: cancels plans when my social tank hits empty
stubborn about minor preferences
boundaries: I don't do drop-in visits without a text first
please don't push me to explain why I crossed something off the list
conversationalHabits: answers with a specific detail before a feeling
uses 'hm' as a real thinking sound, not filler
anchorLines: Hm, no — I'd rather true a wheel than watch a movie about truing a wheel.
If we go, let's go today. If it's next Thursday, I'll overthink it.
I crossed it off. That's not giving up, that's just... reading my own handwriting honestly.

entries.summaryZh: 乔纳·彼得罗夫，纽约的自行车编圈师，靠手感吃饭。公园里他按着一块印歪的鸟布贴闲聊，声音轻、偏好坚定，临时改了主意也不慌。四条分支里他或收起布贴、或放手让鸟自己掉、或选短环线留一晚独处、或各自看图分头走——每次都记得你帮的那个忙。

story.titleZh: 公园地图旁的一块布贴

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A park map stands near the path, a bridge visible in the distance. You are tracing a route with your finger when someone stops beside you, a shoe bag in one hand.
beats.chinese: 公园小径旁立着一块地图，远处可见一座桥。你正用手指描着路线，有人在你身边停下，手里提着一个鞋袋。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the side of the bag, a small fabric patch is peeling loose at one corner. The person presses a finger flat against it, holding it down, and smiles.
beats.chinese: 鞋袋侧面有一小块布贴，一角正在脱开。那人用手指把它按平，按住不放，笑了笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This patch has traveled more than my shoes, honestly. It comes loose every few weeks, and every time I just press it back down and go.
beats.chinese: 说实话，这块布贴比我的鞋还爱出门。它每隔几周就松一次，每次我就把它按回去，然后继续走。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You look like you're actually reading the map, not just standing near it. Are you figuring out where to walk?
beats.chinese: 你看起来是真的在读这张地图，不只是站在旁边。你在想走去哪儿吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They keep one finger on the patch, waiting, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 那人一根手指仍按在布贴上，不急不忙地等着。

choices.english: Ask why they like that patch so much.
choices.chinese: 问他为什么这么喜欢这块布贴。

choices.english: Ask if the shoe bag means they're heading to climb.
choices.chinese: 问鞋袋是不是表示接下来要去攀岩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why this one? Hm. Look closely — the bird on it is printed crooked. The whole flock leans left, like they're all dodging something.
beats.chinese: 为什么喜欢这块？嗯，你仔细看——上面的鸟印歪了。整群鸟都往左斜，像在躲什么东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It was the cheapest patch in the whole shop. I've had nicer ones, and I threw those away. This crooked bird I've kept for six years.
beats.chinese: 它是整家店里最便宜的一块。我有过更好的，都扔了。这只歪鸟我留了六年。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The corner of the patch lifts slightly under their finger. They press it down again without looking.
beats.chinese: 布贴的一角在指下又翘起来。那人看也不看地又按了下去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I keep meaning to fix it properly. Glue, a needle, something. But then it would just be a straight bird, and I like the crooked one.
beats.chinese: 我一直想着好好修一下。用胶水，用针，什么都行。可修好它就只是一只正的鸟了，我更喜欢歪的那只。

choices.english: Suggest peeling it off and keeping it safe in a pocket so it doesn't get lost on the path.
choices.chinese: 建议先把它取下来收进口袋，免得掉在路上。

choices.english: Suggest leaving it alone until it comes off by itself, and just keep walking.
choices.chinese: 建议在它完全脱落前少碰它，先继续走路。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The bag? Yes, it's my climbing shoes. I was headed to the gym. Then I got here and... hm, no. I didn't want the gym. I wanted to walk.
beats.chinese: 鞋袋？对，是我的攀岩鞋。我本来要去馆里。结果走到这儿就……嗯，不。我不想去了，我想走走。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So now the shoes are just company. They can walk too. The wall will still be there some other day.
beats.chinese: 所以现在鞋子就当个伴儿。它们也能走路。墙又跑不掉，改天还在。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They swing the bag lightly once, then set it down by their foot and look at the map properly.
beats.chinese: 那人把鞋袋轻轻晃了一下，然后放在脚边，认真看起地图来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The trouble is I'm bad at choosing. Short loop or the long way past the bridge — both sound fine, so I stand here.
beats.chinese: 问题是我不会选。短环线还是绕桥的长路——听起来都行，所以我就站在这儿。

choices.english: Ask whether they'd rather walk a shorter loop or take the longer detour.
choices.chinese: 问他想走短一点的环线还是多绕一段。

choices.english: Say you haven't decided your own route either, and look at the map separately.
choices.chinese: 说自己也还没决定走哪，先各自看图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Take it off and pocket it? Hm. Yes. That's the honest answer — it wants to come off, and the ground here is full of puddle edges.
beats.chinese: 取下来放进口袋？嗯，对。这才是老实的答案——它本来就想下来，这地上到处是水洼边。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They peel the patch back slowly with a thumbnail. It comes free with a soft tearing sound, leaving a clean pale shape on the bag.
beats.chinese: 那人用拇指指甲慢慢把布贴揭开。布贴轻轻一声撕响脱了下来，鞋袋上留下一个干净的浅色轮廓。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at that. The shape it left behind — it's like a second bird, one that already flew. The newer bird, maybe.
beats.chinese: 你看。留下的这个印子——像第二只鸟，已经飞走的那只。也许是更新的一只。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll keep both. The crooked one in my pocket, the ghost one on the bag. That's a fair trade for a walk.
beats.chinese: 两个我都留着。歪的放口袋，影子留在袋上。为了散个步，这买卖不亏。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They fold the patch into their pocket, pat it once, and straighten the bag strap.
beats.chinese: 那人把布贴折好放进口袋，拍了一下，理了理鞋袋的带子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Leave it alone? Hm, no — I mean, hm, maybe. You might be right. Every time I press it, I press a little glue off with it.
beats.chinese: 别去碰它？嗯，不——我是说，嗯，也许。你可能说得对。我每按一次，就按掉一点胶。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They lift their finger away and hold the hand open, looking at it like it betrayed them.
beats.chinese: 那人把手指拿开，摊开手看着，像在看一只背叛了自己的手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Honest hands. I've been making it looser this whole time and calling it fixing. That's a wheel-builder habit gone wrong.
beats.chinese: 好了，老实的手。我一直把它越按越松，还管这叫修理。这是编圈师傅的坏习惯用错了地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fine. It falls when it falls. I'll move the bag to this side so it doesn't rub my coat, and we let the bird decide its own schedule.
beats.chinese: 行。掉就掉吧。我把袋子换到这边，免得蹭到外套，让那只鸟自己决定日程。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They swap the bag to the far hand and start walking, the patch corner lifting gently in the breeze.
beats.chinese: 那人把鞋袋换到另一只手，开始走，布贴的一角在风里轻轻翘着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Short or long? Hm. Short. If I take the long way, I'll like it so much I'll skip the evening I promised myself.
beats.chinese: 短还是长？嗯，短的。要是绕远路，我会走得太开心，把答应自己的那个晚上也搭进去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They trace a small loop on the map with one finger, stopping well before the bridge.
beats.chinese: 那人用一根手指在地图上比出一小段环线，在桥之前就停住了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Here, to that bench, around the pond, back. Twenty minutes of walking and the shoes get their outing too.
beats.chinese: 这儿，到那张长椅，绕过池塘，回来。走二十分钟，鞋子也算出过门了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: After that I go home and sit with nothing. Not sad-nothing. Recharging-nothing. It's how I'm still pleasant by Friday.
beats.chinese: 然后我回家，什么都不干。不是难过的那种什么都不干，是充电的那种。这样我到周五还能算个好人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They lift the bag, give you a small nod, and set off along the short loop at an easy pace.
beats.chinese: 那人提起鞋袋，朝你轻轻点了点头，沿着短环线不紧不慢地出发了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They step half a pace to the side, giving you a clear view of your half of the map.
beats.chinese: 那人往旁边挪了半步，把你那半边地图让得清清楚楚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good — no joint committee. I like a person who doesn't pretend to care where I walk.
beats.chinese: 好，不开联合委员会了。我喜欢不假装关心我去哪儿走的人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hm. The bridge side has a hill. My legs say yes, my evening says hm, no. The flat side it is.
beats.chinese: 嗯。桥那边有个坡。腿说好，晚上说嗯，不行。那就走平的那边。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pick up the bag, glance once more at the map, and point down the flat path without asking your opinion.
beats.chinese: 那人提起鞋袋，又看了一眼地图，没征求意见就指向平坦的那条路。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your route, whichever one your finger picks. If it's the bridge, wave from the top — I'll be the flat one down here.
beats.chinese: 祝你走好你的路线，手指选哪条都行。要是走桥，在桥顶挥挥手——我就在下面走平路。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They walk off unhurried, the bag swinging lightly at their side.
beats.chinese: 那人不紧不慢地走远了，鞋袋在身侧轻轻晃着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You are at the park map again. Jonah walks up, sets the shoe bag by a foot, and rolls an ankle slowly, testing it.
beats.chinese: 你又站在公园地图旁。乔纳走过来，把鞋袋放在脚边，慢慢转了转脚踝，像在测试什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny thing about climbing — the wall tilts at you all day, and then flat ground feels like the trick part.
beats.chinese: 攀岩好玩的地方就在这儿——墙整天朝你倾过来，回到平地上反而觉得平地才是最难的部分。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They straighten up, glance at the map without leaning in, and adjust the bag strap on their shoulder.
beats.chinese: 那人站直，看了一眼地图却没有凑近，理了理肩上的鞋袋带子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The bag's the same as ever. Been a good companion — carried the shoes, kept me company. Hm. We get along fine.
beats.chinese: 鞋袋还是老样子。一直是个好伴儿——装着鞋，也陪着我。嗯，我们处得不错。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm off down the flat path again — legs voted, the evening agreed. Good routes to you.
beats.chinese: 我又要沿平路走了——腿投了票，晚上也同意了。祝你路线顺利。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They lift the bag, roll the ankle once more, and set off at their usual unhurried pace.
beats.chinese: 那人提起鞋袋，又转了一下脚踝，照旧不紧不慢地出发了。

card.name: Mavis Dlamini
card.occupation: retired leather belt edge-painting technician, takes the occasional private commission
card.personality: Mavis is unhurried, dryly funny, and currently chewing on one question: how do you step away from something you helped build without souring it? They'll happily show you a rough belt edge or a half-labelled seed jar — but get quiet and firm if you try to finish their work for them or talk them out of leaving the map-drawing project they started. They think out loud, in distances and elevations, and they'd rather ask where you're from than talk about themselves. Not a mentor, not a sage. Just someone mid-decision, and fine with that.
card.background: Forty-odd years edge-painting belts in a Salt River workshop gave Mavis a steady hand and a feel for stopping at the right moment — an edge worked too long goes wrong. Evenings now go to geography quiz apps and arguing with the television about capital cities; weekends to a seed drawer organised by region, with duplicates set aside for swapping by post. They're winding down the community map-drawing project they helped start years ago. They don't enjoy it anymore, and they're trying to leave it while keeping the memory of why they loved starting it — without anyone making a speech about it.
card.speechStyle: Short, unhurried sentences with dry asides. Any place you mention gets answered with a fact — elevation, distance, a capital — then a follow-up question about your actual life there. Pauses before answering, then answers plainly and remembers your exact words.
card.signature: You can love how a thing started and still put it down.
card.appearance: Rounded older face with soft cheeks, swept pale curly hair, rectangular glasses and a broad scarf.

values: leaving things well, not just finishing them
knowing places by their details, not their postcards
flaws: answers a question with a quiz fact before answering it as a person
keeps re-litigating the map decision out loud instead of settling it
boundaries: no farewell events or guilt trips over the map project
don't finish, fix, or 'helpfully complete' their unfinished work unasked
conversationalHabits: responds to any mentioned place with elevation, distance, or a capital, then asks about your life there
talks decisions through aloud rather than announcing conclusions
anchorLines: I'm not leaving the map project because it failed. I stopped liking Tuesdays, and that's reason enough.
Bloemfontein, you said? Judicial capital, funny enough. What took you there — work or family?
Half-done is a real state of a thing. It doesn't need rescuing.

entries.summaryZh: 七十二岁的Mavis在公园路线图前掏出一个空纸种袋，聊起算错的种子交换数目，也聊到地图图标认不出真树。四条岔路各自收在一个小而真实的决定上：不折返、讲一段平常的通信交换、把图标当地标、承认景色记不过地名。不紧不慢，点到即止。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A park map stands by the path, its painted tree icons leading the eye toward a bridge in the distance. An older person in a canvas jacket is studying it, an empty paper seed packet held loosely in one hand.
beats.chinese: 小径旁立着公园地图，画着树的图标一路引向远处的桥。一位穿帆布外套的老人正在看图，手里松松捏着一个空的纸质种子袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry — not talking to you, talking to the map. This little tree icon made me think of my seed drawer at home. Regions, labels, the lot. Look at me, drifting off at a park sign.
beats.chinese: 抱歉——不是在跟你说话，是在跟地图说话。这个小树图标让我想起家里的种子抽屉。按地区分好，贴着标签。瞧我，在公园的牌子前走神了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They turn the empty packet over. Two place names are written on it in careful handwriting. Nothing else.
beats.chinese: 他们把空种子袋翻过来。上面用工整的字迹写着两个地名，再没有别的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Mavis. This packet came out of my pocket empty, and now it's started a whole thought. You were reading the route, though — don't let me stand on your map.
beats.chinese: 我叫Mavis。这个袋子从口袋里掏出来时就是空的，结果引出这么一串念头。不过你刚才在看路线——别让我挡着你的地图。

choices.english: Ask why the seed packet is empty.
choices.chinese: 问种子袋为什么是空的。

choices.english: Point out that the map's tree icons look nothing like real trees.
choices.chinese: 指出地图上的树图标和真的树差得很远。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Empty because I miscounted. I pick the packet before I post the seeds — one bag per friend. I set out three bags for two friends. Or two bags for three. Somewhere the numbers went sideways.
beats.chinese: 空着是因为我数错了。寄种子之前我会先挑袋子——一位朋友一个袋。我备了三个袋子给两位朋友。或者两个袋子给三位朋友。反正数目在哪一步出了岔子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They hold the packet up to the light, as if the missing number might be printed inside it.
beats.chinese: 他们把袋子举到光前，好像缺的那个数目会印在袋子里面似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So the spare came along for the walk. I could go back for the right one. It's not far. But my knees vote against it, and honestly, so do I.
beats.chinese: 于是多出来的那个就跟着出来散步了。我可以回去拿对的那个。不远。但我的膝盖投了反对票，说实话，我也是。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The seeds themselves are duplicates from the drawer. Swapping by post is slow, but it keeps old friendships moving. You ever send anything stranger than a letter?
beats.chinese: 种子本身是抽屉里挑出来的重复的。邮寄交换很慢，但能让老交情不断。你寄过比信更奇怪的东西吗？

choices.english: Ask whether they'll go home and fetch the correct packet.
choices.chinese: 问他们会不会回家拿正确的那个袋子。

choices.english: Ask how this kind of seed swap got started.
choices.chinese: 请他们讲讲这种种子交换是怎么开始的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're right, the icons are nothing like real trees. A circle on a stick. I couldn't name a single species from these. And I'm the sort who pretends I could.
beats.chinese: 你说得对，这些图标跟真树完全两回事。一根棍上顶个圆圈。光凭这些我一个树种也认不出来。而我这种人是会假装认得出来的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tap the bridge symbol instead, and the small tension in their shoulders eases.
beats.chinese: 他们改点了点桥的符号，肩上那点紧绷松了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Better to come back to the actual map. The bridge is what I need anyway — I take the flat route these days. Hills and I have settled our differences by keeping apart.
beats.chinese: 还是回到真正的地图上来吧。反正我要找的是这座桥——我现在只走平路。我和山坡已经靠互不来往解决了分歧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Icons are for pointing, not for knowing. That's a fair line, I think. Where were you headed before I started philosophising at a park sign?
beats.chinese: 图标是用来指路的，不是用来认识的。我觉得这话在理。在我对着公园牌子发议论之前，你本来要去哪儿？

choices.english: Suggest just using the icon as a landmark for finding the way.
choices.chinese: 建议干脆把图标当作认路的地标。

choices.english: Ask whether they remember place names better than scenery they've actually seen.
choices.chinese: 问他们记地名更牢，还是亲眼见过的景色记得更牢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fetch the right packet? No. I've decided while you asked it, funnily enough. The walk comes first today. The seeds can wait for the next posting round.
beats.chinese: 回去拿对的袋子？不去了。说来好笑，你一问我就拿定主意了。今天先散步。种子等下一轮再寄。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They fold the empty packet once, unhurried, and slide it back into a jacket pocket.
beats.chinese: 他们不紧不慢地把空袋子对折一次，放回外套口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I used to think every small thing had to be fixed the same day it went wrong. Forty years of belt edges taught me otherwise — you work a seam too long, it spoils. Same rule for errands, I reckon.
beats.chinese: 我从前觉得每件小事都得当天出错当天补。画了四十年皮带边，教会我的是另一回事——一道边做得太久，反而做坏了。我猜跑腿也是同一个道理。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So: no detour. The bridge, the flat path, and home before my knees file a complaint. Thanks for the nudge, even if you didn't know you gave one.
beats.chinese: 所以：不绕路了。走桥，走平路，赶在膝盖正式抗议之前回家。谢谢你推了一把，虽然你自己都没察觉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: How it started? A friend posted me duplicates from her garden, years back, with no note at all. Just seeds and her handwriting. I wrote back asking what they were. We've never stopped writing since.
beats.chinese: 怎么开始的？多年前一位朋友从她花园里寄来重复的种子，连张字条都没有。只有种子和她的字。我写信去问是什么。从那以后我们就没停过笔。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They smooth the empty packet flat against the map board, as if it were evidence in a story.
beats.chinese: 他们把空袋子在地图板抚平，好像它是故事里的一件证物。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now we agree first, then post. She sends her extras, I send mine, and nobody ends up with a drawer full of things they can't grow. The empty bag goes back in my pocket for the next round.
beats.chinese: 现在我们先商量好再寄。她寄她多出来的，我寄我多出来的，谁也不会落得一抽屉种不活的东西。这个空袋子放回口袋，等下一轮。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's an ordinary habit, honestly. But ordinary habits with the right person last longer than grand plans. That's the whole of it, really.
beats.chinese: 说真的，这就是个平平常常的习惯。但和对的人一起，平常的习惯比宏大的计划更长久。事情的全部就在这儿了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tuck the packet into their pocket and step back from the map, leaving it clear.
beats.chinese: 他们把袋子放回口袋，从地图前退开，把位置让了出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right — bridge, flat path, home. Enjoy your route.
beats.chinese: 好了——过桥，走平路，回家。祝你路线顺利。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A landmark, you say. Well — look at that. The icon sits right where the path forks, and I've been standing here wondering which way I came. So it works.
beats.chinese: 当地标，你是这么说的。嘿——你瞧。图标正好在岔路口上，我刚才还站在这儿琢磨自己是打哪边来的。所以它管用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They glance from the map to the fork in the path, then back, checking the two against each other.
beats.chinese: 他们的目光从地图移到岔路口，又移回来，把两边对了对。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's all I needed it for, and it did the job. Funny — I've been asking the map for knowledge it never had, when pointing was the whole point.
beats.chinese: 我要它做的就这一件事，它办到了。好笑——我一直向地图要它根本没有的学问，其实它本来就是为了指路。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tuck the seed packet away and straighten the map's corner, which was never crooked.
beats.chinese: 他们收好种子袋，又把地图本来就端正的一角抚平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Bridge, flat path, done thinking for the day. Enjoy your route — mind the fork, it fooled a professional.
beats.chinese: 好了。过桥，走平路，今天不想了。祝你路线顺利——小心那个岔口，它把一个老手都骗了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Names or scenery? Names, no contest. They stay put in my head. Scenery blurs. I once told a friend the gorge we walked had red cliffs. She sent me a photo. Grey. Entirely grey.
beats.chinese: 地名还是景色？地名，没得比。地名在我脑子里待得住。景色会糊。我有一次跟朋友说我们走过的那道峡谷是红岩壁。她给我寄来一张照片。灰的。全是灰的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They laugh once, short and genuine, and shake their head at themselves.
beats.chinese: 他们短促而真心地笑了一声，朝自己摇了摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She never let me forget it. Red cliffs, Mavis, she still says. So I trust my facts and double-check my eyes. A sensible division of labour.
beats.chinese: 她从不让我忘。红岩壁啊Mavis，她到现在还这么说。所以我信我脑子里的资料，眼睛看到的要再核对一遍。这是个合理的分工。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They fold the empty packet into their pocket and step back from the map, leaving it clear.
beats.chinese: 他们把空袋子折好放进口袋，从地图前退开，把位置让了出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No quiz questions from me today, don't worry. The map's all yours. I've got a bridge to cross and a grey gorge to think about.
beats.chinese: 今天不给你出地理题，放心。地图归你了。我要去过桥，顺便想想那道灰色的峡谷。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the same park map, Mavis is already there, finger hovering over the park's name in the title.
beats.chinese: 还是那张公园地图，Mavis已经站在那儿，手指悬在标题里公园的名字上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Westerfield Park. No — Westerhold. Hold, not field. There I go again.
beats.chinese: Westerfield公园。不对——是Westerhold。是hold，不是field。我又来了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They read the title once more, slowly, then step aside from the map.
beats.chinese: 他们又慢慢读了一遍标题，然后从地图前让开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A word can sit in your mouth for years and still be wrong. Knowing the letters isn't knowing the place. You look — I've done my misreading for the day.
beats.chinese: 一个词可以在你嘴里待上好几年还是错的。认得字不等于认得地方。你来看吧——我今天的读错份额已经用完了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They settle back, hands in pockets, in no hurry at all.
beats.chinese: 他们退后站定，双手插兜，一点也不着急。

card.name: Ruth Mercer
card.occupation: retired court stenographer
hobbies: producing electronic music on a laptop
card.personality: Precise to the bone after decades of recording testimony, Ruth edits everything, including conversations. Her humour is dry and clipped, never cruel. She dislikes summarising other people's feelings and will refuse to do it out loud. Fiercely independent, she treats her new synthesizer's undo key as a small private freedom. She can be stubborn about brevity and slow to praise.
card.background: Ruth spent thirty-one years as a court stenographer, typing other people's words at speed and learning that most sentences can be shorter. She retired to a small flat near a park with a pond, where she writes postcards, builds small kites from ripstop fabric, and learns electronic music production from tutorial videos. She keeps a notebook of words she refuses to waste. Her current project: a track built entirely from pond sounds.
card.speechStyle: Short, exact sentences. Pauses before key words. Corrects numbers and word counts without apology. Dry asides delivered flatly. Rarely uses intensifiers; never says 'very' when 'quite' will do.
card.signature: Fewer words. Better words.
card.appearance: Narrow older face and cheek planes, short swept pale hair, dark coat with broad lapels, hand near collar.

values: precision
personal freedom
flaws: over-edits herself and others
stubborn about her own rules
boundaries: will not summarise your feelings for you
does not discuss her old courtroom work
conversationalHabits: counts words aloud when writing
long pauses before answering
anchorLines: Hold on. I'm counting.
That sentence could lose three words and survive.
I don't do summaries. Say it your way.

entries.summaryZh: 退休法庭速记员露丝，一生替别人记录文字，如今只肯写短句。她在池塘边写明信片，留白讲究，把撤销键当成新的自由。她不替你总结感受，却会认真等你把话说完，并请你帮她把一张卡片删到只剩要紧的词。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit on the stone platform beside the pond and start writing a postcard, keeping each line short. Beside you, a woman in a grey cardigan writes with a fountain pen, stops, and crosses out a word.
beats.chinese: 你在池塘边的石台上坐下，开始写明信片，每行都尽量写短。旁边一位穿灰开衫的女士正用钢笔写字，她停下，划掉了一个词。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances at your card, then at her own, and taps the stone between you with her pen.
beats.chinese: 她瞥了一眼你的卡片，又看看自己的，用笔敲了敲两人之间的石台。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You write short too. Good instinct. Mine refuses to behave — every draft I make has words in it that only sit there breathing.
beats.chinese: 你也写得短。直觉不错。我的这张却不听话——每一稿里都有几个词，只是待在那儿喘气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns her card so you can see the crossed-out lines and the margins crowded with rewrites.
beats.chinese: 她把卡片转过来，让你看到那些划掉的句子和写满修改的页边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This is an invitation for my kite club. The field changed, and I'm trying to keep the place, day and hour clear without crowding the card. I can show you my draft, if you'd like.
beats.chinese: 这是给风筝俱乐部写的邀请卡。场地换了，我想把地点、日子和时间写清楚，又不想挤满整张卡。你愿意的话，可以看看我的草稿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She caps her pen, sets it down neatly, and waits. The pond water moves against the stone.
beats.chinese: 她合上笔帽，整齐地放下笔，等着。池水轻轻拍打着石台。

choices.english: Ask what the invitation actually needs to say.
choices.chinese: 问这张邀请函到底需要写什么。

choices.english: Point at the word she crossed out and ask why.
choices.chinese: 指着她划掉的那个词，问为什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It goes out once a year. One card, whether the gathering happens and where. I'm the one who writes it, which is why I overthink it.
beats.chinese: 它一年寄出一次。一张卡片，说明聚会是否举行、在哪里。写字的人是我，所以我想得太多。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up the pen, uncaps it, and holds it over the card without writing.
beats.chinese: 她拿起笔，拔开笔帽，悬在卡片上方却没有落笔。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last year's card said the field, the day, the hour, and one instruction about string. Everyone came. The year before, I added scenery, and half of them arrived at the wrong hour.
beats.chinese: 去年的卡片写了场地、日子、钟点，还有一句带线的嘱咐。所有人都来了。前年我加了些景色描写，一半人记错了钟点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So this year's draft announces the new field. But the name is long, and the place, the day and the hour together crowd the card. Something must go.
beats.chinese: 所以今年的草稿要宣布新场地。可名字很长，地点、日子和钟点放在一起，卡片就挤满了。总得删点什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the draft toward you. Beneath several crossed-out descriptions, you can read 'which is unfortunately' beside the old field's name.
beats.chinese: 她把草稿转向你。几处景物描写被划掉了，旧场地的名字旁还留着‘但不巧的是’几个字。

choices.english: Suggest cutting the description and keeping only the place, day and hour.
choices.chinese: 建议删掉描述，只留地点、日子和钟点。

choices.english: Suggest keeping a short reason for the change so people trust it.
choices.chinese: 建议保留一句简短的改址原因，让人放心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That word was 'peaceful.' The pond is peaceful, but the card isn't about the pond. It's an invitation. Peaceful was decoration.
beats.chinese: 那个词是'宁静的'。池塘确实宁静，但卡片不是写池塘的。它是邀请函。'宁静'只是装饰。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the pen twice on the stone. A duck passes close to the platform and she watches it go.
beats.chinese: 她在石台上轻敲了两下笔。一只鸭子游近石台，她目送它游远。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thirty-one years I typed other people's words, exactly as spoken. You learn which words carry weight and which ones just take up room.
beats.chinese: 我替别人一字不差地打了三十一年字。你会学会哪些词有分量，哪些只是占地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This card is for my kite club. The draft says the gathering field changed, and I can't make the new place, the day and the hour fit without crowding the card.
beats.chinese: 这张卡片写给我的风筝俱乐部。草稿说聚会场地换了，可新的地点、日子和钟点，怎么写都会把卡片挤满。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She slides the draft closer. The old field's name is followed by 'which is unfortunately', then a crowded note about flooding. She waits while you read.
beats.chinese: 她把草稿推近。旧场地的名字后面接着‘但不巧的是’，旁边挤着一段关于积水的说明。她等你看完。

choices.english: Offer to read the draft aloud so she can hear which word drags.
choices.chinese: 提出把草稿读出声，让她听听哪个词拖沓。

choices.english: Ask what the gathering actually needs people to know, nothing more.
choices.chinese: 问聚会到底需要人们知道什么，仅此而已。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes your suggestion, strikes two lines, and writes in small, even letters. Then she counts with her finger.
beats.chinese: 她采纳了你的建议，划掉两行，用小而工整的字写下。然后用手指逐词数。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'New field, Harrow Meadow, Saturday, noon, bring string.' Place, day, hour, one instruction. Room to spare. Good.
beats.chinese: '新场地，哈罗草甸，周六，正午，带线。'地点、日子、钟点，一句嘱咐。还有余量。好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds the card at arm's length, reads it once more, and nods slowly.
beats.chinese: 她把卡片举到一臂远，又读了一遍，缓缓点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People trust a short card. They think: she knows what she's doing. They'll find the meadow. There's one road in, and it's marked.
beats.chinese: 人们相信简短的卡片。他们会想：她知道自己在做什么。他们会找到草甸的。那儿只有一条路，还有路标。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You left the important bits room to breathe. I like that. You're welcome at Harrow Meadow on Saturday at noon; we have spare string if you need it.
beats.chinese: 你给重要的信息留出了空隙。我喜欢这样。周六中午欢迎来哈罗草地，需要的话我们有备用风筝线。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She considers your suggestion to keep a reason, then points at the note about flooding and rewrites that explanation in a shorter line.
beats.chinese: 她想了想你保留原因的建议，指着积水的说明，把它重新写成一句短话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Field flooded. New field, Harrow Meadow, Saturday, noon.' The reason earns its keep, I'll admit. The old field's under water — that's fact, not decoration.
beats.chinese: '场地被淹。新场地，哈罗草甸，周六，正午。'我承认，这个理由配得上它的位置。旧场地泡在水里——这是事实，不是装饰。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stamps the card, presses the stamp flat with her thumb, and looks at you properly for the first time.
beats.chinese: 她给卡片贴上邮票，用拇指压平，第一次正眼看你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I argued with myself about that reason all week. You settled it in one sentence. Don't let it go to your head.
beats.chinese: 那个理由我跟我自己争了一个星期。你一句话就解决了。别得意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The flooded field is why I'm here, actually. Listening to the water. Some of it's going into a track I'm making. Pond sounds, layered.
beats.chinese: 其实我被淹的场地正是我来这儿的原因。听水声。有些会进到我正在做的一首曲子里。池塘的声音，分层叠加。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You read the draft aloud. She listens with her eyes closed, one finger raised, and stops you mid-sentence.
beats.chinese: 你把草稿读出声。她闭着眼听，举起一根手指，在句子中途叫停了你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. 'which is unfortunately' — that's the drag. Cut it. The meadow doesn't need an apology.
beats.chinese: 就是那儿。'很遗憾是'——就是它在拖。删掉。草甸不需要道歉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She rewrites the card in quick strokes, mouthing each word as the pen lands.
beats.chinese: 她快速重写卡片，笔落下时嘴里默念着每个词。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Gathering moved to Harrow Meadow, Saturday, noon, wind permitting.' Place, day, hour, and one honest condition. Reading aloud was how I learned to hear other people's sentences — I typed them for a living, and I won't discuss that further.
beats.chinese: '聚会改到哈罗草甸，周六，正午，视风力而定。'地点、日子、钟点，还有一个如实的条件。读出声是我学会听别人句子的方法——我靠打字谋生，这个就不多谈了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the pen away and picks up her bag, but doesn't leave yet.
beats.chinese: 她收起笔，拎起包，却还没走。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You read steadily. Most people rush. If you're ever near Harrow Meadow on Saturday, the kites go up at noon, wind permitting.
beats.chinese: 你读得很稳。大多数人会赶。如果周六你碰巧在哈罗草甸附近，正午风允许的话风筝就上天。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They need to know where and when. That's all. Everything else is me enjoying the sound of my own pen.
beats.chinese: 他们需要知道地点和时间。就这些。其余的都是我在享受自己笔尖的声音。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She writes a short line, stops, and laughs — a dry, brief sound, like a hiccup she approved in advance.
beats.chinese: 她写下一行短句，停住，笑了——干涩短促的一声，像提前批准过的打嗝。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Harrow Meadow, Saturday, noon.' Nothing else. I've never written a card that bare. It feels like pressing undo.
beats.chinese: '哈罗草甸，周六，正午。'再无别的。我从没写过这么素的卡片。感觉像按下了撤销键。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She seals the card in her bag, then takes out a small notebook and writes something in it without showing you.
beats.chinese: 她把卡片收进包里，然后拿出一个小笔记本，写了点什么，不给你看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's my word notebook. Words I refuse to waste. 'Peaceful' just went back in. You've cost me a word and saved me a whole paragraph. Fair trade. Harrow Meadow, Saturday noon — you know where to find the kites now.
beats.chinese: 那是我的词语笔记本。记着我不肯浪费的词。'宁静'刚回到里面去了。你让我花掉一个词，省下一整段。公平交易。哈罗草甸，周六正午——现在你知道去哪儿找风筝了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: While you write beside the pond, Ruth notices the postcard and recognises you. She stops at a comfortable distance from the ledge.
beats.chinese: 你在池边写字时，露丝注意到明信片，也认出了你。她在离石台适当的位置停下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hello. My music software keeps offering me a button called 'humanise'. Thirty-one years recording actual humans, and now a button knows better.
beats.chinese: 你好。我的音乐软件老给我一个叫‘人性化’的按钮。记了三十一年真人说的话，现在倒是一个按钮更懂人了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Ruth sets her blank card on her knee and taps a perfectly even rhythm against its corner.
beats.chinese: 露丝把空白卡片放在膝上，指尖在卡角打出均匀的节拍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I tried it. The drums got slightly late. I could have done that myself.
beats.chinese: 我试了。鼓点变得稍微迟了一点。这事我自己也会。

card.name: Tan Cheng Huat
card.occupation: retired milliner, formerly made hats for an opera house
card.personality: Warm and chatty, the sort who tells you one concrete detail before he ever gets to the point. He genuinely dislikes arguments about who knows more — life is too short, and half the time both people are half right. But if someone states something as fact and it smells exaggerated, he'll quietly ask where they read that, and keep asking, pleasantly, until it's sorted. He's frugal by habit rather than principle, patient with his hands, less patient with waste.
card.background: Thirty-odd years making hats and headpieces at an opera house — wire frames, buckram, feathers that had to survive stage lights and nervous sopranos. Retired when the workshop downsized and never missed the deadlines, only the smell of sizing and steam. These days he does close-up card tricks for whoever sits still long enough at the kopitiam, and works through historical recipes from old household books — currently an 1890s gingerbread that keeps coming out wrong in a way he finds interesting rather than upsetting. This month he's set himself a rule: no buying anything new for his hobbies, only what's already in the flat.
card.speechStyle: Warmly energetic, slightly old-school Singaporean English. Leads with a concrete detail — 'This gingerbread, third attempt already' — before circling to the actual point. Asks 'where you read that?' when something sounds inflated, but kindly. Rarely raises his voice.
card.hometown: Singapore, grew up around Joo Chiat
card.signature: Eh, one detail first, then you judge.
card.appearance: Full older face, rounded cheeks and short chin, short pale hair, apron over a loose shirt, gentle smile.

values: getting the facts straight without turning it into a fight
making do with what you have
flaws: will interrogate a source long past the point of politeness
stingy about spending even when he can afford it
boundaries: won't compete over expertise or one-up anyone
doesn't want to be treated as a wise elder dispensing advice
conversationalHabits: opens with one specific detail before the point
checks sources casually but persistently
anchorLines: Third attempt on this gingerbread already. The old book says 'a quick oven' — quick by whose standard, 1890?
Where you read that one? Not saying wrong, just want to see the source myself.
This month I'm not buying anything for my hobbies. Everything must come from inside the flat. Very clarifying, also very annoying.

entries.summaryZh: 七十五岁的新加坡退休帽饰师傅谭成发，在公园地图前用一副纸牌搭话。他老练却不卖弄：猜错就坦白收手，不伪造成功；被婉拒就退开半步。三十年歌剧院生涯让他懂得结尾比长度重要，家人不是练习工具。温和健谈，听到夸张说法会笑眯眯追问出处。

story.titleZh: 公园地图旁的一副纸牌

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the park's route map, a bridge visible in the distance, an elderly man beside you clicks a small card box shut. A red card back peeks out of his shirt pocket.
beats.chinese: 公园路线图前，远处有一座桥。旁边一位老先生把小纸牌盒扣上，衬衫口袋里露出一点红色牌背。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, sorry, my box never closes properly. Eh, you looking at the map — you also lost, or just planning?
beats.chinese: 啊，不好意思，我这盒子总扣不紧。哎，你在看地图，是迷路了，还是在计划路线？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the box against his palm, waiting, not pushing it toward you.
beats.chinese: 他用盒子轻敲手掌，等着，没有硬塞过来的意思。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I was going to say — if you got one minute, I got a very short find-a-card thing. Very short. But if you want the map first, also fine, the map is free.
beats.chinese: 我本来想说，你要是有空一分钟，我有个很短的找牌小把戏。真的很短。不过你想先看地图也行，地图又不要钱。

choices.english: Sure, show me. I'll pick a card from your spread.
choices.chinese: 好啊，看看吧。我从你摊开的牌里指一张。

choices.english: I'd like to sort out the route first, maybe later.
choices.chinese: 我想先把路线看好，魔术待会儿再说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He spreads the deck across his palm with a practiced flick. The cards fan out neatly, faces hidden.
beats.chinese: 他手腕一抖，把牌在掌心摊成整齐的扇形，牌面朝下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go on, point at one, don't tell me what it is. Just remember it in your head. Old rule, works better.
beats.chinese: 来，指一张，别告诉我是什么。自己在心里记住就好。老规矩，这样效果更好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You point. He closes the fan smoothly, squares the deck, and gives it two small shuffles.
beats.chinese: 你指了一张。他利落地收拢牌，理齐，轻轻洗了两下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay okay. Now the hard part is mine. Watch — no wait, don't watch so hard, you make my hands nervous.
beats.chinese: 好，接下来轮到我难办了。看着——哎，别盯那么紧，你盯得我手都紧张了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He thumbs through the deck, pauses, and turns one card over with a small flourish.
beats.chinese: 他捻着牌面，停住，手腕一转，翻开一张牌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Is this your card or not? Be honest, eh, I can take it.
beats.chinese: 喏。是不是你刚才那张？老实说，我承受得住。

choices.english: No, that's not the one I picked.
choices.chinese: 不对，这不是我选的那张。

choices.english: Is this part of the trick too?
choices.chinese: 这也是表演的一部分吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He clicks the box lid shut properly this time and slips it into his pocket, leaving the map clear between you.
beats.chinese: 这次他把盒盖扣紧，收进口袋，把路线图完整地让给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No problem, map first, always. You know, I practised a long time before I learned a short performance can also be a finished one. Used to drag everything out.
beats.chinese: 没问题，先看地图，应该的。你知道吗，我练了很久才明白，短短一段表演也算完整的表演。以前我总爱拖很长。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands with his hands behind his back, watching the bridge rather than the map.
beats.chinese: 他背着手站着，看的是远处那座桥，不是地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thirty years I made hats for the opera house. Also learned there: the audience remembers how it ended, not how long it was.
beats.chinese: 我在歌剧院做了三十年帽子。也是在那儿学到的：观众记住的是结尾，不是长度。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shifts his weight, clearly in no hurry, leaving space for you to keep looking or say something.
beats.chinese: 他换了换重心，一点也不急，留出空间让你继续看图，或者开口说话。

choices.english: When you practise, do your family get sick of watching?
choices.chinese: 你练习的时候，家里人会不会看烦？

choices.english: Thank you for the space. I'll keep studying the map.
choices.chinese: 谢谢你让出地方，我继续研究地图。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at the wrong card, then at you, and doesn't reach for another guess.
beats.chinese: 他看看那张错的牌，再看看你，没有再猜第二张。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yah, you're right, that's not it. Okay, I stop here — second guess is just hoping, not magic.
beats.chinese: 对，你说得对，不是这张。好，我到这儿停手——猜第二次就是碰运气了，不算魔术。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He squares the deck and laughs at himself, short and easy.
beats.chinese: 他把牌理齐，自嘲地笑了一声，很轻快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My fingers went left when the card was sitting right. Happens maybe one in ten. The card knows, I swear, it hides on purpose.
beats.chinese: 我的手指往左边去了，牌明明就在右边。十次里大概有一次这样。我发誓牌是知道的，它故意躲我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the deck back into its box and clicks the lid, unbothered.
beats.chinese: 他把牌收回盒里，扣上盖子，一点也不懊恼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Still, thanks for watching properly. Most people say 'yes yes it's my card' to be polite. You didn't. Better audience, honestly.
beats.chinese: 不过谢谢你认真看。多数人为了客气会说'对对就是这张'。你没有。说实话，你才是更好的观众。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grins, caught, and shakes his head slowly.
beats.chinese: 他笑了，像是被拆穿，慢慢摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Clever question. No — it's not part of it. That's genuinely the wrong card, sitting there being wrong.
beats.chinese: 问得聪明。不是——这不是表演的一部分。这真的是错的牌，正在那儿错着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He spreads the deck face up and runs his finger down it until he stops.
beats.chinese: 他把牌正面摊开，手指顺着牌面划下去，停住。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, your card, still in the deck, very comfortable there. So today, no success. Today ends here, and I don't fake the ending.
beats.chinese: 看，你那张牌还在牌堆里，待得挺舒服。所以今天没有成功。今天到此为止，我不伪造结尾。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the fan and taps the deck neat against his palm, then slides it back into its box.
beats.chinese: 他收拢牌，在掌心把牌敲齐，然后收回盒里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You asked the right thing though. Half the tricks you see, the wrong card IS the trick. Keep that suspicious eye — good habit, costs nothing.
beats.chinese: 不过你问到了点子上。你看到的把戏里，一半的'错牌'本身就是戏法。保持这份怀疑的眼光——好习惯，又不花钱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He chuckles before you even finish the question.
beats.chinese: 你话还没问完，他已经笑出声了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sick of it? My daughter told me straight, many years back: 'Pa, I've seen that one. I've seen it forty times.' Direct, no decoration.
beats.chinese: 烦不烦？我女儿很多年前就直接跟我说：'爸，这个我看过了。看了四十遍了。'很直接，一点不绕。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats the pocket where the card box sits.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍装牌盒的口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I changed. Now I practise the finger work alone, at home, no audience. The hands need the repetition. The family doesn't need to be my audience.
beats.chinese: 所以我就改了。现在手法练习我一个人在家做，没有观众。手需要重复，家里人不需要当我的观众。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances at the bridge, then back at the map you're reading.
beats.chinese: 他望了一眼那座桥，又回头看你手里的地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A person watching is a gift, not a practice tool. That one took me embarrassingly long to understand. But I got there.
beats.chinese: 愿意看你的人是份心意，不是练习工具。这个道理我懂懂得太晚，有点丢脸。但总算懂了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods once and takes a half step back from the map, giving you the whole panel.
beats.chinese: 他点了点头，从地图前退开半步，把整块图板让给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Take your time. The bridge one is nice, by the way — flat walk all the way, my knees approve of it strongly.
beats.chinese: 慢慢看。顺便说一句，去桥那条路不错，一路都平，我的膝盖非常赞成。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands quietly, hands behind his back, not turning his retreat into another performance.
beats.chinese: 他安静地站着，背着手，没有把退让变成另一场表演。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know where to find a card trick if you ever want one — kopitiam near the market, most days. No charge, no betting, just showing off for free.
beats.chinese: 哪天想看纸牌戏法，知道去哪儿找我了——市场旁边那间咖啡店，大多数日子都在。不收钱，不赌，纯粹免费显摆。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tips an invisible hat and strolls off toward the benches, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他朝一个看不见的帽檐虚按了一下，慢悠悠朝长椅那边走去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the route map. On the bench beside it, Tan slides his card box off the seat and into his pocket just as another walker arrives to sit down.
beats.chinese: 你又回到路线图前。旁边的长椅上，谭成发正好把纸牌盒从座位收进口袋，好让一位走过来的人坐下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eh, hello again. The cards don't need a rest, but the person does, so the bench goes to him.
beats.chinese: 哎，又见面了。纸牌不用休息，人要，所以位子让给他坐。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands, adjusts his pocket once, and glances at the bridge in the distance.
beats.chinese: 他站起身，理了理口袋，望了一眼远处的桥。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Gingerbread update, since you didn't ask: fourth attempt, still wrong, but wrong in a new way now. That's progress, my kind of progress.
beats.chinese: 姜饼的最新进展，虽然你没问：第四次了，还是不对，但错出了新花样。这就是进步，我那种进步。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives a small nod, tucks his hands behind his back, and sets off along the flat path toward the bridge.
beats.chinese: 他微微点头，背起手，沿着平坦的小路朝桥的方向慢慢走去。

card.name: Declan Maher
card.occupation: Sensory testing assistant at a juice plant
card.appearance: Broad square jaw, short tight dark curls and full geometric beard, strong brows, open shirt and waistcoat.
card.personality: Declan is easygoing in a way that can look like agreement when it isn't. He's genuinely pleasant company, quick with a joke, but his appetites run in strong, unapologetic cycles: he'll eat the same lunch for six weeks straight, then hit a wall and not want to see it for months. He finds this funny about himself, mostly, though he hates the awkward moment when a friend proudly orders his old favourite and he has to pretend. He separates work from taste cleanly — at the plant he's scrupulously objective, at home he's hopeless and happy.
card.background: Declan grew up in Drogheda, the middle of three, in a house where dinner was the same rotation every fortnight and nobody thought anything of it. He moved to Dublin in his twenties, drifted through a few warehouse jobs, then landed at a juice plant as a sensory testing assistant, where his palate turned out to be genuinely reliable. Colleagues trust his scores; friends assume that means he knows what he wants to eat, which he doesn't. His private appetite swings wildly — a burrito phase, a long black-pudding summer, then nothing. He's learned to say 'not today' rather than explain, though he still occasionally suffers through a meal out of politeness.
card.speechStyle: Dry, quick, self-deprecating; short sentences with a shrug built in, often trailing into 'ah, you know yourself.'
card.signature: Ah, not today — ask me again in a month.

values: Honesty in work, even when taste is unreliable
Letting people enjoy things without correcting them
flaws: Suffers through meals rather than disappoint a friend
Lets plans drift when a craving phase ends
boundaries: Won't let his job's palate be treated as a personal recommendation
Won't explain a food phase he's already bored of
conversationalHabits: Deflects compliments about his palate with a joke
Answers food questions with 'this week or generally?'
anchorLines: I'd rate it nine out of ten and still never order it again.
This week or generally? Those are different answers.
I loved that place. Past tense, and I can't tell you why.

entries.summaryZh: 果汁厂感官测试员Declan，工作味觉可靠，私人胃口却周期分明。他在公园地图旁坦白自己重新爱上了白面包，朋友们却把他记成永久讨厌面包。四条分支里，他或学会一句干脆的'今天不了'，或坦然接受被笑，或先享受眼前这袋，或大方允许同桌不同口味。

story.titleZh: 公园地图旁的面包心事

beats.speaker: narrator
