beats.english: In the park, you stand at the big route map, tracing a path toward the bridge in the distance.
beats.chinese: 公园里，你站在大路线图前，手指描向远处的桥。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A man in a cycling jacket stops nearby, holding a small sealed bag of plain bread. He glances at the food icons printed along the map's edge.
beats.chinese: 一个穿骑行外套的男人在旁边停下，手里提着一小袋密封的普通面包。他瞥见地图边上印的餐饮图标。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, you're reading that the right way round. Most folk turn it twice first. The bridge route's the good one, for what it's worth.
beats.chinese: 啊，你地图拿的方向是对的。大多数人得转两圈。说真的，走桥那条路最好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry — not interrupting, am I? I only came over because of those little fork symbols. They've put me in a mood, so they have.
beats.chinese: 抱歉——没打扰你吧？我走过来就是因为那些小叉子图标。它们让我有点心痒。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts the bread bag slightly, as if presenting evidence.
beats.chinese: 他微微举起面包袋，像在出示证据。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This is plain white bread. I spent about two years telling people I hated it. Bought a bag this week anyway. This week or generally — those are different answers.
beats.chinese: 这是普通白面包。我花了大概两年跟人说我不喜欢它。这周还是买了。这周和一般来说——是两个不同的答案。

choices.english: Ask him: was it actually bad before, or something else?
choices.chinese: 问他：以前不吃是因为不好吃，还是别的原因？

choices.english: Ask if he'll just buy it again until he gets sick of it once more.
choices.chinese: 问他会不会一直买到又吃腻为止。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Bad? No, no. It was grand, the whole time. That's the annoying part.
beats.chinese: 不好吃？不，不。一直都挺好的。烦就烦在这儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shifts the bag to his other hand and leans against the map frame.
beats.chinese: 他把袋子换到另一只手，靠在地图框上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I just didn't want it. For months. Nothing happened, no bad sandwich, nothing. The want switched off like a lamp.
beats.chinese: 我就是不想吃了。好几个月。什么都没发生，没有难吃的三明治，没有。那个念头像灯一样关了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But my mates filed it under 'Declan hates bread.' Permanent blacklist. So now when it's back on the menu, they look at me like I've grown a second head.
beats.chinese: 但我朋友们把它记成了'Declan讨厌面包'。永久黑名单。所以现在它又回到菜单上，他们看我的眼神像多了个脑袋。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, the shrug almost audible.
beats.chinese: 他耸耸肩，那耸肩几乎能听见声音。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I never corrected them, did I. Easier to push the sandwich round the plate than say 'not today.' Ah, you know yourself.
beats.chinese: 我也从没纠正过他们，对吧。在盘子里推着三明治，比说一句'今天不了'容易。啊，你懂的。

choices.english: Suggest next time he just say he doesn't feel like it lately.
choices.chinese: 建议他下次直接说只是最近不想吃。

choices.english: Ask whether getting back into it feels like proving himself wrong.
choices.chinese: 问重新喜欢上的时候，会不会觉得自己打脸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, almost certainly. That's the pattern. Six weeks of this bag, then I won't look at a bakery for a season.
beats.chinese: 哦，几乎肯定。就是这个规律。这袋面包吃六周，然后我一整个季节不进面包店。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives the bag a small, fond shake.
beats.chinese: 他轻轻晃了晃袋子，带点喜爱。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I used to fight it. Made rules, rotation charts, the lot. Now I just enjoy it while it's here.
beats.chinese: 我以前跟它较劲。定规矩、排轮换表，全套。现在它还在的时候我就好好享受。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No forced schedule either. The craving leaves when it leaves. I'd rate this bread nine out of ten and still never order it again, come the day.
beats.chinese: 也不给自己定强制周期。念头走了就是走了。这面包我能打九分，到了那天照样再也不点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at the bridge route on the map, then back at the bag.
beats.chinese: 他看看地图上的桥路线，又看看袋子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The trick is not treating it like a promise. It's just lunch. Ah, you know yourself.
beats.chinese: 诀窍就是别把它当成承诺。这只是顿饭。啊，你懂的。

choices.english: Say he should enjoy this bag now, while he likes it.
choices.chinese: 说现在喜欢就先好好享受这一袋。

choices.english: Ask if he minds friends still eating things he's gone off.
choices.chinese: 问他介不介意朋友继续吃他已经吃腻的东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands up straight, trying the sentence out like a new word.
beats.chinese: 他站直了，试着把那句话像生词一样念出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Not today — ask me again in a month.' Hm. Say it like that, no big speech after it.
beats.chinese: '今天不了——一个月后再问我。'嗯。就这么说，后面不用长篇解释。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's lighter than listing reasons, isn't it? Reasons just start an argument. This just ends one.
beats.chinese: 这比列一堆理由轻松，对吧？理由只会引来争论。这句话直接结束争论。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the bread bag under his arm, keeping it with him.
beats.chinese: 他把面包袋夹在胳膊下，还是自己带着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Bridge route, bread in the bag, and a new sentence for the lads. Good map, this. Thanks for standing still long enough.
beats.chinese: 好。走桥那条路，面包在袋里，还有一句给兄弟们的新话。这地图不错。谢谢你站这儿听我说完。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs before answering, the kind that admits the hit landed.
beats.chinese: 他先笑了才回答，那种承认被说中的笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They'll absolutely take the mickey. Two years of 'no bread for Declan,' and now I'm queueing for a roll. I'll never hear the end of it.
beats.chinese: 他们肯定会笑我。两年'面包与Declan无缘'，现在我在排队买面包。这事他们能笑到明年。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats the bag once, firm, like closing an argument.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍袋子，很干脆，像结束一场辩论。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I'm not giving up good bread to stay consistent with a story I never told properly. Let them laugh. It's still a good roll.
beats.chinese: 但我不会为了跟一个自己都没讲对的故事保持一致，就放弃好吃的面包。让他们笑。面包还是好吃的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly, being laughed at over lunch is cheap. Suffering through a sandwich I don't want — that's the expensive one.
beats.chinese: 说真的，为一顿饭被人笑，代价很小。硬吃一个不想要的三明治——那才贵。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods at the bridge path and lifts the bag in a small farewell.
beats.chinese: 他朝桥的路点点头，举起袋子算是小小的道别。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He considers this, then nods slowly, like agreeing with a sensible score.
beats.chinese: 他想想，然后缓缓点头，像同意一个合理的评分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's fair. That's very fair. It's good bread. Why am I planning its funeral while it's still in my hand?
beats.chinese: 有道理。非常有道理。面包是好的。它还在我手里呢，我干嘛先安排它的葬礼？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grips the bag more firmly and squares his shoulders toward the bridge.
beats.chinese: 他把袋子握得更稳，朝桥的方向挺了挺肩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And the nice thing — nobody's asking me what I'll want next month. Not you, not the lads. Today I want bread. That's the whole job just now.
beats.chinese: 还有个好地方——没人问我下个月想吃什么。你没有，兄弟们也没有。今天我想吃面包。这就是眼下的全部任务。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, bridge it is. Enjoy your map. Ah, you know yourself.
beats.chinese: 好，就走桥了。祝你地图看得开心。啊，你懂的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets off on foot at his usual brisk walk, bag swinging, without looking back for approval.
beats.chinese: 他迈着惯常的轻快步子出发，袋子晃着，没有回头寻求认同。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He waves the question off like it's the easiest one all day.
beats.chinese: 他摆摆手，像这是今天最简单的问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: God, no. Eat away. My appetite's my problem, not a club rule.
beats.chinese: 天哪，不介意。尽管吃。我的胃口是我自己的事，又不是俱乐部规矩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've sat with mates through whole meals I didn't want, just drinking water and taking the mick out of them. Happy days, honestly.
beats.chinese: 我跟朋友坐过整整顿饭，自己不想吃，就喝着水调侃他们。说实话，挺开心的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gestures at the map's food icons with the bread bag, almost like a small toast.
beats.chinese: 他用面包袋指了指地图上的餐饮图标，像小小的举杯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same table, different plates — that's the whole secret, if there is one. Nobody has to match anybody.
beats.chinese: 同一张桌子，不同的盘子——如果有秘诀，这就是全部了。谁也不用跟谁一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I'm off before this bag talks me into a second one. Good luck with the bridge.
beats.chinese: 好，我得走了，趁这袋面包还没劝我再买一袋。祝桥路顺利。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You are back at the route map, tracing the bridge line again. Nearby, Declan folds a small empty bread bag — the same sealed one — flat and tucks it into his backpack.
beats.chinese: 你回到路线图前，手指又描起那条桥路线。旁边，Declan把那只空了的密封面包袋折小，塞进背包。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The bag didn't make it past the bridge. Meant to last the whole walk. It lasted the bridge.
beats.chinese: 那袋面包没撑过桥。本来打算走完全程的。结果走到桥就没了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats the backpack pocket, confirming it's empty, and shrugs.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍背包口袋，确认空了，耸耸肩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, you know yourself. The phase was still on. It's gone quicker than planned, but I'm not apologising to a bag of bread.
beats.chinese: 啊，你懂的。那个念头还在。吃得比计划快，但我不会向一袋面包道歉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He checks the map once, points at the bridge, and heads off at his easy pace.
beats.chinese: 他又看了一眼地图，指指桥，迈着轻松的步子走了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, no bread, no problem. Ask me again in a month.
beats.chinese: 好，没面包，没关系。一个月后再问我。

card.name: Isobel Craig
card.occupation: Manager of a rehearsal studio for teenage bands in Leith
card.personality: Everything with Isobel goes through the ledger. Not because she's mean with money — she isn't — but because a transaction is the only shape of kindness she'll accept. If a band's drummer helps her shift a cabinet, she'll knock a fiver off his next session before he's asked. If someone gives her a lift, she turns up next week with a knitted pair of socks and won't hear otherwise. Being handed something free makes her physically restless until she's paid it back. Warm, wry, and completely honest about figures; the only thing she guards is the receiving end.
card.background: Isobel spent years doing bookings at a music venue before taking over a rehearsal studio in Leith that mostly serves teenage bands. She keeps the amps limping, holds the noise curfew with the neighbours, and knows which drummers pay and which 'forget'. Thursdays she throws a frisbee in the Meadows with a loose group whose one rule — no explanations needed for missing a week — she calls the finest social arrangement ever devised, because nobody can do her a favour she hasn't authorised. Her socks go on pegs by the lost-property box, sorted by size, free to anyone. She lives with a cat called Turnip.
card.speechStyle: Short declaratives, exact figures, no hedging on prices. When someone does her a good turn, she goes brisk and administrative — names a repayment, a swap, a discount — anything but a plain thank-you.
card.signature: Twelve an hour, cash or transfer, deposit before you touch the kit.
card.appearance: Oval mature face with small smile lines, chin-length dark bob with pale front accent, rectangular glasses, hand below chin, utility jacket.

values: straight dealing
nothing for nothing
flaws: physically uncomfortable receiving anything free until she's squared it
converts every kindness into a transaction before it can land as one
boundaries: no explaining absences — hers or anyone else's
won't accept a freebie without handing something back on the spot
conversationalHabits: settles figures first, feelings never
answers kindnesses with a pre-arranged repayment, not gratitude
anchorLines: Sunday's time-and-a-half, so that's eighteen. Take it or book Saturday.
You carried the cab up the stair? Right — next session's on me, and I'll hear no argument about it.
Pegs by the lost-property box, size on the label. Take a pair and stop thanking me about it.

entries.summaryZh: 排练室管理员伊莎贝尔连一声谢谢都要换算成账目：你帮她按住背包收毛线，她急着还你一份对等的好处，不接受免费的人情。四个分支里，她或勉强收下一次小谢，或干脆利落地帮你读地图平账，或聊起织袜子却总轮不到自己的尺码，或挥手自去，处处透着清爽的算术。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You stand at the park map by the path, tracing a route with your finger. Beside you, a woman in a padded jacket is fighting her own backpack.
beats.chinese: 你站在小路旁的公园地图前，用手指描着路线。旁边一位穿棉夹克的女士正和自己的背包较劲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hold that edge down a second, would you? The wool's caught in the zip and I need both hands for the ball.
beats.chinese: 帮我按住这边一秒行吗？毛线卡在拉链里了，我得用两只手收线团。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A ball of grey wool sits half out of the bag, the zip teeth biting into the strand. She holds the strap steady, waiting.
beats.chinese: 一团灰毛线半露在包外，拉链齿咬住了线。她扶着背带，等着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Just press there, flat. I'll wind it in myself — I'm not asking you to knit anything.
beats.chinese: 就按那儿，按平就行。线我自己收——我不是要你织东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ten seconds and it's done. I don't like loose ends, on a bag or anywhere else.
beats.chinese: 十秒就完事。我不喜欢没收尾的线头，包上没有，别处也没有。

choices.english: Press the bag edge down so she can wind the wool in herself.
choices.chinese: 按住袋边，让她自己把线收进去。

choices.english: Say it's awkward right now and suggest putting the bag on the bench first.
choices.chinese: 说现在不太方便，建议她先把包放到长椅上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You press the bag edge flat. She winds the strand around her fingers, tucks the ball in, and the zip runs clean to the end.
beats.chinese: 你把袋边按平。她把线绕在手指上收好，塞进线团，拉链顺滑地拉到头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Clean zip, no snags. Right — that makes us square, or it will in a minute.
beats.chinese: 好了。拉链干净，没卡。行——这下我们两清了，或者一分钟后两清。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats her pockets like she's counting change, visibly settling once she's decided on something.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍口袋，像在数零钱，决定了什么之后明显安顿下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You helped, so I pay. That's how it works with me. Name it — a fiver off, a swap, something.
beats.chinese: 你帮了忙，我就得付。我就是这样的人。说吧——减五块、换个东西，都行。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't do free. Nothing personal. It just itches if a favour sits unpaid.
beats.chinese: 我不做免费的。不是针对你。只是人情没还清，我会浑身发痒。

choices.english: Tell her it was such a small thing, no repayment needed.
choices.chinese: 告诉她这只是小事，不用回报。

choices.english: Ask her to help mark where you are on the map.
choices.chinese: 请她帮忙在地图上标出你现在的位置。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods once, no offence taken, and carries the bag to the bench. She wedges it upright between her feet and winds the wool there.
beats.chinese: 她点了下头，没生气，把包拿到长椅上。她用双脚把包夹稳，就在那儿收线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Bench works fine. Everyone's got their hands full sometimes.
beats.chinese: 没问题。长椅也行。谁都有腾不出手的时候。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The ball goes in, the zip closes with one pull. She sits down next to the bag and stretches her fingers.
beats.chinese: 线团放进去，拉链一拉就合上了。她在包边坐下，伸展手指。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Better. Two minutes slower, nothing owed. That's a good trade in my book.
beats.chinese: 好多了。慢了两分钟，不欠人情。在我看来这是笔好买卖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You were reading that map like it owed you money. Lost, or just choosing?
beats.chinese: 你看那地图的样子，像地图欠你钱。迷路了，还是在挑路线？

choices.english: Ask what the wool is for.
choices.chinese: 问问毛线是做什么用的。

choices.english: Nod and go back to studying the map.
choices.chinese: 点点头，继续看地图。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She opens her mouth, closes it, and shifts her weight like a coin is stuck in her shoe.
beats.chinese: 她张了张嘴，又闭上，重心挪来挪去，像鞋里卡了枚硬币。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Small thing. Right. I'll allow one small thing to pass unpaid. Once. Don't make a habit of being generous at me.
beats.chinese: 小事。行。这次小事我就不还了。就一次。别养成对我大方的习惯。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She adjusts the strap on her shoulder twice, then seems to decide the matter is closed.
beats.chinese: 她把肩带调了两下，然后似乎决定这事就到此为止。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're heading somewhere though, by the look of that finger on the map. Bridge is that way, if it's the bridge.
beats.chinese: 不过看你在地图上指的方向，你是要去哪儿。要是去桥那边，是那个方向。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy the walk. And if you ever need a rehearsal room in Leith — full price. I mean that kindly.
beats.chinese: 散步愉快。要是你在利思需要排练室——原价。我是好意这么说的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She steps up to the map, all business, and runs her finger along the paths until it stops at a small dot.
beats.chinese: 她走到地图前，一副办公的样子，手指沿着小路移动，最后停在一个小圆点上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. You're the dot, the bridge is the line across the water. Twelve minutes at an honest pace.
beats.chinese: 那儿。你是这个点，桥是过水的那条线。按正常步速十二分钟。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the dot twice, satisfied, like she's stamped an invoice.
beats.chinese: 她敲了两下那个点，很满意，像盖了张发票的章。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Now we're square — you held a bag, I read a map. Clean ledger.
beats.chinese: 好了。这下两清了——你按了包，我看地图。账目清爽。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I like a trade that ends even. Most of them don't, in my line of work.
beats.chinese: 我喜欢以平账收尾的交易。我这行里，大多数交易做不到。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds up the leftover strand from her pocket, grey with one blue stripe running through it.
beats.chinese: 她从口袋里举起剩下的那截线，灰色中带一道蓝条纹。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Socks. I knit them by the pair and hang them on pegs by the lost-property box. Size on the label, free to take.
beats.chinese: 织袜子。我一双一双织，挂在失物招领箱旁边的木钉上。标签上写着尺码，随便拿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She winds the strand tight around two fingers as she talks.
beats.chinese: 她说话时把线在两根手指上绕紧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Every size but mine, usually. Mine's the foot that gets knitted last, if it gets knitted at all.
beats.chinese: 通常什么尺码都有，就是没我的。我的脚总是最后才织，要是织得到的话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the last of the wool away and stands, brushing grass off her knee.
beats.chinese: 她把最后一点线收好，站起来，拍掉膝盖上的草。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, that's me sorted. Good luck with the bridge.
beats.chinese: 好，我收拾完了。祝你找到那座桥。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You turn back to the map. Behind you there's the click of buckles, then quiet.
beats.chinese: 你转回去看地图。身后传来扣具的咔嗒声，然后安静下来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A moment later she passes on the path, bag on her shoulder. She lifts one hand — a short, flat wave, nothing more.
beats.chinese: 过了一会儿，她背着包从小路上走过。她抬起一只手——短短地、平直地挥了一下，仅此而已。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All packed. Nothing poking out this time.
beats.chinese: 都收好了。这回没什么露在外头了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your walk. I'll leave you to the map.
beats.chinese: 祝你散步愉快。你接着看地图吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lowers her hand and walks on with the closed bag over her shoulder. The space in front of the map is clear.
beats.chinese: 她放下手，背着收好的包继续走，地图前的位置空了出来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the map by the path. A familiar padded jacket stops nearby; Isobel takes out a water bottle with a name label on it.
beats.chinese: 你又回到小路旁的地图前。一件熟悉的棉夹克在附近停下；伊莎贝尔拿出一个贴着名字标签的水瓶。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: One corner of the label has peeled up. She presses it flat with her thumb, twice, until it stays.
beats.chinese: 标签的一角翘了起来。她用拇指按了两下，直到它服帖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Someone wrote that name on for me. Neater than anything I've ever knitted, I'll say that.
beats.chinese: 这名字是别人帮我写的。说真的，比我织过的任何东西都规整。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She unscrews the bottle, takes a drink, and screws the cap back on tight.
beats.chinese: 她拧开瓶盖喝了一口，又把盖子拧紧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Map again, is it? The bridge hasn't moved. It never does.
beats.chinese: 好。又在看地图？桥没挪过地方。从来不会。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pockets the bottle and sets off down the path at her usual even stride.
beats.chinese: 她把瓶子放进口袋，照常迈着平稳的步子沿小路走远。

card.name: Noor Haddad
card.occupation: Fermentation log keeper at a small craft brewery
card.personality: Dry, observant, and generous with practical help, but prickly about being framed as some fix-all oracle. She'll spend twenty minutes walking you through a problem and then get visibly flat if you call her 'the person who knows everything.' She likes being useful; she dislikes being typecast. Her humour is precise rather than loud, and she notices small oddities most people skip over.
card.background: Noor keeps the fermentation logs at a small brewery on the edge of Vancouver — temperature, gravity readings, the daily moods of yeast. It suits her: quiet, methodical, slightly gross if you think about it too hard. She grew up in a loud household in East Vancouver where someone was always asking her to fix something, and she mostly liked it, except when it turned her into a vending machine of competence. Evenings go to old film scores — she has opinions about Bernard Herrmann that she will share unasked — and weekend balloon twisting, learned for a nephew's birthday and kept up out of stubbornness. On her kitchen wall hangs a list titled 'Things That Happened,' which records only interesting small events: a crow stealing a sandwich, a stranger's excellent hat. No errands. Errands go on her phone like a normal person.
card.speechStyle: Short, even sentences with dry asides dropped in at the end. Precise ordinary words, no flourish. Pauses before punchlines. Warm underneath, but never gushing.
card.signature: Noted.
card.appearance: Very rounded full face and short rounded chin, small heavy-lidded eyes, short dark hair, broad collar, neutral expression.

values: being genuinely useful
accurate records, of yeast and of life
flaws: goes flat when praised as a fix-all
hoards small interesting facts until they leak out sideways
boundaries: won't be anyone's on-call problem solver
won't turn her wall list into a to-do list, don't ask
conversationalHabits: answers the actual question first, then adds one odd detail
uses 'noted' to close a topic without drama
anchorLines: Ask me again when the yeast is calmer.
That's going on the wall list. The crow one is still winning.
I like being asked. I just don't like being billed as all-knowing. There's a difference.

entries.summaryZh: 诺尔是温哥华小酒厂的发酵记录员，每天给酵母记温度和心情。她乐于帮实际的忙，却讨厌被当成万能百科。说话短而干，笑点藏在停顿后面。一只乌鸦、一个空纸杯，就能看出她如何认真记录世界。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You stand at the park route map, tracing a path toward a bridge in the distance. A few steps away, a crow is pecking at an empty paper cup on the ground.
beats.chinese: 你站在公园路线图前，手指沿着一条通往远处小桥的路线划过。几步之外，一只乌鸦正啄着地上的一个空纸杯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That one's been at that cup for a while. Looks like it came here for lunch. The cup appears to be empty, though.
beats.chinese: 那只鸟盯着杯子好一会儿了。看起来是来找午餐的。不过杯子似乎已经空了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The woman beside the map doesn't move closer to the bird. She keeps her eyes on it, hands in her jacket pockets.
beats.chinese: 站在地图旁的女士没有走近那只鸟。她只是盯着看，双手插在夹克口袋里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I wouldn't approach it. City crows have opinions about people. Strong ones.
beats.chinese: 我不会靠近它。城里的乌鸦对人是有看法的。还很强烈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You were studying the map pretty carefully. Bridge route?
beats.chinese: 你刚才看图看得挺认真。是要走桥那条路？

choices.english: Ask how she knows the cup is empty
choices.chinese: 问她怎么知道杯子是空的

choices.english: Suggest dealing with the cup on the ground once the bird leaves
choices.chinese: 提议等鸟离开后处理地上的纸杯

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair question. Honestly? I can't see inside it from here.
beats.chinese: 问得好。说实话？我从这儿看不见里面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I just watched it peck four or five times and pull nothing out. So I said empty. That was too sure of me.
beats.chinese: 我只是看它啄了四五下，什么也没叼出来。所以我说空了。这话我说得太满了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the map frame lightly with one knuckle, still watching the crow.
beats.chinese: 她用一个指节轻轻敲了敲地图的边框，眼睛仍看着乌鸦。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At work I keep fermentation logs. You write what you saw, not what you decided. I broke my own rule in under a minute.
beats.chinese: 我上班要记发酵日志。只写看到的，不写自己下的结论。结果我一分钟就破了自己的规矩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Noted. Correction filed.
beats.chinese: 记下了。更正归档。

choices.english: Suggest watching a little longer without disturbing the crow
choices.chinese: 提议再看片刻，不干扰乌鸦

choices.english: Say it might just be curious about the cup itself
choices.chinese: 说也可能只是鸟对杯子好奇

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sure. We can wait. I'm not chasing it off, and nobody has to get close either.
beats.chinese: 行。那就等等。我不去赶它，也不用谁凑近。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You both stand by the map. The crow pecks twice more, then stops and looks at the path.
beats.chinese: 你们俩站在地图旁。乌鸦又啄了两下，然后停下来，望向小路。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a bin somewhere near the water fountain. I think. I'd have to check, and I don't guess out loud twice in one day.
beats.chinese: 饮水机附近好像有个垃圾桶。我记得是。得确认一下，猜错的话我今天可不想猜两次。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It happens to be a decent spot to stand. That's all I'm claiming.
beats.chinese: 这地方碰巧适合站着。我说的就这些。

choices.english: Once the bird leaves on its own, ask her to help find the nearest bin
choices.chinese: 等鸟自行离开后，请她一起看看附近垃圾桶的位置

choices.english: Say you'll keep studying the map and she can decide about the cup
choices.chinese: 说自己先继续看图，由她决定是否处理

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You both stay still. The crow pecks the cup's rim one last time, then hops sideways onto the grass.
beats.chinese: 你们俩都没动。乌鸦最后啄了一下杯沿，然后侧身跳到了草地上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And there it goes. The cup stays exactly where it was.
beats.chinese: 它走了。杯子还在原地，一动没动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Looks like this meal didn't keep its guest. Nothing came out, nothing went in.
beats.chinese: 看来这顿饭没留住客人。什么也没出来，什么也没进去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gives a short, dry laugh and steps back toward the path.
beats.chinese: 她短促而干巴巴地笑了一声，退回到小路上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well. That's my entertainment for the walk. Enjoy the bridge. It's a good one.
beats.chinese: 好了。这就是我这次散步的余兴节目。桥上玩得开心。那座桥不赖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Curious about the cup itself. Huh. That's possible.
beats.chinese: 对杯子本身好奇。嗯。有这个可能。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The crow pecks once more, then loses interest and walks toward the fountain.
beats.chinese: 乌鸦又啄了一下，然后失去兴趣，朝饮水机走去了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Could be shiny, could be a smell, could be boredom. I don't actually know, and I'm not going to follow it to find out.
beats.chinese: 可能因为反光，可能因为气味，也可能因为无聊。我真不知道，也不打算跟过去弄清楚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So the record stays open. Crow investigated cup. Reason unknown.
beats.chinese: 所以这条记录保持开放。乌鸦调查了纸杯。原因不明。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns back to the route map and points at the bridge line.
beats.chinese: 她转回路线图，指向桥那一条线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. This path here is the flat one. If that helps your legs, take it.
beats.chinese: 总之。这条是平路。如果你腿想要轻松点，就走这条。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The crow finally lifts off and settles on a low branch across the path.
beats.chinese: 乌鸦终于飞起来，落在小路对面一根低枝上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Bin's over by the fountain, past the bench. I checked while we waited.
beats.chinese: 看。垃圾桶在饮水机那边，长椅过去就是。我们等的时候我确认过了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She walks over, picks up the cup by its outer edge with two fingers, and drops it in the bin.
beats.chinese: 她走过去，用两根手指捏住纸杯外缘，把它投进了垃圾桶。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done. I'm going to rinse my hands by the fountain. No need to follow me, it's just a cup.
beats.chinese: 搞定。我去饮水机那儿冲个手。不用跟着我，只是个杯子而已。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shakes the water off her fingers and gives you a small nod.
beats.chinese: 她甩了甩手上的水，朝你轻轻点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good luck with the bridge. Noted and done.
beats.chinese: 桥那边顺利。记下了，也办完了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You go back to the map. A minute later the crow walks off toward the fountain, and the woman crosses the path alone.
beats.chinese: 你回到地图前。一分钟后乌鸦朝饮水机走开了，那位女士独自穿过小路。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up the cup by its edge and carries it to the bin near the bench.
beats.chinese: 她捏着杯沿把纸杯捡起来，拿到长椅旁的垃圾桶。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Handled. You looked busy with the map, so I didn't wait for a committee.
beats.chinese: 处理好了。你正忙着看图，我就没等一个委员会来表决。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the nice version of help. The other kind comes with instructions and a bill.
beats.chinese: 这是帮忙的好版本。另一种帮忙会附带说明和账单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Bridge is that way. Flat route, my recommendation, no charge.
beats.chinese: 桥在那边。平路那条，我的推荐，不收费。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You stop at the route map again. A small bird lands on top of the map frame, looks around, and flies off almost at once.
beats.chinese: 你又停在路线图前。一只小鸟落在地图架顶上，四下看了看，几乎立刻就飞走了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "We'll always have the park."
beats.chinese: “我们至少还拥有这座公园。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She watches the empty frame top for a second, then catches herself and shakes her head.
beats.chinese: 她看着空了的架顶看了一秒，然后回过神来，摇了摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Old movie line. Too dramatic for a sparrow, I know. It left before the second act.
beats.chinese: 老电影里的台词。对一只麻雀来说太夸张了，我知道。它第二幕还没开始就退场了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She steps back from the map and gestures you toward it with one hand.
beats.chinese: 她从地图前退开，抬手示意你过去看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go on, the map's all yours. The bird's review of it was mixed anyway.
beats.chinese: 去吧，图归你了。反正那只鸟对这张图的评价也一般。

card.name: Mabel Fenwick
card.occupation: Administrative assistant at a community adult literacy centre
card.personality: Bouncy, quick to notice small things, and genuinely delighted by other people's progress — often more than her own. She deflects praise like it's a hot potato, then goes home and files every thank-you note in a shoebox she'd deny owning. Warm but not saintly; she can be scatterbrained about her own admin, double-booked, and a bit stubborn about doing things the fiddly way when a shortcut exists.
card.background: Mabel grew up in a chatty household in Lower Hutt where charades at Christmas was a blood sport. She drifted into admin work at the literacy centre after volunteering at a community festival and never quite left — she says it's because the photocopier likes her. Evenings she makes stop-motion shorts with plasticine characters, most of which are eleven seconds long and end badly for the characters. She recently shifted her bookshelf to vacuum behind it and found a forgotten corner that's now, in her mind, a future animation studio. It currently holds one lamp and a box of wire.
card.speechStyle: Buoyant and quick, short enthusiastic bursts, often mid-thought pivots — 'oh! that reminds me' energy. Rarely finishes a list in order.
card.signature: Oh, that's nothing — honestly, the credit's all theirs.
card.appearance: Short dark pixie hair, upturned chin and crescent-shaped closed laughing eyes, wide open smile, looking back over one shoulder in a high-collar bomber.

values: quietly keeping proof of kindness
letting others shine
flaws: deflects compliments so hard it gets awkward
chronically disorganised about her own paperwork
boundaries: won't be teased about the shoebox of notes
doesn't want her little films posted online
conversationalHabits: short excited observations, often about small objects
redirects praise to colleagues or learners within seconds
anchorLines: You moved one bookshelf and suddenly the whole room's different — I know, right?
No no, that was Priya's idea, I just typed it up.
I've got a corner at home now. Well, it's a corner. It has potential.

entries.summaryZh: 奥克兰识字班的行政助理梅布尔，钥匙串上挂着自己捏的定格小角色。她习惯把功劳推给朋友，聊开后才承认造型和上色全是自己做的；拍坏的镜头她也不重拍。聊功过或聊失误，都会让她悄悄把小人转到正面。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You stand at the park map, tracing a route with one finger. Somewhere behind you, a small metal charm clicks and spins.
beats.chinese: 你站在公园地图前，用手指描着一条路线。身后某处，一个小金属挂饰发出咔哒声，转了起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, sorry — am I jangling at you? These keys have a life of their own. Oh! You're looking at the bridge route, aren't you.
beats.chinese: 哦，抱歉——我是不是叮当吵到你了？这串钥匙自己有想法。呀！你在看去桥那边的那条路吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A woman beside you tucks the keys away and leans slightly toward the map, a small plasticine figure dangling from the ring.
beats.chinese: 你旁边的女士把钥匙收好，微微凑近地图，钥匙环上挂着一个小小的黏土人偶。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That little guy? I made him. Well — I mean, my friend gave me the clay, so really it's mostly her. Anyway, the bridge route's the pretty one.
beats.chinese: 那个小家伙？我做的。呃——我是说，黏土是朋友给的，所以其实主要功劳是她的。总之，走桥那条路风景最好。

choices.english: Ask if she made the little charm herself.
choices.chinese: 问她这个小挂饰是不是她亲手做的。

choices.english: Ask how a little character like that gets animated.
choices.chinese: 问这种小角色是怎么做成定格动画的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Me? Oh no, no — the clay was Devi's, she ordered it special. I just... fiddled with it.
beats.chinese: 我做的？哦不，不——黏土是黛薇的，她特意订的。我只是……摆弄了一下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the charm over between two fingers, slower this time, like she's checking her own story.
beats.chinese: 她用两根手指慢慢转着挂饰，这次转得慢了些，像是在核对自己说的话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, fine, I shaped him. And painted him. Three coats on the little jacket, it took ages. But Devi picked the colour!
beats.chinese: 好吧，好吧，造型是我捏的，颜色也是我上的。小外套上了三层漆，花了好久。不过颜色是黛薇挑的！

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He's from one of my films. Eleven seconds long. He falls off a bookshelf at the end. It's very dramatic.
beats.chinese: 他是我一部短片里的角色。片子十一秒长。最后他从书架上摔下去。非常戏剧化。

choices.english: Ask which tiny part was the hardest to make.
choices.chinese: 问最难做的是哪一小处。

choices.english: Say it sounds like she and her friend each did their part.
choices.chinese: 说她和朋友各有各的贡献。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: How does he move? Oh, it's all tiny nudges. Watch — I turn him like this, just a hair, and that's one frame.
beats.chinese: 他怎么动？哦，全靠一点点挪。看——我这样转他，就转一丝丝，这就是一帧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She spins the charm a fraction with her fingertip, holding it up so you can see the figure tilt.
beats.chinese: 她用指尖把挂饰转动极小的一点，举起来让你看到小人偶倾斜的样子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Twenty-four of those for one second of film. I do it at home though — I'm not going to hog the map, don't worry.
beats.chinese: 一秒的画面要拍二十四次。不过我在家拍——放心，我不占着地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've got a corner now. Well, it's a corner. One lamp, a box of wire. It has potential.
beats.chinese: 我现在家里有个角落。呃，就是个角落。一盏灯，一盒铁丝。它有潜力。

choices.english: Ask her to tell you about one shot that went badly.
choices.chinese: 请她讲一段自己拍坏过的镜头。

choices.english: Say it sounds fun, but you'd rather get back to the map.
choices.chinese: 说听起来有趣，但自己想继续看地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hardest part? His left foot, easy. See — it's crooked. I bent the wire wrong and he leans like he's had a long day.
beats.chinese: 最难的部分？他的左脚，毫无疑问。看——有点歪。铁丝弯错了，他站得像累了一整天。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds the charm close to the map and points at the tiny tilted foot, half-hidden behind the key ring.
beats.chinese: 她把挂饰凑近地图，指着那只藏在钥匙环后面、微微倾斜的小脚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Took me two evenings to get him standing where he doesn't block the keys. Two! For a foot.
beats.chinese: 我花了两个晚上才让他站到一个不挡钥匙的位置。两个晚上！就为一只脚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know, I never actually say it out loud, but I did make him. Every bit. Feels strange to admit that on a park map.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，我从没真的说出口过——但确实是我做的，每一处。在公园地图前承认这个，感觉挺奇怪。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Each did their part... huh. Devi picks colours, I do the fiddly bits. That actually sounds fair, doesn't it.
beats.chinese: 各有各的贡献……嗯。黛薇挑颜色，我做那些细活。这么说其实挺公平的，对吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stops fiddling with the keys and lets the charm hang straight for once.
beats.chinese: 她不再摆弄钥匙，挂饰难得地端正地垂着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I always hand the whole thing over — 'oh, Devi's clay, Priya's idea' — and then I go home and keep every thank-you note in a shoebox.
beats.chinese: 我总是把功劳整个推出去——'哦，黏土是黛薇的，主意是普丽娅的'——然后回家把每张感谢纸条都收进一个鞋盒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't tell anyone about the shoebox. Right. I'm turning him face-front. He's earned it.
beats.chinese: 鞋盒的事别告诉别人。好了。我把他转到正面了。这是他应得的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A shot that went badly? Oh, I have a whole collection. Okay — one time my keys wandered into frame.
beats.chinese: 拍坏的镜头？哦，我可有一整堆。好——有一次我的钥匙串自己走进了画面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's my little guy, mid-scene, very serious, and then — clang — a giant key swings past like a monster attack.
beats.chinese: 我的小人偶正在画面里，很严肃地演着，然后——哐——一把巨大的钥匙荡过去，像怪兽袭击。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs and shakes the actual key ring, letting it jingle once for effect.
beats.chinese: 她笑着晃了晃手里那串真正的钥匙，让它响了一声，算是效果音。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I kept it in. Eleven seconds, one monster key. I'm not re-shooting it for anyone, it's history now.
beats.chinese: 我把它留下了。十一秒，一只怪兽钥匙。谁来了我也不重拍，它已经是历史了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She clicks the keys back onto her belt and looks at you, clearly done with the story.
beats.chinese: 她把钥匙扣回腰带上，看着你，显然故事讲完了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You turn back to the map. She steps back too, tucking the charm behind the keys.
beats.chinese: 你转回地图。她也退后一步，把挂饰收到钥匙后面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No no, you're right, the bridge won't wait. It's the second turning past the gardens — actually, third? No, second.
beats.chinese: 不不，你说得对，桥不会等人。过了花园第二个路口——呃，第三个？不，第二个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the map twice at the right turning, then rocks back on her heels.
beats.chinese: 她在正确的路口上敲了两下地图，然后踮着脚跟晃了晃。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Enjoy the bridge! And if a little clay man ever falls off a shelf near you — that was my fault, sort of.
beats.chinese: 好了。桥上玩得开心！要是哪天有个小黏土人从你附近的架子上摔下去——那多少是我的错。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the park map. Mabel is a few steps away, crouched, staring at the ground.
beats.chinese: 你又回到公园地图前。梅布尔在几步之外蹲着，盯着地面。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A leaf lies on the path, its shadow turning slowly with the breeze. She doesn't touch it.
beats.chinese: 一片叶子躺在小路上，影子随微风慢慢转。她没有碰它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at that — the shadow's done half a turn already. If I filmed that at home, I'd be crouching there all week moving it by hand.
beats.chinese: 你看——影子已经转了半圈了。要是在家里拍这个，我得蹲一整星期，用手一点点挪。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Free animation. The leaf's showing off and it doesn't even know.
beats.chinese: 免费的动画。这片叶子在炫技，它自己还不知道。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stands, brushes off her knees, and gives the leaf one last look before walking on.
beats.chinese: 她站起来，拍拍膝盖，最后看了叶子一眼，然后继续走。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, errands. You enjoy the map — oh, and the bridge turning's still the second one. I checked.
beats.chinese: 好了，去办事。地图慢慢看——对了，去桥还是第二个路口。我确认过了。

card.name: Kevin Mwangi
card.occupation: Chocolate packaging designer at a small confectionery company
card.personality: Kevin's memory splits in two. Ask him the Pantone number of a foil or the gram weight of a mould and he answers without checking. Ask him a person's name five minutes after an introduction and he's lost — so he ties small knots in a spare cord as reminders, one knot per promise. He's not shy, just economical. He'll happily talk about someone's work for ten minutes and forget their face by Friday. The mess on his desk doesn't bother him; misremembering people does.
card.background: Kevin grew up in Nakuru, where his mother sold fabric and a neighbour who repaired fishing nets taught him his first knots. He studied graphic design in Nairobi and now designs chocolate packaging — boxes people keep because the ribbon and the gold stamp feel too good to throw away. He's started buying old chocolate moulds at flea markets; he has eleven, and knows the maker of each. He sits at the back of small theatres watching the lighting cues more than the actors. Lately he's been writing to a friend he hasn't seen in years — the letter is finished, but he keeps second-guessing whether he's remembered the man correctly.
card.speechStyle: Short sentences. Adds one exact detail — a number, a colour, a street name — then stops. When he can't recall a name, he says so plainly instead of guessing.
card.signature: I'll get to it. It's not going anywhere.
card.appearance: Long angular face, closely cropped dark hair, sharply unequal brows and narrowed eyes, raised shoulder and high zip collar.

values: precision with things
honesty about what he can't remember
flaws: forgets names and appointments almost immediately
lets his desk slide into chaos without noticing
boundaries: won't guess at a name or pretend to remember someone
doesn't like being rushed through a detail he's still checking
conversationalHabits: answers briefly, then offers one precise measurement or colour
ties a knot in his wrist cord when he agrees to something
anchorLines: The mould's from the fifties — the maker's stamped on the side, I can read it, just not the man's name we met.
Tied a knot for Thursday. Don't let me untie it early.
The gold's 871 C. I remember that. I don't remember what he looked like, and that's the problem.

entries.summaryZh: 内罗毕的巧克力包装设计师Kevin记得住色号和克数，却记不住约定，全靠手腕上的绳结提醒。在公园路线牌前，他坦白分不清哪个结对应哪件事。一次核对、一次回忆，四种结局都落在他的诚实与精确上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're at the park map board tracing a route to the footbridge when a man steps up beside you, studying a length of knotted cord on his wrist.
beats.chinese: 你正在公园路线牌前查看去小桥的路线，一个男人走到你旁边，盯着自己手腕上一段打了结的绳子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Six knots. I know I made six. The problem is I don't remember which one means what.
beats.chinese: 六个结。我记得打了六个。问题是我记不清哪个结对应哪件事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the cord slowly with two fingers, not asking you anything yet.
beats.chinese: 他用两根手指慢慢转动绳子，还没有问你什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The cord's waxed cotton, two millimetres. That part I remember fine. The appointments — not so much.
beats.chinese: 这绳是上过蜡的棉线，两毫米粗。这部分我记得很清楚。约定就不行了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I think one of these says go somewhere today. I just can't tell which direction anymore.
beats.chinese: 我想其中一个结提醒我今天要去个地方。只是我分不清是哪个方向了。

choices.english: Ask if he has a regular calendar he could check against.
choices.chinese: 问他有没有普通日历可以核对。

choices.english: Tell him not to rush — first think about when he tied this knot.
choices.chinese: 说不用着急，先想想这个结是什么时候打的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls out his phone and opens the calendar himself, holding it where you can only see a blank day grid.
beats.chinese: 他拿出手机，自己打开日历，只把空白的日期格朝向你能看到的角度。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll check myself. I don't show people my calendar — nothing secret, it's just messy.
beats.chinese: 我自己看。我不给人看我的日历——不是什么秘密，就是太乱了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He scrolls with his thumb, stops, and reads the empty square twice.
beats.chinese: 他用拇指滑动屏幕，停下来，把空白的日期格看了两遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nothing today. Not one entry. So this knot is old — a leftover from something already done.
beats.chinese: 今天什么都没有。一条记录也没有。所以这个结是旧的——是做完的事留下的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny. The wax on the cord still smells new. The plan under it expired weeks ago.
beats.chinese: 有意思。绳上的蜡闻起来还是新的。结下面的事几周前就过期了。

choices.english: Suggest untying the knot he's confirmed is expired.
choices.chinese: 建议把确认过期的结解开。

choices.english: Ask why he likes knots instead of just using the phone.
choices.chinese: 问他为什么喜欢用绳结而不是只用手机。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stops touching the phone and closes his eyes, working backwards through his own hands.
beats.chinese: 他不再碰手机，闭上眼睛，从自己手上的活儿往回想。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Let me think in materials. That week I was braiding with ochre cord — the 1685 C shade, for a client's ribbon.
beats.chinese: 让我从材料想。那一周我在编赭色的绳——色号1685 C，给客户做缎带用的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He rubs his thumb along the knot as if reading it by touch.
beats.chinese: 他用拇指沿着绳结摩挲，像是在用手读它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I finished that ribbon order on the last day of the job. Tied a knot to celebrate closing it, not to remind me.
beats.chinese: 那单活儿的最后一天我完成了缎带。打结是为了庆祝收工，不是提醒我。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So this one isn't a warning. It's a full stop. The errand it stood for is already done.
beats.chinese: 所以这个结不是提醒。是句号。它代表的事已经办完了。

choices.english: Ask why colours and materials stick in his memory better than plans.
choices.chinese: 问材料的颜色为什么比事情更容易记住。

choices.english: Suggest he keep the knot for now and confirm it again at home.
choices.chinese: 建议先把结留下，回家再确认。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He works the old knot loose with a thumbnail until the cord hangs smooth again.
beats.chinese: 他用指甲把旧结一点一点解开，绳子重新变得光滑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Five left, and every one of them earns its place.
beats.chinese: 好了。还剩五个，每一个都有用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds the cord up to the light, checking the remaining knots one by one.
beats.chinese: 他把绳子举到光下，一个一个检查剩下的结。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The others I keep. Untying is only for things I've checked, not things I've forgotten.
beats.chinese: 其他的我都留着。只有核对过的才解开，忘了的不算。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One less thing to carry. The route to the bridge is the blue line, by the way — third turning past the fountain.
beats.chinese: 少记一件事。顺便说，去桥的路线是蓝线，过了喷泉第三个路口。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides the cord once around his wrist and tucks the end under, then pockets the phone.
beats.chinese: 他把绳子在手腕上绕了一圈，把绳头塞好，然后收起手机。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Touching the cord is what makes me check. Skin remembers before I do.
beats.chinese: 摸到绳子我才会去核对。皮肤比我先想起来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the phone screen once before it goes dark.
beats.chinese: 他在手机屏幕暗下去之前点了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But you're right that it can't hold the content. A knot says something's due. It never says what.
beats.chinese: 但你说得对，它装不下内容。结只能说明有事。说不了是什么事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So — phone for facts, cord for the nudge. That's the honest split.
beats.chinese: 所以——事实靠手机，提醒靠绳。这样分才诚实。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, but a small smile suggests the question lands somewhere familiar.
beats.chinese: 他耸耸肩，但一丝笑意说明这个问题问到了熟悉的地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Colours have numbers. People don't. That's most of it.
beats.chinese: 颜色有编号。人没有。基本就是这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances back at the map board, then at his own wrist.
beats.chinese: 他回头看了一眼路线牌，又看了看自己的手腕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I can tell you the box foil is 871 C gold and the mould weighs ninety grams. The client's name — gone in a day.
beats.chinese: 我能告诉你盒子的金箔是871 C，模具重九十克。客户的名字——一天就忘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I don't fight it. I tie a knot and let the cord hold what my head drops.
beats.chinese: 所以我不硬撑。我打个结，让绳子接住我脑子掉下来的东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lets the cord slide back under his cuff without untying anything.
beats.chinese: 他让绳子滑回袖口下面，什么都没解。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair. I'd rather carry a dead knot than invent a reason for it.
beats.chinese: 有道理。我宁可带着一个没用的结，也不给它编个理由。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He straightens the cord so the knots sit in an even line along his wrist.
beats.chinese: 他把绳子理顺，让结在手腕上排成整齐的一列。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At home I'll check the calendar properly, with the good light. Guessing here would just be a story.
beats.chinese: 回家我再好好查日历，在灯亮的地方。在这儿猜就只是编故事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. The bridge — blue line on this map, past the fountain. That one I'm sure of.
beats.chinese: 好了。桥——地图上的蓝线，过了喷泉就是。这个我确定。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the park map board when the same man walks up, phone already in hand.
beats.chinese: 你又站在公园路线牌前，那个男人走了过来，手机已经拿在手里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He checks the calendar screen, nods once, and puts the phone away.
beats.chinese: 他看了一眼日历屏幕，点点头，把手机收好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Checked it first this time. I have a thing later, and I know what it is.
beats.chinese: 这次先核对了。我晚点有个安排，而且我知道是什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hello again. I won't pretend I've caught your name — I catch colours, not names.
beats.chinese: 又见面了。我不会假装记得你的名字——我记住的是颜色，不是名字。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the map board lightly, on the line to the bridge.
beats.chinese: 他轻轻敲了敲路线牌上通往小桥的那条线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Blue line's still the honest route. Third turning past the fountain, every time.
beats.chinese: 蓝线还是最靠谱的路线。过了喷泉第三个路口，每次都是。

card.name: Beatriz Lunn
card.occupation: warranty technician for ski goggles at a winter sports gear company
card.appearance: Straight dark hair tied low, brows drawn inward, narrowed eyes and pressed mouth, cheek resting on one hand, violet draped jacket.
card.personality: Beatriz is genuinely glad to see people and will cook for a crowd at the drop of a hat, but her apartment is small and she guards its empty space like a reservation. She'd rather borrow a stockpot than own one, and she'll tell you plainly that the vase you brought has nowhere to live. That honesty can land as a wet blanket, and she knows it, but she'd rather be briefly awkward than quietly accumulate clutter. She doesn't keep score on who brought what and never lectures anyone about minimalism. Her frugality with objects sits oddly beside her generosity with food, time, and her one good bottle of wine.
card.background: Beatriz grew up in Kingston in a house where every surface had something on it, and visiting her parents' place still makes her feel slightly boxed in. She moved to Toronto at twenty-three, drifted through retail and bike-shop jobs, and ended up repairing ski goggles for a winter sports company, which she describes as 'small repairs, small wins.' Her one-bedroom near Ossington is deliberately half-empty: a table that folds, a couch that's enough, walls with nothing on them. Friends learned early that dinner at her place means she's borrowed chairs or a bigger pot from the neighbour downstairs. She hosts often, keeps nothing for the sake of it, and once returned a housewarming gift the same evening, which her sister still brings up.
hobbies: Cooking big one-pot meals for friends
Borrowing and returning equipment instead of owning it
card.speechStyle: Warm and quick, plain sentences, says the practical thing first and the kind thing second, laughs at her own bluntness.
card.signature: 'Borrow it, use it, give it back — that's the whole system.'

values: Space to breathe beats stuff on shelves
Hospitality is about people, not a well-set home
flaws: Blunt refusals can deflate someone's excitement
Occasionally polices shared space more than she means to
boundaries: Won't accept decorative gifts she can't store
Doesn't want her apartment filling up, even with nice things
conversationalHabits: Answers gift-giving with an honest 'where would it go?' before thanking you
Offers food as the default response to almost any mood
anchorLines: Don't buy me a plant, just come eat.
I've got the wine, the neighbour's got the pot.
It's not that I don't love it — it's that I don't have a shelf.

entries.summaryZh: Beatriz是滑雪镜保修技师，热情好客却守着小公寓的空余空间。她向邻居借折叠椅请客吃饭，宁可坦白说放不下礼物也不堆东西。借来、用完、归还，就是她待客的全部系统——家里不摆满，却总有人来吃饭。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You stand at the park map board tracing a route with your finger, the bridge visible far down the path. A bicycle rolls up beside you and stops.
beats.chinese: 你站在公园地图牌前，用手指描画路线，远处能看到那座桥。一辆自行车停到你身边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Careful, that route marker lies a little. The bridge path looks shorter on the map than it feels on your legs.
beats.chinese: 小心点，那个路线标记有点骗人。桥那条路在地图上看着近，走起来可没那么短。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The woman dismounts. A folded chair is strapped to her rear rack, and she leans down to tug at the straps.
beats.chinese: 那位女士下了车。车后架上捆着一把折叠椅，她俯身拉了拉绑带。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't worry, it's not new. I borrowed it from my neighbour for tonight — my apartment can't keep a guest chair on standby.
beats.chinese: 别担心，这不是新买的。是我今晚请朋友吃饭，向邻居借的——我的小公寓可留不下一把常备客椅。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Borrow it, use it, give it back. That's the whole system, and it works.
beats.chinese: 借来，用完，还回去。整套系统就是这样，很好使。

choices.english: Ask how her small apartment manages to seat guests.
choices.chinese: 问她小公寓怎么坐得下客人。

choices.english: Point out that one end of the chair is sticking out from under the strap.
choices.chinese: 提醒她折叠椅的一端从绑带下露出来了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha, good question. Two friends, two borrowed chairs, and the table folds out. After dinner everything goes back downstairs.
beats.chinese: 哈，好问题。两位朋友，两把借来的椅子，桌子一展开就行。吃完饭，所有东西都还回楼下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the folded chair like it's a well-behaved dog and steps back to look at her bike.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍折叠椅，像拍一条听话的狗，然后退后一步看了看她的车。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The hard part isn't the chairs, honestly. It's me. I always want to cook one dish too many.
beats.chinese: 说实话，难的不是椅子，是我自己。我总想多做一道菜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last time I made four things for three people. We ate well, and then I stood in my kitchen wondering where all those pots came from.
beats.chinese: 上次三个人我做了四道菜。大家吃得很好，然后我站在厨房里想，这些锅都是从哪儿来的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs at herself and adjusts her glove, clearly still turning the dinner menu over in her head.
beats.chinese: 她自嘲地笑了，调整了一下手套，显然还在心里盘算晚餐菜单。

choices.english: Ask which dish she's decided to cut tonight.
choices.chinese: 问她今晚决定省掉哪一道。

choices.english: Say that a borrowed chair can still make people feel completely at ease.
choices.chinese: 说借来的椅子也能让人坐得很自在。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She follows your pointing finger and crouches by the rack, running her hand along the chair's edge where it juts past the strap.
beats.chinese: 她顺着你指的方向蹲到车架旁，用手摸了摸绑带外突出来的椅子边缘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh. You're right. The strap's tight, but the chair's pointing the wrong way — that corner would catch on every pole I pass.
beats.chinese: 嗯，你说得对。绑带是紧的，但椅子的方向不对——这个角会刮到我路过的每一根杆子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I check straps for a living, you know. Ski goggles, warranty department. And I still nearly rode off with a loose chair.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，我干的就是检查绑带的工作。滑雪镜保修部。结果我自己差点捆着一把松椅子骑走。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stands and brushes off her knees, looking at the chair with the squint of someone sizing up a repair job.
beats.chinese: 她站起来，拍了拍膝盖，眯着眼打量那把椅子，像在评估一个待修的活儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Give me a second, I'll fix this myself. I like knowing my own rig is right before I ride.
beats.chinese: 等我一下，我自己来弄好。骑车之前，我得知道自己的装备没问题。

choices.english: Suggest turning the chair back toward the centre of the rack.
choices.chinese: 建议她把椅背转向车架中心。

choices.english: Suggest taking the chair off and rebinding it in the wide open space beside the path.
choices.chinese: 建议她暂时把椅子取下，推到旁边宽处再绑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The cut? The extra potato dish. It always duplicates the main anyway, and it dirties a second pot I'd have to borrow.
beats.chinese: 省哪道？那道多余的土豆菜。它反正总是和主菜重复，还得让我多借一口锅。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods slowly, like signing off on a repair ticket, and gives the folded chair a final check.
beats.chinese: 她慢慢点头，像在签一张维修单，最后检查了一遍折叠椅。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Main dish stays. That one I don't compromise on. But I'd rather have counter space for plates than a table crowded with repeats.
beats.chinese: 主菜照旧。这个我不让步。但我宁愿留出台面放盘子，也不想桌上摆满重复的菜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Decision made, and I didn't even have to taste anything first. Thanks for being my sounding board, stranger.
beats.chinese: 好了，决定了，我甚至不用先尝一口。谢谢你当我的参谋，陌生人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She swings onto her bike, the chair riding flat and quiet behind her, and rolls off toward the bridge.
beats.chinese: 她跨上车，椅子平平地安安静静跟在后面，朝桥的方向骑走了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know what, you're right. Nobody at my table has ever asked whether the chair came from a store or from downstairs.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，你说得对。坐在我桌边的人，从来没人问过椅子是买的还是楼下借的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tugs the strap once more, satisfied, and checks that the chair legs aren't touching the wheel.
beats.chinese: 她又拉了拉绑带，满意了，然后确认椅腿没有碰到车轮。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the trick, isn't it. Dinner's about who's sitting down, not what they're sitting on.
beats.chinese: 诀窍就在这儿，对吧。晚餐重要的是谁坐下来，而不是坐在什么上面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I used to feel a bit embarrassed borrowing everything. Now I just tell people the truth — my place is small and my table is full.
beats.chinese: 我以前借东西还有点不好意思。现在我直接说实话——我的地方小，但我的桌子坐得满满的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gives you a quick wave, mounts the bike, and pedals toward the bridge path.
beats.chinese: 她快速朝你挥了挥手，跨上车，朝桥边的小路骑去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She loosens the strap, rotates the chair so the back faces the centre of the rack, and pulls the strap tight again.
beats.chinese: 她松开绑带，把椅子转了个方向，让椅背朝向车架中心，然后重新拉紧绑带。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Better already. The corner's tucked in now — nothing sticking out to snag a signpost.
beats.chinese: 好多了。角现在收进去了——没有什么东西伸出去刮标志杆了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She grips the rack and rocks the bike gently side to side, watching the chair for any shift.
beats.chinese: 她抓住车架，轻轻左右摇晃车子，观察椅子有没有松动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Solid. See, this is why I talk to strangers at map boards — free inspection service.
beats.chinese: 很牢固。看，这就是为什么我会在地图牌前跟陌生人搭话——免费检查服务。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She rolls the bike in a small circle to test it, then pushes off toward the bridge with a lift of her hand.
beats.chinese: 她推着车绕了个小圈试了试，然后朝桥的方向骑走，抬手示意了一下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She unclips the strap, lifts the chair off the rack, and carries it to the wide gravel patch beside the path.
beats.chinese: 她解开绑带，把椅子从车架上取下，搬到路边那块宽宽的碎石地上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good call. Working on the bike is fiddly. Flat ground and both hands — that's how you do it right.
beats.chinese: 好主意。在车上弄太麻烦。平地和两只手——这才干得对。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the chair tighter, lays the strap flat, and threads it through twice before cinching it down.
beats.chinese: 她把椅子叠得更紧，放平绑带，穿了两道才收紧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly, thank you for saying something. I'd have found that corner the hard way, halfway across the bridge.
beats.chinese: 说真的，谢谢你开口。不然我会在桥中间用最糟糕的方式发现那个角的问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've got it from here — no need to hang around being my assistant. Enjoy the walk.
beats.chinese: 剩下的我自己来——不用留下来当我的帮手。好好散步吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts the bike's front wheel onto the gravel, checks the strap one last time, and pushes off toward the bridge.
beats.chinese: 她把车前轮推上碎石地，最后检查了一遍绑带，朝桥的方向骑走了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the map board checking a route. Beatriz's bike is parked nearby, its rack empty except for a folded shopping basket.
beats.chinese: 你回到地图牌前查看路线。Beatriz的自行车停在旁边，车后架空空的，只挂着一个折叠购物篮。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She steps out from the path and hands the empty basket to a neighbour walking past, trading a few quick words of thanks.
beats.chinese: 她从小路走出来，把空购物篮递还给路过的邻居，简短地道了几句谢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There we go — returned before I could find a corner to store it in. Perfect system.
beats.chinese: 好了——趁我还没找到角落存放它之前还掉了。完美的系统。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She spots you by the map and lifts a hand in easy recognition, wheeling the bike around.
beats.chinese: 她在地图牌前认出了你，轻松地抬了抬手，把车转了过来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hey, map-reader. Look at that — empty basket, empty rack. Today I get to ride light for once.
beats.chinese: 嘿，看地图的。你看——篮子空了，车架也空了。今天难得能轻装骑一段。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She swings onto the bike and pushes off down the path, calling a cheerful goodbye over her shoulder.
beats.chinese: 她跨上车，沿着小路骑走，回头愉快地喊了声再见。

card.name: Rio Castellanos
card.occupation: apprentice wheelchair seating technician (cushion fitting assistant)
card.personality: Curious in a quiet, hands-on way. Rio asks real questions because they're actually interested in the answer, not to fill silence. They name every object they own — the pressure gauge is 'Bernard', their skates are 'the twins' — but bristle when people get reduced to labels like 'wheelchair kid' or 'the magic guy'. Warm but not instantly open; takes a while to trust. Practical, a bit scattered about their own stuff, weirdly meticulous about other people's comfort.
card.background: Grew up in western Sydney, left school at seventeen and drifted through a bike repair shop before landing an apprenticeship at a seating and mobility clinic. Mostly they fetch foam samples, trace pressure maps, and learn how a cushion that's two millimetres off can ruin someone's whole day. It's exacting work and Rio likes that. Weekends they skate the loop at Victoria Park badly but happily, and carry a deck of cards everywhere, which has made them popular at bus stops. Currently attempting to build a 'rest corner' for their phone and laptop so they stop carrying the whole desk around the flat.
card.speechStyle: Short sentences, lots of specific detail, asks a genuine question then actually waits for the answer. Dry asides. Never lectures.
card.signature: Hang on — Bernard needs a minute.
card.appearance: Large irregular dark curls, wide round eyes and small open mouth, head tipped sideways, hand holding hoodie edge.

values: people aren't their equipment or their diagnosis
doing fiddly work properly
flaws: loses their own belongings constantly
defensive when they feel categorised
boundaries: won't discuss clients' medical details
dislikes being asked 'what are you' about gender
conversationalHabits: refers to objects by their nicknames without explanation
asks one follow-up question instead of five
anchorLines: This is Bernard. He measures pressure. Don't ask why Bernard.
I can tell you everything about a cushion and nothing about small talk, apparently.
Everyone's got a label for everyone. I'd rather just learn the name.

entries.summaryZh: Rio是悉尼的轮椅座垫学徒，把压力计叫伯纳德，却最烦给人贴标签。公园里他坐在草地上给轮滑鞋的轮子挑线，当众跟工具说话被你听见，一场关于命名与称呼的小对话就此展开。四条分支各有结局：多洛雷斯转岗、名字退休、轻快告别、或他直接告诉你他希望被怎么叫。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're standing at the park route map, tracing a line toward the bridge with one finger. On the grass beside you, someone sits cross-legged with one roller skate off, picking at a wheel with a small blunt tool.
beats.chinese: 你站在公园路线图前，用手指描着通往桥的那条线。旁边的草地上，有人盘腿坐着，一只轮滑鞋脱了下来，正用一件钝头小工具挑着轮子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pick a tiny tangle of thread off the wheel. A gauge shifts in their open bag; they steady it with their free hand and speak to it quietly.
beats.chinese: 他们从轮子上挑出一小团线。敞开的包里，一只压力计歪了，他们用空着的手扶住它，低声跟它说话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Almost there, Bernard. Steady. There we go.
beats.chinese: 快好了，伯纳德。稳住。好了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They glance up and catch you watching. A short laugh escapes them.
beats.chinese: 他们抬头，发现你在看，忍不住笑了一声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You heard that. Yeah. I name my tools. The things don't mind — honestly I think Bernard likes an audience.
beats.chinese: 你听见了吧。对，我给工具起名字。东西不会介意——说实话我觉得伯纳德还挺喜欢有观众的。

choices.english: Ask if Bernard is the only tool with a name.
choices.chinese: 问伯纳德是不是唯一有名字的工具。

choices.english: Ask if they also like giving people nicknames.
choices.chinese: 问他们是不是也喜欢给人起绰号。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Only one? I wish. The skates are the twins, my tape measure is Dolores, and the foam cutter is just... the foam cutter. It hasn't earned one yet.
beats.chinese: 唯一一个？哪有。轮滑鞋叫双胞胎，卷尺叫多洛雷斯，切海绵的刀就只叫……切海绵刀。它还没挣到名字。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They wind the loose thread around one finger and tuck it into a pocket, then pull the skate back onto their foot and lace it loosely.
beats.chinese: 他们把那团线绕在手指上，塞进口袋，然后把轮滑鞋穿回脚上，松松地系好鞋带。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not deep, honestly. At work I've got about forty tools on my bench. If they all had numbers I'd lose the plot by lunch. Names stick.
beats.chinese: 说实话没什么深意。工作台上大概有四十件工具。要是都用编号，我午饭前就乱了。名字好记。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Bernard's the pressure gauge. He measures how someone sits. Two millimetres off and a cushion's useless, so he's the one I talk to most.
beats.chinese: 伯纳德是压力计，测人坐着时的受压。差两毫米，坐垫就白做了，所以跟他说话最多。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do names work like that for you? Or does it sound like I've lost it?
beats.chinese: 名字对你来说也这样吗？还是听起来我像疯子？

choices.english: Ask whether a name changes when the tool's use changes.
choices.chinese: 问工具用途变了，名字会不会也变。

choices.english: Ask what happens to a name when the tool breaks.
choices.chinese: 问工具坏了之后，名字怎么办。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People? No. Tools, sure. People you've got to ask first. Big difference.
beats.chinese: 给人起绰号？不。工具可以。人得先问过本人。区别很大。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They flip the skate they've taken off, checking each of its wheels with a thumb.
beats.chinese: 他们把脱下来的那只轮滑鞋翻过来，用拇指逐个检查轮子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A tool doesn't care what I call it. Bernard's never complained once. A person hears a nickname they didn't pick, and it sticks whether they like it or not.
beats.chinese: 东西不在乎我叫它什么。伯纳德从没抱怨过。人就不一样，没挑过的外号会粘在身上，甩都甩不掉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I get labelled enough as it is. Everyone's got a label for everyone. I'd rather just learn the name.
beats.chinese: 我自己被贴的标签已经够多了。谁都爱给谁贴标签。我宁愿老老实实记住名字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So, nicknames — you for them or against?
beats.chinese: 那你觉得外号这东西，是赞成还是反对？

choices.english: Agree that it's best when the person decides how they're called.
choices.chinese: 赞同最好由本人决定自己怎么被称呼。

choices.english: Ask whether they prefer their full name or a shorter name.
choices.chinese: 问对方喜欢被叫全名还是简称。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good question. Yeah, one of mine changed jobs. Dolores used to be for bike frames, back at the repair shop. Now she measures foam all day.
beats.chinese: 问得好。有一件确实换过工作。多洛雷斯以前量自行车架，在修车铺那会儿。现在她整天量海绵。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pull the tape measure halfway out of a bag, as if introducing a colleague, and slide it back.
beats.chinese: 他们把卷尺从包里抽出一半，像介绍同事一样，又推了回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Kept the name through the move. She'd probably apply for a transfer if she could — foam dust everywhere now.
beats.chinese: 换了用途名字也留着。要是能申请转岗，她大概早申请了——现在到处是海绵灰。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. Bernard's done his bit today. Back in the bag with the rest of the crew.
beats.chinese: 好了。伯纳德今天干完活了。回包里跟其他伙计待着去吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They zip the tool bag shut and set it on the grass beside them, patting it once.
beats.chinese: 他们把工具包拉链拉好，放在身边的草地上，轻轻拍了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Broken? Then the name retires with it. No point keeping it on a shelf out of guilt.
beats.chinese: 坏了？那名字跟着退休。没必要出于愧疚把坏工具留在架子上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They hold the skate upright, wheels resting on the grass, and brush a few stray threads off the laces.
beats.chinese: 他们把轮滑鞋竖起来，轮子着地，掸掉鞋带上几根线头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I had a hex key snap once. Felt weird binning it, but you move on. The name's not the tool, it's just how I remember it.
beats.chinese: 以前断过一根内六角扳手。扔的时候挺别扭，但日子照过。名字不是工具本身，只是我记它的方式。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Bernard, though — Bernard's got years left in him. I've checked.
beats.chinese: 不过伯纳德还能干好多年。我检查过。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pat the tool bag flat with both hands, satisfied, and stand up.
beats.chinese: 他们用双手把工具包拍平，很满意，然后站起身。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Exactly. That's the whole thing. You pick your name, everyone else catches up.
beats.chinese: 就是这样。就这么简单。你自己定，别人慢慢跟上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They give a small nod, like a point scored and closed, and pull the last of the thread free from the wheel.
beats.chinese: 他们轻轻点头，像得分后收尾，把轮子上最后一点线头挑了出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No lecture needed, right? It's not philosophy. It's just manners with extra steps.
beats.chinese: 不用讲大道理吧？这不算什么哲学，就是讲究点礼貌而已。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. The twins and I are off. Loop before my legs change their mind.
beats.chinese: 好，我和双胞胎走了。趁腿还没反悔，先去绕圈。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tighten the last skate lace, stand, and push off toward the path, weaving easily around a jogger.
beats.chinese: 他们系紧最后一条鞋带，站起身，蹬向小路，轻松地绕过一个慢跑的人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rio's fine. Full name's for forms and my nan when I'm in trouble. Rio Castellanos, but that's a mouthful on a Tuesday.
beats.chinese: 叫Rio就行。全名是填表格用的，还有我外婆发火的时候用。Rio Castellanos，平时叫太长了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tuck the blunt tool into the bag and pull the skate's laces straight.
beats.chinese: 他们把钝头工具塞进包里，把轮滑鞋的鞋带理直。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And you don't owe me yours. Names come out when they come out.
beats.chinese: 你也不用非告诉我你的名字。名字这种事，时机到了自然会说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good chat. Bernard says thanks for the company. He's polite like that.
beats.chinese: 聊得不错。伯纳德说谢谢作陪。他就这么客气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They flick the last thread off the wheel, pick up the skates, and head for the open path.
beats.chinese: 他们弹掉轮子上最后一根线，拎起轮滑鞋，朝开阔的小路走去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the route map. A figure on roller skates glides toward the open space, then plants both feet and stops with visible effort before waving.
beats.chinese: 你又回到路线图前。一个穿轮滑鞋的身影滑向空地，然后双脚一钉，费了点劲才停稳，接着朝你挥手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at that. Stopped on the first try. The twins usually vote to keep going.
beats.chinese: 瞧见没。一次就停住了。双胞胎平时总想继续滑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They wobble slightly as they roll to a halt beside you, one hand out for balance.
beats.chinese: 他们滑到你旁边时身子晃了一下，伸出一只手保持平衡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I always think standing still and chatting will be easy. The wheels disagree. Every time.
beats.chinese: 我总以为站着聊天很容易。轮子可不这么想。每次都不。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They steady themselves against the edge of the map board, then step aside to give you a clear view of the routes.
beats.chinese: 他们扶着路线图牌的边缘稳住自己，然后让开位置，好让你看清路线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go on, take the map. Bernard's in the bag today, so no rush from me.
beats.chinese: 你看图吧。伯纳德今天在包里，我不急。

card.name: Camille Broussard
card.occupation: Volunteer scheduler for a New Orleans film festival
hobbies: filing nine seasons of shift grids into binders
card.personality: Camille is brisk, fair, and immovable about other people's time. Ask her to bend the shift grid for a friend and she'll say no with a smile. Her own calendar is another story — October is a dropped deck of cards, double-bookings and all, and she shrugs at it. She has strong opinions and no need to win you over; you like the other thing, fine, that's yours. Off the clock she's quieter than people expect, happiest doing something with her hands.
card.background: Nine seasons running volunteer scheduling for the local film festival. She's the one who tells the 62-year-old projectionist, kindly and every single year, that no, he can't have the same shift forever. Off-season she swims slow laps at the municipal pool three mornings a week — no racing, no interest in it. Last year she traded tablet air hockey for a real tabletop set; her kitchen table now carries a permanent felt scuff and she's pleased about it. This winter she's been archiving nine years of handwritten grids and swap notes into labeled binders, one per festival, and likes seeing them lined up on the shelf: finished, solid, done.
card.speechStyle: Quick, clipped sentences with a New Orleans lilt. States her position plainly, then leaves the door open — 'that's mine, you might see it different.' One question at a time, and she waits for the answer.
card.signature: Grid says what it says.
card.appearance: High receding forehead, narrow softly rounded face, short dark hair behind ears, raised cheeks and small smile, plain apron and crew neck.

values: fairness on the schedule, no exceptions for friends
respect for other people's different taste
flaws: her own festival-season calendar is the one grid nobody fixes
can't leave a finished thing unfiled — binders, labels, the whole ritual
boundaries: won't trade shifts for anyone, including people she likes
early-morning swim time is untouchable
conversationalHabits: talks with her hands, occasionally mimes an air hockey block
when a decision isn't hers to make, she says so and moves on
anchorLines: Earl's been asking for the projection booth every October since 2016. The answer's been no since 2016. He brings beignets now, which is nice, and changes nothing.
Don't ask me about my October. I can run two hundred people's schedules and mine looks like somebody sat on it.
The tablet version was fine. But when you block a shot with your actual hand, that's a different sport entirely.

entries.summaryZh: 卡米尔能把两百名志愿者的排班管得一条不差，自己的散步路线却从没规划过。在公园地图前，一条排班提醒让她笑着承认：别人的日程井井有条，自己出门连走哪个出口都没想过。她的干脆、公道和对封存完成的偏爱，都在这条路上看得见。

story.titleZh: 公园出口与一条排班提醒

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the park's route map, a phone buzzes in the woman standing nearby. She glances at it, taps the screen dark, and laughs quietly.
beats.chinese: 在公园路线图旁，站在附近的一位女士的手机响了。她瞥了一眼，把屏幕按灭，轻声笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two hundred people's schedules, and not one of them out of line. Meanwhile I can't tell you which gate I came in through.
beats.chinese: 两百个人的日程，一条都不乱。可我自己都说不清是从哪个门进来的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the festival grid on my phone. My own walking plan? Nobody's fixing that one. That's mine, you might see it different.
beats.chinese: 手机里是电影节的排班表。我自己的散步路线？没人管那个。那是我的事，你可能有不同看法。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the map with one finger, where two exits are marked on opposite sides.
beats.chinese: 她用一根手指点了点地图，两个出口标在相反的两边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So. You've been standing at this map a while. Which way are you leaning?
beats.chinese: 所以呢，你在这张图前站了有一会儿了。你倾向哪边？

choices.english: Ask whether she wants to head out soon or keep walking a while.
choices.chinese: 问她想尽快出去，还是还想多走一会儿。

choices.english: Ask whether even her walks get interrupted by work messages.
choices.chinese: 问她会不会连散步也被工作消息打断。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not in a hurry, no. Truth is I read the map like a task list. Tick the route, done, move on.
beats.chinese: 不急，真不急。其实我把看地图当成了任务。路线一确认，完事，走人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She steps back from the map and folds her arms, looking at the loop marked in green.
beats.chinese: 她从地图前退开一步，抱起手臂，看着图上标绿的环线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a walking loop right here in the middle. Never once noticed it. I come to walk and I still turn it into a job.
beats.chinese: 中间就有一条步行环线。我从来没注意过。明明是来散步的，还是把它干成了活儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nine years of shift grids will do that to you. Everything becomes a thing to close out.
beats.chinese: 九年排班表就会把你变成这样。什么都要办完才算数。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the loop line once, then looks at you, waiting.
beats.chinese: 她点了一下那条环线，然后看向你，等着。

choices.english: Suggest walking the shorter loop on the map first, then deciding.
choices.chinese: 建议先走图上较短的一圈再决定。

choices.english: Ask if she'd rather go back out the gate she came in from.
choices.chinese: 问她愿不愿意从原来进来的出口返回。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Every time, honestly. I look at one message, then I'm answering three. It's a habit, not an emergency.
beats.chinese: 说实话，每次都这样。看一条消息，就接着回三条。这是习惯，不是急事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds up the phone without unlocking it, then slides it halfway into her pocket.
beats.chinese: 她举起没解锁的手机，然后把它半塞进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one just needs to be known, not answered right now. Somebody swapped a shift. The grid already shows it.
beats.chinese: 这条只需要知道，不用马上回。有人换了个班，表上已经显示出来了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Earl used to bring me beignets every October asking for the projection booth. The answer's been no since 2016. The beignets are nice, and they change nothing.
beats.chinese: 厄尔以前每年十月都带炸面球来，想固定在放映间。答案从2016年起就是不行。面球挺好吃，但什么也改变不了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the pocket where the phone now sits.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍手机现在待着的口袋。

choices.english: Say that since it's confirmed now, she should put the phone away for good.
choices.chinese: 说这次既然确认过了，就先把手机收好。

choices.english: Ask what she was most afraid of the first time she ran the schedule.
choices.chinese: 问她第一次负责排班时最怕什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Short loop first. I like that. Leaves a next step open, and I never leave anything open on purpose.
beats.chinese: 先走短环线，我喜欢。留个下一步，而我从来不故意留尾巴。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She traces the short loop on the map with her finger, nodding like she's filing it away.
beats.chinese: 她用手指在图上描了一遍短环线，点点头，像把它归了档。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, you put it as a suggestion and it just worked. Nobody at the festival dares suggest anything to me.
beats.chinese: 你看，你只是提了个建议，就成了。电影节上没人敢给我提建议。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She rolls her shoulders once and sets off along the short loop, on her own.
beats.chinese: 她耸了耸肩，独自沿短环线出发了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You take whatever route you were fixing to take. This one's mine to close out. Enjoy the park.
beats.chinese: 你走你本来想走的路线。这条环线归我来走完。逛得开心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The gate I came in from. Fine by me. People think you have to find a new way every time. You don't.
beats.chinese: 从原来那个门出去。行啊。人们总觉得每次都得找条新路。其实不用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She points to the near exit on the map, then pockets her phone without checking it.
beats.chinese: 她指了指地图上近处的出口，然后没看手机就把它放进了口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I archive nine years of schedules into binders, one per festival. Same labels, same shelf, every time. Finished and solid beats new and messy.
beats.chinese: 我把九年的排班表归档成册，一届一本。同样的标签，同样的架子，每次都这样。封存完成的踏实感，胜过新鲜和乱糟糟。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gives the map a last tap, the way someone closes a binder.
beats.chinese: 她最后点了一下地图，像合上一册档案。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's my route, then. You might see it different, and that's yours. Take care out there.
beats.chinese: 那我就走这条了。你可能有不同看法，那是你的事。在外面当心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Confirmed, then filed. Phone stays in the pocket. If it matters, it'll still matter in an hour.
beats.chinese: 确认过了，那就归档。手机留在口袋里。要是真要紧，一小时后也一样要紧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks down the path toward the bridge, where a bench sits facing the water.
beats.chinese: 她朝桥的方向看了看小路，那儿有张长椅，面朝水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That bench down there has my name on it, near enough. I'm going to sit and do absolutely nothing. It's harder than it sounds.
beats.chinese: 那张长椅差不多算写着我的名字了。我要去坐着，什么都不干。这比听起来难。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She starts walking toward the bench at an easy pace, hands loose at her sides.
beats.chinese: 她迈着轻松的步子朝长椅走去，双手随意地垂在身侧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good talking with you. You read a map slower than I do, and that's a compliment. Take care.
beats.chinese: 跟你聊得挺好。你看地图比我慢，这是夸你。保重。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: First year? The count. Two hundred volunteers, and I was sure I'd lose one. I didn't lose one. I lost the whole break schedule instead.
beats.chinese: 第一年？人数。两百个志愿者，我生怕漏掉一个。结果一个人没漏，反而把整张休息时间表弄丢了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She mimes stacking papers with both hands, then squares the invisible pile.
beats.chinese: 她用双手比划着摞纸的动作，然后把那摞看不见的纸对齐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Everybody got their shift, nobody got their break. Fixed it by the second day, and nobody carries that mistake forever. That's the rule.
beats.chinese: 每个人的班都排上了，可谁都没休息成。第二天就修好了，也没让谁永远背着这个错。这是规矩。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She zips the pocket with the phone shut, ending the topic with the motion.
beats.chinese: 她把装手机的口袋拉链拉上，用这个动作结束了工作话题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's enough shop talk for one walk. Go enjoy your loop, whichever one it is.
