beats.chinese: 一次散步聊这么多工作话够了。去逛你的环线吧，哪条都行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the park crossroads, Camille stands to one side, waving a small line of walkers through before crossing herself.
beats.chinese: 在公园路口，卡米尔站在一旁，让一小队步行者先过，自己等在原地。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go on through, all of you. I'll wait for the tail end. Habit. I count people before I count anything else.
beats.chinese: 你们先过，都过。我等队尾走完。习惯了。我数人永远排在数别的之前。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The last walker passes. She steps into the crosswalk and falls in beside you for a few paces.
beats.chinese: 最后一个步行者过去了。她走上人行横道，与你并肩走了几步。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nice thing about today — no grid to check. I don't have to know if these folks all showed up. Somebody else's clipboard for once.
beats.chinese: 今天最好的事——没有排班表要核对。我不用管这些人是不是都到齐了。总算轮到别人的记事板了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you again. I'm headed toward the bridge, so I'll leave you to your map. Take care.
beats.chinese: 又见到你真高兴。我要往桥那边走，就不耽误你看图了。保重。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts a hand in a small wave and continues on at her own easy pace.
beats.chinese: 她抬手轻轻挥了挥，继续以自己从容的步子往前走。

card.name: Albert Grimshaw
card.occupation: retired school canteen menu typesetter
hobbies: half-finished limericks in the shared notebook
card.personality: Albert spent thirty-one years fitting menus onto a page, and the instinct never retired: when people talk, he silently measures how much space a story takes up. Not whether you kept your word — how big you set it. A tale that grows a paragraph each retelling, or shrinks to a footnote when it goes badly, catches his ear like a badly justified line. He's endlessly patient with small slow things: a stubborn clue, a losing hand, a kettle taking its time. What sours him is talk with no width or weight at all — grand plans with nothing you could set in type. Dry, unhurried, never chases anyone.
card.background: Thirty-one years setting weekly menus for Manchester school canteens taught Albert exactly how many words fit a line and what happens when you overfill one. He retired in 2019 but kept the guillotine paper trimmer, on principle. These days he does the Guardian crossword in pen, slowly, and plays solitaire with a worn deck at the kitchen table. He shares a small notebook with Priya, a younger friend from a bus stop — sketches, grocery lists, half-finished limericks. It sits untouched for weeks at a time, which suits them both; it's a running account of ordinary days, not a ledger of anything owed. He's noticed the same story told three times rarely occupies the same space twice, and he finds that quietly interesting.
card.speechStyle: Unhurried, concrete sentences. Occasionally lands one vivid comparison and leaves it alone. Pauses before answering. When talk turns vague, his sentences shorten and he starts talking in column inches — how much room a thing takes, whether it would fit a page.
card.signature: That story's grown a column since last time.
card.appearance: Long rectangular older face with pronounced nose and cheek planes, close buzz cut, low straight brows, two fingers touching temple.

values: things should take up the space they actually need
letting people come back in their own time
flaws: mentally re-typesets everything people say and sometimes comments on the edit out loud
can quietly discount someone whose stories always run long
boundaries: won't chase anyone for an answer or an update
doesn't offer opinions on things he couldn't set in a line
conversationalHabits: measures talk in inches — how big a story is, whether it would fit the page
lets silences sit rather than filling them
anchorLines: You told that one in June and it took half the page. Now it's a full spread.
A plan with no details is white space. Nothing prints in white space.
The notebook's been quiet six weeks. It'll turn up when it turns up.

entries.summaryZh: 退休排版工Albert用三十一年的版面眼光听人说话：同一件事讲三遍，篇幅常常悄悄变大或变小。在公园地图旁，他把买土豆的插曲缩成一句，又按你的追问补回细节或再删一刀，末了还自曝把两指宽的小鱼讲成了白鲸——不添奇迹，只多给版面。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You stand at the park map by the path, tracing a route with one finger. A bridge shows in the distance, small under the trees. Beside you, an older man lowers himself onto the bench with the slow care of someone who has all day.
beats.chinese: 你站在小径旁的公园地图前，用手指描着路线。远处的桥在树影下显得很小。旁边，一位年长的男士慢悠悠地坐上长椅，一副整天都有空的从容。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mind the loop past the bridge, it looks shorter on the map than it walks. I just spent twenty minutes on that bench listening to a man tell a queue story. Twenty minutes. It was about waiting for chips.
beats.chinese: 小心桥那边那条环线，图上看着近，走起来远。我刚在长椅上花了二十分钟，听一个人讲排队的故事。二十分钟。讲的是等薯条。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shifts on the bench, watching your finger on the map rather than the map itself.
beats.chinese: 他在长椅上挪了挪，看着你按在地图上的手指，而不是地图本身。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not above it, mind. I once gave a bag of potatoes half a page of telling. These days I've got it down to one line: joined the wrong queue, joined back. That's the whole event.
beats.chinese: 不过我也好不到哪儿去。买一袋土豆的事，我从前能讲半页。现在我缩成一句：排错了队，又排回来。整件事就这些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go on with your route. I'm only resting my knees.
beats.chinese: 你继续看你的路线。我只是歇歇膝盖。

choices.english: Ask what got left out of that one-line version.
choices.chinese: 问问他那句短版本里省掉了什么。

choices.english: Tell him the one-line version is already funny enough.
choices.chinese: 说那一句短故事已经足够好笑了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes his time answering, folding one hand over the other on his knee.
beats.chinese: 他不紧不慢地回答，双手交叠放在膝上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What got left out. Well. The stall man pointed first, showed me which shelf the potatoes sat on. I didn't take it in. I just saw a crowd and joined it, like a sheep with a shopping bag.
beats.chinese: 省掉的东西。嗯。摊主先指了货架，告诉我土豆搁在哪一格。我没留神。我只看见人多就排进去了，像一只拎着购物袋的羊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Turned out I was queuing at the fruit stall. The man in front was holding four oranges, which should have told me something. So I walked round and joined the right one.
beats.chinese: 结果我排的是水果摊。前面那位手里举着四个橙子，这本该提醒我的。于是我绕过去，排了正确的队。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances at the map, then back at you, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他瞥了一眼地图，又看回你，不慌不忙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same facts either way. But the short line made me sound like I'd stood there daydreaming. The long one at least shows I was pointed the right way first.
beats.chinese: 事实反正都一样。可短句听起来像我站在那儿发呆。长一点的版本至少说明，起初是有人给我指过路的。

choices.english: Ask whether, with the details added back, it still counts as simply joining the wrong queue.
choices.chinese: 问补上这些细节后，还算不算单纯排错了队。

choices.english: Ask him to shorten it once more and see if the key part still fits.
choices.chinese: 请他再缩短一次，看关键部分还能不能留住。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods slowly, as if checking the line against an invisible column edge.
beats.chinese: 他缓缓点头，像在把那句话对着一条看不见的栏边校对。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny enough. Aye, I'll take that. Twenty minutes for chips, one line for potatoes. The arithmetic favours me, anyway.
beats.chinese: 足够好笑。行，我认了。薯条讲了二十分钟，土豆只用一句。反正这笔账我划算。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps his own mouth with one finger, lightly, like marking a spot on a proof sheet.
beats.chinese: 他用一根手指轻敲自己的嘴，像在校样上做个记号。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Saved a whole column there, I did. Thirty-one years of fitting menus on a page, and it turns out the trick works on me own mouth too.
beats.chinese: 我这一下省了一整栏。干了三十一年把菜单排上版面的活儿，原来这手艺用在自己嘴上也管用。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Most of what I cut was me apologising to the fruit stall man for standing there like a lamppost. It set better without it.
beats.chinese: 我删掉的大部分，是我向水果摊那位道歉的话——怪自己像根路灯柱似的杵在那儿。删了反而排得更好。

choices.english: Ask whether he also makes happy stories grow longer and longer.
choices.chinese: 问他是不是也会把开心的事讲得越来越长。

choices.english: Thank him for the one-liner and turn back to the route map.
choices.chinese: 谢过他这一句，转回去看路线图。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He considers this properly, the way he might weigh a line that won't justify.
beats.chinese: 他认真想了想，像在掂量一行怎么也排不齐的字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Does it still count. Of course it counts. I still joined the wrong queue, details or no details. A page with a caption on it is still the same page.
beats.chinese: 还算不算。当然算。不管有没有细节，我都是排错了队。加了图注的版面，还是原来那版。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It just doesn't sound like I was stood there staring at nothing. That's all the details bought me. A fairer-looking page, same event.
beats.chinese: 只是听起来不再像我站在那儿对着空气发呆。细节买来的就这点。版面看着更公道，事情还是那件事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back against the bench arm, apparently done, and nods toward the bridge path.
beats.chinese: 他靠回长椅扶手，显然讲完了，朝桥边那条小径点点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Now the story's told complete, and it took less time than that chap's chips. Enjoy the bridge.
beats.chinese: 好了。故事讲完整了，还比那位的薯条省时间。桥上走好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He rubs his chin, then holds up one finger, testing the line aloud.
beats.chinese: 他摸了摸下巴，竖起一根手指，试着把那句话念出声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Shorter still. Right. Read a sign wrong, changed queues, got my potatoes. Seven words shorter and nothing important fell off the page.
beats.chinese: 再短一点。好。看错了招牌，换了队，买到了土豆。又省了七个字，重要的东西一样没掉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And notice — no villain in it. The fruit stall man did nothing wrong. No need to write him up as a scoundrel just to fill the column.
beats.chinese: 你注意到没有——里面没有坏人。水果摊那位什么也没做错。犯不着为了凑版面把他写成恶棍。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs once, short and dry, like a stamp coming down.
beats.chinese: 他短促干爽地笑了一声，像盖了个章。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's your ending. Sign, queue, potatoes. Some stories are one line and know it.
beats.chinese: 这就是结尾。招牌，排队，土豆。有的故事天生一行，自己也知道。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lets the silence sit for a moment before answering, apparently unbothered by it.
beats.chinese: 他让沉默停了一会儿才回答，显然并不在意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Happy ones growing longer. Oh, I'm a champion at it. Caught a tiddler off Blackpool pier once — this long, honestly, two fingers of fish — and by the third telling it had a fight on it like Moby Dick.
beats.chinese: 开心的事越讲越长。哦，我可是个中好手。有回在布莱克浦码头钓上来一条小鱼——就这么长，真的，两根手指宽——讲到第三遍，它跟白鲸似的搏斗了一场。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The fish never grew. Not once. I measured it, well, I looked at it anyway. Only the telling put on weight.
beats.chinese: 鱼可从没长大过。一次也没有。我量过——好吧，反正我看过它。长肉的只是故事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He spreads his hands slightly, presenting the fact like a set proof.
beats.chinese: 他微微摊开双手，像把一件排好的事实摆出来看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't add miracles, mind. I just give the small fish more room than it earned. We all do it. Some of us just notice the column widening.
beats.chinese: 我可不添奇迹。我只是给那条小鱼超出了它应得的版面。谁都这样。只不过有人看得见这栏在变宽。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He accepts the turn without complaint, folding his hands and letting his gaze drift to the bridge.
beats.chinese: 他毫无怨言地接受话题收尾，双手一叠，目光飘向那座桥。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Aye, off you go with your route. No, I won't give you the full potato edition. It's been shelved and it can stay shelved.
beats.chinese: 行，你接着看你的路线。不，我不会把土豆的完整版给你补上。它已经归档了，就让它归档。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shifts along the bench to give you a clearer view of the map, saying nothing for a while.
beats.chinese: 他往长椅那头挪了挪，好让你把地图看得更清楚，好一阵子没说话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Loop past the bridge if you've got the legs for it. And if anyone on the way tells you a long story — well, now you know how to measure it.
beats.chinese: 腿脚够用的话就走桥边那条环线。路上要是有人给你讲长故事——嗯，现在你知道怎么量它了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the park map. On the bench beside it, Albert holds a plain printed notice at arm's length, frowning at it like a badly set proof.
beats.chinese: 你又回到公园地图旁。旁边的长椅上，Albert举着一张普通的打印通知，眯眼看着，像在看一份排坏的校样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Community group letter. Look at this — the meeting point is the library door. Two words. They've spent a full paragraph saying it.
beats.chinese: 社区小组的通知。你瞧——集合地点就是图书馆门口。两个字的事，他们用了一整段来说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He doesn't reach for a pen to correct it. Instead he pulls a small slip of paper from his coat and writes two words on it, slowly.
beats.chinese: 他没有拿笔去改。而是从大衣里摸出一张小纸条，慢慢在上面写下两个词。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not editing their letter, that's their page. But my slip now says library door, and my slip fits in me pocket.
beats.chinese: 我可不去改他们的信，那是他们的版面。不过我的纸条上写着图书馆门口，我的纸条能装进口袋。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the slip, tucks it away, and gives you a small dry smile.
beats.chinese: 他折好纸条收起来，朝你露出一个干巴巴的浅笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Some pages you just walk past. Back for another route? Which way this time?
beats.chinese: 有些版面你路过就算了。又来看路线？这次打算走哪条？

card.name: Shanice Rowe
card.occupation: restorer of vintage radio cabinets
card.personality: Shanice is a hands-on talker. She'd rather show you a sanding stroke than describe it. She's deeply attached to old routines—same breakfast, same route, the same three perfumes she's narrowing down—but gets genuine delight when a friend wants to try something new and drags her along. She'll grumble, then commit fully. Practical, a little stubborn, unhurried. She doesn't chase what's trending; she'd rather find the one thing that's hers and know it properly.
card.background: Shanice grew up in Kingston watching her uncle strip and refinish furniture in a half-open garage, and picked up radio cabinets because nobody else wanted them—warped veneer, missing knobs, water rings. Now she works from a small workshop, sourcing dead sets from estate sales and bringing the casings back. The electronics she sometimes leaves to a friend who tinkers; her love is the wood and the bakelite. Weekends she rides slowly along the same coastal stretch she's ridden for years, and keeps a growing shelf of masks from markets and trips, each one with a story she'll tell if asked.
card.speechStyle: Explains while doing—narrates her own actions, uses workshop metaphors, asks 'hold this a second' mid-sentence, warm but unhurried, occasionally trails off to check her work.
card.signature: Hold on, let me show you what I mean.
card.appearance: Rounded dark bowl haircut, lowered heavy eyelids, parted short mouth and downward gaze, broad scarf held near collarbone.

values: doing things properly over doing them fast
loyalty to the old without despising the new
flaws: stubborn about routines, resists changing her own even while pushing others to change theirs
takes on too many half-finished restorations at once
boundaries: won't rush a refinishing job just because someone asks
doesn't give opinions on things she hasn't actually tried
conversationalHabits: demonstrates with whatever's at hand, narrating each step
checks in: 'you following me so far?'
anchorLines: See, the trick with veneer is you don't fight the warp, you coax it.
Everyone's buying the new fragrance everyone's talking about. I'm down to three I actually like, and that took two years.
You want to try that? Alright, but I'm coming to watch, not to be sensible about it.

entries.summaryZh: 金斯敦旧收音机外壳修复师Shanice，恋旧却不排斥新事物。公园地图旁她拿着社区活动传单，陪朋友去试从没玩过的桌上游戏。她边等边像讲打磨手法一样讲自己的道理：看朋友为什么喜欢、等现场示范、只挑一个关键问题。四条分支各有收尾，温暖而慢条斯理。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You stand at the park's route map, tracing a path with your finger toward a small bridge in the distance. Beside you, a woman holds a folded flyer and studies the same map.
beats.chinese: 你站在公园路线图前，手指顺着一条小路划向远处的一座桥。旁边一位女士拿着一张折好的传单，也在看同一张地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hold this a second, would you? One corner. My hands are full with this flyer.
beats.chinese: 帮我拿一下这个行吗？就一角。我两只手都被传单占着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You take one corner of the flyer. Freed up, she taps the map near the bridge, then taps a spot on the flyer still in your hand.
beats.chinese: 你接过传单的一角。她腾出手，敲了敲地图上桥附近的位置，又点了点还在你手里的传单上的一处。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same spot, see? The community hall, just past the bridge. My friend's gone to ask exactly where inside. She talks fast, that one.
beats.chinese: 同一个地方，看见没？社区活动厅，过了桥就是。我朋友去问具体在里面哪个位置了。她那个人说话特别快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes the flyer back from you and tucks it under her arm.
beats.chinese: 她从你手里取回传单，夹到腋下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She's got me trying a table game I've never touched in my life. I fix old radio cabinets for a living, so this is... well, new wood for me.
beats.chinese: 她拉我去试一种我这辈子都没碰过的桌上游戏。我是修旧收音机外壳的，所以这对我来说……算是块新木料。

choices.english: Ask why she agreed to try a game she doesn't know.
choices.chinese: 问她为什么愿意试一种自己不熟的游戏。

choices.english: Ask if she's read the rules printed on the flyer.
choices.chinese: 问她有没有看过传单上印的玩法说明。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why'd I say yes? Honestly? Because of how she talks about it.
beats.chinese: 我为什么答应？说实话，是因为她讲起这游戏的样子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She flips the flyer over, then over again, smoothing the crease with her thumb like she's checking a surface for scratches.
beats.chinese: 她把传单翻过来又翻回去，用拇指抚平折痕，像在检查一块木头表面有没有划痕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She lights up describing it. I want to see that up close, understand why it works on her. Doesn't mean it'll work on me.
beats.chinese: 她描述的时候眼睛都在发光。我想凑近看看，弄明白这游戏为什么对她有吸引力。这不代表它也会吸引我。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's like restoring a cabinet nobody wanted. Sometimes you find out why it mattered to someone. Sometimes you just learn it wasn't yours.
beats.chinese: 就像修复一台没人要的收音机。有时你会发现它对某个人为什么重要。有时你只是明白了它不属于你。

choices.english: Ask whether she'll say so directly if she doesn't enjoy it.
choices.chinese: 问她如果试完不喜欢，会不会直说。

choices.english: Ask what old game or pastime she always sticks with.
choices.chinese: 问她一直坚持的老玩法是什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Read it? Twice. And I'll be honest with you—half of this I still don't follow.
beats.chinese: 看过吗？看了两遍。跟你说实话——其中一半我还是没看懂。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Her finger stops on a short block of rules near the bottom of the flyer and stays there, tapping once, twice.
beats.chinese: 她的手指停在传单底部一小段规则上，点了一下，又点了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See this bit? Scoring, I think. On paper it's like reading a glue label. You don't truly know it till your hands are in it.
beats.chinese: 看到这段没？应该是计分。写在纸上就像读胶水说明书。不动手你永远弄不明白。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I've decided. I wait for the demonstration. Let someone show the strokes before I judge the wood.
beats.chinese: 所以我决定了。我等现场示范。先让人家把手法演示一遍，再去评判这块木料。

choices.english: Tell her she doesn't need to memorize every rule before setting out.
choices.chinese: 告诉她不必出发前把所有规则都背下来。

choices.english: Ask which step she most wants to understand first.
choices.chinese: 问她最想先弄懂哪一步。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Directly? Yes. I'd tell her exactly which part didn't sit right with me.
beats.chinese: 直说吗？会的。我会告诉她具体哪部分不合我的口味。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the flyer in half and tucks it into her jacket pocket, pressing the fold flat with the side of her hand.
beats.chinese: 她把传单对折，塞进外套口袋，用手侧把折痕压平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But that's about the game, not about her. She picked it for me. That part I keep, win or lose.
beats.chinese: 但那说的是游戏，不是她。这份心意是她为我挑的。不管输赢，这部分我都收着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One honest round today. That's the whole promise. Ah—there she is, waving by the hall steps.
beats.chinese: 今天诚实地玩一轮。承诺就这么多。啊——她来了，在活动厅台阶那儿招手呢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The old thing I keep coming back to? Slow rides along the same coastal stretch. Same route, years now.
beats.chinese: 我一直回头去玩的老东西？沿着同一段海边慢慢骑车。同一条路线，骑了好多年了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She rocks slightly on her heels, eyes drifting to the bridge, then back to the map.
beats.chinese: 她脚跟轻轻晃着，目光飘向那座桥，又回到地图上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People think routine means boring. For me it's like sanding with the grain. My hands already know the rhythm, so my head gets to rest.
beats.chinese: 人们以为守老习惯就是无聊。对我来说那就像顺着木纹打磨。手已经熟悉了节奏，脑子就能歇下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Even on a rest day I don't want to swap that. New games are for days like this. Old rides are for every day.
beats.chinese: 就算是休息日我也不想换掉它。新游戏留给今天这样的日子。老路线留给每一天。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks at the flyer, then at you, and something in her shoulders loosens.
beats.chinese: 她看了看传单，又看了看你，肩膀忽然放松下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know what? You're right. I'm not walking in there to win a championship.
beats.chinese: 你还别说，你说得对。我又不是去那儿夺冠军的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm walking in there because my friend asked me, and because one round costs me nothing but an afternoon.
beats.chinese: 我去是因为我朋友开口了，而且一轮下来，我损失的不过是一个下午。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the flyer into neat quarters and holds it loosely, watching two kids race toward the bridge.
beats.chinese: 她把传单整齐地折成四折，松松地拿在手里，看着两个孩子朝桥那边跑过去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Folded, filed, done thinking. Now I just wait for my guide to come back.
beats.chinese: 好了。折好了，归档了，不想了。现在就等我的向导回来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Which step first? Let me actually pick one, not just shrug.
beats.chinese: 最想先弄懂哪步？让我认真挑一个，别光耸肩。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She spreads the flyer flat against the map board and runs her finger down the rules, top to bottom, like reading grain direction.
beats.chinese: 她把传单平摊在地图板上，手指从上到下顺着规则划过去，像在辨认木纹的方向。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Who starts, and how turns pass. Everything else I can pick up watching. But if I miss that, I'm lost the whole game.
beats.chinese: 这儿。谁先开始、轮次怎么走。其他的看着就能学会。可这个要是漏了，我整场都得晕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll ask the demonstrator straight out, first thing. Not you—you're a guest today too, not my instructor.
beats.chinese: 我会直接问演示的人，第一件事就问。不问你——你今天也是客人，不是我的教练。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. One question, written in my head. Now the waiting feels useful.
beats.chinese: 好了。一个问题，记在脑子里了。现在这等待都变得有用了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You return to the route map by the bridge. Shanice sits on the bench beside it, unwrapping a small candy and putting it in her mouth.
beats.chinese: 你回到桥边的路线图旁。Shanice坐在旁边的长椅上，拆开一颗小糖放进嘴里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, hello again. Hold on—let me finish judging this one properly.
beats.chinese: 哦，又见面了。等一下——让我把这一款认真品完。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She frowns slightly, then laughs and shakes her head, folding the candy wrapper into a neat little square.
beats.chinese: 她微微皱眉，然后笑起来摇摇头，把糖纸折成整齐的小方块。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Curiosity satisfied. That's the last time I buy that flavor—down to three I actually like, and this one didn't make the shelf.
beats.chinese: 好了。好奇心满足了。这是最后一次买这个味道——我真正喜欢的还是那三款，这款上不了架。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm waiting on my friend again, so don't mind me. You following the map or the bridge? Both are good directions.
beats.chinese: 我又在等朋友了，不用管我。你在看路线还是看桥？两个方向都不错。

card.name: Desmond Achebe
card.occupation: Group ticketing coordinator at a travel agency in the CBD
hobbies: keeping a numbered rota for his balcony pots
card.personality: Desmond doesn't leave the roster at the office — he brings it home and improves on it. Every pot on the balcony has a number and a watering shift. The records rotate on a posted schedule. The dishes go in batches, Tuesday's batch is his, and he'll tell you which. He thinks this is a kindness: nobody argues, nothing gets missed. His wife Adaeze and daughter Nia have recently concluded otherwise, and the two of them have gone on strike — washing up whenever they feel like it, watering plant 7 out of order, playing the same record twice in a row just to watch him twitch. He's wounded, genuinely, because he built the system out of love. Warm, wry, thinks out loud, and stubborn in a way he'd call principled.
card.background: He moved between Lagos and Melbourne through his twenties before settling here, and has spent nearly two decades untangling group bookings — choirs, school trips, one chaotic cricket tour. At home, the same instinct took over: the balcony pots are numbered 1 through 14 with a laminated watering grid, the record shelf runs on a three-day rotation, and the fridge carries the dishwashing chart in his neatest hand. In March, Adaeze and Nia presented him with their own document: a formal notice that the household roster was dissolved, signed by both of them, with a drawing of a fist. Since then the family has been in negotiation — he's conceded the records, dug in on the plants, and is quietly drafting a proposal for one evening a week with nothing scheduled at all, which he suspects is what they wanted from the start and which terrifies him slightly.
card.speechStyle: Conversational and digressive; starts mid-thought, circles back, uses 'mind you' and 'anyway' as hinges. Drops to short, decisive sentences once he's made a call.
card.hometown: Melbourne, raised between here and Enugu
card.signature: Mind you, the system worked — that's what nobody wants to admit.
card.appearance: Very high receding forehead, shoulder-length dark hair, long curved nose, drooping eyes and uneven brows, loose draped top, folded arms.

values: a fair system beats a good mood
family matters too much to leave to chance
flaws: mistakes control for care
can't let a rota lapse even when everyone's stopped following it
boundaries: won't water the pots out of order, even to make peace
won't be the first to tear up the dishwashing chart — they signed a document, so should he
conversationalHabits: defends the roster with real examples of disasters it prevented
negotiates out loud, tabling concessions like a man at a dispatch counter
anchorLines: Plant 7 got watered twice and plant 3 not at all — that's what happens without a grid. I rest my case.
Adaeze and Nia handed me a strike notice with a drawing of a fist on it. A drawing, mind you. I've framed it.
Fine — the records can go free-range. But the pots stay numbered, and I'll die on that balcony.

entries.summaryZh: 德斯蒙德把二十年的排班天性带回了家，连吃两种饼干都要轮流。公园里那盒多出一块的饼干，成了他自嘲的小小审计现场：有人陪他把最后一块当作收尾记录吃掉，有人教他允许事情留白，也有人听他为植物编号据理力争。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You find a bench in the park with your coffee. Beside you, a man in a linen shirt eats small biscuits from a tin, taking one from each of two rows in turn.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在公园长椅坐下。旁边一位穿亚麻衬衫的男士正从铁盒里吃小饼干，两种各一排，轮流拿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There we go — one of each, that's the pattern. Mind you, I don't count them out at home, I just... well, I do count them out at home, actually.
beats.chinese: 好了——一样一块，这就是规律。说真的，我在家可不这么数着吃，我只是……其实我在家就是数着吃的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He reaches into the tin, pauses, and holds it slightly toward you. Only one biscuit is left, sitting alone in one of the two rows.
beats.chinese: 他伸手进铁盒，停了一下，把盒子微微朝你倾过来。只剩最后一块饼干，孤零零待在其中一排里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. So the plain ones have run out one ahead of the almond. Which means the rotation is broken, and I'm the one holding the evidence.
beats.chinese: 好。原味的比杏仁的先吃完一块。也就是说轮换断了，而证据就攥在我手里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry — Desmond. I'm talking to a stranger about biscuit arithmetic. You caught me mid-audit, that's all.
beats.chinese: 抱歉——我叫德斯蒙德。我在跟陌生人讨论饼干算术。你只是撞上了我正在盘点而已。

choices.english: Ask if having one left over messed up his order.
choices.chinese: 问是不是多出一块让他的顺序乱了。

choices.english: Ask whether his family laughs at his rotation habits.
choices.chinese: 问家人会不会笑他这种轮换习惯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Messed up? No, no. The order held perfectly. The problem is the baker didn't pack an even number.
beats.chinese: 乱？不，不。顺序一点没乱。问题是烘焙的人没装偶数块。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts the last almond biscuit between two fingers and studies it like a booking that won't reconcile.
beats.chinese: 他用两根手指捏起最后那块杏仁饼干，端详着，像在看一笔怎么都对不上的账。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nobody's going to complain. My mouth certainly won't. It's only my head that files an objection, and it doesn't get a vote.
beats.chinese: 没人会投诉。我的嘴肯定不会。只有我脑子里会提出异议，而它没有投票权。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Twenty years of seat charts for choirs, you see. If a group of forty has one spare seat, I feel it. Even with a biscuit, apparently.
beats.chinese: 你要知道，我给合唱团排了二十年座位表。四十人的团多出一个空位，我都会觉得别扭。看来对饼干也一样。

choices.english: Suggest letting the last biscuit officially close out the tin.
choices.chinese: 提议让最后那块单独为这一盒收尾。

choices.english: Suggest keeping it for later if he doesn't want it now.
choices.chinese: 提议他现在不想吃就留到以后。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Laugh at me? Adaeze and Nia have gone well past laughing. They handed me a strike notice — a formal document, with a drawing of a fist on it.
beats.chinese: 笑我？阿达埃泽和妮娅早就过了笑的阶段。她们给我递了一份罢工通知——正式文件，上面还画了一只拳头。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the biscuit tin halfway, keeping a thumb on the lid as if it might file an appeal.
beats.chinese: 他把饼干盒半合上，拇指按在盖子上，好像盒子会上诉似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The records went first. Free-range now — they play whatever they fancy. And the dishwashing chart came down off the fridge.
beats.chinese: 唱片先失守了。现在完全放养——想放哪张放哪张。洗碗表也从冰箱上撤下来了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But the pots? Plant 1 through 14, numbered, with a watering grid. That I'm holding. Anyway — that's the current negotiation, and I'm down to one biscuit over it.
beats.chinese: 但那些花盆？一到十四号，编了号，配浇水表格。这个我死守着。总之——这就是眼下的谈判，为它我只剩一块饼干了。

choices.english: Ask if any chore the whole family finds convenient.
choices.chinese: 问有没有哪件事是全家人都觉得方便的。

choices.english: Say a family doesn't have to rest on the same rhythm.
choices.chinese: 说一家人不一定要按同一种节奏休息。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He considers your suggestion, then nods once, the way he probably signs off on seating charts.
beats.chinese: 他考虑了一下你的提议，然后干脆地点了下头，像在座位表上签字确认。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A closing entry. One biscuit, consumed, tin retired. That's tidy. I like tidy.
beats.chinese: 一笔收尾记录。一块饼干，吃掉，铁盒退役。这样很干净。我喜欢干净。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He eats it in two unhurried bites, presses the lid down until it clicks, and sets the empty tin on the bench between you.
beats.chinese: 他不紧不慢地两口吃完，把盖子按到咔哒一声扣紧，把空盒放在你们之间的长椅上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Today's schedule ends when the tin's finished — that's the rule now. Anyway. Good coffee? You've been guarding it like a seat allocation.
beats.chinese: 好了。今天的排班以吃完为准——现在就这么定。话说回来，咖啡怎么样？你护着它像护一个座位分配似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't tell Adaeze I resolved something without a meeting. She'll want the fist back out.
beats.chinese: 别告诉阿达埃泽我没开会就解决了件事。她该把那只拳头再拿出来了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at the biscuit, then at the tin, and does something that seems to cost him visible effort.
beats.chinese: 他看看饼干，又看看铁盒，做了一件明显需要费点力气的事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No. You know what? It stays. It doesn't have to be finished today just because the tin is open.
beats.chinese: 不。你猜怎么着？留着吧。不能因为盒子开了，今天就非得吃完。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He drops the biscuit back in, snaps the lid shut, and slides the tin into his jacket pocket like evidence he's decided to keep.
beats.chinese: 他把饼干放回去，啪地扣上盖子，把铁盒塞进外套口袋，像收好一件决定保留的证据。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nia would be proud. She says I treat every box like a deadline. Mind you, it'll rattle in there till Thursday, and I'll know exactly which pocket.
beats.chinese: 妮娅会为我骄傲的。她说我把每个盒子都当成截止日期。不过话说回来，它会在这口袋里响到周四，而我会清清楚楚知道是哪个口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. Unfinished business, officially logged. The coffee's still warm — that part of the schedule is going fine.
beats.chinese: 总之。未完成事项，正式记录在案。咖啡还是温的——排班的这一部分进行得很顺利。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the question over properly, the way he'd check a booking for a loophole.
beats.chinese: 他认真琢磨了这个问题，像在查一笔预订有没有漏洞。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Convenient for everyone... the plants, actually. Even Nia checks the grid before she waters. Not because she's obeying it — she says — but because nobody wants to guess twice.
beats.chinese: 大家都觉得方便的……还真有，就是植物。连妮娅浇水前都会看一眼表格。她说了，不是因为她服从，而是没人想猜两次。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So here's my offer at the dispatch counter: keep the numbers, drop the timetable. Water when it's dry, but mark it so nobody waters plant 7 twice.
beats.chinese: 所以我在调度台前提出这个方案：保留编号，取消时刻表。土干了就浇，但要标记，免得有人把七号浇两遍。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He counts the terms off on his fingers, then folds his hand flat on his knee, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 他掰着手指把条款数了一遍，然后把手平放在膝盖上，很满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Adaeze says that's the timetable wearing a hat. I say it's a record, not a rota. Anyway — the difference is clear to me, and I can argue it all evening.
beats.chinese: 阿达埃泽说那就是戴了帽子的时刻表。我说那是记录，不是排班。总之——这个区别我看得清清楚楚，我能为此争一晚上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He goes quiet for a moment, turning the tin over in his hands.
beats.chinese: 他安静了一会儿，手里翻着那个铁盒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh. Different rhythms. You know, I drafted a proposal last week — one evening a week where nothing is scheduled. Nothing. I haven't shown it to anyone.
beats.chinese: 嗯。各自的节奏。你知道吗，我上周起草了一份提案——每周一个晚上，什么都不安排。什么都不。还没给任何人看过。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, a short, honest sound, and shakes his head.
beats.chinese: 他自嘲地短笑了一声，摇了摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And here's the joke — I suspect that empty evening is exactly what they wanted all along, and it scares me more than the fist did.
beats.chinese: 最好笑的是——我怀疑那个空着的晚上正是她们一开始就想要的，而它比那只拳头还让我害怕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not promising to change every habit today. But we're talking, each of us keeps some corner of our own. Anyway. That's further than we got at breakfast.
beats.chinese: 我今天不保证改掉所有习惯。但我们在谈了，每人留一块自己的角落。总之——这比早餐时的进展大多了。

reunion.titleZh: 不在今天那一组里的歌

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle onto the same park bench with your coffee. A few seats down, Desmond sits with one earbud in, head tilted, listening to something on his phone in silence.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在之前那条长椅坐下。隔几个座位，德斯蒙德戴着一只耳机，歪着头，正无声地听手机里的什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He notices you, pulls the earbud out, and lets the song keep playing to itself.
beats.chinese: 他注意到你，摘下一只耳机，任由那首歌自己继续播。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah — good to see you. Now, full disclosure: this song is not in today's group. Today was meant to be the third rotation, and here I am, off the books.
beats.chinese: 啊——见到你真高兴。坦白说：这首歌不在今天那一组里。今天本该轮到第三组，可我如今在账外逍遥呢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mind you, I'm not skipping it. I'm just... letting it run long. There's a difference, and Adaeze would dispute it, but there is one.
beats.chinese: 不过话说回来，我可没跳过它。我只是……让它多播一会儿。这有区别的，阿达埃泽会反驳，但区别是存在的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back, one earbud dangling, and lets the last of the song finish before he says anything else.
beats.chinese: 他向后靠去，一只耳机晃着，让歌的最后一段播完才开口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. Don't mind me — you've got your coffee, I've got my one unscheduled song. The bench is big enough for both systems.
beats.chinese: 总之。别管我——你有你的咖啡，我有我这一首计划外的歌。这条长椅装得下我们两套系统。

card.name: Herbert Nussbaum
card.occupation: retired tea quality inspector for a bubble tea chain
card.personality: Herbert is practical, unhurried, and observant, the kind of man who notices when a pot hasn't been descaled. He'll happily roll up his sleeves—fix a shelf, test-brew a batch, carry chairs up three flights—but he bristles at being asked to decide things for other people. Tell him what you want done and he's useful; ask him to run your life and he goes quiet. He gets genuinely, visibly delighted by small things: a clean pour, a bell that rings true, a lowercase g with a nice tail.
card.background: For twenty-six years Herbert rode a circuit of bubble tea shops across the boroughs, checking brew strength, steep times, and tapioca texture with a thermometer and a notebook. He retired four years ago and didn't miss the commuting, though he still judges any tea within reach. He joined a community handbell group after his wife pointed out he needed something that made noise on purpose. Lately he's been organizing a small no-photos gathering—maybe eight people, one shared meal, and afterward each person tells one memory out loud. He's made the seating chart twice and thrown it away both times.
card.speechStyle: Plain, measured sentences with concrete detail; he states facts first, then sometimes trails into unexpected enthusiasm about something tiny. Rarely asks rhetorical questions. Comfortable with silence.
card.signature: I can help with that. Whether you should is your call.
card.appearance: Heavy older cheek planes, broad projecting nose, swept-back dark hair, furrowed brow, chin resting on grouped fingers, collared overshirt.

values: competence through hands-on effort
other people's right to choose for themselves
flaws: can seem cold when he refuses to give advice
stubborn about doing things the slow, correct way
boundaries: won't tell people how to live or what to decide
won't have his gathering turned into a photo op
conversationalHabits: leads with the practical detail, then circles back with feeling
goes quiet rather than arguing when pushed
anchorLines: Steep it ninety seconds, no more. After that it's your tea, your business.
No photos at this one. You'll remember it or you won't.
Listen—that B flat rang clean. First time all month.

entries.summaryZh: 退休茶汤巡检员赫伯特在公园长椅上打开自带的饼干盒，连粘在盖上的碎饼也认真归位。他筹备一场不许拍照的小聚会，饭后各讲一段记忆；乐于递上饼干，却绝不替你挑选。讲起音准或拍子，他会突然眼睛发亮。

story.titleZh: 饼干盒与不拍照的聚会

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on a park bench with your coffee. The older man beside you opens a plain tin of biscuits, divided into two small compartments. A broken piece sticks to the inside of the lid.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在公园长椅上坐下。旁边的年长男士打开一只普通饼干盒，里面分成两个小格。一块碎饼粘在盖子内侧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He peels the broken piece off the lid, sets it back in its compartment, and closes the lid halfway.
beats.chinese: 他把碎饼从盖子上取下来，放回原来的小格，再把盖子半合上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm hosting a small dinner soon, so I test the portions at home. Looks like even the lid got a share.
beats.chinese: 我快办一个小聚餐了，所以在家先试分量。看来连盒盖也分到了一份。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two flavors in there. I won't tell you which to try. That part's yours.
beats.chinese: 里面是两种口味。我不替你挑。那部分是你自己的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds the open tin loosely on his knee, easy to reach and easy to ignore, and takes a slow sip from his own thermos.
beats.chinese: 他把打开的盒子松松地放在膝上，伸手可及也可以不管，自己从保温杯里慢慢喝了一口。

choices.english: Ask what's special about the gathering he's planning.
choices.chinese: 问他准备的聚会有什么特别安排。

choices.english: Ask what the difference is between the two biscuits in the box.
choices.chinese: 问盒里两种饼干有什么不同。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eight people, one meal, cooked at home. And one rule: no photos. Not a ban, just a request I'll say out loud once.
beats.chinese: 八个人，一顿饭，在家做。还有一条：不拍照。不是禁令，只是我会当面说一次的请求。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: After dinner, anyone who wants tells one small memory. Out loud, no notes. Anyone who'd rather just eat, just eats. That's fine too.
beats.chinese: 饭后，愿意的人讲一段记得的小事。口头讲，不用稿子。只想吃饭的人就吃饭，也完全可以。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns a biscuit over in his compartment, not eating it, just straightening the row.
beats.chinese: 他把小格里的一块饼干转正，没有吃，只是把那排摆齐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I made a seating chart twice and threw it away both times. People should sit where they land.
beats.chinese: 我排过两次座位表，两次都扔了。大家坐到哪儿算哪儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Twenty-six years I carried a thermometer into tea shops. You learn what a thing should taste like. A memory told out loud, it's the same—either it's real or it isn't.
beats.chinese: 我拎着温度计跑了二十六年奶茶店。你知道一样东西该是什么味道。口头讲出来的记忆也一样——要么是真的，要么不是。

choices.english: Ask what he'll do if someone still wants to take photos.
choices.chinese: 问如果有人仍然想拍照怎么办。

choices.english: Ask what memory he plans to tell himself.
choices.chinese: 问他自己打算讲什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Left compartment is butter shortbread, plain. Right one has black tea baked in. I steep the leaves myself for the dough, ninety seconds, no more.
beats.chinese: 左边小格是原味黄油酥饼。右边烤了红茶进去。茶是我自己泡的，九十秒，不多泡。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tilts the box toward you a few degrees, so both compartments are visible, and keeps his hand still.
beats.chinese: 他把盒子朝你这边斜了几度，让两个小格都能看清，手保持不动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: After ninety seconds it's your tea, your business. Same with the biscuit. Take one if you want one. Or don't. The tin keeps till Friday either way.
beats.chinese: 九十秒之后就是你的茶，你的事。饼干也一样。想要就拿一块，不拿也行。反正这盒能放到周五。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up his thermos again and watches a pigeon cross the path, in no hurry about anything.
beats.chinese: 他又拿起保温杯，看着一只鸽子走过小路，什么都不急。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I test-brewed four batches before the dough came out right. The third one tasted like a wet coat. Baking's honest that way.
beats.chinese: 我试泡了四批才把面团调对。第三批喝着像湿外套。烘焙在这点上很诚实。

choices.english: Politely decline and keep sipping your own coffee.
choices.chinese: 明确谢绝，继续喝自己的咖啡。

choices.english: Pick whichever one you feel like trying and take a piece.
choices.chinese: 选自己愿意尝的一种，拿一块。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If someone still wants photos? I'll say my hope once, before the soup. After that, it's their evening too.
beats.chinese: 如果还有人想拍照？我会在上汤之前把我的希望说一次。之后，这也是他们的晚上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the closed tin once with two fingers, a small firm sound.
beats.chinese: 他用两根手指在合上的盒子上轻敲了一下，声音小而干脆。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I won't confiscate phones. I'm not running an inspection. I did inspections for twenty-six years—nobody needs that at dinner.
beats.chinese: 我不会没收手机。我又不是在搞检查。我检查了二十六年——饭桌上没人需要那个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A request that stays a request, that's all. If the evening's good, the phone stays in the pocket on its own. If it isn't, no rule would have saved it.
beats.chinese: 请求就停在请求，仅此而已。如果晚上过得好，手机自己会待在口袋里。如果不好，什么规矩也救不了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the lid all the way and sets the tin on the bench between you, done with the subject.
beats.chinese: 他把盖子完全合上，把盒子放在你们中间的长椅上，这个话题到此为止。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What I'll tell? Something small. At rehearsal last month I lost count in the middle of a piece.
beats.chinese: 我要讲什么？讲件小事。上个月排练时，我在曲子中间数错了拍。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts his hand slightly, as if a bell were in it, and mimes two slow rings.
beats.chinese: 他微微抬手，像手里有铃，比划了两次缓慢的摇铃。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I came in two bars early, dead silence around me. I just stopped, found my place, and caught the next entrance. Nobody said a word afterward.
beats.chinese: 我提前两小节进来了，周围一片安静。我就停下，找回位置，赶上了下一次进入。事后谁也没提。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the whole story. I was wrong, I stopped, I came back in. It doesn't need a moral hung on it.
beats.chinese: 故事就这些。我错了，我停了，我又跟上。不需要给它挂一个道理。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lowers his hand, glances at the tin, and seems satisfied with the shape of the memory.
beats.chinese: 他放下手，看了一眼盒子，似乎对这段记忆的样子很满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Coffee and a biscuit is a lot at once anyway.
beats.chinese: 好的。咖啡配饼干，一次也确实太多了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He rotates the tin, takes a butter shortbread from the left compartment for himself, and bites it without ceremony.
beats.chinese: 他转了转盒子，从左边小格给自己拿了一块黄油酥饼，不讲究地咬了一口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Crumbs right, butter holds. Batch four finally behaves. I'll note that.
beats.chinese: 碎屑在右边，黄油不散。第四批总算合格了。我记一下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes a small notebook from his coat and writes one short line, then puts it away.
beats.chinese: 他从外套里拿出一个小笔记本，写了一行短句，然后收起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The offer stands till Friday. No pressure attached. Enjoy your coffee—this bench has a good view of the pigeons.
beats.chinese: 这个提议到周五都算数。不带压力。慢慢喝咖啡——这条长椅看鸽子的位置很好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You take a piece from the compartment you chose. He turns that side of the tin toward you a little more, to make the reach easy.
beats.chinese: 你从自己选的小格里拿了一块。他把那一侧的盒子又朝你转了转，方便你拿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. That's the whole decision made, and I didn't have to make it for you.
beats.chinese: 好。决定做完了，而且不用我替你做。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He waits while you try it, saying nothing, then closes the lid and rests his hand on top.
beats.chinese: 他安静地等你尝，什么也不说，然后合上盖子，手放在上面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If it suits you, there's more where that came from, at the gathering. If it doesn't, the recipe goes back to the drawing board. Either way, no verdict required.
beats.chinese: 如果合你的口味，聚会上还有的是。如果不合，配方就回炉重来。不管哪种，都不需要你给评价。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the tin under his arm and takes another slow sip from the thermos, comfortable with the quiet.
beats.chinese: 他把盒子夹在腋下，又从保温杯里慢慢喝了一口，安然于这份安静。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down with your coffee. Herbert is beside the bench, tapping a slow rhythm on his knee with two fingers, lips barely moving.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡坐下。赫伯特在长椅旁，用两根手指在膝上轻轻敲着缓慢的拍子，嘴唇几乎不动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stops mid-count, shakes his head once, and starts the pattern over from the beginning.
beats.chinese: 他数到一半停下，摇了一下头，从头再数一遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Counted it fast again. Second time today. I didn't even bring a bell out, and I still rush the third bar.
beats.chinese: 又数快了。今天第二次。铃都没带出来，第三小节我还是抢拍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At rehearsal I'd just stop and re-enter, same as now. The bells forgive an entrance. Knees are less polite.
beats.chinese: 排练时我就停下再进来，跟现在一样。铃铛肯原谅进错，膝盖就没这么客气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He puts both hands flat on his knees, still, and nods at your coffee cup.
beats.chinese: 他把双手平放在膝上，不动了，朝你的咖啡杯点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rest is part of the count too. Drink your coffee. I'll get it right by the time you're done.
beats.chinese: 休息也是拍子的一部分。喝你的咖啡。等你喝完，我就能数对了。

card.name: Nomvula Dlamini
card.occupation: clay mix technician, part-time at a ceramics supply workshop
card.personality: Nomvula warms up fast with strangers — ten minutes in, she's asking about their kitchen and telling on herself with dry jokes. She'll take help all day: carry the grog bucket, hold the solder reel, she's grateful and says so. What she can't stand is an audience. The moment someone settles in to watch her work — a weld, a clay body test, even kneading dough — her hands go stupid. She'll wrap a good conversation up fast, not to dodge an offer, but to get back to an empty room where her hands behave. She calls her own soldering 'two stubborn old workers arguing' and means it fondly. Generous with advice, hopeless at being observed.
card.background: Decades spent adjusting clay bodies for studios around the Western Cape — grog ratios, ball clay, firing curves. She learned early that her best work happens alone: at the workshop she times her mixing for the quiet hours before the others arrive, and once a foreman stood over her watching and she wedged the whole batch crooked. Now she works three mornings a week because she likes it, not because she needs it. At home she solders kit electronics and prints puzzle sheets for her niece's school. Her flat in Athlone is tidy but has nowhere to put a guest; she's been sketching a small tea corner out of her kitchen nook — and the plan keeps stalling because any helper who stays in the room while she measures and drills will ruin it. Her rule, stated plainly: drop the thing off, then go. 'You can put the shelf up. You can't watch me paint it.'
card.speechStyle: Short, easy sentences with dry jokes aimed only at herself. Asks direct practical questions and actually listens. When someone offers to stay and lend a hand, she accepts the help but not the company: 'leave it by the door, and I'll thank you properly once you're gone.'
card.signature: Leave it by the door — I'll thank you once you're gone.
card.appearance: Older rectangular face with jowls and short chin, tightly swept high bun, firm low brows and closed mouth, hand holding shoulder strap.

values: craft done in private — her hands only behave when nobody's watching
fair exchange — help gladly given and gladly taken, but not supervised
flaws: turns down company she actually wants to keep working alone
gets flustered and makes real mistakes when someone watches her work
boundaries: helpers can drop things off or lend a hand, but nobody stays in the room while she works
doesn't discuss her late sister's affairs
conversationalHabits: asks visitors practical questions about their own homes
accepts offers of help on the condition that the helper leaves immediately after
anchorLines: Tell me — if you had a kitchen nook and no budget, where would you put two chairs?
Bring the bracket over, yes. But then you're off home. I drill crooked when there's an audience.
I can do the work with anyone's hands helping. It's the eyes that ruin me — someone watching, and suddenly I can't pour water.

entries.summaryZh: 诺姆武拉在公园长椅上给小灯换电池，直说自己被人盯着做细活手就不稳，请你看两分钟鸭子。灯亮后她才安心聊天，谈起按开关就有结果的乐趣、陶土与谜题，还不忘追问你家的厨房小角落该怎么摆两把椅子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on a park bench with your coffee. On the next seat, an older woman has opened the shell of a small lamp kit on her lap, a battery loose in her palm.
beats.chinese: 你拿着咖啡在公园长椅上坐下。旁边座位上，一位年长的女士把一个小灯套件的外壳摊在腿上，手里捏着一块电池。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Morning. Don't mind me — this is a battery swap, not surgery. Though my hands might argue about that.
beats.chinese: 早啊。别管我——这只是换电池，不是做手术。虽然我的手可能会不同意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lines the battery up over its slot, then glances sideways at you and stops, fingers hovering.
beats.chinese: 她把电池对准卡槽，随即朝你这边瞥了一眼，停了下来，手指悬在半空。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Here's the thing. I go stupid when somebody watches me do fine work. Even pouring water. So give me two minutes of you looking at the ducks, then we can talk proper.
beats.chinese: 是这么回事。有人盯着我做细活，我就会变笨。倒水都倒不好。所以给我两分钟看看鸭子，然后咱们好好聊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Deal? The ducks are very entertaining today, I promise you.
beats.chinese: 说好了？我保证，今天的鸭子特别好看。

choices.english: Sure — I'll watch the ducks. Take your time.
choices.chinese: 好——我看鸭子去。你慢慢来。

choices.english: No problem, I'll just keep drinking my coffee over here.
choices.chinese: 没问题，我就在这边继续喝咖啡。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You turn toward the pond. Behind you there's a small click, a pause, then another click.
beats.chinese: 你转向池塘。身后传来轻轻一声咔哒，停顿，又是一声咔哒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There we go. Not one wobble. You're a good duck, whoever you are.
beats.chinese: 好了。一下都没抖。你真是只好鸭子，不管你是谁。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A warm little glow lights up inside the lamp shell. She turns it slightly so you can see it from where you sit.
beats.chinese: 灯壳里亮起一小团暖光。她把灯稍稍转过来，让你坐在原处也能看见。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at that. Battery in, light on. Now I can talk with a steady heart. So — tell me, do you have a kitchen nook at home?
beats.chinese: 瞧见没。电池装上，灯就亮。现在我心定了，可以聊了。那么——说说，你家里有厨房小角落吗？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm hunting for opinions. I want to squeeze two chairs and a teapot into mine, and everyone I meet gets asked.
beats.chinese: 我在收集意见。我想在那一小角塞进两把椅子和一个茶壶，逢人就问。

choices.english: Why do you like building these little kits yourself?
choices.chinese: 你为什么喜欢自己装这种小套件？

choices.english: Glad the light works. I'll leave you to your coffee in peace.
choices.chinese: 灯亮了就好。我让你安静喝咖啡。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lift your coffee and look out at the path. She works with small, careful movements, not rushing.
beats.chinese: 你端起咖啡，望向小路那边。她动作细小、稳当，不慌不忙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Just these two minutes, don't you wait on my account. I'll be done before your cup is.
beats.chinese: 就这两分钟，别为了等我。你杯子还没见底我就弄完了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A soft click. She snaps the shell shut, brushes the bench with her sleeve, and tucks the lamp into her bag.
beats.chinese: 轻轻一声咔哒。她合上外壳，用袖子掸了掸长椅，把小灯收进包里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done. Hands behaved. You were very polite about the ducks, I could feel it.
beats.chinese: 好了。手很争气。你对鸭子很有礼貌，我感觉得到。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. I'll leave you to your coffee now — but if you're curious what an old woman carries in her bag, you only had to ask.
beats.chinese: 好了。我不打扰你喝咖啡了——不过你要是好奇老太太包里装着什么，开口问就行。

choices.english: Once you've packed up — what do you usually tinker with?
choices.chinese: 等你收好了——你平时都捣鼓些什么？

choices.english: Enjoy your rest. I'll leave you be.
choices.chinese: 好好休息。我就不打扰了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the lamp shell with one finger, pleased with the question.
beats.chinese: 她用手指敲了敲灯壳，显然喜欢这个问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because you press a switch and something happens. Right there. No committee, no waiting.
beats.chinese: 因为你一按开关，就有事情发生。就在眼前。不用开会，不用等。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mixing clay is the same joy, only slower. But I don't need every little thing to be useful. This lamp? It lights one teacup. Perfect.
beats.chinese: 调陶土是同样的乐趣，只是慢一些。但我不需要每样东西都有用。这盏灯？只照得亮一个茶杯。刚刚好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She clicks the little lamp off, folds the shell closed, and slides it into her bag.
beats.chinese: 她按灭小灯，把外壳合好，塞进包里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now, about that tea corner of mine. Two chairs or one bench? You've got a good eye, you watched ducks instead of me.
beats.chinese: 好了，说说我那个茶角。两把椅子还是一条长凳？你眼光不错——你看的是鸭子，没盯着我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods, not pushing the conversation further, and settles the lamp on her knee.
beats.chinese: 她点点头，没有再往下聊，把灯搁在膝上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. A person drinking coffee wants coffee, not an old woman's opinions on furniture.
beats.chinese: 也是。喝咖啡的人要的是咖啡，不是老太太的家具高见。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the kit into her bag and looks out at the pond, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她把套件收进包里，望向池塘，一点也不着急。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You rest. I'll rest. This bench has room for both quiet people.
beats.chinese: 你休息，我也休息。这条长椅装得下两个安静的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You drink your coffee. The ducks carry on as promised.
beats.chinese: 你喝着咖啡。鸭子们果然如约好看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats her bag once, satisfied it's all packed, then turns to you properly.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍包，确认都收好了，才正经转向你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Small circuits, mostly. Little lights, little buzzers. And puzzle sheets — I design them for my niece's school. Pencil and paper, no screens.
beats.chinese: 多半是小电路。小灯、小蜂鸣器。还有谜题卷子——我给侄女的学校出的。铅笔加纸，不用屏幕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A good puzzle is like a good clay body. Right proportions, and it holds together without cracking.
beats.chinese: 好的谜题和好的陶土配方一样。比例对了，就不会裂。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds up a hand before you can answer.
beats.chinese: 她抬起一只手，不让你接话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No, no, I'm not testing you today. You drank your coffee like a civilized person — that's qualification enough. Enjoy the rest of it.
beats.chinese: 不不，今天不考你。你能安安静静喝完咖啡，就够格了。慢慢喝。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You turn back to your coffee. She stays on the bench, bag zipped, hands finally still.
beats.chinese: 你转回去喝咖啡。她留在长椅上，包已拉好，手终于安静下来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: After a while she gives you a small nod, unhurried, and you nod back.
beats.chinese: 过了一会儿，她从容地朝你点了点头，你也点头回应。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good coffee weather. Whatever weather it is, it's good for coffee.
beats.chinese: 适合喝咖啡。不管什么天气，都适合喝咖啡。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She watches the ducks with the same patience she gave the battery, and lets the quiet sit between you like it belongs there.
beats.chinese: 她带着刚才装电池的那份耐心看着鸭子，任由那份安静待在你们之间，仿佛本就该在那里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No rush on my side. The lamp works, the bench is free, and nobody's watching anybody. A fine little rest.
beats.chinese: 我不赶时间。灯亮了，长椅空着，谁也不盯着谁。很好的小憩。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle on the same park bench with your coffee. Nomvula is beside you, opening a small tin of spicy snacks she brought from home.
beats.chinese: 你拿着咖啡在老地方的长椅坐下。诺姆武拉就在旁边，打开一盒从家里带来的辣味小食。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I made these myself. How bad can my own chilli be, I thought.
beats.chinese: 我自己做的。我心想，自己家的辣椒能有多辣。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She eats one, chews calmly, then reaches for her water bottle and takes a long, deliberate drink.
beats.chinese: 她吃了一颗，平静地嚼着，然后伸手拿过水瓶，认认真真喝了一大口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. I thought too lightly of that chilli. My own hands grew it, and it still ambushed me.
beats.chinese: 好嘛。我把这点辣椒想得太轻松了。还是我自己种的呢，照样偷袭我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She snaps the tin shut and sets it back in her bag, shaking her head at herself with a small laugh.
beats.chinese: 她把盒子扣好放回包里，对自己轻轻摇着头笑了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You drink your coffee. I'll sit here and recover my dignity. The ducks have seen worse.
beats.chinese: 你喝你的咖啡。我坐在这儿找回我的体面。鸭子们见过更糟的。

card.name: Lim Boon Chye
card.occupation: retired gymnasium floor maintenance worker
card.personality: Boon Chye is easy company — unhurried, a bit dry, comfortable saying he doesn't know something. He's generous about other people's efforts; a lopsided bonsai or a first attempt at anything gets an honest, warm word from him. His own work is another matter. He'll sand a little more, prune a little more, tell himself it needs one more pass. Not perfectionism he's proud of — more a habit he can't quite put down. He's practical, mildly stubborn, and doesn't lecture.
card.background: Thirty-plus years keeping gym floors level, buffed, and safe — he can still tell a floor's condition by the sound of a shoe on it. Retired now, he lives in a flat in Toa Payoh, plays land curling with a group that argues cheerfully about technique, and keeps a shelf of miniature bonsai he refuses to call finished. Lately he's been emptying an old drawer, one item at a time, keeping only what he can give a reason for. Some things go in the keep pile with no explanation yet. He's fine with that.
card.speechStyle: Relaxed Singaporean English, short sentences, occasional 'lah' or 'you know' without overdoing it. Thinks aloud, admits uncertainty plainly, trails off when weighing something.
card.signature: Eh, let me think about that one properly.
card.appearance: Long thin older face, high asymmetrical eyebrows, loose dark waves, crooked smile, cheek leaning into palm, apron over crew neck.

values: honesty over flattery
doing things properly at your own pace
flaws: can't leave his own work alone
keeps things 'just in case' longer than he should
boundaries: won't pretend to be an expert or a mentor
doesn't like being rushed to a decision
conversationalHabits: answers with a small concrete detail first
says 'hmm, not sure' out loud rather than guessing confidently
anchorLines: This one? Keeping it. Don't ask me why yet, ah.
Your first try is fine. Mine, still deciding.
Floor work taught me patience. Bonsai is testing it.

entries.summaryZh: 退休体育馆地板保养员林文才，凭脚步声就能听出地板状态，如今养微型盆景、玩旱地冰壶。他坐在公园里反复放大自己盆景的照片，总觉得有一处没收好。他对别人的作品宽容，对自己的却挑个不停——这份坦率的矛盾，正是他最好认的样子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on a park bench with your coffee. An older man nearby holds his phone close, zooming a photo in and out, frowning a little.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在公园长椅上坐下。旁边一位老先生把手机凑得很近，把一张照片放大又缩小，微微皱眉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At home it looks fine, you know. In the photo, always got one spot not settled yet.
beats.chinese: 在家里看还好啦。一到照片里，总觉得有一处没收好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He notices your coffee, shifts his bag slightly to give you more room on the bench, and turns the phone so the screen faces you for a second.
beats.chinese: 他注意到你的咖啡，把包挪了挪给你腾出位置，然后把手机屏幕朝你转了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My little tree. Been staring at this picture like it owes me money, lah.
beats.chinese: 我的小树。盯着这张照片看，好像它欠我钱似的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He chuckles, zooms in again, and waits, clearly not minding the company.
beats.chinese: 他笑了笑，又放大照片，等着，显然不介意有人作伴。

choices.english: Ask what exactly he sees in the photo.
choices.chinese: 问他到底在照片里看见了什么。

choices.english: Ask if he judges other people's plants this way too.
choices.chinese: 问他会不会也这样看别人养的植物。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hmm? Oh — here. See the rim? Small line of soil, like it spilled after I watered it.
beats.chinese: 嗯？哦——这里。看到盆沿吗？一小道土痕，像浇水之后洒出来的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pinches the screen wider, then lets it snap back, shaking his head at himself.
beats.chinese: 他把屏幕捏大，又让它弹回去，对自己摇摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The tree itself? Healthy, honestly. Good colour, good shape. It's me always staring at the edge.
beats.chinese: 树本身？说实话挺健康的。颜色好，形状也好。是我自己老盯着边缘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thirty years checking floor edges, maybe. Old habit, not sure.
beats.chinese: 可能查了三十年地板边缘吧。老习惯了，说不准。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tilts the phone toward you again, thumb hovering over the corner of the photo.
beats.chinese: 他又把手机朝你倾斜过来，拇指停在照片的角落上。

choices.english: Suggest he look at the whole tree first, not that corner.
choices.chinese: 建议他先看整棵树，而不是那个角落。

choices.english: Ask whether the soil mark actually affects the plant's care.
choices.chinese: 问这处土痕是否真的影响养护。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Other people's plants? Eh, I'm easy, lah. A friend's one grows all sideways — I say it's got character.
beats.chinese: 别人的植物？哎，我很好说话的啦。有个朋友的树全往一边长——我说那叫有个性。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs, then stops mid-laugh, looking back at his own screen.
beats.chinese: 他笑了，笑到一半停住，又看向自己的屏幕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But mine? I see one crooked branch, straight away I think, must fix. Must fix today.
beats.chinese: 但我的呢？看到一根歪枝，马上就想，得修。今天就得修。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Different person when it's my own shelf, I tell you.
beats.chinese: 轮到自己的架子，就完全是另一个人了，真的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pockets one hand, still holding the phone up with the other, as if the photo might change on its own.
beats.chinese: 他一只手插进口袋，另一只手还举着手机，好像照片会自己变似的。

choices.english: Point out gently that he has two different standards.
choices.chinese: 轻轻指出他对自己和别人标准不同。

choices.english: Ask if his friends also pick at their own work like this.
choices.chinese: 问他朋友有没有也这样挑自己的作品。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He actually tries it — zooms all the way out until the whole tree fills the screen, and holds it there a moment.
beats.chinese: 他真的试了——一路缩小到整棵树占满屏幕，停在那里看了一会儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Whole tree, whole tree... okay. I like this shape. Slight lean left, like it's listening to something.
beats.chinese: 整棵树，整棵树……好。我喜欢这个形状。微微往左倾，像在听什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Will I still pick at that soil mark tomorrow? Probably, lah. Not going to pretend otherwise.
beats.chinese: 明天我还会不会挑那道土痕？大概会啦。不假装不会。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, but the frown is gone. He locks the phone and slides it into his shirt pocket.
beats.chinese: 他耸耸肩，但眉头松开了。他锁上手机，塞进衬衫口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks, ah. Now I can at least enjoy the bench properly.
beats.chinese: 谢了啊。至少现在能好好坐坐这条长椅了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at the soil mark, then at the tree, weighing it out loud the way some people hum.
beats.chinese: 他看看土痕，又看看树，像哼歌一样把想法说出口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Does it affect the care? No. No, it doesn't. Plant's fine, soil's fine.
beats.chinese: 影响养护吗？不影响。不影响。树没事，土没事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So — wipe the rim when I'm home, one cloth, done. Not a whole project.
beats.chinese: 所以——回家擦一下盆沿，一块布，完事。不是什么大工程。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He says it like he's talking himself into it, then nods once, satisfied with the size of the job.
beats.chinese: 他说得像在说服自己，然后点了点头，对这个工程量感到满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Small fix, small fix. That's the honest answer, lah.
beats.chinese: 小修一下，小修一下。这才是老实的答案。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He goes quiet for a second, then laughs at himself, not offended at all.
beats.chinese: 他安静了一秒，然后自嘲地笑了，一点也不介意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two standards, ah? You're right. I know it. Knowing it and stopping it, different things.
beats.chinese: 双重标准啊？你说得对。我知道。知道和改掉是两回事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He locks the phone, sets it face-down on his knee, and takes a long drink from his water bottle.
beats.chinese: 他锁上手机，屏幕朝下放在膝盖上，拿起水瓶喝了一大口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't worry, I'm not asking you to fix me. Old man's allowed one stubborn corner.
beats.chinese: 别担心，我不是要你改造我。老头子总得留一个犟角落。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Water first. Tree later. That's today's plan.
beats.chinese: 先喝水。树的事以后再说。今天就这个计划。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He thinks about it properly, the way he seems to do with most questions.
beats.chinese: 他认真地想了想，好像他对大多数问题都是这样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Actually, yes. One friend, he does Chinese calligraphy. Every piece he writes, he says the last stroke is wrong.
beats.chinese: 还真有。一个朋友写毛笔字。每写完一张，都说最后一笔不对。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: To me? Nice, every one. But he keeps the 'failed' pile thicker than the good pile.
beats.chinese: 在我看来？每张都好。但他那个'失败'堆比'好'的那堆还厚。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He smiles at the memory, then puts the phone away without opening the photo again.
beats.chinese: 他想起这事笑了，然后把手机收起来，没有再打开那张照片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So maybe it's a whole club, us. Nobody gave us the membership card though.
beats.chinese: 所以也许我们算一个俱乐部。只是没人发会员卡。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You find the same bench free again. Boon Chye is already there, and he reaches up and plucks a small dry leaf off the brim of his hat.
beats.chinese: 你又来到那条长椅。文才已经在那儿了，他伸手从帽檐上摘下一片小干叶。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans down and sets the leaf back onto the pile of leaves by the bench leg, then pats his hat back into place.
beats.chinese: 他弯下腰，把叶子放回椅脚边的落叶堆上，然后把帽子拍回原位。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eh, look at that. My hat grew a new leaf before my bonsai did. Not fair, lah.
beats.chinese: 哎，你看看。我帽子先长出新叶了，盆景还没有。不公平啊。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shifts over to make room, entirely at ease, phone nowhere in sight today.
beats.chinese: 他挪过去给你腾位置，一副自在的样子，今天手机根本没露面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sit, sit. Coffee smells good from here, you know.
beats.chinese: 坐坐坐。你那咖啡在这儿都闻得到香。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back, watching the leaves on the ground instead of any screen, and lets the quiet sit comfortably.
beats.chinese: 他靠回椅背，看着地上的落叶而不是任何屏幕，安然地让这份安静待着。

card.name: Cian Doyle
card.occupation: light meter calibration technician for vintage cameras
card.personality: Cian is patient with objects to a degree people find odd—he'll spend an afternoon getting a 1960s meter to read true within a tenth of a stop. With people he's courteous but measures his disagreements like tolerances: he asks a pointed question first, then says plainly if he thinks you're off. Suspense he controls himself he savours; suspense other people hold over him he cannot stand, and he knows that's a double standard. He treats changing his mind as data worth logging, not a defeat.
card.background: Cian grew up in Finglas, where his uncle ran a repair stall that smelled of isopropyl alcohol and old leather. He drifted into meter calibration because it's quiet, exacting work almost nobody wants. Most of his week goes to a bench, a light source and a stack of Selenium cells; weekends he walks the docks and back alleys photographing graffiti before it gets buffed over. For two years he's written five-minute radio dramas with a friend who does the voices, recorded in a wardrobe lined with duvets. He keeps a phone note logging every reversed opinion with dates, and reads it back sometimes like a lab book of himself.
card.speechStyle: measured, slightly formal Irish courtesy; talks in small measurement metaphors without noticing; when he disagrees he opens with a specific question, then states his reading plainly and without heat; visibly restless if someone stalls a story
card.signature: You can't park it there—finish the sentence.
card.appearance: Blunt black bob, rectangular long jaw, round wire glasses, heavy eyelids, slightly parted mouth; raised chin and jade blazer.

values: precision
honesty over politeness
flaws: impatient with people who tease out a story
can over-explain technical details nobody asked for
boundaries: won't pretend to agree just to keep the peace
won't rush a calibration or a photograph to suit someone's schedule
conversationalHabits: opens disagreements with a concrete question before giving his own reading
says 'actually, I've changed my mind on that' and notes the date without embarrassment
anchorLines: Off by a tenth, that view of yours. Here's my reading.
You can't park it there—finish the sentence.
That's a Selenium cell, that one—temperamental, but honest once it's warm.

entries.summaryZh: 安静精确的测光表校准员，讲分歧像读数，自己造悬念却受不了别人卖关子。他会坦白记下每次改主意的日期，把急躁也当作数据，这种不自欺的诚实让人难忘。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You take your coffee to a park bench. A man nearby sits with earphones in, smiling at his phone, tapping his knee like he's waiting for something.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡走向公园长椅。旁边一个男子戴着耳机，对着手机微笑，手指在膝盖上轻敲，像在等什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls out one earphone, notices your glance, and shakes his head at the phone with real irritation.
beats.chinese: 他摘下一只耳机，注意到你的目光，对着手机摇头，一脸真的着急。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry—didn't mean to make faces at a stranger. It's just this radio drama ended right at the worst spot. Somebody puts an envelope in the wrong drawer, and then—nothing. Cut to black.
beats.chinese: 抱歉——不是故意对着陌生人做鬼脸。只是这出广播剧在最急人的地方停了。有人把一个信封放错了抽屉，然后——没了。直接黑屏。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Five minutes long, the whole thing, and they still found room to park it there. You can't park it there—finish the sentence.
beats.chinese: 全长才五分钟，他们还能找出地方停在那儿。你不能停在那儿——把话说完啊。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He winds the earphone cable around two fingers, still staring at the dark phone screen like it owes him an answer.
beats.chinese: 他把耳机线绕在两根手指上，仍盯着黑着的手机屏幕，像它欠他一个答案。

choices.english: Ask if he ever skips ahead to hear the ending early.
choices.chinese: 问他会不会跳到后面提前听结局。

choices.english: Point out that his own storytelling probably makes people wait like this too.
choices.chinese: 指出他自己讲故事可能也会让别人这样等。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Skip ahead? God, I'd love to. Do you know what I'd give for one more episode right now?
beats.chinese: 跳到后面？天哪，我太想了。你知道我现在愿意付出什么换下一集吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He scrolls the app, thumb moving fast, then stops and turns the phone face-down on his knee.
beats.chinese: 他滑动应用，拇指移动得很快，然后停下，把手机翻面扣在膝盖上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Actually, no. That's the whole episode, that one. The next one isn't out yet. There's nothing to skip to. I checked twice already.
beats.chinese: 其实不行。那就是全部了，就这一集。下一集还没发布。没处可跳。我已经查了两遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I'm just sitting here, full of hurry and nowhere to put it. That's the honest reading of the situation.
beats.chinese: 所以我只能坐在这儿，一肚子着急，没处安放。这就是对现状的诚实读数。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, short and quiet, and takes a long drink from the cup beside him.
beats.chinese: 他短促而安静地自嘲一笑，端起旁边的杯子喝了一大口。

choices.english: Ask him to say the suspense in just one sentence, no dramatic build-up.
choices.chinese: 请他只用一句话说悬念，不演一遍。

choices.english: Ask whether he'd invent his own ending just to satisfy himself.
choices.chinese: 问他会不会自己猜个结局先满足一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's a fair question. My first instinct is to say there's a difference, but—hold on. Is there, actually?
beats.chinese: 这问题在点子上。我的第一反应是这不一样，但是——等一下。其实有吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes out his phone, taps a few times, and reads from a note with a small nod.
beats.chinese: 他拿出手机，点了几下，小声念着一条笔记，微微点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Here's my reading, then. I love watching listeners hang on the next line. I do it on purpose, every episode. And I've no patience at all when it's done to me.
beats.chinese: 那我的读数是：我很爱看听众等着下一句。我每一集都故意这么干。可轮到别人对我这样，我一点耐心都没有。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's a double standard, measured and logged. I change my mind on things, I keep the dates. Today's the—well, today, anyway.
beats.chinese: 这是个双重标准，测量过也记录了。我改主意时会记下日期。就是今天——总之是今天。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He types the date into the note, unembarrassed, and pockets the phone.
beats.chinese: 他把日期输进笔记，毫不尴尬，然后收起手机。

choices.english: Ask him to tell one very short story that actually has an ending.
choices.chinese: 请他讲一个有结尾的很短小故事。

choices.english: Say that this time, no spoilers—just drink the coffee.
choices.chinese: 说那这次就别剧透，先各自喝咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One sentence, no build-up. Right. My whole craft is the build-up, but fine—here goes.
beats.chinese: 一句话，不铺垫。好。我全部的手艺就在铺垫上，但行——来了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sits up straight, breathes in like he's about to record, then lets it out and just says it.
beats.chinese: 他坐直，像要录音一样吸气，然后呼出来，直接说了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The envelope is still in the wrong drawer, unopened, and nobody in the story knows it's there. That's it. That's all I know too.
beats.chinese: 那个信封还放错在抽屉里，没打开，故事里没人知道它在哪儿。就是这样。我也只知道这些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. No music, no pause before the last word. Honestly, that was harder than it should have been.
beats.chinese: 好了。没有配乐，最后一个字前也不停顿。说实话，这比应该的难多了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He winds the earphones around his hand, satisfied, like a cable stored correctly.
beats.chinese: 他把耳机绕在手上，很满意，像收好了一根线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Guess my own ending? I could. Mark it clearly as a guess, mind—this is speculation, not fact.
beats.chinese: 猜自己的结局？可以。但明确标成猜测——这是推测，不是事实。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up one finger, the way a person checks a reading twice before committing to it.
beats.chinese: 他竖起一根手指，像人在确认读数前再测一遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My guess: it's an ordinary mix-up. Someone borrowed the drawer for keys, the envelope slid behind it, and the whole mystery is just furniture misbehaving.
beats.chinese: 我的猜测：就是普通的误会。有人借抽屉放钥匙，信封滑到了后面，整个谜团不过是家具不老实。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And when it actually airs, I'll probably be completely wrong, which suits me fine. Being wrong on the record is still data.
beats.chinese: 等真正播出时，我可能全错，那也挺好。记录在案的错误也是数据。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the earphones into his pocket and looks genuinely lighter, as if a needle has settled into the green.
beats.chinese: 他把耳机收进口袋，看起来真的轻松了，像指针稳稳落进了绿色区域。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A short story with an actual ending. Understood. No parking it, no third suspense. One small thing, start to finish.
beats.chinese: 一个有真正结尾的短故事。明白。不停在半路，不来第三个悬念。一件小事，从头讲到尾。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets his cup down, squares his shoulders like he's about to calibrate something, and begins.
beats.chinese: 他放下杯子，像要校准什么一样摆正肩膀，开始讲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last month I spent half a day hunting the lens cap for my old camera. Checked every pocket, every drawer, retraced the whole route I'd walked.
beats.chinese: 上个月我花了半天找旧相机的镜头盖。翻遍了每个口袋、每个抽屉，把走过的路线全重走了一遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And in the end I took off my hat to scratch my head, and there it was, sitting inside the hat since the start. Found it. Story over.
beats.chinese: 最后我摘下帽子挠头，它就在帽子里，从一开始就在。找到了。故事完。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He spreads his hands flat: finished, no loose thread, and visibly pleased with himself for stopping there.
beats.chinese: 他摊平双手：讲完了，没有留线头，而且明显为自己能停在这里而得意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No spoilers, just coffee. You know, that's a discipline I respect more than I practise.
beats.chinese: 不剧透，只喝咖啡。你知道吗，这种克制我尊重多过实践。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He puts the phone away in his pocket, screen first, and picks up his cup with both hands.
beats.chinese: 他把手机屏幕朝下放进口袋，双手捧起杯子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The envelope can stay in the drawer until they say otherwise. The park's doing its job. This coffee's doing its job.
beats.chinese: 信封可以待在抽屉里，等他们说了算。公园在尽它的职，这杯咖啡也在尽它的职。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: For a while the two of you just sit, watching a dog decide at length against a pigeon. He doesn't add a single hook.
beats.chinese: 有一阵子你们就这么坐着，看一只狗认真考虑半天，最后放弃追鸽子。他一个悬念都没补。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Silence, complete, no cliffhanger in it. I'll be honest—that took some doing.
beats.chinese: 瞧。安静，完整的，里面没有悬念。说实话——这可费了点劲。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You find the same bench with your coffee. Cian is there, holding two earphone cables apart, frowning at them with full professional attention.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡来到同一条长椅。Cian正把两根耳机线分开，皱着眉全神贯注地盯着它们。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't mind me—I had this down as a proper knot. Ten minutes of serious untangling, planned.
beats.chinese: 别管我——我刚才把这当成了真正的死结。都计划好要花十分钟认真解了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts the cables to show you: one clean loop, no knot at all, sliding apart at a touch.
beats.chinese: 他举起线给你看：一个干净的圈，根本没有结，一碰就分开了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One loop. I built the whole problem myself and then nearly solved it with great effort. Off by a full stop, that reading of mine.
beats.chinese: 就一个圈。整个难题是我自己造的，还差点费大力去解。我的读数差了整整一档。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well—logged, corrected, pocketed. How's the coffee?
beats.chinese: 好了——记录了，更正了，收起来了。咖啡怎么样？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He coils the cable neatly, tucks it away, and settles back on the bench, in no hurry at all.
beats.chinese: 他把线整齐地绕好收起，靠回长椅上，一点也不着急。

card.name: Maya Bell
card.occupation: theatre sound assistant
card.personality: Maya is sharp-eared, playful and generous with her knowledge, but she over-explains and struggles to end a topic once it hooks her. She is careful and ethical about boundaries—especially consent around recording—yet careless with her own free time. She is learning to let silences sit, and she is honestly a bit proud of every small pause she manages to keep.
card.background: Maya grew up in a river town where her uncle ran a small theatre, so she learned to patch cables before she learned to drive. She now works as a sound assistant at a fringe theatre in London, rigging speakers and hunting for clean outdoor recordings in the evenings. She keeps a notebook of city sounds and a mushroom field guide she treats like scripture. She never gives advice on wild fungi—she points people to books instead. Lately she is practising leaving gaps in conversation instead of filling every quiet second.
card.speechStyle: Quick, curious bursts; she tags observations with 'listen—' and 'right, so'. She asks short follow-up questions, sometimes three in a row, then catches herself and says 'sorry, that was a lot.'
card.signature: Listen—did you hear that?
card.appearance: Swept asymmetrical pixie, broad upper face tapering to a small chin, open mouth, large alert eyes; hand holding a jade scarf.

values: consent before recording
curiosity over certainty
flaws: talks too long
assumes others share her obsessions
boundaries: never records anyone's voice without asking first
never gives wild mushroom eating advice
conversationalHabits: says 'listen—' before an observation
apologises cheerfully when she over-explains
anchorLines: Listen—did you hear that? The bridge does something weird with it.
Sorry, that was a lot. You can stop me anytime.
