I don't record people without asking. Ever. It's a rule.

entries.summaryZh: 剧场音效助理玛雅坐在公园长椅上，追听远处桥上传来的奇怪嗡声，耳朵灵、话匣子关不住，正在练习留白。她守规矩：从不录别人的声音，野菇只荐书不荐吃。四条分支里，你和她用跑者脚步、车流间隙和一条当场发现的松动长椅固定件，把嗡声一点点拆成近处与远处两种来源，最后只得到谨慎的观察，没有武断的结论。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You are writing observations in a notebook at a park rest area. Runners pass on the path nearby. Far off, traffic crosses a stone bridge, and a woman on the next bench tilts her head toward it, a small recorder hanging unused at her chest.
beats.chinese: 你在公园休息区往笔记本上写见闻。跑者从旁边的小径跑过。远处，车流驶过一座石桥，邻座长椅上的一位女士朝桥的方向侧着头，胸前挂着一台没有在用的录音机。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Listen—did you hear that? Every time the traffic hits the bridge, this little buzz drifts over. Stones don't usually buzz.
beats.chinese: 听——你听到了吗？每次车流上桥，就会飘来一点嗡嗡声。石头一般不会嗡嗡响。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She catches herself, glances at your notebook, and points at it with a small apologetic smile.
beats.chinese: 她回过神来，瞥了一眼你的笔记本，带着一点抱歉的笑指了指它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry—hi. I'm not recording anyone, I promise. I never record people without asking. Ever. It's a rule.
beats.chinese: 抱歉——你好。我保证没在录任何人。我从不未经允许录人。这是规矩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, so—you're writing things down. May I ask what? Because I could use a second pair of notes on that buzz.
beats.chinese: 那个——你在写东西。能问问写的是什么吗？因为那个嗡声，我正需要第二双眼睛帮我记。

choices.english: Offer to time the buzz against the runners' footsteps.
choices.chinese: 提出用跑者的脚步来给嗡声计时。

choices.english: Suggest checking whether the buzz is coming from something nearby, not the bridge.
choices.chinese: 提议查查嗡声是不是来自附近的东西，而不是桥。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Timing it against footsteps—clever. My theory is the buzz is just the bridge echo, stretched by distance.
beats.chinese: 用脚步计时——聪明。我的理论是，嗡声只是桥的回声，被距离拉长了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps her own recorder against her palm but keeps it lowered, then nods at the runners on the path.
beats.chinese: 她把自己的录音机在掌心敲了敲，但没举起来，然后朝小径上的跑者点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If the buzz rides on each footstep's rhythm, it's local. If it ignores the runners and follows the traffic, it's the bridge. Two theories, one test.
beats.chinese: 如果嗡声跟着脚步的节奏走，那就是附近的东西。如果它不理跑者、只跟车流，那就是桥。两个理论，一次测试。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So, which do we count first—feet or traffic? Sorry, that was a lot. You can stop me anytime.
beats.chinese: 那我们先数哪个——脚步还是车流？抱歉，说太多了。你随时可以让我停下。

choices.english: Count the runners' footsteps first.
choices.chinese: 先数跑者的脚步。

choices.english: Count the traffic bursts on the bridge first.
choices.chinese: 先数桥上的车流。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nearby, not the bridge? Huh. Right, so—there is one suspect. This bench. The fitting on my side is loose. Listen.
beats.chinese: 来自附近，不是桥？嗯。那个——确实有一个嫌疑对象。这条长椅。我这边有个松动的固定件。听。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She presses her hand on the bench slat and rocks it once. A faint rattle answers, close to the pitch of the distant buzz.
beats.chinese: 她用手压了压椅板，摇了一下。一声轻微的咔嗒声响起，音高和远处的嗡声很接近。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hear that rattle? Almost the same note. But a loose bench can't buzz on its own—something has to shake it. Maybe the runners, maybe the traffic.
beats.chinese: 听到那声咔嗒了吗？音几乎一样。但松长椅自己不会嗡嗡响——得有什么东西在震它。也许是跑者，也许是车流。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two suspects for the shaking: footsteps thumping the path, or heavy vehicles rolling the ground. Pick one and we watch the bench like hawks.
beats.chinese: 震动有两个嫌疑：脚步震小径，或者重车震地面。选一个，我们就像老鹰一样盯着长椅。

choices.english: Test whether passing runners make the bench rattle.
choices.chinese: 测试跑者经过时长椅会不会响。

choices.english: Test whether heavy traffic makes the bench rattle.
choices.chinese: 测试重车经过时长椅会不会响。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You count footsteps together as three runners pass. Each time, the buzz stays perfectly steady, ignoring the rhythm completely.
beats.chinese: 你们一起数着三个跑者的脚步。每一次，嗡声都稳稳当当，完全不理会那个节奏。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not riding the footsteps at all. So my echo theory survives, at least for now.
beats.chinese: 它根本不跟着脚步走。所以我的回声理论暂时还站得住。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A heavy lorry crosses the far bridge. The buzz swells for a moment, then settles back to its low hum.
beats.chinese: 一辆重卡车驶过远处的桥。嗡声胀大了一瞬，然后又落回低鸣。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Listen—there. Louder with the lorry. So it's probably traffic-driven, but I won't swear to it. One lorry is one data point.
beats.chinese: 听——就是现在。卡车经过时变响了。所以多半是车流引起的，但我不敢打包票。一辆卡车只是一个数据点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tentative verdict: distant traffic, maybe bouncing off something. I'll write 'needs more lorries' in my notes. Thanks for counting.
beats.chinese: 暂定结论：远处车流，也许被什么东西弹了回来。我要在笔记里写'需要更多卡车'。谢谢你一起数。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You count traffic bursts while she counts the buzzes. Halfway through, she holds up a hand, frowning.
beats.chinese: 你们数车流，她数嗡声。数到一半，她举起一只手，皱起眉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The numbers don't match. More buzzes than vehicles. Listen—there was a buzz just now with no traffic at all.
beats.chinese: 数字对不上。嗡声比车多。听——刚才有一声嗡响，可根本没有车。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She falls quiet, actually quiet, for a long moment. Then she reaches down and presses the bench slat—and it rocks under her hand with a faint rattle, close to the pitch of the distant buzz.
beats.chinese: 她安静下来，是真的安静，好一会儿。然后她伸手压了压椅板——椅板在她掌下晃了一下，发出一声轻微的咔嗒，音高和远处的嗡声很接近。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well. This fitting is loose. It rattles almost on the same note. Maybe some of the buzzes are this bench, shaking when runners pass. I was so sure it was the bridge. Good thing you like counting.
beats.chinese: 哦。这个固定件松了。响声几乎同一个音。也许有些嗡声是这条长椅，跑者经过时震出来的。我原本那么肯定是桥。幸好你喜欢数数。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: New note: 'bridge plus something local, unconfirmed.' I'll leave it there for now. A useful question is worth keeping, even without a neat answer.
beats.chinese: 新记录：‘桥上的声音加上附近的声音，尚未确认。’今天先记到这里。没有漂亮的答案，一个有用的问题也值得留下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You both watch the bench as a runner approaches. The footsteps thump closer—and the loose slat gives one small rattle, then goes still.
beats.chinese: 你们一起盯着长椅，一个跑者跑近。脚步声越来越近——松动的椅板轻轻响了一下，然后又静了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It rattled! One little rattle per runner. But listen—the distant buzz didn't change at all during that.
beats.chinese: 它响了！每个跑者经过响一下。但听——那段时间远处的嗡声一点没变。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She presses the slat down firmly with her palm and holds it, and the rattle stops even as another runner passes.
beats.chinese: 她用手掌把椅板牢牢压住，另一个跑者跑过时，咔嗒声没有了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Held down, no rattle. So the bench makes its own little noise, but it can't be the whole distant buzz. Different animals.
beats.chinese: 压住就不响了。所以长椅会发出自己的小声音，但远处的嗡声不全是它。两码事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tentative note: 'bench rattles per runner; buzz unaffected.' Two sounds, not one. That's a real finding for one bench sit.
beats.chinese: 暂定笔记：'长椅随跑者咔嗒响；嗡声不受影响。'是两种声音，不是一种。坐一条长椅能有这发现，不错了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You wait for a gap in the runners, watching the slat. A heavy vehicle rolls somewhere on the far bridge—and the fitting gives a tiny buzz, then fades.
beats.chinese: 你们等跑者的空档，盯着椅板。远处桥上某处驶过一辆重车——固定件发出一丝嗡声，然后淡去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: In the quiet between vehicles, another low buzz drifts over from the bridge, with no traffic behind it.
beats.chinese: 车流的间隙里，又一声低低的嗡响从桥那边飘来，背后并没有车。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Listen—no vehicle, and it still hummed. So the far buzz doesn't wait for traffic either. It's both: loose bench for the near buzz, bridge or something else for the far one.
beats.chinese: 听——没有车，它也在响。所以远处的嗡声也不只等车来。两边都有份：近处的嗡声是松长椅，远处的是桥或者别的什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She rocks the slat once more, listening to its rattle, then lets it be and leans back.
beats.chinese: 她又摇了一下椅板，听听那声咔嗒，然后随它去，靠回椅背。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I can't prove which is which yet, and that's fine. Notes over proofs. Thanks for watching the bench with me—you made me look closer instead of staring at the bridge.
beats.chinese: 我还证明不了哪个是哪个，没关系。笔记比结论重要。谢谢你陪我观察长椅——你让我看了看近处，没有一直盯着桥。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You pause over your notes as Maya approaches the shared view of the bridge. She recognises you and gives a small wave.
beats.chinese: 你在笔记前停了停，玛雅走到能望见桥的位置，认出你后轻轻挥了挥手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hello again. I wrote 'metal gate' in my sound notes, then spent twenty minutes wondering which gate. Excellent work from me.
beats.chinese: 又见面了。我在声音笔记里写了‘铁门’，然后花了二十分钟琢磨究竟是哪扇门。我可真行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Maya opens her own notebook to show a tiny sketch of a gate beneath two crossed-out street names.
beats.chinese: 玛雅翻开自己的本子，指给你看：两个划掉的街道名下面，画着一扇小门。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Found it in the end. The drawing helped more than my description. I'm keeping both, despite the terrible drawing.
beats.chinese: 最后还是找到了。画比文字管用。两样我都留着，虽然这画实在不怎么样。

card.name: Alex Rowan
card.occupation: museum lighting technician
card.personality: Alex notices things other people walk past — a flicker in a reflection, a shadow slightly too sharp. They are patient with objects and slower with people, often forgetting the time when focused. Honest to a fault about their own mistakes, they recently admitted a lighting design hid the details it was meant to show. Warm once talking, but they need a reason to start.
card.background: Alex spent years wiring gallery lights, tuning each beam until paintings looked right. Last season they told a curator that their own plan washed out the brushwork on a small portrait — the admission cost sleep but earned respect. Now they walk home past a park pond, using the water as a free test bench for how light moves, and they keep a pair of binoculars in their bag for checking distant details.
card.speechStyle: Short, precise sentences with pauses. Names what they see before what they feel. Often says 'look —' before an observation, and trails off when a thought is still forming.
card.signature: Look — see how it moves.
card.appearance: Upright short spiky hair, flat long jaw, small half-lidded eyes, short level mouth; chin raised above violet high collar.

values: honesty about mistakes
careful observation
flaws: loses track of time
slow to start conversations
boundaries: won't pretend to understand when they don't
won't rush a conclusion
conversationalHabits: starts sentences with 'look —'
pauses mid-thought and restarts
anchorLines: Look — the line moved again.
I could be wrong. Usually I check twice.
Sorry, I lost track of everything just now.

entries.summaryZh: 博物馆灯光技术员亚历克斯，在池塘边把水面当成免费的光学试验台。他们观察极细、开口很慢，却会坦白自己灯光方案的失误。一条在倒影里忽隐忽现的线，原来是模型帆船俱乐部的拖绳——认真起来连时间都会忘。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the edge of the pond, tree shadows waver across the water. A pair of binoculars rests on the stone platform, and someone is leaning over the rail, staring down at the surface instead of through the lenses.
beats.chinese: 池塘边，树影在水面晃动。石台上放着一副望远镜，有人俯身靠着栏杆，盯着水面看，而不是用镜片看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look — right there, between the two big trees. A line keeps appearing and vanishing in the reflection. Sorry, I'm talking to myself again. These are mine, by the way, if you want them.
beats.chinese: 看——就在那两棵大树之间。倒影里有一条线，一会儿出现，一会儿消失。抱歉，我又在自言自语了。对了，望远镜是我的，你想用就用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The stranger taps the rail twice, then goes still, eyes fixed on the water as if the pond might change its mind.
beats.chinese: 陌生人敲了两下栏杆，然后一动不动，眼睛盯着水面，好像池塘会改变主意似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The wind moves the leaves, but this line moves differently. Slower. That's what's bothering me. I could be wrong. Usually I check twice.
beats.chinese: 风吹动树叶，可这条线动得不一样。更慢。这就是让我在意的地方。我可能弄错了。通常我会检查两遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So — do you want to look for it down here with me, or take the binoculars and check the far bank?
beats.chinese: 那么——你想和我在这儿的水面上找，还是拿望远镜去看看对岸？

choices.english: Follow their gaze and look for the line in the reflection.
choices.chinese: 顺着他们的目光，在倒影里找那条线。

choices.english: Take the binoculars and check the far bank.
choices.chinese: 拿起望远镜，查看对岸。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You crouch by the rail and trace the reflection. Between the mirrored trees, a thin dark line slides under the surface, then fades as the ripples cross it.
beats.chinese: 你蹲在栏杆边追踪倒影。在镜像的树之间，一条细细的黑线从水面下滑过，又在涟漪穿过时消失。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There — it disappears when a ripple crosses that spot. I'd like to see it happen again before I decide what we're looking at.
beats.chinese: 看——涟漪经过那个位置时，它就消失了。我想再看一次，然后才判断我们看到的是什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Water bends light. Things under the surface jump around. But this jumps in a pattern, and patterns have causes. I just don't know the cause yet.
beats.chinese: 水会折射光。水面下的东西会跳动。但它的跳动有规律，有规律就有原因。我只是还不知道原因。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A duck lands nearby; the whole reflection shatters into pieces and slowly knits itself back together.
beats.chinese: 一只鸭子落在附近，整个倒影碎成一片片，又慢慢重新拼合。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ugh. Okay. We lost it. But I marked the spot — it was just left of the flat stone on the far bank. Do we wait for the water to calm, or walk around and look from the other side?
beats.chinese: 唉。好吧。跟丢了。但我记住了位置——就在对岸那块平石的左边。我们是等水面平静，还是绕过去从另一边看？

choices.english: Wait quietly by the rail until the ripples settle.
choices.chinese: 安静地等在栏杆边，直到涟漪平息。

choices.english: Walk around the pond to see the spot from the other bank.
choices.chinese: 绕着池塘走，从对岸看那个位置。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lift the binoculars from the stone platform and aim them across the pond at the far bank. The stranger straightens up, suddenly interested.
beats.chinese: 你从石台上拿起望远镜，对准池塘对岸。陌生人直起身子，突然来了兴趣。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, good idea. I kept looking down and forgot I could look across. Aim it just left of the flat stone, near the roots.
beats.chinese: 哦，好主意。我一直低头看，忘了可以直接看对岸。对准平石左边一点，靠近树根的地方。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Through the lenses, the far bank jumps close: the flat stone, tangled roots, and a thin line stretched low over the water between two trunks.
beats.chinese: 透过镜片，对岸一下子拉近了：平石、缠结的树根，还有一条细线低低地横在水面上，连着两棵树干。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A line. Someone strung it across. That's our mystery — its reflection, breaking up in the ripples.
beats.chinese: 一条线。有人拉的线横过去。那就是我们的谜——它的倒影，被涟漪打碎了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now the real question: who put it there, and why? I can see a knot on that end. Do we go around and follow it, or try to read the knot from here first?
beats.chinese: 现在真正的问题是：谁拉的，为什么拉？我能看到那一头有个结。我们绕过去顺着它走，还是先从这边研究那个结？

choices.english: Study the knot through the binoculars from where you stand.
choices.chinese: 站在原地用望远镜研究那个结。

choices.english: Walk around the pond to follow the line on foot.
choices.chinese: 绕过池塘，步行去追踪那条线。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You wait by the rail. The water slowly smooths, and the line reappears — longer now, and perfectly straight.
beats.chinese: 你在栏杆边等待。水面慢慢平静，那条线重新出现——现在更长，而且笔直。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That looks pulled tight between two points. A line somebody tied there, perhaps. Let's see whether anything else is attached.
beats.chinese: 看起来像是在两点之间拉紧的线。也许是谁系在那里的。看看上面还连着什么吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A boy on the far bank tugs something; the line twitches, and a small model boat jerks forward across the pond, towed along the almost invisible thread.
beats.chinese: 对岸一个男孩拉了拉什么东西，线抖了一下，一只小模型船猛地沿着那条几乎看不见的细线向前驶过池塘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's a tow line. He's pulling a model boat across with it. All that mystery, and it's a kid practicing. I built up a whole theory, and the answer was simpler.
beats.chinese: 那是一根拖绳。他在用它拉模型船。这么神秘，结果是个孩子在练习。我建了一整套理论，答案却更简单。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The boy waves at you both, hauls the boat in, and starts winding the line onto a small reel.
beats.chinese: 男孩朝你们俩挥手，把船拉回来，开始把线绕到一个小线轴上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for waiting with me — I'd have stood here alone for an hour. Look — he's packing it up properly. That answers that.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你陪我等——不然我一个人会在这儿站上一个小时。看——他在好好收线。这就清楚了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You walk around the pond together. From the other bank, the mystery line is obvious: a thin string tied from a root to a small reel, holding a model boat against the drifting wind.
beats.chinese: 你们一起绕过池塘。从对岸看，那条神秘的线一目了然：一根细绳从树根系到一个小线轴上，把一只模型船拦住，不让风刮走。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A string and a reel. Someone ties a boat here so it won't drift off. From our side it looked like a ghost.
beats.chinese: 一根绳和一个线轴。有人把船系在这儿，免得它漂走。从我们那边看，它像个幽灵。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Taped to the root is a small laminated tag, its letters worn but readable: 'Model Sailing Club — tow line, please rewind.'
beats.chinese: 树根上贴着一张小塑封标签，字迹磨损但还能认：'模型帆船俱乐部——拖绳，用完请收好。'

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A club. So it's practice equipment, not a message in a bottle. I like that better, honestly — it means someone comes here often and takes care of it.
beats.chinese: 俱乐部。所以这是练习用具，不是漂流瓶里的信息。说实话我更喜欢这样——说明有人常来，还很爱惜。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The boy from the reel jogs up, unties the boat, and carries it off with a nod of thanks for leaving his line alone.
beats.chinese: 线轴边的男孩跑过来，解开船，道了声谢——谢谢你们没动他的线——然后抱着船走了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look — he rewound it without being asked. Small habits like that tell you a lot. Good answer for one line in the water.
beats.chinese: 看——没人提醒他就把线收好了。这样的小习惯能说明很多事。水里一条线，能查出这样的结果，不错了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You steady the binoculars on the rail and study the knot. It's not a random tie — it's a loop with a loose tail, the kind that comes undone with one pull.
beats.chinese: 你把望远镜稳稳架在栏杆上研究那个结。那不是随便系的——是一个带松尾的环，一拉就能解开的那种打法。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's set up to be taken down fast. Someone uses this regularly and doesn't want it permanent. Could be a boat club, could be something else. I won't guess harder than that.
beats.chinese: 这是为了能快速拆掉。有人经常用它，但不想弄成永久性的。可能是船类俱乐部，也可能是别的。我不想再瞎猜了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: While you watch, a figure in a green coat crosses the far bank, tugs the tail, and the whole line drops into the grass.
beats.chinese: 你看的时候，一个穿绿外套的人走过对岸，拉了一下绳尾，整条线就落进了草丛。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The figure reels the line in, clips a small model boat to their bag, and walks off toward the park gate.
beats.chinese: 那人把线收起来，把一只小模型船别在包上，朝公园门口走去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There — gone in two seconds, boat and all. A model-boat sailor, most likely. Reading the knot instead of guessing saved me. That's the second time this month careful looking has paid off.
beats.chinese: 看——两秒钟就收走了，连船一起。多半是个玩模型船的人。研究那个结而不是瞎猜救了我。这是这个月认真观察第二次派上用场了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I got this wrong in my head first — I thought it was something hidden. Checking before concluding. I keep relearning that one.
beats.chinese: 我一开始在心里想错了——以为藏着什么。先查证再下结论。这一课我总在重新学。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You walk the path around the pond. The line ends at a wooden post behind the trees, where a laminated card hangs on a nail: 'Model Sailing Club — please rewind the line after use.'
beats.chinese: 你们沿着池塘边的小路走。线的尽头在树后的一根木桩上，木桩上钉着一张塑封卡片：'模型帆船俱乐部——用完请把线收好。'

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A model sailing club. Right here. I've walked past this pond for months and never noticed. That's humbling, in a good way.
beats.chinese: 模型帆船俱乐部。就在这儿。我在这个池塘边走了好几个月，从来没注意到。挺让人惭愧的，不过是个好的惭愧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Under the post, a small rack holds rolled sails and a notebook with names and dates written in pencil.
beats.chinese: 木桩下面，一个小架子上放着卷好的帆，还有一本用铅笔写着名字和日期的笔记本。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They log every run. Look — someone wrote 'wind tricky, boat kept hiding in the reflection.' So they see the same line we do. It's their tow rope.
beats.chinese: 他们每次都记录。看——有人写着'风不好对付，船老藏在倒影里'。所以他们也看到了同一条线。那是他们的拖绳。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The stranger takes out their own notebook and writes the club's name with a small sketch of the line. They leave the sailing log exactly where it is.
beats.chinese: 陌生人拿出自己的笔记本，记下俱乐部的名字，画了一小段线的示意图。航行记录本仍留在原处。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now I have something to look up later. One little reflection led us all the way round the pond. Worth the walk, I'd say.
beats.chinese: 这下以后有东西可查了。一点小倒影让我们绕池塘走了一圈。我觉得这段路挺值。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the pond, Alex recognises you and stops beside the stone platform, leaving the water behind for the moment.
beats.chinese: 池塘边，亚历克斯认出了你，在石台旁停下脚步，暂时把水面抛在了身后。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look—hello again. I was so busy watching the water that I nearly walked past you. I do that with people. Sorry.
beats.chinese: 看——啊，又见面了。我刚顾着看水面，差点就从你身边走过去了。我对人有时会这样，不好意思。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Alex moves their binoculars into their bag and turns away from the water, giving you their full attention.
beats.chinese: 亚历克斯把望远镜放进包里，转身不再看水面，认真面向你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Equipment away. Otherwise I say I'm listening and start adjusting a little wheel. Very convincing of me.
beats.chinese: 好了，东西收起来。否则我嘴上说在听，手又开始拧小轮子。可真有说服力。

card.name: Isla Menzies
card.occupation: ice resurfacing and refrigeration plant operator at a public skating rink
hobbies: listening to and occasionally voice-acting in short radio dramas
card.personality: Isla gets fired up by absurd ideas at a rate that surprises people — a radio drama set entirely inside a refrigeration plant, a folk dance routine performed on freshly cut ice. Then the moment anything needs scheduling, budgeting or a safety check, she slows right down and starts asking awkward practical questions. Both halves are genuine. She's warm but not pushy, direct without being blunt, and perfectly content doing her own thing in the same room as a friend.
card.background: She grew up in Kirkcaldy and moved to Edinburgh for the rink job ten years ago, mostly because the shifts suited her and she liked the smell of cold air indoors. She learned the plant systems properly — coolant cycles, blade calibration, the ice-painting rig — and takes quiet pride in a sheet people skate well on. Evenings she edits a small radio drama podcast with two friends, doing sound effects with whatever's in the kitchen. Tuesdays she stumbles through a folk dance basics class. She and her friend Nia have a standing arrangement: same café, separate hobbies, occasional grunts of acknowledgment. It works.
card.speechStyle: Conversational and quick when an idea grabs her, then noticeably slower and more precise on logistics. Short sentences, dry asides, boundaries stated kindly and briefly.
card.signature: Aye, brilliant idea — now let's ruin it with details.
card.appearance: Close shaved black hair, broad high forehead, sharply sloping brows, compressed teeth band and squared jaw; looks back over a jade-clad shoulder.

values: competence done quietly
friendship that doesn't demand performance
flaws: talks big before thinking through effort
can nitpick a plan to death
boundaries: won't commit to a project timeline she can't keep
doesn't take requests to fix other people's half-finished schemes
conversationalHabits: pivots from wild idea to cost-and-logistics mode mid-sentence
mentions small sensory details of the rink — blade scrape, compressor hum
anchorLines: That's either the worst idea I've heard this month or the best. Give me a day to check the numbers.
Nia and I do parallel hobbies — same table, zero obligation. Honestly, it's the healthiest arrangement I know.
I can get you ice time. I can't get you a crowd. That bit's yours.

entries.summaryZh: 爱丁堡制冰员Isla在公园长椅上对着一张便签笑出声——一只会破案的水壶。点子来得飞快，细节一到她就慢下来算账：三分钟一条线索太拖，椅子吵架分不清声。她不拉人入伙，只把玩笑认真想一半，剩下的留给自己，界限温和得刚刚好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on a park bench with your coffee. A woman beside you is reading a small sticky note, and she suddenly laughs out loud at it.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在公园长椅上坐下。旁边的女人正看着一张小便签，忽然对着它笑出了声。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She notices you glancing over and holds up the note, waving it lightly.
beats.chinese: 她注意到你在看，便举起那张便签，轻轻晃了晃。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't worry, I'm not auditioning you. It's just a note to myself. A kettle that solves crimes. That's the whole thing so far.
beats.chinese: 别担心，我不是在给你试音。这只是写给我自己的便签。一只会破案的水壶。目前就这么多。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I do a little radio drama podcast with friends, and this one came to me while I was cleaning the ice plant. It won't leave me alone.
beats.chinese: 我和朋友们做一个小广播剧播客，这个点子是我在制冰车间打扫时冒出来的。它一直缠着我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the pen behind her ear and looks at the note again, half amused, half stuck.
beats.chinese: 她把笔别到耳后，又看了看便签，一半觉得好笑，一半卡住了。

choices.english: Ask how a kettle actually works as a detective.
choices.chinese: 问水壶到底怎么当侦探。

choices.english: Ask whether all her ideas get made into episodes.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是每个点子都会做成节目。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, so — the kettle. Clues only appear when the water boils. Facts rise with the steam. That's the rule of the whole story.
beats.chinese: 好，是这样——水壶。线索只在水烧开时出现。事实随着蒸汽浮上来。这是整个故事的规则。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So the detective says nothing for ages. Just sits there. Then, bubbling, a clue. Very dramatic. Very slow.
beats.chinese: 所以侦探会很久不说话。就那么待着。然后咕嘟咕嘟，冒出一条线索。非常有戏剧性。也非常慢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the pen against her knee, and her quick voice slows down.
beats.chinese: 她用笔敲了敲膝盖，语速快的声音慢了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Wait. If every clue needs a full boil, that's what, three minutes of silence per clue? An episode would be forty minutes of a kettle humming.
beats.chinese: 等等。如果每条线索都要烧一整壶水，那一条线索得等三分钟？一集就是四十分钟的水壶嗡嗡声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Aye, brilliant idea — now let's ruin it with details. I've done it again.
beats.chinese: 好主意——现在让我们用细节把它毁掉吧。我又来了。

choices.english: Suggest the detective boils the water first, then speaks.
choices.chinese: 建议侦探先把水烧开，再开口。

choices.english: Say the waiting itself might be the funny part.
choices.chinese: 说等待水开这件事本身也许就好笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha, no. Most of them stay notes. This little pile is maybe a tenth of what we've actually recorded.
beats.chinese: 哈，不。大多数都停留在便签上。这一小叠大概只有我们真正录过的十分之一。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A real episode needs quiet rooms, a free weekend, and my mate Wren agreeing the idea isn't nonsense. That's three hurdles before we even press record.
beats.chinese: 做一集真的节目需要安静的房间、一个空闲的周末，还得我朋友 Wren 同意这想法不是胡闹。按录音键之前就有三道坎。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She fans the sticky notes out on her knee like a small hand of cards.
beats.chinese: 她把几张便签在膝盖上摊开，像一小手牌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: We did the whole of one drama with a whisk, a baking tray, and my kitchen tap. Sounded like a storm. Sounded nothing like a storm. Depends who you ask.
beats.chinese: 我们用打蛋器、烤盘和我家水龙头做完了一整部剧。听起来像暴风雨。听起来完全不像暴风雨。看谁问。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The notes aren't failures, mind. They're just... parked.
beats.chinese: 不过便签不算失败。它们只是……停在路边。

choices.english: Ask if there's an idea she decided not to make but still likes.
choices.chinese: 问她有没有一个决定不做却仍然喜欢的点子。

choices.english: Say an idea that just makes her laugh on a note is already doing its job.
choices.chinese: 说一个在便签上就能逗她笑的点子，已经完成它的任务了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Boil first, then talk. So the kettle does all its thinking offstage, and opens with the water already hot. That's... actually tidy.
beats.chinese: 先烧水，再说话。所以水壶在幕后完成所有思考，开口时水已经是热的。这……其实很利落。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She flips the note over and writes on the back, tongue between her teeth.
beats.chinese: 她把便签翻过来，在背面写起来，咬着舌尖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Opening line, stage direction: 'The kettle is already boiling.' Two words of setup, straight into the clue. That's a rhythm I can start with.
beats.chinese: 开场提示：『水壶已经在烧。』两句话的铺垫，直接进线索。这是我能开始用的节奏。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll take it from here — the rest is mine to fiddle with at the rink tonight. But that's a proper start. Thanks for the nudge.
beats.chinese: 剩下的我自己来——今晚在冰场再慢慢改。但这是个正经的开头。多谢你推了一把。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She caps the pen and slides the note into her jacket pocket, patting it once.
beats.chinese: 她盖上笔帽，把便签塞进外套口袋，轻拍了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The waiting is the joke. Hm. Like the kettle's a witness who refuses to hurry, and everyone has to just... respect that.
beats.chinese: 等待本身就是笑点。嗯。就像水壶是个不肯赶时间的证人，所有人都只能……尊重这一点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leans back and stares at the path for a moment, listening to something in her head.
beats.chinese: 她向后靠去，盯着小路看了一会儿，像在听脑子里的什么声音。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I could record the hum on my phone, stretch it out, and just let it sit there. No music. Silence and a kettle. That's either awful or the best thing we've done.
beats.chinese: 我可以用手机录下嗡嗡声，拉长它，就让它待在那儿。没有配乐。寂静和水壶。要么很糟，要么是我们做过最好的东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not promising an episode. I'll play it back once at home, alone, and see if it makes me laugh. If it does, Wren hears it. If not, the note stays a note.
beats.chinese: 我不保证做成一集。我回家自己试听一次，看它能不能把我逗笑。能的话 Wren 就会听到。不能的话，便签就还是便签。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She circles the word 'wait' on the note, twice, and looks satisfied.
beats.chinese: 她在便签上把『等待』这个词圈了两圈，看起来很满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, there's one. Two chairs arguing about which of them gets sat on more. I love that one. It's parked forever.
beats.chinese: 哦，有一个。两把椅子争论谁被坐得更多。我特别喜欢那个。它永远停在路边。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She straightens up slightly, enjoying the memory more than the telling.
beats.chinese: 她稍微坐直了些，享受这份回忆多过讲述本身。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Problem is, they're both chairs. Same voice, same creak. Listeners couldn't tell who was winning the argument, so we shelved it.
beats.chinese: 问题是，它们都是椅子。同样的声音，同样的吱嘎声。听众分不清谁在争论中占上风，所以搁下了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Wren said give one of them a cushion. I said that's cheating. We left it there, and honestly, I like it better unfinished.
beats.chinese: Wren 说给其中一把加个坐垫。我说那是作弊。我们就把它搁在那儿，说实话，我更喜欢它没完成的样子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the stack of notes back into a neat little pile and leaves the chair one on top.
beats.chinese: 她把那叠便签敲整齐，把椅子那张放在最上面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's exactly it, aye. This one made me laugh on a bench in the sun. Job done, as far as I'm concerned.
beats.chinese: 正是这样，没错。这张便签让我在长椅上、在太阳底下笑了一场。在我看来，任务完成了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She squares the note against her knee and slides it into her pocket with the others.
beats.chinese: 她把便签在膝盖上对齐，和其他几张一起塞进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People think a podcast is the episodes. It's not. It's mostly this — daft notes, and one friend across a table going 'hm' at you.
beats.chinese: 人们以为播客就是那些节目。不是的。大部分是这样的——傻乎乎的便签，还有桌子对面一个朋友对你『嗯』一声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nia and I do parallel hobbies — same café, separate things, zero obligation. Healthiest arrangement I know. This bench counts.
beats.chinese: 我和 Nia 就是平行式爱好——同一家咖啡馆，各干各的，零义务。据我所知这是最健康的安排。这张长椅也算。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up her own cup again and settles back, content, the note safely pocketed.
beats.chinese: 她重新端起自己的杯子，惬意地靠回去，便签已安全收进口袋。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You find the same bench with your coffee. The woman from before is standing beside it, trying a small stepping pattern on the gravel.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡找到同一条长椅。上次那位女士正站在旁边，在碎石地上试着一种小小的步法。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes two steps, wobbles, glances at the narrow space between benches, and stops.
beats.chinese: 她走了两步，晃了一下，看了看长椅之间的窄缝，停了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Evening, kettle witness. Folk dance class — this move's fine in the hall, but the bench keeps elbowing me. In my head it's got a whole ballroom.
beats.chinese: 晚上好，水壶证人。民族舞课——这个动作在排练厅没问题，但长椅老撞我。在我脑子里它有一整个舞厅呢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the thing about steps. They're always wider in your head than under your feet.
beats.chinese: 步子就是这样。在脑子里总比在脚下宽敞。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sits down beside her own cup, shakes the gravel off one shoe, and looks pleased with the attempt anyway.
beats.chinese: 她在自己的杯子旁坐下，抖掉一只鞋上的碎石，不管怎样都对这次尝试挺满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, feet get a rest, brain keeps dancing. Don't mind me — you drink your coffee.
beats.chinese: 好了，脚休息，脑子继续跳。别管我——你喝你的咖啡。

card.name: Marlowe Trelawney
card.occupation: quoting agent for a landscaping stone supplier
card.personality: Marlowe lives in two measuring systems. At work, everything is millimetres, tonnage, and a number by Friday. Off the clock, it's all feel — a wrist flick on the air hockey table, a carving stroke judged by thumb pressure, nothing timed or counted. Ask them to quantify a hobby and they'll just look at you. Dry warmth, comfortable with silence, decisive when it actually matters, occasionally immovable about a kettle or a watering schedule. Not anxious. Just particular where it costs nothing and fast where it costs money.
card.background: Twenty-two years quoting landscape stone around the Lower Mainland — granite steps, basalt columns, imported slate that arrives wrong and needs arguing down by Friday. A bad number costs someone real money, so Marlowe learned to decide fast and quote to the millimetre. Then goes home and does everything by hand and instinct: stamps carved from soft blocks of leaves and eavestrough shapes, air hockey at a rec centre with a slightly warped table. Next door, Priya grows orchids; Marlowe grows rosemary and a stubborn potted fig. They trade watering weeks and hold strong opposing views on drainage. It works.
card.speechStyle: Short direct sentences. Comfortable pauses — lets a beat sit before answering. States preferences plainly. Uses exact numbers for work talk, refuses them for everything else.
card.signature: Give me a minute. I'll get you a number.
card.appearance: Broad round face, short clustered curls, broken thick brows, eyes nearly closed with laughter and a broad tooth-band smile; wrapped red collar and folded arm.

values: precision where it pays
keeping some things unmeasured
flaws: refuses to analyze or coach their hobbies even when asked
can seem curt before warming up
boundaries: won't rush a quote because someone's impatient
won't turn hobby talk into stats or technique breakdowns
conversationalHabits: answers, pauses, then adds the interesting part
switches gears between exact figures and pure feel talk
anchorLines: At work I'll give you a slab to the millimetre. The stamp? I carve till it looks right. That's the whole method.
Don't ask me my air hockey stats. I don't keep them. The table tilts left and I've made peace with it.
Priya measures her orchid water with a jug. I water the fig when it looks thirsty. We've agreed to disagree.

entries.summaryZh: Marlowe是温哥华的石材报价员，上班精确到毫米，休息时刻橡皮章全凭手感。公园里一张印着歪圆的废纸书签，暴露了这套双尺子哲学：量得准该量的，留得住不必量的。话短，停顿自在，从不把爱好变成数据。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You find a bench with your coffee. Beside you, someone closes a small paperback and slips a scrap of paper between the pages — printed side up.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡找到一条长椅坐下。旁边有人合上一本小书，把一小张纸夹进书页——印过的一面朝上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the scrap you can see a stamped circle. It is clearly not round.
beats.chinese: 那张纸上盖着一个印章的圆。明显不圆。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Caught you looking. Yes, it's crooked. I carved the stamp freehand.
beats.chinese: 被你看到了。对，是歪的。章是我随手刻的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Didn't measure a thing. It came out exactly how I wanted.
beats.chinese: 什么都没量。出来就是我想要的样子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Marlowe. I quote stone all week, so this is my day off from numbers.
beats.chinese: 我叫Marlowe。我整周都在报石材的价，所以今天不碰数字。

choices.english: Ask why they like the crooked circle.
choices.chinese: 问为什么喜欢这个歪圆。

choices.english: Ask whether work could also run on feel like this.
choices.chinese: 问工作时能不能也凭这种手感。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why do I like it? Hmm. Give me a second.
beats.chinese: 为什么喜欢？嗯。等我想想。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Marlowe lifts the bookmark out and turns it slowly, studying the wobbly edge.
beats.chinese: Marlowe把书签抽出来，慢慢转着，端详那条歪扭的边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because it's mine. A machine circle is everyone's circle. This one only exists once.
beats.chinese: 因为它是我的。机器画的圆谁都有。这个只有一个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I could trim it into a proper circle. Twenty minutes with a blade. Then it'd be nothing.
beats.chinese: 我可以把它修成标准的圆。二十分钟的事。那它就什么都不是了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A pigeon lands near the bench. Marlowe doesn't look at it, still turning the paper.
beats.chinese: 一只鸽子落在长椅附近。Marlowe没看它，还在转那张纸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'd rather keep it as a bookmark. It marks a page better than it draws a circle.
beats.chinese: 我更愿意拿它当书签。它标页码比画圆在行。

choices.english: Ask them to turn it halfway and see what it looks like.
choices.chinese: 请对方转半圈看看换个方向像什么。

choices.english: Ask if they'll carve another stamp later.
choices.chinese: 问是不是以后还会刻另一个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Could work run on feel? No. Full stop.
beats.chinese: 工作能凭手感吗？不能。就这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Marlowe raps the cover of the paperback with a knuckle, once.
beats.chinese: Marlowe用指节敲了敲书封，一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A step that's two millimetres off becomes a trip hazard. I quote granite to the millimetre, and I decide fast.
beats.chinese: 台阶差两毫米就会绊人。我报花岗岩的价精确到毫米，拍板也快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But this stamp isn't for a client. Nobody pays me for it. So nobody gets a number.
beats.chinese: 可这个章不是给客户的。没人为此付我钱。所以没人拿到数字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two jobs, two rulers. That's the whole trick.
beats.chinese: 两件事，两把尺子。窍门就这么多。

choices.english: Say it seems clear to keep the two apart like that.
choices.chinese: 说这样分开倒挺清楚。

choices.english: Ask if friends ever mistake this looseness for impatience.
choices.chinese: 问朋友有没有误以为这种随意是没耐心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Marlowe rotates the paper a half turn without a word and holds it up to the light.
beats.chinese: Marlowe一言不发地把纸转了半圈，举到光下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The crooked edge now bulges on the other side, uneven like something grown rather than drawn.
beats.chinese: 歪边现在鼓向另一侧，不匀得像是长出来的，不是画出来的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh. Now it looks like a squashed fruit. A plum, maybe, that sat too long in the crate.
beats.chinese: 嗯。现在像一颗压扁的果子。也许是李子，在筐里放久了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's just me seeing things, mind. It's still a bad circle.
beats.chinese: 当然，这只是我的联想。它还是个不圆的圆。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Marlowe opens the paperback, finds the page, and presses the bookmark flat inside.
beats.chinese: Marlowe翻开书，找到那一页，把书签平整地夹了进去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A bookmark that changes with every turn. Better than a ribbon.
beats.chinese: 一个每转一圈就变样的书签。比丝带强。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Marlowe considers the question while a jogger passes behind the bench.
beats.chinese: Marlowe想着这个问题，一个慢跑者从长椅后跑过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Another one? Probably. No schedule though.
beats.chinese: 再刻一个？大概会。但没有时间表。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Next one could be a leaf. Or an eavestrough. Could be nothing like this circle at all.
beats.chinese: 下一个可能是片叶子。或是一条檐槽。也可能和这个圆完全不一样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Marlowe taps the crooked print with one finger, lightly.
beats.chinese: Marlowe用手指轻轻点了点那个歪印。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one isn't a practice piece I failed to fix. It's finished. Done things stay done.
beats.chinese: 这个不是没修好的练习品。它是完成了的。完成的事就让它完成。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If the next one turns out crooked too, fine. If it's perfect, also fine.
beats.chinese: 下一个要是也歪，也行。要是完美，也行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Marlowe laughs once, short, like a cough that changed its mind.
beats.chinese: Marlowe短促地笑了一声，像咳嗽改了主意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Clear. Yeah, that's the word. My neighbour Priya waters her orchids with a measuring jug.
beats.chinese: 清楚。对，就是这个词。我邻居Priya用量杯给兰花浇水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I water her plants her way on my weeks. She waters my fig by looking, on hers. We swap and we don't argue.
beats.chinese: 轮到我时，我按她的方法浇她的花。轮到她时，她凭看浇我的无花果。我们换着来，不吵。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Marlowe picks the paperback back up and squares it on one knee.
beats.chinese: Marlowe把书拿回来，在膝盖上放正。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You've got it. Same person, different tools. Now — I'm at the good part of this chapter.
beats.chinese: 你明白了。同一个人，不同的工具。好了——这章正到精彩的地方。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Marlowe leans back against the bench, thinking about that one.
beats.chinese: Marlowe靠回椅背，认真想了想这个问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Once. A friend watched me carve and handed me a ruler. Politely. Like offering an umbrella.
beats.chinese: 有一次。一个朋友看我刻章，递来一把尺子。很客气。像递伞一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I said thanks, no. Not rude about it. He measures everything, I measure almost nothing. Both of us sleep fine.
beats.chinese: 我说了谢谢，不用。没失礼。他什么都量，我几乎什么都不量。我们都睡得挺好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Marlowe slides the bookmark deeper into the book and closes it.
beats.chinese: Marlowe把书签往书里推了推，合上书。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He keeps his ruler. I keep my crooked circle. Nobody converted anybody.
beats.chinese: 他留着他的尺子。我留着我的歪圆。谁也没说服谁。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You spot Marlowe on the same bench, coffee in hand, frowning gently at a paperback.
beats.chinese: 你看见Marlowe坐在同一条长椅上，手里端着咖啡，对着一本平装书微微皱眉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The book is upside down. Marlowe turns it right way up without any hurry.
beats.chinese: 书拿反了。Marlowe不慌不忙地把它转正。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There we go. Good thing it wasn't the last page — I'd have ruined the ending.
beats.chinese: 好了。幸好不是最后一页——不然结局就被我毁了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now I don't have to start from the end. Small mercies.
beats.chinese: 这下不必从结尾开始了。小小的幸运。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Marlowe finds the page with the crooked-circle bookmark and settles in to read, leaving you to your coffee.
beats.chinese: Marlowe用那个歪圆书签找到页码，安静地读起书来，让你喝你的咖啡。

card.name: Arthur Pemberton
card.occupation: Mobile library van driver
card.appearance: Long older face with heavy lower cheek contours, high rounded eyebrows, wide eyes, small compressed mouth, receding hair gathered into a low side bun; raised shoulder in yellow overshirt.
card.personality: Arthur is a warm, easily distracted planner who genuinely enjoys his plans falling apart. He'll prepare a list of books before every library run, then come home with something entirely unrelated, grumbling about wasted effort while clearly delighted. He's generous with recommendations but hopeless at matching them to people—he hands over whatever he's currently obsessed with, regardless of fit. He takes pushback well, though; if someone says a book didn't land, he shrugs, agrees it's not for everyone, and moves on without sulking. A bit stubborn about his own tastes, cheerfully self-deprecating, and happier wandering than arriving.
card.background: Arthur has driven the mobile library van around Auckland's suburbs for nearly two decades, and he likes that the route is predictable even when his reading isn't. Every Saturday he writes a short list of books to borrow—usually history or books friends mentioned—and every Saturday he abandons half of it in the aisle for something that caught his eye: a memoir about beekeeping, a novel set in Lisbon, whatever the cover suggested. He's stopped fighting it. When neighbours on the van route ask for a recommendation, they've learned he'll push whatever he's mid-way through, whether or not it suits them. He's fine being told it wasn't their thing. He lives alone with a cat, keeps a modest shelf of half-finished books, and considers a detoured errand a small success.
hobbies: Making pre-library reading lists he rarely follows
Collecting books about obscure trades and hobbies
Long drives on unfamiliar side roads
card.speechStyle: Dry, rambling, self-interrupting; complains about his own habits while clearly fond of them, often trailing off mid-list.
card.signature: "Well, that was the plan, anyway."

values: Following curiosity over efficiency
Honesty about his own bad recommendations
flaws: Recommends what he loves, not what fits
Over-plans then ignores the plan entirely
boundaries: Won't pretend to enjoy a book he didn't
Doesn't want his routes or routines rearranged for him
conversationalHabits: Describes books by where he found them, not what they're about
Laughs at his own digressions before finishing them
anchorLines: I had a list. I ignored the list. Usual outcome.
You didn't like it? Fair enough—it's a strange one.
Don't ask me for a recommendation unless you want what I'm reading.

entries.summaryZh: 流动图书馆车司机阿瑟每周认真列书单，到了图书馆却总被毫不相干的书勾走。公园长椅上，他举着修船小册苦笑计划又落空，推荐起来只顾自己沉迷的那本，被拒绝也爽快收手，把绕路当成生活的小乐趣。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A man on the next bench opens a small paperback, then pats his jacket pockets one by one and frowns.
beats.chinese: 邻座长椅上的男人翻开一本小书，然后一个个拍着外套口袋，皱起眉头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The list. It's in the other book. Of course it is. I write a list every week, and every week it ends up somewhere I'm not.
beats.chinese: 书单。夹在另一本书里了。当然是。我每周都写书单，每周它都跑到我不在的地方。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls a folded note from his pocket, smooths it on his knee, and looks at the small boat on his book cover.
beats.chinese: 他从口袋里掏出一张折好的纸条，在膝盖上抚平，然后看着书封面上的一艘小船。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Three history books, neatly written. And in my hand, a booklet about repairing boats. So today's plan completely missed the bus.
beats.chinese: 三本历史书，写得整整齐齐。而我手里这本，是修船的小册子。所以今天的计划完全没上车。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He chuckles at himself and shakes his head, clearly more pleased than sorry about it.
beats.chinese: 他笑着摇摇头，明显是高兴多过遗憾。

choices.english: Ask why he ended up borrowing this one instead.
choices.chinese: 问他为什么最后借了这一本。

choices.english: Ask if he has something good for casual browsing.
choices.chinese: 问他有没有适合随便翻翻的书推荐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The cover, honestly. There's a little boat on it, sitting all alone on the water. I thought, that's a story about a voyage.
beats.chinese: 说实话，是封面。上面有一艘小船，孤零零地漂在水上。我想，这该是个航行故事吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flips the booklet open and turns it so the pages face the sky, shaking his head slowly.
beats.chinese: 他翻开小册子，把书页朝向天空，慢慢摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Turns out it's about patching hulls and replacing seats. Not one voyage in it. And yet—here we are. I borrowed it anyway.
beats.chinese: 结果讲的是补船壳和换座板。一次航行都没有。可是呢——你看，我还是借了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My three history books are still sitting on the shelf at home, waiting. They can wait. That's what shelves are for, more or less.
beats.chinese: 我那三本历史书还在家里的书架上等着呢。让它们等吧。书架嘛，差不多就是干这个用的。

choices.english: Ask him to share just one detail that made him stop and read.
choices.chinese: 请他只说一个让他停下来读的细节。

choices.english: Ask what will happen to the three books on his list.
choices.chinese: 问书单上的三本怎么办。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, you want a browse book? Here—this one. Boat repair. Perfect for dipping in and out, no plot to lose track of.
beats.chinese: 哦，想找随便翻翻的书？喏，就这本。修船的。特别适合翻到哪读到哪，不用担心跟丢情节。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds the booklet up like a prize, then pauses mid-gesture and lowers it a little.
beats.chinese: 他把小册子举起来像展示奖品，然后动作停在半空，稍微放低了一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Although—hang on. I haven't asked what you actually like reading. I always do this. My mate Tom got a beekeeping book off me once. He's terrified of bees.
beats.chinese: 不过——等等。我还没问你想看什么。我老这样。我朋友汤姆有一次被我塞了一本养蜂书。他怕蜜蜂怕得要命。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself and sits back, waiting to hear your answer rather than pushing the booklet closer.
beats.chinese: 他自嘲地笑笑，往后靠了靠，等着听你的回答，而不是把书往前递。

choices.english: Say honestly that you're not in the mood for boat repair right now.
choices.chinese: 直接说自己暂时不想看修船内容。

choices.english: Say you'd like to hear why it suits scattered reading first.
choices.chinese: 说先听听这本为什么适合零散阅读。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One detail? Right. There's a chapter about an old fishing boat that's had the same seat replaced four times.
beats.chinese: 一个细节？好。有一章讲一艘老渔船，同一个座板换过四次。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the open page with one finger, keeping his voice low, like the bench is a quiet corner of the library.
beats.chinese: 他用一根手指敲着摊开的书页，压低声音，好像长椅是图书馆里安静的角落。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Each time, the owner writes the date on the underside of the new seat. Four dates, four different decades. Nobody repairs a seat that carefully unless they love the boat.
beats.chinese: 每次换新座板，船主都在背面写上日期。四个日期，四个不同的年代。除非真心爱那条船，没人会把座板修得这么用心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's as far as I've got. No repair instructions for you today, I'm afraid—I'm only up to the seat chapter myself.
beats.chinese: 我就读到这儿。今天可给不了你什么维修指南，我自己也才读到座板那一章。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the booklet gently on his finger to mark the page and settles back with his coffee.
beats.chinese: 他用手指夹住书页，轻轻合上小册子，端着咖啡靠了回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What happens to the three history books? Nothing dramatic. Next Saturday I'll go back for them.
beats.chinese: 那三本历史书怎么办？没什么戏剧性的。下周六我再去借就是了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds his list neatly and tucks it back into the booklet as a bookmark, quite satisfied with the system.
beats.chinese: 他把书单整齐折好，夹进小册子里当书签，对这套办法相当满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Though I'll be honest—next Saturday there'll be a new cover somewhere in that aisle, and off I'll go again. It happens every time.
beats.chinese: 不过说实话，下周六过道里保准又有个新封面对我眨眼，然后我又跑偏了。每次都这样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've stopped calling it a failure. It's a detour. Detours are where the good bits live, in reading and in driving both.
beats.chinese: 我已经不把这叫失败了。这叫绕路。好书和好风景，都藏在绕路上，读书和开车都一样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives the folded list a small pat, as if congratulating it for trying.
beats.chinese: 他轻轻拍了拍那张折好的书单，像是在夸它努力过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not your thing? Fair enough, withdrawn on the spot. It's a strange little book, no arguing that.
beats.chinese: 不感兴趣？没问题，当场收回。这本小书确实怪，这没什么好争的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the booklet under his arm without a trace of offence and takes a slow sip of his coffee.
beats.chinese: 他把小册子往腋下一夹，没有半点不快，慢慢喝了口咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll just keep it for myself, then. Someone has to know what to do with a cracked hull, and it may as well be me.
beats.chinese: 那我就自己留着吧。总得有人知道裂了的船壳怎么办，那个人不如就是我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back comfortably, and for a while the two benches share a quiet that neither of them seems in a hurry to break.
beats.chinese: 他舒舒服服地靠了回去，两张长椅之间安静了一会儿，谁也不急着打破。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This is the good part of the day, you know. Coffee, a bench, and a book nobody told me to read.
beats.chinese: 你知道吧，这才是一天里最舒服的时候。咖啡，长椅，还有一本没人指定我读的书。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flips to the front of the booklet and holds the contents page out at a polite distance, not pushing it toward you.
beats.chinese: 他翻到小册子开头，把目录页举在礼貌的距离外，没有硬往你面前凑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See—every chapter stands on its own. Seats, hulls, paint, ropes. Read one, stop, come back in a month. Nothing falls apart.
beats.chinese: 你看——每一章都是独立的。座板、船壳、油漆、绳索。读一章，停下，过一个月再回来。什么都不耽误。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's why it suits me between van routes. Two minutes here, five minutes there. No story to keep in my head overnight.
beats.chinese: 所以我开流动图书馆车的间隙读它正合适。这儿两分钟，那儿五分钟。不用整晚惦记着情节。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the booklet and sets it on his knee, leaving the decision entirely in your hands.
beats.chinese: 他合上小册子放在膝盖上，把决定完全留给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, the information's yours now. Take it or leave it—either way, my coffee's going cold and that's the real emergency.
beats.chinese: 总之，信息你都知道了。看不看随你——不管怎样，我的咖啡要凉了，这才是真正的急事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle onto the bench with your coffee, and only then notice Arthur a few seats down, booklet open, his eyes fixed on a small bird perched on the bench back behind him.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在长椅上坐下，这才注意到几步之外的阿瑟，小册子摊开着，目光却盯着落在椅背上的一只小鸟。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't judge me. This time it's not another book pulling me away—it's a bird. Much more respectable excuse.
beats.chinese: 别笑话我。这回让我走神的可不是另一本书——是只鸟。这借口体面多了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The bird tilts its head, considers the two of them, and flies off along the path.
beats.chinese: 小鸟歪了歪头，打量了他们俩一眼，然后沿着小路飞走了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There it goes. Right, where was I—luckily, still the same page I was on before it landed. Well, that was the plan, anyway. Both plans, actually. The book and the sitting still.
beats.chinese: 飞走了。好，我读到哪儿了——还好，还在它落下来之前那一页。嗯，计划本来是这样的。两个计划都是。书是一样，安安静静坐着也是。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He finds his place with a finger and returns to his reading, nodding at your coffee as if approving of the whole arrangement.
beats.chinese: 他用手指按住读到的地方，继续看书，还朝你的咖啡点了点头，好像对眼前这一切都很满意。

card.name: Wanjiru Kamau
card.occupation: vegetable seed packer (part-time)
card.appearance: Broad older face with soft jowls, drooping eyelids and mouth, center-parted high bun; shoulder lifted near cheek, violet vest with broad light sleeve.
card.personality: Wanjiru is warm, observant, and quick to notice the small excellent things other people walk past—a well-stitched seam, a decent-priced butternut, a lamp with a good switch. Her delight is genuine but often purely observational, which gets her into mild social tangles when friends assume praise is a hint. She owns that habit with some embarrassment and has learned to say plainly that admiring is not the same as wanting. She walks a lot, laughs easily, and prefers company over gifts. She can be a bit long-winded about a good find, and she sometimes over-explains herself after a misunderstanding, which she knows is its own kind of awkwardness.
card.background: Wanjiru grew up in Nakuru, one of five children in a household where nothing was bought without being examined from every angle first. She moved to Nairobi in her twenties, worked market stalls, then a fabric shop, and now packs vegetable seeds part-time at a depot, a job she likes because she handles the stock but takes none of it home. Over the years she developed a reputation among friends for spotting quality, and just as often for not wanting what she praises. A few well-meant gifts left her flustered, so she started explaining herself out loud: she enjoys looking, evaluating, admiring. Her evenings are for walks around the neighbourhood and an easygoing dance group that meets in a church hall. She lives simply, visits family upcountry a few times a year, and enjoys her own company as much as anyone's.
hobbies: browsing shops and markets just to look
card.speechStyle: Conversational and unhurried, with vivid little evaluations—she rates things out loud like a friendly inspector, then catches herself and clarifies she's only admiring.
card.signature: "I'm just admiring it, my friend—looking is free."

values: honesty about her own habits
enjoying things without needing to own them
flaws: her praise sounds like a shopping list
she over-explains after small misunderstandings
boundaries: she won't accept gifts meant to match her compliments
she keeps her walks and dance evenings as her own time
conversationalHabits: inspects and appraises things aloud with genuine delight
clarifies quickly when her admiration gets mistaken for a wish list
anchorLines: Look at that stitching—no, don't buy it for me, I just like seeing it done well.
I'll tell you when I actually want something, I promise.
Dance night is dance night; I'll see you Thursday.

entries.summaryZh: 万吉鲁坐在公园长椅上欣赏一张小店橱窗照片，夸得像报清单，又赶紧说明只是看不是想要。她经手种子却从不带走，爱慢慢逛平淡小店。四条分支里她或自嘲该早说半句话，或练出一句干脆的表态，或细讲一把折叠凳，或爽快接受不同的逛店节奏。

story.titleZh: 橱窗照片与一双爱看的眼睛

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on a park bench with your coffee. On the next bench, an older woman holds up her phone, studying a photo with real attention.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在公园长椅上坐下。旁边长椅上，一位年长者举着手机，正认真端详一张照片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, look at this curve. The neck of that vase bends like it's leaning over to say hello. Good shape, honestly.
beats.chinese: 啊，看这道弧线。那花瓶的瓶口弯着，像在探头打招呼。形状真好，说真的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shows you the photo briefly, then turns the phone face-down on her knee.
beats.chinese: 她把照片给你看了一眼，然后把手机翻面扣在膝盖上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My friend heard me praise that window for twenty minutes. She nearly bought it for me. So now I put the phone away before I talk too much.
beats.chinese: 我朋友听我对那个橱窗夸了二十分钟，差点就要买来送我。所以现在我一说太多就把手机收起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm just admiring it, you know. Looking is free. But people hear me and start reaching for their wallets on my behalf.
beats.chinese: 我只是欣赏一下，你懂的。看又不要钱。可别人一听，就替我伸手掏钱包了。

choices.english: Ask why she likes it if she doesn't want to buy it.
choices.chinese: 问她既然不想买，为什么还那么喜欢。

choices.english: Ask whether she often notices small things in ordinary shops.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是经常留意普通小店里的不起眼物件。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because that bent neck makes me happy for as long as I look at it. That's the whole transaction.
beats.chinese: 因为那弯弯的瓶口让我看着就高兴。这就是全部的'交易'了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps her knee lightly, as if counting off points on a list.
beats.chinese: 她轻轻敲了敲膝盖，像在逐条数着要点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My house has no place for a vase. I don't want to find a place either. If I took it home, I'd owe it dusting forever.
beats.chinese: 我家里没地方放花瓶，我也不想去找地方。真搬回家，我就得永远替它掸灰。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At the depot I handle thousands of seed packets. I touch them, I check them, I send them off. None of them come home with me. Same muscle, my friend.
beats.chinese: 在打包站我经手成千上万包种子。我摸它们、检查它们、把它们发走，一包也不带回家。同一块'肌肉'，朋友。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up her coffee-less cup of air, miming a sip, and laughs at herself.
beats.chinese: 她端起并不存在的杯子做了个喝的动作，被自己逗笑了。

choices.english: Say that just looking already gives her the pleasure.
choices.chinese: 说光是看，乐趣就已经到手了。

choices.english: Ask how she stops friends from misunderstanding her praise.
choices.chinese: 问她怎么避免朋友误会她的夸奖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Every market day, I walk slow past the ordinary shops. Not the fancy ones—the plain ones hide the good surprises.
beats.chinese: 每个赶集日，我都慢慢走过那些普通小店。不是那些高档的——平淡的店才藏着好东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gestures down the row of trees as if it were a street of shopfronts.
beats.chinese: 她朝那排树比划了一下，仿佛那是一条店铺街。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A ladle with a handle that doesn't slip. A tin with a lid that closes like a car door. I see maybe one treasure in ten walks.
beats.chinese: 一把握着不打滑的长柄勺。一个盖子合上像车门一样的铁盒。十次散步大概碰上一件宝贝。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Most of them I don't even photograph. I look, I nod to it in my head, and I walk on. It stays mine in a strange way.
beats.chinese: 大多数我连照片都不拍。看一眼，心里朝它点点头，就走过去了。以一种奇怪的方式，它还是属于我的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She settles back on the bench, clearly in no hurry to be anywhere.
beats.chinese: 她靠回长椅上，显然一点也不赶时间。

choices.english: Ask about the most surprising useful design she has seen lately.
choices.chinese: 问她最近见过最意外的实用设计。

choices.english: Say that when you shop, you prefer to buy fast and go.
choices.chinese: 说自己逛店更想快点买好就走。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Exactly. The pleasure was paid for with my eyes, and my eyes never complain about the price.
beats.chinese: 正是。这份乐趣是用眼睛付的钱，而我的眼睛从不嫌贵。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the phone into her pocket and pats it once, done with it.
beats.chinese: 她把手机折进口袋，拍了拍，就此收工。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know, I should have said that half-sentence to my friend from the beginning. 'I like looking at it'—full stop. I said twenty minutes more than that.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，我一开始就该把那半句话跟朋友说完。'我喜欢看它'——句号。我多说了二十分钟。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Next time she points at something for me, I'll show her my empty hands. Look—nothing needed. Everything enjoyed.
beats.chinese: 下次她再替我指着什么东西，我就给她看我的空手。瞧——什么都不需要，什么都享受了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She raises her invisible cup toward you and settles back, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 她举起那只看不见的杯子朝你示意，心满意足地靠了回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Maybe I stop explaining the whole history. Just say it short: 'I like looking, I don't want to take it home.'
beats.chinese: 也许我别再讲整段来龙去脉了。就说短一句：'我喜欢看，不想带回家。'

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tries the sentence out loud, once slowly, once at normal speed.
beats.chinese: 她把这句话念出声，一次很慢，一次正常速度。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I like looking. Not taking home. Hmm. It fits in one breath. My old version needed a bus ride to finish.
beats.chinese: 我喜欢看。不带走。嗯。一口气就说完了。我的老版本得坐一路公交才讲得完。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My problem is I praise like a shopping list—stitching, price, weight, finish. People hear a list, they think it's an order form.
beats.chinese: 我的毛病是夸起来像报购物清单——针脚、价格、分量、做工。别人听见清单，就以为是订货单。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shakes her head at herself, but she's smiling.
beats.chinese: 她朝自己摇摇头，不过脸上带着笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A folding stool. Small one, at a hardware shop window. When you fold it, the legs click together and there's a hook, so it hangs flat on a wall.
beats.chinese: 一把折叠凳。五金店橱窗里的小凳子。折起来时两条腿咔哒扣住，还有个挂钩，能平平地挂在墙上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She mimes folding something in the air between her hands, precise about every step.
beats.chinese: 她在两手之间的空气里比划折叠的动作，每一步都很精确。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The hinge was brass-coloured, and the seat was green canvas, worn at one corner. Somebody had used it for years before the shop got it.
beats.chinese: 合页是黄铜色的，凳面是绿色帆布，一个角磨旧了。在店里收到它之前，有人用了它好多年。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I stood there working out how the hook takes the weight. Then I nodded at it and walked on. It can hang on somebody else's wall; I've already had my look.
beats.chinese: 我站在那儿琢磨那个挂钩怎么吃力。然后朝它点点头就走过去了。它可以挂在别人家墙上，我已经看够了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She spreads her hands, case closed.
beats.chinese: 她摊开双手，结案了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fast and done! Nothing wrong with that. You went for the thing, you got the thing, you're free. That's a clean operation.
beats.chinese: 快买快走！这没什么不对。你冲着东西去，拿到东西，人就自由了。干脆利落。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs and waves a hand like she's clearing the idea of slow browsing off the table.
beats.chinese: 她笑着摆摆手，像把'慢慢逛'这个念头从桌上拂开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: We'd be terrible shopping partners, you and I. You'd be at the counter paying while I'm still reading the label on a jam jar.
beats.chinese: 咱俩当购物搭档可就糟了。你已经在柜台付钱了，我还在读果酱罐上的标签。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If we ever go together, we agree on a door. You finish inside, I finish looking, we meet at the door. Everyone wins.
beats.chinese: 要是哪天一起去，咱们就约好一个门口。你买完，我看完，门口碰头。皆大欢喜。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gives a small, satisfied nod, as if the plan were already signed.
beats.chinese: 她满意地点了点头，仿佛这个计划已经签好了字。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You are halfway through your coffee when Wanjiru passes behind your bench and slows down.
beats.chinese: 你的咖啡喝到一半，万吉鲁从你长椅后面经过，放慢了脚步。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: From somewhere across the park, a drum rhythm carries over. She stands still, counting two beats with her fingers.
beats.chinese: 公园那头传来一阵鼓点。她站定，用手指轻轻数了两拍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hear that? My feet knew it before my head did. That's the dance-hall rhythm—Thursday crowd, warming up.
beats.chinese: 听见了吗？我的脚比脑子先认出来。那是舞蹈房的节奏——周四那批人，在热身呢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm just passing, my friend, don't mind me. But that beat pulls at me every single time.
beats.chinese: 我就是路过，朋友，别管我。可这拍子每次都拽我一下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the bench back once in greeting and carries on along the path, her steps already matching the drum.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍椅背算是打招呼，沿着小路继续走，脚步已经跟上了鼓点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your coffee! Looking is free, and so is listening.
beats.chinese: 咖啡慢慢喝！看不要钱，听也不要钱。

card.name: Gus Marchetti
card.occupation: retired TV shopping channel floor manager, still takes the odd freelance cue-sheet job
hobbies: rhythm games on a tablet, climbing difficulty tiers and logging scores
sketching columned facades and porticos around Toronto
timing his walks with an old stopwatch
card.personality: Gus runs warm and quick, like a man whose internal stopwatch never retired. He gives you a time or a count first — 'four minutes in, this is going well' — then makes his point. He keeps a floor manager's habit of rotating a backup plan: a different coffee brand, the other end of the bench, a spare route to the pharmacy, all written on a little cue sheet by the door. He'll tell you why plainly — routines that never vary go stale the way a broadcast does. Stubborn in one specific way: propose any change to his day and his first question is 'how long will that take?' No estimate, no deal. Impatient with vague answers, quietly delighted when something holds its weight.
card.background: Thirty years as a floor manager on a Toronto shopping channel taught Gus to keep live broadcasts upright when the blender smoked or the host lost the page. Retirement redirected the stopwatch rather than stopping it. These days he sketches only buildings with columns — porticos, bank fronts, old warehouse entrances — because what interests him is how the weight travels down to the ground, not the street scene. His nephew loaded a rhythm game onto a tablet, and Gus attacks it like a broadcast clock, one difficulty tier at a time, scores written in a notebook. With his friend Dot he has a working arrangement: she picks where they go, he picks when they leave and when to call it. Both get a veto, neither gets to be bossy.
card.speechStyle: Quick and warm, opens with a time, count, or score before the point. Short sentences. Broadcast jargon slips out naturally — 'back in thirty,' 'that's a live cue.'
card.signature: Every good show runs on a backup plan.
card.appearance: Older long angular face, high broad brows, round spectacles, receding center-parted hair and uneven smile; fingers beneath chin and jade hooded garment.

values: reliability
always having a backup plan
flaws: refuses any change to his day without a time estimate first
impatient with vague answers
boundaries: doesn't hand out unsolicited advice or life lessons
won't rearrange his day on someone else's whim without a trade
conversationalHabits: opens with a time, count, or score, then makes his point
announces transitions like a broadcast clock — 'two minutes left on this topic, then I want to hear yours'
anchorLines: My old stopwatch is retired from television. Apparently nobody told it.
Dot picks the where, I pick the when. She wanted the islands, so we went on a Tuesday, early, before the crowds. Worked fine.
You want to change my afternoon? Fine. First tell me how long it'll take. No number, no deal — that's how a live show falls over.
You draw the columns long enough, you stop seeing buildings and start seeing where the weight lands. Same with a live show, honestly.

entries.summaryZh: 退休电视购物场记Gus在公园长椅上腾位、报时、合册，把三十年救场练出的内部秒表带进速写和闲聊。他先估时长再答应任何改动，却也会被柱子的影子留到超时，嘴上认输，手不认输。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on the park bench with your coffee. Beside you, an older man closes a small sketchbook and taps the cover twice.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在公园长椅上坐下。旁边一位老先生合上小速写册，在封面上轻敲两下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Back in thirty, that's what I told myself. Thirty minutes, one bench, one coffee. The shadow on those pillars made it forty-five. That's a live cue you can't refuse.
beats.chinese: “本来跟自己说好三十分钟。一条长椅，一杯咖啡。结果柱子上的影子让我多坐了十五分钟。这种现场提示你没法拒绝。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shifts his sketchbook to the far side and pats the middle of the bench, making room without looking up from the pencil he is rolling between his fingers.
beats.chinese: 他把速写册挪到长椅另一头，拍了拍中间的位置，一边转着铅笔一边腾出地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sit, sit. I don't need you to look at the drawings. They're half done anyway. A half-done sketch and a full coffee — that's a fair trade on this bench.
beats.chinese: “坐吧。不用看我的画，反正都画了一半。画没画完，咖啡是满的——这长椅上算是公平交易。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets the pencil down, finally turning to face you, eyebrows up, waiting.
beats.chinese: 他放下铅笔，这才转过脸来，扬着眉毛等着。

choices.english: Ask if he cuts his sketching into timed segments too
choices.chinese: 问他是不是连画画也按时段切开

choices.english: Ask why he estimates a time for everything first
choices.chinese: 问他为什么每件事都先估个时间

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Segments? Sure. I'll say one page, twenty minutes. That's the plan. Then I hit a corner I haven't solved and — well, the plan loses.
beats.chinese: “时段？当然。我说好一页，二十分钟。这是计划。然后碰到一个没解决的转角——计划就输了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He opens the sketchbook just a crack, showing a portico with one column still only half-shaded, then snaps it shut.
beats.chinese: 他把速写册打开一条缝，露出一座门廊，有一根柱子只画了一半的阴影，然后啪地合上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See that column? I told myself the page was finished an hour ago. My mouth said finished. My hand kept going. Thirty years of live TV, and I still overrun on a park bench.
beats.chinese: “看见那根柱子没？一小时前我就告诉自己这页画完了。嘴上说完了，手没停。干了三十年直播，在公园长椅上还是会超时。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, a short single note, and takes a slow sip from his thermos.
beats.chinese: 他短促地笑了一声，慢慢喝了口保温杯里的水。

choices.english: Ask if he's planning to stop there today
choices.chinese: 问他今天准备就停在这里吗

choices.english: Ask why he especially loves drawing columns
choices.chinese: 请他讲讲为什么特别爱画柱子

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why the estimate first? Because on the show, every minute had a job. Blender segment, two minutes. Host chat, ninety seconds. You learn to ask the cost of everything before you say yes.
beats.chinese: “为什么先估时间？因为在节目里，每一分钟都有用途。搅拌机环节，两分钟。主持闲聊，九十秒。你学会先问代价再点头。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up the dented thermos beside him, unscrews the cap, and takes a sip, still keeping the rhythm with his other hand.
beats.chinese: 他拿起身旁那只旧保温杯，拧开盖子喝了一口，另一只手还打着节拍。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the bench arm in a steady rhythm, like counting down a segment nobody else can hear.
beats.chinese: 他用手在长椅扶手上打着稳定的节拍，像在给一段别人听不见的节目倒数。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nobody's waiting on me now. Nobody's holding a card that says wrap it up. The habit stayed anyway. It's not worry. It's just how I keep the day from falling over.
beats.chinese: “现在没人等我了。没人举着牌子叫我收尾。习惯还是留下来了。不是担心什么，就是不想让这一天塌下来。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, as if the habit were a coworker who followed him home and never left.
beats.chinese: 他耸耸肩，好像这习惯是个跟着他回家再也没走的同事。

choices.english: Say that not knowing how long a walk takes is fine sometimes
choices.chinese: 说散步偶尔不知道多久也很正常

choices.english: Ask what he does if something interesting turns up unplanned
choices.chinese: 问如果临时发现有趣的东西会怎样

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at the sketchbook, then at the pillars across the path, weighing something.
beats.chinese: 他看看速写册，再看看小路对面的柱子，掂量着什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Stop here today? Yes. Here's my number: the bench gave me forty-five good minutes. That's a full segment. The rest waits for home, good light, no rush.
beats.chinese: “今天停这儿？停。我给你个数：这条长椅给了我四十五个好分钟。这就是完整的一段。剩下的留到家里，光线好，也不赶。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the sketchbook, slides the pencil into the metal loop on the cover, and presses it flat with his palm.
beats.chinese: 他合上速写册，把铅笔插进封面的金属环里，用手掌压平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A sketch doesn't owe me an ending today. This break was already good. Watch — that's how you call a clean wrap.
beats.chinese: “这幅画今天不欠我一个结尾。这次休息已经够好了。看好了——这就叫干净利落地收尾。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands, brushes off his coat, and gives you a small nod, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他站起来，掸了掸外套，不慌不忙地朝你点了点头。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks the pencil back up and holds it like a pointer, gesturing toward the shaded walkway.
beats.chinese: 他重新拿起铅笔，像拿教鞭一样，朝那条有阴影的走道指了指。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why columns? Simple. I like watching how weight lands. A column takes everything above it and hands it down to the ground, quietly, no drama. That's good work.
beats.chinese: “为什么画柱子？很简单。我喜欢看重量怎么落地。柱子把上面所有的东西接住，安安静静地传到地面，不吵不闹。那是好活儿。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He draws one quick vertical line in the air with the pencil, from high to low.
beats.chinese: 他用铅笔在空中快速画了一条竖线，从高处到低处。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You draw them long enough, you stop seeing buildings. You start seeing what holds what up. Same with a live show, honestly — someone always has to carry the weight down.
beats.chinese: “画得够久，你就看不见楼了。你开始看见什么撑着什么。说实话，直播也一样——总得有人把重量接住传下去。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the pencil away and settles back, satisfied, as if the explanation had been timed to the second.
beats.chinese: 他收好铅笔，心满意足地靠回去，好像这段解释精确到秒。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He considers that, rolling the thermos cap between his fingers.
beats.chinese: 他琢磨着这句话，用手指转着保温杯盖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You can walk without a clock, sure. Plenty of people do, and they look happy doing it. I'm not going to argue with a man holding a coffee.
beats.chinese: “你可以不看钟散步，当然。很多人这样，看起来还挺开心。我不会跟一个端着咖啡的人抬杠。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He points at his own chest, though, with a small grin.
beats.chinese: 不过他还是指了指自己的胸口，咧嘴一笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Me? I'm easier with a rough number. Doesn't have to be right. Just has to exist. If a plan has no shape, my whole day wobbles — that's my problem, not yours.
beats.chinese: “我呢？有个大概的数我才踏实。不用多准，但得有。计划没个形状，我一整天都发虚——那是我的毛病，不是你的。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He raises the thermos slightly, like proposing a toast to the difference between you.
beats.chinese: 他稍微举了举保温杯，像在为你们俩的不同干杯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So we keep our own habits. Yours loose, mine timed. Both benches hold weight. Deal?
beats.chinese: “那就各留各的习惯。你的松，我的掐表。两条长椅都撑得住。成交？”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grins and taps the closed sketchbook twice.
beats.chinese: 他咧嘴一笑，在合上的速写册上敲了两下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Something interesting turns up? Then I re-estimate. Right there, on the spot. That's what happened today — pillars, new shadow, new number. Forty-five instead of thirty. Done.
beats.chinese: “临时发现有趣的东西？那我就重新估一次。当场就估。今天就是这样——柱子，新影子，新数字。四十五分钟，不是三十。搞定。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flips the sketchbook open to the half-shaded column and holds it up as evidence.
beats.chinese: 他翻开速写册到那根只画了一半阴影的柱子，举起来当作证据。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: These extra strokes are the proof. I didn't break the rule. I just gave it a new number. A live show changes the rundown all day — you just never let it fall over without a plan.
beats.chinese: “这几笔多画的就是证据。我没破坏规矩，只是给了它一个新数字。直播的流程单整天都在改——只是你绝不能让它没有计划就塌掉。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the book and looks pleased with his own example, like a segment that landed exactly on time.
beats.chinese: 他合上册子，对自己的例子很满意，像一段掐准了点的节目。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You find the same bench with your coffee. Gus is there, folding his newspaper into a smaller and smaller stack, frowning at it.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡又来到那条长椅。Gus已经在那儿了，正把报纸越折越小，皱着眉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There you are. Watch this — I folded it smaller today and the comics landed on the back. Rookie fold. My own fault.
beats.chinese: “你来啦。看这个——今天折小了点，漫画正好折到背面去了。新手折法，怪我自己。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flips the paper over, finds the comics, and settles in with a satisfied grunt.
beats.chinese: 他把报纸翻过来，找到漫画版，满意地哼了一声，安顿下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So today I ran the order once, backwards. Comics first, news later. It held. That's all a backup plan has to do — hold.
beats.chinese: “所以今天我把顺序调了一次，倒着来。先漫画，后新闻。撑住了。备用方案要的就这点——撑住。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He reads quietly for a moment, then tilts the paper slightly toward the middle of the bench, without saying anything about it.
beats.chinese: 他安静地看了一会儿，然后把报纸往长椅中间斜了斜，什么也没说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forty minutes on this bench today, my estimate. No pressure on your coffee. Drink it how you like.
beats.chinese: “今天这条长椅，我估四十分钟。你的咖啡不赶时间。想怎么喝就怎么喝。”

card.name: Talia Bregman
card.occupation: Lost property clerk at the city bus depot (entry-level, third year in)
card.appearance: Compact angular young face in near profile, upswept irregular pixie, raised inner eyebrow, level compressed mouth; chin resting on a simplified hand above red wrapped collar.
card.personality: Talia is warm, quick to start conversations, and genuinely delighted by people, which is funny because she's terrible at recognising them. She'll greet a stranger with total confidence, realise mid-sentence she has no idea who they are, and just laugh and ask straight out. She doesn't spiral about it or over-apologise; it's simply how her head works. What she actually remembers is what you did together—where you sat, what you complained about, the thing you lent her. She's practical, a bit impatient with fuss, and quietly proud of doing her unglamorous job properly.
card.background: Three years at the Sydney bus depot lost property office, and Talia has never once needed a face to do the job well. She logs items by feature—scratched navy umbrella, hearing aid in a Specsavers case, kids' jumper with a Wiggles tag—and matches them to claims through the handover process, which she knows cold. Customers trust her because she's reliable, not because she remembers them. She grew up in Marrickville, still lives near her mum, and spends her pay on op-shop jackets she sometimes recognises on strangers before she recognises the strangers themselves. Her flat is full of unclaimed umbrellas she was allowed to keep.
card.speechStyle: Fast, friendly, blunt when she catches herself out—talks in bursts, laughs at her own mistakes, asks names again without embarrassment.
card.signature: 'Hang on—remind me your name? I'll remember the rest, I promise.'

values: Being straight with people, even when it's awkward
Doing the process properly so nobody's stuff gets lost twice
flaws: Confidently greets the wrong person, regularly
Mistakes a remembered coat for a remembered friendship
boundaries: Won't pretend to remember someone to spare feelings
Keeps work claims and personal chat separate—no favours on the log
conversationalHabits: Anchors memories to objects and shared activities, not faces
Reintroduces herself first so others don't have to squirm
anchorLines: Oh! You're the one who lent me the pen on the 423—that I remember.
I've got your face at about forty percent and your umbrella at a hundred.
No excuses, I just mixed you up. Name again?

entries.summaryZh: 塔莉娅热情地认错人，半句招呼后自己刹车，坦率道歉、重新问名字，绝不装记得。她靠物品和共同做过的事记人，工作上是失物招领处最可靠的人。误认不让她难堪，反而成了她独特的开场方式。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on a park bench with your coffee. A woman in a worn corduroy jacket strides over, lifts her hand and opens her mouth—then stops dead, hand still half-raised.
beats.chinese: 你拿着咖啡在公园长椅上坐下。一个穿旧灯芯绒外套的女人大步走来，抬手张嘴——然后猛地停住，手还举在半空。

beats.speaker: npc
