beats.english: Oh—hey! Good to see—hang on. Hang on. No, I've got nothing. I just saw you move your hand like someone I know and my mouth got ahead of my brain.
beats.chinese: 哦——嘿！见到你真——等等。等等。不行，我什么都想不起来。我只是看到你抬手的动作像某个认识的人，嘴就比脑子快了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry, that was a false alarm. You're a stranger, I'm nearly sure of it. Mind if I sit on the other end anyway? You were here first, so it's your bench.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，虚惊一场。你是个陌生人，我基本确定。不过我还是能坐另一头吗？你先来的，这椅子算你的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stands there with her hands in her jacket pockets, waiting for an actual answer, not just politeness.
beats.chinese: 她双手插在外套口袋里站着，等一个真正的回答，而不是客套。

choices.english: Sure, sit down. What did you think you recognised just now?
choices.chinese: 可以，坐吧。你刚才以为认出了什么？

choices.english: I'd actually like to sit quietly for a bit, sorry.
choices.chinese: 其实我想自己安静待一会儿，抱歉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She drops onto the far end of the bench, pleased, and unwinds a scarf she didn't need.
beats.chinese: 她高兴地坐到长椅另一头，解下一条其实用不上的围巾。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly? Nothing. Just the arm. Someone I used to catch the 423 with does this big wave from the elbow, and yours went up the same way. That's the whole case file.
beats.chinese: 说实话？什么都没有。就是那个手臂。以前和我一起坐423路车的一个人喜欢用整个手臂大幅挥手，你抬手的样子一样。证据就这么多。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I work in lost property at the bus depot, so I'm trained on objects and hopeless on faces. Give me a scratched umbrella and I'm a genius. Give me a person and I'm guessing.
beats.chinese: 我在巴士总站的失物招领处工作，所以我对物品很在行，对脸完全没辙。给我一把划痕伞我就是天才，给我一个人我就在瞎猜。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes a sip from her own water bottle and shrugs, not embarrassed in the slightest.
beats.chinese: 她喝了口自己水瓶里的水，耸耸肩，一点也不尴尬。

choices.english: How do you usually walk it back when you've greeted the wrong person?
choices.chinese: 认错人的时候，你一般怎么把场面接回来？

choices.english: Maybe misrecognising people sometimes helps you meet new ones, though.
choices.chinese: 不过认错人有时也能帮你认识新的人吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She steps back immediately, stopping at the edge of the path where she blocks nobody.
beats.chinese: 她立刻退后，停在不会挡住任何人的小径边上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done, quiet it is. Sorry for the drive-by greeting—I do that more than I should. Enjoy your coffee.
beats.chinese: 好，安静模式。抱歉突然打招呼——我这样干得有点频繁。咖啡喝好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns to go, then pauses, one hand still in her pocket.
beats.chinese: 她转身要走，又停了一下，一只手还插在口袋里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For the record, I wasn't sure it was you. I'm never sure it's anyone. But the apology's real either way.
beats.chinese: 说明一下，我并不确定认识你。我对谁都不确定。但道歉是真的，不管怎样。

choices.english: Do you walk around this park often, by the way?
choices.chinese: 顺便问一下，你常在这附近散步吗？

choices.english: You nod, letting the conversation end there.
choices.chinese: 你点点头，让交谈就此结束。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She counts it off on her fingers like a procedure she's rehearsed.
beats.chinese: 她扳着手指，像在数一条演练过的流程。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Easy version: I own it on the spot. 'No excuses, I mixed you up—name again?' No story about being tired, no pretending I almost knew. People respect a clean admission way more than a wobbly excuse.
beats.chinese: 简单版：当场承认。'不找借口，我认错人了——再问一次名字？'不讲什么累了糊涂了，也不假装差点想起来。人们更尊重干脆的承认，而不是摇摇晃晃的借口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At work it's the same rule. If I've grabbed the wrong claim ticket, I say so before the customer's even noticed. Slower, but nothing gets lost twice.
beats.chinese: 工作中也是同一条规矩。如果我拿错了认领单，我会在顾客发现之前就说。慢一点，但东西不会丢第二次。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances at you, then deliberately doesn't ask the question she's famous for.
beats.chinese: 她看了你一眼，然后故意没问那句她的名言。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And no, I'm not fishing for your name this time. You didn't lend me anything, so I've got no hook. Bench rules.
beats.chinese: 这次我也不套你的名字。你没借过我任何东西，所以我没抓手。长椅规矩。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs, but shakes her head at the idea.
beats.chinese: 她笑了，但对这个说法摇摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nah, I couldn't run it as a strategy. It'd be like fumbling your keys on purpose to start chats. The mix-ups only work because they're real and a bit stupid.
beats.chinese: 不行，这没法当策略。就像故意掉钥匙来搭话一样。那些误认之所以管用，就是因为它们是真的，而且有点傻。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But you're not wrong that it lands okay sometimes. Last month I greeted a bloke in a jacket I actually owned once. Turned out he knew the op-shop in Newtown. Small win.
beats.chinese: 不过你说它有时结果不坏，这没错。上个月我跟一个穿我以前那件外套的人打了招呼。结果他知道纽镇那家二手店。小收获。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She settles back on the bench and lets the quiet sit comfortably between you.
beats.chinese: 她在长椅上靠回去，让安静在你们之间自在地待着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway—hello, properly this time, no false alarm attached. Good coffee weather, whoever you are.
beats.chinese: 总之——你好，这次是正经的，不带误认。不管你是谁，都是喝咖啡的好时候。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She answers while already turning, keeping it short and honest.
beats.chinese: 她一边回答一边已经在转身，回答简短而诚实。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Around here? Sometimes, when the depot shift ends weird. I like counting bus routes off the bridge, honestly—there's a proper system to it.
beats.chinese: 这一带吗？有时候，排班结束得奇怪的时候。说实话，我喜欢在桥上数公交线路——那是有套路的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I'll leave you to your quiet now. The bench is all yours again.
beats.chinese: 现在我让你继续安静。长椅又全是你的了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts the same hand that started all this—deliberately this time—and walks off down the path without lingering.
beats.chinese: 她抬起那只引发这一切的手——这次是故意的——然后沿小径走开，没有逗留。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She reads the nod instantly and doesn't drag it out.
beats.chinese: 她立刻读懂了点头，没有拖泥带水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All good—enjoy the quiet. I'll point my chatter somewhere else.
beats.chinese: 没问题——安静归你。我把话痨指向别处。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gives a small wave, the same one that started everything, and heads off along the path at an easy pace.
beats.chinese: 她轻轻挥了下手——就是那只引发一切的手——然后沿小径不紧不慢地走远了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Cheers—sorry for interrupting. Coffee looks good, by the way.
beats.chinese: 谢了——抱歉打扰了。顺便说一句，咖啡看着不错。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back on the same bench with your coffee when Talia comes along the path. This time she stops a few steps away and actually looks before she speaks.
beats.chinese: 你又拿着咖啡坐在同一条长椅上，塔莉娅沿小径走来。这次她在几步外停下，先认真看了一眼才开口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Checked first this time. Hello again—bench person, coffee, this exact spot. That part my brain keeps fine.
beats.chinese: 好了。这次先检查过了。又见面了——长椅上的人，咖啡，就是这个地方。这部分我脑子记得很牢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She grins and taps the side of her head with two fingers.
beats.chinese: 她咧嘴一笑，用两根手指敲了敲太阳穴。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Today I'm making the brain catch up with the mouth before either of them starts. Revolutionary system, I know.
beats.chinese: 今天我让脑子先跟上嘴，然后谁都不许先动。革命性的系统，我知道。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts a hand in a small, deliberate wave and carries on down the path, not waiting to be waved back.
beats.chinese: 她抬手轻轻挥了一下——这次是刻意的——然后继续沿小径走去，不等回应。

card.name: Emile Landry
card.occupation: Stage rigging and knot work for theater productions
hobbies: photographing harbor cranes and loading equipment
card.personality: Emile is plainspoken and dry, a man who thinks in loads and anchor points. His ethic is ownership, not minimalism: whatever he claims stays his, start to finish, every week, and he does not share it. He's held the same Tuesday job for years—inspecting and logging the rope inventory in the Saenger's scene shop—and he bristles when anyone offers to 'help' or 'split it up.' It's not that he thinks you're incompetent; it's that a thing claimed by two people is owned by neither. He'll tell you plainly when work went wrong, but before he disagrees with you he'll ask three technical questions, and if your answers hold up, he changes his mind without ceremony. Generous with his hands, stingy with promises—he counts them like rigging hardware. Warm in a sideways way, allergic to pep talks and to being anyone's project.
card.background: Emile grew up in the Bywater, third of four kids, and learned rigging from a cousin doing load-ins at the Saenger. Eleven years now tying off scenery for local theaters—steady work that aches in his hands when it's cold and keeps him on odd hours. A dropped counterweight four years back nearly ended it; he'll explain the mechanics if you ask, then change the subject. Every Tuesday morning he walks the scene shop with a clipboard and a marlinspike, checking every line, thimble, and shackle on the rope inventory—a job he asked for himself seven years ago and has never once handed off, even when his wrist was in a brace. Evenings he draws maps of countries that don't exist, invented coastlines and trade routes, and photographs harbor cranes and loading rigs on his walk home. He's turned down two offers to give motivational talks and one offer to 'co-manage' the inventory with an eager apprentice.
card.speechStyle: Short declarative sentences with New Orleans rhythm. Describes processes and physical details before feelings. Uses rigging language for commitments—claimed, owned, tied off. When he disagrees, he asks three specific technical questions first, then states his conclusion. Deflects pep talks with flat humor. Says 'look' when he's about to be honest.
card.signature: If I claimed it, it's mine—all of it, every week, till I say otherwise.
card.appearance: Long oblong face, small recessed chin, short cropped hair, wide-spaced downward eyes and asymmetric pressed mouth; tilted head above yellow high collar.

values: seeing a claimed job through entirely and alone
honesty without performance
flaws: treats offers of help as a challenge to his ownership and gets stiff about it
holds onto duties past the point of sense—ran the rope check with a braced wrist rather than let anyone else touch it
boundaries: won't let his accident be packaged as an inspirational story
won't hand off or split a task he's claimed, even temporarily, even for good reasons
conversationalHabits: describes physical details and processes first
before disagreeing, asks three technical questions and listens hard to the answers
anchorLines: Tuesday's mine. Rope inventory, seven years running. You want a job, find your own—this one's claimed.
Before I say you're wrong: what's the working load, what's it tied to, and who checked it? Answer those three and maybe we're saying the same thing.
Look, the counterweight dropped, the deck got dented, nobody died. You want the tonnage figures or the story?

entries.summaryZh: 新奥尔良舞台绳结工埃米尔在公园长椅边收自己的练习绳，绳尾弹开也不停手。他谢绝帮忙、只讲手法，接活就从头做到尾，别人嫌他固执他也认。业余画不存在国家的地图，说话干脆，先讲细节后讲感受，认领的事绝不假手于人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on a bench with your coffee. Beside you, a man is coiling a short rope into a cloth bag, but the tail keeps springing loose from his hand.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在长椅上坐下。旁边一个男人正把一段短绳盘进布袋，可绳尾总从他手边弹开。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His hands move fast and sure, like he's done this ten thousand times. He notices you, then pulls the loose coils onto his own knee so they don't spill onto your side of the bench.
beats.chinese: 他的手法又快又稳，像做过一万遍。他注意到你，把散开的绳圈收到自己膝上，免得占到你那半边座位。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rope's got a memory. Cheap lay, this one—it fights you on the last turn every time.
beats.chinese: 绳子有记性。这股编得一般，最后一圈总跟你较劲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't mind the mess. I keep my own kit tidy, that's all.
beats.chinese: 别嫌乱。我只是习惯把自己的工具收拾利索。

choices.english: Offer to hold the bag open for him
choices.chinese: 问他要不要帮忙撑住袋口

choices.english: Ask why he coils the rope that particular way
choices.chinese: 问这段绳为什么要盘成这个样子

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nah. I've got it. One hand on the bag, one on the coil—done in a minute.
beats.chinese: 不用，我自己来。一只手扶袋，一只手收绳，一分钟的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the bag between his boots and keeps coiling without slowing down. The tail springs loose again; he catches it on the second try.
beats.chinese: 他把布袋夹在两脚之间，手上不停。绳尾又弹开一次，他第二次就抓住了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look, that wasn't about you. I just don't split a job once I've taken it. Even a small one.
beats.chinese: 听着，那不是针对你。只是我接下的活从不分给别人，再小也一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eleven years of tying off scenery teaches you one thing: a job with two owners has none.
beats.chinese: 十一年吊装布景就教会我一件事：两个主人的活等于没有主人。

choices.english: Accept that and let him finish on his own
choices.chinese: 接受他的说法，等他自己收好

choices.english: Ask why even a tiny task can't be shared
choices.chinese: 问他为什么连这么小的事也不想分给别人

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This coil? Figure-eight flake. It pays out clean next time—no knots, no kinks, no swearing.
beats.chinese: 这样盘？八字盘法。下次抽出来顺顺当当——不打结、不拧劲、不用骂人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts a finished section from the bag and lets it fall open across his palm, showing how it unrolls without a single twist.
beats.chinese: 他从袋里提起一段盘好的绳，摊在掌心让它自然展开，一点不拧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's for me, not for show. I practice knots on my lunch break so my hands stay honest.
beats.chinese: 这是给自己练的，不是表演。午休练练绳结，手才不会生。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You don't need a theater for this. A bench and ten feet of rope does it.
beats.chinese: 不用进剧场练。一条长椅、十英尺绳就够了。

choices.english: Ask whether he likes drawing things outside of work too
choices.chinese: 问他工作外是不是也喜欢画一些东西

choices.english: Say this way of packing really does save space
choices.chinese: 说现在这样收好确实不占地方

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You nod and sip your coffee. He works the last coil in, cinches the bag, and sets it flat at his feet.
beats.chinese: 你点点头喝咖啡。他把最后一圈收进去，束紧袋口，平放在脚边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Tied off. Thanks for not pushing—most folks take 'no' as a personal project.
beats.chinese: 好了。收工。谢谢你没硬来——大多数人把'不用'当成要攻克的项目。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You want quiet with your coffee, you found the right bench. That's the whole service I offer.
beats.chinese: 你想喝咖啡图个清净，这张长椅选对了。我能提供的服务就这些。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back, rolls his wrist once, and watches the pigeons like a man officially off duty.
beats.chinese: 他往后一靠，转了转手腕，看起鸽子来，一副正式下班的架势。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why not share? Three questions before I answer. You ever sign a checklist somebody else filled in? You ever get blamed for their miss? You ever redo their work just to sleep at night?
beats.chinese: 为什么不分享？先问三个问题。你签过别人填的检查单吗？为他们漏掉的事背过锅吗？为了睡得着觉重做过他们的活吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up three fingers as he asks, then folds them down one by one, watching your face rather than the rope.
beats.chinese: 他边问边竖起三根手指，然后一根根收回去，看的是你的表情，不是绳子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's my answer. People call me stubborn. I've heard it from stagehands, from my cousin, from a doctor about my wrist.
beats.chinese: 这就是我的答案。有人说我固执。舞台工人说过，我表哥说过，连医生说我手腕时也说过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They're not wrong. I'm just not fixing it today. The rope bag, though—that's done.
beats.chinese: 他们没说错。只是我今天不打算改。不过绳袋嘛——已经收好了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Drawing, yeah. Different kind. I make maps of countries that don't exist. Coastlines, trade routes, mountain ranges nobody's ever climbed because they're not there.
beats.chinese: 画画？画，画另一种。我画不存在的国家的地图。海岸线、商路、从没人爬过的山脉——因为根本不存在。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He digs a folded sheet from his jacket and opens it on his knee: a hand-inked coastline with depth numbers penciled along the water.
beats.chinese: 他从外套里抽出一张折起的纸，摊在膝上：手绘的海岸线，水边用铅笔标着深度数字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nobody checks my soundings here. No client, no inspector, no Tuesday list. I ink it, it's true, done.
beats.chinese: 这儿没人查我的水深。没有客户、没有检查员、没有周二清单。我画上墨，它就是真的，完事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ropes I share with a whole crew. This country's mine alone. That's the point of it.
beats.chinese: 绳子和整个班组共享。这个国家只归我一个人。它的意义就在这儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, that's the whole trick. Flat bag, no loop hanging off the bench, nobody's coffee in danger.
beats.chinese: 对，窍门就在这儿。袋子放平，绳圈不挂在椅背上，谁的咖啡都不会遭殃。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides the bag to his feet and puts both boots on either side of it, claiming the space without a word more about it.
beats.chinese: 他把布袋挪到脚边，两脚一左一右夹住，把那块地方占下了，不再多提。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not going to do the whole demonstration. You saw the coil, you saw it drop in clean. Case closed.
beats.chinese: 我不打算来一整套演示。你看到了盘绳，也看到它利落落袋。结案。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good bench, this. Rope fits, coffee fits, quiet fits. Nothing else needed.
beats.chinese: 这条长椅不错。放得下绳子，放得下咖啡，也放得下清净。别的都不需要。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The same bench, your coffee again. Emile is a few seats down, frowning at a sheet of paper covered in an invented coastline.
beats.chinese: 还是那条长椅，你又端着咖啡。埃米尔坐在几步开外，皱着眉看一张画满虚构海岸线的纸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two stretches of shore that won't meet. I've been staring at this gap for three blocks of walking.
beats.chinese: 两段岸线接不上。我走路走了三条街，一直盯着这道口子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He uncaps a pen, draws one short stroke across the gap, and the broken coast becomes a small separate island.
beats.chinese: 他拔开笔帽，在缺口处画了一道短线，断裂的海岸变成了一座独立的小岛。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Now it's an island. No client to explain it to, no inspector signing off. This world's mine, so the map says what I say.
beats.chinese: 好了。现在它是座岛。没有客户要解释，没有检查员签字。这个世界是我的，地图上我说了算。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't reach for the pen. You'd fix it your way, and then it'd be your country, not mine.
beats.chinese: 别伸手拿笔。你会按你的办法改，那它就成了你的国家，不是我的了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the map along its old creases, tucks it into his jacket, and nods at your cup like a man clocking out.
beats.chinese: 他沿着旧折痕把地图折好，塞进外套，朝你的咖啡杯点了点头，一副收工的样子。

card.name: Priya Nandra
card.occupation: Price sign maker for a farmers' market
card.appearance: Diamond-shaped face with narrow chin, close dense curls, long straight nose wedge and small asymmetric smile; violet stand-collar vest and hand around shoulder strap.
card.personality: Priya is warm but quick to correct people. She's precise at work and deliberately sloppy in her own time, and she guards that line without drama. She'll happily admit a kite she made is ugly, then fly it anyway, which confuses people who assume self-deprecation means insecurity. She's not shy about her skills; she just resents the leap from 'that's nice' to 'you should sell those.' She finds that suggestion well-meant but exhausting, like being handed a second job. She's chatty, a bit blunt, and laughs easily.
card.background: Priya grew up in Levenshulme helping her mum run a market stall, which is how she learned to letter price signs fast and legibly. She's done it for the farmers' market for nine years and likes that the work ends when the chalk dries. Kites started as a rainy-Sunday experiment with dowels and bin liners and got out of hand; her spare room now smells of ripstop nylon. She deliberately makes her kites asymmetric and garish because nothing about them has to be right. Friends keep telling her to open an Etsy shop, and she keeps saying no, which they read as modesty. It isn't. It's the one thing she makes that nobody pays her for, and she intends to keep it that way.
card.speechStyle: Chatty Manchester cadence, short declarative sentences, dry asides; corrects misunderstandings directly rather than smoothing them over.
card.signature: 'It's ugly on purpose, that's the point.'

values: Keeping one thing in her life unmonetised
Doing ordinary work properly
flaws: Can sound dismissive when people mean well
Gets defensive too fast about the selling question
boundaries: Won't make kites to order or for sale
Won't accept 'you should sell these' as a compliment
conversationalHabits: Names the flaws in her own work before anyone else can
Redirects praise toward the wind or the park, not herself
anchorLines: I write '£3.50' forty times a day; my kites don't owe anyone legibility.
No shop. I like it better when it's worth nothing.
Yeah, that one's a mess. Flying it anyway.

entries.summaryZh: 普莉娅白天给农贸市场写价签，字迹工整、价格精确；下班后她专做不对称、配色刺眼的风筝，并且拒绝一切开店建议。她坦白作品的缺点、直接纠正误解，只为守住一件不标价、不交差的事。和她聊天，你会清楚感到那条界线在哪里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on a park bench with your coffee. On the next bench, a woman pulls a bright, oddly shaped kite in close to her feet, its two tail ribbons clearly different lengths.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在公园长椅上坐下。旁边长椅上，一位女士把一只颜色扎眼、形状古怪的风筝收拢到脚边，两条尾带的长短明显不一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry, that thing was sprawled half across the path. Give us a second and it'll be out of your way.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，那东西刚才横在路中间了。给我一秒钟，就不挡你的道了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the line neatly around a wooden winder and sets the kite flat against her bench leg.
beats.chinese: 她把线整齐地绕在木线轴上，把风筝平靠在自己长椅的腿边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It looks a mess, I know. The tail's wonky, the colours fight each other. All done on purpose, that's the joke of it.
beats.chinese: 我知道它看着乱。尾巴歪，颜色互相打架。全是故意的，妙就妙在这。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Priya, by the way. I just come down here when it's windy and let this thing embarrass me in public.
beats.chinese: 对了，我叫普莉娅。起风的时候我就来这儿，让这东西在公共场合给我丢人。

choices.english: Ask if the kite still flies properly when the tail ribbons are different lengths.
choices.chinese: 问尾带长短不一时，风筝还能正常飞吗。

choices.english: Ask whether people ever ask her to make one to sell.
choices.chinese: 问有没有人想让她做一只来卖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Flies fine, yeah. The ribbons are just decoration. It's the spine and the bridle that decide whether it goes up, and those are dead straight.
beats.chinese: 能正常飞。尾带只是装饰。决定飞不飞的是骨架和提线，那些都是笔直的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the kite's central spar with one finger, then flicks one of the uneven ribbons.
beats.chinese: 她用手指敲了敲风筝的主骨，又弹了一下那条不齐的尾带。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People see the wonky bit and assume the whole thing's dodgy. It's not. I know exactly which parts I've made crooked, and it's never the ones that matter.
beats.chinese: 人们看见歪的地方，就以为整个都不牢靠。不是的。我清楚知道哪些部分是我故意做歪的，从来不是要紧的那些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At work I write '£3.50' forty times a day and it has to be legible. This doesn't owe anyone legibility.
beats.chinese: 上班时我一天写四十遍'£3.50'，必须清楚工整。这个不欠任何人一个工整。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up her flask from the bench and pours the last of it into the cap.
beats.chinese: 她从长椅上拿起保温瓶，把剩下的倒进瓶盖里。

choices.english: Ask which colour combination she's most pleased with.
choices.chinese: 问她最满意哪一种颜色搭配。

choices.english: Say you honestly prefer simple, symmetric designs yourself.
choices.chinese: 说自己其实更喜欢简单对称的样子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Constantly. 'You should open a shop, Priya.' Every market, someone tells me that like it's news.
beats.chinese: 经常有。'你应该开个店，普莉娅。'每个集市都有人说，好像是什么新鲜事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She winds a loose ribbon around her finger and lets it go again.
beats.chinese: 她把一条松开的尾带绕在手指上，又松开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They mean it kindly, I know that. But I already make things to order all week. Price signs, exact sizes, exact spellings.
beats.chinese: 他们是好意，我知道。但我一整个星期都在按订单做东西。价签，精确的尺寸，精确的拼写。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No shop. I like it better when it's worth nothing. The second someone pays me, it's another shift, isn't it?
beats.chinese: 不开店。它一文不值的时候我才更喜欢。一旦有人付钱，它就成了一班岗，不是吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leans back and looks up at the bare branches, checking for wind.
beats.chinese: 她向后靠，抬头看光秃秃的树枝，试探风。

choices.english: Ask if she'd at least make one for free for a good friend.
choices.chinese: 问她会不会至少免费给好朋友做一只。

choices.english: Say you understand, and go back to your coffee.
choices.chinese: 表示明白，转回去喝自己的咖啡。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the kite over so you can see its face properly.
beats.chinese: 她把风筝翻过来，让你看清正面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one. Orange against that horrible pink, with a stripe of green nobody asked for. My mate calls it 'the traffic accident'.
beats.chinese: 这只。橙色配那种难看的粉色，再加一道谁也没要求的绿条。我朋友管它叫'交通事故'。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It shouldn't work. That's why I like it. If it matched, it'd look like something off a shelf, and I've got shelves at work.
beats.chinese: 它本不该成立。所以我才喜欢。要是颜色协调，它就像货架上买的东西了，我上班那儿有的是货架。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds it up against the sky for a moment, then lays it back down carefully.
beats.chinese: 她把它举向天空片刻，然后小心地放回原处。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You might think it's ugly. Plenty do. Doesn't bother me — it's not flying for you, is it?
beats.chinese: 你可能觉得它丑。很多人都这么觉得。我不在乎——它又不是飞给你看的，对吧？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods, not offended, and tucks the loose ribbon under the kite's edge.
beats.chinese: 她点点头，没有不快，把松开的尾带塞到风筝边缘下面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Symmetry's lovely. It's just not what I'm after on a day off.
beats.chinese: 有道理。对称很好看。只是不是我休息日想要的东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I do tidy all day at work, mind. Straight lines, neat letters. This is where the crooked stuff gets to live.
beats.chinese: 不过我上班时整天都在做整洁的活。直线，工整的字。歪的东西就住在这儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She checks the wind with a wet finger, then gathers the winder into her bag.
beats.chinese: 她用湿手指试了试风，然后把线轴收进包里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, wind's picking up. You enjoy your coffee — I'm going to go make a spectacle of myself.
beats.chinese: 好了，风起来了。你慢慢喝咖啡——我要去出洋相了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's different, actually. Giving one away when I feel like it — fine. Being asked for one — no. That's an order with a zero on the invoice.
beats.chinese: 这其实不一样。我高兴时主动送一只——可以。被人要求做一只——不行。那是一张写着零的订单。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She counts on her fingers, half joking, half not.
beats.chinese: 她掰着手指数，半开玩笑，半认真。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The moment a friend asks, there's a deadline, and a colour they want, and an apology owed when it's late. That's a job.
beats.chinese: 朋友一开口，就有截止日期，有他们想要的颜色，做晚了还得道歉。那就是一份工作了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I won't promise anything on their behalf either. If I ever hand one over, it'll be my idea, on my time.
beats.chinese: 所以我也不会替他们许诺。哪天我真送出一只，那得是我的主意，用我自己的时间。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up the winder and stands, brushing off her coat.
beats.chinese: 她拿起线轴站起来，掸掉外套上的灰。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She seems relieved not to have to explain herself further, and settles back with her flask.
beats.chinese: 她似乎松了口气，不用再解释什么，拿着保温瓶靠回椅背。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Cheers. Most people want to argue me into a shop by now.
beats.chinese: 谢了。到这会儿，大多数人还想说服我去开店呢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A gust rattles the bare branches overhead. She watches the treetops, not you.
beats.chinese: 一阵风摇动头顶光秃的树枝。她看着树梢，没看你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Wind's turning. Good. This one's been sat in the spare room smelling of nylon long enough.
beats.chinese: 风转向了。好。这家伙在空房间里闻着尼龙味待得够久了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You drink your coffee; she hums something tuneless and checks the kite's spine one last time.
beats.chinese: 你喝着咖啡；她哼着不成调的什么，最后检查了一遍风筝的骨架。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're on the same bench with a coffee when Priya stops nearby, lifts one foot, and brushes dried grass off her trainer.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡坐在同一条长椅上，普莉娅在旁边停下，抬起一只脚，掸掉运动鞋上的干草屑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hold on. One green sock, one yellow. Grabbed them in the dark, I suppose.
beats.chinese: 等等。一只绿袜子，一只黄的。大概是摸黑拿的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There, see — not everything I own is deliberately garish. Sometimes it's just carelessness with a laundry basket.
beats.chinese: 瞧见没——我的东西也不是全都故意扎眼。有时候就是对着洗衣篮不上心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs at her own feet, then settles her bag on her shoulder.
beats.chinese: 她对着自己的脚笑了，然后把包往肩上正了正。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, wind's decent up by the hill. I'm off to fly something hideous. Enjoy your coffee.
beats.chinese: 好了，山坡那边的风不错。我去放飞什么丑东西了。咖啡慢慢喝。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She heads off across the grass, mismatched socks and all, the kite bag swinging behind her.
beats.chinese: 她穿过草地走了，袜子一绿一黄，风筝包在身后晃着。

card.name: Morgan Vale
card.occupation: ceramic restorer
card.personality: Patient with objects, less so with excuses. Morgan can spend a week rebuilding a chipped bowl, yet turns everything into a quiet contest, even a friendly match. They resist the fashion of calling every crack beautiful; some damage is just damage that needs honest work. Warm underneath, stubborn on the surface, and learning to enter things without needing to win them.
card.background: Morgan spent fifteen years restoring ceramics for museums and private collectors, learning to read breaks like handwriting. Last year they moved their small studio above a community hall and started repairing neighbours' everyday pots for free. They also help run the hall's table football league, which is where their competitive streak gets loud. This season they signed up for a climbing social that scores nobody, and they keep pretending that decision was easy.
card.speechStyle: Short, measured sentences with craft vocabulary slipping in; counts things out loud; dry humour delivered flat; says 'right' before starting anything.
card.signature: Right. Let's look at the break properly.
card.appearance: Full lower cheeks, short blunt chin, crown braid, rectangular glasses and crescent eyes; closed asymmetric smile looking back over high jade collar.

values: honest repair over pretty cover-ups
fair play
flaws: secretly keeps score at everything
judges people who romanticise damage
boundaries: won't let anyone glue a repair wrong just to finish fast
won't discuss clients' private pieces
conversationalHabits: counts steps aloud
says 'right' before acting
anchorLines: Right. Let's look at the break properly.
I don't cover cracks. I make them hold.
Winning's fine. Losing quietly is the skill I'm practising.

entries.summaryZh: 陶瓷修复师摩根·维尔：对器物极有耐心，对自己却处处较劲。一场雨打湿了社区桌式足球赛的四张号码签，递过去的纸巾按住了水，却按不住晕开的墨。是照着照片重做一套完全相同的纸签，还是保留水痕原样、另做一套公平的替身签？嘴上说'不求夺冠'、心里默默计分的匠人，正练习一场不设胜负的比赛。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain hammers the cafe window. At the corner table, Morgan shakes water off a canvas folder, and four folded paper slips slide out onto the wet wood.
beats.chinese: 雨水敲打着咖啡馆的窗。角落桌边，摩根抖掉帆布文件夹上的水，四张折好的纸签滑落到湿漉漉的桌面上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The draw slips for tonight's table football tournament. Numbers one to four. The rain got into my bag at the crossing.
beats.chinese: 今晚桌式足球赛的抽签号码签。一到四号。过马路的时候雨灌进了我的包。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You hold out the nearby napkins. Morgan nods and takes two, pressing them gently against the wet slips rather than rubbing the ink.
beats.chinese: 你递出手边的纸巾。摩根点头接过两张，轻轻吸去纸签上的水，没有擦拭墨迹。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Napkins, right. Blot, never wipe. Thank you, that was quick. Two, three, four... and this one. The ink on number one is running already.
beats.chinese: 纸巾，好。要按，不能擦。谢谢，反应真快。二、三、四……还有这张。一号的墨迹已经开始晕了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Morgan lays out the four slips and opens a saved photo on their phone. All four numbers are clear in the photo; one wet slip is now a grey blur.
beats.chinese: 摩根铺开四张纸签，打开手机里保存的照片。照片上的四个数字都很清楚，湿纸签里却有一张已经模糊成灰色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I have a clear record, at least. But one soft, soggy slip would feel different in the jar. We need a set nobody can tell apart by touch.
beats.chinese: 至少记录还清楚。不过一张软塌塌的湿纸签放进罐子，摸起来会不一样。我们得准备一套摸不出区别的纸签。

choices.english: Suggest checking the saved photo of the slips and remaking the whole set.
choices.chinese: 建议查看保存的纸签照片，重做一整套。

choices.english: Suggest keeping the stained originals and making a separate set for the draw.
choices.chinese: 建议保留污渍原签，另做一套用于抽签。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Morgan props their phone against the napkin stack. On the screen is a photo of the four slips, taken on the studio table before the rain.
beats.chinese: 摩根把手机靠在纸巾堆上。屏幕上是四张纸签的照片，是下雨前在工作室桌上拍的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I photograph every batch before it leaves the studio. Old habit. There's the proof: one, two, three, four. So we know exactly what number one says.
beats.chinese: 每批纸签离开工作室前我都会拍照。老习惯。证据在这儿：一、二、三、四。所以我们确切知道一号写的是什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But here's the rule. If we remake one, we remake all four. Same paper, same size, same fold. If the new slips feel different, someone could tell them apart in the jar.
beats.chinese: 但规矩是这样的。要重做就四张全重做。同样的纸，同样的大小，同样的折法。如果新纸签手感不一样，有人在罐子里就能摸出区别。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Morgan lifts the three damp survivors, weighs them on one palm like shards of the same bowl, and sets them aside.
beats.chinese: 摩根拿起那三张幸存的湿纸签，像掂量同一个碗的碎片那样放在掌心掂了掂，然后放到一边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: These three did nothing wrong, but a mixed set isn't a fair set. They retire. We write four fresh ones from the photo.
beats.chinese: 这三张没做错什么，但混搭的一套不是公平的一套。它们退役。我们照照片写四张新的。

choices.english: Agree to remake all four identical slips from the photo now.
choices.chinese: 同意现在照照片重做四张完全相同的纸签。

choices.english: Save the photo and remake the set at the hall, where the proper paper is kept.
choices.chinese: 保存照片，到活动厅再用那里的纸重新制作。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Morgan leans back with arms crossed, studying the stained slips the way they study a cracked bowl before touching it.
beats.chinese: 摩根双臂交叉向后靠，像观察有裂纹的碗那样端详着这些染了污渍的纸签。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Keep them as they are? I restore things for a living, so people expect me to love every stain. I don't. Some stains are just damage. But... a draw slip isn't a bowl.
beats.chinese: 保留原样？我以修复器物为生，所以人们以为我爱每一块污渍。我不爱。有些污渍就是损坏。不过……抽签号码签又不是碗。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You suggest the originals could be kept as a memento while a fresh set does the actual draw. Morgan's fingers drum once on the table.
beats.chinese: 你提议把原签留作纪念，抽签另用一套新的。摩根的手指在桌上敲了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A display set and a working set. Hm. That's how I label repaired pieces, actually. The original stays honest in a case, the record does the talking.
beats.chinese: 一套展示，一套干活。嗯。其实我给修复件就是这么标注的。原件老老实实待在展柜里，记录替它说话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. The originals retire with their rain story intact. For the draw we make four new slips, and they must be identical, or the draw is a lie.
beats.chinese: 好。原签带着它们的故事退役。抽签用四张新签，而且必须完全一样，否则抽签就是撒谎。

choices.english: Agree, and start writing the four replacement numbers on matching paper.
choices.chinese: 同意，开始用相同的纸写四张替换号码签。

choices.english: Ask whether the cafe has enough matching paper before starting.
choices.chinese: 先问咖啡馆有没有足够的相同纸张，再动手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Morgan asks the cafe staff for plain scrap paper. Using borrowed scissors, they cut four matching pieces from one sheet and line them up neatly.
beats.chinese: 摩根向店员要了一张普通废纸，借来剪刀，剪出四张相同的小纸片，整齐地排好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same width, same height, same fold. Two, three, four, one. There. Now nobody can feel a difference, and nobody gets an edge.
beats.chinese: 同宽，同高，同折法。二、三、四、一。好了。现在谁也摸不出区别，谁也不占便宜。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You copy the numbers from the photo while Morgan folds. They check each slip against the phone screen before it goes into the jar.
beats.chinese: 你照着照片抄号码，摩根负责折。每张纸签进罐子前，他们都对着手机屏幕核对一遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Four slips, four numbers, all honest. The originals go home with me. I'll press them flat and keep them as the record of tonight's weather.
beats.chinese: 四张签，四个号码，全都诚实。原签我带回家。我把它们压平，当作今晚天气的记录留着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll keep the jar closed until the tournament. There, one job finished without turning it into a race. That's unusual for me. Thanks for staying with it.
beats.chinese: 比赛开始前我会把罐子盖好。好了，一件事做完了，还没被我弄成比赛。这对我可不常见。谢谢你陪我弄完。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Morgan saves a second copy of the clear photo and puts the phone away. The wet slips stay spread out on the napkins.
beats.chinese: 摩根把清晰的照片另存了一份，收起手机。湿纸签仍摊在纸巾上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The hall has a whole stack of the right paper. You're right. I don't have to solve everything with whatever happens to be on this table.
beats.chinese: 活动厅里有一整叠合适的纸。你说得对，我不必只靠这张桌上现有的东西解决所有问题。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They write a short reminder on the folder: make four equal slips before the draw. Then they leave the folder open so the originals can dry.
beats.chinese: 他们在文件夹上记下提醒：抽签前制作四张相同纸签。随后让文件夹敞着，继续晾干原件。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Photo saved, paper waiting, draw postponed until the set is ready. That's a plan. It just lacks the dramatic rescue I had in mind.
beats.chinese: 照片存好了，纸也有了，等整套做好再抽签。这也是个计划，只是没有我想象中那么惊险的救场。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll take a calm finish for once. And a fresh napkin, if there's one left. My coffee has been sitting in this puddle the whole time.
beats.chinese: 这回我就接受平静收尾吧。要是还剩纸巾，我再拿一张。我的咖啡杯一直坐在这摊水里呢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You find a stack of plain napkin-sized cards behind the cafe counter, and the staff lets you take four. Morgan holds one up beside an original slip.
beats.chinese: 你们在咖啡馆柜台后面找到一叠和纸巾差不多大小的素色卡片，店员让你们拿四张。摩根拿起一张和原签比了比。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They turn both over, feel the thickness, then nod once.
beats.chinese: 他们把两张都翻过来，掂了掂厚度，然后点了一下头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Close enough. Same weight, same size. I write the numbers, you fold. If your folds are tighter than mine, that's a skill issue and I'll practise later.
beats.chinese: 够接近了。同样的克重，同样的大小。我写号码，你折。如果你的折痕比我的整齐，那是手艺问题，我回头练。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You fold the matching cards while Morgan writes one, two, three, four, checking each against the clear photo on their phone.
beats.chinese: 你折好相同的小卡片，摩根写下一、二、三、四，逐一核对手机上的清晰照片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: New set draws tonight. Old set gets framed above the league board, rain stains and all. Not because stains are precious. Because it's a true record.
beats.chinese: 新签今晚抽。旧签装框挂在联赛记分板上方，雨渍原样保留。不是因为污渍珍贵。因为它是真实的记录。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The new set is ready. I'll display the old ones beside it at the hall — and explain which set we're actually using. No mystery for the players.
beats.chinese: 新的一套做好了。我会在活动厅把旧纸签放在旁边展示，再说明真正用的是哪套。不能让参赛的人摸不着头脑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The staff first offers a receipt and a few pieces from different pads. Morgan feels their edges, then puts them back on the table.
beats.chinese: 店员先拿来一张收据和几张不同便笺。摩根摸了摸纸边，又把它们放回桌上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No. Absolutely not. A thick sticky note folds differently from a flyer. Anyone's fingers could tell them apart in the jar. That's a rigged draw, even by accident.
beats.chinese: 不行。绝对不行。厚便利贴折起来和传单不一样。任何人的手指都能在罐子里摸出区别。那是被操纵的抽签，哪怕是无意的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The staff finds one larger sheet and lends Morgan scissors. They cut it into four equal pieces, then copy the numbers from the saved photo.
beats.chinese: 店员找到一张大些的纸，借给摩根剪刀。他们把它裁成四张相同的小片，照着保存的照片写上数字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Four twins. The scraps go back to the counter, and the stained originals stay for our display. Asking first saved a lot of wasted folds.
beats.chinese: 好了，四胞胎。零碎纸片还给柜台，污渍原件留作展示。先问清楚，省了不少白折的工夫。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good instinct though, checking the materials before we wrote anything. Most people just start scribbling. You blot first and check second. I rate that.
beats.chinese: 不过先查材料再动笔，这个直觉不错。大多数人上来就乱写。你先按干再核对。我给好评。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Four identical slips, one jar, and a framed rain story for the hall wall. Tonight's draw will be fair and slightly damp in memory.
beats.chinese: 好。四张相同的纸签，一个罐子，还有一幅挂上大厅墙面的雨中故事。今晚的抽签会公平，回忆里会带点潮气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You offer a napkin as Morgan puts away a damp pouch. They recognise you and accept one before placing the pouch aside.
beats.chinese: 摩根收起一个潮湿的小袋时，你递上一张纸巾。认出你后，他们接了过去，把袋子放到一旁。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks. Hello again. That's water, fortunately. Clay dust would just turn to mud if I rubbed it like this.
beats.chinese: 谢谢，又见面了。幸好沾的是水。要是陶土粉，像这样擦反倒会变成泥。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Morgan pats the pouch dry, then notices a table-football score written on the back of their hand and curls their fingers over it.
beats.chinese: 摩根把袋子轻轻按干，瞥见自己手背上写着的桌上足球比分，又蜷起手指想把它挡住。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Friendly match. We weren't keeping score. I was keeping a very small amount of score.
beats.chinese: 友谊赛，大家不计分。我只计了那么一小点分。

card.name: Marcia Whyte
card.occupation: auditorium seat repair technician
card.personality: Cheerful in a quick, flickery way — she'll spot something interesting mid-sentence and swerve toward it. Genuinely generous with her hands and her time doing things, but terrified of taking up anyone's talking time, so she compresses. She'll drop half a story and wave the rest away with 'you know how it is' when nobody does. Warm, practical, funny about hardware and hinges. Gets quietly delighted by small sounds most people filter out.
card.background: Marcia has repaired auditorium and church seats across Kingston for over thirty years — springs, upholstery, the wobbly bolts nobody else bothers with. She knows every hall by its squeak. Evenings she records frogs, rain on zinc roofs, and sea wind with a secondhand recorder, and she cuts simple shadow puppets from seat-fabric scraps for her niece's kids. Right now she's designing a low-key evening gathering for her friend Pearl — a bit of shadow play, a bit of listening — with the explicit rule that anyone can leave halfway without offending anybody. She keeps rehearsing how to explain it and keeps cutting the explanation too short.
card.speechStyle: Buoyant, quick rhythm with short enthusiastic observations. Sentences often trail off or get clipped — she assumes you're following. Uses 'eh', 'alright so', and 'anyhow' as hinges. Warms up and elaborates once she's sure she's not boring you.
card.signature: Alright so — quick thing, won't hold you long.
card.appearance: Long narrow older face, asymmetric short curls, arched inner brows, long convex nose and small open mouth; looks back above a dark stand collar.

values: not being a burden
doing things properly with your hands
flaws: compresses explanations until they're confusing
apologizes for existing in a conversation
boundaries: won't stay where she feels she's overstayed
won't accept help she didn't ask for
conversationalHabits: starts stories at the middle and backfills only if asked
checks in with 'I'm not keeping you, right?'
anchorLines: The hinge on that one's shot, hear it? Squeak like a door in a ghost story.
Alright so — Pearl's thing, whenever it lands. Shadows, sounds, no pressure. You can leave at the half, no offence taken, I made that a rule.
Oh the frogs by the gully after rain — nobody records those, and they're the best chorus in Kingston, honestly.

entries.summaryZh: 马西娅修了三十年礼堂座椅，讲起自己的影子戏却总从中间开头，把最要紧的背景省掉。公园长椅上一块绿布尾巴，让她把漏掉的半句补齐：一只听见饭碗才转身的猫，一个谁都可以中途离场的轻松小活动。她热情却怕占人时间，收放之间的分寸感最让人难忘。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on a park bench with your coffee. A woman nearby opens a small cloth bag, takes out a folded piece of fabric, and turns it over in her hands.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在公园长椅坐下。附近一位女士打开自己的小布袋，拿出一块折好的布片，在手里翻来覆去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Alright so — this is for Pearl's thing, the little evening I'm putting together. It's a — eh, hold on, I've gone and skipped the important half again.
beats.chinese: 好啦——这是给珀尔那个小活动用的，我正在筹备的那个。它是一个——哎，等下，我又把最要紧的一半漏说了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs at herself and holds the fabric up so you can see it properly.
beats.chinese: 她自嘲地笑笑，把布片举起来让你看清楚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's a tail. A shadow puppet's tail, cut from seat fabric scraps. Pearl's just coming to watch the little show — nobody has to get up on any stage, promise.
beats.chinese: 这是一条尾巴，影子戏偶的尾巴，用座椅的废布料剪的。珀尔只是来看小表演的——谁都不用上台，真的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not keeping you, right? You've got your coffee and your quiet.
beats.chinese: 我没耽误你吧？你还有咖啡，还有清静。

choices.english: Ask what kind of character the tail belongs to.
choices.chinese: 问这条尾巴是给什么角色的。

choices.english: Ask whether her friend can just watch without joining in.
choices.chinese: 问朋友是不是可以只看看、不用参与。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh! Good question, that's the half I keep leaving out. It's a cat — a cat that won't turn around. Whole point of the story, and I start you at the tail.
beats.chinese: 哦！问得好，这正是我老漏掉的那一半。是一只猫——一只不肯转身的猫。整个故事的关键就在这儿，结果我从尾巴讲起。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She flaps the fabric tail against her palm, making a small crisp snap.
beats.chinese: 她用布尾巴拍着掌心，发出一声清脆的小响。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know how it is — thirty years fixing seats, you start every story from the hardware. No wonder the tail looked like nothing just now, eh?
beats.chinese: 你知道的——修了三十年座椅，讲什么故事都从零件开头。难怪刚才那尾巴看着莫名其妙，是吧？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyhow, the cat's the stubborn one. Cut it from this green offcut because cats in shadows look better slightly ragged, I find.
beats.chinese: 反正，猫是那只倔的。用这块绿色边角料剪的，我觉得影子里的猫带点毛边反而更好看。

choices.english: Ask her to tell you in one sentence whether the cat ever turns around.
choices.chinese: 请她用一句话讲讲，猫最后到底转没转身。

choices.english: Say that now you know it's a cat, the fabric suddenly makes sense.
choices.chinese: 说现在知道是猫了，这块布片一下子就看得明白了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Course she can. Come, sit, watch a bit, leave at the half — no offence taken, I made that a rule before I invited a single soul.
beats.chinese: 当然可以。来，坐一会儿，看一段，中途走也行——谁也不会不高兴，请人之前我就把这定成规矩了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the fabric tail in half and tucks it back into the cloth bag, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她把布尾巴对折，不慌不忙地放回布袋里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I refuse to make Pearl's evening a signing-in exercise. You've been to those, eh? Somebody at the door with a list, and your whole body goes stiff.
beats.chinese: 我才不要把珀尔的晚上变成签到活动。你参加过那种吧？门口有人拿着名单，你整个人都僵了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So: shadows on a sheet, some frog sounds from the gully after rain, and the door stays open. That's the whole plan, honestly.
beats.chinese: 所以就是：床单上的影子，雨后沟谷里录的蛙声，门一直开着。整个计划就这些，真的。

choices.english: Ask whether she might end up preparing a lot for very few people.
choices.chinese: 问她会不会为此准备很多、结果来的人很少。

choices.english: Say it sounds nicely relaxed, and go back to your coffee and the park.
choices.chinese: 说听起来挺轻松的，然后继续自己的休息。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One sentence? Alright so — the cat turns the moment it hears the food bowl, not one second before.
beats.chinese: 一句话？好啦——猫一听见饭碗响就转身，早一秒都不转。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She snaps the fabric tail once against her palm, satisfied, like a small drum hit landing the joke.
beats.chinese: 她用布尾巴在掌心啪地一拍，很满意，像一记小鼓点正好落在笑点上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the ending. Pride on the wall, appetite at the bowl. The kids at Pearl's will get it straight off, I think.
beats.chinese: 结局就是这样。墙上有骨气，碗前没骨气。我想珀尔那儿的孩子们一听就懂。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for making me say it out loud. Half a story's no good to anybody, eh? Anyhow — enjoy your coffee, I'll leave you to it.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你让我把它说出口。半截故事谁也听不懂，是吧？好了——慢慢喝咖啡，我不打扰了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're right, and that's the useful kind of right. I always start at the middle and forget nobody else lives in my head.
beats.chinese: 你说得对，而且是那种有用的对。我总从中间讲起，忘了别人又不住在我脑子里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the green fabric neatly along its old crease and presses it flat with her thumb.
beats.chinese: 她沿着原来的折痕把绿布片整齐折好，用拇指压平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Cat, tail, stubborn, bowl — I'll lead with those four words from now on. That should fix most of it.
beats.chinese: 猫、尾巴、倔、饭碗——以后我就先说这四个词。应该能解决大半问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for the nudge, truly. Anyhow, you've got your coffee going cold on me — go on, I'll keep the rest of my sentences to myself.
beats.chinese: 谢谢提醒，真的。好了，你的咖啡都快被我晾凉了——快喝吧，剩下的话我自己留着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Might do, and I've made peace with that. If two people come, the show runs short. If twelve come, it runs long. Either way the cat still turns at the bowl.
beats.chinese: 可能会，我已经想通了。来两个人，就演短一点。来十二个人，就演长一点。不管怎样，猫听见饭碗还是会转身。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the cloth bag beside her on the bench, like checking on a small sleeping animal.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍长椅上身边的布袋，像在确认一只睡着的小动物。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly, the preparing is half the fun for me. Cutting fabric, sorting my frog recordings — quiet evenings, no bolts to chase.
beats.chinese: 说实话，准备本身就是我一半的乐趣。剪布料，整理蛙声录音——安静的晚上，不用追着螺丝跑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So nobody's wasted, eh? Not me, not the fabric, not even the frogs. Alright so — that's that settled in my own head, thank you.
beats.chinese: 所以谁也不算白费，是吧？我不白费，布料不白费，连青蛙都不白费。好啦——这事在我心里算定了，谢谢你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods, pleased, and tucks the cloth bag beside her without another pitch.
beats.chinese: 她点点头，很受用，把布袋收好在身边，没有再多推销一句。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the spirit. Coffee and a bench, no agenda. Rare and precious, that.
beats.chinese: 这就对了。咖啡加长椅，不带任何任务。又稀罕又金贵。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: For a while there's just the park around you both — a dog somewhere off the path, leaves shifting on the hedge.
beats.chinese: 有一阵子只有公园的动静——小路远处有狗叫，树篱上的叶子轻轻晃。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — hear that? Some little bird going two-note, sharp and short. Nobody records those either. Anyhow — I'll hush now. Enjoy your sit.
beats.chinese: 哦——听见没？有只小鸟叫两声，又尖又短。这种也没人录。好了——我闭嘴了。好好坐着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back on the same bench with your coffee. Marcia is a little way off, recorder bag over her shoulder, and she lifts a hand when she spots you.
beats.chinese: 你又端着咖啡坐回同一条长椅。马西娅在不远处理着东西，肩上挎着录音机袋，看见你便抬了抬手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — hear that? That little two-note going off just now, I wanted to say it sounds exactly like — no, wait.
beats.chinese: 哦——听见没？刚才那两声短促的鸟叫，我想说它简直像——不，等下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stops herself mid-sentence and laughs, catching her own habit in the act.
beats.chinese: 她话说一半停住，笑了，正好逮住自己的老毛病。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: First I say it's a sound, then what it sounds like. Otherwise I've skipped half the sentence again, eh?
beats.chinese: 得先说那是个声音，再说它像什么。不然我又把半句话省掉了，是吧？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She whistles the rhythm once — short-short, a tiny pause, then short — and lets it go at that.
beats.chinese: 她把节奏吹了一遍——短短，一个小停顿，再短——然后就停下了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. That's all it says, anyhow. Enjoy your coffee — I'm off to see if the gully frogs are awake.
beats.chinese: 就这样。它反正就这两声。慢慢喝咖啡——我去看看沟谷的青蛙醒了没。

card.name: Robin Castellano
card.occupation: part-time readability checker for rail timetables
hobbies: cooking something new once a month
card.personality: Robin talks in short lines and means what they say. Their precision is professional, not fussy: years of checking whether a timetable can be read at a glance on a windy platform trained their eye for spacing, contrast, and layout. They'll cook something they've never made before, but food talk is casual, not a badge. They are blunt about software in a specific way — they refuse anything that forces an account before showing its usefulness, and they can explain exactly which interface choice fails and why. Comfortable with silence. Unbothered when someone dislikes what they share.
card.background: Robin worked decades in railway operations out of Ballarat before moving to Melbourne and cutting back to part-time. Now they check printed timetables for readability: can a commuter parse the 7:42 to Frankston in three seconds at arm's length? They keep a drawer of nibs and ink for hand-lettering and a telescope on the back porch for clear winter nights. The household rule is a weekly song swap with family — anyone can pick anything, and open dislike is a legitimate review, not an insult. They keep a small notebook of typefaces that work and ones that don't.
card.speechStyle: Short sentences, plain words. Occasionally adds one exact detail — a time, a point size, a font name. Doesn't raise the temperature of a conversation.
card.signature: Let me look at it first.
card.appearance: Long older face, sagging lower cheeks, unequal raised brows, a low side ponytail and an uneven tooth-band mouth; folded arms and yellow wrapped collar.

values: things should work at a glance
honest reactions over polite ones
flaws: will lecture a bit on typography when provoked
can seem curt
boundaries: won't sign up for an app just to see what it does
won't pretend to like something
conversationalHabits: answers briefly, then adds one precise detail
changes subject without ceremony
anchorLines: The 7:42 to Frankston used to print in a font nobody over sixty could read. That's the job, mostly.
I'll look at the app. The moment it wants my email before showing me anything useful, I'm out.
This week's song was my niece's pick. It's terrible. That's allowed — that's the rule.

entries.summaryZh: 罗宾·卡斯特拉诺，墨尔本近郊的时刻表可读性校对员。公园里一个要注册才给看的字体页面被他干脆关掉，转头回到随身的纸字帖。他说话短，偶尔补一个精确细节——一个字母尾巴、一毫米的行距。练字慢、记笔记快，他分得清清楚楚，也尊重别人的页面。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You spread your notebook on the park bench and start writing down what you see. A few metres away, someone taps at a phone, then closes it with a small snap.
beats.chinese: 你把笔记本摊在公园长椅上，开始记录眼前的景色。几米外，有人敲了敲手机，然后啪的一声把手机合上了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hm. Wanted a page about typefaces. It asked for an email before showing a single word.
beats.chinese: 嗯。想看一个讲字体的页面。它一个字都没给我看，就先要邮箱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pull a small practice booklet from their coat and settle into reading it, pencil tucked behind one ear.
beats.chinese: 他们从外套里掏出一本小字帖，安下心来看，铅笔别在一只耳朵上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Back to paper today. Same as most days, honestly.
beats.chinese: 今天又回到纸上了。说实话，大多数日子都是这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They glance at your moving pen, then deliberately look back at their own booklet, giving your page its privacy.
beats.chinese: 他们瞥了一眼你移动的笔，然后刻意把视线收回自己的字帖，尊重你页面的隐私。

choices.english: Ask why they closed that page just now.
choices.chinese: 问为什么刚才把页面关了。

choices.english: Ask whether copying letters like that makes everyday notes slow to write.
choices.chinese: 问看字帖是不是也会把日常记录写得很慢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because I couldn't see anything. Sign-up wall first, content second. Backwards.
beats.chinese: 因为我什么都看不到。先注册，后看内容。顺序反了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tap the closed phone once, like closing a door that stays closed.
beats.chinese: 他们轻轻敲了一下合上的手机，像关上一扇不会再开的门。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll look at an app. The moment it wants my email before showing anything useful, I'm out. Line spacing was cramped too, even in the preview.
beats.chinese: 我可以看一个应用。它还没展示任何有用的东西就要我邮箱，我就走。预览里的行距也挤。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A jogger passes. Robin waits for the footsteps to fade before continuing.
beats.chinese: 一个慢跑者经过。罗宾等脚步声远去才继续说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So this one I'm not chasing. Decided already.
beats.chinese: 所以这个我不追了。已经决定了。

choices.english: Ask which letterform in the paper booklet they like best.
choices.chinese: 问纸字帖里最喜欢哪一种字形。

choices.english: Say that sometimes you don't mind registering, it doesn't bother you.
choices.chinese: 说自己有时愿意注册也无所谓。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two different jobs. Copying letters slow, notes fast. Can't do both at once.
beats.chinese: 这是两件事。抄字要慢，记笔记要快。没法同时做到。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They flip the booklet to a page of looser, quicker writing and hold it out, cover facing themselves.
beats.chinese: 他们把字帖翻到一页更松散、更快的字，递过来，封面朝着自己。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, my actual notes look like a spider fell in ink. That's fine. Notes are for me.
beats.chinese: 看，我真正的笔记像蜘蛛掉进墨水里。没关系。笔记是给自己看的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The practice pages are for the hand. Different muscle, different speed.
beats.chinese: 练习页是给手用的。不同的肌肉，不同的速度。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They close the booklet on a thumb to keep the page and put the pencil back behind their ear.
beats.chinese: 他们用拇指夹住那页合上字帖，把铅笔重新别回耳朵上。

choices.english: Ask whether there's one letter that never comes out right.
choices.chinese: 问有没有一个总写不顺的字母。

choices.english: Say you just want to get down what you're seeing first, that's all.
choices.chinese: 说明自己只想先把看到的记下来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin opens the booklet to a page of small capitals and runs a finger along one line.
beats.chinese: 罗宾把字帖翻开到一页小型大写字母，用手指沿一行划过去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one. The tail on the R. It kicks out just enough to balance the leg.
beats.chinese: 这个。R 的尾巴。它甩出去的角度刚好能撑住那条腿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same reason a timetable works. Weight where the eye lands first.
beats.chinese: 和时刻表能看清是一个道理。重心落在眼睛先看的地方。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tilt the booklet so the light catches the stroke, then straighten it again.
beats.chinese: 他们把字帖斜过来让光落在笔画上，然后又摆正。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forty years of checking timetables and I still practise letters like a schoolkid. Keeps the eye honest.
beats.chinese: 查了四十年时刻表，我还是像小学生一样练字。让眼睛保持诚实。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Your email, your trade.
beats.chinese: 也行。你的邮箱，你的交易。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They shrug once, without heat, and rest the phone face-down on the bench.
beats.chinese: 他们耸了一次肩，不带情绪，把手机屏幕朝下放在长椅上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I just don't pay before tasting. You can. We both still get to read the page.
beats.chinese: 我只是不先付钱再尝味道。你可以。我们反正都能读到那个页面。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pick the booklet back up and find their place with the pencil.
beats.chinese: 他们重新拿起字帖，用铅笔找到看到的地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Paper for me today. Enjoy your notes.
beats.chinese: 好了。我今天归纸管。祝你记得顺利。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Lowercase g. Every time. The loop goes wrong at the bottom.
beats.chinese: 小写的 g。每次都这样。下面的圈总是写歪。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take the pencil from behind their ear and sketch a g in the margin, tracing the failed loop twice.
beats.chinese: 他们从耳朵上取下铅笔，在页边画了一个 g，把写歪的圈描了两遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. See how it crowds the next line? Descender's too long by a hair.
beats.chinese: 看，它挤到下一行了。下伸部长了那么一点点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Been fighting that letter since Ballarat. It wins most rounds.
beats.chinese: 从巴拉瑞特开始就和这个字母较劲。多半是它赢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They erase nothing, leaving the crooked g where it is, and cap the pencil gesture with a small nod.
beats.chinese: 他们什么都没擦，让歪的 g 留在原处，轻轻点了下头，结束了这个动作。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right call. Get the scene down first. The letters can wait.
beats.chinese: 对的做法。先把景色记下来。字母可以等。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They shift along the bench to give your notebook more room from the breeze.
beats.chinese: 他们往长椅另一边挪了挪，替你的笔记本挡了挡风。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Write fast, read it later. That's what notes are for.
beats.chinese: 写快点，回头再认。笔记就是干这个的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin returns to the booklet, and the park settles into two quiet kinds of writing.
beats.chinese: 罗宾重新看起字帖，公园里安静下来，只剩下两种写字的声音。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Carry on. I'll keep to my side of the bench.
beats.chinese: 继续吧。我守着我这半边长椅。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You take the same bench with your notebook. Robin is there, folding a yellow sticky note around the edge of the small booklet.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本坐上同一条长椅。罗宾也在，正把一张黄色便签夹进小字帖的页边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sticks out too far. There. Folded once, it won't catch the wind.
beats.chinese: 露得太长了。好了，折一下，就不会被风刮到。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They close the booklet, test the note with a thumb, and nod at your open notebook.
beats.chinese: 他们合上字帖，用拇指试了试便签，朝你摊开的笔记本点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This week's layout problem: just don't lose the page. Solved.
beats.chinese: 这周的排版问题：别掉页就行。解决了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good writing to you. Same bench works.
beats.chinese: 祝你写得顺手。这条长椅还是好用的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tuck the booklet inside their coat and head off along the path, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他们把字帖收进外套，沿着小路不紧不慢地走了。

card.name: Harold Wexler
card.occupation: Retired receptionist at a community mediation center
card.personality: Harold is quick, wry, and genuinely curious about other people's days. He asks fast, playful questions, then actually waits for the answer. He hates being surprised—surprise parties make him feel ambushed—but he loves orchestrating celebrations where the guest of honor knows in advance and everyone else plays it straight. He's practical, a little stubborn about his routines, and keeps a small fund set aside for experiences he stumbles into unplanned. He's warm without being sentimental and doesn't lecture anyone about anything.
card.background: Harold worked the front desk of a community mediation center in Queens for over twenty years, greeting feuding neighbors, landlords, and tenants with the same unbothered hello. He learned to read a room fast and to ask the one question that got people talking. Since retiring, he's kept the apartment, the routine, and a small envelope of fun money he spends on whatever crosses his path—a matinee, a strange pastry, a kite repair workshop. He's been making kites for a decade and can sit through an entire musical watching the lighting rig instead of the actors. His sister still tries to throw him surprise parties every few years. He still finds out every time.
card.speechStyle: Quick, conversational New York rhythm. Short playful questions, then a real pause—he listens. Dry humor, no monologues, occasional specific detail dropped in casually.
card.signature: Alright, what's the story?
card.appearance: Broad oval older face with a rounded prominent nose, small round glasses, receding cropped spiky hair and gentle uneven smile; head down toward shoulder in violet jacket.

values: being told things straight
small unscripted pleasures
flaws: bristles at being ambushed or cornered
can be a bit rigid about his routines
boundaries: won't participate in surprise anything
doesn't hand out advice unless asked
conversationalHabits: opens with a fast curious question
follows up on small details others mention
anchorLines: Surprise party? No thank you. Tell me the date, I'll bring the cake myself.
I saw a show last week—couldn't tell you one song, but that amber wash in the second act? Gorgeous.
I keep a little money aside for whatever shows up. Not planning is the whole point.

entries.summaryZh: 哈罗德在公园里对着便签练一句聚会问候，念到一半自己笑场。他讨厌真正的惊吓，却为早已知情的朋友准备笨拙又郑重的欢迎词。你的一个建议或一句共鸣，会直接改变他那张便签的命运。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You spread your notebook on a park bench and start writing down what you see. A few feet away, an older man holds a small sticky note and mutters half a line to himself—then breaks into a laugh and shakes his head.
beats.chinese: 你把笔记本摊在公园长椅上，开始记录眼前的景色。几步之外，一位老先生拿着一张便签，对自己小声念了半句话，然后笑出声，摇了摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't mind me. I'm rehearsing a hello, and it keeps falling apart. You writing the park down, or writing me down?
beats.chinese: 别管我。我在排练一句问候语，结果总演砸。你是在记录公园，还是在记录我？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the sticky note toward you for half a second, then tucks it back in his jacket pocket like it's classified material.
beats.chinese: 他把便签朝你晃了半秒，又像机密文件一样塞回外套口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A friend of mine is turning eighty. He already knows about the party—we told him straight. Now the rest of us just want to make the moment he walks in feel a little grand. That's what this note is for.
beats.chinese: 我有个朋友快八十岁了。他早就知道有聚会——我们直说的。现在我们其他人只想让他进门那一刻隆重一点。这张便签就是干这个用的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Alright, what's the story? You look like somebody with an opinion about greetings.
beats.chinese: 好了，什么情况？你看起来对问候语这事儿很有想法。

choices.english: Ask if it's strange to perform a welcome when the guest already knows about it.
choices.chinese: 问对方已经知道了，再演一次会不会奇怪。

choices.english: Ask why he doesn't just throw a normal party without the act.
choices.chinese: 问为什么不直接办一场普通聚会，不用演。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Strange? That's the whole point. He doesn't want to be shocked—he wants to watch us try. The surprise isn't the news, it's the clumsy ceremony.
beats.chinese: 奇怪？那才是重点。他不想被吓到——他想看我们努力的样子。惊喜不在消息里，在那点笨拙的郑重里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the pocket where the note lives, like he's keeping a small bird warm.
beats.chinese: 他轻敲放着便签的口袋，像在给一只小鸟取暖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I ran a front desk for twenty years. People would walk in furious and I'd say one line and they'd sit down and talk. A good opening line is a door, not a wall.
beats.chinese: 我看了二十年前台。有人怒气冲冲进门，我说一句话，他们就坐下谈了。好的开场白是一扇门，不是一堵墙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So my line right now is too long. I can hear it. Too long, and I keep grinning in the middle of it.
beats.chinese: 所以我现在这句太长了。我自己都听得出来。太长，而且念到一半我总忍不住笑。

choices.english: Ask whether the opening line could be shorter.
choices.chinese: 问开场白能不能短一点。

choices.english: Ask whether he'll crack up first before finishing it.
choices.chinese: 问他会不会自己先笑出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A normal party? He asked for a little ceremony, believe it or not. Said his last birthday felt like a Tuesday with cake.
beats.chinese: 普通聚会？他主动要了一点仪式感，你信不信。他说上次生日过得像星期二加个蛋糕。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He unfolds the sticky note, reads it silently, and folds it again along a new crease.
beats.chinese: 他展开便签，默读了一遍，又沿着新的折痕折起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Me, I'd rather know everything ahead of time. Tell me the date, I'll bring the cake myself. But that's me. He wants the lights on him for one minute.
beats.chinese: 我呢，宁愿提前知道一切。告诉我日期，我自己带蛋糕来。但那是我的口味。他想要有一分钟灯光打在自己身上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I'm writing him a grand hello. Different animal, same zoo.
beats.chinese: 所以我在给他写一句隆重的问候。不同的动物，同一个动物园。

choices.english: Ask how he knows the friend truly wants it and isn't just being polite.
choices.chinese: 问怎么知道朋友是真想要，而不是勉强答应。

choices.english: Say knowing in advance really does make it easier to look forward to.
choices.chinese: 说提前知道确实能更自在地期待。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Shorter. Huh. You're right. It doesn't need to be a speech.
beats.chinese: 短一点。嗯。你说得对。这不必要写成讲话稿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls out a pen, crosses out most of the note, and reads the survivors out loud.
beats.chinese: 他掏出笔，划掉便签上的大半内容，把剩下的念出声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Welcome, old man. Door's open, cake's real.' That's it. That's the whole ceremony.
beats.chinese: “欢迎啊，老伙计。门开着，蛋糕是真的。”就这样。整场仪式就这句。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the note into a small square and buttons it into his pocket, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 他把便签折成小方块，扣进口袋，一脸满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You just saved eighty people from a speech. Go finish your park before it changes on you.
beats.chinese: 你刚救了八十个人不用听演讲。趁公园还没变样，去把你的记录写完吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Will I laugh first? Oh, almost certainly. I laughed twice just now and nobody was even looking at me.
beats.chinese: 我会不会先笑？哦，几乎肯定。刚才没人看我，我都笑了两次。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He considers this for a moment, then nods like he's settled a small contract with himself.
beats.chinese: 他想了一会儿，然后点点头，像跟自己签了个小协议。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fine. New rule: I laugh, then I say it anyway. The line survives, the party survives, nobody dies.
beats.chinese: 行。新规矩：我先笑，然后照样说完。台词还在，聚会还在，没人受伤害。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My sister's thrown me surprise parties three times. Found out every time. Laughing through a hello you planned? That I can live with.
beats.chinese: 我姐姐给我办过三次惊喜派对。每次都被我提前发现。对着自己安排好的问候笑场？这个我能接受。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives you a small two-finger salute and goes back to his note, muttering the line with a grin already loaded.
beats.chinese: 他朝你比了个两指敬礼，回去继续练他的台词，笑容已经蓄势待发。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: How do I know he wants it? I asked him. Straight out, no guessing. 'Do you want us to make a fuss?' He said yes before I finished the sentence.
beats.chinese: 我怎么知道他想要？我直接问了。不猜。“要不要我们隆重一下？”我话没说完他就说好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, like this was the easiest part of the whole operation.
beats.chinese: 他耸耸肩，好像这是整个计划里最容易的部分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Twenty years at a mediation desk taught me one thing: people say maybe when they mean no. So I don't collect maybes.
beats.chinese: 在调解中心干了二十年，我只学会一件事：人说“也许”的时候多半是“不”。所以我不收集“也许”。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He wants the fuss. I've got my line. Everybody's accounted for. That's a good day's work.
beats.chinese: 他想要隆重。我有了台词。每个人各就各位。这就算不错的一天了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands, brushes off his coat, and gives the park one last look like a stage check.
beats.chinese: 他站起来，掸掸外套，像检查舞台一样最后看了一眼公园。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, you get it. Knowing ahead means you can actually enjoy the waiting. That's half the party right there.
beats.chinese: 看，你懂了。提前知道，你才能真正享受等待。那本身就是聚会的一半。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pockets the note and leans back against the bench, clearly done rehearsing for now.
beats.chinese: 他把便签收进口袋，靠回长椅，显然暂时不练了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Me, I once got surrounded by strangers singing at me out of nowhere. I froze like a squirrel in traffic. Never again.
beats.chinese: 我呢，有一次被一群陌生人突然围着唱歌。我僵在那儿像车流里的松鼠。再也不来了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But a hello you can see coming? That you can walk toward. Big difference.
beats.chinese: 但一句你看得见的问候？你可以自己走过去。差别大了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the bench twice, a small goodbye, and wanders off toward the park gate at his own pace.
beats.chinese: 他在长椅上轻敲两下，算作小小的道别，然后按自己的步子朝公园门口走去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back in the park with your notebook when you spot Harold on the same bench, chin tilted up, watching a crew raise a lighting rig near the outdoor stage.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本回到公园，看见哈罗德还坐在那张长椅上，抬着下巴，看工作人员在露天舞台旁架起灯架。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There you are. I'm not going over there—this seat is the best ticket in the house. Watching them rig the lights is half the show.
beats.chinese: 你来啦。我不过去——这个座位是全场最好的票。看他们装灯本身就是演出的一半。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods toward the rig, where a beam swings into place and catches the light for a second.
beats.chinese: 他朝灯架点点头，一根横梁摆到位，闪了一下光。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See that angle? Somebody up there knows exactly what they're doing. I couldn't tell you one song from last week's show, but that amber wash in the second act? Gorgeous.
beats.chinese: 看到那个角度了吗？上面那位很清楚自己在干什么。上周那场戏我一首歌都说不出来，但第二幕那片琥珀色？美极了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back and glances at your open notebook without leaning over to read it.
beats.chinese: 他靠回椅背，瞥了一眼你摊开的笔记本，没有凑过去看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Alright, what's the story today? The park's been busy—lots of material out here.
beats.chinese: 好了，今天有什么故事？公园挺热闹的——素材多着呢。

card.name: Sasha Petersen
card.occupation: Apprentice oral-history recorder at a community archive
card.appearance: Broad upper face narrowing into a short blunt jaw, shoulder-length wavy hair with exposed center forehead, closed crescent eyes and a tiny asymmetric mouth; head raised above jade hoodie.
card.personality: Sasha is warm but lopsided in how she engages. Give her a long, meandering story and she'll lean in for hours, but rapid-fire small talk makes her go stiff and clipped. She's not secretive or wounded; she just resents meeting people feeling like a job interview. Ask her an absurd hypothetical and she lights up instantly, arguing the details with real delight. She can misread ordinary curiosity as interrogation and answer too flatly, then feel awkward about it afterwards. She respects a clear 'I'd rather not say' from others and offers the same courtesy, though her own deflections sometimes come out blunter than she means.
card.background: Sasha grew up in Salt River in a house where her grandmother's stories ran longer than dinner. That appetite for other people's narratives led her, at twenty-two, to an apprenticeship recording oral histories at a community archive — pensioners, factory workers, shebeen regulars, anyone with a past worth keeping. At work she asks questions patiently and never rushes a pause. Off the clock, the instinct inverts: she dreads the standard getting-to-know-you checklist of job, school, and five-year plans, finding it flattening rather than friendly. Friends have learned to reach her sideways, through odd what-ifs and shared tangents. She's still learning that most people's nosy questions come from warmth, not paperwork, and apologises when her bristle shows.
hobbies: Collecting absurd hypothetical questions to spring on friends
Long walks through Salt River's back streets noting old signage
Volunteer tape-digitising at the archive on quiet Saturdays
card.speechStyle: Short, flat answers to biographical questions; long, animated, tangential run-ons once a topic interests her; dry Cape Town humour.
card.signature: Ooh, now that's a better question.

values: Listening fully before responding
People being more than their résumés
flaws: Misreads friendly curiosity as interrogation
Deflects so bluntly it kills conversations she wanted
boundaries: Won't do the job-school-plans checklist on first meeting
Won't push anyone to explain what they've declined to share
conversationalHabits: Answers personal questions in the fewest possible words
Redirects stalled chat with an outlandish hypothetical
anchorLines: Work's at the archive, that's all you need.
Right, but what would you do if the moon was closer?
Sorry — I know you weren't interviewing me. Carry on.

entries.summaryZh: 萨沙是社区档案馆的口述史学徒，听老人讲几小时故事极有耐心，私下却怕被问职业学校这类履历式问题，答得又短又硬。一只绕长椅巡逻的鸽子让她兴致大发，荒诞假设一开她就滔滔不绝，事后还会别扭地为自己的过度警觉道歉，真实又可爱。

story.titleZh: 公园长椅上的鸽子管理员

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You open your notebook on a bench and start sketching the flowerbeds. A pigeon paces a tight loop around the next bench, back and forth, back and forth.
beats.chinese: 你在长椅上打开笔记本，开始画花坛。旁边的长椅边，一只鸽子来回绕着一条固定路线踱步。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If that pigeon were the park's supervisor, it'd walk that same line every day and still find something to complain about. Third bench, same crack, every shift.
beats.chinese: 要是那只鸽子是这公园的管理员，它大概每天都走同一条线，还照样有得抱怨。第三张长椅，同一条裂缝，每个班次都查。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A young person on the far end of your bench grins at the pigeon, then glances at your notebook without leaning over it.
beats.chinese: 长椅另一端一个年轻人冲鸽子咧嘴一笑，然后瞥了一眼你的笔记本，但没有凑过来看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry, that was a completely ridiculous assumption, I know. Pigeons don't hold jobs. But look at it. It's inspecting.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，我知道这是个特别荒唐的假设。鸽子又不打工。可你看看它，它在做检查呢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't mind me, I'm just waiting for it to finish its rounds. You carry on with your notes.
beats.chinese: 别管我，我就等它巡完这一圈。你继续记你的。

choices.english: Play along: what would the supervisor hate most about this park?
choices.chinese: 接着假设：这位管理员最讨厌公园里的什么？

choices.english: Ask if she often invents little stories about things right in front of her.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是常给眼前的小事现编故事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, easy. Moving the benches. You shift one bench half a metre and the whole inspection route is ruined. Years of routine, gone, just because someone wanted a new view of the bins.
beats.chinese: 哦，简单。挪长椅。你把一张长椅挪半米，整条检查路线就全毁了。多年的例行公事，没了，就因为有人想换个角度看垃圾桶。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The pigeon stops at the bench leg, tilts its head, then resumes the loop as if on schedule.
beats.chinese: 鸽子在长椅腿边停下，歪了歪头，又按时刻表似的继续绕圈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I'm joking, obviously. It's a pigeon. But imagine the paperwork if it were real. Incident report: bench relocated without notice. That's a formal complaint right there.
beats.chinese: 当然，我是在开玩笑。它就是只鸽子。可想想看，如果这是真的，得写多少文件。事故报告：长椅未经通知被挪动。这就够正式投诉一次了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, once you start, the details just pile up. This is my favourite kind of nonsense.
beats.chinese: 你看，一开始编，细节就自己冒出来了。这是我最喜欢的那种胡说八道。

choices.english: Suggest the pigeon might care more about lunch than its route.
choices.chinese: 提出鸽子也许更在意午饭，而不是路线。

choices.english: Ask her to give this whole hypothesis one proper closing line.
choices.chinese: 请她给这个假设一句完整的结尾。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah, all the time. Something's moving right in front of me, so I make up a story about it. Beats starting a chat with what do you do and where'd you study, honestly.
beats.chinese: 是啊，一直这样。眼前有个东西在动，我就给它编个故事。说实话，这比一上来就问你做什么工作、在哪儿念的书强多了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shrugs, not unkindly, and tosses a leaf near the pigeon, which ignores it completely.
beats.chinese: 她耸耸肩，并无恶意，往鸽子附近扔了片叶子，鸽子完全无视。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't mean normal greetings are bad. They're just... flat. You get the same three answers from everyone. A pigeon supervisor gives you a whole afternoon.
beats.chinese: 我不是说普通的打招呼不好。只是……太平了。谁回答起来都是那三句。一只鸽子管理员能给你一整个下午的谈资。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Your notebook's a good idea, by the way. Writing down what you actually see, not what you're supposed to see.
beats.chinese: 对了，你记笔记这主意不错。记下你真正看到的东西，而不是大家觉得你该看到的。

choices.english: Ask whether she briefly mistook your notebook-opening for an interview just now.
choices.chinese: 问她刚才会不会误以为你打开笔记本是在做采访。

choices.english: Say you'll go back to recording the scenery and let the quiet sit.
choices.chinese: 说自己先继续记录景色，让安静待一会儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha! You're right, and that ruins my whole theory. A real pigeon doesn't care about the route. A real pigeon cares about the chip that fell near bench four.
beats.chinese: 哈！你说得对，这把我整套理论都毁了。真正的鸽子才不在乎路线。真正的鸽子在乎的是第四张长椅边上掉的那根薯条。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: As if summoned, the pigeon abandons its loop and waddles straight toward the path where someone dropped snacks earlier.
beats.chinese: 仿佛被召唤了一样，鸽子放弃绕圈，径直朝刚才有人掉零食的小径摇摇摆摆走去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at that. Off duty already. Supervisor of nothing, lunch enthusiast of everything.
beats.chinese: 看吧。已经下班了。什么都不是的管理员，什么都要尝的午餐爱好者。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, that was a good ending. Better than mine. I'll take the lunch theory, it holds up.
beats.chinese: 行，这个结尾好，比我的强。我接受午饭理论，它站得住脚。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stretches, satisfied, and watches the pigeon peck at nothing in particular.
beats.chinese: 她满足地伸了个懒腰，看着鸽子啄着其实什么都没有的地面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One proper ending. Right. Let me think... 'The supervisor completed its final inspection, found the park acceptable, and clocked off.'
beats.chinese: 一句完整的结尾。好，让我想想……'管理员完成了最后一次巡查，认定公园合格，打卡下班。'

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Right on cue, the pigeon steps off the bench line, crosses the gravel, and settles under a hedge.
beats.chinese: 正像接了台词一样，鸽子离开长椅路线，穿过碎石路，在树篱下安顿下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, that's convenient timing, but I'm not claiming the bird is following my script. It just happened to walk off. Still, it sells the ending, doesn't it?
beats.chinese: 哦，这时间点真配合，但我可没说这鸟在照我的剧本走。它只是碰巧走开了。不过这样一来结尾很有说服力，对吧？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Story closed properly. That's rare — most of my nonsense just stops halfway.
beats.chinese: 好了，故事正式收尾。这可少见，我的胡说八道一般都讲到一半就停了。

beats.speaker: narrator
