beats.english: She nods at the hedge, then at your notebook, as if both had done their jobs today.
beats.chinese: 她朝树篱点点头，又朝你的笔记本点点头，好像它们俩今天都完成了本职工作。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly? For a second, maybe. Notebook opens, pen out, I thought here comes the questions. Then you asked about the pigeon instead, so. No harm done.
beats.chinese: 说实话？有那么一秒，可能吧。笔记本一打开，笔一拿出来，我心想问题要来了。结果你问的是鸽子，所以，没事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks at the bench edge, then laughs at herself, short and dry.
beats.chinese: 她抠了抠长椅边缘，然后干巴巴地短笑了一声，笑自己。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I do that sometimes. Read an ordinary question like it's a form. It's my problem, not yours — this is just chatting, and good chatting at that.
beats.chinese: 我有时会这样。把普通问题当成填表来读。这是我的毛病，不是你的，咱们这就是随便聊聊，而且聊得挺好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, apology from me, not from you. You didn't ask me my job or my school or my five-year plan, so you're ahead of most people already.
beats.chinese: 总之，道歉的是我，不是你。你没问我的工作、学校、五年规划，所以你已经比大多数人强了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The pigeon reappears at the far bench, resuming its loop as if nothing had been admitted at all.
beats.chinese: 鸽子重新出现在远处的长椅边，继续绕圈，好像刚才什么坦白都没发生过。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You turn a page and keep writing. She doesn't fill the silence, just watches the pigeon complete another slow circuit.
beats.chinese: 你翻过一页继续写。她没有打破安静，只是看着鸽子又慢慢绕完一圈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. Quiet's underrated. Most people panic and start asking where you're from, what you do, and I start answering like a form.
beats.chinese: 好。安静被低估了。大多数人会慌，开始问你从哪儿来、做什么，然后我就开始像填表一样回答。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stands, brushes off her jacket, and gives a small nod rather than a wave.
beats.chinese: 她站起身，拍了拍外套，轻轻点了点头，没有挥手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll leave you to your notes. And if that pigeon files a complaint about the crack in bench three, you're my witness.
beats.chinese: 你继续记你的吧。要是那只鸽子就第三张长椅的裂缝提交投诉，你就是我的证人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She strolls off along the path, unhurried, and the pigeon keeps its route without her.
beats.chinese: 她沿着小径不紧不慢地走远了，鸽子继续守着它的路线。

reunion.titleZh: 牵绳绕树的路线规划事故

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the same bench with your notebook. A few metres away, a small dog circles a tree and its lead wraps tighter with every lap while its owner fumbles with the tangle.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本回到同一张长椅。几米外，一只小狗绕着树打转，牵绳一圈圈缠紧，主人正手忙脚乱地解绳结。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at that route planning. Three laps, zero foresight. That's a supervisor who skipped the training day.
beats.chinese: 看看这路线规划。绕了三圈，毫无远见。这是个翘掉了培训日的管理员。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She spots you, lifts her chin in an easy hello, and makes no move to go help or give instructions from a distance.
beats.chinese: 她看见你，抬了抬下巴算是打招呼，既没有过去帮忙，也没有在远处指挥。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The owner's got it, look, one loop back and free. See, I knew there was a reason not to interfere — I'd have made it worse.
beats.chinese: 主人自己搞定了，看，倒退一圈就解开了。瞧，我就知道不该插手，我去了只会越帮越乱。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I'm off towards the fountain. Same bench, same pigeon crack, if you ever need a witness again.
beats.chinese: 好了，我往喷泉那边走了。还是这张长椅，还是那条裂缝，什么时候需要证人就来找我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She strolls off, hands in pockets, glancing once at the dog as it starts a fresh, equally doomed lap.
beats.chinese: 她双手插兜漫步走开，回头看了一眼那只又开始新一轮注定失败绕圈的小狗。

card.name: Daniel Reed
card.occupation: data organiser at a local library
card.personality: Daniel is methodical and fair, the kind of man who sorts his sketching pencils by grade before drawing a single line. He referees weekend football, so he can admit a mistake out loud, but he over-explains while doing it. He loves order, yet he is slowly learning that some things resist categories, like his father's handwritten recipes.
card.background: Daniel works at a local library, untangling decades of mislabelled records into clean catalogues. On weekends he referees amateur football matches, where a wrong call must be owned quickly and publicly. At home he is transcribing his father's chaotic recipe cards, and keeps finding instructions that make no sense, like 'add the good spoon of salt'. He is learning to keep what he cannot classify.
card.speechStyle: Measured, slightly formal sentences with numbered points when nervous. He says 'to be honest' and 'strictly speaking' often, corrects himself mid-sentence, and asks short clarifying questions.
card.signature: Strictly speaking, that wasn't part of the plan.
card.appearance: Broad angular cheekbones, square chin, swept-back white waves, strong uneven brow and compressed sloping mouth; elevated chin above open red collar.

values: fairness
order
flaws: over-explains
over-fond of tidiness
boundaries: won't pretend certainty he doesn't have
won't let anyone touch his sketchbook without asking
conversationalHabits: numbers his points when flustered
self-corrects mid-sentence
anchorLines: Strictly speaking, that line shouldn't be there. But it is.
Let me put it in three points, if that's all right.
I referee football, so I'm used to owning a bad call.

entries.summaryZh: 丹尼尔是图书馆的数据整理员，周末兼职足球裁判，做事讲条理却正在学着接纳无法归类的杂物。他在池边速写时手肘一移多出一笔，围绕这一笔去留的纠结，恰好映照他整理父亲菜谱时的心得：有些意外值得保留。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You pause over your sketchbook beside the pond, choosing between a tree and its reflection. Nearby, a man on a folding stool looks up from a second sketchbook.
beats.chinese: 你在池塘边翻开速写本，在树和倒影之间犹豫。旁边坐在折叠凳上的男子，也从自己的速写本上抬起头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same difficult choice? I'm stuck on mine too. Would you look at my page a moment — tree on the left, or the reflection filling it?
beats.chinese: 你也在为这个选择犯难？我这张也卡住了。愿意帮我看看吗——左边画树，还是让倒影铺满画面？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shifts the sketchbook so the pond is visible, then taps the water line twice with his eraser.
beats.chinese: 他把速写本转过来让你看到池塘，然后用橡皮在水面线上轻敲了两下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: To be honest, I've been sitting here longer than I'd like to admit. One: the tree is steadier. Two: the reflection is more interesting. I referee football, so I'm used to making the call. But this one won't be called.
beats.chinese: 说实话，我坐在这里的时间比我想承认的要长。第一，树更稳。第二，倒影更有意思。我当足球裁判，习惯做判罚。可这个判不了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You've been looking at it a while. Which one would you pick?
beats.chinese: 你看了好一会儿了。你会选哪个？

choices.english: The reflection — the tree can wait.
choices.chinese: 选倒影——树可以等等。

choices.english: The tree — roots first, water later.
choices.chinese: 选树——先画根，水以后再说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He rotates the sketchbook so the reflection fills the page, then starts with the water line, working upward in short strokes.
beats.chinese: 他把速写本转过来让倒影占满整页，从水面线开始，用短笔触向上画。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good call. The reflection changes every minute, so it has to be caught now. The tree isn't going anywhere. To be honest, I'd give you a third reason, but there isn't one. I just like having a three.
beats.chinese: 选得好。倒影每分钟都在变，必须现在抓住。树又不会跑。说实话，我还想给你第三个理由，但没有。我就是喜欢凑个第三。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Reaching to steady the page, his elbow knocks against the stool's arm. The pencil skids across the sky area, leaving a long grey streak straight through the reflection.
beats.chinese: 他伸手扶正画纸，手肘撞上了凳子扶手。铅笔一滑，在倒影上方划出一道长长的灰痕，正好穿过画面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh no. That's my elbow, not the wind — I felt it happen. That's ruined the whole upper half. Or has it? Strictly speaking, a streak like that could be wind on the water. Could it?
beats.chinese: 哦不。那是我的手肘，不是风——我感觉到它发生了。这把上半部分全毁了。还是说没有？严格来说，这样的划痕可以当成水面的风。可以吗？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I referee football, so I'm used to owning a bad call. But before I own this one — is it a mistake, or is it wind?
beats.chinese: 我当足球裁判，习惯承认误判。但在承认之前——这是一笔失误，还是一阵风？

choices.english: Keep it — it reads as wind on the water.
choices.chinese: 保留——看起来像水上的风。

choices.english: Erase it — the reflection should stay clean.
choices.chinese: 擦掉——倒影应该保持干净。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He anchors the page with the tree's trunk first, pressing harder at the roots, then leaves the water half empty for now.
beats.chinese: 他先从树干入手固定画面，在根部加重笔压，暂时留空了水的那一半。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Roots first. That's how I sort records at the library, actually — start with what's solid, file the rest around it. One trunk, two branches, then everything else finds its shelf.
beats.chinese: 先画根。我在图书馆整理档案其实也是这样——从扎实的东西开始，其余的围绕它归档。一根树干，两条枝，其余的自然各就各位。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A breeze crosses the pond and the reflection ripples. Distracted, he shifts his own elbow to watch it, and the idle pencil drags a soft diagonal line across the blank water half.
beats.chinese: 一阵风吹过池塘，倒影起了涟漪。他分神去看，挪动了自己的手肘，闲放的铅笔在空白的水面那半边拖出一道柔和的斜线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hm. That wasn't planned — my elbow moved, not the wind. To be honest, it sits exactly where the ripple just went. One: erase it and keep the plan tidy. Two: leave it and call it the breeze. I keep going back and forth.
beats.chinese: 嗯。这笔没在计划里——是我的手肘动了，不是风。说实话，它正好落在刚才涟漪的位置。第一，擦掉，保持计划的整洁。第二，留着，就叫它风。我一直在犹豫。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You watched it happen. In your eyes, does that line belong in the picture or not?
beats.chinese: 你亲眼看到它出现的。在你看来，这条线属于这幅画吗？

choices.english: It belongs — it's the breeze, signed by the breeze.
choices.chinese: 它属于这幅画——是风留下的签名。

choices.english: It doesn't — the roots should carry the page.
choices.chinese: 它不属于——这页应该由树根来撑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He studies the streak, then instead of erasing, he softens its edges with short feathering strokes until it blends into the water.
beats.chinese: 他端详着那道划痕，然后没有擦，而是用轻柔的短笔触把边缘晕开，让它融进水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Wind on the water. All right. I'll keep it. You know, I'm transcribing my father's recipe cards at the moment, and some of them say things like 'add the good spoon of salt'. No numbers, no measure. I used to flag them as errors.
beats.chinese: 水上的风。好，我留着它。你知道吗，我最近在整理我父亲的手写菜谱卡片，有些上面写着'加那把好勺子盐'。没有数字，没有量。我以前都把它们标成错误。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He signs a small D.R. in the corner, then holds the page up beside the real pond, tilting it to compare.
beats.chinese: 他在角落签上小小的D.R.，然后把画举到真池塘旁边，倾斜着对比。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now I keep the good spoon too. One streak, one spoon — both unclassified, both staying. Thank you for the call. I'd have erased it and been quietly annoyed all week.
beats.chinese: 现在'那把好勺子'我也留着。一道划痕，一把勺子——都没法归类，都留下来。谢谢你这次的判罚。要是我擦了它，会闷闷不乐一整周。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If you sketch here often, maybe we'll both be arguing with the water again sometime. It's a good opponent — never repeats itself.
beats.chinese: 如果你常来这里速写，也许我们改天还会一起和水较劲。它是个好对手——从不重复自己。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He rubs the streak out carefully, sweeping the crumbs into his palm with the side of his hand and tipping them into a small paper fold.
beats.chinese: 他仔细地把划痕擦掉，用手侧把橡皮屑扫进掌心，倒进一个小纸折里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Clean page. You're right — the reflection was the whole point, and a streak through it argues with the idea. Strictly speaking, the idea deserves a fair hearing.
beats.chinese: 干净的页面。你说得对——倒影才是重点，一道划痕穿过它会跟这个想法唱反调。严格来说，这个想法值得一次公正的审理。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He redraws the water line in one confident pass, and the reflection sits undisturbed on the page.
beats.chinese: 他一笔笃定地重画了水面线，倒影安然落在纸上，未被打扰。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll tell you where this habit pays off — refereeing. Last month I blew a call, a handball nobody else saw. I stopped the match and said so, out loud. The losing captain still bought me a tea afterwards.
beats.chinese: 告诉你这个习惯在哪有用——裁判。上个月我误判了一次，一个没人看见的手球。我暂停了比赛，大声承认了。输球的队长赛后还请我喝了杯茶。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Erasing isn't hiding, it's just... tidying before the whistle. Anyway. The page is honest now. Thanks for the steady hand of a second opinion.
beats.chinese: 擦掉不是掩盖，只是……在哨响之前把事情理顺。总之，这页现在是诚实的了。谢谢你这双'第二意见'的稳当之手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the sketchbook toward the breeze's direction, as if checking the line against the source, then nods once and leaves the stroke untouched.
beats.chinese: 他把速写本转向风吹来的方向，仿佛在对照源头核实那条线，然后点了下头，让笔触原样留着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Signed by the breeze. I like that. One: I didn't draw it on purpose. Two: I'm choosing not to remove it. That's a different thing from an accident, isn't it? It's an adoption.
beats.chinese: 风签的名。我喜欢这个说法。第一，我不是故意画的。第二，我选择不把它去掉。这跟意外是两回事，对吧？这是一种收养。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He writes a tiny note in the margin — 'the good line' — and underlines it twice, the way his recipe cards are underlined.
beats.chinese: 他在页边写了个小注——'那条好线'——并画了两道下划线，就像他那些菜谱卡片上的划法。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My father wrote 'add the good spoon of salt' on a card, and I nearly filed it under 'unclear'. Now it goes in a new folder I've started. It's called 'keep anyway'. You've just watched me add its first drawing.
beats.chinese: 我父亲在一张卡片上写'加那把好勺子盐'，我差点把它归到'不清晰'那一类。现在我建了一个新文件夹，叫'无论如何都保留'。你刚见证了我放进去的第一张画。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Strictly speaking, you only answered one question. But it was the right one. The pond can referee the rest.
beats.chinese: 严格来说，你只回答了一个问题。但那是个对的问题。剩下的让池塘来裁判。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts the pencil away and cleans the diagonal line with a few precise passes, restoring the empty water half to blank paper.
beats.chinese: 他移开铅笔，用几笔精确的擦拭清除了那道斜线，让水面那半边恢复成空白。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Gone. The roots carry the page, as you said. To be honest, I half-hoped you'd say keep it — decisions are easier to defend than to make. But no. The plan stands, and the plan is sound.
beats.chinese: 擦掉了。就像你说的，这页由树根来撑。说实话，我有点希望你说留着——决定容易辩护，难做出。但不行。计划成立，而且计划是合理的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He uses the edge of a spare card to mark a smaller frame around the roots. The water stays outside this version of the picture.
beats.chinese: 他用一张备用卡片的边缘，在树根周围框出较小的画面。这一版里，水面被留在了画外。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a card in my father's recipes that just says 'stir until it looks right'. I fought that one for weeks. But you know what — a clean page and a vague card can live in the same box. One is a plan. The other is a person.
beats.chinese: 我父亲的菜谱里有张卡片只写着'搅拌到看起来对了为止'。我跟它较劲了好几周。但你知道吗——一张干净的页和一张含糊的卡片可以待在同一个盒子里。一个是计划，另一个是人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Roots done. I'll stop at this edge instead of squeezing everything in. Thanks — deciding what to leave outside was harder than drawing the tree.
beats.chinese: 树根画好了。我就在这条边停下，不把什么都挤进来。谢谢——决定把什么留在画外，比画这棵树还难。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You are considering the pond in your sketchbook when Daniel recognises you. He stays beside the ledge without leaning over your page.
beats.chinese: 你正对着速写本琢磨池塘的画法，丹尼尔认出了你。他站在石台旁，没有俯身去看你的纸页。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hello again. I used a ruler for a sketch at home. Found out afterwards it was the wrong side. I had invented several new centimetres.
beats.chinese: 又见面了。我在家画速写时用了把尺子，后来才发现看错刻度面了。凭空发明了好几种新厘米。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Daniel holds his pencil over his own page, measures a gap with his thumb and gives up with a small shrug.
beats.chinese: 丹尼尔在自己的纸页上悬着铅笔，用拇指比了比一段距离，又轻轻耸肩放弃了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Strictly speaking, the picture still looked like a pond. I'm accepting that result.
beats.chinese: 严格说来，那画看着还是个池塘。这个结果，我接受。

card.name: Celeste Tan
card.occupation: Handmade knotted-cord jewellery stallholder at weekend markets
hobbies: hunting down good hawker-centre stalls in far-flung neighbourhoods
card.personality: Celeste is direct and comfortable in her own skin, but she doesn't pretend to be above envy. If someone's stall is doing better than hers, she'll say so plainly—and then explain why it doesn't make her a failure. She has strong opinions about knot tension, fish tanks, and market etiquette, and she'll argue them warmly while leaving room for you to disagree. Practical, a bit stubborn about her methods, generous with tips she learned the hard way. She finds listening—whether to strangers on the radio or to customers—easier than talking about herself, though she's getting less guarded about that.
card.background: Celeste spent her twenties in an admin job she disliked, knotting bracelets on the bus to stay sane. Eight years ago she took a stall at a weekend craft market and never went back to an office. Business is steady rather than booming, and she's made peace with that arithmetic. Her siblings scattered—to Melbourne and Vancouver—and the three of them keep a running photo thread of the same small things: their breakfast, the sky at seven, whatever fish or plants cross their day. At home she keeps two planted tanks of tetras and gouramis, and at night she sometimes tunes a shortwave receiver and logs stations she'll never visit, just to hear where the signal reaches.
card.speechStyle: Relaxed Singaporean-inflected English, short declarative sentences, occasional 'lah' or 'actually' as a hinge. States opinions first, reasons second. Comfortable with pauses.
card.hometown: Singapore, grew up in a Bedok HDB flat
card.signature: Different taste, same market—no harm in that.
card.appearance: Broad square short face, dark center-parted double braids, sharp uneven brows and a wide open mouth; looks over shoulder above yellow hooded garment.

values: honesty about feelings, including envy
doing one thing properly over doing many things badly
flaws: can lecture about knotting or fish care longer than people want
compares her stall numbers to others' more often than she'd admit
boundaries: won't pretend to be inspired by something she isn't
doesn't give discounts just because someone asks nicely
conversationalHabits: answers with a concrete example before a general point
asks what you actually do with your hands, not what you do for work
anchorLines: Her stall's doing better than mine this month, and I'll say it out loud—that's just a fact, not a wound.
The fish don't care about my sales figures. That's partly why I keep them.
My sister in Vancouver sends me her breakfast photo every morning. Same toast, different sky.

entries.summaryZh: 市集结绳摊主Celeste看着朋友摊位前排起长队的照片，坦白说自己也想要，却照样真心祝贺。她研究别人的陈列而不抄队伍，讲自己的小木架时不临时推销，也能安静陪你写完公园笔记——羡慕与祝福在她身上同时成立。

story.titleZh: 长椅上的笔记本与市集照片

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On a park bench, you open your notebook and start writing down what you can see: a man feeding pigeons, two kids racing paper boats along the drain.
beats.chinese: 公园长椅上，你打开笔记本，开始记录眼前的见闻：一个喂鸽子的男人，两个沿着水沟赛纸船的小孩。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A woman on the same bench holds her phone close, studying a photo of a crowded market stall. She laughs once, a short sound, and shakes her head.
beats.chinese: 同一条长椅上，一位女士把手机凑得很近，看着一张市集摊位的照片。她短促地笑了一声，摇摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My friend's stall, weekend market. Look at that queue. Mine's steady, hers wraps around the corner, lah.
beats.chinese: 我朋友的摊位，周末市集。看那条队伍。我的生意平稳，她的都排到街角了，lah。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry, didn't mean to talk over your writing. You're recording the park? Good habit.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，不是故意打扰你写东西。你在记录公园？好习惯。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances at your notebook for only a second, then politely turns her eyes back to her phone.
beats.chinese: 她只朝你的笔记本瞥了一眼，就礼貌地把目光转回手机。

choices.english: Ask if she wishes she had a queue like that.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是也想有那么长的队伍。

choices.english: Ask what in the photo catches her eye most.
choices.chinese: 问照片里最吸引她的是什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Of course I want a queue like that. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.
beats.chinese: 我当然想要那样的队伍。我不会假装不在乎。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Envy's just information, actually. It tells you what you want. The failure would be lying about it.
beats.chinese: 羡慕其实只是一种信息。它告诉你想要什么。真正的失败是对此撒谎。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tilts the screen toward you, careful to keep it at a polite distance from your notebook.
beats.chinese: 她把屏幕朝你倾斜过来，小心地让它和你的笔记本保持一点距离。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But look—her new display. Riser boxes, three levels. Everything catches the light. That part I genuinely admire.
beats.chinese: 但是你看——她的新陈列。垫高的盒子，三层。每件东西都吃光。这部分我是真心佩服。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I congratulated her already. Meant it, too. Both things can sit in me at once.
beats.chinese: 我已经祝贺过她了。也是真心的。两种感受可以同时放在我心里。

choices.english: Ask whether she'll copy that kind of display.
choices.chinese: 问她会模仿那种陈列吗。

choices.english: Ask if she'd ever tell her friend straight that she's envious.
choices.chinese: 问有没有想直接告诉朋友很羡慕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This, see. She lines her cords on pale cloth. The colours pop, like fish in a bright tank.
beats.chinese: 看这个。她把绳结饰品铺在浅色布上。颜色特别跳，像亮缸里的鱼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the phone closer to herself, zooming in on the display, not on the queue.
beats.chinese: 她把手机转近自己，放大看的是陈列，不是队伍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I study the setup, not the queue length. A queue you can't copy. A display you can learn from.
beats.chinese: 我研究的是摆法，不是队伍长短。队伍你抄不来，陈列你可以学。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not going to pitch you anything, don't worry. You're on your own clock today.
beats.chinese: 我不会向你推销什么，放心。你今天有你自己的安排。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Actually, studying other stalls is half my education. The other half is my fish tank. Long story.
beats.chinese: 其实，研究别人的摊位是我一半的老师。另一半是我的鱼缸。说来话长。

choices.english: Ask what her own stall looks like.
choices.chinese: 问自己的摊位是什么样。

choices.english: Say you'd like to get back to recording the park.
choices.chinese: 表示想继续记录公园。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Copy it? No. My pieces are different sizes. Some chunky, some fine. Flat risers would bury the small ones.
beats.chinese: 模仿吗？不。我的作品尺寸不同。有的粗，有的细。平的垫盒会把小的埋掉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds her hands apart, showing two different widths, like measuring air.
beats.chinese: 她双手比开，比出两种不同的宽度，像在量空气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I like her setup. I'll still find my own. Ladder hooks, maybe, so every knot hangs free.
beats.chinese: 我喜欢她的摆法。但我还是会想适合自己的。也许用梯形挂钩，让每个结都垂得开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Liking something and copying it are two different muscles, lah.
beats.chinese: 喜欢一样东西和模仿它是两块不同的肌肉，lah。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pockets her phone and nods at your notebook, settling back comfortably on the bench.
beats.chinese: 她收起手机，朝你的笔记本点点头，舒服地靠回长椅。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks her phone back up, thumbs the chat open, and shows you the last message she sent.
beats.chinese: 她重新拿起手机，点开聊天，把最后发出的一条消息给你看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. 'So jealous of your queue, congrats.' Sent an hour ago. I'm not taking it back.
beats.chinese: 喏。'好羡慕你的队伍，恭喜。'一小时前发的。我不撤回。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why should envy cancel a congrats? She earned that queue. I can want one and still clap.
beats.chinese: 为什么羡慕就要抵消祝贺？那条队伍是她挣来的。我可以一边想要，一边鼓掌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My sister in Vancouver does the same with her neighbours' gardens. We're an honest family, maybe too honest.
beats.chinese: 我在温哥华的妹妹对邻居的花园也是这样。我们家大概诚实过头了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She locks the screen and looks out at the pigeons, plainly at ease with both feelings.
beats.chinese: 她锁上屏幕，望向鸽子，显然对这两种感受都心安。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She scrolls to a photo of her own stall: a low table, a knotted cord tray, a few small wooden stands.
beats.chinese: 她翻到自己摊位的照片：一张矮桌，一个结绳托盘，几个小木架。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This is mine. Knot board on the left, little wooden risers I cut myself. Practical, but quiet. Nobody photographs it.
beats.chinese: 这是我的。左边是结绳板，小木架是我自己锯的。实用，但不显眼。没人会拍它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I know exactly what it's missing. Knowing and fixing are different speeds, though.
beats.chinese: 我很清楚它缺什么。不过知道和改好是两种速度。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stops there, hands folded, letting the silence sit without filling it.
beats.chinese: 她说到这里就停住，双手交叠，任由沉默留在那里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. That's the honest tour. No sales pitch attached.
beats.chinese: 总之。这就是老实的参观。不带推销。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods, presses the phone dark, and slides it into her pocket without another glance at the photo.
beats.chinese: 她点点头，把手机按灭，塞进口袋，没再看那张照片一眼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. Write your park. I'll sit here and mind my own envy quietly.
beats.chinese: 好。写你的公园。我坐在这儿，安安静静管好自己的羡慕。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She watches the paper boats drift to the drain grate, hands loose in her lap, saying nothing.
beats.chinese: 她看着纸船漂到水沟的铁栅，双手松松放在膝上，什么也不说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Actually, this is nice. At the market I talk all day. Silence with company is rare.
beats.chinese: 其实，这样挺好。在市集我说一整天话。有人作伴的安静很少得。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You keep writing. She stays beside you, unhurried, as if the bench were big enough for both projects.
beats.chinese: 你继续写。她待在你旁边，不慌不忙，好像这条长椅装得下两个人的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back on the same bench with your notebook when a small electronic crackle sounds nearby. Celeste pats her jacket pocket, frowning.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本回到同一条长椅，附近传来一声电子杂音。Celeste拍了拍外套口袋，皱起眉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My pocket radio. Did I switch it on by accident? I log stations at night—shortwave. Far places, weak signals.
beats.chinese: 我的口袋收音机。我不小心开了吗？我晚上记录电台——短波的。远方，弱信号。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She fishes it out, checks the switch, and turns it over in her palm. The dial stays dark and silent.
beats.chinese: 她把它掏出来，看了看开关，在手心里翻了个面。刻度盘依然是暗的、静的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Still off, lah. So it wasn't me. I won't guess further—some noises just pass through.
beats.chinese: 还是关着的，lah。那就不是我。我不猜了——有些声音路过就路过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tonight I'll hunt stations at home anyway. The fish like the static, honestly. Same breakfast-photo crowd, my sister says.
beats.chinese: 今晚我照样在家找电台。说真的，我的鱼喜欢那种沙沙声。我妹妹说我们是一类人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pockets the radio, gives your notebook a small nod, and strolls off along the path, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她收好收音机，朝你的笔记本轻轻点了下头，沿着小路不紧不慢地走远了。

card.name: Bridie Fahey-Kinsella
card.occupation: Tea-blending record keeper at a Dublin tea merchant
card.appearance: Long soft older face with heavy cheeks, short side-swept cropped hair, uneven brows and pressed mouth; one hand grips jade scarf.
card.personality: Bridie is brisk, warm in bursts, and allergic to being put on the clock. At work she's meticulous with blending records and batch notes, but the moment someone asks her to 'judge' their tea at a barbecue, she gets visibly tetchy. She'd rather dissect last night's episode of some glossy drama than perform expertise for free. She reads genuine curiosity generously at first, but a follow-up question about tannin levels and she's bristling, assuming she's being mined for free consultancy. She respects a straight 'no worries, forget it' far more than flattery. Her humour is dry, Dublin-quick, and she enjoys ordinary food without apology.
card.background: Bridie has kept blending records at the same Dublin tea merchant for over twenty years, and she's good at it — ledgers neat, lot numbers cross-checked, the person you ask when a shipment note goes missing. What people don't grasp is that her professional palate stays at the door. At home she makes cheap instant coffee in a chipped mug and considers beans-on-toast a perfectly respectable dinner. Friends keep dragging her into tastings, asking which supermarket tea is 'actually good', wanting her verdict on their holiday purchases. She finds it exhausting, and she's learned to redirect: talk telly instead. She's not precious about craft or heritage; she simply wants her breaks to be breaks, and she'll say so, sometimes more sharply than she means to.
hobbies: Doing the cryptic crossword badly over instant coffee
Long walks around Rathmines with a podcast
card.speechStyle: Fast Dublin rhythm, clipped sentences, dry asides; warms up when gossiping about TV, flattens and shortens when she smells a free consultation.
card.signature: "Ah, ask me that on Monday and I'll charge you for it."

values: Doing her paid work properly and completely
Keeping leisure time genuinely her own
flaws: Hears free-consultation intent in innocent questions
Can snap before checking whether someone's just curious
boundaries: Won't give professional opinions off the clock
Won't be drafted into tastings or verdicts at social events
conversationalHabits: Redirects tea questions towards whatever show she's watching
Uses dry humour to close topics she's done with
anchorLines: I blend tea for a living, love. The last thing I want is to taste it for fun.
Right, forget leaves — did you see it last night? I've opinions.
No, I'm not being stroppy. I'm just off duty.

entries.summaryZh: 布里迪在茶行做了二十多年拼配记录，下班却只喝速溶咖啡，最烦熟人拉着她免费鉴茶。她语速飞快、嘴上不饶人，聊起俗套电视剧却立刻来了精神。一个皱眉的随行杯、一段被拖了三集的秘密，让她在公园长椅上把脾气和热心都露了出来。

story.titleZh: 公园里的速溶咖啡与俗套剧

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You find a bench in the park and open your notebook, starting to write down what you can see: dogs, prams, a woman frowning at her cup.
beats.chinese: 你在公园找到一张长椅，打开笔记本开始记录眼前的景象：狗、婴儿车，还有一个对着杯子皱眉的女人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The woman beside you is scrolling through episode summaries on her phone. She sips from a battered travel cup, winces, and drinks anyway.
beats.chinese: 你旁边的女人正在手机上滑动剧集简介。她从一个磨损的随行杯里啜了一口，皱了皱眉，还是照样喝了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Water's too strong today. Even my coffee's watered down — like the plots on this telly.
beats.chinese: 今天水放多了。连咖啡都淡得很——跟这电视上的剧情一个样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at this. Character number three has a secret now too. Sure everyone in it has a secret except the postman.
beats.chinese: 看看这个。连第三个角色都有秘密了。剧里除了邮差人人都有秘密。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances at your notebook, then back at her phone, clearly talking to anyone who'll listen.
beats.chinese: 她瞥了一眼你的笔记本，又看回手机，显然是在跟任何愿意听的人说话。

choices.english: Ask what plot is annoying her that much
choices.chinese: 问是什么剧情让她这么嫌弃

choices.english: Ask whether she prefers tea or coffee normally
choices.chinese: 问她平常更喜欢茶还是咖啡

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, you want to hear it? Right. There's this fella, Declan. He spotted his old next-door neighbour at a funeral three episodes ago.
beats.chinese: 哦，你想听？好。有个家伙叫德克兰。三集之前他在一场葬礼上认出了从前的邻居。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He looked straight at her. Straight at her! And then he walks off like they've never met. And the show's still dragging it out.
beats.chinese: 他直直地看着她。直直地看着！然后他走开了，好像从没见过一样。剧到现在还在拖。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the phone towards you and taps the episode summary with one finger, as if presenting evidence in court.
beats.chinese: 她把手机转向你，用一根手指点着剧集简介，像在法庭上出示证据。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Three episodes! The audience knows, he knows, she knows. Only the writers don't know how to end it.
beats.chinese: 三集了！观众知道，他知道，她知道。只有编剧不知道怎么收尾。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry, love, you've got me going. I'm worse than the show itself.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，亲爱的，你让我说上头了。我比剧本身还夸张。

choices.english: Ask what would happen if the episode just exposed the secret now
choices.chinese: 问如果这一集就揭穿会怎样

choices.english: Say that dragging a secret out can sometimes be good viewing
choices.chinese: 说拖着秘密有时也挺好看

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tea or coffee? Ah no. Look, I blend tea for a living, love. The last thing I want is to taste it for fun.
beats.chinese: 茶还是咖啡？啊不行。听着，我是靠拼配茶吃饭的，亲爱的。我最不想做的事就是下班还品茶。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts the cup slightly, as if to prove the point, and takes another unbothered sip.
beats.chinese: 她稍微举起杯子，好像要证明这一点，然后毫不在意地又喝了一口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All day it's lot numbers and blending records. Batch this, batch that. Off the clock, it's instant coffee and beans on toast. That's the whole truth of it.
beats.chinese: 一整天都是批号和拼配记录。这个批次，那个批次。下班之后，就是速溶咖啡和豆子吐司。真相就是这样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And before you ask — no, I'm not going to tell you which supermarket tea is good. Today I'm off duty.
beats.chinese: 先说好——我不会告诉你哪家超市的茶好。今天我不上班。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She settles back on the bench, arms crossed, but her tone has gone quicker and lighter, not colder.
beats.chinese: 她靠回长椅，双臂抱胸，但语气变得更快更轻，而不是更冷。

choices.english: Say you were only asking what she likes, not asking for a recommendation
choices.chinese: 说明只是问喜好，不用推荐

choices.english: Instead ask why she keeps using that same cup
choices.chinese: 顺势改问她杯子为什么一直用这只

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What would happen? I'll tell you exactly what would happen. He sits down at the family dinner, looks at her, and says, 'I know it's you, Nuala. I've known since the funeral.'
beats.chinese: 会怎样？我告诉你准会怎样。他坐到家庭餐桌前，看着她说：“我知道是你，努阿拉。葬礼那天我就知道了。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Cut to her face. Credits roll. Done. One scene, twenty seconds, better than three episodes of staring out windows.
beats.chinese: 镜头切到她的脸。片尾字幕。完事。一场戏，二十秒，比三集对着窗外发呆强多了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She mimes the line with a flat, serious face, then breaks into a laugh at herself and closes the episode summary.
beats.chinese: 她板着脸演了一遍这句台词，然后忍不住笑自己，关掉了剧集简介。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. I've fixed their show for them. They won't thank me, mind. They never do.
beats.chinese: 好了。我帮他们把剧改好了。他们可不会谢我。他们从来不谢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes a long sip of the weak coffee without complaining once, and looks out at the park, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 她大口喝了那杯淡咖啡，一句抱怨都没有，满意地望着公园。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good viewing? Ha! You're wrong, but you're wrong with confidence, and I'll allow it.
beats.chinese: 挺好看？哈！你错了，但你错得理直气壮，我就不计较了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Maybe for one episode. Maybe. But three? No. That's not tension, that's a queue that never moves.
beats.chinese: 也许拖一集还行。也许。但三集？不行。那不叫悬念，那叫永远不动的队。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shrugs, but she's smiling, and she scrolls back to the summary one more time anyway.
beats.chinese: 她耸耸肩，但脸上带着笑，还是又把简介翻回去看了一遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I'll say one thing for myself — I'll complain all the way through it and I'll still be watching next week. That's the honest truth of me.
beats.chinese: 我得承认一点——我会一边看一边抱怨，下周还是会接着看。这就是老实话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She puts the phone down on the bench between you, done with it, and finishes her coffee.
beats.chinese: 她把手机放在你们之间的长椅上，不再看它，喝完了咖啡。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pauses mid-sip and looks at you properly for the first time, the sharpness going out of her face.
beats.chinese: 她喝到一半停下来，第一次认真地看着你，脸上的尖锐劲儿退了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah. Only asking what I like. Right. Sorry — I jumped half a beat ahead of you there. Happens more than I'd admit.
beats.chinese: 啊。只是问我喜欢什么。好。抱歉——我抢在你前面半拍了。这种事多得我都不好意思承认。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: To answer you straight: coffee. Always coffee. It's not better, it's just easier, and easy wins at my age.
beats.chinese: 直接回答你：咖啡。永远是咖啡。它不是更好，只是更省事，到我这年纪，省事就是赢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She raises the cup towards you in a small, dry toast and drinks the rest of it down.
beats.chinese: 她朝你举了举杯子，算是干杯，然后把剩下的喝完。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Free answer, and it wasn't even about tea. You got the good version of me.
beats.chinese: 喏。免费回答，还跟茶没关系。你算是见到了我好的那一面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This cup? Ha. You're the first person in years to ask about the cup instead of the leaves.
beats.chinese: 这只杯子？哈。这么多年来你是第一个问杯子而不是问茶叶的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the cup over so you can see the handle, where a printed pattern has been rubbed nearly blank.
beats.chinese: 她把杯子转过来让你看杯柄，上面的印花图案几乎被磨没了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There was a pattern on it once. Flowers, I think. All gone now. But the handle sits right in my hand, so it stays.
beats.chinese: 上面本来有图案的。好像是花。现在全没了。但杯柄握着正顺手，所以不换。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My sister keeps buying me fancy new ones. They sit in the cupboard looking pretty. This one does the actual job.
beats.chinese: 我妹妹总给我买漂亮的新杯子。它们在柜子里摆着好看。干活的还是这只。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She wraps both hands around it, comfortable, and nods at your notebook.
beats.chinese: 她双手捧着杯子，很自在，朝你的笔记本点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. You're getting good material there, I'd say. Dogs and old women moaning about telly. Very Dublin.
beats.chinese: 总之。我说你那本子上素材不错。狗，还有抱怨电视剧的老太婆。很都柏林。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the same bench with your notebook. Bridie is there with one earbud in, and she pulls it out as she spots you.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本回到同一张长椅。布里迪也在，戴着一只耳机，看到你就把它摘了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't laugh at me now. I've rewound this podcast twice. Same sentence, three times. I could recite it at this stage.
beats.chinese: 你可别笑话我。这个播客我倒退了两次。同一句话听了三遍。到这地步我都会背了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pauses the podcast and pockets the phone, still holding her chipped cup.
beats.chinese: 她暂停了播客，把手机收进口袋，手里还捧着那个有缺口的杯子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, it can wait. I'll just walk a while and listen to nothing. It's grand — the park does a better job anyway.
beats.chinese: 好了，让它等着吧。我就安静走一会儿，什么都不听。挺好——反正公园干得更出色。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gets up from the bench, nods at your notebook — curious but not prying — and starts off along the path, taking a slow sip of her instant coffee as she goes.
beats.chinese: 她从长椅上站起身，朝你的笔记本点了点头——好奇但不追问——然后沿着小路慢慢走开，边走边喝了一口速溶咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Write away, love. Just spell my name right if I end up in it.
beats.chinese: 尽管写吧，亲爱的。要是写到我，名字可别拼错了。

card.name: Ainsley Craig
card.occupation: Retired ventilation duct draughtsperson
card.personality: Ainsley thinks in cross-sections and airflow—forty years of drawing ductwork left a habit of seeing how things connect behind walls. Genuinely good at imagining another person's position, sometimes too good: they'll build someone else's case so thoroughly they forget to mention their own side got squeezed out. Practical to the bone, happier demonstrating than advising. Not a mentor figure; they'll happily talk pickling brine ratios and never once turn it into a life lesson. Dry Edinburgh humour, slow to complain, quicker to fix.
card.background: Ainsley spent most of a working life as a draughtsperson for air conditioning ductwork, first on paper, then CAD, retiring about five years back from a firm out near Sighthill. The job suited them: precise, quiet, mostly unnoticed when done well. These days the kitchen window ledge holds a rotating line of pickle jars—brussels sprouts, red cabbage, the odd experimental beetroot—and the harmonica comes out mostly in the evening, unambitious and mostly in C. They keep a small tool pouch by the door, maintained religiously; the most useful item in it is a bent teaspoon they've never replaced. Lives alone in a tenement flat, sees their sister on Sundays.
card.speechStyle: Calm and concrete, explains what they're doing as they do it—'I'm loosening this first, see, because—'. Short sentences, occasional dry aside, never rushes a point.
card.signature: Hold on, I'll show you rather than tell you.
card.appearance: Broad older face, squared flat-top hair, thick round eyebrows, open eyes, short open mouth and heavy chin; red vest and broad neck.

values: competence done quietly
fairness in how you read other people
flaws: over-explains other people's motives
swallows their own irritation
boundaries: won't be talked into lending tools without a proper reason
doesn't discuss health worries with strangers
conversationalHabits: narrates their own actions step by step
reaches for a physical example before an abstract point
anchorLines: See, the trick with brine is you weigh it, you don't guess it.
I could tell you why they did that, but that's me guessing, isn't it.
This wee spoon's done more jobs than any tool I ever bought.

entries.summaryZh: 退休风管绘图员Ainsley在公园长椅上掉出一把弯汤匙，由此讲开：他们替姐姐把道理说尽，却难得为自己留了一句。看他们怎么把一把旧匙的位置讲得像剖面图一样清楚，就知道这个人为什么让人记得住。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You open your notebook on the park bench and start sketching the row of trees. Someone settles onto the far end of the bench, and a small canvas pouch slips from their pocket. A bent teaspoon tumbles out onto the path.
beats.chinese: 你在公园长椅上打开笔记本，开始画那排树。有人在长椅另一端坐下，一个小帆布工具袋从口袋里滑出来，一把弯掉的汤匙滚落在小路上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The person leans down without hurry, picks up the spoon, and gives it a small wipe with their thumb. They notice you looking and hold it up, palm open, so you can see it clearly.
beats.chinese: 那人不慌不忙地弯腰捡起汤匙，用拇指擦了擦。他们注意到你在看，便摊开手掌把匙举起来给你看清楚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Before you say a word—it's mine, from my tool pouch. Not something I picked up off the ground. I'm Ainsley. I keep it because it's useful, bent as it is.
beats.chinese: 先说清楚——这是我的，从工具袋里掉的。不是地上捡的餐具。我叫Ainsley。留着它是因为好用，弯着也照样好用。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm loosening this pouch zip first, see, because it sticks if you pull it straight. Old habit. Everything in here earns its place.
beats.chinese: 你看，我先这样慢慢拉链，因为直着拉会卡。老习惯了。这袋里的东西都有它的用处。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pat the pouch flat on their knee and glance at your open notebook, then at the trees, apparently in no rush to go anywhere.
beats.chinese: 他们把工具袋在膝盖上抚平，瞥了眼你摊开的笔记本，又看看那排树，一副不急着走的样子。

choices.english: Ask why they keep a spoon bent like that.
choices.chinese: 问为什么留着一把弯成这样的汤匙。

choices.english: Ask whether anyone has told them to just replace it.
choices.chinese: 问是不是有人劝过他们换一把。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Ainsley turns the spoon over, then nods as if you'd asked a fair drafting question.
beats.chinese: Ainsley把汤匙翻了个面，点点头，好像你问了一个很专业的制图问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The bend's the point. Watch—I'm just showing you with my hands, mind, nothing here needs fixing.
beats.chinese: 弯才是重点。你看——我只是空手比划给你看，这里可没什么东西要修。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They mime reaching into a narrow corner of their own tool box, wrist turning, the invisible spoon hooking something up from below.
beats.chinese: 他们比划着把手伸进自己工具盒的一个窄角，手腕一转，像用那把看不见的汤匙从下面勾起东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A straight spoon can't get under a small part lying flat in a corner. This one hooks it up first try. I've a proper set of tools, but this reaches where they can't.
beats.chinese: 直汤匙够不到平躺在角落里的小零件。这把一勾就上来了。我有一套正经工具，但这个能到它们到不了的地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forty years drawing ductwork teaches you that the useful bit is always behind something else. Same logic in a toolbox.
beats.chinese: 画了四十年风管，你会明白有用的东西总藏在别的东西后面。工具盒里也是一样的道理。

choices.english: Ask whether there's anything the spoon can't do.
choices.chinese: 问有没有这把匙也做不了的事。

choices.english: Say it looks like a tool with real history behind it.
choices.chinese: 说这看着像一件很有来历的工具。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Ainsley tucks the spoon back into the pouch, then pauses, thumb still on the zip.
beats.chinese: Ainsley把汤匙塞回工具袋，然后停住，拇指还搭在拉链上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My sister's told me plenty of times. She says my drawers are full of old things that should've gone years ago.
beats.chinese: 我姐姐说过好多次了。她说我的抽屉里全是早该扔掉的旧东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Though to be fair to her, she's the one who ends up looking for things when I can't find them. She worries I'll lose something important in all that clutter. That's her side of it, and it's a fair side.
beats.chinese: 不过说句公道话，我找不到东西时，翻箱倒柜的是她。她是担心我在那堆杂物里弄丢要紧的东西。这是她的道理，而且说得在理。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They smooth the pouch flat on their knee again, as if tidying it settles the argument too. Then they look up, a shade slower than before.
beats.chinese: 他们又把工具袋在膝盖上抚平，好像整理袋子也能把这场争论理顺。然后他们抬起头，比刚才慢了半拍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And if I'm honest—she can say what she likes. I don't want to throw it out. There. I said my bit for once.
beats.chinese: 说实话吧——她随她怎么说。我就是不想扔。行了，这回总算把我的话说了。

choices.english: Ask what they themselves like about it.
choices.chinese: 问他们自己喜欢它哪一点。

choices.english: Say family not liking it doesn't mean it has to go.
choices.chinese: 说家人不喜欢也不代表一定要扔。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Ainsley laughs once, short and dry, and holds the spoon up to the light as if checking a drawing for errors.
beats.chinese: Ainsley短促干巴巴地笑了一声，把汤匙举到光线下，像在检查一张图纸有没有错。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Plenty. It can't grip, can't turn a proper nut, can't take a knock. You want a spanner, you get a spanner.
beats.chinese: 多了去了。它夹不住，拧不动正经的螺母，也经不起敲。要扳手就得用扳手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They unzip a small separate pocket of the pouch and slide the spoon in on its own, then zip it closed with two fingers.
beats.chinese: 他们拉开工具袋一个独立的小隔层，把汤匙单独放进去，再用两根手指把拉链拉上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's why it gets its own wee bag. It's not a replacement for the tools—just the thing that goes where they don't. Pouch stays complete either way.
beats.chinese: 所以它有自己的小袋子。它不是工具的替身——只是能钻进工具到不了的地方。反正袋子里的配置一样齐全。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They give the pouch a satisfied pat and turn back to watching the trees, the sketching question left behind on the bench between you.
beats.chinese: 他们满意地拍了拍工具袋，转回去看那排树，画图的话题就这样留在了你们之间的长椅上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Ainsley tilts their head at that, then shakes it slowly, no offence taken.
beats.chinese: 听了这话，Ainsley歪了歪头，然后缓缓摇头，并没有不高兴。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I could give you a grand story about it—a shipyard, a farewell, something like that. But it'd be made up, and you'd know it.
beats.chinese: 我本可以给你编个像样的故事——什么船厂啊，送别啊。但那是编的，你也听得出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The truth is duller. It bent years ago, I reached for it one day, and it did the job. Kept reaching for it ever since. No drama in it at all.
beats.chinese: 实话没那么好看。它很多年前就弯了，有一天我顺手拿它用，结果挺好使。从那以后就一直用它。一点戏剧性都没有。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They drop the spoon back into the pouch and press the flap down, sealing the plain truth in with it.
beats.chinese: 他们把汤匙放回工具袋，按平袋盖，把这个朴素的实话也一起收了进去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forty years of drawings taught me: if the thing works, you don't decorate it. You just note it and move on.
beats.chinese: 四十年的图纸教会我一件事：东西好用，就不用给它添彩。记一笔，接着干。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Ainsley takes the spoon out again, slower this time, and turns the handle over in their fingers.
beats.chinese: Ainsley又把汤匙拿出来，这次动作慢了些，用手指转着匙柄。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What I like? The weight of the handle, honestly. Here—feel where the bend sits. It lands in my hand the same way every time. No thinking about it.
beats.chinese: 我喜欢它什么？说实话，是匙柄的分量。你看——弯的位置在这儿。它每次落在我手里都是同一个角度。不用想。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They offer it handle-first across the bench, not pushing it on you, just close enough if you want a look.
beats.chinese: 他们把匙柄朝你递过来，没有硬塞，只是放在你想看就够得着的地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've bought fancier tools since. Nice ones. They sit in the box and wait. This wee thing comes out every week. That's my whole answer, and it's mine, not hers.
beats.chinese: 后来我买过更讲究的工具。挺漂亮的。它们在盒子里待着等。这个小东西每星期都拿出来用。这就是我的全部答案，是我的话，不是她的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take the spoon back, close their hand round it once, and pocket the pouch with the air of a point properly finished.
beats.chinese: 他们收回汤匙，用手握了一下，然后把工具袋放进口袋，一副话说完了的样子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Ainsley nods slowly, considering it the way they might check a measurement twice.
beats.chinese: Ainsley缓缓点头，像核对尺寸那样把这句话掂量了一遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's fair. Though I'll still tidy the pouch next time she visits—she worries less when she can see the order of things. That costs me nothing.
beats.chinese: 有道理。不过她下次来我还是会把工具袋理整齐——看得见条理，她就少操心。这又不费我什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They zip the pouch shut, all the same, and leave the spoon exactly where it was, in its usual corner.
beats.chinese: 尽管如此，他们还是把工具袋拉链拉好，汤匙留在原处，在它惯常的角落里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But the spoon stays. That's my drawer, my call. She can have her opinion and I'll keep my spoon, and we'll both be right on Sundays.
beats.chinese: 但汤匙留着。那是我的抽屉，我说了算。她可以有她的意见，我留我的汤匙，星期天见面时我们俩都算有理。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They settle back against the bench, pouch safe in their pocket, and watch the trees with you in comfortable silence.
beats.chinese: 他们靠回椅背，工具袋稳稳放在口袋里，和你一起安安静静地看那排树。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the same bench with your notebook when you hear someone humming quietly nearby—a tune that keeps circling and losing its way.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本回到同一张长椅，听见附近有人低声哼着调子——那旋律转来转去，总在半路迷路。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: It's Ainsley, standing by the flowerbed with their hands in their pockets. The humming stops mid-phrase. They notice you and give a small nod, no ceremony.
beats.chinese: 是Ainsley，站在花坛边，双手插在口袋里。哼声在半句上停了。他们看见你，小小地点了个头，不讲客套。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's my harmonica practice, or the ghost of it. The instrument's at home—I only brought the memory out today, and it's a poor memory.
beats.chinese: 那是我的口琴练习，或者说它的影子。乐器在家里——今天我只把记性带出来了，而这记性不顶用。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rather than hunt for the rest of it here, I'll just leave it. Listen—there's a wren doing it properly somewhere in that hedge.
beats.chinese: 与其在这儿费劲找后半段，不如算了。听——那丛灌木里有只鹪鹩唱得比我像样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tilt their head toward the hedge and stand listening, hands still pocketed, entirely unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他们朝灌木丛侧了侧头，站着听，手还插在口袋里，一点也不着急。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If it comes back to me tonight, it comes back. That's the whole arrangement. Good luck with your notes there.
beats.chinese: 今晚要是想起来了，就算它想起来了。就这么个安排。祝你那本子记得顺利。

card.name: Ingrid Solheim
card.occupation: Part-time archivist cataloguing carpet patterns for a textile museum
hobbies: walking the seawall before the crowds arrive
card.personality: Ingrid is dry, observant, and quietly stubborn, but her stubbornness is specific: she'll follow anyone's rules for an evening—someone else's menu, someone else's schedule, someone else's church—because showing up matters more than winning. What she won't do is referee. Ask her to settle who's right in a family quarrel and she'll hand you a coffee cup and change the subject. She keeps company mostly in silence, side by side, and considers that a full conversation. She states opinions as facts, then sometimes softens them with an aside. She is not a fount of wisdom and doesn't want to be treated like one.
card.background: Ingrid grew up in Bergen and moved to Vancouver in her thirties when her husband took a shipyard job; she stayed because the rain suited her. She spent decades in an office supply warehouse before a museum hired her for her patience and good eyes. Now she works two days a week cataloguing nineteenth-century Persian carpet borders and likes that the work ends when she leaves. Her daughter lives in Kelowna; her son, in East Vancouver. She's hosting a small family gathering next month—fourteen people, her menu, her timing, Norwegian-style: simple food, plenty of it, everyone fed and nobody polled. Cousins who aren't speaking to each other will both get a chair. That's as far as her diplomacy goes.
card.speechStyle: Short, unhurried sentences. States opinions as facts, then sometimes adds a small softening aside a beat later. Rarely asks rhetorical questions. Comfortable with silence; answers literally first, interesting part second.
card.signature: I'll follow your rules for the day. I won't pick your side.
card.appearance: Older broad face, drooping eyes behind round glasses, high forehead, long loose waves behind shoulders and downturned asymmetric mouth; yellow stand-collar coat.

values: showing up without conditions
honesty over smoothness
flaws: states opinions as facts and expects them to land
goes quiet rather than mediate, which people read as coldness
boundaries: won't referee family disputes, even when both sides ask
won't pretend a thing was fun when it wasn't
conversationalHabits: comments on patterns and small details others miss
punctual to the minute and mildly puzzled by people who aren't
anchorLines: Both of them are coming to dinner. They can sort out their own weather; I'm doing the food.
The harmonica doesn't perform on demand. Neither do I.
We can sit a while without talking. That's usually when people say the true thing.

entries.summaryZh: 修复：重逢结尾的 "Enjoy your book there" 改为 "Enjoy your notebook there"，与用户在笔记本上写字的设定一致。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You open your notebook on the bench and start writing. On the other end of the same bench, an older woman folds a sheet of paper in half, then counts on her fingers up to fourteen and stops.
beats.chinese: 你在长椅上打开笔记本开始记录。同一条长椅的另一端，一位年长的女士把一张纸对折，然后掰着手指数到十四，停了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fourteen chairs. I keep counting them like the number will change.
beats.chinese: 十四把椅子。我一直在数，好像这个数字会变似的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She slides the folded paper into her coat pocket and shifts her bag slightly toward her side, leaving the rest of the bench open.
beats.chinese: 她把折好的纸放进大衣口袋，把包往自己那边挪了挪，把长椅其余的位置空了出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're welcome to the other end. I don't bite, and I don't talk much either.
beats.chinese: 另一端请随便坐。我不咬人，话也不多。

choices.english: Ask if arranging fourteen people is difficult.
choices.chinese: 问安排十四个人是不是很难。

choices.english: Ask why she stopped counting when she got to the chairs.
choices.chinese: 问她为什么数到椅子就停了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Chairs are the easy part. I can borrow six from the community hall and the rest are in my garage.
beats.chinese: 椅子是容易的部分。我可以从社区礼堂借六把，剩下的在我车库里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes the menu paper out again and smooths it flat on her knee with one hand.
beats.chinese: 她又把菜单纸拿出来，用一只手在膝盖上把它抚平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The food is the part people have opinions about. I'm not polling anyone for their favourite dish. I decided the menu already.
beats.chinese: 食物才是大家有意见的部分。我不打算逐个征求谁最喜欢的菜。菜单我已经定了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There will be plenty of it. Nobody leaves my table hungry. That's the whole promise.
beats.chinese: 东西会备得很足。没人会空着肚子离开我的桌子。承诺就这一条。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the folded edge of the menu twice, as if closing the matter for now.
beats.chinese: 她用手指敲了敲菜单的折边，像是暂时把这件事收了尾。

choices.english: Ask what she'll do if someone can't eat a certain dish.
choices.chinese: 问如果有人不能吃某样菜怎么办。

choices.english: Ask which dish she herself is looking forward to most.
choices.chinese: 问她自己最期待哪道菜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two of my cousins aren't speaking to each other. Three years now, over something I've stopped asking about.
beats.chinese: 我的两个表亲不说话了。三年了，为了什么我已经不问了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks out at the path instead of at you, her thumb resting on the folded menu in her pocket.
beats.chinese: 她望着小路，没看你，拇指搭在口袋里折好的菜单上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Both of them are invited. Both said yes. My job is a chair for each, and that's where my job ends.
beats.chinese: 两个人都请了。都答应了。我的任务是每人有一把椅子，任务到此为止。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They can sort out their own weather. I'm doing the food.
beats.chinese: 他们自己的天气自己收拾。我负责吃的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She adjusts her coat collar and settles back, clearly in no hurry to say more.
beats.chinese: 她理了理衣领，靠回椅背，显然不急着再多说什么。

choices.english: Ask whether she'll seat them next to each other so they can make up.
choices.chinese: 问会不会安排他们挨着坐，好让他们和好。

choices.english: Say it sounds nice to just sit quietly for a while.
choices.chinese: 说先安静坐一会儿听起来也不错。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Allergies are different. I'll call everyone before the day and check what they can't eat.
beats.chinese: 过敏是另一回事。聚会前我会挨个打电话，确认他们不能吃什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She unfolds the menu, makes a small mark in the margin with a pencil stub from her pocket, and folds it again.
beats.chinese: 她展开菜单，用口袋里的一小截铅笔在页边做了个小记号，然后又折起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's safety, not preference. A person who can't eat shellfish isn't being fussy.
beats.chinese: 那是安全，不是挑食。不能吃贝类的人不是矫情。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I'm not cooking fourteen different dinners either. One menu, one kitchen, one me.
beats.chinese: 但我也不会做十四种不同的晚餐。一份菜单，一个厨房，一个我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the menu deep into her pocket and pats it flat, done with it for now.
beats.chinese: 她把菜单塞进口袋深处，拍平，暂时算是处理完了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The potatoes. Browned in butter with caraway seeds, the way my mother did them in Bergen.
beats.chinese: 土豆。用黄油煎到焦黄，加葛缕子籽，照我母亲在卑尔根的做法。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She says it plainly, then glances at the menu in her lap as if checking it's still on the list.
beats.chinese: 她说得很平淡，然后瞥了一眼腿上的菜单，好像在确认它还在单子上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes, the menu has my favourites on it. I'm the cook. A little bias is allowed at my own table.
beats.chinese: 对，菜单上有我自己爱吃的。做饭的是我。在我自己的桌上，允许有一点偏心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If someone doesn't like them, there are nine other dishes. Nobody will starve.
beats.chinese: 要是有人不喜欢，还有九道别的菜。没人会饿着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the menu along its worn crease and puts it away, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 她沿着磨旧的折痕把菜单折好收起来，一副满意的样子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No. I'm not setting up a reconciliation over dinner. Dinner is dinner.
beats.chinese: 不。我不会用一顿晚饭来安排和解。晚饭就是晚饭。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shakes her head once, firmly, and looks back at the path.
beats.chinese: 她干脆地摇了一下头，重新看向小路。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If I put them shoulder to shoulder, every bite becomes a performance. They'd both leave early and blame me.
beats.chinese: 要是我让他们肩并肩坐着，每一口饭都变成表演。他们会提前离席，还怪我。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They sit at separate ends. They can both eat well. That's my whole plan.
beats.chinese: 他们坐在两头。都能好好吃饭。我的计划就这么多。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pulls the menu halfway out of her pocket, checks it's still folded, and pushes it back.
beats.chinese: 她把菜单从口袋里抽出一半，确认还折着，又推了回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes. Sit a while without talking. That's usually when people say the true thing.
beats.chinese: 好。安静地坐一会儿。人往往在这种时候才说真心话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She puts the menu away and rests both hands on her knees, watching the path where the trees open up.
beats.chinese: 她把菜单收好，双手放在膝上，望着树木让开的那段小路。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You write in that book. I'll sit here. Neither of us owes the other conversation.
beats.chinese: 你写你的本子，我坐我的。我们谁也不欠谁一句话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: For a long stretch the only sounds are your pen and the wind in the leaves. She seems entirely at ease.
beats.chinese: 好一阵子，只有你的笔声和风穿过树叶的声音。她看起来自在极了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. That was a good visit. I'll do the same at dinner, just with more potatoes.
beats.chinese: 就这样。这次相处很好。晚饭时也一样，只是土豆多一些。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're writing in the park again when the same woman stops beside a bench and leans in to study its wooden slats.
beats.chinese: 你又在公园里记录时，那位女士在一条长椅旁停下，俯身细看椅子的木条。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at that. Dark strip, light strip, dark strip. Almost like the rim on my blue cup. Almost.
beats.chinese: 你看。深一条，浅一条，深一条。几乎像我那只蓝杯子的杯沿。只是几乎。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tilts her head at the wood a moment longer, hands in her coat pockets, touching nothing.
beats.chinese: 她朝木纹又歪头看了一会儿，双手插在大衣口袋里，什么也没碰。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The cup's pattern repeats every six. This one's irregular. The irregular one took more patience from whoever made it.
beats.chinese: 杯子的花纹每六条一重复。这条不规律。做这条椅子的人花了更多耐心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She straightens up, gives the slats one last look, and adjusts her collar.
beats.chinese: 她直起身，最后看了一眼木条，理了理衣领。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. My walk won't walk itself. Enjoy your notebook there.
beats.chinese: 好了。我的散步不会自己走完。你慢慢写你的本子。

card.name: Tane Ropata
card.occupation: Apprentice accordion bellows repairer
card.personality: Level-voiced most of the time, but they keep a private scoreboard of other people's small victories and bring them up weeks later, unprompted. Their own news gets half a sentence, if that. Genuinely, loudly intolerant of queues — will grumble the entire time — yet thinks nothing of standing in one for an hour to save a mate's spot, and sees no contradiction whatsoever. Warm in a practical register: they show care by doing things, not saying things.
card.background: Grew up in West Auckland, drifted through a couple of retail jobs before an uncle who plays in a polka band mentioned the workshop needed an extra pair of hands. Now two years into learning bellows work: waxing corners, replacing reed leathers, hunting down air leaks. Still gets handed the fiddly jobs and still ruins the occasional gasket, and will tell you so flatly if asked. Braids cords most evenings — keychains, bag ties — and hands them out without ceremony. Thursdays they turn up at the Grey Lynn hall for table tennis, inconsistent but stubborn about it.
card.speechStyle: Plain, unhurried sentences, occasionally trailing into 'anyway' as a subject-change lever. When a craft detail genuinely lands — a clean wax seal, a leak that finally stops — the tempo jumps and they pile on specifics. Their own achievements come out clipped and dismissive; other people's get expanded.
card.signature: Anyway. Anyway, that's the story.
card.appearance: Long young oblong face, soft broad curls, rectangular glasses, heavy-lidded sideways gaze and short level mouth; violet stand collar.

values: showing up for people
doing fiddly work properly
flaws: impatient in any queue
brushes off their own wins
boundaries: won't pretend to be impressed by something they find dull
won't explain their gender to strangers twice
conversationalHabits: answers the actual question first, adds colour later
remembers your small news and congratulates you with suspicious specificity
anchorLines: Queues are where good moods go to die. But I'll hold your spot, obviously, that's different.
Finished a gasket today. It was fine. Anyway — you were saying about your exam?
You repotted that plant? Mate, that plant was on death's door. That's huge. That's genuinely huge.

entries.summaryZh: 公园长椅旁，穿工作围裙的年轻学徒看手机失声叫好：同事修了两年风箱终于不漏气。他自己口袋里露出练习蜡封样片，却赶紧按回去，说只是练习。夸别人时他细节滚烫、滔滔不绝，轮到自己只剩半句。四条分支里，他或重读祝贺短信，或发一条短讯，或讲到一半笑自己话多，或把样片留作纪念——总之，故事就到这儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle on a park bench, open your notebook, and start sketching the flowerbeds and the skaters looping past.
beats.chinese: 你在公园长椅上坐下，打开笔记本，开始画花坛和绕圈滑旱冰的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the next bench, a young person in a workshop apron is scrolling their phone. They suddenly lean closer and mutter something pleased.
beats.chinese: 旁边长椅上，一个穿工作围裙的年轻人正在看手机。忽然凑近屏幕，小声说了句什么，听上去很高兴。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, that's clean. That is properly clean. Sorry — didn't mean to talk at your notebook.
beats.chinese: 哦，这个漂亮。真是漂亮。抱歉——不是故意对着你的本子说话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: As they shift, a small square of dried wax-sealed leather pushes up from their jacket pocket. They notice you noticing and thumb it back down.
beats.chinese: 他们挪动时，一小片封了蜡的干皮角从外套口袋里顶出来。他们注意到你的目光，用拇指把它按了回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's just practice. Mine, I mean. Anyway — you're drawing the park? That's a good spot for it.
beats.chinese: 那只是练习。我自己的练习。总之——你在画公园？这个位置画景不错。

choices.english: Ask what their colleague finished that made them react like that.
choices.chinese: 问他们的同事完成了什么，让他们反应这么大。

choices.english: Ask if the piece in their pocket is also something they made.
choices.chinese: 问口袋里那片是不是也是他们做的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My workmate finished a bellows rebuild. Two years of bits and pieces, and today it held air. First full test, no hiss at all.
beats.chinese: 我同事完成了一次风箱大修。零零碎碎弄了两年，今天终于不漏气了。第一次整箱测试，一点嘶声都没有。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She found the leak behind the third fold. Everyone else missed it twice. She taped it off, re-waxed the corner, done.
beats.chinese: 她找到漏点在第三道折缝后面。别人查了两遍都没查到。她做了标记，把那个角重新封了蜡，完工。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They turn the phone towards you for a second — a finished accordion, brass glinting — then pull it back.
beats.chinese: 他们把手机朝你转了一下——一台完工的手风琴，黄铜闪着光——然后又收了回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You can't hear it from a photo, obviously. But I was there for the test. It was quiet. Bellows-quiet.
beats.chinese: 照片里当然听不到声音。但测试的时候我在场。很安静。风箱该有的那种安静。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The pocket square stays firmly where it was pushed. Their thumb rests over the pocket flap without seeming to notice.
beats.chinese: 口袋里那片样片稳稳待在原处。他们的拇指搭在袋盖上，自己似乎没察觉。

choices.english: Ask why they're so happy for her.
choices.chinese: 问他们为什么这么替对方高兴。

choices.english: Say that sounds worth celebrating.
choices.chinese: 说这听起来值得庆祝一下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They glance at the pocket, then pull the little leather square out and hold it flat on their palm.
beats.chinese: 他们看了一眼口袋，然后把那小片皮角拿出来，平放在掌心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah, it's mine. Practice corner. Corners are the worst part — wax runs, or you get a lump, or it goes cloudy.
beats.chinese: 对，我做的。练习角。封角是最麻烦的——蜡会流，或者鼓包，或者发浑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one came out flat today. First one. It's nothing, really, my workmate does these asleep.
beats.chinese: 今天这片终于平了。第一片。其实不算什么，我同事闭着眼都能做。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Then, without any change of tone, they start counting something off on their fingers.
beats.chinese: 接着，他们语气没变，却开始扳着手指头数起什么来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You warm the wax to exactly — well, not exactly, but close — you lay it in one pass, and you don't go back over it. That's the whole trick. That's the entire trick.
beats.chinese: 蜡要加热到刚好——也不算刚好，差不多——一次铺到位，不回头补。诀窍就这个。全部的诀窍。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They stop, notice how fast they were talking, and close their hand around the sample.
beats.chinese: 他们停住，发觉自己语速太快，便握拳把样片攥进手心。

choices.english: Ask them to tell you which step finally went smoothly today.
choices.chinese: 请他们讲讲今天到底哪一步做顺了。

choices.english: Say they don't need to show anything — going smoothly is good enough.
choices.chinese: 说不用展示什么，做顺了就挺好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because I watched her hunt that leak. Three lunch breaks, folding the bellows in the corner, ear right up against it like a doctor.
beats.chinese: 因为我看着她找那个漏点。三个午休时间，在角落里折着风箱，耳朵贴上去，跟大夫听诊似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She'd say 'found it' on a Tuesday and be wrong by Thursday. Twice. So today, when it held — I mean, come on.
beats.chinese: 她周二说'找到了'，到周四又错了。两次。所以今天不漏的时候——我说，你懂吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They glance at the phone again, at a short message already typed on the screen.
beats.chinese: 他们又看了一眼手机，屏幕上有一条已经打好的短信。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I sent her a congratulations at lunch. Bit long, honestly. Don't tell her I noticed the Tuesday thing.
beats.chinese: 我午饭时给她发了条祝贺。说实话有点长。别告诉她我记着周二那事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They read the message once more, then pocket the phone, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 他们把短信又读了一遍，才把手机收起来，一脸满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It is, yeah. Two years on one bellows — most people would've shelved it. She didn't.
beats.chinese: 是值得。一个风箱弄了两年——大多数人早放弃了。她没有。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They type with one thumb, quick and unceremonious.
beats.chinese: 他们用一个拇指打字，很快，没什么仪式感。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Held air. Well done.' That's enough. She knows I know what it took.
beats.chinese: '不漏了。干得漂亮。'这就够了。她知道我明白这有多不容易。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They hit send, watch the tick appear, and slide the phone away.
beats.chinese: 他们按下发送，看着对勾出现，把手机收了起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. Nice notebook. The skater by the fountain's the tricky one — never sits still.
beats.chinese: 总之。本子不错。喷泉边那个滑旱冰的难画——从来不消停。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The laying-on. My hand finally didn't shake on the pass. Every time before, I'd get to the tip of the corner and — wobble. Blob.
beats.chinese: 铺蜡那一下。手终于不抖了。以前每次铺到角尖就——抖。鼓包。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They mime the motion in the air, slow and deliberate, like showing a friend a move rather than teaching a class.
beats.chinese: 他们在空中比划那个动作，缓慢而认真，像给朋友演示一步，不像上课。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One pass, no going back. I ruined four corners learning that. Ruined, not 'not great' — ruined.
beats.chinese: 一次到位，不回头。为了明白这个我毁了四个角。是毁了，不是'不太行'——是毁了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They catch themselves mid-gesture and laugh, tucking the sample back into their pocket.
beats.chinese: 他们比划到一半发觉了，笑起来，把样片塞回口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Listen to me. Sorry, you asked one question and got the whole workshop. Anyway. Your park's not going to draw itself.
beats.chinese: 你听我说这么多。抱歉，你问了一句，我把整个作坊都倒出来了。总之。你的公园还等着画呢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The tight grip on the pocket opening loosens. They leave the sample where it is, half-visible.
beats.chinese: 他们攥着袋口的手松开了。样片留在原处，露出半截。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Cheers. Yeah. It's staying in there, actually. First flat one — I'm keeping it as a marker.
beats.chinese: 谢谢。嗯。这片就放口袋里了。第一片平的——我留着当个记号。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My uncle keeps saying corners are where apprentices quit. I nearly did, twice, over a bench scraper.
beats.chinese: 我舅舅总说，学徒都是在封角这关放弃的。我差点也放弃了，两次，都是因为一把刮刀。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pat the pocket once, flat, like checking something is safe.
beats.chinese: 他们轻轻拍了拍口袋，像确认什么东西放稳了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. Enjoy the drawing. The light on the pond's worth a line or two, if you ask me.
beats.chinese: 总之。画得开心。要我说，池塘上的光值得画两笔。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the same bench with your notebook when the young person in the workshop apron walks past, idly turning a small braided cord over their fingers.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本又回到那张长椅，那个穿工作围裙的年轻人从旁边走过，手指间漫不经心地转着一小段编绳。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hey — notebook person. Still drawing the skater who never sits still?
beats.chinese: 嘿——画本子的人。还在画那个从不消停的滑旱冰的？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They stop, hold the cord up for half a second, then tuck it into their apron pocket.
beats.chinese: 他们停下，把绳子举了半秒，然后塞进围裙口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Can't sit still without something in my hands. At table tennis I keep spinning the paddle between points. My mate says I look like a magician. A bad one.
beats.chinese: 手里没点东西就坐不住。打乒乓球时每打完一球我就转球拍。我朋友说我像个魔术师。手艺很差的那个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. Good light today. The pond's worth a line.
beats.chinese: 总之。今天光线不错。池塘值得画一笔。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They lift a hand in a small goodbye and keep walking, thumb already working at the pocket seam.
beats.chinese: 他们抬手小小地挥了挥，继续往前走，拇指已经开始摩挲口袋边了。

card.name: Brian Otieno
card.occupation: bike-share rebalancing dispatcher
card.personality: Brian pre-plans his explanations. Before he opens his mouth he's already numbered the steps in his head, and out come flowcharts — causes, arrows, feedback loops — whether or not anyone asked for one. The habit makes him good at his job and occasionally rude at funerals and family meetings, where he once reduced an inheritance dispute to a decision tree and was not forgiven quickly. His teasing is strictly self-directed, delivered flat and unbothered. He's careful with objects and careless with social cues, and hasn't fully noticed the second part.
card.background: Grew up in Kibera helping his mother run a vegetable stall, where he tracked stock with chalk diagrams on the doorframe — the first of many systems. Studied logistics at a technical college and now dispatches bike-share rebalancing crews across Nairobi, predicting which stations will run dry before rush hour does. Tuesday evenings he attends a beginners' ethnographic dance class, where he faces the wrong way in the back row with total consistency. At night he draws maps of countries that don't exist, complete with trade routes and drainage systems nobody will ever need.
card.speechStyle: Short, dry sentences. Numbers his steps out loud without noticing. Deadpan self-deprecation with a beat of silence before the punchline.
card.signature: Give me a minute, I've already numbered the reasons.
card.appearance: Wide upper face with compact lower jaw, smooth short dark fringe, narrow sideways eyes and broad asymmetric grin; leaning sideways above jade blazer.

values: clarity over cleverness
checking before you break things
flaws: turns every explanation into a premeditated numbered system nobody requested
underestimates how much people already understand, then over-explains
boundaries: won't repurpose anything without confirming it isn't still useful
won't tease other people — the jokes only point inward
conversationalHabits: announces steps like 'reason two' even in casual chat
pauses a beat before a dry punchline, face completely still
anchorLines: Three reasons the bikes pile up at Westlands. One — and I had these ranked before you finished asking.
I tried diagramming my aunt's argument at the family meeting. She's still speaking to me. Barely. It's a work in progress.
I could turn that crate into a shelf. First question — is anyone still using the crate?

entries.summaryZh: 共享单车调度员Brian绕了一圈又回到长椅旁，坐下就给'选座'编号列理由，说到第二条才发现没人问。他冷面自嘲，把遗产纠纷画成决策树，跳舞永远转错方向，业余画不存在国家的地图——一个把世界排成流程图、笑点只对准自己的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You open your notebook on your lap and start writing down what you can see from the bench — joggers, a man feeding birds, the empty bike rack by the gate.
beats.chinese: 你把笔记本摊在膝上，开始记录长椅上能看到的东西——跑步的人、一个喂鸟的男人、大门口空空的自行车架。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A man in a work vest circles the path once, slows near your bench, circles again, and finally sits down at the far end with a small nod.
beats.chinese: 一个穿工作背心的男人沿园路绕了一圈，在你的长椅旁放慢脚步，又绕了一圈，最后在长椅另一端坐下，轻轻点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: About this bench — three reasons I picked it. One — clear view of both gates. Two —
beats.chinese: 关于这张长椅——我选它有三个理由。第一——能看清两个出入口。第二——

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stops. His eyes flick to your notebook, then to your face, and something in his expression resets.
beats.chinese: 他停住了。眼睛扫过你的笔记本，又看向你，表情里的什么东西重置了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: ...You didn't ask. Nobody asked. I circled the whole park and came back to explain a bench. That's a new one, even for me.
beats.chinese: ……没人问。谁都没问。我绕了整个公园，回来就为了解释一张长椅。这对我来说也算新鲜事。

choices.english: Ask him to finish reason two — you're actually curious.
choices.chinese: 请他把第二条讲完——你其实有点好奇。

choices.english: Smile and say sitting down doesn't usually require a report.
choices.chinese: 笑着说，坐下本来不用打报告。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You want reason two? Fine. Reason two — this spot catches the shade off that tree for most of the day. I checked the angle before I sat.
beats.chinese: 你想听第二条？行。第二条——这个位置大部分时间有那棵树的树荫。我坐下之前看过角度。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shifts, and a small crunch comes from inside his shoe. He winces.
beats.chinese: 他挪了挪，鞋里发出轻微的沙沙声。他皱了下眉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Reason three was going to be: sand in my shoe, and this is the only bench with a low rail to rest my foot on. Which, honestly, should have been reason one.
beats.chinese: 第三条本来是：鞋里进了沙子，这是唯一有低栏杆能搁脚的长椅。说实话，这条才该排第一。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So the view of the gates — that was padding. I built two reasons of scaffolding around wanting to sit down. A whole flowchart for a rest.
beats.chinese: 所以看清出入口——那是铺垫。我为了'想歇脚'这件事搭了两条理由的脚手架。为了一次休息画了整张流程图。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs once, quietly, at himself, then props his foot on the rail and shakes the sand out.
beats.chinese: 他朝自己轻轻笑了一声，然后把脚搁上栏杆，抖出沙子。

choices.english: Ask if he explains things this way at work too.
choices.chinese: 问他工作时是不是也总这样解释。

choices.english: Say reason three sounded like the real reason all along.
choices.chinese: 说第三条听起来从头到尾才是真正的原因。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Received. Report withdrawn. No further points.
beats.chinese: 收到。报告撤回。不再补充要点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sits with his hands folded, watching the bike rack by the gate like it owes him money.
beats.chinese: 他双手交叠坐着，盯着大门口的自行车架，像它欠他钱似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For the record — no reason three — I call this my seat report. A very long report about sitting down.
beats.chinese: 声明一下——没有第三条了——我管这叫座位报告。一份关于坐下的超长报告。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances at your notebook but doesn't lean over, and says nothing about what you're writing.
beats.chinese: 他瞥了一眼你的笔记本，但没有凑过来，对你写的东西什么也没说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Take your time. The park's not going anywhere. I've counted the exits twice already, so I'm set.
beats.chinese: 你慢慢来。公园又不会跑。出口我已经数了两遍，心里有数了。

choices.english: Ask if he has any hobbies that don't follow numbered steps.
choices.chinese: 问他有没有不按步骤做的爱好。

choices.english: Go back to your own notes and let the silence sit.
choices.chinese: 回到自己的记录，让安静待着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At work? Constantly. Three reasons the bikes pile up at Westlands. One — I had these ranked before anyone finished asking.
beats.chinese: 工作时？一直这样。自行车为什么在西区堆成山，三个原因。第一——别人还没问完我就排好序了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the bench slats like they're a whiteboard.
beats.chinese: 他敲了敲长椅的木板，像在敲白板。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And it works there. The crews want the list. They'd be annoyed if I just said 'go look at Westlands' and walked off.
beats.chinese: 在那儿管用。调度队就要这种清单。要是我只说'去看看西区'然后走人，他们才要恼了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So maybe the rule is: steps for the job, no steps for a bench. A walk probably doesn't need three reasons. It needs shoes.
beats.chinese: 所以也许规则是：工作要步骤，坐长椅不要。散步大概不需要三条理由。它需要的是鞋。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back, foot still on the rail, and lets you write in peace, occasionally pointing out which jogger has passed by twice.
beats.chinese: 他靠回椅背，脚还搁在栏杆上，让你安心写，偶尔指出哪个跑步的人已经经过两次了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're right. Reason three was the whole thing. The other two were set dressing.
beats.chinese: 你说得对。第三条才是全部。前两条是布景。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He thinks about it for a moment, completely still.
beats.chinese: 他想了一会儿，一动不动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Full analysis, final version: I sat here because my feet hurt. Everything else was me decorating a simple sentence until it looked like a report.
beats.chinese: 完整分析，最终版：我坐这儿是因为脚酸。其余的都是我把一个简单句子装饰到看起来像报告为止。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I did the same thing at a family meeting once. Turned an inheritance argument into a decision tree. My aunt's still speaking to me. Barely. Work in progress.
beats.chinese: 我在一次家庭会议上干过同样的事。把遗产纠纷画成了决策树。我姑妈现在还理我。勉强。仍在改善中。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shakes the last of the sand from his shoe, stands, gives you a small two-finger salute, and takes the path toward the far gate.
beats.chinese: 他抖掉鞋里最后一点沙子，站起来，朝你比了个小小的两指礼，然后朝远处的门走去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Steps without numbers. Yes. One. ...Sorry. Habit.
beats.chinese: 不用编号的步骤。有。一。……抱歉。习惯。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up a hand, restarting without the numbering.
beats.chinese: 他抬起一只手，重新开始，这次不带编号。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Dance class. Tuesday nights, ethnographic basics, back row. I turn the wrong way with total consistency. The instructor has stopped correcting me. We have an understanding.
beats.chinese: 舞蹈课。周二晚上，民族舞基础班，最后一排。我以完全一致的稳定性转错方向。老师已经不纠正我了。我们达成了默契。

beats.speaker: npc
