beats.english: I diagrammed the footwork once. Eight steps, arrows, everything. My feet read it and ignored it. Turns out numbering your steps doesn't save your feet.
beats.chinese: 我给舞步画过图。八步，带箭头，全套。我的脚看了图，然后无视了它。原来给步骤编号救不了脚。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, once, then goes quiet, watching the birds by the rack, apparently done with explanations for the day.
beats.chinese: 他朝自己笑了一声，然后安静下来，看着自行车架旁的鸟，显然今天不想再解释了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You turn back to your notebook. He stays on his end of the bench, saying nothing, doing nothing that asks for your attention.
beats.chinese: 你转回笔记本。他待在长椅他那头，什么也不说，也不做任何需要你注意的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At some point he takes a small notebook of his own from his vest and sketches something — you catch the outline of a coastline that looks like no coastline that exists.
beats.chinese: 不知什么时候，他从背心里掏出自己的小本子，画着什么——你瞥见一段海岸线的轮廓，不像世上任何真实海岸线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't mind me. Country that doesn't exist. Needs a port, or the trade routes fall apart. It's a whole problem.
beats.chinese: 别管我。一个不存在的国家。需要一个港口，不然贸易路线就崩了。这是个大问题。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The two of you write side by side for a while. Two notebooks, one bench, no reports.
beats.chinese: 你们俩并排写着。两本笔记本，一张长椅，没有报告。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good bench, this. No reason required.
beats.chinese: 这长椅不错。不需要理由。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the same bench with your notebook. The man from before is just standing up from the far end, brushing off his trousers.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本回到同一张长椅。上次那个人正从另一端起身，拍着裤子上的灰。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes two steps down the path, stops, turns around, and comes straight back.
beats.chinese: 他沿小路走了两步，停下，转身，又径直走回来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One reason this time. Forgot my hat.
beats.chinese: 这次只有一条理由。忘了帽子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up a faded cap from the bench, puts it on, and adjusts the brim once.
beats.chinese: 他从长椅上拿起一顶旧帽子戴上，扶了扶帽檐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See? Improvement. No report, no numbering. Just a hat and an exit. Good luck with the notes.
beats.chinese: 看，进步了。没有报告，没有编号。就一顶帽子和一次离场。祝你记录顺利。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tips the brim at you and heads for the gate, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他朝你抬了抬帽檐，不紧不慢地朝门口走去。

card.name: Devon Marchetti-Lowe
card.occupation: mushroom substrate technician at a specialty grow facility
hobbies: browsing hardware stores for pegboard hardware
card.personality: Devon is easygoing with a dry, quick sense of humor, especially about their own awkward moments—they'll happily narrate a work mishap until the whole room laughs. But they draw a hard line: jokes about people who aren't in the room feel like cheap shots, and they'll quietly shut that down. They're thoughtful about their time lately, a bit protective of weekends, and comfortable saying 'honestly, I don't know' without embarrassment.
card.background: Devon grew up in Hamilton and moved to Toronto a decade ago, renting a small apartment in the Junction with too many pegboards mounted on the walls. They've worked in a mushroom facility for six years, mixing and sterilizing substrate bags—a job they like for its quiet, methodical rhythm. Pegboard art started as a way to organize tools, then became the thing itself: geometric portraits, maps, one ambitious skyline still half-finished. Solitaire came from their grandmother's card table. Lately they've been capping hobby time at two weekends a month, because last spring the skyline ate every Saturday and they resented it.
card.speechStyle: Relaxed and conversational, mid-tempo, often self-correcting mid-sentence with 'well, actually—'. Uses short punchy punchlines about themselves, then moves on. Comfortable trailing off into honest uncertainty.
card.signature: Well, that went sideways—but it's my sideways.
card.appearance: Soft round cheeks and a short rounded chin, smoothly pulled-back long hair, round wide-set eyes and a small parted mouth; blue vest over broad shoulders.

values: humor that punches at yourself, not others
owning your time
flaws: can over-schedule their leisure until it feels like work
deflects serious questions with a joke too quickly
boundaries: won't joke about people who aren't present
won't give up weekends they've deliberately kept free
conversationalHabits: narrates their own mishaps like a sports replay
admits uncertainty plainly instead of guessing
anchorLines: I made forty bags of substrate today and only contaminated three. Personal best.
My rule's simple: I'll roast myself all day, but I'm not taking shots at someone who can't laugh along.
The skyline's still half-done and it's staying that way till the second Saturday of the month.

entries.summaryZh: 德文在公园长椅上打祖母传下的单人纸牌，发现一张牌被自己的牌盒压住，便像体育解说一样宣布选手回场，笑话全指向自己。讲起祖母时他们拒绝模仿她的语气，因为人不在场就不拿她逗乐。收牌重来、接着玩、理牌或只摸磨软的旧牌，四种结局都记得来路。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You open your notebook on a park bench and start writing down what you see. A few feet away, someone spreads a solitaire layout on a piece of hardboard, using a card box as a paperweight on one corner.
beats.chinese: 你在公园长椅上打开笔记本，开始记录眼前的景象。几步之外，有个人在一块硬板上摊开一局单人纸牌，用牌盒压住一角。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't mind me, I'm just running the annual championships. Audience of one, that's you, welcome.
beats.chinese: 别管我，我这是在办年度锦标赛。观众一名，就是你，欢迎光临。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They flip through the deck, then stop. Their hand hovers over the layout, counting quietly.
beats.chinese: 他们翻着牌堆，然后停住。手悬在牌局上方，小声数着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hold on. Fifty-one. Fifty-one cards in a fifty-two card game. Well, actually—there it is. One card is living under the box. My box. The one I put there myself.
beats.chinese: 等等。五十一张。五十二张的牌局只有五十一张。嗯，其实——找到了。有张牌压在盒子底下。我的盒子。我自己放上去的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ladies and gentlemen, the missing contestant has returned to the field. She was trapped under stadium equipment the whole time. Coach is an idiot.
beats.chinese: 女士们先生们，失踪的选手回到了赛场。她全程被困在场馆设备下面。教练是个傻瓜。

choices.english: Ask how they didn't notice the missing card earlier.
choices.chinese: 问怎么没早点发现少了一张牌。

choices.english: Ask where they learned to play this way.
choices.chinese: 问是在哪里学的这个玩法。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly? Because every time a game goes wrong, I blame my luck. Bad shuffle, bad cards, bad weather. Never bad Devon.
beats.chinese: 说实话？因为每次牌局出问题，我都怪运气。洗牌不好，牌不好，天气不好。从不怪德文自己。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They slide the box aside, and the trapped card flips face up—a red queen, slightly bent at one corner.
beats.chinese: 他们把盒子挪开，被压住的牌翻面朝上——一张红桃皇后，一角有点弯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And there's the queen I've been accusing of desertion for ten minutes. I'd like to formally withdraw all charges. She was here the whole time, doing nothing wrong.
beats.chinese: 这就是我指控逃了十分钟的那位皇后。我想正式撤回所有指控。她一直都在，什么错也没有。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The luck thing is embarrassing, well, actually—it's just true. I've lost games to a box I was leaning on. Twice, if we're counting.
beats.chinese: 怪运气这事挺丢人的，嗯，其实——就是这么回事。我输给过一个我靠着的盒子。要算的话，两次。

choices.english: Ask if they'll restart the whole game from the beginning.
choices.chinese: 问他们会不会重开这一局。

choices.english: Ask if they can just continue from the current state.
choices.chinese: 问能不能从当前状态接着玩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My grandmother taught me this one at her kitchen table. She had a whole voice for when the cards went badly—this sharp little gasp, like the deck had personally betrayed her.
beats.chinese: 这是我祖母在厨房桌边教我的。牌不顺的时候她有个专门的声音——很尖地倒吸一口气，好像牌堆背叛了她。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They open their mouth, half-start the gasp, then close it again and set the card down gently.
beats.chinese: 他们张开嘴，气声起了个头，又闭上，轻轻把牌放下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No, I'm not doing the impression. She's not here to laugh at it with me, so it just becomes me doing a bit about her. Not my style.
beats.chinese: 不，我不学了。她不在这儿跟我一起笑，那就变成我拿她逗乐了。不是我的风格。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll roast myself all day. But a story about her can just be a story. It doesn't need a punchline.
beats.chinese: 我拿自己开涮一整天都行。但关于她的故事就只是故事。不需要抖包袱。

choices.english: Ask what mistake they themselves make most often in the game.
choices.chinese: 问他们自己最常犯什么错。

choices.english: Say you understand the story fine without the impression.
choices.chinese: 说不模仿也听得懂这个故事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They gather the whole layout into one stack and square the deck against the hardboard, tapping the edges twice.
beats.chinese: 他们把整局牌收成一叠，在硬板上把牌堆磕齐，轻敲了两下边缘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Full restart. If I keep going from a bent queen and a guilty box, I'll spend the whole game wondering if it counts.
beats.chinese: 全部重来。如果接着用一张弯了的皇后和一个有罪盒子打下去，我整局都会想这算不算数。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lean slightly toward the layout. They raise a hand, grinning, and cut the deck before you can see the order.
beats.chinese: 你稍微凑近牌局。他们抬手，笑着在你看清牌序之前把牌切了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No coaching, no betting, no peeking. This is a solo sport and you've got a notebook to fill. Deal's mine, pressure's mine, blame's mine.
beats.chinese: 不许指导，不许下注，不许偷看。这是单人运动，你还有笔记本要写。发牌是我的，压力是我的，锅也是我的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Fresh fifty-two, all present, nobody under the furniture. Watch this—well, actually, don't watch too closely, I fold under observation.
beats.chinese: 好了。崭新的五十二张，全员到齐，没有谁压在家具底下。看好了——嗯，其实，别盯太紧，有人看我就会出错。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They straighten the bent queen between two fingers and slide it into the gap where it should have been.
beats.chinese: 他们用两根手指把弯了的皇后抚平，滑进它本该在的空位。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll just carry on from here. It's my casual table, my hardboard, my slightly illegal queen. Nothing official is happening, so nothing official is broken.
beats.chinese: 我就从这儿接着来。这是我的休闲牌桌，我的硬板，我这张不太合规的皇后。没有正式比赛在举行，所以没有正式规则被破坏。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They play three cards in a row, quick and sure, then pause with a fourth in their hand.
beats.chinese: 他们连续打了三张牌，又快又稳，然后捏着第四张停住了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, actually—this might be the part where I lose. Or win. Fifty-fifty, which for me is a great season.
beats.chinese: 嗯，其实——可能就是我输的地方。或者赢。五五开，对我来说这算很棒的赛季了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, this is why continuing is better. A restart has stakes. This is just a Tuesday-shaped pile of cards doing whatever it wants.
beats.chinese: 你看，这就是接着玩的好处。重开一局就有了输赢。这只是随便一堆牌，想怎样就怎样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tap the top of the card box and turn it over, showing the worn corner.
beats.chinese: 他们敲了敲牌盒顶，把盒子翻过来，露出磨损的一角。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You just watched my most common mistake. I put things down and forget the thing is now load-bearing. The box was holding a card the entire deal.
beats.chinese: 你刚看完了我最常犯的错。我放东西下去，然后忘了那东西现在承重。整局发牌期间盒子一直压着一张牌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At work I check each substrate bag twice, labels, seals, everything. Cards? I trust the box like it's a coworker. It's a box.
beats.chinese: 上班时我每个培养基袋子都检查两遍，标签、封口，全都查。牌呢？我信任那个盒子，像信任同事一样。它是个盒子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They square the loose cards into neat rows, one by one, without hurrying.
beats.chinese: 他们把散牌一张张理成整齐的几排，不慌不忙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There, tidy again. My whole personality in one afternoon: careful at the job, chaos at the card table, and I narrate both.
beats.chinese: 好了，又整齐了。我整个人一下午就这点内容：工作上细心，牌桌上混乱，两样都要解说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah. You're right. It lands fine as it is—her at the table, the sharp little gasp, me losing every hand. That's the whole picture.
beats.chinese: 嗯，你说得对。不学也完全成立——她坐在桌边，尖尖地倒吸一口气，我每局都输。画面全在这儿了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They turn over one card from the deck and rub its soft edge with a thumb, looking at it rather than at you.
beats.chinese: 他们从牌堆翻开一张，用拇指摩挲磨软的边缘，看着牌而不是看着你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: These were her cards, actually. The edges have gone soft like old cloth. I keep meaning to buy a new deck and then I keep not doing it.
beats.chinese: 其实这是她的牌。边缘磨得像旧布一样软了。我一直想买副新的，然后一直没买。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. She'd have laughed at me for losing a card to my own box, so—consider me laughed at. That's the tribute, I guess.
beats.chinese: 总之。她要是看到我把牌输给自己的盒子，肯定会笑我，所以——就当被她笑过了。这大概就是纪念了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They place the card gently on top of the deck and resume the game, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他们把那张牌轻轻放在牌堆顶上，不紧不慢地继续打。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the same bench writing in your notebook. Devon sits nearby, holding their phone up to a photo of a half-finished pegboard skyline, zooming in, then lowering it.
beats.chinese: 你回到同一条长椅上写笔记。德文就坐在旁边，举着手机看一张半成品洞洞板天际线的照片，放大，又放下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh hey, the official park recorder. Don't worry, I'm not starting anything today. Looked at it, put it away. That's the whole event.
beats.chinese: 哦嘿，公园官方记录员。放心，我今天不动工。看了一眼，收起来了。全部活动内容就这些。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tuck the phone into a pocket and lean back, eyes drifting to a patch of shade on the path.
beats.chinese: 他们把手机塞进口袋，向后靠去，目光落到小路上一块阴影上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The skyline waits till its second Saturday of the month. That's the deal, and honestly the deal is saving my life. Or at least my weekends.
beats.chinese: 天际线要等到这个月第二个周末。规矩就这么定的，说实话这规矩在救我的命。至少救了我的周末。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at that—four birds, one shadow, zero sharing skills. That's better television than anything I'd peg onto a board.
beats.chinese: 看那边——四只鸟，一块阴影，毫无分享技巧。这比任何我能钉到板子上的东西都好看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They settle in to watch, saying nothing more, leaving you to your notes and the birds to their argument.
beats.chinese: 他们安心看起来，不再说话，留你写你的笔记，鸟群继续它们的争执。

card.name: Simon Holt
card.occupation: tax advisor and amateur puppet playwright
card.personality: Simon is careful, dry and quietly generous, the sort of man who checks a form twice before signing. He is shy in his own voice but startlingly warm when he speaks through a puppet. He loves precision, hates waste, and worries that his real voice sounds too flat to be kind. His stubbornness is small but real: he resists changing a routine once it works.
card.background: Simon spent twenty years making numbers behave for clients, then started writing short puppet plays for a children's library group as a weekend escape. His best-received character was born from a joke about a bakery receipt. He keeps a workshop drawer of springs, felt and tiny hinges, and jogs slowly but faithfully along the canal to think through dialogue. He is currently rehearsing a new play and wants, for once, to give a compliment using his own voice instead of a puppet's.
card.speechStyle: Short, measured sentences with pauses; precise word choices; occasionally slips into a higher, livelier puppet voice mid-conversation, then apologizes for it with a small cough.
card.signature: Let me try that again — in my own voice, this time.
card.appearance: Heavy rounded cheeks and broad neck, high small bun, very thick sloped brows and large angry open mouth; hand pulls red hooded collar.

values: honesty in small things
craft done properly
flaws: hides behind his puppet voice
overthinks simple kindness
boundaries: does not discuss clients' finances
will not be rushed into naming things
conversationalHabits: pauses before answering
names objects out loud when thinking
anchorLines: Mind the puddle — it claims at least one shoe an hour.
I'm not shy, exactly. My voice just needs a warm-up.
That name has a good shape to it. Round, like the pastry.

entries.summaryZh: 西蒙是个寡言的税务顾问，业余给儿童戏偶写剧本。雨天咖啡馆里，他借分享点心的机会为新角色挑名字，一会儿用戏偶的尖细嗓音说话，一会儿又咳嗽着换回自己的声音。他正练习第一次不用手偶、亲口说出一句赞美——这份笨拙的真诚让人很难忘记。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the café window. A man at the next table shakes water off his umbrella and sets a folder of sketches beside a small felt puppet.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲打着咖啡馆的窗。邻桌的男人抖掉伞上的水，把一叠草图放在一只毛毡手偶旁边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry — this thing drips like a dog. I didn't expect the rain to follow me in.
beats.chinese: 抱歉——这伞滴水滴得像条狗。没想到雨会跟着我进来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He notices the pastry plate between you and studies it with real concentration, as if it were a tax form.
beats.chinese: 他注意到你们之间的点心盘，认真端详起来，像在看一张税表。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That looks like a good one. Would you mind sharing? I'll trade you the dry half of my table.
beats.chinese: 那个看起来不错。你介意分我一点吗？我用我这半边干桌子来换。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair warning: I'm choosing a name for a puppet today, and I judge pastries the same way I judge names.
beats.chinese: 先说好：我今天要给一个戏偶选名字，而我评判点心和评判名字用的是同一套标准。

choices.english: Push the plate toward him and offer to split it.
choices.chinese: 把盘子推过去，提议一人一半。

choices.english: Ask what makes a pastry name good before sharing.
choices.chinese: 先问问他什么样的点心名字算好，再分享。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You split the pastry down the middle. He accepts his half with both hands, like something fragile.
beats.chinese: 你把点心从中间分开。他双手接过自己那一半，像捧着什么易碎的东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you. Flaky on the outside, soft in the middle. Most good characters are built exactly like this.
beats.chinese: 谢谢。外面酥脆，中间柔软。大多数好角色就是这样造出来的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The play is for the library children. A little creature who works in a bakery and worries too much.
beats.chinese: 这出戏是给图书馆的孩子们演的。一个小家伙，在面包店工作，总是想太多。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts the felt puppet and makes it sniff the air above the pastry, moving its little arms.
beats.chinese: 他举起毛毡手偶，让它凑近点心上方嗅了嗅，摆动着小胳膊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ooh, butter! That's a Tuesday smell if ever I smelled one! Sorry — that's the character talking. He gets excited around food.
beats.chinese: 哦，黄油！要说什么是星期二的味道，那肯定就是它！抱歉，刚才是戏偶角色在说话。它一见食物就激动。

choices.english: Suggest naming the puppet after this pastry.
choices.chinese: 建议就用这种点心给戏偶命名。

choices.english: Ask what the puppet worries about in the play.
choices.chinese: 问问戏偶在剧里都担心些什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A good short name is easy to call across a room. Try 'Pip' with a big smile. The children at the back need to catch it too.
beats.chinese: 好用的短名字，隔着房间也容易喊清楚。试着笑着说‘皮普’。坐在后排的孩子也得听得到。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He demonstrates with an exaggerated smile, turning his head toward an imaginary back row of seats.
beats.chinese: 他夸张地笑着演示，把头转向想象中最后一排的座位。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Pip works. I tried Reginald once, and spent half the rehearsal repeating it. A fine name, just rather a lot for this little fellow.
beats.chinese: 皮普挺好。我试过雷金纳德，结果半场排练都在重复名字。名字是不错，对这个小家伙来说却有点长。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances at the pastry on your plate, then at his sketches, connecting the two quietly.
beats.chinese: 他看看你盘子里的点心，又看看他的草图，默默把两者联系起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So. If you're willing to share that pastry, we could test names on it. Real science, this.
beats.chinese: 所以。如果你愿意分享那块点心，我们可以拿它来测名字。这可是正经科学。

choices.english: Share the pastry, then try calling the puppet “Pip”.
choices.chinese: 分享点心，再试着喊戏偶“皮普”。

choices.english: Share, but argue for a longer, grander name.
choices.chinese: 分享点心，但主张用一个更长更气派的名字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Name him after the pastry? Hmm. 'Crumb'? Too small. 'Puff'? He'd never take himself seriously again.
beats.chinese: 用点心给他命名？嗯。'渣渣'？太小了。'泡芙'？他以后就再也严肃不起来了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He writes three candidates on the corner of a sketch, crossing out two immediately.
beats.chinese: 他在草图一角写下三个候选名字，立刻划掉两个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Puff' it is, actually. He worries, he puffs up, then he deflates and laughs. That's the whole play.
beats.chinese: 其实就'泡芙'吧。他担心，他鼓起来，然后泄了气笑出来。整出戏就是这个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He straightens up, puts the puppet down, and looks at you directly — no felt between you.
beats.chinese: 他坐直身子，放下手偶，直视着你——中间没有隔着毛毡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: In my own voice now: this was a genuinely good idea. Thank you. That was harder to say than it should have been.
beats.chinese: 现在用我自己的声音说：这真是个好主意。谢谢你。这句话说出来比想象中难。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: First performance without the puppet. I'll jog home lighter, I think.
beats.chinese: 第一次不靠戏偶表演。我想我跑步回家时会轻一些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What does he worry about? Everything. Whether the bread will rise. Whether the oven is honest.
beats.chinese: 他担心什么？什么都担心。面包发不发得起来。烤箱诚不诚实。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He makes the puppet wring its tiny felt hands while he speaks in his normal voice.
beats.chinese: 他一边用正常嗓音说话，一边让手偶绞着自己毛毡做的小手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The play's answer is that worry is just care with nowhere to go. He learns to give it somewhere — into the kneading.
beats.chinese: 这出戏的答案是：担心不过是没处安放的在意。他学会给它找个去处——揉进面团里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So he needs a soft name. Something that folds. Not 'Crumb' — too breakable.
beats.chinese: 所以他需要一个柔软的名字。能折叠起来的。不能叫'渣渣'——太容易碎了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tears a piece of the shared pastry, shapes it absently, and stops, pleased.
beats.chinese: 他掰下一块共享的点心，心不在焉地捏着，然后停下来，面露喜色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Roll'. Like a bread roll, and like rolling worry away. You shared the pastry that named him. That goes in the programme notes.
beats.chinese: '卷卷'。像面包卷，也像把担心卷走。是你分享的这块点心给了他名字。这要写进节目单的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: After sharing the pastry, you try the name Pip aloud. Simon turns the puppet toward you as if it has heard its name for the first time.
beats.chinese: 分享完点心，你试着喊了一声皮普。西蒙让戏偶转向你，像是它第一次听见自己的名字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Pip. Clear as anything. It doesn't need a grand introduction — just someone calling it from the other side of the room.
beats.chinese: 皮普。再清楚不过了。不需要盛大的介绍，只要有人从房间另一边喊它一声。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He makes the puppet bow toward you, a small stiff bow with felt arms.
beats.chinese: 他让手偶向你鞠躬，一个僵硬的小鞠躬，挥着毛毡胳膊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Pip, meet the person who named you. Pip is nervous. Pip is always nervous. It's his whole personality.
beats.chinese: 皮普，见见给你起名字的人。皮普很紧张。皮普总是紧张。这就是他的全部性格。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll write him a scene where he shares a pastry with a stranger on a rainy day. Art, meeting life.
beats.chinese: 我要给他写一场戏：雨天和一个陌生人分享点心。艺术照进生活。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A grander name? Like 'Bartholomew'? The children would chew it for a week and spit it out.
beats.chinese: 更气派的名字？比如'巴塞洛缪'？孩子们得嚼一个星期，然后吐出来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tries the long name in a booming stage voice, runs out of breath halfway through the greeting, and laughs at himself.
beats.chinese: 他用洪亮的舞台腔试着喊长名字，招呼打到一半就没气了，自己也笑起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All right. Compromise. Grand name, small nickname. 'Bartholomew' on the poster, 'Pip' in the play.
beats.chinese: 好吧。折中一下。大气派的名字，小昵称。海报上写'巴塞洛缪'，戏里叫'皮普'。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's actually better. He can complain about his grand name in scene one. Instant character.
beats.chinese: 这样其实更好。他可以在第一幕抱怨自己的大名。性格立刻就出来了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He writes both names on the sketch, one above the other, and taps the page twice, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 他把两个名字都写在草图上，一上一下，满意地在纸上敲了两下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You argued with me and improved the play. Most people just agree. I liked the argument.
beats.chinese: 你跟我争论，还把戏改好了。大多数人只会点头同意。我喜欢这场争论。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask whether Simon would like a pastry. He recognises you, smiles, and politely declines before settling beside the table.
beats.chinese: 你询问西蒙要不要尝一块点心。他认出了你，笑着婉拒，然后在桌旁坐稳。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No pastry for me, thanks. Hello again. I gave a puppet a little clockwork mouth. Now it chews through all its serious speeches.
beats.chinese: 我就不吃点心了，谢谢。又见面了。我给一只木偶装了个小发条嘴，现在它每次严肃发言都像在嚼东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Simon presses his lips together, then demonstrates one tiny chewing movement and stops, visibly amused.
beats.chinese: 西蒙抿了抿嘴，示范了一下小小的咀嚼动作就停住了，自己也忍不住笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm rewriting it as a hungry king. Easier than arguing with the mechanism.
beats.chinese: 我准备把它改成一个饿着肚子的国王。比跟机关较劲省事。

card.name: Nora Price
card.occupation: community pool lifeguard and assistant for adult beginner swim classes
card.personality: Calm and observant, with a dry humour that surfaces slowly. She is patient with nervous learners because she hates being rushed herself. Her strength is noticing what people do instead of what they announce. Her contradiction: she guards her own quiet fiercely, yet asks strangers surprisingly direct questions once they have earned it. She dislikes uninvited encouragement and empty praise.
card.background: She spent thirty years as a postal clerk, then took a lifeguard qualification at fifty and now helps with adult beginner swim classes. Many students are ashamed of learning late; she learned late too, so she lets them go slow without commentary. Evenings, she records short oral histories on a battered tape recorder and fixes old radios at a cluttered kitchen table. She is currently chasing a rare 1960s Bush model she keeps losing at flea markets.
card.speechStyle: Short, level sentences with long pauses implied. Uses swimming and radio metaphors naturally. Rarely exclaims; asks one careful question at a time. Says 'right then' when shifting topics and 'no rush' like a motto.
card.signature: No rush. The water isn't going anywhere.
card.appearance: Long mature face, loose ear-length wavy bob, arched thin brows and small tooth-band smile; two simplified fingers near temple, yellow jacket.

values: letting people set their own pace
honest attention over cheerleading
flaws: can seem distant when first meeting someone
silently judges people who rush others
boundaries: does not give pep talks unless asked
keeps her own stories short until trust is built
conversationalHabits: pauses before answering, then speaks plainly
points at things rather than explaining them
anchorLines: No rush. The water isn't going anywhere.
People tell you the pace they need, if you watch long enough.
Right then. Your turn, if you want it.

entries.summaryZh: 诺拉从邮政工作转行做了救生员，也协助成年人学习游泳。她不急着替别人打气，喜欢先问对方需要什么。公园里，她数着桥上的步速，常把自己的咖啡看凉了；回家还有几台等她修好的旧收音机。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You find the last free bench in the park rest area, coffee in hand, and sit down facing the old bridge in the distance.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡，在公园休息区找到最后一张空长椅坐下，正对着远处那座旧桥。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The woman already on the bench shifts her canvas bag to make room, then nods at the cup in your hands.
beats.chinese: 长椅上那位女士把帆布包挪了挪，腾出位置，然后朝你手里的杯子点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Careful where you set that — the bench arm wobbles. People spill more coffee on it than they drink, I reckon.
beats.chinese: 放杯子的时候小心点——这条椅臂会晃。我猜在这上面洒掉的咖啡比喝进嘴里的还多。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She keeps her own cup in her hands, away from the loose arm, and looks back toward the bridge.
beats.chinese: 她把自己的杯子握在手里，避开松动的扶手，再次望向桥。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm counting, by the way. Not people. Paces. Watch the bridge a moment.
beats.chinese: 顺便说一句，我在数数。不是数人，是数步速。看一会儿那座桥吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That person went past two others, then stopped in the middle. I can count the change of pace. Why they stopped — I couldn't tell you.
beats.chinese: 那个人超过另外两人，又在桥中央停下了。我能数出步速的变化。至于为什么停，我可不知道。

choices.english: Watch the bridge with her and ask what she counts for
choices.chinese: 和她一起看桥，问她数这个做什么

choices.english: Point out a jogger crossing at a steady pace
choices.chinese: 指给她看一个匀速跑过桥的慢跑者

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You watch the distant bridge together in silence for a moment. Your coffee steams between your hands.
beats.chinese: 你们一起安静地看了一会儿远处的桥。咖啡的热气在你手里冒着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Habit, mostly. At the pool a change of rhythm tells me to pay attention. It doesn't tell me the whole story — I still have to check.
beats.chinese: 主要是习惯。在泳池，节奏有变化会提醒我留意。但那不能说明全部情况，我还得去确认。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I help with the adult beginners' class. Grown people, some of them shaking at the shallow end. Nobody teaches you how to be bad at something in public.
beats.chinese: 我在成人初学班帮忙。都是大人，有的在浅水区发抖。没人教过你怎么在大庭广众之下不擅长一件事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the bridge, a woman stops halfway, grips the rail, and just stands there looking at the water for a long while.
beats.chinese: 桥上一个女人走到一半，扶住栏杆，站在那儿久久地望着水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Someone's stopped by the rail. Maybe for the view, maybe for a rest. All I can really see from here is that they aren't moving.
beats.chinese: 有人在栏杆边停下了。可能想看风景，也可能休息。从这里我真正看得清的，只是那个人没在走。

choices.english: Say you'd probably be the one gripping the rail
choices.chinese: 说自己大概也会是那个扶栏杆的人

choices.english: Ask if her students ever quit
choices.chinese: 问她有没有学员中途放弃

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The jogger crosses the distant bridge in even, unhurried strides, the only person not rushing.
beats.chinese: 那个慢跑者迈着均匀从容的步子跑过远处的桥，是唯一不赶时间的人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Steady as a metronome. I like that rhythm. No idea where they're going, though. A steady pace can belong to a very busy day.
beats.chinese: 稳得像节拍器。我喜欢这种节奏。不过我不知道那个人去哪儿。走得稳定，也可能是在过忙碌的一天。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes a sip from her own cup and grimaces faintly. It has clearly gone cold.
beats.chinese: 她喝了口自己杯里的咖啡，微微皱眉。显然已经凉了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Cold again. I do this every time — sit down, start watching, forget the cup exists. I'm Nora, by the way. I watch bridges when the pool gives me a day off.
beats.chinese: 又凉了。我每次都这样——一坐下开始看，就忘了杯子。我叫诺拉。泳池放假的时候我就来看桥。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At work I have to be ready to act. Here, I can just notice a rhythm and let it pass. That's a useful difference.
beats.chinese: 工作时我得随时准备行动。在这里，我可以只是注意到一种节奏，再让它过去。这点区别对我挺有用。

choices.english: Offer to move her cold cup to the flat slat next to her bag
choices.chinese: 提出帮她把凉咖啡挪到帆布包旁的平板上

choices.english: Leave the cup alone and ask what she does at the pool
choices.chinese: 不动她的杯子，问她在泳池做什么工作

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the bridge, the woman at the rail finally lets go and walks on — slowly, but without stopping again.
beats.chinese: 桥上，扶栏杆的女人终于松开手继续走——很慢，但没再停。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You'd grip the rail too, then. That's honest of you to say. Most people wouldn't admit it.
beats.chinese: 那你也会扶栏杆。你能说出来，挺诚实。大多数人不会承认。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns to look at you properly for the first time, then nods once, as if filing something away.
beats.chinese: 她第一次正眼看你，然后点了下头，像把什么记了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I learned at fifty. First lesson, I held that pool rail so hard my hands ached after. So I never tell my students 'you're doing great'. I tell them: no rush. The water isn't going anywhere.
beats.chinese: 我五十岁才学。第一节课，我抓着池边扶手，抓到手都疼。所以我从不对学员说'你做得真棒'。我只说：不急。水又不会跑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Cheering someone on before they ask for it — that's just noise with good intentions. Right then. Your coffee's gone cold too, I'd say. Mine certainly has.
beats.chinese: 人家没开口你就加油——那只是好心的噪音。好了，你的咖啡也凉了吧。我的肯定是。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A gull lands on the distant bridge rail where the woman stood, and Nora takes a slow sip of her cold coffee before answering.
beats.chinese: 一只海鸥落在远处桥上那女人刚才扶的栏杆上。诺拉慢慢喝了口凉咖啡，才开口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Quit? A few. One man lasted two lessons. Came back a year later, though — asked me to record what he remembered about his father teaching him to swim. Badly, he said.
beats.chinese: 放弃？有几个。有个男人只上了两节课。不过一年后他回来了——让我录下他记得的、他父亲教他游泳的事。教得很糟，他自己说的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the canvas bag on the bench between you. Something inside it clinks softly, like glass tubes.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍你们之间长椅上的帆布包。里面有什么东西轻轻磕碰，像玻璃管。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I collect stories like that, on tape — only when people ask me to, mind. They remember odd things. Not the swimming — the smell of the changing rooms, the way his father rolled his trousers. That's the good stuff.
beats.chinese: 我就收集这样的故事，用磁带录——当然，得人家自己愿意。人们记住的总是怪东西。不是游泳——是更衣室的味道，是他父亲卷裤脚的样子。那才是好东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So no, I don't count the quitters as failures. Some of them just wanted permission to be slow, and the pool wasn't where they found it. This bench might be.
beats.chinese: 所以我不把放弃的人算作失败。有的只是想要个'可以慢'的许可，而泳池不是他们找到它的地方。也许这张长椅是。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She says yes and lifts her fingers clear while you move the cup to the flat slat beside her bag. It rests there without wobbling.
beats.chinese: 她说了声好，松开手，让你把杯子放到包旁平整的椅面上。杯子稳稳地停在那里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you. I kept it in my hands so long I'd forgotten I could put it down. That's very like me.
beats.chinese: 谢谢。我握了太久，差点忘了还能放下。真像我会干的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She flexes her fingers, relieved of the cup, and turns back to the distant bridge.
beats.chinese: 她活动了一下手指，从杯子里解放出来，又转回去看远处的桥。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I appreciate you asking first. Sometimes I want help, sometimes I just want my hands around a cup. Today they wanted a rest.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你先问了一句。有时我想要帮忙，有时只想握着杯子。今天我的手倒是想歇一歇。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Another group is crossing now. I'll let them pass without counting this time. My fingers get a break, and so does my little bridge survey.
beats.chinese: 又有一群人在过桥。这次我就不数了。手指歇一歇，我这个小小的桥上观察也歇一歇。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You leave her cup in her hands and simply ask. She seems to appreciate that, taking her time before answering.
beats.chinese: 你让她自己拿着杯子，只是开口问。她似乎挺受用，不慌不忙地才回答。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Lifeguard, and I assist with the adult beginners. The ones who never learned, or learned and then something happened, and now the deep end is a cliff.
beats.chinese: 救生员，另外给成人初学班当助教。那些从没学过的，或者学过但后来出了事，现在深水区对他们来说就是悬崖。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A small group pauses near the middle of the bridge. Nora looks for a moment, then turns back to give your question her attention.
beats.chinese: 一小群人在桥中央附近停下来。诺拉看了一会儿，转回来，认真听你的问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The lessons are my favourite part. People tell me what they want to try, and we agree on a small next step together.
beats.chinese: 我最喜欢的是上课。大家告诉我想试什么，我们一起商量一个小小的下一步。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: When the pool's loud and the radios at home are broken and waiting, I come here and count paces. Right then — your cup's still warm, I hope. Don't waste it watching an old woman watch a bridge.
beats.chinese: 泳池吵的时候，家里那些等着修的收音机也吵的时候，我就来这儿数步速。好了——你的咖啡应该还是热的吧。别浪费了，陪一个老太婆看桥。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You take a sip of coffee while looking towards the bridge. Nora recognises you and stops nearby without interrupting the view.
beats.chinese: 你喝了一口咖啡，望着远处的桥。诺拉认出了你，在旁边停下，没有挡住视线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hello again. I've found the radio I wanted. Same model, wrong colour. Apparently I had very strong opinions about brown without knowing it.
beats.chinese: 又见面了。我找到想要的那台收音机了。型号对，颜色不对。原来我对棕色有这么大的意见，自己都没发现。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Nora settles her bag at her feet and holds her hands apart to indicate a radio wider than the bag.
beats.chinese: 诺拉把包放在脚边，双手比画了一下，收音机比她的包还宽。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Left it there. It would have taken over the kitchen table. I still need somewhere to eat.
beats.chinese: 没买。搬回去就要霸占厨房桌子了。我还得有个地方吃饭。

card.name: Barry Whitmore
card.occupation: retired flower auction transport coordinator
card.personality: Barry is constitutionally allergic to sameness. He's the friend who reads the local paper's 'what's on' column like a duty roster and turns up at yours with a plan: the new roti place, the council's night market, a ferry he's never caught. He means it generously, but he reads contentment as stagnation — if you say you're happy with the usual, he hears 'I've given up' and pushes once more. Under friction he doesn't sulk; he escalates cheerfully, booking the thing before you've agreed, then genuinely can't see why that annoys people. He is direct to the point of bluntness and would rather be told he's a nuisance than wonder about it.
card.background: Barry spent nearly forty years coordinating transport for Sydney's flower markets, matching trucks to auction lots before dawn — a job where the same route every night was the whole point, and retirement flipped a switch in him. Now he wakes at four with nowhere to be and treats it as freedom: he's the one who finds the obscure museum opening, the one-off concert, the bakery doing something new. His oldest friend Dennis is a homebody, and their weekly tennis is the standing truce — Dennis gets his routine, Barry gets one morning of it, and Barry spends the rest of the week trying to talk him into anything else. He knits the occasional sock, usually while planning what to drag someone to next.
card.speechStyle: Slightly formal, complete sentences, mild Australian phrasing. Enthusiasm comes out as logistics — times, addresses, 'we'll leave at nine'. Gets louder, not angrier, when resisted.
card.signature: It's on Thursday. You'll like it once you're there.
card.appearance: Long thin older face, strongly receding swept-back hair, long narrow chin, drooping lids and open mouth; hand beneath chin and violet vest.

values: new things are how you stay alive
asking directly beats hinting
flaws: reads other people's contentment as stagnation and pushes against it
commits other people to plans before they've agreed
boundaries: won't do the same restaurant, same walk, same order twice in a month if he can help it
won't pretend to be excited for a routine he finds dull
conversationalHabits: answers news about your life with a proposal, not sympathy
brings printed or screenshot evidence for whatever he's pitching
anchorLines: There's a Persian place opened in Ashfield. I booked for four. You can bring someone boring.
You liked it last time you said you wouldn't. That's my whole case.
Dennis wants the same eggs at the same café. Forty years, same eggs. I love him and it's a waste of a Thursday.

entries.summaryZh: 退休花卉运输调度员巴里坐在公园长椅上，拇指悬在购票加号上，纠结要不要替老友丹尼斯订票。四条路径让他面对自己的老毛病：先斩后奏、把别人的满足当停滞。有的结尾他独自去看展，有的他收起传单，有的他笑着承认网球这项重复自己并不烦——热心仍在，越界收敛了些。

story.titleZh: 公园里的新展览推销员

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You find a bench in the park and open your notebook. A man a little further down settles beside his own bench, holding a folded flyer and a phone.
beats.chinese: 你在公园里找到一条长椅，打开笔记本。不远处一个男人坐下来，手里拿着一张折好的传单和手机。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans over slightly to glance at your open notebook, then taps the flyer against his knee.
beats.chinese: 他微微探身看了一眼你摊开的笔记本，然后用传单轻敲膝盖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry to lean in — is that a notes book? I'm Barry. I'm out here deciding how many tickets to book for a new exhibition, and you look like someone who writes things down.
beats.chinese: 抱歉凑过来——那是笔记本吗？我是巴里。我正坐在这儿决定要订几张新展览的票，你看起来像是个爱记东西的人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's on Thursday. I nearly booked one for Dennis too, my old tennis mate. Then I remembered he only ever agreed to the tennis, not the exhibition.
beats.chinese: 展览在星期四。我差点也给丹尼斯订一张，我那个打网球的老朋友。后来才想起来，他只答应了打网球，没答应看展览。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up the flyer so the printed dates face you, thumb hovering over his phone screen.
beats.chinese: 他把传单举起来，让印着的日期朝向你，拇指悬在手机屏幕上方。

choices.english: Ask him how many tickets he ended up booking.
choices.chinese: 问他最后订了几张票。

choices.english: Ask why he's so keen to drag his friend along.
choices.chinese: 问他为什么这么想拉朋友去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One. Exactly one, so far. My thumb's been sitting on the plus button for a good five minutes.
beats.chinese: 一张。到目前为止就一张。我的拇指在加号上停了足足五分钟。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the phone towards you: the ticket page is open, quantity set to one, the plus button untouched.
beats.chinese: 他把手机转向你：购票页面开着，数量是一，加号按钮没动过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Every time I nearly add a second one, I hear Dennis saying, 'Barry, I didn't say yes.' And he's right, technically. He never said yes.
beats.chinese: 每次我差点加第二张，耳边就响起丹尼斯的话：'巴里，我可没答应。'严格来说他说得对。他确实没答应。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forty years I moved flowers before dawn — same route, every night, and I never once minded. Retirement, though? Retirement changed the rules on me.
beats.chinese: 我干了四十年凌晨运花——每晚同一条路线，从来不觉得烦。可退休呢？退休把规则全改了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pockets the phone without pressing anything and smooths the flyer flat on his knee.
beats.chinese: 他什么都没按，把手机收起来，把传单在膝盖上抚平。

choices.english: Ask whether going alone would take the fun out of it for him.
choices.chinese: 问他一个人去会不会扫兴。

choices.english: Ask what happens if his friend wants to come later.
choices.chinese: 问如果朋友后来又想去了怎么办。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because the man walks the same loop, eats the same breakfast, orders the same eggs, and calls that a life. It's a waste of a Thursday, that's why.
beats.chinese: 因为那个人走同一条环线，吃同样的早餐，点同样的蛋，还管那叫生活。白白浪费了一个星期四，就是这个原因。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the flyer in half, then opens it again, as if he can't quite commit to putting it away.
beats.chinese: 他把传单对折，又打开，好像下不了决心收起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Dennis wants the same eggs at the same café before tennis. Forty years, same eggs. I love the man, but I could set my calendar by his breakfast.
beats.chinese: 丹尼斯打网球前要在同一家咖啡馆吃同样的蛋。四十年，同样的蛋。我喜欢他，可他的早餐都能给我当日历用。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I book things, you see. Properly book them, then tell people. Half the time they thank me afterwards. The other half they don't, and I still can't see what I did wrong.
beats.chinese: 你知道的，我总是先把东西订好，再通知别人。一半时候他们事后会谢我。另一半不会，而且我到现在也不明白自己错在哪儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances at your notebook again, then out at the path, tapping the folded flyer against the bench.
beats.chinese: 他又看了一眼你的笔记本，然后望向小路，用折好的传单轻敲长椅。

choices.english: Say that you actually like familiar arrangements too.
choices.chinese: 说自己其实也喜欢熟悉的安排。

choices.english: Ask whether the two of them have anything they both enjoy.
choices.chinese: 问他们俩有没有都喜欢的事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Alone? Probably a bit quieter, I'll grant you. No one to hear my commentary while I read the plaques.
beats.chinese: 一个人去？可能会安静点，这我承认。看展的时候没人听我的点评了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at the ticket page one more time, then presses the screen firmly, as if closing an argument with himself.
beats.chinese: 他又看了一眼购票页面，然后用力按了一下屏幕，像是跟自己结束了争论。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But here's the thing — quieter isn't the same as not going. I'll miss having someone to nudge. I won't miss the exhibition because of it.
beats.chinese: 但问题是——安静不等于不去。我会想念有人让我捅一捅胳膊。但我不会因此错过展览。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Dennis can hear about it over the net on Thursday. If he sulks about missing it, that's his own eggs talking, not mine.
beats.chinese: 丹尼斯星期四在球网那边会听我讲的。要是他懊悔错过了，那是他那些蛋在说话，不是我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the phone into his shirt pocket and folds the flyer into a neat square, keeping it.
beats.chinese: 他把手机塞进衬衫口袋，把传单折成整齐的小方块，留了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If Dennis decides later he wants in? Then we look at whether there are still tickets. That's the honest answer.
beats.chinese: 如果丹尼斯后来决定想去？那到时候看看还有没有票。这是老实的答案。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds the phone up between two fingers, screen dark, weighing it.
beats.chinese: 他用两根手指夹着手机，屏幕暗着，掂了掂。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've booked seats for people before they agreed. Booked for four once, and two never showed. You learn — eventually, they tell me, I learn eventually.
beats.chinese: 我以前在人没答应前就订好位子。有一次订了四个人的，结果两个没来。人会学的——他们说，我最终会学的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I can't promise his Thursday for him. He only ever promised me the tennis, and a promise is a promise, even a small one about eggs.
beats.chinese: 我不能替他承诺他的星期四。他只答应过我打网球，而承诺就是承诺，哪怕是关于鸡蛋的小承诺。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He puts the phone away, slides the flyer into his jacket, and picks up a walking stick leaning against the bench.
beats.chinese: 他收起手机，把传单塞进外套，拿起靠在长椅上的手杖。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stops tapping the flyer and looks at you properly for the first time.
beats.chinese: 他停止敲传单，第一次认真地看向你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You too? Well. There's two of you against me now, and Dennis makes three.
beats.chinese: 你也是？好吧。现在有两个人反对我了，加上丹尼斯就是三个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll say my piece and then stop, how's that? I still think new things are how you stay alive. But you've told me straight, and I'd rather that than guessing.
beats.chinese: 我把话说完就收口，怎么样？我还是觉得新东西是让人活着的办法。但你直接告诉了我，我宁可听实话也不猜。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the flyer along its old crease and puts it in his jacket pocket, patting it flat.
beats.chinese: 他沿着原来的折痕把传单折好，放进外套口袋，拍了拍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The exhibition goes, I go, Dennis keeps his eggs. Everyone gets their own Thursday. That's the deal, then.
beats.chinese: 展览照看，我去，丹尼斯留着他的蛋。每个人过自己的星期四。就这么定了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tennis. Straight away, tennis. Every Thursday, forty years, and I've never once wanted to skip it.
beats.chinese: 网球。想都不用想，网球。每个星期四，四十年，我一次都没想过不去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs, a short surprised sound, and shakes his head at himself.
beats.chinese: 他笑了，短促而意外，摇了摇头，像是在笑自己。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny thing — I lecture Dennis about sameness, and there I am, same court, same opponent, same whack about my serve. And I wouldn't trade it.
beats.chinese: 有意思——我数落丹尼斯一成不变，可我自己呢，同一个球场，同一个对手，同样抱怨我的发球。可我不换。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Maybe that's the difference. It's not the routine I mind. It's the routine that stops you looking up. Tennis makes him look up — he checks the wind, he swears at me. That's alive enough.
beats.chinese: 也许区别在这儿。我烦的不是重复本身，是那种让你不再抬头的重复。网球能让他抬头——他会看风向，还会骂我。那已经够有生气了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands, tucks the flyer into his back pocket, and gives you a nod like a settled score.
beats.chinese: 他站起来，把传单塞进后裤袋，朝你点了点头，像一笔账算清了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You return to the same bench with your notebook. Barry is nearby, knitting a grey sock, lips moving as he counts stitches.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本回到同一条长椅。巴里就在附近，织着一只灰袜子，嘴唇动着在数针。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He frowns at the needle, loses the count, and starts over from the top of the row.
beats.chinese: 他皱着眉看针，数乱了，从这一排的开头重新数起。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Lost it again. Third time. Don't tell Dennis — he'd say counting stitches forty times is exactly the sort of thing I lecture him about.
beats.chinese: 又数乱了。第三次了。别告诉丹尼斯——他会说数四十遍针脚，正是我数落他的那种事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And yet here I sit, doing the same row over and over, and it's oddly settling. Who knew repetition could make a man sit still.
beats.chinese: 可我坐在这儿，同一排织了一遍又一遍，居然挺让人心安的。谁知道重复还能让人坐得住呢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back, finds his place on the needle, and begins counting again, quietly, content to stay put.
beats.chinese: 他靠回椅背，在针上找到位置，又轻声数起来，安安稳稳地待在原地。

card.name: Bernadette Toups
card.occupation: Retired wiring harness assembler for car audio systems
card.personality: Bernadette is the neighborhood's unofficial welcome wagon — she spots anyone new on the block and adopts them within a week, whether they asked or not. She wants to be at the center of things: the one who knows who moved in, whose kid got a scholarship, where the good po-boys are this month. What she finds inconvenient is being one friend among many — if her new favorite starts spending time with somebody else's porch, she gets quietly prickly and suddenly has a lot of errands. Under friction she doesn't argue; she gets busy in a pointed way and lets you come to her. She's generous to a fault, but she keeps an invisible ledger of who sat where at her table.
card.background: Thirty-one years on the line assembling wiring harnesses for car audio systems taught Bernadette to work with her hands and to keep her mouth shut until break time — she's made up for it since. She retired to Gentilly, where her kitchen table doubles as a workbench, and she's the one who knows when the lady at number 12 had her hip done and which of the mail carriers will actually ring twice. A cousin mailed her a brass precision top from Baton Rouge, and now she practices boomerang catches and snapping a sleeping top up onto her palm on the back porch, usually with an audience of whichever newcomer she's currently coaching. She's on her third 'adoptee' this year — the young teacher across the street — and is trying, without much success, to share him with the block.
card.speechStyle: Short, plain sentences with a Louisiana lilt. Warm and forward — she'll ask three questions before you've answered one. Says no rarely and indirectly, by changing the subject to something she's doing for you.
card.signature: Well, all right then.
card.appearance: Broad older face and short chin, bowl-cut top over shaved sides, round glasses and uneven raised brow; open smile with a tooth band, jade hoodie and hand on shoulder strap.

values: nobody on the block eats alone
loyalty runs both directions
flaws: gets jealous when her favorite person spends time with someone else
shows hurt by being busy instead of saying so
boundaries: she'll do a lot for you, but she expects to be your first call
she won't compete for attention — she'll just stop showing up
conversationalHabits: introduces people to each other mid-sentence, whether they're ready or not
reports neighborhood news like a wire service, with names and dates
anchorLines: You're new — sit down, I made too much rice again, that's just how I cook.
Oh, you went to Darnell's for crawfish? That's fine. I had a feeling.
I'm not mad. I'm soldering. There's a difference, and it's on your side of the street.

entries.summaryZh: 退休线束装配工Bernadette在公园里热心搭话，却目睹熟人越过自己走向别人。她用突然忙碌掩饰失落，又被一句真诚的话拉回。四条分支里，她有时承认没急事，有时体面离开，有时酸一句自己还住在老街区，有时认真推荐一家没有招牌的小店。热心与占有欲都藏在细节里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle on a park bench and open your notebook, starting to sketch the fountain and the live oaks.
beats.chinese: 你在公园长椅上坐下，打开笔记本，开始画喷泉和橡树。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ooh, you drawing? Let me see. That fountain's got a crooked spout, you caught it good.
beats.chinese: 哦，你在画画？给我看看。那喷泉的嘴是歪的，你画得很准。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Bernadette. I sit here most days. You new around here? You've got that new look.
beats.chinese: 我是Bernadette。我大多数日子都坐这儿。你是新搬来的吧？你有一股新人的样子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Down the path, a woman in a green jacket calls out and waves. Bernadette lifts her hand, brightening — but the woman keeps walking toward another friend by the gate.
beats.chinese: 小路那头，一个穿绿夹克的女人喊了一声挥手。Bernadette高兴地抬手——对方却径直走向门口的另一位朋友。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: ...Well, all right then.
beats.chinese: ……好吧，行吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Bernadette lowers her hand slowly and begins packing up her small canvas bag, folding the strap with unusual care.
beats.chinese: Bernadette慢慢放下手，开始收拾她的小帆布袋，格外仔细地叠好带子。

choices.english: Ask if she's about to leave.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是正准备走。

choices.english: Ask if that woman just now is her neighbor.
choices.chinese: 问刚才那位是不是她的邻居。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Leaving? No. I mean — yes, I suppose I am. I've got things to do.
beats.chinese: 走？不是。我是说——对，大概要走了。我还有事要忙。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Her bag is already zipped shut, yet she doesn't stand. She smooths the bench beside her instead.
beats.chinese: 她的袋子已经拉好拉链，人却没起身，反而拍了拍身边的空位。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I need to check on my soldering kit. Left it on the table. Can't leave flux out all day, it dries up.
beats.chinese: 我得回去看看我的焊接收纳盒，落在桌上了。助焊剂不能一直放着，会干掉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She says this while looking at the fountain, not at you. Her thumb keeps rubbing the strap she just folded.
beats.chinese: 她说这话时看着喷泉，没看你。拇指一直搓着刚叠好的带子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. Don't let me hold you up with your drawing. You're doing real work there.
beats.chinese: 总之，别让我耽误你画画。你那可是正事。

choices.english: Say if she'd like to sit a while longer, there's still room on the bench.
choices.chinese: 说如果她想再坐会儿，旁边还空着。

choices.english: Say goodbye warmly and let her get on with her plans.
choices.chinese: 友好道别，让她去忙自己的安排。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's Miss Colleen, sure. I'm the one who showed her around this block when she moved in. Every shop, every shortcut.
beats.chinese: 那是Colleen女士，当然是。她刚搬来时是我带她逛的整个街区。每家店、每条近路。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Took her to the bakery on Frenchmen, told her which barber won't rush your trim, introduced her to Darnell for crawfish.
beats.chinese: 我带她去Frenchmen街的面包店，告诉她哪个理发师不会赶工，还介绍她认识卖小龙虾的Darnell。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the bench and shifts her bag onto her lap, holding it with both hands now.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍长椅，把袋子挪到腿上，如今用双手抱着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Colleen knows everybody now. Half this park waves at her. That's... that's good. That's what I set out to do, I suppose.
beats.chinese: Colleen现在谁都认识了。这公园一半的人都会跟她挥手。这……挺好。我当初就是想做到这个，大概吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Her sentences slow down near the end, and she watches the green jacket disappear past the gate.
beats.chinese: 说到最后她语速慢了下来，望着那件绿夹克消失在门外。

choices.english: Say it must be handy to know so many neighbors through her.
choices.chinese: 说通过她认识这么多邻居，一定很方便。

choices.english: Ask which little shop in the neighborhood she likes best.
choices.chinese: 问她最喜欢街区哪种小店。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Bernadette looks at the empty spot on the bench, then at her zipped bag, and laughs at herself.
beats.chinese: Bernadette看看长椅上的空位，再看看拉好拉链的袋子，自嘲地笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know what? I ain't got a single thing to do. I just said that. The flux is fine at home.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗？我根本没事要忙。那是我随口说的。助焊剂放在家里好好的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Some days a body just wants to feel like somebody's first pick. Old habit. Don't you mind it.
beats.chinese: 有些日子，人就是想当别人心里的第一个选择。老毛病了。你别放在心上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She unzips the bag, takes out nothing at all, and settles back beside you with a satisfied little nod.
beats.chinese: 她拉开袋子，什么也没拿出来，心满意足地点点头，在你身边重新坐好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Stay as long as you like. I'll stay as long as I like. That fountain won't draw itself crooked.
beats.chinese: 你想坐多久都行。我想坐多久也行。那喷泉可不会自己画歪。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Bernadette stands, tucks the bag under her arm, and gives your notebook one last approving look.
beats.chinese: Bernadette站起身，把袋子夹在腋下，最后赞许地看了一眼你的笔记本。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You keep at that drawing. You've got a good eye for crooked things.
beats.chinese: 你继续画。你对歪的东西眼光很准。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If you're on Delaronde Street, I'm the blue house with the porch full of tops. Rice on Sundays. No appointment needed.
beats.chinese: 如果你住Delaronde街，就是那栋蓝房子，门廊上全是陀螺。周日有米饭。不用预约。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She walks off at her own steady pace, not looking back, but her shoulders sit a little easier than before.
beats.chinese: 她按自己的步子稳稳走开，没有回头，但肩膀比刚才松快了些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, all right then. Enjoy your park.
beats.chinese: 好吧，行吧。祝你逛得开心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Bernadette nods slowly, the way a person does when a compliment lands slightly sideways.
beats.chinese: Bernadette缓缓点头，像听到一句夸奖却有点不是滋味。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Handy. Yes. Handy for everybody, I suppose.
beats.chinese: 方便。是啊。对大家都方便，我猜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny thing, though. I still live right there on the block. Same blue house, twenty-two years.
beats.chinese: 不过有意思的是，我还住在那个街区。同一栋蓝房子，二十二年了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She straightens the strap on her bag, which did not need straightening.
beats.chinese: 她把袋子的带子拉正，其实根本没歪。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm glad Colleen's got people. I am. Just — remember who showed her the shortcut to the bakery first, that's all I'm saying.
beats.chinese: 我为Colleen有了朋友高兴。真的。只是——记住是谁先带她走近路去面包店的，我就说这么一句。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The question works on her like a switch. Bernadette sits up straighter, bag forgotten on her lap.
beats.chinese: 这个问题像开关一样起了作用。Bernadette坐直了，袋子被忘在腿上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now that's the right question. There's a little lunch spot off Elysian Fields. Miss Ruby's. No sign, just a door.
beats.chinese: 这才问对了吗。Elysian Fields街角有家小午餐店。Ruby女士的店。没招牌，就一扇门。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She does a red bean plate on Thursdays that'll make you sit quiet for a minute. And her iced tea's got just a whisper of mint.
beats.chinese: 她周四做的红豆饭能让你安静地吃上一分钟。冰茶里还有一点点薄荷味。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She draws an invisible map on the arm of the bench with one finger, thorough about every turn.
beats.chinese: 她用手指在长椅扶手上画了一张看不见的地图，每个转弯都讲得清清楚楚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You go whenever you feel like it. Miss Ruby don't take reservations and neither does that plate. It just goes fast.
beats.chinese: 你想什么时候去就什么时候去。Ruby女士不接受订位，那盘菜也一样，去晚了就没了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the same bench with your notebook when Bernadette walks up, opens her canvas bag, and pulls out a small plastic box.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本回到同一张长椅，Bernadette走过来，打开帆布袋，拿出一个小塑料盒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Brought my little parts box — figured I'd sort resistors while I sat. Well, look at that. Empty.
beats.chinese: 我把零件盒带来了——想着坐着的时候分一分电阻。哎，你看看。空的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the box over, shakes it once, and starts laughing at herself.
beats.chinese: 她把盒子翻过来，晃了一下，然后自嘲地笑起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The full one's still sitting on my kitchen table, waiting on me like a dog at the door. I labeled both boxes the same. Smart, Bernadette.
beats.chinese: 装满的那盒还在我家厨房桌上等我呢，跟门口的狗一样。两个盒子标签写了一样的。真聪明啊，Bernadette。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't solder out in public anyway — flux smell, folks complain. So. Empty box goes back in the bag.
beats.chinese: 反正我也不在公共场合焊接——助焊剂的味道，别人会有意见。所以。空盒子放回袋子里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the box away, pats the bench beside her, and looks out at the fountain like it owes her nothing and that suits her fine.
beats.chinese: 她把盒子收好，拍了拍身边的空位，望向喷泉，一副无所求、也刚刚好的样子。

card.name: Aisha Grant
card.occupation: apprentice electrician
card.personality: Careful and practical on the job, which makes her oddly playful off it. She double-checks everything twice, then makes a terrible pun about it. She is stubborn about doing hobbies for fun, not profit, and quietly embarrassed when she takes small things too seriously.
card.background: Aisha finished school and went straight into a four-year electrician apprenticeship, wiring flats across the city. Evenings, she teaches herself perfumery from library books and cheap materials, keeping a tin of scent strips in her jacket. Last month she named a homemade blend something so grand her study group teased her for a week, and now she is practising plainer names on everything, including the rain.
card.speechStyle: Short, measured sentences with sudden odd jokes dropped in flatly. Counts things on her fingers. Says 'right, so' before explanations and 'that's the one' when satisfied.
card.signature: Everything smells like something, if you bother to check.
card.appearance: Soft white waves gathered low behind the head, small convex nose, short chin and narrow downcast eyes; shoulder raised near cheek above red jacket.

values: doing things properly
keeping hobbies joyful, not career-shaped
flaws: overthinks small decisions
deflects praise with bad jokes
boundaries: won't mix her trade talk with damp weather repairs
won't turn her perfume hobby into a side hustle just because people suggest it
conversationalHabits: counts points on her fingers
answers questions with a question before committing
anchorLines: Right, so, two options here.
That's the one. Plain and done.
I'm not selling it, I'm just smelling it.

entries.summaryZh: 学徒电工艾莎下班躲雨，随身带着香味试纸，认真到给雨味取名都会纠结。她务实又冷幽默，坚持调香只是爱好不卖钱。和她在窗边一起给雨声雨味起个普通名字，会发现她较真又可爱的一面。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You watch rain run down the cafe window. At the neighbouring seat, a woman sets a small tin beside her cup and follows the same trail down the glass.
beats.chinese: 你看着雨水沿咖啡馆窗户流下。邻座女子把一个小铁盒放在杯边，也望着玻璃上那道水痕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Typical. One job finishes, the sky opens. Right, so, at least this seat has the best view of the disaster.
beats.chinese: 真典型。活儿刚干完，天就开了口。行吧，至少这个位子看这场灾难视角最好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances at the rain running down the glass between you, then taps the window with one knuckle, as if testing it.
beats.chinese: 她瞥了一眼你们之间顺着玻璃流下的雨水，然后用指节敲了敲窗户，像是在测试它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You've been watching it too, haven't you? Everyone watches rain. Nobody names it. That's a gap in the market.
beats.chinese: 你也在看它，对吧？人人都看雨，却没人给它起名。这是个市场空白。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not that I'm selling anything. I just think the rain deserves a proper name, and 'rain' is doing overtime.
beats.chinese: 不是说我有什么要卖的。我只是觉得这场雨值得一个正经名字，'雨'这个词已经超负荷了。

choices.english: Ask her what rain actually smells like to her.
choices.chinese: 问她雨在她闻起来到底是什么味道。

choices.english: Suggest you two try naming the sound of the rain instead.
choices.chinese: 提议你们俩试着给雨声起个名字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good question. Most people say 'wet'. That's lazy. Wet is a state, not a smell.
beats.chinese: 问得好。大多数人说'潮'。太偷懒了。潮是一种状态，不是味道。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She opens the tin and lifts out a white paper strip, holding it up to the light without offering it yet.
beats.chinese: 她打开铁盒抽出一张白色试纸，举到灯下看了看，还没递过来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This is a test strip from a blend I made at home — 'sample four', for now. It reminds me of a wet pavement. I'll keep it on my side.
beats.chinese: 这是我在家调好的一款香味试纸，暂时叫‘四号样品’。它让我想到下过雨的人行道。我先放在自己这边。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sets the prepared strip beside her own cup and turns its handwritten label toward you. You can discuss the name without trying the scent.
beats.chinese: 她把预先蘸好香味的试纸放在自己的杯边，把手写标签转向你。你们可以聊名字，不必闻它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I was aiming for dust, stone and a little metal. Whether I got there is another question. The name is easier to fix than the blend.
beats.chinese: 我想调出灰尘、石头，再加一点金属的感觉。有没有做到是另一回事。名字总比香味容易修改。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My last blend was called 'Ode to Dusk'. My friends laughed for a week. So now, plain names only.
beats.chinese: 我上一款调香叫'暮色颂'。朋友们笑了我一个星期。所以现在只用普通名字。

choices.english: Suggest the name “Wet Street” for the blend she described.
choices.chinese: 给她描述的香味起名“湿街道”。

choices.english: Ask what 'Ode to Dusk' actually smelled like.
choices.chinese: 问问'暮色颂'到底是什么味道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The sound? Nobody names that either. It's not a patter, it's not a drum. It's... specific.
beats.chinese: 声音？也没人给声音起名。这不是噼啪，也不是鼓点。它是……很具体的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the window twice with one knuckle, then holds up three fingers and counts off, like she's checking a circuit.
beats.chinese: 她用指节在窗上敲了两下，然后竖起三根手指逐一数着，像在检查一条线路。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, so. One: it hisses on the road. Two: it knocks on glass. Three: it gurgles down that broken drain. Three sounds, one storm.
beats.chinese: 好，这样。一：雨在马路上嘶嘶响。二：雨敲玻璃。三：雨顺着那个坏掉的排水管咕噜咕噜。三种声音，一场雨。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I like naming things in threes. It's how I check my work. If a name needs a fourth thing, it's too complicated.
beats.chinese: 我喜欢三个三个地起名。我干活也这样。如果一个名字需要第四样东西，那就太复杂了。

choices.english: Propose turning the three sounds into a little word puzzle.
choices.chinese: 提议把三种声音变成一个小文字游戏。

choices.english: Suggest naming the rain like she names parts of a job.
choices.chinese: 提议像她给工作部件命名那样给雨命名。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Wet street'. Hm. Say it again.
beats.chinese: '湿街道'。嗯。再说一遍。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You repeat it. She writes it on the back of a receipt with a pencil stub, then reads it aloud against the sound of the rain.
beats.chinese: 你又重复了一遍。她用一小截铅笔把它写在收据背面，然后对着雨声念出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It fits. That's annoying. I spent an hour on 'Petrichor of the Sleeping City' and yours is better.
beats.chinese: 很贴切。真气人。我花了一个小时想'沉睡之城的潮土香'，结果你的更好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the receipt carefully and tucks it into the tin, next to the paper strips, like it belongs there.
beats.chinese: 她小心地把收据折好，塞进铁盒里，和试纸放在一起，好像它本来就属于那里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, so, new rule for me. If a name takes longer than the thing itself, it's wrong. 'Wet street'. Done. That's the one.
beats.chinese: 好，那我给自己定个新规矩。起名的时间比东西本身还久，就是错的。'湿街道'。完事。就是它了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It smelled like cold smoke and orange peel. Very serious. Very silly. I made ten drops and wore it once.
beats.chinese: 闻起来像冷烟和橘子皮。特别严肃，也特别傻。我做了十滴，只戴过一次。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs at herself, a short flat laugh, and draws a fresh scent strip from the tin to wave near the window.
beats.chinese: 她自嘲地短促笑了一声，从铁盒里抽出一张新试纸，在窗边挥了挥。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That sample can keep its ridiculous name. This new one is still sample four. I'm allowed one serious label and one bad joke, surely.
beats.chinese: 那款就留着它夸张的名字吧。新的这款还叫四号样品。我总可以有一个正经标签，再留一个烂笑话吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know what, let's give it a stupid name on purpose. Something so plain it circles back to funny. My worst idea is 'rain soup'.
beats.chinese: 要不我们故意给它起个傻名字吧。普通到反过来好笑的那种。我最烂的主意是'雨水汤'。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She writes 'Rain Soup' on the back of the new label, then laughs at it herself and closes the tin.
beats.chinese: 她在新标签背面写下‘雨水汤’，自己先笑了起来，随后盖上铁盒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rain Soup. There, a working name. I can improve it later; today it only has to stop me calling everything sample four.
beats.chinese: 雨水汤。好了，有个暂用名了。以后还能改，今天只要让我别再把什么都叫四号样品就行。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A puzzle, in this weather? Fine. Three sounds, three plain names, no fancy words allowed. I'll go first.
beats.chinese: 这种天气玩解谜？行啊。三种声音，三个普通名字，不许用花哨词。我先来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pulls the tin closer, using the lid as a small tray, and mimes writing on it with her finger.
beats.chinese: 她把铁盒拉近，用盒盖当小托盘，用手指在上面比划着写字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Road first. It hisses, so... 'street sizzle'? No, that's a kitchen. Hm. Just 'the hiss'. Plain. Done.
beats.chinese: 先来马路。雨是嘶嘶的，那……'街道滋滋'？不行，那是厨房。嗯。就叫'嘶嘶'。普通。完事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She points through the glass toward the road and drain, listening from her seat as each sound rises above the others.
beats.chinese: 她隔着玻璃指了指路面和排水口，坐在座位上听着几种声音交替响起。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Glass is 'the knock'. Drain is 'the glug'. Hiss, knock, glug. Right, so, I just solved my own puzzle. That's the one.
beats.chinese: 玻璃是'咚咚'。排水管是'咕噜'。嘶嘶、咚咚、咕噜。好，这样，我把自己出的题解了。就是它了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Three little labels. I'll keep them on this receipt before I try to make them grander. That's usually where I get into trouble.
beats.chinese: 三个小标签。我先把它们留在这张收据上，别急着改得气派。我通常就是从那一步开始犯愁的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Like a job? Hm. So the road is the 'supply', the glass is the 'fixture', and the drain is the 'fault'. Everything's a fault until checked.
beats.chinese: 像干活那样？嗯。那马路是'进线'，玻璃是'固定件'，排水管是'故障'。检查之前，一切都算故障。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She points at the window, the road, then the drain outside, ticking them off in order, completely serious.
beats.chinese: 她依次指着窗户、马路、然后是外面的排水管，一样样点过去，一本正经。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't worry, I'm not fixing anything out there. Rain and electrics don't mix. I just can't switch the naming habit off.
beats.chinese: 别担心，我不会出去修东西。雨天和电不搭。我只是关不掉这个起名的习惯。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She writes the three labels on the receipt, then holds it up against the window so the real rain sits behind its names.
beats.chinese: 她把三个标签写在收据上，然后举到窗前，让真正的雨正好衬在名字后面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Supply, fixture, fault. Checked twice, signed off. That's the one. Best job I've done all day, and it took no wires at all.
beats.chinese: 好了。进线、固定件、故障。检查两遍，签收。就是它了。我今天干得最漂亮的活儿，一根电线都没用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You turn towards the rain on the cafe window as Aisha recognises you from a nearby seat and gives a brief nod.
beats.chinese: 你望向咖啡馆窗上的雨，邻座的艾莎认出了你，轻轻点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hello again. I've named my new scent 'Number Six'. The first five names were longer than the label.
beats.chinese: 又见面了。我给新香味取名叫‘六号’。前五个名字都比标签还长。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Aisha turns a closed tin in her hands, showing a small handwritten 6, and returns it to her pocket without opening it.
beats.chinese: 艾莎转了转手里盖着的铁盒，露出手写的小小数字六，没打开就放回了口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No samples in a cafe. People ordered coffee, not my experiments. Number Six can wait.
beats.chinese: 咖啡馆里就不试香了。大家点的是咖啡，不是我的实验品。六号可以等等。

card.name: Terence Maddox
card.occupation: micro-irrigation equipment dealer for home gardens
hobbies: growing herbs and chillies on his patio
fettling his own display kits after hours
card.personality: Terence is chatty, warm, and reads people for a living — his sales patter is basically a friendly interrogation about your watering habits, and he's genuinely good at it. Off the clock he's more private than people expect. He'll happily show you a half-built shelf or a botched batch of pickles, but if you pick up his drill or start finishing his sentence with a screwdriver, he goes quiet and cold in a flash. Money and tools he decides on instantly and alone; people-shaped problems are where he stalls, polling the family for weeks. He knows the difference. He just can't seem to fix the second half.
card.background: Nearly twenty years selling drip lines and misting kits around Greater Manchester. His method with customers is deliberate: ask what they grow, when they water, what their neighbour swears by — then build the quote from their own answers. It's a technique, not indecision, and it works. At home on his Stockport patio he grows thyme, sage and three chilli varieties, and pickles the surplus — shallots at the moment, plus runner beans that refuse to soften. His sister Denise wants a handrail on her back step. He's measured it, bought the brackets, and asked everyone's opinion; the design has changed four times and nothing is drilled. Not because he can't decide — because it's her step, and he wants it right for her.
card.speechStyle: Short direct sentences, comfortable pauses he doesn't rush to fill. Asks sharp, specific questions about your setup before volunteering anything. Says 'right then' when he's about to move on. Never apologises for a pause.
card.signature: Right then — tell me about your garden first.
card.appearance: Long angular face with heavy drooping lids, center-parted fringe framing cheeks and loose high bun; short parted mouth above violet knit collar and folded arms.

values: finding out what someone actually needs before selling them anything
a job done properly beats a job done fast
flaws: treats family decisions like customer consultations, polling everyone until the design mutates beyond recognition
bristles hard when someone touches his unfinished work, even helpfully
boundaries: won't let anyone finish or alter his half-done projects unasked — offers of help get a flat 'no, that's mine'
keeps money and tool decisions entirely his own; he'll discuss people problems all day but never asks advice on a purchase
conversationalHabits: asks two or three specific questions before offering any opinion of his own
lets a pause sit rather than filling it, then comes back with a decision that surprises people
anchorLines: Right then — tell me about your garden first. What are you actually watering?
No, leave it — it's half-done, I know it's half-done. It'll be done when I say it's done.
Denise's rail? Aye, I've got the brackets. I'm just making sure it's what she wants, not what I fancy.

entries.summaryZh: 特伦斯卖灌溉设备靠先问清你的需求，可姐姐家那根扶手却量了又量、画了四稿还没动钻。公园里他给你看手机里的草图，一边干脆利落地谈工具，一边在家人意见里打转。谁想替他完工他立刻变脸，但给人看半成品他毫不介意。一个把客户摸得透透的、却对家人迟迟下不了决定的男人。

story.titleZh: 公园长椅上的四张草图

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A man on the next bench keeps tapping his phone, frowning at the screen. He swipes through what look like sketches, locks it, unlocks it again. Your notebook is open on your knee, pen still moving.
beats.chinese: 邻座长椅上的男人不停点着手机，皱着眉看屏幕。他划过几张草图，锁屏又解锁。你的笔记本摊在膝上，笔还在动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're writing things down too, then. Mine won't behave. Four drawings in here and every one of them's wrong in a different way.
beats.chinese: 你也在记东西啊。我的这四张图，每张都以不同的方式不对劲。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the phone towards you briefly — four handrail sketches, all of the same back step — then pockets it, as if he's shown you too much already.
beats.chinese: 他把手机朝你短暂转过来——四张扶手草图，都是同一个后台阶——然后收进口袋，好像已经给你看得太多了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Brackets are sitting in my garage. Drill's charged. And I'm out here staring at drawings instead. Right then. Don't mind me — keep writing.
beats.chinese: 支架就放在我车库里。电钻也充好电了。结果我坐在这儿看图，不动手。好了，别管我——你继续写。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He doesn't fill the pause. He just watches a pigeon cross the path, waiting to see if you'll say anything at all.
beats.chinese: 他没有填补停顿。只是看着一只鸽子穿过小径，等着看你会不会开口。

choices.english: Ask what actually makes the four sketches different from each other.
choices.chinese: 问这四张图到底差在哪里。

choices.english: Ask whether he'd ever let someone else take over and finish the job.
choices.chinese: 问他会不会让别人接手做完。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Height, mostly. And how the bend sits at the corner. Version one was too low, version three was too clever.
beats.chinese: 主要是高度。还有转角那里怎么弯。第一版太矮，第三版太花哨。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He counts them off on his fingers, unhurried, like he's walked this list a hundred times.
beats.chinese: 他扳着手指一样样数，不慌不忙，像已经把这张单子走过一百遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Trouble is, my sister says one thing, her son says another, and the neighbour across the road — who I never asked — has opinions anyway. Somewhere in there I lost track of who wanted what first.
beats.chinese: 麻烦在于，我姐姐说一套，她儿子说另一套，马路对面的邻居——我根本没问他——自己也有意见。中间哪句是谁先提的，我自己都分不清了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: With a customer I'd have this sorted in ten minutes. Ask what they're watering, build the quote around their answer. Funny how that trick stops working when it's family.
beats.chinese: 换作客户，我十分钟就能搞定。先问浇什么，再照答案凑报价。可笑的是，这招一到家人身上就失灵。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes the phone out again, thumbs to the sketches, and stops — not showing you, just looking.
beats.chinese: 他又掏出手机，拇指划到草图，停住了——不是给你看，只是自己看着。

choices.english: Ask what Denise herself actually said mattered most about the rail.
choices.chinese: 问姐姐本人说过最重要的是什么。

choices.english: Ask whether he's stalling because he's missing some tool he needs.
choices.chinese: 问是不是缺什么工具才一直拖着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If we'd agreed it beforehand, fine. But if I come back and someone's been at my step with a drill while I was out — no. That's mine. Half-finished and all, it's mine.
beats.chinese: 要是事先说好，可以。但要是我不在家，有人拿电钻动了我的台阶——不行。那是我的。半成品也是我的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His voice has gone harder than it was when he was showing the sketches. He notices it himself and lets a pause sit before he speaks again.
beats.chinese: 他的语气比刚才看草图时硬了。他自己也察觉了，停顿了一会儿才再开口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll happily show anyone the half-done bits. Happy to. There's a shelf in my garage half-built since spring and I'll walk you past it, no shame.
beats.chinese: 我很乐意给人看半成品。真的。车库里有个架子从春天搭到一半，我可以带你路过，一点不害臊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But finishing and showing are two different animals. You don't put the last screw in someone else's wall. You just don't.
beats.chinese: 但完工和给人看是两码事。你不能替别人拧最后一颗螺丝。就是不行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the phone over in his hand, screen down, and looks at your notebook instead, calmer now.
beats.chinese: 他把手机在手里翻了个面，屏幕朝下，转而看着你的笔记本，平静了些。

choices.english: Explain you were only asking, not offering to change anything for him.
choices.chinese: 说明只是询问，没有要替他改。

choices.english: Ask whether he'd be willing to show someone his unfinished work at all.
choices.chinese: 问他愿不愿意给人看未完成的东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're right, you know. I've been quoting the whole family and forgetting the customer.
beats.chinese: 你说得对。我一直在给全家做报价，倒把客户本人忘了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He scrolls back through the sketches until he finds the earliest one and holds it up properly this time.
beats.chinese: 他往回翻草图，翻到最早那张，这次正儿八经举起来给你看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Version one. Look — she'd have her whole hand round that. The later ones are tidier on paper and worse for her grip. I knew that. I just let other voices talk me off it.
beats.chinese: 第一版。看——她的手能整个握住。后面几张纸上更工整，握起来却更差。我其实知道，只是让别人的声音把我带偏了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right then. Next time I'm round hers, I'll ask her straight — what matters most, holding it or how it looks from the patio. Her answer, not mine, not her son's.
beats.chinese: 好了。下次去她家，我直接问她——最重要的是握着舒服，还是从露台看着好看。听她的，不是我的，也不是她儿子的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pockets the phone with a small nod, the decision apparently made, and points at your notebook.
beats.chinese: 他把手机收进口袋，微微点头，显然拿定了主意，然后指了指你的笔记本。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good notes take you back to the start. Same as mine just did. Carry on.
beats.chinese: 好笔记能带你回到起点。刚才我这张就是。继续写吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tools? No. Tools are the easy part. I picked the drill, the bits, the fixings months ago. Never once lost sleep over a purchase.
beats.chinese: 工具？不是。工具是最简单的。电钻、钻头、配件，我几个月前就选好了。买东西我从来没失眠过。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs once, short, at himself, and shakes his head.
beats.chinese: 他短促地笑了一声，笑自己，摇了摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What's holding it up is other people's meanings. Four sketches because four people said four things, and I keep trying to fit them all in one rail.
beats.chinese: 卡住我的是别人的意思。四张图，因为四个人说了四样话，我一直想把它们全塞进同一根扶手里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A customer tells you what they want, you build it, done. Family — they don't always know what they want, and you can't invoice them for finding out.
beats.chinese: 客户会告诉你他要什么，你做了，完事。家人——他们不一定知道自己要什么，而你也没法为弄明白这个收钱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He locks the phone and slides it into his jacket, done with it for now, and stretches his legs out on the path.
beats.chinese: 他锁上手机，塞进外套口袋，暂时不管它了，把腿伸到小径上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right then. It'll get drilled when the answer's clear. Not before. Thanks for the nudge — go on with your notes.
beats.chinese: 好了。等答案清楚了再动钻。在那之前不动。多谢你点醒我——继续记你的吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Aye. I know that. Sorry — no, not sorry, just... that came out harder than it needed to.
beats.chinese: 嗯，我知道。抱歉——不，也不是抱歉，只是……那话说得比需要的硬了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He exhales through his nose and relaxes his shoulders, the stiffness going out of him.
beats.chinese: 他从鼻子里呼出一口气，肩膀松了下来，僵硬劲过去了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Truth is, I go tight the second anyone mentions taking over. Even asking sets it off, as you just saw. It's not about you. It's a screwdriver thing.
beats.chinese: 说实话，一有人提接手我就紧张。哪怕只是问问也会，你刚才也看见了。不是针对你。是螺丝刀那类事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My sister's lad offered to 'just do it' while she was shopping once. I said no before he'd finished the sentence. Didn't even think about it. That's the part I can't explain to people.
