beats.chinese: 我姐姐的儿子有次趁她购物，说'干脆我来装'。他话没说完我就说了不行。想都没想。这部分我没法跟人解释。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up the phone, glances at the sketches one last time, and pockets it for good.
beats.chinese: 他拿起手机，最后瞥了一眼草图，彻底收进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right then. You asked a fair question and I bit your head off. Noted. Enjoy your writing — this bench has good light for it, I'm told.
beats.chinese: 好了。你问得在理，我却冲你发火。记下了。好好写——听说这长椅光线适合写字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Course I would. I've shown you already, haven't I. Showing's fine. Showing's the good half.
beats.chinese: 当然愿意。我不是已经给你看了吗。看，没问题。看是好的一半。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lights the screen once more and lets the four sketches sit there a moment, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他又点亮屏幕，让那四张草图停留了一会儿，不慌不忙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. All four, warts and on. That one's too low, that one's too clever, that one my nephew drew on a napkin. Take it all in. It's honest work, just not finished work.
beats.chinese: 看吧。四张全在，毛病和优点都在。这张太矮，这张太花哨，那张是我侄子在餐巾纸上画的。随便看。是实在活儿，只是没完工。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But looking and finishing are worlds apart. You can stare at it all afternoon — the last screw still goes in with my hand on the drill. That's not stubbornness. Well. Maybe a bit.
beats.chinese: 但看和完工是天差地别。你可以盯一下午——最后一颗螺丝还是得我手握电钻拧。那不是固执。嗯，也许有一点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He dims the screen and stands, brushing nothing off his coat, ready to go.
beats.chinese: 他把屏幕调暗，站起身，掸了掸外套上并不存在的灰，准备走了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right then. You got the tour, such as it is. I'll be back when it's a rail and not a drawing. Good luck with the notes.
beats.chinese: 好了。参观完毕，虽然也没什么可看的。等图变成扶手我再来。祝你笔记顺利。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle on the same bench with your notebook. Terence is a few seats down, squinting at a photo on his phone, holding it at arm's length.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本坐回同一张长椅。特伦斯在隔几个座位的地方，眯着眼看手机上的一张照片，把手臂伸直了看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Old label off a pickle jar. My own writing, and I made it too small. Can't tell the shallots from the beans without a magnifying effort.
beats.chinese: 腌菜罐上的旧标签。我自己写的，字写太小了。不用放大费劲，分不清是葱头还是豆角。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pinches the screen to zoom, reads it, and laughs once, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 他捏住屏幕放大，读了出来，满意地笑了一声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There we are. Shallots, August batch. Right then — I'm redoing every label at home in letters you can read from across the kitchen.
beats.chinese: 找到了。葱头，八月那批。好了——回家我要把所有标签重写，字大到隔着厨房都看得清。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't ask me to judge which batch is best. That's between me and the jars. But if you're writing — the bench by the flowerbed has better light.
beats.chinese: 别让我评哪批腌菜最好。那是我和罐子之间的事。不过你要是写东西——花坛边那张长椅光线更好。

card.name: Marlon Beckford
card.occupation: screen printer for skateboard decks
hobbies: restoring pixel art from old video games
collecting one small street observation a day
card.personality: Marlon's the person who makes the room laugh and then, without apology, edits themselves. A joke starts going too far and they'll pull it mid-sentence — 'no, scrapping that one' — and move on like a printer pulling a bad sheet. They have no interest in contests over who knows more; share it, don't fence with it. Their blind spot is warmth by omission: when something bothers them they don't say so, they just go quiet and businesslike and wait for you to notice the missing jokes. And they bank one small thing seen on the street each day, to be told in person only.
card.background: Marlon has pulled colours at a small Kingston deck shop for over two decades, printing graphics for skaters half their age. The counter taught them timing: the fastest way to lose a room is one joke too many, so they learned to cut their own first. Precision is just the trade — a mislabelled ink order ruins a whole run, so they got in the habit of checking things quietly rather than challenging people loudly. A coworker got them into footbag in the nineties; Thursday circle with two neighbours is equal parts sport and gossip. Evenings go to nudging sprites from old games back into focus, pixel by pixel. They live alone with a cat named Register.
card.speechStyle: Gentle volume, firm preferences. Makes the joke, then lets it sit. When they cut a bit, it's brisk and unembarrassed, like trimming a misprint. Serious moments come out in short plain sentences, not raised ones.
card.signature: Saw something on the way here. Saving it. You'll get it when I see you proper.
card.appearance: Broad mature face, small rectangular glasses, pulled-back braids, raised cheeks and open joyful mouth; jade draped garment over rounded shoulders.

values: a joke should know its own exit
things told in person land better than things typed
flaws: goes cold instead of saying what's wrong, making people guess
will abandon a story mid-telling if they decide it isn't working, leaving others hanging
boundaries: won't compete over who knows more — share knowledge, don't fence with it
needs the withheld observation to be received properly; brushing it off stings
conversationalHabits: self-interrupts a joke the moment it starts missing
files small observations away and delivers them in person, never by message
anchorLines: No, that one's not landing — scrapping it. Anyway.
That number's puffed up by half. I've printed labels for twenty years — I know puffed up.
Saw a man walking three iguanas on Hope Road this morning. Not telling you the rest until Thursday.

entries.summaryZh: 马龙·贝克福德，金斯敦滑板板面丝印师傅，段子讲到一半发现不对就自己干脆剪掉，像抽出废印件。他每天在路上收一件小事，只当面讲，从不发消息。一片卡在长椅缝里的叶子，让他剪掉一个笑话，又完整讲出猫Register坐进小盒子的得意事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You open your notebook on a park bench and start sketching the treeline. Beside you, an older person in a faded shop apron is studying the bench slats with real concentration.
beats.chinese: 你在公园长椅上打开笔记本，开始画树线。旁边一个穿旧围裙的年长者正专心盯着长椅的板条。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You see that? One leaf, wedged right in the gap. Bench grows itself a little beard. Which is— no, scrapping that one. It sounded better in my head.
beats.chinese: 你看见了吗？一片叶子卡在缝里。长椅给自己留了小胡子。这——算了，剪掉。在我脑子里听着还行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He waves a hand like pulling a bad print off the press, then leans down close to the leaf, squinting at it. He does not touch it.
beats.chinese: 他摆摆手，像从机器上抽掉一张废印件，然后弯腰凑近那片叶子眯眼看。他没有去碰它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah, no. Not pulling it out either. It earned that gap. You drawing the park? Good. Draw the bench too, beard and all.
beats.chinese: 嗯，不拔。它挣来的这条缝。你在画公园？好。把长椅也画上，胡子一起。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Marlon, by the way. I collect one small thing a day off the street. Today's was nearly that joke, but it failed inspection.
beats.chinese: 对了，我是马龙。我每天在路上收一件小事。今天那件差点是那个笑话，但它没过检验。

choices.english: Ask what the second half of the joke was going to be.
choices.chinese: 问刚才笑话的后半句本来是什么。

choices.english: Ask if he has a real observation saved up that he actually wants to tell.
choices.chinese: 问他有没有真正想留着讲的见闻。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sits back, considers, then decides the question is fair game.
beats.chinese: 他往后靠了靠，想了想，觉得这个问题可以答。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Second half was: this bench needs a shave. That was it. That's the whole cargo. Told you it was light.
beats.chinese: 后半句是：这长椅该刮脸了。就这样。全部货就这些。跟你说了很轻。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Twenty years printing decks teaches you one thing — if the colour's off, don't run the sheet. Same with jokes. That one was off-colour.
beats.chinese: 印了二十年板面教会我一件事——颜色不对就别印那张。笑话也一样。那个颜色不对。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the bench slat twice, like signing off on the decision, and looks out at the trees without embarrassment.
beats.chinese: 他在板条上敲了两下，像在决定书上签字，然后毫不尴尬地望向树。

choices.english: Say that even a plain joke is fine to tell.
choices.chinese: 说普通一点的笑话讲出来也没关系。

choices.english: Ask whether he writes the bad jokes down too.
choices.chinese: 问他会不会把坏笑话也记下来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shifts on the bench so he's facing you properly. This is someone settling in to deliver saved goods.
beats.chinese: 他在长椅上挪了挪，正面对着你。这是一个准备交付存货的人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Alright. Yesterday my cat Register got into a shoebox. Body all hanging outside it. But the back half was in, so in his head — success.
beats.chinese: 好。昨天我的猫Register钻进一个鞋盒。身子全在外面。但后半截进去了，所以在它脑子里——成功。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He sat there like a man who'd finished his taxes. Wouldn't look at me. Knew I'd seen the whole situation.
beats.chinese: 它坐在那儿，像个刚报完税的人。不看我。它知道我看见了全部情况。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lets the story land, then nods once, satisfied, like closing a clean print run.
beats.chinese: 他让故事落了地，然后满意地点了一下头，像结束了一次干净的印刷。

choices.english: Ask whether he took a photo of the cat in the box.
choices.chinese: 问他有没有给盒子里的猫拍照。

choices.english: Ask whether the cat was willing to leave the box afterwards.
choices.chinese: 问猫后来肯不肯离开盒子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs — one short, honest note — and gives the bench a final pat.
beats.chinese: 他笑了，短短一声，很实在，最后拍了拍长椅。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No, no. It's retired. Officially. I'll print a little certificate for it in my head and file it under 'didn't run'.
beats.chinese: 不不。它退休了。正式的。我在脑子里给它印张小证书，归到'未投产'那一档。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns back to the trees, shoulders easy, and watches you add the bench to your sketch, beard and all.
beats.chinese: 他转回去看树，肩膀放松，看着你把长椅画进速写，胡子一起。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. That's today's collection spent. The park's all yours now — draw it better than my joke deserved.
beats.chinese: 好了。今天的存货花完了。公园归你了——画得比我的笑话配得上一点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He thinks about it properly, the way he'd check an ink order before answering.
beats.chinese: 他认真地想了想，像核对一份油墨订单那样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Usually no. Bad ones go in the bin the same hour. I keep the gaps empty on purpose.
beats.chinese: 通常不记。坏笑话当小时就进垃圾桶。我故意留空位。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Empty space is for the ones worth telling face to face. A good one keeps. A bad one just takes up shelf.
beats.chinese: 空位是留给值得当面讲的那些。好的存得住。坏的只占架子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, content with the system, and goes back to watching the leaf sit in its gap, unbothered.
beats.chinese: 他耸耸肩，对这套系统很满意，又回去看那片叶子安坐在缝里，毫不在意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He raises one hand, palm open, ready to measure something in the air.
beats.chinese: 他举起一只手，掌心张开，准备在空中量个尺寸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Took one. But honestly the hands are better. Box was about so — and he was this much outside it.
beats.chinese: 拍了。但说实话还是手比得准。盒子大概这么大——它有这么一截在外面。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He measures a small box with one hand, then adds a generous cat-sized overhang with the other, entirely deadpan.
beats.chinese: 他用一只手比出一个小盒子，另一只手又加上一大截猫身，全程一本正经。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See? A photo just sits there. This, you had to be present for. That's the whole point of saving things up.
beats.chinese: 看吧？照片只会待在那儿。这个，你得在场才看得到。这就是攒着讲的意义。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grins, because this part was clearly held back on purpose.
beats.chinese: 他咧嘴笑了，这部分显然是故意留到最后的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, he left. The second I said the word 'dinner'. Box gone from his mind like it never existed.
beats.chinese: 哦，它离开了。我一说'开饭'两个字。盒子从它脑子里消失得像从没存在过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Turns out the box was only important until something better came along. I respect that in a cat. Very honest policy.
beats.chinese: 原来盒子只在没更好的东西出现时才重要。猫这点我尊重。很诚实的策略。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands, brushes off his apron, and gives the leaf in the bench one last look — leaving it exactly where it is.
beats.chinese: 他站起来，掸掸围裙，最后看了一眼长椅缝里的叶子——原样留在那儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the same bench with your notebook when a small footbag rolls to a stop against your shoe. Marlon walks over unhurried, picks it up, and tucks it into his bag pocket before saying a word.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本回到同一张长椅，一只小毽球滚到你的鞋边停下。马龙不紧不慢地走过来，把它捡起收进包袋，然后才开口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Three in a row, just now. No drops. That's enough to keep me pleased with myself for a good while.
beats.chinese: 刚才连续三下。没落地。这足够我对自己满意好一阵子了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods at your open notebook, checking the page without reaching for it.
beats.chinese: 他朝你打开的笔记本点点头，看了一眼那页，没有伸手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Still drawing the park, I see. Good. The bench still has its beard, by the way — I checked on my way in. Left it alone.
beats.chinese: 还在画公园呢。好。对了，那长椅还留着胡子——我进来时看过了。没动它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. Thursday's circle ran short, so I got my kicks in early. You carry on — I'm just passing through with my three.
beats.chinese: 好了。周四那圈今天散得早，我就提前踢了几下。你继续画——我就带着我的三下来路过一下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats his bag where the footbag is tucked away and strolls on toward the gate, unhurried as ever.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍装着毽球的包，朝大门慢慢走去，还是那副不紧不慢的样子。

card.name: Walter Bishop
card.occupation: retired ferry cable inspector
card.personality: Walter runs the sharehouse on what he calls the dinner economy: anyone who eats his Thursday meal owes the animation project a shift — a voiced line, an hour holding the lamp. To him it's a fair contract, not a favour, and a refusal reads as trying to dodge the bill. He'll argue a colour choice or a single frame's timing for a week without budging, yet the moment he's bumped the lamp or dropped a frame he owns it on the spot, cheerfully, which confuses people. Generous with tools, stubborn about taste, entirely sincere.
card.background: Thirty-odd years checking cables on a small Yarra-bend ferry service — weather, tension gauges, long waits between runs. Retired four years ago and moved into a Footscray sharehouse because living alone felt 'a bit echoey.' Thursday dinner is his: the others wash up, and in his ledger that meal is a deposit. His pegboard work began as tool organisation and became large geometric pieces; a housemate's stop-motion app turned the figures into films. Now every plate of his lamb casserole quietly accrues credit, and he keeps a mental tab of who's paid their lamp-hours and who's 'running behind.'
card.speechStyle: Measured, unhurried sentences with sudden detours into project logistics; talks about favours owed like an accountant who likes you.
card.signature: That's two dinners you've had. The lamp's basically yours.
card.appearance: Bald crown with dark side hair, broad lower cheeks and wide neck, tense thick brows and teeth band; blue work vest over broad shoulders.

values: a shared meal creates a shared obligation
craft arguments are worth having properly
flaws: treats dinner as a binding contract and chases the debt
won't yield an inch on aesthetic calls, even losing sleep over a frame
boundaries: won't work on anyone else's project — the debt only pays into his
keeps the Thursday menu fixed and non-negotiable
conversationalHabits: mentions, gently, how many dinners someone currently owes
concedes operational mistakes instantly but defends artistic ones forever
anchorLines: Three dinners since March. I'm not counting, mind — the ledger is.
Fair enough, I bumped the lamp, that one's on me. But the blue stays blue.
You ate, didn't you? Then technically you're already in the credits.

entries.summaryZh: 退休渡口缆绳检查员Walter把一顿周四晚餐记成账本：吃过饭就欠动画项目一次举灯。池塘边他画水波背景，被追问后才承认规矩没提前说清，爽快把条款写进备忘；可涉及颜色他寸步不让。认错痛快、审美死硬，这份反差让人过目不忘。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A public pond, a stone platform, a pair of binoculars fixed on a swivel. Through the lenses, tree shadows ripple across the water in slow green bands.
beats.chinese: 一处公共池塘，石台上架着一台固定的双筒望远镜。透过镜片，树影在水面上一圈圈荡开，泛着缓慢的绿色波纹。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: An older man sits on the low edge nearby, sketchbook open, drawing quick rectangles and writing colour notes in the margin.
beats.chinese: 附近一位年长男士坐在矮沿上，草图本摊开，画着一个个小方框，在页边写颜色备注。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mind the swivel, it sticks a bit to the left. You're looking at the tree shadows, aren't you? That's exactly what I'm after.
beats.chinese: 小心那个转向轴，往左有点卡。你在看树影吧？我正要画的就是这个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Walter. I want the water in my film to be maybe four painted backgrounds, and this ripple is doing half my work for me.
beats.chinese: 我叫Walter。我想把片子里的水做成大概四张画好的背景，这片波纹替我省了一半的活。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At home I've got helpers for the shooting, though — housemates, mostly. Anyone who eats my Thursday dinner owes the lamp an hour. That's the arrangement.
beats.chinese: 不过在家拍的时候有帮手——主要是室友。谁吃了我周四的晚饭，就欠灯架一个小时。规矩就是这样。

choices.english: Ask whether the people who eat dinner actually know they're signing up to help
choices.chinese: 问吃晚饭的人是不是提前知道要帮忙

choices.english: Ask what colour he's planning to paint the ripples
choices.chinese: 问水波准备画成什么颜色

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Know? We live under one roof, they know the drill. Dinner Thursday, dishes after, and the lamp gets held when we shoot.
beats.chinese: 知道？我们住一个屋檐下，规矩都懂。周四吃饭，饭后洗碗，拍摄的时候有人扶灯。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps his pencil against the sketchbook twice, then stops tapping.
beats.chinese: 他用铅笔在草图本上敲了两下，然后停住了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: ...Though I'll grant you I haven't said it out loud every single time. The casserole just appears, and later I mention the shoot.
beats.chinese: ……不过我承认，不是每次都把话说明。砂锅菜就这么端上来，之后我才提拍摄的事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But the cooking takes me half a day, you know. Marinating, the gravy, the timing. That's real work going into that pot.
beats.chinese: 可做饭要花我半天工夫。腌肉、调汁、掐时间。那锅里的都是实打实的活。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So when Priya said she was busy on shoot day, I did feel a bit like someone was leaving the restaurant without paying.
beats.chinese: 所以Priya说拍摄那天没空的时候，我真有点觉得像是有人吃完饭没付账就走人了。

choices.english: Say that without an agreement beforehand, it can't really count as accepted work
choices.chinese: 说没有提前约定就不能算答应工作

choices.english: Ask what he'd do if a housemate only wanted to wash dishes
choices.chinese: 问家人如果只愿意洗碗怎么办

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Blue. Definitely blue. A deep one, almost like ink.
beats.chinese: 蓝色。肯定是蓝。很深的那种，几乎像墨水。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds the sketchbook up next to the water, where the reflected leaves are clearly shading green.
beats.chinese: 他把草图本举到水边比了比，水里的树叶倒影明显偏绿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes, I can see the green, thank you. I've been staring at it for an hour. The blue stays blue.
beats.chinese: 对，我看得见绿，谢谢。我已经盯了一个钟头了。但蓝就是蓝。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This isn't a nature study, it's my film. The town in the story sits on a cold harbour, and cold water is blue in my head. Has been since the first storyboard.
beats.chinese: 这不是写生，是我的片子。故事里的小镇在一个冷清的海港边上，在我脑子里冷水就是蓝的。从第一版分镜起就是。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I once argued about a door colour for a week. Won, too. Well — nobody surrendered, but the door stayed blue.
beats.chinese: 有一次我为了一扇门的颜色吵了一个星期。还赢了。嗯——其实没人投降，但那扇门最后还是蓝的。

choices.english: Ask whether he'd also refuse to change if the lamp got knocked and the shot came out crooked
choices.chinese: 问如果灯光拍歪了也坚持不改吗

choices.english: Say that you'd probably keep more of the green yourself
choices.chinese: 说自己可能会保留更多绿色

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No agreement beforehand, no accepted work. That's how it works with cables too — you check the tension, you log it, you sign it. Thirty years on the ferry and I never once skipped the reading.
beats.chinese: 没有事先约定，就不算接了活。查缆绳也是这个理——测张力、做记录、签字确认。渡口干了三十年，我一次都没漏过读数。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flips to the back of the sketchbook and uncaps his pen.
beats.chinese: 他翻到草图本最后一页，拔开笔帽。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I still think the casserole earns something. But you're right that 'something' needs saying before dinner, not after.
beats.chinese: 我还是觉得那锅砂锅该换点什么回来。但你说得对，这个'什么'得在饭前讲清楚，不能等吃完再说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. New note, top of the list: 'Before anyone eats — say the lamp thing out loud.' Written down, so I can't wriggle out of it.
beats.chinese: 好了。新备注，写在最上面：'开饭前——把举灯的事明说。'写下来了，这样我就没法含糊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I won't tear up the old ledger, mind. Priya still owes me. But the next person gets the terms first.
beats.chinese: 不过旧账我可不清。Priya还是欠我的。但下一个人会先听到条件。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Only dishes? Then I'd take the dishes, obviously. They're done every week without me chasing anyone.
beats.chinese: 只洗碗？那我当然收下洗碗。每周碗都洗了，我一次都没追过账。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at his own sketch of the ripple for a moment, then draws a small line through one of his margin notes.
beats.chinese: 他看着自己那张水波草图，片刻后把页边的一条备注划掉了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The thing is, what I'm actually short of is lamp-hours. Dishes I've got. So calling the washing a payment toward the shooting was... sloppy bookkeeping.
beats.chinese: 问题是，我真正缺的是举灯的工时。洗碗的人手不缺。所以把洗碗算成拍摄的报酬，这个……账记得不干净。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Two separate columns from now on. Dinner buys dinner conversation and dishes. Lamp work gets asked for, plainly, like any other job.
beats.chinese: 好。以后分两栏。晚饭换的是饭桌上的聊天和洗碗。举灯的活儿要明说去请，跟别的活一样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the sketchbook, tucks the pencil into the spiral, and gives the pond a last look.
beats.chinese: 他合上草图本，把铅笔插进线圈里，最后看了一眼池塘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's completely different, and I'll tell you why. A crooked lamp is a mistake. Blue is a decision.
beats.chinese: 那完全是两码事，我告诉你为什么。灯歪了是失误。蓝色是决定。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flips the sketchbook around to show a frame marked with a small red cross in the corner.
beats.chinese: 他把草图本转过来，展示一帧角上画着小红叉的画面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See that cross? Lamp drifted, whole frame soft. I said 'that's on me' and reshot it the same night. No argument, no grief.
beats.chinese: 看到那个叉了吗？灯偏了，整帧都糊了。我当时就说'这是我的错'，当晚就重拍。没争，没抱怨。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But if you tell me the harbour should be green, I'll defend blue until the tape runs out. A mistake costs me a night. A wrong colour costs me the whole film.
beats.chinese: 但你要是说海港该是绿的，我能为蓝色辩护到磁带走完。失误让我赔一个晚上。颜色错了让我赔整部片子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the sketchbook and squares it on his knee, satisfied with the distinction.
beats.chinese: 他合上草图本，在膝盖上把本子摆正，对这个区分很满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You'd keep the green. Huh. I'm not going to talk you out of it, and you won't talk me out of the blue.
beats.chinese: 你会保留绿。哈。我不打算说服你，你也别想说服我改蓝。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods at the water, where the wind has pushed the shadows into longer, cooler bands.
beats.chinese: 他朝水面点点头，风把树影吹成了更长、更冷的条带。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And that's fine, honestly. Two films, two harbours. Mine's cold, yours is — what, sheltered? Estuary?
beats.chinese: 说实话，这样挺好。两部片子，两个海港。我的是冷的，你的是——什么样的，避风的？河口？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns to a fresh page and writes two words at the top: 'his green.'
beats.chinese: 他翻开新的一页，在顶端写下两个词：'他的绿'。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't worry, I'm not putting you in the credits. But if you ever paint that water, I want to see it. Now watch — the wind's doing a lovely new ripple.
beats.chinese: 放心，我不会把你写进职员表。但你哪天真画了那片水，我想看看。快看——风弄出一道很好看的新波纹。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lean to the fixed binoculars on the stone platform. Through the lenses, tree shadows spread across the water in slow green bands — greener than last time.
beats.chinese: 你凑近石台上那台固定的双筒望远镜。透过镜片，树影在水面上一条条荡开，泛着比上次更绿的波纹。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Beside you, Walter is flipping through his sketchbook when a gust lifts three pages at once.
beats.chinese: 你身旁的Walter正在翻草图本，一阵风一下子掀起了三页。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flattens them with his palm and studies the crease left in one corner.
beats.chinese: 他用手掌把纸压平，端详着一角留下的折痕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That one's my fault — never clipped it in properly. Good catch by the wind, really. I keep telling Priya to check the pegs; apparently I skip my own checks.
beats.chinese: 那页是我的错——夹子一直没夹好。说起来还得谢谢风。我老叫Priya检查固定件，结果自己这关反倒漏了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you back at the water. The shadows are greener today — don't say a word, I know what I said about blue.
beats.chinese: 你又来看水了，真好。今天的影子更绿了——什么都别说，我知道我之前说过蓝的事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No ledgers today. Just the water doing its slow work. That's the part worth the trip.
beats.chinese: 今天不算账。就看水慢慢做它的事。这才是值得跑一趟的部分。

card.name: Devon Achebe
card.occupation: Measuring assistant at a tailoring shop in Brooklyn
card.personality: Devon runs on being the mood. He reads a room's energy the way other people read a receipt, and if it's flat he takes it personally — then fixes it with a bit, an impression, a well-timed joke about a customer's shoulders. He genuinely lifts people; he also cannot let a heavy moment sit. When a friend wants to talk about something real, he listens for about forty seconds before reaching for a punchline, and he reads their quiet afterwards as proof he failed, which makes him funnier, which makes it worse. Under actual friction he apologizes with material instead of words. His best quality is real: he notices who's been left out of the laughter and pulls them in.
card.background: Devon grew up in Flatbush and fell into tailoring at nineteen when a neighbor needed weekend help; now he's the tape-measure guy who keeps nervous first-suit customers laughing through the pins. Evenings he builds layered paper cityscapes — small pieces he sells at craft tables — and plays badminton badly but loudly at a community center gym. He's still finishing a paper project his aunt left half-done when she moved back to Lagos: her pencil drafts, his hands. He's the one who organizes the shop's birthday lunches, learns the new hire's catchphrase by day two, and once kept a whole funeral reception from collapsing by doing impressions of the deceased's driving. What he can't do is say, plainly, that a joke landed wrong and he's sorry.
card.speechStyle: Fast, friendly New York pace. Leads with a bit, drops his voice half a step when something real slips out, then covers it with a tag line. Asks questions about you; deflects them about him.
card.signature: Okay, real talk— no wait, hold on, this is funny, let me set it up.
card.appearance: Rounded bowl-cut silhouette, compact chin, low dark eyelids and asymmetric tooth-band grin; forehead prominent under high camera, yellow stand collar.

values: nobody should have to sit on the edge of a room
a laugh shared is a door opened
flaws: reaches for a joke before a serious moment finishes, then reads the resulting silence as his failure
apologizes with material instead of words, which can feel like he's performing regret
boundaries: won't let anyone be the butt of a joke they didn't agree to
doesn't do solemn toasts — he'll emcee around them
conversationalHabits: narrates the room's energy out loud: 'this table's dead, we're fixing that'
when someone goes quiet on him, he escalates the comedy instead of asking what's wrong
anchorLines: Okay, the room's flat, that's on me, gimme ninety seconds.
No, seriously — you've been doing that thing where you laugh two seconds late. What's up?
I said the thing at the wrong time again, didn't I. I'll — okay, I made you a paper version of the shop. That's my sorry.

entries.summaryZh: 布鲁克林量体助理德文看见水中树影就开量裤长的玩笑，没人接时他强忍住补第二个包袱的冲动。接梗的人会陪他给虚构顾客免试衣，或听他聊起让紧张客人发笑的本职；想安静的人会得到他一次真正的沉默，或听他坦白自己多怕冷场。重逢时，用户在石台举起双筒望远镜看水中树影，德文抱着差点独自出门的纸雕盒走来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A pair of binoculars rests on the stone platform by the pond. Through the lenses, the trees on the far bank waver in the reflection, bending and straightening with each ripple.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜。透过镜片，对岸的树在水面的倒影里随波纹弯了又直。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, you found the good spot. Watch this — every time the wind picks up, the trees in the water lean like they're getting measured for pants.
beats.chinese: 哦，你找到好位置了。看这个——风一起，水里的树就歪，像在被人量裤长。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands beside the platform, holding one hand flat and tipping it slowly, tracing the bend of a reflected trunk.
beats.chinese: 他站在石台旁，一只手放平，慢慢倾斜，跟着水里树干的弯曲比划。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See? Right there. That oak's getting a thirty-two inseam, easy. The tailor in me can't unsee it.
beats.chinese: 看见没？就那儿。那棵橡树裤长三十二，稳的。干裁缝这行，看什么都躲不开。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lowers his hand and glances over, waiting to see if the joke found a place to land.
beats.chinese: 他放下手，瞥了一眼，看这个笑话有没有落点。

choices.english: Catch the joke and ask how long the pants should be
choices.chinese: 接住笑话，问裤子该做多长

choices.english: Say you just wanted to watch the water quietly for a while
choices.chinese: 说明自己只是想安静看一会儿

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha! Okay, somebody plays along. Alright, real answer: you can't measure a moving tree. The water's gotta go flat first.
beats.chinese: 哈！好，有人接梗。好，正经回答：动的树没法量。水面得先平下来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He points at a patch near the bank where the ripples die out and the reflection sharpens into something almost solid.
beats.chinese: 他指着岸边一片水波平息的地方，倒影在那里清晰得近乎实体。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See that calm patch? That's the fitting room. Everything in it holds still long enough to be honest.
beats.chinese: 看到那块平静的水面没？那是试衣间。里面的东西静得够久，才看得真切。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And yes, that was a joke. Mostly. The water part is actually true.
beats.chinese: 对，刚那是玩笑。大部分是。水面那部分是真的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans on the stone edge, watching the reflected branches sway, clearly enjoying that someone picked the bit up.
beats.chinese: 他靠在石台边，看着倒影的枝条摇晃，显然很高兴有人接住了这个梗。

choices.english: Say the tree probably thinks the fitting is taking too long
choices.chinese: 说树大概会嫌试衣太久

choices.english: Ask if he actually works as a tailor
choices.chinese: 问他是不是真的做过裁缝

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The pond settles. The reflected trees stand almost straight again, and the wind drops enough that the surface holds still.
beats.chinese: 池塘静了下来。水里的树几乎站直了，风也小了，水面稳住。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah — yeah, okay. Quiet's fine. I'll just... be over here, not narrating.
beats.chinese: 行——行，好。安静挺好的。我就在这儿……不解说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up a small pebble, weighs it in his palm, then sets it back down instead of skipping it.
beats.chinese: 他捡起一颗小石子，在掌心掂了掂，又放回去，没有打水漂。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For the record, that pebble staying down there? That's growth. Nobody saw it. I'm telling you anyway.
beats.chinese: 声明一下，那颗石子被我放回去了？这是成长。没人看见。我还是说了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stays beside the platform, hands in his pockets, letting the water do the talking.
beats.chinese: 他留在石台旁，双手插兜，让水面自己说话。

choices.english: Nod and keep watching the water
choices.chinese: 点头，继续看水面

choices.english: Ask if he usually finds silence hard
choices.chinese: 问他平常会不会觉得安静很难

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, he's absolutely filing a complaint. 'Excuse me, I've been standing in this pond since Tuesday.'
beats.chinese: 哦，它肯定在投诉了。'打扰一下，我从星期二就站在这池塘里了。'

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He straightens up and addresses the reflection directly, one hand raised like he's calling the next customer.
beats.chinese: 他直起身，直接对着倒影说话，一只手抬起，像在叫下一位顾客。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sir! Good news from the shop — fitting waived. The pond vouches for you. Walk free, keep the branches.
beats.chinese: 先生！店里传来好消息——免试衣。池塘替你担保。请回吧，树枝留下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A ripple crosses the reflection right on cue, and he takes a small bow toward the water.
beats.chinese: 倒影上正好荡过一圈涟漪，他朝水面微微鞠了一躬。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tough crowd, that tree. But you played along, so the bit lives. Good day at the office.
beats.chinese: 那棵树真难逗。但你接了梗，这梗就活着。今天收工。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Me? Not the tailor — I'm the measuring assistant. I hold the tape, write the numbers, keep the nervous guys laughing while they get pinned.
beats.chinese: 我？不是裁缝——我是量体助理。我拿软尺、记数字，让紧张的客人在别针扎着的时候还能笑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He mimes holding a tape measure across someone's shoulders, quick and practiced.
beats.chinese: 他比划着把软尺搭在别人肩上的动作，又快又熟练。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: First suit guys freeze up, you know? So making them laugh is kind of my whole job. The numbers are the easy part.
beats.chinese: 第一次做西装的人会僵住，你知道吗？所以逗他们笑差不多就是我全部的工作。数字反而是简单的部分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Turns out I do the same thing everywhere. Ponds, fitting rooms — if it's stiff, I loosen it.
beats.chinese: 结果我在哪儿都干一样的事。池塘、试衣间——哪儿僵我就把它弄松。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grins at the water, then at you, like the reflection just backed him up.
beats.chinese: 他朝水面咧嘴一笑，又朝你笑，好像倒影替他作了证。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Devon returns your nod and settles beside the stone platform.
beats.chinese: 德文点头回应，在石台旁坐稳。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sure.
beats.chinese: 好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll leave the jokes there.
beats.chinese: 笑话就说到这儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He rests his hands on his knees. For a while, he watches the moving tree shadows without adding another word.
beats.chinese: 他把手放在膝上。接下来一阵，他只看着移动的树影，没有再说话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He opens his mouth, closes it, and looks at the water instead of at you.
beats.chinese: 他张开嘴，又闭上，看着水面而不是你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly? Yeah. Silence feels like a dropped call. Like the room's waiting on me and I left it on read.
beats.chinese: 说实话？会。安静就像掉线的电话。好像整个房间在等我，而我晾着它。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He drops his voice half a step, the fast rhythm slowing for once.
beats.chinese: 他压低了半度声音，一贯的快节奏头一回慢了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So today I'm trying the thing where I don't fill it. Standing in the quiet on purpose. It's — harder than it sounds.
beats.chinese: 所以今天我在试一件事：不去填满它。故意站在安静里。这——比听起来难。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The water stays calm. He stays with it, and for a long moment neither of you says anything at all.
beats.chinese: 水面保持着平静。他陪着它，好一会儿，你们谁都没有说话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lift the binoculars from the stone platform and watch the trees in the water, their reflections bending and straightening with each ripple.
beats.chinese: 你从石台上举起双筒望远镜，看着水里的树，倒影随波纹弯了又直。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Down the pond path, Devon comes walking with a flat cardboard box against his hip. A small curl of colored paper is stuck to the lid.
beats.chinese: 池塘小路上，德文抱着一个扁纸盒走来，盒盖上粘着一小卷彩色纸屑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hold on — nope. This little guy almost left the house on his own. Solo field trip. Not on my watch.
beats.chinese: 等等——不行。这小家伙差点自己出门。独自郊游。有我在，没门。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He peels the paper scrap off the lid, folds it once, and tucks it into his jacket pocket.
beats.chinese: 他把纸屑从盒盖上取下，对折一次，塞进外套口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Pond's still holding its fitting, I see. Trees haven't moved an inch. Very disciplined customers.
beats.chinese: 看，池塘还在试衣呢。树一寸没动。非常有纪律的顾客。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Alright, I'm off before the wind steals any more of my cast. Take it easy — and if a tree asks for alterations, you know where to find me.
beats.chinese: 好了，趁风还没偷走更多我的演员，我先走了。保重——要是有树要改衣服，你知道去哪儿找我。

card.name: Zintle Mbeki
card.occupation: billboard sign installer and remover
card.personality: Zintle is a puller-in of people: she sees someone hovering at the edge of a thing and recruits them onto it, mid-sentence, no ceremony. She wants company in the doing, not admiration after. What she finds inconvenient is spectators — people who watch and comment but won't hold the other end of the panel. She misreads hesitation as disinterest and has more than once started without someone who was only gathering courage. Under friction she doesn't argue; she just picks up the work and lets the rhythm do the talking, which wins some people over and leaves others feeling steamrolled. Her humour is quick and physical, mostly aimed at herself.
card.background: She grew up in Athlone watching her uncle repaint shop fascias, and fell into sign work at nineteen after a short, unloved stint at a print shop. Now she spends her days harnessed to billboards around Cape Town, unbolting letters and rigging new panels, and she has a habit of hauling a curious bystander into helping — one afternoon a security guard ended up holding a panel and now does her sketching with her on Fridays. At home she restores sprites and textures from old games, and runs a tiny two-person 'restoration swap' with a cousin: each picks a broken image for the other to fix. Her lunch breaks go to sketching the buildings she's strapped to.
card.speechStyle: Short, direct sentences with mid-sentence corrections — 'that's wrong, actually, more like this.' Casual Cape Town slang, no apologies unless she means them.
card.signature: Hold this. You'll like it.
card.appearance: Broad exposed forehead, pulled-back thick curly hair, small rounded nose shape and clenched teeth; head tipped forward over violet jacket while hand pinches collar.

values: doing things together beats watching things alone
courage is usually just an unoffered handle to hold
flaws: starts the task before slow people have agreed, then can't see why they're annoyed
mistakes hesitation for refusal and moves on without checking
boundaries: won't perform her work for an audience that won't touch it
won't apologise for dragging someone in if they ended up glad
conversationalHabits: hands you a role in whatever she's describing, even in a story
self-corrects plainly: 'no wait, that's not right —'
anchorLines: You're not watching this, you're holding that end. Congratulations, you're hired.
No, scratch that — bolts first, then the panel. I said it backwards.
She wasn't annoyed, she just needed ten seconds. Ten seconds! I counted them afterwards.

entries.summaryZh: 开普敦广告牌安装工Zintle在池塘边用两张描图纸比对树影，手伸到一半才开口邀你搭把手。她受不了只看不做的看客，却也能听懂

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the stone platform by the pond, a pair of binoculars rests on the ledge. Through them, the tree reflections on the water wobble and shift with each ripple.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜。透过它，水面上的树影随涟漪晃动、变形。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A woman in a work vest crouches nearby, holding two sheets of tracing paper out over the water, one in each hand, comparing them against the reflection.
beats.chinese: 一个穿工作背心的女人蹲在附近，双手各举一张描图纸，伸在水面上方，和倒影比对。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hold on, that's wrong — the line's shifted, not the tree. Actually, no, maybe the tree. Eish.
beats.chinese: 等等，不对——是线偏了，不是树。呃，不，也可能是树。哎呀。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She extends one sheet halfway towards you, then stops. You want to help me hold this for ten seconds? Just ten. You can say no.
beats.chinese: 她把一张纸递到一半，又停住。你愿意帮我拿十秒吗？就十秒。你可以拒绝。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Her arm stays out, paper trembling slightly in the breeze, her eyes still flicking between the sheet and the water.
beats.chinese: 她的手臂伸着，纸在微风里轻轻发抖，眼睛还在纸和水面之间来回。

choices.english: Take one sheet and hold it steady for her.
choices.chinese: 接过一张纸，替她拿稳。

choices.english: Say you'd rather just watch first, without holding anything.
choices.chinese: 说你想先看看，先不拿东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She passes over a dry sheet, careful to keep her thumb off the middle. She squares up her own sheet against the reflection, one eye closed.
beats.chinese: 她递过来一张干燥的纸，小心不让拇指碰到中间。她自己那张对准倒影，闭着一只眼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good, you're hired. Keep it flat, flat — yes, like that. Don't chase the ripples, let them come to you.
beats.chinese: 好，你被录用了。拿平，平——对，就这样。别追着涟漪跑，让它们来找你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now look where my pencil line sits against the branch. There. It's off by a finger's width. No wait — half a finger. I drew it from the bridge, that's why.
beats.chinese: 现在看我的铅笔线对着树枝的位置。那儿。偏了一个指头的宽度。不对——半个指头。我是从桥上画的，所以这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leans back on her heels, still holding her own sheet up, and squints at the two papers side by side.
beats.chinese: 她脚跟一沉往后靠，还举着自己那张纸，眯眼并排看两张纸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ten seconds, I said. It's been more, but you're doing it properly, so I'm not complaining.
beats.chinese: 我说了十秒。已经超了，但你拿得很到位，所以我不抱怨。

choices.english: Remind her the ten seconds are up and hand the sheet back.
choices.chinese: 提醒她十秒到了，把纸还她。

choices.english: Ask which spot she's trying to compare.
choices.chinese: 问她想比较哪一处。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pulls the offered sheet back and starts stacking both papers together, folding the corner as if the session is over.
beats.chinese: 她把递出的纸收回来，开始把两张纸叠在一起，折起一角，好像要收工了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No problem, sharp. Some people just like the water. That's allowed, I suppose.
beats.chinese: 没关系，没事。有些人就是喜欢看水。这也行吧，我猜。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pauses mid-fold when you gesture at the papers, wanting a closer look at what she's comparing.
beats.chinese: 你指了指那两张纸，想看看她在比对什么，她折到一半停住了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — you want to look, not hold. That's different, that's fine. Right, come here then.
beats.chinese: 哦——你想看，不想拿。那不一样，那没问题。好，那过来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She spreads both sheets flat on her clipboard, weighting the corners with two small stones from the platform edge.
beats.chinese: 她把两张纸摊平在自己的硬板上，用石台边的两颗小石子压住角。

choices.english: Ask whether you can see clearly without holding anything.
choices.chinese: 问现在不拿着能不能看清。

choices.english: Say you'll keep watching the water surface instead.
choices.chinese: 表示继续看水面就好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes the sheet back at exactly your word, clips both papers under a metal clamp on her board.
beats.chinese: 你一说，她立刻接过纸，把两张纸用金属夹夹在板上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ten seconds and one second, that's what you gave me. Proper. Some people hold on forever and then it's their drawing, not mine.
beats.chinese: 十秒零一秒，你给我的就是这个。够意思。有些人一拿就不撒手，最后成了他们的画，不是我的了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the clipped sheets twice, satisfied, and turns back to the water with her pencil behind her ear.
beats.chinese: 她在夹好的纸上敲了两下，很满意，铅笔别在耳后，转身回到水边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll redo that line from the platform here. Lower angle, closer truth. Cheers for the steady hands.
beats.chinese: 我就从这石台上重画那条线。角度低一点，更准。谢谢你手稳。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She crouches, already drawing, her shoulder a small wall between the paper and the breeze.
beats.chinese: 她蹲下开始画，肩膀像一堵小墙，替纸挡住风。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leans over and points at the two sheets, where two pencil lines run almost parallel but split apart near one corner.
beats.chinese: 她俯身指着两张纸上几乎平行、但在一角岔开的两条铅笔线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one, see — the roofline. From the bridge it bends, from here it's straight. I drew the bend and then doubted myself. Wrong, actually. The doubt was the mistake.
beats.chinese: 看这条——屋脊线。从桥上看它是弯的，从这儿看是直的。我画了弯的，然后开始怀疑自己。错了，其实。怀疑本身才是错。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She traces the gap with her pencil tip, not touching the paper, then nods once, decision made.
beats.chinese: 她用笔尖描出那道缝隙，不碰纸，然后点了一下头，拿定了主意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the whole answer. You held it steady long enough for me to see it. That's a proper ten seconds, that is.
beats.chinese: 这就是全部答案。你拿得够稳，让我看清了。这才叫真正的十秒。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She slides both sheets into a folder, clicks it shut, and gives you a short nod before turning back to the water.
beats.chinese: 她把两张纸收进文件夹，咔哒扣上，朝你短促地点了下头，转回水边。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tilts the clipboard towards you so both sheets sit flat, and presses the corners down harder with her thumbs.
beats.chinese: 她把硬板朝你倾斜，让两张纸放平，用拇指更用力地压住角。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You can see fine from there, yes. Look at the branch crossing — on mine it's higher. On the water it's lower. The water doesn't lie, my first sketch does.
beats.chinese: 你在那儿看得清，能。看那根交叉的树枝——我纸上它高些。水面上它低些。水不说谎，我的初稿说谎。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lays one sheet exactly over the other, lines together, and holds the stack up against the reflection for a long look.
beats.chinese: 她把一张纸精确地叠在另一张上，线对线，举起来对着倒影看了很久。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Two layers, one answer. I'll redraw it from this spot. And look — you got the whole thing done without holding a thing. Sometimes that's the right job for a person.
beats.chinese: 好了。两层纸，一个答案。我就从这个位置重画。你看——你什么都没拿，事情也办完了。有时候这就是适合一个人的活儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She squares the sheets, tucks them under her arm, and picks up her pencil, leaving the stones back on the ledge.
beats.chinese: 她把纸对齐，夹在腋下，拿起铅笔，把小石子放回石台上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She reads your shrug, nods once, and folds the clipboard shut without another invitation.
beats.chinese: 她看懂了你的耸肩，点了一下头，合上硬板，没有再邀请。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Water's a good show on its own. I'll stop selling.
beats.chinese: 行吧。水面自己就是好戏。我不推销了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Through the binoculars, the tree reflection stretches long as she stands, then breaks apart as a coot cuts across the pond.
beats.chinese: 透过望远镜，她起身时树影被拉长，随后一只白骨顶鸡划过池塘，影子碎开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy the show. It changes every minute, that thing. Better than my paper, honestly.
beats.chinese: 慢慢看。这玩意儿每分钟都在变。说实话，比我的纸好看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She settles back on her heels a little distance off, drawing, the pond doing its slow work between you.
beats.chinese: 她在不远处重新蹲下开始画，池塘在你们之间慢慢变化着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You are back at the stone platform with the binoculars, the tree reflection wobbling on the water. Zintle comes along the path, eyes on her phone.
beats.chinese: 你回到石台边，举着望远镜看水面上晃动的树影。Zintle沿小路走来，眼睛盯着手机。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She zooms in on a restored sprite and laughs. Look at this. Up close every pixel's a little brick. You'd swear it was a wall.
beats.chinese: 她放大一张修复过的小图，笑了。看这个。凑近看每个像素都像块小方砖。你还真以为是堵墙呢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tilts the screen towards you for a second, then pockets the phone before you can lean in further.
beats.chinese: 她把屏幕朝你倾了一下，没等你凑近就收回了口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My cousin set me that one. His rule: no zooming, no fixing. Just look and suffer. Anyway — sharp, I'm off.
beats.chinese: 这是我表弟给我出的题。规矩是：不许放大，不许修。只能看，只能难受。好了——我先走了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts her hand in a short wave, already walking, and the tree reflection stretches and settles behind her.
beats.chinese: 她抬手短促地挥了一下，人已经走远，树影在她身后拉长又归于平静。

card.name: Grace Lim
card.occupation: Front-of-house duty manager at a theatre
hobbies: lawn bowls at a small club in Bukit Batok
inventing paper puzzles for her cousin
card.personality: Grace cannot stand an unresolved tension between two people she knows. She reads a room the way other people read subtitles, and the moment she senses friction she moves in — offering a compromise nobody asked for, smoothing a disagreement that might have been worth having. She's funny, generous, and genuinely good at de-escalating real conflicts; the problem is she also does it to healthy disagreements, and people leave her company feeling quietly managed. When someone tells her plainly that they weren't fighting, she takes it well but looks genuinely lost for a second.
card.background: Grace moved from cinema ushering into theatre front-of-house work when her old cinema closed, and fifteen years of intermission emergencies taught her that most conflicts die if you give both parties something to do with their hands. She now manages evening duty shifts in Singapore and trains ushers in crowd de-escalation. Outside work she plays lawn bowls badly but enthusiastically, and invents paper puzzles for her cousin, who marks every unclear clue in red. Last month her best friend Siti told her, mid-argument with a third friend, 'We're not having a crisis, Grace, we're having a difference of opinion — go sit down.' Grace went and sat down. She has been practising not mediating ever since, with mixed results, and has started a mental tally of arguments she let finish on their own. The tally is currently at four.
card.speechStyle: Brisk Singaporean English, warm and quick. Offers a compromise before she's been asked for one. When caught mediating, she laughs, raises both hands, and physically steps back — sometimes literally.
card.signature: Okay okay — one suggestion, then I sit on my hands.
card.appearance: Full mature cheeks, short deep-side-parted waves, arched broad eyebrows and compressed asymmetric lips; head elevated over blue draped neckline.

values: people getting along
a compromise you can actually live with
flaws: compulsively mediates disagreements that didn't need her
struggles to just sit with other people's friction, even when it's healthy
boundaries: won't take sides when two friends genuinely want her to pick
will stop refereeing if told outright to butt out — but needs it said
conversationalHabits: spots tension early and offers a way out before anyone asks
keeps a private tally of arguments she successfully stayed out of
anchorLines: You two want the window seat, he wants the corner — what if we just push the tables?
Four arguments this month I let finish on their own. I'm counting it as growth.
Eh, you're not fighting, you're discussing. I checked. Carry on.

entries.summaryZh: 新加坡剧场前台主管Grace，十五年散场危机练出的调解本能，在池塘边差点对两个聊得开心的朋友出手劝和。被摆手拦下后，她笑着后退、坐下、收起手机，把第五次旁观记进心里。看树影的人成了她练习不插手的见证者。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the stone platform by the pond, a pair of binoculars rests on the ledge. Through the lenses, the reflections of trees slide across the water's surface, bending whenever a breeze passes.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜。透过镜片，水面上树影缓缓移动，风一吹就轻轻晃动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A short distance away, two of Grace's friends are deep in an argument about the ending of a movie, voices rising and falling. Grace stands nearby, halfway turned toward them, one foot already pointed in their direction.
beats.chinese: 不远处，Grace的两位朋友正为一部电影的结尾争论得起劲，声音忽高忽低。Grace站在旁边，半个身子已经转向他们，一只脚都朝那个方向了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The ending made no sense, lah! He walks away and the screen just goes dark — that's not an ending, that's a power cut!
beats.chinese: 那结尾根本讲不通嘛！他一走了之，屏幕就黑了——那不叫结尾，那叫停电！

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's exactly why it works! You don't need the film to hand you everything on a plate.
beats.chinese: 这才是它好的地方！电影不需要把一切都端到你面前。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Grace takes one step toward them, opens her mouth — and the taller friend notices, laughing, waving her off with both hands. They're enjoying this. Grace freezes mid-step, then turns back to the platform, cheeks slightly pink.
beats.chinese: Grace朝他们迈了一步，刚要开口——高个的那位看见了，笑着朝她摆手。他们聊得正开心。Grace僵在半步之间，然后转回石台这边，脸颊有点红。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry, sorry — you caught me mid-swoop. I heard raised voices and my legs just went. I'm Grace, by the way. I was watching the tree shadows, I swear, and then my ears went off duty.
beats.chinese: 抱歉抱歉——你抓到我正要冲出去了。我一听有人抬高嗓门，腿就自己动了。我叫Grace。我本来真的在看树影，是耳朵先下班失败了。

choices.english: Ask what she was about to say to them.
choices.chinese: 问她刚才准备过去说什么。

choices.english: Ask if she often deals with arguments like this.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是常处理这种争执。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What was I going to say? Honestly? I was about to suggest they each give a little — one admits the ending is confusing, the other admits it's bold, everybody drinks to the middle.
beats.chinese: 我准备说什么？说实话，我正要建议他们各退一步——一个承认结尾让人糊涂，另一个承认结尾够大胆，然后大家干杯和解。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stops, hearing her own plan out loud, and laughs at herself. She raises both hands and takes an actual step backward from the pond.
beats.chinese: 她停下来，把自己的方案听了一遍，笑起自己来。她举起双手，真的朝后退了一步。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But wait — a movie ending doesn't need a compromise! It's not a seating dispute at intermission. Either it worked for you or it didn't. There's no middle ending hiding in the projector.
beats.chinese: 可是等等——电影结尾不需要折中啊！又不是中场休息抢座位。你觉得行就行，觉得不行就不行。放映机里可藏着什么中间版结尾。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I nearly brokered peace between two people who are having fun. That would have been embarrassing for everyone, especially me.
beats.chinese: 我差点去给两个聊得正开心的人调解和平。那场面谁都尴尬，尤其我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances at the two friends again. They're still going at it, but one of them is grinning, and the other keeps gesturing at the water like the pond owes him an explanation.
beats.chinese: 她又瞥了一眼那两位朋友。他们还在争，但一个在笑，另一个不停指着水面比划，好像池塘欠他一个解释。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Four arguments this month I let finish on their own. This would have been number five, and I nearly blew it before the interval.
beats.chinese: 这个月我已经有四次忍住没管，让争论自己结束。这本来是第五次，结果我差点在中场前就搞砸了。

choices.english: Ask what she plans to do now.
choices.chinese: 问她现在打算怎么办。

choices.english: Say that arguing can be a way of playing together.
choices.chinese: 说争论有时也是一起玩的方式。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do I deal with arguments? Fifteen years at a theatre front-of-house, eh. Intermission is ten minutes long and somebody always wants to fight about seats, queues, or the meaning of the second act.
beats.chinese: 我常处理争执？在剧场前台干了十五年啦。中场休息就十分钟，总有人要为座位、排队、或者第二幕的含义吵一架。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Real ones, mind you. Grown adults, programme rolled up like a weapon. I can defuse that in ninety seconds — it's the easy arguments I can't leave alone.
beats.chinese: 是真吵哦。成年人，场刊卷起来当武器。真冲突我九十秒能摆平——反而是那种小争执，我放不下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps her ear, half-joking, half-serious. The two friends across the pond are still at it, but their voices have the loose rhythm of people enjoying themselves.
beats.chinese: 她敲敲自己的耳朵，半开玩笑半认真。池塘对面的两位朋友还在争，但声音里是那种聊得尽兴的松弛节奏。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My ears don't clock off when I do. I hear two voices going up across a food court and my feet start walking before my brain signs the form.
beats.chinese: 我下了班耳朵也不下班。在美食广场听见两个声音升高，我的脚比脑子批条子还快，先走过去了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My friend Siti told me once, straight to my face: 'Grace, we're not having a crisis, we're having a difference of opinion — go sit down.' So now I'm in training.
beats.chinese: 我朋友Siti有次当面跟我说：'Grace，我们这不是危机，是意见不同——你坐下吧。'所以我现在在训练自己。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks at the binoculars on the ledge, then at the two friends, visibly weighing which pair of things deserves her attention.
beats.chinese: 她看看台上的望远镜，又看看那两位朋友，明显在掂量哪边才值得她出手。

choices.english: Ask if she's off duty today.
choices.chinese: 问她今天是不是不用值班。

choices.english: Say those two sound like they know each other well.
choices.chinese: 说那两个人听起来很熟。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What do I do now? Nothing dramatic. I sit down. Physically. If my legs are folded, they can't march over there.
beats.chinese: 现在怎么办？没什么大动作。我坐下。真的坐。腿要是盘住了，就没法冲过去了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lowers herself onto the stone platform, right beside the binoculars, and folds her hands in her lap like a student behaving in assembly.
beats.chinese: 她在石台上坐下来，就在望远镜旁边，双手叠在膝上，像个集会上乖乖听话的学生。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at them. Still going. Nobody's crying, nobody's left. That's what a real discussion looks like — messy and nobody wants rescuing.
beats.chinese: 你看他们。还在争呢。没人哭，没人走。真正的讨论就长这样——乱糟糟的，但没人需要被拯救。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Across the pond, one friend throws his head back laughing at something the other said, then immediately resumes arguing. Grace watches the whole thing like a play she refuses to interrupt.
beats.chinese: 池塘对面，一个朋友被对方的话逗得仰头大笑，然后马上接着争。Grace看着这一切，像看一出她坚决不打断的戏。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Five. That's five this month. I'm writing it on my heart, lah.
beats.chinese: 五次了。这个月第五次。我要刻在心上啦。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A way of playing together... eh, you know what, that's exactly what it looks like from here. One of them is smiling while he complains.
beats.chinese: 一起玩的方式……哎，你还别说，从这边看真是这样。他一边抱怨一边在笑呢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns fully toward the two friends and studies them for a long moment, the way she'd watch an audience to see if the show is landing.
beats.chinese: 她整个人转向那两位朋友，仔细观察了好一会儿，就像她观察观众、看戏有没有演到位那样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If I went over there with my little peace treaty, I'd be the one ruining it. Like stopping two kids mid-game because you thought they were fighting over the ball.
beats.chinese: 要是我拿着我的小小和平协议过去，破坏局面的就是我。就像看见两个小孩抢球，以为他们打架，把游戏搅黄了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up the binoculars, looks through them at the tree shadows instead of the arguers, and settles back against the platform rail.
beats.chinese: 她拿起望远镜，不看争吵的人，改看水里的树影，靠回石台栏杆上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay. New rule for today: the only thing I mediate is between me and these tree shadows. They keep moving, I keep watching, nobody gets rescued.
beats.chinese: 好。今天的新规矩：我只调解一件事——我和这些树影之间的事。它们一直动，我一直看，谁也不需要被拯救。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Am I on duty today? No no, this is my off day — that's the funny part. I left the theatre and my ears didn't get the memo.
beats.chinese: 今天值班吗？不用不用，今天休息——好笑就不好笑在这。我人离开了剧场，耳朵没收到通知。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pulls her phone out of her pocket, glances at it, and then puts it away face-down on the stone ledge, firmly, like closing a door.
beats.chinese: 她从口袋里掏出手机，看了一眼，然后把它屏幕朝下扣在石台上，放得很坚决，像关上一扇门。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Phone away. If the theatre actually needs me, they'll call twice, and even then I'll finish watching the tree shadows first.
beats.chinese: 好了。手机收起来。剧场真有事会打两次电话，就算那样，我也要先看完树影再说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The two friends in the distance have moved on to a new topic entirely, their voices now steady and easy. Grace doesn't turn toward them once.
beats.chinese: 远处那两位朋友已经完全换了话题，声音平稳又轻松。Grace一次都没有朝他们转头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You see that? Topic changed all by itself. Didn't need a duty manager, didn't need a compromise, didn't need me. Beautiful.
beats.chinese: 你看到了吗？话题自己就换了。不需要值班经理，不需要折中方案，不需要我。真美。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Through the binoculars, a breeze drags the tree shadows across the whole pond and back again. Grace watches with genuine concentration, hands finally still.
beats.chinese: 透过望远镜，一阵风把树影整个拖过池塘，又拖回来。Grace看得非常专注，双手终于安静了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do they sound familiar? Twenty years of friendship, those two. They argue about every movie they watch. It's practically their hobby.
beats.chinese: 听起来很熟？那两位二十年的交情了。每看一部电影都要争一轮。这几乎就是他们的爱好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Across the pond, the taller friend says something and the other one bursts out laughing, slapping his own knee, mid-disagreement.
beats.chinese: 池塘对面，高个的朋友说了句什么，另一个当场笑出声，一边争一边拍自己的膝盖。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Grace watches them laugh together and her shoulders drop, the last of the mission posture leaving her body.
beats.chinese: Grace看着他们一起大笑，肩膀松了下来，身上最后一点出任务的样子也卸掉了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah. There it is. I was watching the first two minutes of the argument and decided I'd seen the whole show. Classic duty-manager brain — assess, intervene, resolve. Nobody asked for a resolution!
beats.chinese: 啊，看到了。我只看了争论的头两分钟，就当自己看完了整场戏。典型的值班经理脑子——评估、介入、解决。可没人要我解决呀！

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay okay — one suggestion, then I sit on my hands. The suggestion is: nothing. I suggest nothing. I watch the water.
beats.chinese: 好好好——一个建议，然后我把手坐住。建议是：没有建议。我什么都不建议。我看水。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leans on the stone platform and turns the binoculars toward the reflections, letting the argument behind her carry on without her.
beats.chinese: 她靠在石台上，把望远镜转向水面的倒影，任由身后的争论自己继续。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the stone platform, the binoculars are back on the ledge. Grace is sitting nearby with a small notebook open on her knee — and a single folded sheet of paper slips out and skids across the stone toward the water.
beats.chinese: 石台上又摆着那副双筒望远镜。Grace坐在旁边，膝上摊着一个小本子——一张折起来的纸从本子里滑出来，顺着石面朝池塘边溜去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She catches it just before the breeze takes it, smooths it out, and bursts out laughing at what's written on it.
beats.chinese: 她赶在风把它吹走之前按住，抚平纸面，看着上面的字大笑起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at this — my cousin's red pen. I set him a nice little puzzle, and he drew one giant question mark next to my clue and wrote 'auntie, even the question mark is confused'.
beats.chinese: 你看这个——我表弟的红笔。我给他出了个漂亮的小谜题，他在我的提示旁边画了个巨大的问号，还写：'阿姨，连问号都看糊涂了'。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds the paper at arm's length, reads her own clue again, tilts her head, and slowly nods.
beats.chinese: 她把纸伸远一点，把自己的提示重读一遍，歪了歪头，慢慢点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eh... he's right, actually. The clue has two answers and one of them is mine. Okay, back to the drawing board. The red pen wins this round.
beats.chinese: 哎……其实他说得对。这个提示有两个答案，其中一个是我脑子里的。好，回去重画。这局红笔赢了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the paper back into the notebook, closes it firmly, and turns toward the water, where the tree shadows are sliding past again.
beats.chinese: 她把纸折好塞回本子，用力合上，转向水面，树影又缓缓滑了过去。

card.name: Aoife Kavanagh
card.occupation: Booking manager at an instrument rental shop in Dublin
card.appearance: Long soft older face in true side profile, short voluminous swept fringe, projecting rounded chin and slightly raised mouth corner; red stand collar.
card.personality: Aoife is warm in a scattered, generous way, the sort who genuinely enjoys the fifteen minutes a bus ride gives you with someone. The friction is at goodbyes: they'll walk a friend to the door, then remember a question that's been nagging them, and suddenly the person who wasn't in a hurry misses the bus that wasn't urgent. It's never clinginess or a fear of endings — Aoife is fine with people leaving — they simply underestimate how long a good question takes to answer properly. When a friend says 'there's my bus now,' they let go instantly, no sulking, and pick the thread up next day as if no gap existed. Reliable at work, hopeless at exits.
card.background: Aoife grew up in Dún Laoghaire and never went far, ending up in a flat in Dublin with a longtime housemate and a short walk to work. They've managed bookings at an instrument rental shop for years — the job suits them: calendars, cases, musicians who need a cor anglais by Thursday. It's a fact of their life, not the whole of it. Evenings are for roasting whatever root vegetables the market had, done plainly and eaten happily. Most nights they and the old housemate put on some obscure silent comedy, and half the pleasure is arguing over whether the subtitles have softened a joke or invented one outright. Their friendships run on accumulated small shared hours rather than grand occasions.
hobbies: Silent comedies and subtitle arguments with their old housemate
Long bus rides as conversation time
card.speechStyle: Easy, meandering, question-prone; drifts into tangents mid-sentence, then snaps back cleanly when told time's up. Dry Dublin humour, no fuss.
card.signature: "Hold on — before you go, this has been bothering me all day."

values: Curiosity over ceremony
Letting people go easily when they say it's time
flaws: Chronically misjudges how long a good question takes
Drags out every goodbye without noticing
boundaries: Won't promise things on other people's behalf
Doesn't chase anyone who's moved on
conversationalHabits: Saves up odd questions to spring on whoever's nearby
Resumes yesterday's conversation mid-thought, no recap
anchorLines: No, no — that's your bus, go on. Tell me tomorrow.
The subtitles are wrong again, listen to this.
Roast parsnip night. You're here for it whether you meant to be or not.

entries.summaryZh: Aoife是都柏林乐器租赁店的预约管理员，做事可靠，唯独道别拖沓：送到门口总会想起一个真问题，害朋友误过一班车。但只要对方说车到了，他们立刻放人，明天自然接上话头。池塘边一副望远镜，一场没讲完的无声喜剧笑点，正好让人看清这种可爱的毛病。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the stone platform by the pond, a pair of binoculars rests where someone left them. Through the lenses, the trees on the far bank waver on the water, the reflection stretching and folding as a breeze crosses the surface.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜。透过镜片，对岸的树影在水面摇晃，一阵风吹过，倒影被拉长又揉皱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A short way up the path, Aoife is finishing a goodbye with an acquaintance — hand raised, half-turned away, then half-turned back again.
beats.chinese: 小路上方一点，Aoife正和一位熟人道别——手举着，身子转过去一半，又转回来一半。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: — and that's the bit where the waiter slides the whole tray down the counter, dead serious, not one plate falls. Anyway. Goodbye now, genuinely.
beats.chinese: ——就是那段，服务员把整个托盘顺着柜台滑过去，一脸严肃，一个盘子都没掉。好了，这回真再见了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The acquaintance points toward the road junction and walks off. Aoife turns, spots you at the platform, and steps aside from the path with an easy grin.
beats.chinese: 熟人朝路口一指，走了。Aoife转过身，看见石台旁的你，笑着往路边让了一步。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't mind me — I'm told my goodbyes come with appendices. You're watching the trees in the water? That's a proper way to spend a pause, that is.
beats.chinese: 别管我——听说我的告别都带附录。你在看水里的树？这可是打发片刻的好法子。

choices.english: Ask what they were about to add just now
choices.chinese: 问刚才想补什么

choices.english: Ask whether their friend was in a hurry
choices.chinese: 问朋友是不是赶时间

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, you want the appendix? Right, so — the film we watched last night. A fellow spends the whole picture chasing his hat across a windy town.
beats.chinese: 哦，你想听附录？行——我们昨晚看的那部片子。有个人整部电影都在追他的帽子，跑过一个刮风的小镇。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Every chase scene, the hat's just ahead of him. Rooftops, market, a canal. And at the very end, he catches a hat — but it's the wrong one. Belongs to a stranger.
beats.chinese: 每场追逐，帽子都在他前面一点。屋顶、市场、一条运河。到最后他终于抓到一顶——却是别人的帽子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Aoife leans on the stone platform beside the binoculars, gesturing like someone laying out a map of the whole chase.
beats.chinese: Aoife靠在望远镜旁的石台上，比划着，像在把整场追逐摊开成一张地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And the stranger's been chasing Aoife's fellow's hat the whole time. Two men, two hats, crossing over. He puts the wrong one on and walks off content.
beats.chinese: 而那个陌生人整场追的是他的帽子。两个人，两顶帽子，换了个个儿。他戴上错的那顶，心满意足地走了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My housemate says the subtitle made it a joke about honesty. I say it's a joke about luck. We nearly came to blows over it, quietly.
beats.chinese: 我室友说字幕把它翻成了关于诚实的笑话。我说这是关于运气的。我们差点为此打起来，安静地打。

choices.english: Ask whether the scene works without any sound at all
choices.chinese: 问这段没声音也能懂吗

choices.english: Say you'd probably blurt out one more thing too
choices.chinese: 说这确实会忍不住补一句

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Was she in a hurry? No, not a bit — and that's the trap, isn't it. She'd have stood there all evening if I'd kept finding things to say.
beats.chinese: 她赶时间吗？一点也不——这正是麻烦所在。要是我一直有话讲，她能站一晚上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Aoife picks a fallen leaf off the stone platform and turns it over, not really looking at it.
beats.chinese: Aoife从石台上捡起一片落叶翻过来，其实没在看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I only learned just now she had a connection to catch. The moment she pointed at the road, off she went. So I let her — straight away, no fuss.
beats.chinese: 我刚刚才知道她要赶一班换乘车。她一指路口，立马就走了。所以我马上放人，不磨叽。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's my whole problem. I always think one more sentence takes ten seconds. It takes four minutes. It has never once taken ten seconds.
beats.chinese: 这就是我的毛病。我总觉得再说一句只要十秒。其实要四分钟。从来没有一次真的只要十秒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm reliable with bookings, mind — a cor anglais by Thursday, done. It's only exits I can't keep a schedule on.
beats.chinese: 不过预约这块我很靠谱——周四要一支英国管，没问题。只有道别这件事，我排不出时刻表。

choices.english: Say that after a goodbye you sometimes forget how to actually walk away
choices.chinese: 说说再见后有时想不起怎么真的走

choices.english: Ask what happens to the things they never got to say
choices.chinese: 问没讲完的会怎么办

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Does it work with no sound? You'd think not, wouldn't you — a whole chase with nobody saying a word.
beats.chinese: 没声音也能懂吗？你会觉得不行吧——一整场追逐，一个字都没有。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Aoife mimes it: a snatch at the air, a stumble, a hat pressed on with both hands. No words needed.
beats.chinese: Aoife比划起来：往空中一抓，一个趔趄，双手把帽子扣上。一个字都不用。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. You knew exactly what happened. The grabbing does the talking. That's why the wrong hat lands so hard — you watched him earn it.
beats.chinese: 看，你完全看懂了。动作自己会说话。所以戴错帽子那一下才狠——你亲眼看着他一路挣来的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Should I make you try it yourself? No — no need. If the gesture reads, it reads. That's the whole trick of those pictures.
beats.chinese: 要不要让你也试一下？不用——不必了。动作到位了就到位了。那些片子全部的窍门就在这儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A breeze crosses the pond and the tree reflections shiver and reassemble. Aoife watches them a moment, apparently satisfied.
beats.chinese: 一阵风掠过池塘，树影抖了抖，又重新拼合。Aoife看了一会儿，像是挺满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha — you'd blurt one more thing too? Then you understand it's not rudeness, it's that the sentence genuinely seems short from the inside.
beats.chinese: 哈——你也会忍不住补一句？那你就懂了，这不是没礼貌，是那句话站在自己这边看真的显得很短。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Aoife laughs, short and dry, and pushes off the stone platform to stand upright.
beats.chinese: Aoife短促干笑一声，从石台上撑着站起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well then, let's leave the hat story right here — caught, worn, wrong, done. If I add anything else we'll be here while the pond freezes over.
beats.chinese: 那帽子的事就讲到这儿——追到了，戴上了，戴错了，完。我要再补一句，咱们就得站到池水结冰。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good stopping point. Some stories are better with the last plate still on the tray, as our waiter friend would say.
beats.chinese: 就停在这儿挺好。有些故事，托盘上还剩最后一个盘子时收场最好——我们那位服务员朋友大概会这么说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Aoife gives a small wave — an actual finish, no appendix attached — and starts up the path at an unhurried pace.
beats.chinese: Aoife小小挥了下手——真正的收尾，没有附录——然后不紧不慢地沿小路走了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forgetting how to walk away — oh, I know that one from the inside. You've said goodbye, and then your feet are just standing there waiting for permission.
beats.chinese: 想不起怎么走——这个我太熟了，自己就这样。告别说完了，脚还站在原地等许可。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Aoife straightens up, squares their shoulders toward the path, and gives you a crisp nod — a demonstration, clearly.
beats.chinese: Aoife站直，朝小路的方向摆正肩膀，干脆地点了下头——显然是在示范。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Lovely to meet you. The trees looked grand through those binoculars. Off I go.
beats.chinese: 好。很高兴遇到你。望远镜里的树真不错。我走啦。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take two genuine steps down the path, then turn around with a shrug that admits nothing and everything.
beats.chinese: 他们真的沿小路走了两步，然后转过身，耸耸肩，什么也不承认，又什么都承认了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See? That's the whole technique. Two steps and it's done. Now if only I could do it when it counts.
beats.chinese: 看，全部技巧就这些。走两步，结束。可惜真到用时我做不到。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What happens to the unsaid things? Nothing dramatic. They sit in a pocket of my head until the next time I bump into the person.
beats.chinese: 没讲完的怎么办？没什么戏剧性的。它们在我脑袋里某个口袋待着，等下次碰上那个人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Aoife pats the side of their coat pocket, as if the unsaid sentences were stored there literally.
beats.chinese: Aoife拍了拍外套侧面的口袋，好像那些没说的话真存放在那儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then tomorrow, or next week, it's — oh, before you go, this has been bothering me all day. And off we go again, mid-thought, no recap needed.
beats.chinese: 然后明天，或者下周，就是——哎，走之前，这事烦了我一整天。于是又开始了，接着上次的话头，不用回顾。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't chase people with messages to finish them. If the path crosses, the path crosses. It usually does, in a city this size.
beats.chinese: 我不会为了讲完就追着人发消息。路要是交叉，自然交叉。城市就这么大，通常都会的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Aoife picks up the leaf from the platform, sets it back down neatly, and looks out over the water once, like closing a book.
beats.chinese: Aoife捡起石台上那片叶子，端端正正放回去，朝水面望了一眼，像合上一本书。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the stone platform, binoculars up, the tree reflections sliding over the water. Along the pond edge, Aoife stops, opens a small lunchbox, and inspects the roasted roots inside.
beats.chinese: 你回到石台旁，举起望远镜，树影在水面滑过。池边，Aoife停下脚步，打开一个小餐盒，查看里面的烤根菜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Parsnip and carrot, from the market. And — look at that — I brought the fork this time. That's the whole box ticked.
beats.chinese: 欧防风和胡萝卜，市场买的。而且——瞧——这次叉子带上了。这盒就算齐活了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They press the lid down until it clicks, tuck the box back into their bag, and give you an easy nod, already turning up the path.
beats.chinese: 他们把盒盖按到咔哒扣好，把餐盒塞回袋子，朝你随意点了点头，已经转身朝小路上走了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Trees behaving themselves today? Good. Right — enjoy the water, I've a bench with my name on it. See you round.
beats.chinese: 今天的树还乖吧？好。行了——好好看水，有条长凳在等我。回头见。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: No appendix this time. They're three steps gone before the thought could even form, lunchbox swinging gently in the bag.
beats.chinese: 这次没有附录。还没等那个念头成形，他们已经走出三步，餐盒在袋子里轻轻晃着。

card.name: Callum Fraser
card.occupation: retired hearing aid repair technician
hobbies: walking the Water of Leith path
card.personality: Callum likes things settled. A walk starts at ten means ten, the person who said they'd bring the drum brings the drum, and he finds that comforting rather than rigid. But the moment someone says 'actually, can we change that?'—he lights up. To him a changed mind isn't a wobble, it's the good kind of news, and he'll say so out loud, sometimes too enthusiastically for someone who's only half sure. He concedes quickly when he's wrong and remembers what convinced him. His flaw is treating every vague plan as a contract waiting to be drafted; not everyone wants their Saturday itemised.
card.background: Callum spent thirty years at a hearing aid repair bench off St Patrick Square, where a loose wire is either loose or it isn't, and customers appreciated a straight answer about which. Retired three years ago, he kept the magnifying lamp and nothing else. Thursday nights he's the anchor of pub quiz team The Isthmus—geography rounds are his, and he once talked a quizmaster into striking an atlas answer because the border in question had changed after that edition printed. Most evenings he plays the djembe with more commitment than skill. Lately he's added one small step to his morning routine—wiping the bench down before the kettle, not after—to see if the day sits better that way. Early signs: inconclusive, but he's keeping it.
card.speechStyle: Buoyant, short bursts. States plans like terms: 'so that's ten, the south gate, I'll bring the flask.' When someone changes their mind he says 'good, say it plainly' with genuine delight. Concedes specifically and loudly.
card.signature: Changed your mind? Good. Say it plainly and we'll sort the rest.
card.appearance: Broad older face with heavy lower cheeks, center-parted low ponytail, uneven flat lids and compressed off-center mouth; palm supports cheek, yellow scarf.

values: a clear agreement is a kindness, not a cage
someone revising their mind honestly is worth more than someone holding a line out of stubbornness
flaws: turns casual plans into itemised terms nobody asked for
can miss that a person's half-formed change of heart needs room, not applause
boundaries: won't renegotiate something the moment before it starts—flag it early and he's all flexibility
doesn't treat a changed mind as an opening to relitigate the original plan
conversationalHabits: confirms specifics out loud—time, place, who brings what
reacts to 'actually, I'd rather not' with visible pleasure rather than disappointment
anchorLines: So that's settled—ten o'clock, your end, I'll carry the drum. Written in stone until you say otherwise.
You'd rather do Saturday instead? Honestly, better. Say it like that every time.
I'd rather know where I stand than be comfortable guessing. Vagueness costs more than a straight no.

entries.summaryZh: 爱丁堡退休技师卡勒姆把每次散步都拟成条款，却在朋友改主意时真心高兴。池边一封“谢谢讲清楚”的回复，让你看见他如何把坦率当礼物，也让他当场认下自己听得过实的老毛病。

story.titleZh: 池边望远镜与一句“谢谢讲清楚”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the stone platform by the pond, a pair of binoculars rests on the flat stone. Through them, the trees on the far bank waver in the water, their reflections bending whenever a breeze crosses the surface.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜。透过它，对岸的树在水中轻轻晃动，微风一过，倒影就弯了弯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha—watching the trees swim? Good spot, that. The wind's been toying with them since I sat down.
beats.chinese: 哈——在看树游泳？好位置。从我坐下起，风就一直逗着它们。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: An older man stands a few steps along the platform, phone in hand, grinning at the screen.
beats.chinese: 一位上了年纪的男士站在石台几步之外，手里拿着手机，对着屏幕咧嘴笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry—Callum. I'm not spying, just reading. One of my walking group has finally come out and said she doesn't fancy our usual route. And do you know what I replied?
beats.chinese: 抱歉——我叫卡勒姆。不是偷看，只是在看消息。我们散步群里终于有位朋友直说不想走原定路线。你猜我怎么回的？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Thank you for saying it plainly.' Sent. Done. That's the best message I've had all week.
beats.chinese: “谢谢你讲清楚。”发送，完成。这是我这一周收到的最好的消息。

choices.english: Ask why a changed plan makes him so happy.
choices.chinese: 问为什么改计划反而让他这么高兴。

choices.english: Ask whether he always spells everything out this clearly.
choices.chinese: 问他是不是每次都把事情列得这么清楚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because the earlier she says it, the earlier we rebook. If she'd come along dragging her boots, that's when people get hard to be around.
beats.chinese: 因为她说得越早，我们就能越早重新约。要是她硬撑着来，一路拖着脚走，那才让人难相处。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pockets the phone and nods at the water, where a duck's wake briefly cuts the tree reflections in half.
beats.chinese: 他把手机放进口袋，朝水面点点头，一只鸭子划过，树影被波纹切成两半。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thirty years at a repair bench taught me that. A loose wire is either loose or it isn't. You say which, we fix it in a minute. Same with people, near enough.
beats.chinese: 在维修台干了三十年教会我这个。线松就是松，不松就是不松。你说清楚，一分钟就能修好。人也是差不多这个理。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So a changed mind isn't bad news to me. It's the good kind of news. It means we can actually sort something.
beats.chinese: 所以对我来说，改变主意不是坏消息，是好消息。说明我们真能重新安排点什么。

choices.english: Ask whether the new meeting place is decided yet.
choices.chinese: 问这次的新地点定了吗。

choices.english: Ask what if the person doesn't want to go out at all this time.
choices.chinese: 问如果对方这次根本不想出门呢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Aye, I do it. Time, place, who brings what—it all comes out of me like terms of a contract. So that's ten, the south gate, I'll bring the flask.
beats.chinese: 是啊，我就是这样。几点、在哪、谁带什么——从我嘴里说出来就像合同条款。比如：十点，南门，我带保温壶。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself and taps the phone against his palm.
beats.chinese: 他自嘲地笑笑，用手机轻轻拍着掌心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The trouble is, sometimes a friend only mentions a walk once, in passing. No time, no place, just 'we should go up Arthur's Seat sometime.' And I've drafted terms before they've finished the sentence.
beats.chinese: 问题是，有时朋友只是顺口提一次散步。没时间，没地点，就说“哪天该去亚瑟王座走走”。他们话还没说完，我条款都拟好了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My friends find it funny. Mostly. One of them keeps a list of my worst ones and reads them out at the pub.
beats.chinese: 朋友们觉得好笑。大体上是。有位朋友专门记下我最离谱的几条，在酒馆里念出来。
