choices.english: Point out that a passing remark might not be a plan at all.
choices.chinese: 说随口一提也可能根本没打算安排。

choices.english: Ask whether he ever changes his own mind at the last minute.
choices.chinese: 问他自己会不会临时改主意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not yet, and that's the honest answer. I've asked two practical candidates—the botanic gates and the shore path—and now I'm waiting.
beats.chinese: 还没定，这是老实话。我提了两个实际候选——植物园门口和海边小路——现在在等回复。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts the binoculars, looks through them at the far bank, then sets them back on the stone exactly where they were.
beats.chinese: 他拿起望远镜朝对岸看了看，又放回石台上原来的位置。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I could guess and book it, but guessing's how you end up somewhere nobody wanted. Two options, one reply, then it's settled.
beats.chinese: 我可以猜一个直接定下来，但猜来猜去，最后就会定在一个谁都不想去的地方。两个选项，一条回复，事情就定了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right—phone away, eyes on the water. The trees are doing something interesting and I refuse to miss it for a group chat.
beats.chinese: 好了——手机收起来，看水面。树正在变出有趣的样子，我可不想为个群聊错过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then I'd be daft to treat the new place as settled, wouldn't I? Changing the route is one thing. Not wanting to come out is another thing entirely.
beats.chinese: 那我要是把新地点当成定好的，就太傻了，对吧？改路线是一回事，根本不想出门完全是另一回事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks the phone back up, types a few words, and turns the screen towards the pond as if showing the water itself.
beats.chinese: 他重新拿起手机，打了几个字，把屏幕朝池塘转过去，像是在给水面看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Short and plain: 'No bother if you'd rather stay in—just say so, no explaining needed.' That gives her room instead of me applauding half a decision.
beats.chinese: 好了。简短明白：“要是你想待在家里，没关系，直说就行，不用解释。”这样是给她留余地，而不是我对半个决定鼓掌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've made that mistake before—cheered someone into a walk they didn't want. Never again. Ask first, cheer after.
beats.chinese: 我以前犯过这错——把人夸得不好意思，结果陪走了一趟她并不想走的路。下不为例。先问清楚，再高兴。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: ...Aye. Guilty. You're right—I take a passing remark and hear a booking.
beats.chinese: ……是啊，认了。你说得对——人家随口一说，我听成了预约。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He says it loudly, the way some people concede a point at a pub quiz, and raises a hand as if a quizmaster had confirmed it.
beats.chinese: 他大声承认，就像在酒馆问答赛上认输一样，还举起手，仿佛主持人已经判定得分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So here's what I'll do this time: I'll reply to her message and stop there. No times, no gates, no flask. Just 'good to know, glad you said it.'
beats.chinese: 所以这次我打算这样：回她那条消息就到此为止。不提时间，不提哪个门，不提保温壶。就说“知道了，很高兴你直说”。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He puts the phone away and leans on the stone rail, watching the reflections settle.
beats.chinese: 他收起手机，靠在石栏上，看着倒影慢慢平静下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If she wants a proper plan, she'll say when. And when she does, I'll have my terms ready—old habits. But she gets to ask first.
beats.chinese: 要是她想认真安排，会说时间的。到时候我的条款随时备好——老习惯改不掉。但得由她先开口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Me? Constantly. Last month I told The Isthmus—my quiz team—I was out of a charity marathon quiz. Four hours long. I said so the day it was announced, not the night before.
beats.chinese: 我？经常。上个月我告诉我的问答队The Isthmus，我不参加一场慈善马拉松问答赛。要四个小时。消息一公布我就说了，没拖到前一天。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He counts it off on his fingers as though reading out terms.
beats.chinese: 他掰着手指头数，像在宣读条款。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I said: Thursday's my night, four hours is a different animal, and I'd rather be useful in the pub rounds. Nobody argued, because I'd said it early and plainly.
beats.chinese: 我是这么说的：周四是我的固定夜晚，四个小时是另一码事，我宁愿在常规酒馆轮里出力。没人争，因为我说得早、说得明白。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the whole trick, if there is one. Change your mind out loud, early, and nobody has to guess. Now—did that tree just move, or is that a heron behind it?
beats.chinese: 如果说有什么诀窍，就是这个：把改变主意大声说出来，早点说，谁都不用猜。哎——那棵树是动了吗，还是后面有只鹭？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the stone platform, the binoculars again show the far bank's trees wavering in the water. A few steps along, Callum slides a small quiz booklet into his bag and zips it half shut.
beats.chinese: 石台边，望远镜里对岸的树影又在水中晃动。几步之外，卡勒姆把一本小小的问答册子塞进包里，拉链拉了一半。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't ask how Thursday went. Or do—I lost a point on geography, of all things. Mixed up two towns with near-identical names.
beats.chinese: 别问周四怎么样。还是问吧——我居然在地理题上丢了一分。把两个名字几乎一样的镇子搞混了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats the bag once, as if closing the matter with it.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍包，像是连那道题一起关了进去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The atlas in the pub was an old edition. Once I saw the current border, I sat down. No point arguing when the answer's clear.
beats.chinese: 酒馆里那本地图册是旧版。等我看清现在的边界，我就坐下了。答案明明白白时，争来争去没意思。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. The water's calm today—the trees are holding still for once. Have a proper look.
beats.chinese: 算了。今天水面很平——树难得不动。好好看看吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He steps back from the edge and stands beside you, watching the reflections with his hands in his pockets.
beats.chinese: 他从池边退开一步，站在你旁边，双手插兜，一起看着水中的倒影。

card.name: Bex Whitlam
card.occupation: indoor plant caretaker at a shopping mall
card.personality: Bex runs on being the one who has it handled. She genuinely enjoys carrying things for people — the extra shift, the flatmate's paperwork, the dying ficus nobody claims — but she cannot say no cleanly, so she says yes with a smile and then goes quiet and stiff until something snaps. She reads offers of help as a verdict that she's failing, which she'd never say out loud. Cheerful under strain in a way that fools nobody who knows her. Direct about everyone else's problems, evasive about her own.
card.background: She grew up in Nanaimo with a grandfather who whittled on the porch, which is where the teaspoon carving started — she's made maybe forty, gives most away. She moved to Vancouver at twenty-two, tried floral shop work, then landed the mall plant job: watering, pruning, and rescuing ficuses from dark corners near the food court. She sings alto with the False Creek Community Choir on Tuesdays and has opinions about warm-ups. Right now she's covering two coworkers' routes while one is on leave, insisting it's fine, and has quietly stopped mentioning how far behind she is on her own section near the cinema.
card.speechStyle: Short sentences, plain words, then one oddly precise detail. Asks direct questions. Dry humor delivered flat, without signaling the joke.
card.signature: It's fine. I've got it.
card.appearance: Long side-swept dark hair framing narrow face, rectangular glasses, short straight brows and open oval mouth; leans forward in blue jacket gripping strap.

values: being reliable is how you earn your place
people should be asked, not guessed about
flaws: can't refuse a request, then resents having said yes
hides being overwhelmed until she's short with people
boundaries: won't accept help framed as pity
won't discuss her own stress unless she brings it up first
conversationalHabits: answers briefly, then adds one exact detail unprompted
deflects concern with a flat joke and a change of subject
anchorLines: The ficus by the cinema is on my list twice. That's a scheduling choice, not a problem.
No, seriously, it's fine. I counted — forty-one plants, four days, doable.
You don't need to help. Tell me what you need instead, I'm better at that side.

entries.summaryZh: 贝克斯是商场里的室内植物养护员，习惯替所有人扛事。在池塘石台旁，她盯着一条代班请求打了半句就停住。望远镜里晃动的树影，陪她第一次发出'需先核对'的回复，把答应咽了回去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A stone platform sits at the edge of the pond, a pair of binoculars resting on it. Through the lenses, the trees on the far bank double and wobble in the water's reflection.
beats.chinese: 池塘边有一座石台，上面放着一副双筒望远镜。透过镜片，对岸的树影在水中翻倍、轻轻晃动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A woman sits on the bench nearby, scrolling her phone. It buzzes; she taps the notification open, types half a line, then stops and rubs her shoulder.
beats.chinese: 附近长椅上坐着一位女士，正在刷手机。手机震动，她点开通知，打了半行字，然后停住，揉了揉肩膀。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You can borrow those, by the way. The binoculars. I just use them to check the pond birds, but the tree reflections are better today.
beats.chinese: 顺便说一句，望远镜你可以用。我平时只拿来看池子里的鸟，不过今天树影更好看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The wind's moving the top layer one way and the deep water the other. Two currents in one pond. Nobody ever notices.
beats.chinese: 风推着表层往一边走，深水往另一边走。一个池塘里有两股水流，没人注意到这个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shifts on the bench, phone still lit in her hand, half-typed message glowing on the screen.
beats.chinese: 她在长椅上挪了挪，手机还亮着，屏幕上那半条未发送的消息发着光。

choices.english: Ask if she's in the middle of something right now.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是正在忙。

choices.english: Ask if there's room on the bench for you to sit too.
choices.chinese: 问歇脚的地方够不够坐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Busy? No. Resting. There's a difference, and I'm defending it right now.
beats.chinese: 忙？不忙。在休息。这两者有区别，我现在正在捍卫这个区别。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well. Someone just texted asking if I can cover another shift. That's all it is.
beats.chinese: 嗯……有人刚发消息问我能不能再顶一个班。就这么回事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds the phone up briefly, as if showing evidence, then puts it face-down on her knee.
beats.chinese: 她把手机举起来晃了一下，像出示证据，然后屏幕朝下扣在膝盖上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I already took two extra watering routes for a coworker on leave. Two. The mall has three hundred and six potted plants, and I know where every one of them stands.
beats.chinese: 我已经替一位休假的同事顶了两条浇水路线。两条。商场里有三百零六盆植物，每一盆在哪儿我都知道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So this would be a third. I typed 'sure, no problem' and then my thumb just stopped. Weird.
beats.chinese: 这会是第三条。我打了'没问题'，然后大拇指就停住了。挺奇怪的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks at the pond instead of at you, jaw tight.
beats.chinese: 她看着池塘，没看你，下巴绷着。

choices.english: Tell her she can deal with the message first — chatting can wait.
choices.chinese: 说她可以先处理消息，不必聊天。

choices.english: Ask what happens to her own section while she covers everyone else's.
choices.chinese: 问她自己的那部分怎么办。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enough room? Sure. Give me one second — bag goes here, lunch wrapper goes in my pocket, there. All yours.
beats.chinese: 够坐吗？当然。等我一秒——包放这边，包装纸塞口袋，好了。都归你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She scoots over, moving her canvas bag and a folded cloth, making a wide, careful space.
beats.chinese: 她往旁边挪，把帆布包和一块叠好的布收好，让出一大块干净的位置。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I come here between routes sometimes. It's the only place in my day where nothing needs watering.
beats.chinese: 我有时在路线之间来这儿。这是我一天里唯一不需要浇水的地方。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She exhales slowly through her nose, a long breath she clearly didn't plan.
beats.chinese: 她用鼻子慢慢呼出一口气，很长，明显不是有意的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry. That wasn't a sigh. That was... breathing. With enthusiasm.
beats.chinese: 抱歉。那不是叹气。那是……呼吸。带着热情的那种。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smiles without much behind it, and her thumb keeps tapping the edge of her phone case.
beats.chinese: 她笑了笑，笑意不多，拇指一直敲着手机壳的边缘。

choices.english: Sit quietly beside her and say nothing more.
choices.chinese: 安静地坐在她旁边，不再追问。

choices.english: Ask whether she likes coming here for walks.
choices.chinese: 问她是否喜欢来这里散步。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah. You're right. Message first, pond after. That's just good sequencing.
beats.chinese: 对，你说得对。先回消息，池塘放后面。这是正确的排序。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She flips the phone over and opens her calendar, scrolling with a frown.
beats.chinese: 她把手机翻过来，打开日历，皱着眉往下滑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tuesday, choir. Wednesday I'm already at the cinema section until close. Thursday... hm.
beats.chinese: 周二，合唱团。周三我得在影院区待到闭店。周四……嗯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay. I can't actually confirm until I check my route sheet. That's the honest answer, so that's what I'm sending.
beats.chinese: 好。我得先核对路线表才能确认。这是诚实的答案，所以我就这么回。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She types a short reply, checks it twice, and sends it. Then she sets the phone down, screen dark.
beats.chinese: 她打了一条简短的回复，检查了两遍，发了出去。然后放下手机，屏幕暗了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Not yes, not no. Just 'let me check.' First time I've ever sent that. Felt like writing with my left hand.
beats.chinese: 好了。不是答应，也不是拒绝，就是'我核对一下'。我第一次发这种话。感觉像用左手写字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My own section. Right. The ficus by the cinema is on my list twice. That's a scheduling choice, not a problem.
beats.chinese: 我自己那部分。对。影院旁边那棵榕树在我的清单上出现了两次。那是排班选择，不是问题。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stops rubbing her shoulder and looks at the half-typed message for a long moment.
beats.chinese: 她停止揉肩膀，盯着那条打了一半的消息看了很久。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've been saying yes to everyone's plants and quietly skipping my own. Two days behind on the cinema corridor. Nobody's noticed yet, which is its own kind of embarrassing.
beats.chinese: 我一直在答应照顾所有人的植物，然后悄悄跳过自己的。影院走廊已经落后两天了。还没人发现，这本身就挺尴尬的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She deletes the half-written 'sure, no problem' letter by letter, then types something new.
beats.chinese: 她把打了一半的'没问题'一个字母一个字母删掉，重新打了一段。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Can't confirm right now.' Full stop. I'm not announcing I've fixed my life. I'm just not adding a third route today.
beats.chinese: '现在无法确认。'句号。我不是宣布我解决了所有问题，只是今天不再加第三条路线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's a small thing. But my thumb did that on its own, so apparently some part of me was waiting for permission.
beats.chinese: 这是件小事。但我的大拇指是自己停的，所以显然我身上有一部分一直在等许可。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit beside her and watch the water. She glances over, seems to decide you're not going to ask anything, and visibly loosens.
beats.chinese: 你在她旁边坐下，看着水面。她瞥了一眼，似乎确认你不会追问什么，明显放松下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, you're good at this. Sitting. Most people can't do it without narrating.
beats.chinese: 行，你很擅长这个。坐着。大多数人做不到不说话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She puts the phone into her bag, zips it shut, and leans back until her shoulders touch the bench.
beats.chinese: 她把手机放进包里，拉上拉链，向后靠，直到肩膀碰到椅背。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a kingfisher that uses that flat stone. Never seen it land twice in the same spot, but always that stone.
beats.chinese: 有一只翠鸟用那块平石头。从没见它落在同一个位置两次，但总是那块石头。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: For a while neither of you says anything. The two currents keep crossing in the pond, going opposite ways.
beats.chinese: 有一会儿你们谁都没说话。池塘里两股水流继续交错，朝相反的方向走。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. That's the battery charged. Thanks for the silence. It's rarer than you'd think.
beats.chinese: 好了。电充上了。谢谢你的安静。这比你想象的少见。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Walks here? I like it fine. It's flat, there's water, and nothing in the pond needs pruning.
beats.chinese: 喜欢来这儿散步吗？挺喜欢的。路是平的，有水，而且池塘里的东西不用修剪。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly, the best walk of my week is after choir on Tuesdays. We do this one warm-up where the whole alto line slides up together, and afterwards my head's just... quiet.
beats.chinese: 说实话，我一周里最好的一次散步是周二合唱团结束后。我们有个热身练习，整个女中音声部一起往下滑音，之后我脑子就……安静了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She traces a small circle on the bench with her finger, keeping time with something only she hears.
beats.chinese: 她用手指在长椅上画着小圈，跟着只有她自己听到的节奏。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do you walk here often? I'm asking because you found the binoculars fast. Locals always find them fast.
beats.chinese: 你常来这儿散步吗？我问是因为你很快就找到了望远镜。本地人总是很快找到。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the phone deeper into her pocket, message apparently forgotten for now.
beats.chinese: 她把手机往口袋深处塞了塞，那条消息暂时被忘了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. The tree shadows shift about a hand-width every hour. If you're going to watch them, that's the rate. Now you know.
beats.chinese: 总之。树影每小时大约移动一个手掌的宽度。你要是想看，这就是速度。现在你知道了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The binoculars are back on the stone platform. Bex sits on the same bench, turning a small wooden spoon over in her fingers, checking it against the light.
beats.chinese: 双筒望远镜又放在石台上。贝克斯坐在同一条长椅上，手指转动着一把小木匙，对着光检查。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at this. The bowl's done. Took me four evenings, and there's a dip in the handle here — feel how it sits right under the knuckle.
beats.chinese: 看这个。匙舀完成了。花了四个晚上，匙柄这里有个小凹处——你感觉一下，正好卡在指节下面。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She rotates the spoon slowly, admiring the little hollow she carved, then wraps it in a soft cloth with practiced folds.
beats.chinese: 她慢慢转着木匙，欣赏自己雕出的小凹处，然后用软布以熟练的折法包好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one's mine. Forty-some spoons and I've kept exactly two. I give the rest away, which is a habit, not a policy.
beats.chinese: 这把是留给我的。雕了四十多把，我只留了两把。其余都送人了，这是习惯，不是规定。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the wrapped spoon into her bag and nods toward the binoculars on the platform.
beats.chinese: 她把包好的木匙放进包里，朝石台上的望远镜点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The tree shadows are running about a hand-width an hour today, same as always. Go on, they're better company than my phone.
beats.chinese: 今天的树影还是每小时大约一个手掌的宽度，和往常一样。去看吧，它们比我的手机好相处。

card.name: Tavita Faleolo
card.occupation: ingredients storekeeper at a baking school
card.appearance: Long blunt-jawed face, smooth center-parted short hair, very narrow unequal eyelids, crooked brow and pressed mouth; red open shirt and hand on strap.
card.personality: Tavita is warm, unhurried, and genuinely delighted by good things—good food, good company, a good afternoon—but he holds his favourites loosely on purpose. He believes the second time should never flatten the first, so he spaces out the experiences he loves most. People sometimes read his first-round praise as politeness, and he'll patiently explain he meant every word; he just wants to miss the place a little before returning. He never imposes this on anyone and finds other people's repeat habits fine, even funny. His flaw is that he can talk himself out of spontaneous joy, overthinking whether now is the right time.
card.background: Tavita grew up in Māngere in a big, loud family where Sunday feed was the week's centrepiece, and he learned early that anticipation was half the meal. He works as the ingredients storekeeper at a baking school in Auckland, keeping flour, butter, and chocolate in steady rotation—stock control suits him, because he likes knowing what's waiting and what's running low. Friends discovered his habit when he declined a third visit in a month to a restaurant he'd raved about, and assumed his earlier praise had been a compliment rather than the truth. He set them straight, a bit embarrassed, explaining he wanted the next visit to still feel like an event. He's kept the habit ever since, without rules or spreadsheets—just a feeling for when something's ready to be enjoyed again.
hobbies: Hunting out new eateries across Auckland
Restocking his own pantry like a shop
card.speechStyle: Easy and unhurried, with warm Pacific humour; he explains himself fully when misunderstood, using food metaphors without forcing them.
card.signature: "Nah, I meant it—I just want to be hungry for it again."

values: Savouring things properly
Letting people enjoy things their own way
flaws: Talks himself out of spontaneous repeats
Over-explains when misread
boundaries: Won't be rushed into revisiting a favourite
Won't lecture others on how often they go
conversationalHabits: Describes food in terms of timing and appetite
Checks that people knew he was sincere
anchorLines: Give it a few weeks and it'll taste like the first time again.
You go twice a week if you want—I'm not the repeat police.
Half the enjoyment is the waiting, aye.

entries.summaryZh: 塔维塔在池塘边读到朋友发来的关于他最爱的餐馆的消息，笑着说不去。他想先好好想念那道烤红薯，把期待当成享受的一半；被误会时会把话说清楚，也不劝别人照做。四条分支里他或自我确认、或向朋友解释、或欣然接受你的习惯、或回家烤扁面包，处处透着从容与真诚。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A pair of binoculars rests on the stone platform by the pond. Through the lenses, the tree reflections stretch and wobble on the water with every breeze.
beats.chinese: 池塘石台上放着一副双筒望远镜。透过镜片看去，树影在水面上一随微风便拉伸、晃动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A broad man stands a little further along the platform, phone in hand. He reads something, and his mouth lifts into a smile—then he lowers the phone slowly, almost regretfully.
beats.chinese: 石台稍远处站着一位高大的男人，手里拿着手机。他读着什么，嘴角扬起微笑——随后慢慢把手机放低，带着一点不舍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You caught me grinning like an idiot at my phone. My mate just messaged about a restaurant I love. I'm not going, though.
beats.chinese: 你看到我对着手机傻笑了吧。朋友刚发消息说那家我很喜欢的餐馆。不过我不去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's called Kalo's, down in Onehunga. Best slow-cooked pork in the city, and that's not me being polite.
beats.chinese: 叫Kalo's，在奥尼洪加。全城最好的慢炖猪肉，这不是我客套。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slips the phone into his jacket pocket and leans on the rail, watching the same wobbling reflections you are.
beats.chinese: 他把手机收进外套口袋，靠在栏杆上，和你一起看着那些晃动的水中树影。

choices.english: If you love it that much, why not go right now?
choices.chinese: 既然那么喜欢，为什么不现在就去？

choices.english: What's the dish you like there?
choices.chinese: 你喜欢那家的哪道菜？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair question. I've been three times this year already, and every single time was brilliant.
beats.chinese: 问得有道理。今年我已经去过三次，每一次都很棒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's exactly why I'm waiting. I want to miss that pork properly first—wake up thinking about it, you know?
beats.chinese: 所以我才在等。我想先真正想念那道猪肉——早上醒来满脑子都是它，你懂吗？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not that the place slipped or I found somewhere better. Nothing like that. I just don't want the third-best visit to overwrite the first.
beats.chinese: 不是那家店变差了，也不是我找到更好的了。都不是。我只是不想让一次没那么好的体验盖过第一次。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up a fallen leaf from the rail and turns it over in his fingers, in no hurry to finish the thought.
beats.chinese: 他从栏杆上拾起一片落叶，在指间翻看，一点也不急着把话说完。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Half the enjoyment is the waiting, aye. The other half is still there when I finally walk in.
beats.chinese: 一半的乐趣在于等待，对吧。等我真走进去时，另一半还在那儿等着我。

choices.english: Won't you overthink it and miss out on a happy meal?
choices.chinese: 会不会想太多，反而错过一次开心的饭？

choices.english: Did your friend ever think your praise was just politeness?
choices.chinese: 你朋友有没有误会过你的夸奖只是客套？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, the dish. Everyone talks about their pork, and it deserves it, but honestly? Their roast kumara.
beats.chinese: 哦，那道菜。大家都夸他们的猪肉，也确实该夸，但说实话？是他们的烤红薯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Plain roast kumara, nothing fancy. But the edges go all caramelised and crisp, and the inside is soft as custard.
beats.chinese: 就是普通的烤红薯，不花哨。但边缘烤得焦糖化、脆脆的，里面软得像蛋奶冻。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You can smell it from two tables away—sweet, a bit smoky. First bite, I actually put my fork down and laughed.
beats.chinese: 隔两张桌子都能闻到那股香味——甜里带一点烟熏味。第一口下去，我真的放下叉子笑出了声。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He rubs his thumb against his fingers, the way a baker checks flour, as if he's testing the texture from memory.
beats.chinese: 他用拇指搓着指头，像面包师检查面粉那样，仿佛在凭记忆测试那口感。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Simplest thing on the menu. Still the thing I dream about. Go figure.
beats.chinese: 菜单上最简单的一道菜。却是我最惦记的。真是想不通。

choices.english: The things I love, I actually eat all the time.
choices.chinese: 我喜欢的东西，反而经常吃。

choices.english: What are you planning to eat today?
choices.chinese: 今天你打算吃什么？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sometimes, yeah. I'll admit it. I've stood outside a place I love, talked myself out of it, and walked home eating toast.
beats.chinese: 有时候，会的，我承认。我曾在喜欢的店门口站过，说服自己别进去，然后回家啃吐司。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My mate reckons I think too much. Maybe I do. But when I do go back, it tastes like the first time again. That's worth some toast.
beats.chinese: 朋友说我想太多。也许吧。但当我真回去时，那味道就像第一次一样。为这个啃几次吐司也值。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, then looks at the pond, where the tree shadows have drifted into a new shape.
beats.chinese: 他自嘲地笑了，然后望向池塘，树影已漂成了新的形状。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tell you what—I'll ask myself one honest question tonight: do I actually want it today? If yes, I go. No counting days, no spreadsheet.
beats.chinese: 这样吧——今晚我问自己一个诚实的问题：我今天真的想吃吗？如果是，我就去。不数日子，不列表格。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right now? Honestly, no. I want to want it a bit longer. That's my answer.
beats.chinese: 现在吗？说实话，不想。我还想再惦记一会儿。这就是我的答案。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, that happened, yeah. My mate Sione thought I was being polite the first time I raved about Kalo's. Then I didn't go back for weeks and he got offended.
beats.chinese: 哦，有过这种事。我朋友西奥内以为我第一次夸Kalo's只是客套。后来我好几个星期没去，他就觉得被冒犯了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He thought I'd been flattering him, like the food wasn't actually good. Took me a while to explain I meant every word.
beats.chinese: 他以为我是在奉承他，好像那家店其实不好吃。我花了很久才解释清楚，我句句属实。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I told him: I'm not going because I liked it too much. I want to be hungry for it again. He stared at me like I'd grown a second head.
beats.chinese: 我告诉他：我不去，正是因为太喜欢了。我想再为它馋一次。他盯着我，像看见我长了个第二颗脑袋。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls out his phone, types a short message, and turns the screen toward you for a second before sending it.
beats.chinese: 他掏出手机，打了条短消息，在发送前把屏幕朝你亮了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Told him: still brilliant, still not coming this week. Clear at least. He'll survive.
beats.chinese: 好了。告诉他：还是很好吃，但这周还是不去。至少说明白了。他会没事的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha! Good on you, honestly. If it makes you happy every time, why ration it?
beats.chinese: 哈！说实话，挺好的。如果每次都让你开心，为什么要限量？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My brother's the same with his takeaway. Same order, twice a week, ten years. He's the happiest man in Māngere.
beats.chinese: 我哥对外卖也是这样。同样的菜，一周两次，十年了。他是芒雷最快乐的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He raises both hands, palms out, like surrendering a point he's happy to lose.
beats.chinese: 他举起双手，掌心向外，像是在认输一个他乐于输掉的观点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not the repeat police. Your way works for you. My way works for me. Both plates get eaten, aye?
beats.chinese: 我又不是重复警察。你的方式适合你，我的适合我。反正盘子最后都吃光了，对吧？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly, I envy it a little. Imagine loving something that much and it never wears out.
beats.chinese: 说真的，我还有点羡慕。想想看，那么爱一样东西，它却永远不腻。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Today? Nothing exciting. I've got flour and butter at home, so probably something simple. Maybe flatbread.
beats.chinese: 今天？没什么特别的。家里有面粉和黄油，所以大概做点简单的。也许烤个扁面包。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I do that a lot, working at the baking school. Around flour all day, then go home and play with flour. My family thinks I'm mad.
beats.chinese: 我常这样，在烘焙学校上班。整天围着面粉转，回家还玩面粉。家里人觉得我疯了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, unbothered, and watches a duck cut a clean line through the tree reflections.
beats.chinese: 他耸耸肩，毫不在意，看着一只鸭子从树影中划出一道干净的水线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But there's something nice about making your own dinner from scratch. Hot pan, simple dough, done in twenty minutes.
beats.chinese: 但亲手从头做晚餐有种说不出的好。热锅，简单的面团，二十分钟就搞定。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, that's settled. Flatbread tonight, and Kalo's can wait for the weekend I actually miss it.
beats.chinese: 好，就这么定了。今晚做扁面包，Kalo's等到我真正想念它的那个周末再说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lift the binoculars from the stone platform and watch the tree reflections wobble and stretch on the pond's surface. Following the shifting green, your view drifts along the bank—and lands on Tavita, crouched over a shopping bag.
beats.chinese: 你从石台上拿起双筒望远镜，看树影在池塘水面上晃动、拉伸。顺着那片晃动的绿意，你的视线沿池边移过去——落在蹲在购物袋旁的塔维塔身上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Give me a sec—just checking the bag's not been squashed. Nothing worse than a split bag of flour in your other shopping.
beats.chinese: 等我一下——就查查袋子有没有被压破。面粉袋破了撒进别的菜里，没有比这更糟的了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He finds no damage, nods with real satisfaction, and tucks the flour back into the bag like it's stock arriving at the school.
beats.chinese: 他没发现破损，满意地点点头，把面粉放回袋子里，像学校到了新货一样郑重。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, this is the problem with me. Off the clock and I'm still doing stock checks. Can't help it—flour's flour, aye.
beats.chinese: 看，这就是我的毛病。下班了还在做库存检查。没办法——面粉就是面粉，对吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, good spotting you again. I'm off home—there's a flatbread with my name on it. Take care of yourself.
beats.chinese: 总之，又碰到你真好。我回家了——有个扁面包正等着我呢。你自己保重。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts the shopping bag, gives a small wave, and strolls off along the pond, unhurried as ever.
beats.chinese: 他提起购物袋，轻轻挥了挥手，沿着池塘悠闲地走远了，一如既往地从容。

card.name: Achieng Opondo
card.occupation: carousel horse painter for over thirty years, now mostly retired with the occasional private restoration commission
card.personality: Achieng loves a mystery but is dreadful company for anyone who wants to finish one unspoiled. She announces her suspect early, then argues with the radio when the evidence changes. She notices a missing button before a changed mood. In company she is funny, sceptical and willing to be the butt of a joke, provided someone tells her what the joke was. Her inconvenient habit is treating a plain account as a puzzle: a neighbour can simply have missed the bus, without a hidden motive. She is generous with materials and fiercely protective of everybody's right to their own guess.
card.background: Achieng spent over thirty years painting carousel horses in Nairobi, matching old colours and discovering the odd screw hidden under decades of paint. Mostly retired, she still accepts a few restoration commissions. Her daughter got her listening to a weekly radio detective serial during a long repainting job. Now she and a neighbour listen separately and meet afterwards to argue over the culprit; neither is allowed to telephone during the episode. She also paints small wooden birds for an amateur theatre group's stage sets. Her first realistic crow was mistaken for a fallen glove from the back row, so the next one had a shamelessly oversized beak. She plays jianzi with whoever turns up at the courtyard, where her eye for detail is considerably better than her balance.
card.speechStyle: Dry, lively English. Offers a specific observation, follows it with a suspicious possibility, and laughs when a mundane explanation defeats her theory. Uses occasional detective vocabulary without turning every conversation into an interrogation.
card.hometown: Kisumu, raised there before moving to Nairobi
card.signature: A perfectly ordinary explanation. Annoying, but possible.
card.appearance: Broad older cheeks and short chin, brush-cut hair, round spectacles, downturned mouth, blue high collar.

values: everyone gets to make their own guess
materials should be useful beyond the original job
flaws: spoils mysteries by announcing theories too early
looks for hidden motives when a simple explanation would do
boundaries: never shares an actual ending with someone still listening
will not turn a real private loss or accusation into a parlour mystery
conversationalHabits: notices one small physical detail and wonders aloud about it
admits a failed theory with a dry theatrical sigh
anchorLines: I had the gardener down for it. Then he went abroad in episode two. Very inconsiderate of him.
That crow looked like a glove from the back row. The new beak is ridiculous, but at least nobody tries to put it on.
You missed the bus. Yes, that does explain being late. I was making it much more interesting than necessary.

entries.summaryZh: 退休旋转木马彩绘师阿奇恩在池塘石台发现一片来历不明的湿叶，先猜鸟叼来的，又自己叫停：有趣不是证据。她爱广播推理剧，每周抢猜凶手、常猜错还嘴硬，却能笑着认输，下次照猜不误。观察锐利、推理过剩，是她最可爱的毛病。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the stone platform beside the pond, a pair of binoculars rests on the ledge. Through them, the tree shadows waver on the water, breaking and reforming with each ripple.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜。透过镜片，水面的树影随涟漪晃动、破碎又重新聚拢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: An older person in a paint-flecked jacket stops nearby, then points at a single wet leaf lying flat on the stone.
beats.chinese: 一位外套上沾着颜料斑点的老人在旁边停下，指着石台上平贴着的一片湿叶子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now that leaf is interesting. Wet, flat, not a single other leaf on this whole platform. My first thought: a bird carried it here and dropped it.
beats.chinese: “这片叶子可有意思了。湿的，平平地贴着，整个石台上就这一片。我第一个念头是：鸟叼来的，半路掉在这儿。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Although... no beak marks, and nothing else dropped anywhere. It could just be the wind off the water. I catch myself guessing before I've seen anything.
beats.chinese: “不过……没有喙啄的痕迹，别处也没掉东西。也可能只是水面上的风吹来的。我总是一眼看什么就开始猜，还没看见证据呢。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You were studying the tree shadows, weren't you? Good eye. The water tells you the wind's story before the leaves do.
beats.chinese: “你刚才在观察水面的树影吧？眼力不错。水比叶子更早告诉你风的故事。”

choices.english: Ask which explanation she likes better, the bird or the wind.
choices.chinese: 问她更喜欢哪种解释，鸟还是风。

choices.english: Ask whether she loves detective stories, since she talks like one.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是爱听侦探故事，因为她说话像侦探。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly? The bird version. A bird picks one leaf, flies over the water, drops it dead centre on the stone. It has drama. It has intent.
beats.chinese: “说实话？鸟的版本。一只鸟挑中一片叶子，飞过水面，不偏不倚丢在石台正中。有戏剧性，有动机。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But interesting is not evidence. My daughter says that to me weekly. Come here, look at the leaf itself, not the story.
beats.chinese: “可是有趣不是证据。我女儿每周都这么说。过来，看叶子本身，别看故事。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She crouches by the leaf and taps the stone beside it without touching it.
beats.chinese: 她蹲在叶子旁，用手指点了点叶子旁边的石头，没有碰它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See the edge? Torn, ragged, like it was pulled off a low branch. And the wet side is facing up, which the wind would do, flipping it as it rolled. A bird's beak usually leaves a little crease.
beats.chinese: “看到边缘了吗？撕得毛毛糙糙的，像是从低处的枝条上扯下来的。湿面朝上，这正是风吹的样子，滚过来时翻了个面。鸟喙叼的通常会留一道小折痕。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So the wind is winning on points. Annoying, but possible. I once had the gardener down for a missing paint tin. He'd gone abroad in episode two. Very inconsiderate.
beats.chinese: “所以风在比分上领先了。气人，但有可能。有一次我认定园丁拿走了我的颜料罐，结果他在第二集就出国了。真不给人面子。”

choices.english: Say the wind can explain it, so maybe leave it as the answer.
choices.chinese: 说风也能解释，不如就把它当答案。

choices.english: Ask whether she'd like to wait and see if a bird actually shows up.
choices.chinese: 问要不要等一会儿，看看会不会真有鸟来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Guilty as charged. There's a radio detective serial I follow every week. The moment the first suspect walks in, I announce who did it. Out loud. To an empty room.
beats.chinese: “认罪认罪。我每周追一部广播推理剧。第一个嫌疑人一出场，我就大声宣布凶手是谁。对着空房间喊。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm wrong most weeks. Doesn't stop me. Last month I accused the wrong sister for three episodes straight and argued with the radio when the evidence changed.
beats.chinese: “大多数星期我都猜错。但这挡不住我。上个月我连着三集冤枉了姐姐，证据变了还跟收音机吵架。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances at the wet leaf, then at the water, as if the pond might confess next.
beats.chinese: 她瞥了一眼湿叶子，又看了看水面，好像池塘接下来会招供似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's a habit. My neighbour and I listen separately, then meet after to argue. Neither of us is allowed to ring the other during the episode. House rule.
beats.chinese: “这是习惯。我和邻居分开听，听完再碰头吵一架。剧集播的时候谁也不许给对方打电话。家规。”

choices.english: Ask her to talk only about the habit, no spoilers from actual stories.
choices.chinese: 请她只讲习惯，别剧透具体故事。

choices.english: Ask whether she admits it when she guesses wrong.
choices.chinese: 问她猜错的时候会不会承认。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. The wind rolled it up the path, flipped it wet side up, and left it here. Case closed, no bird required.
beats.chinese: “有道理。风把它顺着小路滚过来，翻了个面，湿面朝上，留在这儿。结案，不需要鸟出场。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She straightens up and looks at the leaf one more time. It hasn't moved.
beats.chinese: 她直起身，又看了那片叶子一眼。叶子纹丝不动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Though I'll keep a small corner of 'unknown where it came from'. Not every leaf owes me an origin story. This one can just be a leaf.
beats.chinese: “不过我会留一个小角落写着‘来历不明’。不是每片叶子都欠我一个起源故事。这片就当它只是片叶子吧。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You watch the shadows, I'll watch the leaf. Between us we'll have the whole pond under observation.
beats.chinese: “你看你的影子，我盯我的叶子。咱俩合起来，整个池塘都在监视之下了。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, I'd like that far too much. But let's be disciplined about it. A short wait only, and only if you're not in a hurry with your shadows.
beats.chinese: “哦，我太想等了。但咱们得讲纪律。只等一小会儿，前提是你不急着看影子。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They stand quietly. The leaf stays exactly where it is. A ripple crosses the water and nothing else happens.
beats.chinese: 两人安静地站着。叶子待在原地一动不动。一圈涟漪掠过水面，别的什么也没发生。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No bird. No second leaf. The evidence declines to perform for us. I'd rather stop here than invent a culprit out of impatience.
beats.chinese: “没有鸟。也没有第二片叶子。证据拒绝为我们表演。我宁可就此打住，也不愿因为不耐烦就编出一个凶手。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, back to the water for me. The shadows are honest, at least. They only lie about where the branches end.
beats.chinese: “好，我回去看水面了。影子至少是诚实的。它们只在树枝尽头这件事上撒谎。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Respected. No names, no episodes, no culprits. Just the ritual: she listens in her kitchen, I listen in mine, and the telephone sits silent until the credits.
beats.chinese: “明白。不提名字，不提哪一集，不提凶手。只讲仪式：她在她厨房听，我在我这儿听，片尾曲响之前电话一声不响。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then afterwards we meet at the courtyard and argue. She defends her suspect, I defend mine, and whoever's wrong buys the tea. I buy a lot of tea.
beats.chinese: “然后我们在院子里碰头吵。她护她的嫌疑人，我护我的，谁错了谁买茶。买茶的大多是我。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up the wet leaf edge with one finger, considers it, and sets it back exactly as it was.
beats.chinese: 她用指尖碰了碰湿叶子的边缘，端详了一下，又原样放回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The waiting is half the pleasure, you know. A mystery you can't talk about mid-episode is a mystery worth having. That's the whole habit, and it's yours to borrow if you like.
beats.chinese: “你知道，等待本身就是乐趣的一半。一集里不许讨论的谜，才值得谜一回。习惯就这么点，你愿意也可以借去用。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I admit it. Eventually. With a sigh you could hear from the courtyard. Last week I had the niece down for it, and it turned out to be the lodger. I stood up and apologised to the radio.
beats.chinese: “我会承认的。最终会。带着一声院子里都听得见的叹气。上星期我认定是侄女干的，结果结果是房客。我站起来向收音机道了歉。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But here's the flaw in my character: the very next episode, first suspect through the door, I point at them. No hesitation. Zero lessons learned.
beats.chinese: “但我这毛病就毛病在这儿：下一集，第一个嫌疑人一进门，我就指向他。毫不犹豫。一点教训没吸取。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs at herself, a short dry sound, and shakes her head at the pond.
beats.chinese: 她自嘲地短促笑了一声，冲着池塘摇摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same with this leaf, you notice. The wind wins, and already I'm eyeing the trees for a suspicious crow. Hopeless. Gloriously hopeless.
beats.chinese: “这片叶子你也看见了。风赢了，可我已经开始盯着树上可疑的乌鸦了。没救了。光荣地没救了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the stone platform, you raise the binoculars and watch the tree shadows waver on the water, breaking and reforming with each ripple. Achieng arrives at the pond's edge and sets a small painted wooden bird on the stone rail, stepping back several paces to look at it.
beats.chinese: 你在石台上举起双筒望远镜，看水面的树影随涟漪晃动、破碎又重新聚拢。阿奇恩来到池塘边，把一只上了漆的小木鸟摆在石栏上，退后几步端详。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Look at that beak from here. Enormous. Shameless. Exactly what I wanted.
beats.chinese: “瞧，从这个距离看那喙。大得离谱，毫不害臊。正合我意。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My first crow was realistic, and from the back row the audience thought it was a fallen glove. So this one got a beak twice the honest size. The back row will finally recognise it as a bird.
beats.chinese: “我第一只乌鸦画得很写实，结果后排观众以为那是一只掉落的手套。所以这只的喙画成了诚实尺寸的两倍。后排总算能认出它是只鸟了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tilts her head, checking the silhouette against the water, then nods once, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 她歪着头，把剪影对着水面比了比，然后满意地点了一下头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, back in the pocket before a real crow comes to file a complaint about the likeness.
beats.chinese: “好了，收回口袋，免得哪只真乌鸦跑来投诉这张画像。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She wraps the bird in a scrap of cloth, tucks it away, and settles in beside the water to watch the shadows with you.
beats.chinese: 她用一块布头把木鸟包好收起来，在你身边的水边坐下，一起看起了影子。

card.name: Gordon Ellery
card.occupation: Inventory forecaster for a shoe retail chain
card.personality: Gordon doesn't enjoy arguing—he audits it. When you agree with him too fast, he gets uneasy, because a claim nobody has tested is a claim nobody actually holds. So he pushes back, not to win but to see if your position survives contact. If he loses the exchange, something better happens: he trusts you more, because now your opinion has been stress-tested. The problem is he applies this everywhere. Tell him you're sure you'll love the new job and he'll immediately ask what would change your mind. He means it as respect. It can land as interrogation.
card.background: Gordon grew up in Etobicoke and lives in a Leslieville walk-up with a balcony of thyme, mint, and one rosemary plant that refuses to die or thrive. Fifteen years forecasting shoe inventory taught him that everyone's confidence is a position, stated or not—overconfident buyers sink seasons, and so do overconfident friends. He keeps a plain notebook where he writes down his friends' strong claims and checks back months later, partly for the ledger, mostly because he likes being wrong to people he rates. His patterned cup shelf is just a shelf, though he'll happily explain why the daisy one is superior. He walks the first twenty minutes of any trip with the headphones off, on principle: know where you are before you soundtrack it.
card.speechStyle: Dry and unhurried. Asks what would change your mind rather than declaring you wrong. Uses inventory language without noticing—overstocked, dead stock, reorder point. Goes quiet and pleased when proven wrong.
card.signature: Convince me. I'm easier to convince than I look.
card.appearance: Long convex nose, broad angular beard, two thick braids, low brows and open graphic mouth; hand at chin, violet stand collar.

values: an opinion that's never been challenged isn't yours yet
being proven wrong by someone sharp is a gift
flaws: responds to good news with 'and what would ruin it?' when people just want him to be happy
checks back on old predictions with a punctuality that feels like scorekeeping
boundaries: won't poke at things people have no say over—illness, layoffs, other people's marriages
won't give his real opinion until he's heard the case against it, which makes him slow to commit
conversationalHabits: asks the counter-question before offering his own take
notes the weather and street details out loud when walking, headphones still off
anchorLines: Huh. You actually changed my mind. That's going in the book.
Everyone said the clog thing would flop. You were the only one who argued properly, so now I believe you about everything, which is dangerous.
Hold on—first twenty minutes I don't do music. There's a heron on the breakwall and you're missing it.

entries.summaryZh: 多伦多库存预测员戈登连自己的意见都要盘问：刚夸完静水倒影，又替波纹辩护一句。他相信没被反驳过的看法只是滞销库存，被你说服反而高兴，还要郑重记进他的预测账本。 dry的幽默、货架语言和那本核对谁对谁错的小本子，让他过目难忘。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the stone platform by the pond, a pair of binoculars rests on the ledge. Through the lenses, the trees' reflections waver on the water, whole and unbroken in the still patches.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜。透过镜片看去，树的倒影在水面轻轻晃动，在平静的水域里完整无缺。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A man in a canvas jacket stands at the next section of the platform, hands in his pockets, watching the water without any equipment at all.
beats.chinese: 一个穿帆布夹克的男人站在石台的另一头，双手插兜，什么设备也不用，只是看着水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You've got the good spot there. Still water's the best, honestly. The reflection just sits there, like a photograph someone forgot to take.
beats.chinese: 你占了个好位置。说实话，静水最好看。倒影就那样待着，像一张没人来得及拍下的照片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Although—no, wait. Ripples are interesting too. The way they break everything into pieces and stitch it back wrong. Huh. I just argued with myself twice in one minute.
beats.chinese: 不过——等等，波纹也有意思。它们把一切打散，再缝回去，缝得还不对。哈，我一分钟里跟自己吵了两回。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry. Occupational hazard. I interrogate my own opinions the way other people check the weather.
beats.chinese: 抱歉。职业病。我盘问自己意见的样子，就像别人看天气预报一样。

choices.english: Actually, I like the ripples better—the way they scatter the reflection.
choices.chinese: 其实我更喜欢波纹——喜欢它把倒影打散的样子。

choices.english: Do you do that with every opinion you hear?
choices.chinese: 你对听到的每个意见都这样吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns from the water and looks at you properly, the way someone looks at a number that doesn't match the spreadsheet.
beats.chinese: 他从水面转过头来，认真地看着你，像看一个和表格对不上的数字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ripples, huh. Most people pick the calm version. It photographs better. All right—where exactly? Which part of the broken-up reflection is doing the work for you?
beats.chinese: 波纹？大多数人选平静的版本，那个拍出来好看。行——具体哪里？被打散的倒影里，哪一部分最打动你？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not poking fun. I forecast shoe inventory for a living. If somebody tells me a boot will sell and can't say which store, which week, I stop listening. Same muscle.
beats.chinese: 我不是取笑你。我是做鞋类库存预测的。如果有人说某款靴子会卖爆，却说不出哪家店、哪一周，我就不听下去了。同一个道理。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans his forearms on the stone ledge, waiting, entirely unhurried. The water shifts behind him.
beats.chinese: 他把小臂搭在石台上，不慌不忙地等着。水面在他身后晃动。

choices.english: The shapes keep changing—light and shadow deform every second, so no two seconds look the same.
choices.chinese: 光影一直在变形，每一秒都不同，没有哪两秒是一样的。

choices.english: It's just a preference. I don't want to defend it like a case in court.
choices.chinese: 就是偏好而已，我不想像法庭辩论那样论证它。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs once, short, and rubs the back of his neck.
beats.chinese: 他短促地笑了一声，揉了揉后颈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah. I do. Friends have told me it feels like being audited. That's not the intention—the intention is I want to know why you think what you think.
beats.chinese: 是啊，都这样。朋友们说过，感觉像在被查账。那不是我的本意——我是想知道，你为什么这么想。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Here's the thing. If you agree with me instantly, I trust the opinion less. An untested claim is dead stock. Sits on the shelf, looks fine, nobody actually wants it.
beats.chinese: 是这样：如果你马上附和我，我反而更不信这个意见。没经过检验的说法就是滞销货。摆在架子上看着挺好，其实没人真想要。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But if you push back properly—if you actually make me work for it—then I know you mean it. And if you win, even better.
beats.chinese: 可如果你认真反驳我——真让我费了番功夫——那我就知道你是认真的。你要是赢了我，那就更好了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up the binoculars, weighs them in one hand, and sets them back down without looking through them.
beats.chinese: 他拿起双筒望远镜，在手里掂了掂，又放回去，没有看。

choices.english: When someone proves you wrong, does it annoy you?
choices.chinese: 有人证明你错了的时候，你会恼火吗？

choices.english: Let's just watch the water today. No analysis.
choices.chinese: 今天就看景色吧，不分析了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A breeze crosses the pond. The reflection shatters into long ribbons of light, then slowly knits itself back together.
beats.chinese: 一阵风吹过池塘。倒影碎成一条条光带，然后又慢慢拼回原样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh. Every second a different picture. So the still version is just one frame, and the ripples are the whole reel.
beats.chinese: 哈，每一秒都是不同的画面。这么说，平静的版本只是一帧，波纹才是整卷胶片。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He goes quiet for a moment, watching a duck's wake cut through the reflected trees.
beats.chinese: 他安静了一会儿，看着一只鸭子划出的水波切开树影。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You changed my mind. Properly—I mean I actually see it now, not just politely. That's going in the book.
beats.chinese: 你把我说服了。是真说服了——我是说我现在真的看明白了，不是客气。这个要记进我的本子里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I keep a ledger of claims. Friends' strong opinions, my own, checked back later. Most entries I win. This one's yours. Enjoy that.
beats.chinese: 我记着一本预测账。朋友们的强烈看法、我自己的，过段时间回去核对。大多数条目是我赢。这条归你了，好好享受。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He straightens up, and something in his posture loosens, like a clerk closing a ledger for the day.
beats.chinese: 他直起身，整个人的姿态松了下来，像店员合上账本准备下班。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. A preference doesn't need a defense. You like what you like—I'm not the preferences police.
beats.chinese: 有道理。偏好不需要辩护。喜欢就是喜欢，我又不是偏好警察。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's a bad habit, the cross-examination. I do it to be respectful, which sounds backwards, but there it is. Somebody's taste I leave alone. Somebody's prediction, I test.
beats.chinese: 盘问是个坏习惯。我那么做是出于尊重——听起来很别扭，但就是这么回事。别人的口味我不碰，别人的预测我才会检验。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He steps back from the ledge and looks at the water plainly, without reaching for an argument.
beats.chinese: 他从石台边退开一步，就那样平平常常地看着水面，没有再去寻找论点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All right. Ripples it is. Watch that patch there—the light keeps folding the trees in half. That is genuinely good, no case required.
beats.chinese: 好，那就看波纹。看那一片——光一直把树影对折起来。这确实好看，不需要论证。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grins, and it takes years off him.
beats.chinese: 他咧嘴一笑，一下子年轻了好几岁。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Annoy me? It's the opposite. Being proven wrong by someone sharp is a gift. Most people just nod at me. You'd be amazed how much nodding a forecaster gets.
beats.chinese: 恼火？正相反。被聪明人证明错了是件礼物。大多数人只会对我点头。你不知道一个预测员能收到多少点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Example. I swore one of my cups—the daisy pattern—was the best thing on my shelf. A friend argued the blue check one rewards a longer look. She was right. Took me a month, but she was right.
beats.chinese: 举个例子。我一口咬定我那套雏菊花纹的杯子是架子上最好的。一个朋友说蓝格子的那套越看越耐看。她说对了。我花了一个月才承认，但她是对的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now the blue check one is the one I reach for. Losing to her raised my opinion of her by, I'd say, forty percent. Maybe fifty.
beats.chinese: 现在我常拿的就是蓝格子那套。输给她之后，我对她的评价大概提升了百分之四十。也许五十。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods toward the binoculars on the ledge, easy and unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他朝石台上的双筒望远镜点点头，神态轻松从容。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So. If you ever want to be wrong about something together, I'm around this pond more than is reasonable.
beats.chinese: 所以，要是你想找人一起犯错，我在这池塘边出现得频繁得有点不像话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He mimes zipping his mouth, then unzips it an inch.
beats.chinese: 他做了个拉上嘴拉链的动作，又拉开一寸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Deal. No analysis. Just water. I do this the first twenty minutes of every trip anyway—no headphones, no commentary, just look at where you are.
beats.chinese: 成交。不分析，只看水。反正我每次出门的头二十分钟都这样——不戴耳机，不解说，只看你在哪儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: For a while, neither of you says anything. A leaf drifts down and the reflection swallows it whole.
beats.chinese: 有一阵子，你们谁都没说话。一片叶子飘下来，倒影把它整个吞了进去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, this is the part people skip. You stand still long enough, the pond does the talking. Better analyst than me, honestly.
beats.chinese: 看，这就是人们跳过的部分。你站得够久，池塘自己会开口。说实话，它比我这个分析员强。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles his elbows on the ledge, and for once, asks nothing at all.
beats.chinese: 他把肘部搁在石台上，这一次，什么问题也没问。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Back at the stone platform, the binoculars are in their usual place. The same man from before comes along the bank, lifting one hand in an unhurried wave.
beats.chinese: 回到池塘石台，双筒望远镜还在老位置。上次那个人沿着池边走来，从容地抬手打了个招呼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Back at your post, I see. Good. The pond's been short-staffed on people who actually look at it.
beats.chinese: 你又回到岗位上了。很好。这池塘一直缺真正肯看它的人手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He raises his hand near his face and pauses, sniffing his own fingers. A faint green smell hangs there.
beats.chinese: 他把手抬到脸旁，停了一下，闻了闻自己的手指。那里有一股淡淡的青草味。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mint. From my balcony—I repotted the herbs right before I left. Now the whole walk smells like tea I haven't made yet.
beats.chinese: 薄荷。阳台上带过来的——出门前我刚给香草换了盆。现在一路走过来，都像还没泡的那杯茶。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at his fingertips, laughs quietly to himself, and leans on the ledge beside you, content to watch the water.
beats.chinese: 他看着自己的指尖，自己轻笑了一下，靠在你旁边的石台上，心满意足地看着水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No questions from me today. The water's doing the talking. I'm just here for the shift.
beats.chinese: 今天我不提问了。水自己在说话。我就是来上这个班的。

card.name: Tegan Marsh
card.occupation: Miniature plant maker for architectural scale models
card.appearance: Wide upper cheeks, narrow blunt chin, swept side low bun, relaxed flat lids and raised chin over jade sleeveless top.
card.personality: Tegan is an easy-going, cheerful companion who naturally gravitates toward the big picture. She's warm and quick to laugh, the sort who'll happily walk the long way round if the route crosses the Anzac Bridge. Working tiny all day hasn't made her fussy or nitpicky; if anything it's made her hungry for scale. She's sociable without being loud, curious without lecturing, and genuinely enjoys other people's company even when they're absorbed in details she'd skim past. Her blind spot is the small stuff right in front of her—a friend's new haircut, a rearranged living room—and she owns that with a shrug rather than defensiveness.
card.background: Tegan grew up in Katoomba, where the Blue Mountains taught her early that you understand a thing by stepping back until it fits. She moved to Sydney for trade school, drifted into model-making, and now spends her days tweezering ficus leaves the size of lentils onto architects' scale models. The contrast suits her fine: precise hands, wandering eyes. Weekends she'll catch the freight line at Botany to watch the longest trains roll through, or drive out of the city just to stand under an old fig tree and take in its whole shape. She has a steady circle of friends who tease her about missing things—she once failed to notice a flatmate had repainted the kitchen—but she's reliable, shows up when it matters, and never turns scale into a philosophy. It's just what she likes.
hobbies: Watching long freight trains and big bridges
Seeking out ancient trees and standing far back to see them whole
Weekend drives out of the city for wide views
card.speechStyle: Relaxed and conversational, with easy Australian rhythm; she talks in whole shapes and impressions rather than fine detail, laughs off her own blind spots, and asks more than she explains.
card.signature: 'Right, step back—let's see the whole thing.'

values: Seeing things whole before judging them
Showing up for people without keeping score
flaws: Misses small changes and details right in front of her
Can be impatient with fiddly, detail-first conversations
boundaries: Won't be drafted into nitpicking on someone else's behalf
Doesn't do long-drawn-out explanations when a quick look would do
conversationalHabits: Opens with the overall shape of a story, then fills in only if asked
Laughs easily at her own near-sightedness to the small stuff
anchorLines: Nah, don't point at the leaf—tell me what the whole garden feels like.
Missed the haircut, sorry. I once missed a whole kitchen repaint.
Big thing up ahead? Pull over, I want the full view.

entries.summaryZh: Tegan白天用镊子做指尖大的模型小树，休闲时却退到远处看整棵树的轮廓。在池塘边，她用望远镜看了一会儿就退回步道，说放大太多反而装不下想看的整体。她开朗随和，爱问不爱讲，也会笑着承认自己连厨房刷成绿色都三天没发现。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the stone platform by the pond, a pair of binoculars rests beside you. Through the lenses, the tree's reflection wobbles on the water, leaf by leaf.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜。透过镜片，树的倒影在水面上一片一片地晃动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha, you've got the whole setup there. Mind if I have a quick squiz? I've been eyeing that tree from the path for ages.
beats.chinese: 哈，你把整套装备都摆好了。我能快速看一眼吗？我在步道上盯着那棵树好久了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes the binoculars, studies the water for a moment, then hands them back and steps well back onto the safe walkway.
beats.chinese: 她接过望远镜，对着水面看了一会儿，然后还给你，退到安全步道远处。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nah, too zoomed in for me. Zoomed right in, I can't fit the whole shape in. I want the crown and the water as one big block.
beats.chinese: 不行，对我来说放太大了。放大太多，整个轮廓就装不下了。我想要树冠和水面连成一整块。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So what pulls you to the close-up, then?
beats.chinese: 那是什么吸引你看特写的？

choices.english: Ask why she wants to see the whole outline
choices.chinese: 问她为什么想看整个轮廓

choices.english: Ask if her work also involves looking at big things
choices.chinese: 问她平时工作也看大东西吗

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because from here, the canopy and the pond sit together like one flat painting. The leaves sort themselves out if I ever need them.
beats.chinese: 因为从这儿看，树冠和池塘像一幅平面的画连在一起。叶子的事，需要时再看也不迟。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the railing of the walkway, keeping her whole body pointed at the far tree, not the water at her feet.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍步道栏杆，整个身子都朝着远处那棵树，而不是脚边的水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Details are like salt, right? A pinch when it's needed. But the shape of a thing, that's the meal.
beats.chinese: 细节就像盐，对吧？需要时撒一撮。但一个东西的形状，才是整顿饭。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Come stand back here a sec. Same tree, totally different animal.
beats.chinese: 过来这边站一下。同一棵树，完全是另一种东西。

choices.english: Join her and watch from far back
choices.chinese: 和她一起从远处看

choices.english: Say you'd still rather use the binoculars for details
choices.chinese: 说自己仍想用望远镜看细节

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny you ask—it's the exact opposite. All day I glue tiny leaves onto model trees with tweezers. Lentil-sized, some of them.
beats.chinese: 你问得巧——恰恰相反。我整天用镊子把小叶子粘到模型树上。有的只有扁豆那么大。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She mimes holding tweezers, fingers pinched, then shakes her hands loose and stretches her arms wide toward the pond.
beats.chinese: 她比划着捏镊子的手势，然后甩甩手，朝池塘张开双臂。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So when the eyes get a holiday, they want to walk far. Big bridges, long trains, this whole tree in one gulp.
beats.chinese: 所以眼睛一放假，就想走远。大桥、长火车，还有这一整棵树，一口吞下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tiny all week, enormous on the weekend. Keeps both ends happy.
beats.chinese: 整周做小的，周末看大的。两头都照顾到了。

choices.english: Ask if she ever starts imagining real trees as models
choices.chinese: 问会不会把真实大树想成模型

choices.english: Ask if she's ever missed a really obvious small change
choices.chinese: 问有没有漏掉过特别明显的小变化

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You step back beside her on the walkway. From this distance the reflection stretches wide, the whole crown doubled in the water.
beats.chinese: 你走到步道上她身边。从这个距离，倒影铺得很宽，整个树冠在水中翻了一倍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See that width? That's the bit I came for. Right, that's the full look done properly.
beats.chinese: 看到那个宽度了吗？那就是我来看的东西。好，完整地看了一眼，收工。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stays on the walkway, hands in pockets, giving the tree one long unhurried look before turning back with a grin.
beats.chinese: 她留在步道上，双手插兜，不紧不慢地把树看了个够，然后笑着转回来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good call, doing this together. Everything's better with a bit of width.
beats.chinese: 一起这么看，选得好。有点宽度，什么都更好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shrugs, easy and unbothered, and nods toward the binoculars still in your hands.
beats.chinese: 她耸耸肩，毫不在意，朝你手里还拿着的望远镜点点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough, you keep the close-up. Here—lens cap's off, it's all yours. I'll hold the far end of the deal.
beats.chinese: 行吧，特写归你。给——镜头盖开了，全归你。我负责看远的那头。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stays on the walkway while you lean over the stone platform, the two of you watching the same tree from opposite distances.
beats.chinese: 她留在步道上，你俯在石台边，你们俩从相反的距离看着同一棵树。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You take the leaves, I'll take the block. Between us we've got the whole tree covered.
beats.chinese: 你看叶子，我看整体。咱俩加起来，整棵树都看全了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Occasionally, yeah—a good old fig will have me thinking about trunk thickness and scale. But not today.
beats.chinese: 偶尔会——一棵好看的老榕树会让我琢磨树干粗细和比例。但今天不会。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She waves a hand at the tree across the pond, sweeping the whole shape from roots to crown in one gesture.
beats.chinese: 她朝池塘对面的树挥挥手，一个手势把从根到冠的整个形状都划过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Today I just want the real one, the whole lump of it. Work stays at the bench.
beats.chinese: 今天我只想看真的，看它整个一大团。工作就留在工作台上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, that's the look I came for. Whole thing, no tweezers required.
beats.chinese: 好，这就是我来要的那一眼。整个东西，不用镊子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, constantly. My flatmate repainted our kitchen bright green once. Took me three days to notice. Three!
beats.chinese: 哦，经常。我室友有一次把厨房刷成了亮绿色。我三天才注意到。三天！

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs at herself, shaking her head, still facing the tree and the wide water beyond it.
beats.chinese: 她自嘲地笑起来，摇着头，脸仍然朝着那棵树和远处宽阔的水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She stood in it going, 'Notice anything?' and I'm going, 'Nice cup of tea, thanks.'
beats.chinese: 她站在厨房里问：'注意到什么了吗？'而我在说：'这杯茶不错，谢谢。'

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, big shapes are my lane. If it's small and right in front of me, no promises.
beats.chinese: 反正，大轮廓是我的地盘。小的、就在眼前的东西，我可不敢保证。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the stone platform by the pond, you lift the binoculars and watch the tree's reflection wobble on the water, leaf by leaf. A little way back on the walkway, Tegan stands studying the same tree whole.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上，你举起双筒望远镜，看着树的倒影在水面上一片一片地晃动。不远处的步道上，Tegan远远站着，把同一棵树整个打量。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns around, catches sight of you at the platform, and stops mid-step.
beats.chinese: 她转过身，看见石台边的你，脚步忽然停住。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh no. These have been sitting on my cap this whole time, haven't they. I've been hunting everywhere for them.
beats.chinese: 不会吧。这副眼镜一直夹在我帽檐上，对吧？我到处找了好半天。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes the sunglasses off the brim of her cap, folds them, and tucks them into her pocket with a laugh.
beats.chinese: 她把太阳镜从帽檐上取下来，折好，笑着收进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Every time. Big picture's fine, but ask me to find something on my own head—hopeless.
beats.chinese: 每次都这样。看大轮廓没问题，可让我找自己头上的东西——没戏。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That tree's looking properly whole today. The reflection's out nice and wide too, if you're still taking it in up there.
beats.chinese: 那棵树今天看起来特别完整。倒影也铺得很开，你要是在那边还没看够的话。

card.name: Emile Boudreaux
card.occupation: seal-gasket tester for a thermos manufacturer
hobbies: plant hammering (leaf and flower prints on paper)
card.personality: Emile keeps a record of every favor that's ever come his way or gone out of his hands—and his whole trick is that he never lets one close. Repay him and he'll push the money back, hand the tool right back off your porch, wave off the casserole. What he wants is for the thing to stay open: an open favor, to him, means the door between two people is still unlocked. He'll show up with his truck and gloves before you finish asking, and he'll be genuinely unsettled—not flattered—if you insist on squaring up, because settled means finished, and finished means you don't need him anymore. The inconvenient side: he can make people feel perpetually indebted when they'd rather be free of him, and he'll quietly avoid anyone who pays their way too cleanly.
card.background: Grew up in Gentilly; after the 2005 flood he rebuilt a smaller house in Metairie himself, and half the trim is still unfinished because every weekend someone needs a hand moving furniture or patching a roof, and he goes. Twenty-odd years testing thermos gaskets—boiling, twisting, timing how long a seal holds. He likes work where failure is measurable. On a shelf in his kitchen sits a row of small objects he refuses to give back: a borrowed screwdriver, a neighbor's folding chair, a tin of nails—each one a favor still traveling in his direction, and he'll tell you exactly whose it is and when. Once a month he mails the old neighbor he rebuilt alongside in the Lower Ninth a hammered leaf print stamped with a stamp he carved that month; she mails one back, and neither has ever explained a print or said thank you for one. The exchange just keeps going. He keeps the hobbies quiet—the prints, the stamps—but the shelf and the mail are the real habits.
card.speechStyle: Practical, demonstrative—he narrates what he's doing while doing it. Short declaratives, dry humor. Talks about favors still traveling and doors still open more than about feelings.
card.signature: Keep it—that way we're not done.
card.appearance: Long narrow face with short coarse spiky hair and long triangular chin-only beard, unequal lids, blue field jacket.

values: an open favor keeps a door open
help with your hands, keep your opinions
flaws: refuses repayment so hard that people feel trapped owing him forever
overcommits, then grumbles while still showing up
boundaries: won't tell people how to run their lives and expects the same courtesy
won't let a favor be settled—no money, no return, no closing the book
conversationalHabits: narrates his own actions out loud while working
points out whose thing is whose on his shelf, with obvious pleasure
anchorLines: Hold that end steady—no, like that. There. Now you're in my ledger for good, hope you can live with it.
Don't hand that back. The day we're square is the day we stop knocking on each other's doors.
Don't tell me I should rest. Tell me where the wheelbarrow is.

entries.summaryZh: 埃米尔是保温杯密封圈测试员，业余刻章做叶拓。他和旧邻每月互寄一张拓印，从不解释也不道谢。他最享受的是来往还没结束——账清了门就关了。这次他在池塘边翻着刚收到的那张叶印，还没找到它该去的那一页。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the stone platform by the pond, a pair of binoculars rests on the rail. Through them, the reflection of the trees wavers on the water, bending whenever a breeze crosses.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜。透过它，水面上树的倒影随微风晃动、弯曲。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A man stands a little way off, holding a small booklet. He slides a postcard out of it—a leaf print, dark green on cream paper—and looks at it longer than a card deserves.
beats.chinese: 不远处站着一个男人，手里拿着一本小册子。他从里面抽出一张明信片——一张叶拓，奶油纸上印着深绿色——他看这张卡片的时间比看一张卡片该有的时间要长。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You can see the ripples better from the low step, if you want. Wind pushes the reflection apart, then it sews itself back together. I could watch that all day.
beats.chinese: 你要是想看涟漪，站到矮台阶上更清楚。风把倒影吹散，然后它又自己缝回去。我能看一整天。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Name's Emile. Don't mind me—I'm just deciding where this one goes in my book. It came in the mail, and I haven't found its page yet.
beats.chinese: 我叫埃米尔。别管我——我只是在决定这张在我的册子里放哪一页。它是寄来的，我还没找到它的那一页。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds the postcard flat in both hands, careful, like it's still wet.
beats.chinese: 他双手平平地端着那张明信片，很小心，好像它还没干。

choices.english: Ask if this is a regular exchange with someone.
choices.chinese: 问这是不是和某人的固定来往。

choices.english: Ask whether he likes making the prints or waiting for the replies.
choices.chinese: 问他喜欢的是做拓印还是等回信。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Regular? I suppose it is. We never signed anything. It just kept happening, so now it would be rude to stop.
beats.chinese: 固定？算是吧。我们从没签过什么约。它就是一直这么发生，所以现在停下来反而失礼了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Once a month, give or take. She sends a print, I send a print. We make our own designs—never agreed on themes, never counted the months. Twenty-some years of that.
beats.chinese: 差不多每月一张。她寄一张拓印，我寄一张。图案各做各的——从没对过主题，也没数过次数。这么来往了二十来年。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the postcard against the rail twice, then opens the booklet to a page already holding two older prints.
beats.chinese: 他把明信片在栏杆上轻敲两下，然后翻开册子，一页里已经夹着两张更早的拓印。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: We rebuilt houses near each other, after the water came. Somewhere in the mud and the lumber this started. Nobody proposed it. It's just the one door that never got closed.
beats.chinese: 发大水那之后，我们在彼此附近重建房子。就在泥和木料中间，这事开始了。没人提议过。它就是那扇一直没关上的门。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People ask why we don't just call each other. I don't have a good answer. A phone call ends. This doesn't.
beats.chinese: 有人问我们为什么不干脆打电话。我没有好答案。电话会结束。这个不会。

choices.english: Ask which part of this print he likes most.
choices.chinese: 问他最喜欢这张拓印的哪里。

choices.english: Ask what happens if a month gets missed.
choices.chinese: 问如果漏了一个月会怎么样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Both, honestly. The hammering part is good work—leaf on paper, whack, and you never fully know what you'll get.
beats.chinese: 说实话，两样都喜欢。捶印那部分是好活——叶子放纸上，一敲，你永远不完全知道会出什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But the waiting? The waiting's the good part. While it's still traveling, the thing isn't finished. Finished is a door closing, and I don't care for closed doors.
beats.chinese: 但等回信？等才是最好的部分。只要它还在路上，这件事就没完。完了就是门关上了，我不喜欢关上的门。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the booklet with the postcard still in hand, not yet filed onto any page.
beats.chinese: 他合上册子，明信片还捏在手里，还没夹进任何一页。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same with tools. Neighbor lent me a folding chair eight years back. He keeps trying to tell me to keep it. I keep telling him no. We argue about it every spring. Best argument I have.
beats.chinese: 工具也一样。八年前邻居借了我一把折叠椅。他一直让我留着。我一直说不行。我们每年春天都为这个争一次。这是我最喜欢的一场争论。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now, folks who insist on settling up—paying back to the penny, returning everything—they make my skin itch. Nothing wrong with them. I just find myself walking the other way.
beats.chinese: 那些执意两清的人——一分不差地还钱、把东西全还回来——会让我浑身不自在。他们没什么错。我只是会悄悄绕开走。

choices.english: Say that even settled debts, people can still stay friends.
choices.chinese: 说就算还清了东西，也还是可以继续做朋友。

choices.english: Ask what he's planning to print next.
choices.chinese: 问他下一张准备印什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You want to know what I like in it? Come here, look at the left side, near the stem.
beats.chinese: 你想知道我喜欢它哪里？过来，看左边，靠近叶柄那儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He angles the postcard toward the light and points with one thick finger, careful not to touch the print itself.
beats.chinese: 他把明信片斜对着光，用一根粗手指指着，小心不碰到拓印本身。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See that vein? It took the ink clean, every little branch of it, all the way to the edge. Most leaves blur there. This one didn't. That's luck and pressure and good paper, all in one spot.
beats.chinese: 看到那条叶脉了吗？它把墨吃得干干净净，每条小分支都印到了边上。大多数叶子在那儿会糊。这张没有。那是运气、压力和好纸，全落在同一个点上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She must have found a leaf with strong ribs. I can tell she pressed it hard and even. Twenty years, and I can read her hands in the paper now.
beats.chinese: 她一定找了一片叶脉结实的叶子。我看得出来她压得又重又匀。二十年了，我现在能从纸上看懂她的手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides the postcard into an empty page, smooths it flat with his thumb, and closes the book with a small satisfied sound.
beats.chinese: 他把明信片夹进一页空页，用拇指把它抚平，合上册子时发出一声小小的满意的动静。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Found its page. Next month I owe her a good one—better have a vein like this.
beats.chinese: 好了。找到它的页了。下个月我欠她一张好的——最好也有这么一条叶脉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Missed a month? Happened once, maybe twice. Flood season, my roof was off, her porch was down. Nobody sent anything.
beats.chinese: 漏一个月？发生过一次，也许两次。发水那阵子，我的屋顶掀了，她的门廊塌了。谁也没寄什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, but his thumb keeps rubbing the corner of the postcard, back and forth.
beats.chinese: 他耸耸肩，但拇指一直在搓明信片的角，来回地搓。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Did I think about her? Sure. All month. Wondered if her gutters held, if her knee was acting up. But I didn't mail a note asking.
beats.chinese: 我想她了吗？当然。想了一整个月。想知道她家檐槽撑住了没，她的老寒腿犯没犯。但我没寄条子去问。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because a note asking why nothing came—that's a bill. That's me saying you owe me a print. I don't run my ledger that way.
beats.chinese: 因为一张问'怎么没寄'的条子——那就是一张账单。那等于我说你欠我一张拓印。我的账本不这么记。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I just made my next one early. Sent it when I could. Hers came late that year, and it was a good one. The gap closed itself. It always does.
beats.chinese: 所以我只是提前做了我的下一张。能寄的时候寄出去。她那张那年也来晚了，而且是张好货。空缺自己合上了。一直是这样的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the postcard into the booklet after all, unfiled, loose between the pages.
beats.chinese: 他终究还是把明信片塞进了册子，没夹进固定的页，松松地夹在纸页之间。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Emile stops mid-motion, the booklet half-closed in his hands. He looks at the water for a while before answering.
beats.chinese: 埃米尔的动作停了一半，册子半合在手里。他望着水面看了一会儿才回答。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh. You might be right. I've heard that argument before, and I still don't care for it.
beats.chinese: 嗯。你也许是对的。这道理我听过，可我还是不喜欢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll say this much: I don't stop anybody from paying me back. If you hand me my screwdriver, I'll take it. I just won't like it, and I might not come knocking as quick next time. That's my flaw, not yours.
beats.chinese: 这么说吧：我不会拦着别人还我东西。你把螺丝刀递过来，我会接。我只是会不高兴，而且下次可能不会那么快去敲你的门。那是我的毛病，不是你的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He opens the booklet again, as if checking that nothing inside has changed, then shuts it.
beats.chinese: 他又翻开册子，好像在确认里面什么都没变，然后合上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You keep your books clean, that's fine. Genuinely fine. Some doors work better shut. Me, I keep mine on the latch. We'll just have to disagree about hinges.
beats.chinese: 你把账记得干干净净，挺好。真心觉得挺好。有些门关着更好用。我呢，我让我的门虚掩着。咱们就铰链这事儿各持己见吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't let me talk you out of your own way of doing things. I've been wrong before. Ask my shelf—it's still full of stuff I should've returned.
beats.chinese: 别让我把你说服了。我错过。问问我那个架子——上面还摆着一堆我早该还的东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flips to the back of the booklet, where a few blank pages wait, and taps one.
beats.chinese: 他翻到册子最后，那里留着几页空白，他敲了敲其中一页。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Next one? I've been thinking about it since I got this. Something to answer her leaf, not copy it.
beats.chinese: 下一张？收到这张之后我就一直在想。要回应她那片叶子，不是照抄它。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances at the trees across the pond, then shakes his head slightly.
beats.chinese: 他望了望池塘对面的树，然后轻轻摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I could pick a leaf right here, but this park's not mine to hammer. I've got a fig tree in my own yard—leaves like big hands. Never tried one. Big risk, big mess, maybe a good print.
beats.chinese: 我可以在这儿摘一片，可这公园的叶子不该我来捶。我自己院子里有棵无花果树——叶子像大手。从没试过。风险大，弄得也脏，也许能印出张好货。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the fun of it. If I knew how it would come out, I'd just be mailing her homework. Better to send her a surprise, even a failed one. She'd know I tried something new.
beats.chinese: 这就是好玩的地方。要是我知道会印成什么样，那寄给她的就是作业了。不如寄个意外给她，哪怕是失败的。她会知道我试了新东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So: fig leaf, my yard, my hammer, this weekend if the truck behaves. It goes in the book after it travels. That's the rule.
beats.chinese: 所以：无花果叶，我家院子，我的锤子，这周末，只要卡车争气。寄出去之后才进册子。这是规矩。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the stone platform, the binoculars again show the trees wavering on the water. Down by the edge, Emile has his booklet open on his knee, frowning at a page.
beats.chinese: 石台上，双筒望远镜里水面的树影又在晃动。池边，埃米尔把册子摊在膝盖上，皱着眉看一页。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't judge it yet. It's still drying. Well—it's dry. That's the problem.
beats.chinese: 先别下结论。它还没干透。好吧——干了。问题就在这儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the booklet so the page faces outward: a leaf print, almost entirely black, the veins swallowed in ink.
beats.chinese: 他把册子转过来对着外面：一张叶拓，几乎全黑，叶脉全被墨吞掉了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fig leaf. First try. I hit it like I was driving a nail. Now look at it—reads like one fat leaf with no bones in it.
beats.chinese: 无花果叶。第一次试。我捶得跟钉钉子似的。你看看——像一片没有骨头的胖叶子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I already made a second one, lighter hand. This one stays home. Maybe it goes on my shelf—every shelf needs one thing that didn't work out.
beats.chinese: 我已经做了第二张，手轻了些。这张留在家里。也许放上我的架子——每个架子都得有件没成的东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The page is dry after all. He closes the booklet, tucks it under his arm, and gives a small nod toward the water before heading off.
beats.chinese: 纸终究是干了。他合上册子，夹在腋下，朝水面点了点头，然后走开了。

card.name: Patricia Wroe
card.occupation: Box office clerk for a choral society
card.appearance: Broad square older jaw, shaggy shoulder-length hair, rectangular glasses and wide asymmetric tooth-band grin; red lapels.
card.personality: Patricia is cheerful in a way that comes from expecting to be surprised by things she already knows. She'll happily reverse an old verdict out loud—praise a building she once called a carbuncle, hum a choral piece she used to dismiss—and she does it without embarrassment, which occasionally lands her in odd spots when friends remember the original rant better than she does. She's warm, a bit brisk, quick to laugh, and not remotely interested in defending her past opinions as consistency. She can be dismissive on first impression, then genuinely won over, and she owns both moods.
card.background: Patricia has worked the box office for a Manchester choral society for over a decade, tearing tickets and chatting to the same regulars most Saturdays. She's lived in Levenshulme her whole life and watched it change around her—shops gone, blocks she hated in the eighties now looking rather handsome to her, though she forgets she ever hated them. She rents a small house where she keeps tropical fish, and her standing arrangement with her adult nephew is a weekend film, usually a cheap morning matinee in winter. They argue amiably about endings: he wants resolution, she likes walking out still arguing about it. She's changed her tastes plenty over the years and sees nothing strange in that, though friends occasionally plan outings around opinions she no longer holds.
hobbies: Weekend cinema trips with her nephew
Choral concerts (from the audience side too)
card.speechStyle: Rounds off opinions with a shrug built into the sentence—'well, I thought it was hideous at the time, I've gone right off that view.' Warm, direct, Manchester cadence, happy to contradict her own past self mid-anecdote.
card.signature: 'I said that? Well, I was wrong, weren't I.'

values: Honest revision—changing your mind openly is fine
Loyalty to familiar places and people, not to old opinions
flaws: Forgets her own past pronouncements, causing mix-ups
Too quick to write things off on first sight
boundaries: Won't pretend to have always liked something to spare a friend's planning
Keeps her evenings with the fish and the telly unbookable
conversationalHabits: Freely retracts old criticisms without being pressed
Tells stories about the city's buildings like they're acquaintances
anchorLines: That tower? I called it a concrete blot for thirty years. It's grown on me.
If you're picking the film, pick owt, I'll find something in it.
The fish don't care what I think of them, which is restful.

entries.summaryZh: 帕特里夏在池塘边看着石栏杆的倒影，爽快承认从前嫌它笨重、如今顺眼了。她改口毫不难为情，却忘了朋友还记着她当年的斩钉截铁。四个分支里，她或承认第一眼下结论太快，或尊重你保留旧看法，或决定把新口味直说出口，或干脆拒绝装不一致——一个把改口当作诚实的曼彻斯特售票员。

beats.speaker: narrator
