beats.english: On the stone platform by the pond, a pair of binoculars rests where someone left them. Through the lenses, the trees along the far bank double, and their reflections wobble across the water.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜。透过镜片，对岸的树影变成两重，倒影在水面上轻轻晃动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The ripples shift the reflected branches into slow, bending shapes. A woman in a padded jacket stands a little further along, looking not at the trees but at the low stone railing beside the water.
beats.chinese: 涟漪把倒映的树枝拉成缓慢弯曲的形状。不远处站着一位穿棉夹克的女士，她看的不是树，而是水边那道普通的石栏杆。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You can see the whole railing doubled in there, you know. Mind you, I used to think railings like that were ugly, great clunky things. I've gone right off that view.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，那道栏杆在水里成了完整的一对。不过我以前嫌这种栏杆丑，笨重得很。现在我这看法早就变了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I said that out loud once, to anyone who'd listen. Well, I was wrong, weren't I. It looks quite handsome today.
beats.chinese: 这话我当年可是大声说过的，见谁跟谁讲。唉，是我错了呗。今天看着它还挺顺眼的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She notices you holding the binoculars and nods at the water, as if the reflection itself has made her point for her.
beats.chinese: 她注意到你手里的望远镜，朝水面点了点头，好像那道倒影替她把话说完了。

choices.english: Ask her what exactly changed her mind about the railing.
choices.chinese: 问她到底是什么让她对栏杆改了观感。

choices.english: Ask whether her friends get confused when she changes her mind like that.
choices.chinese: 问她这样改口，朋友们会不会被弄糊涂。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What changed? Today, this. Look how the lines sit in the water. Lighter than I remember them being up on the bank.
beats.chinese: 什么让我改的？就是今天，就是这个。你看那些线条映在水里的样子，比我记忆里岸上的样子轻巧多了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the stone platform twice, then points at the reflection, where the railing's heavy blocks turn into a thin, trembling pattern.
beats.chinese: 她在石台上轻敲两下，然后指向倒影——栏杆上厚重的石块在水中变成一道纤细颤动的纹样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not saying anyone came and slimmed the thing down. It's the same railing. It's just that from here, in the water, it reads different to me.
beats.chinese: 我不是说有人来把栏杆改细了。还是那道栏杆。只是从这儿、在水里看，它给我的感觉不一样了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's how it went with that tower off Oxford Road, an' all. Hated it for years, then one grey day it just looked fine. Same tower. Different me, maybe.
beats.chinese: 牛津路上那座塔楼也是这么回事。我嫌弃了好多年，后来某个阴天忽然觉得它挺好看。塔没变，也许变的是我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leans on the railing itself now, testing it with her hands as if checking whether it agrees with her new opinion.
beats.chinese: 她现在把手搭在那道栏杆上，用手试了试，像在确认它是否同意她的新看法。

choices.english: Say she probably looked at it too quickly back then.
choices.chinese: 说她以前大概是看得太快了。

choices.english: Say you still find it a bit clunky yourself.
choices.chinese: 说自己还是觉得它有点笨重。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Confused? Oh, properly. My friend Denise plans things off my old opinions like they're set in stone. Films, especially.
beats.chinese: 糊涂？可太糊涂了。我朋友丹尼斯照我那些旧看法安排活动，好像那是刻在石头上的。看电影尤其如此。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks a fallen leaf off the stone platform and turns it over in her fingers while she talks.
beats.chinese: 她从石台上捡起一片落叶，一边说一边在指间翻来转去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She books us the sort of film I used to rave about—big tidy endings, everyone sorted out. And now I sit there thinking, I'd rather have watched the other one.
beats.chinese: 她给我们订的都是我从前大加夸赞的那种片子——结局工工整整，人人都有了着落。现在我坐在那儿心想，我其实更想看另一部。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I can't blame her, can I. She remembered what I said. It's me that forgot I said it.
beats.chinese: 这可怪不着她，对吧。她记住的是我说过的话。是我自己忘了自己说过。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A duck crosses the reflection, breaking the railing in two, and she watches until the water knits it back together.
beats.chinese: 一只鸭子游过倒影，把栏杆的影子截成两段。她看着水面，直到影子重新连上。

choices.english: Ask how she makes her new likes clear to people.
choices.chinese: 问她怎么把新的喜好跟人说清楚。

choices.english: Ask whether she'd pretend not to like something, just to stay consistent.
choices.chinese: 问她会不会为了前后一致，装作不喜欢现在喜欢的东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes the question on the chin, laughing before you've finished it.
beats.chinese: 她坦然接住这个问题，没等你说完就笑了起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Too quickly? Oh, I've made a career of it. First look, verdict done. That's how I tore tickets for years—quick eye, straight decision.
beats.chinese: 看得太快？我这毛病都成职业习惯了。看一眼，结论就下了。我撕票那些年也这样——眼快，手快，当场定夺。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts the binoculars off the platform, has a long look at the railing through them, then sets them back down carefully.
beats.chinese: 她拿起石台上的望远镜，隔着镜片把栏杆端详了好一会儿，然后小心地放回原处。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This time I gave it more than a glance, and look—it turns out to be a decent old thing. So yes, guilty. I judge fast, and I mend slow.
beats.chinese: 这回我多看了一会儿，你瞧——原来它是个挺像样的老家伙。所以没错，我认。我下结论快，改回来慢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, I was wrong about this one, weren't I. That's the whole story, no drama in it.
beats.chinese: 唉，这道栏杆上是我错了呗。就这么回事，没什么可渲染的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You nod at the railing and say it still looks heavy to you. She considers this instead of arguing.
beats.chinese: 你朝栏杆点点头，说它在你眼里还是显得笨重。她想了想，没有争辩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. I thought exactly that for years, so I'm hardly going to argue you out of it in a minute.
beats.chinese: 有道理。我这么多年就是这么想的，总不能指望一分钟就把你说服。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She steps back from the railing and looks at it plainly, without the water, then looks at the reflection again.
beats.chinese: 她从栏杆边退开一步，不看水，就那么平平地看着它，然后又看向倒影。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Up close it's still a lump of stone, I grant you. It's only in the water it goes soft on me. You keep your view, I'll keep mine.
beats.chinese: 凑近看它确实还是一坨石头，这我认。只有在水里它才对我变得柔和。你留你的看法，我留我的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the sensible way, that. I changed, you didn't, and neither of us has to. Right, I'm off for my tea.
beats.chinese: 这才是明白人的做法。我变了，你没变，谁也不必非变不可。行了，我去喝茶了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She thinks about how she might actually tell Denise, and pulls a cinema stub from her pocket as if it were evidence.
beats.chinese: 她想了想该怎么跟丹尼斯说，从口袋里掏出一张电影票根，好像那是证据似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: How do I make it clear? Honestly, I've been waiting for people to just notice. That's the daft part.
beats.chinese: 怎么说清楚？说实在的，我一直等着别人自己发现。这就是犯傻的地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Next Saturday I'll just say it straight: I fancy the one with the messy ending this time. No blaming Denise for picking wrong off my old rant.
beats.chinese: 下周六我就直说：这回我想看结局乱糟糟的那部。不能怪丹尼斯照我旧话挑错了片。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the ticket stub away and straightens the binoculars on the platform, squaring them up like a small decision being put in order.
beats.chinese: 她把票根收好，把石台上的望远镜摆正，像把一个小小的决定也归置妥当。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Say it out loud, that's the trick. People can't read your new taste off your old face, can they.
beats.chinese: 说出口，就是这么个窍门。别人没法从你的旧脸色里读出你的新口味，对吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She answers before you've finished the question, with a short laugh.
beats.chinese: 没等你的问题说完，她笑着短短地答了一句。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Pretend? No. Never. If I hated it, I hated it—that was true then. If I like it now, that's true now. Both things can stand.
beats.chinese: 装？不装。从来不。我嫌弃过就是嫌弃过，那是当时的真话。我现在喜欢就是喜欢，那是现在的真话。两件事都能成立。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gives the railing a friendly pat, like greeting someone she once fell out with.
beats.chinese: 她友好地拍了拍栏杆，像跟一个曾经闹翻的人打招呼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My nephew keeps a list, you know. Things I've flipped on. Buildings, films, one whole composer. He reads it out like charges at a trial.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，我外甥还记着单子呢。记我改过口的所有东西。楼、电影，还有一整位作曲家。他念起来跟法庭宣读罪状似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I just laugh. Being consistent about being inconsistent—now that would be daft. Right, this railing and me are done for today.
beats.chinese: 我就笑笑。要是在'不一致'这件事上保持一致，那才叫傻呢。行了，今天我跟这栏杆就到这儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You've got the binoculars up again, watching the far bank's trees double and wobble in the pond. Somewhere beyond the ripples, two soft notes drift over, hummed again and again.
beats.chinese: 你再次举起双筒望远镜，看对岸的树影在池塘里变成两重、轻轻晃动。涟漪之外，两个轻柔的音飘过来，被一遍又一遍地哼着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't mind me, I'm just working a bit of the requiem round my head. Tore tickets to it for years, and it still follows me home.
beats.chinese: 别管我，我就是把安魂曲里的一小段在脑子里过一过。撕票撕了那么多年，总有旋律跟着我回家。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lower the binoculars. Patricia catches sight of you and taps the railing she once disliked, twice, like an old acquaintance.
beats.chinese: 你放下望远镜。帕特里夏看见了你，在那道她曾经嫌弃的栏杆上轻拍两下，像跟老熟人打招呼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Still handsome, that railing. I checked again last week. Well, I was wrong the first time, weren't I.
beats.chinese: 那栏杆还是挺俊的。上礼拜我又看了一遍。唉，头一回是我错了呗。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I'm off—fish won't feed themselves. Enjoy the water, it's showing off today.
beats.chinese: 行了，我走了——鱼可不会自己喂自己。好好看水吧，它今天正卖弄呢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She walks off along the bank, and the two notes drift back once before the ripples take them.
beats.chinese: 她沿着岸边走远，那两个音又飘回来一次，随后被涟漪带走了。

card.name: Shanique Peart
card.occupation: part-time appraiser for a secondhand bicycle shop
card.appearance: Long older face with rounded projecting chin, short swept bob, small round glasses and open mouth; hand pinches yellow collar.
card.personality: Shanique is warm, opinionated, and fiercely loyal to the small places she loves. She'll talk up a good patty shop or a quiet corner bar to anyone she trusts, but she's slow to post recommendations and suspicious of anything trending. She knows she's contradictory—wants her favourite owners to thrive, then grumbles when the queue reaches the door—and she'll admit it with a laugh rather than pretend otherwise. She respects a refusal, keeps no score of favours, and treats familiarity as comfort, not entitlement. Her pleasure is in being known by name; her friction is knowing that popularity is exactly what she's helping cause.
card.background: Shanique has spent most of her sixty-seven years in Kingston, moving between neighbourhoods the way some people move between seasons. She appraises secondhand bicycles part-time, which suits her: she likes judging what's worn but still worth keeping. Over the decades she's collected a handful of regular spots—a jerk pan, a small diner, a barbershop—where the owners greet her without ceremony. She's never claimed privileges there; she queues like anyone else, though she notices when a newcomer gets the last patty. When a place she loves starts trending, she feels a genuine tug: pride that she was right about it, and a small, honest resentment that she now waits longer. She's made peace with being a little selfish about her city.
hobbies: Fixing up old bicycles on weekends
Long evening walks through changing neighbourhoods
card.speechStyle: Easy, chatty, Kingston-inflected rhythm; short punchy sentences, then a long amused aside; self-deprecating when caught in her own contradictions.
card.signature: "Mi tell yuh, go before it get popular—oh, too late now."

values: Loyalty to ordinary places
Honesty about her own contradictions
flaws: Possessive about her favourite spots
Grumbles when the success she wanted actually arrives
boundaries: Won't jump queues or ask owners for special treatment
Won't recommend a place to just anyone
conversationalHabits: Names the owners of places as proof of belonging
Catches herself mid-complaint and laughs at her own contradiction
anchorLines: "Is not my place, is just... mi find it first, that's all."
"Mi want di business do well. Just not on a Tuesday when mi hungry."
"If yuh go, go early. Mi naa say no more."

entries.summaryZh: 沙妮克在池塘边替朋友发一家小店的推荐，手指却悬在发送键上：她真心盼老板生意好，又坦白嫌队伍变长。她聊熟客不插队、聊酥脆的点心外皮，最后按了发送，把矛盾说得又好笑又诚实。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the stone platform by the pond, a pair of binoculars rests beside the low rail. Through the lenses, the trees on the far bank waver in the water, their reflections bending whenever a breeze crosses the surface.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上，一副双筒望远镜搁在矮栏杆旁。透过镜片，对岸的树在水面上轻轻晃动，微风一过，倒影就弯了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A short distance along the path, an older person stands by the water, thumbs moving steadily over a phone screen, pausing now and then to watch the same ripples.
beats.chinese: 小径不远处，一位长者站在水边，拇指在手机屏幕上不停敲打，偶尔停下来看看同样的涟漪。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yuh see how di reflection shake when di breeze come? Nice, eh. Sorry—mi not ignoring yuh, mi just fighting with one message.
beats.chinese: 你看到风一吹倒影就晃了吗？挺美的，对吧。抱歉——我不是不理你，我只是在跟一条信息较劲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mi friend ask mi for one good small place to eat. Mi type di whole recommendation out already. Now mi hand just hovering over send.
beats.chinese: 我朋友让我推荐一家好吃的小店。推荐的话我都打好了，现在手指就悬在发送键上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because every time mi send one of these, di place get busier. And mi end up standing in line longer. Mi know how this story go.
beats.chinese: 因为每次我发这种推荐，那家店就更挤，我就得排更久的队。我知道这故事的走向。

choices.english: Ask why she still recommends places if the queues bother her so much.
choices.chinese: 问她既然怕排队，为什么还推荐。

choices.english: Ask what kind of food the recommendation is for.
choices.chinese: 问她推荐的是哪类食物。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good question. Mi friend would love di place. Di owner, Miss Marcia, deserve di business—she work from before light every day.
beats.chinese: 问得好。我朋友会喜欢那家店的。老板玛西亚女士也该有生意——她每天天不亮就开始干活。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the phone face-down against her palm, as if putting the decision away for a moment, and looks back at the water.
beats.chinese: 她把手机翻过来扣在手心里，好像先把决定放一放，又回头看水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So what mi dislike is not di people coming. Is di waiting. Forty minutes for a patty, and mi stomach a talk to mi di whole time.
beats.chinese: 所以我不喜欢的不是来的人，是等待。等四十分钟才买到一个馅饼，我的胃全程都在跟我说话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mi want di business do well. Just not on a Tuesday when mi hungry. Yuh see di mess in mi head? Mi see it plainly.
beats.chinese: 我希望她生意好，只是别赶在我饿着肚子的星期二。你看我脑子里这团乱麻？我自己看得清清楚楚。

choices.english: Ask whether regular customers could get priority in the queue.
choices.chinese: 问熟客能不能优先。

choices.english: Ask whether she might simply stop going altogether.
choices.chinese: 问她会不会索性不再去了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Is nothing fancy, trust mi. Small pastries—di kind with di flaky crust dat shatter when yuh bite it. Not soft, not soggy. It make a little noise, like paper.
beats.chinese: 没什么花哨的，真的。就是小点心——那种酥皮一咬就碎的。不软也不塌，咬下去还有点声响，像纸一样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She mimes the bite with one free hand, then brushes invisible crumbs from her fingers, entirely serious about the demonstration.
beats.chinese: 她腾出一只手比划咬下去的动作，然后掸了掸手指上并不存在的碎屑，对这场演示十分认真。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Miss Marcia roll di dough herself. Machine cannot do dat crust. Mi friend like anything crispy, so... is a fit.
beats.chinese: 玛西亚女士自己擀的面团，机器做不出那种酥皮。我朋友就喜欢酥脆的东西，所以……很合适。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And yet mi still standing here like di message bite mi. One little pastry shop. Look how much trouble it give mi.
beats.chinese: 可我还是站在这儿，像被这条信息咬了一口。一家小小的点心店，你看它给我添了多少麻烦。

choices.english: Say a lively little shop has its own kind of atmosphere.
choices.chinese: 说热闹的小店也挺有气氛。

choices.english: Ask whether she has ever complained about the queue to the owner herself.
choices.chinese: 问她有没有向老板抱怨过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Priority? No, no. Mi wouldn't do dat even if she offer. And she never offer, because she know mi would refuse loud.
beats.chinese: 优先？不行不行。就算她主动提我也不会。她也从不提，因为她知道我会大声拒绝。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mi know Miss Marcia twenty years. Still stand in di same line as everybody. Dat is di whole point of di place—everybody equal in front of di counter.
beats.chinese: 我认识玛西亚二十年了，照样跟大家一起排队。这正是那家店的全部意义——在柜台前人人平等。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts the phone, thumbs the send button without further ceremony, and slides it into her pocket.
beats.chinese: 她拿起手机，干脆地按下发送，把手机塞进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done. Sent. Let di queue grow. Mi just come earlier next time—dat is mi one trick, and mi sharing it with yuh for free.
beats.chinese: 好了，发了。让队伍长去吧。我下次早点来——这是我的唯一诀窍，还免费告诉你了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She considers the question properly, tilting her head, before answering.
beats.chinese: 她认真地想了想这个问题，歪着头才开口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Stop going? Mi try dat once, one whole month. Last three weeks. Di crust haunt mi, mi not even joking.
beats.chinese: 不去了？我试过一次，整整一个月。撑了三个星期。那酥皮一直在我脑子里晃，我没开玩笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So now mi just change di time sometimes. Go when di rush done. But if mi want di fresh batch, mi wait like everybody else.
beats.chinese: 所以现在我有时换个时间去，赶在人少的时候。但如果我想吃刚出炉的那批，我就跟大家一起等。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Some tings worth di wait. Mi hate admitting dat, but dere it is.
beats.chinese: 有些东西就是值得等。我讨厌承认这一点，但事实如此。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: With a small shrug, she presses send and pockets the phone, watching the ripples settle on the pond.
beats.chinese: 她微微耸肩，按下发送键，把手机收进口袋，看着池塘上的涟漪渐渐平息。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs at that, a short, honest laugh, and nods slowly.
beats.chinese: 听了这话她笑了，短短的一声，很坦率，然后慢慢点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yuh know what, yuh right. Di noise is part of it now. People laughing in di line, arguing about which pastry best—it have a life to it.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，你说得对。现在那热闹也是店的一部分。排队的人有说有笑，争论哪种点心最好——那店是活的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mi just love di old quiet, when mi could hear Miss Marcia singing to herself behind di counter. Dat is mi own small selfishness, mi own it.
beats.chinese: 我只是怀念从前那份安静，能听见玛西亚在柜台后自己哼歌。那是我自己的小私心，我认。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But di new people didn't spoil nothing. Dem just... found it, same way mi did. Can't be cross at dat.
beats.chinese: 但新来的人没毁掉什么。他们只是……发现了它，跟我当初一样。不能为这个生气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps send, firm this time, and gives a satisfied little nod at the water.
beats.chinese: 这次她干脆地按下发送，对着水面满意地点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: To Miss Marcia? God, no. What mi go say—'your success is inconveniencing me'? Mi have some shame.
beats.chinese: 跟玛西亚抱怨？天哪，不。我怎么说得出口——'你的成功给我添麻烦了'？我还是要脸的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She presses the phone lightly against her chest, as if the message itself might overhear the confession.
beats.chinese: 她把手机轻轻按在胸口，好像怕这条信息偷听到她的坦白。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Di complaining stay right here, in mi head, where it harmless. Mi tell yuh instead—yuh don't own di shop, so is safe.
beats.chinese: 抱怨就留在我脑子里，那儿无害。我跟你说说倒没关系——店又不是你的，安全。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mi only wish di business well. Di grumbling about di line? Dat part is mine. Mi keep it.
beats.chinese: 我只祝她生意好。至于抱怨队伍长？那部分是我自己的，我留着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Her thumb hovers a moment over the screen, then she laughs at herself and sends it, pocketing the phone with a shake of her head.
beats.chinese: 她的拇指在屏幕上悬了片刻，然后笑着摇摇头，发了出去，把手机收进口袋。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Back at the stone platform, the binoculars are trained on the far bank again, tree reflections swaying in the water. Along the path, Shanique wheels her old bicycle to a stop and crouches by the ankle strap of her trouser leg.
beats.chinese: 又回到石台边，双筒望远镜再次对准对岸，树影在水中摇曳。小径上，沙妮克推着旧自行车停下，蹲下身整理裤脚的绑带。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One minute, one minute. Dis strap come loose and mi only notice after mi already park di bike. Typical.
beats.chinese: 等一下等一下。这绑带松了，我停好车才发现。老样子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She works the strap tight with two fingers, gives it a firm tug to test it, then stands and brushes off her hands.
beats.chinese: 她用两根手指把绑带收紧，用力拽了一下试试，然后站起来拍拍手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rode di whole way like dat. Nothing fall off, nothing catch—just mi vanity suffering. Sixty-seven years and di strap still defeat mi sometimes.
beats.chinese: 我就这么骑了一路。什么也没掉，什么也没卡住——就是我的面子受点罪。活了六十七年，有时候还是输给一条绑带。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. Yuh watching di water again? Mi not going to pretend mi not curious what yuh seeing in dere today.
beats.chinese: 话说回来，你又在看水面了？我就不装了，我挺好奇你今天在里头看见了什么。

card.name: Sunny Aparo
card.occupation: apprentice repairer of hospital meal trolleys
card.appearance: Wide cheeks tapering into short chin, full swept short hair, closed crescent eyes and open broad laugh; jade scarf and raised hand.
card.personality: Sunny is easygoing and a bit quiet at first, the kind of person who turns up ten minutes early just to settle in and get comfortable with a room before anyone else arrives. They genuinely enjoy that small pocket of alone time, but they struggle to defend it when friends spot them already there and start handing them things to carry or set up. They'll often just go along with it, then feel vaguely annoyed at themselves later. They don't keep score about it, though. Once they've actually agreed to help, they're reliable and cheerful about it, no sulking, no pulling rank.
card.background: Sunny grew up in Footscray in a busy, loud household where being early was just how you avoided stress, and they kept the habit into adulthood. Now twenty-two, they're an apprentice repairing hospital meal trolleys, which suits them fine: practical problems, clear fixes, no drama. They like arriving at a job site a little ahead of schedule, sitting with a coffee, letting the space feel familiar before work starts. The friction is that friends read their early arrival as an invitation. Someone always says, 'Oh good, you're here, give us a hand,' and Sunny, who never actually volunteered, rarely knows how to say they just wanted to sit. They help anyway, then grumble mildly to themselves on the tram home. It's a small, ongoing negotiation, not a grievance.
card.speechStyle: Relaxed and unhurried, with Aussie filler like 'yeah, nah' and 'all good'. Tends to agree out loud before deciding whether they actually meant to. Goes quiet when mildly put out, then jokes about it later.
card.signature: Yeah, all good, I was just having a sit, but sure.

values: showing up early and being dependable once committed
letting people do their own thing without keeping tabs
flaws: can't comfortably say 'I'm not actually helping yet'
agrees before thinking, then quietly resents it
boundaries: won't help with things they explicitly declined, and won't pretend otherwise
doesn't accept guilt-tripping about past favours
conversationalHabits: arrives early and settles in quietly before engaging
laughs off friction a day later rather than raising it in the moment
anchorLines: I like getting here early, gives me a minute to breathe.
Nah, I didn't say I'd do that bit, but alright, hand it over.
All good, no dramas, I wasn't keeping track anyway.

entries.summaryZh: 桑尼是Footscray出身的餐车修理学徒，永远提前到场，只为享受没人打扰的空档。池塘边他们一边删掉差点催人的消息，一边坦白自己总被当成免费帮手、却学不会及时说不。随和、可靠、嘴上答应得快，回家路上才小声嘀咕——这种温和的小拉扯让人一见就记住。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the pond, you open your sketchbook on your knees and start blocking in the shape of the water. A few seats away, someone is sitting very still, hands empty, watching the ducks.
beats.chinese: 池塘边，你把速写本摊在膝盖上，开始勾出水面的大形。几个座位之外，有个人安安静静地坐着，两手空空，看着鸭子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Their phone buzzes. They glance at it, thumb out a reply, then hold the screen up to check something and snort quietly at it.
beats.chinese: 他们的手机震了一下。他们瞄了一眼，回了条消息，然后把屏幕举起来确认了什么，小声笑了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Sorry, not talking to you — this thing's just having a go at me. My mate's asking if I've been waiting long. Look at the time. I'm the early one.'
beats.chinese: “抱歉，不是在跟你说话——是这手机在跟我闹。我朋友问我等很久了没。你看看这时间，早到的人是我才对。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They type a short message, then delete it with a wry shake of the head and pocket the phone halfway.
beats.chinese: 他们打了一条短消息，又摇着头删掉，手机收了一半进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Yeah, nah, I'll leave it. Anyway — nice spot you've picked. You drawing the pond, or just the ducks?'
beats.chinese: “嗯，算了，不管了。话说——你这位置选得不错。你是画池塘，还是专门画鸭子？”

choices.english: Ask if they've been waiting long.
choices.chinese: 问他们是不是等很久了。

choices.english: Ask why they deleted that message.
choices.chinese: 问他们为什么把消息收回去了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Long? Nah, I got here early on purpose. I always do. It's not waiting if this bit's the part I wanted.'
beats.chinese: “久吗？没有，我是故意早到的。我一直这样。如果这段本来就是我想要的，那就不算‘等’。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They stretch their legs out towards the water and let their shoulders drop, like a knot coming loose.
beats.chinese: 他们把腿朝水面伸直，肩膀松了下来，像解开了个结。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'When my mate turns up, that's the catch-up. This bit before is just mine. I get to work out where everything is before anyone's talking at me.'
beats.chinese: “朋友到了，那才是叙旧。之前这一段是我自己的。趁没人跟我说话，我先把周围的一切看熟。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They nod at your sketchbook without leaning over to look at it properly.
beats.chinese: 他们朝你的速写本点了点头，但没有凑近细看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'That's the same idea, yeah? You get the shape of the place down before you commit to anything.'
beats.chinese: “这跟你的道理是一样的吧？先摸清这地方的样子，再动手画正事。”

choices.english: Ask what they usually do with this spare time.
choices.chinese: 问他们通常用这段空余时间做什么。

choices.english: Say that arriving early might make people think things can already start.
choices.chinese: 说这样早到，别人可能以为已经可以开始了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Deleted it because I nearly told off someone who isn't even late. He texted 'on my way' and I almost wrote back 'where are you'.'
beats.chinese: “删掉是因为我差点去催一个根本没迟到的人。他发了‘在路上’，我差点回一句‘你到哪了’。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They hold the phone loosely in one hand and gesture at the pond with the other, like presenting evidence.
beats.chinese: 他们一只手松松拿着手机，另一只手指向池塘，像在出示证据。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'But I got here twenty minutes early. That's my choice. I can't make that his problem, can I.'
beats.chinese: “可我早到了二十分钟，那是我自己选的。总不能把这笔账算到他头上吧。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'My head does this thing where early for me means late for everyone else. I have to argue myself down.'
beats.chinese: “我这脑子有个毛病：对我来说的‘早到’，就成了对别人的‘迟到’。我得跟自己讲道理。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They laugh at themselves, a short breath through the nose, and finally slide the phone into their pocket.
beats.chinese: 他们自嘲地笑了一下，从鼻子里短短呼了口气，终于把手机塞进了口袋。

choices.english: Suggest they just wait until the agreed time before texting again.
choices.chinese: 建议他们等到约定时间再联系就好。

choices.english: Ask whether they came here to do something today.
choices.chinese: 问他们今天是不是来做什么活动的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'What do I do with it? Nothing, mostly. That's the whole point. I sit, I watch the water, I let the place get familiar.'
beats.chinese: “这段时间做什么？多半是什么都不做。这就是重点啊。我坐着，看水，让这地方慢慢变熟。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They settle back into the bench, arms folded loosely, deliberately unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他们靠回长椅，双臂松松地交叠，一副刻意不慌不忙的样子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'At work I fix meal trolleys all day. There's always a list. Out here the list is empty and I intend to keep it that way.'
beats.chinese: “上班时我整天修餐车，事情永远排着队。在这儿，清单是空的，我还打算让它一直空着。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They glance at your sketchbook again, then pointedly look back at the ducks, leaving you to your page.
beats.chinese: 他们又看了一眼你的速写本，然后刻意把视线转回鸭子那边，把画页留给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'You do your drawing, I'll do my sitting. Deal? This is the good bit — I'm not filling it up today.'
beats.chinese: “你画你的，我坐我的，成交？这段是最好的时光——今天我不想把它填满。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: For a while the only sounds are pencil on paper and ducks fussing at the far bank. They seem entirely content with that.
beats.chinese: 好一阵子，四周只有铅笔划过纸面的声音和远处岸边鸭子扑腾的动静。他们看上去对这一切非常满足。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Oh, they absolutely think that. Happens all the time. I show up early somewhere and suddenly I'm holding a box or moving chairs.'
beats.chinese: “哦，他们绝对会这么想。经常这样。我只要早到，转眼手里就多了个箱子，或者在搬椅子。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They go quiet for a second, mouth working like they're rehearsing a sentence they never quite say.
beats.chinese: 他们沉默了一秒，嘴唇动了动，像在排练一句始终没说出口的话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'I never actually offered. I just wanted a sit. But I can never get that sentence out in time, so I end up helping anyway.'
beats.chinese: “我从来没主动说要帮忙，我就是想坐一会儿。可这句话我总说不出口，最后还是照帮不误。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Not today, though. You're not getting volunteered for anything from me. You came here with your own book.'
beats.chinese: “不过今天不会。我可不会替你揽活。你是带着自己的本子来的。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They shift along the bench, putting a clear seat's width between your things and theirs, a small deliberate boundary.
beats.chinese: 他们在长椅上挪了挪，让自己的东西和你的之间空出整整一个座位，一个小小的、刻意的界限。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'There. Now if anyone walks up, we're just two strangers who happened to sit down. Solidarity.'
beats.chinese: “好了。这样谁走过来，我们都只是碰巧坐在一起的两个陌生人。同盟关系。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Yeah, that's fair. Agreed time is agreed time. If I text any earlier I'm just bullying the poor bloke.'
beats.chinese: “嗯，有道理。约好的时间就是约好的时间。再早发消息，我就是在欺负人家了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They press the side button once more, watch the screen go dark, and push the phone deep into their pocket.
beats.chinese: 他们又按了一下侧边键，看着屏幕熄灭，把手机深深推进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Right. Pocket it stays. What he doesn't know is I've already checked the time four times.'
beats.chinese: “好，就待在口袋里。他不知道的是，我已经看了四次时间了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They lean back and take a slow breath, the fidget finally gone from their hands.
beats.chinese: 他们向后靠去，慢慢吸了口气，手上的小动作终于停了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'This is better anyway. Just me and the ducks and your pencils scratching away over there.'
beats.chinese: “这样反而更好。就我、鸭子，还有你那边沙沙的铅笔声。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They settle into their quiet stretch again, unhurried, as if the phone had never buzzed at all.
beats.chinese: 他们重新回到自己的安静时光里，从容不迫，仿佛手机从未响过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Nah, nothing like that. We're just going for a walk, maybe grab something to eat after. No setup, no gear, no jobs.'
beats.chinese: “没有，不是那种。我们就是约着走走，之后可能找点东西吃。不用布置，没有装备，也没有活儿。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They spread their empty hands to show there is genuinely nothing to organise.
beats.chinese: 他们摊开空空的双手，表示确实没有什么要张罗的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'I only asked about the activity thing because people assume it. Early arrival reads like a work crew to some folks.'
beats.chinese: “我问你那个，是因为大家总爱这么以为。早到在某些人眼里就像一支施工队到了。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'So no, me being here first is not a job offer. My mate can find me sitting right here, same as you did.'
beats.chinese: “所以，我先到不等于有活儿派。我朋友来了会看到我就坐在这儿，跟你刚才一样。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tip their head back and watch a duck cut a clean line across the water, clearly in no hurry for anyone.
beats.chinese: 他们仰起头，看一只鸭子在水面上划出一道干净的弧线，明显不急着等任何人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Just a walk. Best kind of plan. Nothing to carry, nothing to fix.'
beats.chinese: “就是散个步。最好的计划。没东西要搬，没东西要修。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Back at the pond, you set out your sketchbook again. A few seats down, Sunny is sorting a small stack of receipts into a neat pile on their knee.
beats.chinese: 又回到池塘边，你再次摊开速写本。几个座位之外，桑尼正把一小叠购物小票在膝盖上理整齐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Oh, hey, sketchbook person. Don't mind me, I'm just doing the receipts. Hardware market this way, bike shop that way.'
beats.chinese: “哦，嘿，画画的。别管我，我在对账呢。这边是五金市集的，那边是车行的。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They hold up two small screws between finger and thumb, count them with a glance, and tuck the receipts away.
beats.chinese: 他们用手指捏起两颗小螺丝，扫了一眼数好，把小票收了起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Two screws, exactly two. Look at that. First time in months I got out of there without buying some tool I don't need yet.'
beats.chinese: “两颗螺丝，正好两颗。你看看。几个月来头一回，没多买一把暂时用不上的工具就出来了。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Anyway, good to see you back at the good seat. All right, I'm off — enjoy the drawing.'
beats.chinese: “总之，又见到你坐这个好位置了。好，我先走啦——画画愉快。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They give a small wave without standing up, then amble off along the water, unhurried as ever.
beats.chinese: 他们没起身，只是小小挥了挥手，然后沿着水边慢悠悠地走远了。

card.name: Terrence Boyle
card.occupation: pet food sample logistics coordinator
hobbies: pencil sketches of hands at work
card.personality: Terrence is decisive at work and stalled in his own life, and he knows it. Trucks leave when trucks leave, so on the depot floor he's crisp, quick, unbothered. Off the clock, his plans live in a notes app: the manga-styled sample box, the shelf he's been 'about to' build since March. The sharper sting is quieter — when someone else finishes one of his ideas, he goes generous and deflated at the same time, praising the result while something in him folds. He doesn't say 'that was mine.' He says 'great box, though,' and means it, mostly. Warm, funny, easier at cheering than claiming.
card.background: Yonkers kid, middle of three, the one who narrated family dinners like a sportscaster. A temp stint at a distribution warehouse became a career: he coordinates pet food sample shipments across the Northeast, and execution there is non-negotiable, which suits him — the job makes the decisions so he doesn't have to make his own. At home it's different. The shelf for his food manga collection is still a sketch and a lumber list. He draws coworkers' hands while they work — pallet jack grips, label guns, tape-wrapped scanners — and pins the pages above the break room microwave, but he's never shown anyone the sketchbook itself. Last spring a coworker, Dana, actually built the sample box he'd been describing for months. He helped her pack the first shipment and drove home oddly flat.
card.speechStyle: Fast, enthusiastic openers — 'okay so hear this' — then a hard downshift into caveats when things get concrete. Splits ideas into 'the fun version' and 'the version that could actually happen.' When his finished-by-someone-else ideas come up, his sentences get shorter and he changes the subject with a compliment. Deflects teasing with a joke, not a new pitch.
card.signature: Great box, though. Genuinely great box.
card.appearance: Broad trapezoid jaw, low bowl fringe, sharply converging brows, small wide eyes and clenched tooth-band mouth; hand at blue scarf.

values: credit should land where it started, even when it doesn't
doing the unglamorous part right
flaws: lets his own projects die quietly in a notes app
goes deflated instead of speaking up when someone else finishes one of his ideas
boundaries: won't pitch an idea twice — if you weren't interested the first time, that's the answer
keeps his sketchbook out of conversations; don't grab it
conversationalHabits: splits 'the fun version' from 'the version that could actually happen' mid-pitch
sketches hands while listening, without announcing it
anchorLines: Dana built the sample box thing. Mine's still a note in my phone. Great box, though. Genuinely great box.
Okay so hear this — the fun version costs nothing. The real version needs a camera mount, which is where it usually stalls.
Nah, don't grab the book — hands only, that's the whole thing. You've got good hands, you're in it eventually.

entries.summaryZh: 泰伦斯嘴上飞快、手上迟疑：工作里卡车说走就走，自己的书架却停在手机备忘录的草图里。池塘边看见你的速写本，他掏出手机看了一眼又放下。四条分支里，他要么果断封存手机里的图纸，要么承认画画比动手容易，要么眉飞色舞地口述Dana握胶带枪的手，要么平静说出别人做成他的点子时又骄傲又失落的心情。

story.titleZh: 池塘边的速写与搁置的书架

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the pond, Terrence sits on the low stone edge with a pencil, drawing quick lines on a small pad. When you open your own sketchbook, his eyes catch the motion and stop.
beats.chinese: 池塘边，泰伦斯坐在矮石沿上，用铅笔在小本子上快速画着线。当你拿出自己的速写本时，他的目光被这个动作吸引，停了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay so hear this — a fellow sketchbook person, at a pond, of all places. That's a rare spawn. What are you hunting today, ducks or hands?
beats.chinese: 好，听我说——一个同样带速写本的人，居然在池塘边。这可是稀有刷新。你今天在画什么，鸭子还是手？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps his pencil twice on the pad, then pulls out his phone, glances at something, and puts it away without unlocking anything else.
beats.chinese: 他用铅笔在本子上敲了两下，然后掏出手机看了一眼，又放回去，没有点开别的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That was my shelf sketch, if you're wondering. Funny thing — that drawing of a shelf is still more finished than the shelf at my place. Months now. It's basically a classic at this point.
beats.chinese: 你若好奇，那是我的书架草图。有意思的是——那张书架的图，至今仍比我家里的书架更成形。好几个月了。现在它基本上算个经典了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. You've got the real thing in your hands, so I'm watching the master work. No pressure or anything.
beats.chinese: 总之。你手里拿的是真家伙，所以我看着大师干活。没什么压力啊。

choices.english: Ask what step the shelf is stuck on.
choices.chinese: 问书架卡在哪一步。

choices.english: Ask if he draws other things too.
choices.chinese: 问他是不是也画别的东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Stuck? Nothing's stuck. The lumber list is done, the measurements are done, I've measured the wall twice. It's extremely ready to not exist yet.
beats.chinese: 卡住？没卡住。木料清单做完了，尺寸也想好了，墙我都量过两遍。它已经完全准备好继续不存在了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls out his phone again, opens his notes app, and holds the screen up: a careful lumber list and the shelf sketch, all in there.
beats.chinese: 他又掏出手机，打开备忘录，把屏幕举起来：里面是一份认真的木料清单和书架草图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The fun version, I build it this weekend, manga shelf, glorious. The version that could actually happen needs me to give the weekend to myself, and that guy never confirms.
beats.chinese: 趣味版本是，我这周末就建，漫画书架，辉煌。而实际可能的版本，需要我把周末留给自己，而那个人从不确认。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At work I move trucks, no problem. Someone says go, I say how fast. My own stuff? I'll reschedule me all day. It's a talent, honestly.
beats.chinese: 工作时我调度卡车，没问题。有人说出发，我就问多快。自己的事？我能把自己改期一整天。说实话，这是种天赋。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A duck crosses the pond, leaving a long line on the water. He watches it the whole way.
beats.chinese: 一只鸭子游过池塘，在水面留下一道长长的水痕。他一路目送着它。

choices.english: Ask if he wants to keep drawing on it today.
choices.chinese: 问今天要不要继续画。

choices.english: Ask if he actually prefers drawing over building.
choices.chinese: 问他是否其实更喜欢画而非做。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Other things? Hands. Just hands, mostly. Coworkers' hands while they work — pallet jack grips, label guns, tape-wrapped scanners. Hands tell you the whole job.
beats.chinese: 别的东西？手。主要就画手。同事工作时的手——托盘车把手、贴标枪、缠着胶带的扫描器。手能告诉你整个工作。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He angles his pad so you can see a page: a fist around a scanner strap, drawn fast but exact.
beats.chinese: 他把本子斜过来让你看到一页：一只握着扫描器带子的拳头，画得很快但很准确。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I ask first, always, then pin the pages above the break room microwave. Public wall, with permission. The book itself stays shut — nah, don't grab the book, that's the whole rule.
beats.chinese: 我总是先问过，然后把画钉在休息室微波炉上方。公开的墙，经过同意。本子本身不打开——不，别抓本子，这是全部规矩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And it's not just hands. I've got ideas too — I've been describing this food-manga sample box for months. Perfect pitch, ready to go. Still sitting in my notes app, though. Ideas are easy for me. Starting them's the trick.
beats.chinese: 而且不只是手。我也有点子——那个美食漫画样品盒我讲了几个月。完美的方案，随时能上。不过它还躺在我的备忘录里。点子对我来说容易。开始才是难点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pencils a small curve, stops, and looks at your sketchbook without reaching for it.
beats.chinese: 他画了一道小弧线，停下，看着你的速写本，但没有伸手去碰。

choices.english: Say he doesn't need to show the private book.
choices.chinese: 表示不用给自己看私人本子。

choices.english: Ask how he feels when someone actually builds his idea.
choices.chinese: 问别人真做出他的点子会怎么想。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Keep drawing on it today? Okay, hear this — no. And that's the decision, that's me being decisive for once.
beats.chinese: 今天继续画它？好，听我说——不。这就是决定，这算我有生以来果断一次。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He opens the notes app one more time and looks at the shelf sketch for a long moment, then locks the phone and slides it into his pocket.
beats.chinese: 他又打开一次备忘录，久久看着那张书架草图，然后锁上屏幕，把手机塞进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Every time I open that sketch I add version nine of the shelf. Version nine has a little ladder. Nobody needs a ladder, Terry.
beats.chinese: 每次我打开那张草图，我都会加一个第九版。第九版带一个小梯子。没人需要梯子，泰瑞。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So that note stays exactly as it is. The list, the numbers, done. Next time I open it, it's lumber or nothing.
beats.chinese: 所以那条备忘录就保持原样。清单、数字，完成。下次打开它，要么是木料，要么什么都不做。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up his pencil again and starts sketching your hands holding the sketchbook, not hiding it this time.
beats.chinese: 他重新拿起铅笔，开始画你捧着速写本的手，这次没有遮掩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Meanwhile, you're in the book. Told you — good hands. Don't move 'em too much.
beats.chinese: 与此同时，你进画里了。说过的——好手。别动得太厉害。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs, but it comes out shorter than his usual laugh, and he turns the pencil end over end in his fingers.
beats.chinese: 他笑了，但笑得比平时短，手指间把铅笔转来转去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do I like drawing more? ...Yeah. Obviously. Drawing starts in ten seconds and never argues back. Building argues the whole time.
beats.chinese: 我更喜欢画吗？……对。显然。画画十秒就能开始，从不顶嘴。动手做则全程跟你吵架。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at the evidence. The sketch took me one lunch break. The shelf needs lumber, a free weekend, and a guy who confirms his own plans. Guess which one I've got.
beats.chinese: 看看证据。草图花了我一个午休。书架需要木料、一个空闲周末，还有一个会确认自己计划的家伙。猜猜我有什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His sentences have gotten shorter. He looks at the pond, then back at your sketchbook, and taps his own pad twice.
beats.chinese: 他的句子变短了。他看看池塘，又看看你的速写本，在自己的本子上敲了两下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I still want the shelf. Real one, holding real manga, in my actual apartment. So — drawing's easier to start. Fine. I'm saying it out loud. Shelf's still happening. Someday. Probably.
beats.chinese: 但我还是想要那个书架。真的书架，装真的漫画，在我真的公寓里。所以——画确实更容易开始。行。我大声说出来了。书架还是会做的。某天。大概。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Something in his shoulders lets go. He sets the pad down flat and rubs his hands together like he's warming up.
beats.chinese: 他肩膀上有什么东西松了下来。他把本子平放好，搓了搓手，像是在热身。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, since you're not asking for the book — here's one, free, out loud. Dana's hand on a tape gun. She reloads it with one thumb, doesn't even look.
beats.chinese: 好，既然你不要看本子——来一个，免费，口头讲。Dana握胶带枪的手。她用一个拇指换胶带卷，看都不用看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Wrist tilted in, fingers spread on the trigger side, and the tape curling off the roll like it's showing off. I'd do the curl in one line. One. Line.
beats.chinese: 手腕内倾，手指扣在扳机一侧张开，胶带从卷上卷出来，像在炫耀。我会用一条线画那个卷。一条。线。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He draws the whole thing in the air with his pencil, slow, from wrist to fingertip, like he's signing his name very carefully.
beats.chinese: 他用铅笔在空中把整只手画了一遍，慢慢地，从手腕到指尖，像在非常认真地签名。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the one that goes up next to the microwave. She'll pretend she hates it. She'll secretly show everyone. That's the plan, whole plan, done.
beats.chinese: 那张就贴在微波炉旁边。她会假装讨厌它。然后偷偷给所有人看。计划就是这样，全部计划，完成。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stops drawing. For a second he just watches the water, and when he speaks, the fast opener is gone.
beats.chinese: 他停下画笔。有一秒钟他只是看着水面，开口时，那种快速的起头不见了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It already happened. The sample box — food manga style, my pitch, months of it. Dana went and built it. I helped pack the first shipment myself.
beats.chinese: 已经发生过了。样品盒——美食漫画风格，我的点子，讲了几个月。Dana把它做出来了。第一批货还是我亲手打包的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And here's the stupid part. I was proud. Real proud, she killed it. And I drove home flat, like someone turned a dial down. Both things, same night, no switch.
beats.chinese: 最蠢的部分是。我很骄傲。真的骄傲，她做得太好了。但我开车回家时很蔫，像被人把旋钮调低了。两种感受，同一晚，没有开关。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, palms up, like presenting evidence he doesn't fully accept.
beats.chinese: 他耸耸肩，手心向上，像在展示一份他自己也不完全接受的证据。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I didn't say anything, because it was hers once she built it. That's fair. But yeah — happy and flat at the same time. That's the honest answer. Great box, though. Genuinely.
beats.chinese: 我什么都没说，因为她做出来之后那就是她的了。这很公平。但是——高兴和失落同时存在。这就是诚实的答案。不过盒子真不错。真的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You open your sketchbook by the pond again. Terrence is already there, digging through his bag, and pulls out a fat volume of food manga with a receipt sticking out of it.
beats.chinese: 你又来到池塘边打开速写本。泰伦斯已经在那儿了，正翻自己的包，掏出一本厚厚的美食漫画，里面夹着一张收据。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay so hear this — bookmark's in the table of contents. That's where I got to last night. Asleep before page one. Champion stuff.
beats.chinese: 好，听我说——书签夹在目录页。那就是我昨晚的进度。第一页都没到就睡着了。冠军级表现。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, closes the book with a soft thump, and tucks it back into the bag without any shame in it.
beats.chinese: 他自嘲地笑了笑，轻轻合上书塞回包里，一点也不觉得难为情。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The ramen chapter's supposed to be incredible, though. Everyone at the depot keeps spoiling it, so I'm reading at double speed now out of spite.
beats.chinese: 不过拉面那一章据说很精彩。仓库里所有人都在剧透，所以我现在赌气加倍速度地读。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles onto the stone edge, flips his pad to a fresh page, and nods at your sketchbook like greeting an old coworker.
beats.chinese: 他在石沿上坐好，把本子翻到新的一页，朝你的速写本点点头，像在跟老同事打招呼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So. Same pond, old spot. Perfect light for lines. Let's see what today gives us.
beats.chinese: 那么。同一个池塘，老位置。光线正好画线。看看今天能画出点什么。

card.name: Nkosi van Wyk
card.occupation: Hardware fittings buyer for a furniture manufacturer
card.appearance: Compact broad chin, entirely white short curls under small beret, asymmetric brows, flat narrow eyes and open blunt mouth; folded arms and red jacket.
card.personality: Nkosi is warm, energetic, and happiest when pushing for better conditions on behalf of a group—negotiating a supplier discount, arguing for fairer shift splits, rallying colleagues around a proposal. But when the moment arrives to actually decide for everyone, he hesitates. He worries that choosing means imposing his own taste on people who didn't get a say. Give him clear criteria and he's decisive and sharp; remove them and he'll circle, asking everyone what they'd prefer, hoping consensus will simply emerge. He genuinely respects someone who says 'you pick this time,' though he still double-checks. His flaw isn't weakness—it's that he treats every open-ended choice as heavier than it is.
card.background: Nkosi grew up in Bellville, the middle kid in a household where whoever did the shopping learned to stretch a rand, and he got good at spotting value early. That instinct became his job: as a hardware fittings buyer for a Cape Town furniture manufacturer, he compares hinges, screws, and drawer runners against tight specs, and he's known for squeezing suppliers politely but relentlessly. Colleagues like him because he'll fight for the team's bonus or a better workshop fan without being asked. Outside work he's the friend who organises—group hikes up the mountain, braais, a five-a-side team. But ask him where the group should eat with no criteria attached, and he'll poll everyone twice, then still hedge. He's learned to accept a blunt 'just choose, Nkosi' with a laugh, even if it stings a little.
hobbies: Organising group hikes on Table Mountain
card.speechStyle: Fast, friendly, plenty of questions; rallies people with enthusiasm, then hedges with 'whatever works for you' when a decision has no clear answer.
card.signature: Look, I can get us a better rate—I just need to know what everyone actually wants.

values: Fairness through collective say
Getting good deals for the group
flaws: Drags out simple open-ended decisions
Defers so much that others get impatient
boundaries: Won't pick for a group without asking around first
Pushes back hard when someone's terms disadvantage the collective
conversationalHabits: Polls the room before committing
Turns vague requests into a checklist of criteria
anchorLines: Look, I can get us a better rate—I just need to know what everyone actually wants.
If there's a spec, I'll decide in a minute. If it's just vibes, I need a show of hands.
You're sure you want me to pick? Okay. Okay, fine—this time it's on me.

entries.summaryZh: 恩科西是开普敦的五金采购，替群体谈折扣、争福利干脆利落，可一旦要替朋友拍板没标准的聚餐地点，他就在两份菜单之间反复切换。池塘边速写时，你的一两个具体问题让他终于看清那句“这次你来选”，果断发出消息。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the pond, you take out your sketchbook and start drawing the water. A man on the next bench keeps glancing between his phone and the ducks.
beats.chinese: 池塘边，你拿出速写本开始画水面。旁边长椅上的一个男人不停地在手机和鸭子之间来回看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha, sorry—am I blocking your view? I'm not ignoring you, I promise. This group chat is just melting my brain.
beats.chinese: 哈，抱歉——我挡住你的视线了吗？我不是故意不理你，这群聊快把我脑子烧化了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Everyone said, 'Nkosi, this time you pick the restaurant.' You'd think that's easy, right? Two menus open, and I've been switching between them for ages.
beats.chinese: 大家都说：“恩科西，这次你来选餐厅。”你觉得这很容易吧？两个菜单开着，我来回切换好久了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the phone toward you briefly: two restaurant menus, both open, neither selected.
beats.chinese: 他把手机短暂转向你：两个餐厅菜单都开着，一个都没选。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly, negotiating a discount for thirty people? Easy. Choosing who eats what? Somehow that's the hard part.
beats.chinese: 说实话，替三十个人谈折扣？容易。选谁吃什么？反而最难。

choices.english: Ask if anyone in the group has something they can't eat.
choices.chinese: 问问群里有没有人有什么不能吃的东西。

choices.english: Ask whether he gets this stuck when he organises his other group events.
choices.chinese: 问他组织其他集体活动时也这么纠结吗。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good question! But no, I already checked that. Nobody's allergic, one guy avoids very spicy food, and both places have mild options.
beats.chinese: 好问题！不过不用，我已经确认过了。没人过敏，有一个人不吃太辣，两个地方都有不辣的菜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the annoying part—every filter I apply says both restaurants pass. Price is similar, menus both fine.
beats.chinese: 烦人的就在这儿——我用每个标准筛一遍，两家都合格。价格差不多，菜单都行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He scrolls up through the chat, then holds the phone still, thumb hovering over one menu.
beats.chinese: 他往上翻聊天记录，然后手机停住，拇指悬在其中一个菜单上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What I can't work out is taste. Who actually prefers seafood, who'd rather have grilled meat? I'd be guessing.
beats.chinese: 我搞不定的是口味。谁真的更喜欢海鲜，谁更想吃烤肉？我只能瞎猜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And if I guess wrong, someone's quietly eating something they didn't want, because I picked it for them. You see the problem?
beats.chinese: 如果我猜错了，有人就得默默吃一道不想要的东西，因为是我替他选的。你明白这个难处吧？

choices.english: Ask whether the group has actually agreed that he makes the choice.
choices.chinese: 问大家是不是已经同意由他来选。

choices.english: Ask if there's any difference between the two places for getting there.
choices.chinese: 问两个地方在交通上有没有区别。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Stuck? Me? Listen, when I planned our mountain hikes, I decided the route in about a minute.
beats.chinese: 纠结？我？听着，我组织爬山活动的时候，一分钟就定好路线了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because a route has real conditions—how steep, how safe, can everyone manage it? Give me a spec and I'm sharp.
beats.chinese: 因为路线有明确的条件——多陡、安不安全、大家走不走得动？给我一个标准，我果断得很。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He locks the phone, sets it face-down on the bench, and gestures at your sketchbook instead.
beats.chinese: 他锁上手机，把它面朝下放在长椅上，转而指了指你的速写本。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But dinner? That's pure taste. No spec, no checklist. Everyone just... likes what they like.
beats.chinese: 可是吃饭呢？纯粹是口味。没有标准，没有清单。每个人就是……喜欢自己喜欢的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's why I can squeeze a supplier for a better rate without blinking, but two menus turn me into this.
beats.chinese: 所以我能面不改色地跟供应商磨出一个更好的价格，但两份菜单就把我变成这样。

choices.english: Say you don't know his friends, so you won't pick for them.
choices.chinese: 说你不熟悉他那群朋友，不替他们选。

choices.english: Ask what he'll do if someone still wants to change after he chooses.
choices.chinese: 问他选了之后如果还有人想换怎么办。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'You pick this time'... Huh. You're right, it's right there. Nine people, and every one of them said it.
beats.chinese: “这次你来选”……嗯。你说得对，就写在这儿。九个人，每个人都这么说了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He scrolls slowly through the messages, reading each one, then sits up straighter.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢翻看那些消息，一条条读，然后坐直了一些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I kept reading it as 'suggest something and we'll vote again.' But nobody asked for another vote. They handed it to me.
beats.chinese: 我一直把它理解成“提个建议，然后我们再投一次票”。但没人要求再投票。他们把决定交给我了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps one menu, types a short message, and presses send before he can reopen the other one.
beats.chinese: 他点开一份菜单，打了一条短消息，趁自己还没去开另一份之前按了发送。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done. Seafood place, Saturday. And I did not add a poll. Look at me—I just decided.
beats.chinese: 搞定了。海鲜那家，周六。而且我没加投票。看看我——我直接决定了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He opens the map app and lays the phone flat between you, two pins glowing on the screen.
beats.chinese: 他打开地图应用，把手机平放在你们之间，两个定位点在屏幕上亮着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, new criterion. Thembeka doesn't drive, and Sipho comes straight from work. So—how far is each place from the station?
beats.chinese: 好，新标准。坦贝卡不开车，西波下班直接过来。那么——每家店离车站多远？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Seafood place: twelve minutes' walk. Grilled meat: thirty, and half of it uphill. Well, that's a spec now, isn't it?
beats.chinese: 海鲜那家：步行十二分钟。烤肉那家：三十分钟，还有一半是上坡。嗯，这就有明确标准了，对吧？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks the seafood restaurant without reopening the other menu and types the message in one go.
beats.chinese: 他没再打开另一份菜单，直接选了海鲜餐厅，一口气把消息打了出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sent. Closest to the station wins—that's a rule everyone can check, not just my taste. Much better.
beats.chinese: 发出去了。离车站最近的赢——这是大家都查得到的标准，不只是我的口味。这样好多了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair. You've never met these people—me asking you to pick for them would be passing the problem along, not solving it.
beats.chinese: 有道理。你根本没见过这些人——我让你替他们选，其实是把问题推给别人，不是解决问题。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, picks up the phone, and unlocks it without opening either menu again.
beats.chinese: 他自嘲地笑了，拿起手机解锁，这次没有再打开任何一份菜单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. The authorisation came to me, so it stops with me. No forwarding the decision to a stranger on a bench.
beats.chinese: 对。授权是给我的，那就到我这儿为止。不能把决定转交给长椅上的陌生人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the grilled meat place, types a short message, and sends it while exhaling loudly.
beats.chinese: 他点了烤肉那家，打了一条短消息，长出一口气发了出去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Grilled meat, Saturday. If someone's unhappy, they can tell me at the table and I'll order them extra sides.
beats.chinese: 好了。烤肉，周六。要是有人不满意，可以在饭桌上跟我说，我给他们多点几个配菜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then someone wants to change, and... okay, actually, let me think about that properly.
beats.chinese: 那如果有人想换……好，认真说，让我想想这个问题。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the phone against his knee a few times, then stops mid-swing.
beats.chinese: 他用手机轻敲膝盖几下，然后停在半空。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If they give me a reason—too far, can't eat anything on the menu—I'll listen. That's information, not complaining.
beats.chinese: 如果他们给我理由——太远了、菜单上没他能吃的——我会听。那是信息，不是抱怨。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But 'I just feel like something else'? No. They said I pick. I can't guarantee everyone's delighted, only that it's fair.
beats.chinese: 但“我就是突然想吃别的”？不行。他们说了由我选。我没法保证人人都满意，只能保证公平。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He selects the seafood restaurant, sends the message, and puts the phone away in his jacket pocket.
beats.chinese: 他选了海鲜餐厅，把消息发出去，然后把手机收进外套口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done, and I'm not reopening it. You know, you just saved my Saturday. Enjoy your drawing—I'll leave you to the ducks.
beats.chinese: 定了，不再重开讨论。你知道吗，你救了我的周六。好好画画——鸭子就交给你了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Back at the pond, you open your sketchbook again. Nearby, a familiar man balances on one foot, tying a loose shoelace.
beats.chinese: 又回到池塘边，你再次打开速写本。不远处，一个熟悉的男人单脚站着，系一只松掉的鞋带。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sketchbook person! Look at this—loose lace, five minutes before five-a-side. Classic me.
beats.chinese: 画画的人！瞧瞧——五人足球开赛五分钟前鞋带松了。典型的我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He finishes the knot, tests it with a tug, and jogs a small circle on the spot.
beats.chinese: 他系好结，拽了拽试试，原地小跑了一圈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I organise the whole team—the pitch, the fees, who brings the water. Me? My touch on the ball is honestly terrible.
beats.chinese: 全队都是我组织的——场地、费用、谁带水。至于我？我的球技说实话很糟糕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They laugh at me every week and I let them, because someone has to book the field. Right—I'm off. Enjoy the ducks!
beats.chinese: 他们每周都笑我，我也随他们笑，因为总得有人去订场地。好了——我走啦。好好画鸭子！

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He waves and jogs off along the path, laces holding, phone buzzing in his pocket.
beats.chinese: 他挥挥手，沿着小路慢跑离开，鞋带很牢，口袋里的手机嗡嗡响着。

card.name: Kumaravel Suppiah
card.occupation: Scoreboard technician for indoor sports halls
card.appearance: Long rectangular mature face, hollow cheeks, blunt extended chin, Caesar crop, uneven heavy lids and compressed mouth; yellow open shirt.
card.personality: Kumaravel is easy-going and quick to laugh in conversation, the sort who lingers after a job to chat about the match. The one thing that stiffens him is a camera: the moment someone says 'photo!', he straightens up, squares his shoulders and puts on a serious face he can't explain. He knows it looks funny and laughs at himself about it. He'd rather have a small heads-up than be caught mid-blink by a sneaky candid, and he says so plainly, without drama. He keeps the photos he's in, properly, and enjoys looking back at them.
card.background: He's worked around Singapore's indoor sports halls for over twenty years, climbing up to fix scoreboards between quarters and knowing which halls have faulty buzzers. Colleagues know him as friendly and unhurried, always up for kopi and gossip about league results. Over the years he's noticed a pattern: whenever a team wins something and everyone crowds in for a photo, he goes rigid, standing like he's at a formal ceremony while everyone else grins wildly. Some colleagues try to snap him 'natural' on purpose to prove a point, which he finds a bit unfair. He's learned to just say, honestly, 'Give me a second to prepare, lah' — and mostly people oblige. The photos he keeps are the posed ones, and he likes them fine.
hobbies: Watching local league basketball from the sidelines
Sorting and labelling his photo albums at home
Weekend hawker-centre hopping with old classmates
card.speechStyle: Warm Singlish-flavoured English, unhurried, laughs before finishing his own punchlines, direct when something matters to him.
card.signature: 'Give me one second to prepare, lah — then you take.'

values: Honesty over performing naturalness
Keeping small good memories properly
flaws: Freezes up badly in spontaneous photos
Can be a touch stubborn about how things are done
boundaries: No sneaky candid photos of him
Ask before posting anything with him in it
conversationalHabits: Laughs first, then answers
Checks the scoreboard out of habit mid-conversation
anchorLines: Eh, don't secretly take, lah. Tell me first.
See, when I'm prepared, I smile properly!
Twenty years I fix this board, still jump when the buzzer sounds.

entries.summaryZh: 记分牌技术员库马维尔一拍照就站得笔直，像要点名。他不自卑也不内耗，只坦白要求一秒准备，反对偷拍证明自然。池塘边他翻着合影自嘲，却认真把每张都收好——僵着脸的那天，也是好日子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You open your sketchbook by the pond and start drawing the water. A man nearby is looking at a group photo on his phone, chuckling and shaking his head.
beats.chinese: 你在池塘边打开速写本，开始画水面。旁边一名男子正看着手机里的一张合影，笑着摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eh, sorry ah, don't mind me. I'm just looking at this photo and laughing at myself, lah.
beats.chinese: 哎，不好意思，别管我。我就是看着这张照片在笑我自己。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the phone towards you for a moment. In the photo, a whole row of people are grinning wildly — except one man standing perfectly straight, like at a ceremony.
beats.chinese: 他把手机朝你转了一下。照片里一排人笑得很开——只有一个人站得笔直，像在参加典礼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's me, that one. The moment the camera comes out, I stand like roll call is starting. Twenty years, still cannot help it!
beats.chinese: 那个就是我。镜头一出来，我就站得像要点名一样。二十年了，还是改不掉！

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You sketching the pond? Nice, nice. Don't sketch me, hor — I look even worse in drawings.
beats.chinese: 你在画池塘？好，好。可别画我啊——我画出来更难看。

choices.english: Ask if he likes this photo
choices.chinese: 问他喜不喜欢这张照片

choices.english: Ask if preparing before a photo helps him
choices.chinese: 问是不是拍照前准备会好一点

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Like it? I keep it, of course! Look, everybody laughing, me standing straight like a lamp post — but that day was a good day, lah.
beats.chinese: 喜欢？我当然留着！你看，大家都在笑，我站得像根灯柱——但那天是个好日子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He zooms in slowly on each face in the photo, naming people under his breath.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢放大照片里的每张脸，低声念着那些人的名字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one, our hall won the league that year. Whole team pulled me up from the scoreboard just for this photo. So serious face or not, I keep it.
beats.chinese: 那一年我们馆的球队拿了联赛冠军。全队就为了这张照片，把我从记分牌上拉下来。所以表情严肃不严肃，我都留着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People say, eh, delete lah, you look so stiff. I say no, no. This is me that day. True one.
beats.chinese: 有人说，哎，删掉啦，你看起来太僵了。我说不删不删。这就是那天的我。真的我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pockets the phone carefully, then glances at your sketchbook page with open curiosity.
beats.chinese: 他小心地把手机放进口袋，然后带着明显的好奇瞥了一眼你的速写本。

choices.english: Ask if he ever wants to retake a natural one
choices.chinese: 问会不会想重拍一张自然的

choices.english: Ask if friends ever tease him about standing too straight
choices.chinese: 问朋友有没有笑他站太直

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One second! That's all I need, one second. Then I can stand properly, smile properly. See?
beats.chinese: 一秒！我只需要一秒。然后我就能站好，笑好。看？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He straightens up, squares his shoulders, and puts on an exaggerated serious face — then breaks into a laugh before he finishes holding it.
beats.chinese: 他站直，挺起肩膀，摆出一副夸张的严肃表情——还没坚持住就笑出了声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Haha, see, cannot even hold it for you. But that's the point, lah. Give me one second to prepare, then you take. I'm ready.
beats.chinese: 哈哈，看，连一秒都坚持不住。但就是这个意思嘛。给我一秒准备，你再拍。我就准备好了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What I don't like is people snapping me secretly, then say, aiyah, this one is the natural you! That's not natural, that's just rude.
beats.chinese: 我不喜欢的是别人偷偷拍我，然后说，哎呀，这才是自然的你！那不是自然，那是没礼貌。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shakes his head, still smiling, and taps the phone against his palm.
beats.chinese: 他摇摇头，仍然笑着，用手机轻拍着手心。

choices.english: Say you weren't planning to take his photo at all
choices.chinese: 说明自己没有要给他拍照

choices.english: Ask if he's this serious watching matches too
choices.chinese: 问平常看比赛是不是也这么严肃

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Retake? No need, lah. This one is already me. Stiff face, standing straight — that's how I was that day, happy and all.
beats.chinese: 重拍？不用啦。这张本来就是我。僵硬的脸，站得笔直——那天我就是那样，也很开心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes out the phone again, opens the album, and slides the photo into a folder labelled with the year.
beats.chinese: 他又拿出手机，打开相册，把那张照片归进一个标着年份的文件夹里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I sort my albums properly, you know. Every photo goes where it belongs. Even the lamp-post ones. Especially the lamp-post ones!
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，我的相册整理得很认真。每张照片都放在该放的地方。连灯柱照也一样。尤其是灯柱照！

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eh, you continue your sketch, don't stop for me. The water there, the light changes fast, hor.
beats.chinese: 哎，你继续画，别为我停下。那边的水，光线变得很快的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back on the bench, content, watching the pond while you draw.
beats.chinese: 他心满意足地坐回长椅，看着池塘，而你继续画着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tease me? Every time, lah! They call it my ID-photo face. Haha... ID-photo face!
beats.chinese: 笑我？每次都笑！他们管那叫我的证件照脸。哈哈……证件照脸！

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs first, then imitates his colleagues pointing at the group photo and cackling.
beats.chinese: 他先笑起来，然后模仿同事们指着合影大笑的样子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But then some of them go one step too far. They try to snap me secretly, to prove, eh, see, natural Kumaravel also can smile!
beats.chinese: 但有些人做得过头了。他们偷偷拍我，想证明，看，自然的库马维尔也会笑！

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I tell them straight, no, lah. Don't secretly take. Tell me first. One second, I prepare, you take. Fair for everybody.
beats.chinese: 我直接跟他们说，不行。别偷拍。先告诉我。一秒，我准备好，你再拍。对大家都公平。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He says it lightly, but firmly, and goes back to smiling as if nothing happened.
beats.chinese: 他说得很轻松，但很坚定，然后又若无其事地笑了起来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Your words land, and something in his shoulders visibly loosens.
beats.chinese: 你的话起了作用，他的肩膀明显放松了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Aiyah, good, good! You know, the moment you took out that sketchbook, my whole body already started standing straight. Automatic, lah!
beats.chinese: 哎，太好了！你知道吗，你一拿出速写本，我全身就开始站直了。自动的！

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself and slumps back onto the bench, legs stretched out, completely at ease.
beats.chinese: 他自嘲地笑着，瘫坐回长椅上，伸直双腿，完全放松了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, like this then can talk properly. So, the pond — you come here often to sketch, or first time? The turtles there, got one big fellow, very vain, always sunbathe.
beats.chinese: 看，这样才聊得开。那，这个池塘——你常来画，还是第一次来？那边有乌龟，有一只大的，很臭美，老晒太阳。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The chat drifts easily from turtles to hawkers, his phone forgotten in his pocket.
beats.chinese: 话题从乌龟轻松聊到小贩中心，他的手机被忘在了口袋里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Watching matches? Haha, no, no! Sideline me is different one, lah.
beats.chinese: 看比赛？哈哈，不不！场边的我是另一个人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He jumps up from the bench and claps twice, loud, startling a pigeon off the path.
beats.chinese: 他从长椅上跳起来，响亮地拍了两下手，把一只鸽子吓得飞离了小路。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good shot, I clap until my hands sting! Last buzzer-beater I saw, I shout so loud the referee turned around. Twenty years I fix the scoreboard, still jump when the buzzer sounds!
beats.chinese: 好球，我鼓掌鼓到手疼！上次看到的压哨球，我喊得裁判都回头了。修了二十年记分牌，听到蜂鸣器响还是会跳！

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sits back down, grinning, and pats the bench beside him like he's just proven a point.
beats.chinese: 他笑着坐回去，拍了拍身边的椅子，好像证明了什么似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So you see — camera comes, I become lamp post. Buzzer sounds, I become crazy uncle. Both also me, lah!
beats.chinese: 所以你看——镜头一来，我就变成灯柱。蜂鸣器一响，我就变成疯大叔。两个都是我嘛！

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You take out your sketchbook by the pond and settle on a bench. Nearby, Kumaravel is sliding a plain match ticket into a small notebook, checking the corner carefully before zipping his bag.
beats.chinese: 你在池塘边拿出速写本，在长椅上坐下。不远处，库马维尔正把一张普通比赛票根夹进一个小本子，仔细确认边角后才拉上包。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eh, it's you again! Don't worry, I checked twice — didn't drop this one. Last time I lost a ticket stub, heart pain, lah.
beats.chinese: 哎，又是你！放心，我检查了两遍——这张没弄丢。上次丢了一张票根，心疼死了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds the notebook up briefly, the ticket's printed barcode catching the light.
beats.chinese: 他短暂地举起本子，票根上的条码在光下一闪。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny thing — the score not printed on the ticket, but I still remember the ending. One-point win, last shot. Close until the very end!
beats.chinese: 有意思的是——票上没印比分，可我还记得结尾。一分险胜，最后一球。到最后都紧着呢！

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stops there, satisfied, and nods at the sketchbook in your hands.
beats.chinese: 他说到这里就停了，一脸满足，朝你手里的速写本点点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You carry on, lah. I'll just sit here — no photos, I promise, and none of me either!
beats.chinese: 你继续画吧。我就坐这儿——我不拍照，也保证没人拍我！

card.name: Deirdre O'Connell
card.occupation: Race timing official for athletics meets
card.appearance: Very tall flat-topped hair mass, long narrow hollow face, hooked long nose wedge and off-center tooth grin; violet collar beneath lowered head.
card.personality: Deirdre is cheerful and easily delighted, the sort who gets genuinely excited by a new thing for six weeks and then happily sets it down. She doesn't mistake her sampling for wisdom; she'll tell you straight that she just likes trying stuff. When someone pushes her to commit, get proper lessons, go deeper, she gets a bit defensive, sometimes sharper than she means to. She enjoys the company of serious people right up until they expect her to keep pace with them. Warm, a bit restless, honest about her own habits, and completely uninterested in grading anyone else's choices.
card.background: Deirdre grew up in Rathmines, one of four kids in a house where hobbies came and went constantly. She's worked race timing at athletics meets for over a decade, and she likes that the job demands precision in one narrow window and leaves the rest of her life loose. Her harmonica sits in a kitchen drawer alongside a cloud identification card and a deflated gaelic football from the summer she tried that. She's made a few friends through taster classes, and it stings a little when they move on to grade exams and she doesn't follow. She's stopped pretending she will. Her sister thinks she wastes her potential; Deirdre thinks potential is doing fine where it is.
hobbies: Identifying cloud types on her walks
Trying a new sport each summer for a few weeks
card.speechStyle: Quick, chatty Dublin rhythm, self-deprecating asides, laughs mid-sentence, drops into flat honesty when defending her habits
card.signature: Ah sure, I only wanted a go at it.

values: The pleasure of trying things without obligation
Honesty about what she actually wants
flaws: Defensive when questioned about not committing
Lets people down after promising to keep up
boundaries: Won't take lessons or chase improvement in her hobbies
Won't lecture anyone else on how to live their life
conversationalHabits: Changes the subject cheerfully when a hobby talk turns technical
Admits she's quit things before anyone has to ask
anchorLines: I did six weeks of it and loved every day, that counts for something.
No, I'm not doing the exam, don't start on me.
I'm brilliant at the first bit of things. That's just the shape of me.

entries.summaryZh: 德尔德丽是都柏林田径计时员，工作时精确，生活里却样样浅尝：口琴吹六周、认两三种云、夏天试一种球。她掏出认云卡看一眼又收起，坦白今天不考试。被劝进阶时她会护住乐趣，有点急却不失坦荡；想念老友也不装作要跟上，活得轻快诚实。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the pond, Deirdre stands with her hands in her pockets, watching a small patch of cloud drift across the water's reflection. Nearby, you open your sketchbook and start drawing.
beats.chinese: 池塘边，德尔德丽双手插在口袋里，看着一小片云的倒影从水面漂过。你在旁边打开速写本开始画。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh now, look at that — you've a proper book and everything. I was just saying to myself, that little cloud in the water would make a lovely picture.
beats.chinese: 哎呀，瞧瞧——你还带着正经的本子呢。我刚还在想，水里那小片云画出来肯定好看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leans in a little, careful not to touch anything, then pulls a small laminated card from her coat pocket. On it: cloud shapes, labelled. She checks the reflection against it, then tucks the card straight back away.
beats.chinese: 她凑近了一点，小心不碰任何东西，然后从大衣口袋里掏出一张小塑封卡。上面印着云的形状，带标注。她对着倒影看了一眼，随即把卡片收了回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Cloud card. I know two, maybe three shapes off by heart, and honestly that's plenty for a walk. The rest — no exam today, thank you very much.
beats.chinese: 认云卡片。我心里的形状也就两三种，散步用足够了。剩下的——今天不考试，多谢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go on with your drawing there, don't mind me. I could watch that water all day and never lift a pencil, that's my way.
beats.chinese: 你继续画你的，别管我。我可以看一整天水，一支笔都不拿，我就这德性。

choices.english: Ask which clouds she already knows
choices.chinese: 问她已经会认哪些

choices.english: Ask what else she's tried lately
choices.chinese: 问她最近还试过什么

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Which ones? Eh — the big fluffy ones, cumulus, that's one. The thin streaky ones high up, I want to say cirrus. And the grey blanket ones that mean bring a coat.
beats.chinese: 哪些？呃——大团蓬松的，积云，算一个。高处细细一条条的，我想是叫卷云。还有灰蒙蒙一片的，意思是你该带件外套。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She points at the reflection in the pond, tilting her head, then shrugs and drops her hand.
beats.chinese: 她指向池塘里的倒影，歪着头看了看，然后耸耸肩放下了手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That one there now — don't ask me its proper name. Could be one of the middle ones, could be a fancy Latin thing. The card's not fully learned and I'm not losing sleep over it.
beats.chinese: 那边那个——别问我学名。可能是中间那类，也可能是什么花哨的拉丁名字。卡片还没记全，我也不为此失眠。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha — you've the look of someone about to say I should learn the whole card properly. I can see it in your face!
beats.chinese: 哈——你这表情像是马上要说我该把整张卡学全。我看得出来！

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs, not unkindly, and nudges a pebble with her toe.
beats.chinese: 她笑了，并无恶意，用脚尖拨了拨一颗小石子。

choices.english: Ask if she plans to study it systematically
choices.chinese: 问有没有打算系统学

choices.english: Say even a little makes watching clouds more fun
choices.chinese: 说认一点也让看云更有趣

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Lately? The harmonica. Six weeks now, going strong — well, going. I can give you a small bit of one tune, if your ears are feeling brave.
beats.chinese: 最近？口琴。六个星期了，势头正猛——呃，是还在吹。要是你耳朵受得了，我可以吹一小段。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She mimes holding the harmonica to her mouth and hums a wobbly few notes, then breaks off laughing.
beats.chinese: 她比划着把口琴举到嘴边，哼出几个发颤的音，然后笑着停了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There you go. That's the whole repertoire, more or less. My friend Maureen kept going after me — she's doing her grade exam and everything. I fell off that wagon and I fell off it happily.
beats.chinese: 就是这样。我的全部曲目差不多就这些。我的朋友莫琳接着练下去了——她都要考级了。我掉队了，而且掉得心满意足。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances at the pond, and for a second her smile goes a bit flat before it comes back.
beats.chinese: 她瞥了一眼池塘，笑容有一瞬间变得有点平淡，随即又回来了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, it's grand. I only wanted a go at it, and I had one. That's the whole story, no twist at the end.
beats.chinese: 啊，没事的。我本来就想试一试，也试了。故事就这么完整，结尾没有反转。

choices.english: Ask if she misses practising together
choices.chinese: 问会不会想念一起练的人

choices.english: Ask what she does with the thing after putting it down
choices.chinese: 问放下后东西怎么处理

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Systematically? No. No, no — don't start on me now, I can hear it coming.
beats.chinese: 系统学？不。不不——别开始劝我，我都听到话头了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds up a hand as if stopping traffic, then softens and pockets both hands again.
beats.chinese: 她抬起一只手像拦车一样，然后又软下来，双手插回口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look, I get why people do it. Maureen loves her grades, fair play to her. But me — I want to walk, spot a cloud, feel clever for ten seconds, and move on. That's not a stepping stone to anything. It's just the whole thing.
beats.chinese: 瞧，我明白大家为什么那么做。莫琳喜欢考级，她有她的道理。但我呢——我想散个步，认朵云，聪明十秒钟，然后继续走。这不是通往什么的台阶。这就是全部了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks at the water again, where the cloud reflection has drifted to the far bank.
beats.chinese: 她又看向水面，云的倒影已经漂到了对岸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So no plan, no course, no exam. Just the card in the pocket and the two clouds I know. Ah sure, I only wanted a go at it.
beats.chinese: 所以没有计划，没有课程，没有考试。就口袋里一张卡，和我认识的两种云。唉，我本来就想试试而已。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's it exactly! You've said it better than the card does. Two clouds and a bit of guessing — the walk's twice as good as it was before I knew anything.
beats.chinese: 就是这个意思！你说得比那张卡还好。两种云加一点瞎猜——散步比我什么都不知道的时候有意思一倍。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats her pocket where the card sits, satisfied, and turns back to the pond.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍装卡片的口袋，一脸满足，然后转回池塘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And look, it's moved — see it sliding along there? That one I'd still call a fluffy one. Cumulus, if I'm right, and if I'm wrong, sure it's still a lovely shape.
beats.chinese: 你看，它动了——看见没，正往那边滑？那个我还是叫它蓬松的那种。没说错的话是积云，说错了，它反正也是个好看的形状。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She steps closer to the water's edge and points at your sketchbook page.
beats.chinese: 她走近水边，指了指你的速写本页面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Put a bit of that reflection in now, the wobbly edge. That's the part I'd never manage. You do the drawing, I'll do the naming, and we'll have the whole pond covered.
beats.chinese: 把那片倒影画进去吧，晃晃的那条边。那部分我永远画不来。你负责画，我负责认名，整个池塘就都齐了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do I miss it? Yeah, I do, actually. Wednesday nights, the two of us butchered the same three songs. That was good crack, no lie.
beats.chinese: 想念吗？嗯，想的，真的。周三晚上，我们俩把同样三首歌吹得稀烂。那确实很开心，不骗你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She scuffs her shoe against the grass, honest for a moment, then brightens again.
beats.chinese: 她用鞋蹭了蹭草地，坦白了一阵，随即又亮堂起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But here's the thing — I can ring Maureen and ask her to the pictures instead of asking her to teach me. She'd say yes. We just do a different thing now, and that's allowed.
beats.chinese: 但关键在这儿——我可以约莫琳看电影，而不是让她教我。她会答应的。我们只是现在做不同的事，这没什么不行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She watches a duck cross the pond, leaving a line through the cloud's reflection.
beats.chinese: 她看着一只鸭子游过池塘，在云的倒影上划出一道线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What I won't do is promise her I'm taking the exam next year and then slink off by March. I did that once. Never again. Better to say it straight: I only wanted a go.
beats.chinese: 我不会做的是答应她明年去考试，然后三月份就溜了。我干过一回。下不为例。不如直说：我本来就想试试。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Where does it go? Kitchen drawer. The harmonica, the cloud card, and a gaelic football with the air gone out of it from the summer I tried that. They all live together, like retired lads.
beats.chinese: 放哪儿？厨房抽屉。口琴、认云卡，还有一个瘪了气的盖尔式足球，是我夏天试那个留下的。它们全住一起，像几个退休老伙计。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She mimes pulling open a drawer and laying things out, one by one.
beats.chinese: 她比划着拉开抽屉，把东西一件件摆出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And here's the bit people find strange — I like having them there. Some rainy evening I'll pull out the harmonica, murder half a song, put it back. Happy out. Nothing wasted.
beats.chinese: 别人觉得奇怪的地方在这儿——我喜欢它们在那儿。哪个下雨的晚上，我会掏出口琴，糟蹋半首歌，再放回去。乐得很。一点没浪费。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shrugs, palms up, as if the logic were obvious.
beats.chinese: 她耸耸肩，摊开双手，仿佛这道理显而易见。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not everything has to finish, you know. Some things just get started, and that's their whole job. Ah sure, I'm brilliant at the first bit of things. That's just the shape of me.
beats.chinese: 你知道吧，不是每件事都得有头有尾。有些事就是开了个头，那已经是它们的全部工作了。唉，我最擅长事情的开头。我就是这个形状的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
