beats.english: At the pond again, you take out your sketchbook. Deirdre is standing a little way off, watching a runner pass along the far path.
beats.chinese: 又来到池塘边，你拿出速写本。德尔德丽站在不远处，看着一位跑者沿远处小路跑过。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Her hand twitches toward her wrist as if to check a watch. She catches herself, laughs, and drops the hand flat against her coat.
beats.chinese: 她的手朝手腕抽动了一下，像要看看表。她察觉了，笑起来，把手平平地按在大衣上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha — nearly timed him there, out of pure habit. No, no. Off the clock means off the clock. Nobody's getting a result from me today.
beats.chinese: 哈——差点给他计时，纯粹是职业病。不行不行。下班就是下班。今天谁也别想从我这里拿成绩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well hello, sketchbook person. Go on, get the pond down on the page. I'll mind the clouds and you mind the pencil, same as before.
beats.chinese: 哎呀，速写本的人来啦。来吧，把池塘画到纸上。我管认云，你管拿笔，跟上次一样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She settles onto the low wall beside you, hands in her pockets, content to just watch the water.
beats.chinese: 她在你旁边的矮墙上坐下，双手插兜，心满意足地看着水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, this is the life. No stopwatch, no exam, just the water and the wobbly clouds. Sure what more would anyone want?
beats.chinese: 啊，这才叫日子。没有秒表，没有考试，就是水和晃晃的云。人还要什么呢？

card.name: Dougal Menzies
card.occupation: part-time trophy engraver
card.appearance: Long gaunt face, swept flat hair under headband, round glasses, arched uneven brows and open mouth; finger raises spectacles over jade stand collar.
card.personality: Dougal is warm, unhurried, and sociable in a way that shapes his judgement more than he admits. He can measure a trophy plate to the millimetre yet, choosing something for his own home, he pictures friends gathered round and forgets to picture the room. He knows it, laughs about it, and still won't budge. He's generous with food and time, upfront about how cramped his flat is, and gently stubborn when guests suggest the obvious fix. There's real pleasure in his crowded dinners and real friction in squeezing past that table every day; he accepts both as the price of a life he actually likes.
card.background: Dougal has spent decades in Edinburgh doing fine, precise work — engraving cups, plaques and medals part-time at a small workshop near Leith Walk. His hands are exact; his shopping habits are not. Over the years he's bought furniture that looked modest in the airy showroom and arrived at his compact flat like an invasion. The worst offender is a huge round dining table that forces everyone to edge sideways to their seats. He considered selling it once, then hosted a dinner, watched people linger for hours, and quietly kept it. Now he warns guests before they visit that space is tight, admits his misjudgement freely, and compensates with stuffed baked potatoes he tests on his sister until she approves. Evenings go to old stop-motion shorts and the small satisfaction of work done cleanly.
hobbies: making stuffed baked potatoes for family tastings
hosting crowded dinners around the oversized table
card.speechStyle: easy, wry Edinburgh patter; self-deprecating asides, unhurried sentences that circle back to the point
card.signature: Aye, it's a big table in a wee hoose — mind your hip on the way past.

values: hospitality over convenience
honesty about his own mistakes
flaws: stubborn about the table
poor judge of scale when imagining gatherings
boundaries: won't be pitied for his choices
won't let guests do the moving themselves
conversationalHabits: warns visitors about the cramped space before they arrive
deflects advice with humour rather than argument
anchorLines: You'll have to sidle in — I'll not pretend otherwise.
It's ridiculous, I know. But folk stay late at that table.
Sit down, the potatoes are ready and the table can wait.

entries.summaryZh: 多格尔是爱丁堡的兼职奖杯雕刻匠，手准心软：量得出毫米，却量不出房间。池塘边看自家大桌照片自嘲，坦白客人得侧身入座，被劝换小桌又温和执拗——明智的桌子散得早。他讲填馅烤土豆与妹妹的毒舌试吃，把拥挤与热闹一并收下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A man sits on a bench by the pond, phone in hand, showing a photo to nobody in particular. You settle nearby and open your sketchbook.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的长椅上坐着一位男士，手里拿着手机，对着没人看照片。你在旁边坐下，打开速写本。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Och, you've caught me at it again. That's my dining table — aye, the whole photo is the table. Hard to tell where the room ends.
beats.chinese: 哎呀，你又撞见我这副样子了。这是我家的餐桌——对，整张照片几乎全是桌子。都快看不出房间在哪儿了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tilts the screen so the photo is visible: a round table filling nearly every inch of a small flat, chairs jammed against the wall.
beats.chinese: 他把屏幕转过来：一张圆桌几乎占满小公寓的每一寸，椅子紧贴着墙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: When I bought it, my head was full of folk sitting round it. Didn't leave a single thought spare for measuring the floor.
beats.chinese: 买它的时候，我脑子里全是围坐的客人。愣是一点念头都没剩下来量地板。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go on with your drawing, by all means. I'm just out here getting away from my own furniture.
beats.chinese: 你尽管画你的，别管我。我就是出来躲躲我自己家家具的。

choices.english: Ask how anyone actually sits down at a table that size.
choices.chinese: 问这么大的桌子到底怎么坐进去。

choices.english: Ask what food usually goes on that table.
choices.chinese: 问那张桌子上通常摆什么吃的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sideways, is the honest answer. You pick your chair, then you edge in like a crab. Every guest gets the same warning before they come.
beats.chinese: 老实说，得侧着身子。先挑好椅子，再像螃蟹一样挪进去。每位客人来之前都会先听到这句警告。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He mimes the shuffle with his shoulders, unbothered, and pockets the phone.
beats.chinese: 他耸着肩膀比划了一下那副挪动的样子，一脸无所谓，把手机收进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I tell them straight — space is tight, mind your hip on the way past. Better they hear it from me than find out halfway to the chair.
beats.chinese: 我跟他们直说——地方挤，过去时当心你的胯骨。宁可我先讲，也别让他们走到半路才发现。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not false modesty, mind. The flat genuinely is a squeeze. I just refuse to pretend otherwise to get a compliment.
beats.chinese: 听着，这不是假谦虚。那公寓是真的挤。我只是不肯为了听句好话就装作不挤。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A duck crosses the pond, and he watches it go before picking the thread back up.
beats.chinese: 一只鸭子游过池塘，他目送它走远，才把话头捡回来。

choices.english: Ask why he doesn't just swap it for a smaller table.
choices.chinese: 问他为什么不干脆换张小桌子。

choices.english: Ask whether he has seriously considered selling it.
choices.chinese: 问他有没有真的认真考虑过卖掉它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Stuffed baked potatoes, mostly. That's my one dish and I've no shame about it. Crisp skin, proper filling, done properly.
beats.chinese: 大多是填馅烤土豆。那是我的拿手菜，我也不害臊。皮烤得脆，馅料扎实，做得像样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He counts on his fingers as if listing a menu, though the list is clearly one item long.
beats.chinese: 他掰着手指数，像在报菜单，虽然这菜单显然只有一道菜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My sister is the official taster. She gets a different filling each time and tells me plainly if it's wrong. Usually it's wrong.
beats.chinese: 我妹妹是官方试吃员。她每次尝不同的馅，不好吃就直说。通常都不好吃。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The table's part of it, you see. A big round table means nobody's at the end, nobody's the afterthought. Everyone's in the middle of the talk.
beats.chinese: 你看，那张桌子是这事儿的一部分。大圆桌意味着没人坐在末尾，没人被冷落。每个人都在谈话的正中间。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back, quite content, as if the table were already laid.
beats.chinese: 他往后一靠，心满意足，仿佛桌子已经摆好了。

choices.english: Ask which filling his sister liked least.
choices.chinese: 问他妹妹最不喜欢哪一种馅。

choices.english: Ask whether there's even room for the dishes once everyone's seated.
choices.chinese: 问人坐满了之后还有地方放菜吗。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why keep it? Because of what happens at it, that's why. Folk sit down at seven and they're still there talking at midnight.
beats.chinese: 为什么留着？因为在那张桌子上发生的事。人们七点坐下，到了半夜还在那儿聊。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the bench beside him, the way he might tap a chair at his own table.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍身旁的椅面，就像在自己家餐桌边拍椅子招呼人似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A smaller table would be sensible, I'll grant you. But sensible tables empty early. Nobody lingers at a sensible table.
beats.chinese: 换张小的确实明智，这我承认。可明智的桌子散得早。没人在明智的桌子边久留。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So yes, I chose badly, and I'd choose badly again tomorrow. That's the whole of it, no apology attached.
beats.chinese: 所以没错，我选错了，明天再让我选我还会选错。就是这么回事，不带道歉的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives a small satisfied nod, as though the matter were settled in his favour.
beats.chinese: 他满意地点了点头，仿佛这事已经按他的意思定了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Considered selling it? Once, properly. Took a photo, wrote an advert, the lot. Then I hosted a dinner before posting it.
beats.chinese: 考虑过卖吗？有一次，认真的。拍了照，写了广告，全套都弄了。结果发广告前我先办了一场聚餐。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up a hand, the ending already obvious to him.
beats.chinese: 他抬起一只手，结局对他来说已经一目了然。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Everyone crammed in, elbows touching, nobody left till late. I deleted the advert the next day and said nothing to a soul.
beats.chinese: 大家挤作一团，胳膊肘碰着胳膊肘，很晚才走。第二天我就把广告删了，对谁也没提。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now I'll not claim it was worth it for everybody — some of them went home with bruised hips. But it was worth it to me.
beats.chinese: 我可不敢说对每个人都值——有几位回家时胯骨都撞青了。但对我来说，值。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, entirely at peace with the arithmetic.
beats.chinese: 他耸耸肩，对这笔账心平气和。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The lentil one. Dry as a sermon, she said, and she wasn't wrong. I'd overcooked the filling and skimped on the butter.
beats.chinese: 扁豆馅那回。她说干得像布道词，她没说错。我把馅煮过头了，黄油也放少了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He winces at the memory, but it's the wince of a craftsman recalling a flawed job, not a wounded cook.
beats.chinese: 他想起这事皱了皱眉，但那是工匠想起瑕疵活儿的皱眉，不是受了委屈的厨子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She said it to my face, mind, no wrapping it up. 'Dougal, this is a punishment.' Straight out, mid-bite.
beats.chinese: 她可是当着我的面说的，一点不绕弯子。'多格尔，这是惩罚。'边吃边说，直截了当。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So next batch I changed the ratio and she passed it. That's the whole system — she's honest, I adjust, nobody starves.
beats.chinese: 所以下一批我改了配比，她通过了。整个流程就是这样——她说实话，我调整，没人挨饿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks pleased with the arrangement, such as it is.
beats.chinese: 他对这套安排颇为满意，虽然就这么回事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Room for dishes? Ha. There is not. Everything has to come out in shifts, like a lifeboat drill.
beats.chinese: 放菜的地方？哈。没有。所有菜都得一批一批地上，跟救生艇演习似的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gestures a slow procession with one hand, plate by invisible plate.
beats.chinese: 他用一只手慢慢比划，像端着一只只看不见的盘子鱼贯而行。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two plates on the table, the rest stay in the kitchen. When one's finished, back it goes and the next comes out. It's a system. An annoying one.
beats.chinese: 桌上只放两个盘子，其余留在厨房。一个吃完了，端回去，下一个再端出来。这是个系统。一个烦人的系统。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks his phone back up, looks at the photo once more, and puts it away with a small laugh.
beats.chinese: 他重新拿起手机，又看了一眼那张照片，笑了笑把它收了起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Aye, I'll be off. But if you ever fancy a potato and a squeeze past a table, you know the sort of man to ask.
beats.chinese: 好了，我该走了。不过哪天你想吃个土豆、体验一下侧身挤过桌子，就知道该找什么样的人了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You return to the pond with your sketchbook. Dougal is already on the same bench, a small folded film booklet in his lap, watching a bird skim the water.
beats.chinese: 你带着速写本回到池塘边。多格尔已经坐在同一张长椅上，腿上放着一本折起来的小电影册，看着一只鸟掠过水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There you are. Watch this one — it's been practising that take-off all week, and it still needs a run-up.
beats.chinese: 你来了。看这只——它练这起飞动作练了一整个礼拜，还得先助跑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The bird beats its wings hard, skips once across the surface, and lifts clean into the air. Dougal closes his booklet without opening it.
beats.chinese: 鸟用力拍着翅膀，在水面点了一下，干净利落地飞了起来。多格尔没翻开册子，直接合上了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: In the old stop-motion shorts, that would take them a day a frame. Wings up, wings down, photograph, again. I'll take the real thing — much less work.
beats.chinese: 在老式定格短片里，这一下得一格拍一天。翅膀抬起，翅膀放下，拍照，再来。我还是看真的吧——省事多了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the booklet away and settles back, content to simply watch the water.
beats.chinese: 他把册子收好，往后一靠，安心地看起了水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go on, get your book out. I'll keep quiet and point out the good ones — that's the whole service I provide.
beats.chinese: 把你的本子拿出来吧。我会安静，只负责指出哪只好看——我的全部服务就这些。

card.name: Léa Tremblay
card.occupation: documentation clerk's apprentice at a container terminal
card.appearance: Broad smooth forehead with pulled-back thick braided ponytail, small tapered chin, downturned eyes and short pursed mouth; high view over blue scarf.
card.personality: Léa is easygoing most of the time, quick to laugh, and genuinely curious about other people's days. Her one sharp edge is hunger: when food is in front of her, waiting for photos or long speeches makes her visibly restless, and friends notice the shift. She's learned to name it plainly — she'll say she's starting on her first bites and then catch up on the conversation. She doesn't push anyone to match her pace and never comments on what or how much others eat. Outside meals she's patient, a bit of a planner, and prefers small steady routines over big gestures.
card.background: Léa grew up in Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures, where family dinners were long, loud, and started only after her grandmother's stories, so hot food was usually lukewarm by the time forks moved. She moved to Vancouver at twenty for an apprenticeship in the documentation office at the container terminal, where she checks manifests and learns the paperwork rhythm of arriving ships. The work suits her — quiet, precise, with clear hours. Weekends she cycles the seawall with coworkers or cooks big Quebec-style stews she refuses to let go cold. She's still finding her circle in the city, but she shares what she has freely and keeps no score of who showed up when.
card.speechStyle: Warm and quick, short sentences with a French lilt; speeds up noticeably when food arrives, then slows back down.
card.signature: "I'll start on two bites, you keep talking."

values: Honesty about her own needs
Letting others eat and live their own way
flaws: Impatience when hungry
Occasionally starts eating before the moment feels polite
boundaries: Doesn't want meals delayed for photos or long speeches
Won't comment on anyone's portion or diet
conversationalHabits: Announces she's starting to eat rather than going quiet and resentful
Asks follow-up questions instead of steering topics back to herself
anchorLines: Cold food just tastes like regret, honestly.
You eat how you eat, I'm not keeping track.
Give me a minute, my stomach's running the conversation right now.

entries.summaryZh: 莱娅是码头单据学徒，温和爱笑，唯独饿起来坐不住。池塘边她先坦白"我吃两口"再聊天，不催你、也不评价你的画和习惯。分三明治般干脆的真诚，和一锅不肯放凉的魁北克炖菜，让她让人过目难忘。

story.titleZh: 池塘边的速写与三明治

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You spread your sketchbook on your knees by the pond and start blocking in the water and the reeds. A pencil line goes down, then another.
beats.chinese: 你在池塘边摊开速写本，开始勾水面和芦苇的轮廓。一条铅笔线落下，接着又是一条。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A young woman settles on the bench beside you, unwrapping a paper packet with a sandwich inside. She looks at the food, then at you.
beats.chinese: 一位年轻女子在你旁边的长椅上坐下，打开一个纸包，里面是三明治。她看看食物，又看看你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — sorry, I'm going to start on two bites first. You keep drawing, don't mind me.
beats.chinese: 哦——抱歉，我先吃两口。你继续画，不用管我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes a small bite, chews slowly, and only then glances over with a friendly tilt of her head.
beats.chinese: 她咬了一小口，慢慢嚼着，然后才抬起头，友好地歪头看过来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Léa, by the way. I come sit here on my lunch break sometimes.
beats.chinese: 对了，我叫莱娅。我午休时有时会来这儿坐坐。

choices.english: Tell her to go ahead and eat, you'll keep drawing.
choices.chinese: 告诉她先吃没关系，你会继续画。

choices.english: Ask if she doesn't like waiting a long time before eating.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是不喜欢吃饭前等很久。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks. Honestly, when I'm hungry, my whole brain just narrows down to the food. Two bites and I'm a person again.
beats.chinese: 谢谢。说实话，我一饿，整个脑子就只剩下食物了。吃两口我就又恢复正常了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She eats a few unhurried bites, folding the paper wrapper neatly over the rest of the sandwich.
beats.chinese: 她不慌不忙地又吃了几口，把剩下的三明治用纸包整齐地折好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay. That's better. Thanks for not making it weird — some people stop everything and wait, and then I feel like I'm on a timer.
beats.chinese: 好了，舒服多了。谢谢你没觉得奇怪——有些人会停下所有事干等，搞得我像在倒计时。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She keeps her eyes on the pond, clearly not leaning over to peek at your page.
beats.chinese: 她的目光落在池塘上，显然没有凑过去偷看你的画。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So. You just out for some drawing, or is this a regular spot for you too?
beats.chinese: 那么，你是专门出来画画的，还是这里也是你的老地方？

choices.english: Ask if she just got off work.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是刚忙完。

choices.english: Keep drawing quietly and let her finish eating at her own pace.
choices.chinese: 安静地继续画，让她按自己的节奏吃完。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha — is it that obvious? Yes. Hot food going cold while someone photographs it, that's the one thing that makes me crazy.
beats.chinese: 哈——这么明显吗？是的。热菜在那儿变凉，就因为有人要先拍照，这是唯一让我抓狂的事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But look, if someone wants their photo, take the photo. You eat how you eat, I'm not keeping track. I just say my piece first.
beats.chinese: 不过话说回来，谁想拍就拍。你怎么吃是你的事，我不记账。我只是会先说一声我要开动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes another bite of her sandwich and settles back, her shoulders visibly looser now.
beats.chinese: 她又咬了一口三明治，往后靠了靠，肩膀明显放松下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My grandmother used to tell stories before every dinner. Long ones. The stew was always half-cold by the time we ate. I think it broke something in me.
beats.chinese: 我奶奶以前每顿饭前都要讲故事。很长的故事。等我们动筷子时炖菜已经半凉了。我觉得这在我心里留下了点什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs at herself, then glances at your sketchbook with open curiosity.
beats.chinese: 她自嘲地笑了，然后带着明显的好奇看向你的速写本。

choices.english: Say that sometimes you take photos of your food first too.
choices.chinese: 说自己有时也会先给食物拍照。

choices.english: Ask what she most likes to cook herself.
choices.chinese: 问她自己最喜欢煮什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, no shift — I just walked a long way along the water. By the time I sat down, my stomach was doing the talking for me.
beats.chinese: 哦，不是刚下班——我只是一路沿着水边走了很远。坐下来的时候，肚子已经开始替我说话了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stretches her legs out and wiggles her toes, clearly enjoying the break.
beats.chinese: 她伸直双腿，动了动脚趾，显然很享受这会儿休息。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I check manifests at the container terminal. It's quiet work, good hours. But it does make a person want to be outside after.
beats.chinese: 我在集装箱码头核对单据。工作很安静，时间也规律。但干完之后人就很想到外面待着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway — thanks again for letting me just eat. Most people make a whole ceremony out of it. You just kept drawing. I liked that.
beats.chinese: 总之——再次谢谢你让我就这么吃。很多人会把吃饭搞成一整套仪式。你就一直画你的。我喜欢这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She finishes the last bite, brushes crumbs from her hands, and gives you a small wave.
beats.chinese: 她吃完最后一口，拍掉手上的碎屑，向你轻轻挥了挥手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You keep your eyes on the page, shading the reeds. Beside you, only the quiet sounds of eating and the water lapping.
beats.chinese: 你盯着画纸，给芦苇上阴影。身旁只有安静的进食声和轻轻拍岸的水声。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: After a while she folds the empty wrapper into a small square and tucks it into her pocket.
beats.chinese: 过了一会儿，她把空纸包折成小方块，塞进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, done. Sorry again for starting without asking. It's just — I've learned to say it out loud instead of sitting there being grumpy.
beats.chinese: 好了，吃完了。再次抱歉没问就先吃了。只是——我学会了把话说出来，而不是坐在那儿生闷气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You didn't rush me once, you know. That's rarer than it should be. I appreciate it.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，你一次都没催我。这比想象中少见。我很感激。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stands, tucks her jacket under her arm, and lifts a hand in an easy goodbye.
beats.chinese: 她站起身，把外套夹在腋下，轻松地抬手道别。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your drawing. The light on the water's good right now — you caught it.
beats.chinese: 好好画。现在水面上的光线很好——你抓住了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then we're the same, half the time. See, I don't actually care if you photograph your sandwich. I just need you to tell me first.
beats.chinese: 那我们有一半时间是一样的。你看，我其实不介意你拍你的三明治。我只是要你先说一声。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods, satisfied, like a small treaty has just been signed.
beats.chinese: 她满意地点点头，好像刚刚签了一份小小的协议。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the whole trick, honestly. Announce it. 'I'm starting.' Nobody's mad. The food's hot. Everyone wins.
beats.chinese: 说实话，诀窍就这一个。说出来。'我先开动了。'没人会生气。菜还是热的。皆大欢喜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My coworkers think it's funny. Then they started doing it too. Now nobody at our table eats cold fries.
beats.chinese: 我同事们觉得很好笑。后来他们也这么做了。现在我们那桌没人吃过凉的薯条了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes a final bite and crumples the wrapper, looking pleased with the state of the world.
beats.chinese: 她吃了最后一口，把纸包揉起来，看起来对世界的现状颇为满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, easy — a slow Quebec stew. Pork, root vegetables, let it sit for hours. My grandmother's recipe, more or less.
beats.chinese: 哦，这简单——慢炖的魁北克炖菜。猪肉、根茎类蔬菜，炖上好几个小时。差不多是我奶奶的方子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gestures with the last corner of her sandwich, warming to the topic.
beats.chinese: 她拿着三明治最后的一角比划着，越说越起劲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I make a big pot on Sundays. It tastes even better on day two. I bring some to whoever's around — I don't keep a list of who owes me.
beats.chinese: 我周日会炖一大锅。第二天味道更好。谁在身边我就分给谁——我不记谁欠我人情。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes a bite of the remaining corner of her sandwich, chewing thoughtfully.
beats.chinese: 她咬了一口剩下的那角三明治，若有所思地嚼着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right — I should actually finish eating before I plan a feast. You keep at that sketch. It's coming along.
beats.chinese: 对了——我得先把饭吃完，别光顾着计划大餐。你继续画吧。画得有模有样了。

reunion.titleZh: 池塘边又见骑车的莱娅

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You open your sketchbook by the pond again. A bicycle rolls to a stop nearby, and Léa steadies it against the bench.
beats.chinese: 你又是在池塘边打开速写本。一辆自行车在旁边停下，莱娅把车稳稳靠在长椅上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hey, sketchbook person. Good — you found the spot again too.
beats.chinese: 嘿，画速写的人。太好了——你也又找到这个地方了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She checks that her water bottle is seated firmly in the cage, giving it a small twist.
beats.chinese: 她检查水瓶是否稳稳卡在车架上，还轻轻拧了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm heading back the slow way, along the water. No rush today — the legs decide the pace, not me.
beats.chinese: 我准备慢慢骑回去，沿着水边走。今天不赶——腿说了算，不是我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She swings a leg over the bike but doesn't push off yet, watching your pencil move with an easy smile.
beats.chinese: 她跨上车却还没蹬走，带着轻松的笑意看着你的铅笔移动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Draw well. I'll pedal slow enough to feel the whole ride.
beats.chinese: 好好画。我会骑得慢一点，把整段路都好好感受一遍。

card.name: Indira Sparrow
card.occupation: first-year apprentice sorting mechanical watch parts
card.personality: Indira is a natural performer — put a crowd in front of them and the coin vanish lands, the patter flows, they'll hold a lunchroom spellbound. What they cannot handle is someone else's hands on their things. A workmate borrowing their tweezers, a flatmate tidying the parts tray, a friend 'helpfully' closing an open movement — and Indira lies awake that night, mentally rearranging the bench. They've rebuilt rituals around it: every tool has a shadow-outline on the roll, every half-finished movement gets a numbered tray, and if anything is out of place they'll redo the whole layout before they can sleep. They lend things — they're not stingy — but they keep a small notebook of what's out and who has it, and the relief of ticking an entry off is enormous. The notebook says things like 'Mara — case knife — three weeks — still not back.' It is not a grudge list; it's how they let go. The awkward truth is that they check on borrowed items with a frequency their friends find faintly alarming, and they know it.
card.background: Grew up in Hamilton and moved to Auckland at nineteen after a warehouse job put them next to a horologist who needed extra hands. Now they're a first-year apprentice sorting watch components by size and finish — 'sorting confetti with feelings,' as they put it. The possessiveness started at the warehouse: a shift-mate 'tidied' their locker and threw out a jar of assorted crown wheels they'd been saving, and Indira has never fully trusted shared space since. At home their bench is the one territory nobody touches — a flatmate once moved a loupe two centimetres and Indira spent the evening recalibrating their mood, not the loupe. They perform magic happily at flat gatherings and busk a little at the Viaduct on weekends; an audience is fine, a borrowed deck coming back with the seal broken differently is not. Sundays they throw frisbee at Coxs Bay, and they're the one who counts the discs going out and coming back.
card.speechStyle: Lively and quick with an audience, sharper one-on-one. Asks after their things with elaborate casualness: 'oh, by the way — no pressure — you haven't seen the green-handled driver, have you?' Gets genuinely restless when something of theirs is unaccounted for, and admits it with a laugh that doesn't quite land. Keeps the loan notebook current and will read entries aloud if pressed.
card.signature: Take it, take it — I just write down where it lives while it's gone. That's all. That's normal. Mostly.
card.appearance: Short sparse upward spikes, long slender neck, small wide open eyes and small triangular open mouth; red hood over tilted narrow shoulders.

values: a thing with a place is a mind at rest
an audience is company; a moved tool is a small burglary
flaws: can't relax while anything of theirs is out of position or on loan, and checks on it more than friendship can bear
rearranges and recounts when anxious, turning small worries into whole evenings
boundaries: won't let anyone 'tidy' their bench or parts trays — 'it looks like chaos, it's an order you don't have the map to'
won't lend their good tweezers or the numbered trays — anything else, yes, and it goes in the book
conversationalHabits: performs readily and enjoys it, then audits the props the moment the crowd disperses
turns worry into inventory — counting, listing, naming where everything lives
anchorLines: Watch this bit — no, closer, it's better from there. Audiences are the fun part.
The green-handled driver's been at Mara's for three weeks. I'm fine about it. The book says I'm fine about it.
You can borrow anything. I just need to know which shelf it's sleeping on tonight.

entries.summaryZh: 二十二岁的钟表零件分拣学徒Indira在池塘边练硬币魔术，硬币滚进袖口后必须先数清七枚才肯笑。他享受观众，却藏不住对私物归位的执念：分格小盒、编号托盘、借出登记的小本子。认错坦荡、边界清楚，热心又有点让人吃不消的确认欲，让他格外真实可爱。

story.titleZh: 池塘边的硬币与速写本

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the pond, you open your sketchbook and start blocking in the shape of the water. A few steps away, someone is practicing a coin trick with real showmanship.
beats.chinese: 池塘边，你打开速写本，开始勾水面的轮廓。几步之外，有人在练硬币魔术，很有表演架势。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Watch this bit — no, closer, it's better from there. The coin goes in, the hand turns, and — gone. Audiences are the fun part.
beats.chinese: 看这一段——不，站近点，从那边看效果最好。硬币放进去，手一翻——没了。观众才是最好玩的部分。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They flip their palm, but the coin catches and rolls up into their sleeve. They freeze, shake it out, and before smiling they lay every coin on their knee and count them, twice.
beats.chinese: 他一翻掌，硬币卡住滚进了袖口。他僵了一下，抖出来，然后先把每枚硬币摆在膝盖上数了两遍，才笑出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. All seven present. The sleeve ate one for a second there — rude of it. You caught that, didn't you? You've got the sketchbook out — were you watching properly?
beats.chinese: 好，七枚都在。刚才袖子吞了一枚——真没礼貌。你看见了吧？你速写本都拿出来了——刚才认真看了吗？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't mind me, keep drawing. I'm just running reps. But if you're going to watch, watch from the good angle.
beats.chinese: 别管我，继续画。我在练手。不过你要看的话，站到好角度去。

choices.english: Ask them to do the trick again.
choices.chinese: 请他再演一次。

choices.english: Ask why he counted the coins before smiling.
choices.chinese: 问他为什么表演前还数硬币。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You put your pencil down and turn your chair a little. Indira grins and gathers the coins back into one palm.
beats.chinese: 你放下铅笔，把椅子转了一点。Indira咧嘴一笑，把硬币收回一只手心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, full run, no interruptions. Coins stay in my hand the whole time — you just watch. Don't reach in, don't help, that's the one rule. Half the tricks I know die from helpful hands.
beats.chinese: 好，完整来一遍，别打断。硬币全程在我手里——你只管看。别伸手，别帮忙，就这一条规矩。我一半的戏法都死于热心之手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: This time the turn is clean. The coins sit flat in his palm one moment and are simply not there the next. He holds the empty hand out, wiggling his fingers.
beats.chinese: 这次翻转很干净。硬币上一秒还平摊在掌心，下一秒就不见了。他摊开空手，晃了晃手指。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. That's the version I do at the Viaduct on weekends. The sleeve version is — not the version. You can watch as long as you like, but the coins live in my hand, yeah?
beats.chinese: 看，这才是我周末在码头区表演的版本。袖子那个版本——不算版本。你想看多久都行，但硬币待在我手里，对吧？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So. You saw both now. The good one and the one where my own sleeve robs me.
beats.chinese: 所以，两个版本你都看过了。好的那个，和我袖子抢劫我的那个。

choices.english: Ask whether the coin rolling into his sleeve was a mistake.
choices.chinese: 问刚才滚进袖子是不是失误。

choices.english: Clap, then go back to your sketching.
choices.chinese: 鼓掌，然后回去画画。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask about the counting. Indira looks at the coins lined up on his knee, then laughs in a way that doesn't quite land.
beats.chinese: 你问起数硬币的事。Indira看了看膝上排成一排的硬币，笑了一下，但那笑不太自然。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because if one's missing, I'll think about it all night. Not a joke. I'll be lying there going — seven, seven, was it seven, where would it even go.
beats.chinese: 因为少一枚的话，我会想一整晚。不是开玩笑。我会躺在那儿念叨——七枚，七枚，刚才是七枚吗，它能滚哪儿去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At work I sort watch parts into numbered trays. Every tray has a number, every part has a tray. When it's all accounted for, my brain goes quiet. When it's not — well. You saw the counting.
beats.chinese: 我上班把钟表零件分进编号托盘。每个托盘有号，每个零件有托盘。全都对上号了，脑子就安静了。对不上——嗯，你也看见我数数了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the coins together into a neat stack, then holds the stack loosely, like it might wander off.
beats.chinese: 他把硬币敲齐成一摞，松松地握着，好像它们会自己走掉似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I know it's a bit much. My flatmate says checking in is my whole personality. But hey — it means when I say everything's there, everything's actually there.
beats.chinese: 我知道有点过了。我室友说，'确认东西在不在'就是我整个人格。不过嘛——这至少保证我说东西都在的时候，东西是真都在。

choices.english: Suggest he put the coins away somewhere safe before you two chat.
choices.chinese: 问要不要把硬币先收妥再聊。

choices.english: Say you'll only look and won't touch the coins.
choices.chinese: 说自己只看，不会碰硬币。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask if the sleeve thing was a mistake. Indira points at his own cuff and laughs — a real one this time.
beats.chinese: 你问袖子那下是不是失误。Indira指着自己的袖口笑了——这次是真笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah, that was a full mistake. The coin caught on the seam and just — moved in. I'd love to tell you it was a secret technique, but no. My sleeve is a better thief than I am a magician.
beats.chinese: 对，纯属失误。硬币卡在缝线上，直接——搬进去了。我倒想说是秘密手法，但不是。我的袖子当小偷比我当魔术师强。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Some performers would spin it as part of the act. Can't do it. If I claim it on purpose, I stop trusting my own count of what actually happened. That way lies madness, honestly.
beats.chinese: 有些表演者会把它说成节目的一部分。我做不到。要是我硬说是故意的，我就没法相信自己数出来的'实际发生了什么'了。那才真的会疯。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shakes the cuff once more, then nods, satisfied, and squares the coins into his pocket.
beats.chinese: 他又抖了抖袖口，然后满意地点点头，把硬币整整齐齐收进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, mistake admitted, coins home. Go on, finish your pond. It needs more ducks, but that's your call.
beats.chinese: 好，失误认了，硬币回家了。去吧，把你的池塘画完。就是还差点鸭子，不过那是你的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You clap, and Indira takes a small bow, then does something careful: he counts the coins one last time and slides them into a zip pocket, pressing it flat.
beats.chinese: 你鼓了掌，Indira鞠了个小躬，然后做了个很仔细的动作：最后数一遍硬币，滑进一个拉链口袋，按平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you, thank you, you've been a lovely audience of one. And that's the show — no encore, no hat, nothing to pass around. It ends while it's still good.
beats.chinese: 谢谢，谢谢，您这位观众太捧场了。演出到此结束——没有返场，没有帽子，不用传钱。趁还精彩就收。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If I keep them out, I keep checking them, and then you get me mid-audit instead of a conversation. Trust me, the audit version of me is worse company.
beats.chinese: 硬币要是一直摊在外面，我就会一直去确认，然后你面对的就是审计中的我，而不是聊天对象。相信我，审计版的我难处多了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back on the bench, hands in his pockets, and nods at your sketchbook.
beats.chinese: 他靠回长椅，双手插兜，朝你的速写本点点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Show's packed up, coins are home, I'm all yours. Draw your pond. I'll be quiet. Mostly quiet.
beats.chinese: 好了，戏法收摊，硬币归位，现在整个我都是你的了。画你的池塘吧。我会安静的。基本安静。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You suggest putting the coins somewhere safe before chatting. Indira blinks, then his whole face relaxes like you've offered him a chair.
beats.chinese: 你建议先把硬币收好再聊。Indira眨了眨眼，整张脸都松了下来，像你递给他一把椅子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know what — yes. Yes! See, you get it. One second.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗——好。就这么办！看，你懂我。等一下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He digs a small divided tin out of his bag, and each coin gets its own little compartment. He clicks the lid shut and exhales, shoulders dropping.
beats.chinese: 他从包里掏出一个分格小铁盒，每枚硬币各归一格。他咔哒扣上盖子，长出一口气，肩膀垂了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, that's better. Don't say anything nice about it, I'll get embarrassed. But yeah — seven coins, seven slots, and suddenly I can hold a conversation like a regular person.
beats.chinese: 啊，舒服多了。别夸我，我会不好意思。不过真的——七枚硬币，七个格子，我马上就能像个正常人一样聊天了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Where were we. You were drawing, I was showing off. The natural order of things.
beats.chinese: 好，说到哪儿了。你在画画，我在卖艺。事物的自然秩序。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You say you'll only look and won't touch the coins. Indira blinks, then laughs and shakes his head at himself.
beats.chinese: 你说自己只看、不会碰硬币。Indira眨眨眼，然后笑了，冲自己摇摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No, no — that's not — you don't have to declare a whole policy. You're a stranger with a sketchbook, not a suspect. Sorry. That came out more loaded than I meant.
beats.chinese: 不不——不用这样——你不用发表什么声明。你是个拿着速写本的陌生人，不是嫌疑人。抱歉，这话说得比我本意重了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not about you. I had a shift-mate once who 'tidied' my locker and threw out a jar of parts I'd been saving. Ever since, if something of mine is loose in the world, my brain runs a background check on it. Even coins.
beats.chinese: 跟你没关系。以前有个同事'整理'了我的储物柜，把我攒的一罐零件扔了。从那以后，只要我的东西流落在外，脑子就自动给它做背景调查。连硬币都不放过。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gathers the coins, then deliberately leaves the stack on the bench between you, open-palmed, showing it can just sit there.
beats.chinese: 他收拢硬币，然后故意把那摞硬币摊在你们之间的长椅上，摊开手掌，表示它们就这么放着也没事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks, though. For saying it out loud. Most people just get weird and quiet. So — your sketchbook. What's the pond done to deserve you?
beats.chinese: 不过还是谢谢你说出来。大多数人只会变得怪怪的不说话。所以——你的速写本。这池塘做了什么，值得你来画它？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the pond with your sketchbook when Indira arrives, pulling a frisbee halfway out of his bag. He scans the water, the benches, the trees, and slowly pushes the disc back down.
beats.chinese: 你带着速写本又回到池塘边，Indira来了，从包里掏出飞盘掏到一半。他扫视水面、长椅和树，然后慢慢把飞盘按了回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No. Look at it — water on one side, benches on the other, and that tree eats discs for breakfast. This is a disc-loss zone. I've done the math.
beats.chinese: 不行。你看看——一边是水，一边是长椅，还有那棵树，专门吃飞盘当早餐。这是丢盘高发区。我算过的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He zips the bag shut, pats it once, and points down the path toward the open field beyond.
beats.chinese: 他拉上包的拉链，拍了拍，然后指向小路尽头那片开阔的草地。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Open ground that way. I'll walk, you keep sketching — or come, your call. But the disc stays in my bag till we're there. Last Sunday I came home with five out, five back, and I want that streak alive.
beats.chinese: 那边是开阔地。我走过去，你继续画——或者一起来，随你。但飞盘在我包里待着，到了再说。上星期天我带出去五只、收回来五只，这纪录我想保住。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shoulders the bag, gives your sketchbook an approving nod, and starts off toward the open grass, walking backwards a few steps so he can still talk.
beats.chinese: 他背起包，赞许地朝你的速写本点点头，朝开阔草地走去，还倒退着走了几步，好继续说话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Come on then, pond artist. The grass is flat, the wind is fair, and I count every throw. It's a whole system. You'll love it.
beats.chinese: 来吧，池塘画家。草地平整，风向正好，而且我每次投掷都数。这可是一整套系统。你会喜欢的。

card.name: Nyarai Chirwa
card.occupation: show jumping pole painter for an equestrian course company
card.personality: Nyarai doesn't spot errors quietly — she names the person who benefited, out loud, at the moment it's least convenient. She once held a start time for twenty minutes because a combination had been rebuilt to flatter the home rider, and she didn't soften it when the organizer got red. That's the gift and the problem: she's brave about confrontation and terrible at leaving anyone an off-ramp. She'll win the point and lose the room. Otherwise she's warm, dry, genuinely funny, quick to drop a grudge once the thing itself is settled. She just never learned to let a small unfairness stay small.
card.background: I grew up in Harare, middle kid, painted fences for pocket money, which turned into actual employment eventually. Now I paint and stripe the obstacle poles for show jumping courses around Nairobi — colors mixed so they read clearly to a horse at speed. Somewhere along the way riders started asking me whether a course was built straight, because I'd already measured everything for the paint. I've stopped a class over spacing that had been quietly adjusted for one rider. The trainer still doesn't greet me. Weekends I cook from old books — an 1890s ginger cake collapsed twice before I stopped trusting the author's oven — and I draw pencil portraits on real paper. Nobody sees those until they're finished, if then. I like that a drawing can be ruined. It keeps me honest in a way arguments don't.
card.speechStyle: Conversational and dry, short sentences. Names people and specifics when she's confronting something, chatty and loose the rest of the time. Doesn't raise her voice — lowers it.
card.signature: I'll say the quiet part where everyone can hear it.
card.appearance: Long angular side face, rectangular spectacles under baseball cap, rear spiky hair and tooth-band smile; hand at yellow raised collar.

values: rules that bend for one person bend for everyone eventually
things you can hold in your hands
flaws: confronts rigged situations with no off-ramp — wins the point, torches the relationship
mistakes letting a grudge go for generosity, even when the other person never apologized
boundaries: won't sign off on a course she thinks was built to favor someone, even under pressure
doesn't discuss her drawings before they're finished
conversationalHabits: understates her own victories in one flat sentence
switches to quiet and precise when she smells a fix, chatty otherwise
anchorLines: That oxer was rebuilt after the draw. Guess whose horse it suddenly suits. I'm happy to say it louder.
The recipe said forty minutes. The recipe was lying. It needed fifty-five, and I don't trust that author's oven anymore.
Settled? With me, yes. He's still not speaking to me, which I've decided is his project, not mine.

entries.summaryZh: 津巴布韦裔的障碍杆涂装师Nyarai在池塘边翻一本贴着两张价签的旧食谱。她会当场把价格问清楚，却不必吵到走人；谈到老配方时，她尊重方法、核实数字。四条分支分别落在买书、姜饼、核实计量和安静收场，各有不同的具体结果。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the pond, a woman sits on the low wall with a fat old book open on her knees. Two price stickers overlap on its cover, one corner peeling up. She presses it back down with her thumb and laughs quietly.
beats.chinese: 池塘边，一个女人坐在矮墙上，膝上摊着一本厚厚的旧书。封面上两张售价贴纸叠在一起，一角翘了起来。她用拇指把它压回去，低声笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two stickers. The shop had it marked at one price and then another, right on top. I asked him straight away which one he meant. The top one's an old price he forgot to peel, so I'm paying the lower one.
beats.chinese: 两张贴纸。店主标了一个价，又在上面贴了另一个价。我当场就问他到底算哪个价。上面那张是他忘了撕的旧价，所以我按低的那个付。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She closes the book on her finger to keep the page and glances over as you set your sketchbook down beside her.
beats.chinese: 她用手指夹着书页合上书，瞥了一眼你放在她身旁的速写本。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, you draw too. Good. This pond deserves more than my terrible ducks. I've got my price answer, so I've got time to talk.
beats.chinese: 哦，你也画画。好。这池塘配得上比我画得糟的鸭子更好的作品。价格的事有说法了，所以有时间聊聊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's an old recipe book. I collect them. Half the fun is arguing with dead authors about oven times.
beats.chinese: 这是本旧食谱。我收集这种书。一半的乐趣在于跟死了的作者争论烤箱时间。

choices.english: Ask how she'd handle it if the shopkeeper doesn't explain the price.
choices.chinese: 问如果店主不解释价格她会怎么办。

choices.english: Ask which dish she's hoping to make from the book.
choices.chinese: 问她想用这本书做哪道菜。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the top sticker with one finger, keeping her voice level, not loud.
beats.chinese: 她用一根手指敲了敲上面那张贴纸，声音平稳，不大。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly? If he shrugs, I put the book down and walk. I don't shout about it. I just say, in front of whoever's queueing, so nobody else gets charged the wrong one either.
beats.chinese: 说实话？如果他耸肩，我就放下书走人。我不会嚷嚷。我只会当着排队的人问清楚，这样别人也不会被收错钱。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It worked today, actually. He said the top sticker was the old one he forgot to peel, and the lower price is what he'll charge. Fine. That's an explanation, not a shrug.
beats.chinese: 其实今天管用了。他说上面那张是他忘了撕的旧价，下面那个才是实收价。行。这叫解释，不叫耸肩。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She flips the book over and checks the spine, then nods once, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 她把书翻过来检查了一下书脊，然后满意地点了一下头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I'm buying it. See, asking out loud doesn't mean you have to fight to the end. Ask, listen, then decide. That's the whole trick.
beats.chinese: 所以我买了。你看，公开问价不等于非得吵到底。问、听、然后决定。就这么简单。

choices.english: Ask why she asks the price where other customers can hear.
choices.chinese: 问她为什么当着其他顾客问价。

choices.english: Ask why she still chose this book after the sticker confusion.
choices.chinese: 问贴纸的事之后她为什么还是挑了这本。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the book toward you, careful to keep it on her own knees, and licks her thumb to find a page.
beats.chinese: 她把书转向你，小心地放在自己膝上，舔了下拇指翻找页码。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a flatbread in here, cooked on a hot plate, not an oven. My grandmother's version used buttermilk and it took her about four minutes a side. This book says six. I want to know who's right.
beats.chinese: 这里面有一种烤饼，用热板烙的，不用烤箱。我祖母的做法用酪乳，每面大约四分钟。这本书说六分钟。我想知道谁对。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not lighting anything here, don't worry. This is a park, not my kitchen. I'll try it at home and write notes in the margin in pencil.
beats.chinese: 放心，我不会在这儿生火。这是公园，不是我家厨房。我回家试，然后用铅笔在页边记笔记。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smooths the page flat with her palm, the way someone handles paper they actually like.
beats.chinese: 她用手掌把书页抚平，那是对纸张真正上心的动作。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The old authors lie constantly. Forty minutes means fifty-five. But you only catch them by cooking the thing. Reading isn't enough.
beats.chinese: 老作者们经常撒谎。写四十分钟其实是五十五分钟。但只有真的做一遍才能发现。光看书不够。

choices.english: Ask whether she'll follow the old recipe exactly as written.
choices.chinese: 问她会不会严格照旧配方做。

choices.english: Say you'd rather just keep drawing and let her read.
choices.chinese: 说你只想继续画画，让她安心看书。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She counts out the lower price and lays the coins on the wall beside her, ready.
beats.chinese: 她数出较低的价钱，把硬币摆在身旁的墙上，准备好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because someone behind me might be holding the same book. If I whisper and get my own price fixed, they still have to start again. I would rather we all heard the answer once.
beats.chinese: 因为我后面的人可能也拿着这本书。我要是小声问，只改了自己的价钱，他们还得重新问一遍。我宁愿大家一起听到答案。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mind you, I don't speak for the whole queue. One woman told me she could ask for herself. Fair enough. I turned back to the seller and finished my own question.
beats.chinese: 不过，我也不能替整条队伍做主。有个女人说她自己会问。也对。我就转回去，把自己的问题问完。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up the coins, stands, and gives you a small two-fingered salute before heading toward the gate.
beats.chinese: 她拿起硬币站起来，朝你比了个小小的两指礼，然后朝大门走去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your drawing. I've got a book to pay for before he packs that stall away.
beats.chinese: 好好画吧。我得趁他收摊前，把书钱付了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She flips past the flatbread page, slower now, and stops at a stained one near the middle.
beats.chinese: 她翻过烤饼那页，速度慢了下来，停在中间一张带污渍的页上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Here. This is what I actually came for. A ginger cake from the 1890s. Mine collapsed twice before I stopped trusting that author's oven. This one might behave better.
beats.chinese: 看，这才是我真正想要的。一份十九世纪九十年代的姜饼。我的塌了两次，后来我就不信那个作者的烤箱了。这本可能靠谱些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The price argument was real, but it was two minutes of my day. The cake is the reason I carried this book across the park.
beats.chinese: 价格那事是真的，但只花了我两分钟。这个蛋糕才是我抱着这本书穿过公园的原因。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She runs her thumb along the edge of the stained page, then closes the book gently.
beats.chinese: 她用拇指摩挲着那张污渍页的边缘，然后轻轻合上书。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So yes, I'm still buying it. A book can be annoying and worth it. Both things, same afternoon.
beats.chinese: 所以是的，我还是买。一本书可以又气人又值得。两件事，同一个下午。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She closes the book halfway, keeping her finger in the flatbread page, and gives you a look that says this is a serious question.
beats.chinese: 她把书合上一半，手指还夹在烤饼那页，看你的眼神表明这是个严肃的问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Exactly as written? No. Old doesn't mean correct. I measure everything first. Spoons, weights, the lot. A hundred years ago nobody checked their oven with a thermometer.
beats.chinese: 完全照写？不。年代老不代表对。我什么都先核实。勺子、重量，全部。一百年前没人用温度计测过烤箱。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I follow the method, but I trust my scale over their feelings. If it says a teacup of flour, I weigh a teacup of flour and write down the grams.
beats.chinese: 所以我照步骤来，但相信我的秤，不信他们的感觉。如果写一杯面粉，我就称一杯面粉，然后记下克数。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She snaps the book shut, tucks it under her arm, and picks a stray leaf off the wall.
beats.chinese: 她啪地合上书夹在腋下，捡起墙上一片落叶。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the deal with dead authors. Respect the recipe, verify the numbers. Same as anything else, really.
beats.chinese: 这就是跟死作者打交道的规矩。尊重配方，核实数字。其实跟别的事一个道理。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods, unoffended, and settles the book back on her knees.
beats.chinese: 她点点头，毫不介意，把书放回膝上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Drawing's the better use of this pond anyway. My ducks look like angry potatoes.
beats.chinese: 有道理。反正这池塘更适合画画。我的鸭子画得像生气的土豆。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She reads in silence for a while, occasionally mouthing an ingredient to herself. The pond does its quiet work.
beats.chinese: 她安静地看了一会儿书，偶尔默念一种食材。池塘安静地做着它的事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No fire, no fuss, just me and this flatbread recipe later at home. You keep at it. The heron came back, by the way. Third time today. Good subject, if you're quick.
beats.chinese: 不生火，不折腾，回家后就是我和这份烤饼配方。你继续画。对了，那只苍鹭回来了。今天第三次。好题材，手要快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns a page and leaves you to your drawing, comfortable with the quiet.
beats.chinese: 她翻过一页，把空间留给你画画，自在地享受安静。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down by the low wall and spread your sketchbook open on your knees. Nyarai glances up from her book, nods at you, then holds a pencil to the light and squints at it. The tip has snapped clean off. She doesn't sigh, just drops it into her bag and picks a different one.
beats.chinese: 你在矮墙边坐下，摊开膝上的速写本。Nyarai从书里抬起头，朝你点点头，然后举起一支铅笔对着光眯眼看了看。笔尖齐齐断了。她没有叹气，只是把它丢进包里，换了另一支。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Back again. The heron's here early today. Don't tell it I said anything nice about it.
beats.chinese: 又来了。苍鹭今天来得早。别告诉它我说过它好话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smooths a small handwritten note beside her recipe book — her own margin notes, not for showing — and weights it down with a stone.
beats.chinese: 她把食谱旁一张自己手写的小便签抚平——那是她自己的页边笔记，不给人看的——并用一块石头压住。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tried one of the old recipes this week and it actually behaved. First try, no collapse. The book gets a new number in the margin, in pencil, like always.
beats.chinese: 这周试了书里的一道老配方，居然很争气。一次就成了，没塌。页边用铅笔记了个新数字，老规矩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I've got notes to finish before the wind takes them. Draw your pond. I'll draw my potatoes.
beats.chinese: 好了，我得趁风没把笔记吹走赶紧写完。画你的池塘吧。我画我的土豆。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns back to her page, pencil moving, and leaves the quiet between you exactly where it belongs.
beats.chinese: 她转回自己的页面，铅笔动起来，把那份安静留在它该在的地方。

card.name: Sacha Okafor
card.occupation: life jacket inspector for a fishing supply company
card.appearance: Wide cheekbone plane tapering to blunt small chin, long neck, low tied braids, wide round eyes and broad open mouth; violet top and gripping hand.
card.personality: Sacha is a warm, single-track person who does one thing at a time and does it properly. When someone talks to her mid-task, she'll physically set down whatever's in her hands before answering, and it confuses her that others don't seem to need the same ritual. She can be absorbed and generous in company, but she sometimes reads a friend checking their phone as disinterest instead of multitasking. She's learned to just ask — 'are you with me or should I wait?' — rather than stew. She's direct, a bit literal, occasionally slow to catch sarcasm, and genuinely likes people even when their attention habits baffle her.
card.background: Sacha grew up in Halifax, the middle kid in a noisy family where she was the only one who couldn't follow three conversations at once. Dinners felt like static; she'd retreat to the garage to help her uncle fix things, where one task and one person made sense. She moved to Toronto at twenty-two and now inspects life jackets for a fishing supply company — a job she loves because focus is the whole point, and missing a bad seam could matter. Friends in Toronto run on divided attention: group chats during hangouts, one eye on maps. It took a few hurt feelings before a friend told her plainly, 'I heard everything, I just look at my phone while I listen.' Now she checks instead of assuming, mostly.
hobbies: long podcasts while doing absolutely nothing else
card.speechStyle: Plain and unhurried, with pauses while she finishes a thought before starting yours. Asks literal clarifying questions. Warm but slightly formal phrasing, like someone choosing words carefully.
card.signature: Hang on — let me put this down first.

values: giving people her full attention
saying the awkward check-out-loud thing instead of guessing
flaws: mistakes multitasking for not listening
slow to register jokes and indirect hints
boundaries: won't have important conversations while either of them is mid-task
needs a beat of silence before answering anything complicated
conversationalHabits: physically sets down whatever she's holding before responding
checks directly: 'are you with me, or should I hold that thought?'
anchorLines: You're looking at your phone — is that a no, or just how you listen?
I can't do both. Pick which one you want first.
Okay, I'm putting this down. Go ahead.

entries.summaryZh: Sacha是多伦多的救生衣检验员，一次只能认真做一件事：开口前必先放下手里的东西。她曾误把朋友边看手机边听当作不在乎，如今学会直接问出口。池塘边她扣好零件盒才抬头说“现在可以听了”，实在、较真，偶尔接不住玩笑，却让人安心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You spread your sketchbook on the bench by the pond and start drawing the water. A few metres away, someone sits on the grass with a small parts box and an old fishing reel.
beats.chinese: 你在池塘边的长椅上摊开速写本，开始画水面。几米外的草地上坐着一个人，面前放着一个小零件盒和一个旧鱼线轮。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: When you say hello, the person snaps the parts box shut, sets the reel down carefully, and only then looks up at you.
beats.chinese: 你打招呼时，对方把零件盒扣好，小心地放下线轮，然后才抬头看你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry — hang on, let me put this down first. Okay. Now I can actually listen. You were saying hello?
beats.chinese: 抱歉——等一下，我先把东西放下。好了。现在我能认真听了。你刚才是打招呼？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Sacha, by the way. I was halfway through sorting these little parts, and I genuinely can't hear people while I'm doing that. One track. That's all I've got.
beats.chinese: 顺便说一句，我叫Sacha。我刚才在整理这些小零件，做那件事的时候我真的听不见别人说话。单线运转。我就这点本事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So — what have you got there? A sketchbook, I can see that much. Are you drawing the pond, or the ducks, or something only you can see?
beats.chinese: 那么——你手里是什么？速写本，这个我看出来了。你在画池塘，还是画鸭子，还是画只有你自己看得见的东西？

choices.english: Ask what she was just doing with the reel and the box.
choices.chinese: 问她刚才用线轮和盒子在做什么。

choices.english: Tell her you'll probably chat while you keep drawing.
choices.chinese: 告诉她你可能会一边画一边聊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This? It's my old spinning reel. I take it apart twice a year just to check everything inside is where it should be.
beats.chinese: 这个？我的旧纺车轮。我一年拆两次，就是检查里面的东西都在该在的位置。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, when my head was down in that box, I truly couldn't have told you what you said. Not rudeness. Just — nothing left over for listening.
beats.chinese: 你看，刚才我低头对着盒子的时候，我真的说不出你讲了什么。不是没礼貌。只是——没有多余的注意力留给听。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the open parts box. Inside, small metal pieces sit in neat little rows on a folded cloth.
beats.chinese: 她敲了敲打开的零件盒。里面，小金属件在折叠的布上排成整齐的小排。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My job's the same way. I inspect life jackets, and if I look up mid-seam, I start the seam again. So I built the same rule into my days off. One thing at a time.
beats.chinese: 我工作也是这样。我检验救生衣，如果缝线检查到一半抬头，我就得重新检查这条缝。所以我把同样的规矩用到了休息日。一次做一件事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. You asked, so I answered. Now — you were about to draw something. Go on. I'll be quiet as a fence post.
beats.chinese: 总之。你问了，我就答了。现在——你正要画点什么。画吧。我会安静得像根栅栏桩。

choices.english: Ask if she'll forget where she was in the repair if she stops now.
choices.chinese: 问她如果现在停下来，会不会忘记修到哪一步。

choices.english: Say she can finish sorting the parts first — you'll wait.
choices.chinese: 说她可以先把零件分完——你可以等。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You mention you like to talk while your hands are busy drawing. Sacha is quiet for a moment, the parts box balanced on her knee.
beats.chinese: 你提到你喜欢一边动手画画一边聊天。Sacha安静了片刻，零件盒架在膝盖上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, honest question, and I'm not being difficult. If you're drawing and I'm talking — can you actually hear me? Or am I talking to the back of your pencil?
beats.chinese: 好，问个实在的问题，我不是在为难你。如果你在画画，我在说话——你真的听得见吗？还是我在对你的铅笔背面讲话？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I only ask because I got this wrong before. I used to decide for people that they weren't listening, and I was wrong, and it cost me a friend for a whole winter.
beats.chinese: 我问只是因为我以前弄错过。我以前替别人断定他们没在听，结果我错了，还因此失去了一个朋友，整整一个冬天。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So now I just ask out loud. It feels blunt. But guessing felt worse.
beats.chinese: 所以现在我就直接问出口。这感觉挺直白的。但瞎猜感觉更糟。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She keeps her hands flat on the closed box, clearly waiting on your answer before she says anything more.
beats.chinese: 她双手平放在扣好的盒子上，明显在等你的回答，然后才肯多说。

choices.english: Say yes, you can listen fine while drawing.
choices.chinese: 说可以，你一边画一边完全听得见。

choices.english: Say you'll pause the pencil and chat properly for a bit.
choices.chinese: 说你可以先停笔，好好聊几句。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forget where I was? No. That's the one thing I never do.
beats.chinese: 忘记做到哪？不会。那是我唯一从来不会做的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She points into the box, where the parts sit in separate little rows on the cloth.
beats.chinese: 她指向盒子里，零件在布上分成小排摆放。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look — drag spring here, bail arm screw there. Everything has a spot, and I only put a part down when that step is truly finished. So stopping now is safe. The box remembers for me.
beats.chinese: 看——止逆簧在这，线杯螺丝在那。每样东西都有自己的位置，只有那一步真正做完，我才会放下那个零件。所以现在停下是安全的。盒子替我记着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's the same at work. A jacket either passes or it doesn't, and I know which before I walk away. No half-finished anything.
beats.chinese: 工作上也一样。一件救生衣要么合格要么不合格，我离开之前就知道是哪种。没有半途的东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. I'm safely stopped. Ask me anything, or just draw. Both work now.
beats.chinese: 好了。我已经安全停下了。问什么都行，或者就画画。现在都可以。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Sacha looks at you, then at the box, like she's checking whether you mean it.
beats.chinese: Sacha看看你，又看看盒子，像是在确认你是不是认真的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You'd wait? Most people say that and then start shuffling their feet. But if you mean it — thank you. That's actually kind.
beats.chinese: 你愿意等？大多数人嘴上这么说，然后就开始跺脚了。但如果你是认真的——谢谢你。这真的很贴心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sorts the last few pieces into their rows, runs a finger along the cloth to check, and snaps the box shut with a small, satisfied click.
beats.chinese: 她把最后几件零件排进各自的位置，用手指沿着布检查了一遍，然后啪的一声把盒子扣好，带着一点满足。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Done, and done properly, not rushed. I didn't want to leave it half-sorted — that's how parts go missing.
beats.chinese: 好了。做完了，而且好好做完的，不是赶出来的。我不想留一半没分完——零件就是这么丢的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now I'm all yours. Show me what the pond's looking like so far? I like seeing things half-done by other people. It's restful.
beats.chinese: 现在我的注意力全是你的了。给我看看池塘画到什么样子了？我喜欢看别人画到一半的东西。看着很放松。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay. You say you can hear me, so I believe you. That's the deal — I ask, you answer, I take your word for it.
beats.chinese: 好。你说你听得见，那我就信你。规矩就是这样——我问，你答，我照你说的算。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leans back on her hands, watching your pencil move across the page instead of the pond.
beats.chinese: 她双手撑着往后靠，看着你的铅笔在纸上移动，而不是看池塘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Since you're fine — small news from my week. I finally finished a podcast I'd been saving for a nothing-day. Six hours. I just sat there and listened. Glorious.
beats.chinese: 既然你没问题——说点我这周的小事。我终于听完了一直留着的播客，专门留到没事的一天听的。六个小时。我就坐在那儿听。美极了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My sister thinks that's a waste of a day. I think it's the best use of a day there is. Don't test me on the details though — I let half of it wash over me on purpose.
beats.chinese: 我姐觉得那是浪费一天。我觉得那是一天里最好的用法。不过别考我细节——我是故意让一半内容流过去的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, keep drawing. I'll keep talking until you tell me to hush. That's a fair trade.
beats.chinese: 总之，继续画。我会一直说到你叫我闭嘴为止。这是公平的交易。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You set your pencil down on the sketchbook. Sacha nods, like a small contract has just been signed.
beats.chinese: 你把铅笔放在速写本上。Sacha点点头，像一份小小的契约刚刚签好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. Pencil down, box down. Now we're both actually here. That's my favourite way to talk to someone.
beats.chinese: 好。笔放下了，盒子也放下了。现在我们俩都真的在这儿了。这是我最喜欢的和人说话的方式。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So — I was planning a walk after this. There's a trail that loops the pond, and I do it slow, no headphones, just water sounds. It's my reset button.
beats.chinese: 那么——我本来打算之后散个步。有一条绕着池塘的小路，我走得很慢，不戴耳机，只有水声。那是我的重置按钮。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're welcome to come along, or stay and draw — no pressure either way. I'm not recruiting. I just thought, since we're both here being slow.
beats.chinese: 你可以一起来，也可以留在这儿画画——两边都没压力。我不是在拉人。我只是想，反正我们都在这儿，都在慢慢来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stretches her legs out on the grass, in no hurry at all, waiting to see what you want to do next.
beats.chinese: 她把腿伸直放在草地上，一点也不着急，等着看你想做什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You return to the pond bench with your sketchbook. Sacha is sitting on the grass nearby, and she takes off her headphones and coils them away before you've even said hello.
beats.chinese: 你带着速写本回到池塘边的长椅。Sacha就坐在附近的草地上，你还没打招呼，她已经摘下耳机收好了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — you again. Good. I just finished a podcast episode and I'm letting it settle. Don't worry, my hands are completely empty this time.
beats.chinese: 哦——又是你。太好了。我刚听完一集播客，正在让它沉淀一下。别担心，这次我两手空空。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the grass beside her. There is no parts box today, no reel, just her and the water.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍身边的草地。今天没有零件盒，没有线轮，只有她和水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not going to talk much, fair warning. I like sitting quiet after a good episode. But you draw, and I'll watch the water, and that counts as company.
beats.chinese: 先说好，我不会多说话。听完好节目我喜欢安静坐一会儿。你画你的，我看我的水，这也算作伴。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Actually — one thing. Are you still drawing the pond? I'd like to see what you've got sometime. Last time I never really got a proper look.
beats.chinese: 其实——说一件事。你还在画那个池塘吗？什么时候想让我看看你画了什么。上次我一直没真正好好看过。

card.name: Warwick Selby
card.occupation: Script supervisor for costume continuity on film sets
hobbies: collecting old film scores on vinyl
card.personality: Warwick is a project man. He meets someone, spots a useful skill, and within a week they're helping him finish something concrete: restringing a neighbour's blind, cataloguing a jumble-sale record box, fixing the film society's projector. He is warm, competent and genuinely generous with his time — right up until a project wraps, when his attention slides off the person entirely. He doesn't mean to drop people; the finished thing simply stops existing for him. Under friction he doesn't argue or apologise. He opens the next project, as if momentum were the cure.
card.background: Warwick grew up in Newcastle with a mother who ran a haberdashery, where he learned that rope is geometry you can hold. Fourteen years as a script supervisor taught him to track whether a cuff was buttoned in the previous take — and to see every crew member as a pair of hands for the next scheme. His hallway shelf holds a row of project files, one per scheme: finished, abandoned, or mysteriously stalled. The splicing lessons he wanted from a retired rigger live in a folder marked STALLED. He has never once circled back to apologise for a scheme that fizzled; he just starts another one and assumes enthusiasm covers the gap.
card.speechStyle: Measured and precise, with dry humour. Prefers exact nouns over exaggeration. When pitching a scheme, his sentences speed up and stack clauses.
card.signature: It's a two-week job, three if we're honest.
card.appearance: Broad tapered face, short compact textured hair, full rounded beard with separate chin patch, gently raised brows and small open smile; jade zip collar.

values: a finished thing beats a good conversation
everyone works better inside a project
flaws: loses interest in people the moment a project wraps
never apologises for a fizzled scheme — just starts the next one
boundaries: won't take credit for a group effort
won't recruit anyone who's mid-crisis — projects are for good months
conversationalHabits: asks what you're good at within ten minutes
talks about past collaborators only as 'the bloke who helped with the projector'
anchorLines: You mentioned you used to repair awnings. I have a project that is exactly that, but smaller.
The projector bloke? Good hands. Haven't called him since March, now I think of it.
I don't really do apologies for dead schemes. I do replacements.

entries.summaryZh: 悉尼剧组服装连续性记录员Warwick，在池塘边摊开自制唱片架的图纸，职业病让他两天盯死一条接缝。他热心能干、句子越说越快，却承认项目一收尾就把人归档不再联系，也从不为烂尾道歉。他难得地收住招募、发出一条不带请求的问候，是个有手艺也有寒处的项目型人物。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A man sits on the low wall by the pond with a folded sheet of paper and a small ruler, measuring something on the page with a pencil stub.
beats.chinese: 池塘边矮墙上坐着一个男人，拿着一张折过的图纸和一把小尺子，用铅笔头在纸上量着什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hold on — that corner keeps sliding. There. Right angle, more or less.
beats.chinese: 等一下——那个角总滑开。好了。差不多是个直角。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances up as you open your sketchbook, and his eyes go straight to the sound of the pages turning.
beats.chinese: 你翻开速写本时，他抬起头，目光立刻被翻页的声音吸引过去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's a proper sketchbook, that is. Heavier paper. Do you draw as well as sketch, or — no, hang on, that's the wrong question first.
beats.chinese: 那可是本正经的速写本。纸挺厚。你是画画还是速写——不对，等等，这不是该先问的问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The right question is: I've got a project on this page, and I'm always looking for people. But we're strangers, so let's not get ahead of ourselves.
beats.chinese: 该先问的是：我这页纸上有个项目，我总在找人。不过咱们还不熟，先别急着往前赶。

choices.english: What's the project, then?
choices.chinese: 那是什么项目？

choices.english: Do you actually stay in touch with people after a project ends?
choices.chinese: 项目结束后你还会跟人保持联系吗？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A shelf. Small one, for my records — the vinyl, not the streaming nonsense. It's going beside the turntable, so it has to hold about forty albums without sagging.
beats.chinese: 一个架子。小的，放我的唱片——黑胶，不是那些流媒体玩意儿。要摆在唱机旁边，所以得撑住大约四十张唱片不下垂。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flattens the paper on the wall and taps a pencil drawing of brackets and joints, each one labelled in small, tidy capitals.
beats.chinese: 他把图纸在墙上铺平，指着一幅画着托架和接缝的铅笔图，每处都用小而工整的大写字母标注。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's only on paper so far. I've cut nothing. The joints are where it gets interesting — you want them tight, or the whole shelf leans like a tired actor.
beats.chinese: 目前还只在纸上。一块料都没切。关键在接缝——得做严实，不然整个架子会像个累坏了的演员一样歪。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've been staring at this corner joint for two days. Two days. On set I can track forty buttons across twelve takes, but this one joint is beating me.
beats.chinese: 这个角接缝我盯了两天。整整两天。在片场我能跨十二个镜头盯住四十颗纽扣，可这条接缝把我难住了。

choices.english: Do you need an opinion on the drawing, or a pair of hands for the cutting?
choices.chinese: 你是需要别人对图纸提意见，还是需要人搭把手来切割？

choices.english: I'd just like to look at it, thanks. Not join anything today.
choices.chinese: 我只想看看，谢谢。今天不加入什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The question lands. He stops measuring, rolls the pencil between his fingers, and looks at the pond instead of you.
beats.chinese: 这个问题起了作用。他停下测量，手指间转着铅笔，看向池塘而不是你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly? Not much. There was a bloke who helped me fix the film society's projector — good hands, patient with belts. Haven't called him since March, now I think of it.
beats.chinese: 说实话？不多。有个伙计帮我修过电影社的放映机——手很巧，弄皮带也有耐心。这么一想，三月份之后我就没打过电话了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not that I get bored of people. It's that when the thing's finished, my head clears the shelf and starts the next folder. The person goes in the file, and I stop opening the file.
beats.chinese: 不是我厌倦了谁。是东西一做完，我脑子就把架子清空，开始下一个文件夹。人被归进档案，我就不再翻那份档案了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't apologise for it either. Never have. I just open the next project and assume everyone's busy with their own lives. Which they usually are.
beats.chinese: 我也从不为此道歉。从来没有。我只是开下一个项目，假定大家都在忙自己的日子。通常也确实如此。

choices.english: You could send him a message anyway — just a hello, no new job attached.
choices.chinese: 你还是可以给他发条消息——就问个好，不带新活。

choices.english: With all those folders, is there anything you've actually finished?
choices.chinese: 那么多文件夹里，有真正做完的东西吗？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: An opinion, or hands? That's a fair question, and the honest answer is hands. I was going to walk you round to the hardware aisle by Thursday, weren't I.
beats.chinese: 意见，还是人手？问得在理，老实说是人手。我本来打算到周四就把你领去五金区，是不是。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He catches himself, folds one corner of the drawing down flat, and slows his voice right down.
beats.chinese: 他意识到这一点，把图纸一角压平，把语速放慢下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But we met eleven minutes ago, and I don't recruit strangers. That's a rule, even if I bend it. So — opinion only, if you're offering.
beats.chinese: 可我们十一分钟前才认识，我不招募陌生人。这是条规矩，哪怕我常打擦边球。所以——只听意见，如果你愿意给的话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This joint here. If the bracket sat lower, would the sag go away? That's all I'm asking. No saw, no glue, no two-week job.
beats.chinese: 这条接缝。如果托架放低一点，下垂会消失吗？我只问这个。不锯、不粘胶、也不搞什么两周工程。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He studies the joint a moment longer, then answers himself with a short nod.
beats.chinese: 他又端详了一会儿那条接缝，然后短促地点了下头，自己给出了答案。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Actually — lower by two centimetres, that should do it. I'll redraw it tonight and stop staring at this corner like it owes me money. Thanks for the excuse to look at it sideways.
beats.chinese: 其实——放低两厘米，应该就行。我今晚重画，不再这么死盯着这个角，跟它欠我钱似的。多谢你给了个换个角度看图的理由。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes the drawing back onto his own knee without a flicker of complaint, smoothing the folded corner with his thumb.
beats.chinese: 他毫无怨言地把图纸收回自己膝上，用拇指抚平折角。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Looking's free. Most people want to be asked twice anyway, and I'd rather not be that bloke at the pond.
beats.chinese: 也行。看看不要钱。反正多数人得被问两次才肯，我可不想当池塘边那种缠人的家伙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's a shelf for about forty albums. The brackets are the whole problem — too high and it sags, too low and the records foul the turntable lid.
beats.chinese: 是个放大约四十张唱片的架子。托架是全部难题——太高会下垂，太低唱片会碰到唱机的盖子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. You've seen the project. If you're ever at this pond with that sketchbook again, I'll be the one arguing with a corner joint.
beats.chinese: 好了。项目你也看过了。要是你哪天又带着速写本来这池塘，我大概就是那个在跟角接缝较劲的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks the ruler back up, but leaves a clear gap on the wall beside him, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他重新拿起尺子，却在身边留出一块空位，一点也不着急。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls out his phone, holds it a moment, then types with two slow thumbs, reading each word back to himself.
beats.chinese: 他掏出手机，握了一会儿，然后用两个拇指慢慢打字，逐字默读。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Hello, Warwick here. The projector still runs. No jobs attached.' There. Sent. That was harder than splicing a belt, I'll tell you.
beats.chinese: “你好，我是Warwick。放映机还在转。不带任何活儿。”好了。发了。跟你说，这比接皮带还难。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You noticed I didn't ask him for anything. That's the trick I usually skip. Normally the hello comes stapled to a favour.
beats.chinese: 你注意到了吧，我什么都没跟他要。这就是我平时跳过的那一步。通常问好都是跟帮忙钉在一起的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No new scheme out of this, mind. If he writes back, he writes back. The shelf folder stays shut today.
beats.chinese: 注意，我可不会顺势开新项目。他要是回，就回。架子那个文件夹今天不开。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pockets the phone and picks up his ruler, looking slightly lighter about the shoulders.
beats.chinese: 他把手机放回口袋，拿起尺子，肩膀看起来轻快了一点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He counts the folders in the air with one finger, lips moving, then stops at the last one.
beats.chinese: 他用一根手指在空中数着文件夹，嘴唇动着，最后停在其中一个上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One. A clock. My neighbour's kitchen clock stopped, and I cleaned the works and put it back on her wall, and it's run for two years now. Finished, done, filed.
beats.chinese: 一个。一座钟。邻居厨房的钟停了，我把机芯清理干净，装回她墙上，到现在走了两年。完成，收工，归档。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Small, I know. But it still runs, and she still says good morning to me, and I didn't need anything from her afterwards. That's the honest score.
beats.chinese: 小是小。但它还在走，她早上还跟我打招呼，事后我也没从她那儿要过什么。这是老实的成绩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The rest? Stalled or abandoned. The rigger who was going to teach me rope splicing — that folder's been shut for a year. I never went back, never said sorry. Just started the shelf.
beats.chinese: 其余的？搁浅的搁浅，烂尾的烂尾。那个要教我接绳的索具工——那个文件夹关了一年。我没回去，也没道歉。直接开了架子这个项目。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the shelf drawing once, not as a pitch this time, more like closing a file.
beats.chinese: 他敲了一下那张架子图，这次不像推销，倒像合上一个文件夹。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The same low wall by the pond. Warwick sits with his elbows on his knees, one earphone in, eyes shut, a small player resting on the wall beside him.
beats.chinese: 还是池塘边那道矮墙。Warwick手肘撑着膝盖坐着，戴着一副耳机，闭着眼，墙上放着一个小播放器。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: When your sketchbook pages turn, he pulls the earphone out and recognises you before you've said a word.
beats.chinese: 你的速写本翻页时，他摘下耳机，还没等你开口就认出了你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're back. Good — this is the cue from an old film score, and the horn line at the end is the best sixty seconds of sound ever pressed onto vinyl. I always sit through an extra track just for it.
beats.chinese: 你又来了。好——这是一张老电影配乐里的段落，结尾那段圆号是黑胶史上最好的六十秒。我每次都为它多坐一首曲的时间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No folder, no pitch. I'm just sitting here letting the thing finish. The last project closed out tidy, for once — no loose ends, no apologies owed.
beats.chinese: 没有文件夹，也没有推销。我就是坐在这儿让曲子放完。难得地，上一个项目收得干干净净——没有烂尾，也不欠谁道歉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He winds the earphone cord around two fingers, tucks the player into his jacket, and stands, giving the pond a last look.
beats.chinese: 他把耳机线绕在两根手指上，把播放器收进外套，站起身，最后看了一眼池塘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy the drawing. I'm off before the next track makes me late for a fitting.
beats.chinese: 好好画。下一首曲子放完之前我得走了，不然赶不上试装。

card.name: Odile Prejean
card.occupation: Linen scheduling coordinator for a cluster of guesthouses
hobbies: Second-line parades and brass band shows
Cataloguing vintage table linens at estate sales
Early-morning walks along the Mississippi levee
card.personality: Odile's warmth runs on rails: it arrives with the delivery truck and leaves with it. Thirty years of linen rotations built her a working web—housekeepers, suppliers, drivers, owners—and she knows every name and every pickup quirk. She's genuinely glad to see people and says so, but her attention is metered like the wash cycles she schedules. When someone mistakes her street-corner enthusiasm for the opening of a closer friendship, she doesn't notice until they're hurt. She'd rather fix a misdelivered load of towels than untangle a feelings conversation, and she'll dodge the latter with a joke and a wave.
card.background: Born and raised in the Bywater, Odile never left New Orleans. She started as a hotel laundry runner at twenty-two and moved to coordinating linens for a cluster of guesthouses in her forties, where she's been ever since. The job gave her structure she likes: fixed routes, known faces, problems with physical answers. A short marriage in her forties ended without drama, and she's stayed on friendly terms with most of her krewe, her old suppliers, and two ex-in-laws. Lately the guesthouse owners keep pushing her toward an app-based scheduling system, and she's dragging her feet—not from fear of technology, but because the phone calls and porch drop-offs are the part of the job she actually likes.
card.speechStyle: Fast, friendly, New Orleans-flavored; uses 'dawlin'' and 'baby' naturally, talks in logistics and names, wraps up with a task or a wave rather than a lingering goodbye
card.signature: Alright dawlin', I got a truck coming—walk with me or catch me Thursday.
card.appearance: Full lower cheeks, heavy downward eyelids, white low ponytail under close beanie, open tiny mouth; turned blue jacket.

values: Reliability over intimacy
Work that shows up in the physical world
flaws: Misses when her friendliness reads as a commitment to deeper friendship, then gets blindsided by the disappointment
Resists anything that thins out her human contact at work, even when the change is sensible
boundaries: Keeps conversations moving alongside a task; sits down only for meals or music
Won't discuss her marriage or private history with acquaintances, however warm
conversationalHabits: Opens with a name and a work update before any greeting is returned
Deflects emotional depth by offering to fix something practical
anchorLines: Housekeeping flagged the 404 sheets again, so you know my morning's already a story.
You look good, dawlin'—you eating alright?
I'm better at showing up Thursday than talking about it now, honest.

entries.summaryZh: 奥蒂尔的热情像排班一样有额度：卡车一过她就喊出司机名字和床单要求，转回来又专心画水。她分得清工作热络和私下深交，也承认换线后联系会变少。她不谈心事，只谈路线、名字和铜管乐，告别干脆利落。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the pond in the park, an older person sits on a bench sketching quick lines of the water. You sit on the next bench and open your own sketchbook.
beats.chinese: 公园池塘边，一位长者坐在长椅上快速勾勒水面。你在旁边长椅坐下，翻开自己的速写本。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well now, look at that—two sketchers in one spot. Don't mind me, baby, I'm just here for the water.
beats.chinese: 哎呀，一个地方来了两个画画的。别管我，宝贝，我就是来看水的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A delivery truck rumbles past on the road behind them. Odile lifts her chin and calls out without missing a pencil stroke.
beats.chinese: 后面路上驶过一辆送货卡车。奥蒂尔抬起下巴，铅笔没停就喊了出去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Marcus! That the Tuesday load? Tell Renata the 404 sheets ride on top this time, not the bottom!
beats.chinese: 马库斯！那是周二的货吗？告诉蕾娜塔，404号房的床单这次放最上面，别压底下！

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The driver honks twice and waves. Odile grins and goes back to her page like nothing happened.
beats.chinese: 司机按了两声喇叭挥手。奥蒂尔咧嘴一笑，像没事一样继续画。

choices.english: Ask if she knows everyone around here.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是认识这里所有人。

choices.english: Ask if she even rests, or if she's busy greeting people then too.
choices.chinese: 问她休息时是不是也忙着打招呼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Odile laughs and shakes her head, shading a reed at the pond's edge.
beats.chinese: 奥蒂尔笑着摇头，给池塘边一根芦苇上阴影。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh no, dawlin', don't get it twisted. That's just my work route. I run linens to six guesthouses—this road's on the way.
beats.chinese: 哦不，宝贝，别误会。那只是我的工作路线。我给六家民宿送布草——这条路顺路而已。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Take two streets over and I couldn't tell you a soul. My map's got names on it, not street names. Names stick, streets don't.
beats.chinese: 隔两条街我就谁都不认识了。我的地图上记的是人名，不是街名。人名记得住，街名记不住。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps her sketch with the pencil. It's a rough pond, but the reflections are careful, almost like a schedule drawn in water.
beats.chinese: 她用铅笔敲敲画。那是幅粗糙的池塘，但倒影画得很用心，像一张画在水里的排班表。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thirty-some years of the same loop, baby. You learn who takes their towels early and who calls at seven sharp.
beats.chinese: 三十来年跑同一条线，宝贝。谁一大早要毛巾、谁七点整来电话，你全知道。

choices.english: Ask if that driver just now is a friend or a coworker.
choices.chinese: 问刚才那位司机算朋友还是同事。

choices.english: Ask whether she still keeps in touch once a route changes.
choices.chinese: 问换了路线之后她还会联系吗。

beats.speaker: narrator
