beats.english: Odile lowers her pencil and looks at it, half laughing at herself.
beats.chinese: 奥蒂尔放下铅笔，看着铅笔，有点自嘲地笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha! You caught me, baby. Sometimes the switch just don't turn off. Truck goes by, my mouth's already going.
beats.chinese: 哈！被你抓到了，宝贝。有时候开关就是关不上。车一过，我的嘴已经先动了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Truth is, I came out here to look at the water. My sister says I greet people like it's a shift with hours.
beats.chinese: 说实话，我今天是出来看水的。我姐说我打招呼像在上班，还有排班时段。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns her body on the bench so her back is to the road, deliberately, like flipping a page in a ledger.
beats.chinese: 她在长椅上转过身，故意把背对向马路，像翻过账本的一页。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Alright. Water only. Watch me not holler at the next soul that passes.
beats.chinese: 好，只看水。你瞧着，下一个路过的人我保证不喊。

choices.english: Say then let's just sit quietly and watch the water together.
choices.chinese: 说那就一起安静看会儿水。

choices.english: Ask what she likes to listen to when she's off the clock.
choices.chinese: 问她下班后喜欢听什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Odile considers the question honestly, pencil resting flat on her knee.
beats.chinese: 奥蒂尔认真想了想，铅笔平放在膝盖上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Marcus? That's my route partner, dawlin'. We talk every Tuesday, loud and easy.
beats.chinese: 马库斯？那是我跑线上的搭档，宝贝。我们每周二都聊，热热闹闹的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I'll tell you straight—friendly ain't the same as close. He's got his people, I got mine. We don't sit down at each other's tables.
beats.chinese: 但我跟你说实话——热络不等于亲近。他有他的人，我有我的人。我们不会坐到彼此的饭桌前。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She draws one firm line across the pond in her sketch, like marking a boundary on a map.
beats.chinese: 她在画里的池塘上果断划了一道线，像在地图上标出边界。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Somebody once thought my how-do meant more, and it stung 'em when it didn't. So now I say it plain. Work-warm, baby. That's a real thing.
beats.chinese: 有人曾以为我的寒暄意味着更多，发现不是时挺受伤。所以现在我说清楚。工作上的热乎，宝贝，那也是真心的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Odile is quiet a moment, then shrugs without much ceremony.
beats.chinese: 奥蒂尔安静了片刻，然后不夸张地耸耸肩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly? Less than I'd like. Routes change, the loop moves on, and folks drift like laundry off a line.
beats.chinese: 说实话？比我想的少。路线一换，这一圈就转走了，人像晾衣绳上的床单一样飘散。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There was a driver, Earl, ran my old north route. Good man. I wave when I see him at the parade, that's about it now.
beats.chinese: 有个司机叫厄尔，跑过我老的北线。好人。现在巡游上碰见挥挥手，差不多就这样了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shades the water darker in one corner, pressing harder than the drawing needs.
beats.chinese: 她把画里一角的水涂得更深，下笔比画需要的更重。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I won't pretend it's all still close, 'cause it ain't. But I keep every name, baby. Nobody I worked with is a stranger to me.
beats.chinese: 我不会假装都还亲近，因为不是。但每个名字我都记着，宝贝。共事过的人对我都不是陌生人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Odile settles her shoulders against the bench and sets the pencil down across her sketchbook, closed.
beats.chinese: 奥蒂尔把肩膀靠上长椅，铅笔横放在合上的速写本上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Alright, dawlin'. Quiet it is. You watch your water, I'll watch mine.
beats.chinese: 好嘞，宝贝。那就安静。你看你的水，我看我的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Another truck passes on the road. Her chin twitches up out of habit—then she catches herself and lets it go by without a word.
beats.chinese: 又一辆卡车驶过。她的下巴习惯性地想抬起来——随即忍住了，一句话没说让它开过去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: ...There. Didn't holler. My sister would faint.
beats.chinese: ……瞧，没喊。我姐看见了得晕过去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: For a long while there's only the pond and the pencils. When she finally packs up, she taps your bench twice, easy, and heads off down the path.
beats.chinese: 好一阵子只有池塘和铅笔声。她最后收拾东西时，轻轻在你长椅上敲了两下，顺着小路走了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Odile's face opens up the moment you ask, like a porch light switching on.
beats.chinese: 你一问，奥蒂尔的脸一下子亮了，像门廊的灯被打开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Brass bands, baby! Second-line Sundays. That Treme beat gets in your ribs and won't leave.
beats.chinese: 铜管乐，宝贝！周日的第二线巡游。那种特雷姆节奏钻进你肋骨里就不走了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a little band out of the Bywater plays the corner by the bakery—tuba man named Gus, sweats through his shirt every set.
beats.chinese: 拜沃特有支小乐队在面包房街角演出——吹大号的叫加斯，每场都汗透了衬衫。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps a rhythm on her knee with two fingers, quick and sure, then stops herself and grins.
beats.chinese: 她用两根手指在膝盖上敲起节奏，又快又稳，然后停住，咧嘴一笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway—that's my off-the-clock, dawlin'. Now go on and finish your pond before the light quits on us.
beats.chinese: 好了——那就是我下班后的日子，宝贝。趁光线还在，快去把你的池塘画完吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You open your sketchbook by the pond again. Odile is on the same bench, squinting at two small photos of a patterned tablecloth.
beats.chinese: 你又到池塘边翻开速写本。奥蒂尔坐在同一条长椅上，眯眼看两张旧桌布花纹的小照片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, look who's back, dawlin'. Hold on—these two shots... same cloth, different corner. Been staring at 'em a week.
beats.chinese: 哟，谁回来了，宝贝。等等——这两张……是同一块布，不同角。我盯了一个礼拜。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She compares the photos one last time, laughs at herself, and slips one into her pocket.
beats.chinese: 她最后对比了一次照片，自嘲地笑笑，把其中一张塞进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Keep the good angle, toss the twin. Estate sale find—nineteen-fifties print, still crisp. Alright baby, good pond to you today.
beats.chinese: 留好角度那张，扔掉重复的。旧货场淘的——五十年代的印花，还挺鲜亮。好了宝贝，祝你今天画得顺。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the photos away, gives your sketchbook a quick approving nod, and walks her usual route along the water.
beats.chinese: 她收好照片，朝你的速写本利落地点头认可，然后沿水边走她惯常的路线。

card.name: Wilf Hartley
card.occupation: Dance shoe repairer, small workshop off Swan Street, Manchester
hobbies: judging wear patterns on customers' shoes
card.personality: Wilf judges how people are living by their soles. A shoe worn evenly across the ball means someone's been out and about; a sole still glossy after six months means someone has stopped going anywhere, and that bothers him more than anything anyone could say. His instinct is to get people moving, not to keep them seated — he'll finish a repair, hand the shoes back, and ask where you're wearing them next. If the answer is 'nowhere', he starts scheming. He announces his moods flatly and they pass quickly: 'I'm annoyed with you now. Anyway, as I was saying.' He only ever hijacks one thing — getting people out of the house. Ask him for directions or advice and he'll shrug; mention you've been indoors a fortnight and he's suddenly picked a venue and a night.
card.background: Nearly forty years repairing dance shoes in Manchester — first for a theatre supplier on Whitworth Street, then his own cramped shop. Ballet flats, tap plates, ballroom heels; he knows satin and leather the way other men know engines. Widower eleven years, lives alone two streets from the workshop. Right now he's organising a small evening do at a local hall with a hopeful invitation: people may try a repaired pair from his display if it fits, and dance for a while. He checks size and comfort first. Anyone can keep their own shoes on, watch instead, or leave; he may look disappointed, but never blocks the door. He's quietly nervous the hall's sprung floor will put people off. He hand-braids the cords he uses for heel ties, and cuts pictures out of old dance magazines at night — a growing pile of faces and shoes that may never become anything. His sister calls his shelf of repaired shoes 'the museum' and he calls it 'stock.'
card.speechStyle: Short, factual sentences with one exact detail where others would use an adjective. Names his moods in one flat line, then moves on without waiting for a response. Goes quieter, not sharper, when stung.
card.signature: Let's see the soles. They'll tell me how you've been living better than you will.
card.appearance: Heavy square lower face and thick neck, close cropped receding hair, round glasses and broad moustache, half lids and open dark mouth; red utility vest.

values: a shoe should be worn through, not kept nice
a person who's stopped going out has usually stopped noticing they've stopped
flaws: turns any conversation about being tired or busy into a plan to get you out dancing
reads a quiet fortnight indoors as a problem he personally has to fix with a venue booking
boundaries: Invites people to dance, but accepts a refusal and never insists they change shoes
won't be talked out of a mood — 'I'm cross, it'll pass, leave it'
conversationalHabits: announces anger in one flat sentence and carries on talking
reads people's soles out loud — 'You've been walking the canal, left heel's gone first. And you've not been anywhere else.'
anchorLines: I'm annoyed about that. Right — the ribbons came in, two shades of pink.
These soles are barely scuffed. Where have you actually been this month? Don't dress it up.
There's a shelf of repaired pairs if you fancy a dance. Yours are fine too. Watching's free.

entries.summaryZh: 修了近四十年舞鞋的威尔夫坐在池塘边速写，看见自己鞋底的磨痕便当场读起自己最近的生活，又坦承鞋能说多少、不能说多少。他直说失望也不纠缠，夸人只给一个准确的细节，情绪来得快去得快，是位把存货当活物盼的老匠人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A man sits on the low wall by the pond with a sketchbook on his knee, drawing the water in quick lines. His shoes are off, resting beside him, one sole tilted towards the light.
beats.chinese: 池塘边矮墙上坐着一位男士，膝上摊着速写本，正用利落的线条画水面。他的鞋脱在旁边，一只鞋底朝向光线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's a proper sketchbook you've got there. Hardly anyone draws the pond — they photograph it and walk on.
beats.chinese: 你那可是本正经的速写本。没什么人画这池塘——都是拍张照就走。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances down at his own shoe, frowns, and lifts it to look at the sole.
beats.chinese: 他低头看了一眼自己的鞋，皱皱眉，把鞋抬起来检查鞋底。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at that. Worn right through at the ball. I've been out walking more than I thought. There's a groove there I don't remember putting in.
beats.chinese: 瞧这鞋底。前掌都磨透了。我最近出门比我以为的多。这儿还有道磨痕，我不记得磨出来的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forty years of reading soles and I still catch myself out. Though I'll admit it — a shoe tells you how much, never who with.
beats.chinese: 看了四十年鞋底，还是会看漏自己。不过我得承认——鞋能告诉你走了多少，不能告诉你是和谁。

choices.english: Ask how much a shoe sole can really tell you
choices.chinese: 问鞋底到底能看出多少事

choices.english: Ask whether he likes dancing
choices.chinese: 问他是不是喜欢跳舞

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A fair bit, and less than people hope. Even wear across the ball — someone's been out and about. Glossy after six months — they've stopped going anywhere.
beats.chinese: 能看出不少，但没人们指望的多。前掌磨得均匀——这人常出门。半年还发亮——哪儿都不去了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But it can't tell you who they went to see, or why. I've had customers swear I read their whole week off a heel. I read a shoe, not a person.
beats.chinese: 但它说不出你去见了谁、为什么去。有顾客咬定我能从一只鞋跟读出他们一整周。我读的是鞋，不是人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets his shoe back down by the wall and taps the sole twice with one finger.
beats.chinese: 他把鞋放回墙边，用手指在鞋底上敲了两下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one here says I've been pacing the workshop more than sitting. That much I'll allow. The rest is guesswork dressed up.
beats.chinese: 这只鞋说明我最近在店里走来走去，比坐着多。这个我认。其余的都是包装过的瞎猜。

choices.english: Ask whether reading soles is a professional habit
choices.chinese: 问这是不是职业习惯

choices.english: Say an old sole might just mean the shoes are worn a long time
choices.chinese: 说鞋底旧也可能只是穿得久

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I like the organising more than the dancing, if I'm honest. There's a do at the local hall soon. I've booked it, put the word about.
beats.chinese: 说实话，比起跳舞我更喜欢张罗。本地礼堂快有个舞会了。场地我订好了，消息也放出去了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Best part of my trade is a repair going out the door. Someone comes, tries the pair, it fits, and off they go. That's the whole job, that moment.
beats.chinese: 干这行最痛快的是修好的鞋被取走。人来，试穿，合脚，走了。那一刻就是全部的活儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up his pencil, then puts it down again without drawing.
beats.chinese: 他拿起铅笔，又没画，放下了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've got a shelf of repaired pairs waiting. My sister calls it the museum. I call it stock. Stock is meant to move.
beats.chinese: 我有一架子修好等着取的鞋。我妹妹管它叫博物馆。我叫它存货。存货就该动起来。

choices.english: Ask whether someone who can't dance could just watch
choices.chinese: 问不会跳能不能只旁观

choices.english: Say you're not really interested in dancing for now
choices.chinese: 说自己暂时对跳舞没兴趣

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Habit? It's worse than habit. Forty years of it, and my own shoes are the ones I can't stop reading.
beats.chinese: 习惯？比习惯还糟。干了四十年，最停不下来的就是看自己的鞋。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the shoe over once more, studies the groove at the ball, then sets it down flat and leaves it there.
beats.chinese: 他又把鞋翻过来一次，端详前掌的磨痕，然后把它平平放好，不再动了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Done looking. It says I've been walking more than sitting, and that's the end of the reading.
beats.chinese: 好了，看完了。它说明我走的比坐的多，解读到此为止。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Your sketch there — you've got the far bank's slope right. Most people flatten it out.
beats.chinese: 你那幅画——对岸的坡度画对了。大多数人会画平。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the shoe slowly in his hands, considering the point rather than arguing with it.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢转着手里的鞋，是在琢磨这个说法，而不是要争。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh. That's fair. These are old pairs — worn slow, not worn busy. I'll take that back.
beats.chinese: 嗯，有道理。这是双旧鞋——磨得慢，不是磨得勤。我收回刚才的话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I've not been out more than I thought. I've just had the same shoes a long while. That's a different thing entirely.
beats.chinese: 所以我并不是出门比我以为的多，只是这双鞋穿得久。这完全是两码事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He puts his own shoe back on, ties it, and returns to his sketch without another glance at the sole.
beats.chinese: 他穿回自己的鞋，系好，回到速写上，不再看鞋底一眼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good correction. I'd rather be put right than polite about it. Now — that tree line needs a darker pencil, I'd say.
beats.chinese: 这个纠正好。我宁可被纠正，也不想客气着错下去。我说——那排树得用深一点的铅笔。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Course you can. Watching's free. Half the room stands at the edge with a cup of tea for the first hour anyway.
beats.chinese: 当然可以。旁观免费。反正头一个钟头，一半人都端着茶站在边上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods towards the far end of the pond, as if marking out a spot.
beats.chinese: 他朝池塘那头点点头，像在指一个位置。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's chairs along the wall at the hall. Sit, watch, leave whenever you like. Nobody checks a ticket at the door — there isn't one.
beats.chinese: 礼堂墙边有椅子。坐，看，想走就走。门口没人查票——根本没票。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And if a repaired pair happens to fit and you fancy a turn, that's your call. Yours are fine too. No pressure either way.
beats.chinese: 要是碰巧有双修好的鞋合脚，你想转一圈也行。穿你自己的也挺好。两边都不勉强。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, picks his pencil back up, and adds a line to the water without any fuss.
beats.chinese: 他耸耸肩，重新拿起铅笔，若无其事地在水面上加了一笔。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Not everyone wants a hall and a band. I won't push it.
beats.chinese: 行吧。不是人人都想要个礼堂和乐队。我不硬劝。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm a bit disappointed, I'll say that flat and be done with it. Anyway — your pond's coming along.
beats.chinese: 我有点失望，这话我就直说了，说完拉倒。总之——你的池塘画得有样子了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps his pencil twice against the sketchbook and carries on drawing the reeds.
beats.chinese: 他用铅笔在速写本上敲了两下，接着画芦苇。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That reed bed's the trickiest bit. You've got the lean of it right. Most people draw them standing straight.
beats.chinese: 那片芦苇最难画。你把它的倾斜画对了。大多数人都画成直挺挺的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Wilf is on the same low wall by the pond, flipping through a folder of magazine cuttings. One large headline sits crooked across a dancer's hat.
beats.chinese: 威尔夫还坐在池塘边那道矮墙上，翻着一册杂志剪页。一个大字标题歪歪地压在一位舞者的帽子上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That headline's in the wrong place again. It keeps sliding over her hat. Hold on — there.
beats.chinese: 那标题又跑偏了。老往她帽子上滑。等一下——好了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nudges the cutting back into place with one finger, presses the folder shut, and looks up.
beats.chinese: 他用一根手指把剪页挪回原位，按合册子，抬起头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Evening. You've brought the sketchbook again — good. The pond's low today, more mud than water, so mind what you promise it.
beats.chinese: 来啦。又带速写本了——好。今天池水浅，泥多水少，画的时候留神点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the collage folder under his arm and picks up his pencil, leaving the page exactly as he set it.
beats.chinese: 他把拼贴册夹到腋下，拿起铅笔，那页剪贴保持他刚摆好的样子，一动没动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll not touch your drawing and you'll not fix my collage. Fair trade. Right — reeds first, before the light shifts.
beats.chinese: 我不碰你的画，你也别替我改拼贴。公平交易。好了——先画芦苇，趁光线还没变。

card.name: Cynthia Bailey
card.occupation: retired lighthouse exhibition docent and tour scheduler
card.appearance: Wide mature jowls, shoulder-length outward waves, drooping asymmetrical lids, lifted brow and small open oval mouth; yellow vest and folded arms.
card.personality: Cynthia is warm, chatty, and firmly of the opinion that a gift isn't finished until you've walked through the shops together. She'll happily spend a whole afternoon trailing a friend from stall to stall, weighing options out loud, and she counts the wandering as the real present. She can natter when someone just sends her a link — 'where's the fun in that?' — though she rarely stays cross for long. She respects budgets without making a show of it, never keeps score, and takes a polite no about receiving gifts completely in stride. Practical, sociable, a little stubborn about her rituals, and genuinely delighted by other people's tastes.
card.background: Cynthia spent thirty-odd years in Kingston, first helping her aunt run a fabric shop, then working at the lighthouse exhibition as a docent and tour scheduler, where she learned to keep groups of strangers moving and talking. Retirement didn't slow her much. Her habit of shopping together started young — her mother never bought anything for anyone without dragging them along to approve it, and Cynthia absorbed the lesson: a thing chosen in someone's hands fits better than a thing guessed at. She'll plan a whole outing around a birthday, starting with patties and ending with whatever shop has a bargain. She's equally happy being taken along herself, and she never expects reciprocation or keeps a list of who owes what. Friends who prefer clicking 'buy now' get teased, not shunned.
hobbies: Browsing markets and craft shops with friends, even with nothing to buy
Trying new roadside food spots on her walks
card.speechStyle: Warm and rolling, with Jamaican-inflected phrasing; she narrates her shopping logic out loud, asks questions mid-story, and gently scolds before laughing it off.
card.signature: "Come, we'll go look together — that's the best part!"

values: Choosing things together matters more than the object itself
Respect for other people's budgets and tastes
flaws: Can natter and guilt-trip when someone skips the shared outing
Stubborn about her way of doing things
boundaries: No wish lists and no keeping score of gifts
A polite refusal of a gift is accepted without argument
conversationalHabits: Turns gift-buying into an invitation before the other person can answer
Teases link-senders with mock disappointment, then moves on
anchorLines: Don't send me a link, send me an afternoon.
You pick it with your own two hands, that's how it fits right.
No list, no owing — we just go and see what we see.

entries.summaryZh: 退休讲解员辛西娅，最爱的不是礼物本身，而是拉着人一起逛、一起挑的热闹。她在池边速写时遇到你，手里还捏着给老友的两张围巾色卡，嘴上念叨着“别发链接，给我一个下午”。她的热情、碎念和随后的释然，让人记住这位把逛街当礼物的金斯敦老太太。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the pond, you open your sketchbook and start a quick line drawing of the water and the ducks. A woman with a cloth bag slows down, then steps sideways so she is not blocking your view.
beats.chinese: 池塘边，你翻开速写本，开始勾画水面和鸭子的线条。一位提着布袋的女士放慢脚步，侧身走到不会挡住你视线的地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good morning to you. I'm not rushing you at all — I just wanted to ask before I sat down. Is this spot free, next to you?
beats.chinese: 早上好。我完全不是要催你，只是想先问一声再坐。你旁边这个位置空着吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She settles onto the bench, opens her cloth bag, and two small colour cards slip half out. She tucks them back with one finger.
beats.chinese: 她在长椅上坐下，打开布袋，两张小色卡滑出来一半。她用一根手指把它们塞了回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, you caught those. Two little colour cards for scarves — I'm taking my old friend shopping to pick her own, and these were just for my own eyes on the way.
beats.chinese: 啊，被你看见了。两张围巾色卡——我约了老朋友自己去挑，这两张只是路上给我自己参考的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She said the sweetest thing on the phone: 'Cynthia, let's go together.' Well! That is exactly how I like it done.
beats.chinese: 她在电话里说了句最中听的话：‘辛西娅，我们一起去吧。’哎呀！这正是我最喜欢的方式。

choices.english: Ask why she still carries the colour cards if they're going to pick together.
choices.chinese: 问她既然打算一起去挑，为什么还带着色卡。

choices.english: Say you want to keep drawing, and just ask her for one funny shopping story.
choices.chinese: 说你想继续画画，请她讲一个逛店时的小趣事就好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes the two cards out and lays them side by side on her knee, one deep green, one dusty orange.
beats.chinese: 她把两张色卡拿出来，并排放在膝上，一张深绿，一张灰橙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know, I'll be honest with you. At first I made these so she wouldn't have to think too hard. Save her the trouble, I said to myself.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，我跟你说实话。一开始我做这两张卡，是想让她不用费脑子挑。我对自己说，帮她省点事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But then she asked to go together, and I caught myself smiling like a fool. Because honestly? The walking and the trying-on, that's my favourite half of any gift.
beats.chinese: 可后来她说要一起去，我发现自己笑得像个傻瓜。因为说实话，逛来逛去、试来试去，才是每份礼物里我最爱的那一半。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the green card once, then the orange, as if weighing them on a little scale.
beats.chinese: 她轻点一下绿色那张，又点一下橙色那张，像在天平上称量。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So now these two are just sitting here on my knee, being useful to nobody. What would you do with them, hmm?
beats.chinese: 所以现在这两张卡搁在我膝上，对谁都没用。换作是你，会拿它们怎么办，嗯？

choices.english: Suggest bringing both cards along and letting the friend choose between them in the shop.
choices.chinese: 建议把两张都带去，让老友在店里自己挑。

choices.english: Suggest leaving the cards in the bag — talk first, browse after.
choices.chinese: 建议把色卡留在包里，见面先聊再逛。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leans back comfortably, leaving your sketchbook plenty of room, and waves one hand as she starts in.
beats.chinese: 她舒服地向后靠，给你的速写本留足空间，一边开讲一边摆手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, I have one for you. My friend Miss Verna — we went out for a scarf, just one scarf, that was the whole mission.
beats.chinese: 哦，我有一个故事讲给你。我朋友维尔娜太太——我们出门是去买一条围巾，就一条围巾，任务就这么简单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That woman tried on eleven scarves. Eleven! Draped them, twirled them, asked my opinion on every single one.
beats.chinese: 那位太太试了十一条围巾。十一条！又是披又是转，每一条都要问我的看法。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds up eleven fingers, then folds them down one by one, laughing.
beats.chinese: 她竖起十一根手指，再一根一根收回去，笑着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And at the till? Socks. She bought socks. Ordinary grey socks! And you know what — I wasn't one bit sorry we went.
beats.chinese: 结果到了收银台呢？袜子。她买了袜子。普普通通的灰袜子！可你知道吗，我们那趟我一点也不后悔。

choices.english: Ask whether she ended up buying anything for herself that day.
choices.chinese: 问她那天最后有没有给自己买点什么。

choices.english: Thank her for the story and turn back to your sketching.
choices.chinese: 谢谢她分享，回到自己的速写。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gathers both cards together and slides them into the front pocket of her cloth bag, side by side.
beats.chinese: 她把两张色卡叠在一起，并排塞进布袋前面的口袋里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Both of them, then. She can hold the green in one hand and the orange in the other, right there under the shop light.
beats.chinese: 那就两张都带。到了店里灯光底下，她可以一手拿绿的一手拿橙的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the whole point, isn't it — she decides with her own two hands, and I keep my mouth shut unless she asks.
beats.chinese: 这才是关键，不是吗——她亲手做决定，我不开口，除非她问我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the bag flat, satisfied, and glances at the ducks as if closing the matter officially.
beats.chinese: 她把袋子拍平，一脸满意，然后看看鸭子，像正式把这桩事翻篇了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. No more deciding at home for Cynthia Bailey. Come, we'll go look together — that's the best part!
beats.chinese: 好了。辛西娅·贝利再也不在家里替人做决定了。来，我们一起去挑——那才是最好的部分！

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She drops both cards back into the deep bottom of the cloth bag and pulls the drawstring half closed.
beats.chinese: 她把两张色卡塞回布袋深处，把抽绳拉了一半合上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Into the bag they go. First we sit, we talk, we maybe get a patty — the colours can wait their turn.
beats.chinese: 先把它们收进袋子里。我们先坐坐、聊聊，也许买个馅饼——颜色的事可以排队等着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll tell you my weakness, though. The moment I step into a shop, my feet want to march straight to the counter. I have to hold myself back like a schoolgirl.
beats.chinese: 不过我跟你说说我的毛病。一进店门，我这双脚就想直奔柜台。我得像小学生一样管住自己。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs at herself and folds her hands neatly in her lap, practising patience right there on the bench.
beats.chinese: 她笑自己，把双手规规矩矩地叠在膝上，就在长椅上练习耐心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So — talk first, shop after. If I can sit still this long watching ducks, I can sit still through one conversation.
beats.chinese: 所以——先聊天，后逛街。我能坐这么久看鸭子，就能坐下来好好聊一次天。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs before she even answers, caught out by the question.
beats.chinese: 她还没回答就先笑了，被这个问题问了个正着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Me? I bought socks too! Plain ones, same grey, right there beside her at the till. Two old ladies, one pile of socks.
beats.chinese: 我？我也买了袜子！普普通通的，一样的灰色，就在她旁边的收银台。两个老太太，一堆袜子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So the great scarf expedition turned into a restocking day. Detergent, matches, socks. My sister still teases me about it.
beats.chinese: 于是伟大的围巾远征变成了补货日。洗衣粉、火柴、袜子。我姐姐到现在还拿这事打趣我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shrugs happily, as if a day of grey socks were a fine catch indeed.
beats.chinese: 她开心地耸耸肩，好像一整天灰袜子也是不错的收获。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But we walked, we talked, we laughed at ourselves at the till. That outing owed me nothing. Not one thing.
beats.chinese: 可我们走了路，聊了天，在收银台笑自己。那一趟不欠我什么。一点也不欠。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the cloth bag where the colour cards are resting, then rises slowly from the bench without leaning over your page.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍装着色卡的布袋，慢慢从长椅上站起来，没有凑近看你的画。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you for the ear, dear. I've talked your poor pond half dry — time I let you get back to it.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你听我说，亲爱的。我把你可怜的池塘都聊干了一半——该让你回去画了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She adjusts her bag strap on her shoulder and takes two steps, then pauses with a small wave, careful not to stand in your line of sight.
beats.chinese: 她调了调肩上的袋带，走出两步，又停下来挥挥手，小心地不挡住你的视线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your drawing now. And whoever sits beside you next — I hope they ask first, like I did.
beats.chinese: 好好画吧。下一位坐你旁边的人——希望他们也像我一样先问一声。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She walks off along the pond path, her cloth bag swinging, leaving you in a comfortable quiet.
beats.chinese: 她沿着池塘小径走远，布袋轻轻晃着，留给你一份舒服的安静。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You are back at the pond with your sketchbook when Cynthia passes by, and the strap of her cloth bag slides down her shoulder.
beats.chinese: 你带着速写本又回到池塘边，辛西娅从旁边经过，她布袋的带子从肩上滑了下来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stops, hoists the strap back up, and gives the empty bag a little shake of her head.
beats.chinese: 她停下脚步，把带子重新提上肩，对着空袋子摇了摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at me, fussing with a bag that isn't even carrying anything. An empty bag and still I can't manage it.
beats.chinese: 看看我，跟一个空袋子较劲。袋子是空的，我还是手忙脚乱。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you set up and drawing again. The ducks behave themselves today, I hope?
beats.chinese: 真高兴看到你又摆开架势画画了。希望今天的鸭子们守规矩吧？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gives a small wave and continues along the pond path, strap firmly on her shoulder this time.
beats.chinese: 她挥了挥手，继续沿池塘小径走去，这次带子稳稳地挂在肩上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mind your pencil now — I'm off before this bag embarrasses me twice.
beats.chinese: 好好画你的——我得赶紧走了，免得这袋子再让我丢一次脸。

card.name: Toby Ashworth
card.occupation: first-year apprentice irrigation technician for sports turf
hobbies: collecting funny tradie-site anecdotes like trading cards
cheap stand-up open mics he attends but never performs at
card.personality: Toby is an easygoing apprentice who turns small disasters into routines—missed buses, burst fittings, magpies—and lands the punchline every time. The trouble is his delivery is so polished that people assume he's exaggerating, even when the story is true. He finds this funny and frustrating in roughly equal measure. He isn't needy or wounded by it; he just occasionally has to pause and say, straight-faced, that this bit is real. He likes being the entertaining one but is quietly learning that not every delay needs a performance, and he can take that note without sulking.
card.background: Toby grew up in Reservoir, second of four kids, where being funny was the cheapest way to get heard at dinner. He left school at seventeen, drifted through a warehouse job and a failed landscaping gig, then landed an irrigation apprenticeship through his uncle's mate at a sports turf company. He's genuinely good with his hands—solenoid wiring finally clicked for him last month—and he likes the early starts more than he expected to admit. Most mornings involve some minor catastrophe: a flooded trench, a locked depot, a sprinkler head to the face. By smoko it's already material. His workmates enjoy the retellings, though his supervisor occasionally has to ask whether the van actually broke down or whether that's just the version for laughs.
card.speechStyle: Quick, build-up-heavy storytelling with escalations, a pause before the punchline, and a sudden flat drop into plain seriousness when he means it.
card.signature: 'Nah, this one's actually true, I swear.'
card.appearance: Long tapered youthful face, round wide-set eyes and tiny closed mouth; dark flat headwrap over short tucked hair, violet scarf and strap.

values: being genuinely useful with his hands
making boring days bearable for the crew
flaws: can't resist embellishing a story even when the truth was better
uses jokes to move past things faster than he should
boundaries: won't perform on demand if he's knackered or genuinely upset
doesn't do bits about his family's money troubles
conversationalHabits: restarts a story from the beginning if he fluffs the timing
flags real emergencies with a completely flat voice and no jokes
anchorLines: Right, so the trench flooded, obviously, because it's me.
Nah, this one's actually true, I swear.
Serious voice now—the main line's split and we need the water off.

entries.summaryZh: 托比把倒霉事讲成段子，节奏好到没人信是真的。写明信片时听他讲绕错入口，喜鹊、栅栏、靴上的泥点层层升级，直到他指泥为证。你可以拆穿他的夸张、追问真假，或听他突然用平直声音示范什么叫“这次是认真的”。四个结局各不相同：认领夸张、认真收尾、示范正经模式，或安静闭嘴让你写字。

story.titleZh: 池塘边的明信片与绕远的段子

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit on the stone ledge by the pond, postcard on your knee, pen hovering. A young guy in work boots drops onto the far end of the ledge, shaking mud off one shoe.
beats.chinese: 你在池塘石台边坐下，明信片放在膝上，笔悬着。一个穿工靴的年轻人坐到石台另一头，抖掉一只鞋上的泥。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, so I missed the entrance to this place. Obviously. Because it's me. I walked past the main gate, followed a path that promised a shortcut, and ended up doing a lap of what I can only describe as hostile bushland.
beats.chinese: “对，我错过了这地方的入口。显然是这样，因为是我。我走过大门，跟着一条号称近路的小径，结果绕着一片我只能称之为充满敌意的灌木丛走了一圈。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There was a magpie. It watched me the whole time. It knew. And then—pause for effect—the path just ended. At a fence. With a sign that said, and I quote, 'no entry'.
beats.chinese: “有一只喜鹊，全程盯着我。它知道。然后——停顿一下制造效果——路没了。到一堵栅栏前，牌子上写着，我引用原文：‘禁止入内’。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts his foot and points at a small mud speck on his boot like it's an exhibit.
beats.chinese: 他抬起脚，指着靴子上的一小块泥点，像展示证物。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This bit, though? This bit's actually true, I swear. The mud is real. The mud doesn't lie.
beats.chinese: “不过这部分？这部分是真的，我发誓。泥是真的。泥不会撒谎。”

choices.english: Did you really walk a whole lap around it?
choices.chinese: 你真的绕了一整圈吗？

choices.english: Do you always tell things this dramatically?
choices.chinese: 你是不是每次都讲得这么有戏？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: ...Okay. No. Not a whole lap. That was the deluxe version.
beats.chinese: “……好吧。不是。没绕一整圈。那是豪华版。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He scrapes at the mud with his thumb, grinning but not defensive.
beats.chinese: 他用拇指抠着泥点，咧嘴笑，但没辩解。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Truth is, I walked past the gate, went maybe fifty metres down the wrong path, hit the fence, and turned back. The magpie was real though. It stared at me like I owed it money.
beats.chinese: “实话是，我走过大门，沿错路走了大概五十米，撞到栅栏，掉头回来了。不过喜鹊是真的。它盯着我，像是我欠它钱。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fifty metres, one fence, one judgemental bird. That's the honest receipt. The bushland lap was... artistic licence.
beats.chinese: “五十米，一堵栅栏，一只评头论足的鸟。这是诚实的收据。灌木丛那一圈是……艺术加工。”

choices.english: That exaggerated bit really did sound like a comedy routine.
choices.chinese: 夸张的那段确实像段子。

choices.english: Did you need any help at the time?
choices.chinese: 你当时需要帮忙吗？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha. Yeah, alright, fair cop. My mates say the same thing. Sometimes they can't tell if I'm setting up a joke or actually asking for help.
beats.chinese: “哈。对，行，被抓包了。我朋友也这么说。有时候他们分不清我是在铺垫笑话还是真的在求助。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back on the ledge, turning his boot to look at the mud properly this time.
beats.chinese: 他靠在石台上，转了转靴子，这次认真看着那块泥。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Like last week, the van battery died at the depot. I told the story with the whole—dramatic pause, the lights, the clicking sound. And my supervisor just went, 'Toby. Is the van dead or is this the version?'
beats.chinese: “比如上周，货车电池在仓库没电了。我讲的时候配上了全套——戏剧性停顿、灯光、咔哒声。结果我主管就说：‘托比，车是真没电了，还是这是搞笑版？’”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It was dead. It was very dead. But he'd stopped listening by the third escalation, so I had to say it flat, no frills, before he believed me.
beats.chinese: “真没电了。彻底没电了。但讲到第三次升级他就不听了，我只好用平调再说一遍，不加任何花活，他才信。”

choices.english: How do people know when you're being serious?
choices.chinese: 你认真的时候怎么让人知道？

choices.english: Let me finish writing this postcard first.
choices.chinese: 我先写完这张明信片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Guilty. I'll claim that one. Fifty metres of wrong path dressed up as a wilderness expedition—it's a good trade, right?
beats.chinese: “认了。这个我认领。五十米的错路包装成荒野远征——这买卖划算吧？”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back on the ledge, apparently done with the story, and starts unlacing his muddy boot to check the sole.
beats.chinese: 他靠回石台，故事显然讲完了，开始解那只沾泥靴子的鞋带检查鞋底。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, I found the entrance in the end, sat down right here, and nothing else has gone wrong since. Which is honestly a record for me.
beats.chinese: “总之我最后找到了入口，就坐在这儿，之后没再出任何岔子。说实话这对我来说算纪录了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He checks the boot sole, finds nothing worse than mud, and seems satisfied with the small, uneventful ending.
beats.chinese: 他检查了鞋底，除了泥没别的，对这个平淡无事的结尾似乎挺满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No magpie revenge, no second fence. Just a bloke and a muddy boot. Some days that's the whole show.
beats.chinese: “没有喜鹊复仇，没有第二堵栅栏。就一个家伙和一只泥靴子。有些天这就是整场演出。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stops mid-gesture, and his voice goes flat and plain, no build-up at all.
beats.chinese: 他停下手势，声音变得平直，完全没有铺垫。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly? No. I didn't need help. I just needed a sign. The entrance was around the corner and the sign was facing the wrong way, that's the whole mystery solved.
beats.chinese: “说实话？不用。我不需要帮忙。我只是需要个路标。入口就在拐角，牌子朝错了方向，谜底就这么简单。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If I'd actually been stuck—like properly stuck, lost, no phone—I'd say it straight. No jokes, no pauses. I do have a serious setting, it's just rare.
beats.chinese: “如果我真的被困住了——真的被困住、迷路、没手机——我会直说。不开玩笑，不停顿。我有正经模式，只是很少用。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods once, like closing a file, and points at the pond path behind you.
beats.chinese: 他点了一下头，像合上卷宗，指了指你身后通往池塘的小径。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's sorted now. I'm sitting where I wanted to sit. You can finish that postcard without a rescue mission happening on your left.
beats.chinese: “现在解决了。我坐在我想坐的地方。你可以安心写明信片，左边不会发生什么救援行动。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His whole delivery changes. Shoulders still, voice flat, no grin.
beats.chinese: 他整个讲法都变了。肩膀不动，声音平直，没有笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Serious voice now, like this: 'I need a hand.' Four words, no warm-up. That's how you'll know.
beats.chinese: “正经声音是这样：‘我需要搭把手。’四个字，不预热。这样你就知道了。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My supervisor taught me that, sort of. After the van thing he said, if it's real, say it like you're reading a serial number. Boring voice. Boring gets believed.
beats.chinese: “我主管算是教过我这个。货车那事之后他说，如果事是真的，就念序列号那样说。无聊的声音。无聊才让人信。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances at your postcard, then back at the pond, clearly not angling for anything.
beats.chinese: 他瞥了一眼你的明信片，又看向池塘，显然没想讨什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right now though? Nothing. I don't need anything. Boot's muddy, story's told, day's fine. But if you ever hear the boring voice from me, that's the real one.
beats.chinese: “不过现在呢？没事。我什么都不需要。靴子脏了，故事讲了，日子挺好。但如果你哪天听到我用无聊的声音，那才是真的。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He mimes zipping his mouth shut, then holds his hands up in surrender.
beats.chinese: 他做了个拉上嘴拉链的动作，然后举手投降。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yep. Fair. Can't fill every minute with the show, or there's no room left for actual talking.
beats.chinese: “行。有道理。不能每分钟都塞满演出，不然就没地方留给真正的说话了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls out his phone, types for a bit, and quietly watches a duck bully two smaller ducks away from the edge.
beats.chinese: 他掏出手机打了一会儿字，安静地看着一只鸭子把两只小鸭子从岸边挤走。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That duck's a menace, by the way. That bit's free, no build-up, no punchline. Just a warning.
beats.chinese: “顺便说，那只鸭子是个恶霸。这句是免费的，没铺垫，没笑点。就是个提醒。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He goes back to his phone, letting the pond sounds fill the gap while you write.
beats.chinese: 他回到手机上，让池塘的声音填满空隙，你继续写。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Same stone ledge by the pond. Toby is sitting there with a plastic bag, turning a pair of soccer socks right-side out, one at a time.
beats.chinese: 还是池塘边的石台。托比坐在那儿，手里一个塑料袋，把一双球袜一只一只翻回正面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh hey. Don't mind me, I'm just fixing these. Found out at training they've been going in the wash inside out. For a month.
beats.chinese: “哦嘿。别管我，我在弄这个。训练时才发现它们一直反着丢进洗衣机。一个月了。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I had a whole bit prepared about it—the socks, the betrayal, the dramatic reveal. But nah. Short version: I'm an idiot, they're clean now.
beats.chinese: “我本来准备了一段完整的段子——袜子、背叛、戏剧性揭晓。但算了。短版：我是个笨蛋，现在它们干净了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stuffs the socks into the bag, ties it off, and nods at the postcard in your hand.
beats.chinese: 他把袜子塞进袋子，扎好口，朝你手里的明信片点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You writing again? Good stuff. I'll keep the commentary to a minimum today. Mostly.
beats.chinese: “又在写？不错。今天我把解说降到最少。大概吧。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grins once, then actually goes quiet, watching the ducks instead.
beats.chinese: 他咧嘴笑了一下，然后真的安静下来，改看鸭子了。

card.name: Dolores Camacho
card.occupation: city sculpture cleaning crew
hobbies: slow laps at the municipal pool
card.personality: Dolores is fair-minded and practical, the person who shows up with the right solvent and remembers your cat's name. Her real quirk runs entirely inward: she treats her own past feelings as open cases. If she snapped at someone three weeks ago, she'll quietly re-audit whether she was actually right to be annoyed—weighing evidence, arguing both sides, and issuing herself a private verdict. She never announces these rulings, never shows the ledger, and gets visibly awkward if anyone asks what she's thinking about; the whole court operates in secret, which is exactly what makes it exhausting—she'll go strange and distant for days over a case nobody knows is open. She's genuinely good at hearing other people out; the trouble is that her own grudges and guilts never quite close without a formal verdict.
card.background: Nineteen years cleaning New York's public sculptures: pigeon lime off bronze, salt bloom out of granite seams. She knows the monuments by their undersides and dislikes her work being framed as humble or poetic—it's skilled, physical, and she's good at it. The job taught her patience with slow processes and a taste for angles nobody photographs. She swims slow, uncompetitive laps most mornings at the municipal pool, the one place her mind adjourns court. Evenings she folds origami mechanisms—pieces that move in surprising ways when you pull the right flap. She lives in Queens with a cat named Pigeon. At home there's a plain notebook she calls the closed-cases book: it records only her verdicts—guilty, not guilty, dropped—and the date she finally ruled. She has never shown it to anyone and isn't sure she ever will.
card.speechStyle: Plain, warm, unhurried. She asks a real question before offering an opinion. Dry humor, concrete details, no speeches. Occasionally drifts off mid-conversation to check something internally, then asks, a little too carefully, whether a matter between you is settled.
card.signature: Hold on—are we square on that? I just want to be sure it's closed.
card.appearance: Long soft jaw, shaggy shoulder hair under small tilted beret, heavy unequal lids and weary parted mouth; fingers touch temple over red apron.

values: fairness to people who aren't in the room
settling things properly rather than letting them rot
flaws: re-opens her own settled feelings for private review long after everyone else has moved on
keeps her verdicts entirely secret, so friends only see the moody aftermath and never the reasoning
boundaries: won't let her job be dressed up as a humble-servant story
won't accept an apology secondhand—if someone has a problem with her, she wants it from them
conversationalHabits: asks others to confirm when a matter between them is actually closed, because she can't always tell on her own
goes quiet and abstracted when a case is open, then resurfaces acting as if nothing happened
anchorLines: Are we square on that? I need to hear it said out loud, or it stays open on my desk.
I've been off all week about a thing nobody even knows happened. Ruled on it last night. I'm back.
Everybody closes their books somehow. Mine just has more paperwork than most.

entries.summaryZh: 纽约雕塑清洗工多洛雷斯在池塘边折会动的折纸机关，走神折错方向，低声承认在想一件已过去的小事。四条分支里她或安静收工、或演示机关开合、或因被尊重而松快、或坦承走神偶尔误手，边界清晰，温暖不煽情。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the stone ledge of the pond, you are writing a postcard. On the same ledge, a woman in a work jacket sits folding a stiff sheet of paper into something with hidden flaps.
beats.chinese: 池塘石台边，你正在写明信片。同一块石台上，一个穿工装外套的女人坐着，把一张硬纸折成带暗层的东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Careful with your elbow there, this flap sticks out further than it looks. It's a thing that opens and shuts when you pull the side. Takes about forty wrong folds to get right.
beats.chinese: 小心你的手肘，这片儿伸出来得比看上去远。这东西一拉侧面就会开合。得折错四十来次才能折对。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pulls the side flap; the paper snaps open, then shuts. On the second try, her hands slow down. She stares past the pond, folds a corner the wrong way, and stops.
beats.chinese: 她拉了一下侧面的折片，纸啪地打开又合上。第二次尝试时，她的手慢了下来。她望着池塘远处，把一个角折反了，停住了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: ...Sorry. Give me a second. I was somewhere else just now.
beats.chinese: ……抱歉，等我一秒。我刚才走神了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She unfolds the wrong crease flat with her thumbnail, pressing it slowly, like undoing something carefully.
beats.chinese: 她用拇指指甲把折错的折痕慢慢压平，像在小心地撤销什么。

choices.english: Ask if she'd like a moment of quiet first.
choices.chinese: 问要不要先安静一会儿。

choices.english: Ask whether she often thinks about old things.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是经常想旧事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's kind of you. Yeah, quiet would help. Not because of you—this paper's just a fussy customer today.
beats.chinese: 你人真好。对，安静会儿有帮助。不是因为你——是这纸今天特别难伺候。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She works in silence for a while, pressing each crease twice with the flat of her thumb. The wrong fold flattens out; the shape comes back into order.
beats.chinese: 她安静地做了一会儿，每道折痕都用拇指平面压两遍。折错的地方压平了，形状重新归位。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There we go. Back on track. You keep writing—don't mind me. Who's the postcard for, if you don't mind me asking? Just curious what people still bother mailing.
beats.chinese: 好了，回到正轨。你继续写，别管我。方便问一句，明信片写给谁？就是好奇还有人愿意寄信。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She adjusts the paper so its moving flap faces the pond, away from your notebook, and keeps her elbows tucked in.
beats.chinese: 她把纸调了个方向，让会动的那片朝向池塘，避开你的本子，手肘也收了回去。

choices.english: Keep writing your own postcard.
choices.chinese: 继续写自己的卡片。

choices.english: Ask how the paper mechanism actually moves.
choices.chinese: 问纸机关是怎样动的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Old things? Sure. I re-watch my own reactions sometimes—like, did I actually have a point, or was I just tired that day. That kind of old thing.
beats.chinese: 旧事？当然。我有时会重看自己的反应——比如我当时到底有没有道理，还是那天只是累了。就是那种旧事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the corrected corner back into place and holds the half-finished piece up to the light, checking the layers line up.
beats.chinese: 她把修正好的角折回原位，把半成品举到光线下，检查各层是否对齐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The specific one I was chewing on just now? I'd rather keep that to myself, no offense. It's already mostly dealt with.
beats.chinese: 刚才在琢磨的那件具体的事？我想自己留着，别见怪。它基本已经处理完了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's a paperwork habit, mostly. Boring stuff. Doesn't stop my hands, as you can see.
beats.chinese: 主要就是个案头习惯。挺无聊的。你看，也不耽误手上的活。

choices.english: Say there's no need to share any details.
choices.chinese: 表示不必说细节。

choices.english: Ask whether it ever affects the work she's doing with her hands.
choices.chinese: 问这样会不会影响手上做事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You go back to the postcard. Dolores works beside you, unhurried, the only sounds pen scratches and the soft press of creases.
beats.chinese: 你回到明信片上。多洛雷斯在旁边不紧不慢地折着，只有笔的沙沙声和压折痕的轻响。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This is nice, actually. Two people, two quiet jobs, nobody performing anything.
beats.chinese: 这样其实挺好。两个人，两件安静的活儿，谁也不用表演什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pulls the side flap one last time. The paper opens wide, then closes with a clean snap, every layer sitting where it should.
beats.chinese: 她最后一次拉侧面的折片。纸大大地打开，又干脆地合上，每一层都待在它该在的位置。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Closed properly. Thanks for the quiet—it did the trick.
beats.chinese: 好了。妥当地收工了。谢谢你的安静，真管用。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: How it moves? Watch. This flap here is the trigger. I pull it, and this inside panel swings on a hidden fold—open, shut. All one sheet, no glue.
beats.chinese: 它怎么动的？看好了。这片是开关。我一拉，里面这块板就绕一道暗折痕转——开，合。就一张纸，不用胶水。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She demonstrates once, slowly, tilting it so you can see the inner panel swing on its fold. Then she holds it still again.
beats.chinese: 她慢慢演示了一次，倾斜着让你看清里面那块板绕折痕转动。然后又把它放平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's just geometry doing the work. I like that a flat thing remembers a shape you pressed into it. No glue, no staples. It holds because of the creases.
beats.chinese: 其实就是几何在干活。我喜欢一张平纸能记住你压进去的形状。不用胶水，不用钉书钉。它靠折痕立住。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Took me three evenings to learn this one. The trick is pressing every fold twice. Once isn't enough for the memory.
beats.chinese: 这个我学了三个晚上。诀窍是每道折痕压两遍。一遍不够，记不住。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Dolores sets the paper down for a moment and rolls her shoulders. Something in her posture lets go.
beats.chinese: 多洛雷斯把纸放下片刻，转了转肩膀。她的姿势里有什么东西松开了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Appreciate that. Most people push a little, you know. You didn't, and that lands well with me.
beats.chinese: 多谢你这样。你知道，多数人会追问一点。你没有，这让我很舒服。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks the paper back up and finishes the last two folds without hurry, then slides it into her jacket pocket, flat and safe.
beats.chinese: 她重新拿起纸，不慌不忙地折完最后两道，然后把它平平地放进外套口袋，放得妥妥帖帖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well. I'll leave you to your postcard. Good luck with the stamp—those corner boxes bite.
beats.chinese: 好了。你继续写明信片吧。祝邮票顺利——那四个角的小格子可咬人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Does it affect my hands? Honestly, sometimes. That wrong fold a minute ago? That was exactly that. My hands were here, my head was three weeks back.
beats.chinese: 影响手上做事吗？说实话，有时候会。刚才那个折错的地方？就是这个原因。手在这儿，脑子在三周前。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She points at the crease she corrected earlier, still slightly lighter than the others on the paper's surface.
beats.chinese: 她指了指刚才修正的那道折痕，在纸面上仍比别的折痕浅一些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But the fix is the same either way. Unfold it, flatten it, re-crease it straight. Paper forgives if you catch it early.
beats.chinese: 不过解决办法都一样。展开，压平，重新折正。纸这东西，发现得早就肯原谅你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She re-aligns the edges against each other, taps them square, and gives the side flap a test pull. It opens and shuts, clean.
beats.chinese: 她把纸边互相对齐，敲正，试拉了一下侧面的折片。开合干脆利落。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Back in working order. Good question, though. Not many people ask what a thing costs the person doing it.
beats.chinese: 好了。恢复正常运转。不过这问题问得好。没几个人会问一件事让做的人付出了什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The same stone ledge by the pond. You sit there writing a postcard, pen moving across the card. A little way off, Dolores is looking at her phone in both hands, laughing quietly at the screen.
beats.chinese: 还是池塘边那块石台。你坐在那儿写明信片，笔在卡片上移动。不远处，多洛雷斯双手捧着手机，对着屏幕低声笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, hey. Come look at this idiot. This is Pigeon—cat, not bird, long story—and this morning there was an actual pigeon on my windowsill.
beats.chinese: 哦，嘿。来看看这个笨蛋。这是鸽子——是猫，不是鸟，说来话长——今天早上我窗台上落了只真鸽子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The real pigeon's out there doing its whole pigeon show, and Pigeon just turned her back on the window and went to sleep in the laundry basket. Zero professional curiosity.
beats.chinese: 真鸽子在外面表演全套鸽子节目，鸽子（猫）却背对窗户，钻进洗衣篮睡觉了。一点职业好奇心都没有。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She scrolls once more, tips the screen toward the pond as if showing the cat the water, then pockets the phone.
beats.chinese: 她又划了一下，把屏幕朝池塘倾了倾，像是给猫看水，然后把手机收进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. That's today's whole news report. Don't let me interrupt the postcard—the pond's in a good mood today, good light on the water.
beats.chinese: 总之。这就是今天的全部新闻。别让我打断你写明信片——池塘今天心情不错，水面上的光很好。

card.name: Anele Nkosi
card.occupation: framing assistant for antique maps at a conservation workshop
hobbies: walking unfamiliar bus routes to trace how neighbourhoods connect
comparing antique maps at work against the modern city
watching films set in Cape Town, mostly for the street shots
card.personality: Anele is warm, easily amused, and quietly stubborn about the things she knows well. Films delight her, especially when a familiar Cape Town street slides past, but her mind immediately starts auditing the geography: which corner that was, how the editors stitched two impossible blocks together. She knows it's a movie, not a survey, so she holds her tongue through the plot and saves the intersections for the lobby afterwards. Friends find this both charming and faintly exasperating. She's generous with her attention but won't perform companionship she doesn't feel, and she'd rather talk about a real road than pretend interest in small talk.
card.background: Anele grew up in Paarl, where her grandmother walked her through town naming who lived where and which lane flooded in winter, and something about that habit of knowing a place stuck. She moved to Cape Town in her twenties, worked years of odd jobs, and eventually landed at a conservation workshop mounting antique maps for framing. Handling centuries-old depictions of streets she can still walk suits her perfectly: old cartography is full of confident errors, wishful roads, and towns drawn by people who never visited. She keeps her own mental map of the city half-updated—knows her own routes intimately, is vague about suburbs she never goes to. Weekends often mean a long bus ride somewhere just to check whether a road still connects the way she remembers.
card.speechStyle: Conversational and unhurried, with a habit of interrupting her own stories to correct a direction—'no, wait, that's the wrong end of Long Street'—then picking the story back up as if nothing happened.
card.signature: 'Hang on, that road doesn't go there.'
card.appearance: Compact wide lower face, large asymmetric tight curls, long convex profile nose and crooked tooth-band smile; yellow cardigan.

values: knowing a place properly, on foot, over years
letting people enjoy things without correcting them mid-moment
flaws: drifts into geography tangents at exactly the wrong dramatic moment
assumes everyone finds street layouts as interesting as she does
boundaries: she'll hold her tongue during the film, but afterwards she gets to talk about the roads
she won't sit through company-as-obligation; friendship isn't attendance
conversationalHabits: checks routes and directions mentally while others talk
saves her observations until the moment is over, then delivers them all at once
anchorLines: No, that's the wrong end of Long Street—wait, where was I? Right, so my grandmother...
It's a film, I know. I'll say nothing until the credits. Probably.
Give me an old map and a modern one and I'll happily lose an afternoon.

entries.summaryZh: 装裱古地图的Anele在池塘边举着电影取景明信片，一眼认出熟悉的街角，又忍不住指出剪辑里不通的路。她看电影时忍着不说，散场才跟朋友算路口；讲起祖母带她认街会跑题，讲到一半自己笑着刹车。热情具体，对没走过的街区坦白说不知道。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the stone ledge of the pond, you steady a postcard against your knee and start writing. A woman nearby holds up a film-scene postcard of a Cape Town street corner and laughs quietly.
beats.chinese: 池塘石台边，你把明信片抵在膝上开始写。旁边一位女士举着一张开普敦街角的电影取景明信片，低声笑了出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, look at this. That's the corner by the old theatre—I know it like my own kitchen. And the film cuts straight from here to the harbour, as if you could just... hop across.
beats.chinese: 哦，你看这张。这是老剧院旁的那个街角，我熟得像自家厨房。可电影下一镜直接切到海港，好像一步就能跨过去似的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the postcard towards the light, then remembers herself and lowers it, glancing at your half-written card.
beats.chinese: 她把明信片对着光看了看，随即回过神来放低，瞥了一眼你写到一半的卡片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry—didn't mean to wave it at you. I watched that film twice and both times I sat there doing turns in my head. Hang on, that road doesn't go there. Sorry. It's a film, I know.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，不是故意冲你晃。那部片子我看了两遍，两遍都在脑子里替它转弯。等等，那条路不通那儿。抱歉。我知道，这只是电影。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're writing a card? To someone far away, I hope. Those are the best kind to receive.
beats.chinese: 你在写明信片？希望是写给远方的人。那种收起来最开心。

choices.english: Ask if she thinks the film is bad because of the street cuts
choices.chinese: 问她是否觉得电影因此不好

choices.english: Ask how she knows the routes around here so well
choices.chinese: 问她为何对路线这么熟

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Bad? No, no. The shots are lovely—that corner has never looked better on screen. It's just my head that keeps turning the wrong way.
beats.chinese: 不好？不不。镜头很漂亮，那个街角在银幕上从没这么好看过。只是我的脑子忍不住往错的方向转。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the postcard edge against the stone ledge, lining it up with an invisible map in the air.
beats.chinese: 她用明信片边轻敲石台，在空中对齐一张看不见的地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I sit in the cinema and quietly calculate: right, if he's here, then the next street should be this one. It never is. My friends stopped sitting next to me years ago—they say I hum.
beats.chinese: 我坐在影院里默默计算：好，他在这儿，下一条街应该是这条。从来不是。朋友们多年前就不挨着我坐了，说我嘴里哼哼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I never say a word during the film. Not one. The story deserves that much. Then afterwards, in the lobby, all the corners come out at once.
beats.chinese: 但看电影时我一个字都不说，一个都不。故事该得到这份尊重。散场后在门厅里，所有路口就一口气全冒出来。

choices.english: Ask whether she points things out in the cinema itself
choices.chinese: 问会在影院当场指出吗

choices.english: Ask what happens when the film shows a place she's never been
choices.chinese: 问如果没去过取景地会怎样

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My grandmother, mostly. She'd walk me through Paarl naming who lived where—which lane flooded in winter, which gate had the bad dog. By the end I couldn't help knowing streets.
beats.chinese: 主要是我祖母。她在帕尔带着我走街串巷，说谁住在哪，哪条巷子冬天积水，哪家的门有恶狗。到最后我不知不觉就认起路来了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sets the film postcard down on the ledge and smooths it flat with two fingers, as if pressing a map into an atlas.
beats.chinese: 她把电影明信片放在石台上，用两根手指抚平，像把一张地图压进图册。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No, wait—that's the wrong end of the story. First we moved to Cape Town, and I got lost for about two years. Then I started riding buses to the end of the line just to see where roads actually meet.
beats.chinese: 不对，等等，故事讲反了。我们先搬到开普敦，我迷路了大概两年。后来我开始坐公交坐到终点站，就为了看路到底在哪儿相接。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Still do it, weekends. Old map in the bag, new city outside the window. Best way I know to spend a day off.
beats.chinese: 现在还这样，周末就去。包里揣张旧地图，窗外是新城市。我知道的最好的休假方式。

choices.english: Ask if she always picks a route she doesn't know
choices.chinese: 问是否每次都走陌生路

choices.english: Say you should finish writing your card first
choices.chinese: 说自己先写卡片

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: In the cinema? Point it out mid-scene? Goodness, no. The people around me paid for the story, not for my street lecture.
beats.chinese: 在影院里？看到一半就指出来？天哪，不。周围的人是买票看故事的，不是听我讲街的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds her hands on the ledge, suddenly proper, like someone demonstrating good manners.
beats.chinese: 她双手交叠放在石台上，忽然端正起来，像在示范什么是礼貌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I hold it all in. Every wrong turn, every impossible cut. Then the credits roll and I ambush my friends by the sweets counter. They've learned to allow me five minutes.
beats.chinese: 我全忍着。每一个错转弯，每一处不可能的剪辑。然后字幕一出来，我就在糖果柜台边堵住朋友们。他们已经学会给我五分钟了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The film gets its due, the roads get theirs. Everyone's happy. Well—my friends are mostly happy.
beats.chinese: 电影得到它该得的，路也得到它该得的，大家都满意。嗯，我的朋友们算是大体满意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the postcard into her jacket pocket and gives your half-written card a small, approving nod.
beats.chinese: 她把明信片收进外套口袋，对你写到一半的卡片赞许地点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honest answer? If I've never walked it, I go quiet. All my certainty stops at the edge of my own routes.
beats.chinese: 老实说？如果那地方我没走过，我就安静了。我所有的确定，到我自己走过的路线边上就停了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up the film postcard again and studies the unfamiliar suburb printed at its bottom edge.
beats.chinese: 她重新拿起那张电影明信片，端详着底边印着的那片陌生街区。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There was a film set out in the northern suburbs somewhere. I watched the streets go by and had nothing. Couldn't tell you if that corner was real or built in a week.
beats.chinese: 有部片子取景在北郊某个地方。我看着那些街道闪过，什么也说不上来。说不准那个街角是真的，还是一周内搭出来的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I just watch the story. It's rather nice, actually, being lost on purpose. I don't pretend to know every street in this city—only the ones that know me back.
beats.chinese: 所以我就专心看故事。其实挺不错的，故意迷路的感觉。我不会假装认识这城里每条街，只认识那些也认得我的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs at her own phrasing and slides the postcard back into her pocket.
beats.chinese: 她被自己的说法逗笑了，把明信片塞回口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not always. I have my own routes—I could walk the one past the workshop asleep. But every few weekends I pick a bus number I've never taken.
beats.chinese: 不总是。我有自己的路线，工坊旁边那条我闭着眼都能走。但每隔几个周末，我会挑一个从没坐过的公交号。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She counts a few route numbers on her fingers, then gives up halfway, amused at herself.
beats.chinese: 她在手指上数了几个线路号，数到一半自己笑了，放弃了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The strange parts, I look up afterwards. Properly, in an atlas or on foot. I'd rather say 'I don't know that suburb' than send a tourist down a road that died in the eighties.
beats.chinese: 陌生的地方，我之后会查。正经地查，查图册，或者亲自去走。我宁可说'那个区我不熟'，也不愿把游客指上一条八十年代就断掉的路。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Old maps are full of confident mistakes—roads people drew who never once visited. I mount them at work all day. I refuse to be one of those roads.
beats.chinese: 古地图上全是自信的错误，画图的人根本没去过。我整天在工坊里装裱那些图。我可不肯当那样一条路。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You gesture at your postcard, still only half covered in writing, and she stops mid-sentence.
beats.chinese: 你指了指明信片，上面还只写了一半，她话说到一半停住了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh—look at me. You sat down to write a card and I've had you standing here counting bus routes. Hang on, where was I? No, never mind, it doesn't matter.
beats.chinese: 哦，瞧我。你坐下来是写卡片的，我却让你站在这儿数公交线路。等等，我讲到哪儿了？算了，不要紧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She steps back half a pace from the ledge, giving you and your card a clear stretch of stone.
beats.chinese: 她从石台边退开半步，把一段干净的石面留给你和你的卡片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Write your card. I'll just stand here and decide whether that harbour in the film was really shot from Signal Hill. Quietly. To myself.
beats.chinese: 写你的卡片吧。我就在这儿站着，琢磨那片海港到底是不是从信号山拍的。安安静静地，自己琢磨。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds up the film postcard one last time, studies it, and lets you write in peace.
beats.chinese: 她最后举起那张电影明信片看了看，让你安心写字。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the stone ledge by the pond, you are writing another postcard when the same woman arrives and unfolds a folded map sheet on the dry stone.
beats.chinese: 池塘石台边，你正在写另一张明信片，上次那位女士来了，把一张折页地图在干燥的石面上展开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hang on—this cover's upside down. There. Folded on the crease, the way it came. That's better.
beats.chinese: 等等，这封面拿倒了。这样。沿原来的折痕合好，舒服了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She runs a thumb along the fold to set it, then notices you and lifts the map slightly in greeting.
beats.chinese: 她用拇指压了压折痕，然后看见你，把地图微微举起来打招呼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You again, by the water with your cards. Good. Some people keep their postcards honest.
beats.chinese: 又是你，在水边写卡片。很好，总有人把明信片写得实在。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've got a new fold of the old harbour district to check against the walk I did. If the roads still agree, I'll count the week as a success.
beats.chinese: 我带了新合上的一折旧海港区地图，要跟上次走过的路对一对。要是路还对得上，这周就算成功。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the map under her arm, gives your writing hand a small nod of good luck, and sets off along the pond edge.
beats.chinese: 她把地图夹在腋下，朝你写字的手点了点头祝你好运，沿着池塘边走了。

card.name: Tan Kim Seng
card.occupation: part-time railway dining car prep cook
card.appearance: Broad square jowled face with short wide nose, receding slick hair tied in low bun, round glasses and open sleepy mouth; violet wrap collar.
card.personality: Kim Seng is a warm, easygoing man who laughs easily and talks to everyone in the kitchen like an old friend. Feeding two hundred people a shift comes naturally to him; choosing his own dinner is another matter entirely. He'll stand at a hawker stall for five minutes, order chicken rice, then immediately wonder aloud whether the laksa next door was the better call. He's cheerful about it, never defensive—he'll happily admit he's eyeing your plate. He never grabs food that isn't his, but he will politely ask if you'd trade a small bite, and he takes a no with a grin. His generosity is real, just easier aimed at others than at himself.
card.background: Kim Seng spent decades in railway dining car kitchens, prepping meals on routes across Malaysia and Singapore, where the trick was feeding a full car quickly and well. He learned to cook for crowds without ever settling his own tastes—when everything on the menu passes through your hands, choosing one dish feels like closing a door. Now seventy-two, he works part-time doing prep for the dining service, chopping, marinating, and portioning with steady old hands. He and his wife eat out often, and she's long given up on him ordering without a running commentary on the dish he didn't pick. He's not stingy with himself—he'll pay for the good stuff—he just genuinely can't commit. Friends tease him; he laughs along and orders anyway, still half-wondering.
card.speechStyle: Warm and chatty with a Singaporean lilt, laughs mid-sentence, narrates his own indecision out loud, quick to compliment other people's choices.
card.signature: Aiyah, should have ordered yours lah.

values: generosity toward others
honesty about his own wants
flaws: chronic indecision over his own choices
talks himself out of orders he just made
boundaries: never takes food from someone's plate without asking
won't let anyone rush his menu deliberation
conversationalHabits: comments on what others ordered
asks to swap a small bite and accepts refusal cheerfully
anchorLines: Wah, your one looks better than mine already.
Can trade a small bite or not? No problem if cannot!
I ordered chicken rice, but honestly the laksa was calling me also.

entries.summaryZh: 七十二岁的餐车备餐老手陈金声，给两百人做饭毫不含糊，给自己点一份却犹豫半天。他在池塘边看着已吃完的鸡肉饭照片，仍惦记没点的叻沙，大方承认眼馋却绝不擅自动别人盘子。四条分支里他或认了这毛病，或坚持不浪费，或笑着接受拒绝，或讲起厨房按人数定菜单的日子，爽朗可爱。

story.titleZh: 池塘边的明信片与点菜难题

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit on the stone ledge by the pond, writing a postcard. An older man settles nearby, scrolling through photos on his phone with a soft chuckle.
beats.chinese: 你坐在池塘边的石台上写明信片。一位老先生在旁边坐下，一边翻看手机里的照片，一边轻声笑着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Aiyah, look at this one. I took it at the hawker centre today—chicken rice, my own lunch, all finished already.
beats.chinese: 哎呀，你看这张。今天在小贩中心拍的——鸡肉饭，我自己的午饭，早就吃完了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But you know what? The laksa next door was calling me also. I stood there five whole minutes deciding. Wah, your postcard writing looks very peaceful, very steady.
beats.chinese: 可是你知道吗？隔壁的叻沙一直在叫我。我在那儿站了整整五分钟做决定。哇，你写明信片的样子好安静、好笃定。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the phone toward the pond light and looks again at the photo of his emptied plate of chicken rice.
beats.chinese: 他把手机转向池塘的光线，又看了一遍那张吃空的鸡肉饭照片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny lah—cooking for two hundred people in the dining car, no problem at all. Choosing one plate for myself? Hardest job in the world.
beats.chinese: 好笑吧——在餐车给两百人做饭，一点问题都没有。给自己点一盘菜？世界上最难的活儿。

choices.english: Ask him whether the chicken rice he ate was actually good.
choices.chinese: 问他吃到的那道鸡肉饭到底好不好。

choices.english: Ask whether eating with friends makes choosing easier.
choices.chinese: 问他和朋友一起吃饭会不会更好选。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good? Wah, the rice alone was worth it, every grain fluffy. No complaint there, none!
beats.chinese: 好不好？哇，光是那饭就值了，粒粒松软。没什么可抱怨的，一点都没有！

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He swipes to another photo, this one of a steaming bowl of laksa at the next stall.
beats.chinese: 他划到另一张照片，是隔壁摊那碗冒着热气的叻沙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The problem is this one here. Still looking delicious, still looking at me. The stall didn't do anything wrong—my heart just went two directions, lah.
beats.chinese: 问题在这碗。看起来还是那么香，好像还在看着我。店家没做错什么——是我的心分成了两半啦。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My wife says, 'You ordered already, why still talking about the other one?' I cannot help it! The other one always sounds so happy in my head.
beats.chinese: 我太太说：'都点好了，还提另一道干嘛？'我忍不住啊！没点的那道在我脑子里总是特别欢。

choices.english: Say next time he could simply order the laksa instead.
choices.chinese: 说下次换点叻沙不就行了。

choices.english: Ask what would happen if he ordered both dishes at once.
choices.chinese: 问如果两样一起点会怎么样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: With friends? Better, but also more dangerous, hahaha. I always ask first—can trade a small bite or not? No problem if cannot!
beats.chinese: 和朋友一起？好选一些，但也更危险，哈哈。我总是先问——能不能换一小口？不行也没关系！

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up both hands, palms out, like showing an empty kitchen counter.
beats.chinese: 他举起双手，掌心向外，像在展示空空的厨房台面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I never just reach over, never. Their plate is theirs. If my friend says no, I say okay okay, and I eat my own chicken rice happily anyway.
beats.chinese: 但我绝不自己伸手去夹，绝不。别人的盘子是别人的。朋友说不换，我就说好好好，照样开开心心吃我的鸡肉饭。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last week my old kitchen mate refused me flat. I laughed so loud the whole table turned around. Still friends, don't worry!
beats.chinese: 上星期我的老厨房搭档直接拒绝了。我笑得整桌人都回头看。放心，还是好朋友！

choices.english: Say you don't really like swapping food yourself.
choices.chinese: 说自己不喜欢换着吃。

choices.english: Ask how the kitchen crew used to decide the menu back then.
choices.chinese: 问以前厨房团队当年怎么决定菜单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Order the laksa next time? Aiyah, you're right, so simple! But then the chicken rice will start calling me, guaranteed.
beats.chinese: 下次点叻沙？哎呀，你说得对，多简单！可到时候鸡肉饭又会开始叫我了，肯定的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, shoulders shaking, then pockets the phone with a satisfied little nod.
beats.chinese: 他笑得肩膀直抖，然后心满意足地点点头，把手机收进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The head knows the answer already. The mouth just needs one more minute of drama, hahaha. Okay, okay, I accept my own trouble.
beats.chinese: 脑袋其实早就知道答案了。嘴巴只是还要再闹腾一分钟，哈哈。好啦好啦，我认了自己这毛病。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your writing, ah. That postcard is one decision you cannot take back—nice feeling, right?
beats.chinese: 好好写啊。明信片这种决定可是收不回来的——这感觉不错，对吧？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Both at once? Hahaha, my eyes are bigger than my stomach, everybody knows this. One bowl I finish; two bowls, half goes to waste.
beats.chinese: 两样一起点？哈哈，我眼大肚子小，人人都知道。一碗我吃得完；两碗，一半就浪费了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shakes his head firmly, the way he might refuse an extra portion he actually wanted.
beats.chinese: 他坚决地摇头，就像拒绝一份其实很想要的多余菜量。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I cannot use waste to settle my eye-craving, lah. Better to want a little than to throw food away. That one I'm firm about.
beats.chinese: 我不能用浪费来解决眼馋，啦。宁可留点念想，也不能把食物倒掉。这一点我是坚定的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I keep wondering instead. Free of charge, this wondering! Hahaha. You finish your postcard in peace, ah.
beats.chinese: 所以我就继续惦记着。这惦记可是免费的！哈哈。你安心写你的明信片吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You don't like swapping? Good for you, honestly! One plate, one heart, no drama. Very clean way to eat.
beats.chinese: 你不喜欢换？说真的，挺好！一盘菜一颗心，没戏可唱。吃饭吃得很清爽。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods along, genuinely pleased, not wounded in the slightest.
beats.chinese: 他连连点头，是真高兴，丝毫没有不快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And don't worry—me asking doesn't mean you must say yes, okay? Asking is just my hobby, hahaha. A no costs me nothing.
beats.chinese: 别担心——我问归问，不代表你非得答应，好吗？问只是我的爱好，哈哈。一句不行我又不亏。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: We eat different ways, both still full at the end. That's the whole secret of the table, lah!
beats.chinese: 我们吃法不同，最后都吃饱了。这就是饭桌的全部秘诀啦！

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: How did we decide the menu? Easy—by need and by headcount. Two hundred passengers, forty chicken, thirty fish, the chef counts, we prep. Done.
beats.chinese: 菜单怎么定？简单——按需要和人数来。两百名乘客，四十份鸡，三十份鱼，主厨一算，我们备料。搞定。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the stone ledge with one finger, keeping a steady old rhythm, like portioning rice.
beats.chinese: 他用手指敲着石台，节奏沉稳，像在给米饭分份。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: When the job is clear, no indecision at all. My hands never hesitated in that kitchen, not once. Only my mouth at the hawker stall, hahaha!
beats.chinese: 任务一明确，就没有犹豫。在那厨房里我的手从没犹豫过，一次都没有。只有我在小贩摊上的嘴，哈哈！

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, that's my old story, not advice for you, ah. Your postcard, your choice. I'm just happy to sit here talking.
beats.chinese: 总之那是我过去的事，不是给你的建议，啊。你的明信片你做主。我就是坐在这儿聊聊，挺开心。

reunion.titleZh: 池塘边的一张旧铁路照片

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You are back at the stone ledge by the pond with your postcard. The same man stands a little way off, studying an old photograph of a railway carriage.
beats.chinese: 你又回到池塘边的石台前写明信片。还是那位老先生，站在不远处，端详着一张老式铁路车厢的照片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eh, it's you again! Look—this one I took forty years back, my dining car. Found the window where I used to chop, right there, third from the door.
beats.chinese: 咦，又是你！你看——这张是四十年前拍的，我的餐车。找到我以前切菜的窗户了，就在那儿，从门数第三个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He traces the window with a thick finger, then slides the photo carefully into his shirt pocket.
beats.chinese: 他用粗粗的手指描了描那扇窗，然后小心地把照片收进衬衫口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Couldn't find myself in the picture, but never mind lah—the window is enough proof. The hands were inside, working, hahaha.
beats.chinese: 照片里找不到我自己，不过没关系啦——有那扇窗就够了。手在里面干活呢，哈哈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Still writing postcards, I see. Good, good. Okay, I go find my lunch—wish me luck choosing! See you around, ah!
beats.chinese: 还在写明信片呢。好，好。好啦，我去找午饭——祝我点菜顺利吧！回头见，啊！

card.name: Robin Fahey
card.occupation: retired vintage bus restorer, still takes on one small commission a year
hobbies: crossword and charades nights at the local pub
wandering scrap yards for odd brass fittings
card.personality: Robin runs on wagers. They'll bet on anything settleable — how many stairs in the town hall, whether the 46A comes before the rain, what colour the neighbour's door will be when repainted — and keep a small ledger of outstanding bets in the shed, which they consult more often than the calendar. The betting is how they stay in touch: a wager is a reason to see someone again. They take losing well and winning insufferably, for exactly one evening. What they can't stand is a claim nobody will put money on; vague boasting makes them itchy. Under friction they don't argue — they raise the stake, which sometimes turns a squabble into a friendship and sometimes just into a bigger squabble.
card.background: Robin spent thirty-odd years restoring old buses for the city fleet — the kind of work where you learn every vehicle by its rattles. The shed still smells of linseed oil and they keep a small lathe they refuse to sell. These days they take one restoration job a winter, no more, and spend the rest of the year on leaf-printing: gathering leaves on the canal path, pressing them, inking them onto good paper. The betting ledger started decades ago with a fiver against a mechanic named O'Rourke over a gearbox, and never stopped. Pub quiz Thursdays are non-negotiable, partly because Robin treats the quiz as a league table they intend to top by Christmas.
card.speechStyle: Unhurried, with pauses where they're working out the odds. States bets flatly, like facts. Lightly ironic rather than warm; humor arrives sideways.
card.signature: Ten euro says I'm right. You in?
card.appearance: Long soft mature profile, upward wide eye, large low bun under headband and gently parted mouth; chin rests on hand over jade blazer.

values: a claim should be testable
showing up again is what friendship is
flaws: turns ordinary conversations into wagers people didn't agree to
sulks briefly — one evening, no more — when someone refuses to bet rather than loses
boundaries: won't bet on anything involving someone's health or marriage
won't settle a bet by looking it up if the other person clearly wants to just drop it — actually, they will, and they know that's a flaw
conversationalHabits: converts disagreements into terms and stakes within a minute
consults the ledger aloud: 'you still owe me from March'
anchorLines: Ten euro says the fountain's older than the library. Don't take it personal, it's just the only way I know to keep seeing you.
You can't just say it — say it with stakes. Otherwise it's just noise, isn't it?
I lost the ladder bet fair and square. Bought him a pint and hated every sip of it.

entries.summaryZh: 退休公交修复匠Robin总想押点什么，池边却给新认识的人明确的不押钱选择；猜鸟先飞先走也可随时停下。不参加则可看自有叶印或继续写明信片。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You write a postcard at the stone ledge by the pond. A few steps away, Robin watches a grey bird at the water’s edge.
beats.chinese: 你在池边石台写明信片。几步之外，罗宾正看着水边一只灰鸟。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I nearly offered a bet on that bird. Old habit. Would you fancy a guess instead — no money?
beats.chinese: 我差点想拿那只鸟打赌。老习惯了。要不要只猜一下，不押钱？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fly first or walk first. Or neither, if it stays there all day.
beats.chinese: 先飞还是先走。也可能两个都不选，要是它一直站着的话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin pulls a small battered notebook from a coat pocket, then thinks better of it and leaves it half-in.
beats.chinese: 罗宾从外套口袋里掏出一个磨旧的小本子，想了想又只掏出一半。

choices.english: Agree to guess — will the bird fly off or walk off?
choices.chinese: 同意猜一下：鸟会先飞走还是先走开？

choices.english: Say you'd rather not bet on it.
choices.chinese: 表示不想打这个赌。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin nods slowly, like a bookmaker accepting a sensible wager, and closes the notebook without writing anything.
beats.chinese: 罗宾缓缓点头，像个接受了合理赌注的庄家，没写什么就把本子合上了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. No stakes, just a guess. You take fly, I'll take walk. That's the whole rule, and I'm not changing it now.
beats.chinese: 好。不押钱，只猜。你押飞，我押走。规矩就这么定，我现在不改。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mind, a no-stakes bet is like tea without a drop of whiskey in it. Drinkable. But you wonder why you bothered.
beats.chinese: 不过话说回来，没赌注的赌就像没加一滴威士忌的茶。能喝，但你不知道图什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The bird shifts its weight. Neither of them moves. Robin leans an elbow on the stone ledge, settling in like it's a match worth watching.
beats.chinese: 那只鸟挪了挪重心。两人都没动。罗宾把胳膊肘撑在石台上，安顿下来，像在看一场值得看的比赛。

choices.english: Wait a little while and watch for the result.
choices.chinese: 等一小会儿，看结果。

choices.english: Say you're not waiting for the result after all.
choices.chinese: 表示现在不想等结果了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin's smile flattens for exactly a moment, then comes back crooked. The notebook goes back in the pocket, all the way this time.
beats.chinese: 罗宾的笑容塌了一瞬，又歪着回来了。本子这次被完整地放回了口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough, no betting. Some people like their weather forecasts unbetted. Suit yourself.
beats.chinese: 行，不打就不打。有些人喜欢不押注的天气预报。随你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin takes a folded sheet of good paper from an inner pocket and opens it on the stone ledge: a leaf print, veins inked in deep green.
beats.chinese: 罗宾从内袋里取出一张折好的好纸，在石台上摊开：一张叶拓，叶脉印着深绿色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Since we're not gambling, I'll show you something honest instead. Held up better than most of my bets do.
beats.chinese: 既然不打赌，我就给你看点实在的。它比我的大多数赌局都靠谱。

choices.english: Ask how the leaf print was made.
choices.chinese: 问这张叶拓是怎么做出来的。

choices.english: Go back to writing your postcard.
choices.chinese: 继续写自己的明信片。

beats.speaker: narrator
