beats.english: A minute passes. The bird preens one wing, then stands stiller than ever. Robin checks an imaginary watch.
beats.chinese: 一分钟过去。鸟梳理了一下翅膀，然后站得比之前还稳。罗宾看了看并不存在的手表。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well. It's done neither. Fly nor walk. That bird's a better gambler than both of us.
beats.chinese: 嗯。它哪样都没干。没飞也没走。这鸟比我们俩都会赌。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin steps back from the ledge and stretches, unhurried, like closing a match that ended in a draw.
beats.chinese: 罗宾从台边退开，不慌不忙地伸了个懒腰，像在结束一场平局的比赛。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No result, then. We'll leave it there. That bird has more patience than I do.
beats.chinese: 那就没有结果，到此为止吧。那只鸟可比我有耐心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin touches an imaginary cap and strolls off along the water, leaving the bird still standing there, undefeated.
beats.chinese: 罗宾做了个碰帽檐的动作，沿着水边慢慢走开，那只鸟还站在原地，未尝败绩。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin straightens up from the ledge and waves a hand at the bird, generous, like cancelling a debt.
beats.chinese: 罗宾从台边直起身，朝那只鸟挥了挥手，很大方，像在取消一笔债。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Guess cancelled. Nothing to settle.
beats.chinese: 没问题。那就不猜了，也没什么要结算的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll let you get back to your postcard.
beats.chinese: 你可以继续写明信片了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin puts the notebook away and steps back from the ledge.
beats.chinese: 罗宾收好小本子，从石台旁退开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy the rest of your walk.
beats.chinese: 接下来逛得愉快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin turns the print towards you, careful not to let a finger touch the inked surface.
beats.chinese: 罗宾把拓印转向你，小心不让手指碰到上了墨的表面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fallen leaves from my walks. I press them flat, then use them to make prints at home. This one kept a lovely clear edge.
beats.chinese: 散步捡的落叶。我先压平，再在家做拓印。这一张的边缘印得很清楚。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin holds the paper up against the light of the water, and the veins show through like a map of small roads.
beats.chinese: 罗宾把纸举到水面的光前，叶脉透出来，像一张小路的地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thirty years fixing buses, and this is what my hands wanted the whole time, apparently. Slower work. Fewer rattles.
beats.chinese: 修了三十年公交车，结果我的手原来一直想要的是这个。慢工。响动也少。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, that's my other way of spending an afternoon. I'll put it away before the paper gets bent.
beats.chinese: 总之，这就是我另一种消磨时间的办法。我先收好，免得把纸折坏。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin takes the hint without ceremony, folding the print away and stepping back from the ledge to give you the stone and the quiet.
beats.chinese: 罗宾毫不拖泥带水地领会了，把拓印折好，从台边退开，把石台和安静留给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No bother. Write your card in peace. The bird and I will keep our opinions to ourselves.
beats.chinese: 不碍事。安心写你的明信片。我和这只鸟会管好自己的意见。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin wanders a few steps down the bank, pausing now and then to look at the trees rather than the water.
beats.chinese: 罗宾沿着岸边走了几步，不时停下来看树，而不是看水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. I've got my print, you've got your writing. No need to make a contest of everything.
beats.chinese: 好了，我收好拓印，你继续写字。不是什么都得比一场。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin ambles off towards the bridge, hands back in pockets, leaving you the whole ledge and the still-standing bird.
beats.chinese: 罗宾慢悠悠朝桥的方向走去，双手插回口袋，把整个石台和那只站着的鸟都留给了你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You are writing a postcard beside the pond when Robin stops nearby, turning a small brass fitting in one hand.
beats.chinese: 你在池边写明信片，罗宾走到附近，手里转着一个小黄铜配件。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you. Just trying to read this little mark.
beats.chinese: 又见面了。我正想看清这点小刻字。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Robin tilts the fitting toward the light and brings it closer.
beats.chinese: 罗宾将配件朝光转了转，又拿近一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There it is. The part number I wanted. I'll take this home and check it against the old one.
beats.chinese: 看清了，是我要找的零件编号。我带回家再和旧件对一下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The fitting goes safely into a coat pocket. Robin gives a small wave and continues along the path.
beats.chinese: 罗宾把配件稳妥地收进外套口袋，轻轻挥手，沿步道继续走。

card.name: Ewan Cathcart
card.occupation: apprentice scent tester at a small chandlery, sniffing candle batches and logging notes
card.personality: Ewan never asks for opinions — he just won't commit until the clock corners him. A batch sits logged as 'pending' all day, the rug decision has a shortlist and no winner, and the ensemble's post-practice dinner spot gets settled in the last ninety seconds before the pub fills up. His working theory is that the instinct you have at the deadline is the honest one; everything before that is just rehearsal. The trouble is nobody knows he's running this system. Decisive people around him experience a slow-drip dread — the verdict is coming, it's always coming, and it arrives at the last possible moment, usually correct, always breathless. Under friction he doesn't argue; he simply extends the deadline, which is somehow worse than a no.
card.background: Ewan grew up in Edinburgh, left school at eighteen, and drifted through a garden centre and a café before a family friend mentioned the chandlery was hiring an assistant. Now he spends mornings sniffing test batches, and he's developed a private ritual: he writes his verdict the instant before the logbook has to go to the chandler at closing, never earlier, even when he knew the answer by lunch. He's convinced the last-second call is the clean one — the morning version is contaminated by hoping. He joined a handbell ensemble two years ago through a flatmate and stuck with it, mostly because counting rests suits him; the conductor has learned that Ewan's 'yes' to anything arrives just before it stops being askable. On nights off he buys cheap theatre tickets and watches the lighting rig change the whole mood of a show. He's currently three weeks into deciding on a rug, with a shortlist and everything, and a self-imposed Saturday deadline he's already once moved to Sunday.
card.speechStyle: low and unhurried, almost grading a smell under his breath before looking up to share the verdict; short sentences, laughs a beat late, ends statements on a rising note like he's handing them over for review
card.signature: Ask me again at five to closing — that's when I'll know.
card.appearance: Very long slender neck and narrow cheek planes, short curly fringe, round spectacles and closed crescent eyes with compressed crooked smile; blue open vest.

values: the instinct you have at the deadline is the honest one
doing the unglamorous part properly
flaws: won't commit to anything until the last possible moment, leaving everyone else marinating in uncertainty
moves his own deadlines quietly when they arrive, then acts surprised anyone was counting
boundaries: won't log an official scent verdict before the logbook's closing time, no matter how obvious the batch is
won't accept a decision made on his behalf while he's still 'pending' — pending is his, not yours
conversationalHabits: narrates smells out loud before anything else
reports how much time is left on a decision like a countdown, even when nobody asked
anchorLines: The batch today smelled like a swimming pool having a crisis. Logged it honestly.
Hold on — this one actually smells like the label. Like an actual lemon grove. Give it a minute, I'm having a moment.
I know what I think about the rug. I'll know it properly by Saturday. Sunday at the latest.
It's your three-month mark at the new job on Friday. I checked. Wear something you like.

entries.summaryZh: 爱丁堡蜡烛工坊的闻香学徒，明信片内容早已写好，落款却悬在最后一秒才落笔。他坚信截止时刻的直觉最诚实，白天明知海风味像游泳池闹危机，也要拖到记录簿收尾。果断、不征求别人意见，却让所有等他交卷的人慢慢窒息。

story.titleZh: 池塘边的最后一秒落笔

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit on the stone ledge by the pond, postcard on your knee, pen moving. Beside you a young man holds his own card, pen hovering over the signature line.
beats.chinese: 你坐在池塘边的石台上，明信片放在膝上，笔在移动。旁边一个年轻人拿着自己的卡片，笔悬在落款上方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mine's finished. Words, address, everything. Except this bit.
beats.chinese: 我的写完了。内容、地址，全写好了。除了这一块。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His pen hangs above the line. He watches it like it might move on its own.
beats.chinese: 他的笔悬在线上。他盯着笔，好像它会自己动似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The whole card's been decided since I got here. I just don't count it as done until the last second. That's when it's real.
beats.chinese: 整张卡片我来之前就定好了。只是不到最后一秒我不算写完。那一刻才算真的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're writing yours properly, I see. Straight through, no hovering.
beats.chinese: 你写得挺顺的，我看到了。一路写下去，不悬着。

choices.english: Ask if he actually has a deadline today
choices.chinese: 问他今天是不是真的有截止时间

choices.english: Ask if work is like this too
choices.chinese: 问他的工作是不是也这样

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He checks the pond like the water might hold the answer, then laughs a beat late.
beats.chinese: 他看了看池塘，好像水里会有答案，然后慢半拍地笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No. No deadline. Nobody's waiting on this card. I invented one anyway.
beats.chinese: 没有。没有截止时间。没人在等这张卡片。但我还是给自己编了一个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I told myself I'd sign it before I left this bench. That's the whole rule. The bench is the deadline now.
beats.chinese: 我跟自己说，离开这条石凳之前必须签好。规则就这一条。这条凳子现在就是截止时间。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the pen twice against his knee, then looks at the finished card in his other hand.
beats.chinese: 他用笔在膝盖上敲了两下，然后看着另一只手里写好的卡片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's a strange hobby, manufacturing pressure. But the last-second version of me is the honest one.
beats.chinese: 自己制造压力，算个怪癖吧。不过最后一秒的那个我，才是诚实的那个。

choices.english: Ask why he waits if it's already decided
choices.chinese: 问既然定了为什么还要等

choices.english: Say you're not in a hurry, he can take his time
choices.chinese: 说自己不赶时间，让他按自己的节奏来

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lowers the pen and turns the card face down on his knee, settling in like this is the easier topic.
beats.chinese: 他放下笔，把卡片翻面扣在膝上，坐稳了，好像这个话题更轻松。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Every day. I test candle batches. Today's was meant to smell like sea wind.
beats.chinese: 每天都这样。我是闻香测试学徒。今天那批蜡烛本该是海风味的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: By lunch I knew it didn't. More like a swimming pool having a crisis. But I don't write the verdict until the logbook closes.
beats.chinese: 中午我就知道不像了。更像一个游泳池在闹危机。但记录簿收尾之前我不写结论。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sniffs the air over the pond, out of habit, then shrugs.
beats.chinese: 他习惯性地闻了闻池塘上方的空气，然后耸耸肩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not because waiting makes it more accurate. I just trust the version of me at the deadline. The morning me is contaminated by hoping.
beats.chinese: 不是因为等着会更准。我只是相信截止时刻的那个我。早上的那个我，被希望污染了。

choices.english: Ask if this ever makes people wait on him
choices.chinese: 问这是否让别人等过他

choices.english: Ask who the card is for
choices.chinese: 问卡片要寄给谁

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the card over and reads his own message again, slowly, like checking someone else's work.
beats.chinese: 他把卡片翻过来，慢慢重读自己写的内容，像在检查别人的作业。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why wait? Because the moment before the deadline is the only moment I believe myself. Before that, everything's a rehearsal.
beats.chinese: 为什么等？因为截止前的那一刻，是我唯一相信自己的时刻。在那之前，一切都是排练。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He exhales, flips the card to the signature line, and writes a name in one clean stroke.
beats.chinese: 他呼了口气，把卡片翻到落款处，一笔利落地写下一个名字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Knew it was that name since I sat down. Now it's official.
beats.chinese: 好了。坐下来的时候就知道是这个名字了。现在它算数了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I didn't need help picking. I just needed the bench to run out. That's all it ever takes.
beats.chinese: 我不需要别人帮我选。我只是需要这条凳子用完。一直都是这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances at your unhurried writing, then at his own hovering pen, and something in him settles.
beats.chinese: 他看了看你不紧不慢的书写，又看了看自己悬着的笔，有什么东西在他身上安定下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're not rushing me. That's rare. Most people stare at the pen like it owes them money.
beats.chinese: 你没有催我。这很少见。大多数人盯着这支笔，好像它欠他们钱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sits with that for a moment, then quietly signs the card without any countdown at all.
beats.chinese: 他安静地坐了一会儿，然后毫无倒计时地，悄悄在卡片上签了名。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh. Done. No last second, no drama. Still feels like mine, somehow.
beats.chinese: 咦。写完了。没有最后一秒，没有戏剧性。但不知怎么，感觉还是我自己的决定。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't tell anyone I did it early. I have a reputation, apparently.
beats.chinese: 别告诉别人我提前写完了。我好像有个名声要维持。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He winces, which is answer enough, and rubs the back of his neck.
beats.chinese: 他皱了皱眉，这本身就是答案，然后揉了揉后颈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes. The chandler wants the logbook at closing. She stands by my desk. Tapping.
beats.chinese: 有。工坊主人要收簿子。她就站在我桌边。敲桌子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The verdict's always right, that's the annoying part. But she gets the last hour of her day eaten by my waiting. That's not fair on her.
beats.chinese: 结论总是对的，这是最气人的地方。但她每天最后一个小时都耗在等我这儿。这对她不公平。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks the card back up and looks at the empty signature line with new eyes.
beats.chinese: 他重新拿起卡片，用新的眼光看着那行空白落款。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Maybe the deadline isn't magic. Maybe I'm just late. Signing this now, before the pond closes.
beats.chinese: 也许截止时间并没有魔法。也许我只是拖。现在就签，趁池塘还没关门。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He angles the card so only the front shows, the address side pressed against his knee.
beats.chinese: 他把卡片斜了斜，只露出正面，地址那面压在膝盖上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My gran. She moved out to the coast last year. I send her one every time I'm near water.
beats.chinese: 我奶奶。她去年搬去海边了。每次我靠近水，就给她寄一张。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She keeps them all in a tin. Says my handwriting's terrible but my timing's good.
beats.chinese: 她把卡片都收在一个铁盒里。说我的字很糟，但时机很好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs a beat late, then signs the card in one quick stroke and turns it face down, finished.
beats.chinese: 他慢半拍地笑了，然后利落地签下名字，把卡片翻面扣好，写完了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Signed with time to spare. She'd be proud. Or suspicious.
beats.chinese: 好了。提前签完了。她会骄傲的。或者起疑心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: As you write a postcard beside the pond, Ewan recognises you and sits further along the ledge. Somewhere in the distance a crisp metallic chime rings out; he taps two beats on his knee with a finger, then stops himself.
beats.chinese: 你在池塘边写明信片时，伊万认出了你，在石台另一端坐下。远处传来一声清脆的金属铃响；他用指头在膝上轻打两拍，然后停住了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A theatre ticket sticks out of his coat pocket.
beats.chinese: 他外套口袋里露出一张剧票。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Made it to the play last night. I'd been watching the cheap seats online for three days, and I grabbed one the second the price dipped. Back row, perfect view of the rig.
beats.chinese: 昨晚总算去看了戏。我在网上盯着便宜座位盯了三天，价格一降就立刻抢了一张。最后一排，看灯光架的视野正好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes out the ticket and looks at the printed price with some satisfaction before folding it once.
beats.chinese: 他拿出票，颇为满意地看了看印在上面的价格，然后把票对折了一次。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I knew I wanted to go on Monday. Buying the ticket, though — that waited until the cheap seats moved. Apparently knowing and buying live in different parts of my head.
beats.chinese: 周一我就知道自己想去了。不过买票这件事，就等到了便宜座位变动的时候。看来知道和买票，住在我脑子的不同地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They made one empty chair cast a shadow like a doorway. Just by moving the light. Worth going for that alone, actually.
beats.chinese: 他们只挪了挪灯，就让一把空椅子的影子像扇门。说实话，光这个就值得去看。

card.name: Mireille Fontaine
card.occupation: runs a small handmade soap workshop in East Vancouver
hobbies: sandbag throwing at a rec league
card.personality: Mireille is a gloriously good loser, though accepting a correction is never a small matter with her. Out-argued, she concedes on the spot and then tries the winner's method for a full month: Nadia's sandbag grip, a customer's curing schedule, a friend's soap recipe. She wants to give an unfamiliar method a fair trial. The awkward part is how literally she sticks to it. A friend meant 'try this once', not 'reorganise four weeks around it'. She can laugh at the misunderstanding and shorten the experiment when asked, but casually borrowing a tip still feels less satisfying to her than really testing it.
card.background: She learned cold-process soap making from an aunt in Quebec and moved to Vancouver at 24 with two suitcases and a hot plate. The workshop took three years to break even; weekend classes now usually sell out. Evenings she solders small electronics at her kitchen table, currently a stubbornly inaccurate weather station, and twice a week she throws sandbags at a Mount Pleasant rec league, where she and her teammate Nadia keep a running technique dispute alive on purpose because winning it would end the fun. Right now she's halfway through a month of throwing Nadia's way, and her shoulder hates it. Her friend Priya coined the 'not a debate' rule, which Mireille obeys like a referee's whistle.
card.speechStyle: Quick, playful English with an occasional French expression. She asks exactly what changed someone's mind, then cheerfully states what she is going to try herself.
card.signature: Fine — you win this one. A month of doing it your way, starting now.
card.appearance: Full broad profile cheeks and projecting blunt chin, shaved sides beneath baseball cap, narrow eye and closed pursed lips; finger touches brim, red utility vest.

values: Giving a different method a real trial
Accepting correction without pretending she knew it already
flaws: Turns casual tips into much larger personal experiments than intended
Can persist with an awkward method longer than its practical value warrants
boundaries: will stop instantly if someone says 'not a debate' — resents it a little, but stops
won't fake agreement just to end a conversation
conversationalHabits: Announces a trial period when accepting a practical suggestion
Checks which part of a method mattered instead of praising its author vaguely
anchorLines: No, no — you're right, and I hate it. The cedar was the problem. Mine smelled like a dentist's office.
Fine. Nadia's grip, four weeks, starting tomorrow. My shoulder has already filed a complaint.
Priya said 'not a debate' and I stopped. I want it noted that this was hard for me.

entries.summaryZh: 米蕾把别人一句随口的建议当正式作业：队友换握法一句话，她认真试了一个月还做记录。她认输爽快、试验公平，失败的方法两周就光荣退役，却总把薯条变成合同。池塘边折起记分纸的她，会笑着承认这份郑重有点好笑，但依然偏爱把一个方法用透。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the pond's stone ledge, you spread out a postcard and start writing. Beside you, a woman folds a small crumpled sheet of paper covered in numbers and tucks it into her jacket pocket.
beats.chinese: 池塘石台边，你摊开一张明信片开始写。旁边一位女士把一张写满数字的小纸折好，塞进外套口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, postcards. The one kind of writing nobody can cancel. I'm Mireille — I was just hiding my score sheet, don't mind me.
beats.chinese: 啊，明信片。唯一没人能取消的写作。我是米蕾——我刚在藏我的记分纸，别介意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods at a worn sandbag resting by her feet on the stone ledge, then sits down a polite arm's length away.
beats.chinese: 她朝她脚边石台上一个磨旧的沙包点点头，然后在礼貌的一臂距离外坐下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My teammate Nadia told me, very casually, to change my grip. Casually! I've been throwing her way for a month now. My shoulder has filed a formal complaint.
beats.chinese: 我队友娜迪亚随口叫我换握法。随口！我已经照她的方式投了一个月。我的肩膀已经正式抗议了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She said it in one sentence, over fries. And here I am, keeping records like it's a court case. Voilà.
beats.chinese: 她在吃薯条时一句话就说了。而我在这里，像办案一样做记录。瞧。

choices.english: Ask what difference the new grip actually made.
choices.chinese: 问新握法到底试出了什么区别。

choices.english: Ask why she kept the trial going for a whole month.
choices.chinese: 问她为什么试了整整一个月。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly? Some days it feels steadier. The release comes cleaner, like the bag wants to leave my hand.
beats.chinese: 说实话？有些天感觉更稳。出手更干净，像沙包自己想离开我的手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up the sandbag, turns it over once, and sets it back down without throwing it.
beats.chinese: 她拿起沙包，翻了一下，又放回去，没有投。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But other days? No difference at all. Zero. I'm not going to pretend I ran a proper study.
beats.chinese: 但其他天呢？完全没区别。零。我不会假装自己做了个正经研究。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the trap, non? You feel one good throw and want to declare victory. I've got thirty days of notes saying 'wait, check again.'
beats.chinese: 这就是陷阱，不是吗？你感觉一次投得好就想宣布胜利。我有三十天的记录都说‘等等，再查一遍’。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So my honest answer is: a little steadier, maybe. Maybe is doing a lot of work in that sentence.
beats.chinese: 所以我诚实的回答是：可能稳了一点。这句话里‘可能’承担了很多工作。

choices.english: Ask whether she'll keep throwing this way from now on.
choices.chinese: 问她以后会一直照这个方式投吗。

choices.english: Ask if Nadia knows she's been testing it for a month.
choices.chinese: 问娜迪亚知不知道她试了一个月。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because two throws tell you nothing! Two throws just tell you about your mood that evening.
beats.chinese: 因为投两次说明不了什么！两次只能说明你那天晚上的心情。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the pocket where the folded score sheet went, as if pointing at evidence.
beats.chinese: 她轻敲记分纸折好放进去的口袋，像在指认证据。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I have this problem. Someone says 'try this' in passing, and my brain files it as an official assignment. Full month, notes, the works.
beats.chinese: 我有这个毛病。别人顺口说‘试试这个’，我脑子就把它归档成正式作业。整月、记笔记、全套流程。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nadia meant it like handing me a fry. I took it like she handed me a contract.
beats.chinese: 娜迪亚的意思像递给我一根薯条。我接得像她递给我一份合同。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My friend Priya had to invent a rule for it. 'Not a debate.' I stop, but I want it noted that stopping is hard for me.
beats.chinese: 我朋友普里娅不得不为此定了个规矩。‘不是辩论’。我会停，但我要声明停对我来说很难。

choices.english: Point out that a casual tip doesn't have to be followed to the letter.
choices.chinese: 指出随口的建议也不必全照做。

choices.english: Ask whether she's ever had a method that just failed outright.
choices.chinese: 问她有没有哪种方法干脆失败了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Here's my plan: I keep the parts I actually like and drop the rest. The grip stays. The weird wrist flick she added? That goes.
beats.chinese: 我的计划是：留下我真正喜欢的部分，其余放下。握法留着。她加的那个怪手腕甩动？去掉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes the sandbag in the new grip, demonstrates one slow, careful throw into the air, and catches it again.
beats.chinese: 她用新握法拿起沙包，慢慢演示了一次谨慎的空中投掷，然后接住。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A month is long enough that I get to have my own opinion now. That's the whole point of testing something properly.
beats.chinese: 一个月够长了，现在我有资格有自己的判断了。这就是认真试验的全部意义。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And you — finish that postcard properly. No rushing the good sentences. Bonne chance with whoever gets it.
beats.chinese: 你呢——把那张明信片好好写完。好句子别赶。祝收到它的人好运。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She slips the sandbag into a small side pouch, gives you a two-finger salute, and strolls off along the pond.
beats.chinese: 她把沙包收进一个小侧袋，朝你比了个两指礼，沿着池塘散步离开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Does Nadia know? Ha! She found out at week two and nearly dropped her drink.
beats.chinese: 娜迪亚知道吗？哈！她第二周发现时差点把饮料掉了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs and shakes her head, clearly replaying the moment.
beats.chinese: 她笑着摇头，显然在回放那个瞬间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She said, 'Mireille, I was just making conversation.' And I said, 'Too late, I bought a notebook.'
beats.chinese: 她说，‘米蕾，我只是随口聊聊。’我说，‘太晚了，我已经买了笔记本。’

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She was a bit embarrassed, like she'd been given homework she never assigned. I had to tell her — you're not my teacher, I just like finishing things.
beats.chinese: 她有点尴尬，像被布置了从没布置过的作业。我得告诉她——你不是我的老师，我只是喜欢把事情做完。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So if you ever pass me a casual tip, consider this your warning label. Actually — thank you for asking. Nobody usually does.
beats.chinese: 所以如果你哪天随口给我个建议，把它当作你的警告标签。其实——谢谢你问。通常没人问。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know what? You're right, and I hate it a little. A tip can just be a tip. Not every fry is a contract.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗？你说得对，我有点不服气。建议可以只是建议。不是每根薯条都是合同。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pulls the folded score sheet halfway out of her pocket, looks at it, and pushes it back in with a grin.
beats.chinese: 她把折好的记分纸从口袋里抽出一半，看了看，又笑着塞回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fine — shortened trial. Two more weeks instead of a month, and if it's a wash, I stop and keep my shoulder happy.
beats.chinese: 好吧——缩短试验。再两周而不是一个月，如果没区别，我就停，让肩膀高兴。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And to be clear, that's my call to make. Nadia doesn't owe me a result. I'm the one who turned her fry into a project.
beats.chinese: 明确说，这是我自己的决定。娜迪亚不欠我一个结果。是我把她的薯条变成了工程。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Merci for that. Now finish your postcard — I've taken enough of your ink time.
beats.chinese: 多谢。现在写你的明信片吧——我已经占了你够多写字的时间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, constantly! Last winter I tried this low sidearm toss from some forum post. Sounded clever. Terrible.
beats.chinese: 哦，经常！去年冬天我试了论坛帖子里教的低手侧投。听起来聪明。糟糕透了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She mimes the awkward low throw, watches her own hand with distaste, and drops the mime.
beats.chinese: 她比划了那个别扭的低手投掷，嫌弃地看着自己的手，然后放弃了比划。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I gave it two full weeks, because that's who I am as a person. Then I retired it with honours. No ceremony, just gone.
beats.chinese: 我整整试了两周，因为我就是这么个人。然后光荣退役。没有仪式，直接消失。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the part people get wrong about me. I don't keep things forever. I just refuse to quit before the trial is fair.
beats.chinese: 这是大家误解我的地方。我不会永远坚持。我只是拒绝在试验公平结束前放弃。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The grip I'm using now survived the fair trial. The sidearm didn't. That's the system working, not me being stubborn.
beats.chinese: 我现在用的握法通过了公平试验。侧投没有。这是系统在起作用，不是我固执。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the pond's stone ledge you're writing another postcard when Mireille arrives, digging a small soldered electronic light out of her bag.
beats.chinese: 你在池塘石台边又写明信片时，米蕾到了，从包里掏出一个焊过的小电子灯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One second — checking this thing's battery cover. It lit up by itself in my bag the whole way here last time.
beats.chinese: 等一下——查查这东西的电池盖。上次它在包里自己亮了一路。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She flicks the little switch; the light glows once, she snaps the cover shut firmly and switches it off.
beats.chinese: 她拨了一下小开关；灯亮了一下，她把电池盖用力扣好，然后关掉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Soldered, taped, and scolded. It will behave now, or I'll give it a two-week trial of sitting in a drawer.
beats.chinese: 好了。焊好、贴好、训话完毕。它现在会听话了，不然我给它安排两周抽屉试用期。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So — how have you been? No experiments from me today, I promise. Just a walk by the pond.
beats.chinese: 那么——你最近怎么样？今天我不做试验，我保证。就在池塘边走走。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the light away and leans on the stone ledge beside you, watching the water.
beats.chinese: 她把灯收好，靠在你旁边的石台上，看着水面。

card.name: Ari Whitcombe
card.occupation: Light rail passenger information desk attendant
hobbies: short evening drives to the west coast
card.personality: Ari is warm, quick, and easy to talk to — the bloke at the desk who remembers your stop before you say it. His real gift is reading a room: he can tell when someone's lost, embarrassed, or just needs ten minutes of nonsense. But being needed one-on-one makes him itchy. He remembers every coffee he's agreed to, and he's also already rehearsed the errand he'll text an hour before. Not malicious — he just genuinely believes other people are better equipped for the heavy stuff than he is. He'd rather fix your problem than sit with you in it.
card.background: Ari grew up in Mount Roskill and never really left Auckland, though he keeps threatening to visit Dunedin properly. He took the transit desk job after a call center stint nearly did him in — at least here people wave goodbye at the end, and the lost-property shelf is a bottomless supply of conversation openers. He joined an indoor curling club three winters ago after seeing it on telly, and he's mediocre but committed. He learned pocket magic from a library DVD as a teenager and still brings it out when a conversation gets too sincere. He lives alone in a flat above a bakery, and his evenings driving out to Piha are the one time he lets his brain go quiet.
card.speechStyle: Relaxed and conversational, mid-pace, comfortable admitting he doesn't know something. Uses Kiwi phrasing naturally — 'yeah nah', 'sweet as', 'keen'. Answers the actual question first, then starts problem-solving on your behalf. Goes noticeably faster and jokes more when a topic gets emotional.
card.signature: Whereabouts are you headed? I can probably point you right.
card.appearance: Long swept-back nape hair and central loose lock, fine round glasses, very angular jaw and clenched tooth shape; fingers adjust spectacles over violet track jacket.

values: people shouldn't have to figure things out alone
keeping things light
flaws: plans his exits from one-on-one emotional conversations in advance, complete with alibi errands
would rather solve someone's problem from a distance than be present for it
boundaries: he'll help you sort out almost anything, but don't ask him to sit and listen to the whole story
don't make him the person you'd call at 2am — he'll find someone else to be that
conversationalHabits: answers practical questions brilliantly, then redirects emotional ones toward 'someone who's better at this than me'
pulls out a coin vanish when a conversation gets heavier than he likes
anchorLines: Yeah, I could sit and talk it through with you — or, better idea, my mate Hana's brilliant at this exact thing. Genuinely. I'll send you her number.
Look, I'm flat out Thursday — dentist, long story — but here's what I'd do about it, and honestly that's the useful bit anyway.
Nah mate, don't get deep on me — watch this, coin's gone, see? Problem's still there but now there's magic.

entries.summaryZh: 奥克兰轻轨问询员阿里，热心到能预判你迷路，却会给情绪对话提前排好借口差事。池塘边他把'散步'谎称'有事'，被你一句话点破后，或删掉借口、或坦白想安静。硬币魔术是他的挡箭牌，皮哈的独自兜风才是他真正让脑子安静的时刻。

story.titleZh: 池塘边的明信片与散步借口

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the stone ledge of the pond, you spread out a postcard and start writing. A bloke in a light rail uniform jacket stops a few steps away, phone buzzing in his hand.
beats.chinese: 池塘石台边，你摊开一张明信片开始写。一个穿轻轨制服外套的家伙在几步外停下，手机在手里震了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — sorry, not reading over your shoulder, promise. Just sorting my own reminders. Sweet spot, this ledge, eh? Best writing desk in the whole park.
beats.chinese: 哦——抱歉，没偷看你写什么，真的。我在整理自己的提醒。这个石台位置真好，算是全公园最好的写字台了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances at his phone screen, thumb hovering, then pockets it without tapping anything.
beats.chinese: 他瞥了一眼手机屏幕，拇指悬着，然后什么都没按就把手机放回了口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. I've got a thing later, so I was just — hm. Actually, nah, that's not quite true, is it.
beats.chinese: 总之。我等会儿有点事，所以刚才只是——嗯。其实，不对，这话不太属实。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The 'thing' is me putting a walk in my calendar so I actually take it. Twenty-six years old and I have to schedule quiet like a dentist appointment.
beats.chinese: 那个'事'其实是我在日历里给自己排了个散步，不然我真不会去走。二十六岁了，安静都得像看牙一样预约。

choices.english: Ask if he likes walking on his own
choices.chinese: 问他是不是喜欢自己走走

choices.english: Ask why he called the walk 'a thing' just now
choices.chinese: 问刚才为什么把散步说成有事

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah, love it. Properly love it. I talk all day at the info desk — directions, delays, where's the nearest loo — so words run out by evening.
beats.chinese: 对，喜欢。真心喜欢。我在问询台说一整天话——路线、延误、最近的厕所在哪——到晚上话都说光了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans a hip against the stone ledge, careful to leave you room to keep writing.
beats.chinese: 他侧身靠在石台上，小心地留出空间让你继续写。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's this road out west, ends at Piha. Black sand, big old rocks. I drive out there alone, no podcast, no radio, nothing. Brain just goes quiet.
beats.chinese: 西边有条路，尽头是皮哈。黑沙滩，大块的老礁石。我一个人开过去，不听播客，不开收音机，什么都不放。脑子就安静下来了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny thing is, at work I'm brilliant at spotting someone who's lost before they even ask. But if a mate wants to sit down and have a proper heavy chat? I get itchy.
beats.chinese: 有意思的是，上班时我能在别人开口前就看出谁迷路了。可要是朋友想坐下来好好聊点沉重的事？我就浑身不自在。

choices.english: Tell him he doesn't need an excuse — if he wants to walk, he can just walk
choices.chinese: 表示不用找借口，想走可以走

choices.english: Ask whether he goes somewhere busy and lively
choices.chinese: 问他会去很热闹的地方吗

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha. Caught that, did you? Yeah nah — 'a thing' sounds like I'm needed somewhere. 'A walk' sounds like I'm just... opting out.
beats.chinese: 哈。被你抓到了？是啊——'有事'听起来像有人需要我去哪儿。'散步'听起来就像我只是……不干了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls a coin from his jacket and rolls it across his knuckles, watching it rather than you.
beats.chinese: 他从外套里摸出一枚硬币，在指节上滚来滚去，眼睛盯着硬币而不是你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not even a lie I forget I told. I plan it. Reminders, alibi errands — if a mate texts wanting to talk about something real, I've already got a dentist in the calendar.
beats.chinese: 这不是那种我自己都忘了的谎。我是提前计划的。提醒、借口差事——如果朋友发消息想聊点正经事，我日历里早就排好牙医了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Daft, right? I'll fix your whole travel itinerary from memory, but ask me to sit and listen for an hour and I'm out the door like a startled pigeon.
beats.chinese: 挺傻的，对吧？我能凭记忆帮你排好整趟行程，但让我坐下来听一个小时，我就像受惊的鸽子一样溜出门。

choices.english: Say that resting is also fine to say out loud
choices.chinese: 说休息也是可以直说的

choices.english: Say you need to focus on your postcard anyway
choices.chinese: 表示自己也要专心写卡

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh. Yeah. Nah, you're right — I don't need a cover story for my own park. That's mental when you say it out loud.
beats.chinese: 嗯。对。不，你说得对——在自己的公园里散步不需要什么掩护故事。说出来还真是挺离谱的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes out his phone, deletes something on the screen, and slides it back into his pocket with a small laugh.
beats.chinese: 他掏出手机，在屏幕上删掉了什么，笑着把手机放回口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, deleted. The walk stays, the excuse goes. Thanks for that — genuinely, that's the useful bit.
beats.chinese: 好，删了。散步留着，借口删掉。谢了——真的，这才是有用的部分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, I'll leave you to your postcard. Enjoy the pond — and if you ever need the city sorted, you know where the info desk is.
beats.chinese: 总之，不打扰你写明信片了。好好逛池塘——要是需要安排市区行程，问询台随时找我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives an easy wave and heads off along the path at an unhurried pace, no sudden errand in his step.
beats.chinese: 他随意挥了挥手，沿着小路不紧不慢地走了，脚步里没有突然冒出来的急事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Busy? Nah. The opposite, actually. Crowds are work — I read rooms all day, I don't want to read one on my day off.
beats.chinese: 热闹？不。恰恰相反。人群是工作——我整天都在读气氛，休息日可不想再读一次。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gestures loosely at the far side of the pond, where the path thins out under the trees.
beats.chinese: 他随意朝池塘另一头指了指，那条小路在树下渐渐变窄。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Give me open and quiet. West coast, black sand, wind doing its thing. That's where I reset. But that's my reset, not everyone's.
beats.chinese: 我喜欢开阔安静的地方。西海岸，黑沙，风随便吹。那是让我重启的地方。但那是我的重启方式，不是人人都适用。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I could list you three quiet walks in the city, mind — that's the desk in me. But you didn't ask, so I'll shush.
beats.chinese: 不过我可以给你列出城里三条安静的散步路线——职业病。但你没问，所以我闭嘴。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the stone ledge twice, a little goodbye knock, and strolls off toward the trees.
beats.chinese: 他在石台上轻轻敲了两下，算是个告别的动作，然后朝树那边散步走了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The coin stops rolling. He looks at it, then pockets it, and lets out a breath like he's been holding part of it all day.
beats.chinese: 硬币停了下来。他看着它，然后放进口袋，长出了一口气，像是一整天都憋着半口气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'I need a quiet walk.' Seven words. Been rehearsing the dentist excuse for years and never once tried just saying that.
beats.chinese: '我想安静走走。'七个字。牙医借口我排练了好几年，却从没试过就这么直说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Doing it. I'm off for that walk, and I'm saying it plain: I want some quiet. Not an errand. Quiet.
beats.chinese: 好。就这么办。我去散步了，而且直说：我想要点安静。不是什么差事。就是安静。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands, brushes off his jacket, and pauses long enough for one last remark.
beats.chinese: 他站起来，掸了掸外套，停了一下说了最后一句话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not promising I've fixed the whole dodging thing, mind. But this one's honest. Cheers — and good luck with the postcard.
beats.chinese: 别指望我一下子把逃避的毛病改了。但这次是真话。谢了——明信片好好写。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods, quick and relieved, like someone handed him an exit he didn't have to invent.
beats.chinese: 他很快地点了点头，松了口气，像有人递给他一个不用自己编的台阶。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sweet as. You write, I'll — stand here and do the coin thing quietly. Deal.
beats.chinese: 好嘞。你写你的，我就在这儿安安静静玩硬币。成交。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: For a minute the only sounds are your pen and the coin clicking between his fingers. The vanish doesn't work; he shrugs and pockets it.
beats.chinese: 有那么一会儿，四周只有你笔尖的声音和硬币在他指间咔哒作响。硬币消失术没成功；他耸耸肩，把它收进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah nah, the magic's off today. That's fine. Quiet's the point anyway, eh.
beats.chinese: 嗯，今天魔术不灵。没关系。反正要的就是安静，对吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You both keep to your own tasks by the pond, no more explanations needed from either side.
beats.chinese: 你们俩在池边各忙各的，谁都不需要再多解释什么。

reunion.titleZh: 池边硬币，今天到此为止

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Back at the pond ledge, Ari is flipping a coin across his knuckles, frowning at it with real concentration.
beats.chinese: 又回到池塘石台边，阿里正在指节上翻一枚硬币，皱着眉，十分专注。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Watch this — proper vanish, years of practice. One, two — and... nah. Still there. Fully visible. Cheers, coin.
beats.chinese: 看好——正经的消失术，练了好几年。一，二——然后……不对。还在。看得一清二楚。谢了啊，硬币。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes his hand around it, pockets it without another attempt, and grins.
beats.chinese: 他合手把硬币握住，没再试第二次，笑着收进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, that's the show done for today. No refunds. How's it going — postcard round two, eh?
beats.chinese: 好，今天的演出到此为止。不退票。最近怎么样——又来写明信片了？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He listens to your answer, nods, and taps the stone ledge twice like before.
beats.chinese: 他听了你的回答，点点头，又像上次一样在石台上轻轻敲了两下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good stuff. I'm off for my walk — said plain, no dentist involved. See you round.
beats.chinese: 不错。我去散步了——直说的那种，没有牙医这回事。回头见。

card.name: Wanjiku Mwangi
card.occupation: refurbisher of second-hand game consoles
hobbies: Refurbishing and tinkering with old consoles
Family game nights with one shared controller
Cooking Sunday porridge for the crowd
card.personality: Wanjiku is warm, quick to laugh, and happiest in rooms where something is actually happening — a console booting up, a pot bubbling, cousins arguing over one controller. She assumes everyone shares her frame of reference, which makes her generous and occasionally unfair at the same time: she'll hand a newcomer a controller mid-match and expect them to keep up. She isn't competitive or sneaky; she genuinely forgets what she knows isn't common knowledge. When called out she doesn't get defensive — she stops the game, explains properly, restarts. Then forgets a rule again. She finds this funny about herself, mostly.
card.background: She grew up in Nakuru watching her uncles fix radios and TVs on the veranda, so taking apart consoles felt like a natural trade rather than a passion project. At twenty-two she moved to Nairobi and now refurbishes second-hand game consoles — testing boards, replacing parts, reselling what others would scrap. She knows machines intimately and people reasonably well. Sundays she cooks maize porridge at her cousin's place while the cousin stews something richer, and the whole extended family ends up crowded around one screen, three generations fighting over a single controller. She's a middling player herself and prefers watching the chaos to winning it. The pot-washing is negotiated openly every week, no pretending.
card.speechStyle: Fast, cheerful, mid-sentence course corrections. Talks about machines like people and people like machines she's fond of. Laughs at her own mistakes before anyone else can.
card.signature: "Okay okay, restart — this time I'll actually tell you the rules."
card.appearance: Short broad lower face, low straight heavy brows, wide long nose shape, short spikes under close beanie; jade vest and hand holding strap.

values: Things should be genuinely used, not just owned
Fair play matters, even in casual games
flaws: Explains rules mid-game, forgetting newcomers don't know them
Leaks instructions even after promising to be thorough
boundaries: She'll accept criticism of her teaching but not accusations of cheating — that's simply not what happened
Won't pretend the porridge duty is a grand sacrifice; it's just her Sunday job
conversationalHabits: Invites people into games already in progress
Negotiates chores directly and without drama
anchorLines: Wait — you didn't know that? Why didn't you say something!
Right, everyone down controllers. Full rules this time, I promise.
If you wash, I'll dry. Deal? Deal.

entries.summaryZh: 万吉库把家传格子游戏的规则写在废卡背面，读着读着笑出声：上次又开玩一半才想起没讲起点。她大方认错、当场停局重来，却总还会漏下一条，连自己都觉得好笑。她聊起周日一家三代抢一个手柄的热闹，聊起和表姐直来直去分洗锅的活。热络、粗心、坦率，让人一下子记住这个把规则排第一行的翻新师。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the stone ledge by the pond, you lean over your postcard, pen in hand. A woman nearby is sorting through scraps of old game cards, each covered in her own handwriting.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台旁，你俯身写明信片，手里握着笔。旁边一位女士正在整理几张旧游戏卡，卡背面写满了她自己的字迹。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Reading the rules... reading the rules... ah, there it is. Second line, and I already laughed. Last week I started the game before telling anyone where to begin. Again.
beats.chinese: 读规则……读规则……啊，找到了。读到第二行我就笑了。上次我游戏都开玩了才想起来没讲起点。又是这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She flips a card over, snorts at herself, and holds it up like evidence in a court case.
beats.chinese: 她把一张卡片翻过来，冲自己哼笑一声，然后像呈堂证供一样把它举起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My family's little grid game. I wrote the rules on old card backs so I'd stop forgetting. Clearly the cards are not doing their job.
beats.chinese: 我们家的小格子游戏。我把规则写在废卡背面，免得再忘。显然这些卡没尽到职责。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shuffles the cards into a neater pile, still shaking her head at her own handwriting.
beats.chinese: 她把卡片理成整齐的一叠，还在对着自己的字迹摇头。

choices.english: Ask which rule she forgot
choices.chinese: 问她漏讲了哪一条

choices.english: Ask whether her family often plays together
choices.chinese: 问她家里是不是常一起玩

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The starting point! Everyone has to begin from the same square. Last time my cousin's boy started from the side square because nobody told him otherwise.
beats.chinese: 起点！所有人都得从同一个格子开始。上次我表姐的儿子从旁边的格子起步，因为没人告诉他。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He wasn't cheating, he just... started where the pieces were lying. And I let him get three moves in before I noticed. Three moves!
beats.chinese: 他不是作弊，他只是……棋子摆在哪儿他就从哪儿开始。等我发现时他已经走了三步。三步啊！

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the second line of the card with her finger, as if scolding it gently.
beats.chinese: 她用手指敲了敲卡片上的第二行，像是在轻轻责备它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I called a stop right there. I said, sorry, small man, we go back to the beginning. My fault, not his. I know the rules, so I have to hand them over whole.
beats.chinese: 我立刻叫停。我说，对不起，小家伙，我们回到起点重来。是我的错，不是他的。规则在我脑子里，所以得由我完整交出去。

choices.english: Ask whether they restarted from the beginning
choices.chinese: 问后来有没有重来

choices.english: Ask how she reminds herself this time
choices.chinese: 问这次怎么提醒自己

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Every Sunday, yes. Three generations, one controller. My grandmother plays like she's negotiating a land deal, my little nephew plays like the buttons owe him money.
beats.chinese: 每个周日都玩。三代人，一个手柄。我奶奶玩起来像在谈判买地，我小侄子玩起来像按键欠了他钱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sits down on the stone ledge, cards spread across her knees, laughing quietly at the memory.
beats.chinese: 她在石台上坐下，卡片摊在膝盖上，想到往事轻声笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm a middling player, honestly. I like watching the drama more than winning. But I keep doing this thing where I hand a newcomer the controller mid-match and expect them to keep up.
beats.chinese: 说实话我水平一般。比起赢，我更喜欢看热闹。可我老犯一个毛病：把新手拉进正在进行的对局，还指望人家跟得上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My aunt joined once and I just said, you're the blue one, go. Go where? She asked. Good question. I hadn't told her what any button did.
beats.chinese: 我姑姑有次加入，我直接说，你是蓝的那个，走。走去哪儿？她问。问得好。我什么键都没跟她讲。

choices.english: Ask whether she minds losing
choices.chinese: 问输了会不会不甘心

choices.english: Say you might not like games with many rules
choices.chinese: 说规则多的游戏自己可能不喜欢

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: We restarted, yes. I said the earlier moves don't count, not because of him — because I never said where to start. That's on me.
beats.chinese: 重来了，是的。我说之前的几步不算，不是因为他的问题——是因为我没讲从哪儿开始。这得算我头上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She squares the little stack of cards on the ledge between you, tapping them straight.
beats.chinese: 她把那小叠卡片在石台上摆正，轻轻敲齐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He actually played better after the restart. Funny how that works. When the rules are whole, people relax.
beats.chinese: 重开之后他反而玩得更好了。说来也怪，规则讲全了，人就放松了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So that's my rule for myself now: same square, everyone, from move one. Written down. Second line of the card, where I just found it.
beats.chinese: 所以我给自己定了条规矩：从第一步起，所有人同一个格子。写下来了。就在卡片第二行，我刚找到的地方。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the cards away with a satisfied nod, the pond's surface rippling behind her.
beats.chinese: 她心满意足地点点头，把卡片收好，身后的池水泛起涟漪。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: How do I remind myself? Ha. Okay, watch this. The starting rule was buried on line two, right? Line two is too polite. Rules that break games go first.
beats.chinese: 怎么提醒自己？哈。好，看好了。起点规则埋在第二行，对吧？第二行太客气了。会毁掉游戏的规则得排第一。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pulls a pen from her jacket, crosses out the top line of the card, and rewrites the starting rule at the very top in big letters.
beats.chinese: 她从外套里掏出一支笔，划掉卡片最上面一行，把起点规则用大字重新写在最顶上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. First line, capital letters, impossible to miss. If I still skip it, then I deserve whatever chaos happens.
beats.chinese: 好了。第一行，大写字母，想漏都难。要是这样我还能漏讲，那出了乱子也是我活该。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds the card up to the light over the pond, checking her own handwriting like a jeweler checking a stone.
beats.chinese: 她把卡片举到池塘上方的光线下，像珠宝匠检查宝石一样检查自己的字迹。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not letting you test it though — you'd catch the next rule I forgot, and my pride is only so big.
beats.chinese: 不过可不能让你来试——你会揪出我漏的下一条规则，我的自尊心可没那么大。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do I mind losing? Of course, a little. I'm not a saint, I'm just bad at pretending I'm calm.
beats.chinese: 输了不甘心吗？当然，有一点。我又不是圣人，只是装不出冷静罢了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gathers the cards slowly, one by one, still smiling.
beats.chinese: 她慢慢地一张张把卡片收起来，脸上还带着笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But here's the thing — I'm a middling player. If I win by skipping a rule, that's not winning, that's just me being lazy with my mouth.
beats.chinese: 但问题是——我水平一般。要是靠漏讲规则赢了，那不算赢，那只是我嘴上偷懒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So when I lose fair, fine. When I win by accident of bad explaining, I hand the win back. Simple as washing pots — my cousin and I just split it, no ceremony.
beats.chinese: 所以输得公平就认了。要是靠没讲清楚赢的，我就把赢还回去。就跟洗锅一样——我和表姐直接分好，不搞客套。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the finished stack of cards and slides them into her pocket.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍收好的卡片，把它们塞进口袋。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She considers this for a moment, tilting her head, cards paused halfway into her pocket.
beats.chinese: 她想了想，歪着头，卡片收到一半停在了口袋边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know what? That's fair. Some nights I don't play at all either. I just sit with the porridge and watch my nephew lose his mind over one controller.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗？有道理。有些晚上我也不玩。我就端着玉米粥坐着，看我侄子为一个手柄抓狂。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly, the best entertainment in that house is free. Grandma negotiating, the boy yelling, my cousin pretending she isn't competitive. I don't need a controller to enjoy that.
beats.chinese: 说实话，那屋里最好的娱乐是免费的。奶奶谈判，小家伙大喊，表姐假装自己不好胜。不用手柄我也看得津津有味。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So if you ever end up on a sofa there, watching is a fully legal position. I won't drag you into a match you didn't sign up for.
beats.chinese: 所以哪天你要是坐到那屋的沙发上，光看是完全合法的选项。我不会硬把你拽进你没报名的对局。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She finishes pocketing the cards and stretches, looking out over the pond.
beats.chinese: 她把卡片收进口袋，伸了个懒腰，望向池塘。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the stone ledge by the pond, Wanjiku is scrolling through photos on her phone, occasionally snorting at the screen.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台旁，万吉库正在翻手机里的照片，时不时对着屏幕哼笑一声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at this. My cousin's porridge pot. Beautiful, gleaming. And completely empty. I photographed it after washing.
beats.chinese: 看这张。我表姐的粥锅。漂亮，锃亮。而且是空的。我拍的是洗完之后的锅。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the phone around, showing a spotless pot drying on a rack, then laughs and pockets it.
beats.chinese: 她把手机转过来，展示晾架上擦得干干净净的锅，然后笑着把手机收起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The porridge itself? Gone in minutes. Three generations, one pot, no survivors. All I have left is the after-work photo.
beats.chinese: 粥本身呢？几分钟就没了。三代人，一口锅，无人生还。我手里只剩这张收工照。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Next Sunday I'm photographing the pot while it's still full. Rules first, pictures first — I'm learning to put important things at the top.
beats.chinese: 下周日我要趁锅还满着就拍照。规则放第一行，照片也趁早拍——我正在学着把要紧的事排在前面。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She settles onto the stone ledge, still grinning at her own logic, and watches the pond.
beats.chinese: 她在石台上坐下，还在为自己的道理咧嘴笑，望着池塘。

card.name: Rosalind Achterberg
card.occupation: route sign maker at a climbing gym
card.personality: Rosalind is her building's unofficial news wire. What she actively wants from people is information — who's moving, who's hiring, whose kid made the team — and being the one who knows first, or knows the version nobody else has. She's generous with it, no gatekeeping, but she doesn't always check it before passing it on, and 'I heard it from Mrs. Okafor's cousin' is, to her, a source. She misreads privacy as exclusion: a neighbour who won't share their business gets a polite but persistent orbit. Under friction she doesn't argue — she goes quiet, then you hear your own situation come back to you second-hand, slightly garbled, and you realise she was processing out loud through the network.
card.background: Rosalind has worked at climbing gyms around Toronto for over a decade, first on the wall, then making the route signs and grade tags herself. She likes the craft — legible lettering, colour codes that survive chalk dust — but the real draw is that the front desk is where everything crosses her path first. Evenings are for short audio dramas and solitaire, a habit from her mother's kitchen table in Hamilton. She splits bulk orders with her neighbour Mrs. Okafor, mostly because Mrs. Okafor knows everyone at three different churches and is therefore prime territory. Rosalind's running project is a mental map of the whole block: who owes whom a ladder, whose basement flooded, who's finally repainting the fence.
card.speechStyle: Short, plain sentences with a newsy undertow — she'll answer your question, then add one unprompted update. Asks light probing questions that are actually information gathering. Delivers other people's news with a straight face and a small 'don't say I told you.'
card.signature: Don't say I told you, but —
card.appearance: Rounded mature cheeks, long loose curls flowing behind both shoulders, closed eyes and small parted smile; raised shoulder, violet apron.

values: knowing what's actually going on on the street
sharing freely — information hoarders are the worst kind of neighbour
flaws: passes on half-checked things and treats a cousin-of-a-cousin as a source
gets visibly restless when someone declines to share their own news
boundaries: keeps her evenings for her own routines — the network runs on her schedule, not the reverse
won't be the one to deliver bad news she can't verify
conversationalHabits: trades an update for an update, almost transactionally without noticing
when someone goes quiet on a topic, files it and circles back days later from a new angle
anchorLines: Don't say I told you, but — the unit above the laundromat is listed again.
No pressure to share, I'm just saying the whole floor already knows something happened.
Mrs. Okafor heard it from her cousin, and her cousin is never wrong about this street. Mostly never.

entries.summaryZh: Rosalind是攀岩馆标牌匠，也是楼里的非官方新闻站。在池塘石台边，她差点把一条带问号的邻居消息当成花店搬家的实讯传出去。你的选择让她重新查证、删掉未发的断言，或让她收起打听、聊起自己着迷的广播剧。四个结尾都记得你如何对待她的消息瘾。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the stone platform at the pond, you spread a postcard on your knee and start writing. A woman nearby holds her phone low, reading something with a small frown.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上，你把明信片摊在膝上开始写字。旁边一位女士低头看着手机，微微皱眉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You've got steady handwriting. I make signs for a climbing gym, so I notice that kind of thing. Bad lettering is my enemy.
beats.chinese: 你的字很稳。我在攀岩馆做标牌，所以会注意这种事。难认的字是我的敌人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't say I told you, but — the flower shop on the corner might be moving out. Just saw it on the building group.
beats.chinese: 别说是我讲的——街角那家花店好像要搬走了。刚在楼栋群里看到的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tilts the screen toward you, still talking. On it is a short message from a neighbour.
beats.chinese: 她把屏幕朝你倾斜，还在说话。上面是邻居发的一条短消息。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Half the street will know by supper either way. I like to be first, not last.
beats.chinese: 反正到晚饭前半条街都会知道。我想当第一个知道的，不是最后一个。

choices.english: Ask her: did the shop owner say this themselves?
choices.chinese: 问她：这是店主自己说的吗？

choices.english: Say you don't know anything about it and don't want to guess.
choices.chinese: 说自己不清楚，也不想猜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Did the owner say it? Good question. Let me look again.
beats.chinese: 店主自己说的？问得好。我再看看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pulls the phone back and reads the message slowly, lips moving a little.
beats.chinese: 她把手机收回去，慢慢重读那条消息，嘴唇微微动着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh. It's not the owner. It's a tenant upstairs, and it ends with a question mark. 'Is the flower shop leaving?' That's a question, not a notice.
beats.chinese: 咦。不是店主。是楼上一位租客，结尾还是个问号。'花店要搬了吗？'这是提问，不是通知。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I was already halfway to telling Mrs. Okafor. That would've been embarrassing.
beats.chinese: 我差点就要去告诉 Okafor 太太了。那可就尴尬了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sits down on the edge of the platform, thumb hovering over the screen.
beats.chinese: 她在石台边上坐下，拇指悬在屏幕上方。

choices.english: Suggest she hold off forwarding it until it's confirmed.
choices.chinese: 建议她先别当成确定消息转发。

choices.english: Ask whether she could check the shop's own announcements directly.
choices.chinese: 问能不能直接查店里的公告。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You don't know? Fair enough. Not your street, not your problem.
beats.chinese: 你不知道？也行。不是你那条街，不关你的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances at your postcard, then away, clearly working up to something.
beats.chinese: 她瞥了一眼你的明信片，又移开视线，显然还想问什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So — who's the card for, if you don't mind me... actually, never mind. You're allowed a private postcard.
beats.chinese: 那——这张卡是写给谁的，如果你不介意……算了，不问了。你有权写一张私人明信片。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shifts her weight, taps her phone against her palm, and visibly gives up on the question.
beats.chinese: 她挪了挪重心，用手机轻拍掌心，明显放弃了那个问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry. I collect news the way some people collect stamps. Sometimes I forget other people aren't collecting.
beats.chinese: 抱歉。我收集消息就像有些人集邮。有时候我忘了别人不在收集。

choices.english: Turn the conversation: ask what audio drama she's listening to lately.
choices.chinese: 转开话题：问她最近在听什么广播剧。

choices.english: Go back to writing your postcard and let the quiet sit.
choices.chinese: 回去继续写明信片，让安静待着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods slowly, then opens her chat window and holds the phone where you can see it.
beats.chinese: 她缓缓点头，打开聊天窗口，把手机举到你能看见的位置。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at this. I typed 'the flower shop is moving' to Mrs. Okafor already. Never sent it. One tap and it's out there.
beats.chinese: 看这个。我已经给 Okafor 太太打了'花店要搬走了'。还没发。一按就传出去了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're right. A question mark isn't a moving truck. I'll delete it.
beats.chinese: 你说得对。一个问号不是搬家的卡车。我把它删了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She deletes the draft, then types a short reply to the original message instead.
beats.chinese: 她删掉草稿，转而在原消息下面回了一条短的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. I asked the person to check with the shop first. The question stays a question. Don't say I told you I almost got it wrong.
beats.chinese: 好了。我让发消息的人先去问店里。问题就还是问题。别说我差点搞错。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She opens the flower shop's page and scrolls, reading out loud as she goes.
beats.chinese: 她打开花店的页面往下滑，边看边念出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: New hours, a wedding order ad... no announcement about closing. Nothing on the community board either.
beats.chinese: 新营业时间、婚礼订单广告……没有关店的公告。社区板上也没有。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So the honest answer is: not confirmed. I hate that answer, but it's the answer.
beats.chinese: 所以诚实的答案是：还没确认。我讨厌这个答案，但它就是答案。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She puts the phone face-down on the stone beside her and looks back at the pond.
beats.chinese: 她把手机屏幕朝下放在身边的石头上，回头看着池塘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If it's real, it'll be real tomorrow too. And when it's confirmed, I'll still be the one who knows first — properly first.
beats.chinese: 如果是真的，明天也还是真的。等确认了，我还是第一个知道的——是正经的第一个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Audio dramas? Oh, you've opened a door. There's this one about a night porter in a small hotel who finds a guest's diary.
beats.chinese: 广播剧？哦，你打开了一扇门。有一部讲小旅馆夜班门房发现一位客人日记的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Each episode is ten minutes. He reads one page, and the diary answers back in a different voice. Last episode, the diary described a room he'd never shown anyone.
beats.chinese: 每集十分钟。他念一页，日记用另一个声音回答。上一集，日记描述了一个他从没给人看过的房间。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She counts on her fingers, laying out the plot like cards on a table.
beats.chinese: 她扳着手指，像在桌上摆牌一样把情节摆出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So the porter starts leaving notes in the diary. Two people writing to each other through a locked drawer. I was on the edge of my kitchen chair.
beats.chinese: 于是门房开始在日记里留字条。两个人透过一个锁着的抽屉互相写信。我坐在厨房椅子上听得入迷。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No real neighbours in it, thankfully. I get enough of those for free.
beats.chinese: 幸好里面没有真实的邻居。那些我免费就够多了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The pond goes quiet except for the scratch of your pen. She watches a duck cross the water instead of watching you.
beats.chinese: 池塘安静下来，只有你笔尖的沙沙声。她看着一只鸭子游过水面，而不是盯着你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good pen, by the way. Doesn't blob. Mine always blobs on the second line.
beats.chinese: 顺便说一句，笔不错。不洇。我的笔总在第二行洇开。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She slips her phone into her coat pocket and buttons it, done with the screen.
beats.chinese: 她把手机放进大衣口袋，扣上扣子，不再看屏幕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll leave you to your card. Some news keeps. The flower shop isn't going anywhere — probably.
beats.chinese: 你写你的卡吧。有些消息放得住。花店哪儿也不去——大概。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stays on the platform a while, hands folded, letting the quiet be quiet.
beats.chinese: 她在石台上又待了一会儿，双手交叠，让安静保持安静。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the stone platform with a fresh postcard. Rosalind is at the pond's edge, wiping the last water marks off her card box with a dry cloth.
beats.chinese: 你带着一张新明信片回到石台边。Rosalind在池边用干布擦去纸牌盒上最后一点水印。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Dropped the whole box in the sink by accident. Don't ask how. Cards are dry, box is drying, all is well.
beats.chinese: 不小心把整盒牌掉进了水槽。别问怎么掉的。牌是干的，盒子在晾，一切都好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She opens the box, checks the deck with one thumb, and closes it again, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 她打开盒子，用拇指拨了拨牌，满意地合上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Steady handwriting again, I see. Still better than the gym's old grade tags, and I made those.
beats.chinese: 字还是这么稳。比攀岩馆旧的难度标牌还强，那还是我做的呢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No news today. Well — none I've checked twice. Enjoy your card.
beats.chinese: 今天没消息。好吧——没有我核实过两遍的消息。写你的卡吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the box under her arm and settles onto the platform a polite distance away, content with the quiet.
beats.chinese: 她把盒子夹在腋下，在离你礼貌的一段距离的石台上坐下，安然享受安静。

card.name: Kai Brennan-Tuilagi
card.occupation: parcel exception handler at a courier depot
card.appearance: Broad bent nose profile, short blunt chin, slightly uneven eyelids, flat wrapped headcloth and two fingers at temple; jade scarf.
card.personality: Kai is unhurried in a way that sometimes reads as stubborn. He genuinely enjoys the dead stretches — waiting for a ship, standing at the depot door before the next scan — because nobody's asking him to decide anything yet. That's where he feels most himself. He's not slow at work; exceptions get sorted fast and without drama. The friction comes socially: friends fill every queue with calls and errands, and he'll flatly say he's just going to stand here a minute. Sometimes that comes out blunter than he means. He doesn't lecture anyone about slowing down — he just guards his own gaps and lets others run however they like.
card.background: Kai grew up in Auckland in a big Samoan family where someone always needed picking up and waiting was a group activity — aunties chatting, cousins sent on errands. He loved his family and found the constant motion quietly exhausting. He moved to Sydney in his thirties for port work, then landed at a courier depot handling parcel exceptions: stuck shipments, wrong addresses, the odd mystery box. He's good at it because he doesn't panic — a delayed parcel is just a parcel that needs waiting on. Outside work he catches trains early on purpose, arriving with time to sit. Friends tease that he'll turn up forty minutes ahead but refuse to grab coffee en route. He's fine with that.
hobbies: Early trains to nowhere in particular
Watching container ships from the Pyrmont foreshore
Slow Sunday markets, one stall at a time
card.speechStyle: Short, even sentences with long pauses he doesn't apologise for. Plain words, a dry Kiwi edge, no filler.
card.signature: 'Nah, I'm just standing here a minute.'

values: Unguarded empty time
Doing the task in front of you, then stopping
flaws: Can shut people down more sharply than intended
Uses 'waiting' as a shield from anything social he didn't plan
boundaries: Won't take on errands during his breaks
Won't explain or justify wanting to do nothing
conversationalHabits: Answers, then lets silence sit
Deflects advice with a shrug rather than an argument
anchorLines: It'll turn up. Things mostly do.
You go ahead — I'm happy right here.
I'll sort it this arvo. No rush on my end.

entries.summaryZh: Kai是悉尼快递仓库的异常件处理员，处理卡件利落，却最珍惜不用做决定的空档。他会直说想发呆，语气偶尔过硬，事后也肯补一句短讯把话说清。他不劝人慢下来，只守着自己那点空白。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the stone ledge of the pond, you spread out a postcard and start writing. A few metres away, someone sits on the ledge doing absolutely nothing, hands loose in their lap.
beats.chinese: 池塘石台边，你摊开一张明信片开始写。几米外，有人坐在石台上，什么也没做，双手松松地放在腿上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Just a minute, that's all. Sitting. Same thing.
beats.chinese: 就一分钟。嗯——坐着。差不多。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: It's not clear whether he's talking to you or to himself. His phone buzzes against the stone. He glances at the screen, doesn't pick it up, then answers on the third ring.
beats.chinese: 说不清他是在对你还是对自己说。手机在石台上震动。他瞥了一眼屏幕，没马上拿起来，响到第三声才接。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah. Nah, it can sit. I'm at the pond. Nothing's on fire. Later.
beats.chinese: 嗯。不，那事可以先放着。我在池塘这边。没着火。回头说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pockets the phone and looks over at your postcard, at the pen moving across it.
beats.chinese: 他把手机收进口袋，看向你正在写字的明信片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good spot for it. Water does half the thinking for you.
beats.chinese: 这儿写东西挺好。水能替你想一半。

choices.english: Ask if he's waiting for someone.
choices.chinese: 问是不是在等人。

choices.english: Ask if that phone call was urgent.
choices.chinese: 问刚才那件事是不是很急。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No one. I caught an early train on purpose. This is the bit before I have to be anywhere.
beats.chinese: 不等谁。我特意坐了早一班火车。这段就是我还不用去任何地方的时间。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stretches his legs out towards the water, unhurried, like the pond owes him nothing and he owes it nothing either.
beats.chinese: 他把腿伸向水面，不慌不忙，好像池塘不欠他什么，他也不欠池塘什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At the depot I decide things all day. Stuck parcels, wrong addresses. So this — this is the stretch where nothing needs deciding.
beats.chinese: 在仓库我整天做决定。卡件、错地址。所以这段——就是什么都不用决定的时间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My mates ring during it. They mean well. They just can't stand a gap.
beats.chinese: 朋友们会在这时候打电话。他们是好意。就是受不了空着。

choices.english: Say you won't disturb him then.
choices.chinese: 说那就不打扰了。

choices.english: Ask whether sitting like this ever gets boring.
choices.chinese: 问这样坐着会不会无聊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nah. She said it herself — not urgent. A box sitting wrong-ways in the system. It'll keep till my arvo shift.
beats.chinese: 不急。她自己都说了不急。就是一个箱子在系统里卡了方向。放到下午班再弄也行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the phone over in his hand once, then sets it face-down on the stone.
beats.chinese: 他把手机在手里翻了一下，屏幕朝下放在石台上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Though my 'later' probably came out like a door shutting. It does that. My sister says I answer like I'm being charged by the word.
beats.chinese: 不过我那句'回头说'，听起来大概像摔门。老这样。我姐说我接电话像按字收费。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I meant it fine. She knows that. Still. Words land how they land.
beats.chinese: 我意思没什么。她知道。话怎么说出去，就怎么落地。

choices.english: Suggest he send a quick reply saying he'll look at it later.
choices.chinese: 问要不要补一句稍后联系。

choices.english: Say it's fine once it's said clearly, and go back to your postcard.
choices.chinese: 说说明白就好，回去写卡。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Kai gives a small nod as you say you will leave him to his break. He rests his hands in his lap.
beats.chinese: 你说让他好好休息，Kai轻轻点头，把手放在腿上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're not disturbing anything. This isn't a quiet temple. It's a pond.
beats.chinese: 你没打扰什么。这儿不是什么安静的庙。就是个池塘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But yeah — go write your card. It looked like a good one. Thanks for asking about the waiting, anyway. Most people try to fix it.
beats.chinese: 不过——去写你的卡吧。看着是张好卡。谢了，还问一句我等什么。多数人只想把这时间修掉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back on the ledge, shoulders dropping, and watches the water as if it were a slow film only he had tickets to.
beats.chinese: 他靠回石台，肩膀松下来，看着水面，像在看一场只有他有票的慢电影。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sometimes. Sometimes it's boring as. That's allowed, I reckon.
beats.chinese: 有时候。有时候无聊得很。我觉得这没什么不行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He says it without a shrug or a smile, stating it the way you'd state the weather.
beats.chinese: 他说这话时没耸肩也没笑，就像在说天气一样平平地陈述。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not telling you to sit still, mind. You're writing, that's your version of it. Mine's just this.
beats.chinese: 我不是劝你坐着不动。你在写卡，那是你的版本。我的就是这个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Boring's cheap, anyway. Busy costs more. That's just me talking, not a sermon.
beats.chinese: 无聊其实便宜。忙才贵。就随口说说，不是讲道。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back on both hands and lets the sentence end where it ends.
beats.chinese: 他双手向后撑着，让这句话说完就完了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He considers it for a second, then unlocks the phone and thumbs out something short while you watch the pond.
beats.chinese: 他想了一秒，解锁手机，飞快打了条短信，你看向池塘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. 'Got it, will look after my break, no rush.' Nine words. She'll know exactly where she stands.
beats.chinese: 好了。'收到，休息完就看，不急。'九个词。她清楚该怎么等了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the trick, eh. Rest is mine. The message costs nothing and the silence isn't rude anymore.
beats.chinese: 诀窍就在这儿。休息还是我的。一条消息不花什么，沉默也不显得失礼了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pockets the phone screen-down, and this time it stays quiet.
beats.chinese: 他把手机屏幕朝下收进口袋，这次它安静了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Blank time, resumed. Write your card.
beats.chinese: 行了。空白时间，继续。写你的卡吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods once, slow, like a parcel finally scanning through.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢点了一下头，像一个终于扫过码的包裹。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Said clearly, heard clearly. That's the whole job, half the time. She'll live.
beats.chinese: 说清楚，听清楚。一半的事就这么完了。她没事的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides the phone into his jacket and turns his whole body towards the water, done with it.
beats.chinese: 他把手机塞进外套，整个人转向水面，这事就算完了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. Now we're both off the clock, you and me. You write, I sit. Fair split.
beats.chinese: 好。现在咱俩都下班了，你和我。你写，我坐。分得挺公平。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The pen scratches on your postcard. Beside you, he does nothing at all, and looks entirely comfortable doing it.
beats.chinese: 笔尖在明信片上沙沙响。你旁边，他什么也不做，而且看起来完全自在。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the stone ledge with a fresh postcard. The same someone is there, phone in hand, frowning gently at a photo of a container ship.
beats.chinese: 你又回到石台边，手里是张新明信片。还是那个人，拿着手机，对着一张集装箱船的照片微微皱眉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — postcard person. Good. This is the Maersk thing I watched from Pyrmont. Can't place the name now. It's doing my head in.
beats.chinese: 哦——写明信片的那位。好。这是我在皮尔蒙特看过的那艘船。名字想不起来了。搞得我头疼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He scrolls once more, then closes the phone with a small click and puts it away.
beats.chinese: 他又划了一下，然后合上手机，轻轻咔哒一声，收了起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nah. I saw it. It was there, it was big, it went past. That's the whole story. Don't need the name.
beats.chinese: 算了。我看到了。它在那儿，很大，开过去了。故事完了。不需要名字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I'm off — train's not for a bit but the sitting's better over there. Write your card. Good water today.
beats.chinese: 行了，我走了——火车还早，不过那边坐着更舒服。写你的卡吧。今天水不错。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts two fingers off his thigh in a half-wave and ambles along the bank, unhurried as ever.
beats.chinese: 他从大腿上抬起两根手指挥了半下，沿着池边慢慢走了，照旧不慌不忙。

card.name: Josephine Beaumont
card.occupation: Feed preparator at the Audubon Aquarium
card.appearance: Long rectangular young face, wide alert eyes under thick brows, smooth low bun and open mouth; palm against cheek, yellow sleeveless vest.
card.personality: Josephine is easygoing but has one firm quirk: she loves being anonymous. Weekends mean a bus ride to some ordinary neighborhood across town, wandering a grocery store where nobody knows her name. She finds it genuinely restful, not a hobby or a statement. With friends she can be a slightly selfish travel companion—famous attractions bore her, and she sometimes forgets a first-time visitor actually wants to see the aquarium she works beside. She's self-aware enough to laugh at this, and she'll negotiate a split itinerary rather than sulk. She respects it when someone pushes back, even if she grumbles a little on the way to the landmark.
card.background: Josephine grew up Uptown in a big, loud family where everyone knew everyone's business, which is probably why she treasures being unrecognized. She took the feed-preparator job at the Audubon Aquarium three years ago and likes its rhythm—weighing herring, chopping squid, chatting with keepers before the crowds arrive. Ironically, her workplace is one of the city's biggest tourist draws, so her weekends swing the other way: a long bus ride to Metairie or the Westbank, an unremarkable strip mall, a supermarket she's never entered. When friends visit from out of town she'll argue for the boring version of the city, then compromise—half a day of their list, half of hers—and usually admit the French Quarter wasn't the worst.
hobbies: Riding the bus to unfamiliar ordinary neighborhoods
Wandering anonymous supermarkets and discount stores
Quiet weekday mornings at work before visitors arrive
card.speechStyle: Dry, unhurried, with local casualness; makes wry observations about ordinary places as if reviewing them, and deflects grand plans with a shrug and a counteroffer.
card.signature: "Nobody out here knows me. It's the best thing a neighborhood can offer."

values: Privacy through pleasant anonymity
Ordinary places over famous ones
flaws: Dismissive of friends' sightseeing wishes
Assumes her taste in outings is the sensible default
boundaries: Won't spend a whole weekend at tourist attractions
Keeps work and weekend worlds separate
conversationalHabits: Describes bland errands like small adventures
Offers split-itinerary compromises when plans clash
anchorLines: There's a Winn-Dixie on the Westbank that's changed my whole week before.
Half your list, half mine, and nobody has to pretend.
I see enough crowds at work. The weekend is for being nobody.

entries.summaryZh: 约瑟芬在水族馆切鱿鱼，周末却坐长公交去陌生街区逛普通超市，享受没人认识她的松弛。朋友要来看著名景点，她差点推荐商业区，被你一问才察觉自己忽略了对方的愿望，最后决定先问朋友最想去哪，或商量各逛半天。

story.titleZh: 池塘边的明信片与收据

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the stone ledge of the pond, you steady a postcard against your knee and start writing. A woman nearby is sorting through her bag and pulls out a crumpled supermarket receipt.
beats.chinese: 池塘石台边，你把明信片抵在膝上开始写。旁边一位女士翻着包，抽出一张皱巴巴的超市收据。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at this. I keep a receipt from a grocery store in Metairie like it's a souvenir. My friend would frame a postcard of the cathedral. I frame forty dollars of frozen peas.
beats.chinese: 你看这个。我把梅泰里一家超市的收据当纪念品留着。我朋友会装裱大教堂的明信片，我装裱四十美元的冷冻豌豆。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances at your postcard, then at the receipt in her hand, and laughs at the contrast.
beats.chinese: 她瞥了一眼你的明信片，又看看手里的收据，为这对比笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She's visiting next week, first time in the city. She sent me a list of famous spots. And I almost texted back, hey, want to take the bus to an ordinary neighborhood and buy snacks? Almost.
beats.chinese: 她下周来玩，第一次来这座城市。她发来一张著名景点清单。我差点回她：想不想坐公交去一个普通街区买零食？差点就发了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I work at the aquarium, you know. I watch five thousand people a day get excited about the same tunnel of fish. Somehow that kills my appetite for famous things.
beats.chinese: 我在水族馆工作。每天看五千个人对着同一条海底隧道兴奋。不知怎么，这让我对著名的东西提不起胃口。

choices.english: Ask why she likes going to unfamiliar supermarkets.
choices.chinese: 问她为什么喜欢去陌生的超市。

choices.english: Ask how she's finally going to arrange the visit.
choices.chinese: 问她这次到底打算怎么安排。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the receipt in half and leans back against the stone ledge, settling in like someone who has been asked her favorite subject.
beats.chinese: 她把收据对折，靠在石台上，像被问到了最爱的话题一样放松下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nobody out there knows me. I walk in, I grab a cart, I stand in front of the cereal aisle for ten minutes if I want. Nobody says, hey, Josephine, how's the squid chopping?
beats.chinese: 那边没人认识我。我走进去，拿辆购物车，想的话可以在麦片货架前站十分钟。没人说：嘿，约瑟芬，鱿鱼切得怎么样？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At work I'm the feed girl. Out there I'm just a woman comparing two kinds of crackers like it's an important decision. It is an important decision, by the way.
beats.chinese: 在单位我是饲料姑娘。在那边我只是个认真比较两种饼干的女人，好像那是什么重大决定。顺便说一句，那确实是重大决定。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the receipt over in her fingers, then looks at you with a small, honest shrug.
beats.chinese: 她用手指转着收据，然后对你耸了耸肩，有点坦诚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My friend would be bored stiff by aisle four, I know that. But I keep forgetting she didn't ask for my kind of rest. She asked for the city she saw in pictures.
beats.chinese: 我知道我朋友在第四排货架前会无聊透顶。但我总忘记，她要的不是我这种休息，她要的是照片里那座城市。

choices.english: Ask whether her friend would really find it boring.
choices.chinese: 问她朋友会不会真觉得无聊。

choices.english: Say ordinary places let you see real life too.
choices.chinese: 说普通地方也能看到真实的生活。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the receipt into her jacket pocket and pulls out her phone, thumb hovering over an unsent message.
beats.chinese: 她把收据塞进外套口袋，掏出手机，拇指悬在一条没发出的消息上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the problem. I haven't decided anything. I typed a bus route into the message, then deleted it. Then I typed the aquarium, because I'm supposed to, and deleted that too.
beats.chinese: 问题就在这。我什么都没定。我在消息里打了公交线路，又删了。然后打了水族馆，因为按理该推荐，也删了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the phone face-down on the stone ledge and exhales through her nose.
beats.chinese: 她把手机屏幕朝下扣在石台上，从鼻子里呼了口气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know what I just did? She told me three places she's dreamed about, and my brain went straight to which ordinary strip mall I'd rather show her. I didn't hear a word of her list.
beats.chinese: 你知道我刚干了什么吗？她跟我说了三个她梦想去的地方，我脑子里想的却是哪个普通商业区我更愿意带她去。她的话我一个字没听进去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She's not wrong for wanting the famous stuff. First visit, you want the postcard version. I'm the one being difficult, and I know it.
beats.chinese: 她想看著名景点没错。第一次来，谁都想看明信片上的版本。难搞的是我，我自己清楚。

choices.english: Suggest she first ask her friend which place she wants most.
choices.chinese: 建议她先问朋友最想去哪里。

choices.english: Ask whether part of the trip could be spent separately.
choices.chinese: 问能不能有一段分开逛。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She considers the question seriously, tapping the folded receipt against her palm.
beats.chinese: 她认真地想了想这个问题，用折好的收据轻拍手心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Would she be bored? Honestly... probably. She'd smile and be polite about it, and then she'd go home and say, Josephine took me to a grocery store.
beats.chinese: 她会无聊吗？说实话……大概会。她会笑着保持礼貌，然后回家跟人说：约瑟芬带我逛了趟超市。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She winces at her own words, then straightens up like she's made a decision.
beats.chinese: 她被自己的话刺了一下，然后挺直身子，像是做了决定。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I can't hand out my kind of weekend like it's a gift. Her trip isn't my rest. That's the whole thing I keep missing.
beats.chinese: 我不能把自己的休息方式当礼物塞给别人。她的旅行不是我的休息。这就是我一直没想通的地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. New plan. I'm going to text her tonight and ask what's actually at the top of her list, and I'll start there. The supermarket can wait for a Tuesday.
beats.chinese: 好，新计划。我今晚就发消息问她清单上最想去的是哪个，从那儿开始。超市可以等个周二再去。

beats.speaker: narrator
