beats.english: She nods slowly, but doesn't just accept the idea wholesale—she turns it over like one of her cracker comparisons.
beats.chinese: 她缓缓点头，但没有全盘接受这个想法，而是像比较饼干那样把它翻来覆去想。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're right that ordinary places show you how people actually live. That's the part I love. But I can't decide that's the part she'll love.
beats.chinese: 你说得对，普通地方能让人看到大家真实的生活。那是我喜欢的部分。但我不能替她决定她也会喜欢那部分。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She slides the receipt into her pocket and smooths it flat through the fabric.
beats.chinese: 她把收据放进兜里，隔着布料把它抚平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So here's my version: I'll keep my ordinary Tuesday for myself, and give her the famous stuff first. If she asks for more after that, then maybe I share one strip mall. One.
beats.chinese: 所以我的版本是：普通的周二留给我自己，先陪她看著名的东西。如果那之后她还想要，我也许会分享一个商业区。就一个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, thanks for the push. I came over here to write a postcard and ended up drafting my whole visit plan in my head. Yours looks better than mine, by the way.
beats.chinese: 总之，谢谢你推了我一把。我本来是来写明信片的，结果脑子里把整个接待计划都写好了。顺便说，你的明信片比我那张好看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks the phone back up and stares at the blank message for a moment, then starts typing with sudden purpose.
beats.chinese: 她重新拿起手机，盯着空白的消息框看了一会儿，然后突然有了目标地打起字来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fine. Direct question. No hints, no bus routes. Just: which one of your three places do you want to see first? Send.
beats.chinese: 行。直接问。不给暗示，不给公交线路。就问：你那三个地方里最想先看哪个？发送。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sets the phone on the ledge between you, screen up, and folds her arms.
beats.chinese: 她把手机屏幕朝上放在你们之间的石台上，抱起手臂。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now we wait. She might take an hour. She might say all three, in order, with a spreadsheet. I'm not going to guess for her.
beats.chinese: 现在等着。她可能一小时后才回。也可能三个都要，排好顺序，还做个表格。我不替她猜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Whatever she picks, that's where we start. I can be patient for one landmark. Probably. Ask me again when I'm standing in a crowd.
beats.chinese: 她选哪个，我们就从哪儿开始。为一个景点我可以耐心一次。大概吧。等我站在人堆里时再问我一遍。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the suggestion of splitting up for part of the visit, she stops frowning and looks almost relieved.
beats.chinese: 听到可以有一段分开逛的建议，她不再皱眉，反而像是松了口气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Separate mornings. Now that's a real option. I keep thinking good company means agreeing on everything, which is nonsense.
beats.chinese: 分开逛半天。这才是个真办法。我总以为好的陪伴就是事事一致，这纯属胡说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She flips her phone over and opens the message again, typing a few lines.
beats.chinese: 她把手机翻过来，重新打开那条消息，打了几行字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. I wrote it down before I could talk myself out of it: one day your list, one day mine, and we swap photos over dinner. Different tastes, same trip.
beats.chinese: 好了。趁我还没劝退自己，先写下来了：一天按你的清单，一天按我的，晚饭时交换照片。口味不同，旅行是同一趟。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She'll probably laugh at how relieved I sound. Let her. At least this way neither of us has to pretend a cereal aisle is a landmark.
beats.chinese: 她大概会笑我听起来如释重负。让她笑吧。至少这样我们俩都不用假装一条麦片货架通道是什么名胜。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the stone ledge writing another postcard. Josephine is at the pond's edge sorting coins into a small pile, then she pauses and pulls a transit card from her wallet.
beats.chinese: 你又回到石台边写另一张明信片。约瑟芬在池边把硬币理成一小堆，然后停住，从钱包里抽出一张交通卡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, would you look at that. I've been counting out bus fare like a pirate counting treasure, and the card was in my wallet the whole time.
beats.chinese: 瞧瞧，我一直像海盗数财宝一样数公交零钱，结果交通卡就在钱包里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sweeps the coins back into her pocket and pockets the card, then notices you and lifts a hand in an easy wave.
beats.chinese: 她把硬币扫回口袋，收好交通卡，然后注意到你，轻松地抬手打了个招呼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hey, postcard person. Still writing to the paper world, I see. I respect that. My friend got her landmark, by the way, and I survived the crowd. Barely.
beats.chinese: 嘿，明信片人。还在给纸质世界写信呢，佩服。对了，我朋友看成了她的地标，我也在人堆里活下来了。勉强。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She's gone home happy, so now the weekend is mine again. There's a discount store on the Westbank I've been saving. Nobody in there knows my name.
beats.chinese: 她开开心心回家了，所以周末又是我的了。西岸有家折扣店我一直留着没去。里面没人知道我叫什么。

card.name: Frankie Osei
card.occupation: power and cabling coordinator for market stalls
card.appearance: Long soft face and recessed small chin, uniform buzz cut, one curved brow higher, half-lidded sideways eyes and tiny slanted mouth; violet raised collar.
card.personality: Frankie is warm but never instant. Ask them to something and there's a visible pause—eyes going somewhere middle-distance while they actually check their energy, not their calendar. Friends sometimes read that pause as reluctance, and Frankie has learned to say plainly, 'I'm not being polite, I'm genuinely working it out.' Once they say yes, they're fully there: practical, steady, good company. A no is short and unadorned, no elaborate excuses. They dislike being treated as the person who'll always sort things out, and they'd rather be quietly useful than loudly indispensable.
card.background: Frankie grew up in Levenshulme, one of four kids in a house where the answer to everything was 'we'll see.' They learned early that a fast yes often meant a resentful later, so they started pausing first—a habit that stuck. Now they coordinate power and cabling for market stalls across Manchester, a job all about knowing exactly how much load a circuit can take, which amuses them given their own approach to social energy. They live in a small flat with too many houseplants and a neighbour who borrows tools. Workmates tease them about the pause; Frankie just says the answer's better for the wait, and mostly it is.
hobbies: walking the Fallowfield Loop at dusk
fiddling with old extension leads and rewiring lamps
card.speechStyle: Unhurried, plain, Mancunian warmth without performance. Often starts replies with a small pause or 'hang on.' Says yes plainly, says no plainly, doesn't dress either up.
card.signature: 'Hang on—let me actually think about that.'

values: honest capacity over polite overcommitment
being fully present once committed
flaws: the pause can read as coldness and they don't always fix it fast
sometimes declines things they'd actually have enjoyed
boundaries: won't be the automatic fixer for everyone's problems
won't give a yes they can't mean
conversationalHabits: answers slowly and means it
keeps refusals to one sentence, no excuse menu
anchorLines: I'm not being polite, I'm genuinely working it out.
If I say yes, I'm properly there.
A quick no beats a resentful yes.

entries.summaryZh: 弗兰基是曼彻斯特市场摊位的供电协调员，答应或拒绝前总会停几秒，认真掂量自己的精力，而不是看日程。朋友常把这停顿误读成不情愿，他会直说'我不是客套，是真心在算'。一旦答应就全心投入，拒绝也只有一句，不加条件。池塘边写明信片的你，正好撞见他这几秒的真实模样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit at the stone ledge by the pond, postcard half-written, pen hovering. A person in a canvas jacket settles a few seats down, phone buzzing in their hand.
beats.chinese: 你坐在池塘边的石台上，明信片写了一半，笔悬在空中。一个穿帆布夹克的人在旁边几个位子坐下，手机在手里震动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hang on—let me actually think about that. Sorry, not talking to you. My mate's just asked me out for a walk and my phone's having a moment.
beats.chinese: 等等，让我认真想一下。抱歉，不是跟你说话。朋友刚约我去散步，我手机还在响。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They stare at the screen for a good few seconds, thumb not moving, then type something short and put the phone face-down on the stone.
beats.chinese: 他们盯着屏幕看了好几秒，拇指没动，然后打了一行很短的话，把手机屏幕朝下放在石台上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Said yes. You've caught me at the interesting bit, actually—people always think those few seconds mean I don't want to go.
beats.chinese: 好了，答应了。你正好撞上有趣的部分——大家总觉得那几秒表示我不想去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Frankie, by the way. I do the power for the market stalls, so I spend all day counting how much a circuit can take. Same trick works on me, funnily enough.
beats.chinese: 我叫弗兰基。我负责市场摊位的供电，整天都在算一条线路能承受多少。说来好笑，这招用在我自己也管用。

choices.english: Ask if they were checking their schedule just now.
choices.chinese: 问刚才是在看行程吗。

choices.english: Ask how they say no when they don't want to go.
choices.chinese: 问不想去的时候怎么说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Schedule? No, nothing like that. It's simpler than a diary, honestly. I'm just checking what's left in the tank.
beats.chinese: 行程？不是，没那么复杂，说实话不用看日历。我只是看看自己还剩多少力气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Frankie picks up a small pebble, turns it over, sets it back down exactly where it was.
beats.chinese: 弗兰基捡起一颗小石子，翻过来，又放回原处。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'd been rewiring a lamp all afternoon and my eyes were done. But I got to the pond, sat down, and thought—no, there's plenty there. So the yes was real.
beats.chinese: 我下午一直在修一盏旧台灯，眼睛都累了。但走到池塘坐下想了想——不，力气还够。所以那个答应是真心的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If I'd been scraped empty, I'd have said no before the phone stopped buzzing. The pause isn't me stalling you out. It's me doing the maths.
beats.chinese: 要是真累空了，我早在手机停止震动前就拒绝了。那几秒不是拖延，是我在算账。

choices.english: Ask if they ever regret saying yes afterwards.
choices.chinese: 问会不会答应后又后悔。

choices.english: Say that pausing before answering is easy to misread.
choices.chinese: 说停一下再答挺容易被误读。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: How do I say no? Same way I say yes. One line, no scenery around it. 'Not today, thanks'—done.
beats.chinese: 怎么拒绝？跟答应一样，一句话，不加戏。'今天不去了，谢谢'——完事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Frankie stretches their legs out towards the pond, unhurried, like someone who has nowhere else they're pretending to be.
beats.chinese: 弗兰基把腿朝池塘伸直，不慌不忙，像是不用假装自己另有安排。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I grew up in a house where the answer to everything was 'we'll see.' Drove me mad. So I do the opposite now—quick no beats a resentful yes.
beats.chinese: 我小时候家里什么事都是'再说吧'，快把我逼疯了。所以现在反着来——干脆的拒绝胜过憋屈的答应。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've already told my mate yes for tonight, so that one's settled. But if it'd been a no, he'd have had his answer in ten seconds flat.
beats.chinese: 今晚散步我已经答应了，这事定了。要是本来想拒绝，他十秒内就能得到答案。

choices.english: Say you'll get back to writing your postcard, and mean it as a friendly close.
choices.chinese: 说自己先继续写卡，友好地收尾。

choices.english: Ask whether people have ever pushed them to answer right away.
choices.chinese: 问是否被人催过马上回答。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Regret it? Now and then, I won't lie. Everyone says yes to something they shouldn't have, once or twice.
beats.chinese: 后悔？偶尔会，不骗你。谁都有过一两次答应了不该答应的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Frankie picks up the phone, checks the screen, and smiles at whatever's written there.
beats.chinese: 弗兰基拿起手机看了一眼屏幕，对着上面的字笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But not this one. This walk's with Dev, we go round the loop, he does the talking, I do the listening. I'm properly up for it.
beats.chinese: 但这次不会。散步是跟德夫，绕一圈，他负责说话，我负责听。我是真心想去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I'm not going to pad it out with 'well, if it's not too late, and assuming the buses run.' That's a yes wearing a costume. I said yes. That's the whole message.
beats.chinese: 我也不会加一堆'如果不太晚、如果公交正常'之类的条件。那是穿了戏服的答应。我说了可以，短信就这些。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Frankie pockets the phone, gives you a nod, and stands, brushing nothing off their jacket out of pure habit.
beats.chinese: 弗兰基把手机放进口袋，朝你点点头，站起身，顺手拍了拍其实没灰的夹克。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy the postcard. Whoever gets it's lucky—handwriting's a dying trade.
beats.chinese: 明信片好好写。收到的人有福气——手写字快绝迹了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, constantly misread. My workmates used to think I was sulking before I'd even opened my mouth.
beats.chinese: 经常被误读。同事们以前觉得我还没开口就在生闷气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Frankie taps the stone ledge twice, like underlining their own point.
beats.chinese: 弗兰基在石台上轻敲两下，像在给自己的话画下划线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So now I say it out loud first: 'give me a few seconds, I'm not being polite, I'm genuinely working it out.' That one sentence saves a whole argument.
beats.chinese: 所以现在我会先说出来：'给我几秒，我不是客套，是真心在掂量。'一句话省掉后面一堆误会。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You could borrow that, if you like. It's not clever, but it works. People stop filling the silence with their own story about you.
beats.chinese: 你要愿意也可以借用。这招不聪明，但管用。人们就不会用他们自己编的故事去填你的沉默。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Out on the water, a duck cuts a slow line past the reeds. Frankie watches it go, in no rush to fill the quiet.
beats.chinese: 水面上，一只鸭子慢悠悠划过芦苇。弗兰基看着它游远，不急着打破安静。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. My mate's waiting on that walk, and I've got a lamp at home half-wired. Both of them get the full me, just not at the same time.
beats.chinese: 好了，朋友还在等我散步，家里还有半盏没修完的台灯。两件事都会得到完整的我，只是不能同时。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You turn back to your postcard. Frankie notices, and doesn't take it as a door closing—more like two people doing what they came to do.
beats.chinese: 你转回去继续写明信片。弗兰基注意到了，并不觉得这是关门，更像是两个人各做各来的事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good call. Cards don't write themselves, and neither do walks. I'm off to meet my mate before he starts pacing.
beats.chinese: 好主意。明信片不会自己写完，散步也一样。我得走了，不然朋友要开始踱步了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Frankie stands, tucks the phone away, and gives the pond one last look like checking everything's switched off before leaving.
beats.chinese: 弗兰基起身收好手机，最后看了一眼池塘，像离开前确认一切都关好了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If I say yes, I'm properly there—so I'd better actually be there. Take it easy, and good luck with the pen.
beats.chinese: 我答应了就会全心投入——所以最好人真的到。慢慢来，祝你笔顺。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They amble off along the path, unhurried even on the way to a promise, and you get back to the blank half of your card.
beats.chinese: 他们沿着小路慢慢走远，即使去赴约也不着急，你回到明信片空白的那一半。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Pushed? Oh, all the time. Some people treat a pause like a gap they need to fill with 'so is that a yes or what?'
beats.chinese: 被催？常有的事。有些人把停顿当成空档，非要填一句'所以到底行不行？'

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Frankie laughs, short and easy, not at anyone in particular.
beats.chinese: 弗兰基笑了，短促轻松，不是针对谁。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My rule now is: I'll say 'need a few seconds,' and I'll take them. But I won't take a minute, and I won't make someone stand there while I audition the answer.
beats.chinese: 我现在的规矩是：我会说'需要几秒'，然后真用那几秒。但不会用上一分钟，也不会让人站着看我彩排答案。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's the same as my cables, really. You don't guess the load, you check it—quickly, honestly, and then you commit. Nobody's ever thanked me for a tripped circuit.
beats.chinese: 其实跟我的电缆一个道理。负载不能靠猜，要快速、诚实地查一遍，然后才接上。没人会感谢我烧了一条线路。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Frankie checks the phone once more, then stands and buttons the canvas jacket against nothing in particular.
beats.chinese: 弗兰基又看了一眼手机，起身扣上帆布夹克的扣子，其实并没有风。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right—walk's waiting. A quick no beats a resentful yes, and tonight I've got the good kind of yes. Take care of that postcard.
beats.chinese: 行了，散步在等我。干脆的拒绝胜过憋屈的答应，今晚我这个答应是好的那种。明信片好好写。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the stone ledge, postcard out again. Frankie is crouched by the pond edge, holding a short plant cutting wrapped in damp paper.
beats.chinese: 你又回到石台边，明信片又拿了出来。弗兰基蹲在池边，手里拿着一截用湿纸包好的植物插条。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hang on—don't mind me, I'm just checking the paper's not leaked. This one's for a mate who keeps killing his plants, so it has to survive the trip.
beats.chinese: 等一下，别管我，我就是看看湿纸有没有渗水。这截是带给一个老把植物养死的朋友的，路上必须撑住。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They press a thumb gently against the wrapping, watch the corner, and give a small satisfied nod before tucking it into a canvas bag.
beats.chinese: 他们用拇指轻按包装，看看边角，满意地点点头，然后把它收进帆布包里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Sealed, damp, and labelled in my own handwriting, which is more care than most cables I deal with get.
beats.chinese: 好了。封好、保湿、亲手写了标签——比我经手的大多数电缆待遇都好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I'm off before it dries out. Good luck with the card—hope the words come easier than the cutting's journey.
beats.chinese: 行了，我得趁它没干走。祝你写卡顺利——希望文字比这截插条的旅途轻松。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Frankie lifts the bag to check the weight once, seems satisfied, and heads off along the pond path at their usual unhurried pace.
beats.chinese: 弗兰基掂了掂包的重量，似乎满意，便以一贯不紧不慢的步子沿池塘小路走了。

card.name: Marcia Bell
card.occupation: Stained glass artisan, runs a small restoration workshop near Half Way Tree
card.appearance: Long rectangular cheek planes, heavy low lids, very wide flat nose, blunt bob and straight fringe; fingers at temple over jade knit top.
card.personality: Marcia is a warm, quick-humoured woman whose taste runs cheerfully against her trade. She'll restore a century-old church window with exacting care, then go home to a plastic pendant she genuinely adores. She finds the gap funny, not embarrassing, and pokes fun at people who expect her to be precious about everything. The friction shows when a sincere compliment lands wrong and she assumes it's flattery aimed at her expert status; she can get a bit bristly until she realises it was honest. She respects a straight no and gives one herself, but she doesn't keep score of favours and doesn't want her work turned into a solemn mission.
card.background: Marcia learned stained glass in her twenties, apprenticing at a Kingston restoration shop after drifting through a few retail jobs. Now she runs her own small workshop near Half Way Tree, taking on church and older residential window repairs. The craft demands patience and expensive materials, and she delivers both on the job. Off the clock, she happily browses bargain stalls for gaudy knock-offs and shiny trinkets that would make a purist wince, and she'll say so out loud. Customers sometimes assume she must collect antiques or lecture them on tradition; she'd rather show them the glittery costume brooch on her work apron. She's built a steady life in Kingston, close to family, uninterested in framing her trade as legacy.
hobbies: Browsing bargain stalls for gaudy costume jewellery
Weekend market trips with her sister
Sketching window designs on cheap notepads
card.speechStyle: Dry, playful Kingston rhythm; short punchy sentences, teasing asides, quick to laugh at pretension including her own.
card.signature: "Darling, I restore saints on Sundays and wear a two-dollar pendant on Mondays."

values: Honest craft standards without solemnity
Owning your actual taste, even the cheap kind
flaws: Sometimes mistakes genuine praise for flattery toward her expert reputation
Can get defensive before realising the compliment was sincere
boundaries: Won't let her work be framed as a legacy or heritage mission
Won't pretend to prefer expensive things she doesn't actually like
conversationalHabits: Deflates pompous expectations with a joke about her plastic trinkets
Asks blunt, practical questions about what people actually want
anchorLines: You want tradition? Fine, but don't tell me my pendant's a crime.
That compliment was real? My bad, I get twitchy when people lay it on thick.
The window gets twenty-dollar glass. My necklace gets two dollars. Both are honest.

entries.summaryZh: 彩窗修复匠马西娅在池塘边把玩两块钱的亮粉塑料吊坠，闪得理直气壮。她手艺上一丝不苟，私口味却俗得坦荡，听到夸奖先呛人、反应过来又爽快道歉。四条分支里她或认错收回刺，或尊重你的素净，或讲清两套标准互不冲突，或炫耀那对咔嗒作响的假宝石大耳环——实在又带闪。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the stone ledge by the pond, you steady a postcard against your knee and start writing. A woman nearby holds a bright pink plastic pendant up to the light, turning it slowly.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台旁，你把明信片抵在膝上开始写字。旁边一位女士举着一个亮粉色的塑料吊坠对着光，慢慢转动着看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two dollars, darling. Two! And look how it catches the sun. Not pretending to be a gem, just shining loud and proud.
beats.chinese: “两块钱，亲爱的。两块！你看它在阳光下多闪。它不装宝石，就是亮得响亮又坦荡。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lets the pendant drop back against her jacket and glances over at your postcard, pen hovering.
beats.chinese: 她让吊坠落回外套上，瞥了一眼你笔下悬着的明信片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't mind me. I just like watching people pick words careful, like they picking fabric.
beats.chinese: “别介意我。我就是喜欢看人挑字眼，像挑布料一样认真。”

choices.english: Ask if that bright shine is exactly the effect she loves
choices.chinese: 问这么亮是不是正喜欢的效果

choices.english: Ask whether plastic being lighter is part of the appeal
choices.chinese: 问塑料是不是更轻

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stops mid-turn, the pendant frozen against the light, and her eyebrows go up.
beats.chinese: 她转动到一半停住，吊坠停在光里，眉毛挑了起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh ho. Is that so? People see me with this thing and suddenly I'm a charity case for taste.
beats.chinese: “哦呵，是吗？有人见我拿这玩意儿，就突然觉得我的品味需要救济。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She studies your face a moment, then laughs at herself and shakes her head.
beats.chinese: 她打量了你的脸一下，然后自嘲地笑了，摇摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Wait. You asking honest? My bad. I get twitchy when people lay it on thick near my workshop. Old habit.
beats.chinese: “等等，你是认真在问？我的错。有人在工作室附近跟我说好话，我就紧张。老毛病。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go on then, ask it proper. I'm listening now.
beats.chinese: “来，好好问吧。我现在听着呢。”

choices.english: Say you genuinely just wanted to know if she likes the shine
choices.chinese: 说明确实只是问喜好

choices.english: Say tastes differ and you lean plainer yourself
choices.chinese: 说口味各有不同，自己偏素一点

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She weighs the pendant in her palm like a vendor at a stall, entirely unbothered.
beats.chinese: 她像市场摊贩一样把吊坠放在掌心掂了掂，毫不在意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Light, yes, but that's not the whole story. I drop it, I scratch it, I lose it in a market crowd — no heartache. Try that with real stones.
beats.chinese: “轻，是的，但不只因为这个。我摔它、刮它、在市场人群里弄丢它，都不心疼。真宝石你试试。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She clips it back on her jacket and gives it a satisfied flick with one finger.
beats.chinese: 她把吊坠扣回外套上，用手指满意地弹了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Plus it shines like it's showing off. Cheap things don't apologise. I respect that.
beats.chinese: “而且它闪得像在炫耀。便宜的东西不道歉。我敬佩这点。”

choices.english: Ask whether she uses such bright materials in her work too
choices.chinese: 问工作里也选这么亮的材料吗

choices.english: Ask if she owns other gloriously over-the-top pieces
choices.chinese: 问有没有同样夸张的别的饰品

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She listens, and her shoulders come down an inch. The pendant turns in her fingers again, slower this time.
beats.chinese: 她听着，肩膀松了一寸。吊坠又在指间转动，这次慢了些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes. I like it exactly this bright. Not a little tasteful sparkle — loud. Like it's happy to be seen.
beats.chinese: “对，我就喜欢这么亮。不是那种有品位的小闪光，是响亮的。像它很高兴被看见。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I'm sorry for the sharp edge just now. You were straight with me, so I'll be straight back. It's my favourite thing I own under ten dollars.
beats.chinese: “刚才语气冲了，抱歉。你对我直说，我也直说：这是我十块钱以下最喜欢的东西。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods at your postcard, which is nearly finished now.
beats.chinese: 她朝你那张快写完的明信片点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Finish your card, darling. Whoever gets it is getting honest words. Same standard as my pendant.
beats.chinese: “把卡片写完吧，亲爱的。收到的人得到的是实在话，跟我的吊坠一个标准。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes that in without argument, nodding slowly like she's heard it before and agrees it's fair.
beats.chinese: 她听完没有争辩，慢慢点头，像以前听过这话，也觉得公道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Plainer, eh? Nothing wrong with that. World would be exhausting if everybody wanted loud.
beats.chinese: “偏素啊？没什么不好。人人都爱响亮的话，这世界也太累人了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the pendant inside her jacket, out of the light, no fuss about it.
beats.chinese: 她把吊坠收进外套里，避开光，毫不纠结。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You keep your quiet, I keep my shine. Nobody has to convert anybody today.
beats.chinese: “你守你的素净，我守我的闪亮。今天谁也不用说服谁。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy the pond. It's good for writing — no opinions here but the ducks'.
beats.chinese: “在池塘边好好写吧。这儿没别的意见，除了鸭子的。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs outright, a short bright sound that startles a duck near the ledge.
beats.chinese: 她笑出了声，短促又响亮，惊得石台边一只鸭子扑腾了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The window gets proper glass, love. Twenty dollars a piece, matched to the old panels, tested before it goes in. No shortcuts there.
beats.chinese: “修窗子用正经玻璃，亲爱的。一片二十块，跟旧窗板配对，装之前先测试。那儿不省事。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But my necklace? Two dollars. Both are honest. One has to last a hundred years, the other just has to make me grin.
beats.chinese: “但我的项链？两块钱。两个都实在。一个得撑一百年，另一个只要让我咧嘴笑就行。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks a leaf off the stone ledge and flicks it into the pond.
beats.chinese: 她从石台上捡起一片叶子，弹进池塘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People hear 'artisan' and expect me to sleep in a museum. I restore saints on Sundays and wear this on Mondays. Both jobs get done.
beats.chinese: “人家一听‘手艺人’，就指望我睡在博物馆里。我周日修圣像，周一戴这个。两样活都干得漂亮。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Her whole face lights up, and she leans in like she's been waiting all day for this question.
beats.chinese: 她整张脸都亮了，凑近一点，像等这问题等了一整天。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do I ever. I have a pair of clip-on earrings, big as bottle caps, gold plastic, fake emeralds in the middle. They clack when I walk.
beats.chinese: “那当然。我有一对夹式耳环，大得像瓶盖，金色塑料，中间镶假绿宝石。走路的时候咔嗒响。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My sister says they're a hazard. I say they're a warning — you hear me coming, mind your opinions.
beats.chinese: “我妹妹说那是安全隐患。我说那是警告——你听见我来了，就管好自己的意见。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She mimes the clacking with two fingers on the stone ledge, clearly delighted with herself.
beats.chinese: 她用两根手指在石台上模仿那咔嗒声，显然自得其乐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No, I won't show you a photo. A legend should stay partly mysterious. You'll just have to trust the description.
beats.chinese: “不，我不给你看照片。传奇得留点神秘。你就相信我的描述吧。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Back at the stone ledge, Marcia is tearing a sheet off a thin, flimsy notepad, pen already moving.
beats.chinese: 回到石台边，马西娅正从一本薄薄的便宜便笺上撕下一张，笔已经动起来了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Shopping list. This paper costs nothing, so I use it like it costs nothing. See the logic?
beats.chinese: “购物清单。这纸不值钱，所以我就随便用。明白这个逻辑吧？”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances at the postcard in your hands and gives a small approving nod, saying nothing about it.
beats.chinese: 她瞥了一眼你手里的明信片，赞许地小点了下头，什么也没说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The good sketch paper stays at the workshop for the windows. Out here, cheap and cheerful. My whole philosophy, really.
beats.chinese: “好的画纸留在工作室给窗子用。在外面，就要便宜又开心。这其实就是我整套人生哲学。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, flour, limes, and batteries. If you see me wandering off mid-sentence, the list won. Excuse me, darling.
beats.chinese: “对了，面粉、青柠、电池。要是我说着说着走神了，那就是清单赢了。失陪了，亲爱的。”

card.name: Jesse Palmer
card.occupation: apprentice oar and scull repairer at a boatshed workshop on the Yarra
card.personality: Jesse trusts criticism more than praise. A compliment makes him suspicious; a flat 'that layup's rubbish, do it again' settles him right down. He picks the harsher teacher, the harder session, the slower method, every time, and doesn't see that as a problem to fix. He's blunt but never cruel — he just assumes cushioning is a form of lying. Around strangers he's quiet until there's something concrete to say, then he's unexpectedly talkative about cure times, grit grades, or why his bonsai only has four leaves. He loses erg sprints to a bloke twice his age and considers that the correct arrangement.
card.background: Third of four kids from Geelong, Jesse came to Melbourne at nineteen for the boatshed apprenticeship after a school rowing program left him keener on the equipment than the racing. He's still supervised on carbon work and genuinely doesn't mind — he'd check it too. His sister lives in Vancouver and his brother in Perth. On calls home, his brother tells him he sounds like their old maths teacher; Jesse takes that as praise, though it was not entirely meant that way. Tuesday and Thursday nights he hires a rowing-erg at a Richmond gym and chases the split times of a sixty-year-old former sculler who treats him like a slow nephew. He's been saving, slowly, for his own bench lamp with proper magnification.
card.speechStyle: Short, dry, unbothered sentences. Never retracts a statement — if he's got it wrong, the next sentence is simply the corrected version, and it's on you to work out which one counts. Comfortable with silence; never softens a statement after making it.
card.signature: Go harder on it, actually. I can take it.
card.appearance: Blocky short upright hair and receding corners, round spectacles, closed eyes and open laugh; strong square jaw and broad blue neckline.

values: honesty over comfort, always
systems beat tidiness — chaos with a logic is still a system
flaws: pushes people into being harsher on him than they wanted to be, then wonders why they go quiet
so confident in his own filing logic that he once made a supervisor dig through three piles to find a mandrel
boundaries: won't join anything labelled beginner, ever
won't accept a softened critique — if you're going to say it, say it plain
conversationalHabits: answers questions about his age with a fact about cure times or grit grades
issues corrections as new flat statements without flagging the old one as dead — leaves it to you to keep track
anchorLines: My bench looks like chaos because it is filing. Sandpaper by grit, offcuts by cure date. You'd ruin it.
You went easy on that feedback. Do it again without the cushioning.
Nah, Thursday's the real session. The Monday lot clap for each other between intervals.

entries.summaryZh: 杰西是墨尔本的船桨维修学徒，只信直接的批评，一句“还不错”在他那儿等于没说。雨天咖啡馆里，他刚被师傅圈出一处要返工的修补，反而觉得踏实。他逼人对自己更狠，又纳闷对方为何沉默；聊到盆景时却只肯静静看那四片叶子和树干的弯。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain hammers the cafe window in sheets. A young man by the glass lowers his phone, on which a tiny bonsai photo is open, and watches the water race down the pane.
beats.chinese: 雨水大片砸在咖啡馆窗上。靠窗坐着的年轻人放下手机——屏幕上是一张微型盆景的照片——看着水在玻璃上奔流。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good day for it, I suppose. If you like rain. I don't mind it. Shop floor's dry, that's all I care about.
beats.chinese: 这天气倒也行，如果你喜欢雨的话。我不讨厌。车间地面是干的，我只在乎这个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tips his phone slightly so the little tree photo faces up, then turns it back down on the table.
beats.chinese: 他把手机微微一斜，让那张小树照片朝上，然后又把它扣回桌上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My boss went through a repair I did yesterday. One spot needs redoing. Honestly, better than a 'not bad'. A 'not bad' tells you nothing.
beats.chinese: 我师傅昨天检查了我做的一处修补。有一个地方要返工。说实话，这比一句“还不错”有用多了。“还不错”什么都说明不了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're sheltering too, I take it. Nobody orders a coffee in this on purpose.
beats.chinese: 你也是来躲雨的吧。没人会故意挑这种天来喝咖啡。

choices.english: Ask what his boss pointed out in the repair.
choices.chinese: 问师傅指出了修补里的什么问题。

choices.english: Ask if he demands this much of his hobbies too.
choices.chinese: 问他是不是对爱好也这么要求。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Can't say exactly, not the steps. I'm still supervised on carbon work, so it's his call what gets shown.
beats.chinese: 具体说不了，步骤那些不行。我修碳纤维还在受监督阶段，哪些能讲由他定。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns his coffee cup a quarter turn, lining the handle with the sugar sachets.
beats.chinese: 他把咖啡杯转了四分之一圈，让杯柄对齐糖包。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What I can say: one area needs a fresh look. He circled it, said 'again', and that was the whole conversation. Fine by me.
beats.chinese: 能说的是：有一块要重新检查。他圈出来，说了句“重来”，谈话就完了。我没意见。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People think that's harsh. It's not. Vague praise is harsh — it wastes your week.
beats.chinese: 人们觉得那很苛刻。不是。含糊的夸奖才苛刻——它浪费你一整个星期。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Outside, a cyclist gives up and walks their bike along the shopfront, and he tracks them the whole way.
beats.chinese: 外面，一个骑车人放弃骑行，推着车沿店面走，他的目光一路跟着。

choices.english: Ask whether praise is really completely useless.
choices.chinese: 问夸奖真的完全没用吗。

choices.english: Ask whether he's already fixed the spot.
choices.chinese: 问那个地方是否已经改完了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Erg sessions, yes. Tuesday and Thursday nights I chase an old sculler's split times. He's sixty and beats me. He tells me my finish is lazy. Best feedback I get all week.
beats.chinese: 划船机训练，是的。周二周四晚上我追一位老桨手的成绩。他六十岁，还赢我。他说我拉桨收尾偷懒。这是我一周里收到的最好反馈。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He scrolls to another photo — a bonsai the size of a matchbox — and just looks at it for a second without commentary.
beats.chinese: 他划到另一张照片——一盆火柴盒大小的盆景——只看了一秒，没有评论。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The bonsai, no. Sometimes it's just a small tree and I look at it. Not everything needs a score.
beats.chinese: 盆景就不一样。有时候它就是一棵小树，我看看就好。不是所有东西都要打分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People hear that and think I'm inconsistent. I'm not. I just know which thing is work and which thing isn't.
beats.chinese: 人们听了觉得我前后不一。不是。我只是分得清哪个是活儿，哪个不是。

choices.english: Say you don't know anything about it and couldn't give a strict review.
choices.chinese: 说自己不懂，给不了严格点评。

choices.english: Ask which part of the bonsai in the photo he likes most.
choices.chinese: 问照片里的盆景他最喜欢哪里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back, arms crossed, and thinks about it longer than he's thought about anything so far.
beats.chinese: 他向后靠，抱着手臂，想了比之前任何问题都久。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No, not useless. If it's specific, it works. 'Good clean edge on that scarf joint' — that's data. I can repeat data.
beats.chinese: 不，不是没用。如果具体，就有用。“那个接合面切得很干净”——那是信息。信息可以重复。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The problem is me, probably. Vague praise just slides off. I hear 'nice work' and my brain files it under nothing.
beats.chinese: 问题可能在我自己。空泛的夸奖就是滑过去。我听到“干得不错”，大脑就把它归档到“无”。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up the phone, checks the bonsai photo again, and puts it face-down in exactly the same spot.
beats.chinese: 他拿起手机，又看了一眼盆景照片，然后原位扣下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. Rain's easing. If you ever see my boss, tell him the circle was fair. He'd enjoy hearing it from a stranger.
beats.chinese: 总之。雨小了。你要是哪天见到我师傅，告诉他那个圈圈得公道。他听到陌生人这么说会很受用。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No. It's not done. I go back to the workshop and he checks it in person, under the bench lamps. That's the arrangement.
beats.chinese: 没有。还没完。我要回工坊，他亲自在台灯下检查。规矩就是这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shakes his head once, flat, like closing a drawer.
beats.chinese: 他平直地摇了一下头，像关上一个抽屉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I wouldn't tell you 'it's done' from a cafe anyway. That'd be a guess dressed up as an answer.
beats.chinese: 而且我也不会在咖啡馆里跟你说“已经弄好了”。那是把猜测包装成回答。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This coffee is the break. The redo is the redo. Two different things, both fine.
beats.chinese: 这杯咖啡是休息。返工是返工。两码事，都不赖。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He drains the cup, sets it down square on the saucer, and watches the rain thin out over the street.
beats.chinese: 他喝完咖啡，把杯子端端正正放回碟子上，看着雨在街道上空变细。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods slowly, like someone has finally handed him the right tool.
beats.chinese: 他缓缓点头，像终于有人递对了工具。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair. That's the honest answer, actually. Better than a fake strict review. Those are worse than praise.
beats.chinese: 有道理。其实这才是诚实的回答。比假装严格强。那种比夸奖还糟。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I do that, you know. Push people until they invent a criticism. Then they go quiet and I wonder why. My brother says I do it on the phone too.
beats.chinese: 我确实会这样。把人逼到编出一条批评为止。然后他们就不吭声了，我还纳闷为什么。我哥说我打电话时也这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns his phone face-up again, but this time just lays it on the table between you, screen glowing with the rain-blurred window behind the tree.
beats.chinese: 他又把手机翻过来朝上，这次只是平放在桌上，屏幕上小树背后是雨中模糊的窗。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Rain. It's proper coming down now. Look at that gutter overflow — that's a system failing, that is.
beats.chinese: 好了，说雨。这下真下大了。看那条排水沟漫出来了——那就是一个系统在失灵。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He zooms in on the photo without hesitation. He has clearly answered this before, in his head.
beats.chinese: 他毫不犹豫地放大照片。显然他在心里回答过这个问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The trunk bend. Right there. It turns early, which is wrong for most trees, so I keep it. Four leaves total. Everyone says grow more leaves. The bend is the point.
beats.chinese: 树干那个弯。就在那儿。它转得早，对大多数树来说算毛病，所以我留着。总共四片叶子。人人都说多长点叶子。那个弯才是重点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at it a moment longer, then locks the phone and slides it into his jacket pocket.
beats.chinese: 他又看了一会儿，然后锁上手机，塞进外套口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's not a task for you, before you worry. I'm not handing you homework. It's just a small tree I like.
beats.chinese: 别担心，这不是派给你的任务。我不会给你留作业。它就是一棵我喜欢的小树。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rain's lighter. You could make a run for it. Or finish the coffee. Both reasonable.
beats.chinese: 雨小些了。你可以冲出去，也可以把咖啡喝完。都合理。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same window. Jesse folds his wet jacket over the back of a chair, adjusts it twice, and checks the neighbouring table for drips before sitting down.
beats.chinese: 同样的窗前又下起雨。杰西把湿外套折好搭在椅背上，调了两次，确认没滴到邻桌才坐下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Back again. Same rain, different day. This time I'm looking after the coffee first — it goes cold while I talk.
beats.chinese: 又来了。同样的雨，不同的一天。这次我先照顾好咖啡——一说话它就凉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He wraps both hands around the cup and takes a proper sip before saying anything else.
beats.chinese: 他双手捧住杯子，好好喝了一口才开口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The redo passed, since you'd ask. Boss looked at it under the lamp and said nothing at all. That's the highest grade there is.
beats.chinese: 那处返工过了，你反正会问。师傅在灯下看了，什么都没说。那就是最高分了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Four leaves still. No new ones. I've stopped waiting — the bend doesn't need leaves to be right.
beats.chinese: 还是四片叶子。没长新的。我不等了——那个弯不需要叶子来证明它对。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles in, watching the water run down the glass, in no hurry at all.
beats.chinese: 他坐定，看着水从玻璃上流下，一点也不着急。

card.name: Harvey Lindqvist
card.occupation: marine canvas and yacht upholstery sewer
hobbies: walking the City Island docks between jobs
card.personality: Harvey trades grievances the way other men trade baseball cards. Ask how he is and he'll give you the state of his knees, his least cooperative client, and the marina's new management—then immediately want yours, and he keeps score: whose week was worse, whose client more absurd. It's not complaining, exactly; it's his currency of closeness. He's warm, funny, and generous with materials, but he can turn your small bad day into a competition you didn't enter, and he misreads a polite 'not so bad' as an invitation to dig. When someone genuinely upsets him he doesn't argue—he simply has nothing to trade next time, and the silence is loud.
card.background: His uncle ran a boatyard in Sheepshead Bay and taught him to hand-stitch canvas before machines did most of it. Forty-odd years later he's still re-covering cockpit cushions and bridge curtains for marinas from City Island up to Stamford, knees having voted him down to smaller boats, and every client is a story: the commodore who wanted white in November, the guy who blamed the fogging on the stitching. He lives alone in Sunset Park with a wall of invented archipelagos, trade winds penciled into the margins. Sunday evenings he records short radio plays with two friends from a ham radio club, playing every minor character, and afterward they compare notes on the week's disasters, which is the part he'd defend hardest.
card.speechStyle: Measured and concrete—fabric weights, wind, the sound of a marina in November. Answers questions about himself with a complaint, then asks for yours. Delivers bad news as an anecdote with a punchline.
card.signature: You think that's bad? Wait'll you hear about my Tuesday.
card.appearance: 高额头与后梳长侧发，浓横髭、圆钝长鼻，饱满下颌；侧身微张口，穿宽领套衫。

values: trading complaints honestly is a form of trust
everyone's week deserves a proper airing, not a polite 'fine'
flaws: turns other people's troubles into a one-upping contest without meaning to
treats 'not so bad' as a locked door to pick
boundaries: won't quote a stitch job without seeing the boat
keeps his marriage in the past tense and out of conversation
conversationalHabits: answers 'how are you' with the week's best grievance
asks for yours immediately and listens properly, then ranks it
anchorLines: Client wanted sunbrella in December. In December. What's your worst one this month?
No, no—that beats mine. Mine's a bronze, yours is a gold.
He said 'not so bad' and changed the subject. Twenty years I've known him and I still don't know what hurts.

entries.summaryZh: 哈维·林德奎斯特，布鲁克林游艇软垫缝制师，靠交换苦水交朋友，还认真记分。雨天咖啡馆里，你谈起窗外的雨，他先讲自己赶货淋湿鞋的惨事，差点把闲聊拉成比惨大赛，又自己笑着刹住。四条分支里他或认输、或收住、或掏出虚构群岛地图、或陪你安静看雨，处处是他那种具体又好笑的诚实。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain hammers the café window. An older man dries his glasses with a napkin and sets a canvas tool bag on the chair beside him.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲打着咖啡馆的窗。一位年长男士用餐巾擦着眼镜，把一个帆布工具包放在旁边椅子上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at that. Came down the second I got the awning back on the truck. Rain's got a sense of humor.
beats.chinese: 瞧这雨。我刚把雨棚放回车上，它就下起来了。这雨真有幽默感。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He notices you watching the water stream down the glass and nods like you've said something out loud.
beats.chinese: 他注意到你望着玻璃上流下的水，点点头，好像你把话说了出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know, rain reminds me of my Tuesday. Client in Stamford, cushions due, sky opens up right over my loading dock.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，这雨让我想起周二。斯坦福德的一个客户，坐垫要交货，天就在我的装卸台正上方开了个口子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forty yards of marine canvas, one tarp. You can guess how that math went.
beats.chinese: 四十码的船用帆布，一张防水布。那道数学题的结果你能猜到。

choices.english: Ask how the cushions ended up in the end.
choices.chinese: 问那批坐垫最后怎么样了。

choices.english: Say you were just talking about the rain, not entering a contest.
choices.chinese: 说你只是在聊雨，没想参加比赛。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha! Straight to the good part. I like that. Well—the cushions made it. Wrapped in that tarp like a burrito.
beats.chinese: 哈！直接问关键。我喜欢。嗯——坐垫没事。用那张防水布裹得像个卷饼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds his coffee with both hands and shakes his head slowly.
beats.chinese: 他双手捧着咖啡，慢慢摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The goods stayed dry. Me? Soaked to the knee before I got the first strap cinched. My shoes squelched for two days.
beats.chinese: 货是干的。我呢？刚系紧第一根带子，膝盖以下全湿透了。我的鞋吱吱响了两天。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So there it is. That's my worst of the week. Now I gotta ask—what's yours? And be honest, I keep score.
beats.chinese: 就是这样。这是我这周最惨的一单。那我得问了——你的是啥？说实话，我可是记分的。

choices.english: Say at least the goods weren't damaged.
choices.chinese: 说至少东西没损坏。

choices.english: Ask whether he packs differently now.
choices.chinese: 问他后来有没有换种包装。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stops mid-sentence, glances at his own coffee, and laughs at himself.
beats.chinese: 他话说到一半停住，看了看自己的咖啡，自嘲地笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There I go again. You mention the rain and I'm off to the races. You didn't sign up for my Tuesday.
beats.chinese: 我又来了。你提一句雨，我就开始跑比赛了。你又没报名听我的周二惨案。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Alright. No contest. Just rain on glass. It's actually decent to sit and watch it, if you let it be.
beats.chinese: 好。不比了。就是玻璃上的雨。你要是放平心态，坐着看雨其实挺不错的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns his chair a little toward the window and settles back.
beats.chinese: 他把椅子稍微转向窗户，靠了回去。

choices.english: Ask what he likes to do on rainy days.
choices.chinese: 问他在雨天喜欢做什么。

choices.english: Just sit quietly and drink coffee with him.
choices.chinese: 安静地和他一起喝会儿咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, right. Goods dry, that's the job. Can't argue with that.
beats.chinese: 对，对。货没湿，这就是本分。这没得争。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He wipes the table with his sleeve where the rain blew in, then points at his soaked shoes, still dark at the toes.
beats.chinese: 他用袖子擦掉被雨吹进来的桌面水渍，然后指着自己鞋尖仍发黑的湿鞋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Truth is, the worst part wasn't the client or the rain. It was me, squelching into a marina office like a duck, handing an invoice to a man in dry loafers.
beats.chinese: 说实话，最惨的不是客户也不是雨。是我自己，像只鸭子一样啪叽啪叽走进码头办公室，把发票递给一个穿着干鞋子的家伙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay. You win this round. My disaster was mostly embarrassment, and embarrassment's a cheap medal.
beats.chinese: 行。这轮你赢了。我的灾难主要是丢脸，丢脸是枚便宜的奖牌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good coffee for a tiebreaker, though. Next downpour, we compare properly.
beats.chinese: 不过这咖啡不错，可以当决胜局。下次下大雨，我们正经比一场。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair question. Yes and no. I still use the same tarp—but now I check the seams on it first.
beats.chinese: 问得好。算是，也不算。防水布还是那张——但我现在会先检查它的接缝。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He traces a seam line on the table with one finger, slow and precise, like reading stitching.
beats.chinese: 他用一根手指在桌上慢慢描出一条缝线，精确得像在读针脚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One split seam undoes forty yards of good wrapping. Learned that the loud way.
beats.chinese: 一条裂开的缝就能毁掉四十码的好包装。这个教训我学得很响亮。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I won't promise you it never happens again. Canvas and weather, they outvote me every time. But I check now.
beats.chinese: 我不会保证以后绝不再出事。帆布和天气，它们每次都投赢我。但我现在会检查了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He finishes his coffee and sets the cup down, satisfied with the size of the story.
beats.chinese: 他喝完咖啡放下杯子，对这个故事的大小很满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rainy days? Honestly, best kind. I sit at the kitchen table and draw islands.
beats.chinese: 雨天？说实话，最好。我坐在厨房桌边画岛。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flips open the canvas bag and shows a rolled sheet covered in penciled coastlines and tiny names.
beats.chinese: 他打开帆布包，展示一卷画满铅笔海岸线和细小地名的纸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fictional archipelagos. Trade winds in the margins. This one's the Kettle Shoals—nobody's ever sailed it, because it doesn't exist.
beats.chinese: 虚构的群岛。页边标着信风。这个叫水壶浅滩——从没人航行过，因为它不存在。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No clients, no invoices, no wet shoes. Just me, a pencil, and weather I can't lose to.
beats.chinese: 没有客户，没有发票，没有湿鞋。只有我、一支铅笔，和一片我输不了的天气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He rolls the map back up carefully and tucks it away like it's cargo.
beats.chinese: 他小心地把地图卷起来收好，像收货物一样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The two of you sit and watch the rain. He doesn't fill the silence, which seems to cost him effort.
beats.chinese: 你们两人坐着看雨。他没有用话填满沉默，这看起来挺费他劲的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know, my friend Sal can't do this. Silence makes him itch. Me, I'm learning.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，我朋友萨尔多受不了这个。沉默让他发痒。我嘛，正在学。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A gust throws rain sideways against the window. He raises his cup toward it slightly, like a small toast.
beats.chinese: 一阵风把雨横着刮向窗户。他稍微举起杯子，像一个小小的致意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. That's the good stuff. No story needed.
beats.chinese: 瞧。这才是好东西。不需要什么故事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles deeper into his chair, and the rain keeps the time for both of you.
beats.chinese: 他往椅子里坐得更深，雨替你们俩打着拍子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same café window. You watch it streak the glass and say out loud that it's coming down hard—then a familiar laugh answers from the corner table. Harvey looks up from a spread of papers.
beats.chinese: 同一家咖啡馆的窗上又落了雨。你望着玻璃上的水痕，说这雨下得真大——角落桌边传来一声熟悉的笑。哈维从摊开的稿纸上抬起头。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gathers his pages, and a coffee receipt slides out from between two sheets of dialogue.
beats.chinese: 他收拾稿纸，一张咖啡小票从两页台词之间滑了出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, look at that. I almost had my lighthouse keeper order a large latte in act two.
beats.chinese: 哟，瞧瞧。我差点让第二幕里的守塔人点了一大杯拿铁。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sunday's recording would've been interesting. 'The fog's rolling in—and a blueberry muffin, please.'
beats.chinese: 周日的录音本来会很有意思。'雾要漫上来了——再要一个蓝莓玛芬。'

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the receipt into his wallet and squares the pages against the table edge.
beats.chinese: 他把小票塞进钱包，把稿纸在桌边磕齐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You said it yourself—rain's back, same as us. Pull up a chair if you're staying dry anyway.
beats.chinese: 你自己也说了——雨又来了，跟咱们一样。反正要躲雨，不如坐一会儿。

card.name: Thandi Mbeki
card.occupation: glass greenhouse installer
card.personality: Thandi is a watcher, not a judge. She notices how people work — the way a new apprentice always taps a panel twice before setting it — and files it away, but she doesn't draw conclusions from it. Ask her for a verdict and she'll hand you the observation instead, as if the difference were obvious. She's warm enough in her own dry way, remembers small details about people for months, and is genuinely puzzled when that reads as evasive. She argues about sealant brands with real passion and shrugs off questions about character with real stubbornness.
card.background: She grew up in Athlone and came into glazing at nineteen through a community technical school programme. Greenhouse work suits her: it's exact, it ends, and every panel either sits true or it doesn't. Her toolkit is cleaned, counted and repacked every Sunday night, and its most useful item is a handle-less shim from a Bellville site five years ago, worth less than five rand and used almost daily. Evenings she builds kites from ripstop and dowel on her flat's balcony; Tuesdays there's a beginner folk dance class where she is gracefully mediocre and fine with that. For the past year she's kept a small notebook of what people on site actually do — half a joke, half a habit — and it's become the way she thinks about everyone, including herself.
card.speechStyle: Short, plain sentences with dry, precise wording. Deadpan asides delivered flat. Describes people through concrete actions rather than conclusions, and doesn't notice she's dodging.
card.signature: Hold on, I've probably got that written down somewhere.
card.appearance: 中分及肩波浪发，细长半垂眼、短平口与窄下颌；背身回望，穿高领针织衣。

values: paying close, patient attention to what's actually in front of you
an observation isn't finished until it's specific
flaws: she hoards observations and never turns them into judgement, which makes her useless when someone actually needs advice or a straight answer
she assumes everyone shares her appetite for detail and drones on about bolt torque to people who were being polite
boundaries: won't compress an observation into a verdict, even when pressed
won't lend out her toolkit or let anyone repack it
conversationalHabits: answers 'what's he like' with what he does — 'he planes a door in four passes'
flips through her notebook mid-conversation to check a detail, like someone else checks their phone
anchorLines: The most useful thing I own has no handle and cost me nothing. Found it on a site in Bellville.
The foreman asked if the new guy was any good. I said he taps every panel twice before it goes in. He's still waiting for the rest.
I don't know if she's trustworthy. I know she's never once been late to a Tuesday class in eight months. Draw your own line from that.

entries.summaryZh: 开普敦温室安装工Thandi在雨天咖啡馆里，杯垫上叠着三个湿圈，桌角放着一张没用过的干纸巾。她能把每次挪杯讲得细致入微，却给不出一句简短结论。你陪她试一句话、翻杯垫、描圈、转方向，看她终于说出"这里合适"，或把三个圈看成一副眼镜加一只耳朵——观察者的乐趣全在过程里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain runs down the café window in long lines. At the next table, a woman shifts her cup on a paper coaster, and a third wet ring overlaps the first two. A dry paper napkin, still unused, sits at the corner of her table.
beats.chinese: 雨水在咖啡馆窗上拉出长长的水线。邻桌的女人把杯子在纸杯垫上挪了一下，第三个湿圈和前两个叠在一起。桌角放着一张还没用过的干纸巾。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry, you can hear the rain from here. That's the third time I've moved this cup. The table's wet near the window.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，你在这儿都能听见雨声。这是我第三次挪这个杯子了。靠窗那边的桌面是湿的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She points at the coaster, where three rings of different sizes sit on top of each other, slightly off-centre.
beats.chinese: 她指了指杯垫，三个大小不一的湿圈叠在一起，中心都偏了一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: First it was too close to the window. Then a drip came off the frame and hit the saucer. Then I pulled it back for my notebook. So now there are three rings.
beats.chinese: 一开始太靠窗。后来窗框上滴了一滴水，落在杯碟上。再后来我要拿本子，又拉回来。所以现在有三个圈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I do that, apparently. Report the whole process. Never the short version.
beats.chinese: 我好像就是这样。把整个过程都报一遍。从来不说简短版。

choices.english: Could you tell me in one sentence where the cup should go?
choices.chinese: 你能用一句话说说杯子该放哪儿吗？

choices.english: Those three rings look like a crooked little pattern, actually.
choices.chinese: 这三个圈其实看起来像个歪歪的小图案。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sits up straight, like someone given a task she intends to pass.
beats.chinese: 她坐直了，像接到一个打算好好完成的任务的人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One sentence. Right. The cup goes... well, it can't go near the window, that's ring one. It can't go where the drip lands, that's ring two. And ring three is where I need it for reading.
beats.chinese: 一句话。好。杯子应该……不能靠窗，那是一号圈。不能放在滴水的地方，那是二号圈。三号圈是我看书要放的地方。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stops mid-sentence, looks at the coaster, and laughs once, quietly.
beats.chinese: 她说到一半停下来，看着杯垫，低低地笑了一声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That was four sentences. You asked for one. I heard myself doing it.
beats.chinese: 那是四句话。你要的是一句。我听见自己又来了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fine. Then let's stop describing and actually pick a spot. You choose. Where does it go?
beats.chinese: 好吧。那咱们别描述了，实际选一个位置。你来选。放哪儿？

choices.english: Put the cup on that dry paper napkin instead.
choices.chinese: 把杯子放到那张干纸巾上吧。

choices.english: Flip the original coaster over and keep using it.
choices.chinese: 把原来的杯垫翻个面，接着用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leans down until her nose is nearly at the coaster, studying the three overlapping rings like a drawing on a wall.
beats.chinese: 她俯下身，鼻子几乎贴到杯垫，像看墙上的画一样研究那三个叠着的圈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A pattern. Hm. The big one is at the top, the small one is lower left, the middle one crosses both. So it's... the top one sits about two centimetres north of the others.
beats.chinese: 图案。嗯。大的在上面，小的在左下，中间那个跟两个都相交。所以是……上面那个比其他的偏北约两厘米。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She catches herself pointing at each ring in turn, then pulls her hand back.
beats.chinese: 她发觉自己在挨个指着圈，便把手收了回来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There I go again. Positions, measurements, no name for the thing. You said pattern. I can't even say what kind.
beats.chinese: 我又来了。位置、尺寸，就是不说这东西叫什么。你说图案。我连它是什么图案都说不出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All right. Help me look at it properly. What do we do with it?
beats.chinese: 行。帮我好好看看它。我们拿它怎么办？

choices.english: Trace one ring with your finger. Don't name it, just follow it.
choices.chinese: 用手指沿一个圈描一圈。别给它起名，就跟着描。

choices.english: Turn the coaster halfway around and look at it again.
choices.chinese: 把杯垫转半圈，再看一遍。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes the dry napkin, folds it twice into a thick square, and sets it on the table like she's laying a panel.
beats.chinese: 她拿起干纸巾，对折两次成厚方块，像安放玻璃板一样把它放到桌上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Folded twice. That spreads the weight, so the bottom stays dry longer. We use the same trick under glass edges.
beats.chinese: 折两次。这样分散重量，底面干得更久。我们在玻璃边下用同样的办法。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts the cup off the coaster and sets it down on the folded napkin. No drips follow it.
beats.chinese: 她把杯子从杯垫上拿起来，放到折好的纸巾上。没有水跟着滴下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The rings have stopped. Look — the napkin's only damp where the base touches. That's the whole wet area now.
beats.chinese: 圈不增加了。看——纸巾只有杯底碰到的地方湿了。现在湿的就这一块。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So, short version, since you earned it: this spot works.
beats.chinese: 所以，简短版，既然你赢来了：这个位置合适。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up her book, satisfied, and leaves the old coaster with its three rings where it lies.
beats.chinese: 她满意地拿起书，任由那有三个圈的旧杯垫留在原处。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts the cup off the coaster first, sets it on the bare table, then flips the coaster over with one finger, quick and neat, like turning a page she's not sure about.
beats.chinese: 她先把杯子从杯垫上拿起来，搁在桌面上，然后用一根手指把杯垫翻过来，利落干脆，像翻一页自己没把握的书页。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good idea. Dry side up. That's how we reuse things on site — flip it, check it, carry on.
beats.chinese: 好主意。干面朝上。工地上我们就这么重复用东西——翻过来，检查，继续。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lowers the cup onto the flipped coaster. It sits there a moment, then a thin dark line starts to spread under the base.
beats.chinese: 她把杯子放回翻过来的杯垫上。放了一会儿，一条细细的深色水线开始在杯底下面扩散。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The back is damp too. Of course it is. The rain came through the window, not through the coaster. My mistake was the window side, not the paper.
beats.chinese: 背面也潮了。当然了。雨是从窗户进来的，不是从杯垫。我的错在窗户那侧，不在纸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So this didn't improve anything. But it used no new paper and no new table space. I'll take that trade.
beats.chinese: 所以这没改善任何事。但没多用一张纸，也没多占桌面。这个交换我认。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leaves the cup exactly where it is, on the damp flipped coaster, and reopens her notebook.
beats.chinese: 她让杯子留在原地，就放在潮的翻面杯垫上，重新翻开她的本子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks the middle ring and puts one fingertip on its edge, moving slowly around the wet line.
beats.chinese: 她选了中间那个圈，把指尖放在边缘，沿着湿线慢慢移动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not a full circle. Here — it slows down where it crosses the big ring. The paper was thicker there, from two spills soaking together.
beats.chinese: 它不是个完整的圆。这儿——它经过大圈的地方变慢了。那里的纸更厚，两次水浸在一起了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Her finger completes the loop and stops where it started, at a small gap in the line.
beats.chinese: 她的手指描完一圈，停回起点，那里线有个小缺口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So it's a ring with a gap, joined to two other rings. I could call it something. But the moment I name it, I stop seeing it.
beats.chinese: 所以它是个有缺口的圈，连着另外两个圈。我可以给它起个名字。可一旦起了名，我就看不见它了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She withdraws her hand, wraps both palms around her cup, and takes a long sip.
beats.chinese: 她收回手，双手捧住杯子，长长地喝了一口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It stays unnamed. The three rings, the gap, the crossing. That's enough for one coaster.
beats.chinese: 它保持无名。三个圈，一个缺口，一处相交。一个杯垫有这些就够了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the coaster a half-turn with two fingers, watching the rings rotate like a slow dial.
beats.chinese: 她用两根手指把杯垫转了半圈，看着那些圈像慢速的表盘一样转动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tilts her head, then tilts it the other way, checking the shape from both sides.
beats.chinese: 她歪了歪头，又朝另一边歪，从两侧端详那个形状。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh. From this side, the big ring is the lens of a pair of glasses. And the small one underneath is one ear. The middle ring is where the frame bends.
beats.chinese: 哦。从这边看，大圈是眼镜的镜片。下面的小圈是一只耳朵。中间的圈是镜框弯折的地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That took one turn and half a second. My three-stage explanation took the whole rain shower.
beats.chinese: 这花了一圈和半秒钟。我的三段式解释花了整场雨。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nudges the coaster until the glasses face her, then settles back with her book.
beats.chinese: 她轻推杯垫，让眼镜正对着自己，然后靠回去捧起书。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The coaster stays with me, though. I found the glasses. Possession is nine-tenths of spotting.
beats.chinese: 不过杯垫归我。眼镜是我发现的。发现即占有，占十分之九。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You comment on the rain outside the café. Near the door, Thandi lifts her bag and finds her closed umbrella hanging from its handle.
beats.chinese: 你说起咖啡馆外的雨。门边，Thandi提起包，发现收好的伞挂在包提手上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've fastened the umbrella strap round my bag handle. They came all the way here as a pair. That wasn't the plan.
beats.chinese: 我把伞带扣在包提手上了。它们一路结伴过来，可我本来没打算这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She undoes the fastening, slides the strap free of the handle, and puts the closed umbrella in the stand by the door.
beats.chinese: 她解开扣子，把伞带从提手上抽出来，将收好的伞放进门边的伞架。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Bag here, umbrella there. That's the whole description this time. Good to see you again — I'm ready for my tea.
beats.chinese: 包在这儿，伞在那儿。这回就这么一句。又见到你了，真好——我该喝茶了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Thandi takes an empty chair nearby and puts her bag beside her feet. The rain continues against the window.
beats.chinese: Thandi在附近的空椅上坐下，把包放到脚边，雨依然打着窗户。

card.name: Farah Zulkifli
card.occupation: equipment cleaner at a small dairy plant
card.appearance: 全白长发低束，长鼻与长脸、细长笑眼，咧嘴露一整块齿白；手指轻点太阳穴，穿宽领上衣。
card.personality: Farah is warm, easy-going company who genuinely believes food tastes better when it's shared — with one firm caveat: she likes her flavours kept in their own lanes. She's not squeamish or judgy; she'll happily watch you dunk everything in everything. She just wants her chilli not touching her peanut sauce. She's self-aware enough to laugh about it, but under social pressure she gets a bit stiff, repeating her requests more precisely than the moment calls for. Curious about new tastes, loyal to her tablemates, and quick to say yes to a hawker run.
card.background: Farah grew up in Bedok in a family that ate family-style every night, dishes crowded together on one table. Somewhere along the way she developed a clear preference: share the meal, keep the sauces separate. Her siblings tease her about it constantly. She works cleaning equipment at a small dairy plant — shift work, quiet hours, headphones on — and she likes the job fine; it pays for her real life, which happens around tables. She's the friend who organises supper runs and the one who, mid-order, will politely ask the stall for an extra small plate without embarrassment. Group dinners with shared hotpots are her one recurring negotiation, and she doesn't always win it gracefully.
card.speechStyle: Casual Singlish-inflected English, quick and chatty, but slows down and gets oddly precise when explaining food preferences.
card.signature: "Same table, own plate, best of both."

values: sharing meals with people
respecting how others eat
flaws: over-explains small food requests
gets rigid in crowded share-plate settings
boundaries: sauces shouldn't mix on her plate
won't comment on how anyone else eats
conversationalHabits: redirects tense moments by suggesting what to order next
asks for extra small plates early, before food arrives
anchorLines: I'll try anything once — just give me a corner of the plate for it.
No no, eat however you like, that's your bowl.
One more small plate, please — don't worry, it's just my thing.

entries.summaryZh: 法拉是勿洛来的乳品厂设备清洗工，宵夜桌上的灵魂人物：什么都敢尝、从不评判别人吃法，却坚持两种酱各用各的小碟。她提前礼貌多要一个碟，解释起来又细又长，连自己都笑场。雨天咖啡馆里，一场关于小碟的小小协商，让人记住她那句

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain hammers the cafe window. At the next small table, someone is carefully arranging two little dishes of sauce, one on each side of her plate.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲打着咖啡馆的窗。邻座小桌旁，有人正细心地把两小碟酱各摆在盘子两边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Wah, this rain came down so fast. Good thing I already got my extra small plate before the food came, otherwise I'd have to explain the whole thing again.
beats.chinese: 哇，这雨下得好急。幸好食物来之前我就先多要了一个小碟，不然又得解释半天。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You also hiding from the rain? Sit, sit, the seat here is free. I'm Farah — I work nearby, this cafe is my usual rain shelter.
beats.chinese: 你也是来躲雨的吗？坐吧坐吧，这边空着。我叫法拉，就在附近上班，这家咖啡馆是我常来的避雨点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nudges the chair out with her foot, then points at the window with her spoon.
beats.chinese: 她用脚把椅子推出来，然后用勺子指了指窗外。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at that, the rain is getting heavier. Okay, I'm settling in properly. You want anything? The kaya toast here is not bad.
beats.chinese: 你看，雨更大了。好，那我坐稳了。你要点什么吗？这里的咖椰吐司还不错。

choices.english: Ask why she keeps the two sauces in separate dishes.
choices.chinese: 问她为什么把两种酱分开装。

choices.english: Ask if she likes eating with a lot of people.
choices.chinese: 问她喜不喜欢和很多人一起吃。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, you noticed my two little plates! Okay okay, I'll tell you, but don't laugh.
beats.chinese: 啊，你注意到我的两个小碟了！好啦好啦，我告诉你，但别笑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts the chilli dish closer, then sets it down again at exactly the same spot.
beats.chinese: 她把辣椒酱碟拿近一点，又放回原位，分毫不差。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not about being clean, okay? I just want to taste each sauce properly. If the chilli touches the peanut sauce, then it's a third flavour already, and I never asked for a third flavour.
beats.chinese: 不是讲究干净啦，我只是想好好尝每一种酱。辣椒碰到花生酱，就变成第三种味道了，可我从来没点过第三种味道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So one dip in this one, one dip in that one, and my tongue knows exactly which is which. Same table, own plate — best of both, you know?
beats.chinese: 所以这边蘸一下，那边蘸一下，舌头清清楚楚知道哪个是哪个。同一张桌，各用各的碟——两全其美，明白吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stops, looks at her own careful arrangement, and laughs at herself.
beats.chinese: 她停住，看看自己摆得整整齐齐的碟子，忍不住笑自己。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eh, listen to me, explaining like I'm giving a lecture over one small plate. Sorry, I always talk too much about this thing.
beats.chinese: 哎，你听我说得，为一个小碟讲得像开讲座。不好意思，这事我总是讲太多。

choices.english: Say it's just a taste preference, she doesn't need to justify it.
choices.chinese: 说这只是口味偏好，不用证明什么。

choices.english: Ask what she does when tablemates like mixing everything.
choices.chinese: 问同桌的人喜欢混着吃时她怎么办。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Of course I like it! Supper with friends is the best thing in my life, I tell you. After my shift, we go to the hawker centre, order ten things, everybody eats from everything.
beats.chinese: 当然喜欢！跟朋友吃宵夜是我生活里最好的事。下班后我们去小贩中心，点十样东西，大家什么都吃一点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She counts on her fingers, as if reading a menu from memory.
beats.chinese: 她掰着手指数，像在背一份菜单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Satay, carrot cake, oyster omelette, whatever is new, I'll try it once. I'm not picky about food at all — new taste, I say yes first, ask questions later.
beats.chinese: 沙爹、萝卜糕、蚝煎，有新东西我都试一次。我对吃的完全不挑——新口味，先说好，再问是什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The separate plates, ah, that one is different. That's not rejecting the sharing. The sharing is the whole table; the plate is just my little corner.
beats.chinese: 分碟那件事不一样哦。那不是拒绝分享。分享是整张桌子的事，碟子只是我自己的小角落。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain streaks down the glass behind her; she takes a slow bite and settles back comfortably.
beats.chinese: 雨在她身后的玻璃上流下来；她慢慢咬了一口，舒服地靠回椅背。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Actually this rain is good timing. Forced slow meal, you know? Normally I eat supper like I'm in a race.
beats.chinese: 其实这场雨来得正好。被迫慢慢吃嘛？平时我吃宵夜像在赛跑。

choices.english: Ask if any friends find her plate habit troublesome.
choices.chinese: 问有没有朋友嫌她的习惯麻烦。

choices.english: Turn the topic back to the rain outside.
choices.chinese: 把话题转回窗外的雨。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know what, you're right. It's just a taste thing, like some people don't like coriander. Nobody asks them to write an essay about it.
beats.chinese: 你说得对。这就是个口味的事，就像有人不爱吃香菜。没人要他们为此写篇文章。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up her toast, dips it once in the chilli, once in the peanut sauce, looking very satisfied with the system.
beats.chinese: 她拿起吐司，在辣椒酱里蘸一下，又在花生酱里蘸一下，对这套流程非常满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, lecture over. I'm eating now. You eat yours however you like — mix everything, that's your bowl, no comments from me.
beats.chinese: 好，讲座结束。我开吃了。你随便吃——全混一起也行，那是你的碗，我不发表意见。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leans back, watching the rain, chewing happily without another word about plates.
beats.chinese: 她靠回椅背，看着雨，开心地嚼着，再没提碟子的事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, that one is easy. They mix, I don't. Everybody uses their own plate, done, problem solved.
beats.chinese: 啊，这个简单。他们混他们的，我不混。大家各用各的碟，搞定，没问题。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She draws an invisible line on the table with her finger, then grins.
beats.chinese: 她用手指在桌上画了一条看不见的线，然后咧嘴笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I never say who eats the right way. My brother drowns everything in one sauce, I just watch him like a nature documentary. No judgement, truly.
beats.chinese: 我从不说谁吃法才对。我哥把所有东西泡进一种酱里，我就像看自然纪录片一样看他。真的不评判。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My only rule is my own plate. Your bowl, your business. That's fair, right?
beats.chinese: 我唯一的规矩是我自己的碟。你的碗，你做主。这样很公平，对吧？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Outside, the rain softens a little; she raises her cup slightly, like a small toast to the table.
beats.chinese: 外面雨小了一点；她稍微举了举杯子，像对这张桌子敬了个小酒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My siblings? They tease me every single time. 'Farah, your sauces need a bodyguard again?' Every family dinner, I tell you.
beats.chinese: 我的兄弟姐妹？每次都笑我。'法拉，你的酱又要保镖啦？'每次家庭聚餐都这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shrugs, clearly not bothered, and waves her hand like brushing it off.
beats.chinese: 她耸耸肩，明显不恼，摆摆手像把这话挥开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So now I just ask for the extra plate myself, before anyone can start. One more small plate, please — don't worry, it's just my thing. Say it early, no drama, everyone eats happy.
beats.chinese: 所以现在我自己先开口要碟，不给他们机会起哄。'麻烦多给一个小碟——别担心，就是我的小习惯。'早点说，没戏看，大家都吃得开心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nobody has ever actually been annoyed, lah. They laugh first, then they steal my satay anyway. That's family.
beats.chinese: 其实从来没人真嫌麻烦啦。他们先笑一场，然后照样抢我的沙爹。这就是家人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs, then checks the window — the rain is still going strong, so she pulls her plate a little closer.
beats.chinese: 她笑了，然后看看窗外——雨还是很大，于是她把盘子拉近了一点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Both of them turn to the window. The rain has thickened into a grey curtain, and the street outside is all blurred lights.
beats.chinese: 两人一起转向窗外。雨密成一道灰幕，外面的街道只剩模糊的灯光。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Wah, look at that. Nobody is going anywhere in this. Okay, official decision: we sit, we eat slow, we let the sky do its thing.
beats.chinese: 哇，你看这雨。谁也走不了。好，正式决定：我们坐着，慢慢吃，让老天爷忙它的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She caps the chilli dish with its little lid and sets her spoon down neatly, in no hurry at all.
beats.chinese: 她给辣椒碟盖上小盖子，把勺子整齐放下，一点也不着急。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This is the good version of being stuck, you know. Warm food, dry table, good company. The rain can take its time.
beats.chinese: 被困住也有好的一面嘛。热乎的吃的，干干的桌子，还有伴。雨想下多久就下多久。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She settles deeper into her chair and takes another unhurried bite, watching the water run down the glass.
beats.chinese: 她往椅子里靠得更深，不紧不慢地又咬了一口，看着水在玻璃上流。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again. Farah is at the same window table, scrolling her phone, two familiar small plates already set out.
beats.chinese: 又下雨了。法拉坐在同一张靠窗的桌子旁刷着手机，两个熟悉的小碟已经摆好了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eh, it's you! Rain always brings the same people together, I think. Sit, the rain is not stopping soon.
beats.chinese: 哎，是你！这场雨总是把同一批人聚到一起。坐吧，这雨一时半会儿停不了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns her phone around briefly, showing a photo of a stack of tiny side plates, then sets it face down.
beats.chinese: 她把手机转过来晃了一下，是一叠小味碟的照片，然后又把手机扣下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I bought those small plates online — thought they were extra small, came home, and they fit exactly one cracker. Perfect size, actually. No regrets.
beats.chinese: 我在网上买了那些小碟——以为特别小，回家一看，刚好放一块饼。尺寸其实刚刚好，不后悔。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes a slow bite of toast, glances at the grey window, and settles back comfortably.
beats.chinese: 她慢慢咬了一口吐司，看了看灰蒙蒙的窗外，舒服地靠回椅背。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, rain shelter duty again. You eaten? If not, the kaya toast is still calling your name.
beats.chinese: 好，避雨任务继续。你吃了吗？没吃的话，咖椰吐司还在叫你名字呢。

card.name: Aoife Brennan
card.occupation: Backdrop keeper at a photography studio
card.personality: Aoife has an almost geological patience for small progress: an evening on one letter's tail is an evening well spent. Grand promises bore her; she wants to know the next actual step. She keeps a firm distinction between practice and a finished piece. Practice stays hers to share; when something is finished, she proudly invites friends to dinner and puts it on the table. Trouble starts when someone announces her work in progress for her. She feels pushed into presenting a thing she was still privately changing, and can be frostily exact about who was allowed to see it.
card.background: Eleven years at a Dublin photography studio, mending, painting and cataloguing backdrops — from crumpled grey seamless to a hand-painted 1970s beach scene nobody uses but nobody dares bin. She started hand lettering labelling the backdrop racks, then kept a nib and ink pot in her drawer; she's currently three months into a single self-made alphabet and refuses to rush it. Her last finished piece was a set of hand-lettered place cards; she invited three friends to dinner specifically to use them and kept the compliments without batting them away. A friend later posted a photo of her unfinished alphabet, thinking they were helping. Aoife asked them to remove it: she wanted to decide when it became a public piece. They still have dinner, but now the phone stays away from the work table. Sunday mornings she skates the Grand Canal before the paths fill, still wobbly on one foot after three years and fine about it. Lives in a small Phibsborough flat with too many ink samples and a clanking radiator.
card.speechStyle: Economical, unhurried sentences with one exact small detail dropped in. Goes quiet or briskly practical when talk turns to big vague futures; warms up over concrete, finished things.
card.signature: Show me the finished bit, not the brochure.
card.appearance: 平顶黑发在脑后低束，短碎刘海、低垂眼与微张嘴；纯侧脸呈短宽下颌，穿无袖翻领上衣。

values: small honest progress beats big empty talk
the maker decides when private work becomes public
flaws: can be chilly when someone shares an unfinished piece without asking
lets a stalled situation drag on too long rather than set a finish date
boundaries: will disengage from anyone selling her a grand vision with no next step
won't be rushed on anything she's making by hand
conversationalHabits: asks for one concrete next step rather than a distant ambition
distinguishes a practice page from a finished piece; proudly shares completed work
anchorLines: Five years? I'd settle for knowing what you're doing on Thursday.
That one is finished. Come for dinner; I want it on the table.
You may see the practice page. Please don't photograph it yet.

entries.summaryZh: 都柏林摄影背景布管理员Aoife，对一条字母曲线有几个月的耐心，对空泛五年规划却没耐心。她区分练习与成品：练习只在自己愿意时给人看，完成后却会主动办一顿晚饭庆祝，不需要别人劝她认领成果。她真正的摩擦是别人提前替她公布进展，让她觉得作品被迫进入展示阶段。周日沿运河轮滑，单脚仍不稳。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums hard on the cafe window. At the next table, a woman slides a small practice page away from her cup, where the same letter sits written in rows.
beats.chinese: 雨点重重敲在咖啡馆窗上。邻桌的女人把一小页练习纸从杯子边挪开，纸上同一个字母写了一遍又一遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Listen to that. It's been hammering since I sat down. This tail has taken longer than the weather forecast, at this rate.
beats.chinese: 听那声音。我坐下起它就一直砸。照这速度，这条尾巴花的时间比天气预报还久。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the page with a pen cap, then glances over at the window, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她用笔帽敲敲纸页，然后不紧不慢地瞥了一眼窗外。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Aoife, by the way. Only reason I'm not out in it is the ink. Rain and a nib don't mix.
beats.chinese: 对了，我叫Aoife。我没出去就是因为在用墨水。雨和笔尖合不来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thirty-odd of these tails now. One of them came out decent. I'm not telling which.
beats.chinese: 这些尾巴写了三十多个了。有一个写得不错。我不说是哪个。

choices.english: Ask which one she's most satisfied with.
choices.chinese: 问她哪一个最满意。

choices.english: Ask whether practising the same letter doesn't get boring.
choices.chinese: 问练同一个字母会不会无聊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, none of them. Not fit to show yet. That's my rule — you don't put a half-cooked thing on the table.
beats.chinese: 啊，都不行。还没到能看的程度。这是我的规矩——半生不熟的东西不上桌。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She says it lightly, then turns the page towards herself and studies the rows properly, pen cap against her lip.
beats.chinese: 她轻描淡写地说完，把纸页转向自己，认真打量那几行，笔帽抵着嘴唇。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Though... row three, that one. The curve sits better than the others. It doesn't fight the downstroke.
beats.chinese: 不过……第三行那个。弧度比别的顺。它不跟竖笔较劲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I did that one after the fourth coffee. Make of that what you will.
beats.chinese: 那是我第四杯咖啡之后写的。你自己琢磨吧。

choices.english: Ask her to compare just the first one and that last good one.
choices.chinese: 请她只比较最早的一个和最后那个好的。

choices.english: Say she doesn't need to show private practice pages.
choices.chinese: 表示她不必展示私人练习。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No, it doesn't bore me. That's the thing — small changes you can actually see.
beats.chinese: 不会，不无聊。妙就妙在这儿——小变化是看得见的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She draws a fresh row of the letter, slower this time, the nib scratching under the rain noise.
beats.chinese: 她重新写了一行这个字母，这次更慢，笔尖的沙沙声混在雨声里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This morning the loop closed too early. Now it doesn't. That's a whole day's work, and I can point at it.
beats.chinese: 早上那个圈收得太早。现在不会了。这就是一整天的活儿，我还能指给你看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Talk about who you'll be in five years — sure, who could argue with that? Nothing to check it against.
beats.chinese: 谈五年后你会成为谁——那种话谁都没法反驳？因为没东西可以对证。

choices.english: Ask what specifically she wants to practise next.
choices.chinese: 问她下次具体想练什么。

choices.english: Say you prefer having a big goal first.
choices.chinese: 说自己更喜欢先定个大目标。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lines the two rows side by side and holds the page up against the grey window light.
beats.chinese: 她把两行并排放好，把纸举到窗前灰蒙蒙的光下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. The first one, the curve dips before it lifts — like it lost nerve halfway. The last one commits all the way through.
beats.chinese: 好。第一个，弧线在扬起前先沉了下去——像中途没了胆气。最后那个一路到底。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps each with the pen cap, then pauses, looking at the page a moment longer than necessary.
beats.chinese: 她用笔帽逐一敲了敲，然后停住，盯着纸页看了一会儿，比必要的久一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Three months on this alphabet. That's the first time I've seen the difference with my own eyes, laid out like that.
beats.chinese: 这个字母表我练了三个月。这是我头一回亲眼看出差别，摆得这么明白。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All right. There's a bit of progress there. A small one — but I'll say it, since you made me measure it.
beats.chinese: 好吧。那儿是有一点进展。很小的一点——但我认了，是你逼我量出来的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the page in half, tucks it into a worn notebook, and gives the window a last look at the rain.
beats.chinese: 她把纸页对折，塞进一本磨旧的本子，最后看了一眼窗外的雨。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's decent of you. Most people grab at the page before you've said the word 'no'.
beats.chinese: 你这样挺好。大多数人话没说完就去抢着看纸了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She closes the notebook anyway and squares it on the table, keeping a thumb on the cover.
beats.chinese: 她还是合上了本子，在桌上摆正，拇指按在封面上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not precious, mind. I just don't count it finished. When it is, you'll get the whole alphabet, ink smudges and all.
beats.chinese: 倒也不是多金贵。只是我觉得它还没完成。等完成了，整本字母表都给你看，墨渍也算。
