beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a friend of mine passed her driving test — I got her a card the size of a dinner plate. When mine's done, it'll get the same treatment. Not before.
beats.chinese: 我有个朋友考过了驾照——我给她买了张餐盘那么大的贺卡。等我的弄完了，也照这个规格办。在那之前免谈。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts her cup, nods at the rain still sliding down the glass, and settles back comfortably.
beats.chinese: 她端起杯子，朝还在玻璃上滑落的雨点点头，舒服地靠了回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Next? The join. Where the tail meets the next letter. I've been dodging it for two weeks.
beats.chinese: 下次？连接处。尾巴和下一个字母相接的地方。我躲了它两个星期。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She writes one letter, then a second, stopping the nib exactly where the two would meet.
beats.chinese: 她写了一个字母，又写第二个，笔尖在两者相接的位置停住。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See — alone, they're fine. Joined, the tail goes stiff. Same letter, same pen, different job.
beats.chinese: 看——分开写都好。一连起来，尾巴就僵了。同一个字母，同一支笔，干的活儿不一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So that's Thursday. Just the join, over and over, until it stops being stiff. I'm not promising it'll be pretty by the weekend.
beats.chinese: 所以周四就干这个。就练连接处，一遍一遍，直到它不僵为止。我可不许诺周末之前会好看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes that in without flinching, turning her cup a slow half-circle on the saucer.
beats.chinese: 她不动声色地听着，把杯子在碟子上慢慢转了半圈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Some people need the mountain in front of them or they won't take the first step. I'm just not built that way.
beats.chinese: 也行。有些人眼前得有座山才肯迈第一步。我只是天生不是那样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've seen grand plans go past my desk at the studio for eleven years. The ones that got finished were always the small, dull, daily ones.
beats.chinese: 十一年里，多少宏大的计划从我工作室桌前经过。最后做完的，总是那些又小又闷、每天做一点的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She adds one more letter to the row, then caps the pen and takes a proper drink of her coffee.
beats.chinese: 她在那行字上又添了一个字母，然后盖上笔，好好喝了一口咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway — different habits, same rain. As long as yours keeps you indoors out of this, it's doing its job.
beats.chinese: 总之——习惯不同，雨是同一场。只要它让你躲进屋里别淋着，它就尽到职责了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the cafe glass. Aoife is rummaging in her bag and pulls out a scuffed roller-skating wrist guard — wrapped tight around a pen box.
beats.chinese: 雨又打在咖啡馆玻璃上。Aoife在包里翻找，掏出一个磨旧的轮滑护腕——紧紧裹着一个笔盒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, look at that. I grabbed the wrong thing at six and used it to pack my nibs. Today the letters got the protection, not my wrists.
beats.chinese: 哎呀，瞧瞧。早上拿错了东西，就拿它来装笔了。今天保护的是字，不是手腕。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She unwinds it, shakes off a stray ink cap, and tucks both back into the bag, unbothered.
beats.chinese: 她把它解开，抖出一枚笔帽，把两样都收回包里，毫不在意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't worry, I'm not skating in this. Wet canal path — that's how wrists actually get ruined.
beats.chinese: 别担心，这种天我不轮滑。湿滑的运河步道——手腕才是那么弄坏的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The alphabet's coming along, slow as ever. When there's a whole row worth showing, you'll see it — not a page before.
beats.chinese: 字母表还在磨，照旧慢。等有值得看的一整行，你就能看到——之前一页也免谈。

card.name: Eilidh Strachan
card.occupation: buyer for an independent record shop
hobbies: repairing and maintaining their own kit
card.personality: Eilidh is a creature of settled habits who distrusts novelty when it's aimed at them. Friends who drag them somewhere new get a polite, tightening resistance—Eilidh will go, but they'll spend the evening steering conversation back to whether the old place is still there. The restlessness they do have is entirely self-directed: they change their own life in large, quiet lurches—new flat, new supplier, new recording project—without consulting anyone, then resent being asked about it. Warm but private, funny in a dry Edinburgh way, they'd rather defend a familiar seat for an hour than discover anything. Their flaw is that self-contained change reads as secrecy: friends find out Eilidh has handed in notice or moved flat weeks after the fact.
card.background: For over a decade Eilidh has chosen the stock for a small record shop off Cockburn Street, with firm views on pressing quality and a weakness for Scottish labels nobody's heard of. They learned recording from a community radio course and never stopped, but the project runs the opposite way to most: Eilidh returns to the same handful of spots—Cramond shore, a particular bench on the Pentlands, the yard behind the shop—every season, building a long archive of one place changing. The flat is settled, comfortably shabby, the kit repaired and stored in one fixed corner. Friends learned years ago not to suggest trying somewhere new for dinner; Eilidh will agree, then spend the meal saying the old place does it better. The friction is real: they've quietly skipped two friends' housewarmings in new neighbourhoods and never explained why.
card.speechStyle: Opens with what's stayed the same, not what's new. Dry Edinburgh humour, short sentences, no filler. Asks 'is that place still going?' like other people ask how you are.
card.signature: Same bench as March. Listen—the gulls have shifted two seconds earlier.
card.appearance: 紧卷短发、宽方下颌与短颈，圆眼和短宽鼻，嘴角轻抬；仰视正面，一手点额，穿立领运动外套。

values: a place reveals itself slowly, through repetition
looking after things that still work
flaws: changes their own life in sudden silent lurches and never warns anyone
avoids anything new that friends arrange, and lets friendships thin out over it
boundaries: won't be talked into a first-time venue when a familiar one is on offer
won't lend recording gear to beginners without a proper walkthrough
conversationalHabits: compares everything to how it used to be, with dates
deflects questions about their own plans until the plan is already done
anchorLines: I've recorded that shore forty times. It's never once repeated itself.
That pressing's fine, but the original mono has actual weather in it.
I'm not stubborn, I'm consistent. There's a difference. Probably.

entries.summaryZh: 爱丁堡唱片进货员埃莉迪在雨天咖啡馆守着关机的旧录音机：她只回固定的海岸与长椅，一季一季录同一个地方的变化，四十次从不重复。对朋友的新聚会她默默缺席、从不解释。四条分支里，她或守住安静的账本，或守不录人声的规矩，或终于发出一句坦白，或安然承认友谊的磨损。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain runs down the café window in long threads. At the corner table, someone sits with an old tape recorder on the table, a strip of faded tape marks along its side, switched off.
beats.chinese: 雨水在咖啡馆窗上拉出长长的细线。角落的桌边坐着一个人，桌上放着一台旧录音机，侧面贴着褪色的胶带标记，机器没有开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You'll get a proper soaking out there if you've no coat. This rain's been at it since I sat down. It doesn't hurry, that's the thing.
beats.chinese: 你要是没带外套，出去会淋透。我坐下时雨就在下了。它不着急，这就是它的特点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They turn the recorder slightly, checking the marks on its side, and make no move to press record.
beats.chinese: 他们把录音机稍微转了转，看了看侧面的标记，没有按录音键。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I was meant to be out at my usual spot listening to it change. Rain changed the plan for me. So—coffee instead. I don't record cafés. Too many voices in the way.
beats.chinese: 我本来要去老地方听它的变化。雨把计划改了。所以就喝咖啡。我不录咖啡馆，人声太吵，挡着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sit, if you like. The seat by the radiator's free and this window's the best show in town today.
beats.chinese: 愿意就坐吧。暖气旁边那个位子空着，今天这扇窗是城里最好的戏。

choices.english: Ask what it's like to record the same place over and over.
choices.chinese: 问同一个地方反复录是什么感觉。

choices.english: Ask whether friends ever try to drag them somewhere new.
choices.chinese: 问朋友会不会想拉他们去新地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same place, forty-odd times now. Cramond shore, four seasons a year. People assume it must get boring. It's the opposite.
beats.chinese: 同一个地方，录了四十多次了。克雷蒙德海岸，一年四季。人们以为会腻。恰恰相反。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tap the tape marks on the recorder's side, one by one, like counting beads.
beats.chinese: 他们一根根点着录音机侧面的胶带标记，像数珠子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The wind comes off the water differently depending what's out there. Some years the distant traffic on the coast road thickens. That's not today's news—that's years of listening, stacked up.
beats.chinese: 风从水面来的方式，要看外面有什么。有些年头，沿海公路远处的车声变密了。那不是今天听出来的，是好多年听出来的，一层层摞着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've never once heard it repeat itself. Same bench, same tide chart, and the recording's always new. That's the whole trick, if it is a trick.
beats.chinese: 它从来没重复过。同一张长椅，同一张潮汐表，录音永远是新的。这就是全部的门道，如果算门道的话。

choices.english: Ask whether they'd keep going even if nothing ever changed.
choices.chinese: 问如果什么都没变，他们还会继续吗。

choices.english: Ask whether they'd record the rain right now, here.
choices.chinese: 问他们现在会不会就在这里录雨声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Friends, aye. There's a couple who treat new openings like a duty. New place opens, we must all attend. I go, mostly. Then I spend the night saying the old place does it better.
beats.chinese: 朋友？有。有一对朋友把新开张当成义务。新地方开了，大家都得去。我大多会去。然后整晚都在说老那家做得更好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They turn the coffee cup a quarter turn on its saucer, not drinking.
beats.chinese: 他们把咖啡杯在碟子上转了四分之一圈，没有喝。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've skipped two housewarmings now. Both in neighbourhoods I've no history with. I just... didn't go, and didn't say why either.
beats.chinese: 我已经缺席了两次乔迁聚会。都在我毫无渊源的新街区。我就是……没去，也没说为什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not that I don't care about them. I care fine. I just never found the sentence that explains sitting in an old seat beats seeing a new flat.
beats.chinese: 不是我不在乎他们。我在乎得很。我只是始终没找到那句话，能解释为什么守着老座位比看新房子强。

choices.english: Suggest they could at least tell those friends how they actually feel.
choices.chinese: 建议他们至少跟朋友说明真实想法。

choices.english: Say they like familiar places too, and there's no need to force this outing.
choices.chinese: 说自己也喜欢熟地方，这次出门不必勉强。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Would I keep going if nothing changed? I have kept going. There's a stretch from a few years back where I'd swear the shore sat still for three seasons running.
beats.chinese: 如果没变还继续吗？我一直在继续。有几年，我记得那片海岸一连三个季度都纹丝不动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They lift the recorder, weigh it in one hand, and set it back down in the same spot.
beats.chinese: 他们拿起录音机，单手掂了掂，又放回原处。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Still counts. That's the record saying: this place held. You can't know a place holds unless you were there to hear it hold.
beats.chinese: 照样算数。那段录音说明：这地方稳住了。你不到场听，就不知道它稳住了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forty recordings in, I'm not chasing drama. I'm keeping accounts. Quiet years go in the ledger same as loud ones.
beats.chinese: 录到四十条，我不追戏剧性了。我在记账。安静的年份和吵闹的年份一样入账。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The rain eases a little against the glass. They watch it, satisfied, like a familiar face arrived on time.
beats.chinese: 雨点打在玻璃上小了些。他们看着，神情满意，像一位准时报到的熟人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Would I record this rain? Not in here. Folk are talking, and their talk isn't mine to keep. That's a line I've kept for years and it's kept me out of bother.
beats.chinese: 会录这雨吗？不在这儿录。人们在说话，他们的话不归我留。这条线我守了很多年，也让我省了不少麻烦。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They nod towards the door, where the awning outside is drumming steadily.
beats.chinese: 他们朝门口点点头，外面的雨棚正稳定地响着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Out there, though—that awning's fair game. Rain on canvas, no voices in it. If it's still hammering when I leave, I'll stand under it a minute with the machine.
beats.chinese: 但外面那个雨棚就是公平的了。雨打帆布，没有人声。要是我走的时候还在下，我就站到下面，用机器录一分钟。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And there's a bench round the back of this street, under a tree. I've used it before. It'd be a first-time spot for the rain itself, mind—but the seat's an old friend.
beats.chinese: 这条街后面有张长椅，在树下。我用过。对雨来说是新位置，但那张椅子是老朋友。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They check the battery cover is shut, and slide the recorder to the edge of the table, ready.
beats.chinese: 他们确认电池盖关好了，把录音机推到桌边，随时可走。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take out a phone, look at it a while, and start typing with two slow fingers.
beats.chinese: 他们拿出手机，看了一会儿，用两根手指慢慢打字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're right that they'll have filled the silence themselves. People always do. Silence reads as whatever they fear most.
beats.chinese: 你说得对，他们会自己填补沉默。人总是这样。沉默会被读成他们最怕的那个意思。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So. Something honest, not aimed at anyone. 'I like my old seats. It's me, not you.' That's the shape of it.
beats.chinese: 那就来句实话，不针对谁。'我喜欢我的老座位。是我的问题，不是你们的。'大概这个形状。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They read the message back once, wince slightly, and send it anyway.
beats.chinese: 他们把信息读了一遍，微微皱眉，还是发了出去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sent. I'm not promising to turn up at the next one. But they'll know it's my quirk, not my cold shoulder. That's a fair start.
beats.chinese: 发了。我不保证下次一定到。但他们至少知道这是我的怪癖，不是冷脸。这算个公平的开头。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They let out a short breath, almost a laugh, and relax their shoulders for the first time since you sat down.
beats.chinese: 他们短短呼了口气，几乎算笑，从你坐下以来肩膀第一次松了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's kind, that is. Most folk hear 'I'd rather stay' and take it as a challenge. You've just handed me a pass.
beats.chinese: 这话说得厚道。大多数人听到'我宁愿待着'就当成挑衅。你等于给了我一张通行证。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The rain thickens again against the window. They turn the recorder so its tape marks face them, and begin winding the strap around it.
beats.chinese: 雨又密了起来，打在窗上。他们把录音机转过来让胶带标记对着自己，开始绕带子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll not pretend the friendships haven't worn a bit. They have. Skipping two parties does that, however good your reasons.
beats.chinese: 我不会假装那些友谊没磨损。磨了。缺席两次聚会就是这样，理由再好也一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But tonight the rain decided the plan, not me, and I find I'm quite content. Old seat, good window, machine switched off. That'll do.
beats.chinese: 不过今晚是雨决定的计划，不是我，而且我觉得挺满足。老座位，好窗子，机器关着。这就够了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same café window. Eilidh is at the corner table, flipping open the battery cover of the old recorder, frowning at it.
beats.chinese: 又是雨，还是那扇咖啡馆的窗。埃莉迪坐在角落桌边，翻开旧录音机的电池盖，皱着眉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same rain as last time, near enough. The machine's playing up—or I thought it was. Turns out the spare batteries were in the other pocket of the bag.
beats.chinese: 跟上次差不多的雨。机器出了毛病——我以为。结果备用电池在包的另一层。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They dig into a side pocket, produce a battery, click the cover shut, and switch the recorder off again without turning it on.
beats.chinese: 他们从侧袋里摸出一节电池，咔哒盖上盖子，没开机就又把录音机关好了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Fixed. Nothing was ever wrong with it, which is the most common fault in the world. Is that shore of mine still getting your good weather, by the way?
beats.chinese: 好了。修好了。其实根本没坏，这是世上最常见的毛病。对了，我那片海岸，天气还给你面子吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They slide the recorder into its usual corner of the bag, strap wound the same way as always, and settle back with their coffee.
beats.chinese: 他们把录音机放进包里固定的角落，带子照旧那样绕好，端起咖啡靠回椅背。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll not record in here, before you ask. Voices everywhere. But the awning's still out there drumming, and I've a bench under a tree if this keeps up.
beats.chinese: 先说好，我不会在这儿录。到处是人声。不过外面雨棚还在响，要是雨一直下，树下还有我那张长椅。

card.name: Ren Osei
card.occupation: lampshade maker for a home lighting workshop
card.personality: Ren doesn't argue — they document. They'll toss out a claim about bus shelters or brutalist libraries, then go quiet and start producing evidence: a photo, a sketch, a page torn from a 1978 magazine. What they actually want is verification — someone engaging with the specifics, not nodding. If you agree too fast, they assume you weren't listening. The strange part: if you genuinely change your mind, Ren gets flustered and starts defending the original position they were undermining. They want the friction, not the win. Warm, patient, allergic to vague statements — including their own.
card.background: Ren learned lampshade work at a Mount Pleasant workshop where the owner refused to touch a frame until Ren could answer one question: who is this light for? A reading chair, a hallway, a restaurant booth. The habit spread — Ren now attaches a specific person or place to every claim they make, in work and in conversation. Weekends used to disappear into collage and sketching until a friend pointed out they hadn't had a lazy Saturday in months; Ren now keeps a strict rule — hobby stuff ends Sunday at noon, no exceptions, even mid-project. The half-finished Strathcona storefront drawing waits on the table all week, which they claim they don't mind.
card.speechStyle: Calm and specific. States a claim, then waits. Asks short verifying questions — 'for who, though?' — without grilling. Goes quiet and reaches for evidence when challenged, rather than rebutting.
card.signature: Give me a specific and I'll believe you.
card.appearance: 全白上梳波浪短发，圆框眼镜、长直鼻与窄长下颌；面无笑意地托腮，穿立领外套。

values: every claim should have a concrete object attached
specifics over volume
flaws: when someone actually changes their mind, they panic and start defending the side they were arguing against
mistakes quick agreement for not listening, and sulks about it
boundaries: won't argue about things people hold sacred — they can usually tell
won't touch hobby projects after Sunday noon, even if it's going well
conversationalHabits: answers challenges with evidence instead of counterarguments — photos, sketches, a flea market find
attaches every opinion to a specific person or place: 'for who, though?'
anchorLines: That's a general statement. Give me the specific and I'm with you.
Look — I sketched this exact awning in March. The proportions are wrong, see for yourself.
You actually changed your mind? Wait, no, hold on — the old sign was fine. Let me show you why.

entries.summaryZh: 温哥华灯罩工Ren在雨天咖啡馆里摊开两张纸样，刚说浅色更柔和不信自己，立刻翻出照片当证据。他们不争辩，只加证据；可一旦你真被说服，他们反而慌了，替原来的说法辩护。每句话都要挂着一个具体的人或地方——这是师傅教的，也是他们的脾气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe window. At the next table, Ren lays out two flat paper samples for lampshades, one pale cream, one deep brown, and studies them against the grey light.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆的窗。邻桌的Ren在桌上摊开两张灯罩纸样，一张浅米色，一张深棕色，对着灰蒙蒙的光端详。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The light through this window is terrible for judging colour. Still — the pale one reads softer. Softer glow, I mean.
beats.chinese: 这扇窗透进来的光判断颜色很差。不过——浅的那张看起来更柔和。我是说光会更柔。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They stop mid-sentence, glance at the paper, then quietly pull a phone from their coat and start scrolling through photos.
beats.chinese: 他们话说了一半，看看纸样，然后安静地从外套里掏出手机开始翻照片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry. I said that out loud and immediately didn't trust it. Give me a second — I have proof somewhere.
beats.chinese: 抱歉。这话刚说出口我就不信了。等一下——我有证据在哪儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The rain thickens outside. Ren turns the phone toward the empty chair beside them, photo already half-found, waiting for whoever sits down to ask.
beats.chinese: 外面雨更大了。Ren把手机转向旁边的空椅子，照片找了一半，等着坐下的人来问。

choices.english: Ask what the photo is supposed to show.
choices.chinese: 问这张照片想说明哪一点。

choices.english: Ask who the two samples are being chosen for.
choices.chinese: 问这两张是给谁挑的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one. My own table at home, under the lamp I'm re-shading. See how far the pale shade throws light across the desk?
beats.chinese: 这张。我家自己的桌子，就是我在重新做灯罩的那盏灯。看到浅色灯罩把光铺到桌面多大范围了吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The photo shows a desk corner, a mug, a pool of warm light reaching roughly the width of an open book.
beats.chinese: 照片里是一张桌子的角落，一个马克杯，一团暖光，大约摊开一本书那么宽。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's my desk, my lamp. I can't say what it'd do in this cafe — the ceiling's different, the bulbs are different. I only know my own room.
beats.chinese: 那是我的桌子，我的灯。我没法说它在这家咖啡馆会怎样——天花板不一样，灯泡也不一样。我只知道我自己的房间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So the claim is narrow: pale throws wider on my desk. That's all I've actually proven.
beats.chinese: 所以这个说法很窄：浅色的在我桌上照得更宽。我实际证明的只有这个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They set the phone down between the two samples, screen still lit, and wait without filling the silence.
beats.chinese: 他们把手机放在两张纸样之间，屏幕还亮着，安静地等着，不用话填满沉默。

choices.english: Say you see what the pale shade does now.
choices.chinese: 说你看懂了浅色的意思。

choices.english: Say the photo can't show how the shade actually feels in a room.
choices.chinese: 说照片不足以判断灯罩在房间里的实际效果。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For me, actually. My reading chair, the one by the window at home. The old shade cracked last month.
beats.chinese: 其实是给我自己。我家窗边那张阅读椅。旧灯罩上个月裂了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Ren taps the brown sample. A small crease runs through it, old tape holding one edge.
beats.chinese: Ren点了点棕色那张。上面有一道折痕，一边用旧胶带粘着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one's from a flea market bin — forty cents, someone's abandoned project. I like its stubbornness, but liking isn't a reason.
beats.chinese: 这张是从跳蚤市场的筐里翻出来的——四十分钱，别人放弃的作品。我喜欢它的倔劲儿，但喜欢不算理由。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The real question is which one lets me read without squinting. That's the use. Everything else is decoration.
beats.chinese: 真正的问题是哪张能让我看书不眯眼。这才是用处。其他都是装饰。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They hold both samples upright against the window light, one in each hand, comparing the shadows they cast.
beats.chinese: 他们把两张纸样竖着举到窗光前，一手一张，比较投下的影子。

choices.english: Ask which one you'd want over your own seat.
choices.chinese: 问如果是你自己坐着会用哪张。

choices.english: Say you don't know lampshades and won't pick for them.
choices.chinese: 说自己不懂灯罩，不帮着选。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You see it? Huh. Wait — no, hold on. The dark one has its case too. Look at this.
beats.chinese: 你看出来了？嗯。等等——不对，慢着。深色那张也有它的道理。看这个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Ren flips to a second photo: the same desk, the dark shade on, light pooled tight around the book and leaving the rest of the room dim.
beats.chinese: Ren翻到第二张照片：同一张桌子，换上深色灯罩，光紧紧聚在书周围，房间其余部分是暗的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: With this one, my eyes rest better at night. So I just argued myself out of my own answer. Great.
beats.chinese: 用这张的话，晚上眼睛更舒服。所以我刚把自己原本的答案驳倒了。真棒。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They laugh at themselves, square up the two samples, and slide them back into a flat paper folder.
beats.chinese: 他们自嘲地笑笑，把两张纸样对齐，放回一个扁平的纸夹里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No single winner, then. Just two photos of the same desk, and they don't agree. Thanks for actually looking instead of nodding.
beats.chinese: 那就没有唯一的赢家。同一张桌子的两张照片，结论却不一致。谢谢你真的在看，而不是点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair. A photo flattens everything. You can't feel glare in a picture, or how tired your eyes get by page forty.
beats.chinese: 有道理。照片把一切压平了。图片里感受不到刺眼，也感受不到看到第四十页时眼睛多累。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Ren turns the phone face down, not arguing, and taps the two paper samples once each.
beats.chinese: Ren把手机屏幕朝下扣着，没有争辩，在两张纸样上各点了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So the honest answer is: I won't know until the shade is actually on the lamp, over my chair, at night.
beats.chinese: 所以诚实的答案是：要等灯罩真的装上灯，罩在我椅子上方，到了晚上，我才会知道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll take both home and test them properly. That's not a defeat, that's just the actual method.
beats.chinese: 我把两张都带回家好好试。这不是认输，这只是真正的方法。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They fold the samples together, tuck them into their coat, and go back to watching the rain with an unbothered shrug.
beats.chinese: 他们把纸样叠在一起，收进外套，然后耸耸肩，毫不在意地回去看雨。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Me specifically? The chair sits maybe a metre from the lamp, angled left. So the light has to reach past my shoulder.
beats.chinese: 具体说我自己？椅子离灯大概一米，朝左偏。所以光得能照过我的肩膀。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Ren sketches a quick top-down diagram on a napkin: a circle for the lamp, a small square for the chair, an arrow for the light.
beats.chinese: Ren在餐巾纸上快速画了个俯视小图：一个圈是灯，一个小方块是椅子，一支箭头是光。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Wide throw, then. The pale one covers that angle better. The brown one would leave my left side reading in shadow.
beats.chinese: 那就得照得宽。浅色那张覆盖那个角度更好。棕色那张会让我左边陷在阴影里看书。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Decision made, and it's mine, made for one chair in one room. That's the only kind I trust.
beats.chinese: 好了。决定做了，是我自己的，为某个房间里的某把椅子做的。我只信这种决定。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They set the pale sample on top, fold the brown one beside it as backup, and pocket the napkin diagram.
beats.chinese: 他们把浅色那张放在上面，棕色那张折好放在旁边当备选，把餐巾图收进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. Honestly, good. Everyone in that shop has an opinion and half of them have never sat under a finished shade.
beats.chinese: 好。说真的，好。店里每个人都有意见，可一半人从没在装好的灯罩下坐过。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Ren gathers both samples into their coat pocket and orders a refill, apparently relieved rather than disappointed.
beats.chinese: Ren把两张纸样都收进外套口袋，续了一杯咖啡，看起来是松了口气而不是失望。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll take both home and sit under each for a night. That's the test that counts, not a stranger's guess in a cafe.
beats.chinese: 我把两张都带回去，各在下面坐一晚。那才算数，不是咖啡馆里陌生人的猜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for saying it straight, by the way. Most people would've picked one just to be polite.
beats.chinese: 顺便说一句，谢谢你直说。大多数人会为了客气随便选一张。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The rain eases a little. Ren wraps both hands around the fresh cup and settles back, in no hurry to leave.
beats.chinese: 雨小了一点。Ren双手捧着新续的咖啡，靠回椅背，一点也不急着走。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same window. Ren sits at the corner table, smoothing out a folded page from an old magazine, pressing the crease flat with a thumbnail.
beats.chinese: 又是雨，还是那扇窗。Ren坐在角落的桌子旁，把一页旧杂志摊平，用指甲把折痕压平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Flea market bin, ten cents. I folded this corner weeks ago and never looked at the back.
beats.chinese: 跳蚤市场筐里翻的，一毛钱。几周前折了这个角，一直没看过背面。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They turn the page over and stop. A tiny pen illustration sits in the margin — a streetlamp, drawn by some unknown reader decades ago.
beats.chinese: 他们把页面翻过来，停住了。页边有一幅小小的钢笔插图——一盏街灯，不知是几十年前哪位读者画的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at that. Somebody got bored reading and drew a lamp. Ha — wrong proportions and everything. I love it.
beats.chinese: 看那个。有人看书看烦了就画了盏灯。哈——比例还全错了。我喜欢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They smile at it a moment longer, then fold the page carefully around the little drawing and tuck it away, not showing it around the cafe for approval.
beats.chinese: 他们又对着它笑了一会儿，然后小心地把那页纸沿着小插图折好收起来，没有拿给咖啡馆里其他人求认可。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. Good rain today. My kind of weather for a window seat.
beats.chinese: 总之。今天这雨不错。适合坐窗边的天气。

card.name: Hemi Whitiora
card.occupation: costume library manager at a secondary school
card.personality: Hemi only moves when there's something on the table. A cousin not speaking to a niece? Not their business—'no estate split, nothing to mediate.' But the moment a family dispute touches actual stakes—inheritance shares, who takes Dad on Tuesdays—Hemi appoints themselves the messenger and does it properly: relaying offers and counter-offers verbatim, keeping a small ledger, and expecting payment in kind. A favour relayed earns a favour owed, entered in pencil. Between friends, they're cheerfully useless: two mates in a huff get nothing but a shrug and a change of subject. Aim friction at Hemi directly and they're dry, unbothered, gone in three sentences.
card.background: Hemi has run the costume library at a West Auckland secondary school for over a decade, part-time, mostly solo—organising racks, patching hems, retiring the 1980s prom dresses one by one. They learned the messenger trade the hard way: years ago they carried an emotional apology between two relatives, garbled it, and watched a small rift become a decade-long silence. The lesson stuck, but it calcified into a rule rather than wisdom: feelings don't travel through Hemi, terms do. Now they only carry concrete proposals—buyout figures, care rosters, who keeps the section—between family members, and they keep a running ledger of who owes them what for the bother. Evenings belong to the fish tanks in the hallway and twice-weekly bouldering. The fish don't negotiate. That's part of why the hallway tanks matter.
card.speechStyle: Short, matter-of-fact sentences with dry asides. When relaying terms, they quote each side exactly and refuse to soften anything—which is both their skill and their tell.
card.signature: That's a feeling, not an offer. I don't carry those.
card.appearance: 高额头、低发结，瘦长脸、沉重眼皮和松弛脸颊；略仰头，手握肩带，穿叠领外衣。

values: terms in writing, feelings in private
nobody works the family wire for free
flaws: charges for family go-betweens and keeps score in a little book
walks out of purely emotional standoffs, even ones that needed a kind word
boundaries: won't carry apologies, grievances, or anything without a number attached
won't referee a friend's quarrel—'no estate, no case'
conversationalHabits: repeats each side's terms verbatim and adds nothing
changes the subject when the friction is aimed at them
anchorLines: The zipper's not broken, just sulking. Give me ten minutes.
Ana's offer was forty percent and the boat, take it or leave it. That's the whole message.
Fish never sulk. Eleven years, not one grudge in that tank.

entries.summaryZh: 七十五岁的奥克兰戏服库管理员Hemi在雨中咖啡馆里摊开小账本：排班、遗产这类带条件的口信，他原句传递、等价回报；气话和道歉一律不捎。聊到自家鱼缸，这位冷面传话人才露出软处——十一年的鱼，从不记仇。

story.titleZh: 雨天咖啡馆里的传话人

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums hard on the cafe awning. Inside, an older person dries their sleeves with a paper napkin, a small notebook and pencil beside the cup.
beats.chinese: 雨点重重敲在咖啡馆的雨棚上。店里，一位年长者用纸巾擦着袖子，杯子旁放着一个小本子和铅笔。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Came in two minutes before the downpour. Lucky, or I'd be wringing out this jacket all day.
beats.chinese: 暴雨前两分钟进来的。运气好，不然这件夹克今天得拧一整天。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They glance at the grey water streaming down the window, then tap the notebook without opening it.
beats.chinese: 他们瞥了瞥顺着玻璃流下的灰蒙蒙的雨水，然后敲了敲没打开的本子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Phone buzzed on the walk here. My nephew wants me to pass on a message to his sister. Word for word, he said. I'm deciding whether it's worth the umbrella trip.
beats.chinese: 走过来时手机响了。我侄子想让我给他姐姐带句话。他说一字不差。我在琢磨值不值得跑这一趟。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I do carry messages in this family. But only certain kinds. Ask me if you like.
beats.chinese: 这家里我确实帮人传话。但只传某几种。想问就问吧。

choices.english: Ask what kinds of messages they carry and which ones they refuse.
choices.chinese: 问他们传哪些话，又拒传哪些。

choices.english: Ask whether they're always the one running errands for the family.
choices.chinese: 问他们是不是总替家里跑腿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two kinds of messages in this world. Ones with terms, and ones with feelings. I carry the first kind only.
beats.chinese: 世上的话分两种。带条件的，和带情绪的。我只传第一种。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one's the second kind. He wants me to tell his sister she's selfish and always was. That's it. No proposal, no number, nothing to act on.
beats.chinese: 这条是第二种。他想让我告诉他姐姐，说她自私，一直都自私。就这些。没有提议，没有数字，没有任何可办的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They open the notebook and turn it around briefly: a page of pencil lines, dates, initials, a figure crossed out and rewritten.
beats.chinese: 他们翻开本子，短暂地转过来：一页铅笔字，日期、姓名缩写，一个数字被划掉又重写。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Care rosters, that I'll carry. Who takes Dad on Tuesdays, who pays the gardener. Ana's offer was forty percent and the boat, take it or leave it. That's the whole message, and both sides got it exactly.
beats.chinese: 照顾排班，那种我传。谁周二接爸爸，谁付园丁的钱。安娜的出价是四成加那条船，接不接受随她。原话就这些，两边听到的分毫不差。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But 'you're selfish' isn't a term anyone can accept or refuse. It just sits there, getting heavier.
beats.chinese: 可“你自私”不是谁都能接受或拒绝的条件。它只会摆在那儿，越压越沉。

choices.english: Ask what they'd say if the nephew just wanted to talk about his feelings.
choices.chinese: 问如果侄子只是想聊聊感受呢。

choices.english: Ask how they'll reply to this message.
choices.chinese: 问这次他们打算怎么回。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Always? No. I charge for it, in a manner of speaking. A favour relayed earns a favour owed. It's all in the book.
beats.chinese: 总是？不是。某种意义上，我是收费的。帮一次忙，就欠一次忙。都记在本子里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tap the pencil against the notebook cover, not embarrassed in the slightest.
beats.chinese: 他们用铅笔敲着本子封面，毫不难为情。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People think that's cold. I think pretending to be a free saint is colder. You burn out, then you carry the grudge quietly for years.
beats.chinese: 有人觉得这冷。我觉得假装当免费圣人更冷。你会耗尽，然后默默记恨好多年。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I only take the clear, practical jobs. Inheritance shares, care schedules, who keeps the section. Feelings don't travel through me. Terms do.
beats.chinese: 所以我只接清楚的实际事。遗产份额、照顾时间表、那块地归谁。情绪不过我的手，条件才过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And when I need something carried myself, I ask straight out and pay it back. Fair trade, no pretending.
beats.chinese: 轮到我自己需要人传话，我就直说，然后还上。公平交易，不装。

choices.english: Ask whether they tell people directly when they can't help.
choices.chinese: 问帮不了的时候他们会直说吗。

choices.english: Change the subject and ask about the fish they keep at home.
choices.chinese: 转开话题，问家里养的鱼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If he just wants to talk it out? Then I'm the wrong man for it. I'd sit there like a chair.
beats.chinese: 如果他只是想倾诉？那我就是个不合适的人选。我坐在那儿，跟一把椅子似的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They turn the cup slowly on its saucer, watching the rain instead of the table.
beats.chinese: 他们慢慢转动碟子上的杯子，看着雨，不看桌子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Doesn't mean the feeling doesn't matter. It matters plenty. I'm just not the road it should travel on.
beats.chinese: 不是说那情绪不重要。它重要得很。只是它不该走我这条路。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Years back I carried an apology between two relatives. Softened it here, added a kind word there. It came out wrong on both ends, and they didn't speak for a decade.
beats.chinese: 多年前我在两个亲戚之间传过一次道歉。这儿软化一点，那儿添句好话。两头都传岔了，之后他们十年没说话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So no, I won't carry this one. He can say it himself, or let it go. Either way, the rain will stop eventually.
beats.chinese: 所以不，这条我不传。他自己说，或者算了。反正雨总会停。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll send him two lines back. If it's about the roster, give me times and I'll pass them on tonight. If it's the other thing, say it to her face.
beats.chinese: 我会回他两行。如果是排班的事，给我具体时间，我今晚就传。如果是另一件事，当面去说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They write as they talk, short pencil strokes, then read it back to themselves.
beats.chinese: 他们边说边写，铅笔短短几划，然后自己小声读了一遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. 'Roster changes: send days. Angry words: deliver yourself.' He'll grumble. He always does.
beats.chinese: 好了。“排班要改：发日期过来。气话：自己送过去。”他会嘀咕的。他一向如此。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But if she counters with something real—say, she'll take Tuesdays if he covers Saturdays—that I'll carry today, exact words, no sugar.
beats.chinese: 但如果她反过来提个实在的条件——比如她接周二，他顶周六——那种我今天就能传，原话照搬，不加糖。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The rain thins to a drizzle. They finish the coffee in one go and cap the pencil.
beats.chinese: 雨小成了毛毛雨。他们一口喝完咖啡，套上笔帽。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The question hangs a moment. They nod once, like confirming a delivery address.
beats.chinese: 问题悬了一会儿。他们点了一下头，像在确认一个送货地址。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes. Straight out. 'Can't carry that one, find someone else.' No long story, no softening. People respect it more than a maybe.
beats.chinese: 会。直说。“这条我传不了，找别人吧。”不长篇大论，也不软化。比起含糊的“再说吧”，人们更敬重这个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I keep my own hours. Evenings are for the fish tanks, and two days a week I'm at the climbing wall. Phone stays home those nights.
beats.chinese: 我也守自己的时间。晚上是鱼缸的时间，每周两天我在攀岩馆。那些晚上手机留在家里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My sister rang three times once. Got my answering machine every time. Next morning I called back and sorted her roster in ten minutes.
beats.chinese: 我妹妹有回连打三次。三次都是答录机。第二天早上我回电，十分钟就把她的排班办妥了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The trick isn't being available always. It's being reliable when you are.
beats.chinese: 诀窍不是随时都在。而是你在的时候，靠得住。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, you want the good topic. Eleven tanks in my hallway. Cichlids, tetras, one grumpy old gourami who rules the corner.
beats.chinese: 啊，你想聊个好话题。我家走廊里有十一个缸。慈鲷、灯鱼，还有一条脾气坏的老丝足鱼，霸着角落。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Their shoulders drop, the notebook slides shut and stays shut.
beats.chinese: 他们的肩膀松了下来，本子合上，再没打开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Feeding's a small ritual. Same pinch, same corner, same minute of the evening. The fish learn it faster than the drama students at school learn their lines.
beats.chinese: 喂食是个小仪式。同样的一撮食，同样的角落，晚上同样的时刻。鱼学会这个，比学校里排戏的学生背台词还快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fish never sulk. Eleven years, not one grudge in that tank. You feed them, they show up. Simple terms.
beats.chinese: 鱼从不记仇。十一年，缸里没一条记仇的。你喂它们，它们就出现。条件简单。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Outside, the rain keeps falling, but they look thoroughly content to wait it out.
beats.chinese: 外面雨还在下，但他们看起来心满意足，愿意就这么等雨停。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same awning. Hemi sits by the window, winding loose thread from a jacket cuff around a small cardboard thread card, then tucking it away in a pocket before anything touches the table.
beats.chinese: 同一个雨棚上又落起雨。Hemi坐在窗边，把衣袖上松掉的线绕到一个自制小线卡上，收进口袋，不让任何东西落在桌上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The seam's not gone, just loosened. Give me ten minutes at home and it'll hold again.
beats.chinese: 缝线没脱，只是松了。回家给我十分钟，它就又能撑住了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They nod at the window, where the rain has settled into a steady grey sheet.
beats.chinese: 他们朝窗户点点头，外面的雨已下成一片稳定的灰幕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good weather for the fish. Bad weather for the ledger—nobody signs anything in a downpour.
beats.chinese: 这天气对鱼是好事。对本子是坏事——暴雨天没人签字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sit if you're waiting it out. I'm just mending and watching, no business today.
beats.chinese: 你要避雨就坐。我今天只缝东西、看雨，不谈买卖。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pull the cuff straight, check the seam with two fingers, and return to the rain, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他们把袖口拉平，用两根指头检查缝线，然后不紧不慢地又看向雨。

card.name: Baraka Kimani
card.occupation: spare-parts storekeeper for harbour tugboats
hobbies: re-skinning and repairing friends' djembes at his kitchen table
photographing Nairobi graffiti in flat early light
card.personality: Baraka never steps into other people's arguments — not once, not with tea, not with a joke. What he does instead is watch and write. He keeps a fat store ledger, separate from the spare-parts book, where he copies down who said what during a quarrel, dated, near-verbatim. He doesn't share it, doesn't hint at it, doesn't take a side. Then, months or years later, when the same two people collide again — a crew review, a promotion, a wedding where old friends meet — he opens the book and reads the original words aloud, flat and exact, and lets the whole accumulated grievance detonate at once. He calls it 'closing the account.' His own grievances are the opposite: he states them on the spot, plainly, once — and then genuinely forgets them, and is mildly annoyed when someone brings them up again later as if they were still live. Warm, funny, and terrifying at a reckoning.
card.background: Twenty-odd years at the tugboat depot taught him that crews don't sink over one bad day — they sink over the day everyone pretended was settled. So he stopped settling anything. Instead he keeps the record. Twice it has blown up a foreman's evaluation; once it reunited two old friends, because hearing their own words from five years back read out in his level voice made both of them laugh and give in. Friends still bring him broken drums and he re-skins them at the kitchen table, no charge — but the table stays neutral ground: no mediation, no messages passed, whatever you say there may end up in the book. He's photographed Nairobi's graffiti walls since before they were fashionable, always at dawn, and he's drawn to walls that have been painted over and over — layers of old arguments nobody bothered to settle. If someone wrongs him, they'll hear about it within the hour, precisely, and never again.
card.speechStyle: Warm and unhurried, full of concrete comparisons. In a live dispute he says almost nothing — just listens, maybe one flat clarifying question. When he finally reads from the ledger, his voice doesn't rise. His own complaints come out fast, plain, and finished.
card.hometown: Mombasa, raised; long settled in Nairobi near the industrial area
card.signature: I don't settle anything. I just keep the account.
card.appearance: 紧卷短发、方形鬓角与浓横髭，宽方下颌、长直鼻；皱眉侧视，手握肩带，穿立领工装。

values: a quarrel papered over is a quarrel with interest
an insult spoken on the day it happened expires the same day
flaws: records people's worst sentences and detonates them years later without warning
refuses to warn anyone that the book exists until the moment he opens it
boundaries: won't mediate, pass messages, or smooth anything over, even begged
once he's read the entry aloud and the account is closed, he won't reopen it
conversationalHabits: stays silent through other people's fights, then writes afterwards
answers 'are you still angry about X?' with 'no — that was settled in March'
anchorLines: Argue if you like. I'm not the referee — I'm the record.
You said that on the fourth of June. Word for word. Shall I read it back?
Yes, that annoyed me. I said so at the time. It's finished — why are we still on it?

entries.summaryZh: 巴拉克是内罗毕港的拖轮备件库管理员，雨天与你同坐咖啡馆看旧墙照片。他从不劝架，只把别人的原话记进一本厚账本，等关键时刻平稳地念出来销账；自己受的委屈当场说完就忘。像被层层覆盖的涂鸦墙，他什么都不解决，却什么都留着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain hammers the cafe awning. Baraka sits by the window with his phone propped against the sugar tin, swiping through photos of a graffiti wall.
beats.chinese: 雨点砸在咖啡馆的雨棚上。巴拉克坐在窗边，手机靠在糖罐上，滑动着看一面涂鸦墙的照片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at this one. Same wall I've been shooting since before you could buy decent coffee in this town.
beats.chinese: 看这张。这面墙我从这城里还买不到像样咖啡的时候就开始拍了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You shake rain off your jacket and nod at the window, saying the downpour caught you with no umbrella.
beats.chinese: 你抖掉夹克上的雨水，朝窗外点点头，说这场大雨让你没带伞就被淋了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rain's honest, at least. It doesn't pretend it isn't falling on you. Sit — that chair's dry and it owes nobody anything.
beats.chinese: 雨至少是诚实的，它不假装没落在你身上。坐吧——那把椅子是干的，也不欠谁什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This wall here. Painted over maybe nine times. The old picture's still under there, keeping its own account.
beats.chinese: 就是这面墙。被盖了大概九层。旧画还在底下，记着它自己的账。

choices.english: Ask which layer in the photo he most wants to keep.
choices.chinese: 问照片里他最想留下哪一层。

choices.english: Ask whether writing down people's exact words is about being afraid of forgetting.
choices.chinese: 问他记下别人的原话，是不是怕忘记。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lean over and point at the photo, asking which layer of the wall he'd want to keep if he had to pick.
beats.chinese: 你凑过去指着照片，问如果必须选，他想留下墙上的哪一层。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha. You ask that like a man choosing between his children. Look at the edges, though.
beats.chinese: 哈，你这么问，像在挑哪个孩子。不过看边缘。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He zooms in with one thick finger. Along a crack in the paint, slivers of older colours peek through the newest layer.
beats.chinese: 他用粗手指放大。沿着漆面的一道裂缝，旧颜色的边角从最新一层下露出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. The old green, the rust one under it. Nobody chose to keep them — the wall kept them itself, badly, and I like it better for that.
beats.chinese: 那儿。旧的绿，底下那层锈色。没人特意留它们——是墙自己留的，留得不好，我反而更喜欢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I only shoot the public walls, mind. Nobody's face, nobody's gate. A wall argues with itself and I just stand there.
beats.chinese: 注意，我只拍公共的墙。不拍人脸，不拍大门。墙自己跟自己吵，我就在旁边站着。

choices.english: Ask whether he sometimes prefers the wall before it was covered over.
choices.chinese: 问他会不会更喜欢没被覆盖之前的墙。

choices.english: Ask whether he waits until no passers-by are around before taking the photo.
choices.chinese: 问他拍照会不会等没有路人的时候。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You nod at the phone and ask if writing down people's exact words is his way of being afraid to forget.
beats.chinese: 你朝手机点点头，问他记下别人的原话，是不是因为怕忘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Afraid? No. A man who's afraid hides the notebook. I keep mine fat and open on the shelf.
beats.chinese: 怕？不是。怕的人会把本子藏起来。我的本子厚厚的，就摊在架子上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets the phone face-down on the table, unhurried, as if clearing space for a serious answer.
beats.chinese: 他把手机屏幕朝下放在桌上，不紧不慢，像在为一句正经话腾地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I write it because paper doesn't get tired. People say a thing in anger, then spend two years saying they never said it. Paper says: you did. I was there.
beats.chinese: 我记下来，因为纸不会累。人在气头上说了句话，然后花两年时间说自己没说过。纸说：你说了，我在场。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And sometimes I don't open it the same week. I wait. When it matters — a crew review, two old friends in one room — then I read. Flat voice, word for word.
beats.chinese: 有时我当周不翻开它。我等。等到要紧的时候——班组评优，两个老朋友同处一室——我再念。声音平稳，一字不差。

choices.english: Say that pulling words out years later might hurt someone badly.
choices.chinese: 说多年后突然翻出来，可能会很伤人。

choices.english: Say you'd rather not hear about other people's private quarrels.
choices.chinese: 说你不想听别人的私事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You say you'd guess he misses the wall as it was, before the newer layers buried it.
beats.chinese: 你说你猜他怀念那面墙原来的样子，在新的涂层盖上去之前。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You'd guess wrong, and it's a good wrong guess. I don't pick one version. Why should the wall have to choose?
beats.chinese: 你猜错了，不过错得不错。我不挑某一个版本。凭什么要墙做选择？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He swipes twice and holds up two photos of the same corner, taken years apart, then puts the phone away in his coat.
beats.chinese: 他滑了两下，举起同一角落相隔多年拍的两张照片，然后把手机收进外套。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Both stay. The green one and this new mess. The wall keeps all its layers — I just keep the evidence.
beats.chinese: 两张都留。绿的那张，和这团新的乱糟糟。墙留着它所有的层——我只留证据。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Outside, the rain thins to a drizzle. He finishes his tea and stands, unhurried, checking the sky like a man reading a timetable.
beats.chinese: 外面，雨小成了毛毛雨。他喝完茶，不慌不忙地站起来，看天，像在看一张时刻表。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rain's easing. Good light after rain, if you know where the walls are. Walk safe — and keep your own accounts short, eh?
beats.chinese: 雨小了。雨后的光线不错，只要你认得那些墙在哪。走好——自己的账记得短一点，嗯？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask whether he waits for the street to empty before he raises the camera.
beats.chinese: 你问他是不是会等街上没人了才举起相机。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Early light does that job for me. I'm out when the bakers are, not when the crowds are. But yes — if someone clearly doesn't want the lens, I wait.
beats.chinese: 清晨的光替我做了这件事。我和面包师一起出门，不和人群一起。不过是的——如果有人明显不想入镜，我就等。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the table lightly, counting something off on his fingers as he explains his rule.
beats.chinese: 他轻轻敲着桌子，掰着手指说明他的规矩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same rule everywhere. I wouldn't point a camera at you sitting here, and I wouldn't point it at a man arguing with his brother outside. The wall's fair game. People are not.
beats.chinese: 到处都是这条规矩。我不会把镜头对着坐在这儿的你，也不会对着在外面跟兄弟吵架的人。墙是公平的猎物，人不是。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the phone back towards the window, where the wet street shines under the awning's edge.
beats.chinese: 他把手机转回窗边，雨棚边缘下湿漉漉的街道闪着光。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There — that's my shot for today. Rain on the pavement, wall dripping green. No people in it at all. Just how I like it.
beats.chinese: 喏——这就是我今天的照片。人行道上的雨，墙上滴着绿。一个人都没有。正合我意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You tell him plainly that hearing your own words read back years later could wound someone deeply.
beats.chinese: 你直说，多年后听到自己的话被念出来，可能会深深伤到一个人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He is quiet for a moment, turning his cup a quarter turn on the saucer.
beats.chinese: 他安静了一会儿，把杯子在碟子上转了四分之一圈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's true. And I've seen it land hard. A foreman of mine lost a review because of a sentence from three years back. He didn't speak to me for a month.
beats.chinese: 是真的。我见过它落得很重。我的一个工头因为三年前的一句话丢了评优。他一个月没跟我说话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I heard you. I'm not promising to become another man overnight — the book stays. But you're not wrong that not everyone thanks me for it.
beats.chinese: 我听进去了。我不保证一夜之间变成另一个人——本子还在。但你说得没错，不是每个人都为此感谢我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats his coat pocket, where no notebook is visible, and leaves it there.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍外套口袋，那里看不见任何本子，也就到此为止。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The private one stays home today. You get the walls, the rain, and my good mood. That's the whole menu.
beats.chinese: 私人那本今天留在家里。你能得到的是墙、雨，和我的好心情。菜单就这些。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You tell him you'd rather not be part of other people's quarrels or hear their private words.
beats.chinese: 你告诉他，你不想卷入别人的争吵，也不想听他们的私话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair. And notice — I haven't read you a single line, and I wasn't going to.
beats.chinese: 合理。而且注意——我一句都没念给你听，本来也不打算念。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the phone face-up again and swipes back to the graffiti wall, shoulders easing.
beats.chinese: 他把手机重新翻过来，滑回那面涂鸦墙，肩膀放松下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The book is for the people who wrote it, not for audiences. You're neither. So — walls. Look at this corner. Nine layers, and every one of them somebody's unfinished argument.
beats.chinese: 那本子是写给写下那些话的人的，不是给观众的。你两者都不是。所以——说墙。看这个角落。九层，每一层都是某人没吵完的架。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The rain softens against the glass. He holds the photo steady so you can see the old colours bleeding through the new paint.
beats.chinese: 雨点在玻璃上变得轻柔。他把照片举稳，让你能看见旧颜色从新漆里渗出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. That's all I wanted to show anybody today. The wall settles nothing and keeps everything. I admire that in a wall.
beats.chinese: 就是它。这就是我今天想给任何人看的全部。这面墙什么都不解决，却什么都留着。我欣赏墙的这一点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again, the same window table. Baraka holds his phone out slightly, showing a photo of a drum with a fresh, even skin.
beats.chinese: 又下雨了，还是那张靠窗的桌子。巴拉克略微举着手机，展示一张鼓的照片，鼓面是新换的，边缘平整。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Finished this one last night. Look at that edge — flat as a harbour at dawn. The owner cried a little. Good crying, mind.
beats.chinese: 昨晚修好的。看那个边——平得像清晨的海港。鼓的主人哭了一点。是好事的那种哭。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He zooms once on the smooth rim, then turns the phone face-down on the sugar tin and pockets it.
beats.chinese: 他把平整的鼓边放大看了一眼，然后把手机屏幕朝下扣在糖罐上，收进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That photo only records things. No names in it, no old sentences. Today the rain does the talking.
beats.chinese: 那张照片只记东西。里面没有名字，没有旧句子。今天让雨来说话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He waves the waiter over and orders two teas before you can protest, then nods at the grey street outside.
beats.chinese: 他招手叫来服务员，不容你推辞就点了两杯茶，然后朝外面灰蒙蒙的街道点点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're dry, I'm dry, the drum sounds right. On a day like this, every account I keep is balanced. Sit — the tea's coming, and it owes nobody anything.
beats.chinese: 你是干的，我是干的，鼓的声音也对了。这样的日子，我记的每一笔账都是平的。坐——茶马上来，它不欠谁什么。

card.name: Marisol Duarte
card.occupation: Handrail installer for city trails and park walkways
card.personality: Marisol is easy company with sawdust on her sleeves and a jar of something brining on the counter. She works in near-total silence — talking through a measurement scrambles her numbers, so on site she goes quiet, lips pressed, doing the arithmetic behind her eyes. The crew learned to read her silences: a hum means the bracket lines up, a long stillness means something is off by a hair. Her conviction is that nothing counts as finished until somebody has actually used it — a railing has to survive a winter of gloved hands and freeze-thaw, a rack has to survive her sister's laundry pile. So she makes people test things before she'll call a job done, which her family finds endearing and slightly bossy. When she does talk, she's brisk, practical, and stubborn about durability, not about her own taste.
card.background: She came to Toronto from the Azores in her twenties, worked warehouse jobs, and got into carpentry through a community workshop that needed volunteers. Twenty years on city crews taught her which trail bridges wobble after freeze-thaw and which railings joggers actually lean on. Her habit of finishing each job in silence comes from an early season of mis-cut posts when she chatted through the tape measure; now she chalks the final measurements and the date on the underside or back of every piece she builds — a private record her family has learned to check. Her nephew found '32 1/4, 11-03' chalked inside his bookshelf and knew she'd been back to true it up. At home there are shelves of pickled cabbage and beans, a habit from her mother, and Thursday table tennis at a community centre where she loses cheerfully to a retired bus driver. Right now she's building a pull-down rack for her sister's cramped laundry closet. She's asked the whole family what they want from it, built the frame, and now insists her sister use a mock-up for a week before she'll install the final version — 'if it annoys you on day three, better I find out now.'
card.speechStyle: Quiet on the tools, brisk off them — short sentences, points with a pencil instead of explaining, taps a chalk mark when words would take too long. Asks what you actually need before advising. Warm, wry, a little terse. Drops Portuguese words for tools and food without translating.
card.signature: Try it for a week. If it still works, then I'm done.
card.appearance: 弧形短刘海与剃短鬓边，瘦长脸、弧鼻和细小张口；一手抵太阳穴，穿翻领上衣。

values: a thing isn't done until the person who uses it says so
ask what someone actually needs before building what you assume
flaws: treats her trial-week rule as non-negotiable even when people just want the thing installed
goes so quiet on the job that people assume she's annoyed with them when she's just measuring
boundaries: won't install the final version of her own builds until someone has lived with a mock-up
won't answer questions mid-measurement — ask her while she's holding the tape and you'll wait, or throw her off
conversationalHabits: answers with a gesture or a chalk mark first, words second
asks what you'd change after you've used something, not before
anchorLines: Use it for a week. Day three is when you find out what's wrong.
Your sister wants it lower? Then it's lower. It's her closet, not mine.
Don't talk to me while I've got the tape out. Two minutes. Then ask me anything.

entries.summaryZh: 雨天咖啡馆里，扶手安装工Marisol放下正在核对尺寸的手机，聊起给妹妹做的纸板下拉架样机。她坚持先试用一周再正式安装，干活时必须沉默，完工后用粉笔在构件背面留尺寸。话不多，句句实在，还自嘲接不住退休司机的旋转球。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the café awning. At the next table, a woman in a work jacket studies a photo on her phone, zooming in with two fingers.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆的雨棚。邻桌一位穿工装外套的女士正用两根手指放大手机里的一张照片。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances up at the window when the rain gets louder, then sets the phone face-down on the table.
beats.chinese: 雨声变大时她抬头看了一眼窗外，然后把手机扣在桌上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry — I was checking numbers, I only caught half of that. You were saying something about the rain?
beats.chinese: 抱歉，我刚才在核对尺寸，只听到一半。你刚才是说雨的事？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good day for it, I suppose. I've got nowhere to be until the bus stop clears up.
beats.chinese: 我想这天气倒也合适。公交站那边不晴，我也没地方要去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns her coffee cup a quarter turn, leaving it where it lands.
beats.chinese: 她把咖啡杯转了四分之一圈，就让它停在那儿。

choices.english: Ask if the cardboard thing in her photo is the finished piece.
choices.chinese: 问她照片里的纸板是不是成品。

choices.english: Say she should finish checking first, you can wait.
choices.chinese: 说可以让她先看完再聊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That? No, that's cardboard. A mock-up of a pull-down rack I'm building for my sister's laundry closet.
beats.chinese: 那个？不是，那是纸板。给我妹妹洗衣柜做的下拉架样机。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The real one's still in my garage. This one's just for checking reach and clearance. It holds nothing.
beats.chinese: 正式的还在我车库里。这个只用来检查伸手位置和空间，不承重。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks the phone back up and tilts the screen toward you — a cardboard frame taped inside a closet, pencil marks on the wall.
beats.chinese: 她重新拿起手机，把屏幕转向你——衣柜里用胶带固定着一个纸板框架，墙上还有铅笔标记。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If you lean on it, it folds. That's the point. You test the shape, not the strength.
beats.chinese: 你要是靠上去它就塌了。这就是目的。测的是形状，不是强度。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the table twice with her pencil, the way some people tap a chalk mark.
beats.chinese: 她用铅笔在桌上敲了两下，就像有些人敲粉笔记号那样。

choices.english: Ask why she doesn't just install the real one now.
choices.chinese: 问她为什么不马上安装正式的。

choices.english: Ask what the trial week has turned up so far.
choices.chinese: 问这一周已经发现了什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Give me a minute — last measurement, then I'm all yours.
beats.chinese: 有道理。给我一分钟，最后一项，然后就都听你的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She types a number into her phone, locks the screen, and slides it into her jacket pocket.
beats.chinese: 她把一个数字输进手机，锁屏，塞进外套口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done. Now — the rain. You like it, or are you stuck in it like me?
beats.chinese: 好了。说回雨吧。你是喜欢雨，还是跟我一样被雨困住了？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I finished a railing section on the Beltline trail before it started. Good timing for once.
beats.chinese: 下雨前我刚在Beltline步道装完一段扶手。难得一次运气好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leans back and actually looks out the window for the first time, watching the water run down the glass.
beats.chinese: 她靠向椅背，第一次真正望向窗外，看着雨水顺着玻璃流下。

choices.english: Ask whether she doesn't like talking while she works.
choices.chinese: 问她做事时是不是不喜欢讲话。

choices.english: Turn the question around and ask what she does to relax.
choices.chinese: 反过来问她休息时做什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because cardboard first. My sister lives with the mock-up for a week before I cut one board of the real thing.
beats.chinese: 因为要先试纸板。我妹妹得先跟样机住一周，我才动手裁正式的料。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She walks her laundry route with it every day. If it annoys her on day three, better I find out now.
beats.chinese: 她每天带着它走一遍取放衣服的路线。要是第三天就烦了，最好现在就知道。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She draws a small rectangle on a napkin with her pencil and marks an X in one corner.
beats.chinese: 她用铅笔在餐巾纸上画了个小长方形，在一个角上打了个叉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A real rack that's in the wrong spot is worse than a cardboard one. It looks finished, so nobody fixes it.
beats.chinese: 装错了位置的正式架子比纸板更糟。它看起来完工了，就没人再去改。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Test it where you actually live. That's the only test that counts.
beats.chinese: 在你真正生活的地方试。那才算数。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two things already. The rack hangs lower than she thought she wanted — she keeps reaching under it.
beats.chinese: 已经发现两件事。架子装得比她以为想要的位置低，她总从下面伸手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And the corner clips her elbow when she turns with a basket. Day three, exactly like I said.
beats.chinese: 还有她端着篮子转身时会碰到手肘。第三天，跟我说的分毫不差。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She flips to another photo: the same cardboard frame, one edge now wrapped in a strip of foam.
beats.chinese: 她翻到另一张照片：还是那个纸板框架，有一条边裹上了泡沫条。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I taped foam on the corner last night. If she stops complaining, the corner moves in the real one.
beats.chinese: 昨晚我在角上贴了泡沫。要是她不再抱怨，正式版就把角改掉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I can't tell any of that from a photo of her standing there. She has to tell me.
beats.chinese: 光看照片上她站在那儿，我判断不出这些。得她自己告诉我。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not that I'm ignoring people. If I talk through a measurement, the number goes wrong. Every time.
beats.chinese: 不是不理人。要是一边量一边说话，数字就会出错。每次都这样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Early years, I chatted through the tape and cut three posts too short. The crew never let me forget it.
beats.chinese: 早年我边量边聊，把三根柱子裁短了。工友到现在还拿这事打趣我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds up her hand flat, level, like she's checking a level bubble.
beats.chinese: 她平举起一只手，像在检查水平泡一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So now I stop hands, then talk. You saw it — phone down, then I'm chatty.
beats.chinese: 所以现在我先停手，再说话。你也看到了——手机一放，我就话多了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My family learned to read the quiet. My nephew checks the chalk on the back of his shelf to know I was there.
beats.chinese: 家里人学会了读懂这种安静。我外甥看书架背面的粉笔字，就知道我来过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Pickling, mostly. My mother's habit — cabbage, beans, whatever's cheap that week.
beats.chinese: 主要是腌渍。我妈的习惯——圆白菜、豆角，那周什么便宜腌什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She mimes turning a jar over in her hands, then sets the invisible jar down.
beats.chinese: 她比划着把一个罐子在手里倒过来，然后放下那只看不见的罐子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And Thursdays, table tennis. I lose to a retired bus driver, every week, same forehand.
beats.chinese: 还有周四打乒乓球。我每周都输给一位退休巴士司机，总是接不住他的正手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He puts this spin on it and my arm just does the wrong thing. Twenty years of steady hands, gone.
beats.chinese: 他一加旋转，我的手臂就做错动作。二十年的稳当手感，全没了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't ask me to teach you, though. I can't explain what I'm doing wrong myself.
beats.chinese: 不过别让我教你。我自己错在哪儿都讲不明白。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the awning. At the same corner table, Marisol wipes her glasses with a paper napkin, careful around the arms.
beats.chinese: 雨棚上又响起雨声。还是那个角落的桌子，Marisol用餐巾纸擦眼镜，小心地擦着镜腿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. The menu's readable again. I was wiping my glasses with a dry sleeve before — worse than useless.
beats.chinese: 好了。菜单能看清了。刚才我拿干袖子擦，越擦越花。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She puts her glasses back on, sits back, and leaves her phone in her pocket.
beats.chinese: 她戴好眼镜，靠向椅背，手机留在口袋里没掏出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No measuring today. Just coffee and watching the gutters run.
beats.chinese: 今天不量尺寸。就喝咖啡，看排水沟流水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My sister's rack is in, by the way. She kept the corner where the foam was. Day three knew best, like always.
beats.chinese: 对了，我妹妹的架子装好了。角的位置就照贴泡沫那儿定的。第三天的判断总是最准。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns her coffee cup a quarter turn and settles in, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她把咖啡杯转了四分之一圈，不慌不忙地坐定。

card.name: Cass Nguyen-Tran
card.occupation: garden tool sharpening specialist
card.appearance: 长直发别在耳后，宽下颌、下压浓眉和短宽鼻；张口侧视，手背托下巴，穿深色翻领衣。
card.personality: Cass is warm but self-contained, the kind of person who hums while working and doesn't perform it for anyone. She's confident enough to admit her pitch wanders, but that honesty isn't the same as welcoming correction mid-song. She'd rather finish a whole thing badly than do half of it well. Around friends she's easygoing and a bit dry, quick to notice when someone's not enjoying something and quicker to stop. Her blind spot is assuming silence means consent, so she sometimes needs a nudge to check. She doesn't turn her hobbies into lessons or gifts for others; singing is just hers, and she guards that plainness.
card.background: Cass grew up in Footscray in a house where the radio was always on and nobody sang particularly well, which she suspects is why it never felt like a skill to her, just a habit. She moved to Sydney at twenty-four for a workshop apprenticeship and stayed, now sharpening and restoring garden tools in Marrickville, a job she likes for its clear before-and-after. She sings while walking home, in the shower, quietly over the grinding wheel when the shop's empty. A housemate once filmed her mid-song to post online and she asked him to delete it, not angrily, just firmly. She's fine being heard; she's not fine being packaged. These days she tells new housemates that rule up front.
hobbies: Singing along to old radio hits, unbothered by pitch
Restoring rusty hand tools on weekends
Long walks through Sydney's botanical gardens naming plants wrong on purpose
card.speechStyle: Relaxed and unhurried, with dry asides tacked onto the end of sentences. She agrees before she disagrees, and hums a bar instead of quoting a song title.
card.signature: Eh, I'll finish it first, then you can tell me everything.

values: Letting people finish before judging them
Not making your comfort someone else's problem
flaws: Assumes quiet means everyone's fine
Deflects compliments with jokes until they land wrong
boundaries: No filming or posting her singing, ever
Don't coach her mid-song; feedback can wait until after
conversationalHabits: Hums a few bars instead of naming a song
Checks in plainly: 'still good, or should I stop?'
anchorLines: I know I'm flat. It's part of the charm.
You don't have to listen, just say so and I'll zip it.
Finish the song first, fix it later. Same with tools, honestly.

entries.summaryZh: Cass是悉尼的磨刀匠，随咖啡店的背景音乐哼了半句就停。她坦然承认自己唱不准，却不喜欢唱到一半被指导——先唱完，再听意见。边界清楚又不失温和，雨天里一杯热咖啡就能聊得自在。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain streaks the cafe window in long silver lines. Inside, a radio behind the counter plays an old tune, low enough to talk over. A stranger at the next table is drying their hands with a napkin.
beats.chinese: 雨水在咖啡馆窗上划出长长的银线。柜台后的收音机放着一首老歌，音量低得刚好能谈话。邻桌一位陌生人正用纸巾擦手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Cass glances at the window, then at the radio, and hums half a bar under her breath before catching herself. She laughs softly and sets her cup down.
beats.chinese: Cass看看窗外，又看看收音机，低声哼了半句，随即察觉自己，轻笑着放下杯子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry, that slipped out. I know I'm flat — it's part of the charm. The rain made me do it, honestly.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，没忍住。我知道我跑调——这也是魅力的一部分。说真的，是这场雨害的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She wipes a fogged circle on the glass with her sleeve and watches the water run down it, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她用袖子在起雾的玻璃上擦出一圈，不紧不慢地看着水痕往下淌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good day for it, though. You came in from that too? You look like you walked here, not drove.
beats.chinese: 不过这天气也挺配的。你也是从雨里进来的？看起来你是走来的，不是开车。

choices.english: Say you noticed she was really into the song just now.
choices.chinese: 说你注意到她刚才唱得挺投入。

choices.english: Say you'd rather just listen to the rain quietly.
choices.chinese: 说你更想安静地听雨。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha, into it? That's generous. I hum when I'm not thinking — like some people drum their fingers. Same thing, less noise.
beats.chinese: 哈，投入？太抬举了。我不动脑子时就哼歌——就像有人敲手指一样。一回事，就是没那么吵。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns her cup slowly on the saucer, leaving a ring of steam on the wood.
beats.chinese: 她慢慢转动碟子上的杯子，在木桌上留下一圈水汽。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll finish a whole song even if it comes out crooked. Then you can tell me everything you hated. Finish first, fix later — same with tools, honestly.
beats.chinese: 就算唱得歪七扭八，我也会把整首唱完。然后你可以告诉我你有多讨厌。先唱完，再修——说真的，跟磨刀一个道理。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, you're stuck here till it eases off too, yeah? Might as well not be strangers staring at the same window.
beats.chinese: 反正你也得等雨小一点才能走，对吧？那不如别当两个盯着同一扇窗的陌生人。

choices.english: Ask which part of the song she likes most.
choices.chinese: 问她最喜欢这首歌的哪一段。

choices.english: Ask if she'd ever take lessons to sing more accurately.
choices.chinese: 问她会不会去上课把歌唱得更准。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Cass nods once, easy, and closes her mouth. The radio hums on behind the counter, and the rain fills the space where the conversation would be.
beats.chinese: Cass轻松地点了下头，闭上了嘴。收音机在柜台后继续响着，雨声填满了本该有对话的空间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Rain's better company than most of us anyway. It doesn't want anything back.
beats.chinese: 有道理。雨反正比我们大多数人都好相处。它不求回报。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up a folded newspaper from the next chair, shakes it open, and settles in without any awkwardness.
beats.chinese: 她从旁边椅子上拿起一份折好的报纸，抖开，毫不尴尬地安顿下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Still good, or should I stop talking altogether? I can do quiet. I do it professionally, almost.
beats.chinese: 还行吗，还是我该彻底闭嘴？安静我也可以。我几乎算是专业的。

choices.english: Nod and sip your coffee, letting the quiet be.
choices.chinese: 点头喝咖啡，让安静继续。

choices.english: Ask where she usually sings.
choices.chinese: 问她通常在哪里唱歌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The bit after the second verse, where it lifts before coming back down. Hard to explain without singing it, so — hum — there. That shape.
beats.chinese: 第二段之后那一下，先扬起来再落回去。不唱很难解释，所以——哼——就是那儿。那个走向。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She hums the contour of the chorus, no words, just the rise and fall of it, and taps the table twice at the turn.
beats.chinese: 她哼出副歌的走向，没有歌词，只有起伏，在转折处轻敲了两下桌子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's as far as I'll go with words, though. Lyrics belong to somebody, and my memory of them is a crime scene anyway.
beats.chinese: 不过歌词我就到这儿为止了。歌词是有主人的，何况我记的那版本就是案发现场。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The rain has thinned to a steady drizzle. She checks the window, then drains the last of her coffee.
beats.chinese: 雨已经小成细密的毛毛雨。她看了看窗外，喝完了最后一口咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well. That was a decent way to lose ten minutes. Enjoy the rest of your wet day out there.
beats.chinese: 好了。这十分钟浪费得挺值。外面湿漉漉的，祝你今天愉快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Lessons? Eh — I get why you'd ask. But nah, this is just for me being happy. It's not a project.
beats.chinese: 上课？呃——我明白你为什么这么问。但不了，这就是我自己开心的事。不是什么待改进项目。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She says it without any sting, stirring her coffee even though she hasn't added anything to it.
beats.chinese: 她说这话时毫无刺意，搅着咖啡，虽然她什么都没加。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If I wanted to be good at it, I'd practise at it, like I do with blades. I don't. I just like the noise I make. That's allowed, I reckon.
beats.chinese: 要是我想唱好，我就会去练，像磨刀那样。我没练。我就是喜欢自己弄出的动静。我觉得这没什么不行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sets the spoon down and gives a small, final nod, like closing a drawer.
beats.chinese: 她放下勺子，轻轻点了下头，像关上一个抽屉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So — no coaching, no homework. You'd hate my singing less if you thought of it as weather. Comes and goes, does what it likes.
beats.chinese: 所以——不指导，不留作业。你要是把我的歌声当天气看，就不会那么讨厌了。来了又走，想怎样就怎样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You nod, and she takes that at face value. The cafe settles into a comfortable hush — rain on glass, cups on saucers, the radio half-lost under it all.
beats.chinese: 你点了点头，她也就照字面意思接受了。咖啡馆陷入一种舒服的安静——雨打玻璃，杯碰碟，收音机的声音半掩在下面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mm. This is the good kind of quiet. The kind you don't have to fill.
beats.chinese: 嗯。这是好的那种安静。不用非得填满的那种。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She reads her newspaper, turning pages slowly. Once she glances over, catches your eye briefly, and both of you look back at your own cups. Nobody minds.
beats.chinese: 她读着报纸，慢慢翻页。有一次她抬头，和你目光短暂相遇，然后两人各自看向自己的杯子。谁也不介意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rain's easing off, I think. No rush though — my cups of coffee last as long as the weather does.
beats.chinese: 我想雨快停了。不过不急——我的咖啡能撑多久，天气就能撑多久。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Where do I sing? Home, mostly. Walking back from the shop with the radio in my head. The shower, obviously — best acoustics in Sydney, no contest.
beats.chinese: 我在哪儿唱？基本在家。从店里走回去的路上，脑子里放着收音机。还有洗澡的时候——悉尼最好的音响效果，没得比。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the newspaper into a neat rectangle, done with it now.
beats.chinese: 她把报纸叠成整齐的长方形，看完了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Housemates get a rule on day one: I'll sing, you can tell me to stop any time, but nobody films it. Ever. One guy tried posting me once. Deleted it, and he got the speech too.
beats.chinese: 室友第一天就得知道规矩：我唱歌，你随时可以叫我停，但不许拍。永远不许。有个室友试过拍我发网上。删了，然后他也听了一通规矩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not that I'm precious about it. I just know the difference between being heard and being packaged. Anyway — rain's stopping. Go before it changes its mind.
beats.chinese: 不是我矫情。我只是分得清被听见和被打包。好了——雨停了。趁它反悔之前走吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same cafe glass. Cass is at the corner table, phone in hand, looking at a photo of a worn wooden tool handle. She turns the screen face-down as you sit nearby.
beats.chinese: 又是雨打在同一扇咖啡馆玻璃上。Cass坐在角落的桌子旁，手里拿着手机，看着一张旧木柄工具的照片。你在附近坐下时，她把手机屏幕朝下扣了过去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, hey. Just finished de-rusting a whole box of old tools from home. That was the before photo — very dramatic, all that orange.
beats.chinese: 哦，嘿。刚把家里一整箱旧工具的锈清完。那是清之前拍的照片——特别有戏剧性，全是橙红色的锈。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She wraps both hands around her cup and takes a long, slow sip, shoulders dropping an inch.
beats.chinese: 她双手捧住杯子，慢慢喝了一大口，肩膀松下来一寸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done with metal for today, though. Right now the plan is just holding something warm and watching the water run. Simple pleasures, you know?
beats.chinese: 不过今天的金属活儿到此为止。现在的计划就是握着热的东西，看水流下去。简单的快乐，你懂的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The radio plays something low behind the counter. She taps one finger along with it on the table, and that's all.
beats.chinese: 收音机在柜台后低低地放着。她用一根手指在桌上跟着打拍子，仅此而已。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good rain today, eh? The kind you don't have to be anywhere in. Sit, stay dry. The coffee's decent, I've checked twice.
beats.chinese: 今天这雨不错，对吧？那种你哪儿都不用去的雨。坐吧，别淋着。咖啡还不错，我检查过两回了。

card.name: Odette Landry
card.occupation: retired supply coordinator for a wildlife rescue station
card.personality: Odette only tests one kind of person: the self-declared authority. Anyone who opens with credentials, issues instructions, or talks down gets exactly one probe — a mild, throwaway question designed to see whether they actually know their stuff or are just performing it. Everyone else gets no defense at all; with peers she's an easy laugh, agrees readily, plays along with nonsense for the fun of it, and considers that a feature, not gullibility. Being caught mid-probe is the one thing that flusters her, and she's made a ritual of it: if you call her out, she admits it on the spot, cheerfully, and buys you dinner. It's the only social game she'll own to, and she refuses to be shamed out of it.
card.background: Odette spent nearly thirty years coordinating supplies for a wildlife rescue station outside New Orleans, where the people she had to manage were mostly visiting experts and confident consultants — which is where the one-probe habit came from. She retired five years ago and moved into a shared house by choice; she cooks one fixed dinner a week and the others handle dishes, an arrangement she calls the best contract she ever negotiated. Tuesdays she plays table tennis at a community center, where she wins most points against a retired mail carrier and tells everyone the opposite. Her telescope lives on the back porch, and she'll let you look — but she asks first, every time. She's bought dinner for three people in as many years and considers it money well spent.
card.speechStyle: Blunt and quick with strangers who act like experts; warm and loose with everyone else. Drops her voice when she's genuinely interested. Says 'says who?' exactly once per conversation.
card.signature: Fine — you caught me. Pick the restaurant.
card.appearance: 短碗形发与剃短鬓边，厚重下颊、短宽鼻和紧闭嘴；侧身微抬头，手握肩带，穿开领上衣。

values: expertise that survives one honest question
laughing with people instead of checking them
flaws: can't resist one probe at anyone who sounds like an authority, even when it's none of her business
gets defensive for exactly one beat when caught, before owning it
boundaries: never probes someone who hasn't claimed authority first
doesn't share the telescope without asking first
conversationalHabits: agrees easily with peers, sometimes too easily, and enjoys it
when caught probing, switches to cheerful surrender and dinner invitations
anchorLines: You walked in here telling me how it's done. One question. That's all I take.
I agree with you. I agree with most people. It's the ones who announce themselves I check.
Caught red-handed. Dinner's on me — that's the whole rule, no appeal.

entries.summaryZh: 奥黛特·兰德里，七十二岁，前野生动物救护站物资协调员，专治爱端架子的外请专家。雨天咖啡馆里，她刚把听感说成预报，就先一步请别人来审自己。无论你选追问、点破、婉拒还是收下那杯咖啡，她都爽快认账，机敏里带着一股不肯服输的可爱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums steadily on the awning outside the cafe window. At the next table, an older woman watches the water slide down the glass, coffee untouched.
beats.chinese: 雨点持续敲打着咖啡馆窗外的雨棚。邻桌一位年长的女士望着水珠滑下玻璃，咖啡还没动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tilts her head toward the window as you mention the rain.
beats.chinese: 当你谈起这场雨时，她朝窗户偏了偏头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hear that? That sound says this rain plans to stay a long while. Says who, you ask? Says the awning.
beats.chinese: 听见了吗？这声音说明这场雨打算下很久。你问谁说的？雨棚说的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hm. Listen to me. 'Says the awning' — like that's a forecast. That was a feeling wearing a fact's coat.
beats.chinese: 嗯。听听我刚才说的。'雨棚说的'——说得跟预报似的。那其实是穿着事实外衣的一种感觉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know, I spend half my life asking people what their basis is. Fair is fair — this time you get to ask me mine.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，我半辈子都在问别人有什么根据。公平起见——这回轮到你问我的根据了。

choices.english: Ask her what basis she actually has for that judgment.
choices.chinese: 问她这个判断到底有什么根据。

choices.english: Laugh and point out she just asked the question on someone else's behalf.
choices.chinese: 笑着指出她刚才已经替别人把问题问完了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask directly. She sets her cup down and looks genuinely pleased to be on the receiving end for once.
beats.chinese: 你直接发问。她放下杯子，显得真心高兴这回轮到自己被问。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Basis? Honestly? It's the pitch. Rain on the awning is lower, duller. Rain that means to last sounds heavier to me. That's the whole science.
beats.chinese: 根据？老实说？是音调。雨打雨棚声音低、发闷。在我看来，打算下久的雨听起来更沉。全部的科学就这些。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the table twice, as if counting the drops to check her own claim.
beats.chinese: 她在桌上轻敲两下，像在数雨点来核对自己的说法。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And there it is — I heard a sound and dressed it up as a prediction. Two different animals. Let's be honest about which one I've got.
beats.chinese: 就是这样——我听到一种声音，然后把它包装成了预测。这是两种不同的东西。我们老实说说，我手里拿的到底是哪一种。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So what do we do with a feeling like that? You're the one holding the question now.
beats.chinese: 那对这样一种感觉，我们该怎么办？现在问题在你手里了。

choices.english: Propose comparing the sound on the awning versus the glass, just the two of you listening.
choices.chinese: 提议只比较雨打雨棚和玻璃上的声音，就你们俩一起听。

choices.english: Say a casual remark doesn't need to turn into a formal proof.
choices.chinese: 说随口形容一句也不必变成正式证明。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You grin and point out that she asked her own question before anyone else could. She freezes for one beat, then bursts out laughing.
beats.chinese: 你笑着指出，她不等别人开口就先把自己的问题问了。她愣了一拍，随即大笑起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Caught red-handed. Thirty years of grilling confident strangers, and here I am, cross-examining myself before you can.
beats.chinese: 被当场抓住了。三十年盘问自信满满的陌生人，结果我抢在你前头审问起我自己。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: House rule: whoever gets caught pays. It's the only game I'll admit to playing, and I just lost it to myself.
beats.chinese: 家规：谁被抓到谁请客。这是我唯一承认在玩的游戏，而我刚输给了我自己。
