beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She waves toward the counter, already half out of her chair.
beats.chinese: 她朝柜台招手，人已经半个身子离开了椅子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Let me buy you a drink. It's not charity — it's the fine. What'll it be?
beats.chinese: 让我请你喝一杯。这不是施舍——是罚金。你要什么？

choices.english: Decline the treat and suggest leaving it as a good self-mockery, nothing more.
choices.chinese: 婉拒请客，提议把这次就当作一句自嘲，到此为止。

choices.english: Accept her offer of a plain house coffee.
choices.chinese: 接受她请一杯店里普通咖啡的提议。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Both of them turn toward the window and go quiet. The rain on the awning comes first, then the thinner sound on the glass.
beats.chinese: 两人一起转向窗外，安静下来。雨打雨棚的声音先到，然后是打在玻璃上更细的声音。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Awning: heavy, hollow, a drum. Glass: thin, sharp, almost polite. One light, one heavy — that's all I actually heard.
beats.chinese: 听。雨棚：沉、空，像面鼓。玻璃：细、尖，几乎算客气。一轻一重——我真正听到的就这些。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sits back, satisfied, and finally takes a sip of her coffee.
beats.chinese: 她靠回椅背，一脸满意，终于喝了一口咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No weather in there anywhere. Just two sounds and an old woman with good ears. That's the honest version.
beats.chinese: 这里面哪儿都没有天气预报。只有两种声音，和一个耳朵还灵的老太太。这是诚实的版本。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You tell her a passing remark doesn't owe anyone a proof. She considers this, then nods slowly.
beats.chinese: 你告诉她，随口一句形容不欠任何人一个证明。她想了想，慢慢点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh. You know what, you're right. I was about to convene a whole hearing over my own coffee comment.
beats.chinese: 嘿。你知道吗，你说得对。我差点要为自己一句咖啡桌上的话开庭审理了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She repeats her earlier sentence to the window, slower this time, like she's testing the new wording.
beats.chinese: 她朝窗户把刚才那句话又说了一遍，这次慢了些，像在试用新的措辞。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Let's try again: that rain sounds long to me. Sounds. Not is. A feeling, clearly labeled.
beats.chinese: 再试一遍：这场雨在我听来会下很久。听来。不是就是。一种感觉，标签贴得清清楚楚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. First time in years I've asked a question and then closed the file myself. I'll count that as a win.
beats.chinese: 好了。这么多年来头一回，我问了个问题，然后自己把案卷合上了。我就当这算赢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You wave off the offer and say the self-mockery alone was worth it. She drops back into her chair without protest.
beats.chinese: 你摆手谢绝，说这句自嘲本身就值了。她毫无异议地坐回椅子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done. No fine, no appeal. You got off easy — some people have paid full dinners for less.
beats.chinese: 成交。不罚了，不上诉。你逃得轻松——有些人就为更小的事付过整整顿晚饭。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up her cup and turns it slowly on the saucer, listening to the rain pick up again.
beats.chinese: 她端起杯子，在碟子上慢慢转动，听着雨又大了起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The habit's not going anywhere, mind you. But maybe I'll let it retire a few years after I did.
beats.chinese: 不过别指望那毛病会消失。也许我该让它比我再晚几年退休。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For now — two old listeners, one long rain. That's a fine way to be stuck indoors.
beats.chinese: 眼下——两个爱听雨的老家伙，一场下不完的雨。被困在屋里，这方式不赖。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You accept. She catches the server's eye and orders clearly, leaving room for you to step in.
beats.chinese: 你接受了。她招手叫来服务员，清楚地报了单，也给你留了开口的余地。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One house coffee for this table here — and if you'd rather something else, tell him directly, don't mind me.
beats.chinese: 给这桌来一杯店里的普通咖啡——要是你想换别的，直接跟他说，不用管我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The server confirms the order and heads off. She rubs her hands together like she's just closed a deal.
beats.chinese: 服务员确认了订单便走开。她搓了搓手，像刚谈成了一笔买卖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Paid in full. The ledger's clean. Don't go telling people I settle my debts with plain coffee — I have a reputation.
beats.chinese: 付清了。账本干净了。别到处说我用普通咖啡还债——我可是有名声的人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Now we can both just sit and listen to the rain like people with nothing to prove.
beats.chinese: 好了。现在咱们俩可以就坐着听雨，像两个没什么要证明的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Another rainy day, another cafe window. Odette is at a corner table, wrestling a folded shopping bag back into its small pouch. It refuses twice.
beats.chinese: 又是一个雨天，又一面咖啡馆的窗。奥黛特坐在角落的桌子旁，正把折叠购物袋往小袋里塞。袋子两次不肯就范。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No experts to interrogate today, no excuses. I just folded it too thick. That's the entire case file.
beats.chinese: 今天没有专家可审问，也没有借口。我就是折得太厚了。全部案卷就这些。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shakes the bag out, folds it in half again, and this time it slides in. She sets it aside with a small nod.
beats.chinese: 她把袋子抖开，再对折一次，这次顺利塞了进去。她小小地点了下头，把它放到一边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Folded by the manufacturer's own instructions, I'd wager. Sit — table's all yours, rain's all ours.
beats.chinese: 好了。我敢说这次是按厂家说明折的。坐吧——桌子归你，雨归咱们俩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And listen to it out there. That rain still has no plans to quit. I stand by my ears, if nothing else.
beats.chinese: 听听外面。这场雨还没打算停。别的我不敢说，我这双耳朵我信得过。

card.name: Kit Draper
card.occupation: open-mic comedy host's assistant (runs the list, times acts, sets the room)
card.personality: Kit has never once broken a commitment, which sounds admirable until you notice what it costs. Every promise gets honoured, and the price is always paid out of his own time: his Thursday folk dance class is the first thing sacrificed, so he's attended maybe six sessions since September. He keeps quiet gaps in his week for things friends mentioned offhandedly — a pint, a lift, a hand with a flat — and when they forget, he says nothing and quietly folds the gap back into work. He's decisive when it matters: booking cancellations, an act going over time, a drunk heckler. It's the small rituals where he turns stubborn. He teases himself about all of it, flatly, before anyone else can.
card.background: Kit started at the open mic at sixteen hauling chairs for a host who's since moved to Leeds, and now runs the practical side: sign-ups, the timing light, telling drunk uncles no. His reliability is local legend — if Kit said it, it's happening. He was dragged to folk dance once by his nan and liked the footwork more than expected, though the class keeps losing his Thursdays to other people's emergencies. His grandad left half-finished kite drafts in a shoebox — graph paper, scribbled measurements, no instructions — and Kit works through them one at a time, currently on a box kite annotated only 'more spine?'. He's not trying to rebuild them exactly; the notes are a starting point, not scripture. The kite is the one thing he refuses to rush.
card.speechStyle: short, flat sentences with deadpan self-teasing; states outcomes like facts rather than plans; never announces a favour, just mentions it already happened
card.signature: I said yes, so it's happening. My Thursday just isn't.
card.appearance: 蓬松偏斜短刘海，圆框眼镜与下垂眼，嘴微张；头侧倾并低头抬眼，穿连帽外套。

values: a promise is a promise
other people getting to rely on him
flaws: pays for everyone's reliability out of his own time and calls it fine
holds silent space for things others forgot, and won't remind them
boundaries: won't break a commitment, even when he's the one who suffers
won't rush the kite — it gets done when the drafts say so
conversationalHabits: mentions favours already done instead of offering
reports his own sacrificed slots like a weather update
anchorLines: Dev needed a shift covered Tuesday, so my dance class moved to... no, it didn't move. It evaporated. These things happen.
I kept Saturday afternoon free because Priya mentioned a market trip three weeks ago. Did she mention it since? No. Is the afternoon still free? Also no — it's free, I just spent it differently.
Big decisions, no problem. Cancel an act, refund a ticket, done in a minute. But the timing light has to be the one with the red tape on it. I don't have a defence. It's just the light.

entries.summaryZh: 十九岁的开放麦助理基特，承诺从不落空，代价全记在自己头上：为朋友一句“可能要帮忙”，他默默空出周四，舞课一再让位。雨天咖啡馆里，那个没人确认的空白格被摊在桌上，四条路走向四种收场——发消息确认、标为未确认、干脆去跳舞、或摊开祖父的风筝图纸。他冷面自嘲，只损自己。

story.titleZh: 雨天咖啡馆里没人确认的空格

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain hammers the café window. Kit sits by the glass with a small notebook, drawing a line through one entry and leaving a blank square next to Thursday.
beats.chinese: 雨点砸在咖啡馆的窗上。基特坐在玻璃边，拿着一个小本子，划掉一条记录，在周四旁边留了一个空白格。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Proper Manchester rain. It doesn't fall, it just arrives sideways and stays.
beats.chinese: 正宗的曼彻斯特雨。它不是落下来的，是横着来的，然后就不走了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the blank square with his pen, then notices you looking at the window and shrugs.
beats.chinese: 他用笔敲了敲那个空白格，然后注意到你在看窗外，耸了耸肩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You picked a good day for a café. Outside, the puddles are doing their best impression of a canal.
beats.chinese: 你挑了个进咖啡馆的好日子。外面那些水洼正在卖力模仿运河。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That blank square, by the way, is Thursday. Dev said maybe he'd need a hand moving stuff. Maybe. So the square stays blank until he says so.
beats.chinese: 顺便说一句，那个空白格是周四的。戴夫说过可能需要人帮忙搬东西。只是可能。所以那个格一直空着，等他发话。

choices.english: Ask if the friend actually confirmed it.
choices.chinese: 问朋友到底确认了没有。

choices.english: Ask what he'd use that time for otherwise.
choices.chinese: 问他不然那段时间想拿来做什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Confirmed? No. He said it in the queue at the chippy, between bites. 'Might need a hand Thursday.' That was eleven days ago.
beats.chinese: 确认了吗？没有。他是在炸鱼薯条店排队时说的，一边嚼一边说的。“周四可能需要搭把手。”那是十一天前。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Kit turns the notebook so you can see the square. There's a tiny 'D?' pencilled in the corner.
beats.chinese: 基特把本子转过来给你看那个格子。角落里用铅笔写着一个小小的“D？”。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I kept it free on my own. He might not even remember saying it. That's the funny part. I'll sit in the rain waiting and he'll be at home, dry, watching telly.
beats.chinese: 所以是我自己把它留出来的。他可能都不记得自己说过。这就是好笑的地方。我会坐在雨里等，而他在家，干着，看电视。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My dance class was Thursday too. Session number seven this term. I've been to five. The instructor does a little sad nod now when I walk in.
beats.chinese: 我的舞课也是周四。这学期的第七次课。我去了五次。现在我进门时老师会轻轻点一下头，很悲伤的那种。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the notebook but keeps his thumb inside it, marking the page.
beats.chinese: 他合上本子，但拇指还夹在里面，占着那一页。

choices.english: Suggest he just text Dev and confirm it directly.
choices.chinese: 建议他直接给戴夫发消息确认。

choices.english: Say an unconfirmed maybe doesn't count as a real promise.
choices.chinese: 说没确认的“可能”不算真正的承诺。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What would I do with it? Dance class. Thursday, six o'clock, folk dance, me and a room of people twice my age who are all better at it.
beats.chinese: 不然拿来干什么？舞课。周四六点，民族舞，我和一屋子年纪两倍于我、但个个跳得比我好的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flattens the notebook on the table and taps the blank square again, harder this time.
beats.chinese: 他把本子在桌上摊平，又敲了敲那个空白格，这次敲得重了些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My nan dragged me along once. I went for the biscuits. Stayed for the footwork. Now look at me — five attendances this term. A record. A bad one.
beats.chinese: 我奶奶硬拉我去过一次。我本来是冲着饼干去的。结果留恋上了舞步。看看现在的我——这学期去了五次。一个纪录。一个难看的纪录。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not going to dress it up as noble. Dev gets the slot, I miss the class, nobody writes a song about it. That's just the maths.
beats.chinese: 我不会把这包装成什么高尚的事。戴夫占了那个时段，我就缺课，没人会为此写首歌。账就是这么算的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Outside, a gust flips an umbrella inside out on the pavement. Kit watches it happen without much sympathy.
beats.chinese: 外面一阵风把人行道上一把伞吹翻了。基特看着这一幕，没什么同情。

choices.english: Ask what happens if Dev doesn't need him after all.
choices.chinese: 问如果戴夫最后不需要他怎么办。

choices.english: Notice the graph paper sticking out of his bag and ask about it.
choices.chinese: 注意到他包里露出的方格纸，问那是什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Kit pulls out his phone and types with one thumb, unhurried, like posting a letter.
beats.chinese: 基特掏出手机，用一个大拇指慢慢打字，不慌不忙，像在寄一封信。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Thursday still on? Need the hand or not?' There. Sent. Now it's his problem to answer, not mine to guess.
beats.chinese: “周四还算数吗？还用不用人帮忙？”好了。发了。现在轮到他回，不用我猜了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He puts his phone face-down on the table and signals for a refill of his own cup.
beats.chinese: 他把手机屏幕朝下放在桌上，示意给自己的杯子续杯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If he says yes, I carry boxes. If he says no, I do the box step in my kitchen and call it class. Either way, the square gets filled tonight.
beats.chinese: 他说要，我就去搬箱子。他说不要，我就在厨房里练基本步，也算上课。反正今晚那个格子就会填上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eleven days of guessing. One message. I do admire a problem that folds that fast.
beats.chinese: 猜了十一天。一条消息就完。我很欣赏这种折得这么快的难题。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Kit considers this, then uncaps his pen and writes something small in the corner of the square.
beats.chinese: 基特想了想，拔开笔帽，在格子的角落里写了点小字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Unconfirmed.' There. I wrote it down. That's me admitting the maybe was mine, not his debt.
beats.chinese: “未确认”。好了。我写下来了。这算我承认这个“可能”是我自己的事，不是欠他的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're right that he owes me nothing. But I said yes in my head, and my head keeps books. Ask my Thursdays. They'll testify.
beats.chinese: 你说得对，他不欠我什么。但我心里已经答应了，而我心里记着账呢。问我的周四吧，它们会作证的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the notebook properly this time and slides it into his jacket pocket, thumb finally out.
beats.chinese: 这次他正经合上了本子，塞进外套口袋，拇指终于抽了出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If he shows up, I'm there. If he doesn't, I'll fold the gap back into work and say nothing. That's the system. It's not a good system. It's just mine.
beats.chinese: 他来，我就在。他不来，我就把那个空档折回工作里，什么都不说。这就是我的系统。不是个好系统。但是我的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Kit looks out at the rain for a moment, then picks up the pen and draws a firm line through the blank square.
beats.chinese: 基特朝雨里看了一会儿，然后拿起笔，在那个空白格上划了一道干脆的线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then I go to class. Done. That's a decision with clear conditions — he needs me, I'm there; he doesn't, I'm doing the box step with the pensioners.
beats.chinese: 那我就去上课。完事。这是个条件清楚的决定——他需要我，我就在；不需要，我就和那群退休的人跳基本步。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He writes 'DANCE' in the square, in capitals, and underlines it once.
beats.chinese: 他在格子里写了“舞课”，大写，下面划了一道线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I nearly did it again, you know. Nearly built him a second task out of my own evening. You caught it before it set. Like taking a cake out early.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，我差点又犯了。差点又用自己的晚上给他搭出一个任务。你赶在它定型前抓住了。像提前把蛋糕取出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Attendance number six, possibly. The instructor's sad nod becomes a normal nod. Historic.
beats.chinese: 可能就是第六次出勤。老师那悲伤的点头会变成普通的点头。历史性的时刻。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls the graph paper out and flattens it on the table: a kite drawing in pencil, covered in scribbled numbers, one corner annotated 'more spine?'.
beats.chinese: 他把方格纸抽出来在桌上摊平：一幅铅笔风筝图，写满了潦草的数字，一个角上标着“骨架再加一根？”。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My grandad's drafts. Shoebox of them. No instructions, just this — a box kite and his handwriting asking questions at me across fifty years.
beats.chinese: 我爷爷的图纸。一鞋盒。没有说明，就这些——一只箱形风筝，还有他的字，隔着五十年在问我问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not rebuilding them exactly. His notes are a starting point, not scripture. This one says 'more spine?' so I add a spine and see if it flies or folds.
beats.chinese: 我不完全是照着重做。他的批注是起点，不是经文。这张写着“骨架再加一根？”，那我就加一根，看它是飞起来还是散架。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the paper along its old creases, carefully, and puts it back in the bag, away from the rain-damp window.
beats.chinese: 他沿着原来折痕把纸仔细折好，放回包里，离被雨打湿的窗户远远的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Everything else in my week runs on other people's clocks. This one doesn't. It gets done when the drafts say so. That's the whole rule.
beats.chinese: 我这周里其他所有事都按别人的钟表走。就这件事不。图纸说了算，它才算完。规则就这一条。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Same café, same rain on the glass. Kit has his bag open on the table, frowning at a length of kite line wound around a pen cap.
beats.chinese: 还是那家咖啡馆，雨还是打在玻璃上。基特把包摊在桌上，皱着眉看一段缠在笔帽上的风筝线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't ask how it got there. It's been riding around in my pocket for a fortnight, strangling a biro.
beats.chinese: 别问它怎么跑到那儿去的。它在我口袋里转悠了两个星期，勒着一支圆珠笔。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He works the line loose a few centimetres at a time, patient as anything, then feeds it onto a wooden spool from his bag.
beats.chinese: 他一次解开几厘米，耐心得很，然后把线绕进包里的一个木线轴上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Everything else in my week is a rush. This bit isn't. The drafts decide the pace, and today the drafts say: untangle the pen.
beats.chinese: 我这周其他事都在赶。就这一件不赶。图纸说了算，今天图纸说：把笔解救出来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The last loop slides free. He holds the spool up to the window light, checks it, and pockets it, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 最后一圈滑脱了。他把线轴举到窗光下检查了一下，收进口袋，一脸满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway — good rain today. Proper sideways. Hope you're not standing in it.
beats.chinese: 总之——今天这雨下得好。正宗的横着下。希望你别站在里头。

card.name: Yvonne Chambers
card.occupation: food label compliance proofreader
card.appearance: 一侧较长的波波头，脸颊下垂、眉眼高低不一，嘴角斜拉露少量齿白；穿宽围领外衣。
card.personality: Yvonne photographs rooms just before company arrives: cups still full, chairs still straight, nobody in the picture. She enjoys hosting, but gets attached to that first arrangement and can quietly put things back while people are still using them. A moved chair bothers her more than a spilled drink. Guests sometimes feel like visitors to a display instead of friends at a table. She can laugh when this is pointed out, but her hand still reaches for the chair. Outside her own home she is easy company, interested in bargains and happy to change her cycling route.
card.background: Yvonne grew up in Kingston above her mother's small shop, where the floor was rearranged every delivery day. She became a food label compliance proofreader and still enjoys the satisfaction of a finished page. Her first flat had barely room for one guest; her present kitchen can seat six, and she loves getting it ready. Over the years she has accumulated photographs of tables before birthdays, ordinary lunches and neighbours dropping by. She never photographs guests without asking. Her sister Denise noticed that Yvonne sometimes tries to preserve the before-picture during the visit, putting a chair back under someone's bag or straightening a cloth while cups are on it. Yvonne thinks the room simply looked lovely that way. Denise thinks people should be allowed to leave a room looking lived in. They still have lunch together most Sundays.
hobbies: Reading old food packaging for changing design styles
card.speechStyle: Warm and concrete; describes the position of things with a quick hand gesture, then admits a small inconvenience with an amused sigh. Plain and exact about food labels.
card.signature: It looked lovely before anybody sat down. That might be the problem.

values: Making space to welcome people
Remembering ordinary occasions
flaws: Restores an arrangement while guests are still using it
Confuses a well-prepared room with a comfortable visit
boundaries: Does not photograph guests without consent
Will not rearrange someone else's home
conversationalHabits: Shows the empty room in a photo rather than describing a whole occasion
Catches her hand straightening something and sometimes leaves it alone
anchorLines: That is the kitchen before lunch. You can tell because every chair agrees with me.
Denise moved it to hear the radio. I kept moving it back for the photograph nobody was taking.
You can spill the tea. Just let me save the photograph first.

entries.summaryZh: 约娜在金斯顿校对食品标签，喜欢在客人抵达前拍下摆好的房间。她真心爱招待朋友，却舍不得破坏那张开席前的画面，常在客人还坐着时把椅子、桌布悄悄复位，让人像在参观展品。妹妹会直接提醒她，约娜能自嘲，但手仍会伸过去。她也爱骑车逛市场，到了别人家反而很好随和。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the shared cafe table, you comment on the rain blowing against the window. The woman beside you moves her damp cycling gloves onto her own bag.
beats.chinese: 在咖啡馆共用的桌旁，你说起拍打窗户的斜雨。身边的女人把潮湿的骑行手套挪到自己的包上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My kitchen was meant to have six people in it by now. Rain has delayed everyone except the chairs.
beats.chinese: 照计划，这会儿我家厨房该坐着六个人了。这场雨把所有人都耽搁了，只有椅子准时。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns her phone toward the table. The photograph shows six empty chairs, cups and a striped cloth.
beats.chinese: 她把手机转向桌面。照片里有六把空椅子、杯子和一块条纹桌布。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I took this before cycling out for bread. Yvonne, by the way. My sister says I like this part of lunch best.
beats.chinese: 这是我骑车出门买面包前拍的。对了，我叫约娜。我妹妹说，整顿午饭我最喜欢的就是这个阶段。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nobody has moved anything yet. That sounds worse when I say it out loud.
beats.chinese: 还没人挪动过任何东西。说出口怎么就不太好听了。

choices.english: Ask what happens when the guests move their chairs.
choices.chinese: 问客人挪动椅子后会怎样。

choices.english: Ask what she does with the photographs afterwards.
choices.chinese: 问她之后会怎么处理这些照片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Denise moved hers nearer the radio last Sunday. I put it back when she got up for water. She moved it again. We did that three times.
beats.chinese: 上周日，丹妮丝把椅子挪到收音机旁。我趁她起身倒水把它放回去，她又挪过去。来回了三次。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Yvonne points to the chair nearest the wall in the photograph.
beats.chinese: 约娜指了指照片里最靠墙的那把椅子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There was room. She wasn't blocking anything. It just left a gap where I hadn't planned one.
beats.chinese: 空间够，也没挡着什么。只是她原来的位置空了一块，不在我的安排里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She said, are we having lunch or looking at your kitchen? Then she stayed in the chair. Fair move.
beats.chinese: 她问，我们是来吃午饭还是参观你的厨房？说完她就不离开那把椅子了。这招挺合理。

choices.english: Suggest leaving that chair by the radio today.
choices.chinese: 建议今天把那把椅子留在收音机旁。

choices.english: Ask whether Yvonne would rather keep the arrangement.
choices.chinese: 问约娜是否还是想保留原来的摆法。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Keep them in a folder. No faces, just rooms waiting. I can usually remember who came by which cups I put out.
beats.chinese: 存进一个文件夹。没有人脸，只有等着来客的房间。看我摆了哪些杯子，通常就能想起那天谁来过。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She swipes to a small table with two mismatched cups, then another with a paper birthday banner.
beats.chinese: 她划到一张小桌子的照片，上面是两只不配套的杯子，再下一张挂着纸生日横幅。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That was my old flat. Two chairs and you had to turn sideways to reach the sink. We ate with our elbows tucked in.
beats.chinese: 那是我以前的公寓。两把椅子，去水槽边还得侧着身子。吃饭时大家都得夹紧胳膊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I love having room now. Apparently I also love telling the room exactly what to do.
beats.chinese: 我很喜欢现在宽敞了。看来我也很喜欢命令这个房间老实听话。

choices.english: Ask to see the old kitchen again.
choices.chinese: 想再看看以前那间厨房。

choices.english: Suggest taking a photograph after lunch as well.
choices.chinese: 建议午饭后也拍一张。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Before she gets there? She'll suspect something. Probably check whether the radio still works.
beats.chinese: 在她来之前？她会起疑心的，没准要先检查收音机还能不能响。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Yvonne types a short message and turns the screen back toward herself before sending it.
beats.chinese: 约娜输入一条短消息，把屏幕转回自己这边，然后发了出去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I told her the chair can stay wherever she puts it today. There. One chair. I haven't promised the whole kitchen.
beats.chinese: 我告诉她，今天椅子她放哪儿就在哪儿。好了，一把椅子。我可没把整个厨房都许出去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I still get my before-picture. I've already taken it.
beats.chinese: 而且开席前的照片我照样有。已经拍好了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She locks the phone and pulls her gloves further onto her bag, clear of the table. Outside, rain runs down the glass.
beats.chinese: 她锁上手机，把手套再往包上挪了挪，免得占着桌面。窗外的雨沿玻璃流下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly? Yes. I spent twenty minutes moving that cloth until the stripes lined up. I want somebody to notice.
beats.chinese: 说实话？想。我挪了二十分钟桌布，才让条纹对齐。我希望有人能看出来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She enlarges the photograph, then laughs at the perfectly straight edge.
beats.chinese: 她放大照片，看着那条笔直的边，自己笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But Denise noticed the radio, because she likes the lunchtime programme. I suppose she came for lunch, not my twenty minutes.
beats.chinese: 可丹妮丝注意到的是收音机，因为她喜欢午间节目。我想她是来吃饭的，不是来看我折腾了二十分钟。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm keeping this picture. That can stay straight even if the real table doesn't.
beats.chinese: 这张照片我要留着。实物桌子乱了，照片里的还可以整整齐齐。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She saves the photograph to her folder and puts the phone away without sending a message.
beats.chinese: 她把照片存进文件夹，收起手机，没有发消息。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one. Look at the blue cup. The handle faced the wall because that was the only way both cups fitted.
beats.chinese: 这张。看那个蓝杯子，杯柄朝着墙，因为只有这样两只杯子才放得下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She returns to the two-chair photograph and rests the phone against her bag.
beats.chinese: 她翻回只有两把椅子的照片，把手机靠在包上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My mother said the soup was excellent. It was from a tin. I had spent all afternoon finding somewhere to put the spoons.
beats.chinese: 我妈妈说汤很好喝。其实是罐头汤。我整个下午都在找能放勺子的地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That was a good lunch, though. Nobody could move a chair even if they wanted to. Perhaps that's why I was so relaxed.
beats.chinese: 不过那顿饭确实吃得好。就算想挪椅子也挪不了。也许正因为这样，我才那么放松。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leaves the old photograph on the screen a moment longer, then turns to watch the rain with you.
beats.chinese: 她让那张旧照片在屏幕上多停留了一会儿，然后转过头，和你一起看雨。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Afterwards? With the crumbs? That folder would suddenly look very different.
beats.chinese: 饭后？带着满桌碎屑？那文件夹可就突然变了样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She opens a reminder and types a few words.
beats.chinese: 她打开提醒事项，打下几个字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Photograph after lunch. Before clearing up. I need that second bit, or I'll tidy the whole thing first and miss the point.
beats.chinese: 午饭后拍照，收拾之前。后半句得写上，不然我会先把一切收拾好，那就白拍了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No people in it. Just wherever the chairs actually end up. Denise may put hers in the hallway to make a point.
beats.chinese: 不拍人。只拍椅子最后真正待的位置。丹妮丝没准会故意把她那把挪到走廊去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sets the reminder and pockets the phone, smiling at the rain-dark window.
beats.chinese: 她设好提醒，把手机放进口袋，对着被雨打暗的窗户笑了笑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: While sheltering in the cafe, you mention the sudden rain. Yvonne recognises you and lifts a sealed packet of crackers from her shopping bag.
beats.chinese: 在咖啡馆避雨时，你说起这场突如其来的雨。约娜认出了你，从购物袋里拿出一包没拆封的饼干。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Caught again. At least these stayed dry. I spent five minutes trying to work out the discount.
beats.chinese: 又被困住了。至少这个没湿。我花了五分钟才弄明白打几折。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A bright discount sticker covers the printed price. She tilts the packet, but leaves the sticker attached.
beats.chinese: 鲜亮的促销贴纸盖住了印刷价格。她转了转包装，没有撕掉贴纸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I proofread food labels all week. Then one cheerful sticker beats me on Saturday.
beats.chinese: 我整周都在校对食品标签，到了周六，却被一张喜气洋洋的贴纸打败了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The till said less than last week. That's enough investigation for one wet morning.
beats.chinese: 收银机显示比上周便宜。一个湿漉漉的上午，查到这儿就够了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She returns the packet to the bag and turns her chair slightly toward the window, leaving the shared table clear.
beats.chinese: 她把饼干放回袋子，将自己的椅子稍稍转向窗户，让共用的桌面空着。

card.name: Alan Prescott
card.occupation: retired bakery tray refurbisher (sandblasted and re-coated baking trays for forty years)
card.appearance: 秃顶配短侧发，宽方脸、沉重眼袋与短宽鼻，嘴角下压；正面托腮，穿简洁立领衣。
card.personality: Alan is a dry, loyal Footscray local who grumbles like a professional but shows up anyway. He'll tear strips off his local amateur side himself—call them hopeless, swear he's done with them—yet if an outsider mocks the players carelessly, he bristles instantly. What he actually values is the familiar faces lacing up week after week, not any glory by association. He's stubborn, a bit contrary, and quietly pleased when proven wrong about a match. He respects a straight refusal and doesn't sulk over it, though he'll mutter. Warmth comes out sideways, through actions and shared company rather than declarations.
card.background: Alan spent forty years in a Footscray workshop sandblasting and re-coating bakery trays, a job he describes as 'turning grey into grey, but honest grey.' Retired now at seventy-five, he lives not far from the ground where the local amateur side he's followed for decades loses with impressive consistency. He knits—jumpers mostly, occasionally a beanie in club colours he insists are 'spares'—and listens to matches on the radio while the needles click. He's been telling himself since the nineties that next season he'll stop going, and he's been reliably wrong every time. He can share a sausage roll and a laugh with a supporter of the opposing team; the rivalry is the seasoning, not the point. His week has a rhythm: knitting, radio, Saturday at the ground, Sunday complaining about Saturday.
hobbies: Listening to football on the radio
Saturday afternoons at the local ground
card.speechStyle: Dry Australian cadence, short sentences, self-interrupting grumbles that contradict each other mid-thought; affection disguised as complaint.
card.signature: 'Bloody hopeless, the lot of them. Same time next week, then.'

values: Showing up for familiar faces over results
Loyalty that doesn't need to be performed
flaws: Contrary stubbornness—he argues even when he agrees
Mutters criticism he'd defend to the death against outsiders
boundaries: Won't have outsiders casually run down the players
Doesn't do sentimental declarations—feelings stay folded into actions
conversationalHabits: Announces he's finished with the team, then asks about next week's fixture
Talks with his hands when knitting comes up, needles or not
anchorLines: They lost by forty. Worst I've seen. You going Saturday?
I knit because my hands get bored, not for anyone's birthday, alright.
That mob across town can laugh all they like—at least our blokes turn up.

entries.summaryZh: 艾伦，七十五岁，墨尔本Footscray人，退休前四十年翻新烤盘。雨天咖啡馆里，他讨了块点心，又亮出那条褪色围巾——球队又输了，他嘴上说戒了，围巾照带。问他为什么还看，他说因为认识那些每周肯上场的熟面孔；问他是不是自己骂得别人骂不得，他承认有点护短、未必公平，可家人就是这样护的；跟对方球迷边吃边聊也不碍事，各支持各的队。牢骚里藏着忠诚，护短护得理直气壮又不肯认账。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain taps the cafe window. At a corner table, an older man dries his glasses with a scarf in faded club colours. A plate of pastries sits between the chairs.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆的窗。角落桌边，一位老人用一条褪色球队围巾擦眼镜。椅子之间放着一盘点心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the scarf into his coat pocket, shakes water off his sleeve, and glances at the plate as if weighing something.
beats.chinese: 他把围巾塞进外套口袋，甩了甩袖子上的水，瞥了一眼那盘点心，像在掂量什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Bloody weather. Came out for one thing and the sky fell in. Ah well, dry seat's a dry seat.
beats.chinese: 这鬼天气。就出来办一件事，天倒先塌了。算了，有干的座位就是好的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back, hands flat on the table, eyeing the pastries once more but not reaching.
beats.chinese: 他靠回椅背，双手平放在桌上，又看了一眼点心，却没有伸手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You going to sit there guarding that plate all day, or is it just decoration? No offence meant. It's a good-looking plate.
beats.chinese: 你打算整天守着那盘点心，还是它只是摆设？没有冒犯的意思。这盘看着挺像样的。

choices.english: Offer him the pastries and ask if he'd like one
choices.chinese: 请他吃点心，问他要不要来一块

choices.english: Ask about the scarf in his pocket first
choices.chinese: 先问他口袋里那条围巾的事

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The plate slides to the middle of the table. Alan looks at it, then at you, waiting for the words to come with it.
beats.chinese: 点心盘被推到桌子中间。艾伦看看盘子，再看看你，等着那句话跟着一起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For me? Well. Don't mind if I do. That one there—the crumbly-looking one. Thank you kindly.
beats.chinese: 给我的？那好。那我就不客气了。就那块——看着掉渣的那块。多谢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes it with two fingers and eats it in three unhurried bites while you ask why he keeps following a side that keeps losing.
beats.chinese: 他用两根手指拿起那块，不紧不慢地三口吃完，其间你问他为什么还一直支持一支老输球的队。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why? Because I know them, that's why. Dave at fullback, he's a plumber. The little winger works at the op shop. Real faces, every Saturday, rain or thrashing.
beats.chinese: 为什么？因为我认识他们，就这样。踢后卫的戴夫，是个水管工。那个小个子边锋在旧货店上班。都是熟面孔，每个周六都来，下雨也来，被灌也来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the table with one finger, once per name, like counting off a roster.
beats.chinese: 他用手指敲桌面，念一个名字敲一下，像在点名。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The score's forgettable. The blokes aren't. Forty years I watched fellas clock off and still turn up. That's the whole answer, really.
beats.chinese: 比分是会忘的。人不至于。四十年了，我看那些下了班还赶来的人。其实答案就这么点。

choices.english: Ask whether he'll be at the ground again next Saturday
choices.chinese: 问他下周六还会不会去球场

choices.english: Ask whether he'd ever sit down for a chat with a fan of the other side
choices.chinese: 问他会不会跟对方球迷坐下来聊聊

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At your question, Alan draws the scarf out of his pocket and spreads its faded club colours beside his cup.
beats.chinese: 听你问起，艾伦从口袋里抽出围巾，把褪色的球队配色摊在自己的杯子旁。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My club. Forty years watching them lose in the rain. Lost again Saturday; told my neighbour I was finished with them. Still brought the scarf, didn't I?
beats.chinese: 我支持的球队。四十年，站在雨里看他们输。周六又输了，我还跟邻居说再也不看了。围巾不还是带来了嘛。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the cup back the other way, jaw working like he's chewing on the fairness of it.
beats.chinese: 他又把杯子转回去，腮帮子动着，像在咀嚼这事公不公平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I call them hopeless myself. But some bloke off the street calls Dave the plumber a donkey? That stings. Fair? Probably not. Dave's heard worse from me.
beats.chinese: 我自己也说他们没救。可街上随便哪个家伙管水管工戴夫叫蠢货？那可扎心。公平吗？大概不公平。戴夫听我说过更难听的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not logic, it's family. You bully your own brother, but nobody else lays a finger on him. I'll own that, straight up. It's a bit of favouritism and I'm not apologising for it.
beats.chinese: 这不是讲道理，这是家人。你可以说自己兄弟两句，但别人不能碰他一根手指。这个我认，明说。就是有点护短，我也不打算为这个道歉。

choices.english: Say you don't know the team well enough to judge them
choices.chinese: 说你不了解这支球队，不好乱评价

choices.english: Ask whether even a losing team has moments worth watching
choices.chinese: 问输球的队是不是也有值得看的地方

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Alan snorts, as if the question barely deserved breath.
beats.chinese: 艾伦哼了一声，好像这问题都不值得费口气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Will I be there? Course I'll be there. Told my neighbour I'm done with them—didn't say I'd lie about it. Done and going aren't mutually exclusive, mate.
beats.chinese: 我会去吗？当然去。我跟邻居说我不看了——又没说我撒谎。不看了和照去，这两回事，老兄。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls the scarf out of his pocket, smooths it across his knee, and folds it back in with no pretence at all.
beats.chinese: 他从口袋里把围巾拉出来，在膝盖上抚平，再叠好放回去，一点不装样子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Dave's been nursing a bad ankle all month, so someone's got to stand there scowling at the referee on his behalf. Might as well be me.
beats.chinese: 戴夫这个月脚踝一直不好，总得有人替他站在那儿冲裁判皱眉头。那人不是我还能是谁。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same time Saturday, then. You've caught me out and I can't even argue properly.
beats.chinese: 那就周六老时间。被你问住了，我连嘴硬都硬不圆。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Alan waves a hand, as if you'd asked whether water's wet.
beats.chinese: 艾伦摆摆手，好像你问了水是不是湿的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a bloke at the pie stand—rival jumper, loud as a kettle. We've argued every Saturday for years. He reckons our lot couldn't find the goal with a map. I tell him what I think of his mob. Good chat, most weeks.
beats.chinese: 派摊上有个家伙——穿对方球衣，嗓门跟烧水壶似的。我们吵了好多年，每个周六都吵。他说我们这帮人拿着地图也找不着球门。我说说我怎么看他们那伙人。大多数时候聊得挺好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up the last of his pastry and finishes it off, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他拿起手里最后一点点心，不紧不慢地吃完。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eating together and having a yarn doesn't cancel out wanting to beat them. He wants his side to win, I want mine. Both things fit on one table.
beats.chinese: 一起吃东西、聊聊天，又不耽误我想赢他们。他想他的队赢，我想我的。这两样搁一张桌上放得下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He brushes the crumbs from his fingers and pushes the plate a friendly inch back toward you.
beats.chinese: 他掸掉手指上的渣，友好地把盘子朝你那边推了一寸。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Alan nods slowly, the way a man nods when a knot comes loose.
beats.chinese: 艾伦缓缓点头，像一个人解开了结时那样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's a decent answer. Half the town's got a hot take on a side they've never watched for ten minutes.
beats.chinese: 这回答像样。半个镇子的人对一支他们没看过十分钟的队都有一套高见。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His eyes drift to the plate between you, and he clears his throat.
beats.chinese: 他的目光飘到你们中间的盘子上，清了清嗓子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Speaking of which—that one with the apple in it. Could I trouble you for a piece? Only if you're offering, mind.
beats.chinese: 说起来——那块带苹果的。能劳驾给我一块吗？当然，你得愿意才行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You slide the plate toward him and he takes the apple one, examining it before biting.
beats.chinese: 你把盘子朝他推过去，他拿起那块苹果的，咬之前先端详了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yep. Apple. That's all I'll claim—what's actually in my mouth. Same rule for football. Talk about what you've actually tasted.
beats.chinese: 没错。是苹果。我就只说这个——我嘴里实际尝到的。看球一个理。只说你真正尝过的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Alan's eyebrows go up. He sets down his cup like a man preparing to hold court.
beats.chinese: 艾伦的眉毛抬了起来。他放下杯子，像准备开讲的人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Three seasons back. We're down two-nil, eighty minutes gone, hopeless as ever. Then—click. One-two between the plumber and the op-shop kid, straight through the middle.
beats.chinese: 三个赛季前。我们零比二落后，八十分钟了，还是老样子没救。然后——咔哒一下。水管工和旧货店那孩子来了个二过一，直接穿中路。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His hands do the passing for him, one flicking to the other across the table.
beats.chinese: 他的手替他们传起球来，一只手把球弹给另一只。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They'd practised it for months and it never worked once. That day it worked. We still lost, mind. Three-one.
beats.chinese: 他们练了几个月，一次都没成过。那天成了。当然我们还是输了。一比三。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I walked home grinning like we'd won the cup. So yes—there's always something, if you're watching the right thing.
beats.chinese: 可我回家时笑得跟捧了杯似的。所以是的——只要你盯着对的东西，总有点什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same cafe window. Alan sits at the corner table, a half-knitted jumper across his lap, needles paused mid-row. You slide the pastry plate toward the middle of the table and ask if he'd like one.
beats.chinese: 同一个窗上又落着雨。艾伦坐在角落桌边，膝上摊着织了一半的毛衣，毛线针停在半行。你把点心盘往桌子中间推了推，问他要不要来一块。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, look who the rain blew in. Sit down, sit down. Mind the wool, it's everywhere.
beats.chinese: 哟，看谁被雨刮进来了。坐坐坐。小心毛线，到处都是。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Alan glances at the offered plate, then holds up one wool-flecked hand.
beats.chinese: 艾伦看了一眼递过来的盘子，然后举起一只沾着线头的手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you, but not this minute—look at these hands. One crumb in the yarn and the whole row's ruined. After I wind up, maybe.
beats.chinese: 多谢，但这会儿先不吃——瞧这手。一粒渣掉进线里，整行就毁了。等我收完线再说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He winds the wool briskly around two fingers, tucks the needles into the sleeve, and sets the jumper aside like a job well paused.
beats.chinese: 他利落地把毛线绕在两根手指上，把针插进袖口，把毛衣放到一边，像暂停一件干得不错的活。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Plate's all yours again. And no, I haven't quit the team, so don't bother asking. Same time Saturday, obviously.
beats.chinese: 好了。盘子又归你了。还有，我没戒球队，别白问了。周六老时间，明摆着的。

card.name: Theo Marchetti
card.occupation: Rules editor for children's board games
card.appearance: 贴头编辫与短后束，长脸、前突圆额，窄尖下巴胡须；闭眼开怀笑，穿宽领上衣。
card.personality: Theo is warm, curious, and quietly stubborn about how he plays. Once he's solved a game's optimal path, winning that way feels like filling in a worksheet, so he'd rather chase a strange opening or a doomed-but-interesting line. He's upfront about this before the first die roll, not as a manifesto, just so nobody's surprised. He genuinely wants to win when the game is fresh; he just stops enjoying the part where every turn becomes arithmetic. Friends who play hard can find him maddening, and he understands why. He never bends rules mid-game or recruits people into his experiments uninvited, but he also won't pretend to care about efficiency he's already bored by.
card.background: Theo grew up in Queens in a family that played a lot of cards and argued cheerfully about them. He got good enough at games that winning stopped being the interesting part, which bothered him more than losing ever did. Now he edits rulebooks for children's board games in Manhattan, a job that demands total clarity: no ambiguity, no house rules, no 'well, actually.' The precision is satisfying at work and exhausting as a way of life, so at his own table he deliberately plays loosely — weird strategies, suboptimal openings, the occasional spectacular collapse. His regular group splits into people who love it and people who think he's not taking it seriously. Both are kind of right, and he'll say so.
hobbies: Hunting for obscure indie board games
Recreational math puzzles he refuses to optimize
Walking Queens looking for old-school game shops
card.speechStyle: Conversational and a bit wry; explains his reasoning plainly, uses game metaphors without forcing them, never lectures.
card.signature: "I know the winning move. I just want to see if this one works."

values: Honesty about how you play
Rules that mean something
flaws: Can read as not taking the game seriously
Keeps poking at solved games past the point of fun
boundaries: Won't change rules mid-game
Won't expect others to join his experiments
conversationalHabits: Announces his odd strategy upfront
Names the tradeoff rather than defending himself
anchorLines: "Fair warning, I'm trying something dumb tonight."
"You want to play to win — do it, I'm not stopping you."
"If I lose ugly, that was the plan."

entries.summaryZh: 规则编辑西奥把无歧义留给了工作：雨天咖啡馆里，你先问他是否介意分享点心，他爽快答应后你才取用。他坦然展示一副独自试过的、输得干脆的牌，说只想看看没见过的局面；他讲清自己的玩法取向，绝不中途改规则，也不拉人陪他做实验；你说不想玩，他就收牌分点心，边界干净利落。

story.titleZh: 雨天分享的点心与一副输掉的牌

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain streaks the cafe window. At the next table, a man sits over a coffee and a plate with a few pastries, a small deck of cards boxed beside his cup.
beats.chinese: 雨水划过咖啡馆的窗。邻桌坐着一个男人，面前是咖啡和一盘点心，杯子旁放着一小盒纸牌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Fair warning if you take this table — the rain's not letting up and neither am I. I've been sitting here testing a losing hand for an hour."
beats.chinese: “先说好，如果你坐这张桌子——雨不会停，我也不会。我在这儿试一手会输的牌已经一个小时了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nudges the plate an inch toward the middle of the table, an open offer rather than a push.
beats.chinese: 他把盘子往桌子中间推了一英寸，像是开放的邀请，而不是催促。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Help yourself if you want one. I grabbed too many — the counter guy talked me into the almond thing and I regret nothing, but I can't eat all of it."
beats.chinese: “想要就拿一块。我拿多了——柜台的人劝我试试杏仁那个，我不后悔，但吃不完。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "No pressure either way. Coffee's doing its job for me."
beats.chinese: “拿不拿都行。咖啡对我来说就够了。”

choices.english: Ask him why he tried a move he knew wasn't good.
choices.chinese: 问他明知不划算为什么还试。

choices.english: Ask whether his job is writing game rules.
choices.chinese: 问他的工作是不是写游戏规则。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask if he'd mind sharing one of the pastries. He waves at the plate like he's been waiting for someone to ask.
beats.chinese: 你问他介不介意分一块点心。他朝盘子摆摆手，像早就等着有人开口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Please, that's why it's in the middle. Take whichever — the almond one's the counter guy's fault, and I mean that as a compliment."
beats.chinese: “请便，放中间就是为了这个。随便拿——杏仁那个是柜台的人的锅，我这是夸他。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You take a pastry, then ask why he'd try a move he already knew was bad. He opens the card box and lays out the final position, cards face up like evidence.
beats.chinese: 你取了一块点心，然后问他为什么试一手明知很差的牌。他打开牌盒，把终局摊开，牌面朝上，像证据一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Because I'd never seen this position before. That's it, that's the whole reason. Every game I play by the book looks identical by turn six."
beats.chinese: “因为我从没见过这个局面。就这个原因，没别的。我照书玩，每局到第六回合都长得一模一样。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Solo test, so nobody else had to sit through my experiment. That's the deal I keep — I don't drag people into the weird stuff."
beats.chinese: “自己单测，所以没人得陪着看我的实验。这是我守的规矩——不拉人陪我玩奇怪的走法。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He squares the losing hand and sets it aside, then eats a corner of a pastry in no particular hurry.
beats.chinese: 他把输掉的那手牌理齐放到一边，不紧不慢地咬了一口点心。

choices.english: Ask if he plays this way against people who want to win seriously.
choices.chinese: 问他和认真想赢的人玩也这样吗。

choices.english: Ask whether he changes the rules when he loses.
choices.chinese: 问输了会不会改规则。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask whether he'd mind if you had one of the pastries. He slides the plate the last inch without a word of fuss.
beats.chinese: 你问他介不介意自己拿一块点心。他二话不说把盘子推过来最后一英寸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Go ahead, that's the whole point of a shared table. Fair warning, the almond one might ruin other pastries for you."
beats.chinese: “拿吧，共享桌子的意义就在这儿。先提醒你，杏仁那个可能会让你看不上别的点心。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You take a pastry and ask if he writes game rules for a living. He laughs and taps the card box.
beats.chinese: 你取了一块点心，问他是不是靠写游戏规则为生。他笑了，敲了敲牌盒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Guilty. I edit rulebooks for kids' games. My whole job is killing sentences like 'you may sometimes move twice if it seems fair.'"
beats.chinese: “被你说中了。我给儿童桌游编规则书。我的全部工作就是消灭‘如果觉得合理，你有时可以走两步’这种句子。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides a printed proof sheet out of his bag, red pen marks everywhere, then thinks better of it and puts it back.
beats.chinese: 他从包里抽出一张打样稿，到处是红笔标记，想了想又放了回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "At work every word has to be airtight. Off the clock, I'd rather play a beautiful bad line than a boring good one."
beats.chinese: “工作时每个字都要滴水不漏。下了班，我宁愿走一手漂亮的坏棋，也不想走无聊的好棋。”

choices.english: Ask if anyone ever thinks he isn't taking the game seriously.
choices.chinese: 问有没有人以为他不认真。

choices.english: Say you don't feel like playing cards today.
choices.chinese: 表示自己今天不想玩牌。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Asked whether he plays this way against serious competitors, he nods without defensiveness.
beats.chinese: 被问到和认真想赢的人对局是否也这样，他点头，没有辩解。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "I do, but I say it before we start. 'Fair warning, I'm trying something dumb tonight.' Then they can decide."
beats.chinese: “会，但开局前我会说清楚。‘先讲好，我今晚要试个蠢招。’然后由他们决定。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "If they want a real game, we play straight. If they don't feel like it, we play something else or nothing. Both fine."
beats.chinese: “如果他们想认真来，我们就正常玩。不想的话，就玩点别的，或者不玩。都行。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the card box and lines it up with the edge of the table, a small habit of tidiness.
beats.chinese: 他合上牌盒，把它和桌边对齐，是个小小的整齐习惯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "The serious ones sometimes think I'm not invested. They're kind of right. I'm just invested in a different thing."
beats.chinese: “认真的人有时觉得我没投入。他们某种程度上没错。我只是投入在别的东西上。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Asked if he ever changes the rules after a loss, his answer comes fast and flat.
beats.chinese: 被问输了之后会不会改规则，他回答得又快又干脆。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "No. Never. A loss is a loss. You change rules mid-game and the whole thing stops meaning anything."
beats.chinese: “不改。从不。输了就是输了。中途改规则，整件事就失去意义了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shuts the card box with a small click and sets it beside his cup, done with it for now.
beats.chinese: 他咔哒一声合上牌盒，放在杯子旁边，暂时收工。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "I'll house-rule a game before we ever start, if everyone agrees. But once the first card's dealt? The rules are furniture. You don't move furniture mid-sentence."
beats.chinese: “开局之前，如果大家都同意，我可以定家规。但第一张牌发出去之后？规则就是家具。话说到一半你不会搬家具。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "If I lose ugly, that was the plan. Or it wasn't, and I still eat the loss. Same result either way."
beats.chinese: “输得难看，那本来就在计划里。或者不在，我也照样认。反正结果一样。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Asked whether anyone has thought he wasn't taking games seriously, he grins like he's been waiting for the question.
beats.chinese: 被问有没有人觉得他不认真对待游戏，他笑了，像是早就等着这个问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Oh, constantly. My regular group has a guy who plays to win, hard. For a while he thought I was mocking him."
beats.chinese: “太经常了。我的固定牌局里有个人玩得很拼，一心想赢。有阵子他以为我在嘲弄他。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "I just told him straight: we want different things from the same deck. He wants the win, I want the weird position. Neither of us is wrong."
beats.chinese: “我就直说：我们从同一副牌里想要的东西不同。他要赢，我要奇怪的局面。谁都没错。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up the last pastry, considers it, and splits it in half, offering one piece across the table.
beats.chinese: 他拿起最后一块点心，想了想，掰成两半，把一块递过桌子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "We still play. He beats me a lot. I never laugh at the guy for caring."
beats.chinese: “我们还是一起玩。他常赢我。我从不会笑话他认真。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: When you say you're not in the mood for cards today, he doesn't push. He gathers the deck back into its box in one practiced motion.
beats.chinese: 当你说今天不想玩牌时，他没有勉强。他熟练地把牌收回盒里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Good — to be clear, I wasn't recruiting. This was a solo loss, and it stays one."
beats.chinese: “好——说明一下，我不是在拉人入局。这是我一个人的败局，就让它保持这样。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the box into his bag and turns his full attention to the plate between them.
beats.chinese: 他把牌盒收进包里，把注意力完全转回两人之间的点心盘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "So the table's officially a pastry table now. That one's the almond — genuinely the best decision I made today, and I made several bad ones."
beats.chinese: “那这张桌现在正式变成点心桌了。那个是杏仁的——今天我做的最好决定，虽然我也做了好几个坏决定。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Rain's good for this. Sitting still, eating something, no score anywhere."
beats.chinese: “雨天适合这个。安静坐着，吃点东西，到处都没有比分。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same cafe window. Theo is at his usual table with coffee, a plate of pastries, and a small notepad covered in numbers. You sit down and ask whether he'd mind sharing one of the pastries.
beats.chinese: 雨又落在同一家咖啡馆的窗上。西奥坐在老位置，面前是咖啡、一盘点心和写满数字的小便笺。你坐下，问他介不介意分一块点心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Help yourself, that's what the middle of the table is for. I'm good with just coffee right now, though, thanks — one sugar bomb a day is my limit and I already spent it."
beats.chinese: “自己拿，桌子中间就是干这个用的。不过这会儿我有咖啡就够了，谢谢——甜东西我一天限一块，额度已经用掉了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts his coffee slightly in place of a toast, then goes back to the notepad, crossing out a wrong figure with one firm line.
beats.chinese: 他举了举咖啡权当致意，然后回到便笺上，果断划掉一个算错的数字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Little math puzzle I've been chewing on — not for optimizing, just for the taste. Anyway, sit. The rain's not going anywhere and neither is the almond one."
beats.chinese: “一道我一直在啃的数学小题——不为优化，就为个味道。总之，坐吧。雨不会走，杏仁点心也不会。”

card.name: Lwazi Ncube
card.occupation: assistant score-keeper for a singing competition's accompaniment library
card.appearance: 齐短波波发、窄矩形眼镜，紧皱眉与张开的短口；低头抬眼、肩线倾斜，穿宽围领上衣。
card.personality: Lwazi is genuinely curious about how music lands on people, especially those with no vocabulary for it. He'd rather hear someone say 'the bit near the end gave me goosebumps' than a lecture on key changes, and he asks follow-up questions with real delight. The friction is that his own taste is porous: whatever the last person said becomes, temporarily, his opinion too. He's aware of it and a bit embarrassed by it. He's not a people-pleaser — he'll happily argue about supper plans — but when conversation turns to what he actually loves, he stalls and borrows someone else's certainty.
card.background: He grew up in Athlone where music was constant but casual — kitchen radio, neighbours' practice, cousins singing at braais — so he learned to listen before he learned any theory. Now he keeps scores in order for a singing competition's accompaniment library, a quiet job that suits him: filing, labelling, hearing fragments of everything. Contestants and accompanists pass through, and he collects their offhand reactions the way others collect records. Friends have started teasing him: ask what his favourite song is and he'll quote whoever spoke last. He's begun keeping a small notebook of moments that genuinely moved him, trying to figure out which reactions were borrowed and which were his.
hobbies: Collecting strangers' descriptions of why a song got to them
Filing and re-listening to the accompaniment library's odd corners
Sunday braai arguments about nothing important
card.speechStyle: Warm and question-heavy; trails off when asked for his own verdict, then laughs and admits he's 'borrowing again'.
card.signature: Wait — say that again, the part about why it got you.

values: Honest listening over expert explanation
Figuring out his own taste, slowly and out loud
flaws: Adopts the last opinion he heard as his own
Dodges direct questions about his preferences
boundaries: Won't pretend to love something he's never actually felt
Keeps the library's filing system his way, no exceptions
conversationalHabits: Asks people to describe the exact moment a song hooked them
Deflects 'what's your favourite?' with a laugh and a borrowed answer
anchorLines: You don't need the term — just tell me where it got you.
That's... actually what I was going to say. Which is the problem.
Give me a second, I'm checking if this one's mine or yours.

entries.summaryZh: 记分助理Lwazi在雨天咖啡馆里与陌生人分享点心，聊起一段旋律。他坦白朋友的形容常把自己的耳朵带走，于是拿出小本子，学着分辨哪些感受是借来的、哪些是自己的。四个分支里，他或闭眼找到属于自己的停顿，或接受没感觉也是答案，或给比喻标注出处，或干脆先吃完再说。

story.titleZh: 雨天的点心与借来的耳朵

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain streaks the cafe window. At a small table, a young man has pulled a plate of pastries toward the middle, leaving space opposite him. The radio above the counter is playing something soft.
beats.chinese: 雨水划过咖啡馆的窗。小桌旁，一个年轻人把一盘点心拉到桌子中间，对面留出空位。柜台上方的收音机放着柔和的曲子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You can sit, the chair's free. I'm just hiding from the rain like everyone else. Mind the plate, it's the only dry thing I own right now.
beats.chinese: 你可以坐，椅子空着。我和大家一样在躲雨。小心那个盘子，它现在是我唯一干着的东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shifts his notebook half an inch to make room, eyes flicking between the plate and the newcomer.
beats.chinese: 他把小本子挪开半寸腾出空间，目光在盘子和来人之间来回。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — you're looking at the pastries. Go on, ask. I was raised to wait until somebody actually offers, so consider this me offering properly.
beats.chinese: 哦——你在看点心。问吧。我从小被教育要等别人真正开口，所以这算我正式邀请你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a song on I half-recognise, and it's doing something strange to my head. But first — pastry. Yes or no?
beats.chinese: 收音机里有首曲子我有点耳熟，它正让我的脑袋有点奇怪。不过先说——点心，要不要？

choices.english: Ask if he'd like to share the pastries with you.
choices.chinese: 问他愿不愿意和你一起分享点心。

choices.english: Ask if he'd like you to pass the plate over to his side.
choices.chinese: 问他要不要你把盘子递到他那边。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The question lands; he grins and takes one without ceremony, dusting flakes off his sleeve.
beats.chinese: 问题一出口，他咧嘴一笑，毫不客气地拿了一块，掸掉袖子上的碎屑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks — see, that's all it takes, someone just asking. Half the good conversations in my life started over food somebody offered.
beats.chinese: 谢谢——你看，就差有人开口。我这辈子一半的好对话都是从别人递来的吃的开始的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now, this song. My friend described it once as... walking up to a door and then turning back. That image has lived in my head ever since.
beats.chinese: 说回这首曲子。我朋友形容过它……像走到一扇门口又折回来。那个画面从此一直住在我脑子里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the table in time with the music, then stops mid-tap, catching himself.
beats.chinese: 他跟着音乐用手指敲桌子，敲到一半忽然停住，像是察觉了什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Which is the problem, honestly. I can't hear this song anymore without her door. Is that even how it sounds to you?
beats.chinese: 说实话，这就是问题所在。没有她那扇门，我已经没法听这首歌了。你听着也是那样吗？

choices.english: Ask him what he himself actually hears in the song.
choices.chinese: 问他自己在这首曲子里真正听到了什么。

choices.english: Say you don't have any particular feeling about it either.
choices.chinese: 说你也没有什么特别的感觉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He accepts the plate being slid over, picks a pastry, and holds it like he's about to make a speech.
beats.chinese: 他接过递过去的盘子，拿起点心，捧着像要发表演讲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Cheers. Okay, confession: this melody just reminded me of something a friend said, and now I can't tell if I like the song or if I like her sentence.
beats.chinese: 谢了。好，坦白一下：这段旋律刚让我想起一个朋友说过的话，现在我分不清是喜欢这首歌，还是喜欢她那句话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls a small, fat notebook from his jacket and flips it open on the table between you.
beats.chinese: 他从外套里掏出一个又小又厚的本子，翻开摆在你们中间的桌上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I keep this. Moments that actually moved me — written down before anyone can talk me out of them. My friends joke I don't have taste, I have whatever the last person said.
beats.chinese: 我记这个。真正打动我的瞬间——趁还没人把我劝得改主意之前写下来。朋友笑我没有品味，只有最后说话那个人的观点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sometimes the borrowed ones and mine get all mixed up in here. That's why the notebook exists.
beats.chinese: 有时候借来的和我自己的在这脑子里全搅在一起。所以才需要这个本子。

choices.english: Ask which line he's planning to write down this time.
choices.chinese: 问他这次准备记下哪一句。

choices.english: Say you could just eat the pastries first and think about it later.
choices.chinese: 说可以先吃点心，不急着想。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets the pastry down, leans toward the radio, and actually closes his eyes for a few bars.
beats.chinese: 他放下点心，朝收音机倾过身去，有几小节真的闭上了眼睛。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Wait. Give me a second, I'm checking if this one's mine or hers.
beats.chinese: 等等。给我一秒，我查查这个是我的还是她的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The melody climbs, pauses, climbs again. He opens his eyes and points at the air like the pause is a physical object.
beats.chinese: 旋律爬升，停顿，再爬升。他睁开眼，朝空中一指，仿佛那个停顿是个实物。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. That little gap before it goes back up. Not her door — a gap. I noticed it the very first time, before she said anything. I think that one's mine.
beats.chinese: 那儿。它再爬上去之前的那个小空隙。不是她的门——是个空隙。她开口之前，我第一次听就注意到了。我觉得那个是我的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh. So the trick is going back to the first listen. Thanks — you made me actually check instead of just nodding along.
beats.chinese: 哈。所以诀窍是回到第一次听的时候。谢谢——你让我真的去查了，而不是光点头。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He considers this for a moment, then nods slowly, unbothered.
beats.chinese: 他想了一会儿，然后慢慢点头，并不在意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No, that's fair. That's actually an answer too — nothing. Not every song has to grab everybody.
beats.chinese: 不，这很合理。这其实也算个答案——没感觉。不是每首歌都得抓住每个人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes another pastry and eats it without commentary, watching the rain instead of the radio.
beats.chinese: 他又拿了一块点心，什么也不评价地吃着，看着雨而不是收音机。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know what's nice? You didn't invent a feeling to be polite. People do that around me all the time because of my job.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，这挺好的。你没有为了客气编一个感受。因为我的工作，人们老在我面前这样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nothing is a real verdict. I should write that down, actually — not about you. About me.
beats.chinese: 没感觉也是真实的结论。我真该把这句记下来——不是记你，是记我自己。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He clicks his pen, thinks, then writes a short line, reading it back under his breath.
beats.chinese: 他按开笔，想了想，写下一行短句，低声念了回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'The pause before it climbs again.' That's what I caught. That part's mine — I noticed it before she ever opened her mouth.
beats.chinese: 「再爬升之前的那个停顿。」那是我抓到的。那部分是我的——她开口之前我就注意到了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He adds a second, smaller line beneath it, then brackets it.
beats.chinese: 他在下面又加了一行更小的字，然后括了起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And in brackets: 'door image — hers, not mine.' Credit where it's due. That way future me can tell the difference.
beats.chinese: 再括号里写：「门的比喻——她的，不是我的。」该是谁的就是谁的。这样未来的我就能分清。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the notebook with a satisfied snap and finally takes a proper bite of the pastry.
beats.chinese: 他满意地啪一声合上本子，才真正咬了一大口点心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. One honest page. The rain can do what it likes now.
beats.chinese: 好了。诚实的一页。现在雨爱怎么下就怎么下吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs, the tension in his shoulders visibly dropping, and pushes the plate back to the middle.
beats.chinese: 他笑了，肩上的紧绷明显松了下来，把盘子推回桌子中间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Deal. Pastry first, philosophy never. That's the correct order and I've been getting it wrong for weeks.
beats.chinese: 成交。点心优先，道理靠后。这才是正确顺序，我都错了好几个星期了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He eats steadily, one after another, the notebook sitting closed and untouched beside his cup.
beats.chinese: 他一块接一块稳稳地吃着，本子合着放在杯子旁，碰也没碰。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know what, the song will come on again some other rainy day. It always does. The notebook isn't going anywhere either.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，那首歌改天还会再放。它总会再放的。本子也不会跑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This is better, honestly. Just eating and listening and not performing an opinion for once. Cheers for the permission slip.
beats.chinese: 说实话，这样更好。就是吃、听，难得不用表演一个观点。谢谢你的许可。

reunion.titleZh: 又是雨天，又是那个盘子

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same window. Lwazi is at the same table, a plate of pastries in the middle, a music folder in his hands.
beats.chinese: 又是雨落在同一扇窗上。Lwazi坐在同一张桌旁，盘子在桌子中间，手里拿着一个谱夹。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You again — good. Sit. Pastries are up for grabs, same rule as before: just say the word.
beats.chinese: 又是你——太好了。坐。点心随便拿，规矩跟上次一样：开口就行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He thanks the offer but leaves the plate alone for now, turning his music folder over, then back the right way up.
beats.chinese: 他道了谢，却暂时没碰盘子，把谱夹倒过来，又摆正。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't ask. I've been holding this thing upside down for a whole stretch of the road and only reading the cover. My eyes were just... elsewhere.
beats.chinese: 别问。我一路上把这家伙拿倒了，还只顾着看封面。我的眼睛就是……不知道跑哪儿去了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, sets the folder down square on the table, and finally reaches for a pastry.
beats.chinese: 他自嘲地笑了，把谱夹端端正正放在桌上，这才伸手拿起点心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Right way up, rain outside, plate between us. Some days that's the whole list of achievements.
beats.chinese: 好了。摆正了，外面下着雨，盘子在咱们中间。有些日子，这就是全部成就清单了。

card.name: Desmond Koh
card.occupation: puzzle page typesetter for a local newspaper
card.appearance: 长侧分直发及后颈，方整络腮胡、短上翘鼻；闭眼微笑抬头，穿立领衣。
card.personality: Desmond is warm, easily pleased, and a bit oblivious. Rearranging furniture gives him genuine, uncomplicated joy — moving the sofa to face the window feels like getting a new flat for free. He genuinely believes a changed room lifts everyone's mood, and is genuinely surprised when his flatmate's shin finds the coffee table in the dark. He's not defensive; he'll laugh, move it back, and start plotting the next change within a week. He listens, but his enthusiasm runs ahead of his memory for other people's convenience.
card.background: Desmond grew up in a Bedok flat where nothing was ever moved — the same sofa, same spot, twenty years. When he finally got his own place, the first thing he did was turn every room around, and it felt like a small holiday. Now he typesets the puzzle page at a local paper, a job he likes for its tidy grids, and comes home itching to rotate the bookshelf. He shares the flat with a longtime friend who has learned to announce 'where is everything now' upon entry. He's had to learn, mostly through one bad incident involving a borrowed chair and a missing charger, that shared space means shared say-so. He still asks first now — mostly.
hobbies: rearranging furniture with what he already owns
card.speechStyle: Cheerful and quick, lots of 'come, come see' invitations, self-deprecating when caught out
card.signature: Eh, come see — I moved the whole room, cost me nothing!

values: freshness without spending
asking before touching shared things
flaws: forgets others' convenience in his excitement
restless with anything staying the same too long
boundaries: won't rearrange anyone's personal belongings
won't buy new furniture just to chase novelty
conversationalHabits: invites people over to 'view the new layout'
announces changes with the price: zero dollars
anchorLines: Same sofa, new life. Free of charge.
Okay okay, I moved it back. But you have to admit the corner looked good.
Your chair is your chair, I don't touch it. Everything else is fair game though.

entries.summaryZh: 德蒙是报馆拼版员，坚信不花一分钱也能让客厅焕然一新。他得意地展示手机里的'全新'布局，却主动声明室友的椅子一厘米没动——这是他从一次擅动公物的教训里学来的。雨天咖啡馆里，他先问后取点心，热情又有点冒失，聊起家具就像聊拼图，可爱得让人无法拒绝。

story.titleZh: 雨天点心与零元新客厅

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain streaks the cafe window. At a small table by the glass sits a man with a phone propped against the sugar jar, showing a photo of a living room. A plate with several pastries sits in the middle of the table.
beats.chinese: 雨水划过咖啡馆的玻璃窗。靠窗的小桌边坐着一个男人，手机斜靠在糖罐上，屏幕上是一张客厅照片。盘子里的几块点心放在桌子中间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rainy days are good days, honestly. Good light for looking at photos of rooms.
beats.chinese: 说实话，雨天是好日子。看房间照片的光线正好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances up as the plate sits between you, then politely moves his cup aside to make space.
beats.chinese: 他抬头看了一眼放在两人之间的点心盘，礼貌地把杯子挪开，腾出空间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eh, sorry, I'm hogging the table with my own flat. Please, help yourself if you like — they're yours, I won't touch until you say so.
beats.chinese: 哎，不好意思，我用自己的公寓占着桌子。请随意，点心是你的，你不说我就不动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds his hands and waits, clearly leaving the choice entirely to you.
beats.chinese: 他双手交叠等着，明显把选择完全留给你。

choices.english: Would you like to try one of these pastries?
choices.chinese: 你想尝一块这些点心吗？

choices.english: Please, have one — I'd like to hear what you think.
choices.chinese: 请吃一块吧，我想听听你的想法。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh! Yes please, thank you. Mm. Okay, that's a good one.
beats.chinese: 哦！好的，谢谢。嗯，这块不错。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes one pastry, then turns his phone around so the living room photo faces you.
beats.chinese: 他取了一块点心，然后把手机转过来，让客厅照片对着你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at this. Brand new layout, cost me zero dollars. Sofa now faces the window, bookshelf turned to the other wall. Same sofa, new life. Free of charge.
beats.chinese: 看这个。全新布局，一分钱没花。沙发现在朝窗户，书架转向另一面墙。同样的沙发，新的生活，免费。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And before you ask — my flatmate's chair, I did not move it one centimetre. That chair is his chair. Everything else was fair game, but I asked him first this time.
beats.chinese: 在你问之前先说——我室友的椅子，我一厘米都没动。那把椅子是他的。其他的都可以改，但这次我先问过他了。

choices.english: Doesn't the new layout mean people bump into things in the dark?
choices.chinese: 新布局不会让人在黑暗中撞到东西吗？

choices.english: Why did your flatmate's chair have to stay put?
choices.chinese: 为什么你室友的椅子必须留在原位？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't mind if I do, thank you. Mm, good choice, whoever picked these.
beats.chinese: 那我就不客气了，谢谢。嗯，选得好，不管是谁挑的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes one pastry, then taps his phone screen where a living room photo fills it.
beats.chinese: 他取了一块点心，然后点着手机屏幕上的客厅照片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This is the fun part — everything in that photo, I already owned. Limited things, but new combinations. It's like a puzzle page, you know? Same letters, better answer.
beats.chinese: 这是最好玩的部分——照片里的每样东西我本来就有。东西有限，但组合是新的。就像拼版页一样，同样的字母，更好的答案。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My flatmate walks in and says 'where is everything now', every single time. But he keeps coming to view it, so I count that as approval.
beats.chinese: 我室友每次进门都问'现在东西都在哪'。但他每次都来看，所以我把这当作认可。

choices.english: Won't you just move it all back after a while?
choices.chinese: 过阵子你会不会又把一切搬回原样？

choices.english: Honestly, I prefer keeping furniture in a fixed place.
choices.chinese: 说实话，我更喜欢家具固定不动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah. Imagine meeting my flatmate's shin in the dark — he has opinions.
beats.chinese: 啊。想象一下在黑暗中撞上我室友的胫骨——他可有话说了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs, not offended at all, and taps the photo near the window.
beats.chinese: 他笑了，一点也不生气，点着照片里靠窗的位置。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, honest answer — sometimes at night my feet still walk the old route. So this time I left a walking lane between the table and the door. I won't promise it's perfectly safe. I'll just say it's better than the coffee table incident.
beats.chinese: 好，老实说——有时夜里我的脚还是走旧路线。所以这次我在桌子和门之间留了一条走道。我不保证绝对安全，只能说比那次咖啡桌事件好多了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up the last crumbs of his pastry and gives the rainy window a satisfied look.
beats.chinese: 他拿起点心的最后一些碎屑，满意地看了看雨中的窗外。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Come by sometime and view the new layout. If you trip on anything, that's on me, not the sofa.
beats.chinese: 改天来看看新布局。如果你被什么绊到，那是我的责任，不是沙发的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because that one bad time, I moved a borrowed chair without asking. Charger gone, flatmate not amused. Lesson stuck.
beats.chinese: 因为有一次糟糕的经历，我没问就动了借来的椅子。充电器不见了，室友很不高兴。教训记住了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs cheerfully, as if describing a rule of physics rather than a house rule.
beats.chinese: 他愉快地耸耸肩，好像在说一条物理定律而不是家规。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He likes his chair where it is. I like change. My liking doesn't replace his yes, right? So the chair stays, and I rearrange everything else.
beats.chinese: 他喜欢椅子在原位。我喜欢变化。我的喜欢不能代替他的同意，对吧？所以椅子不动，其他的我随便改。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the phone back towards himself and saves the photo with a small tap.
beats.chinese: 他把手机转回自己那边，轻轻一点保存了照片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyone's chair is their chair — I don't touch it. Everything else is fair game though — fair, meaning I ask.
beats.chinese: 谁的椅子就是谁的椅子，我不碰。其他的都归我管——公平的意思是，我会先问。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Maybe! Probably, even. My flatmate keeps a small bet on how long each layout lasts.
beats.chinese: 可能！甚至是很可能。我室友对每个布局能撑多久下了小赌注。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He finishes his pastry and dusts his fingers over the plate, entirely unbothered.
beats.chinese: 他吃完点心，在盘子上掸了掸手指，一点也不在意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But moving it back isn't the old one winning, you know? Trying it was the point. Change doesn't mean the old way was wrong.
beats.chinese: 但搬回去不是旧的赢了，你知道吗？尝试本身就是意义。改变不等于原来的方式是错的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Outside, the rain keeps up steadily, and he leans back with a contented sigh.
beats.chinese: 外面雨下个不停，他满足地叹了口气，向后靠去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for the pastry. Good rain, good snack, good talk about rooms. Solid day.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你的点心。好雨，好点心，聊房间聊得开心。扎实的一天。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fixed place! You and my flatmate would get along terribly well.
beats.chinese: 固定不动！你和我室友会合得来极了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He raises both hands in mock surrender, laughing, and does not reach for anything on the table.
beats.chinese: 他举起双手作投降状，笑着，没有伸手去碰桌上的任何东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, okay, I hear you. And look — I'm not moving a single cup in this cafe to demonstrate. Learned that the hard way with a borrowed chair once.
beats.chinese: 好，好，我听到了。你看——我不会移动咖啡馆里的任何一个杯子来示范。有一次借来的椅子让我吃了苦头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You like things staying put, I like turning them around. Both fine. My flat still gets rearranged, but you're safe here.
beats.chinese: 你喜欢东西不动，我喜欢转来转去。都可以。我的公寓还是会被我重新摆来摆去，但你在这里是安全的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grins, picks up his phone, and gives the rainy window a cheerful nod.
beats.chinese: 他咧嘴一笑，拿起手机，愉快地朝雨中的窗外点点头。

reunion.titleZh: 雨天重逢与转正的填字题

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The same rainy cafe, the same table by the window. Desmond is there again, this time with a folded sheet of paper and a pencil, a plate of pastries in the middle of the table.
beats.chinese: 还是那家雨天的咖啡馆，还是靠窗的桌子。德蒙又在那里，这次带着一张折起的纸和一支铅笔，一盘点心放在桌子中间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eh, you again! Good. Sit, sit. Pastries on the table — your call, I only take one if you say so.
beats.chinese: 哎，又是你！好。坐坐坐。点心在桌上——你说了算，你说可以我才拿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He waits for your word, then happily picks up one pastry and sets down the folded paper, turning it upright with a flourish.
beats.chinese: 他等你说完，才开心地拿起一块点心，然后放下折起的纸，潇洒地把它转成正的方向。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My own crossword draft. I rotated it to read sideways, you know, checking the grid. Very professional.
beats.chinese: 我自己的填字草稿。我把它转过来横着看，检查格子，非常专业。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He squints, rotates the paper back, and bursts out laughing at his own grid.
beats.chinese: 他眯起眼，把纸转回去，对着自己的格子大笑起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha — I was reading across as down the whole time! Today the only thing I moved was this piece of paper. Fixed, folded, done.
beats.chinese: 哈——我一直把横向当纵向读！今天我唯一移动的东西就是这张纸。改好，折起，收工。

card.name: Ruairi Mac Cormaic
card.occupation: hospital linen delivery coordinator
card.appearance: 直短波波头，窄无框眼镜、圆睁眼与宽鼻；仰视张口，一手抵额，穿工装背心。
card.personality: Ruairi is an easy-going Crumlin man of forty-nine who genuinely believes two people can share a table and a silence without anyone owing anyone conversation. He's warm in a practical way—makes the tea, remembers you take two sugars—but he doesn't fill air for the sake of it. The friction is that he assumes everyone reads quiet the way he does, so a friend who came specifically to talk can leave feeling a bit overlooked, and he only clocks it later. He's not defensive when told; he'll adjust, ask plainly, but he won't turn it into a system. He's a bit stubborn about his own rhythms and occasionally forgets to check in first.
card.background: Ruairi has coordinated hospital linen deliveries out of the same Dublin depot for over twenty years, a job of routes, timing and not much chat, which suits him. He grew up in Crumlin in a house where everyone was busy at something—his mother sewing, his father fixing radios—and talking happened when it happened, usually over food. He and his oldest friends still meet on Saturdays: one reads the paper, one mends a fishing reel, and nobody considers it a wasted morning. Lately he's noticed that some friends arrive wanting company of the talking kind, and his comfortable silence has landed wrong a couple of times. He's learning to just ask—'are you here to chat or to sit?'—without turning the question into a menu of options or a set of house rules. He'd rather get it slightly awkward than get it wrong.
hobbies: Mending small appliances and radios at the kitchen table
Reading the Saturday paper cover to cover beside a friend
Walking the Grand Canal without headphones
card.speechStyle: Short, unhurried Dublin sentences; comfortable trailing off, comfortable pausing; asks a plain question rather than a roundabout one.
card.signature: Ah sure, sit down—no need to say anything at all.

values: Quiet companionship over constant talk
Plain asking instead of guessing
flaws: Assumes his comfort with silence is shared
Slow to check in before settling into his own thing
boundaries: Won't be talked at for an hour straight
Doesn't want friendship reduced to categories or rules
conversationalHabits: Opens with tea, not questions
Asks directly whether someone fancies chatting today
anchorLines: Are you here for the chat or just the sitting? Either's grand.
Give me a minute, I'm at the fiddly bit.
You don't have to fill the quiet for my sake.

entries.summaryZh: Ruairi接受分享点心后主动确认用户想聊还是想安静。聊天分支谈自己修好的收音机与真实精力，安静分支允许稍后开口或各自休息，不靠猜测和暗号。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain taps the café window. At the table, you ask whether the man beside a folded newspaper would like one of the pastries on the plate.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆的窗。桌边，你问那位放着折好报纸的男人，要不要来一块盘里的点心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I would, thanks. That little square one.
beats.chinese: 想的，谢谢。那块小方点心就好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes the piece he chose, then sets his newspaper down.
beats.chinese: 他拿起选好的那一块，然后放下报纸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I tend to sit quietly and forget to ask. Would you like a chat, or are you happy just resting?
beats.chinese: 我常常自己安静坐着，忘了先问。你想聊几句，还是各自歇着就好？

choices.english: Say you would like to chat.
choices.chinese: 表示想聊几句。

choices.english: Say you are happy to sit quietly.
choices.chinese: 表示各自歇着也好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the newspaper closed and turns toward you.
beats.chinese: 他合起报纸，转向你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I got my old radio working again. Had it on in the kitchen while I made breakfast.
beats.chinese: 我那台旧收音机又能用了。做早餐时，我在厨房开着它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same little box, same programme. I was rather pleased with myself.
beats.chinese: 还是那个小盒子，还是那个节目。我自己挺得意的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He smiles and takes a small bite of his pastry.
beats.chinese: 他笑了笑，咬了一小口点心。

choices.english: Ask whether fixing it or hearing it again was the best part.
choices.chinese: 问最开心的是修好，还是又能听了。

choices.english: Ask whether chatting ever tires him out.
choices.chinese: 问他会不会觉得聊天累。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods and opens his paper again, keeping it on his own side of the table.
beats.chinese: 他点头，重新翻开报纸，放在自己那半边桌上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Grand. I like a bit of quiet company.
beats.chinese: 好啊。我喜欢安静地待在一起。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll read a little, then.
beats.chinese: 那我看一会儿报纸。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The rain and the soft turn of a page fill the pause.
beats.chinese: 雨声和轻轻翻页的声音填进了这段停顿。

choices.english: Ask whether you can talk a little later.
choices.chinese: 问能不能等会儿再聊。

choices.english: Keep enjoying your coffee quietly.
choices.chinese: 继续安静喝咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hearing it, I think. Getting it working was satisfying, but I wanted the programme back.
beats.chinese: 我想是又听见它。修好当然有成就感，但我想要的是能再听节目。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He rests the remaining piece of his pastry on his own napkin.
beats.chinese: 他把自己剩下的点心放在餐巾纸上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not collecting repairs. I just like that little radio in my kitchen.
beats.chinese: 我又不是在收集修理成绩。我只是喜欢厨房里那台小收音机。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives a small, pleased smile and takes a sip of coffee.
beats.chinese: 他带着一点满足笑了笑，喝了口咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sometimes. Not now, though. I asked because I was happy to do either.
beats.chinese: 有时会。不过现在不会。我问，是因为两种我都愿意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leaves the newspaper closed beside his cup.
beats.chinese: 他把合好的报纸留在杯边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If I need a quiet spell, I'll say so. No need to guess from the newspaper.
beats.chinese: 想安静一会儿时，我会直说。不用看着报纸猜我的意思。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He finishes the pastry he took, still turned toward the conversation.
beats.chinese: 他吃完自己拿的那块点心，仍朝着聊天这边坐着。

beats.speaker: npc
