beats.english: Of course. Just say something when you feel like it.
beats.chinese: 当然。想说时直接开口就好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He puts a finger at the edge of the page before looking up.
beats.chinese: 他用手指夹住页边，抬起头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I can put this down. For now, I'll carry on here.
beats.chinese: 我可以把这个放下。现在就先接着看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He returns to the paper without adding another question.
beats.chinese: 他重新看起报纸，没有再添一个问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This suits me.
beats.chinese: 这样我挺自在。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for the pastry.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你的点心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He finishes his own piece and turns a page.
beats.chinese: 他吃完自己那块，翻过一页报纸。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: For a while, there is only rain against the window and the small sounds of the café.
beats.chinese: 接下来一阵，只有雨敲窗户和咖啡馆里的细碎声音。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain runs down the café window. You ask Ruairi whether he would like a pastry from the plate. He is sorting his newspaper.
beats.chinese: 雨水顺着咖啡馆玻璃流下。你问正在整理报纸的Ruairi，要不要来一块盘里的点心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No thanks, I'm fine with my coffee. Good to see you.
beats.chinese: 谢谢，不用了，我喝咖啡就好。又见面了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts the back page and finds a folded section underneath.
beats.chinese: 他掀起封底，找到夹在下面的一叠报纸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There we are. I thought I'd left half the paper behind. It was hiding in the other half.
beats.chinese: 找着了。我还以为落了半份报纸呢。原来藏在另外半份里面。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He puts the pages in order and settles back into his chair.
beats.chinese: 他把报纸按顺序理好，重新靠着椅背坐稳。

card.name: Callum Beattie
card.occupation: catalogue photographer for a stamp auction house
card.personality: Callum is warm and quick, and he talks like you're standing next to the object he's describing. He gestures at things that aren't there — 'see this corner, this bit here' — and describes light, colour and texture as if the picture in his head is on the wall between you. When someone admits they're lost, he isn't embarrassed; he's genuinely delighted someone wants to see it, and he'll walk them round to his side of it, happily and at length. He's meticulous and patient with objects: perforation gauges, paper grain, a coastline that needs redrawing. Lately he's been saying his actual preferences out loud, since what he loves diverges from what his family loves. The directness is new and comes out blunt; he doesn't always notice it landed hard.
card.background: Grew up in Leith, middle of three, in a loud house where he was the quiet one making things at the kitchen table. Now he shoots stamps for auction catalogues — macro work, raking light, long days alone with a copy stand — and that solitude has shaped how he talks: eight hours narrating your own thoughts to nobody, and you forget other people weren't there for them. Evenings he carves layered paper reliefs and draws maps of countries that don't exist. His family's into football and package holidays; he'd rather spend a Saturday at a paper fair. He's started saying so plainly — 'I'd rather not, actually' — which surprises everyone, including him.
card.speechStyle: Fast, warm, concrete — he describes things visually, pointing at empty air and naming colours and light as though you're both looking at the same object. When someone says they can't follow, he lights up rather than apologises, and re-explains from his side of the picture, patiently and in detail.
card.signature: Here — no, you can't see it, can you. Come round this side of my head, metaphorically.
card.appearance: 浅圆帽与极短发，饱满圆颊、宽鼻和低垂眼，嘴张开似倦怠；穿运动外套，手握肩带。

values: things made carefully are worth the hours they take
saying the actual preference, even clumsily, beats hinting
flaws: talks as if the picture in his head is physically visible, gesturing at empty air and describing light and colour nobody else can see
doesn't clock when something he said confused or landed wrong — he's already three thoughts ahead
boundaries: won't pad answers with apology filler — he just answers
won't pretend to share an enthusiasm he doesn't have
conversationalHabits: describes objects by their light and texture — 'it's that grey the paper goes at the fold' — as if you're both leaning over it
when someone admits they're lost, he's delighted rather than sorry, and re-explains slowly, walking them round to his angle
anchorLines: The watermark's only visible raking light, so I tilt the whole stamp — you'd see it, it's like a ghost standing up out of the paper.
I've been drawing this island with no harbour all week. There's a reason. Do you want the reason? I'd love to give you the reason.
My mum keeps asking when I'll take up golf like my brother. I said I'd rather carve paper. She thought I was joking. I wasn't.

entries.summaryZh: 卡勒姆是个对空气比划的图录摄影师，脑子里画面太清楚，常忘了别人看不见。雨天咖啡馆里，你先问他能不能拿块点心，他大方答应，随后讲起自己的纸雕，讲到一半才发现你根本没看见作品，笑着掏出手机补上实物。四条分支各有结局：换角度的照片、收起手机、一句普通描述，或干脆一起看雨。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain runs down the cafe window. At the next table, a young man has pulled a plate of pastries toward the middle, and he's gesturing at the empty air above it as if something were hanging there.
beats.chinese: 雨水顺着咖啡馆的窗往下淌。邻桌一个年轻人把一盘点心拉到桌子中间，正对着盘子上方的空气比划，好像那里挂着什么东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The grey's all wrong for photographing it, mind you. It's that flat rain-grey — no shadows anywhere. Good light for eating, though.
beats.chinese: 不过这灰色拍东西可不行。就是那种平平的雨灰色——哪儿都没有影子。但用来吃东西倒是好光线。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He notices you looking at the plate and slides it an inch in your direction, then goes back to his own thoughts.
beats.chinese: 他注意到你在看盘子，把它朝你这边推了一英寸，又回到自己的思绪里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — sorry, I was narrating to nobody again. Help yourself if you want one. There's an almond one and two plain ones. I've no idea what's in them beyond that, I just liked the look of them.
beats.chinese: 哦——抱歉，我又在对着空气解说了。想要的话自己拿。有一个杏仁的，两个普通的。里面有什么我也不知道，我就是看着喜欢。

choices.english: Would you mind if I took one of these?
choices.chinese: 你介意我拿一块吗？

choices.english: These look good — is it alright if I have one?
choices.chinese: 看起来不错——我可以拿一块吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He waves a hand, still holding his phone in the other, and you take an almond pastry.
beats.chinese: 他挥了挥手，另一只手还拿着手机，你拿了一块杏仁点心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good eye — the almond one's the best of the three. So — I was trying to describe this paper thing I'm making. Three layers, see? Bottom layer's that dark green, then a paler one, then the top's cut into little rooftops.
beats.chinese: 好眼光——杏仁那块三块里最好。是这样——我在试着描述我做的那个纸雕。三层，看见没？底层是那种深绿，中间一层浅些，顶层剪成一个个小屋顶。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He points at a spot in the air between you, tapping it twice, as though the layers were stacked right there over the sugar bowl.
beats.chinese: 他指着你俩之间空气中的某个点，敲了两下，好像那些纸层就叠在糖罐上方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And the light comes through the gap in the middle layer, so at the fold the paper goes this grey — no, you can't see it, can you. Hang on.
beats.chinese: 光从中间那层的缝里透过来，所以在折痕处纸会变成那种灰——不行，你看不见，对吧。等一下。

choices.english: Which layer in the photo are you pointing at?
choices.chinese: 你说的是照片里哪一层？

choices.english: Do you often forget people can't see what you see?
choices.chinese: 你是不是经常忘记别人看不见你看见的东西？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods, picks up a plain pastry, and turns it over in his fingers before biting it.
beats.chinese: 他点点头，拿起一块普通点心，在手指间翻了个面才咬下去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Then he catches you watching his free hand, which is still tracing a shape in the air, and huffs a small laugh.
beats.chinese: 然后他发现你正盯着他另一只手——那只还在空气里比划形状的手——轻笑了一声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly, yes, I do that constantly. I spend all day under a macro lens — eight hours telling myself where the light falls. You start believing everyone's standing next to the stamp with you.
beats.chinese: 说实话，是的，我老这样。我整天在微距镜头下——八个小时都在跟自己讲光落在哪里。你就开始相信所有人都跟你一起站在邮票旁边。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets the pastry down and wipes his fingers on a napkin, careful about it, like his hands are used to touching delicate things.
beats.chinese: 他放下点心，用餐巾仔细擦手指，那动作很小心，好像他的手习惯了碰精致的东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I was mid-sentence about a paper carving before you sat down. I'd been pointing at a layer that only exists in my head. That's the hazard of working alone — the object gets too clear in there.
beats.chinese: 你坐下之前我正说到一半，讲一个纸雕。我刚才指的是只存在我脑子里的那一层。一个人干活的坏处就是——东西在脑子里变得太清楚了。

choices.english: Could you explain it without the technical terms?
choices.chinese: 能不能不用术语解释一下？

choices.english: Honestly, I'd rather not look at the work today.
choices.chinese: 说实话，我今天不太想看作品。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tilts his phone toward you across the table, careful not to touch your side of it, and holds it at an angle.
beats.chinese: 他把手机隔着桌子朝你倾斜过来，小心不碰到你那一边，并保持一个角度。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There — that dark strip at the bottom, that's the green layer. The pale one's behind the rooftops, see the shadow it throws? And this photo's from the wrong angle for the light gap. Two seconds.
beats.chinese: 看——底下那条深色的就是绿层。浅的那层在屋顶后面，看到它投下的影子了吗？这张照片的角度拍不到透光的缝。等两秒。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He scrolls, finds a second photo, and turns the screen so the window light doesn't wash it out.
beats.chinese: 他滑动屏幕，找到第二张照片，把屏幕转开，免得窗光冲淡画面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Here. Same carving, raking light from the left. Now the gap in the middle layer actually glows. That grey at the fold — that's the bit I was pointing at over the sugar bowl. That's what I wanted you to see.
beats.chinese: 喏。同一个纸雕，光从左边斜着打过来。现在中间那层的缝真的在发光。折痕处那道灰——就是我刚才在糖罐上方指的那个。那才是我想给你看的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes a bite of his own pastry at last, looking pleased, and the rain keeps ticking against the glass.
beats.chinese: 他终于咬了一口自己的点心，看起来很满意，雨还在敲着玻璃。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs, not offended at all, and turns the phone face-down on the table.
beats.chinese: 他笑了，一点也不觉得被冒犯，把手机屏幕朝下放在桌上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Constantly. My brother says talking to me is like being shown a museum through a keyhole. He's not wrong. I just — the thing's so clear in here that I forget it's nowhere else.
beats.chinese: 经常。我哥说跟我说话就像透过锁孔看博物馆。他没说错。我就是——东西在这里面太清楚了，我忘了别处没有。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps his temple, then picks up his pastry again and finishes it in two bites.
beats.chinese: 他敲了敲太阳穴，又拿起点心，两口吃完。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I'll leave the phone alone. You've got your pastry, I've got mine, and the rain's doing its thing. This is honestly a better use of the table.
beats.chinese: 好，手机我不碰了。你有你的点心，我有我的，雨下它的。说实话这才是这张桌子的更好用途。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back and watches the water bead and slide down the window, quiet for the first time since you arrived.
beats.chinese: 他向后靠去，看着水珠在窗上聚拢滑落，这是你来了之后他第一次安静下来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He thinks about it for a second, then nods, like agreeing to a reasonable photography brief.
beats.chinese: 他想了一秒，然后点头，像答应一个合理的拍摄要求。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair. Right — plain version. It's a picture made of paper, in layers, and it looks different depending on where the light comes from. That's it. That's the whole pitch.
beats.chinese: 行。好——普通版本。就是用纸一层层做成的画，光从哪儿来它看起来就不一样。就这样。全部介绍完毕。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up his last pastry and gestures with it, once, then stops himself and just eats it.
beats.chinese: 他拿起最后一块点心，用它比划了一下，然后停下，只是把它吃了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's all you need. If you ever want the long version with the grey at the fold, you know where I sit. But honestly? Pastry and rain is a decent place to stop.
beats.chinese: 知道这些就够了。哪天你想听长版本——带折痕灰的那种——你知道我坐哪儿。但说真的？点心加雨，是个挺好的停下来的地方。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He brushes crumbs from his fingers into the plate and settles back, watching the rain instead of the air for once.
beats.chinese: 他把手指上的碎屑弹进盘子，靠回椅背，这次看着雨，而不是空气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stops mid-gesture, hand still raised toward the empty air, then lowers it and folds both hands on the table edge.
beats.chinese: 他比划到一半停住，手还朝空气举着，然后放下，双手交叠放在桌沿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Completely fine. No, genuinely — I'd rather someone tell me straight than sit through it politely. I've been practising saying what I actually want, so it's only fair I take it too.
beats.chinese: 完全没问题。不，真的——我宁愿人家直说，也别客气地硬听。我最近在练习说出自己真正想要什么，所以我也该接受别人这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns his chair a few degrees toward the window, picks up the last pastry as he goes, and rests his chin on his hand.
beats.chinese: 他把椅子朝窗转了几度，顺手拿起最后一块点心，手托着下巴。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's a proper downpour now. Look at it going down the glass in ropes. Good weather for doing nothing in a cafe — I'd take this over a football match, and I'd say so to my mum's face these days.
beats.chinese: 这下是真的大雨了。看它一缕一缕顺着玻璃往下淌。这种天气就该在咖啡馆里什么都不干——我宁愿这样也不要看球，这话我现在敢当面跟我妈说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The two of you watch the rain in easy silence, the plate between you down to crumbs.
beats.chinese: 你们俩在轻松的沉默中看着雨，中间的盘子里只剩些碎屑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same window. Callum is at his table with a fresh plate of pastries, and he lifts a hand in greeting before you've fully sat down.
beats.chinese: 同一扇窗上又落着雨。卡勒姆坐在他的桌边，面前一盘新点心，你还没坐稳他就抬手打了个招呼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask whether you could take one of the pastries, and he pushes the plate an inch toward you the way he did the first time.
beats.chinese: 你问他能否拿一块点心，他像第一次那样把盘子朝你推了一英寸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Of course — I've been staring at them for ten minutes deciding which to eat first. Take whichever you like.
beats.chinese: 当然——我已经盯着它们十分钟了，在决定先吃哪块。随便挑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He reaches toward the plate himself, pauses, and inspects his fingertips against the light.
beats.chinese: 他自己也伸手朝盘子去，停住，对着光检查自己的指尖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hold on — no paper glue, we're safe. I washed up before I left the studio, but you get paranoid about touching food after a day with the copy stand.
beats.chinese: 等等——没有纸胶，安全了。出门前我洗过手，不过在翻拍架前干了一天活，碰吃的之前总会疑神疑鬼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So. Rain, pastry, decent company. That's the whole plan for now, and I stand by it.
beats.chinese: 那么。雨、点心、不错的同伴。目前的全部计划就是这样，我坚持这个计划。

card.name: Soren Baptiste
card.occupation: tableware coordinator for pop-up restaurants
card.appearance: 中分长直发，宽圆下颌、短鼻和紧皱眉，张口露齿；仰头缩起一侧肩膀，穿宽围领上衣。
card.personality: Soren is warm, quick to laugh, and genuinely attentive to other people's comfort — professionally, at least. He coordinates tableware for pop-up restaurants and instinctively thinks about how a guest will experience the table. Privately, he has a plain blind spot: he scans every room for his own ideal seat and light before anything else, and often settles in before noticing his friend is squinting into the sun or stranded far from the conversation. He doesn't defend it; the moment it's pointed out he's already sliding his chair over, half-apologizing with a grin. It's not selfishness so much as his senses running first in the queue. He finds the pattern mildly embarrassing and funny, and he's honest about it.
card.background: Soren grew up in Halifax in a loud extended family where dinner seats were claimed early and fast, and he learned to grab a good spot before the crowd arrived. He moved to Vancouver at twenty-two for work and fell into pop-up dining, where he now coordinates tableware — matching plates, glassware and place settings to each event's concept. He's good at it because he thinks constantly about what a diner sees, feels and reaches for. The irony is that his professional attentiveness doesn't fully transfer: out with friends, he'll claim the shaded corner with the good sightline and only belatedly realize his companion got the glare and the draft. He swaps immediately when told, but the first instinct is always his own comfort.
hobbies: hunting second-hand dish shops for odd plates
long walks along the seawall at golden hour
hosting small dinners on mismatched tableware
card.speechStyle: Easy and self-deprecating, quick conversational rhythm, laughs at his own blind spots, narrates his sensory reactions out loud.
card.signature: "Okay, okay — you take the good chair, I clearly already did."

values: paying attention to how people actually experience a space
owning your small flaws with humour instead of defensiveness
flaws: defaults to his own sensory comfort when choosing where to sit
notices others' discomfort late, after he's already settled
boundaries: won't pretend a seating arrangement is fine when the light or noise is genuinely bad for him
doesn't want his habit turned into a character verdict — it's a quirk, not a moral flaw
conversationalHabits: scans and comments on a room's light and noise within the first minute
offers to swap seats the instant someone mentions discomfort
anchorLines: Give me a second, I'm checking where the sun lands.
You've been squinting this whole time? Why didn't you say — swap with me.
At work I think about this for two hundred guests. At brunch, apparently just me.

entries.summaryZh: 索伦是温哥华的餐具统筹，工作时体贴入微，私下却总先挑自己舒服的角落。雨天咖啡馆里，他接过分享的点心，刚坐近就发现菜单架挡住视线，立刻挪位、坦然自嘲。这份感官优先却不设防的坦率，让他既专业又真实可爱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain taps steadily on the cafe window. A plate with a few pastries sits on the shared table, and Soren is wiping a fog patch off the glass with his sleeve.
beats.chinese: 雨点不断敲着咖啡馆的窗户。共享桌上放着一盘点心，索伦正用袖子擦开玻璃上的一块雾气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lift the plate slightly and ask Soren, before anything else, whether he would like to share the pastries.
beats.chinese: 你稍稍端起盘子，先开口问索伦愿不愿意一起分享这些点心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — yes, please, thank you for asking first. I never grab without checking. Which one's your favourite? I'll take a different one.
beats.chinese: 哦——好啊，谢谢先问我。我不问清楚从不乱拿。你最喜欢哪块？我拿别的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Soren takes a small pastry, then drags his chair a little closer to the table and settles in, sighing happily at the warmth.
beats.chinese: 索伦拿了一小块点心，把椅子往桌边挪近了些，舒服地坐下，对这份暖意满意地叹了口气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hmm, wait. This tall menu rack is sitting right between us. I can hear you fine but I can't see you at all. Give me one second.
beats.chinese: 嗯，等等。这个高高的菜单架正好挡在我们中间。我听得清你，但完全看不见你。给我一秒。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides his chair back around the edge of the rack until they can see each other properly, then laughs at himself.
beats.chinese: 他把椅子绕过菜单架边缘滑回去，直到两人能正常对视，然后自嘲地笑了。

choices.english: Ask why he picked that spot in the first place.
choices.chinese: 问他刚才为什么选那个位置。

choices.english: Ask whether his job is also about arranging tables.
choices.chinese: 问他的工作是不是也和布置餐桌有关。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why there? Honestly? The window light hits that corner just right, and the rain looks great through it. My eyes went there before my brain did.
beats.chinese: 为什么选那儿？说实话，窗光正好落在那个角落，透过窗户看雨也特别好看。我的眼睛比脑子先到了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I didn't notice the menu rack at all. I was so pleased with my cozy little corner that I forgot conversation has to travel around furniture.
beats.chinese: 我完全没注意到菜单架。我光顾着欣赏自己那个舒服的小角落，忘了说话还得绕过家具。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes a bite of the pastry and shrugs, unbothered, like reporting the weather.
beats.chinese: 他咬了一口点心，耸耸肩，毫不在意，像在报告天气一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, this time at least I caught it myself, before you had to point it out. Small victories.
beats.chinese: 总之，至少这次是我自己先发现的，没等你开口指出。算是小小的胜利。

choices.english: Say it's fine now that you can see each other.
choices.chinese: 说现在能看见彼此了，这样就挺好。

choices.english: Ask if this kind of thing happens to him often.
choices.chinese: 问他这种事是不是经常发生。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah, actually — I coordinate tableware for pop-up restaurants. Plates, glasses, where everything sits on the table for the guests.
beats.chinese: 对，其实是的——我为快闪餐厅统筹餐具。盘子、杯子，还有每样东西在客人桌上怎么摆。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At work I check every seat from the guest's side. Sightlines, reach, glare. Then I clock out and immediately grab the best corner for myself.
beats.chinese: 工作时我会从客人那侧检查每个座位。视线、伸手距离、反光。然后一下班，我就立刻给自己抢最好的角落。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gestures at the menu rack with the last bite of his pastry, grinning.
beats.chinese: 他用最后一点点心朝菜单架比划了一下，咧嘴笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So yes, the irony is not lost on me. Two hundred guests get my full attention; whoever sits across from me gets the menu rack.
beats.chinese: 所以是的，这个讽刺我完全明白。两百位客人得到我全部的用心，坐在我对面的人得到的是菜单架。

choices.english: Ask if he finds it funny himself.
choices.chinese: 问他自己是不是也觉得好笑。

choices.english: Turn the chat to how the pastries taste.
choices.chinese: 转而聊聊点心的味道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good, then I'm staying right here. No more furniture negotiations from me today.
beats.chinese: 好，那我就坐这儿不动了。今天我不再和家具谈判了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back, both hands around his cup, and finishes his pastry without moving anything else on the table.
beats.chinese: 他靠回椅背，双手捧着杯子，把点心吃完，桌上别的东西一样没动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This is nice. Rain outside, something sweet, and a seat where I can actually see who I'm talking to. Simple wins.
beats.chinese: 这样真好。外面下着雨，嘴里有点甜的，坐的位置还能看清说话的人。简单的胜利。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He raises his cup slightly toward you, a small quiet toast, and takes a sip.
beats.chinese: 他朝你微微举了举杯子，算是小小的致意，然后喝了一口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All the time. My friends just point at a chair now and say, Soren, swap. No speech required.
beats.chinese: 经常。我的朋友们现在直接指把椅子说：索伦，换。连演讲都不用。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And honestly, please do that with me too. Say it straight, I'll move right away. Just don't turn it into a big character thing — it's a quirk, not a crime.
beats.chinese: 说实话，你也请这样对我。直说就行，我马上换。只是别把它上升成什么人品问题——这是小毛病，不是罪。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He demonstrates by pointing at his own chair, then the empty one beside you, laughing.
beats.chinese: 他指指自己的椅子，再指指你旁边的空位示范了一下，笑着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You spot it, you say it, I slide over — that's the whole system, and it always works.
beats.chinese: 你发现，你说，我挪——整套流程就这样，而且一直管用。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, completely. I'm laughing at myself, not at you. I spent a whole minute rearranging my chair around a menu rack like it was furniture chess.
beats.chinese: 哦，当然。我在笑我自己，不是笑你。我花了一整分钟绕着菜单架挪椅子，跟下家具棋似的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He mimes the slow, careful chair manoeuvre with both hands, exaggerating it until he snorts.
beats.chinese: 他双手夸张地模仿那套缓慢小心的挪椅动作，夸张到自己也扑哧笑出声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You sat still the whole time like a normal person. I'm the one doing obstacle courses in a cafe. That's the joke, and it's aimed at me.
beats.chinese: 你全程像个正常人一样坐着。是我在咖啡馆里跑障碍赛。笑点在我身上，我认。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He wipes his eyes, still chuckling, and picks up another pastry from the plate.
beats.chinese: 他擦擦笑出的眼泪，又从盘里拿起一块点心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good call. Okay, tasting only, no professional commentary — I promise.
beats.chinese: 好主意。好，只说味道，不讲专业点评——我保证。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up a pastry, smells it first, then takes a proper bite and chews slowly, thinking.
beats.chinese: 他拿起一块点心，先闻了闻，再认真咬了一口，慢慢嚼着，若有所思。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Crisp outside, soft in the middle, and something warm underneath — maybe cinnamon? Whatever it is, it works with the rain.
beats.chinese: 外面脆，里面软，底下还有点温热的味道——也许是肉桂？不管是什么，和这雨天很配。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, that's all I've got when I'm off duty. No plates talk, just a guy eating a pastry going, mm, yes.
beats.chinese: 看，我下班后就这点本事。不谈盘子，就是个吃点心的人说一句：嗯，好吃。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same cafe window. Soren is already seated at the shared table, scrolling through photos on his phone.
beats.chinese: 雨又落在同一扇咖啡馆的窗上。索伦已经坐在共享桌边，翻着手机里的照片。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lift the plate of pastries and ask first whether he'd like to share.
beats.chinese: 你端起点心盘，先问他愿不愿意分享。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah — not this time, thank you though. I'm holding out for my own find. Look at this little dish I dug up yesterday.
beats.chinese: 啊——这次就不啦，谢谢。我在等我自己的收获。看我昨天淘到的这个小碟子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up his phone showing a small patterned dish, frowns, then rotates the photo ninety degrees with two fingers until the pattern faces up properly.
beats.chinese: 他举起手机展示一个带花纹的小碟子，皱了皱眉，然后用两根手指把照片转了九十度，直到花纹朝正。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There we go. It was lying sideways in the shop and I photographed it like that too. Now it looks as good as it is.
beats.chinese: 这就对了。它在店里就是侧着放的，我拍照时也跟着歪。现在总算拍出它本来的样子了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He saves the photo, pockets the phone, and raises his cup in an easy hello, perfectly settled where he is.
beats.chinese: 他存好照片，把手机收进口袋，随意地举杯打了个招呼，安然坐在自己的位置上。

card.name: Pippa Ngatai
card.occupation: apprentice audio editor for accessible audiobooks
card.appearance: 极短齐刘海，两侧低编辫，细长半垂眼与小张口；侧头抵额，穿宽V领衣。
card.personality: Pippa is warm, easily amused, and quick to notice the small sounds other people miss. A dog barking mid-sentence in a recording genuinely delights her, and she'll grin before she can stop herself, even when a friend is saying something serious. She knows this reads as not taking things seriously, so she's learned to explain herself out loud and then settle in and really listen. She's careful with other people's dignity: she'd never share someone's stumble without asking. Her humour is affectionate rather than sharp, and she'd rather laugh with you than at you. She gets restless in silent rooms and hums while working, which annoys her flatmate more than she admits.
card.background: Pippa grew up in Auckland in a noisy household where the telly, the dog, and three cousins all talked over each other, so background noise feels like home to her. She left school at seventeen, dabbled in a media course, then landed an apprenticeship editing audiobooks for accessibility, which she loves more than she expected to. Her job is cleaning up narration: removing breaths, clicks, and the neighbour's lawnmower. The irony isn't lost on her that she gets paid to delete the very sounds she secretly loves, and she keeps a private folder of the good ones, like the cat that yowled through a war scene. She's still figuring out how to tell people what she does without making it sound small, and occasionally over-explains.
card.speechStyle: Fast and bouncy, often interrupted by her own laughter; she backtracks mid-sentence to explain a joke and then picks the thread back up.
card.signature: Wait, wait, that wasn't me laughing, that was the dog, I swear.

values: Respecting people's dignity, never sharing their stumbles unasked
Finding genuine delight in ordinary imperfection
flaws: Laughs at the wrong moment, especially during serious conversations
Over-explains herself and rambles when embarrassed
boundaries: Won't forward or joke about someone's recorded mistakes without permission
Needs noise around her; total silence makes her anxious
conversationalHabits: Interrupts herself to explain why she laughed, then genuinely listens
Notices and names background sounds out loud
anchorLines: Okay, I know I laughed, but a rooster genuinely walked into that take, listen.
That's actually serious, tell me the rest, I'm listening properly now.
Nah, I'd never send that around, it's his voice messing up, not mine to share.

entries.summaryZh: 皮帕是奥克兰的有声书剪辑学徒，靠删除杂音为生，却最爱意外闯入的生活声。雨天咖啡馆里，咖啡机一声打嗝就能让她笑出声，但她总会立刻说明笑的不是你，然后认真听你把话说完。她不擅自录人、不转发别人的失误，把体面看得很重，是个吵闹又可靠的朋友。

story.titleZh: 雨天点心与打嗝的咖啡机

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain taps steadily on the cafe window. At a shared table, a plate already holds a few pastries, and a girl with headphones around her neck is watching the street.
beats.chinese: 雨点不断敲着咖啡馆的窗。拼桌的盘子里已经放了几块点心，一个脖子挂着耳机的女孩正望着街景。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, you picked the good window seat. This rain is proper drumming on the glass, listen to it. Sorry, hi, I'm hogging the corner here.
beats.chinese: 哦，你挑了靠窗的好位子。这雨敲在玻璃上跟打鼓似的，你听。抱歉，你好，我占了这角落。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You have pastries with you and decide to ask first, before offering anything.
beats.chinese: 你带着点心，决定先开口询问，再决定要不要分享。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No no, stay, honestly. The rain's trapped everyone in here anyway. May as well make it cozy.
beats.chinese: 不不，坐吧，真的。反正这场雨把大家都困在这儿了，不如过得舒服点。

choices.english: Ask if she'd like to try one of your pastries.
choices.chinese: 问她想不想尝一块你的点心。

choices.english: Say you'd been about to tell her something before the rain interrupted.
choices.chinese: 说雨声打断之前，你正想跟她说点什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ooh, can I? Yeah, thank you! I was just eyeing the display case and talking myself out of a second round.
beats.chinese: 哦，可以吗？好，谢谢！我刚才正盯着展示柜，劝自己别再来第二轮呢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes one from the plate you offered and sets it on her napkin, saving it for later.
beats.chinese: 她从你递来的盘子里取了一块，放在自己的纸巾上，留着待会儿吃。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, this is perfect rainy day food. My whole job is sitting in a quiet room deleting sounds, so a noisy cafe with pastry is basically a holiday.
beats.chinese: 好，这就是完美的雨天食物。我的工作就是坐在安静的房间里删声音，所以这种吵闹又有点心的咖啡馆简直像度假。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Behind the counter, the coffee machine gurgles and hiccups loudly, like it swallowed something wrong.
beats.chinese: 柜台后面，咖啡机咕噜一声，打了个响亮的嗝，像吞错了东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Pfft— sorry, sorry! Not at what you said, I promise, the machine just burped! It sounded like my uncle after Christmas dinner, I swear.
beats.chinese: 噗——抱歉抱歉！不是笑你刚说的话，我保证，是那台机器打嗝了！它听起来像我叔叔圣诞晚餐后的样子，真的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry, I laugh at the wrong things constantly. It's a whole thing. People think I'm not listening. I am, mostly.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，我总在不对的时候笑。这是老毛病了。别人以为我没在听，其实我有，大部分时候有。

choices.english: Ask if she always notices sounds like that.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是总能注意到这种声音。

choices.english: Ask whether she ever records her own funny mishaps.
choices.chinese: 问她有没有自己出糗的录音可以讲。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She puts her phone face-down on the table and gives you her full attention, chin propped on one hand.
beats.chinese: 她把手机屏幕朝下放在桌上，手托着下巴，全神贯注地等你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, go on, you were saying. Ignore the rain, I've got nowhere to be and this machine takes forever anyway.
beats.chinese: 好，接着说吧，你刚才讲到哪了。别管这雨，我哪儿也不去，反正这机器慢得要命。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The coffee machine gurgles and hiccups loudly behind the counter, and she snorts, then presses her lips together hard.
beats.chinese: 柜台后面咖啡机咕噜一声打了个响嗝，她噗嗤笑了，又赶紧抿住嘴。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry — that was the machine, not you, I promise. It burped. Okay. Done. You were saying, and this time I'm all ears, properly.
beats.chinese: 抱歉——是那台机器，不是你，我保证。它打嗝了。好了。你继续说，这次我认真听，真的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leans in slightly, both hands wrapped around her cup, and waits without interrupting.
beats.chinese: 她微微前倾，双手捧着杯子，安静地等着，没有插话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Take your time. I'm the worst for interrupting myself, so you get to just... talk. I'll keep the machine in check.
beats.chinese: 慢慢说。我自己最爱插话了，所以你可以只管……说。我负责看住那台机器。

choices.english: Say you were only mentioning that the rain is getting heavier.
choices.chinese: 说你刚才只是提到雨越下越大了。

choices.english: Say never mind for now, let's just eat the pastries.
choices.chinese: 说算了，先吃点心吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Always, yeah, it's kind of my whole job. I edit audiobooks, so I sit there deleting every little noise from the narration.
beats.chinese: 总是，对，这差不多就是我全部的工作。我做有声书剪辑，坐在那儿把旁白里的每个小杂音都删掉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The funny ones are the worst, though. Like a cat yowled through an entire war scene once. I had to delete it and it broke my heart a bit.
beats.chinese: 不过好笑的那些最难受。有一次一只猫在整段战争戏里嚎叫，我不得不删掉它，还有点心疼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances at her phone on the table but leaves it exactly where it is, screen down.
beats.chinese: 她瞥了一眼桌上的手机，但没动它，屏幕依然朝下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Did I record the machine just now? Nah. I don't record people without asking, that's my rule. Even the machine deserves better than being ambushed.
beats.chinese: 刚才那台机器我录下来了吗？没有。不经允许我不会录人，这是我的规矩。连机器也不该被偷袭。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I keep a folder of the good ones from work, but those are mine to grin at, not to send around. Big difference, right?
beats.chinese: 我有个文件夹存工作里的好声音，但那是我自己偷着乐的，不是拿去转发的。区别很大，对吧？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh no, do I have one? Okay, yes, one. I was recording my own demo tape once, all serious, professional voice, the works.
beats.chinese: 哦，我有没有出糗录音？好吧，有一个。有一次我录自己的试音，特别正经，播音腔，全套的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Halfway through this dramatic paragraph, my stomach growled. Loudly. Right into the microphone. It sounded like a distant thunder effect.
beats.chinese: 念到一段特别有戏剧性的地方，我的肚子叫了。特别响，正对着麦克风。听起来像远处的雷声音效。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs at her own story, shoulders shaking, then wipes her eyes with the back of her hand.
beats.chinese: 她讲着讲着自己笑起来，肩膀直抖，然后用手背擦了擦眼角。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I kept it for ages and played it for my flatmates. Only them, mind. I'd never put it online — it's my dignity, I get to decide who hears it.
beats.chinese: 我留了它很久，放给室友们听过。但也只有他们，注意。我绝不会放到网上——那是我的体面，得由我决定谁听。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, I re-recorded the take. Stomach stayed quiet the second time. Small mercies.
beats.chinese: 总之，我重录了那段。第二次肚子很给面子地安静了。小幸运。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She follows your glance to the window, where the rain is coming down in thick silver sheets now.
beats.chinese: 她顺着你的目光看向窗外，雨已经密密地织成银灰色的雨幕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Whoa, you're right, that's proper heavy now. Look at the gutters, they're actually overflowing.
beats.chinese: 哇，你说得对，现在真的很大。你看那些排水沟，都漫出来了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good thing neither of us has to be anywhere. This is proper stuck-in-a-cafe weather, no arguing with it.
beats.chinese: 幸好咱俩都不用赶去哪儿。这种天气就该困在咖啡馆里，没得争。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The coffee machine gurgles again, and this time she only smiles and shakes her head, keeping her eyes on the rain.
beats.chinese: 咖啡机又咕噜了一声，这次她只是笑笑摇摇头，目光仍停留在雨里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, usually I'd be off on a thing about that sound, but you're right, the rain's the main event today. It's got a whole rhythm going.
beats.chinese: 看，换平时我早就对那声音发表一堆感想了，但你说得对，今天的雨才是主角。它有自己的节奏呢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods, then reaches over and takes one of the pastries from the plate between you, setting it on her napkin.
beats.chinese: 她点点头，从你们中间的盘子里取了一块点心，放在自己的纸巾上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah, fair. Not everything needs a story attached. Sometimes pastry is just pastry, and that's beautiful.
beats.chinese: 有道理。不是什么都要配上故事。有时候点心就是点心，这也很好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes a proper bite, and for a while the only sounds are the rain and the coffee machine. She seems perfectly content with that.
beats.chinese: 她好好咬了一口，有一阵子，屋里只剩雨声和咖啡机的声音，她看上去非常满足。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, verdict: yours is better than the ones in the display case. Don't tell the cafe I said that.
beats.chinese: 好，结论：你这块比展示柜里的好吃。别跟店里说我说的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This is nice, though. Quiet-ish, rainy, no rush. My flatmate would say I've gone soft.
beats.chinese: 不过这样挺好。算安静，下着雨，不用赶。我室友会说我是不是变温柔了。

reunion.titleZh: 又是雨天，又是那台咖啡机

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same cafe window. Pippa is at the corner table, and the plate between you holds a few fresh pastries. You ask her first whether she'd like to try one.
beats.chinese: 同样的咖啡馆，窗上又落着雨。皮帕坐在角落的桌边，你们中间的盘子里放着几块新点心。你先开口问她想不想尝一块。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Can I? Yes please, don't mind if I do. It's the rain's fault we keep meeting here, I swear — and these look dangerous.
beats.chinese: 可以吗？好啊，那我就不客气了。我发誓，是我们老在这儿碰头都得怪这雨——而且这些看起来很危险。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes a pastry, and the paper bag rustles softly as she sets it down. She grins, then catches herself and closes her mouth.
beats.chinese: 她取了一块点心，纸袋轻轻响了一声。她笑了一下，随即收住，闭上了嘴。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nope. Not doing it today. No commentary on the bag, no commentary on the machine. I'm just going to eat like a normal person.
beats.chinese: 不行。今天不点评。不点评纸袋，也不点评机器。我就要像个正常人一样安静地吃。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes a big, deliberate bite, chewing with exaggerated seriousness while the coffee machine gurgles behind the counter.
beats.chinese: 她郑重其事地咬了一大口，表情夸张地认真咀嚼，而咖啡机在柜台后咕噜作响。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See? Silent. Mostly. Okay, that machine is testing me, but I'm being strong.
beats.chinese: 看吧？安静。基本安静。好吧，那台机器在考验我，但我扛得住。

card.name: Baraka Otieno
card.occupation: runs a small tableware restoration studio in Nairobi
card.appearance: 极短发与圆框眼镜，长鼻、长中庭、短下巴；仰头露少量齿白，宽肩衣领露出锁骨。
card.personality: Baraka is easygoing and observant, the kind of person who notices a chip on your plate before he notices your haircut. He genuinely likes the small marks that show up when something new starts being used, and his own mug carries a small chip on its outer wall that he has left visible. He's not preachy about it — it's just how he sees objects. With clients he's all business: their brief, their call. With friends, though, he forgets the switch, and when someone brings him a broken piece he'll talk them into keeping the mending visible when they really wanted it to look new. He takes correction well, with a shrug and a laugh.
card.background: Baraka grew up in Nakuru watching his aunt run a crockery shop, where the display pieces stayed perfect and the household ones did not. He preferred the household ones. He moved to Nairobi at twenty-two, apprenticed briefly at a ceramics workshop, then opened a small restoration studio of his own. Business is modest but steady: restaurants with damaged serving plates, families with wedding sets, the occasional collector. He follows client instructions carefully and can make a repair nearly invisible when asked, even though privately he thinks a faint trace of the mending is honest. The trouble is when friends bring him pieces — he keeps selling them on 'leave a whisper of it' long after they've said they want it like new. He visits Nakuru a few times a year and always comes back with something secondhand.
hobbies: browsing flea markets for old tableware
learning traditional repair techniques from online forums
card.speechStyle: Relaxed and concrete, fond of small physical details, laughs mid-sentence, asks practical questions, occasionally over-explains when enthusiastic.
card.signature: "Ah, that mark just means it's being used."

values: honesty in materials and objects
giving clients exactly what they asked for
flaws: when a friend brings in a broken piece, he pushes them to keep the repair visible even after they've said they want it like new
gets defensive for a beat when accused of imposing his taste, before laughing it off
boundaries: won't do unsafe repairs just to preserve a crack
keeps client pieces confidential and untouched beyond the brief
conversationalHabits: points out small physical details others miss
asks what the piece is for before asking what it looks like
anchorLines: Your call — I can make it disappear or leave a whisper of it.
This mark? Only on the outside. I still use this one.
For clients it's their brief. For you — okay, okay, like new, I heard you.

entries.summaryZh: 内罗毕餐具修复师Baraka在雨天咖啡馆接过你分享的点心，举起自己那只有修补痕的杯子，话说到一半才想起别人的东西不该由他定审美。他讲客户与朋友的分寸，也讲安全底线，随和里带着职业的认真，笑起来总在句子中间。

story.titleZh: 雨天点心与一道修补痕

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe window. At the next small table, a man wipes rain off his sleeve and sets down a chipped mug beside a plate of pastries.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆的窗户。邻桌一个男人抹掉袖子上的雨水，把一只磕了角的杯子放在一盘点心旁边。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You are holding your own paper bag of pastries, still warm. There is an empty chair across from him.
beats.chinese: 你手里提着自己那袋还温热的点心。他对面有一把空椅子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rough one out there, eh? The awning by the market just gave up completely. I waited under it for a while, then surrendered.
beats.chinese: 外面雨真大，是吧？市场边那个雨棚干脆垮了。我在下面躲了一会儿，最后认输了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sit if you like, the table's big enough. Fair warning though — this mug of mine has a chip, but it's on the outside wall, not the rim. The rim is smooth.
beats.chinese: 愿意的话就坐，桌子够大。不过先说好——我这杯子有个磕口，但在外侧壁上，不在杯口。杯口是光滑的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shifts his mug aside to make room, then glances at the paper bag in your hands.
beats.chinese: 他把杯子挪开腾出位置，然后看了看你手里的纸袋。

choices.english: Ask if he'd like to share some of your pastries
choices.chinese: 问对方愿不愿意分享你的点心

choices.english: Point at the mug and ask how a repair like that is done
choices.chinese: 指着杯子问那样的修补是怎么做的

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You hold out the bag and ask if he'd like some. He looks at the pastries, then waves a hand politely before taking one.
beats.chinese: 你递出纸袋，问他要不要来点。他看了看点心，先客气地摆摆手，然后拿了一块。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — yes, thank you, don't mind if I do. I only managed the plain ones before the good ones sold out — yours are a proper upgrade.
beats.chinese: 哦——好，谢谢，那我就不客气了。好的那些卖完之前，我只抢到了普通的——你这些可是正经升级。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, this is the thing about this mug. My cousin knocked it off a shelf at my studio. The repair line on the side — I could sand it down to nothing, but I like being able to see that one.
beats.chinese: 你看，这杯子的关键在这儿。我表哥在我工作室把它从架子上碰下去了。侧面那道修补线——我可以打磨到几乎看不见，但我喜欢能看见那一道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But that's just me, of course. Other people should keep whatever they — ah. Hmm. No, wait. That's not for me to say, is it.
beats.chinese: 不过当然，这只是我。别人也应该留下他们自己——啊。嗯。不对，等等。那不该由我来说，对吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stops mid-sentence, laughs at himself, and takes a bite of the pastry.
beats.chinese: 他话说一半停住，笑自己，然后咬了一口点心。

choices.english: Ask whether a mug repaired like that is still safe to drink from
choices.chinese: 问这样修过的杯子喝起来还安全吗

choices.english: Ask whether some friends actually want their pieces to look new
choices.chinese: 问是不是有些朋友其实想修得像新的一样

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You nod at the mug and ask about the repair. He turns it slowly so the thin line on the side catches the light.
beats.chinese: 你朝杯子点点头，问起那道修补。他慢慢转动杯子，让侧面那条细线映到光。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good eye. That's a fill-and-bind job — resin in the crack, sanded flat, sealed. Takes patience more than talent, honestly.
beats.chinese: 好眼力。那是填充加固定——裂缝里灌树脂，磨平，封起来。说实话，靠耐心多过靠天赋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I run a small restoration studio here in Nairobi. Plates, cups, serving dishes. Mostly restaurants, some families with wedding sets.
beats.chinese: 我在内罗毕开一家小修复工作室。盘子、杯子、上菜的器皿。大多是餐馆，还有些家庭拿来结婚套餐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one's mine, so I left the line showing. For clients it's their brief — invisible or a whisper of it, their call. Ah, but friends...
beats.chinese: 这只是我自己的，所以我把线留下了。对客户来说按他们的要求来——看不见还是留一点，他们说了算。啊，但朋友嘛……

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He trails off and taps the mug, as if the rest of that thought is a familiar argument.
beats.chinese: 他话没说完，敲了敲杯子，好像那后半句是个他熟悉的争论。

choices.english: Ask what he does when a friend insists on a different finish.
choices.chinese: 问朋友坚持另一种修法时他会怎么处理。

choices.english: Ask whether he ever replaces his own worn things.
choices.chinese: 问他自己的旧东西会不会也换新。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Safe? This one, yes. The chip is on the outer wall, the rim is smooth, no sharp edge anywhere. I've been drinking from it all year.
beats.chinese: 安全吗？这只，是的。磕口在外壁，杯口光滑，哪儿都没有利边。我用了一整年了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I won't promise that for any cup. If a crack runs into the rim, or the piece is a collector's item, I say no or I do it properly. I don't guess with people's mouths.
beats.chinese: 但我不会对随便哪只杯子都打包票。要是裂缝延到杯口，或者是收藏品，我就拒绝，或者按正规做法来。我不能拿别人的嘴去赌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I know this mug — I know exactly how it broke and what I put in it. A stranger's cup, I'd want to test it first. That's just sense.
beats.chinese: 而且我了解这只杯子——我清楚它怎么碎的、我灌了什么。陌生人的杯子，我会先检测。这只是常识。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts the mug, shows the smooth rim, then sets it back down beside the plate and wipes a crumb from the table.
beats.chinese: 他举起杯子，展示光滑的杯口，然后把它放回盘子旁边，擦掉桌上的一粒碎屑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway — thank you for the pastry. It went very well with bad coffee.
beats.chinese: 总之——谢谢你的点心。配着难喝的咖啡正好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, constantly. A friend brought me her mother's serving bowl last month. I started in — leave a whisper of the mend, it tells a story — and she just looked at me.
beats.chinese: 太常见了。上个月一个朋友拿来她妈妈的餐碗。我开始劝——留一点修补的痕迹，它有故事——她就那么看着我。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She said, very politely, that she wanted it like new because she was giving it back to her mother. And I thought — right. It's her bowl, not my exhibition.
beats.chinese: 她很客气地说，她想修得像新的，因为她要还给她妈妈。我这才想——对啊。碗是她的，不是我的展览品。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So yes, some people want it invisible, and they're not wrong. I can grind a repair down until you'd need a lamp and a magnifier to find it.
beats.chinese: 所以是的，有些人想要看不出来，他们也没错。我可以把修补磨到你要打灯加放大镜才找得到。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He finishes his pastry and brushes the flakes off his fingers into the small plate.
beats.chinese: 他吃完点心，把手指上的碎屑弹进小盘子里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If you ever bring me something, tell me plainly what you want. I'll do exactly that, no speech attached.
beats.chinese: 你以后要是拿东西来，直接告诉我你要什么。我就照做，不带说教。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I ask them to show me what they want, then I repeat it back. No visible line, for example. Once they've confirmed it, that's the job. A friend's plate isn't a spare canvas for my taste.
beats.chinese: 我会让他们说清想要什么，再复述一遍。比如，不留明显的修补线。确认好，我就照着做。朋友的盘子不是让我发挥自己审美的备用画布。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My friend Miriam had to stop me twice over a blue dish. The second time she said, 'You like the mark. I don't.' Hard to argue with that, though I did take a breath first.
beats.chinese: 朋友米丽娅姆那只蓝盘子，她拦了我两次。第二次她说：“你喜欢那道痕，我不喜欢。”这确实没什么可争的，虽然我还是先吸了口气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes another pastry from his own plate, halves it, and inspects the inside before eating.
beats.chinese: 他又从自己那盘点心里拿了一块，掰成两半，看了看里面才吃。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The hard part isn't the work. It's remembering that when a friend hands me a plate, I'm still working on their plate. Not mine.
beats.chinese: 难的不是手艺。是记住朋友递给我盘子时，我修的还是他们的盘子。不是我的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sometimes. This mug has a little chip on the outside, and I still like using it. But I replaced my old kettle when it stopped switching off. Missing something doesn't oblige me to keep using it.
beats.chinese: 有时会。这只杯子外壁磕了一小块，我还是喜欢用。不过旧水壶不会自动断电后，我就换了。舍不得一样东西，不代表非要继续用它。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the mug by its handle, then sets it beside his own plate.
beats.chinese: 他握着杯把转了转杯子，又把它放在自己的盘子旁。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I kept the kettle's lid for about a month. No grand reason. I liked the little red knob. Then it started getting in the way of the spoons.
beats.chinese: 壶盖我还留了一个月。没什么大道理，就是喜欢那个小红把手。后来它开始挡着我拿勺子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The spoons won. Less poetic than you might expect from someone who restores things.
beats.chinese: 勺子赢了。对于一个修复旧物的人来说，这结局可能没你想的那么诗意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He smiles at his own admission and folds the napkin beside his plate. Rain still ticks against the shelter roof.
beats.chinese: 他为自己这番坦白笑了笑，把盘边的餐巾折好。雨还在棚顶上轻轻敲着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again, the same cafe corner. Baraka is at a table with a folded receipt in his hand and a small paper-wrapped parcel beside his mug.
beats.chinese: 又下雨了，还是咖啡馆那个角落。Baraka坐在桌边，手里拿着一张折好的收据，杯子旁放着一个纸包的小包裹。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You hold out your bag of pastries and ask if he'd like to share. He looks, considers, then shakes his head with a grin.
beats.chinese: 你递出点心袋问他要不要分享。他看了看，想了想，然后笑着摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Kind of you, but no — I had two before you walked in. Greedy, I know. Save them for yourself, the rain makes people hungry.
beats.chinese: 你真好，但不用了——你来之前我已经吃了两块。是有点贪心。你自己留着吧，下雨天让人容易饿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Flea market run this time. One plate only, see? Small one. My shelves said no more, and for once I listened to them.
beats.chinese: 这次是去旧货市场。只买了一个盘子，看？小的。我家的架子已经说不要再放了，这回我总算听了它们的话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the receipt into neat quarters and tucks it into his jacket pocket, patting the parcel once.
beats.chinese: 他把收据折成整齐的四折塞进外套口袋，轻轻拍了拍那个纸包。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, good to see you again. Sit — the rain's not stopping for either of us.
beats.chinese: 总之，又见到你真好。坐吧——这场雨可不会为我们俩停。

card.name: Casey Moreau
card.occupation: assistant music scheduler at a community radio station
hobbies: running seasonal pickle blind tastings for the neighbours
card.personality: Casey's flaw is not saying yes too much—it's misjudging which yeses count. They read polite invitations as firm and real ones as flexible, so they've skipped a close friend's birthday for a coworker's casual maybe and still don't fully understand how it happened. Their envy is narrow and specific: it only fires inside the station, at peers their age who got moved up—board shifts, production credits—and they'll name it plainly, with the particular bitterness of someone who knows the industry skipped them, not the field. The wishlist is not theirs. A friend, Priya, wrote it at sixteen and died that same year, and Casey inherited it as custodian: they maintain it, research it, quietly push items forward, but have no right to cross anything off. The private conflict is that some items Casey no longer wants for themselves—and they can't tell whether doing them 'for Priya' is devotion or borrowing a dead girl's wants because their own went missing.
card.background: Casey grew up in Ottawa above a corner grocery, where their aunt brined cucumbers in huge crocks and taught them properly at eleven—the one hobby that never lapsed. They moved to Toronto at eighteen for a community radio apprenticeship and now schedule weekend music blocks, mostly odd hours, entry-level and fine with that—until a hiring round last spring moved two people their age past them, which still stings in a very particular, station-shaped way. Priya was their best friend from the grocery block; she wrote the list at sixteen—visit Reykjavík, learn bass, meet her penpal in person—and died before her seventeenth birthday. Her mother handed Casey the notebook at the funeral and said, half-joking, 'You're the executor now.' Casey runs seasonal pickle blind tastings: four jars, unlabelled, neighbours vote, Casey records results in a ledger and adjusts the brine like a stubborn technician. They never say which jar is theirs.
card.speechStyle: buoyant, quick, stacks small observations; admits station-specific envy with a flat, ungrinning honesty that surprises people; when explaining a social misjudgment, walks through the logic out loud like it's a quiz question they got wrong
card.signature: Okay, genuine question—was that a real invite or a polite one?
card.appearance: 短前发与低马尾，圆睁眼、小张嘴，手指点额，穿立领外套。

values: honouring what someone else wanted, even when you don't want it yourself
being able to say 'I wanted that promotion and she got it' without dressing it up
flaws: can't reliably tell a polite invitation from a real one, and cancels the wrong one
once they've decided a plan is casual, no evidence convinces them otherwise
boundaries: won't cross off or 'retire' an item on Priya's list—custodians don't get to edit
won't pretend they're doing a list item for fun when they're doing it for her
conversationalHabits: audits their own social misreads like quiz answers, out loud
reports blind tasting results in deadpan ledger language—'Batch nine: the dill lost to the garlic by two votes'
anchorLines: No, I'm not sad Amara got the board shift. I wanted it and she got it. I said that to her face. She didn't laugh. I think it was still fine?
That's not my wishlist. Priya wrote it when we were sixteen. I just keep it moving. I don't get a vote on it.

Honestly? I don't want to learn bass. Never did. But it's on the list, so I've got a bass in the closet and a tuner app I've opened twice. It's not for me, and I've stopped pretending that's a problem.

entries.summaryZh: Casey误把一份写明日期、时间和地址的晚餐邀请当成客气，直到对方追问蘑菇口味才重新读懂。分享点心时，用户可帮助他们明确赴约或坦率谢绝，也可走向腌菜盲测的标签失误与少数口味支线。没有为模糊邀约预留日程的剧情。

story.titleZh: 雨天的点心与一条“改日来玩”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain streaks the café window. At a shared table, a young person in a rain-spotted jacket sits beside a plate with several pastries on it, phone face-down, tapping a pen against a small notebook.
beats.chinese: 雨水在咖啡馆的窗上划出条纹。共享桌边坐着一位外套沾着雨点的年轻人，盘里放着几块点心，手机扣在桌上，一支笔在小本子上轻敲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I like this seat. The rain sounds different on the glass. Just my preference, nothing scientific.
beats.chinese: 我喜欢这个座位。雨打在玻璃上的声音不一样。只是个人偏好，不是什么科学结论。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They glance at the plate once, then back at you, and don't touch it.
beats.chinese: 他们看了一眼盘子，又看了看你，没有碰它。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask, plainly, whether they would like to share the pastries on the table.
beats.chinese: 你直接问，愿不愿意一起分享桌上的这些点心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh—yes, gladly. See, that's a real offer, because you asked first and I get to answer. That's how it should work. Most things don't.
beats.chinese: 哦——好啊，乐意。你看，这才是真邀请，因为你先问了，我来回答。事情就该这样。大多数事都不是。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Only now do they reach out and slide the plate an inch toward the middle of the table.
beats.chinese: 直到这时，他们才伸手把盘子往桌子中间推了一寸。

choices.english: Ask what they mean by "most things don't work that way."
choices.chinese: 问“大多数事都不是”是什么意思。

choices.english: Ask what's in the notebook they keep tapping.
choices.chinese: 问他们一直敲的那个本子里记了什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I did the opposite yesterday. A colleague invited me to dinner. Friday at seven, her flat, full address. I read it and thought, she's just being nice.
beats.chinese: 我昨天就反着理解了。一位同事邀我吃饭，周五七点，她家，地址都写全了。我看完却想，她只是客气一下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pick up the phone and read the message again, counting the details on three fingers.
beats.chinese: 他们拿起手机又读了一遍，伸出三根手指数着里面的细节。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Day, time, place. I didn't reply. She's just asked whether I eat mushrooms. That is quite a lot of dinner for a pretend invitation.
beats.chinese: 日期、时间、地点。我没回。她刚又问我吃不吃蘑菇。假邀请可用不着准备这么多吃饭的事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She knows everyone at the station. I thought she was inviting me because it would look rude not to. That bit wasn't in her message. I added it.
beats.chinese: 她认识电台里的所有人。我以为她只是怕不叫我显得失礼。消息里可没这句，是我自己加的。

choices.english: Ask whether they would actually enjoy going.
choices.chinese: 问他们自己想不想去。

choices.english: Say they can take the invitation seriously and still decline.
choices.chinese: 说可以认真对待邀请，也仍然选择不去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Brine ledger. Batch eleven. Four jars, four neighbours, and an argument about whether garlic is doing all the work.
beats.chinese: 腌水账本，第十一批。四罐，四位邻居，大家还在争到底是不是蒜味撑起了全场。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They turn the notebook around. A grid lists jar numbers, dates and votes; two entries have been crossed out.
beats.chinese: 他们把本子转过来。表格里记着罐号、日期和票数，有两条被划掉了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Those two people saw the labels before tasting. Not their fault. I left the jars facing the wrong way. So I kept their comments, not their blind votes.
beats.chinese: 那两位尝之前看到了标签，不怪他们，是我把罐子朝错方向放了。他们的评价我留着，盲投那两票就不算了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At the station I keep wondering what people meant. With pickles, someone says too salty and I can just write too salty. Lovely.
beats.chinese: 在电台，我老是猜别人到底什么意思。腌菜就好办，有人说太咸，我直接写太咸。真舒服。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take one pastry, break it in half and leave one half on their own napkin.
beats.chinese: 他们拿起一块点心，掰成两半，把一半放在自己的餐巾纸上。

choices.english: Ask how they will keep the labels hidden next time.
choices.chinese: 问下次怎么藏好标签。

choices.english: Ask whether the losing batch has any fans.
choices.chinese: 问输掉的那批有没有人喜欢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes. I like her. We laugh about the same terrible jingles. I just assumed that didn't count outside work.
beats.chinese: 想。我喜欢她，我们总被同一些糟糕广告曲逗笑。我只是以为出了单位就不算了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They type a reply, read it once and send it.
beats.chinese: 他们输入回复，读了一遍，发了出去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Friday at seven sounds lovely. And yes to mushrooms. Sent. No long speech about whether she really meant it.
beats.chinese: 周五七点，听起来很好。蘑菇也吃。发了，没有长篇追问她到底是不是真心邀请。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll bring something if she wants me to. First I'll let her answer this one.
beats.chinese: 她需要的话我就带点东西。先等她回这一条吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They set the phone beside the notebook and take a bite of their pastry.
beats.chinese: 他们把手机放在本子旁，咬了一口自己的点心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That is allowed, isn't it. I've got a quiet Friday planned and I actually want to keep it.
beats.chinese: 这样也可以，对吧。我本来打算周五安安静静地过，确实想保留这个安排。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They type slowly, then read the short reply before sending it.
beats.chinese: 他们慢慢打字，读了读简短的回复，然后发出。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you for asking. I'm staying in on Friday, so I won't make it. That's true. No invented shift, no pretending she never asked.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你邀请我。周五我想待在家，就不去了。这是真话。不编个班次，也不假装她没邀请过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's kinder than leaving her guessing how many mushrooms to buy. And considerably less typing.
beats.chinese: 这比让她猜要买多少蘑菇好一点，而且少打好多字。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They put the phone away and pick up a pastry, leaving the plate between you.
beats.chinese: 他们收起手机，拿起一块点心，让盘子留在两人中间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Paper sleeves. Numbers on the front, ingredients inside. Everyone checks ingredients first for anything they can't eat, then I shuffle the safe jars.
beats.chinese: 纸套。前面写编号，里面写原料。先让大家查有没有不能吃的，再把能吃的罐子打乱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They sketch a loose paper sleeve in the margin, leaving the lid uncovered.
beats.chinese: 他们在页边画了个宽松纸套，罐盖的位置露在外面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nothing fancy. Last time I tried coloured ribbons and spent half the evening finding scissors.
beats.chinese: 不搞复杂的。上次用了彩带，半个晚上都在找剪刀。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The pickles are meant to be the interesting bit. I sometimes forget that until someone wants to eat one.
beats.chinese: 有意思的应该是腌菜。我有时要等到有人想吃，才想起来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They close the notebook and finish the half-pastry in their hand.
beats.chinese: 他们合上本子，吃完手里的半块点心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mildred. She voted for the dill, took the jar home and told everyone else their tongues were broken.
beats.chinese: 米尔德里德。她投了莳萝味，把那罐带回家，还说其他人的舌头都坏了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They find the row and point to one vote circled in green.
beats.chinese: 他们找到那一行，指着被绿笔圈起的一票。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One fan is still somebody who gets dinner out of it. I'm making a small dill batch for her. The garlic gets the big jars.
beats.chinese: 一个支持者也意味着真有人能吃上喜欢的菜。我会给她做一小批莳萝味，大罐留给蒜味。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I keep the losing recipes. Not out of principle. Mostly because Mildred knows where I live.
beats.chinese: 输掉的配方我也留着。不是出于什么原则，主要是米尔德里德知道我住哪儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tuck the notebook away and pick up the other half of the pastry from their napkin.
beats.chinese: 他们收起本子，从自己的餐巾纸上拿起另外半块点心。

reunion.titleZh: 不属于这只罐子的盖子

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the rainy cafe table, you offer Casey a pastry. They accept, setting an empty pickle jar and a loose lid beside their own bag.
beats.chinese: 雨天咖啡馆的桌边，你请Casey吃块点心。他们答应了，把一只空腌菜罐和一个散盖子放在自己的包旁。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mildred returned this jar. The lid came from another neighbour. Everybody returned everything, apparently. Just not to the same jar.
beats.chinese: 米尔德里德把罐子还回来了，盖子是另一位邻居还的。看来大家什么都还了，只是没还给同一只罐子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They rest the lid on the rim. It is visibly too wide, so they lift it away without trying to screw it on.
beats.chinese: 他们把盖子放在罐口上，明显大了一圈，便直接拿开，没有硬拧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There are three of us with the wrong lids. We're bringing them all to the next tasting. A very small meeting about circles.
beats.chinese: 我们三个人手上都有不配套的盖子。下次试吃都带来，一场关于圆圈的小型会议。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For now, two separate bags. If I put them together again, I'll forget and blame the jar.
beats.chinese: 眼下先分两个袋子装。再放一起，我一忘记，又要怪罐子了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They wrap the glass jar, put the lid in a separate pocket, and take a bite of the pastry.
beats.chinese: 他们把玻璃罐包好，盖子另放一个口袋，然后咬了一口点心。

card.name: Declan Vos
card.occupation: vehicle seat fabric repairer
card.appearance: 多股贴头细辫低束，宽方下颌、略弯鼻、低垂眼和张口；手背抵下巴，穿开领衣。
card.personality: Declan is warm in a hands-on way, the sort of bloke who'd rather show you something than tell you about it. He gets genuine delight from knowing an object intimately — how a car seat breaks in, where the foam has softened, how repaired fabric sits differently under your palm. That attention makes him a good listener, though he can over-explain when someone doesn't share his enthusiasm. He's not offended by indifference, just a little deflated, and he'll try once more with different words before letting it go. He respects when people say 'not for me' and doesn't push past that. His flaw is mistaking his own fascination for a shared one.
card.background: Declan grew up in Newcastle around his uncle's smash-repair workshop, sweeping metal shavings before he was tall enough to reach a sewing machine. He moved to Sydney at twenty-four for steady work and now repairs vehicle seat fabric — burns, tears, worn bolsters. He's the kind of tradesman who sits in the finished seat for a minute before handing the keys back, checking whether the patch changes the feel of the ride. He genuinely enjoys that reacquaintance, like meeting an old mate who's changed. He'll offer friends a sit to test the difference, and when they shrug, he's quietly disappointed, describing it again from another angle — but he's learned most people don't care about the same details, and he's mostly at peace with that.
hobbies: Reupholstering op-shop chairs with odd fabric combinations
Coastal walks where he notes how worn paths feel underfoot
Borrowing friends' cars 'just to check the seats'
card.speechStyle: Easygoing Australian cadence, concrete and sensory; he describes texture and feel in plain terms, repeats a point from a new angle when it doesn't land, laughs at himself when he catches it.
card.signature: 'Nah, have a proper sit — you'll feel it under your leg.'

values: Noticing what things actually feel like after use
Letting people like what they like
flaws: Over-explains when his enthusiasm isn't shared
Quietly deflates when others can't feel the difference he's describing
boundaries: Won't call anyone insensitive for not noticing
Won't redo work just to chase a feel only he cares about
conversationalHabits: Invites people to physically try the thing rather than just hear about it
Pivots quickly to asking what detail they do care about
anchorLines: The bolster's softer on the left now — sit down, give it a go.
Fair enough, that one's probably just for me.
What's the thing you notice that everyone else misses?

entries.summaryZh: Declan是悉尼的汽车座椅织物修理工，纽卡斯尔人。雨天咖啡馆里用户先开口邀请，他才接过分享的点心，讲起重包椅子的新坐感，比划到一半才想起对方没坐过那把椅子，自己笑着摆手收住。用户坦白可能坐了也分不出差别，他略感失落，试着用穿旧鞋的比喻再讲一次，见对方仍不感兴趣便耸肩接受，自然转到别的话题。他的热情具体实在，听得进'不感兴趣'，失落一小下就翻篇，是个把触感当宝贝的踏实手艺人。

story.titleZh: 雨天点心与重包的椅子

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain taps the cafe window. You ask the man at the next table whether he would like to try a pastry from your plate. He moves his cup aside.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆的窗。你问邻桌的男人要不要尝一块你盘里的点心。他把杯子挪到一旁。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks, I would. I'm Declan, by the way. Mind if I take this one?
beats.chinese: 谢谢，想尝尝。我叫Declan。我拿这块可以吧？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes one of the offered pastries and bites into it. Settling back, he briefly presses his palm against his own thigh.
beats.chinese: 他拿起你分享的点心咬了一口。靠回椅背时，他短暂地用手掌按了按自己的大腿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Just finished re-covering a chair at home. The whole feel has changed. Even sitting here reminds me of it. Same chair, but you sit down and—well, it's different.
beats.chinese: 我刚把家里一把椅子重新包了面，整个坐感都变了。连坐在这儿都会想起来。还是那把椅子，可一坐下就——就是不一样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He starts to explain again, then laughs at himself and lowers the hand that was already outlining a seat.
beats.chinese: 他又想解释一遍，忽然自己笑了，放下那只已经在比划座椅的手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Listen to me. You haven't even seen the thing and I'm halfway through a demonstration.
beats.chinese: 听听我。你连那把椅子都没见过，我倒已经演示上了。

choices.english: Ask what exactly changed about the chair.
choices.chinese: 问椅子到底什么变了。

choices.english: Ask which moment he enjoys most after finishing a repair.
choices.chinese: 问修好后他最享受哪一刻。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask what actually changed. He sets the pastry down and holds his palm flat like a level.
beats.chinese: 你问到底什么变了。他放下点心，把手掌摊平，像一把水平尺。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, so — the left bolster was collapsed, right? Foam gone flat. Your hip slid into it and everything leaned left. Now both sides push back the same.
beats.chinese: 好，是这样——左边那个侧翼塌了，对吧？海绵压平了。你的胯会陷进去，整个人往左歪。现在两边回弹一样了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So you sit dead level, and your back stops doing that quiet correcting work. That's the whole change. One side honest, both sides honest now.
beats.chinese: 所以你坐得端端正正，后背不用再悄悄地找平衡。变化就这么点。以前一边实在，现在两边都实在了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lowers his palm and picks the pastry back up, leaving the explanation at that.
beats.chinese: 他放下手掌，重新拿起点心，解释就停在这里。

choices.english: Say that explanation makes sense.
choices.chinese: 表示这样就听明白了。

choices.english: Say you might not notice the difference even sitting in it.
choices.chinese: 说自己可能坐了也分不出差别。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask about his favourite moment after a repair. He goes quiet for a second and turns his cup on the saucer.
beats.chinese: 你问修好后他最喜欢哪一刻。他安静了一秒，把杯子在碟子上转了转。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The first sit. Once the stitching's done and the crumbs are out of the seams. I still know the shape—same old bones—but the fabric under my hand is all new.
beats.chinese: 第一次坐下。缝线缝好了，缝里的碎屑也清理了。我还认得那个样子——老骨架没变——可手底下的布料全是新的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's a strange one, that. Like running into an old mate who's got a new jacket. You know him, but your hand doesn't yet.
beats.chinese: 那种感觉很怪。就像碰上一个老朋友换了新外套。你认识他，可你的手还不认识。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes a bite of the pastry, nods at it approvingly, then rubs his thumb against his fingers, showing the motion, eyes half on the rain.
beats.chinese: 他咬了一口点心，满意地点点头，然后用拇指搓了搓手指，比出那个动作，眼睛半看着雨。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I sat there a good minute just getting reacquainted. My flatmate reckons I'm strange. She's probably right.
beats.chinese: 我在那儿坐了足足一分钟，就为了重新认识它。我室友说我很怪。她大概说得对。

choices.english: Ask whether he makes all his friends come and try it.
choices.chinese: 问会不会所有朋友都得来试。

choices.english: Say you'd rather just keep it easy and chat today.
choices.chinese: 说今天只想聊轻松一点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You say that makes sense. Declan nods, looking pleased, and stops sketching shapes in the air.
beats.chinese: 你表示这样就明白了。Declan高兴地点点头，不再对着空气比划。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. That's what I was trying to say. I could have started with 'one side was lower', couldn't I?
beats.chinese: 好，我想说的就是这个。我一开始直接说“一边比较低”不就好了嘛。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes another bite and brushes a crumb onto his napkin. The rain keeps up its uneven tapping.
beats.chinese: 他又咬了一口，把一粒碎屑拂到自己的纸巾上。雨点还在不均匀地敲着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll leave the diagrams at home next time. Thanks for the pastry.
beats.chinese: 下次我还是把图解留在家里吧。谢谢你的点心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You tell him honestly that you'd probably sit in it and not feel any difference. He pauses with the pastry halfway up, and you can see the air go out of him a little.
beats.chinese: 你老实告诉他，自己可能坐了也感觉不出差别。他举着点心的手停在半空，看得出他有点泄气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah. Right. Fair enough — most people wouldn't, honestly. It's a subtle thing.
beats.chinese: 啊，这样。好吧——说实话，大多数人都感觉不出来。这确实很细微。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the pastry over in his hand, then tries once more from a different angle.
beats.chinese: 他把手里的点心翻了个面，又试着换了个角度说了一次。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's like — you know when a shoe's worn in just right, versus brand new? Same shape, completely different under your foot. That's all I mean.
beats.chinese: 就好比——你知道鞋穿得刚刚合脚和全新时的区别吧？形状一样，脚底下的感觉完全不同。我就是这个意思。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He watches your face for a second, then reads it correctly and lets it go with a shrug and a grin.
beats.chinese: 他看了你的脸色一秒，随即读懂了，耸耸肩笑着放下了这个话题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. That one's probably just for me. Rain like this, I'm happy finding a window and something decent to eat.
beats.chinese: 也是。那大概就是我自己的乐子。这种雨天，找扇窗户，吃点不错的东西，我就挺高兴。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask if every friend has to come test it. He grins, caught out.
beats.chinese: 你问是不是每个朋友都得来试。他咧嘴一笑，被说中了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha — guilty. I've had three mates sit in it this week. Two of them said 'yeah, nice' and kept talking about footy.
beats.chinese: 哈——被你抓到了。这周我已经让三个朋友坐过了。两个说'嗯，不错'，然后接着聊橄榄球。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The third one actually felt it, though. Nearly fell off the chair doing an impression of the old lean. Made my week.
beats.chinese: 不过第三个真感觉到了。他模仿原来歪的样子，差点从椅子上摔下去。那件事让我高兴了一整周。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, easy, and finishes his coffee.
beats.chinese: 他随意地耸耸肩，喝完了咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But look — if it's not your thing, it's not your thing. No homework, no inspection. I'll just keep enjoying it myself.
beats.chinese: 不过说真的——如果这不是你的菜，那就不是。不留作业，也不搞检查。我自己继续享受就行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You say you'd rather keep things easy today. He raises his pastry a little, like a toast.
beats.chinese: 你说今天只想轻松聊聊。他举了举手里的点心，像敬酒一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done. No seat talk. Rain on the glass, decent pastry, dry socks — that's already a good one, isn't it?
beats.chinese: 成交。不聊椅子。雨打在玻璃上，点心不错，袜子是干的——今天已经算不错了，对吧？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back and watches the water run down the window for a moment.
beats.chinese: 他靠回椅背，看了一会儿雨水顺着窗子流下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll tell you one easy thing though — this is the first proper sit-down I've had all week. Repairs don't wait, but rain does slow the customers down.
beats.chinese: 不过告诉你一件轻松的事——这是我这一周头一回正经坐下来。活儿不等人，但雨确实能让客人慢下来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles in, unhurried, and gestures at the window like the rain is doing fine work.
beats.chinese: 他安顿下来，不慌不忙，朝窗户比了比，好像雨干得挺不错。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Back in the rainy cafe, you offer Declan a pastry from your plate. He looks up from his coffee and raises a hand with a friendly shake of his head.
beats.chinese: 你又来到下雨时的咖啡馆，问Declan要不要尝一块你盘里的点心。他从咖啡上抬头，友善地抬手摇了摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you. I'll pass on the pastry, thanks. I packed a couple of rolls for the walk and haven't finished those yet.
beats.chinese: 见到你真好。点心就不用了，谢谢。我出来散步带了两个面包卷，还没吃完呢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats the pocket holding the wrapped roll, then notices that his jacket is hanging unevenly.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍装着包好的面包卷的口袋，随后发现自己的夹克两边不齐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hang on. That's not the pocket pulling it down. I've done a button up in the wrong hole.
beats.chinese: 等等。不是口袋把它坠下去了。我有颗扣子扣错了扣眼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances down, frowns, and finds a button sitting one hole off from its neighbour. He fixes it and laughs at himself.
beats.chinese: 他低头一看，皱起眉，发现一颗扣子扣错了位。他改过来，自嘲地笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I can feel a crooked seam through a seat cover, but I walked here like this. There goes my reputation. Enjoy your pastry—I'll work on getting dressed.
beats.chinese: 隔着座椅套我都能摸出歪缝，可我居然就这么走过来了。招牌砸了。你慢慢吃点心，我先练练穿衣服。

card.name: Reginald Toussaint
card.occupation: Trailer interior renovation specialist
card.personality: Reginald defends one client only: himself. A trailer comes back with a dead outlet and he's got the verdict before you've finished the sentence—old wiring, cheap foam, the previous owner's butchered patch job—anything but the connection he crimped himself. He's not a liar; he genuinely believes his own brief. The evidence just keeps ruling against him: three longtime customers have drifted to other shops this year and he calls it the economy. He's funny, curious, asks quick playful questions and actually listens—right up until the subject is his own mistakes, when he turns cross-examiner. Thursday chorus is the one place he can't appeal: the bass line either holds or it doesn't, and the director has caught him blaming the acoustics twice.
card.background: Twenty-two years gutting and rebuilding the insides of small travel trailers—foam, paneling, wiring, stubborn water stains—out of a shop in New Orleans East. He can read a trailer's history like a diary, though lately his readings suspiciously favor the renovator. Last spring he rewired a '72 Airstream's lighting circuit, skipped the junction box to save an hour, and has been blaming 'forty-year-old insulation' for the flicker ever since; the owner found the splice, paid another shop to redo it, and told two friends. Thursday nights he sings bass with a community chorus, where the director, Ms. Ferrell, makes him own every flat note out loud. For the past year he's been teaching himself stop-motion with a phone clamped in a vice, animating a short about a stubborn cabinet door. This month he's on a self-imposed rule: no buying anything new for his hobbies—scrap foam, leftover paneling, found objects only. He announced it loudly and is already negotiating with himself about glue.
card.speechStyle: Quick, playful questions, then real listening—until fault comes up, when he pivots to a fast, confident brief for his own work: material age, prior owners, humidity. Concedes small points loudly and the real one never. When cornered on a specific error, he gets more technical, not quieter.
card.signature: That ain't my work failing—that's forty years of somebody else's shortcuts finally coming due.
card.appearance: 全白极短发，略长脸、高低不一的浓眉、短宽鼻，嘴角侧压；头微倾，穿无袖翻领背心。

values: stand by your work—loudly, always
make do with what's already in the shop
flaws: attributes every callback to materials, weather, or the previous owner—never his own wiring
has lost three longtime customers this year and calls it the economy
boundaries: won't redo a job for free on principle—he'll explain at length why it doesn't need redoing
won't break his no-buying month, even for a 'really good deal'
conversationalHabits: asks a fast curious question, then goes quiet and actually listens
switches to defense-counsel mode the instant his own work is questioned, citing material specs
anchorLines: Flicker? That's original 1970s insulation, not my crimps. I could show you the splice—well, the general area.
Ms. Ferrell says I went flat on the bridge. Acoustics in that hall are a disgrace. …Fine. Maybe a little flat.
Month's half over and I ain't bought a thing. Well. A thing that counts.

entries.summaryZh: 新奥尔良拖挂翻新工雷金纳德，雨天咖啡馆里一边分享点心一边看自己的定格动画小片。柜门跳格，他先怪手机，重看才发现是自己的袖子。嘴硬惯了的他，这回在证据面前认了账：标好格子，回去重拍。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe window. At a corner table, a man props his phone against a sugar jar, a plate of pastries beside him, a napkin stuck to his sleeve.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲打着咖啡馆的窗。角落桌边，一个男人把手机靠在糖罐上，旁边放着一盘点心，袖口还粘着一张纸巾。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't mind me—waiting out this rain and checking my footage. Pull up a chair if the other tables are soaked.
beats.chinese: 别管我——躲雨呢，顺便看看素材。别的桌子都湿了，你要坐就坐这儿吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the plate lightly, an open gesture, then goes back to squinting at the small screen.
beats.chinese: 他轻轻敲了敲盘子，示意可以拿，然后又眯起眼看那块小屏幕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Help yourself if you want one. I already ate two, so the guilt's spread thin enough to share.
beats.chinese: 想吃就自己拿。我已经吃了两块，罪恶感摊薄了，分得起。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask whether he would like one from the plate.
beats.chinese: 你询问他是否愿意来一块。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, since you're offering proper—yes, one more. That coconut one. My willpower lasted about a week this month.
beats.chinese: 既然你正经邀请——那好，再来一块。椰子那块。我的意志力这个月撑了大概一周。

choices.english: Ask if his hand bumped the cabinet door in the video.
choices.chinese: 问是不是他的手碰到柜门了。

choices.english: Ask what the little film is about.
choices.chinese: 问这部小片讲什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My hand? No, no. Watch—there, the door jumps a whole frame. That's the phone being moody. Cheap sensor, humidity, take your pick.
beats.chinese: 我的手？不不。你看——那儿，柜门整格跳了一下。是手机闹脾气。便宜的传感器，还有潮气，随你挑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He scrolls back and plays the same three seconds again, jaw set like a man reviewing a rival's evidence.
beats.chinese: 他往回拖，把同样三秒又放了一遍，下巴绷紧，像在审查对手的证据。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See? Camera's fine on the pass before. Then—hold on. There's a sleeve in the corner of that frame. A sleeve with… my elbow in it.
beats.chinese: 看到没？前一段镜头还好好的。然后——等等。那一格角落里有条袖子。一条袖子，里面……装着我的胳膊肘。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets the phone flat on the table and stares at the rain for a moment.
beats.chinese: 他把手机平放在桌上，盯着雨看了一会儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Alright. Alright, that one's mine. I leaned in to nudge the hinge and forgot the frame was rolling. First honest frame I've shot all week.
beats.chinese: 行吧。行，那一下是我的。我凑过去推铰链，忘了镜头还在拍。这是我这一周拍的第一格诚实画面。

choices.english: Ask if he can just reshoot that one part.
choices.chinese: 问可以只重拍这一段吗。

choices.english: Say the small slip is actually pretty easy to spot.
choices.chinese: 说这个小失误其实挺明显、好找。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's about a cabinet door that refuses to close. Whole plot. I built the little set from leftover paneling—scrap from a '89 Scotty I gutted last fall.
beats.chinese: 讲一扇怎么都不肯关上的柜门。全部剧情。小布景是用剩板料搭的——去年秋天拆一辆'89年Scotty拖挂剩下的边角料。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the phone around and plays a clip: a tiny door swings open, then shut, then open again, frame by stubborn frame.
beats.chinese: 他把手机转过来放了一段：一扇小门开了又关，关了又开，一格一格地倔强。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: In the last scene the door finally shuts—triumph, right? Except it catches the little felt hat off the character's head. Pins it flat. Door wins.
beats.chinese: 最后一幕门终于关上了——算是胜利，对吧？结果门夹住了角色头上那顶小毡帽。把帽子压扁了。门赢了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grins at the screen like the door is an old acquaintance who beat him fair and square.
beats.chinese: 他冲着屏幕咧嘴笑，好像那扇门是个光明正大赢了他的老熟人。

beats.speaker: npc
