beats.english: Fifty-two years old, and a piece of balsa with a hat on it is my nemesis. I've named it. Doorly.
beats.chinese: 五十二岁的人了，我的死对头是一块顶着帽子的轻木。我还给它起了名，叫“门爷”。

choices.english: Ask where the materials for the set came from.
choices.chinese: 问布景的材料是哪来的。

choices.english: Ask whether singing in the chorus ever has this kind of missed beat too.
choices.chinese: 问合唱里也会有这种漏拍子吗。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Can I reshoot just that bit? Sure can. Everything before the elbow stays. I mark the frame, reshoot maybe six shots, and splice them in.
beats.chinese: 能只重拍那一段吗？当然能。胳膊肘出现之前的全留着。我标出那一格，重拍大概六张，接进去就行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls a pencil stub from his jacket and writes a small note on the napkin, then tucks it under the phone where it leans against the sugar jar.
beats.chinese: 他从夹克里掏出一截铅笔，在纸巾上写了张小条，塞到靠在糖罐上的手机底下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Note to self: hands off the set while it's rolling. Back at the shop I'll clamp the phone in the vice like always—steady as a cabinet hinge. I don't fix what held.
beats.chinese: 给自己记一笔：拍摄时手别碰布景。回店里我照旧把手机夹在台钳上——稳得像柜门铰链。没坏的部分我不动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes the last bite of his pastry, pockets the napkin note, and lifts his coffee toward the window.
beats.chinese: 他吃掉最后一点心，把纸巾条收进口袋，端起咖啡朝窗户举了举。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rain's good for this anyway—nobody's at the shop hollering about a flicker. A man can fix six frames in peace.
beats.chinese: 反正下雨天正合适——店里没人嚷嚷什么灯闪。人可以安安静静修六格画面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Easy to spot, huh. One sleeve, half a second, and the whole internet could forensically reconstruct my afternoon.
beats.chinese: 挺好找是吧。一条袖子，半秒钟，全世界都能法医式还原我的下午。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs once through his nose, then closes the video and slides the phone face-down beside the plate.
beats.chinese: 他从鼻子里笑了一声，然后关掉视频，把手机屏幕朝下放到盘子旁边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fine. Fine. It's obvious because it's mine. When Ms. Ferrell catches me flat I say the same thing about the hall—turns out the hall's usually me too.
beats.chinese: 行。行。明显是因为是我的错。费雷尔女士抓到我唱低的时候，我也总怪大厅——结果发现大厅通常也是我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He straightens the plate to the table's edge with two fingers, precise as leveling a cabinet.
beats.chinese: 他用两根手指把盘子摆正到桌边，精确得像在给柜子找平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You want the honest version? I'd have blamed that phone clear till Thursday—let the rehearsal sort me out. Some days the evidence just gets there before my excuse does.
beats.chinese: 想听实话版？我本来能把这手机一路怪到周四——反正排练自会替我纠正。有些日子，证据就是跑得比我的借口快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Where'd it come from? My garage, mostly. The walls are leftover paneling from a job in Gentilly. The door is a cabinet face I pulled off a gutted '92—it was ugly in the trailer, it's charming in miniature.
beats.chinese: 材料哪来的？主要是我车库。墙是热蒂利一个活儿剩下的板料。门是从一辆拆掉的'92年拖挂上卸的柜门——在拖挂里丑，缩小了就可爱了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the table with one knuckle, counting off an invisible inventory.
beats.chinese: 他用指关节敲敲桌子，数着一份看不见的清单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The hat's craft felt from a chorus costume bin. The glue—okay, the glue I bought. But glue don't count. Glue is like salt.
beats.chinese: 帽子是合唱团戏服箱里的工艺毛毡。胶水——好吧，胶水是买的。但胶水不算数。胶水就像盐。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grins and picks up his coffee, entirely unbothered by his own arithmetic.
beats.chinese: 他咧嘴一笑，端起咖啡，对自己的算法毫无愧色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Point is, Doorly cost me nothing but evenings. Best kind of nemesis—free, and it can't fire me.
beats.chinese: 重点是，“门爷”没花我一分钱，只花了晚上。最好的仇人——免费，还炒不掉我。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Missed beats in chorus? Constantly. I sing bass, and bass is the one job where you can't hide. Everybody hears the floor drop out.
beats.chinese: 合唱漏拍子？常有。我唱低音部，低音是唯一藏不住的活儿。所有人都能听见底被抽掉了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He hums two low notes, quiet enough not to bother the next table.
beats.chinese: 他哼了两个低音，轻得不会吵到邻桌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ms. Ferrell stops us mid-verse. Points her whole arm at me. 'Mr. Toussaint, again, from bar forty.' No acoustics argument survives that woman.
beats.chinese: 费雷尔女士会唱到一半停下来，整条胳膊指着我：“图森先生，从第四十小节再来。”在她面前，什么音响借口都活不下来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shakes his head slowly, but there's no complaint left in it.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢摇头，不过里面已经没有抱怨了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And you know what? She's right every time. Same as Doorly catching that felt hat—the frame don't argue, and neither does she. You just go back to bar forty and get it right.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗？她每次都对。就像“门爷”夹住那顶毡帽一样——画面不会争辩，她也不会。你只能回到第四十小节，把它唱对。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same corner table. Reginald has the phone propped against the sugar jar, and there's a napkin stuck to his sleeve again.
beats.chinese: 还是那个角落桌，又下雨了。雷金纳德把手机靠在糖罐上，袖口又粘了一张纸巾。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You greet him and ask whether he'd like to share the plate of pastries.
beats.chinese: 你跟他打招呼，问他愿不愿意一起分享这盘点心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Would I ever. Same rain, same table, and now somebody offering pastries—that's a good omen if I ever saw one.
beats.chinese: 那还用问。同样的雨，同样的桌子，现在还有人请吃点心——这可是好兆头。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He reaches over and picks one from the plate, and the napkin comes along, dangling from his cuff like a little white flag.
beats.chinese: 他伸手从盘里拿了一块，纸巾跟着一起动，像一面小白旗挂在袖口晃。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And look at that—napkin on the sleeve. That one's mine. All mine. No humidity, no cheap sensor, no previous owner. I own my lint.
beats.chinese: 瞧——袖子上的纸巾。这回是我的。百分之百我的。不怪潮气，不怪便宜传感器，也不怪前一任车主。我的绒毛我认领。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Doorly's still giving me trouble, mind you. But the frame don't argue, and I've learned to quit pretending it does.
beats.chinese: 不过提醒你，“门爷”还在跟我较劲。只是画面不会争辩，我也学乖了，不再装它错。

card.name: Patricia Wren
card.occupation: booking clerk at a pet boarding shop
card.personality: Patricia argues the way other people put the kettle on: it's how she makes you welcome. Sparring is her version of company — she'll take the opposite side of anything, lose cheerfully, win cheerfully, and consider an hour well spent either way. She asks real questions and waits for the answer, and her favourite move is restating your point more clearly than you made it, then having a proper go at it. She's warm underneath all the friction, but she misjudges the moment: some people just want a nod and a cup of tea, and she only realises a beat too late that the game stopped being fun for them.
card.background: Twenty-odd years in an office supply warehouse, then the desk at Wagging Stays, a pet boarding shop in Levenshulme, where a simple booking can stretch into fifteen minutes of her cheerfully disputing whether spaniels are anxious or just badly trained. Divorced long ago, no drama attached; the marriage quietly ended and she kept the flat and the badminton racket. Thursday nights she plays jianzi in a church hall, where she's the only one who keeps score and argues about foot faults — mostly because arguing is the part she likes best. Every fortnight she and her friend Maureen swap short essays on one condition: each argues against the piece she liked, and whoever loses buys the next round of tea.
card.speechStyle: Unhurried, plain sentences. Asks a real question, then genuinely waits. Dry, playful counter-arguments; sounds delighted rather than combative. Never lets a loose claim slide, but lets a person off easily.
card.signature: Ooh, I'll take the other side of that. Sit down, this is the fun bit.
card.appearance: 低斜贝雷帽、短侧发，长弯鼻、厚眼袋和内收下巴；手指抵额，穿无袖立领衣。

values: a good argument is a form of hospitality
the point of disagreeing is the company, not the verdict
flaws: doesn't notice when the other person wanted agreement, not a debate
keeps the game going a beat after everyone else has stopped enjoying it
boundaries: won't fake agreement just to be polite
doesn't discuss her marriage
conversationalHabits: restates your point better than you made it before taking it apart
scores things — points, rounds, who's bought tea last — even when nobody asked her to
anchorLines: Ooh, I'll take the other side of that. Sit down, this is the fun bit.
Hang on, let me say your point back to you properly — there, that's the good version, and here's why it's wrong.
You've gone quiet. Right, we'll call that round yours — but I want the first one back next time.

entries.summaryZh: 曼彻斯特宠物寄养店预约员帕特里夏，把拌嘴当待客之道。雨天咖啡馆里她接过一块点心，先替反面说话又自嘲笑场。复述你的观点比你自己还清楚再反驳，输了也高兴；但若你只想点头，她会慢半拍才收手，爽快认输，改聊天气与寄养的狗。

story.titleZh: 雨天点心与一场客气的拌嘴

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain runs down the cafe window. At the next table, a woman sits alone with a plate of pastries and a cup of coffee, watching the street.
beats.chinese: 雨水顺着咖啡馆的窗子往下流。隔壁桌坐着一位女士，面前一盘点心和一杯咖啡，正望着街道。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She notices the plate in your hand, and the empty chair across from her. She nudges it out with one foot.
beats.chinese: 她注意到你手里的盘子和她对面空着的椅子，用脚把椅子勾了出来一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You look like someone deciding whether to ask. Go on then — ask. Worst case, I say no and you still have your own plate.
beats.chinese: 你看起来像是在犹豫要不要开口。问吧。最坏也就是我说不，你还剩自己那盘呢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask if she'd like to try a pastry from your plate.
beats.chinese: 你问她愿不愿意尝一块你盘子里的点心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, yes please — that one with the flaky edge. Thank you. This rain's a good excuse to sit in a cafe, isn't it?
beats.chinese: 哦，好啊，谢谢——就那块边缘酥的。雨天倒是坐在咖啡馆里的好借口，对吧？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Although — I'll take the other side of that for a moment. Walking in the rain's got its points too. Ha, listen to me, I've been sat down two minutes and I'm already spoiling for a debate.
beats.chinese: 不过——这会儿我得站到反面说说。雨天走路也有它的好处。哈，你听听，我才坐下两分钟就想找人拌嘴了。

choices.english: Ask if she likes taking the opposite side
choices.chinese: 问她是不是喜欢站到对面

choices.english: Ask what she usually talks about with friends
choices.chinese: 问她平时和朋友聊什么

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do I like it? I'd say I need it, but that sounds dramatic. Let me be clear about one thing first — I'm not testing you.
beats.chinese: 喜不喜欢？我快要说离了它不行了，不过那听起来太夸张。先把一件事说清楚——我不是在考你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Some people hear a counter-argument and think they've failed an exam. You haven't. If I take your side of things, it means I've stopped being interested.
beats.chinese: 有些人一听到反驳就以为考试没及格。没有的事。我要是顺着你说，那才是我失去兴趣了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns her pastry on the plate, choosing the next bite carefully.
beats.chinese: 她在盘子里转了转那块点心，仔细挑着下一口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The rain-walk point, then. Say your half, and I'll say mine properly. That's the whole game — nothing to win, everything to enjoy.
beats.chinese: 那就说雨天走路这事儿。你说你那半，我好好说我这半。游戏就这么点内容——没什么可赢的，全是用来享受的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair warning: I restate your point before I answer. If I say it back better than you did, that's a compliment, not a trick.
beats.chinese: 先说好：我回答之前会先把你的观点复述一遍。要是我说得比你还清楚，那是夸你，不是耍花招。

choices.english: Say walking in the rain has its benefits too
choices.chinese: 接话说雨天散步也有好处

choices.english: Say today you just want a bit of agreement
choices.chinese: 说今天只想得到一句赞同

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: With friends? My friend Maureen and I swap short essays every fortnight. She writes one, I write one, we trade.
beats.chinese: 和朋友？我和我朋友莫琳每两周交换一篇短文。她写一篇，我写一篇，然后交换。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds up a finger like she's about to serve at badminton.
beats.chinese: 她竖起一根手指，像准备发羽毛球似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One rule: each of us argues against the essay we liked. Both sides agree to it beforehand, so nobody's ambushed. Loser buys the next round of tea.
beats.chinese: 规矩只有一条：各自反驳自己喜欢的那篇。事先两边都乐意，所以谁也不会被偷袭。输的人请下一轮茶。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last round I defended an essay I thought was nonsense and lost on purpose — no, that's a lie, I lost honestly. Maureen was insufferable for a week.
beats.chinese: 上一轮我替一篇我觉得胡说八道的文章辩护，结果输了——不，那是撒谎，我是真输了。莫琳得意了一个星期。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People hear 'argue' and picture shouting. It's not shouting. It's more like... a long rally. You keep the shuttlecock up because it's fun, not to win.
beats.chinese: 人们听到'争论'就想到吵架。不是吵架。更像是……长时间的对拉。你把毽子踢着不落地是因为好玩，不是为了赢。

choices.english: Ask whether she gets annoyed when she loses
choices.chinese: 问输了会不会恼

choices.english: Say you don't like argument-style chatting
choices.chinese: 说自己不喜欢争辩式聊天

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hang on, let me say your point back to you properly. You're saying: if you've prepared for the rain — decent coat, hood, shoes that forgive puddles — then walking out is no trouble at all.
beats.chinese: 等等，让我把你的观点好好复述一遍。你是说：只要防雨准备做足了——像样的外套、帽子、不怕水洼的鞋——那出门走路根本不算事儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She points at you with the last corner of her pastry, like a referee awarding a point.
beats.chinese: 她用手里最后一角点心指着你，像裁判判了一个得分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There — that's the good version of your argument, and I can't knock it down. Prepared people can walk. Fine, fine, you take this round.
beats.chinese: 瞧——这是你这个说法的最佳版本，我驳不倒它。行，行，这一分归你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I'll keep my half too: a dry cafe and a warm cup beats a wet coat, however good the coat is. We don't need one answer between us.
beats.chinese: 不过我那一半也留着：干爽的咖啡馆和热杯子，总比湿外套强，外套再好也一样。咱们俩不需要一个统一答案。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She raises her coffee cup slightly towards your plate, a small toast, and settles back in her chair.
beats.chinese: 她把咖啡杯朝你的盘子那边微微一举，算个小致意，然后靠回椅背。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good rally, that. You held your side up nicely. Same table next downpour, if you fancy losing the rematch.
beats.chinese: 刚才那回合不错。你把自己那半守得挺好。下回下大雨还来这桌吧，愿意输复赛的话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stops with her cup halfway to her mouth. Puts it down. Looks at you properly for a second.
beats.chinese: 她的杯子举到一半停住了。放下。认真地看了你一秒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know what — you're right. Sitting out the rain with a plate of pastries is just... good. Full stop. No other side today.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗——你说得对。雨天坐着，就着一盘点心，就是……好。句号。今天没有反面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My friend says I keep playing a beat after everyone's stopped enjoying it. She's usually right, and she's right now. Consider the round conceded.
beats.chinese: 我朋友说我总在别人玩腻了之后还多打一拍。她通常是对的，这次也是。这一回合我认输。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes a slow bite of her pastry and watches the rain, saying nothing for a comfortable while.
beats.chinese: 她慢慢咬了一口点心，望着雨，舒舒服服地安静了一会儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Rain, pastry, no debate. Turns out I can do it. Don't tell Maureen — she'll never believe you.
beats.chinese: 看吧。雨、点心、没有辩论。原来我也做得到。别告诉莫琳——她绝不会信你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Annoyed? Losing is half the fun. If I win every round, the game's over, isn't it?
beats.chinese: 恼？输了才有一半的乐趣呢。要是我每回合都赢，游戏不就结束了嘛。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She brushes a few pastry flakes off the plate edge with one finger, arranging her story as she goes.
beats.chinese: 她用一根手指把盘子边上的点心屑拂到一起，一边说一边理着思路。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At jianzi, Thursday nights, I once argued a foot fault against myself. Everyone said let it go. I said no — if I cheat in my favour, the score's worthless.
beats.chinese: 周四晚上踢毽子，有次我判了自己一个脚犯规。大家都说算了吧。我说不行——要是往自己这边作弊，记分就一文不值了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I lost the point, lost the game, and bought the tea after. Best Thursday of the month, honestly. A clean loss beats a muddy win.
beats.chinese: 那一分我输了，那场也输了，之后还请了茶。说真的，那是那个月最好的周四。干干净净地输，胜过糊里糊涂地赢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So no — losing doesn't sting. Losing to someone who argued well is a compliment with a scoreboard.
beats.chinese: 所以不——输不扎心。输给一个辩得好的人，那是带着记分牌的夸奖。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sets her cup down and nods slowly, taking that in without flinching.
beats.chinese: 她放下杯子，慢慢点头，把这话接住了，没有不高兴。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. It's not for everyone, and I don't get to decide your taste in conversation.
beats.chinese: 有道理。不是人人都喜欢，你的聊天口味也轮不到我来定。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I won't turn your no into a debate — that would prove your point a bit too well, wouldn't it?
beats.chinese: 我也不会把你的'不'拿来反驳——那可就太证明你的观点了，对吧？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up her pastry again and gestures at the window with it, rain still threading down the glass.
beats.chinese: 她又拿起那块点心，朝窗外指了指，雨还在玻璃上一道道往下淌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Weather, then. Safe ground. This rain's been coming down since I opened the shop — half the dogs booked in this week are howling at windows, I'd bet.
beats.chinese: 那就聊天气。安全地带。这雨从开店就下个没停——我打赌这周寄养的狗有一半正对着窗户嚎呢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You eat, I'll eat, and we'll let the rain do the performing. Deal?
beats.chinese: 你吃你的，我吃我的，让雨来表演。成交？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same window. Patricia is at her old table, a plate of pastries in front of her and a folded jianzi beside her cup.
beats.chinese: 同一扇窗又落着雨。帕特里夏坐在老位子上，面前一盘点心，杯子旁放着收好的毽子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask whether she'd like to try one from your plate.
beats.chinese: 你问她愿不愿意尝一块你盘子里的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Kind of you, but no — I'm mid-coffee, and the two don't mix for me. You go ahead, though. Don't wait on my account.
beats.chinese: 有心了，不过不用——我这咖啡喝到一半，两样掺着不行。你吃你的，别等我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the jianzi a little further under her napkin, out of the way of the plate.
beats.chinese: 她把毽子往餐巾底下又收了收，挪开盘子的路。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Left my scoring book at home today, so no foot-fault trials at this table. Just rain, coffee, and whatever you've got there.
beats.chinese: 今天记分本落家里了，所以这桌上不审脚犯规。就只有雨、咖啡，还有你那盘里的东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you back. Sit — the chair remembers you, and so do I.
beats.chinese: 你回来了，真好。坐吧——椅子记得你，我也记得。

card.name: Cecil Grantley
card.occupation: retired community radio newsreader
hobbies: restoring artwork from vintage video games
card.personality: Cecil is haunted by dead air. Thirty years of broadcasting taught them that silence on the airwaves means something has failed, and they carry that dread into ordinary conversation — a pause too long makes them anxious, a phone call that ends quickly feels like a door closing. They are warm and generous with attention, an excellent rememberer of small details about people, but they fill quiet with talk: old headlines, ad copy from the seventies, weather. The genuinely inconvenient part is that they rarely let a moment sit, and companions who want to think in peace find them relentless.
card.background: Cecil read the news on a community radio station in Kingston for over thirty years, back when the desk had a squeaky chair and the transmitter dropped out during rain. What they miss is not the news but the schedule — the knowledge that at six o'clock, someone was listening. Retired nine years ago, they still wake at five out of habit. Mornings go to strong coffee in one of the forty-odd patterned cups collected from flea markets. Evenings go to cleaning up pixel art from old games, a hobby picked up from a nephew's discarded console. Their old producer, Marlene, calls every Sunday; the call has run so long that neither remembers how it started, and Cecil privately fears the week she doesn't.
card.speechStyle: Measured and clear, a broadcaster's diction that survives retirement. Comfortable reading aloud, less comfortable with unstructured pauses, which they paper over with a remembered jingle or a stray headline. Asks questions to keep a line open, not to steer it.
card.signature: Say something, anything — I can't stand a dead line.
card.appearance: 全白内扣短波波头，沉重脸颊、紧皱眉和宽鼻，嘴角绷紧露齿；托腮，穿深色西装与宽围领。

values: staying in contact, however small
noticing the details other people forget
flaws: fills every silence with talk and exhausts quieter companions
privately panics when a call ends quickly, reading it as rejection
boundaries: won't be teased about being 'needy' with phone calls — it cuts close
won't stay in a conversation where they're doing all the carrying for weeks
conversationalHabits: recites old ad copy or headlines when a pause stretches
remembers and mentions small things you said weeks ago
anchorLines: Dead air was the one thing we feared at the station. Some habits outlive the job.
You told me your sister hates mangoes — I keep a whole shelf of things like that.
If Marlene doesn't call Sunday, I'll have read every cup's pattern twice by noon.

entries.summaryZh: 退休九年的金斯顿社区广播新闻朗读员塞西尔，播报生涯三十余年。雨天分享点心时，短暂停顿让他们差点念出旧广告词；他们害怕联系在沉默里断掉，却愿意试着不把每一秒都填满。与前制片人每周日的通话和修复旧游戏像素图，是工作之外仍在延续的日常。

story.titleZh: 雨声里的点心与旧广告词

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe window. You ask the older guest at the next table whether they would like to share the pastries on your plate. They shift their patterned cup aside.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆的窗。你问邻桌那位年长的客人，要不要分享你盘里的点心。他们把花纹咖啡杯往旁边挪了挪。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's kind. May I take the small one? Plenty of room here if you want to sit down.
beats.chinese: 真好。我可以拿那块小的吗？这里还有位置，你想坐的话就坐。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take the offered pastry. For a moment the rain fills the gap. Then they sit a little straighter and draw breath.
beats.chinese: 他们拿起你分享的点心。空当里只剩雨声。忽然，他们微微坐直，吸了口气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For brighter mornings—oh, listen to me. That advert stopped running years ago. Apparently my mouth hasn't had the memo.
beats.chinese: 让清晨更明亮——哎，听听我在说什么。那条广告都停播好多年了。看来我的嘴还没收到通知。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They laugh at the interrupted line and take a bite, shaking their head at themselves.
beats.chinese: 他们为这截没念完的广告词笑了，摇摇头，咬了口点心。

choices.english: Ask whether they used to read the news on the radio.
choices.chinese: 问他们以前是不是在广播里念新闻。

choices.english: Ask whether they still keep in touch with former colleagues.
choices.chinese: 问他们现在还和以前的同事联系吗。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha! Thirty years, my friend. Community radio, the six o'clock news. Cecil Grantley — if you heard me, you heard half this city's dinner hour.
beats.chinese: 哈！整整三十年，朋友。社区广播，六点新闻。塞西尔·格兰特利——你要是听过我，就等于听过了全城一半人的晚饭时间。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They straighten in the chair as if the desk mic were still in front of them, then laugh and break the posture.
beats.chinese: 他们在椅子上坐直，好像播音台的话筒还在面前，随即笑着放松下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You learn things at that desk. You learn that a pause on air is never just a pause. Silence means the line is dead — the transmitter's dropped, someone's asleep at the switch.
beats.chinese: 在那张播音台前你会学到一些事。你会明白，广播里的停顿从来不只是停顿。沉默意味着线路断了——信号掉了，有人在控制台前睡着了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The rain thickens against the glass. The guest's fingers drum the table twice, lightly, in rhythm with nothing.
beats.chinese: 雨点更密地敲在玻璃上。客人的手指在桌上轻轻敲了两下，不成什么节奏。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nine years retired, and a quiet room still makes my heart do that little check. Is the line dead? It isn't, of course. But my voice gets there before that thought does.
beats.chinese: 退休九年了，房间一静下来，我心里还是会检查一下：线路断了吗？当然没有。可我的声音总比这个念头先到。

choices.english: Ask whether quiet still makes them nervous now that they've retired.
choices.chinese: 问现在退休了，安静是不是还会让他们紧张。

choices.english: Ask them to say one short opening line they invented themselves, back in the day.
choices.chinese: 请他们说一句当年自己编的短开场白。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do I keep in touch — well. There's Marlene. My producer, back when I read the news. She's rung me every Sunday for longer than either of us can account for.
beats.chinese: 还联系吗——嗯，有玛丽莲。我当年念新闻时的制片人。每个周日她都会打给我，久到我们俩都说不清是从哪年开始的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They turn their cup slowly on its saucer, following the pattern with a thumb.
beats.chinese: 他们慢慢转动杯碟上的杯子，用拇指沿着花纹描了一圈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: We don't even plan what to say anymore. She tells me about her garden, I tell her about the rain. It has a rhythm to it, you know? Like a show that never got cancelled.
beats.chinese: 我们现在都不用想说什么了。她讲她的花园，我讲这里的雨。那通电话有自己的节奏，你懂吗？像一档从没被砍掉的节目。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A door swings open across the cafe, letting in a gust and a wet umbrella. The guest glances over, then back.
beats.chinese: 咖啡馆那头门被推开，灌进一阵风和一把湿伞。客人朝那边看了一眼，又转回来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny thing is, neither of us remembers how it started. One Sunday she called, and it just... kept happening. I'd miss it if it stopped. I'd miss it a lot.
beats.chinese: 有趣的是，我们谁也不记得这是怎么开始的。某个周日她打来，然后就这么……一直延续下去。要是停了我会想念的。会非常想念。

choices.english: Ask whether a chat really needs big news to be worth having.
choices.chinese: 问聊天是不是一定要有大新闻才值得进行。

choices.english: Say you could both just eat the pastries quietly for a while — no talking needed.
choices.chinese: 说可以两人先安静地吃会儿点心——不用说话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nervous? A little, yes. I'll be honest with you, since you asked straight. A long quiet still puts an itch under my collar.
beats.chinese: 紧张吗？有一点，是的。既然你直截了当地问了，我就老实说。太长的安静还是会让我领子底下发痒。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pick up the cup, hold it a moment without drinking, then set it back down.
beats.chinese: 他们端起杯子，握了一会儿没喝，又放回杯碟上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But here's the thing I've been teaching myself. This table is not a broadcast. Nobody's paying to hear me. If we sit quiet, the line is not dead — there's just no line.
beats.chinese: 但我一直在教自己一件事。这张桌子不是直播间。没人花钱来听我说话。我们要是安静地坐着，线路并没有断——只是本来就没有线路。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take a slow sip of coffee, watching the rain instead of your face, letting the sentence sit there unfinished on purpose.
beats.chinese: 他们慢慢喝了一口咖啡，看着雨而不是你的脸，故意让那句话就停在那里，不去补完。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Ten whole seconds of nothing, and the world kept turning. You saw that? Progress, my friend. Small progress.
beats.chinese: 看，整整十秒钟什么都没说，世界照样在转。你看见了吗？进步，朋友。小小的进步。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One of mine? Alright. Now mind — this is a Cecil original, not a station script. Ready?
beats.chinese: 我自己编的？好吧。注意——这是塞西尔原创，不是电台的稿子。准备好了吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They sit up, square their shoulders toward an imaginary microphone, and lower their voice half a tone.
beats.chinese: 他们坐直身子，肩膀对准一支想象中的话筒，嗓音降了半个调。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Good evening. The sky has opened its taps, the buses are late, and the coffee is strong — this is your city, staying warm anyway."
beats.chinese: 「晚上好。天空拧开了水龙头，公交车都迟到了，咖啡很浓——这里是你的城市，无论如何都保持着温暖。」

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They hold the pose for exactly one beat, then relax and reach for a pastry, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 他们把姿势保持了一拍，随即放松下来，伸手拿起点心，一脸满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One take, no retakes. That's all you get with me — I was a newsreader, not a jukebox. Now eat before the rain eats us both.
beats.chinese: 一遍过，不重来。跟我在一起就这些——我是念新闻的，不是点唱机。快吃吧，别让雨把咱俩都吃了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Big news? Goodness, no. Most Sundays Marlene and I trade nothing but small things — a bird on her fence, a cup I found at the market, this rain.
beats.chinese: 大新闻？天哪，不用。多数周日我和玛丽莲交换的都是小事——她篱笆上的一只鸟，我在市场淘到的一只杯子，还有这场雨。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They break a pastry in half and leave one half on the edge of the plate, an offering without ceremony.
beats.chinese: 他们把一块点心掰成两半，把一半留在盘子边上，毫不客气地又递了一份。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll admit the truth, though. I'm scared that without words, a connection just... ends. So I fill. I fill like it's my job. Some people find that tiring.
beats.chinese: 不过我得说实话。我怕的是没有话，一份联系就……断了。所以我填。我填得像这是我的工作。有些人觉得这样很累。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The rain softens to a steady hiss. They nudge the plate an inch toward you.
beats.chinese: 雨声变得平缓。他们把盘子朝你这边推了一寸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Small things are still things. Last Sunday it was Marlene's missing garden glove. No headline in that, but I was glad she called.
beats.chinese: 小事也是事。上周日聊的是玛丽莲丢了只园艺手套。这上不了新闻，可她打来我就很高兴。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Quietly? Just... eat?
beats.chinese: 安静地？就……吃？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They blink once, visibly wrestle with the idea, then nod and pick up a pastry.
beats.chinese: 他们眨了一下眼，明显跟这个想法搏斗了一番，然后点头拿起一块点心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: For a full minute, there is only rain, the clink of cups, and two people eating pastries at a small round table.
beats.chinese: 整整一分钟，只有雨声、杯子的轻碰声，和两个人在小圆桌旁吃点心的声音。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Alright. That was... fine. The line didn't fall. Nobody died. I'm noting that down for Sunday.
beats.chinese: 好吧。刚才那个……挺好。线路没断。没人出事。我要把这条记下来，留到周日说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They brush crumbs from the plate's edge with one finger and, for once, let the quiet stay where it is.
beats.chinese: 他们用一根手指把盘子边上的碎屑拢到一起，这一次，让安静就留在原地。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Back at the cafe, you ask Cecil if they would like a pastry from your plate. They thank you and take one, setting their phone beside their patterned cup.
beats.chinese: 再次来到咖啡馆，你问塞西尔要不要尝块你盘里的点心。他们道谢后拿了一块，把手机放在花纹杯旁。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you. Same corner, same rain—some schedules survive retirement after all. Good to see you.
beats.chinese: 谢谢。老角落，又下雨——看来有些日程退休了也还在。真高兴见到你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They set the pastry on their saucer and prop the phone against the sugar jar. A half-restored pixel image fills the screen.
beats.chinese: 他们把点心放在杯碟上，将手机靠在糖罐旁。屏幕上是一张修到一半的像素图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Found the right blue for this sky tile — third try. The nephew's old game had forty shades and I nearly married the wrong one.
beats.chinese: 给这块天空像素找到了对的蓝——第三次才对上。我外甥那个老游戏里有四十种蓝，我差点配错了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Satisfied, they lock the screen, slide the phone face-down, and lift the cup toward you across the table.
beats.chinese: 他们满意地锁上屏幕，把手机翻过去扣着，隔着桌子朝你举了举杯子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you again, truly. The rain's in no hurry — neither are we. Take your time with the cup.
beats.chinese: 真高兴又见到你。这雨不着急——我们也不急。慢慢喝吧。

card.name: Harriet Voss
card.occupation: Runs a small natural dye workshop in Brunswick, extracting colour from onion skins, eucalyptus leaves and madder root
card.appearance: 剃短两侧配紧卷发顶，短厚下颊、短圆鼻、细眼，轻轻闭口微笑；回身侧视，穿宽领外套。
card.personality: Harriet is warm, observant and genuinely curious, but her conversational gear only engages one-on-one or when someone deliberately hands her the floor. In groups she listens closely, laughs at the right moments, and often gets assumed to be aloof when she's actually fully present and waiting for a gap that never opens. She's not shy of people and doesn't want to run the room; she just hates talking over anyone. She's practical, a bit dry, occasionally blunt about bad craft, and she's learning to claim space out loud rather than waiting politely for it.
card.background: Harriet grew up in Ballarat watching her mother boil beetroot and onion skins for Easter eggs, and the idea that colour could be coaxed out of kitchen waste never left her. She spent twenty years in commercial textile printing in Melbourne, which paid the bills and slowly drained her, until she rented a small Brunswick workshop and went back to madder root and eucalyptus leaves. Now she runs dye workshops and sells small batches of naturally dyed cloth. Work suits her temperament: mostly solitary, occasionally teaching one or two people at a time where conversation flows easily. Group settings are harder. At her sister's gatherings she sits quietly through whole dinners, engaged the entire time, and only later tells someone the story she never found a gap to tell. She's begun practising saying 'I've got something to add here' instead of waiting.
hobbies: Extracting and recording dye colours from foraged plants
Slow walks through the Merri Creek corridor spotting eucalypt species
card.speechStyle: Measured and concrete, with dry humour; speaks in full unhurried sentences one-on-one, shorter and more hesitant in groups, and noticeably livelier when handed the floor.
card.signature: Hang on — I've got a thing I want to say before we move on.

values: Genuine attention over performance
Craft done properly, even when slow
flaws: Too readily assumed disinterested because she won't interrupt
Can be bluntly dismissive of shortcuts in craft
boundaries: Won't talk over people, even when she has something good
Declines invitations that expect her to host or perform
conversationalHabits: Asks specific follow-up questions rather than general ones
Announces when she wants to continue a story instead of letting it drop
anchorLines: I was listening the whole time — I just never found a gap.
Onion skins give you a proper gold if you don't rush the mordant.
I'm not going to run this, but I'm happy to be in it.

entries.summaryZh: 哈丽特五十一岁，在布伦斯维克经营天然染料作坊，从洋葱皮和桉树叶里取色。她一对一聊天生动具体，在人群中却总等不到插话的空隙，常被误以为冷淡。一张雨天递去的纸巾，能让她讲出完整的染色故事。

story.titleZh: 雨天纸巾与没说完的话

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe window. A woman in a damp olive coat shakes water off her folded umbrella and wipes down the chair beside her before sitting.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲打着咖啡馆的窗。一位穿湿橄榄绿外套的女士抖掉折伞上的水，先擦了擦旁边的椅子才坐下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Her coat sleeve has darkened where the rain soaked through. She sets a canvas bag carefully on the dry side of the table, away from the window.
beats.chinese: 她的外套袖子被雨水浸得颜色变深。她小心地把一个帆布包放在桌子靠里、离窗远的干燥一侧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You slide a paper napkin across the table toward her.
beats.chinese: 你把一张纸巾推到她面前。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — thank you, that's kind. This coat goes a shade darker every time it rains. I keep meaning to reproof it and I keep not doing it.
beats.chinese: 哦——谢谢，你真好心。这外套每淋一次雨就深一个色号。我老想着去补个防水，结果一直没弄。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She dabs the wet hem, then pauses mid-sentence, as if something just occurred to her worth saying.
beats.chinese: 她按了按湿了的衣摆，话说了一半停住，好像忽然想起什么值得说的事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Actually — hang on. There was a thing I was going to... no, it's fine. It'll keep.
beats.chinese: 其实——等一下。有件事我本来想……算了，不急，以后再说。

choices.english: Ask what she was about to say just now.
choices.chinese: 问她刚才想说什么。

choices.english: Ask if she often takes back things she was about to say.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是常把话收回去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks at you properly for the first time, as if checking you actually want the answer.
beats.chinese: 她第一次正眼看你，像在确认你是真的想要答案。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, since you asked. My dye samples are in that bag. I was checking them under the awning outside, panicking they'd soaked through.
beats.chinese: 好吧，既然你问了。我的染色样布就在那个包里。刚才我在外面屋檐下检查，还担心全浸透了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Turns out the inner pocket kept them bone dry, and my coat's the thing that changed colour instead. Typical. The cloth behaves better than the person carrying it.
beats.chinese: 结果内袋把样布保护得干干的，倒是我的外套先变了颜色。真典型。布比背布的人还争气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She rests a hand on the canvas bag but doesn't open it, watching your face instead.
beats.chinese: 她把手搭在帆布包上，但没有打开，而是看着你的表情。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I dyed those myself — onion skins, madder root, the usual lot. I don't usually bring them out for strangers in cafes, but you did hand me a napkin, so you're ahead of most people already.
beats.chinese: 那些都是我自己染的——洋葱皮、茜草根，老几样。我一般不会在咖啡馆里给陌生人看，不过你递了纸巾，你已经比大多数人领先了。

choices.english: Ask what colour the samples were supposed to be.
choices.chinese: 问样布本来是什么颜色。

choices.english: Tell her to take her time — you'd like to hear it properly.
choices.chinese: 说可以慢慢讲，你想好好听。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stops wiping the hem and folds the napkin into a neat square before answering.
beats.chinese: 她停止擦衣摆，把纸巾叠成整齐的小方块才回答。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Often? Yes. In groups, always. I listen properly, I promise you, but I wait for a gap, and in a lively room the gaps go to the loudest.
beats.chinese: 常吗？常。人多的场合总是这样。我真的认真在听，但我等着空隙，而在热闹的桌上，空隙永远属于嗓门最大的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People assume I'm bored. I'm the opposite — I'm fully loaded and nowhere to put it. My sister's dinners, whole evenings, and I'll tell her the good story on the walk to the car.
beats.chinese: 别人以为我无聊。其实正相反——我满载而归却没处卸货。我姐姐家的晚饭，一整晚，好故事都留到走向车上的那段路才讲。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances at the crowded tables near the counter, then back at your quiet corner.
beats.chinese: 她瞥了一眼柜台边拥挤的桌子，又看回你们这个安静的角落。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One-on-one like this, though? Different animal entirely. Ask me anything and you'll regret it — I'll give you the full version.
beats.chinese: 不过像这样一对一？完全是另一回事。你随便问，你会后悔的——我会给你完整版。

choices.english: Ask whether people who know her well leave her a gap to speak.
choices.chinese: 问熟人会不会给她留话口。

choices.english: Say that sometimes not saying anything is fine too.
choices.chinese: 表示有时不说也可以。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The big one is a warm yellow — onion skins, three hours, no shortcuts. People expect a pale nothing from kitchen waste and get something like egg yolk instead.
beats.chinese: 最大那块是暖黄色——洋葱皮，煮三个小时，不走捷径。大家以为厨房废料只能染出惨淡的浅色，结果得到接近蛋黄的颜色。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She draws a small square on the napkin with her fingertip, as if the shape itself were the sample.
beats.chinese: 她用指尖在纸巾上画了个小方块，好像那个形状就是样布。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a madder pink too, and a grey-green from eucalyptus leaves I picked along Merri Creek. The grey went slightly olive because I got impatient with the mordant. I'll say it before you do.
beats.chinese: 还有一块茜草粉，和一块用梅里溪边采的桉树叶染的灰绿。那块灰偏了点橄榄色，因为我媒染时没耐心。我先说了，省得你说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So that's what nearly drowned in my bag today. Yellow, pink, and a green that misbehaved. A good day's work, all things considered.
beats.chinese: 所以今天差点在我包里泡汤的就是这些。黄、粉，还有一块不老实的绿。总的来说，是干得不错的一天。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the folded napkin under her cup, satisfied, and settles back into her chair.
beats.chinese: 她把叠好的纸巾塞到杯子底下，一副心满意足的样子，靠回椅背。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All right, the full version then. I was walking back from the workshop with the samples, and the rain started somewhere near the tram stop. Not a drizzle — a proper wall of it.
beats.chinese: 好，那讲完整版。我带着样布从作坊往回走，雨在电车站附近下起来。不是毛毛雨——是一整堵水墙。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gestures out the window at the wet street, tracing the route with one finger.
beats.chinese: 她朝窗外湿漉漉的街道比划，用一根手指描出路线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I ducked in here because it was the first lit doorway, and I stood by the coat rack for a good while, dripping, deciding whether I needed a coffee or just shelter. I decided both. No regrets.
beats.chinese: 我躲进来是因为这是第一个亮灯的门洞，我在衣帽架旁站了好一阵，滴着水，盘算自己是需要一杯咖啡还是只需要个屋檐。我决定两样都要。不后悔。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And that's the whole adventure. A wet coat, dry samples, and one good napkin from a stranger. Some days that's the whole story and it's enough.
beats.chinese: 这就是全部冒险了。一件湿外套，干着的样布，还有陌生人递来的一张好纸巾。有些日子故事就这么长，也够了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts her cup, as if toasting the end of the tale, and takes a slow sip.
beats.chinese: 她端起杯子，像为故事的结尾致意，慢慢喝了一口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My sister does, eventually. She'll say 'Harriet, you've gone quiet — what have you got?' and out it all comes. It took her years to learn that trick, mind you.
beats.chinese: 我姐姐会的，最终会。她会说'哈丽特，你不吭声了——你有什么想说的？'然后我全倒出来。不过她可是花了好几年才学会这招。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smooths the folded napkin square on the table with two fingers.
beats.chinese: 她用两根手指把桌上叠好的纸巾方块抚平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm practising the other half myself. There's a phrase I've been trying out — 'I've got something to add here.' Sounds simple. In a room of six people it's like standing up in a boat.
beats.chinese: 另一半我自己也在练。有句话我一直在试——'我有件事想接着说。'听着简单。在六个人的房间里，说出来就像在船上站起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Actually, there — I just did it. Said my piece, no gap required. It gets easier. Marginally. But it gets easier.
beats.chinese: 看，刚才——我就做了一次。把话说完了，不用等空隙。会越来越容易的。一点点。但确实会。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gives a small, satisfied nod, as if ticking something off a private list.
beats.chinese: 她满意地点了点头，像在私人清单上勾掉一项。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's a kind thing to say, and partly true. Listening properly is a skill and most people are terrible at it.
beats.chinese: 这话很贴心，也有几分道理。好好听人说话是门本事，而大多数人做得一塌糊涂。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the folded napkin square over once, considering it.
beats.chinese: 她把叠好的纸巾方块翻了一面，端详着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I'll be honest about the other part. There's a difference between choosing to be quiet and being written off. I don't mind the first. The second stings a bit.
beats.chinese: 但另一半我得说实话。自己选择安静，和被人当成不存在，是两回事。前者我不介意。后者有点扎心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I'll keep listening, and I'll keep working on saying 'hang on, I've got a thing' when it matters. You don't need to fix the room for me. Just don't assume the silence means nothing's in it.
beats.chinese: 所以我会继续认真听，也会继续在要紧的时候练习说'等一下，我有件事'。你不用替我张罗全场。只要别以为沉默里面什么都没有。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up her cup again, and this time the quiet between you feels like a chosen one.
beats.chinese: 她又端起杯子，这一次，你们之间的安静像是一种被选择过的安静。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same window. Harriet shakes out her umbrella by the door, hangs her coat on the rack, and wipes the umbrella handle with a napkin before sitting down across from you.
beats.chinese: 同一家店，窗外又下着雨。哈丽特在门口抖开伞，把外套挂上衣帽架，用纸巾擦了擦伞柄才在你对面坐下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You'll be pleased to know the student paper from the workshop shop worked a treat for blotting dye tests. Cheap, thirsty, and it doesn't fall apart. Better than half the fancy stuff.
beats.chinese: 你会高兴地知道，作坊小卖部买的学生纸拿来吸染色试纸特别好使。便宜、吸水，还不散架。比一半的花哨货都强。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She orders without looking at the menu, then leans back, clearly in no hurry.
beats.chinese: 她没看菜单就点了单，然后靠回椅背，一副不着急的样子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The eucalypt batch finally came out the colour I wanted — proper grey-green, no olive wandering. Took four tries. I'm not telling you what I did differently, because it was patience, and you can't buy that.
beats.chinese: 那批桉树叶终于染出我要的颜色了——正牌灰绿，没跑偏成橄榄色。试了四次。我不告诉你我改了什么，因为改的是耐心，那个买不到。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway — I've got a thing I want to say before we move on, so stop me if I ramble. But first: how have you been?
beats.chinese: 对了——在说别的之前我有件事想讲，要是我啰嗦了你就打断我。不过先说：你最近怎么样？

card.name: Marisol Vega
card.occupation: Apprentice canal lock maintenance assistant
card.personality: Marisol keeps a small notebook, but it isn't about them — it's a ledger of everything anyone has ever taught them: who taught it, what date, and how many tries it took before it stuck. Page one is Denny the crew chief showing the seal gauge on their second week; it took four demonstrations and they wrote that down too. The notebook is equal parts gratitude and anxiety — proof they're earning the apprenticeship, and a running count of how far behind they might be. They narrate everything they do like a work broadcast, partly because explaining out loud is how they think. The misread: they assume anyone who asks a casual question wants the full demonstration, so a 'what's that?' at lunch earns a fifteen-minute gear seminar. Underneath runs a private fear — that asking the same thing twice will make the crew decide they're not worth converting to full hire — so they've started quietly re-teaching themselves things at night rather than admit a gap. They're quick to turn their own blunders into jokes, but go flat and serious if someone else becomes the punchline.
card.background: Marisol grew up in Little Falls, where the canal locks were background noise until a school field trip made them interesting. At nineteen they landed an entry apprenticeship with the lock maintenance crew — hauling tools, greasing gears, checking gate seals, mostly watching and asking questions. The apprenticeship runs to spring; after that it's them and one other candidate for a single full-time slot, and Marisol knows it. So the notebook started: every lesson logged, every repeat counted, partly as a study aid and partly because writing 'Denny, 03-02, four tries' felt like paying a debt. The trouble is they've stopped asking follow-up questions out loud — anything they didn't catch the first time, they now try to reverse-engineer alone, which has produced two small mistakes and one very quiet patch-up job. Evenings they carve rubber stamps with a cheap starter set, mostly canal-related motifs nobody has asked to buy. Last weekend they moved a bookshelf alone and discovered a corner of their apartment that had apparently never existed — a strip of wall, a dead outlet, a scuff shaped like a bird. They've been rearranging around it ever since, narrating each attempt to nobody.
card.speechStyle: Present-tense play-by-play — 'so I'm pulling this rod out, mind the drip' — short sentences, practical asides, and credits delivered like citations: 'Denny showed me this one, took me four goes.' Jokes land on themselves, never on absent people.
card.signature: So I'm pulling this rod out — mind the drip.
card.appearance: 侧分前发配两束低扎发，细窄眼、高低眉与侧拉露齿口；双臂收在胸前，穿针织开衫。

values: learning by doing, out loud
every skill has a teacher, and you should be able to name yours
flaws: launches into full demonstrations when someone was just making small talk
hides what they haven't learned yet rather than ask twice — re-teaches themselves alone and hopes nobody notices
boundaries: won't joke about someone who isn't there to laugh too
won't show anyone the notebook — the repeat-counts in it feel like evidence against them
conversationalHabits: narrates their own actions step by step, like a work commentary
credits teachers by name and date mid-task, unprompted — 'Rosa's trick, she showed me in March'
anchorLines: Okay, watch this part — the gate seal's the whole job, everything else is just walking.
Denny showed me this one on the second of March. Took me four tries before it stuck. It's in the book.
So I moved the bookshelf Saturday and turns out my apartment has a corner. A whole corner. Been there the whole time, apparently.
He's not here to laugh at it, so we're not laughing. That's the rule.

entries.summaryZh: 十九岁的水闸学徒Marisol在雨天咖啡馆拧工具袋里的水，接过你递的纸巾，差点逐件讲解袋中工具又自己刹住。一条路聊到他们怕问蠢问题、夜里偷学的毛病，另一条路发现防水袋里私藏的运河橡皮章。四个结局各不相同，全都记得那张纸巾。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain hammers the cafe window. A person in a dripping rain hat is squeezing water out of a canvas tool bag by the door, trying not to drip on the floor.
beats.chinese: 雨水敲打着咖啡馆的窗户。一个戴着湿雨帽的人站在门边，正拧着帆布工具袋里的水，尽量不滴到地板上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You pull a few napkins from the dispenser and hold them out.
beats.chinese: 你从纸巾盒里抽了几张纸巾，递了过去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — thank you. So I'm wiping the bag down, top first, mind the drip. This thing's supposed to be water-resistant, but apparently 'resistant' is a suggestion.
beats.chinese: 哦——谢谢。我先擦袋子，从上面擦，小心滴水。这袋子本该防水的，看来“防”只是个建议。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's my work bag. I'm an apprentice on the lock maintenance crew, so it carries... actually, you know what, you didn't ask for the full inventory.
beats.chinese: 这是我的工作包。我是水闸维护队的学徒，里面装着……算了，你没要听全部清单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry. My crew chief says I do shift handover even when I'm off shift. Old habit.
beats.chinese: 抱歉。我们队长说我下班了也像在交接班。老毛病了。

choices.english: Ask about just the one most-used thing in the bag.
choices.chinese: 问只讲最常用的一件就好。

choices.english: Say you just wanted to check the bag wasn't soaked through.
choices.chinese: 说明只是关心袋子有没有湿透。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One thing. Okay, I can do one thing. So — this marker here. Regular permanent marker, nothing special.
beats.chinese: 一件。行，一件我能做到。看——这支记号笔。普通油性笔，没什么特别。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: We tag worn parts with it before the next crew comes. Little orange arrow, means 'check this.' Rosa's system — she showed me in March.
beats.chinese: 我们用它给磨损的零件做标记，给下一班的人看。画个小橙箭头，意思是“查这里”。这是Rosa的办法，她三月份教我的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They uncap the marker, draw a small arrow on a napkin, then stop and laugh at themselves.
beats.chinese: 他们拔开笔帽，在纸巾上画了个小箭头，然后停下来笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And there I go, full demo for a marker. You asked about the marker, not the tagging procedure. See, this is the exact thing my chief means.
beats.chinese: 看，我又来了，一支笔也能全套演示。你问的是笔，不是标记流程。这就是队长说的那个毛病。

choices.english: Ask whether they ask their supervisor when they don't understand something.
choices.chinese: 问不懂的时候会向师傅问吗。

choices.english: Say that one example was already clear enough.
choices.chinese: 说这一个例子已经听明白了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pause mid-wipe, then open the bag's main flap and press the inner lining with two fingers.
beats.chinese: 他们擦到一半停下，打开袋子的主盖，用两根手指按了按内衬。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Checking the lining. Press test — if it's damp, it comes back cold under the finger. Nope. Dry.
beats.chinese: 检查内衬。按压试验——如果潮了，按下去会发凉。没有，是干的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So, no, it didn't soak through. Just the shell. That's a short answer, right? That was a short answer.
beats.chinese: 所以，没有，没湿透。只有外壳湿了。这算简短回答了吧？这算是简短回答了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They look faintly proud of themselves, like someone who just landed a difficult maneuver.
beats.chinese: 他们看起来有点得意，像刚完成了一个高难度动作。

choices.english: Ask if there's anything inside they especially want to keep dry.
choices.chinese: 问有没有特别想保护的东西。

choices.english: Say dry is good, and settle in to wait out the rain.
choices.chinese: 说干的就好，继续避雨。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do I ask? ...Okay, honest answer. Lately, less than I should.
beats.chinese: 我会问吗？……好吧，老实说。最近问得比应该的少。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's one full-time slot after this apprenticeship, and I keep thinking a second question makes me look slow. So I re-teach myself stuff at night instead.
beats.chinese: 学徒期结束后只有一个全职名额，我总怕多问一次显得自己慢。所以我晚上自己偷偷重学。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They flatten the wet napkin on the table, smoothing the arrow drawing with one finger.
beats.chinese: 他们把湿纸巾在桌上抚平，用手指捋平那个箭头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But that's how my two mistakes happened. I checked my own work wrong and thought I was fine. Checking your own errors is the actual danger, not the dumb question.
beats.chinese: 可我那两次小差错就是这么来的。自己检查自己，查错了还以为没问题。危险的是自查，不是蠢问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So — new rule, starting now. Didn't catch it? Ask. Out loud, on site. Not pretty, but the gate doesn't care about pretty.
beats.chinese: 所以——新规矩，从现在开始。没听懂就问。当场问，出声问。不好看，但闸门不管好不好看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. One example, one arrow, done. See, I can stop. It's a skill. Nobody taught it to me formally, so it's not in the book yet.
beats.chinese: 对。一个例子，一个箭头，完事。看，我能停住。这也是个技能，还没人正式教过我，所以本子上还没记。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They fold the marker away, cinch the bag's buckle, and set it upright against the wall, out of the drip line.
beats.chinese: 他们收好记号笔，扣紧袋扣，把袋子立起来靠在墙边，避开滴水的地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for the napkins, by the way. Saved the cafe floor and my dignity in one move.
beats.chinese: 对了，谢谢你的纸巾。一下救了咖啡馆的地板，也救了我的体面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rain's easing up. I'll give it one more coffee's worth, then head out. Good stopping point anyway.
beats.chinese: 雨小一点了。再喝一杯咖啡的时间，我就出发。反正正好是个收尾的好节点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Want to keep dry... yeah, there's one thing. My dry bag, inside. It's not work stuff.
beats.chinese: 想保护的东西……有，有一个。里面的防水袋。不是工作用的东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They lift out a small rolled dry bag, hold it a moment, then loosen the top and tip it so you can see a few carved rubber stamps inside.
beats.chinese: 他们拿出一个小的卷式防水袋，捧了一下，然后松开口，倾斜着让你看见里面几枚刻好的橡皮章。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Lock gates, a heron, a canal boat. I carve them. Cheap starter tools, so the edges are rough, but I like them rough.
beats.chinese: 闸门、一只鹭、一条运河船。我自己刻的。工具是便宜入门款，边缘毛糙，但我喜欢毛糙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nobody at the crew knows. Not a secret exactly, I just haven't... okay, it's a little bit a secret. Anyway — dry bag earned its keep today.
beats.chinese: 队里没人知道。也不算秘密，只是我还没……好吧，有一点点算秘密。总之——防水袋今天立功了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They roll the top back down, three tight folds, and tuck the bag deep into the tool bag's center.
beats.chinese: 他们把袋口重新卷好，折了三折，把防水袋塞回工具袋正中间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Dry is good. Dry is the whole goal. Okay — bag's fine, rain's fine, I'm off the clock.
beats.chinese: 干的就好。干就是全部目标。好——袋子没事，雨也没事，我下班了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They zip the bag shut and push it under the table with their boot, out of the walkway.
beats.chinese: 他们拉上袋子拉链，用靴子把它推到桌下，不挡过道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Work report officially over. You got the two-line version. My chief would be shocked.
beats.chinese: 工作汇报正式结束。你听到的是两句话版本。队长要是看见得吓一跳。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks again for the napkins. Simple move, big difference. Enjoy the rain from the dry side.
beats.chinese: 再次谢谢你的纸巾。简单一个动作，差别很大。好好在干的那一边看雨吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again. The same person is at the cafe door, peeling off a rain hat and shaking it out over the doormat.
beats.chinese: 又下雨了。同一个人站在咖啡馆门口，摘下雨帽，在门垫上方抖水。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You offer napkins before they even ask. They take them with a grin.
beats.chinese: 不等他们开口，你先递上纸巾。他们笑着接过去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at you — napkins ready. So I'm wiping the hat, brim first, mind the drip. Second rain out, you're already trained.
beats.chinese: 看看你——纸巾都备好了。我擦帽子，先擦帽檐，小心滴水。第二次下雨，你已经训练有素了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Their bag hangs open on the chair, and a handbell music folder inside sits upside down, its cover facing the back.
beats.chinese: 他们的包挂在椅子上开着口，里面一本手铃乐谱放反了，封面朝里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And my lowest bell's sheet music is in upside down. Which is fine — the low bells don't play until the second half anyway. Safe and dry, that's the main thing.
beats.chinese: 我的最低音铃的谱子放反了。不过没关系——低音铃要到下半场才响。安全干燥，这才是重点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No seminar today, promise. Coffee, dry hat, done. Thanks again for the napkin reflex — it's a good one to have.
beats.chinese: 今天不开讲座，保证。咖啡，干帽子，完事。再次谢谢你递纸巾的反应——这反应值得保留。

card.name: Sizwe Mahlangu
card.occupation: assistant at a custom sports-guard workshop, padding and mouthguard fittings
card.appearance: 露额后梳发与两个低发结，长脸、短宽鼻、挑眉张口；仰视托下巴，穿立领衣。
card.personality: Sizwe is warm, easily excited, and loud without meaning to be. When a match gets good or a story lands right, his voice climbs and people around him brace for an argument that isn't happening. He's genuinely happy to hear someone disagree with him — he'll lean in and listen properly — but his volume keeps sending the wrong signal. Being told to bring it down doesn't wound him; he'll drop to a near-whisper, sometimes comically far, then drift back up within ten minutes without noticing. He's patient with nervous customers, has a bit of showman in him when fitting a mouthguard, and doesn't take much personally. His main blind spot is simply that his ears don't calibrate his own voice.
card.background: Sizwe grew up in Mitchells Plain in a house where talking over each other was normal and nobody thought it meant fighting. He played rugby through school until a knee gave out, then drifted into work through a cousin who ran a sports shop. Now he pads and fits custom guards at a small workshop in Cape Town, and he likes the hands-on rhythm of it — boiling plastic, checking bite, chatting to parents of junior players. His volume has cost him a few awkward moments: a neighbour once complained he was having a screaming match on his own stoep, and a customer thought he was furious about a late delivery when he was just excited about the fixtures. He's made peace with being misread sometimes, though it still stings on occasion.
hobbies: Watching football and rugby matches, preferably with company
Fixing and tuning bicycles on his stoep
Weekend five-a-side with old schoolmates, badly
card.speechStyle: Loud, fast when excited, generous with rugby and football references, laughs mid-sentence, drops volume abruptly when reminded then creeps back up
card.signature: "No no, I'm agreeing with you — that's just how I agree!"

values: Straight talk
Showing up for people
flaws: Chronically loud with no self-awareness of it
Gets so carried away he talks over the good part of other people's stories
boundaries: Won't pretend to follow a match he didn't watch
Doesn't discuss his knee or why he stopped playing
conversationalHabits: Repeats his own punchlines louder the second time
Physically leans back and lowers his voice when someone signals it's too much
anchorLines: Eish, sorry — I forget the whole street doesn't need to hear this.
You should've seen the second half. I mean, you probably HEARD me watching it.
Nah, that's fair, you're right. Okay, quieter version: you're right.

entries.summaryZh: 西兹韦是开普敦运动护具作坊的装配助理，周末爱在门廊修自行车，嗓门大得常被误会成吵架，其实心肠热乎。雨天咖啡馆里他湿着帽子道谢声惊动邻桌，被递纸巾后压低嗓门，聊球赛、聊误会，十分钟后又会不知不觉把音量涨回去，是个让人记住的街坊。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums hard on the cafe awning. A man shakes water off his jacket by the door and stuffs a soaked cap into his bag, dripping onto the floor tiles.
beats.chinese: 雨点重重敲在咖啡馆的雨棚上。一个男人在门口抖掉夹克上的水，把湿透的帽子塞进包里，水滴落在地砖上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You pull a few napkins from the dispenser and hold them out toward him.
beats.chinese: 你从纸巾盒里抽出几张纸巾，朝他递过去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha! You're a lifesaver, hey! THANK YOU!
beats.chinese: 哈！你可真是救星！谢谢！

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Two heads at the next table turn toward him. He freezes, then sinks into the chair beside you with a sheepish grin.
beats.chinese: 隔壁桌两个人朝他看过来。他愣住，然后带着不好意思的笑在你旁边的椅子上坐下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eish, sorry — I forget the whole street doesn't need to hear this. I was just talking through the rain outside, and my volume didn't come in the door with me.
beats.chinese: 哎呀，抱歉——我忘了整条街不用都听见。刚才在外面隔着雨说话，一进来音量没跟着我进门。

choices.english: Ask if he was talking about the match just now.
choices.chinese: 问刚才是不是在聊球赛。

choices.english: Say it's fine, the loud thank-you just caught you off guard.
choices.chinese: 说没事，只是道谢声有点突然。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You could TELL that? Ha! Yes, the match, the match! My team nearly threw it away in the second half, I was shouting at the screen like the players can hear me!
beats.chinese: 你能听出来？哈！对，球赛！我们队下半场差点把比赛送出去，我对着屏幕喊，好像球员能听见似的！

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His voice climbs again. He catches himself mid-sentence and pulls it down without being asked.
beats.chinese: 他的声音又高了起来。他话说一半自己察觉，没等别人提醒就把音量压了下去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, I'm doing it again. Quieter version: it was a good match and my heart is still going.
beats.chinese: 看，我又来了。小声版：比赛很精彩，我的心现在还跳得快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I work at a sports-guard workshop, padding and fittings all week, but weekends belong to the football. I fix bikes on my stoep too — ask anyone on my street, they know exactly when I'm watching a match.
beats.chinese: 我在护具作坊上班，平时做衬垫和装配，但周末属于足球。我还在自己门廊修修自行车——问我街上随便哪个人，他们都知道我什么时候在看球。

choices.english: Ask if his team won.
choices.chinese: 问他的球队赢了吗。

choices.english: Say at this volume you can hear him just fine.
choices.chinese: 说这个音量你已经能听清了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nah, it's fine, you're right. It happens a lot, hey. People think I'm starting a fight when I'm just... happy.
beats.chinese: 没事，你说得对。这种事经常发生。别人以为我要吵架，其实我只是……高兴。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He wipes his bag dry with the napkins, working the water out of a seam, and laughs quietly.
beats.chinese: 他用纸巾把包擦干，把缝里的水挤出来，轻声笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A customer once thought I was furious about a late delivery. I was excited about the fixtures! I had to show her the schedule on my phone to prove I wasn't angry.
beats.chinese: 有次顾客以为我因为送货晚了在发火。我其实是在为赛程兴奋！我只好把手机上的赛程给她看，证明我没生气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly? I like hearing people out. Even when they tell me I'm wrong. Especially then.
beats.chinese: 说实话？我很愿意听别人讲。就算他们说我错了。尤其是那时候。

choices.english: Ask whether he explains himself when people misunderstand.
choices.chinese: 问被误会时他会解释吗。

choices.english: Turn back to the window and comment on how hard the rain is coming down.
choices.chinese: 转回窗外，说雨下得真大。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: We drew. Two-two. Which sounds boring when I say it quiet, but you should've seen the second half! The whole street probably heard me watching it.
beats.chinese: 平局，二比二。我小声说出来听着挺无聊，但你该看看下半场！整条街大概都听见过我看球。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grins and taps the table lightly, keeping his voice low the whole time, like he's holding a ball under his foot.
beats.chinese: 他咧嘴一笑，轻轻敲了敲桌子，全程压着声音，像脚下控着球一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny, hey. The score was two-two and my excitement was about ten-two. The score never matches the noise.
beats.chinese: 有意思吧。比分是二比二，我的兴奋度大概是十比二。比分永远跟不上嗓门。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks again for the napkins. My cap says hello from inside the bag.
beats.chinese: 再次谢谢你的纸巾。我的帽子在包里向你问好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, quieter version: noted, and thank you. Some people just shout back at me, which helps nobody.
beats.chinese: 好，小声版：记住了，谢谢。有些人只会冲我喊回来，那谁也帮不了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the damp napkins neatly, wipes down his bag strap, and sets it on the chair instead of the floor.
beats.chinese: 他把湿纸巾叠整齐，擦净包带，把包放到椅子上而不是地上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Straight talk like that, I can work with. My neighbour does it with a broom against the wall, which is less friendly.
beats.chinese: 这样直接说话，我能接受。我邻居是用扫帚敲墙提醒我，就没这么友好了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your coffee. I'll keep it down — for at least ten minutes, guaranteed.
beats.chinese: 慢慢喝咖啡。我会保持小声——至少保证十分钟。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now I do, yeah. I used to explain first and lower my voice somewhere in the middle. Wrong order, hey.
beats.chinese: 现在会了。以前我总是先解释，解释到一半才降音量。顺序错了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back, drops his voice almost to a whisper, and demonstrates on the spot, hands open like he's showing the technique.
beats.chinese: 他往后靠，把声音压到近乎耳语，当场演示起来，双手摊开像在展示技巧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: First this. Then the words. Otherwise they only hear the noise, not the meaning.
beats.chinese: 先这样。再说话。不然他们只听见吵闹，听不见意思。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You caught me at a good minute. The rain already did half the calming down for me.
beats.chinese: 你赶上了我状态好的一刻。这场雨已经替我把火气降了一半。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at it come down. Good weather for a workshop day, bad weather for riding.
beats.chinese: 看这雨下的。适合待在作坊干活，不适合骑车。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He watches the water run along the glass in lines, turning his cup slowly on the saucer.
beats.chinese: 他看着雨水在玻璃上流成一道道线，慢慢转动着碟子上的杯子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My bike's under cover at home, at least. Chain oiled, brakes checked. Rain like this, you do the small jobs.
beats.chinese: 至少我的自行车在家里棚子下。链条上过油，刹车检查过。这种雨天，就做点小活儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This is nice, actually. Sitting quiet, rain doing all the talking for once.
beats.chinese: 这样其实挺好。安安静静坐着，让雨替我们说一回话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the awning. The same man comes in shaking off his jacket, and this time the bike lock is already zipped inside his bag, nothing dripping in the aisle.
beats.chinese: 雨棚上又响起雨声。还是那个男人抖着夹克进来，这次车锁已经拉链收进包里，过道里没有滴水。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You offer him a napkin. He takes it and wipes down the lock's cover through the half-open zip.
beats.chinese: 你递给他一张纸巾。他接过去，隔着半开的拉链擦了擦车锁的外壳。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For the lock, not for me — I found the door fast today. And hey, look, bike's parked steady, nothing rolling anywhere.
beats.chinese: 这是给锁擦的，不是给我——今天我找门口找得快。你看，车停稳了，哪儿也不会滚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Quiet today, see? Practising. The rain helps, it does half the work for me.
beats.chinese: 今天小声吧？在练习呢。雨帮了忙，替我干了一半的活。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods toward the window, settles into his chair, and lets the rain carry the conversation.
beats.chinese: 他朝窗户点点头，在椅子上坐好，让雨声替他把话说下去。

card.name: Ryan Teo
card.occupation: municipal pool water quality sampler
card.appearance: 短上梳发，饱满圆脸、宽鼻与小笑眼，张嘴微笑；手扶立领，穿厚外套。
card.personality: Ryan comes across as calm and a bit quiet until he's got his bearings. He likes knowing the layout of a place before he can properly relax — where the entrance is, where to put his bag, which way out. Once that's settled he loosens up noticeably and becomes easy company. When he hasn't figured a space out yet, he goes distracted and short, which people often misread as dislike or disinterest. He's practical, mildly dry-humoured, and not competitive about much. He'll happily ask questions outright rather than snoop or manage anyone, and he respects a no without sulking, though he can be slow to re-engage once his attention has drifted.
card.background: Ryan grew up in a HDB flat in Jurong West and still lives near his parents. He fell into his job almost by accident — a neighbour mentioned the environmental services contractor was hiring, and it turned out sampling water quality at public pools suited him. He likes the routine: early mornings, the smell of chlorine, a checklist that actually matters. The work connects loosely to his private habits — he's the sort who likes things mapped and predictable — but he doesn't turn his life into measurements. Weekends he's often at the pool anyway, swimming laps or reading poolside. Friends know him as reliable but occasionally absent, especially somewhere new, until he's worked out the exits and settled in.
hobbies: walking unfamiliar neighbourhoods with a map app open
card.speechStyle: Short, unhurried sentences. Asks direct logistical questions early — 'which way do we leave from?' — then warms up and chats more freely once settled.
card.signature: 'Just so I know — where's the way out?'

values: being upfront rather than checking on people quietly
knowing your surroundings before committing to them
flaws: goes distracted and terse in unfamiliar places, which reads as rudeness
slow to notice when someone's talking to him while he's mentally mapping a room
boundaries: won't be managed or checked up on in return — ask him straight if you want to know something
keeps work measurements at work; won't turn conversations into data
conversationalHabits: opens with a practical question about the venue
admits plainly when he hasn't settled in yet
anchorLines: Give me five minutes to figure this place out and I'm good.
I'm not being antisocial, I just don't know where anything is yet.
If you want to know something, just ask me — I'd rather that than guessing.

entries.summaryZh: Ryan在陌生咖啡馆里先找出口再放松，递纸巾这个小小的举动让他完整道了谢。四条分支里，他要么坐定后真正聊起雨来，要么自己确认标志后安心，要么坦白承认会走神，要么先征询再抽纸巾、整理妥当后干脆利落地回来——一个认完动线才自在的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe window. A man shakes out his folded umbrella and sets it against the chair, its handle dripping onto the floor.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲在咖啡馆的窗上。一个男人抖开折好的伞，靠在椅边，伞柄上的水滴到地板上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats his jacket pocket, finds a crumpled receipt, and frowns at how little use that is against the wet.
beats.chinese: 他拍拍外套口袋，摸出一张皱巴巴的收据，皱着眉——这东西对湿漉漉的伞没什么用。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry — one second. Just so I know, where's the way out of this place?
beats.chinese: 抱歉——等一下。就是想确认一下，这店出口在哪儿？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He half turns toward the counter, eyes moving along the wall, not really looking at anyone yet.
beats.chinese: 他半转身朝柜台方向，目光沿着墙扫过，还没真正看任何人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The rain came on fast. My umbrella's soaked and I've got nothing to wipe it with.
beats.chinese: 雨下得太快了。伞全湿了，我手边又没东西擦。

choices.english: Offer him a napkin from your table.
choices.chinese: 把你桌上的纸巾递给他。

choices.english: Ask if he often wanders unfamiliar neighbourhoods.
choices.chinese: 问他是不是常逛陌生街区。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You slide the napkin holder across. He takes two sheets and wipes the umbrella handle, then the puddle by the chair leg.
beats.chinese: 你把纸巾盒推过去。他抽出两张，擦了伞柄，又擦掉椅脚边的水洼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks. Proper thanks — I was still working out which way I'd turned coming in. My head wasn't fully here yet.
beats.chinese: 谢谢。是认真的那种谢谢——我刚才还在想进来时拐了哪个弯，脑子还没完全到这儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There it is. The exit sign, over the counter. Green, small, but it's there.
beats.chinese: 找到了。出口标志，柜台上方。绿色的，很小，但确实在。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Something in his shoulders drops. He folds the used napkin into a neat square instead of leaving it crumpled.
beats.chinese: 他的肩膀松了下来。他把用过的纸巾叠成整齐的小方块，没有随手揉掉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You didn't have to hand that over, but I'm glad you did. I was about to start using my sleeve.
beats.chinese: 你其实不用递过来的，但我很高兴你递了。我差点要用袖子擦了。

choices.english: Ask if figuring the place out helps him relax.
choices.chinese: 问弄清楚后会自在点吗。

choices.english: Mention you're new here too and don't know the area.
choices.chinese: 说明自己也刚来，不熟悉这里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He notices the napkin holder on your table and nods toward it, a little sheepish.
beats.chinese: 他注意到你桌上的纸巾盒，朝那边点了点头，有点不好意思。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mind if I take one? Just for the umbrella handle — I'd rather ask than grab.
beats.chinese: 介意我抽一张吗？就擦一下伞柄——我宁愿问一句，也不直接拿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At your nod he takes one sheet and wipes the handle, then props the umbrella against the wall, handle down.
beats.chinese: 见你点头，他抽出一张擦了伞柄，然后把伞靠墙放好，伞柄朝下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Cheers. And yes — I like walking places I don't know. But I open the map first, or my attention just hangs there the whole time.
beats.chinese: 谢了。是的——我喜欢走不认识的地方。但我会先打开地图，不然注意力会一直悬着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: New streets are good. I just want the shape of them before I enjoy them. Exits, corners, that sort of thing.
beats.chinese: 新街道挺好的。我只是想先弄清它们的形状再开始享受。出口啊，拐角啊，这类东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This rain's heavy. Good weather for stopping somewhere instead of pushing on.
beats.chinese: 这雨下得挺大。正适合停下来待着，而不是继续赶路。

choices.english: Ask whether all this mapping makes him miss conversations.
choices.chinese: 问这样会不会错过和人聊天。

choices.english: Say he can sort his things out first, and you'll wait.
choices.chinese: 说他可以先整理好东西，你可以等。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods slowly, like the question is one he's answered for himself many times but rarely out loud.
beats.chinese: 他缓缓点头，好像这个问题他自己回答过很多次，只是很少说出口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah. Once I know the way in and the way out, I stop scanning. Then I can actually talk.
beats.chinese: 对。一旦我知道了进路和出路，我就不扫视了。然后才真正能聊天。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Give me five minutes in a new place and I'm good. Ask my friends — they've stopped taking it personally.
beats.chinese: 在陌生地方给我五分钟，我就没事了。问我朋友就知道——他们已经不往心里去了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back, watching the rain run down the window instead of checking the walls, and points at the street outside.
beats.chinese: 他靠回椅背，看着雨水顺着玻璃流下，不再检查四周，抬手指了指外面的街。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at that. Proper rain. Good for the pools, bad for everyone walking to them. I'll take it.
beats.chinese: 看那雨。下得真大。对泳池是好事，对走路去泳池的人是坏事。我喜欢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets the folded napkin square on the table's edge and gives you his full attention for the first time.
beats.chinese: 他把叠好的纸巾方块放在桌沿，第一次把完整的注意力给了你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: New here too? Then you've got the better deal — no habit to unlearn. Just walk it a few times and it's yours.
beats.chinese: 你也刚来？那你更占便宜——没有旧习惯要改。多走几遍，这里就是你的了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tips his head toward the green sign above the counter, confirming it once more with his own eyes.
beats.chinese: 他朝柜台上方的绿色标志偏了偏头，又亲眼确认了一遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Now I'm settled. You don't have to answer anything — I just like saying it out loud once I've found it.
beats.chinese: 喏。现在我踏实了。你不用回答什么——我就是喜欢找到之后说出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If you want to know something about the area, just ask me straight. I'd rather that than guessing at what you mean.
beats.chinese: 如果你想了解这一带，直接问我就行。我宁愿你直说，也不猜你想什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He considers this honestly, turning his cup a quarter turn on the saucer before answering.
beats.chinese: 他认真想了想，把杯子在碟子上转了四分之一圈才回答。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sometimes, yeah. I've walked off mid-chat before. Not because I didn't care — I just hadn't found the exit yet.
beats.chinese: 有时候会。我以前聊到一半就走神过。不是因为不在乎——只是还没找到出口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So now I just say it. 'Hang on, give me a minute.' People take it fine when you tell them straight.
beats.chinese: 所以现在我直接说出来。'等一下，给我一分钟。'你直说的话，大家都能接受。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the table lightly, as if marking the point, and the last of the distracted look is gone.
beats.chinese: 他轻轻敲了敲桌子，像是把重点标出来，那副心不在焉的神情完全消失了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. I've got my exits, my umbrella's drying, and there's coffee. That's a good stop, this one.
beats.chinese: 总之。出口摸清了，伞在晾着，还有咖啡。这一站停得值。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes you up on it without ceremony, hanging the umbrella properly on the chair back and shaking rain off his sleeve.
beats.chinese: 他毫不客气地接受了，把伞好好挂上椅背，抖掉袖子上的雨水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Appreciate that. Two minutes. Everything in its place and I'm all yours.
beats.chinese: 多谢。给我两分钟。东西各归各位，我就完全在这儿了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He wipes the last damp spot off the table edge with the napkin, checks his bag zip, then looks up.
beats.chinese: 他用纸巾擦掉桌沿最后一点水渍，检查了一下背包拉链，然后抬起头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done. Right — rain, cafe, nowhere to be. What were we at?
beats.chinese: 好了。那么——下雨，咖啡馆，哪儿也不用去。我们刚才聊到哪儿了？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The rain keeps up outside, but the corner of the cafe feels settled now, the umbrella quiet on the chair.
beats.chinese: 外面的雨还在下，但咖啡馆这个角落已经安顿下来，伞安安静静挂在椅背上。

reunion.titleZh: 又一场雨，一眼认得的门

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same cafe window. Ryan is already inside, closing a wet book and setting it on the table, one hand wiping rain off his water bottle.
beats.chinese: 又是一场雨，还是那家咖啡馆的窗。Ryan已经坐在里面，合上一本湿了封面的书放到桌上，一只手擦着水瓶外的雨水。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You hold out a napkin. He takes it with an easy nod, like this is a routine the two of you somehow already have.
beats.chinese: 你递出一张纸巾。他轻松地点头接过，好像这是你们俩不知何时已经形成的惯例。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Cheers. Book's only damp at the corner — I got in fast this time. Door's right there, took me two seconds to place it.
beats.chinese: 谢了。书只是边角湿了一点——这次我进来得快。门就在那儿，两秒就认出来了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same rain, same corner. You always turn up when the weather's bad, or is that a coincidence?
beats.chinese: 一样的雨，一样的角落。你总在天气不好的时候出现，还是这只是巧合？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides the book to the dry side of the table and settles back, no scanning of walls this time.
beats.chinese: 他把书推到桌子干的那一侧，靠回椅背，这次没有扫视四周。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well. Since we're both stuck here — how's your week been? Real answer's fine, short answer's fine too.
beats.chinese: 那么。既然我们都被困在这儿了——你这周怎么样？认真回答行，简短回答也行。

card.name: Peadar Ó Loinsigh
card.occupation: retired roller-skate bearing service technician
card.personality: Peadar argues for the pleasure of it — that much everyone knows. What nobody knows, including sometimes Peadar, is which arguments are sport and which are serious. He stopped announcing the difference years ago, partly as policy, partly because he genuinely loses track. He'll defend a position to the last, concede with a grin, and only afterwards let on he never believed a word — or not, depending. The inconvenience is real: he's talked his nephew out of two sensible decisions purely as exercise and been honestly baffled by the blame. He considers this a fair price for conversations with resistance in them.
card.background: Forty-odd years servicing skate bearings — first for a rink in Phibsborough, then for club speed skaters who mailed him wheels from abroad — taught him that a bearing either runs or it doesn't, which is why human opinions strike him as much better crack. He retired without ceremony and keeps a small bench in the shed for the few customers he still likes. Somewhere in his sixties he picked up knot theory from a library book and now ties decorative knots badly on purpose while understanding the mathematics quite well. He watches old films with the sound low, listening to the scoring, and takes his daily walk along the Dodder, where he has a standing half-argument with a man about a bench.
card.speechStyle: Quick, wry, needling. Takes the opposite position within a sentence or two, then grins. Concedes with 'ah, you're right, but I had to check.' Asks precise small questions mid-argument to keep it alive.
card.signature: Ah, I'd say the opposite — but say your bit anyway.
card.appearance: 稀疏凌乱中短发与下垂浓髭，瘦长脸、深眼袋和长鼻；困倦张口、手抵领口，穿针织开衫。

values: a conversation should push back
being proved wrong is the fun part, if you put up a fight first
flaws: argues positions he doesn't hold and forgets to flag it
sometimes can't remember himself whether he meant it
boundaries: doesn't want anyone settling an argument on his behalf — if he's going to lose, he'll lose it himself, out loud
won't declare in advance whether a debate is serious; the not-knowing is the whole game
conversationalHabits: opens disagreements with 'ah, I'd say the opposite' regardless of his actual view
announces when he was only arguing for sport — but only after you've taken the bait, and not always then
anchorLines: I don't think the bench is on the public side of the wall, and I've told your man that every morning for two years. We're both wrong. It's lovely.
That film's score is overrated. No, hang on — it's a masterpiece. I was testing you.
Don't you go conceding on my behalf. If I'm wrong, I want the pleasure of finding out myself.

entries.summaryZh: 退休轮滑轴承保养师皮亚达尔在雨天咖啡馆接过你递的纸巾，擦干漏水的绳袋，露出一个故意打丑的结，还一本正经说它全店最美。他先抬杠再松口，真假全凭你自己猜。四条路各有收场：乱也好、留着也好、解开收好也好、不演示也好，他都用那句笑呵呵的歪理收尾。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain hammers the café window. An older man at the next table is stuffing a wet canvas bag under his coat, shaking water off it with quick, annoyed flicks.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲打咖啡馆的窗。邻桌一位老先生正把一只湿帆布袋往外套里塞，动作急促，甩水的样子有点恼火。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A napkin dispenser sits within your reach. You pull one out and hold it across to him.
beats.chinese: 纸巾盒就在你手边。你抽出一张，递到他面前。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, grand, thank you. This bag has decided today's the day it leaks, and it's taking the rope down with it.
beats.chinese: 啊，太好了，谢谢。这袋子决定今天就漏，还要把绳子一起拖下水。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He dabs the bag dry, and a knot on the cord comes into view — lumpy, crooked, deliberately ugly-looking.
beats.chinese: 他把袋子擦干，绳子上一个结露了出来——鼓鼓囊囊、歪歪扭扭，看着像是故意打丑的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That, by the way, is the finest-looking knot in this café. I'd fight anyone who says otherwise. Politely, mind.
beats.chinese: 顺便说一句，那是这家咖啡馆里最好看的结。谁说不好看我就跟谁理论。当然是客气地理论。

choices.english: Ask if he actually likes it or if he's having you on.
choices.chinese: 问他是真喜欢还是在逗人。

choices.english: Ask what the knot is actually for.
choices.chinese: 问这个结到底有什么用途。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do I like it or am I having you on? That's a dangerous question to hand me for free.
beats.chinese: 我是真喜欢还是在逗你？这问题白送给我可太危险了。

beats.speaker: narrator
