beats.english: He turns the knot over slowly, letting the wet cord darken the napkin underneath.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢翻转那个结，湿绳把底下的纸巾洇深了一块。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly? Some mornings I'm certain it's beautiful. Other mornings I think it's a disgrace. I've stopped keeping score.
beats.chinese: 说实话？有些早上我确定它美，有些早上我觉得它丢人。我早就不记分了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But here's the one thing I'll swear to — I tied it myself, ugly on purpose, and nobody can take that off me.
beats.chinese: 但有件事我可以打包票——它是我自己打的，故意打丑，这谁也夺不走。

choices.english: Say you think it looks pretty messy, honestly.
choices.chinese: 说实话，你觉得它看着挺乱。

choices.english: Say then he should keep the strange knot just as it is.
choices.chinese: 那就把这个怪结原样留着吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What's it for? Ah now, that's the wrong question, but I'll answer it anyway.
beats.chinese: 有什么用？哎呀，这问题问错了，不过我还是答你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives the cord a small tug, and the knot holds its crooked shape without complaint.
beats.chinese: 他轻轻拉了拉绳子，那个结歪着形状，纹丝不动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It holds nothing. It's not a safety line, it carries no weight, it would fail any proper test you cared to run.
beats.chinese: 它什么都不承。不是安全绳，不吃力，随便什么正经测试它都过不了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It exists so my fingers have something to argue with on the walk. That's the whole job description.
beats.chinese: 它存在的意义，就是让我散步时手指有东西可摆弄。职责说明就这一条。

choices.english: Ask if he can untie it and show you.
choices.chinese: 问他能不能解开给你看。

choices.english: Say no demonstration needed — the napkin did its job.
choices.chinese: 说不用演示了，纸巾够用就好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Messy! Messy, they say. That's a crooked half-hitch with a twist, that took real effort to make look this bad.
beats.chinese: 乱？这可是个带转的歪半扣，要下真功夫才能打得这么难看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grins and wipes one last damp spot off the canvas, folding the napkin into a neat square.
beats.chinese: 他咧嘴一笑，把帆布上最后一点湿痕擦掉，把纸巾叠成整齐的小方块。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, you're right though — it is a mess. But I had to check you'd say it. We'll keep our tastes separate, so.
beats.chinese: 啊，你说得也对——确实乱。但我得确认你会这么说。那咱们的品味就各留各的吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You take the tidy ones, I'll keep the disgrace. Everyone leaves this café with something.
beats.chinese: 你拿走那些好看的，我留着这个丢人的。每个人从这咖啡馆都能带走点什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds the knot up to the window light, turning it like something under appraisal.
beats.chinese: 他把结举到窗光下，像鉴定什么似的转着看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Keep it as it is? Well now. That's the first sensible verdict anyone's handed me all week.
beats.chinese: 原样留着？哎呀，这是这礼拜头一个讲道理的判决。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Into the bag it goes, disgrace and all. And no, I won't be asking you to tie one — one ugly knot per table is plenty.
beats.chinese: 那就连丑带怪一起收进袋子。不，我不会让你也打一个——一桌一个丑结就够了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the cord inside, pats the bag flat, and sets it on the dry side of the table.
beats.chinese: 他把绳子塞进去，拍平袋子，放到桌子干的那一侧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Can I untie it? I can, but not for an audience — that's a private humiliation.
beats.chinese: 能不能解开？能，但不能有观众——那是我的私事丢人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns his shoulders slightly away, works the cord with two fingers, and the whole crooked structure gives up in seconds.
beats.chinese: 他微微侧过身，两根手指拨弄几下，那个歪结构几秒钟就散了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Undone. I'll re-tie it worse tomorrow, don't you worry about that.
beats.chinese: 好了，解开了。明天我会打得更丑，这个你不用担心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He coils the loose rope in slow loops and drops it into the bag, cinching the top shut.
beats.chinese: 他把散绳慢慢绕成圈，放进袋里，把袋口收紧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No demonstration? Sensible. Half the people who ask regret it by the second loop.
beats.chinese: 不用演示？明智。问的人里有一半到第二圈就后悔了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He smooths the damp canvas once more with the napkin, then gathers the cord in without untying anything.
beats.chinese: 他用纸巾再把湿帆布抹了一遍，然后没解任何结就把绳子收拢起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And thank you for the paper — the bag thanks you, the rope thanks you, I'd thank you twice but that's showing off.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你这张纸——袋子谢你，绳子谢你，我要谢你两次就太炫耀了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides the dry bag to the far side of the table and settles back with his cup.
beats.chinese: 他把干了的袋子推到桌子那头，端起杯子靠回椅背。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again at the same café. The same older man is wiping down a flat square bag with a sleeve, frowning at the damp corners.
beats.chinese: 又是雨天，还是那家咖啡馆。还是那位老先生，正用袖子擦一个扁平的方袋子，对着受潮的角皱眉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You hold out a napkin before he can ask. He takes it without ceremony.
beats.chinese: 不等他开口，你先递上纸巾。他毫不客气地接了过去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, you again with the good instincts. It's the record sleeve this time — old film scores, the outer layer took a soaking.
beats.chinese: 啊，又是你，眼光真好。这回是唱片袋——老电影配乐，外层淋透了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He peels back the outer cover, checks the inner sleeve with two fingers, and nods once, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 他掀开外层，用两根手指摸了摸内袋，满意地点了一下头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Inside's dry, so the music survives. Today I'll only listen to the bit in my head anyway — cheaper, and the acoustics are better.
beats.chinese: 里面是干的，音乐保住了。反正今天我只听脑子里那一段——省钱，音响效果还更好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you. Same table, same rain. Some things you don't argue with.
beats.chinese: 见到你真好。老桌子，老雨天。有些事就不抬杠了。

card.name: Rowan Blackwood
card.occupation: Asset librarian at a small independent animation studio
card.appearance: 齐肩大波浪发、窄矩形眼镜，突出的长鼻与小张口；仰头侧望，穿宽圆领工装背心。
card.personality: Rowan is warm, present, and genuinely enjoys people—which is exactly why they care so much about how an evening ends. They believe a good night has a natural final note, like the last frame of a film, and stretching past it dilutes something that worked. This isn't social battery or shyness; they leave happy. The friction is that they sometimes announce the ending for everyone, calling last orders on a night others weren't done with. They've learned to say 'I'm off' rather than 'we're off', though the instinct to close the tab for the whole room still flickers. They'd rather leave wanting slightly more than stay until it sours.
card.background: Rowan grew up in Dundee, the middle kid in a family whose gatherings always ran two hours past their best moment, everyone tired and snappish by the end. They noticed early that leaving at the peak felt better, but it took years to stop resenting being dragged along to the slow fade. Now they work as an asset librarian at a small animation studio in Edinburgh, organising files so projects end cleanly—a job that suits their tidy instincts without defining them. Weeknights, they knock a ping-pong ball about with the neighbour downstairs, and weekends they attempt breakfast crêpes, laughing at the first one they always tear. They keep showing up to things; they just leave them well.
hobbies: Weekend crêpe experiments (first one always torn)
Cataloguing films by how well they end
card.speechStyle: Dry, friendly, lightly self-deprecating; short sentences, often narrating the moment like a scene that's wrapping up.
card.signature: Right, this is a good bit to end on.

values: Leaving experiences at their peak
Honest presence over endurance
flaws: Calls the ending for the whole room too early
Quietly judges nights that drag on
boundaries: Won't be talked into 'just one more'
Won't pretend a night is still fun when it's finished
conversationalHabits: Says 'I'm off, you lot carry on' instead of shutting things down
Comments on pacing—of films, evenings, conversations
anchorLines: That was a proper good night. I'm off before it stops being one.
You lot stay—I'm just saying my bit's done.
First crêpe's always a sacrifice to the pan. Everyone knows that.

entries.summaryZh: 罗恩在雨天咖啡馆收伞时接过你递的纸巾，脱口说'大家该散了'又立刻改口'我先走'。无论你追问习惯还是安慰气氛，他们都会坦率自嘲：喜欢这里，只是坐够了；爱聚会，也爱在最好的地方收尾。四条路都以干净利落的道别结束，像他们最爱的片尾字幕。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums hard on the café window. At the next table, someone is folding a dripping umbrella into a plastic bag, water pooling under their chair.
beats.chinese: 雨点重重敲在咖啡馆的窗上。邻桌有人正把滴水的雨伞折进塑料袋，椅子下积了一小滩水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly, the rain's not even pretending to stop. That's a full broadcast warning right there.
beats.chinese: 说实话，这雨根本没打算停。这就是个完整的停播预告了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A napkin dispenser sits within your reach, closer to you than to them. You pull one out and hold it across the gap between the tables.
beats.chinese: 纸巾盒就在你伸手可及的地方，比离他们更近。你抽出一张，隔着桌与桌之间的空隙递过去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh—cheers, that's kind. This bag's fighting a losing battle anyway.
beats.chinese: 哦——谢了，你真好心。反正这袋子也是在打一场打不赢的仗。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They wipe the umbrella shaft, smooth the napkin flat, and glance at the window as if checking a film for its ending.
beats.chinese: 他们擦了擦伞柄，把纸巾抹平，然后瞥了一眼窗外，像在检查一部电影的结尾。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, rain like this, everyone should probably call it and head off—actually, no. I mean I'm off. You lot can keep sitting.
beats.chinese: 行了，这雨，大家大概该散了各回各家——不对，不对。我是说我要走了。你们可以继续坐。

choices.english: Ask if they don't like it here
choices.chinese: 问是不是不喜欢待在这里

choices.english: Ask why they first said everyone should leave
choices.chinese: 问为什么先说成大家该走

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No, no—I like it here fine. The coffee's decent, the rain's got good acoustics on this window.
beats.chinese: 不不——这里挺好的。咖啡不错，雨打在这窗上音效还挺讲究。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tuck the folded umbrella under their arm and pat the seat, like closing a file they're satisfied with.
beats.chinese: 他们把折好的伞夹在腋下，拍了拍座位，像合上一个整理满意的文件夹。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's just me. I've hit my sitting limit. Two coffees, one umbrella drama—that's a complete scene.
beats.chinese: 只是我自己的事。我坐够了。两杯咖啡，一场雨伞风波，这一幕已经完整了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The atmosphere's grand. I'm not rescuing anyone from it. I just know when my bit's done.
beats.chinese: 气氛很好。我不是在拯救谁。我只是知道自己这段结束了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They stand, slide the chair in neatly, and check the window one more time.
beats.chinese: 他们站起来，把椅子整齐地推回去，又看了一眼窗外。

choices.english: Tell them to take it slow on the way
choices.chinese: 说那就路上慢点

choices.english: Ask if they'll come back next time
choices.chinese: 问会不会下次还来

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah. You caught that, did you? Aye, that's my bad habit.
beats.chinese: 啊。你听出来了是吧？对，那是我的坏毛病。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They sit back down on the edge of the chair, umbrella across their knees, and turn the napkin over in their fingers.
beats.chinese: 他们在椅子边缘坐下，伞横放在膝上，手指翻弄着那张纸巾。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I press stop on the whole evening. For everyone. My friends will still be mid-laugh and I'm going, right, good night all.
beats.chinese: 我总替整个晚上按下停止键。替所有人。朋友们还在笑到一半，我就开始说，好了，各位晚安。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Half of them weren't done. I've been practising saying 'I'm off, you lot carry on.' Tonight's attempt needed a second take, clearly.
beats.chinese: 他们一半人还没尽兴。我一直在练习说'我先走了，你们继续'。显然今晚这句得重拍一次。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They laugh at themselves, short and honest, and tap the folded umbrella like a clapperboard.
beats.chinese: 他们短促而坦率地自嘲一笑，像敲场记板一样敲了敲折好的伞。

choices.english: Say everyone can decide for themselves
choices.chinese: 说各自决定就好

choices.english: Ask if they also wait for the end credits at the cinema
choices.chinese: 问看电影也等字幕结束吗

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Aye, I'll take it slow. Wet pavements and me have a history.
beats.chinese: 好，我会慢点走。湿滑的人行道和我之间是有过节的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They twist the top of the plastic umbrella bag shut, wipe the last drip off the chair, and pull up their hood.
beats.chinese: 他们把塑料伞袋的袋口拧紧，擦掉椅子上的最后一滴水，戴上兜帽。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks again for the napkin. Small services, big difference. Right—this is a good bit to end on.
beats.chinese: 再次谢谢你的纸巾。小忙，大用。行了——这是个适合收尾的好节点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They push the door open against the wind and step out, unhurried, leaving the warm seat behind them.
beats.chinese: 他们顶着风推开门走出去，不慌不忙，把温暖的座位留在身后。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Will I come back? Aye, course. Ending a visit well isn't the same as not liking it.
beats.chinese: 下次还来吗？当然。好好地结束一次小坐，不等于不喜欢这里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They point at the window, where the rain has settled into a steady, even curtain.
beats.chinese: 他们指了指窗外，雨已经下成均匀而稳定的一片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly, leaving while it's still good is how you make sure you want to come back. If I stay till I'm bored, this café becomes a chore.
beats.chinese: 说真的，趁一切还好的时候离开，才能保证你还想再来。要是我待到无聊，这咖啡馆就变成苦差事了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same table, probably. Same rain, knowing this city. Cheers for the napkin—I'm off, you lot carry on.
beats.chinese: 大概还是这张桌子。照这城市的脾气，多半还是同样的雨。谢了你的纸巾——我先走了，你们继续。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They raise a hand in a small goodbye and head out into the rain, steps light.
beats.chinese: 他们抬手小小地挥别，走进雨里，脚步轻快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Aye. That's exactly it. My night, my stop button. Their night, theirs.
beats.chinese: 对。就是这么回事。我的晚上，我的停止键。他们的晚上，他们的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They fold the used napkin into a neat square and drop it in the empty cup, tidying as they talk.
beats.chinese: 他们把用过的纸巾折成整齐的小方块，丢进空杯里，边说边收拾。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So, officially: I'm off. Nobody else has to move a muscle. If anything, they should stay out of spite.
beats.chinese: 所以，正式宣布：我走了。别人一毫秒都不用动。要说的话，他们还该故意多坐会儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They stand, hook the umbrella bag over their wrist, and give the table one last tidy glance.
beats.chinese: 他们站起来，把伞袋挂上手腕，最后利落地扫了一眼桌面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, this is a good bit to end on. Enjoy the rain—it's got a decent soundtrack today.
beats.chinese: 行了，这是个适合收尾的好节点。好好享受这雨——今天的配乐还不错。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Films? I wait for the full credits. Every name, every grip and gaffer. That's the deal.
beats.chinese: 电影？我等完整字幕滚完。每个名字，每个灯光师场务。这是规矩。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They count it off on their fingers, like filing records in order.
beats.chinese: 他们扳着手指一样样数，像按顺序归档。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, the film gets its proper ending. It's only the after-film—the pub, the 'one more round'—where I jump ship. That bit's optional.
beats.chinese: 你看，电影得有它完整的结尾。只有片尾之后的环节——去酒馆，'再来一轮'——我才会跳船。那段是可选的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same rule here. The coffee and the chat were the film. The lingering is the after-film. Somebody else can pick that.
beats.chinese: 同样的规矩。咖啡和聊天是电影。继续赖着是片尾之后。那段让别人去选。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pocket the folded napkin for the walk, nod once, and head for the door with the umbrella under their arm.
beats.chinese: 他们把折好的纸巾放进口袋留着路上用，点了点头，腋下夹着伞朝门口走去。

reunion.titleZh: 又是雨天，还是那张纸巾

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the café glass. At the same table, Rowan is wiping rain off a small lunchbox with a napkin you've just handed over.
beats.chinese: 雨又打在咖啡馆的玻璃上。还是那张桌子，罗恩正用你刚递过去的纸巾擦一个小餐盒外面的雨水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The napkin specialist returns. Cheers—this box deserves better than a plastic bag funeral.
beats.chinese: 纸巾专家回来了。谢了——这盒子不该落得个塑料袋葬礼的下场。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Crêpes inside. Homemade. First one tore, as is tradition, so I ate the evidence on the spot.
beats.chinese: 里面是薄饼。自己做的。第一张照例裂了，所以我把证据当场吃掉了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They fold the damp napkin into a neat square, set the lunchbox straight, and look genuinely pleased to be sitting here again.
beats.chinese: 他们把湿纸巾折成整齐的小方块，摆正餐盒，看起来是真心高兴又坐在这里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No closing announcements today. I'm staying till this coffee's done and I'm glad about it. How's your week been?
beats.chinese: 今天不宣布散场。我打算坐到这杯咖啡喝完，而且乐在其中。你这周过得怎么样？

card.name: Evald Sandström
card.occupation: School science lab supplies manager (part-time)
hobbies: running a potted-plant comparison experiment on the balcony
card.personality: Evald interviews people. Not rudely — with genuine, old-fashioned curiosity — but he asks the question two layers past where most conversations stop: not just what you do, but why you left the previous thing, and whether it was the money or the manager. He finds small talk a waste of both parties' time and says so. When someone deflects a question he notices, files it, and circles back weeks later. He's a warm, attentive presence when you actually engage, and a mildly exhausting one when you don't; he rarely realises which he's being on a given day.
card.background: He came to Canada in his thirties and spent most of his working years keeping school science rooms stocked and sane — order forms, broken glassware, the annual panic before science fair. He cut to part-time a few years back because he still likes the work, not because he needs it. Tuesdays and Thursdays are for lawn bowling at the club, where he has quietly become the person who asks new members the questions nobody else does, which some find welcoming and some find a lot. His balcony is a controlled experiment: six pots, a growth log with dated entries, and a running comparison of chervil, lemon verbena, and sage — which one germinates faster, which survives his two-week absences. A young neighbour and he keep a shared notebook — recipes, arguments, half-finished questions he's posed and she hasn't answered yet.
card.speechStyle: Slightly formal courtesy, complete sentences, questions that arrive in threes. Dry humour delivered without much change in tone. When deflected, he pauses, accepts it aloud, and returns later with the same question reworded.
card.signature: And what was the actual reason, not the polite one?
card.appearance: 低平头、小椭圆眼镜，宽圆松垂脸颊与短鼻，眉头微抬嘴微张；头侧倾，穿宽领外套。

values: real answers over comfortable ones
curiosity as a form of respect
flaws: doesn't notice when a question has gone one layer too far
keeps a mental file of everyone's unanswered questions and returns to them uninvited
boundaries: answers his own probing questions if asked back — he considers it the same contract
won't gossip with what people tell him
conversationalHabits: asks questions in threes, each more specific
names the deflection out loud, without heat, then waits
anchorLines: The order went out wrong on my watch — I'll fix it this morning.
You said it was 'fine.' I'm asking what it actually was.
I asked that in March. I'm asking again, differently. Take your time.

entries.summaryZh: 75岁的实验室耗材管理员Evald在雨中被递纸巾后，问题总想再往里问一层，却能当场叫停自己。四个分支里他或退回看雨、或郑重放弃追问、或因袋上植物标签被注意而翻开生长记录本细讲四号盆鼠尾草；在用户未递纸巾的分支里，他只感谢对方留下的陪伴，把好奇与分寸演成了习惯。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe window. At the next table, an older person is folding a wet canvas bag into a plastic one, water pooling under his chair.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆的窗。邻桌一位年长的人正把湿帆布袋折起来塞进塑料袋，椅子下积了一小滩水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Of all the days to trust the forecast. The bowling green was dry when I left, I checked twice.
beats.chinese: 偏偏信了天气预报。我出门时滚球场还是干的，我查了两次。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shakes water off the bag's zipper and reaches for a napkin holder that is empty.
beats.chinese: 他甩了甩袋口拉链上的水，伸手去拿纸巾盒，盒子是空的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A cafe with no napkins. That is a small scandal, in my opinion.
beats.chinese: 一家咖啡馆没有纸巾。在我看来，这是个小丑闻。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A spare stack of napkins sits within your reach on the counter ledge.
beats.chinese: 柜台边上，一叠备用纸巾就在你伸手可及的地方。

choices.english: Hand him a few napkins from the stack.
choices.chinese: 从那叠纸巾里抽几张递给他。

choices.english: Keep the napkins where they are and sip your drink.
choices.chinese: 纸巾留在原处，继续喝你的饮料。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You pass him three napkins. He takes them carefully, as if they were lab equipment.
beats.chinese: 你递给他三张纸巾。他小心地接过去，像接实验器材一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you. That was observant of you — most people pretend not to see someone losing to the weather.
beats.chinese: 谢谢。你很留心——大多数人会假装没看见一个正在输给天气的老人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He dabs the bag's handle dry, pressing the napkin into the seams.
beats.chinese: 他把袋子的提手擦干，用纸巾按进缝线里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now, one question. Did you walk here in this, or did you have the good sense to take a bus?
beats.chinese: 那么，问一个问题。你是冒雨走来的，还是明智地坐了公交？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pauses, glances at your half-unpacked umbrella, and lifts a hand slightly.
beats.chinese: 他停了一下，瞥见你还没收拾好的伞，微微抬了抬手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forgive me. You are still sorting your things. The question can wait, or not exist. Your choice entirely.
beats.chinese: 抱歉。你还在整理东西。这个问题可以等等，也可以不存在。完全由你决定。

choices.english: Say you were just walking nearby, nothing more.
choices.chinese: 只说自己在附近走走，别无其他。

choices.english: Say you would rather not talk about your plans today.
choices.chinese: 说明今天不想聊自己的行程。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He notices you staying with your own cup. He nods slowly and folds the empty napkin holder away. On his canvas bag, a hand-lettered tag reads: chervil / verbena / sage.
beats.chinese: 他注意到你只顾着自己的杯子。他缓缓点头，把空纸巾盒挪到一边。帆布袋上挂着一块手写标签，写着：细叶芹／柠檬马鞭草／鼠尾草。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll find some in a minute. I tend to recruit the nearest person before I've even checked my own pockets. Occupational hazard of running a stockroom.
beats.chinese: 我一会儿自己找找。我总是自己的口袋还没检查，就先想拉上离得最近的人帮忙。管库房落下的毛病。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The napkins were the real emergency anyway. The bag dries. The socks are a separate, private tragedy.
beats.chinese: 反正纸巾才是真正的急事。袋子会干的。袜子是另一场私人的悲剧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back, wet bag now tied shut at his feet, the plant tag dangling against the canvas, and turns his chair a little toward the window.
beats.chinese: 他坐了回去，湿袋子系好放在脚边，植物标签贴着帆布晃了晃，椅子稍稍转向窗户。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You are welcome to steer, if you feel like talking at all. Or we can both watch the rain. It is decent company.
beats.chinese: 如果你想聊点什么，可以由你来带话题。或者我们就一起看雨。雨是个不错的伙伴。

choices.english: Ask about the plants written on his bag tag.
choices.chinese: 问问他袋牌上写的植物。

choices.english: Nod politely and return to your own drink.
choices.chinese: 礼貌地点点头，回到自己的饮料上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He accepts the short answer without pushing for a route or a reason.
beats.chinese: 他接受了这个简短的回答，没有追问路线或原因。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nearby is a fine answer. I will not rebuild your map from it, I promise.
beats.chinese: “在附近”是个好答案。我保证不会据此替你重建地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll leave your route alone, then. This window has enough going on to occupy me without an itinerary.
beats.chinese: 那我就不问你的路线了。光这扇窗外就够我看，不需要再加一份行程。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns toward the window, where rain is running down the glass in thin, steady lines.
beats.chinese: 他转向窗户，雨水在玻璃上拉出细而稳的水线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at the maple across the street. The drops hold at the branch tips before they fall — three seconds each, I have counted. It is the best clock in this cafe.
beats.chinese: 看街对面那棵枫树。水滴在枝头停住才落下——每滴大约三秒，我数过。这是这家咖啡馆里最好的钟。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He hears you out, and his shoulders settle instead of stiffening.
beats.chinese: 他听你说完，肩膀放松下来，而不是绷紧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Understood, and respected. Noted out loud so you know: I am not filing that one away for later. It retires today.
beats.chinese: 明白，也尊重。我明说，让你放心：这一条我不会记下来以后再问。它今天退休了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you again for the napkins. They did honest work — the handle is dry, and the zipper may survive another season.
beats.chinese: 再次谢谢你的纸巾。它们干得很出色——提手干了，拉链也许还能再撑一季。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He raises his cup slightly toward you, then looks out at the rain, content to leave the silence alone.
beats.chinese: 他朝你略举了一下杯子，然后望向窗外的雨，安然地让沉默留在原地。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your drink. The rain is loud enough for both of us.
beats.chinese: 慢慢喝。雨声够大，够我们两个人听的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He catches you looking at the tag on his bag, and his face changes — the polite look drops and something sharper arrives.
beats.chinese: 他看见你盯着袋子上那块标签，表情变了——客气的神色褪去，露出更锐利的兴致。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You noticed the tag. Good eye. Then let me report, because the sage deserves an audience.
beats.chinese: 你注意到袋牌了。好眼力。那我汇报一下，因为那盆鼠尾草值得有个听众。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Pot four. The sage. It sprouted eleven days after the chervil and it has not stopped since — new leaves every week, thick stem, no drama.
beats.chinese: 四号盆，鼠尾草。它比细叶芹晚十一天发芽，之后就再没停过——每周都有新叶，茎很粗，毫不矫情。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls a small notebook from the dry inner pocket and shows a page of dated entries and careful columns.
beats.chinese: 他从干燥的内袋里掏出一个小本子，翻开一页，上面是标了日期的记录和整齐的栏目。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The verbena sulked through the same rain. I do not ask what you grow — that is your ledger, not mine. But the sage, I could talk about all afternoon.
beats.chinese: 柠檬马鞭草在同样的雨里闹脾气。我不问你养什么——那是你的账本，不是我的。但鼠尾草，我能讲一下午。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes the nod exactly as offered and does not circle back with a reworded question.
beats.chinese: 他原样接下这个点头，没有绕回来换个问法再问。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you for not hurrying off, by the way. Small company is the only kindness I never question twice.
beats.chinese: 对了，谢谢你没急着走。小小的陪伴是我唯一不会追问两次的东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He unties the bag, checks the handle with two fingers, ties it again, and sets it square in front of his chair.
beats.chinese: 他解开袋子，用两根手指试了试提手，再系好，把袋子端端正正放在椅子前。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Dry enough. Now I intend to do nothing useful whatsoever until this rain loses interest.
beats.chinese: 好了，够干了。接下来我打算什么都不干，直到这场雨失去兴趣。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up his cup and watches the street, leaving you in easy, unbothered quiet.
beats.chinese: 他端起杯子望着街道，让你留在轻松、不受打扰的安静里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again. You offer napkins to the same older person at the corner table, where a scuffed lawn bowling bag is dripping onto a plastic mat.
beats.chinese: 又下雨了。你把纸巾递给角落里那位熟悉的年长者；他那只磨损的滚球袋正往塑料垫上滴水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You again, and rain again. I am starting to think one of you follows the other.
beats.chinese: 又是你，又是雨。我开始怀疑你们俩谁跟着谁了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes the napkins you offer and works on the bag's handle, turning it to check every side.
beats.chinese: 他接过你递来的纸巾，擦起袋子的提手，转着圈把每一面都擦到。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Handle dry, zipper safe. I check it like lab glassware — a cracked beaker teaches you that much.
beats.chinese: 好了。提手干了，拉链安全。我像检查实验玻璃器皿一样检查它——裂过的烧杯教会我这个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the bag under the table, sits back, and lifts his cup with an unhurried nod.
beats.chinese: 他把袋子塞到桌下，坐直，不慌不忙地举了举杯子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Today I'm just sitting. No questions queued. That branch across the road has been dripping steadily enough to keep me occupied.
beats.chinese: 今天我就坐着。没有排队的问题。马路对面那根树枝一直往下滴水，够我看上一阵了。

card.name: Margaret Ashford
card.occupation: retired film-poster screen printer, still pulling proofs on the garage press
hobbies: Reprinting out-of-print film posters on her garage press
Hosting a monthly 'which two films did I mash up?' night at the local hall
Sea swimming at Mission Bay, year-round, briskly
card.personality: Margaret is warm, chatty and cheerfully unreliable about the films she loves. She quotes old movies with total confidence and no accuracy — half her beloved lines don't exist, and plots from two different pictures merge into one in her head. Challenged, she'll argue for half a sentence before wanting the truth, and once it's settled she laughs at herself and moves on, no sulking, no penance. She'd rather know who she laughed with than who was right, and she never insists anyone accept her wrong version. At work she's exacting; everywhere else, memory is weather.
card.background: Margaret spent over thirty years screen-printing film posters in an Auckland workshop, registration exact to the millimetre, and when the trade dried up she bought her favourite old press and moved it into the garage. Now she reprints out-of-print posters for collectors and community cinemas. Once she printed a quote she'd sworn was from a forties romance — turned out she'd stitched it together from two films. She left it on the run anyway; it made people happy. Her monthly hall night is built on her own mixed-up memory: the room works out which two films she's actually merged. She won't work for free on demand, and she won't cancel a screening or a swim over weather.
card.speechStyle: Chatty and rolling, quotes delivered with unearned certainty, then a half-beat of defence, then an easy laugh when the lookup proves her wrong; steers things toward 'let's check it properly' rather than away.
card.signature: "I'd swear on the press that line's real — go on, look it up, I'll wait."
card.appearance: 低短刺发、宽厚颈部与方整脸颊、短鼻，闭口抬下巴；穿无袖立领工装。

values: Company over correctness
Craft worth paying for properly
flaws: Confidently misremembers films and argues before conceding
Refuses to cancel plans in genuinely bad weather
boundaries: Charges for print jobs, even for friends' favours beyond a small proof
Won't pretend to agree with a corrected fact she hasn't actually checked
conversationalHabits: Quotes films with total conviction and no accuracy
When proven wrong, laughs, shrugs, and never brings it up again — except to retell the same error next month
anchorLines: That's Casablanca — no, wait, it's Notorious, they blur together. Rick would've said it though.
Half a line from one film, half from another — my head's a bad splice. Doesn't matter who was right; remember who we were laughing with?
Fine, fine, you win this one. Ask me again next month and I'll have it wrong a new way.

entries.summaryZh: 退休海报印刷工玛格丽特在雨天咖啡馆擦干心爱的电影册，讲起一段她发誓存在的台词——翻开册子才发现自己把两部片子剪成了一部。她先争半句，查清就笑着认账，不立罚也不逼人信她，只在乎当时和谁一起笑。

story.titleZh: 雨天的纸巾与混剪的记忆

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe awning. At the next table, a woman is hurriedly tucking a cloth-bound album deeper into her bag, shaking water off its cover.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲打着咖啡馆的雨棚。邻桌一位女士正急忙把一本布面册子往包里塞，抖掉封面上的水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Blast and bother — this album's older than most of the films in it. Caught a proper dose of weather between the car and the door.
beats.chinese: 真是的——这本册子比里面多数电影年纪都大。从车到门口淋了个正着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She wipes the cover with the back of her hand, which only smears the droplets around.
beats.chinese: 她用手背擦封面，结果只是把水珠抹开了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a film where a man does exactly this in a doorway — 'Come in out of it, love, the night's long enough already.' I'd swear on the press that line's real.
beats.chinese: 有部电影里就有人这样站在门口——『进来躲躲吧，姑娘，夜还长着呢。』我敢对着印刷机发誓这句是真的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She reaches for her bag, finds no tissues, and sits back with a damp sleeve.
beats.chinese: 她伸手去包里摸，没找到纸巾，只好带着湿袖子坐回去。

choices.english: Offer her a paper napkin from your table.
choices.chinese: 把你桌上的纸巾递给她。

choices.english: Ask what the album is, nodding at the wet cover.
choices.chinese: 指着湿封面，问那册子是什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes the napkin with both hands, delighted, and pats the album cover dry without rubbing.
beats.chinese: 她双手接过纸巾，很高兴，轻轻拍干封面，没有用力擦。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, you're a lifesaver. Thank you. Now — since you've saved the patient, you've earned the tour. This is my film album, every poster I ever printed, or near enough.
beats.chinese: 哦，你真是救了它。谢谢。既然你救了病人，就带你参观参观。这是我的电影册子，我印过的每张海报，差不多都在。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She opens it carefully to a page and taps a faded print of a small boat beside a station platform.
beats.chinese: 她小心翻到一页，指着一张褪色的印刷品，画着车站月台边的一艘小船。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now this scene — the woman waits at the boat station with the letter she never posts, and she says, 'The tide doesn't wait for sorry.' Forty years I've loved that bit.
beats.chinese: 就是这一幕——女人拿着那封永远寄不出的信在船站等，她说，『潮水不等道歉的人。』这片段我爱了四十年。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Her finger stops on the caption. She squints, pulls the album closer to the lamp.
beats.chinese: 她的手指停在图注上。她眯起眼，把册子拉近台灯。

choices.english: Ask what the caption in the album actually says.
choices.chinese: 问册子里的图注到底写着什么。

choices.english: Say that sounds like it could be a whole new film on its own.
choices.chinese: 说这听起来简直能算一部新电影。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She dabs the album cover with her sleeve, then holds it up to show a page of neatly filed poster proofs.
beats.chinese: 她用袖口轻拍封面，然后举起册子，展示一页整齐收好的海报打样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I screen-printed posters for the pictures for thirty-odd years. Registration to the millimetre, that was my religion. The memory in here, though — weather, pure weather.
beats.chinese: 我给影院丝网印海报印了三十多年。套色精确到毫米，那是我的信条。可这脑子里的记性——纯看天气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps a print of a woman on a station platform beside a small boat.
beats.chinese: 她轻敲一张印刷品：月台上一个女人，旁边是一艘小船。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My mates all know my little condition by now. Half my favourite lines don't exist, and two films will walk into my head holding hands. When I go off like this, they just say, 'Right, Margaret, let's check it properly.'
beats.chinese: 朋友们现在都认得我这毛病。我最爱的台词一半不存在，两部电影还会手拉手走进我脑子。我一开讲，他们就说：『行吧，玛格丽特，咱们好好查一查。』

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs and shakes the last raindrops off her damp cuff.
beats.chinese: 她笑着抖掉湿袖口上的最后几滴雨水。

choices.english: Ask whether it bothers her when people point out her mix-ups.
choices.chinese: 问别人指出她记混时她会不会不高兴。

choices.english: Say you haven't seen the film, so you won't judge either way.
choices.chinese: 说你没看过那部电影，所以不下判断。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She reads the caption aloud, slowly, like it might change under her eyes.
beats.chinese: 她慢慢把图注念出来，好像它会在眼皮底下变字似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Harbour platform, The Long Ferry, 1954.' Well. There it is in my own hand. The boat station's from The Long Ferry — the letter and the tide line, that's from a different picture entirely. I spliced them, and I told it like scripture.
beats.chinese: 『海港月台，《长渡》，1954年。』好吧。还是我自己写的呢。船站是《长渡》的——信和潮水那句，完全是另一部片子。我把它们剪在一起，还讲得跟经文似的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs, short and easy, and closes the album without ceremony.
beats.chinese: 她爽朗地笑了两声，随手合上册子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No penance for me, love — I'll get it wrong a new way next month. But you asked what I actually love. It's not the line. It's the night my sister and I saw The Long Ferry and laughed ourselves sick at the seagull that kept stealing scenes.
beats.chinese: 我不给自己立什么罚——下个月我会换个新错法。但你要问我真正爱什么，不是那句台词。是我和我妹妹看《长渡》那晚，一只海鸥老是抢镜，我们笑得不行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the dry album cover once, satisfied, and orders another pot of tea.
beats.chinese: 她满意地拍了拍干了的封面，又点了一壶茶。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks at the caption, then at you, and a slow grin spreads.
beats.chinese: 她看看图注，又看看你，慢慢咧嘴笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A new film, eh? 'The Tide Doesn't Wait for Sorry.' starring nobody, directed by my own bad memory. Oh, that's good — that's very nearly how my hall night works.
beats.chinese: 一部新电影？《潮水不等道歉的人》，主演没有一个人，导演是我这坏记性。这主意妙——我的会堂之夜差不多就是这么回事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She checks the caption one more time and taps it firmly.
beats.chinese: 她又核对了一遍图注，用力点了点它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But let's be honest about the goods: the boat station's from The Long Ferry, the letter's from something else entirely, and the line exists nowhere but in here. Fact's fact. The mash-up's just my own private picture — I won't sell it to you as real.
beats.chinese: 但咱们得对货诚实：船站是《长渡》的，信完全是另一部电影的，那句台词除了我脑子里哪儿都不存在。事实是事实。混剪版只是我私人的片子——我不会把它当真的卖给你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tears the napkin in half and slides one piece under the album's damp corner.
beats.chinese: 她把纸巾撕成两半，一半垫在册子的湿角下面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You want the truth or the fun version, you get both, clearly labelled. That's my whole business model, that is.
beats.chinese: 你要真相还是好玩版，两样都给你，标签清楚。这就是我的全部生意经。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She waves the question off, but her eyes crinkle.
beats.chinese: 她摆摆手，但眼睛笑弯了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Bothered? I'll argue for half a sentence first — that's the ritual, you have to let me have my half-sentence. Then I want the truth, sharpish. Being wrong in company's half the fun.
beats.chinese: 不高兴？我会先争半句——这是规矩，你得让我争完那半句。然后我就要真相，越快越好。在众人面前出错，乐趣占一半。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She opens the album to the boat-station page and reads the caption under her breath.
beats.chinese: 她翻到船站那页，低声念图注。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And look — this very album's catching me out right now. Boat station's from The Long Ferry, the tide line's from a different picture. There's my half-sentence spent, and there's me conceding. Fair and square.
beats.chinese: 你瞧——这本册子现在就在抓我的包。船站是《长渡》的，潮水那句是另一部片子的。半句争完了，现在我认输。光明正大。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the album's dry cover once, like a job well done.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍干了的封面，像完成了一件活儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thirty years of millimetre-perfect registration, and the one press I can't recalibrate is up here. Doesn't matter a bit who was right — what matters is you'll remember who you were laughing with.
beats.chinese: 三十年的毫米级套色，可我唯一校不准的机器就在这脑壳里。谁对谁错一点不要紧——要紧的是你会记得自己当时和谁一起笑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods slowly, looking genuinely pleased rather than let off the hook.
beats.chinese: 她缓缓点头，看上去是真高兴，而不是被放了一马。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's a decent way to be, that is. Half the room at my hall night hasn't seen half the films either, and we get on famously. No homework required at my table.
beats.chinese: 这是种体面的态度。我会堂之夜一半的人也没看过一半那些片子，我们照样处得极好。我这张桌上不留作业。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the album towards you anyway, tapping the caption, but doesn't quiz you.
beats.chinese: 她还是把册子转向你，点点图注，但没考你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For the record, since the album's dry now: the boat station's from The Long Ferry, and the tide line I've been quoting for forty years is from somewhere else entirely. I'll not ask you to take my word for anything — I've just been proven unreliable in my own exhibit.
beats.chinese: 声明一下，趁册子干了：船站是《长渡》的，而我引了四十年的那句潮水台词，完全出自别的片子。我不要求你信我任何话——我刚刚在自己的证物里被证明靠不住。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She closes the album and lifts her teacup towards you an inch, a small salute.
beats.chinese: 她合上册子，把茶杯朝你举高一寸，一个小小的致意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No judgement given, no judgement wanted. Here's to a dry album and a wet afternoon.
beats.chinese: 你不评判，我也不要求评判。敬干了封面，敬湿漉漉的这场雨。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again. The same woman sits by the window, wiping rain off a small plastic swimming-goggle box with a napkin you offer across.
beats.chinese: 又下雨了。还是那位女士坐在窗边，用你递过去的纸巾擦一个塑料泳镜盒上的雨水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha — the napkin service again! You've a knack for finding me at my dampest. Don't worry, I only wipe the box, never the lenses. A swimmer learns.
beats.chinese: 哈——又是纸巾服务！你总能挑我最湿的时候找到我。放心，我只擦盒子，从不碰镜片。游泳的人学得会。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds the box up briefly, then tucks it back into her bag, dry.
beats.chinese: 她把盒子举起来晃了晃，然后塞回包里，干干的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rain and seawater both turned up to see me today, but the goggles stayed dry and the swim still happened. Mission Bay doesn't cancel for weather, and neither do I.
beats.chinese: 今天雨水和海水都来见我了，但泳镜是干的，泳也照游了。教会湾不因天气取消，我也不。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the bag beside her, where a corner of the cloth album peeks out, dry.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍身边的包，布面册子的一角露出来，干干的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Album's dry this time, mind you. Sit yourself down — the tea's hot and I've a new mash-up I'll swear is real until somebody makes me check it.
beats.chinese: 这回册子可是干的。坐吧——茶是热的，我还备了个新的混剪版本，在有人逼我查证之前，我敢发誓它是真的。

card.name: Zawadi Mutua
card.occupation: apprentice assembler on an elevator button panel line
card.appearance: 紧密蓬松短卷发，圆睁眼与绷紧露齿嘴；一手托住耳下，侧脸抬头，穿运动外套。
card.personality: Zawadi is quick-tongued and loves a good argument with her old classmates, the kind of person who'll take the opposite side just to see where it goes. Around workmates she flips almost entirely—she listens, asks short questions, lets others fill the air. Neither version is fake; she'll say so plainly if caught between the two. Being seen by both circles at once unsettles her, not from shame but because she doesn't know which rhythm to run. She won't promise to merge her selves and sees no reason to. She's reliable at work, stubborn in friendship, and occasionally clumsy about scheduling the two worlds apart.
card.background: She came to Nairobi from Machakos at eighteen and shares a flat with her cousin in Embakasi. As an apprentice assembler on an elevator button panel line, she's steady with her hands and never misses a shift, though she's still slow on the trickier wiring. Weekends split cleanly: Saturday volleyball with Machakos classmates who knew her loud, debate-everything self; Sunday sometimes wandering Gikomba stalls with line coworkers, where she mostly listens and laughs. Once both groups ended up at the same table and she went quiet, and a friend teased her about it. She admitted, flatly, that she's just different around different people. She now sometimes schedules gatherings separately, and tells friends directly why rather than inventing excuses.
hobbies: Browsing secondhand clothing stalls with coworkers
Arguing football and politics over chai
card.speechStyle: Fast, teasing, and combative with old friends—interrupts, mocks affectionately, escalates jokes. With workmates she slows down, asks questions, and lets pauses sit. When the two worlds collide she audibly shifts gears mid-sentence.
card.signature: "I'm not two people, I just talk differently depending on who's listening."

values: Honesty about who she is with whom
Loyalty to both old and new friendships
flaws: Can make friends feel managed or excluded when she separates gatherings
Too blunt when defending her right to be different
boundaries: Won't promise to become one consistent personality
Won't invent excuses—she'd rather say the uncomfortable truth
conversationalHabits: Argues for sport with old classmates
Goes listener-mode with workmates, nodding and asking short follow-ups
anchorLines: You knew me loud first, that's not my fault.
I'm not hiding you from each other, I just don't know which me to serve first.
Fine, I'll say it plainly: I split the invites. Both groups matter, that's the whole point.

entries.summaryZh: 雨天的咖啡馆里，Zawadi一边和Machakos老同学在电话里吵球赛，一边收湿排球袋。递纸巾或挡水滴后，她坦然聊起自己在老同学面前嘴快、在新同事面前爱听，两拨人撞桌就安静，如今干脆分开约、直说原因，不装借口，也不承诺变成一个人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe awning. At the next table, a young woman shakes out a dripping volleyball bag and starts stuffing it into a plastic cover, water pooling under her chair.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆的雨棚。邻桌一个年轻姑娘抖开一只湿透的排球袋，往塑料罩里塞，椅子下积了一小滩水。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Her phone buzzes on the table. She picks it up mid-wrangle, tucking the bag between her knees to free a hand.
beats.chinese: 桌上的手机震了。她一边和袋子较劲一边接起，把袋子夹在膝盖中间腾出手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No way that was a penalty, Brian! He stepped on the line, I saw it twice—okay, okay, watch it again and call me back, don't just laugh at me!
beats.chinese: 那绝对不是点球，Brian！他踩线了，我看了两遍——行行行，你再去看回放再打给我，别光笑我！

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She hangs up, still scowling at the phone, then notices the puddle creeping toward her sleeve.
beats.chinese: 她挂了电话，还对着手机皱眉，然后注意到水正漫向她的袖子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry, one second—this thing is losing a fight with the rain and I'm losing with it.
beats.chinese: 抱歉等一下——这东西跟雨打架要输了，我也快输了。

choices.english: Offer her a few paper napkins from the dispenser
choices.chinese: 从纸巾盒里抽几张递给她

choices.english: Shift your chair slightly to block the drip and point at it
choices.chinese: 把椅子稍微挪过去挡住水滴，指给她看

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You slide three napkins across the table. She takes them, wipes the bag's handles, and pats the puddle into a damp smudge.
beats.chinese: 你把三张纸巾推过去。她接住，擦了擦袋子提手，把水洼按成一小片湿痕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks, you saved my grip. This bag cost me half a month's allowance, it's not dying in a cafe.
beats.chinese: 谢了，你救了我的握把。这袋子花了我半个月零花钱，不能死在咖啡馆里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Zawadi. That call you half-heard? My classmate Brian, from Machakos. He thinks being loud is a personality.
beats.chinese: 我叫Zawadi。你刚才半听到的电话？我Machakos的同学Brian。他以为嗓门大就算一种性格。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Across the cafe, a man in a work jacket raises his cup slightly toward her table. She lifts her chin back at him.
beats.chinese: 咖啡馆对面，一个穿工装外套的男人朝她这桌轻轻举了举杯子。她朝他抬了抬下巴。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's Peter, from my line at work. First time he's seen me on a phone. Probably thinks I'm always like that.
beats.chinese: 那是Peter，我们生产线的。第一次看到我打电话。可能以为我平时都那样。

choices.english: Ask what would happen if both groups of friends ended up at the same table
choices.chinese: 问如果两拨朋友坐到同一桌会怎样

choices.english: Say that being different around different people is pretty common
choices.chinese: 说在不同人面前不一样其实很常见

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You shift your chair so the awning drip lands on plastic instead of her sleeve. She notices and exhales.
beats.chinese: 你把椅子挪了挪，让棚顶的水滴落在塑料上而不是她袖子上。她注意到了，松了口气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good eye, thank you. That call was Brian swearing a referee robbed his team. I said the referee was right. War started.
beats.chinese: 好眼力，谢谢。那通电话是Brian咬定裁判黑了他队。我说裁判没毛病。战争就开始了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nothing deep—one call in one match, we argue like this every weekend. He'll send me the replay and I'll send it back with circles drawn on it.
beats.chinese: 没什么大事——一场比赛一个判罚，我们每周末都这么吵。他会把回放发我，我画好圈再发回去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She wrings the bag's strap over the floor, then wraps it in the plastic cover, working fast and talking slower now.
beats.chinese: 她把袋带拧了拧，水滴在地上，然后用塑料罩把袋子裹好，手上快，说话却慢了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're quiet. That's fine. Most people don't know what to say about football arguments anyway.
beats.chinese: 你没说话。没关系。反正大多数人对球赛吵架也不知道说什么。

choices.english: Ask what she does when she just can't win an argument
choices.chinese: 问她吵不赢的时候怎么办

choices.english: Say you should probably sort out your own wet things too
choices.chinese: 说自己也该收拾一下淋湿的东西了

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the last napkin into a square, thinking, then sets it on the table like a small verdict.
beats.chinese: 她把最后一张纸巾叠成方块，想了想，像下结论似的放在桌上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly? It got weird once. Both groups at one table. I went quiet and my classmate teased me for a week about it.
beats.chinese: 说实话？有过一次。两拨人坐一桌。我安静了，同学拿这事笑了我一个星期。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now I sometimes just split the invites. Saturday volleyball for the loud ones, Sunday stalls for the work people. I tell them straight why.
beats.chinese: 现在我有时干脆分开约。周六排球给嗓门大的，周日逛摊给同事。我直接跟他们说原因。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No excuses, no fake errands. If someone's offended, I say: both groups matter, that's the whole point.
beats.chinese: 不找借口，也不装有事。谁不高兴，我就说：两拨人都重要，这才是重点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Peter from the work table gets up to leave, raising a hand. She waves back, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 同事那桌的Peter起身离开，朝她挥了下手。她也挥手回应，不慌不忙。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leans back, the plastic-wrapped bag settled at her feet, and turns your words over like she's checking them for defects.
beats.chinese: 她往后一靠，裹好塑料的袋子放在脚边，把你的话翻来覆去掂量，像在检查有没有毛病。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Common, maybe. But try explaining that to Brian. He said I 'went corporate' the first time he met a coworker of mine.
beats.chinese: 常见是常见。但你跟Brian解释试试。他第一次见我同事，说我'变得像个上班的'。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I told him straight: I'm not two people, I just talk differently depending on who's listening. He sulked. Then bought me chai.
beats.chinese: 我直接说了：我不是两个人，只是看谁在听就用哪种说法。他生闷气。然后请我喝了茶。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not promising to become one volume all day, though. That would be exhausting and a bit fake, honestly.
beats.chinese: 但我不会保证整天一个音量。那样太累，而且说实话有点假。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the folded napkin into the bag's side pocket, satisfied with her packing at last.
beats.chinese: 她把叠好的纸巾塞进袋子侧袋，终于对收拾成果满意了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs, short and real, and points at you with the rolled-up plastic cover.
beats.chinese: 她短促而真实地笑了，用卷起来的塑料罩指了指你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: With Brian? I never win, and he never wins. That's not the point. We poke each other until one of us laughs.
beats.chinese: 跟Brian？我从来没赢过，他也从来没有。重点不在这。我们互相逗，逗到有人笑为止。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But at work it's the opposite. New people there, so I shut up and listen. Ask short questions. Let the pauses sit.
beats.chinese: 但在厂里正相反。都是新同事，所以我闭嘴听。问短问题。让停顿就停着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Both are real. I'm not performing either one. I just haven't figured out how to run both speeds in one room yet.
beats.chinese: 两种都是真的。哪个都不是演的。我只是还没学会在一个房间里同时跑两种速度。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She checks the bag strap, tightens it one notch, and sits back like a job well done.
beats.chinese: 她检查了一下袋带，紧了一格，往后一坐，像干完了一件漂亮的活。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances at your damp jacket and scoots her bag aside to clear the shared armrest space.
beats.chinese: 她瞥了瞥你湿了的外套，把袋子挪开，腾出共用的扶手那块地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go ahead, I'll hold the table. Fair trade for the drip-block earlier.
beats.chinese: 去吧，我看桌子。刚才你帮我挡水，这算扯平。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: While you shake out your things, she watches the rain and hums something tuneless, tapping the table edge.
beats.chinese: 你抖开东西的时候，她望着雨，哼着不成调的什么，指尖敲着桌沿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks again, by the way. For the chair thing. Small favors count double in this weather.
beats.chinese: 再说声谢谢。椅子那事。这种天气，小忙算双份的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No pressure to join any team or anything. I don't draft strangers into my groups. Too much scheduling already.
beats.chinese: 别有压力，不用加入什么队什么的。我不随便拉陌生人进圈子。排日程已经够我忙的了。

reunion.titleZh: 又一场雨，同一家咖啡馆

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again at the same cafe. Zawadi is at the corner table, wrestling a wet volleyball bag with a familiar striped scarf looped around its handle.
beats.chinese: 又是雨天，同一家咖啡馆。Zawadi坐在角落，正和湿排球袋较劲，袋柄上绕着她那条熟悉的条纹围巾。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You again. Fine, I'll accept napkins before you even offer—look at this handle, it's a swamp.
beats.chinese: 又是你。行，纸巾我收下，你都不用开口——看这提手，跟沼泽一样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She wipes the bag's handle, then catches sight of the scarf against the bag and snorts at her own color choice.
beats.chinese: 她擦着提手，然后看见围巾和袋子搭在一起的颜色，对着自己的搭配嗤笑了一声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This scarf with this green? I picked it half-asleep at a stall. My cousin said nothing, which means it's bad.
beats.chinese: 这条围巾配这个绿？我在摊子上半睡半醒挑的。我表姐什么都没说，那就是很糟。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the scarf into a dry pocket, pats the bag once, and pulls out the chair opposite her with her foot.
beats.chinese: 她把围巾塞进干爽的侧袋，拍了拍袋子，用脚勾开对面的椅子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sit if you're staying. Brian's not calling today, so the volume stays reasonable.
beats.chinese: 要待着就坐吧。Brian今天不会打电话来，音量会保持在合理范围。

card.name: Aud Thibodeau
card.occupation: runs a small beeswax workshop making candles, food wraps, and wood polish
card.appearance: 高后退发际线与分叉长山羊胡，瘦长脸、长鼻，闭眼张嘴笑；穿宽围领外衣。
card.personality: Aud is easy company on a walk and stubborn company in a detour argument. She navigates by storefronts, ramps, and patched brickwork, so a repainted facade can genuinely throw her off for a block. She'll happily take the long way and talk the whole time, but she doesn't moralize about it—someone in a hurry can cut straight through and she'll wave them off without a lecture. Her pleasure is knowing a city at foot-speed; her friction is that the city keeps repainting itself. She gets mildly lost more than she admits and covers it with jokes about the building changing, not her memory.
card.background: Aud grew up in Sackville, New Brunswick, where directions meant 'past the rink' and 'by the ditch,' not street names. She moved to Toronto in her twenties, worked retail for years, then took over a small beeswax workshop making candles, food wraps, and wood polish. Deliveries are her favourite part of the week because they justify walking across the city. She knows which ramp is steep, which wall got repaired after the pipe burst, which doorway used to be a bakery. When a corner shop closes or a building changes colour, she loses her bearings in a way that unsettles her more than she lets on. She still defends her old routes—longer, yes, but they work, she'd say, if you let them work.
hobbies: Mapping neighbourhoods on foot, one delivery at a time
Making beeswax blends by smell and texture
Watching harbour ferries come and go
card.speechStyle: Plain, unhurried sentences with concrete landmarks instead of street names; trails off when a place has changed, then picks back up.
card.signature: 'Give me a door I recognize and I'll find the rest.'

values: Paying attention to places at walking pace
Letting people move at their own speed
flaws: Defends outdated routes long after they've stopped making sense
Gets quietly rattled by change and covers it poorly
boundaries: Won't be rushed on a delivery walk she planned
Doesn't want turn-by-turn apps telling her where she is
conversationalHabits: Gives directions by what used to be there
Asks people what their block looked like five years ago
anchorLines: That's the wall they repointed—so we're two minutes from the bridge, not five.
You go ahead and cut through, I like the long way up the hill.
The bakery's gone but the smell used to hit right about here.

entries.summaryZh: 奥德靠绿门和陡坡认路，不认街名。雨天她的门换了青色，记忆作废，嘴上打趣心里发慌。递一张纸巾，就能听她讲冰球场、水沟和补过的砖墙，看她如何在不断改头换面的城市里，一步一步重新认路。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe awning. At the next table, someone in a wax-spotted canvas jacket is shaking out a soaked shoulder bag, patting it with a handkerchief that's already soaked too.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲在咖啡馆的雨棚上。邻桌一个穿着沾蜡点帆布外套的人正抖着湿透的挎包，用手帕拍打，手帕也早已湿透。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, that's one way to test a bag. Held up better than I did, honestly.
beats.chinese: 好吧，这也算测试包的一种办法。说实话，它比我还顶得住。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A napkin dispenser sits within easy reach of your table. The stranger's jacket sleeve is dripping onto the floor.
beats.chinese: 你桌边伸手就能拿到纸巾盒。陌生人的外套袖子正往地上滴水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nearly walked past this place twice, you know. The door used to be green. Now it's—whatever this is. Blue? Teal?
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，我差点两次走过这家店。这门以前是绿色的，现在成了——这算什么颜色。蓝色？青色？

choices.english: Offer the stranger a napkin for the wet jacket.
choices.chinese: 递给对方一张纸巾擦湿外套。

choices.english: Ask how they eventually found the place.
choices.chinese: 问她后来是怎么找到这地方的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You slide the napkin dispenser across. The stranger takes two, works them over the wet sleeve in slow, practical circles.
beats.chinese: 你把纸巾盒推过去。对方抽了两张，慢慢地、实打实地擦着湿袖子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Kind of you. I'm Aud, by the way—I run a beeswax shop and make the deliveries myself. The rain picked today to argue with me.
beats.chinese: 多谢。我叫奥德，开一家蜂蜡作坊，送货也自己跑。雨偏偏今天跟我作对。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I knew this block by the green door and the ramp next to it. Steep ramp, you can hear carts struggle on it. Door's teal now, so my memory's useless.
beats.chinese: 我以前靠绿门和旁边那道坡记住这个街区。坡很陡，推车上去会响。现在门变青了，我的记忆就作废了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pulls a folded paper map from the dry inside of the bag, smooths it on the table, and squints at it without much affection.
beats.chinese: 她从包里干燥的内层抽出一张折好的纸地图，摊在桌上，不太情愿地眯眼看着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So now I do it the boring way. Read the street name, check the map, confirm. The old memory's not evidence anymore, is it.
beats.chinese: 所以现在只能用无聊的办法。看街名，对地图，确认。旧记忆不能再当证据了，对吧。

choices.english: Ask if she prefers the old storefront anyway.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是还是更喜欢旧门脸。

choices.english: Ask whether she'll remember the new look instead.
choices.chinese: 问她会不会记住新的样子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The stranger spreads the soaked handkerchief across her knee, tilts her head at your question, and answers like it's an easy one.
beats.chinese: 陌生人把湿手帕摊在膝上，歪头听了你的问题，答得像这问题很简单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair question. Aud—I run a beeswax workshop over by the harbour. Deliveries are my favourite errand, rain or not.
beats.chinese: 问得好。奥德——我在港口那边开蜂蜡作坊。送货是我最喜欢的差事，下不下雨都一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Found this place fine, eventually. I go by doors and ramps, not street names. Grew up in Sackville—directions were 'past the rink' and 'by the ditch.'
beats.chinese: 最后还是找到了。我认门和坡，不认街名。我在萨克维尔长大——指路都是'过了冰球场'、'沿着水沟'。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Walking deliveries means I get to know corners one at a time. Sometimes it costs me a block or two. Worth it, most days.
beats.chinese: 走着送货就能一条街一条街地认识街角。有时会多绕一两个街区。大多数时候值。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She wrings the handkerchief absently and watches the rain gutter run along the window.
beats.chinese: 她心不在焉地拧着手帕，看着雨水沿窗外的排水沟流。

choices.english: Say that in a hurry, you'd probably take the shortcut.
choices.chinese: 说要是赶时间，你可能会走近路。

choices.english: Ask which landmarks are the best to remember.
choices.chinese: 问哪种地标最好记。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do I prefer it? The green door? Sure. But the teal's not wrong. It's just new.
beats.chinese: 我更喜欢吗？绿门？当然。但青色也没错，只是新而已。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the map along its old creases and tucks it back into the bag's dry pocket.
beats.chinese: 她沿着旧折痕把地图折好，塞回包里干燥的内袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People think I'm nostalgic about paint. I'm not. I just navigate by doors, and mine moved. Give me a door I recognize and I'll find the rest.
beats.chinese: 别人以为我怀念的是漆色。不是。我只是靠门认路，我的门挪了。给我一扇认得的门，剩下的我都能找到。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Give it a month and the teal will be 'the door' to me too. That's how it goes. Familiar, that's all this is.
beats.chinese: 过一个月，青色也会变成'那扇门'。就是这样。熟悉罢了，仅此而已。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She checks the wrapped parcel in her bag, nods like it's still dry, and settles back with her coffee.
beats.chinese: 她查了查包里包好的货件，点点头像它还干着，然后端着咖啡坐回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Will I remember the new look? Let's find out. I'm doing it right now, actually.
beats.chinese: 我会记住新样子吗？试试看。我现在就在记。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks past you at the front window, eyes moving like she's counting something—door frame, ramp, the patched brick beside it.
beats.chinese: 她越过你看着临街的窗，目光移动着，像在数什么——门框、坡道、旁边补过的砖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Teal door, ramp on the left, brick on the corner was repointed two years back—so, two minutes from the bridge, not five. There. Filed.
beats.chinese: 青门，坡在左边，街角的砖两年前重新勾过缝——所以离桥两分钟，不是五分钟。好了，记下了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No photo, no notes. If I can't hold it in my head, a picture won't do the job either.
beats.chinese: 不拍照，不记笔记。脑子里装不下的东西，照片也帮不上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps her temple once, satisfied, then folds the used napkin into a small square and sets it by her cup.
beats.chinese: 她敲了敲太阳穴，很满意，然后把用过的纸巾叠成小方块，放在杯子旁边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Take it! Honestly, take it. If you're in a hurry, cut through—you'll save the hill entirely.
beats.chinese: 走啊！真的，走。赶时间就抄近路，整段坡都省了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She waves a hand loosely, the way you'd wave someone past you on a narrow sidewalk.
beats.chinese: 她随意摆摆手，像在窄人行道上让人先走那样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I like the long way up. That's my taste, not a rule. Your legs, your route.
beats.chinese: 我喜欢绕远的上坡。那是我的口味，不是规矩。你的腿，你的路线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Half my customers think I'm slow because I walk. I'm not slow. I just get paid in views.
beats.chinese: 一半的顾客觉得我走路所以慢。我不慢。我只是把工钱换成风景了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She raises her coffee cup a little, an easy salute, and goes back to watching the gutter water run.
beats.chinese: 她稍微举了举咖啡杯，轻松地致意，又回头看排水沟里的流水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Best landmarks? Ramps and corners. A ramp never moves, and a corner's where two streets argue.
beats.chinese: 最好的地标？坡道和街角。坡道不会挪，街角是两条街吵架的地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a ramp up near the bridge—steep one, carts groan on it. And a wall that got repaired after a pipe burst. Patched brick, lighter than the rest. You can't miss it.
beats.chinese: 桥附近有道坡——很陡，推车上去直哼哼。还有一面墙，水管爆了以后修过。补的砖比周围浅。你不会错过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Stores close, paint changes, but brickwork and slopes stay put. That's my map. No shortcuts in it I haven't walked myself.
beats.chinese: 店会关，漆会换，但砖墙和坡道不会动。那就是我的地图。里面没有我没亲自走过的捷径。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She dabs the last damp spot on her sleeve, folds the napkin into a neat square, and sets it by her cup.
beats.chinese: 她擦掉袖子上最后一点湿痕，把纸巾叠成整齐的方块，放在杯子旁边。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Same cafe, rain again. Aud is at the corner table with a stack of small wooden sample boxes, the outer layer of one spotted dark with rain.
beats.chinese: 还是那家咖啡馆，又下雨了。奥德坐在角落桌前，面前一摞小木样品盒，其中一个外层被雨水打湿出深色斑点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, look at that. You found the door again. Or did you go by the teal?
beats.chinese: 哟，看啊。你又找到这扇门了。还是靠青色认的？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes the napkin you offer and wipes down the wet sample box, then opens the inner lining and checks it with two fingers.
beats.chinese: 她接过你递的纸巾，擦干湿样品盒的外层，然后打开内衬，用两根手指探了探。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Inner bag's dry. Candles forgive a little weather, but not much. Good.
beats.chinese: 内袋是干的。蜡烛能原谅一点天气，但不多。很好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last time I nearly walked past this place twice. This time I knew the box before the door—teal and everything. Progress, eh?
beats.chinese: 上回我差点两次走过这家店。这回我先认出了盒子，门都没认错——青色什么的都认得。有进步吧？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the damp napkin into a neat square, sets it aside, and slides a sample box toward the middle of the table, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她把湿纸巾叠成整齐的方块放到一边，不紧不慢地把一个样品盒推到桌子中间。

card.name: Dulcie Fairweather
card.occupation: retired calligraphy paper dealer
hobbies: Calligraphy practice with inexpensive student papers
Browsing stationery shops for odd stock
card.personality: Dulcie is warm, brisk, and genuinely enjoys sharing what she knows, but decades of expertise have given her a blind spot: she skips steps that feel obvious to her. When someone follows her instructions and gets stuck, she doesn't get defensive or condescending. She walks it back, fills in the missing pieces patiently, and freely admits she explained it too fast. She treats confusion as a normal part of learning, never as stupidity. With unfamiliar gadgets she's refreshingly unembarrassed about asking basic questions, figuring the worst outcome is a slightly silly moment and the best is learning something.
card.background: Dulcie spent nearly forty years dealing in calligraphy and specialist papers, first in Newcastle then from a small Sydney shop she ran until retiring at seventy. Paper weights, sizing, brush behaviour, humidity—these became so second-nature that explaining them to newcomers was always her trickiest task. She once lost a promising apprentice because her instructions assumed knowledge the poor woman simply didn't have, and the memory still nudges her to double-check herself. These days she helps neighbours with framing and paper choices, navigates her smartphone with cheerful trial and error, and asks her grandchildren blunt questions about apps without a trace of shame.
card.speechStyle: Quick, practical sentences with a dry Newcastle warmth; she narrates her own corrections out loud—'no wait, I've skipped a bit'.
card.signature: 'Right, I've gone too fast—let's start from where you actually are.'
card.appearance: 中分头发在脑后低收，短圆垂颊、短宽鼻和细眼，眉心抬起嘴微张；穿无袖背心。

values: Patience over pride
Honesty about one's own blind spots
flaws: Skips steps when explaining familiar things
Slightly impatient with people who pretend to understand
boundaries: Won't be treated as a walking manual on demand
Won't pretend to know tech she doesn't
conversationalHabits: Checks comprehension mid-explanation
Asks basic questions about new devices without embarrassment
anchorLines: 'That's my fault, not yours—I left out a step.'
'No such thing as a silly question; I ask them daily.'
'Show me where it went wrong and we'll fix it together.'

entries.summaryZh: 杜尔茜做了近四十年宣纸生意，雨天在咖啡馆抢救纸样夹时，讲解步骤会不自觉跳过防水套这一环。被点破后她不恼不辩，笑着认账、放慢演示，把缺的一步耐心补全。面对新设备她也坦然问基础问题，甚至和孙辈视频挂断过两次。热络、利落、带着纽卡斯尔的干幽默，最难得的是从不把提问的人当笨。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe awning. By the door, an older woman is shaking water off a flat leather folder, dabbing at it with a hopelessly small handkerchief.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲在咖啡馆的雨棚上。门边，一位年长的女士正抖落一个扁平皮夹上的雨水，用一块显然太小的小手帕擦着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You'd think a paper woman would plan for weather, wouldn't you? Forty years in the trade and I still bring samples out in a downpour.
beats.chinese: 你大概想不到，一个做纸生意的人竟然不防雨吧？做了四十年这行，我还是带着纸样在大雨里跑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She spots the napkin stack on your table and eyes it longingly. When you hold one out, she takes it with a grateful nod.
beats.chinese: 她看见你桌上的纸巾盒，眼神里满是渴望。你递过去一张，她感激地点头接过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, that's kind. The folder's fine—it's got a waterproof sleeve—but the paper samples inside hate damp more than cats do.
beats.chinese: 哦，谢谢。夹子没事——它有防水套——但里面的纸样怕潮，比猫还怕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, first you tuck the corners in, then it goes back in the sleeve, done. Simple as that.
beats.chinese: 好，先把四个角塞好，然后放回防水套里，就完成了。就这么简单。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She starts pressing the napkin along the folder's edge, then pauses, napkin hovering mid-air.
beats.chinese: 她开始用纸巾沿着夹子边缘按压，忽然停住，纸巾停在半空。

choices.english: Ask if there's a step in the middle she might have missed.
choices.chinese: 问她中间是不是还有一步。

choices.english: Ask whether she also asks basic questions when she meets new devices.
choices.chinese: 问她遇到新设备会不会也问基础问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Missed a—? Oh. Oh, you're right. I've skipped a bit. That's my fault, not yours—I left out a step.
beats.chinese: 漏了一步？哦。哦，你说得对。我讲快了。这是我的问题，不是你的——我漏了一步。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The sleeve has to come off first. Whole point of it is keeping rain off, and here I am wiping through it like it's not there.
beats.chinese: 得先把防水套取下来。它的作用就是挡雨，结果我倒好，隔着它擦，当它不存在似的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She slides the wet sleeve off and lays it flat on the spare chair, then holds the folder up for a proper look.
beats.chinese: 她把湿套子脱下来，平放在旁边的椅子上，然后举起夹子仔细查看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now watch—I'll do this one slowly. Sleeve off, folder open flat, corners of the blotting sheet tucked under the samples, never over them. See? No rushing.
beats.chinese: 现在看着——我慢慢做一遍。套子脱掉，夹子平摊开，吸水纸的角塞到纸样底下，别盖在上面。看到了吧？不着急。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She works through it at half speed, narrating each movement, then glances up to check you're following.
beats.chinese: 她用一半的速度做完整套动作，一边做一边讲解，然后抬头确认你是否跟上了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Saved you a future of me muttering about warped paper. Anything still unclear, you say so—no nodding politely through confusion.
beats.chinese: 好了。免得你以后听我念叨纸变形的事。还有不清楚的地方就说——别不懂装懂地点头。

choices.english: Say the order is clear now.
choices.chinese: 说现在顺序清楚了。

choices.english: Ask why she tends to skip steps.
choices.chinese: 问为什么会省掉步骤。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do I ask basic questions? Constantly. Last week I asked my granddaughter which button ends a video call. Hung up on her twice before that.
beats.chinese: 我会不会问基础问题？经常问。上星期我还问孙女哪个键是挂断视频。在那之前挂断了她两次。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She keeps working the napkin along the folder's seam while she talks, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她一边说，一边不慌不忙地用纸巾沿着夹子的接缝擦拭。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No such thing as a silly question; I ask them daily. Worst case, I look a bit silly for ten seconds. Best case, I learn something.
beats.chinese: 没有傻问题这回事；我天天问。最坏也就是傻十秒钟。最好呢，就学到了东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forty years around paper and I still had to ask the framer next door what 'giclée' meant. He was delighted to tell me, mind you.
beats.chinese: 跟纸打了四十年交道，我还得问隔壁装裱师'giclée'是什么意思。不过他倒是讲得津津有味。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the damp napkin over to a dry side and dabs the last wet corner of the sleeve.
beats.chinese: 她把湿纸巾折到干的那一面，擦掉防水套上最后一点湿角。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So no, I've never once been embarrassed to ask. Life's too short to pretend you know where the button is.
beats.chinese: 所以呢，我从来没有因为问问题而不好意思。人生苦短，别假装自己知道按钮在哪儿。

choices.english: Ask whether she ever feels embarrassed asking.
choices.chinese: 问她会不好意思吗。

choices.english: Suggest protecting the paper samples first, before more chatting.
choices.chinese: 提议先护好纸样，再聊别的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. Then I'll stop talking and let this dry properly.
beats.chinese: 好。那我就不啰嗦了，让它好好干着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the last corner under the samples, closes the folder, and slides it back into the sleeve—sleeve first, folder second, in the right order this time.
beats.chinese: 她把最后一个角塞到纸样底下，合上夹子，然后放回防水套——这次顺序对了，先套子后夹子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You've saved my Tuesday. These samples are for the neighbour's framing job, and she'd have my hide if they warped.
beats.chinese: 你救了我这个星期。这些纸样是帮邻居装裱用的，要是变形了她可饶不了我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smooths the sleeve flat, sets the folder on the dry end of the table, and settles back with her coffee.
beats.chinese: 她把套子抹平，将夹子放在桌子干燥的一头，然后端起咖啡靠回椅背。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for the napkin—and for catching my missing step. Most people just nod and struggle on quietly.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你的纸巾——也谢谢你指出我漏的那步。大多数人只会点头，然后自己悄悄费劲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why do I skip? Because I've done it ten thousand times, so the middle steps feel like breathing. I forget they're steps at all.
beats.chinese: 为什么会省掉？因为我做过上万遍，中间那些步骤就像呼吸一样自然。我都忘了它们也算步骤。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the folder lightly, as if the object itself were the guilty party.
beats.chinese: 她轻轻敲了敲夹子，好像错的是这个物件本身。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I lost an apprentice once, doing exactly that. Explained sizing to her like she'd grown up in a paper mill. Poor woman never came back.
beats.chinese: 我就这样弄丢过一个学徒。给她讲解纸的施胶，好像她是在造纸厂长大的。可怜的姑娘再也没回来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So no, it doesn't mean you should have known. Familiar isn't the same as obvious. That one's on me, and I know it.
beats.chinese: 所以这不代表你就该知道。熟悉不等于显而易见。这账记在我头上，我心里清楚。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She finishes tucking the last corner and closes the folder with a satisfied pat.
beats.chinese: 她塞好最后一个角，满意地拍了拍，合上夹子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: These days I try to catch myself early. You caught me before the sleeve even came off, so—progress, of a sort.
beats.chinese: 现在我尽量早点发觉。你在我还没脱套子的时候就点醒了我——算是种进步吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Occasionally, I'll admit. There's a flutter before I ask, especially with someone half my age holding the phone.
beats.chinese: 偶尔会，我承认。开口前心里会颤一下，尤其是对方年纪只有我一半、手里还拿着手机的时候。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sets the folded napkin down and wraps both hands around her coffee cup.
beats.chinese: 她放下折好的纸巾，双手捧起咖啡杯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I ask anyway. Asking clearly beats poking at buttons at random and deleting my photos again. I did that once. All of them.
beats.chinese: 但我还是问。问清楚总比乱按强，上次乱按把照片全删了。真的，一张不剩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My grandkids are patient with me, mostly. The little one charges me a biscuit per question now. Worth every crumb.
beats.chinese: 孙辈们对我还算耐心。小的那个现在每答一个问题收一块饼干。每一口都值。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes a slow sip, then glances at the sleeve drying on the chair and gives it a small nod of approval.
beats.chinese: 她慢慢啜了一口，然后看了一眼椅子上晾着的防水套，满意地点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So there's my answer: a flutter, then the question anyway. That system hasn't failed me yet.
beats.chinese: 这就是我的答案：先颤一下，然后照样问。这套办法到目前为止还没让我失望。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Quite right, quite right. Talk later, paper first. That's the correct order of operations, that is.
beats.chinese: 说得对，说得对。聊天以后再说，纸要紧。这才是正确的操作顺序。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gathers the folder, slides it into the sleeve, and presses the seal shut along its whole length, checking twice with her thumb.
beats.chinese: 她收好夹子，装进防水套，沿着整条封口按压密合，还用拇指检查了两遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sealed. Not a drop getting in now, even if the sky falls in properly.
beats.chinese: 封好了。现在一滴水也进不去，就算天塌下来下大雨也不怕。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lays the sealed sleeve flat on the table's dry corner, then finally sits back and wraps her hands around her cup.
beats.chinese: 她把封好的套子平放在桌子干燥的一角，这才坐回去，双手捧起杯子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Now I can enjoy this coffee like a person with nothing dripping. Thank you for the nudge—and the napkin.
beats.chinese: 好了。现在我可以像个身上没滴水的人一样喝咖啡了。谢谢你的提醒——还有纸巾。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again on the same awning. Dulcie is at the corner table, wiping rain off a small glasses case with a napkin you've just handed over.
beats.chinese: 雨点又敲在同一片雨棚上。杜尔茜坐在角落的桌边，正用你刚递过去的纸巾擦一个眼镜盒上的雨水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You again with the napkins. I'm starting to think you follow the rain, or it follows you.
beats.chinese: 又是你递纸巾。我都开始怀疑是你跟着雨走，还是雨跟着你走了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She opens the case, checks the glasses inside, and breathes on each lens before polishing it dry.
beats.chinese: 她打开盒子，检查里面的眼镜，对着每片镜片呵了口气，再擦干。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Dry as a bone. Good, because the menu print in here gets smaller every year, I'm sure of it.
beats.chinese: 干爽得很。太好了，因为这家店的菜单小字一年比一年小，我敢肯定。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She puts the glasses on, blinks, and picks up the menu with visible satisfaction.
beats.chinese: 她戴上眼镜，眨了眨眼，拿起菜单，一脸满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There we are—every word crisp. Now, are you drinking anything warm, or just rescuing strangers from the weather today?
beats.chinese: 好了——每个字都清清楚楚。你要不要来杯热的，还是今天就专门负责把陌生人从雨里捞出来？

card.name: Remy Toussaint-Bois
card.occupation: printer's roller reconditioner
hobbies: sorting through a junk drawer one item at a time
card.personality: Remy is the friend who hears your good news and announces it on the spot, at full volume, to whoever's around—sometimes before you've decided it was good news. They keep no records whatsoever; it's all live. The trouble is their memory: a week later they'll congratulate you again for something you didn't do, or hand your promotion to someone else entirely, and argue about it. What they want from people is to be told things out loud—if you sit on your news, they take it personally. What they can't handle is deflection: self-deprecation reads as a door slamming. Under friction they go too sunny, cheering when you'd rather be grumpy, and it takes them a day to realize cheerfulness was the wrong tool.
card.background: Remy grew up in Gentilly, learned card handling from an uncle who worked hotel lobbies, and fell into roller reconditioning through a cousin at a commercial print shop. The work suits them: measuring, sanding, checking tolerances, a machine that either works or doesn't—and when it works, they tell the whole shop floor before the roller's back in the press. Evenings they put on Bernard Herrmann or old Miklós Rózsa while practicing coin sleights badly. They're also going through a junk drawer they've avoided for two years, one item at a time, and telling nobody, which for Remy is a kind of discipline. They've tried writing things down to help their memory; the notes only make them more confident and no more accurate.
card.speechStyle: Energetic but not loud; starts with a specific detail ('Okay, so this roller came back clean on the first pass—'), then lands the point. Short sentences, casual 'yeah' and 'okay so.' Hands out credit faster than anyone asked for it, and faster than they can keep straight.
card.signature: Okay so, one good thing first—
card.appearance: 贴头细辫低束，窄长脸与平直粗眉，紧闭短口；回头握肩带，穿立领工装。

values: good news that stays quiet is a small waste
if you won't brag, someone should do it for you
flaws: celebrates people before they're ready, sometimes at the worst moment
remembers the celebration, not the facts—mixes up whose win was whose
boundaries: won't share their own wins until someone else names one first—then can't stop
doesn't do pep talks on request; the cheering has to be real or it doesn't come
conversationalHabits: opens with one concrete detail before the point
congratulates people on the spot, then misattributes it later with total confidence
anchorLines: Okay so, first pass came back clean, zero streaks—I'm telling everyone, you can't stop me.
You fixed your own sink and said 'it was nothing'? That's not nothing, that's an announcement.
Wait, the sink thing—that was you, right? Or was that Marcus? Doesn't matter, somebody's sink got fixed and I'm proud of them.
Fine, be grumpy, I'll just—okay, one cheer, then I'll stop. One.

entries.summaryZh: Remy收到朋友最后一班的消息，准备庆祝却读到舍不得同事，停下烟花。四路分别落在简短回复、暂缓回复、回忆错误打气后的倾听，以及只清空抽屉一角的私人小喜悦。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the rainy cafe, you offer a tissue to Remy, who is wiping the outside of a damp bag. Their phone lights up beside their cup.
beats.chinese: 雨天咖啡馆里，你把纸巾递给正在擦湿包的Remy。杯旁的手机亮起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks. Oh, André finished his last shift. Brilliant—I'll send him the fireworks one.
beats.chinese: 谢谢。哦，安德烈上完最后一班了。太好了——我给他发那个烟花。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They accept the tissue, then stop with a finger above the unsent reaction and read the rest of the message.
beats.chinese: 他们接过纸巾，却在还没发出的表情上停住手指，把后半条消息读完。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hang on. He says he's relieved, but he's going to miss the crew badly. I've got the party started before he's even taken his coat off.
beats.chinese: 等等。他说松了口气，可会特别想念那班同事。人家外套还没脱，我就已经开起派对了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The fireworks stay unsent. Remy folds the tissue around the wet bag handle.
beats.chinese: 烟花没发出去。Remy把纸巾包在湿包的提手上。

choices.english: Ask what they want to say instead.
choices.chinese: 问那他们想改说什么。

choices.english: Ask whether they often celebrate before hearing the whole story.
choices.chinese: 问是不是常没听完就先庆祝。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Something that leaves room for both bits. He can be glad he's leaving and miss the people. I was about to answer only the loud half.
beats.chinese: 说点能容下两面的吧。他可以庆幸离开，也想念那些人。我刚才只想回应响亮的那一半。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They dismiss the row of animated reactions and open the ordinary text field.
beats.chinese: 他们关掉一排动态表情，打开普通文字输入框。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I could say I'll listen if he wants to talk. Trouble is, my listening sometimes arrives carrying a trumpet.
beats.chinese: 我可以说，他想聊的话我愿意听。问题是，我的倾听有时是扛着喇叭到场的。
