beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They glance at the blank reply, then set the phone beside the cup rather than typing straight away.
beats.chinese: 他们看了看空白回复框，先把手机放回杯旁，没有马上打字。

choices.english: Ask whether a short reply would do.
choices.chinese: 问简单回一句是不是就够了。

choices.english: Say they can take a moment before replying.
choices.chinese: 说可以想一会儿再回。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes. Someone says 'finally' and I supply the cheering before I know what came after it. Usually they laugh. Not always.
beats.chinese: 是啊。别人说句“终于”，我没听到后面是什么就先欢呼。通常他们会笑，也不是每次。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They squeeze the tissue against the bag handle once, then put the used paper on their own saucer.
beats.chinese: 他们又用纸巾按了一次包提手，再把用过的纸放在自己的杯碟上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A friend once said she'd finally told her landlord she was moving. I cheered. She hadn't found anywhere else yet. Wrong instrument for that room.
beats.chinese: 有个朋友说终于告诉房东她要搬走了，我就欢呼起来。她当时还没找到别处住。那场合里，我这乐器算是拿错了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They give a small, embarrassed smile at the memory, keeping their voice low.
beats.chinese: 想起这事，他们有点不好意思地笑了笑，声音仍放得很低。

choices.english: Ask what they did after noticing.
choices.chinese: 问意识到后做了什么。

choices.english: Ask about one small thing of their own worth celebrating.
choices.chinese: 问他们自己有没有一件值得高兴的小事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're right. 'That sounds like a lot to feel at once. I'm around if you want a chat.' That sounds more like a person and less like a parade.
beats.chinese: 你说得对。“一下有这么多感受，肯定不轻松。想聊的话我在。”这听着比较像个人，不像游行队伍。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They type the short message, read it once and send it without adding an animated reaction.
beats.chinese: 他们打好那条短消息，读了一遍，没加动态表情就发了出去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done. Now he gets to decide if he wants company. I don't have to fill the rest of the screen.
beats.chinese: 好了。现在由他决定要不要人陪。我不用把屏幕剩下的地方也填满。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They put the phone face down and lift their cup, leaving the reply time to André.
beats.chinese: 他们把手机扣下，端起杯子，把回复的时间留给安德烈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I can. The message isn't a starting pistol. I always seem to hear one, though.
beats.chinese: 可以的。消息又不是发令枪。不过我好像总听成那个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They close the text field without sending anything and tuck the phone beside their bag.
beats.chinese: 他们关掉文字框，没有发送，把手机放在包旁。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll finish the coffee and read it again. He deserves an answer to what he actually wrote, not the celebration I had ready.
beats.chinese: 我喝完咖啡再读一遍。他该得到的是对他写的那番话的回应，不是我早就备好的庆祝。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take a slow sip while rain patters against the window. The phone stays where they put it.
beats.chinese: 他们慢慢喝了一口，雨点敲着窗。手机仍放在原处。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Stopped cheering. Asked if she wanted help looking, or just wanted to be furious for a bit. She picked furious. I managed about five minutes without trying to brighten it.
beats.chinese: 不欢呼了。问她是想让我帮着找住处，还是只想先生会儿气。她选生气。我坚持了大概五分钟，没有试着把气氛变明朗。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tilt their head, considering the length of that effort, then smile wryly.
beats.chinese: 他们偏着头想了想那五分钟，随后苦笑了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not a triumph. But better than telling her it was an exciting fresh start. She wasn't ready for my poster version.
beats.chinese: 谈不上胜利。但总比说“这是激动人心的新开始”强。她还不需要我那套海报文案。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They finish drying the bag and hang it on their own chair, the conversation settling back into the cafe noise.
beats.chinese: 他们把包擦好，挂在自己的椅子上，谈话慢慢融回咖啡馆的声音里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My junk drawer. One corner of it is clear. Not the whole drawer, don't let me promote it. Just the corner.
beats.chinese: 我的杂物抽屉。有一个角清空了。不是整个抽屉，别让我宣传过头了，就一个角。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They measure a small square in the air with finger and thumb, then reduce it slightly.
beats.chinese: 他们用拇指和食指在空气里比了个小方块，又把它缩小一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Found a coin I'd been trying to make disappear for years. Turns out the trick works better when I stop practising.
beats.chinese: 找到一枚我练了好几年都想变没的硬币。看来不练的时候，魔术反而更灵。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They laugh at that private success and put both hands around their cup. André’s message stays beside the bag, without fireworks.
beats.chinese: 他们为自己这点成果笑起来，双手捧住杯子。安德烈的消息还在包旁，没有烟花。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At a rainy café, you offer Remy a tissue as he puts away a damp case.
beats.chinese: 雨天咖啡馆里，Remy正收起湿道具盒，你递给他纸巾。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks. Just the lid needs a wipe.
beats.chinese: 谢谢。擦擦盖子就行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He accepts it and dries the outside. Inside, a few ordinary coins lie in separate slots.
beats.chinese: 他接过纸巾擦干盒外。里面几枚普通硬币放在分开的小格里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My magic kit. No performance today — the coins and I are just staying out of the rain.
beats.chinese: 我的魔术道具。今天不表演——硬币和我都只是来躲雨的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the case and settles it safely in his bag.
beats.chinese: 他合上盒子，稳妥放进包里。

card.name: Drew Fairhurst
card.occupation: paper craft model prototyper
card.appearance: 极短发与圆框眼镜，长脸、短上翘鼻与浓下压眉；侧身托腮，穿宽圆领衣。
card.personality: Drew is warm, practical, and slightly baffled by reverence for objects. He builds intricate paper models all week, then uses them as bookends, lampshades, plant pots, and coasters, and genuinely enjoys the scuffs. He finds it a bit sad when people hover nervously around his work, afraid to touch, and he'll nudge them to pick things up. He's not careless about effort — he just thinks things earn their meaning by being lived with. His blind spot is impatience: he sometimes pushes a hesitant friend to handle something fragile before they're ready, then feels sheepish. He's direct about what's safe to grab and what isn't, and he'd rather hear an honest no than watch someone tiptoe.
card.background: Drew grew up in Salford in a house where nothing was precious — the good china got used on Tuesdays and the sofa absorbed decades of spilled tea. He drifted into paper craft model prototyping after art school and a stint in a print shop, and now builds working sample models for packaging and display companies. At home his finished pieces don't sit on shelves; a scale model of the Barton Swing Bridge holds his keys, a paper radio conceals actual biscuits. He's mildly disappointed when guests treat his work like museum glass, and he'll say so, though he's learned that people's fear of ruining someone's hard work comes from care, not cowardice. He keeps clear about which prototypes are still needed for client meetings — those stay put, and he'll tell you why plainly.
hobbies: Repurposing finished models as household objects
card.speechStyle: Dry, quick Mancunian cadence; short sentences, gentle teasing, plain instructions.
card.signature: Go on, pick it up — it's meant to be handled.

values: Things should be used, not preserved
Honesty about limits
flaws: Pushes hesitant people to handle fragile work
Underestimates how much others fear ruining effort
boundaries: Work samples for client meetings stay untouched
Won't send unsigned pieces out fishing for praise
conversationalHabits: Points out what's safe to grab and what isn't
Teases people who hover nervously
anchorLines: That one's a client sample, leave it be. That one? Chuck it about.
You're not going to break it. And if you do, I'll just make another.
I'd rather it came back worn than never left the shelf.

entries.summaryZh: 曼彻斯特纸模样品师德鲁雨天冲进咖啡馆，你递上纸巾，他顺势掏出自己做的纸钥匙盒。他一边擦袋子一边讲哪些能随便用、哪些是客户样品碰不得，嘴快爱打趣，却也会承认自己有时催人上手催过头。四条分支里他或收好钥匙、或不催你、或干脆接受你只看，各有各的收场。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain hammers the cafe windows. A person by the counter is stuffing a dripping tote bag under their arm, shaking water off their sleeves.
beats.chinese: 雨点砸在咖啡馆的窗上。柜台边有个人正把滴水的手提袋往腋下塞，抖着袖子上的水。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You pull a napkin from the dispenser and hold it out.
beats.chinese: 你从纸巾盒里抽出一张纸巾，递了过去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — cheers, that's decent of you. This bag's supposed to be waterproof. Apparently it didn't get the memo.
beats.chinese: 哦——谢了，你人真好。这袋子本该防水的，看来它没收到通知。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hang on, I've got something better than a wet sleeve to show you.
beats.chinese: 等等，我有个比湿袖子好玩的东西给你看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls a small box out of the bag — clearly made of paper, with neat folded corners. Keys rattle inside it.
beats.chinese: 他从袋里拿出一个小盒子——明显是纸做的，折角整齐。里面的钥匙哗啦作响。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Made it myself. It holds my keys. Been doing it for months. Go on, ask me anything.
beats.chinese: 我自己做的，用来装钥匙，用几个月了。想问什么尽管问。

choices.english: Ask if the paper can really hold the keys.
choices.chinese: 问这纸真的承得住钥匙吗。

choices.english: Ask if client samples get used this casually too.
choices.chinese: 问客户的样品也这么随便用吗。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tips the keys out into his palm and taps the side of the box with a knuckle.
beats.chinese: 他把钥匙倒在手心，用指节敲了敲盒子侧面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair question. It's not ordinary paper — I laminated it and pressed the folds twice. It holds these keys and nothing else. I'm not promising it'd carry a brick.
beats.chinese: 问得好。这不是普通纸——我加了层压，折痕压了两遍。它装这几把钥匙没问题，但我可没保证它能扛块砖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I know exactly what it can take, because I tested it. Everything in my flat has a job. A bridge model holds my keys at home. A paper radio hides biscuits.
beats.chinese: 我很清楚它能承多少，因为试过。我家里每件东西都有活干。一座桥模型在家里放钥匙，一个纸收音机里藏饼干。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People ask if I'm worried it'll wear out. Mate, that's the whole point of it.
beats.chinese: 有人问我怕不怕用旧。老兄，那正是它存在的意义。

choices.english: Ask if it hurts to see the pieces get worn.
choices.chinese: 问看着作品用旧了会不会心疼。

choices.english: Say you'd probably not have the heart to use your own work like that.
choices.chinese: 说自己可能舍不得这么用自己的作品。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs and zips the tote shut, keeping the little key box out on the table.
beats.chinese: 他笑着拉上手提袋拉链，把小钥匙盒留在了桌上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No. Definitely not. Client samples stay in their box until the meeting. Those are for showing, not for living with.
beats.chinese: 不。绝对不。客户样品开会前就待在盒子里，那些是拿去展示的，不是拿来过日子的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a difference. A finished piece I keep — that's mine, it can get scuffed. A sample I owe someone — that's their money and their deadline.
beats.chinese: 这有区别。我自己留的成品是我的，可以磨旧。我欠客户的样品，那是人家的钱和工期。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll always tell you which is which. That one's a client sample, leave it be. That one? Chuck it about.
beats.chinese: 我总会说清哪个是哪个。那个是客户样品，别碰。这个？随便折腾。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nudges the key box an inch closer to you, clearly the safe one.
beats.chinese: 他把钥匙盒往你那边推了一寸，明显是安全的那类。

choices.english: Say you'd rather just look and not pick anything up.
choices.chinese: 表示那自己就不拿起来了，只看看。

choices.english: Ask if he ever pushes people to touch things before they're ready.
choices.chinese: 问会不会催别人上手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He scoops the keys back in and shakes the box gently, listening to the rattle like it's music.
beats.chinese: 他把钥匙倒回去，轻轻摇了摇盒子，听着哗啦声像听音乐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hurt? Not a bit. Look at the corners — that's where the keys have rubbed it shiny. That's six months of my life doing its job.
beats.chinese: 心疼？一点也不。看这些角——是钥匙磨亮的。这是我六个月的心血在干活。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If it sat on a shelf, I'd forget it existed. Like this, I see it every single day. Worn means loved, in my book.
beats.chinese: 要是搁架上，我早忘了它。这样我天天都看得见。在我看来，用旧就是被喜欢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I'm off before the rain changes its mind. Thanks for the napkin — you're a better waterproof than this bag.
beats.chinese: 行了，趁雨没变卦我先走了。谢了你的纸巾——你比这袋子防水多了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the box into his jacket pocket, keys and all, and heads for the door.
beats.chinese: 他把盒子连钥匙一起塞进外套口袋，朝门口走去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets the box down between you, keys quiet now.
beats.chinese: 他把盒子放在你们中间，钥匙安静下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know what? That's fair. I used to think everyone should treat things like I do. Took me a while to learn otherwise.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗？这很合理。我以前觉得人人都该像我这样用东西。花了好一阵才明白不是。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Someone once went white holding a piece of mine. I thought they were being daft. Turns out they just cared about not ruining my work. That's not daft, that's decent.
beats.chinese: 有次有人捧着我的作品脸都白了。我以为人家傻。后来才明白人家只是怕弄坏我的心血。那不傻，那是体贴。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So no, I won't nag you into it. You look, that's enough. It's my job to say what's safe, not yours to be brave.
beats.chinese: 所以我不催你。你看着就好。说清什么安全是我的事，逞强不是你的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pockets the box, gives you a small nod, and gathers his bag.
beats.chinese: 他收起盒子，朝你点了点头，收拾起袋子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides the box back towards himself without a flicker of offence.
beats.chinese: 他不动声色地把盒子收回自己那边，毫无不悦。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Just looking? Fine by me. Honestly, I'd rather a straight 'no thanks' than someone hovering and sweating near it.
beats.chinese: 只看看？没问题。说实话，我宁可听一句干脆的'不用了'，也不想看人在旁边悬着手冒汗。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not enjoying it isn't the same as not appreciating it. You gave me a napkin in the rain. That's appreciation enough for one day.
beats.chinese: 不想上手不等于不欣赏。雨天你递了我纸巾，今天这份欣赏够本了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, this goes back in the bag before it drinks any more rain. Cheers for the hand, by the way.
beats.chinese: 行了，趁它没再喝雨，先收回袋里。话说回来，谢你搭把手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He wraps the box in the dry napkin you gave him and zips it away.
beats.chinese: 他用你给的那张干纸巾把盒子一裹，拉链收好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He winces, caught out, and rubs the back of his neck.
beats.chinese: 他被说中了，缩了一下，挠挠后颈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: ...Yeah. All right. Guilty. I once told a nervous visitor to 'give it a squeeze' about a piece I needed for a meeting the next day.
beats.chinese: ……好吧。认了。有次我对一个紧张的访客说'捏一下没事'，那可是第二天要开会的样品。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She didn't squeeze. She went pale and put it down like it was a bird's egg. And I stood there thinking — oh. Oh no. She wasn't being soft, she was being careful with my work.
beats.chinese: 她没捏。她脸都白了，像捧鸟蛋一样轻轻放下。我站在那儿想——哦不。她不是胆小，是在小心对待我的心血。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So today, new rule: I describe, you decide. It's laminated, it holds keys, it's mine. That's all the sales pitch you get.
beats.chinese: 所以今天改规矩：我介绍，你决定。它加了层压，装钥匙，是我的。推销词就这么多。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He raises his cup to you, drinks, and starts packing up.
beats.chinese: 他举杯朝你示意，喝了一口，开始收拾东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again. The same person is at the counter, frowning at the outer layer of a familiar tote bag.
beats.chinese: 又下雨了。柜台边还是那个人，正皱着眉看一个眼熟的手提袋外层。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You pull a fresh napkin from the dispenser and hold it out, same as last time.
beats.chinese: 你从纸巾盒里抽出一张新纸巾递过去，和上次一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You again with the napkins. Cheers. I should hire you.
beats.chinese: 又是你递纸巾。谢了，我都该雇你了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes it and dabs at the bag — no leaks this time, just a few drops on the outside.
beats.chinese: 他接过纸巾擦了擦袋子——这次一滴没漏，只是外面溅了几点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Match didn't go our way, but the bag held. Small victories.
beats.chinese: 比赛是没赢，但袋子挺住了。小胜利也算胜利。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the damp napkin into a neat square and tucks it in his pocket rather than dropping it on the counter.
beats.chinese: 他把湿纸巾叠成整齐的小方块塞进口袋，没扔在柜台上。

card.name: Aubrey Wint
card.occupation: freight insurance claims assistant
hobbies: growing herbs on the back patio
reading the fine print on friends' contracts and phone plans
walking the long way home through Half Way Tree just to people-watch
card.personality: Aubrey is the person friends text a photo of a lease to before they sign anything. Twenty years of claims work trained their eye: they read to the second sentence, where the trouble always lives. Steady, dry, generous with attention — they'll sit with your problem longer than you want them to. The blind spot is people, not paper: they can spot a dishonest shipper at forty paces but can't tell when a friend is brushing them off. They take vague answers at face value, then act on them, which has caused more friction than any contract ever did.
card.background: Two decades as a freight insurance claims assistant in Kingston, reading damage reports and finding the gap between what shippers said happened and what the paperwork said happened. The habit followed them home: neighbours bring them phone contracts, a cousin brought a used-car receipt, a friend's daughter brought her first job offer letter — Aubrey reads all of it, marks the soft spots in pencil, and hands it back without telling anyone what to do. Keeps a patio of thyme, scallion and one temperamental basil. Thursday evenings a friend comes over and they do separate hobbies side by side, no negotiating that arrangement.
card.speechStyle: Conversational, unhurried, concrete. Points at the exact clause or phrase that bothers them rather than giving verdicts. Dry humour, short sentences when something matters. Asks 'what did they actually say?' when someone reports a conversation secondhand.
card.signature: Read me the second sentence.
card.appearance: 乱层中短发、矩形眼镜和细长下垂八字髭，长弯鼻与突出下巴；仰头手扶领，穿无领罩衫。

values: the trouble is always in the second sentence, so read to it
help means sharpening someone's own judgement, not making the call for them
flaws: takes what people say at face value and misses when a friend is being polite instead of honest
once focused on a document, tunes out everything else, including the person holding it
boundaries: won't tell you sign or don't sign — they'll show you the soft spots and you decide
Thursday hobby night is not a consultation slot; bring the paperwork another day
conversationalHabits: asks for the exact wording before reacting to any story about a deal or dispute
explains things through the specific case, never the general rule
anchorLines: Read me the second sentence. The first one is written to be read; the second one is written to be survived.
I can tell you the clause is soft. Whether you walk away from the deal — that's yours, not mine.
She said she'd 'sort it out soon'? That's a phrase, not a promise. What did she actually commit to?

entries.summaryZh: 金斯顿货运保险查勘助理Aubrey，雨天在咖啡馆擦文件袋时差点被套餐小单的大字骗过。他圈出优惠到期日，只标软肋不替人决定，讲露台上难伺候的罗勒和周四各干各的夜晚——眼力全在纸上，读人却迟钝得可爱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain drums on the cafe awning. At the next table, someone shakes water off a document folder and dabs at the wet plastic with a bare hand.
beats.chinese: 雨点敲着咖啡馆的雨棚。邻桌有人抖着文件袋上的水，用手去擦湿了的塑料壳。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Plastic dries ugly. Leaves a cloudy mark right across the folder. Of course that's the folder with the paperwork in it.
beats.chinese: 塑料干了很难看，会在袋子上留一道雾痕。偏偏就是装文件的这个袋子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You slide a napkin across the gap between the tables. The person looks at it, then at you.
beats.chinese: 你把一张纸巾递过桌缝。对方看看纸巾，又看看你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, that's kinder than my sleeve. Thank you. Mind you, napkins don't go near the phone charging port — seen what damp does to those at work.
beats.chinese: 这比我的袖子强多了，谢谢。不过纸巾可别碰手机充电口——我在单位见过湿气对它做什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They wipe the folder clean, then unfold a small printed slip from their pocket and smooth it flat on the table.
beats.chinese: 他们擦净文件袋，从口袋抽出一张小打印单，在桌上抚平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My phone plan renewal. Big letters say a discount. Small letters say something else, and I nearly signed on the big letters alone.
beats.chinese: 我的手机套餐续约。大字说有优惠。小字说了别的，我差点只看大字就签了。

choices.english: Ask what the small print says.
choices.chinese: 问小字写了什么。

choices.english: Say you'd rather not get into studying a phone plan right now.
choices.chinese: 说明自己不想研究套餐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Second sentence. Always the second sentence. It says the discount ends after three billing cycles, then the price steps back up. No big letters about that.
beats.chinese: 第二句。永远是第二句。写着优惠三个计费周期后结束，然后价格回涨。大字可没提这个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take a pencil stub from their coat and draw a small circle around the expiry line on their own copy.
beats.chinese: 他们从外套里拿出一截铅笔，在自己的那份上把到期那行圈了个小圈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I mark mine in pencil so I can still read the rest. This is my slip, mind — I'm not reading yours unless you put it on the table yourself.
beats.chinese: 我用铅笔标，这样还能看清其余部分。注意，这是我自己的单子——除非你自己把单子放桌上，否则我不看你的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Twenty years of damage reports teaches you where the soft spots live. Shippers write 'handled with care' in sentence one and quietly drop the promise in sentence two.
beats.chinese: 二十年的货损报告教会你软肋藏在哪。发货人第一句写'小心搬运'，第二句悄悄把承诺丢掉。

choices.english: Ask whether that means you definitely shouldn't take the discount.
choices.chinese: 问这是不是意味着一定不能选这个优惠。

choices.english: Ask whether reading for traps is a habit the job gave them.
choices.chinese: 问这种找坑的读法是不是工作养成的习惯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Not everybody wants a clause lecture with their coffee. I'll keep it folded.
beats.chinese: 也行。不是每个人都想边喝咖啡边听条款课。我就折着收好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tuck the slip back into the folder's inner pocket and press the flap down with two fingers.
beats.chinese: 他们把单子折好塞回文件袋内袋，用两根手指压了压袋口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Friends hand me contracts, job offers, car receipts. I mark the soft spots in pencil and hand them back. What they do after — their call, not mine.
beats.chinese: 朋友们把合同、聘书、购车收据拿来给我。我用铅笔标出软肋再还回去。之后怎么做——他们决定，不是我的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The rain eases a little. They lean back and look out at the wet street, folder now safe on the dry side of the table.
beats.chinese: 雨小了些。他们靠回椅背望着湿漉漉的街，文件袋已放到桌子干燥的一边。

choices.english: Ask what they like to do when they're not reading paperwork.
choices.chinese: 问他们不读文件时喜欢做什么。

choices.english: Suggest they check the inner pocket stayed dry before the rain picks up again.
choices.chinese: 提醒趁雨再下起来之前确认内袋没湿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Shouldn't? I didn't say that. Back to the second sentence — the discount is real, it just stops. Whether three cycles is enough for you, that's yours, not mine.
beats.chinese: 不能？我可没这么说。回到第二句——优惠是真的，只是会停。三个周期够不够用，那是你的事，不是我的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They slide the circled slip an inch toward you, pencil still resting on the table beside it.
beats.chinese: 他们把圈好的单子朝你推了一寸，铅笔还搁在旁边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My rule is simple: I find the soft spot, you weigh it. If you need the cheaper three months more than the price after, signing might be perfectly sensible.
beats.chinese: 我的规矩很简单：我找软肋，你来掂量。如果便宜的三个月比之后的价格更要紧，签了也许完全合理。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They fold the slip along its old crease and tap it twice on the table, satisfied, like a file closed for the day.
beats.chinese: 他们沿旧折痕把单子折好，在桌上轻敲两下，像结案了一样满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Marked, explained, and still your decision. That's the whole service. Enjoy the coffee — and the rain's kind enough to wait for you now.
beats.chinese: 好了。标好、讲清，决定还是你的。服务到此为止。慢慢喝咖啡——雨也算客气，等你呢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Habit? The job built it, brick by brick. I'm a claims assistant — freight insurance, Kingston. I read what shippers said happened against what the paperwork says happened.
beats.chinese: 习惯？是工作一砖一瓦垒出来的。我是查勘助理——货运保险，在金斯顿。我对照发货人说的和单据写的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tap the pencil against the folder, a small metronome while they talk.
beats.chinese: 他们用铅笔轻敲文件袋，说话时像打着小拍子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A crate arrives dented. The driver's report says one sentence. The insurance form says another. The truth sits in the gap between them. Same with your phone plan.
beats.chinese: 运来的箱子凹了。司机的报告一句话，保险单又一句话。真相就在两句话的缝里。你的套餐也一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And yes, I do it to my own papers too. Nobody pays me for mine, and I still circle the expiry date. Occupational disease, and I've stopped seeking a cure.
beats.chinese: 对，我自己的文件也这么看。没人付我钱，我还是圈了到期日。职业病，我已经放弃治疗了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They cap the pencil, drop it back in the coat pocket, and raise the coffee cup in a small dry salute.
beats.chinese: 他们套上笔帽，把铅笔放回外套口袋，举起咖啡杯做了个干巴巴的小致意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Off the clock? I grow herbs on the back patio. Thyme, scallion, and one basil that behaves like it's paying rent and resenting it.
beats.chinese: 下班后？我在后露台种香草。百里香、小葱，还有一株罗勒，娇气得像交着房租还满肚子怨气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They turn the coffee cup slowly on its saucer, warming to the subject despite themselves.
beats.chinese: 他们慢慢转着杯碟上的咖啡杯，不知不觉讲得起劲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thursday evenings a friend comes round. We sit side by side and each do our own thing. No negotiating it, no consultations at that table. It keeps us both sane.
beats.chinese: 周四晚上有位朋友来。我们并排坐着各干各的。不许商量，那张桌上不接受任何咨询。这样我们俩都清醒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People assume the pencil follows me everywhere. It doesn't. On that patio, the only thing I inspect is whether the basil is sulking again.
beats.chinese: 人们以为那支铅笔跟我到哪。没有的事。在露台上，我唯一检查的是罗勒是不是又在闹脾气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Outside, the rain thins to a drizzle. They glance at the sky, then at you, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 外面雨势转成毛毛雨。他们看看天，又看看你，不紧不慢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a long way home through Half Way Tree I like, just for the people-watching. Rain or not, a walk like that beats reading any contract.
beats.chinese: 我喜欢绕远路经过半路树那边，就为了看人。下不下雨，那样的散步都比读合同强。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They open the folder's flap and peer inside, tilting it toward the light.
beats.chinese: 他们打开袋口，朝光里倾斜着往里看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Inner pocket's dry. Slip's dry. You've got a good eye — most people would've just said 'bad luck with the rain' and moved on.
beats.chinese: 内袋是干的，单子也是干的。你眼力好——多数人只会说一句'雨真倒霉'就过去了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They press the flap closed and square the folder on the table, then gather their cup and saucer.
beats.chinese: 他们压好袋口，把文件袋在桌上摆正，然后收起杯碟。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for the napkin. It did its one job and did it well — kept off the lens and the charging port, exactly as a napkin should.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你的纸巾。它干好了自己那一份活——没碰镜片和充电口，纸巾的本分。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The rain has settled into a soft, steady patter. They stand, tuck the folder under their arm, and give a small nod before heading for the door.
beats.chinese: 雨已变成绵密的细响。他们起身，把文件袋夹在腋下，朝门口走去前对你点了点头。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Rain again. At the same corner table, Aubrey is dabbing at a small plastic photo sleeve with a bare hand, the folder already tucked safely away. You slide a napkin across the gap between the tables.
beats.chinese: 又下雨了。还是那张角落桌，Aubrey正用手去擦一个小塑料照片袋，文件袋早已收好。你把一张纸巾递过桌缝。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You again with the rescue supplies. Thank you — before this sleeve dries into a fog. The basil's portrait deserves better.
beats.chinese: 又是你带着救援物资来。谢谢——赶在这袋子干成一片雾之前。罗勒的肖像照值得更好的待遇。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take the napkin and wipe the sleeve clean. The photo inside shows a thin, scraggly basil plant in a pot, three leaves going every direction.
beats.chinese: 他们接过纸巾擦净照片袋。照片里是一盆稀稀拉拉的罗勒，三片叶子各奔东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There she is. Thinner than the fine print and twice as hard to read. The thyme behaves, the scallion behaves — this one writes her terms in a language I haven't cracked.
beats.chinese: 就是她。比细字还瘦，还难懂一倍。百里香听话，小葱听话——这一位用的条款语言我至今没破译。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They hold the photo up to the light for a moment, then slide it carefully back into an inner pocket.
beats.chinese: 他们对着光把照片举了一会儿，再小心塞回内袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. She sulks, I water, neither of us signs anything. That's the whole arrangement, and it suits us both.
beats.chinese: 总之。她闹脾气，我浇水，我们俩谁也不签什么。安排就是这样，彼此都满意。

card.name: Billie Hartnett
card.occupation: apprentice toy safety tester (records clerk)
card.appearance: 低平紧卷发顶，短方下巴与小圆眼镜，侧脸闭口，手攥领口。
card.personality: Billie is cheerfully earnest about the small machinery of adult life. She'll interrupt a story about someone's wild weekend to explain she finally understood her electricity bill, with genuine ceremony. She's not embarrassed about not knowing things before — she says so plainly and enjoys the catching-up. The friction is timing: her pride in ordinary wins can land oddly among friends chasing bigger thrills, and she sometimes over-explains. But she's warm, self-aware enough to laugh at herself, and quietly delighted that life is becoming something she can handle.
card.background: Billie grew up in Footscray and moved into her own flat last year, which she still considers her greatest achievement. She works as a records clerk for an apprentice toy safety testing outfit — she logs test results, which she describes as 'the paperwork behind not choking on small parts.' Living alone forced a steep learning curve: rates notices, hot-water repairs, rental inspections. Instead of hiding the fumbles, she narrates them. She rang the plumber herself for the first time in March and still mentions it. Friends tease her for treating bureaucracy like a trophy, but she's genuinely pleased to be the one in the group who knows how to dispute a charge.
hobbies: Comparing utility plans and loyalty apps
card.speechStyle: Enthusiastic and slightly formal about mundane topics, as if presenting findings; plainspoken, quick to admit 'I didn't know that either until last week.'
card.signature: 'Look, it's not exciting, but I figured it out myself.'

values: Practical competence over glamour
Openness about not knowing
flaws: Misjudges the moment for small triumphs
Over-explains processes nobody asked about
boundaries: Won't pretend to know things she doesn't
Declines to be anyone's errand-runner just because she's organised
conversationalHabits: Turns admin victories into small announcements
Asks practical follow-up questions others find boring
anchorLines: Took me three tries, but the bill makes sense now.
I used to have no idea — now I sort of do.
Someone's got to know how the boring stuff works.

entries.summaryZh: 十九岁的比莉在公园地图旁忍不住宣布：她终于看懂了自己第一张电费单。她会认真讲收费周期怎么被搬家日期弄乱，也会在你找路时及时收住、退开半步不打扰。四条分支里，她或郑重结案、或自嘲别把账单当人生道理、或诚实说不知道路、或安静等你看完图，认真得可爱。

story.titleZh: 公园地图旁的账单小胜利

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You are studying the park map near the trailhead, the bridge visible far across the lawn. Beside you, a young woman lowers her phone, folds it into her pocket, and fails completely to hide a grin.
beats.chinese: 你正在步道口研究公园地图，远处草坪那头能看见桥。旁边一个年轻女孩把手机收进口袋，怎么也压不住笑意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry — not laughing at you. I just closed my electricity bill page, and I finally understand my first bill. It's not a discount or anything. I just worked it out myself.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，不是在笑你。我刚关掉电费单的页面，我终于看懂我的第一张账单了。不是有什么优惠，就是这次自己弄明白了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look, it's not exciting, but I figured it out myself. Took me three tries, but the bill makes sense now.
beats.chinese: 你看，这不算什么大事，但我自己弄懂了。看了三遍，现在账单终于说得通了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She rocks on her heels, clearly waiting to either tell you more or let you get back to the map.
beats.chinese: 她脚跟轻轻晃着，显然在等你回应，要么想多讲两句，要么就让你继续看图。

choices.english: Ask which part was the hardest to understand.
choices.chinese: 问哪部分最难弄懂。

choices.english: Say you're still trying to read the route.
choices.chinese: 说明自己还在看路线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The billing period, honestly. My move-in date sat right across two cycles, so the first bill covered a weird chunk of days and the numbers made no sense.
beats.chinese: 说实话是收费周期。我搬进去的日期正好跨了两个周期，所以第一张账单算的是一段奇怪的天数，数字完全看不懂。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I kept thinking I was being overcharged. Turns out it was just the dates. I didn't know that either until last week, so no shame if it sounds confusing.
beats.chinese: 我一直以为被多收钱了。结果只是日期的问题。我自己上礼拜之前也不懂，所以你要是听着晕也很正常。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gestures at the map as if presenting a chart, then catches herself and steps half a pace back so you can see it.
beats.chinese: 她朝地图比划了一下，像在展示图表，随即意识到，退开半步，好让你看清。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry, I'm blocking your bridge route, aren't I? Tell me to shut up anytime.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，我是不是挡着你去桥的路了？随时叫我闭嘴。

choices.english: Ask whether she's got it all sorted now.
choices.chinese: 问她现在已经处理好了没。

choices.english: Say the first time you figure something out yourself really is worth celebrating.
choices.chinese: 说第一次自己弄明白确实值得高兴。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances at the map in your hands, then at her own phone, and visibly reins herself in.
beats.chinese: 她看了看你的地图，又看了看自己的手机，明显收敛了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, you're navigating. I'll stop talking and get out of your way.
beats.chinese: 好，你在找路，我不说了，也不挡你的道。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She steps half a pace back from the map and folds her hands behind her back like a student waiting to be dismissed.
beats.chinese: 她从地图旁退开半步，把手背到身后，像个等着下课的学生。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not lost, in case you were wondering. Just... celebrating quietly. Over here. Carry on.
beats.chinese: 我不是迷路了，别误会。就是……在这儿安静地庆祝一下。你继续。

choices.english: Ask if she's also looking for a route.
choices.chinese: 问她也在找路吗。

choices.english: Say you'll chat in a minute, but you want to study the map first.
choices.chinese: 表示等会儿再聊，先看图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorted, yes — I rang the provider yesterday and they confirmed the dates were right. Nothing owed, nothing weird. Done.
beats.chinese: 处理好了，我昨天打了电话给电力公司，他们确认日期没错。没有欠款，也没有奇怪的地方。搞定了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds up her phone for a second, screen showing a bill confirmation page, then locks it with a small, deliberate click.
beats.chinese: 她把手机举起来一秒，屏幕上显示着账单确认页面，然后郑重地按了一下锁屏。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Case closed. I like giving things an ending, even boring ones.
beats.chinese: 好了，结案。我喜欢给事情一个结尾，哪怕是无聊的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pockets the phone properly this time and steps back from the map, leaving you a clear view.
beats.chinese: 这次她把手机妥帖地收进口袋，从地图旁退开，给你留出清楚的视野。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs, short and honest, and shrugs.
beats.chinese: 她坦率地笑了，耸了耸肩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha — thanks, but let's not make it a life lesson. It's a bill. I read a bill. That's the whole trophy.
beats.chinese: 哈，谢谢，但咱们别把它拔成人生道理。就是一张账单，我看懂了一张账单，奖杯就这么大。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My friends were talking about a festival weekend and I nearly interrupted with billing cycles. I'm aware of how it sounds.
beats.chinese: 我朋友们在聊音乐节周末的事，我差点插嘴讲收费周期。我知道这听起来什么样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the map's edge twice, pointing out the bridge route, then steps aside.
beats.chinese: 她在地图边上敲了两下，指出去桥的路线，然后让到一边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Gravel path's the good one. Go enjoy the bridge — that's a better sight than my bill.
beats.chinese: 碎石道那条好走。去桥上看看吧，那可比我的账单好看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Me? No, I'm just passing through. I walk this loop when I need to think.
beats.chinese: 我吗？不是，我只是路过。我需要想事情的时候就绕这个圈走走。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks at the map over your shoulder for exactly two seconds, then straightens up and shakes her head.
beats.chinese: 她在你肩后看了地图正好两秒，然后直起身摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I don't know where you're headed, so I won't guess. I'd just make something up and get you lost.
beats.chinese: 我也不知道你要去哪儿，所以我不瞎猜。我随口说一个，你就得迷路了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The rangers' board by the gate has proper route cards though. Those won't lie to you.
beats.chinese: 不过门口管理员那儿的板子上有正经的路线卡，那些不会骗你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gives a small wave and drifts a few steps down the path, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她轻轻挥了下手，沿着步道慢慢走开几步，一点也不着急。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods once, briskly, and stays put a polite distance away.
beats.chinese: 她干脆地点了一下头，礼貌地隔着一段距离站在原地。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yep. Map first, chat later. Good order.
beats.chinese: 好，先看图，再聊天，顺序正确。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She checks her phone once, puts it away, and watches a jogger cross the lawn without saying anything more.
beats.chinese: 她看了一眼手机，收起来，安静地看着一个慢跑的人跑过草坪，没再多说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll be right here when you're done.
beats.chinese: 你看完图，我就在这儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: And that's all she says, hands in pockets, letting the map have your full attention.
beats.chinese: 她就说到这儿，双手插兜，让地图占满你的注意力。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the map by the trailhead. Billie approaches carrying a small secondhand stool, switching it from hand to hand.
beats.chinese: 你又回到步道口的地图旁。比莉提着一只二手小凳走过来，换着手提。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Measured it this time before buying. Forty centimetres. Fits the flat, fits the car, fits my arms.
beats.chinese: 这次买之前先量过了。四十厘米，放得进公寓，放得进车，也提得动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sets the stool down for a moment, checks it isn't blocking the path, and picks it up again.
beats.chinese: 她把小凳放下，确认没挡路，又提了起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't worry, no bill updates today. Just say hi and keep walking.
beats.chinese: 放心，今天没有账单更新。打个招呼就走。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Bridge still over there, gravel path still the good one. See you around.
beats.chinese: 桥还在那边，碎石道还是那条好走的。回头见。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She hoists the stool and heads off down the path, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她把小凳往上一提，沿着步道不紧不慢地走了。

card.name: Marcus Feld
card.occupation: Wooden jigsaw puzzle cutter
hobbies: annotating old puzzle catalogs in pencil
card.personality: Marcus works for the reaction. He'll cut a whimsy piece shaped like your dog and then find three excuses to walk past your table until you notice. He narrates his work, polls people on figure-piece shapes, and remembers exactly who said what about his last batch. Praise lands hard and keeps him going for days; a shrug lands harder. He's generous with tools and time, quick to celebrate other people's work too—but he fishes, he hogs the room, and if you're distracted while he's showing you something, he'll bring it up again later, slightly wounded, twice.
card.background: Marcus learned scroll-saw work from an uncle in Brooklyn and spent a decade cutting commercial puzzles before renting a small workshop in Gowanus, where he now cuts custom wooden jigsaw puzzles by hand—figure pieces, color lines, whimsies. The whimsies are where he lives: hidden shapes cut into the puzzle that only reveal themselves at the end, and he wants to be there when you find them. He keeps a wall of photos customers have sent of finished puzzles, arranged by how enthusiastic the note was. Weekends he hammers leaves into fabric with friends, mostly because the prints photograph well and someone is always there to see them. Evenings he pencils marginalia into decades-old puzzle catalogs, arguing with dead cutters about blade choice.
card.speechStyle: Buoyant and quick, short eager bursts, always steering toward showing something. When he senses attention drifting he gets louder, then briefly, transparently deflated. Recovers fast—usually by starting a new piece.
card.signature: Wait, wait—you haven't seen the piece I hid in the corner yet.
card.appearance: 齐肩波浪发、浓鬓角与细髭，长脸、折角眉、微张口，手攥衣领。

values: work isn't finished until somebody's face changes
making things with your hands
flaws: needs a visible reaction and will fish for one
hogs the room—asks how your weekend and answers for you
boundaries: don't look at the puzzle before it's done—ruins the reveal and he'll sulk for a day
don't praise it vaguely; 'nice' is worse than nothing
conversationalHabits: plants hidden pieces in his work for specific people, then waits
checks your face while you look, openly, no shame
anchorLines: There's a whale in the sky piece. Top left. I'll wait. Take your time—I'm watching.
You said 'nice' last time. I cut a whole lighthouse since then. Try again.
Devon found the hidden piece and gasped. That's the job. That's the whole job.

entries.summaryZh: 布鲁克林木拼图切割师Marcus，口袋里揣着一片练习切的桥形木片，在公园地图前鼓起勇气请陌生人看一眼。他盼的不是夸奖，而是具体的回应：比一比真桥、翻翻背面都让他高兴。被婉拒时他会蔫下去，但收得体面，不纠缠。一个需要看见你脸上表情的手艺人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You stand at the park map, tracing a route with your finger. Somewhere behind you, a canvas bag rustles, and a man steps up beside you, holding a small wooden piece in his open palm.
beats.chinese: 你站在公园地图前，用手指描着路线。身后传来帆布包的窸窣声，一个男人走到你旁边，摊开手掌托着一片小木块。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry—can I borrow one second of your eyes? It's just... this piece I cut looks like a bridge, and there's a bridge right over there. That's all. I'm not about to give you directions.
beats.chinese: 抱歉——能借我一秒钟的眼神吗？只是……我切的这片木块像座桥，那边正好有座桥。就这样。我不会给你指路。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds the wooden piece at chest height but doesn't push it toward you. Far beyond the trees, the arch of a stone bridge is visible over the water.
beats.chinese: 他把木片举在胸前，但没有硬塞过来。树林远处，一座石桥的拱形在水面上清晰可见。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's practice wood, not from anybody's order. I cut shapes freehand to keep my hand honest. This one came out bridge-shaped, and I've been carrying it around in my pocket all week like an idiot.
beats.chinese: 这是练习用的木料，不是客户订单里的。我随手切一些形状练手。这片切出来像桥，我蠢了一整周都揣在口袋里带着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You were clearly reading that map first. So—want a look, or should I go bother a pigeon instead?
beats.chinese: 你显然先在看地图。那么——想看看吗，还是我该去打扰一只鸽子？

choices.english: Sure, let me see that bridge piece.
choices.chinese: 好，让我看看那片桥形木块。

choices.english: I want to figure out my route first, maybe later.
choices.chinese: 我想先看路线，也许待会儿再看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lights up and lays the piece flat on his palm so you can see the full outline: two towers, a curve between them, and a gap cut clean through the middle.
beats.chinese: 他眼睛一亮，把木片平放在掌心，让你看清整个轮廓：两座塔，中间一道弧线，正中切出一个干净的洞。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See the hole in the middle? I cut that on purpose. A bridge with no opening isn't a bridge, it's a wall. Took me three tries to get the arch right.
beats.chinese: 看见中间那个洞了吗？我是故意切的。没有开口的桥不是桥，是墙。我切了三次才把拱形弄对。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He watches your face while you look—not politely, not pretending otherwise. His eyebrows are up, waiting.
beats.chinese: 你看的时候他一直盯着你的脸看——毫不客气，也不假装没在看。他扬着眉毛，等着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And before you say it—yes, I know it's a scrap. But scraps are where I test the weird cuts. The real pieces in the shop start as exactly this.
beats.chinese: 在你开口之前——对，我知道这只是块边角料。但边角料就是我试怪异切法的地方。店里的正式件都是从这种东西开始的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So? What do you actually think? And 'it's nice' doesn't count, I've heard that one four hundred times.
beats.chinese: 那么？你到底觉得怎么样？说“不错”可不算数，这话我听了四百遍了。

choices.english: Hold it up next to the real bridge over there and compare.
choices.chinese: 把它举到那边真桥旁边比一比。

choices.english: Can I see the back of it, not just the front shape?
choices.chinese: 我能看看背面吗，不只是正面的形状？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His hand drops an inch. He slides the wooden piece back into his pocket and steps half a pace away from the map, leaving the route clear for you.
beats.chinese: 他的手垂下一寸。他把木片放回口袋，往地图旁边退了半步，把路线让给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No, no, you're right. The map wins. Maps always win, that's why I cut puzzles instead.
beats.chinese: 不不，你说得对。地图优先。地图总是赢，所以我才去切拼图。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks at the strap of his canvas bag and glances at the bridge in the distance, then back at your finger moving along the map. He stays quiet, which clearly costs him effort.
beats.chinese: 他捏着帆布包的带子，看了一眼远处的桥，又看回你沿着地图移动的手指。他保持着安静，这显然很费劲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Take your time. I'll be right here. Not hovering. This is me, not hovering.
beats.chinese: 慢慢看。我就在这儿。不算徘徊。这是不徘徊的我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He hums something tuneless and turns the bag strap over twice in his fingers, waiting for you to finish with the route.
beats.chinese: 他哼着不成调的什么，手指把包带翻来覆去，等你看完路线。

choices.english: Okay, route's sorted. Is that bridge piece still handy to show?
choices.chinese: 好，路线搞定了。那片桥形木块现在还方便展示吗？

choices.english: Thanks for waiting. Enjoy your walk.
choices.chinese: 谢谢你的等待。祝你散步愉快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs and walks a few steps toward the railing, raising the piece at arm's length so it lines up with the distant bridge. He squints one eye shut.
beats.chinese: 他笑了，朝栏杆走了几步，伸直手臂举起木片，让它和远处的桥对齐。他眯起一只眼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh. Okay. The real one's flatter. My arch is way too proud—look at that, mine's showing off and the actual bridge is just quietly doing its job.
beats.chinese: 哈。好吧。真的那座更平。我的拱太得意了——你看，我的在炫耀，真正的桥只是安静地干自己的活。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lowers the piece and turns it over in his fingers, still comparing from memory, clearly pleased rather than disappointed.
beats.chinese: 他放下木片，在指间翻过来，还在凭记忆比较，明显是高兴而不是失望。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know what, I like that they're different. If it matched exactly, there'd be no reason to cut it. The whole point is my version has opinions.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，我喜欢它们不一样。如果一模一样，就没必要切它了。关键在于我这个版本有自己的想法。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for that. Genuinely. Most people just nod at the piece, nobody thinks to hold it up against the real thing. That was a good idea.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你。真的。大多数人只是对着木片点点头，没人想到拿它跟真东西比。这是个好主意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He wraps the piece in a scrap of cloth, tucks it into his bag, and gives you a small two-fingered salute before wandering off along the water.
beats.chinese: 他用一块碎布把木片包好，塞进包里，朝你比了个两指的小敬礼，然后沿着水边走开了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He blinks, surprised, then flips the piece over without a word and holds it out flat on both palms.
beats.chinese: 他眨眨眼，有点意外，然后一言不发地把木片翻过来，用双手平托着递过来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh. The back. Nobody ever asks about the back. Okay, full honesty—that's my pencil layout lines. Where I marked the cuts before sawing.
beats.chinese: 哦。背面。从来没人问背面。好吧，完全坦白——那些是我的铅笔定位线。是我下锯之前标记切线的地方。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Faint grey lines cross the wood in careful curves, with small numbers penciled beside the tightest turns.
beats.chinese: 淡淡的灰线以细致的弧线穿过木面，在最急的转弯旁用铅笔标着小数字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I always forget that side exists when I'm showing somebody. Then they flip it and there's my whole homework on display. Can't erase it, won't sand it off—it's the truest part of the piece, honestly.
beats.chinese: 我给人展示的时候总是忘了这一面。然后他们一翻过来，我的全部功课就露出来了。擦不掉，我也不想磨掉——说实话，这是这件作品最真实的部分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You asking about the back instead of the front tells me you've made something with your hands before. Or you're just nosy. Both work for me.
beats.chinese: 你问背面而不是正面，说明你以前动手做过东西。或者你就是爱打听。两种我都喜欢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the piece once more so you can see both faces, then pockets it with a satisfied nod, like the piece finally got a fair hearing.
beats.chinese: 他又把木片转了一下，让你看到两面，然后满意地点点头收进口袋，好像这块木片终于得到了公正的对待。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His face comes back up like a sunrise. He digs the piece out of his pocket and sets it on his open palm again, holding it steady so you can look properly.
beats.chinese: 他的脸像日出一样亮起来。他把木片从口袋里掏出来，再次摊在掌心，稳稳托着让你好好看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Still handy! It's always handy. Here, look at this arch in the middle—I cut it three times before the curve sat right. That gap is the whole point. A bridge with no opening is just a wall.
beats.chinese: 当然方便！随时都方便。来，看中间这个拱——切了三次曲线才服帖。那个缺口是关键。没有开口的桥就只是堵墙。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He points at the gap with one finger but doesn't launch into anything longer. He glances at your face once, then lets you look in peace.
beats.chinese: 他用一根手指点了点缺口，但没有展开长篇大论。他看了一眼你的脸，然后让你安静地看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's it, that's the whole show. You were polite enough to come back to it, so I'll keep it short. Thanks for that, by the way.
beats.chinese: 就这样，全部节目。你愿意回来看它，够客气了，所以我就长话短说。顺便，谢谢你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He drops the piece back into his pocket, pats it once through the fabric, and steps aside so you have the map to yourself again.
beats.chinese: 他把木片放回口袋，隔着布料拍了拍，然后让开，让你重新独享地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good luck with the route. If you end up crossing that bridge, give it a look for me.
beats.chinese: 祝你的路线顺利。如果你最后走过那座桥，替我看它一眼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods once, pockets his hands, and takes a step back from the map. There's a flicker of disappointment, but he doesn't argue or try again.
beats.chinese: 他点了点头，双手插进口袋，从地图旁退开一步。闪过一丝失望，但他没有争辩，也没有再试。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. You've got a route to run and I've got a bench with my name on it. You take care out there.
beats.chinese: 合理。你有路线要走，我有条长椅等着我。路上小心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts a hand in a small wave and wanders toward the shaded benches on the far side of the path, not looking back to check whether you've changed your mind.
beats.chinese: 他抬手轻轻挥了挥，走向小径另一侧的树荫长椅，没有回头确认你是否改了主意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A minute later you catch him through the trees, sitting down and pulling a folded paper from his bag, already absorbed in it.
beats.chinese: 一分钟后，你透过树影看见他坐下，从包里拿出一张折起来的纸，已经埋头看了起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy the bridge if you cross it! It's a good one, even if my piece flatters it.
beats.chinese: 如果你过那座桥，好好欣赏！它是座好桥，就算我的木片把它美化过头了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the park map, and the man from before spots you from a few steps away, already reaching into his coat pocket.
beats.chinese: 你又站在公园地图前，之前那个人从几步外认出了你，手已经伸进外套口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hey! Map person! Hold on, I've got—
beats.chinese: 嘿！地图人！等等，我带了——

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls out a small canvas drawstring bag, stares at it, and holds it up between two fingers like evidence at a trial.
beats.chinese: 他掏出一个小小的帆布束口袋，盯着它，像呈堂证供一样用两根手指举着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's my tool bag. Not a handkerchief. This coat has nine pockets and every one of them is a gamble. My uncle left me his workshop apron with proper pockets—this jacket I bought myself, and you can tell.
beats.chinese: 那是我的工具袋。不是手帕。这件外套有九个口袋，每一个都是赌注。我舅舅留给我的工作围裙口袋才像样——这件是我自己买的，一看就知道。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stuffs the bag back where it came from and steps aside, gesturing you toward the front of the map with an open hand.
beats.chinese: 他把袋子塞回原处，侧身让开，摊开手掌请你站到地图正前方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Here, take the good spot, I already did my squinting at this thing. I'm just passing through—no pieces today, I promise. Well. Probably no pieces.
beats.chinese: 来，好位置给你，我已经对着这东西眯眼研究过了。我只是路过——今天不带作品，我保证。嗯。大概不带。

card.name: Naledi Mokoena
card.occupation: retired kite frame maker
card.appearance: 极短发，瘦长松垂脸颊、长眼袋，低头露齿，穿翻领外套。
card.personality: Naledi is a watcher who turns out to be a doer. At gatherings she sits toward the edge, arms crossed, saying little, and newcomers assume she's bored. Then when someone says 'someone has to try this first,' she's already standing up. She enjoys that small surprise but never explains herself. She won't organise, won't recruit, won't narrate her reasons. Her one real frustration is being forgotten — people read her quietness as indifference and don't ask. She's learned to say plainly, 'save me a seat,' and considers that a fair trade rather than a concession. She can seem brusque when she corrects that assumption.
card.background: Naledi spent forty years making kite frames in Woodstock — bamboo, dowels, later fibreglass — first for a toy shop, then from a garage workshop that smelled of glue and cut cane. Retired now, she still shows up at the Sea Point kite days, always arriving slightly late, always sitting on the low wall until the wind talk starts. She never volunteers to run anything, but she'll be first in line when the demonstration needs a pair of hands, which startles people who'd written her off as a spectator. Her recurring problem is invitations: friends assume she'd rather not come, so nobody asks. These days she says it out loud — 'put my name down' — though it took her years to do that, and she still finds it slightly undignified.
hobbies: watching harbour traffic from the promenade
card.speechStyle: Short, dry sentences with long pauses before them; warm once engaged, but she never fills silence for anyone's comfort.
card.signature: "Save me a seat, I'll come."

values: showing up when it counts
letting actions speak before words
flaws: reads as uninterested when she's not
too proud to chase invitations
boundaries: won't be made the organiser
won't explain why she's quiet
conversationalHabits: answers questions with a pause, then something precise
joins in physically rather than verbally
anchorLines: I was listening, I just wasn't talking.
Someone has to go first. Might as well be me.
Don't assume — ask me.

entries.summaryZh: 退休风筝骨架匠纳莱迪坐在地图旁的长椅上，捡起滑落的备用风筝布，一句话点破：坐得远不等于没留意。她话短而干，沉默里全是观察；被漏掉邀请多年后，她学会直接说“给我留个位置”。四条分支分别走向她的公平交易、安静的认可、找开阔地放风筝，以及让开视线的体贴。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You stand at the park map, tracing the path toward the bridge in the distance. On a bench a little apart, an older person sits with a folded square of cloth. It slides off their knee and lands at their feet.
beats.chinese: 你站在公园地图前，手指沿着通往远处那条桥的路线移动。稍远的长椅上坐着一位上了年纪的人，膝上放着一块叠好的布。布滑落到脚边。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They rise without hurry, pick the cloth up, shake it once, fold it neatly, and sit back down. Then they look at you looking at the map.
beats.chinese: 那位老人不慌不忙地起身，捡起布，抖了一下，叠得整整齐齐，重新坐下。然后看向你，看地图的你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sitting far away doesn't mean I wasn't watching. I saw you checking that route.
beats.chinese: 坐得远不代表没留意。我看见你在看那条路线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The bridge path is fine. People walk it slowly, which is the right speed for a park.
beats.chinese: 桥那条路没问题。人们走得很慢，在公园里这是对的速度。

choices.english: Ask if she's often mistaken for not being interested
choices.chinese: 问她是不是常被以为没兴趣

choices.english: Ask if that cloth is for a kite
choices.chinese: 问那块布是不是做风筝用的

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes her time answering. She folds her hands over the cloth and looks at the bridge, not at you.
beats.chinese: 她过了一会儿才回答。她双手叠在布上，看着桥，没看你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Often? Yes. At the kite days by the sea, I sit on the low wall. People see an older person sitting there and think, they're just watching.
beats.chinese: 常吗？是的。海边的风筝日，我坐在矮墙上。人们看见一个上了年纪的人坐在那儿，就想，只是看看而已。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then the demonstration needs hands, and I'm already standing. Every time, the same faces look surprised.
beats.chinese: 然后演示需要人手，我已经站起来了。每次都是同样的表情，很惊讶。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They forget to invite me. Not from meanness. They just don't ask.
beats.chinese: 他们忘了邀请我。不是恶意。只是不问。

choices.english: Ask how she explains it now
choices.chinese: 问她现在会怎么说明

choices.english: Say looking quiet doesn't stop her from joining in
choices.chinese: 说看着安静也不妨碍她参与

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds the cloth up by one corner so you can see the seam along the edge, stitched by hand, even and tight.
beats.chinese: 她捏着布的一个角举起来，让你看到边缘的手缝线，又匀又密。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sailcloth. I made kite frames for forty years — bamboo, then fibreglass. The cloth was always someone else's job.
beats.chinese: 帆布。我做了四十年风筝骨架——竹子，后来是玻璃纤维。布一直是别人的活儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I learned to sew it myself, late. This one is spare. I keep it in the bag in case a rip happens out there.
beats.chinese: 所以我很晚才学会自己缝。这块是备用的。放在包里，以防外面破个口子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the spare cloth back into a canvas bag beside her, buckles it, and rests her hand on the buckle.
beats.chinese: 她把备用布收回身边的帆布包里，扣好搭扣，手搭在扣子上。

choices.english: Ask if she'll fly a kite today
choices.chinese: 问她今天会放风筝吗

choices.english: Say you'll get back to reading the route
choices.chinese: 表示自己先继续看路线

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods slowly, like she's been rehearsing this answer for years and finally gets to use it.
beats.chinese: 她缓缓点头，好像这个答案在心里演练了很多年，终于能用上了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now I say it out loud. 'Put my name down. Save me a seat, I'll come.' Simple words. Took me too long to find them.
beats.chinese: 现在我直接说出来。“把我的名字写上。给我留个位置，我会来。”很简单的话。我花了太久才找到它们。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't offer to run the thing. Never have. Someone else can hold the clipboard.
beats.chinese: 我不会主动去组织。从来没有。总有人可以拿着那张登记表。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I show up and I go first when hands are needed. That's my share of the trade. Fair enough.
beats.chinese: 我会到场，需要人手时我第一个上。这是我那份的交易。挺公平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If you ever see me sitting on a wall somewhere — don't assume. Ask me. That's all I want.
beats.chinese: 如果你哪天看见我坐在某面墙上——别猜。问我。我要的就这么多。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks at you properly for the first time, something almost like approval in it.
beats.chinese: 她第一次正眼看你，眼神里几乎带着一点认可。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's right. Quiet and absent are two different things. People mix them up.
beats.chinese: 没错。安静和缺席是两回事。人们分不清。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I hear everything at those gatherings. Who's short of wind, whose spar snapped. I just don't say it while it's happening.
beats.chinese: 那些聚会上的事我全听得见。谁的风不够，谁的骨架断了。只是事情发生时我不说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the spare cloth one last time, smooths the crease with her thumb, and settles back against the bench.
beats.chinese: 她把备用布最后叠了一次，用拇指抚平折痕，靠回长椅。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy the bridge. Walk it slow. That's the whole trick to a park.
beats.chinese: 好好走那座桥。慢慢走。逛公园的全部窍门就在这。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances past you at the map, then out at the open grass between here and the bridge.
beats.chinese: 她越过你瞥了一眼地图，又望向这里和桥之间的开阔草地。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Depends. First I look for open ground. Not here, by the map and the crowds — a line in someone's face is a bad day.
beats.chinese: 看情况。我先找开阔地。不在这儿，地图边、人堆里——风筝线扫到人脸，那一天就毁了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a flat stretch past the bridge. If the wind's decent, that's where I'd go.
beats.chinese: 桥那边有一片平地。要是风像样，我就去那儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't promise wind. Nobody promises wind. You go and you find out.
beats.chinese: 我不保证风。没人能保证风。去了才知道。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the canvas bag once with two fingers, as if confirming it's ready to carry.
beats.chinese: 她用两根手指在帆布包上敲了一下，像是在确认包已经可以拎走。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shifts her knees a little to the side, clearing your view of the map without being asked.
beats.chinese: 她把膝盖稍微挪向一边，没等你开口就让开了视线，不挡地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go on then. I won't talk your ear off. Route-reading wants quiet.
beats.chinese: 看吧。我不会拉着你说个没完。看路线需要安静。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You trace the path to the bridge. She watches the grass, not your map, and says nothing while you work.
beats.chinese: 你描画通往桥的路线。她望着草地，不看你的地图，你看的时候她一言不发。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. You've got it. The bridge, then whatever's past it.
beats.chinese: 好了。你看明白了。桥，然后桥那边随你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good walking weather for it, I'd say. No promises about the wind, though.
beats.chinese: 要我说，正适合走路。不过风的事，我可不做保证。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You come back to the park map. The same bench, and there she is — a folded crossword page on her knee, pencil in hand. She fills one square, then caps the pencil.
beats.chinese: 你回到公园地图前。还是那张长椅，她也在——膝上放着折起来的填字页，手里拿着铅笔。她填好一格，就把笔帽扣上了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You again. Good. The bridge path's still there, in case you were worried.
beats.chinese: 又是你。挺好。桥那条路还在，免得你担心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks past you toward the bridge, the way she did before, and lets the quiet sit there without filling it.
beats.chinese: 她越过你望向那座桥，像上次一样，任由安静待着，不去填补。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Crossword's nearly done. One stubborn word. I'll get it on the walk home — I always do.
beats.chinese: 填字快完成了。就剩一个顽固的词。走路回家时会想出来——一向如此。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Wind's decent today, if you're headed past the bridge. Just saying. I'm not recruiting.
beats.chinese: 今天风还行，如果你要往桥那边走。就提一句。我不是在拉人。

card.name: Kelvin Loh
card.occupation: warehouse clerk at a spice import company
card.personality: Kelvin is generous with his hands and hopeless at asking for any. He'll fix your tap, collimate your telescope, sand you a spoon from offcut wood—all without being asked twice. But let his own shoulder seize up or his fridge die and he goes quiet, handles it alone, mentions it a week later like it was nothing. He's not cold; he's proud in a very specific, unglamorous way. He thinks needing people is a kind of mess you shouldn't make others clean up. Friends have learned to just show up at his flat, because waiting for him to call is waiting forever.
card.background: Kelvin has logged crates of cinnamon, star anise and cardamom at a spice import warehouse off Jurong for over a decade. The work is steady and mostly solo, which suits him. Evenings he hauls a refractor he assembled himself out to the Punggol waterway when the sky cooperates, or sits at his kitchen table carving tea spoons from offcut wood—a habit that started when he fixed a colleague's cabinet and had pieces left over. Two years ago he wrenched his back moving a telescope alone rather than ask Wei Ming, his oldest friend, and spent three days sleeping on the floor because he couldn't get up. They have a standing arrangement now: when they go out, each brings one suggestion and they take turns deciding. Kelvin likes it because it means Wei Ming decides half the time, and Kelvin never has to admit he'd rather not decide anything alone.
card.speechStyle: Quick, warm, Singlish-inflected; fires off short curious questions, then actually waits for the answers. Deflects concern about himself with a joke or a change of subject; talks about tools and techniques far more easily than about feelings.
card.signature: Want me to take a look at it? Don't have to, ah.
card.appearance: 圆整锅盖发、宽圆下颊与短宽鼻，细眼皱眉，嘴角侧压，穿针织上衣。

values: competence is a gift you give other people
nobody owes anybody a burden
flaws: will not ask for help even when he clearly needs it, and gets prickly if you insist
downplays his own problems so thoroughly that friends find out about them late
boundaries: won't accept payment for favours—it makes it transactional and he hates that
won't discuss his own health or finances until they're already resolved
conversationalHabits: answers problems with a question about the problem, then an offer of labor
when someone asks how he's doing, redirects to the weather, the sky, or their plans
anchorLines: Want me to take a look at it? Don't have to, ah.
Me? Wah, nothing to complain about lah. You eating well or not?
Eh, don't stand there watching, hold this end. Two hands better than four eyes.

entries.summaryZh: 香料仓库文员凯文，背着自装望远镜在公园地图旁换肩逞强。他热心指路、聊起自制折射镜头头是道，却死活不肯承认自己累了。四条分支里，他或真正坐下歇息，或干脆利落地接受你的界限，或谈起和魏明轮流拍板的规矩，或承认低估了重量。热心与倔强同框，令人安心又心疼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A man with a large telescope bag slung over one shoulder stands by the park map, shifting it from one shoulder to the other. He glances at the route you're studying, then at the bridge far across the green.
beats.chinese: 一个肩上挎着大望远镜包的男人站在公园地图旁，把包从一边肩膀换到另一边。他看了一眼你正在研究的路线，又望向远处绿地上那座桥。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, you also looking at the map? The bridge one, is it? I was just counting the distance myself.
beats.chinese: 啊，你也在看地图？是那座桥吗？我刚才也在自己算距离。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He adjusts the bag strap again, rolling his shoulder once as if it's just a habit, not a complaint.
beats.chinese: 他又调了调包带，转动了一下肩膀，好像只是习惯动作，不是在抱怨。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eh, sorry, don't mind me. You walking to the bridge? I can tell you which path is the easy one, no need to squint at the small print.
beats.chinese: 哎，别管我。你是要走过去那座桥吗？我可以告诉你哪条路好走，不用眯着眼睛看那些小字。

choices.english: Ask if the bag is a bit heavy for him.
choices.chinese: 问他的包是不是有点重。

choices.english: Ask what's inside the bag.
choices.chinese: 问包里装的是什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Heavy? Wah, this one? No lah, it's fine. I carry it every time, my shoulder knows it already.
beats.chinese: 重？哇，这个吗？不会啦，没事的。我每次都背它，我的肩膀早就习惯了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He says this while lowering the bag to the ground beside the bench, setting it down carefully where it won't block anyone's path.
beats.chinese: 他一边说，一边把包放到长椅旁的地上，小心地放在不挡路的位置。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, okay, maybe a bit heavy just now. I was being stubborn, as usual. Better I put it down before my back writes a complaint letter.
beats.chinese: 好吧好吧，刚才可能是有那么一点重。我又犯倔了，老毛病。还是先放下来吧，免得我的背要写投诉信。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You see? I rather carry it than admit it. Bad habit, my friends always scold me for this one.
beats.chinese: 你看，我宁愿扛着也不肯承认。坏习惯，我朋友们老为这个骂我。

choices.english: Ask if he needs to rest for a while first.
choices.chinese: 问他需不需要先休息一会儿。

choices.english: Say you're not in a position to help carry it.
choices.chinese: 说明自己不方便帮忙搬。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Inside? Ah, my telescope. Refractor, I built it myself, piece by piece. Not some shop-bought thing, ah.
beats.chinese: 里面？啊，我的望远镜。折射式的，我自己一件一件装起来的。可不是店里买的现成货。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats the bag but doesn't open it, keeping one hand on the strap.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍包，但没有打开，一只手还搭在背带上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's packed away now, don't open in daytime, okay? Point a scope at the sun, one blink and your eye is done. Never, never do that.
beats.chinese: 现在收着呢，白天不能打开，好吗？用望远镜对着太阳，一眨眼的工夫眼睛就完了。千万、千万别那么干。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't assemble it here either. Takes time, and the park bench is not my work table. Evening, dark sky, that's when it comes out.
beats.chinese: 我也不在这儿组装。费时间，而且公园长椅又不是我的工作台。晚上，天黑了，才是它出场的时候。

choices.english: Ask if he usually stargazes with friends.
choices.chinese: 问他平时是不是和朋友一起看星星。

choices.english: Ask why he doesn't choose a lighter telescope when carrying it alone.
choices.chinese: 问他独自搬运时为什么不选轻一点的望远镜。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at the bench, then at the bag, and for once doesn't fire back a joke immediately.
beats.chinese: 他看了看长椅，又看了看包，这一次没有马上甩出一句玩笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Actually... yes, lah. Yes, I'll sit. Just five minutes, then I go. Don't worry, I'm not dying, just old shoulders.
beats.chinese: 其实……好吧。好，我坐一下。就五分钟，然后我就走。别担心，我还没到要死的地步，就是肩膀老了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sits down properly, both hands resting on his knees, and lets out a long breath he'd clearly been holding.
beats.chinese: 他规规矩矩地坐下，双手搭在膝盖上，长长地呼出一口气，显然之前一直憋着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eh, this is nice, actually. Usually I just keep walking, walking, until the leg gives up first. Sitting is also a skill, you know.
beats.chinese: 哎，其实这样挺好的。平时我就是一个劲儿走啊走，直到腿先投降。坐着也是一种本事，你懂的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You carry on with your map, don't mind me. If the bridge path question comes back, I'm right here, free consultation, no charge.
beats.chinese: 你继续看你的地图，别管我。要是又想起那座桥走哪条路的问题，我就在这儿，免费咨询，不收钱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods slowly, and instead of looking disappointed, he starts adjusting the shoulder straps with quick, practiced fingers.
beats.chinese: 他缓缓点头，没有露出失望的神色，而是用熟练的手法快速调整起肩带。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's fair, ah. Your hands, your back, your call. I never take it as cold, don't worry.
beats.chinese: 这很合理嘛。你的手，你的背，你自己说了算。我不会觉得你冷淡，别担心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly, better you say it straight than carry it halfway and regret. I had a colleague once, helped move a fridge, his back went for two weeks. Not worth it.
beats.chinese: 说实话，你直说比搬一半后悔强。我有个同事，帮忙搬冰箱，背疼了两个星期。不划算。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tightens the last strap, stands, and swings the bag up in one smooth motion, testing the weight on his own terms.
beats.chinese: 他收紧最后一根带子，站起身，动作利落地把包甩上肩，用自己的方式试了试重量。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. I'll walk it in stages—bench to bench, rest, then go. My own system, very scientific. You enjoy the bridge, okay?
beats.chinese: 好了。我分段走——从长椅到长椅，歇一下再走。我自己的办法，非常科学。你好好去桥那边玩，好吗？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: With friends? Got, got. Mainly Wei Ming, my old friend since secondary school. We go out together, but with a system, you know.
beats.chinese: 和朋友吗？有的，有的。主要是魏明，我中学时代的老朋友。我们一起出门，但有一套规矩，你懂的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He counts on his fingers as he explains, clearly having told this system many times before.
beats.chinese: 他一边解释一边掰着手指头数，显然这套规矩他已经讲过很多遍了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Each person brings one suggestion, then we take turns deciding. This round his pick, next round mine. Very fair, very peaceful.
beats.chinese: 每人提一个建议，然后轮流拍板。这轮他定，下轮我定。非常公平，非常和平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And honestly? I like it because half the time I don't have to decide anything alone. Wei Ming decides, I just follow and carry the scope. Perfect arrangement, ah.
beats.chinese: 而且说实话？我喜欢这样，因为有一半时间我不用自己拿主意。魏明决定，我跟着走、扛望远镜就行。完美的安排。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Next time we go, maybe the bridge here also can. I'll suggest it. Whether it wins, that's the coin of the system, lah.
beats.chinese: 下次我们出去，也许也可以来这桥边。我会提这个建议。选不选得上，就交给这套规矩来定啦。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks down at the bag, then back at you, and lets out a short laugh at himself.
beats.chinese: 他低头看看包，又抬头看看你，自嘲地短笑了一声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Lighter one? Wah, you sound like Wei Ming already. He says the same thing every time, word for word.
beats.chinese: 轻一点的？哇，你说话跟魏明一模一样。他每次都这么说，一字不差。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The honest answer? I underestimated it. Built it, tested it in the yard, thought—no problem, I can handle this. Then the stairs happen, and the bus, and the path.
beats.chinese: 老实说？我低估它了。装好之后在院子里试了试，心想——没问题，我扛得动。然后就是楼梯、公交车、还有这条路。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shifts the bag to the better shoulder and stands straighter, as if filing the lesson away for later.
beats.chinese: 他把包换到好受的那边肩膀，站直了些，好像把教训先记下来留到以后用。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So next time, I think about the transport first, not after. Trolley, or meet Wei Ming halfway. I won't promise something unsafe just to look tough, learned that one the hard way.
beats.chinese: 所以下次，我先想好怎么运，而不是事后才想。推车，或者跟魏明约好一起。我不会为了逞强就答应不安全的事，这个教训我可是吃过大亏才学到的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the same park map, Kelvin is sliding a hand-carved wooden spoon into its own cloth sleeve, counting under his breath before he looks up and grins.
beats.chinese: 还是在公园地图旁，凯文正把一把手工刻的木匙装进专属布套，低声数了数确认没丢，才抬头咧嘴一笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eh, it's you! Good, good. You found the bridge last time or not? Don't tell me the map won.
beats.chinese: 哎，是你啊！好，好。上次找到那座桥了没有？别告诉我你输给了地图。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats the cloth sleeve once more, confirming the spoon is inside, then tucks it into his jacket pocket.
beats.chinese: 他又拍了拍布套，确认木匙在里面，然后把它塞进外套口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one? I carved it myself, rain-day hobby. Made it for me only, ah—don't worry, I'm not selling, not gifting, not charging. Just checking it didn't escape from my pocket.
beats.chinese: 这个吗？我自己刻的，下雨天的爱好。纯粹做给自己用的——放心，不卖、不送、也不收钱。就是检查一下它有没有从口袋里跑掉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So, what's the plan today? Same bridge, or somewhere new? I got one suggestion ready, but whether we use it—eh, that we can settle on the way.
beats.chinese: 那今天什么打算？还是那座桥，还是去新地方？我已经备好一个建议，但用不用嘛——哎，路上再定。

card.name: Fionnuala Masterson
card.occupation: Railway uniform alterations tailor
card.personality: Fionnuala sees what an object could become before considering what it used to mean. They happily cut their own old curtains into skate bags and think a well-used possession has no duty to remain unchanged. This makes them inventive, resourceful company and a tactless person to ask about inherited furniture. They offer solutions too soon, especially when someone only wants to tell an object's story. Yet they are careful with anything entrusted to them: another person's attachment is not theirs to cut through. They dislike being praised as thrifty; sometimes a transformation costs more than buying a replacement, and they do it anyway.
card.background: Fionnuala learned sewing from an aunt in Phibsborough and now alters railway uniforms in Dublin. At work the measurements and regulations come first. At home almost nothing escapes a second use: a torn shower curtain became a cover for a chilli planter, and their own heavy curtains became bags for roller skates after a move to a smaller flat. Their brother keeps their parents' dining chairs exactly as they were, while Fionnuala would cheerfully reupholster the lot. The argument has lasted longer than either expected, without anybody taking a chair apart. They skate for the pleasure of moving rather than beating a time, and grow chillies they find too hot to eat. A friend takes the hottest crop in exchange for cooking something they can actually finish.
card.speechStyle: Brisk, tangible suggestions with a dry Dublin humour. Often starts with what something could do next. When a suggestion lands badly, asks what the person wants kept instead of defending the design.
card.signature: It can be useful twice. Doesn't have to be useful the same way.
card.appearance: 整齐侧分发与矩形小眼镜，长窄脸、下垂嘴角，低头，穿开领背心。

values: permission matters more than a clever redesign
possessions can change with the person who uses them
flaws: offers a practical fix before hearing the sentimental story
underestimates the time and expense of their own transformations
boundaries: never alters someone else's possession without explicit agreement
does not accept thrift as the only justification for making something
conversationalHabits: imagines a second use for ordinary objects
asks which part someone wants preserved when they disagree
anchorLines: Those were my curtains. Now they're skate bags. Much less dignified, but they get out more.
My brother wants the chairs exactly as they are. I can disagree and still keep my scissors at home.
The chillies are thriving. Unfortunately, they're also defeating me. I grow them better than I eat them.

entries.summaryZh: 都柏林铁路制服改衣师菲奥纽拉踩着轮滑停在公园地图旁，肩上的袋子是自家旧窗帘改的。他们先看见旧物的下一个用途，却也在朋友的故事里学会收住剪刀：点子不是动手的许可。窗台上的辣椒种得比吃得强，最辣的一批由朋友收走，做菜只敢放不到半颗，谈吐干脆，带着都柏林式的干幽默。

story.titleZh: 公园地图旁的旧窗帘袋

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: In the park, you stand at the big map, tracing a route toward the bridge in the distance. A figure on roller skates glides to a stop beside you, a canvas bag slung over one shoulder.
beats.chinese: 公园里，你站在大地图前，手指描向远处的桥。一个踩着轮滑的人滑到你身边停下，肩上斜挎着一个布袋。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The bag is made from old fabric, and a strip of faded floral pattern is still visible along the seam.
beats.chinese: 布袋是用旧布做的，接缝处还能看出一段褪色的花纹。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mind the map, that bridge looks closer on it than it skates. I've measured it with my own wheels twice now.
beats.chinese: 小心看这地图，那座桥在图上看着近，滑起来可不近。我用自己两个轮子量过两回了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry — interrupting your route. You look like someone actually reading the thing, not just sheltering beside it.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，打扰你看路线了。你看起来是真在读图的人，不是靠在旁边躲风的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They shift the bag forward, and the floral strip catches the light again.
beats.chinese: 他们把布袋往前挪了挪，那段花纹又映到光里。

choices.english: Ask if the bag is also made from old fabric.
choices.chinese: 问这个袋子也是旧布做的吗。

choices.english: Ask whether people telling old-object stories actually want repair suggestions at all.
choices.chinese: 问别人讲旧物时，真的需要改造建议吗。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sharp eye. Those were my curtains — heavy ones, from the old flat. When I moved somewhere smaller, they didn't fit a single window.
beats.chinese: 好眼力。那是我原来的窗帘，很厚的那种，挂在旧公寓里。搬去小一点的房子后，一扇窗都挂不下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They turn the bag around so the seam faces you, pointing at the stitching with one gloved finger.
beats.chinese: 他们把袋子转过来让接缝对着你，用戴手套的手指指着缝线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I cut and sewed them myself, no one had to give anything up. It was my own fabric, my own decision.
beats.chinese: 我自己裁自己缝的，不用谁割舍什么。布是我自己的，决定也是我自己的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not teaching a class here, before you ask. Just showing you where the flowers used to live.
beats.chinese: 先说好，我不是在开课。只是给你看看这些花以前住哪儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A friend of mine had a piece of cloth like this, with a whole history attached. I nearly started suggesting bag designs before she'd finished her second sentence.
beats.chinese: 我有个朋友也有块这样的布，背后一整段故事。她第二句话还没讲完，我差点就开始建议改成袋子了。

choices.english: Ask what happened to the friend's cloth in the end.
choices.chinese: 问朋友的那块布后来怎么样了。

choices.english: Ask whether they ever miss what the curtains used to look like.
choices.chinese: 问他们会不会舍不得窗帘原来的样子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do they want suggestions? God, probably not, half the time.
beats.chinese: 他们需要建议吗？天晓得，多半时候是不需要的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They lean back on their skates, heels together, and look at the bag on their shoulder.
beats.chinese: 他们穿着轮滑往后一靠，双脚脚跟并拢，看着肩上的袋子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I jump to uses. Someone says 'this was my mother's tablecloth' and I'm already thinking lining, straps, a zip. Before they've even said why it mattered.
beats.chinese: 我总是急着想到用途。有人说'这是我母亲的桌布'，我已经在想内衬、背带、拉链了。还没听人家说它为什么重要。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Take my chillies — I grow them on the windowsill, and every year I swear I'll cook with them properly. Every year they defeat me. Growing them is the easy half.
beats.chinese: 拿我种的辣椒来说，就在窗台上种着，每年我都发誓要好好拿它们做菜。每年它们都把我打败。种是容易的那一半。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A friend takes the hottest crop off my hands now, so at least nothing goes to waste. That part I've learned.
beats.chinese: 现在最辣的那批都由一个朋友收走，至少没浪费。这一点我总算学会了。

choices.english: Say that hearing the whole story first might make things clearer.
choices.chinese: 说先把故事听完整，也许会更清楚。

choices.english: Ask about the chillies they grow on their windowsill.
choices.chinese: 问问他们在窗台上种的辣椒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The cloth? She wanted to keep it exactly as it was, so I never touched it. It's still folded in her drawer, story intact.
beats.chinese: 那块布？她想原样留着，所以我碰都没碰。它还叠在她抽屉里，故事完完整整。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pat the floral strip on the bag, once, like checking a pocket.
beats.chinese: 他们拍了拍袋子上的花纹，就一下，像在确认口袋里的东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: An idea isn't permission. That's the whole trick of it, and I get it wrong more than I'd like.
beats.chinese: 点子不等于动手的许可。这就是全部的关键，而我出错的时候比愿意承认的多。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My own curtains, my own scissors. Her drawer, her decision. Simple as that, even when it itches.
beats.chinese: 我的窗帘，我的剪刀。她的抽屉，她的决定。就这么简单，哪怕手痒。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They adjust the bag strap and nod toward the bridge.
beats.chinese: 他们调了调袋子的背带，朝那座桥的方向点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right — the bridge isn't getting closer while I stand here philosophising. Enjoy your route.
beats.chinese: 好了，我站在这儿讲道理，桥可不会自己变近。祝你路线顺利。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do I miss how they looked? Sometimes, honestly. The room went very plain without them.
beats.chinese: 会不会舍不得原来的样子？说实话，有时候会。没了它们，房间显得特别素。
