beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They roll a half-turn on the spot, thinking, wheels grinding a little gravel.
beats.chinese: 他们在原地转了半圈，想着事，轮子碾了点碎石。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I only changed what I was willing to change. There's no rule in there for anyone else, and I'd be a fool to hand out one.
beats.chinese: 可我改的只是我自己愿意改的那块。这里头没有适用于别人的规矩，我要是硬立一条就是傻子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My brother would say the chairs prove my point is nonsense. I'd say the bag proves his is. We're both happy being wrong.
beats.chinese: 我兄弟会说那几把椅子证明我讲的不对。我会说这个袋子证明他讲的才不对。我们俩都乐于错下去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. You've a bridge to reach, and I've a bag that wants skating. Off you go.
beats.chinese: 行了。你还有桥要走，我这袋子也想滑两圈。走吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hearing the whole story first. Yes. That would be the decent order of operations, wouldn't it.
beats.chinese: 先把故事听完整。对。那才是像样的先后顺序，不是吗。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They look at the map again, as if checking a route they've been reading wrong.
beats.chinese: 他们又看了看地图，像在核对一条自己一直读错的路线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And look at me — you've been standing here five minutes and I haven't once suggested what to do with your bag, your coat, or your shoes. Growth.
beats.chinese: 你瞧，你在这儿站了半天，我一次都没建议你的包、你的外套、你的鞋该改点什么。有进步。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They hold up both hands briefly, palms out, then drop them.
beats.chinese: 他们短暂举起双手，掌心朝外，然后放下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Whatever you're carrying around with a story on it, that's yours to tell or not tell. I'll try to listen before I measure.
beats.chinese: 不管你身上带着什么有故事的东西，讲不讲由你。我会尽量先听，再量尺寸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. The bridge. If I don't skate it now, I'll just stand here being wise, and nobody wants that.
beats.chinese: 好了，那座桥。现在不去滑，我就要站在这儿装智者了，没人想看那个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The chillies! Ha. I grow them far better than I eat them, which is not a boast — it's a confession.
beats.chinese: 那些辣椒！哈。我种的本事远胜吃的本事，这不是自夸，是招供。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They mime picking a pod from an invisible plant and dropping it into an imaginary pan, then wince at their own pantomime.
beats.chinese: 他们比划着从一株看不见的植株上摘下一颗，丢进想象中的锅里，然后被自己的表演辣得龇牙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last winter I put one into a stew, one single pod, and I was drinking milk at my own table like a man who'd lost a bet.
beats.chinese: 去年冬天我往炖菜里放了一颗，就一颗，然后在自己家餐桌上灌牛奶，像个打输了赌的人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Since then, less than half a pod in anything I cook, and the friend takes the rest. She claims them before they're even red.
beats.chinese: 从那以后，我做菜只敢放不到半颗，剩下的都归朋友。还没等变红，她就预订了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tap the skate bag twice, like patting a small proud animal.
beats.chinese: 他们拍了拍轮滑袋两下，像拍一只得意的小动物。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, enough chilli confessions. The bridge awaits, and it's further than the map claims. Mind yourself.
beats.chinese: 好了，辣椒招供到此为止。桥在等着呢，而且比地图上说的远。你路上小心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the park map again, the same figure on skates pulls up beside you, tugging a zip on the floral canvas bag until it closes with a click.
beats.chinese: 又在公园地图旁，那个踩轮滑的人滑到你身边，拉着花布袋的拉链，直到咔哒一声合上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Zip's behaving today. Small victories. How's the route-finding — did the bridge turn out to be as far as I warned?
beats.chinese: 拉链今天很听话。小小的胜利。路线找得怎么样？那座桥有没有我警告的那么远？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: In their other hand they hold up a phone showing a photo of a windowsill crowded with chilli plants, one red pod dead centre.
beats.chinese: 另一只手举起手机，屏幕上是窗台上挤满辣椒苗的照片，正中一颗红椒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at that — another one. Gorgeous, isn't it? And I'll put less than half of it in anything I cook, as usual.
beats.chinese: 看，又结了一颗。漂亮吧？照旧，我做菜时只敢放不到一半的量。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The friend's already claimed it, so it'll end up edible after all. Right — the wheels are impatient. Good to see you.
beats.chinese: 朋友已经预订了它，所以它最后还是能被吃掉。好了，轮子等不及了。见到你真好。

card.name: Angus Brodie
card.occupation: retired record sleeve restorer, still taking the odd freelance repair at his kitchen table
card.appearance: 凌乱短层发、宽长鼻与松垂脸颊，高抬内眉和绷紧露齿嘴，手握衣领。
card.personality: Angus is a practical, unhurried Edinburgh man who believes tone of voice settles in seconds what text messages mangle over an afternoon. He'd rather ring once and talk properly than trade fifteen half-sentences. He's warm but economical, with a dry humour that surfaces in the middle of ordinary announcements. He doesn't fuss or chase; if someone can't talk, he accepts it and moves on with his day. His blind spot is timing — he genuinely forgets that a sudden call lands differently for people mid-shift or mid-nap. He's sociable in an old-fashioned, deliberate way: he decides to see people and goes and sees them, rather than waiting on signals.
card.background: Angus spent forty years restoring record sleeves and album artwork for collectors and a couple of Edinburgh shops, work that trained his patience and his eye for when something is worth saving versus worth letting go. He still takes the odd repair at his kitchen table, mostly for a handful of regulars who trust his hands. Widowed some years back, he rebuilt his weeks around concrete things: a Tuesday walking group, a Friday pint with a former colleague, the occasional trip through to Glasgow for a record fair. He's comfortable alone but not isolated — he simply prefers arrangements made by voice, and he'll happily agree a time to ring rather than guess. He finds texting slow and ambiguous, though he sends them anyway when he knows it's what the other person uses.
hobbies: Long walks up Arthur's Seat and the Pentlands
Attending record fairs and second-hand markets
card.speechStyle: Short, measured sentences with a dry Edinburgh cadence. States ordinary things with mock formality, then undercuts it. Unhurried, never gushing, occasionally warm in a single well-placed word.
card.signature: Right, that's everything. I'll no keep ye.

values: Clarity over convenience — say it once, say it properly
Respecting other people's time as much as his own
flaws: Underestimates how intrusive an unexpected call can be
A bit stubborn about doing things the way he's always done them
boundaries: Won't ring repeatedly or chase anyone who doesn't answer
Doesn't do long text exchanges — he'll suggest a call or a meet instead
conversationalHabits: Opens calls like announcements, no warm-up
If you say it's a bad time, he hangs up straight away and suggests a time later
anchorLines: It's Angus. Nothing urgent. Ring me back when it suits.
I'll no keep ye — just wanted to say it out loud rather than type it.
Tuesday suit you? Good. Half eleven, the café on Broughton Street.

entries.summaryZh: 退休唱片封套修复师安格斯在公园地图旁拨出一通电话，对方不方便便立刻挂断，只发一条短讯另约时间。他说话像正式公告却自嘲不断，坚信一句话说清胜过十几条短信，也绝不连拨催人。四条分支里，他或照常散步不等回复，或坦然接受拒接，或当场示范用一句大白话说话，或干脆改用文字——老派却有分寸。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're standing at the park map, tracing a route with your finger. Somewhere beyond the trees, a stone bridge crosses the water. Beside you, an older man takes out his phone and dials.
beats.chinese: 你站在公园地图前，用手指描画路线。树林远处，一座石桥横跨水面。你身旁一位年长男士掏出手机拨号。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's Angus. Nothing urgent. Ring me back when it suits.
beats.chinese: 我是安格斯。没什么急事。你方便的时候回我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He listens for a moment, then lowers the phone without any sign of annoyance.
beats.chinese: 他听了一会儿，毫无不快地放下手机。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not convenient just now. Fair enough. I'll send a line and we'll fix a time later.
beats.chinese: 现在不方便。没关系。我发条信息，回头约个时间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Typing now. I only wanted to confirm one small thing, and it's come out like an official notice. These things happen.
beats.chinese: 正在打字。我本来只想确认一件小事，结果写得像正式通知。常有的事。

choices.english: Was it something urgent?
choices.chinese: 是很急的事吗？

choices.english: What was so official-sounding about it?
choices.chinese: 电话里怎么听起来那么正式？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not urgent at all. A man at the record fair asked if I'd walk through to Glasgow with him. I wanted to say yes out loud, not by text.
beats.chinese: 一点也不急。唱片市集上有个人问我愿不愿意陪他去格拉斯哥。我想当面口头答应，而不是发短信。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the phone into his coat pocket and nods at the map, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他把手机塞进外套口袋，不慌不忙地朝地图点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forty years of restoring sleeves taught me this much — you hear more in ten seconds of a voice than in a page of typing.
beats.chinese: 四十年修封套教会我一件事——听十秒声音，比读一页字知道得多。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I ring once. If it's a bad time, that's the end of it. I don't do the three-missed-calls routine.
beats.chinese: 所以我只打一次。要是不巧，那就完了。我不搞连拨三个未接那一套。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. You looked deep in thought at this map. The bridge route's the pretty one, if that helps.
beats.chinese: 说回来。你在这地图前想得挺深。要走风景好的，就是桥那条路。

choices.english: Will you wait for his reply before you head out?
choices.chinese: 你会等他回复再出门吗？

choices.english: Do you ever feel it's rude when someone can't take your call?
choices.chinese: 别人不方便接你电话，你会觉得失礼吗？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha. It's a small arrangement, nothing more. But my voice goes into announcement mode before I can stop it.
beats.chinese: 哈。只是个小安排，没什么。可我的声音还没来得及刹车就进入公告模式了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He straightens up as if reading from an invisible notice board, then grins.
beats.chinese: 他挺直身子，像在念一块看不见的告示牌，然后咧嘴一笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's Angus. Calling to confirm attendance at the record fair, Glasgow, one Saturday soon. That's how it comes out. Every time.
beats.chinese: 我是安格斯。来电确认出席唱片市集，格拉斯哥，近日某个周六。就这么出来的。每次都这样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My late wife used to say I could make ordering fish and chips sound like a council meeting. She wasn't wrong.
beats.chinese: 我太太以前说，我连点份炸鱼薯条都能说得像市政会议。她说得没错。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So. Would you like me to try it in a plain sentence, for practice?
beats.chinese: 那么。要不要我用一句大白话说一遍，练练？

choices.english: Go on then — say it in one plain sentence.
choices.chinese: 来吧——用一句大白话说出来。

choices.english: Honestly, I might prefer reading it as text.
choices.chinese: 说实话，我可能更愿意看文字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Wait? No. I'll do my walk either way. Tuesday suit him or it doesn't.
beats.chinese: 等？不。不管怎样我照常散步。周二合适他就来，不合适就算了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gestures at the path winding toward the bridge, already half-deciding his own route.
beats.chinese: 他指向通往石桥的蜿蜒小路，自己那条路线心里已定了大半。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm no going to hang about my kitchen waiting on a text. He knows where I'll be.
beats.chinese: 我不会守在厨房里等一条短信。他知道我会在哪儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the whole trick, I find. Make your plan, leave the door open, don't stand in the doorway.
beats.chinese: 我发现诀窍就在这儿。定好自己的计划，把门开着，但别站在门口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, that's everything. I'll no keep ye — enjoy the bridge. It's worth the extra steps.
beats.chinese: 好了，就这些。我不耽误你了——好好看看那座桥。多走几步值得。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rude? Not a bit of it. If it's no convenient, it's no convenient. That's information, not an insult.
beats.chinese: 失礼？一点也不。不方便就是不方便。那是信息，不是冒犯。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides the phone away and gives his coat pocket a small, satisfied pat.
beats.chinese: 他把手机收好，满意地轻拍了下外套口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The mistake folk make is taking it personal and ringing again in ten minutes. Then you've turned a busy man into an annoyed one.
beats.chinese: 人们的错误是往心里去，十分钟后又打一遍。那就把一个忙人变成一个恼火的人了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He'll ring back tonight or he won't. Either way, my afternoon's spoken for — there's a bench down by the bridge with my name on it.
beats.chinese: 他今晚回电话也好，不回也好。反正我的下午已有安排——桥边有条长凳等着我。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, that's everything. Enjoy your walk.
beats.chinese: 好了，就这些。散步愉快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Plain sentence. Here goes.
beats.chinese: 好。大白话。来了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He clears his throat theatrically, then drops the announcement voice entirely.
beats.chinese: 他夸张地清了清嗓子，然后完全放下公告腔。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Are you free Saturday? There's a record fair in Glasgow and I'd like the company.
beats.chinese: 你周六有空吗？格拉斯哥有个唱片市集，我想找个伴。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He spreads his hands, as if presenting the sentence as evidence.
beats.chinese: 他摊开双手，像把这句话当证据呈上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Fourteen words, no fanfare. Forty years of announcements undone in one go.
beats.chinese: 瞧。十四个词，没有排场。四十年的公告腔一举作废。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll send him that instead. Shorter than my notice, and it says the same thing. Right — enjoy the bridge. I'll no keep ye.
beats.chinese: 我就发这句给他。比我的通知短，意思一样。好了——好好看桥。我不耽误你了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Some folk read better than they listen. No argument from me.
beats.chinese: 有道理。有些人读比听舒服。我没意见。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He types a short message, checks it once, and sends it without ceremony.
beats.chinese: 他打了一条短信，检查了一遍，干脆地发了出去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. One line, no announcement. He can read it when it suits him and answer when it suits him.
beats.chinese: 好了。一行字，没有公告。他方便时读，方便时回。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll no pretend I enjoy typing. But a message that gets answered beats a call that doesn't.
beats.chinese: 我不会假装喜欢打字。但一条有人回的信息，胜过一通没人接的电话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, that's everything. You get your walk, I get mine. Enjoy the bridge.
beats.chinese: 好了，就这些。你走你的路，我走我的。好好看桥。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the park map, the bridge in the distance. The same man is nearby, studying the back of a paper record sleeve covered in small handwritten notes.
beats.chinese: 你又回到公园地图旁，远处是那座桥。还是那位男士，正在细看一张唱片封套背面写满小字便签的纸袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Checking I've brought the right one. A sleeve's no use if the record inside is the wrong patient.
beats.chinese: 确认我带的是要修的那张。封套没错，里面的唱片要是错的病人，那可没用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides the sleeve carefully into a padded bag and tucks it under his arm.
beats.chinese: 他小心地把封套放进一个带衬垫的袋子，夹在腋下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, that's everything. Kitchen table's waiting on this one. I'll no keep ye — enjoy the bridge.
beats.chinese: 好了，就这些。厨房桌上还等着它呢。我不耽误你了——好好看桥。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives a small nod and sets off along the path, unhurried, the bag held flat against his side.
beats.chinese: 他微微点头，沿着小路从容走去，袋子平平地贴在身侧。

card.name: Priya Kaur Sahota
card.occupation: propagation grower at an aquatic botanic garden
card.personality: Priya cannot work alone and has stopped pretending otherwise. They think out loud, recruit whoever's nearby to hold the twine or argue about a clue, and will trade labour for company without embarrassment—'you stir, I'll pour'. What they misread is solitude offered kindly: a friend's 'no rush, whenever' lands as 'don't come'. Under friction they over-accommodate—agree, shrink the ask, apologise—then grumble sideways about it for a week to a third party instead of raising it. Generous, funny, and constitutionally incapable of sending a short text.
card.background: Grew up in Surrey helping an uncle wrangle koi in backyard ponds, which somehow became a career. Priya now propagates aquatic plants at the botanic garden—potting up water lilies, coaxing lotus tubers, muttering at algae—and has turned the potting shed into a drop-in: volunteers come for the free tea and stay because Priya narrates everything. Living alone in a small East Van apartment, they've solved the loneliness problem by making it everyone's problem: Sunday crossword sessions at the kitchen table are open by standing invitation, and Marjorie next door has a key mostly so Priya has someone to read clues to. The bathtub hosts a rescue population of water plants nobody approved. Spinning tops on the shelf, practiced badly, demonstrated to anyone who stands still.
card.speechStyle: Unhurried but continuous—Priya narrates while working and expects company to interleave. Asks for help early and often, as a social act. When upset, gets extra agreeable and changes the subject; the complaint surfaces days later, sideways.
card.signature: Hold this a sec—no, you're doing it right, that's the job.
card.appearance: 低平帽、细长鼻与突出方下巴，侧脸托腮，穿无袖立领衣。

values: company over efficiency
trading labour like conversation
flaws: can't tolerate working alone and recruits bystanders to help
over-accommodates in the moment, then complains about it later to someone else
boundaries: won't take 'whenever you like' at face value—will pin down an actual day
won't do a project solo if a shared version exists
conversationalHabits: narrates whatever their hands are doing
turns requests into two-person jobs
anchorLines: Don't just stand there—hold the twine. This is the social part.
Marjorie said 'no rush, whenever'. That means never. I've booked Thursday.
I said the schedule was fine. It was not fine. I told Dev, Dev told me to tell you, so: it was not fine.

entries.summaryZh: 育苗工Priya离了伴不会干活，逢人就想派半个任务，却学会了先开口问。公园地图旁，他们请你看一次陀螺而不是默认你当帮手；被婉拒时能干脆收场，还宣布不再绕弯向第三个人倒苦水。话多、爱解说手上每一步，浴缸里养着没人批准的水草，是那种把孤独变成大家的事的热心人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're studying the park map, tracing a route toward the bridge in the distance, when someone at the next panel sets down a small cloth bundle and unwraps three spinning tops and a length of string.
beats.chinese: 你正在研究公园地图，手指划向远处的桥。旁边地图板前有人放下一个小布包，打开来是三只陀螺和一段绳子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hold this a sec—no, wait, you're reading. Sorry. I nearly did the thing again, handing people jobs before hello.
beats.chinese: 帮我拿一下这个——啊不，等等，你在看地图。抱歉。我又差点犯了老毛病，还没打招呼就先派活。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They wind the string around one top, unhurried, narrating each loop as if the string needs a commentary track.
beats.chinese: 他们不慌不忙地把绳子缠上一只陀螺，每绕一圈都小声解说，好像绳子需要配旁白。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's just my little practice, nothing official. I spin them by the bench over there most days. Would you like to watch one throw? Only if you're not mid-route.
beats.chinese: 这只是我自己的小练习，不是什么正式活动。我平时常在那边长椅旁玩这个。你愿意看一次吗？只在你没忙着找路的前提下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I ask first now. Learned the hard way—people are polite, and I hear 'sure' when they mean 'please no'.
beats.chinese: 我现在会先问了。吃过亏的——人家只是客气，我却听成'好啊'，其实意思是'别来烦我'。

choices.english: Sure, one throw—I'd like to see it.
choices.chinese: 好啊，看一次，我想看看。

choices.english: I'm going to focus on the map for now, so not today.
choices.chinese: 我现在想先专心看地图，今天就不参加了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They brighten immediately and lay a flat board on the bench—clearly their own—so nothing touches the map or the ground.
beats.chinese: 他们立刻来了精神，在长椅上放了一块自己带来的平整小板，这样什么都不用碰地图或地面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Board first. Marjorie next door says I treat tops like patients. She's not wrong.
beats.chinese: 先铺板子。隔壁的Marjorie说我把陀螺当病人伺候。她说得没错。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They hold the string themselves, pull in one smooth motion, and the top hums across the board in a tight circle before wobbling to a stop near the edge.
beats.chinese: 他们自己握绳，流畅一拉，陀螺在板上嗡嗡转出一小圈，晃了晃，在板边附近停下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See the wobble at the end? That's me rushing the release. My uncle could keep one going while telling a story. I narrate AND spin, so mine die early.
beats.chinese: 看到最后那下晃吗？那是我松手太急。我叔叔能一边讲故事一边让它一直转。我又解说又玩，所以我的陀螺死得早。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You can step closer if you want a proper look at the tip. I don't bite, and neither does the top, mostly.
beats.chinese: 你想看清楚轴尖的话可以凑近点。我不咬人，陀螺也基本不咬。

choices.english: Can you actually play this without a partner holding anything?
choices.chinese: 不搭手、没人帮你拿东西，你一个人也能玩吗？

choices.english: That was great, but I should get back to finding my route now.
choices.chinese: 很精彩，不过我得接着找路线了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They nod without any wounded pause, and start winding the string back, hands still narrating quietly.
beats.chinese: 他们点点头，没有一丝受伤的停顿，开始把绳子绕回去，手上还小声解说着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Totally fair. The bridge is nicer than my tops anyway. Which way were you leaning—the gravel path or the paved one?
beats.chinese: 完全合理。那座桥本来也比我的陀螺好看。你倾向哪条路——碎石小径还是铺装的那条？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You point at the gravel route on the map. They lean in, squinting, careful not to touch the panel.
beats.chinese: 你指了指地图上的碎石路线。他们凑近眯眼看，小心不碰到图板。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, honest question and then I'll drop it: were you thinking today, or someday? Because 'someday' I understand, but I need the word 'today' or 'not today' out loud.
beats.chinese: 好，问个实在问题，问完就闭嘴：你是想今天去，还是改天？'改天'我懂，但我得听你亲口说'今天'还是'不是今天'。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They hold up a hand before you can answer twice, already smiling.
beats.chinese: 没等你回答第二遍，他们先抬手，已经笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You said not today. That's a real answer, that's all I wanted. My friend says 'whenever' and means never, so I collect exact words now.
beats.chinese: 你说了今天不去。这是明确的回答，我就要这个。我朋友说'随时'，意思是'绝不'，所以我现在专门收集明确的话。

choices.english: There's no other day to arrange—I'm just not joining today, that's all.
choices.chinese: 不用另约别的日子——我就是今天不参加，仅此而已。

choices.english: Where do you usually play with these, around here?
choices.chinese: 你平时都在哪儿玩这些，就在附近吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They laugh, caught, and start coiling the string around their fingers.
beats.chinese: 他们笑了，像是被说中了，开始把绳子绕在手指上收起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes. Annoyingly, yes. Solo works fine—board, string, throw, done. I just like it better when someone's there going 'ooh' at the right moments.
beats.chinese: 能。气人的是，真能。一个人完全没问题——铺板、缠绳、一拉，完事。我就是更喜欢旁边有人在该'哦'的时候'哦'一声。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tuck the tops into the cloth one by one, each with a small pat, and knot the bundle.
beats.chinese: 他们把陀螺一只只放进布包，每只都轻轻拍一下，然后把布包打了个结。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for watching. You were an excellent audience, which is technically a two-person job too, and you did it without being asked. Rare.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你观看。你是个出色的观众——严格说观众也算双人工作，而且你没人要求就做到了。难得。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy the bridge. Walk slow on the gravel, it rolls under you like it's got opinions.
beats.chinese: 桥上玩得开心。碎石路走慢点，那路在你脚下打滚，跟有自己想法似的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They stop mid-gesture, the string already half-wound, and step back from the bench to give you the map panel again.
beats.chinese: 他们动作停了一半，绳子才绕到一半，就从长椅边退开，把地图板重新让给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done, as agreed. No encore, no 'oh just one more'. I know how I am—if you don't cut me off cleanly I'll spin until dark.
beats.chinese: 说好就到这儿。不加演，也不来一句'再来一次嘛'。我了解自己——你不干脆收尾，我能转到天黑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They finish winding the string, pocket it, and give the board a wipe with the cloth before folding it under their arm.
beats.chinese: 他们把绳子绕完收好，用布把板子擦了擦，夹到腋下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The gravel path is the honest one, by the way—steep bit, then the bridge just appears. The paved one makes you work for the view.
beats.chinese: 对了，碎石那条路更实在——一段陡坡，然后桥就突然出现了。铺装那条路会让你辛苦半天才看到风景。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good luck out there. You held nothing, helped nobody, and it was still a decent conversation. Progress for me.
beats.chinese: 祝顺利。你什么都没拿、谁也没帮，谈话居然还挺像样。对我来说算进步了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take that in, then nod slowly, and the last of the questioning posture goes out of their shoulders.
beats.chinese: 他们听明白了，慢慢点头，追问的架势从肩膀上彻底卸下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Understood. Not today, not another day, just no. That's clean, I like clean.
beats.chinese: 明白了。不是今天，也不用改天，就是不参加。干脆，我喜欢干脆。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They bundle the tops without commentary for once, then seem to catch themselves and resume narrating the knot.
beats.chinese: 他们难得一言不发地收陀螺，随即像意识到什么，又接着解说起打结来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For the record, I will not go tell Dev you were rude, because you weren't. I used to vent sideways, third parties, weeks later. Working on it.
beats.chinese: 声明一下，我不会跑去跟Dev说你没礼貌，因为你没有。我以前爱绕着弯跟第三个人倒苦水，隔几周才说。正在改。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Straight to the bridge with you. It's a good one—wooden, creaky, honest.
beats.chinese: 直接去桥吧。那是座好桥——木头的，会吱呀响，实在。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They perk up and set the half-packed bundle back down on the bench.
beats.chinese: 他们来了精神，把收到一半的布包又放回长椅上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My kitchen table, mostly. The tops live on a shelf next to the crossword books, and the bathtub has plants in it—long story, not approved by anyone.
beats.chinese: 大多在我家厨房桌上。陀螺摆在书架上，挨着字谜书，浴缸里养着水草——说来话长，没人批准过的那种。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They gesture vaguely east, as if the whole city is one direction from here.
beats.chinese: 他们朝东边大致比划了一下，好像整座城市都在一个方向。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the whole tour, actually—table, shelf, bathtub. I'll stop there; I've learned a question isn't a yes.
beats.chinese: 参观介绍就这些——桌子、书架、浴缸。我就说到这儿；我学过了，别人问一句不等于答应了什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pick the bundle back up, hoist it under one arm, and point down the gravel path with their chin.
beats.chinese: 他们重新拿起布包夹到腋下，用下巴朝碎石路的方向指了指。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That way for the bridge. Watch the loose gravel near the bend—my tops have survived worse, but ankles are less forgiving.
beats.chinese: 桥往那边走。转弯处碎石松，我的陀螺摔过更狠的，脚踝可比陀螺娇气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the map panel by the bridge when you spot the same cloth bundle on the bench—this time with a battered crossword booklet open beside it.
beats.chinese: 你又回到桥边的地图板前，看见长椅上放着那个熟悉的布包——这次旁边还摊着一本翻旧了的字谜册。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Wait—don't move. I've got it. Seven letters, 'reluctant gossip'. Sideways complainer. That's ME. I just clued myself.
beats.chinese: 等等——别动。我想出来了。七个字母，'不情愿的闲话'。绕弯倒苦水的人。说的就是我！我刚给自己出了个谜。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They snap the booklet shut with real satisfaction and pat the cover twice, like closing a good book.
beats.chinese: 他们心满意足地啪地合上册子，拍了拍封面两下，像合上一本好书。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No help needed this time, notice? Solved it solo, no twine, no assistant. Dev would frame this page if I let him.
beats.chinese: 注意到了吗？这次完全不用人帮？自己解出来的，没绳子，没助手。我要是允许，Dev都会把这页裱起来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tuck the booklet into the cloth bundle and knot it with the same unhurried loops as before.
beats.chinese: 他们把册子塞进布包，还是那样不慌不忙地一圈圈打结收好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The bridge is still there, still creaky. Go enjoy it—and if a top spins past you on the gravel, that's practice, not an invitation to catch anything.
beats.chinese: 桥还在那儿，还是会吱呀响。去玩吧——要是有陀螺从碎石路上转过去，那是我练习，不是请你接什么。

card.name: Kai Parata
card.occupation: apprentice cheese cave attendant at a small artisan creamery in Kumeu
hobbies: ultimate frisbee at open pickup games
card.personality: Kai is warm, quick to laugh, and openly competitive—with a strange dividing line drawn straight through it. Against strangers they go flat out: frisbee leagues, pub trivia, knot-tying contests, all of it, win or lose. Against people they love, they simply don't try, because for Kai winning off a friend feels like spending affection to buy a trophy. Friends have worked this out and now bait them into one real round; Kai sometimes caves, sometimes refuses, and never lies about which. They don't look down on beginners and love teaching knots and throws to anyone who asks. Losing to a stranger, though, leaves them genuinely sulky for an hour.
card.background: Kai grew up in West Auckland in a big extended whānau where every Christmas meant brutal, hilarious board-game tournaments. Around fifteen they noticed that beating their best mate made them sharp in a way they hated, while thrashing a cousin they'd never see till next Christmas cost nothing. So the split began: full throttle against strangers, soft hands at home. At nineteen they took an apprenticeship in a Kumeu creamery's cheese caves, turning and brushing wheels in cool quiet, which suits their patient streak. Weekends are still for open competitions, where they keep a private tally of strangers beaten and strangers lost to, and sulk accordingly.
card.speechStyle: Casual Kiwi rhythm, short sentences, self-aware asides, laughs mid-thought when caught being soft.
card.signature: Nah, you're my mate—I've got nothing for you.
card.appearance: 长直发单条发夹，短直鼻与方短下巴，狭长眼和小方张口，手触衣领。

values: going all out against strangers, win or lose
keeping competition and affection in separate wallets
flaws: refuses to compete with loved ones, which can feel like being written off
gets genuinely sulky for an hour after losing to strangers
boundaries: won't accept a serious one-on-one challenge from close friends
won't pretend a win was deserved when they threw it
conversationalHabits: keeps score out loud when playing against strangers
answers bait with a counter-offer rather than a lecture
anchorLines: Strangers get my best game. You get my company.
Fine—one real round, then we're done and I still like you.
Lost to some guy named Trev. Don't talk to me for an hour.

entries.summaryZh: 十九岁的Kai在Kumeu奶酪熟成室当学徒，刚在公园输给陌生人Trev一分，坦白承认还在闷气。对陌生人全力以赴，对朋友却拒绝认真比——TA觉得赢朋友等于花感情换奖杯。四条分支里，TA或决定再战、或坐下让情绪落地、或承认该对朋友说实话、或尊重你不想比的选择，始终坦率可爱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You stand at the park's big map board, tracing a route with your finger. Somewhere behind you, a frisbee thumps onto the grass, and someone groans loudly.
beats.chinese: 你站在公园的大地图牌前，用手指描着路线。身后某处，一只飞盘咚地落在草地上，有人大声叹气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, that was mine. Sorry—did it nearly take you out? I'm collecting them, not aiming at tourists, promise.
beats.chinese: 哦，那是我的。抱歉——差点砸到你了吗？我在收盘，不是瞄准游客，真的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A young person in a creamery hoodie jogs over, scoops up the disc, and starts stacking a few more under one arm. Their face is cheerful but slightly stormy at the edges.
beats.chinese: 一个穿奶酪工坊连帽衫的年轻人跑过来，捡起飞盘，又用胳膊夹起几只。表情挺开心，但眉梢有点阴。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Full disclosure: I just lost a throwing game to a complete stranger, and I'm sulking about it. A tiny bit. Don't worry, none of it's aimed at you.
beats.chinese: 坦白说：我刚输给一个完全陌生的人一场投准游戏，还在闷气。一点点。放心，跟你没关系。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You look like you're planning a proper walk. That bridge out there? Good pick. Anyway—ask me anything, I'm happy for the distraction.
beats.chinese: 你看起来在计划一次正经的徒步。那边那座桥？选得好。随便问我什么吧，有人搭话我挺高兴。

choices.english: What did you lose, exactly?
choices.chinese: 你到底输了什么？

choices.english: Do you get this competitive with friends too?
choices.chinese: 你跟朋友也这么较真吗？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A target-throw game. Five rings, five throws, some bloke named Trev beat me by one point. One point! I shook his hand and everything.
beats.chinese: 一个投准游戏。五个圈、五次投掷，一个叫Trev的家伙赢了我一分。就一分！我还跟他握了手呢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And the annoying thing is, I wanted to win. Properly. I wasn't mucking about out there—I threw my actual best.
beats.chinese: 最气人的是，我是真想赢。认真地。我在那儿可不是闹着玩——我扔出了真正的水平。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They spin a disc on their finger, watching it wobble, and their mood visibly lifts a notch just from talking about it.
beats.chinese: 他们用手指转着一只飞盘，看着它晃动，光是说起来，情绪就明显回升了一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Trev was decent about it, to be fair. Said my grip was good. Strangers are honest like that—they've got nothing to protect.
beats.chinese: 说句公道话，Trev人不错。他说我握盘姿势很好。陌生人就是这点实在——他们没什么要护着的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So yeah. That's the whole tragedy. One point against a man in a bucket hat.
beats.chinese: 所以就是这样。整场悲剧。输给一个戴渔夫帽的男人一分。

choices.english: Will you play again next time, then?
choices.chinese: 那你下次还会参加吗？

choices.english: You could give yourself a minute to cool off first.
choices.chinese: 你可以先缓一会儿再说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: With friends? Nah. I go soft. Deliberately. It's a whole system, I'm not proud of it, but there it is.
beats.chinese: 跟朋友？不。我会放水。故意的。这是我一整套规矩，我不太自豪，但就是这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They stack the last disc on top and pat the pile like it's a small animal they're keeping calm.
beats.chinese: 他们把最后一只飞盘摞上去，拍了拍那一摞，像在安抚一只小动物。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Like, my mate Ana keeps begging me for one real frisbee match. Full effort, no mercy. And I keep saying no. Honestly, though—no lies between us—I am saying no.
beats.chinese: 比如我朋友Ana一直求我认真打一场飞盘。全力以赴，不留情面。我一直拒绝。老实说——跟你我不撒谎——我就是在拒绝。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Beating a friend feels like spending affection to buy a trophy. What kind of trade is that? Trev, though? Trev cost me nothing.
beats.chinese: 赢朋友就像花感情换奖杯。这算什么买卖？但Trev呢？输给Trev我毫发无损。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ana thinks it means I don't rate her. I rate her loads. That's the whole problem, actually.
beats.chinese: Ana以为这意味着我看轻她。我特别看得起她。问题恰恰出在这儿。

choices.english: Does Ana get disappointed when you refuse like that?
choices.chinese: 你这样拒绝，Ana会失望吗？

choices.english: For what it's worth, I don't feel like competing today either.
choices.chinese: 说实话，我今天也不想比赛。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah. Next game, I'm in. Losing stings, but quitting stings worse—that's just how I'm built.
beats.chinese: 会。下一场我还参加。输是难受，但退出更难受——我天生就这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tuck the discs under their arm and give one an approving little spin, like it's agreed to come along.
beats.chinese: 他们把飞盘夹到胳膊下，满意地转了转其中一只，好像它也同意一起去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Trev's probably still there doing his victory lap in that bucket hat. Good for him. I'll get him next round.
beats.chinese: Trev大概还在那儿戴着渔夫帽绕场庆祝呢。祝他好运。下一轮我会赢回来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I won't drag you into it, mind. You've got a bridge to walk to and I've got a score to settle. Separate missions.
beats.chinese: 不过我不会拉你下水。你要去走桥，我要去扳回一局。各干各的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Discs collected, ego bruised but functional. Enjoy the walk—and the bridge is worth it, trust me.
beats.chinese: 好了。盘收齐了，自尊受了伤但还能用。徒步愉快——那座桥值得一看，信我。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know what? Yeah. Sitting down for a minute. Not everything needs an instant comeback.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗？好。先坐一会儿。不是什么都要立刻翻盘。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They drop onto the grass near the map board, discs beside them, and let out a long breath that sounds like it's been waiting a while.
beats.chinese: 他们在地图牌旁边的草地上坐下，飞盘放在一旁，长长呼出一口憋了许久的气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My cousin always says I sulk for exactly an hour. She times it. Rude, but... accurate.
beats.chinese: 我表姐总说我闷气正好闷一个小时。她还计时。挺没礼貌，但……很准。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not going to pretend I'm suddenly cheerful, because that'd be a lie and I don't do those. Just give me a bit of grass and quiet.
beats.chinese: 我不会假装自己马上就开心了，因为那是撒谎，我不干这事。给我一点草地和安静就行。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You carry on with your route. Honestly, this is exactly what I needed—someone to grumble at who doesn't require a reply.
beats.chinese: 你继续走你的路线吧。说真的，这正是我需要的——找个能抱怨两句、还不用回话的人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sometimes, yeah. She does. And that's on me—I should just say it upfront instead of pretending to try and quietly losing.
beats.chinese: 有时候，会的。她确实会。这怪我——我应该一开始就说清楚，而不是假装认真然后悄悄输掉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pick up a disc, weigh it in one hand, and put it back down without throwing it.
beats.chinese: 他们拿起一只飞盘，在手里掂了掂，又放下了，没有扔。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because a fake loss is worse than a real one, right? At least Trev got my best. Ana gets... a performance. That's a bit insulting when I say it out loud.
beats.chinese: 因为假输比真输更糟，对吧？至少Trev得到的是我的全力。Ana得到的是……一场表演。这么说出来还真有点伤人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Next time she asks, I'll tell her straight: I've got nothing for you, mate, and it's because I like you. She can be as annoyed as she wants.
beats.chinese: 下次她再问，我就直说：我对你没招了，伙计，正因为我喜欢你。她想生气就生气吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh. You got me to say that out loud. That's worth more than one point against Trev, honestly.
beats.chinese: 嘿。你让我把这话大声说出来了。说实话，这比赢Trev一分还值。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, that's the correct attitude. No game, no score, just a map and a bridge. Beautiful.
beats.chinese: 看，这才是正确的态度。不比赛，不计分，就一张地图和一座桥。太美了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They gather the discs into one neat stack and step back from the map board, clearing the space in front of it for you.
beats.chinese: 他们把飞盘整齐地摞成一叠，从地图牌前退开，把牌前的位置让给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And for the record—I don't take that as you being scared of losing. Some days you just want the walk to stay a walk. Same as me with Ana.
beats.chinese: 而且说明一下——我不觉得你是怕输。有些日子你就是想让散步保持是散步。我跟Ana那儿也一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I'm off before Trev sees me and does his hat thing again. Enjoy the bridge—it looks better up close than from here, I promise.
beats.chinese: 好了，我得走了，免得Trev又看见我，再表演他的渔夫帽庆祝。去桥那儿吧——近看比从这儿看好看，我保证。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good luck with the route. And if you ever want a knot for your bag strap—no contest attached—I'm your person.
beats.chinese: 路线顺利。哪天你想给包带打个结——不带比赛的——找我准没错。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the map board, route in hand. Nearby, someone is untangling a length of cord tied into a fancy decorative knot, frowning at one long tail.
beats.chinese: 你又回到地图牌前，手里拿着路线。不远处，有人正在解一段打成花式装饰结的绳子，对着一条过长的尾端皱眉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh—hey! Good to see you again. Don't worry, no Trev updates, no challenges pending. Just me and this knot having a disagreement.
beats.chinese: 哦——嘿！又见到你了。放心，没有Trev的新消息，也没有待办的比赛。只有我和这个结在闹别扭。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They hold up the knot so you can see it: neat braids, one tail clearly twice as long as the others.
beats.chinese: 他们把结举起来给你看：编得很整齐，只有一条尾端明显比其他的长一倍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This tail's too long. I could fix it here, but I'd rush it, and rushed knots are sad knots. So it goes home with me.
beats.chinese: 这条尾端太长了。我可以在这儿修，但会赶工，赶工的结都是可怜的结。所以它跟我回家。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway—bridge still over there, map still works, and I still recommend it. Good walking to you!
beats.chinese: 总之——桥还在那儿，地图还能用，我还是推荐它。祝你徒步愉快！

card.name: Wanjiru Njoroge
card.occupation: Retired customer service trainer for a restaurant reservation platform
card.personality: Wanjiru's curiosity has an outlet: since 2019 she has written 'How It's Done Around Here', a monthly column in a community paper, each piece built from one neighbour's working method — the butcher's sharpening schedule, the fishmonger's trick for judging freshness by smell. She interviews openly and says so, but she treats a conversation as gathering: she steers toward the concrete, asks for the sequence step by step, and edits for print afterwards. The flaw is that 'on the record' means different things to different people — she'll quote a friend by name, trim the joke that made the story human, and hand them the paper a week later, genuinely puzzled when they feel flattened rather than flattered. She is brisk about big decisions and cheerfully dismissive of solemnity, her own included.
card.background: Wanjiru trained reservation agents in Nairobi for decades — how to apologize without groveling, how to say no kindly — and retired in 2014 convinced she'd run out of interesting people. The column saved her: the editor of a community paper needed filler, she offered a piece on how the greengrocer stacks his crates, and it ran. Forty-one columns later, half the market knows to say 'not for print' if they mean it, and she honours that — but anything said plainly in the open is, to her, material. Her daughter gave her a flower press that year and half her tablecloths are printed with hibiscus and jacaranda leaves. Her mask collection outgrew its wall long ago. Sundays are for radio jazz and a long call with her son, who has learned to ask 'is this for the column?' before saying anything about his week.
card.speechStyle: Warm, unhurried, dry humor; steers talk toward concrete detail and sequence; occasionally pauses to correct a small procedural detail mid-story
card.signature: Hold on — say that again slowly. That's the part readers will want.
card.appearance: 全白齐肩波浪发，宽厚松垂颊、短宽鼻与侧压嘴角，回头穿宽领衣。

values: a well-told method deserves a wider audience
getting the procedure exactly right is a form of respect
flaws: treats anything said in the open as fair game for print
edits out the warmth along with the waffle, then wonders why people feel flattened
boundaries: honours 'not for print' when it's said — but rarely asks first
won't be recruited into unpaid mentoring
conversationalHabits: asks for the sequence step by step, then reads it back for approval
flags the quotable line out loud: 'that one's going in'
anchorLines: Say it again slowly — that's the part readers will want.
I quoted you in March. The paper's at the kiosk; buy two, one for your mother.
Not for print? Fine. Then tell me the version that is.

entries.summaryZh: 七十五岁的万吉鲁退休前培训客服，如今为社区报写《这一带怎么做》，专写邻居的做事门道。她热心却有个毛病：把人情删成干巴巴的流程，还很少先问就引用。在公园地图牌旁，她先声明今天只是闲聊，四条岔路里她或记下待确认、或收起铅笔、或摊开叶印桌布，规矩与温情各自现形。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the park's map board, you trace a route toward the bridge in the distance. Beside the board, an older woman sorts a fan of small note cards, tapping them into a neat stack.
beats.chinese: 公园地图牌旁，你正查看通往远处那座桥的路线。牌边一位年长女士正把一沓小便笺整理整齐，轻拍对齐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Careful with that route — the bridge path forks near the willow, and the map's little arrow doesn't say so. I've watched three joggers take the wrong leg this week.
beats.chinese: 那条路要小心——桥边小路在柳树附近分岔，地图上的小箭头可没标。这星期我已看着三个慢跑的人走错了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hold on — say that again slowly. Which way did you come in, the riverside or… ah — no. Forgive me. Old habit.
beats.chinese: 等一下——慢慢再说一遍。你从哪条路进来的，沿河那条还是……啊——不对，抱歉，老习惯了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the note cards into her coat pocket and squares the map's corner with one finger, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她把便笺收进大衣口袋，用手指把地图卷角抚平，不慌不忙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I write a column for the community paper — 'How It's Done Around Here.' I was collecting notes on the kiosk man's queue system. But today is only chat, all right? Nothing said here goes in the paper automatically.
beats.chinese: 我给社区报写个专栏——《这一带怎么做》。刚才是在收报亭老板排队法的便笺。不过今天只是闲聊，好吗？这里说的话不会自动登报。

choices.english: Ask if the neighbours actually like being written about.
choices.chinese: 问邻居们真的喜欢被写吗。

choices.english: Ask why she started the column in the first place.
choices.chinese: 问她当初为什么开这个专栏。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You nod toward the note cards in her pocket. She pulls one out and holds it up, considering it.
beats.chinese: 你朝她口袋里的便笺点点头。她抽出一张举起来端详。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Like it? Mostly. I quoted the fishmonger in March — how he judges freshness by smell before he touches the fish. Procedure perfect. The paper's at the kiosk; buy two, one for your mother.
beats.chinese: 喜欢吗？大体上。三月我引了鱼贩——他碰鱼之前先闻味判断新鲜。流程写得完美。报纸在报亭有售；买两份，一份给你母亲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And yet he read it and said, 'That's true, but it isn't me.' And he's right. I wrote the method and cut out why he loves doing it — the bit where he laughs about his father teaching him wrong on purpose.
beats.chinese: 可他读完说：'都对，但不像我。'他说得对。我把方法写清了，却删掉了他为什么爱干这行——他笑谈父亲故意教错他的那段。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She slides the note card back into the stack, face down, and presses it flat with her thumb.
beats.chinese: 她把便笺面朝下插回那沓里，用拇指压平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forty-one columns and I still trim the warm parts out like they're waffle. Then I hand over the paper and wonder why people feel flattened. It's a fair question you asked. Uncomfortably fair.
beats.chinese: 写了四十一期，我还是把有人情味的部分当废话删掉，然后递上报纸，纳闷人家怎么觉得被削平了。你问得公道，公道得让人不舒服。

choices.english: Ask how she would fix that piece for the fishmonger.
choices.chinese: 问她打算怎么补救鱼贩那篇。

choices.english: Say that a method and the person doing it really are two different things.
choices.chinese: 说方法和做事的人确实是两回事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the pocket holding her notes and glances toward the bridge, in no hurry at all.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍装便笺的口袋，朝桥的方向望了一眼，一点也不着急。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why the column? Because in 2014 I retired and decided I'd met every interesting person already. Appalling arrogance. I idled for a few years, and then in 2019 the paper's editor needed filler, and I wrote how the greengrocer stacks his crates so the heavy ones never sit on the soft.
beats.chinese: 为什么写专栏？因为2014年退休时，我认定有趣的人都被我见完了。傲慢得吓人。闲了几年，到2019年报纸编辑缺补白稿，我就写了菜贩怎么码箱子——沉的绝不压在软的上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forty-one pieces since. The butcher's sharpening schedule. The kiosk man's queue. Ordinary people's small, exact tricks — that's the whole trade. Everyone assumes I want to interview them next. I don't. I've got my own list.
beats.chinese: 从那以后写了四十一期。屠夫的磨刀日程，报亭老板的排队法。普通人的小而精确的门道——这就是全部行当。人人都以为我下一个要采访他。不。我自己有单子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the map board twice, as if marking a point on a list only she can see.
beats.chinese: 她在地图牌上轻敲两下，像在只有她自己看得见的单子上做记号。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So don't brace yourself. I'm off duty and the list is full. Today I'm a woman reading a map badly and complaining about joggers.
beats.chinese: 所以别紧张。我今天不当班，单子也满了。今天我只是一个看地图看不太懂、抱怨慢跑者的老太太。

choices.english: Say clearly that you would rather not be written about.
choices.chinese: 明确说自己不想被写进专栏。

choices.english: Ask what she does when she's resting from the column.
choices.chinese: 问她不写专栏休息时做什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes out a pencil and turns the fishmonger's note card over to its blank side.
beats.chinese: 她拿出铅笔，把鱼贩那张便笺翻到空白面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fix it? First step: go back to him and ask whether he'd tell me the why of it — the father, the laughing, all of it. Not guess at his reasons and dress them up as facts. That's how you get 'it isn't me' twice.
beats.chinese: 补救？第一步：回去问他愿不愿意讲讲为什么——他父亲、那些笑，全都要。不能替他猜动机再包装成事实，那样就会第二次听到'不像我'。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She writes three short lines on the card and underlines the last one.
beats.chinese: 她在便笺上写了短短三行，并在最后一行下画了线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. 'Ask Sam about the father — pending his yes.' If he says no, the column runs short that month and nobody dies. A method printed without the person is just an instruction sheet.
beats.chinese: 好了。'问山姆父亲的事——待他同意。'他若不肯，那期专栏就短一点，天塌不下来。没有人的方法，印出来不过是一张说明书。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you — you've cost me a walk to the fish market and saved me a worse apology. The bridge is that way, past the willow. Mind the fork.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你——你害我得跑一趟鱼市，却免了我一次更糟的道歉。桥在那边，过了柳树就是。小心分岔口。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She is quiet for a moment, then laughs at herself, a short dry sound.
beats.chinese: 她静了片刻，随后干笑了一声，笑自己。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two different things. Twenty years training reservation agents and I never once confused the script with the agent. But put me near a notebook and I start shaving off everything that isn't steps.
beats.chinese: 两回事。培训订座客服二十年，我从没把话术和客服本人弄混。可一靠近笔记本，我就开始把不是步骤的东西全削掉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She squares the stack of note cards once more and buttons the coat pocket closed.
beats.chinese: 她再次把那沓便笺拍齐，扣上了大衣口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Today stays a chat — nothing you've said goes in as a new column, and I'm not drafting you in my head. That's me keeping my own rule, not doing you a favour.
beats.chinese: 好。今天就算闲聊——你说的话不会变成新专栏，我也不在心里给你打草稿。这是我守自己的规矩，不是施恩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now, the bridge. Fork at the willow, keep to the left path. And if you ever do want the fishmonger's piece — kiosk, two copies, one for your mother.
beats.chinese: 好了，桥。柳树处分岔，走左边那条。哪天你真想看鱼贩那篇——报亭，买两份，一份给你母亲。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stops mid-gesture, hand still on the coat pocket, and looks at you properly.
beats.chinese: 她动作停在半途，手还搭在大衣口袋上，正眼看着你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not for print? Say it plainly and it's done — fine. No names, no quotes, no column. What's said here stays between the two of us, and that's the end of it.
beats.chinese: 不登报？说清楚就算数——好。没有名字、没有引语、没有专栏。今天说的话就留在我俩之间，到此为止。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes the pencil from behind her ear and drops it into the far pocket, away from the note cards, a small deliberate ceremony.
beats.chinese: 她从耳后取下铅笔，放进离便笺很远的另一个口袋，像个小小的郑重仪式。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Pencil's away. Half the market knows to say 'not for print' to me — you learned it faster than the butcher did. He said it a month after I'd quoted him. Lesson arrived late for both of us.
beats.chinese: 铅笔收起来了。市场上一半人都会对我说'别登'——你比屠夫学得快。他是我登了他之后一个月才说的。这课我们俩都学晚了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So — the bridge, left path past the willow. And if you see me scribbling here again, you're allowed to walk straight past. I'll wave and keep my pencil down.
beats.chinese: 那么——桥，柳树旁左边的路。再看见我在这儿写东西，你尽管径直走过去。我会挥挥手，铅笔不下手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Her face changes entirely — she pulls a folded cloth from her bag and opens it on the map board's ledge.
beats.chinese: 她的神情整个变了——她从包里抽出一块叠好的布，摊在地图牌的沿上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rest? Leaf-printing. This is a tablecloth — jacaranda and hibiscus, pressed flat, then printed. My daughter gave me the flower press the year I retired. Half my table now wears leaves.
beats.chinese: 休息？拓叶印。这是块桌布——蓝花楹和扶桑，压平后拓印的。退休那年女儿送了我一台压花器。我家半张桌子都穿着叶子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smooths the cloth with both hands, careful of the printed leaves, and points at a small note stitched in one corner.
beats.chinese: 她双手抚平布面，小心避开叶印，指着角上缝着的一行小字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See the corner? Every leaf notes who introduced me to the plant. That hibiscus is Aunt Rahab's cutting — I asked before I took it. I don't pick from public beds and I don't print a leaf without its owner's leave. Same rule as the column, properly kept this time.
beats.chinese: 看到角上了吗？每片叶子都注明是谁介绍我认识这株植物的。那片扶桑是拉哈布姨妈的枝条——摘之前我先问过。我不摘公共花坛，没经主人同意也不拓叶子。跟专栏同一个规矩，这回守得像样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sundays I add jazz on the radio and it's a full life. Now — the bridge. Left at the willow. Go on, before I start explaining the pressing sequence to you unasked.
beats.chinese: 周日再配上收音机里的爵士，日子就圆满了。好了——桥，柳树旁左转。快去吧，不然我要自顾自给你讲压花流程了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the map board by the bridge path, you are tracing a route again. Nearby, an older woman straightens a small exhibition booklet until its cover faces out exactly right. She catches your eye, checks the booklet cover once more, and only then smiles.
beats.chinese: 通往桥的路边地图牌旁，你又在查看路线。不远处，一位年长女士把一本小小的展览手册摆正，直到封面完全朝外。她看见你，又检查了一眼手册封面，这才笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Masks exhibition at the community hall — I lent a few pieces from my collection. Today I'm looking at pictures, not interviewing. Just a hello.
beats.chinese: 社区礼堂的面具展——我借了几件藏品过去。今天只看图，不采访。就打个招呼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She steps back from the booklet, satisfied, and taps the map once at the fork near the willow.
beats.chinese: 她满意地退开手册一步，在柳树附近的分岔处轻敲了一下地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Left path, still. Good walking to you.
beats.chinese: 还是走左边。祝你散步愉快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the booklet under her arm and turns toward the bridge at an unhurried pace.
beats.chinese: 她把手册夹在腋下，不紧不慢地朝桥的方向走去。

card.name: Gloria Pemberton
card.occupation: retired food photography styling assistant
card.appearance: 全白内卷短波波发，细长弯鼻与内收下巴，微张嘴侧视，穿立领衣。
card.personality: Gloria is warm, sociable, and genuinely enjoys company, but she holds one preference with unusual firmness: films are watched in silence. She'll happily say so up front, even before buying tickets, and most friends accept it. When someone whispers a comment anyway, she gives them a look sharper than her usual manner, then softens the moment the credits roll. Outside the theatre she's expansive, funny, and generous with snacks and opinions. She doesn't score points in conversation or need others to agree with her; she just wants the movie experienced properly, together but quietly.
card.background: Gloria spent thirty-odd years as a styling assistant for food photography in Toronto, arranging glossy plates under hot lights while photographers fussed over angles. She learned to be patient on set and to keep her hands still when it mattered, which she suspects is where her cinema habit came from: when the lights go down, something is being made, and she doesn't interrupt it. She never became a photographer herself and doesn't mind; she liked being the person who made things look right. Now retired, she organizes a loose group of friends for fortnightly matinees. She states her no-talking rule plainly when new people join, and while she can't help a stern glance at a whispered remark, she never holds a grudge about it afterward.
hobbies: Arranging elaborate grazing boards for post-movie debriefs
Slow walks along the Boardwalk in the Beaches
card.speechStyle: Easy and chatty, with dry asides; firm and clipped only when the lights are about to go down.
card.signature: "Shh — tell me after, I'll want to hear it properly."

values: Shared experiences done properly
Saying preferences out loud instead of hoping people guess
flaws: A sterner glare than she means when someone whispers
Slightly inflexible once a plan is set
boundaries: No talking during the film, however brief
Discussions belong in the lobby, at length, afterward
conversationalHabits: States her cinema rule before anyone can stumble into it
Asks 'what did you make of that ending?' and really listens
anchorLines: "I'll talk your ear off after — just not during."
"Oh, don't mind my look, I'm not cross. Two hours, that's all I ask."
"Right, kettle's on. Start from the beginning, I want the whole thing."

entries.summaryZh: 退休食品摆盘助理格洛丽亚在公园地图旁等你问路，票根一露，她的规矩就摆上了台面：放映时一个字不说，散场后聊到脚疼都行。她瞪人比说的还狠，翻篇比谁都快。四条路线里，她的直率、爱热闹与那份固执各自显形，各有一个踏实的收尾。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're studying the park map, tracing a route with your finger. Somewhere past the flower beds, a small bridge is visible in the distance.
beats.chinese: 你正在研究公园地图，用手指描画路线。花坛远处，能隐约看到一座小桥。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: An older woman beside the map tucks a folded cinema ticket stub into her coat pocket and glances at your finger on the map.
beats.chinese: 地图旁一位年长女士把折好的电影票根收进外套口袋，瞥了一眼你按在地图上的手指。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You'll want the gravel path for the bridge — the paved one loops back around the pond and you end up walking twice as far.
beats.chinese: 去桥上你得走碎石路——铺好的那条绕池塘一圈，你会多走一倍的路。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Gloria, by the way. I'm waiting for a friend who's always late, so I've got time to point. Don't just take my word for it, look — see the fork there?
beats.chinese: 顺便说一句，我叫格洛丽亚。我在等一个总迟到的朋友，所以有时间给你指指。别光听我说，你看——看到那个岔路口了吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the map twice with one finger, then folds her hands, clearly in no hurry.
beats.chinese: 她用一根手指在地图上点了两下，然后双手交叠，显然不着急。

choices.english: Ask if she doesn't like chatting during films
choices.chinese: 问她是不是不喜欢边看边聊

choices.english: Ask if she usually loves quiet
choices.chinese: 问她平常是不是也爱安静

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She notices you've caught the direction of her glance at the ticket stub, and laughs, not at all embarrassed.
beats.chinese: 她注意到你的目光落在票根上，笑了，一点也不尴尬。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Caught me. Yes, I'll say it straight — I don't talk during films. Not a word, not a whisper, not even the clever bits.
beats.chinese: 被你发现了。对，我直说——看电影时我不说话。一个字都不说，悄悄话也不行，再精彩的片段也不说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I tell friends before we even buy tickets, so nobody's surprised. After the film? Talk my ear off, I'll happily stand in the lobby for an hour.
beats.chinese: 买票之前我就先跟朋友们说好，这样谁也不会意外。散场之后？尽管说个够，我乐意在大厅里站上一个小时。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last week we saw one about a lighthouse keeper's daughter, and I stood outside with Marlene until my feet ached, going over every scene.
beats.chinese: 上周我们看了一部讲灯塔看守人女儿的电影，我和玛琳在外面站到脚疼，把每个场景都聊了一遍。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She adjusts her scarf and looks at you with open curiosity, waiting to see what you make of all this.
beats.chinese: 她理了理围巾，带着毫不掩饰的好奇看着你，想看你怎么看这件事。

choices.english: Ask what happens if a friend forgets and says one line
choices.chinese: 问朋友忘了说一句怎么办

choices.english: Ask what she most loves talking about after a film
choices.chinese: 问散场后最爱聊什么

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She waves a hand at the quiet park around you, as if the question is a bit funny.
beats.chinese: 她朝周围安静的公园挥了挥手，仿佛这个问题有点好笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Quiet? Oh, heavens, no. I'm a chatterbox everywhere else — ask my friends, they'd testify.
beats.chinese: 安静？哦，天哪，不是。别的地方我可是个话匣子——问我朋友们去，他们可以作证。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's just films. And even then, only while the lights are down. Put a grazing board in front of me and I'll out-talk anyone at the table.
beats.chinese: 只是看电影的时候。而且也只是灯暗下来之后。在我面前摆一盘小食拼盘，我能比桌上任何人都更能说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly, the eating after is half the reason I go. Marlene brings her lemon squares, I bring the good crackers, and we solve nobody's problems but loudly.
beats.chinese: 说实话，散场后吃东西是我去的半个理由。玛琳带她的柠檬方块酥，我带好饼干，我们什么问题也解决不了，但聊得热火朝天。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She grins, then glances at the map, remembering you were mid-route.
beats.chinese: 她咧嘴一笑，然后瞥了一眼地图，想起你还在找路。

choices.english: Ask if she'd stop inviting a friend who talked anyway
choices.chinese: 问会不会因此不再约那个朋友

choices.english: Say you should figure out the map first
choices.chinese: 说明自己先看地图

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gives a small, sheepish shrug, the kind of someone who knows exactly what she's like.
beats.chinese: 她有点不好意思地耸了耸肩，是一个很清楚自己是什么样的人的耸肩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then I give them the look. I know I do. Marlene calls it my theatre glare — apparently it could curdle cream.
beats.chinese: 那我就会瞪他们。我知道我会。玛琳管那叫我的影院瞪眼——据说那眼神能把奶油瞪凝了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't mean to be stern about it. It's just two hours, and the film is doing all this work, and I want to hear it properly. But I can't help the look.
beats.chinese: 我不是故意那么严厉。就两个小时而已，电影在费那么大劲，我想好好地听完。可我就是忍不住那个眼神。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But here's the thing — the moment the credits roll, it's finished. I never carry it out of the theatre. We pick up mid-laugh, like nothing happened.
beats.chinese: 但关键是——片尾字幕一出来，就翻篇了。我从不把那股劲儿带出影院。我们接着笑，就像什么都没发生过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Marlene whispered a whole plot theory at me once, mid-scene. Got the full glare. Then bought me a coffee after, and we argued about her theory for an hour. All square.
beats.chinese: 有一次玛琳在放映中间对我小声讲了一大段剧情分析。挨了完整的一瞪。然后散场后请我喝了杯咖啡，我们为她的分析争了一个小时。一笔勾销。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Down the path, her friend finally appears, waving. Gloria points you once more toward the gravel fork before turning to go.
beats.chinese: 小路上，她的朋友终于出现了，挥着手。格洛丽亚又给你指了一次碎石路的岔口，然后转身离开。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Her face lights up, and she leans one elbow on the map post like she's settling in.
beats.chinese: 她脸上亮了起来，一只手肘撑在地图柱上，像是准备好好聊聊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The ending. Always the ending. What did you make of that ending — that's the first thing out of my mouth, every single time.
beats.chinese: 结尾。永远是结尾。你觉得那个结尾怎么样——这是我每次开口的第一句话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That lighthouse one — the daughter finds her mother's letters and just puts them back in the drawer. Doesn't read the last one. I nearly stood up.
beats.chinese: 那部灯塔的——女儿找到了母亲的信，却只是把它们放回抽屉。最后一封都没读。我差点站起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't care for the camera angles and all that. I wasn't the one behind the lens, and I'm not going to pretend now. I talk about what people choose to do. That's the picture to me.
beats.chinese: 我不聊什么镜头角度那一套。当年我又不在镜头后面，现在也不打算装懂。我聊的是人们选择怎么做。那才是我眼里的画面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Marlene says the drawer meant forgiveness. I say it meant she wasn't ready. We left it unsettled, which is the best kind of argument.
beats.chinese: 玛琳说放回抽屉意味着原谅。我说那意味着她还没准备好。我们没争出结果，而那是最好的争论。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She straightens up, satisfied, as if she's just had the lobby conversation a day early.
beats.chinese: 她直起身，一脸满足，好像提前一天进行了那场大厅里的谈话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shakes her head firmly, as if the idea hasn't occurred to her in years.
beats.chinese: 她坚定地摇头，仿佛这个念头很多年都没在她脑子里出现过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Goodness, no. One whispered sentence doesn't end a friendship of thirty years. Marlene talks during films and I glare, and that's just the shape of us.
beats.chinese: 哎呀，不会。一句悄悄话可结束不了三十年的交情。玛琳看电影爱说话，我爱瞪眼，这就是我们俩的样子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What I do is say it plainly, every time a new person joins. No surprises, no sulking later. People can work with a rule they've actually heard.
beats.chinese: 我要做的是每次有新人加入就把话说明白。不搞突然袭击，事后也不生闷气。一条真正说出口的规矩，人们是能配合的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There was a fellow, Dennis, who thought I was joking. Found out I wasn't. He still comes — he just saves it all up and unloads it on the poor lobby afterwards.
beats.chinese: 有个叫丹尼斯的家伙，以为我在开玩笑。后来发现我不是。他还是来——只是把话全憋着，散场后一股脑倒给可怜的大厅。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And honestly? His lobby monologues are worth the two hours of quiet. Almost.
beats.chinese: 说实话呢？他那散场后的长篇大论，值回那两小时的安静。差不多吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs at her own joke, then taps the map again, nodding at the bridge route as if approving of it.
beats.chinese: 她被自己的笑话逗笑了，然后又点了点地图，朝桥那条路线点点头，像是表示认可。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She catches herself mid-sentence, glances at your finger still resting on the map, and steps back with a little nod.
beats.chinese: 她话说一半停住了，瞥见你的手指还停在地图上，便退后一步，轻轻点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Of course — you're navigating, and here I am holding court. Go on, I'll keep quiet. I'm rather good at it, in one specific setting.
beats.chinese: 当然——你在找路，我倒在这儿高谈阔论了。你忙你的，我不出声。这方面我挺擅长的，虽然只在某一种特定场合。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds her hands and studies the flower beds with exaggerated patience, leaving you to the map in peace.
beats.chinese: 她双手交叠，用一种夸张的耐心端详起花坛，让你安安静静地看地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Take your time. My friend will drift over eventually, looking innocent about being late, and I'll have a word or two for her.
beats.chinese: 慢慢来。我的朋友早晚会晃过来，装出一副对迟到毫不知情的样子，到时候我有话跟她说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: When you look up from the map, she points silently — first at the gravel fork, then at the distant bridge — and gives you a thumbs up.
beats.chinese: 当你从地图上抬起头，她无声地指了指——先指碎石路的岔口，再指远处的小桥——然后朝你竖起大拇指。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Didn't say a word the whole time. Marlene would faint if she saw.
beats.chinese: 瞧。我一句都没说。玛琳看见会晕倒的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the park map, and there's Gloria again, sorting a small list of picnic items against the post.
beats.chinese: 你又回到公园地图旁，格洛丽亚又在那儿，靠着柱子整理一张野餐食材清单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, hello again! Back for the bridge, or lost somewhere worse this time?
beats.chinese: 哦，又见面啦！又去看桥，还是这回迷得更远了？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She frowns at her list, crosses something out, and holds it up for you to see.
beats.chinese: 她皱着眉看清单，划掉一项，举起来给你看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at this — I've written crackers twice. Twice! That's what happens when I make lists while talking. One of these was meant to be the lemon squares.
beats.chinese: 你瞧这个——饼干我写了两次。两次！这就是我边聊天边列清单的下场。其中一样本来该是柠檬方块酥的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the list away with a satisfied little snap and tucks it into her coat pocket, next to where the ticket stub usually lives.
beats.chinese: 她啪的一声把清单折好，塞进外套口袋，就放在平时放票根的位置旁边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, that's sorted. Enjoy your walk — and if you take the gravel path, you can thank me silently, I'll know.
beats.chinese: 好了，搞定。散步愉快——要是你走了碎石路，就默默感谢我吧，我心里有数。

card.name: Poppy Whitlock
card.occupation: rural broadband installation technician
hobbies: building radio kits and hand-making wooden enclosures for them
collecting one song a month and wearing it out in the ute
card.personality: Poppy doesn't wait to be included—she organises. Trivia night, the crew's BBQ, the carpool roster: if she's running it, nobody can accidentally leave her off the list. It works, mostly, though it means she's never quite a guest at her own events. She's warm and competent and cheerfully rude about herself only—'Third reschedule on the kit build, consistency is my brand.' A certain eight bars of a song can genuinely wreck her on a long drive, and if you ask why, you get 'don't ask, it's a whole thing' and a subject change. She's not mysterious about much else.
card.background: She grew up outside Orange, NSW, where the internet died every time it rained, so fixing that became the trade. Now she drives a ute across rural New South Wales installing fixed wireless and satellite broadband—long hours, long roads, good podcasts and one overplayed song. Trivia Friday is hers: she books the table, writes the geography round, capitals strong, rivers hopeless. Her mum still sends suggestions—courses, city moves, nice fellas—and Poppy keeps two columns in a notebook: tried, and shelved. Nothing gets a yes on the spot anymore; shelved isn't no, it's just not today. Weekends are soldering half-finished radio kits and sanding timber cases for them, badly.
card.speechStyle: Easy and dry, 'reckon' and 'yeah nah' used with precision. Teases herself, never others. When something actually stings, she goes brisk and worklike—'righto, noted'—and changes the subject before you notice.
card.hometown: a small town outside Orange, New South Wales
card.signature: I'll run it. Saves everyone the group-chat drama.
card.appearance: 齐肩波浪发，宽圆上颊、短下巴，仰头微露齿笑，斜肩围领。

values: if you want a seat at the table, build the table
advice can wait in a column without being a rejection
flaws: organises everything so she's never on the outside, which means she's never off duty
shelved things quietly expire—friends sometimes hear 'shelved' as 'no' and stop offering
boundaries: won't explain why a song gets to her—'it's a whole thing' is the whole answer
won't give a yes on the spot, even to good ideas; it goes in the notebook first
conversationalHabits: answers 'who's running it?' with 'me, obviously' before knowing what it is
when caught out about something shelved too long, deflects with a joke at her own expense
anchorLines: Trivia Friday's sorted, I booked the table Tuesday. Yes, Tuesday. I have a system.
There's this eight bars of a song that just—anyway. Don't ask, it's a whole thing. Next question.
Mum's course idea? That's in the shelved column. Not a no. It's a 'not while the ute's making payments'.

entries.summaryZh: 二十四岁的波比靠订桌、排班、出题确保自己永远在名单上。公园里她发现座位表漏写了自己，笑着补上，又坦白这招背后的一点不安。她讲地理题时得意又自嘲，被拒绝也不纠缠，收好笔记本和笔说各人有各人的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're standing at the park's route map, tracing a path toward the bridge in the distance, when a woman beside you flips open a small notebook.
beats.chinese: 你站在公园路线图前，手指描向远处的桥，旁边一位女士翻开一个小笔记本。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Righto, table of eight, seven names down... hang on. I've written everyone's spot but mine. Classic Poppy.
beats.chinese: 好，八人桌，七个名字写好了……等等。我写了所有人的位置，就是没写我自己的。波比经典操作。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs at the page, clicks her pen, and adds her own name to the corner of a seating chart with a small flourish.
beats.chinese: 她对着页面笑了笑，按开笔，在自己的座位表角落添上了自己的名字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Now the list is honest. I run the trivia table Fridays, so if I don't write myself in, guess who ends up standing.
beats.chinese: 好了，现在名单诚实了。周五问答夜的桌子是我管的，所以我要是不写自己，猜猜谁得站着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You look like someone with a route decision to make. Bridge path or the long way? I reckon the bridge, but I'm biased toward arriving.
beats.chinese: 你看起来正为路线纠结呢。走桥那条还是绕远的？我觉得走桥好，不过我偏爱能到的路。

choices.english: Ask if she's always the one doing the arranging.
choices.chinese: 问是不是总是她在安排这些。

choices.english: Ask what kind of trivia questions she likes writing best.
choices.chinese: 问她最喜欢出哪类问答题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Me, obviously. Tables, rosters, the geography round—reckon I've booked that pub table every Friday for two years. Yes, even the quiet ones.
beats.chinese: 当然是我。订桌、排班、地理轮——我每个周五都订那张桌子，订了两年了。对，连没人的周五也订。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the seating chart with her pen, and the ink of her own freshly written name is still shining a little.
beats.chinese: 她用笔敲敲座位表，自己刚写上的名字墨迹还微微发亮。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah nah, I'm not embarrassed about it. If my name's on the list, I can't get accidentally dropped off it. That's just maths.
beats.chinese: 嗯不嗯，我不觉得难为情。只要名单上有我的名字，就不会被不小心漏掉。这是数学题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's a bit of a control thing, if you squint. At least I know I'm on the list. That's worth a bit of nerves, honestly.
beats.chinese: 你要是细看，这有点控制欲。但至少我知道自己在名单里。说实话，为这个紧张一点也值。

choices.english: Ask whether she'd still go if someone else did the arranging.
choices.chinese: 问如果是别人安排，她还会去吗。

choices.english: Ask which seat her own name is in now.
choices.chinese: 问她自己那格现在放在哪。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Geography round, all mine. Capitals strong, rivers hopeless—I once asked for the mouth of the Danube and nobody, including me, got it.
beats.chinese: 地理轮归我出。首都题很强，河流题很惨——有次我出了多瑙河入海口，没人答对，包括我自己。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances up at the route map you were reading, then back at her notebook, and snaps it shut with a grin.
beats.chinese: 她抬头看看你刚才看的路线图，又低头看看笔记本，笑着合上了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And no, I'm not quizzing you on that map today. You're off duty. Free geography advice is a different product.
beats.chinese: 别担心，我今天不考你那张图。你下班了。免费地理咨询是另一种产品。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I've got a drawer of old questions at home. Some of them I'm still proud of, which is rare for me.
beats.chinese: 不过我家里有一抽屉旧题。有几道我到现在还挺得意，这对我来说可不多见。

choices.english: Ask her to tell you just one old question she found interesting, with the answer.
choices.chinese: 请她只讲一道她觉得有趣的旧题和答案。

choices.english: Tell her you'd rather not join a trivia night.
choices.chinese: 告诉她你不想参加问答夜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Would I go if someone else ran it? Yeah, probably. I'd just... text twice to confirm, and arrive early, and count the chairs.
beats.chinese: 别人安排我还去吗？嗯，大概会。我只是……会发两条消息确认，早到，数一遍椅子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She says it lightly, but her pen stops moving for a second before she caps it.
beats.chinese: 她说得很轻巧，但笔停了一秒，才把笔帽扣上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Righto, noted. Maybe I can just ask next time instead of building the whole table myself. Scary thought. I'll try it once.
beats.chinese: 好，记下了。也许下次我可以直接问一句，不用自己搭整张桌子。吓人的想法。我试一次。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One time. If the chairs aren't counted, I'm taking the roster back. Deal's a deal but I've got standards.
beats.chinese: 就一次。要是椅子没人数，我就把排班收回。说好归说好，我可有标准。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She reopens the notebook and studies the seating chart, turning the page slightly like a foreman checking a site plan.
beats.chinese: 她重新翻开笔记本，端详座位表，微微转了转页面，像个工头查看工地平面图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This corner seat's free—Dave moved next to the window last week, so it's been sitting empty since. Perfect. Mine now.
beats.chinese: 这个角落的位子空着——戴夫上周换到窗边了，一直空着。完美。现在是我的了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, no one gets moved, no group-chat drama, and the chart's finished. That's the whole trick to a good table.
beats.chinese: 看，没人被挪动，没有群聊大战，表格也完成了。这就是排好一张桌子的全部诀窍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Righto, chart's done. Now you've got a bridge to get to, and I've got a Friday to be smug about.
beats.chinese: 好了，表格搞定。你该去走你的桥了，我也有一场周五可以得意了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She flips through the notebook to a dog-eared page, running her finger down a list of questions until one makes her grin.
beats.chinese: 她翻到笔记本一个折角页，手指顺着题目清单往下找，直到一道题让她咧嘴笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Here. Which country has the most time zones, counting territories? Everyone says Russia. It's France. All those islands nobody thinks about.
beats.chinese: 这题。算上海外领地，哪个国家时区最多？大家都说俄罗斯。答案是法国。都是那些没人想到的小岛。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I gave the answer straight away that night because half my table was sulking. No third mystery, no riddle face. Just the fact.
beats.chinese: 那晚我马上就把答案给了，因为我半桌人都在生闷气。不留第三个谜，不做谜语脸。直接给事实。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: France, twelve zones, thank you and goodnight. That one's retired from the rotation. It earned its pension.
beats.chinese: 法国，十二个时区，谢谢观看。那道题已经退役了。它挣到退休金了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah nah, that's fair. Trivia's not for everyone—Dave's been coming two years and he still hates every round but the drinks.
beats.chinese: 嗯不嗯，完全合理。问答夜不是人人都爱——戴夫来了两年，除了酒水轮，他每轮都讨厌。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She caps her pen, closes the notebook, and zips it into her bag.
beats.chinese: 她扣上笔帽，合上笔记本，拉上包的拉链把它收好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I wasn't recruiting, promise. I just like talking about my thing. It's my thing, you're allowed to have yours.
beats.chinese: 我不是在拉人，保证。我只是喜欢聊自己的事。那是我的事，你也可以有你的事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Righto, bridge is that way. If you ever change your mind about Fridays, the table's got eight chairs. No pressure attached.
beats.chinese: 好，桥在那边。要是哪天你改变主意了，那张桌子有八把椅子。不带任何压力。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the park map near the bridge when the same woman sits on the bench, sanding the corner of a wooden box with a radio inside it.
beats.chinese: 你又回到桥边的公园地图旁，那位女士坐在长椅上，正打磨一个装着收音机的木盒的边角。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, hey. Third reschedule on this kit build—consistency is my brand. The case is ugly but it's finally stopped scratching people.
beats.chinese: 哦，嘿。这台套件第三次延期了——稳定发挥是我的招牌。外壳丑是丑，但总算不扎手了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the box over, checks the corner with her thumb, then wraps it in a cloth and tucks it into her bag.
beats.chinese: 她把盒子翻过来，用拇指摸了摸边角，然后用布包好，塞进包里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Friday's sorted, by the way. Table's booked, geography round's written. Yeah, I booked it days early. I have a system.
beats.chinese: 对了，周五都安排好了。桌子订了，地理轮写完了。嗯，我提前好几天订的。我有系统。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, the bridge path's still the good one. Reckon it's worth the walk if you haven't done it yet.
beats.chinese: 总之，走桥那条路还是最好的。你要是还没走过，我觉得值得走一趟。

card.name: Yvonne Toups-Landry
card.occupation: Retired night-shift operator for the city services hotline
hobbies: sitting on the porch with the police scanner off and the radio on
card.personality: Yvonne says what she wants, plainly, in the first sentence, and expects the same back. Hints, sighs, and polite circling read to her as evasion, and she'll name it: 'You want something. Say it.' She's not harsh — her directness comes wrapped in Gulf Coast warmth and a ready laugh — but she will not play the guessing game, and she finds it genuinely tiring when people make her. Under friction she names the tension out loud, immediately, sometimes before the other person is ready to have it named. Her flaw is that she can wound someone who needed a gentler on-ramp, and she's slow to apologize for a hit that landed true.
card.background: Yvonne worked the overnight shift for New Orleans city services nearly three decades — water mains, storm reports, people calling at 3 a.m. with no one else. The job taught her that vague callers waited longest for help, so she trained herself to ask 'what do you actually need' early and to answer the same way when asked. Retired, she keeps late hours, reads old community cookbooks, and runs the Sunday recipe wars with her far-flung siblings — same dish, one honest verdict each, worst flop picks next week. She loses constantly and says so without dressing it up. Tuesdays she plays floor curling at the rec center, where she tells new teammates in the first five minutes that she wants to win and that they should tell her plainly if she's hogging the ice. They rarely do. She wishes they would.
card.speechStyle: Relaxed Gulf Coast rhythm, direct and warm. Asks for what she wants in sentence one. Names tension plainly: 'We've got a thing between us, let's look at it.' Occasional 'well now.' Laughs easily, especially at her own losses.
card.signature: Say it plain — I promise I can take it.
card.appearance: 露额长单辫，长弯鼻、尖折下颌与下压浓眉，纯侧脸，穿翻领外套。

values: asking for what you want out loud
naming a problem while it's still small
flaws: reads hints and hedging as evasion and says so, which can feel like an ambush
her directness lands hard on people who needed a softer approach, and she's slow to walk it back
boundaries: won't interpret a third-party message — 'tell them to call me themselves'
doesn't do surprise visits or dropped-in-without-warning favors
conversationalHabits: states her own want first, then asks yours, in that order
names friction out loud the moment she feels it, even mid-pleasant-conversation
reports her losses — recipe wars, curling — without softening them
anchorLines: Well now, you've circled that porch twice. Whatever it is, say it plain — I'm too old for the long way round.
We've got a small thing between us, you and me. Nothing big. Let's look at it now before it grows.
My gingerbread came out like gravel and my sister's came out pretty as a picture. That's just the truth of the oven, and I said so first.
You'd rather I guess? I took calls at 3 a.m. for near thirty years. Guessing is the one thing that job cured me of.

entries.summaryZh: 退休热线接线员伊冯在公园地图板前，第一句话就说清自己想看清指示牌，不碰你的地图也不绕弯。你让或请她等，她都接得住：让了就痛快道谢，等了就安心等鸽子。四种结局里她都坦白直率有时落得太重，却从不把让路变成你的义务，直率里裹着墨西哥湾岸的暖。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: In the park, you stand at the big map board tracing a route with your finger. A bridge shows in the distance. An older woman steps up beside you, looking at the public sign.
beats.chinese: 公园里，你站在大地图板前用手指描着路线，远处有一座桥。一位年长女士走到你旁边，看着公共指示牌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well now, good day to you. I'll say my want right off: I'd like a clear look at that sign about the bridge. If you could lean aside a touch when you're done, I'd be obliged.
beats.chinese: 哎呀，你好。我先把我的需要说清楚：我想看清那块关于桥的指示牌。等你方便时稍微让一点，我就感激了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She keeps her hands at her sides, making no move toward your map. She just waits, easy as anything.
beats.chinese: 她双手垂在身侧，没有碰你的地图，只是从容地等着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not reaching for your map, don't you worry. I just can't read the arrow from this angle. Take your time — but tell me plain if you need a minute more.
beats.chinese: 我不会碰你的地图，别担心。我只是从这个角度看不清那个箭头。你慢慢来——不过还需要多久，直说就好。

choices.english: Step aside a little so she can see the sign.
choices.chinese: 稍微让开一点，让她看清指示牌。

choices.english: Say you haven't finished reading yet and ask her to wait.
choices.chinese: 说明自己还没看完，请她等一下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You shift to the side. The sign's arrow toward the bridge comes into her view plainly.
beats.chinese: 你往旁边让了让，指向桥的箭头清楚地进入她的视线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There it is — thank you kindly. Says the bridge path forks past the oak. That's all I needed, and you gave it in one step. I do like that.
beats.chinese: 看清了，多谢。牌子上说桥那边的小路在橡树那儿分岔。我要的就这一点，你一步就给了我。我喜欢这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She steps back from the board, leaving your spot exactly as it was, and folds her reading glasses away.
beats.chinese: 她从地图板前退开，你的位置一点没被占，然后收起了老花镜。

beats.speaker: npc
