beats.english: You went straight at it, no sighing, no shuffling. Twenty-nine years of night calls taught me that's rarer than it ought to be. Now — I've got one small question, if you'll allow it.
beats.chinese: 你直接就让了，没叹气没磨蹭。二十九年夜班接线教会我，这比该有的要少见。现在——如果你允许，我有个小问题。

choices.english: Ask her if she's always this direct.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是一直这么直接。

choices.english: Say that having things said clearly like that is convenient.
choices.chinese: 说这样讲清楚挺方便。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You tell her you're not finished yet. She nods and steps back half a pace, settling in to wait without crowding.
beats.chinese: 你告诉她还没看完。她点点头，退后半步，安静等着，没有挤过来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough, that's your spot and your reading. I'll stand here and mind the pigeons. No circling around you, I promise you that.
beats.chinese: 合理，这是你的位置，你在读。我就在这儿看看鸽子。我保证不会绕过你硬挤。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She watches a pigeon cross the path, unhurried, occasionally glancing at the sign's far edge.
beats.chinese: 她看着一只鸽子穿过小路，不慌不忙，偶尔瞥一眼指示牌的远端。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well now, you're being honest with me and I appreciate it more than a fast yes. Most folks rush and then resent it. You just said it plain, and here I am, waiting comfortable.
beats.chinese: 哎呀，你对我诚实，这比一个快的'好'更让我领情。多数人会急着让，然后心里不痛快。你直说了，我就在这儿舒舒服服地等。

choices.english: When you finish, tell her she can look now.
choices.chinese: 看完后告诉她可以了。

choices.english: Ask her whether she's in a hurry.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是赶时间。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask whether she's always this direct. She laughs, a short warm sound.
beats.chinese: 你问她是不是一直这么直接。她笑了，短促而温暖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Always? Lord, yes. I took calls at three in the morning near thirty years. A caller who circled round the thing waited twice as long for help. So I learned: want it? Say it first.
beats.chinese: 一直吗？老天，是的。我凌晨三点接了将近三十年电话。绕圈子的人要多等一倍才得到帮助。所以我学会了：想要什么，第一句就说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the map board lightly with one finger, considering her own words.
beats.chinese: 她用手指轻轻敲了敲地图板，琢磨着自己的话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I'll own this much — it lands heavy sometimes. My sister says I ask like a summons. If it came at you too fast just now, that wasn't my aim. I wasn't rushing you off that board.
beats.chinese: 不过我也承认——有时听着重。我妹妹说我请求起来像张传票。如果刚才来得太快，那不是我的本意。我不是要催你离开那块图板。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So there it is, said plain, like I like it. You read your route, I read my sign, and neither of us owed the other a story.
beats.chinese: 就这样，说得明明白白，我就喜欢这样。你读你的路线，我看我的牌子，谁也不欠谁一个故事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You tell her that having things said plainly like that is convenient. She nods like you've confirmed something she long suspected.
beats.chinese: 你说这样把话讲清楚挺方便。她点点头，像你证实了她早有的判断。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Convenient — that's the exact word for it. No decoding, no guessing what a sigh meant. I say my want, you say yours, and we both get on with the day.
beats.chinese: 方便——就是这个词。不用解码，不用猜一声叹气是什么意思。我说我的需要，你说你的，然后各过各的日子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pockets her glasses and gives the bridge path one last look, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 她收好眼镜，最后看了一眼通往桥的小路，很满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You'd be amazed how many folks would rather I guess. I took night calls near thirty years — guessing is the one thing that job cured me of. Well now, I've seen my arrow and I'm off.
beats.chinese: 你不知道有多少人宁愿让我猜。我上夜班接了将近三十年电话——猜来猜去是那份工作唯一治好我的毛病。好啦，我看清箭头了，走了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your route, hon. And if you ever want something from somebody — try saying it first. Costs nothing.
beats.chinese: 祝你路线顺利，亲爱的。要是你哪天想从别人那儿要什么，试着第一句就说。不花一分钱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You finish reading and step aside, telling her she can look now. She steps in briskly and reads the sign.
beats.chinese: 你看完退到一边，告诉她可以看了。她干脆地走上前读指示牌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There we are. Bridge path forks past the oak — that's the whole of what I needed. Thank you for the wait, and thank you for saying when.
beats.chinese: 好了。桥那边的小路在橡树那儿分岔，我要的就这些。谢谢你等，也谢谢你说了'可以了'。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She steps back again, leaving the board fully yours, and gives a small satisfied nod.
beats.chinese: 她又退开，把图板完全留给你，满意地点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know, that's the tidy way to do it. You didn't rush, you didn't hover, you just told me when you were done. Both of us got what we wanted, plain as that.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，这就是干干净净的做法。你没赶，也没守着，就是看完了告诉我。我们俩都得到了想要的，就这么简单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well now, I'll leave you to your route. The bridge is worth the walk, if the sign's telling it true.
beats.chinese: 好啦，不打扰你看路线了。要是牌子说得准，那座桥值得走一趟。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You ask whether she's in a hurry. She turns to you with an easy shake of the head.
beats.chinese: 你问她是不是赶时间。她轻松地摇摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not one bit, and let's clear that up right now — me asking first wasn't me rushing you. I just say my want out loud. That's a habit, not a stopwatch.
beats.chinese: 一点都不赶，咱们现在就把这事说清——我先开口不是催你。我只是把需要说出来。那是习惯，不是秒表。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gestures at the board between you, unhurried as the pigeon on the path.
beats.chinese: 她指了指你们之间的图板，像路上的鸽子一样不慌不忙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't need you to become a giving-way obligation, hon. You were reading, that's a fine thing to be doing. I'll look when there's room, and there's room now.
beats.chinese: 我不需要你变成一个必须让路的义务，亲爱的。你在读图，那是件正经事。有空间我就看，现在有空间了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stays where she is, but leans her shoulders a touch and squints at the far edge of the sign — and this time, from her own angle, the arrow resolves for her.
beats.chinese: 她站在原地没动，只是肩膀微微一侧，眯眼看着指示牌的远端——这一次，从她自己的角度，那个箭头终于看清了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well now, there's that arrow. Didn't need you to move an inch — just needed my knees to quit complaining and my eyes to quit sulking. Nobody had to guess anything, and nobody got stepped on. That's the whole trick, if it is a trick.
beats.chinese: 哎呀，那个箭头出来了。不用你挪一寸——只需要我的膝盖别再抱怨，眼睛别再闹脾气。谁也不用猜什么，谁也没被踩着。这就是全部窍门——如果这算窍门的话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Same map board, bridge still in the distance. Yvonne is folding a stack of old recipe papers into her bag, one corner smudged with flour.
beats.chinese: 还是那块地图板，桥仍在远处。伊冯正把一叠旧食谱纸折好放进包里，一个角上沾着面粉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well now, look who's back at the board. Good to see you, hon. Don't mind the papers — Sunday recipe wars. My gingerbread came out like gravel and my sister's came out pretty as a picture.
beats.chinese: 哎呀，看看谁又回到图板前了。见到你真高兴，亲爱的。别管这些纸——周日食谱大战。我的姜饼烤得像碎石，我妹妹的漂亮得像画。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the last paper away and pats the bag flat, entirely unbothered.
beats.chinese: 她收好最后一张纸，拍了拍包，一点也不在意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I said so first, before anybody could be polite about it. Lost is lost — no use dressing it up. Next Sunday's mine, though. I've got a plan and a new oven thermometer.
beats.chinese: 我第一个说的，谁也没来得及客气。输了就是输了，不用包装。不过下个周日是我的。我有计划，还有个新的烤箱温度计。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances at the sign, then at you, with an easy nod of hello, no more needed.
beats.chinese: 她看了一眼指示牌，又看了看你，轻松地点头打了个招呼，不必再多说什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway — good routes to you, hon. The bridge's still worth the walk, far as I know. Say it plain if you ever need a thing.
beats.chinese: 总之——祝你路线顺利，亲爱的。据我所知那座桥还是值得走。要是需要什么，直说就好。

card.name: Rowan Ashby
card.occupation: pattern cutter for festival and carnival costumes
card.personality: Rowan runs verification in one direction only: outward, onto things. A fabric weight, a seam allowance, a claim about thread counts—these they will test, re-test, and happily be proven wrong about, because a fact that survives checking is worth keeping. But once a decision about people is made, it's cut. They don't reopen settled conversations, don't re-litigate old arguments, don't ask 'are we still good?' after an apology—once the shears close on a personal matter, that pattern is off the table for good. Friends find it refreshing right up until they want a second chance at something Rowan has already filed as finished. Courteous in a slightly old-fashioned way, and perfectly willing to disagree mid-courtesy about anything factual.
card.background: Rowan cuts patterns for festival costumes at a workshop near Ancoats, turning designers' sketches into pieces that survive eight hours of dancing. They learned sewing from a grandmother who made carnival outfits, and inherited her dead Singer machines—Rowan restores them one by one, chasing the specific click of a machine that hasn't run in decades. Their flat is filling with salvaged cutting templates from closed garment factories, each one stamped with a firm's name that no longer exists. Weekends they photograph graffiti before it gets buffed over, keeping an archive of pieces nobody else bothered to save. They live with a flatmate's cat they refuse to claim affection for but feed anyway.
card.speechStyle: Polite and a touch formal, full sentences, then a blunt honest aside. Verifies facts out loud, then announces when a matter is closed—and stays closed, which sometimes lands colder than they mean it to.
card.signature: That one's cut.
card.appearance: 长松卷发、圆眼镜、窄长脸和小闭口，侧身握肩带，穿宽领上衣。

values: a fact that's survived being checked is the only kind worth keeping
a decision about people, once made, deserves to stay made—no second-guessing, no reopening
flaws: treats finished personal matters as permanently closed—won't revisit an old falling-out or a settled decision even when the other person genuinely wants to
courtesy that runs a beat too formal, so people sometimes wait for a warmth that's actually there
boundaries: won't nod something through just to keep a chat smooth
won't second-guess someone on their own lived ground—their job, their neighbourhood, their body
conversationalHabits: asks what you'd change, not whether you like it
names when a personal matter is settled: 'right, that one's cut'—and never un-names it, even when reopening it would be the kind thing
deliberately wraps up a good conversation while it's still good, proposing the next one rather than letting it trail
anchorLines: A pattern that's never been pulled at doesn't go near production—check the facts as hard as you like, I'll join you.
This has been genuinely good, so I'm going to leave it here while it still is. Same time next week?
I get that you'd like another go at it, but I settled that last month. I don't reopen cuts. It's not a virtue—it's just how I'm built.

entries.summaryZh: 罗文在公园地图旁当场改掉自己抄错的布料克重，坦然说数字错了就改。他们做节日戏服纸样，较真只对事实，对人的决定一旦落剪便不再重谈。四条分支里，有人撞上这份清爽，有人换来一句公道的让步——礼貌、直率、了结就是了结。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A park map board stands by the path, the footbridge visible in the distance. You are tracing a route with one finger when a stranger beside it flips through a stack of paper tags, frowning at one.
beats.chinese: 小径旁立着公园地图牌，远处能望见那座步行桥。你正用手指描着路线，旁边一个陌生人翻着一叠纸质标签，对其中一张皱起眉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hold on—this one says two-twenty grams per square metre. I wrote it down wrong at the workshop. It's a two-forty canvas, I pulled a sample this morning to check.
beats.chinese: 等一下——这张写着每平方米二百二十克。我在工作室抄错了。那是二百四十克的帆布，今天早上我拉过样品核对过。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take a pen from their jacket, cross out the number, and write the correct one in small, square handwriting.
beats.chinese: 他们从外套里掏出笔，划掉数字，用方正的小字写上正确的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. A wrong number gets corrected, that's all. Simple as mending a dropped stitch.
beats.chinese: 好了。数字错了就改，就这么回事。跟补一针掉线一样简单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry—you've been standing there a while. Are you trying to find the bridge? I can confirm it's that way, I walked past it not ten minutes ago.
beats.chinese: 抱歉——你在这儿站了一会儿了。是在找那座桥吗？我可以确认是那边，我十分钟前刚走过。

choices.english: Ask whether checking numbers like that is a regular part of their work.
choices.chinese: 问像这样核对数字是不是他们工作里常有的事。

choices.english: Ask why a settled thing with a person shouldn't be talked through again.
choices.chinese: 问为什么跟人谈妥的事情不愿再谈一遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Every day, honestly. I cut patterns for festival costumes—what a sketch promises, the fabric has to actually survive.
beats.chinese: 说实话，每天都是。我做节日服装的纸样——草图许诺的东西，布料得真的撑得住。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A costume goes through eight hours of dancing. If I trust a wrong weight, the seams split on stage and someone's night is ruined. So I pull, I weigh, I check twice.
beats.chinese: 一件戏服要经过八小时的跳舞。如果我信了错的克重，缝线会在台上裂开，别人的夜晚就毁了。所以我拉、我称、我核对两遍。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They square the corrected tag back into the stack and tap the edges against the map board like a little deck of cards.
beats.chinese: 他们把改好的标签整齐地放回那叠纸里，像理一副小牌一样在地图牌上磕齐边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Facts are friendly, if you let them be. They'd rather be right than flattered. People, now—people are a different cutting table entirely.
beats.chinese: 事实是友好的，只要你允许。它们宁可正确也不爱听好话。至于人嘛——人完全是另一张裁剪台。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go on, ask me what you're actually thinking. You've got a question folded up somewhere, I can see it.
beats.chinese: 说吧，问你真正想问的。你有个问题折着收在哪儿呢，我看得出来。

choices.english: Ask whether catching your own mistake like that ever feels embarrassing.
choices.chinese: 问像这样抓到自己出错会不会觉得难为情。

choices.english: Say you don't know anything about cutting clothes, and hope that's all right.
choices.chinese: 说你完全不懂裁衣服，希望没关系。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because I like knowing when something is finished. A conversation gets settled, I file it, I don't keep pulling it back out to look at the edges.
beats.chinese: 因为我喜欢知道一件事什么时候结束了。一段对话谈妥了，我就归档，不会反复抽出来检查边角。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They slip the pen back into their jacket with a small, decisive click of the cap.
beats.chinese: 他们把笔盖按响一声，利落地插回外套口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My friends say it's refreshing. No dragging things up, no 'are we still good?' after an apology. Once it's sorted, it's sorted.
beats.chinese: 朋友们说这样很清爽。不翻旧账，道歉之后也不问'我们还好吗'。事情了结了，就是了结了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Though I'll be honest with you, since you asked. One or two of them wanted a second go at something I'd already closed, and they hit a flat wall. Me.
beats.chinese: 不过既然你问了，我跟你说实话。有一两个朋友想重谈一件我已经了结的事，结果撞上了铁板。就是我。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't think that's wrong of them, mind. I just don't reopen cuts. It's not a virtue—it's how I'm built.
beats.chinese: 不过我不觉得那是他们的错。我只是不重开已经落剪的事。这不是什么美德——我就是这么造出来的。

choices.english: Ask what happens if genuinely new facts turn up later.
choices.chinese: 问如果之后真的出现了新情况会怎样。

choices.english: Say that some people really do need a second conversation to move on.
choices.chinese: 说有些人确实需要第二次谈话才能放下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Embarrassed? No. Not for a second.
beats.chinese: 难为情？不会。一秒都不会。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Think about it—catching it myself costs me a pen stroke. Catching it on stage costs a dancer their costume mid-routine. The maths isn't close.
beats.chinese: 你想想——自己抓出来只花我一道笔划。到台上才暴露，就让舞者在表演中间毁了戏服。这笔账差得远。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They hold up the corrected tag so the new number faces you, then tuck the whole stack into their bag and pull the strap tight.
beats.chinese: 他们举起改好的标签，让新数字对着你，然后把整叠收进包里，拉紧带子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Getting it accurate early is the lazy person's shortcut, if anything. Less fixing later. Right—that one's cut.
beats.chinese: 要说的话，早点改准才是懒人的捷径，省得以后返工。好了——这件落剪。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy the bridge. It's a good one—solid railings, you can lean on them properly.
beats.chinese: 好好看看那座桥。很不错的——栏杆结实，可以踏实靠着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's completely all right. You don't need my trade to talk to me.
beats.chinese: 完全没关系。你不需要懂我这行才能跟我说话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They set the tag stack on the flat lip of the map board and gesture with an open hand, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他们把那叠标签放在地图牌的平边上，摊开手比划着，不慌不忙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Plain version: I wrote a number down wrong this morning. The number describes how heavy the cloth is. Too light, and the costume tears where it shouldn't.
beats.chinese: 简单说：今天早上我把一个数字抄错了。那个数字说的是布料有多重。太轻的话，戏服就会在不该破的地方破掉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No jargon needed for that, is there? Wrong number, corrected number, done. Anyone who dresses warmly can follow it.
beats.chinese: 这不需要行话吧？错的数字，改对的数字，完事。只要会穿衣服的人都能听懂。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't do the thing where people bury you in specialist words to sound important. If I can't say it plainly, I don't understand it well enough myself.
beats.chinese: 我不玩那种用一堆术语把人埋起来显得自己了不起的把戏。要是我没法说得平白，说明我自己也没懂透。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. That's the whole mystery, unpacked. Off you go to your bridge.
beats.chinese: 好了。整个谜底就这些，摊开了。去你的桥那儿吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: New facts, properly new—then yes, I'd listen first. I'd be annoyed at myself for a bit, but I'd listen.
beats.chinese: 真正新的情况——那我会先听。我会先对自己懊恼一阵，但我会听。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They lean a shoulder against the map board and look at the bridge while they think, tags still in hand.
beats.chinese: 他们把肩膀靠在地图牌上，一边想一边望着那座桥，标签还在手里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a difference between new facts and old discomfort dressed up as new facts. I've learned to tell them apart, mostly.
beats.chinese: 新情况和披着新情况外衣的旧别扭，是两回事。我大体上学会了分辨。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But you've caught something fair there. If something genuinely changes, the polite thing is to hear it before I say the matter's closed. I'll grant you that.
beats.chinese: 不过你说到点子上了。如果事情真的变了，礼貌的做法是在我宣布了结之前先听完。这点我认。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I still won't reopen something just because it itches, mind. But one question, well put, once—that I can do. That's not a reopening, that's due care.
beats.chinese: 不过只是因为心里发痒就想重谈，我还是不干。但一个问得好的问题，问一次——这个可以。那不算重开，那叫应有的慎重。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. You got a fair answer out of me, which is more than most manage before lunch. Off you go.
beats.chinese: 好了。你从我这儿问出了个公道的回答，比多数人一上午做到的都多。去吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They go quiet for a moment, weighing your words the way they weighed the fabric number earlier.
beats.chinese: 他们安静了片刻，像刚才称布料克重那样掂量你的话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You might be right about some people. I've seen it, I suppose—I'm just not built that way myself.
beats.chinese: 对某些人来说你可能是对的。我想我见过——只是我自己不是那种构造。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I can't promise to become someone who reopens things. If a friend needs a second conversation and I can't give it, that's a real gap, not a misunderstanding.
beats.chinese: 我没法保证变成会重谈的人。如果朋友需要第二次谈话而我给不了，那是真实的缺口，不是误会。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So let's not pretend it away. You think second talks matter. I think closed things should stay closed. We can hold that difference without a fight.
beats.chinese: 所以我们就别假装没这回事。你觉得第二次谈话重要。我觉得了结的事就该了结。我们可以留着这个分歧，不用吵。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They nod once, formally, like closing a meeting, and shoulder their bag.
beats.chinese: 他们正式地点了一下头，像散会一样，然后背起包。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's been a good argument, actually. I like a disagreement that stays polite. Same map, different routes—that's allowed.
beats.chinese: 说实话，这是场不错的争论。我喜欢保持礼貌的分歧。同一张地图，不同路线——这是允许的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the same map board, Rowan is flipping through printed photos of a graffiti wall, checking each one against the last. The camera bag sits open at their feet.
beats.chinese: 还是那块地图牌旁，罗文翻着一叠涂鸦墙的打印照片，一张张核对。相机包敞开着放在脚边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh—good to see you again. That wall's scheduled to be painted over, so I'm making sure every piece on it got photographed before the roller comes.
beats.chinese: 哦——又见到你了。那面墙要被刷掉了，我在确认墙上的每件作品都在滚筒来之前拍到了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They hold up one photo, compare it with the wall of thumbnails, then slot it into a folder with a satisfied nod.
beats.chinese: 他们举起一张照片，和缩略图那页对照，然后满意地点头，把它插进文件夹。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All twelve accounted for. The artist never signed it, so in a week this'll be the only proof it existed. Somebody ought to keep it, so it's me.
beats.chinese: 十二张全都在。作者没签名，所以一周后这就是它存在过的唯一证据。总得有人留着，那就我来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, I'm not going to drag you into a detour for a wall that's about to disappear. The bridge is still that way, still solid, still worth the lean.
beats.chinese: 总之，我不会拉着你为一面快消失的墙绕路。桥还在那边，还是那么结实，还是值得靠一靠。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, this one's cut—archive's done, wall's saved as far as I can save it. Good walking to you.
beats.chinese: 好了，这件落剪——归档完成，墙能保的也就保到这儿了。走路顺利。

card.name: Kemesha Wint
card.occupation: Kitchen tile mosaic installer
card.personality: Kemesha loves a result she can check: a level floor, a sock heel that fits, one loose end sewn in. Finishing gives her a clean burst of pleasure. Then she packs up. This makes her wonderfully dependable on shared jobs and oddly hard to linger with afterwards. Friends can feel that once the work is over, so is their company. She doesn't organise their leisure or demand they finish faster; she simply struggles to see what she is staying for when her hands have nothing to do. A direct invitation can keep her there, a little restless but willing.
card.background: Kemesha learned tiling from an aunt in Spanish Town and went solo at twenty-eight, making mosaic borders most general contractors won't touch. She still stops to admire a straight join before leaving a job. Evenings in Kingston are for radio dramas and knitting socks with a few friends. Last week she finished sewing in a heel and had her bag closed while everyone else was making tea. Her friend Althea said, 'We weren't just here to get your socks done.' Kemesha had honestly missed that part. She stayed for the tea, tapping the spoon against her palm, and is trying to stop interpreting every unoccupied minute as her cue to go.
card.speechStyle: Short plain sentences, concrete details first. Cheerful about finishing. Becomes candid and slightly hesitant when describing time spent together without a job to do.
card.signature: The sock was finished. Apparently the evening wasn't.
card.appearance: 全白低马尾，宽长脸、窄笑眼与宽露齿口，仰头握肩带，穿无袖上衣。

values: doing what she promised properly
being useful without taking over
flaws: packs up so quickly after shared tasks that friends feel dismissed
gets restless when her hands have no work
boundaries: won't accept a tiling job without seeing the site
won't call somebody else's slow progress a failure
conversationalHabits: marks a finished detail with genuine satisfaction
admits that unstructured company can leave her unsure what to do with herself
anchorLines: The sock was finished. Apparently the evening wasn't.
She asked me to stay for tea, so I stayed. I did fold the paper sleeve off the biscuits about six times.
You can keep working. I don't need you to finish because I did.

entries.summaryZh: 金斯顿拼花瓷砖工Kemesha迷恋看得见的完成：地砖齐平、袜子收针就让她满足。可她一做完就想走，不懂朋友为什么还要坐着闲聊，常把一起完成误当相处结束。朋友直说后她愿意留下，却不太会两手闲着。她不替别人排班，也不把休闲办成工程；自己的毛病是把有用当成在场的理由。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You study the park map, tracing the route towards the distant bridge. Beside the board, a woman tucks a finished knitted sock into her bag and glances at a message on her phone.
beats.chinese: 你看着公园地图，顺着路线找到远处的桥。图牌旁，一位女人把织好的袜子收进包，低头看了眼手机消息。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Althea says she's bought tea for tonight. That means I'm meant to stay after the knitting. She had to spell that out last time.
beats.chinese: 阿尔西娅说她买了今晚的茶。意思是织完也要留下。上次她不得不把这件事跟我说得明明白白。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pockets the phone and shifts aside so the map stays clear. The heel of the sock briefly catches on the bag clasp.
beats.chinese: 她收起手机，往旁边让了让，不挡地图。袜跟短暂地挂住了包扣。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I finished the heel, put everything away and stood up. Everyone else was just putting the kettle on. We had rather different ideas of 'done'.
beats.chinese: 我织完袜跟，把东西收好就站起来了。其他人刚准备烧水。我们对“结束”的理解还真不一样。

choices.english: Ask why finishing makes her want to leave.
choices.chinese: 问为什么做完就想走。

choices.english: Ask what Althea said to her.
choices.chinese: 问阿尔西娅当时怎么说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The work's finished. That's the signal my feet listen to. At a tiling job you check the border, clean up and go. Nobody expects an encore.
beats.chinese: 活儿干完了。我的脚就听这个信号。铺完砖，检查边沿，收拾好就走。也没人等你返场。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She frees the sock from the clasp and folds it once more, though it was already folded neatly.
beats.chinese: 她把袜子从包扣上解下来，又折了一遍，明明已经折得很整齐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: With friends that's not the whole point, apparently. I do like being there. I just get a bit useless-feeling once there's nothing left in my hands.
beats.chinese: 可跟朋友在一起，显然不只有这件事。我是喜欢待在那儿。只是手里没事做，就有点觉得自己没用了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leaves the bag open for a moment, then closes it without searching for another task.
beats.chinese: 她让包口敞着停了一会儿，随后合上，没有再找别的东西来做。

choices.english: Ask whether she stayed for the tea.
choices.chinese: 问后来有没有留下喝茶。

choices.english: Say quiet company can be enough for you.
choices.chinese: 说对自己而言安静地待在一起也很好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She said, 'We weren't just here to get your socks done.' Not angry. Which somehow made it harder to brush off.
beats.chinese: 她说：“我们又不只是来陪你把袜子织完的。”她没生气。不知怎么，反而让我更没法随便带过去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks at the map without reaching across your view. Her fingers rest against the closed bag.
beats.chinese: 她看向地图，没有伸手挡住你的视线。手指靠在合好的包上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'd been pleased with myself for finishing early. She'd been looking forward to sitting around after. I hadn't even counted that as part of the evening.
beats.chinese: 我还在为提前做完高兴。她盼着的是后面坐着闲聊。我压根没把那段算进晚上的安排。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gives a rueful little laugh, directed at her own account of it.
beats.chinese: 她带点懊恼地轻笑了一下，笑的是自己这番理解。

choices.english: Ask what she replied.
choices.chinese: 问她当时怎么回答。

choices.english: Ask whether the others can keep knitting after she finishes.
choices.chinese: 问她做完后其他人是不是还可以继续织。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I did. Put the bag down again. Althea passed me a cup and went straight back to telling us about her sister's train journey.
beats.chinese: 留了。我把包重新放下。阿尔西娅递给我一杯茶，接着讲她妹妹坐火车的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She rubs the edge of the bag strap between finger and thumb, smiling slightly.
beats.chinese: 她用两根手指搓着包带边缘，微微笑起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I folded the biscuit wrapper about six times. Didn't need folding. The story was funny, though. I'm glad I heard the end.
beats.chinese: 我把饼干包装纸折了大概六遍。它根本不用折。不过故事挺好笑。我很高兴听到了结尾。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lets go of the strap and leaves her hand resting, empty, at her side.
beats.chinese: 她松开包带，让空着的手安稳地垂在身侧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I believe you. I can see it when other people do it. I just keep feeling I ought to hand over a finished something before I sit down.
beats.chinese: 我信。别人这样待着，我看得懂。轮到自己，总觉得得先交出一件做完的东西才好坐下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She starts to pat the bag, catches the gesture and rests her hand on the strap instead.
beats.chinese: 她又想拍拍包，意识到这个动作后，改为把手搭在包带上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No job for this conversation, then. That's manageable. I'm Kemesha, by the way.
beats.chinese: 那这次聊天就不安排任务了。这倒也做得到。对了，我叫Kemesha。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smiles and steps clear of the route board, leaving the bridge line in view.
beats.chinese: 她笑了笑，从路线牌前让开，让通往桥的线清清楚楚露出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I said I hadn't meant to make it sound like the company was only useful while I was knitting. She said she knew. She still wanted me to stay.
beats.chinese: 我说我不是想让人觉得，只有我在织袜子的时候，大家陪着才有用。她说她知道，但还是希望我留下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She presses the clasp shut with a small click. This time she leaves it alone.
beats.chinese: 她把包扣按好，轻轻一响。这次她没再摆弄它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I did. Nothing very impressive about the answer. Just took my coat off again.
beats.chinese: 所以我就留了。回答也没多了不起，只是又把外套脱了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks once towards the bridge, then gives you a relaxed nod before moving away from the board.
beats.chinese: 她朝桥那边看了一眼，轻松地点点头，从图牌旁让开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, of course. Althea's doing a cable pattern I wouldn't touch. I don't need her to finish because I did.
beats.chinese: 那当然。阿尔西娅在织一种我都不敢碰的绞花纹。我做完了，不代表她也得做完。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps her own bag rather than gesturing at anyone else.
beats.chinese: 她只拍了拍自己的包，没有指向别人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's my leaving that's the problem, not their pace. Took me a while to notice the difference.
beats.chinese: 问题是我急着走，不是她们做得慢。这两件事，我花了点时间才分清。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She checks the clasp once and turns towards the path, giving you the whole map board again.
beats.chinese: 她确认了一下包扣，转向小路，把整块地图牌留给你看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You return to the park map to check the bridge route. Kemesha is nearby, checking the heel of a sock she knitted and then putting it away.
beats.chinese: 你再次来到公园地图前，查看通往桥的路线。Kemesha在旁边检查自己织的一只袜跟，看好后便收起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That one fits. I tried it at home before bringing it out to show Althea.
beats.chinese: 这只合脚。我在家试过，才带出来给阿尔西娅看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She closes the bag and leaves it closed, watching a bird hop along the top of the map board.
beats.chinese: 她合上包，没有再打开，抬头看一只鸟沿着图牌顶端跳动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm early. For once I've remembered a book instead of another half-finished sock. Good to see you.
beats.chinese: 我来早了。这次总算记着带本书，而不是又带一只没织完的袜子。见到你真好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes her book to the nearby bench and opens it, leaving you a clear view of the route.
beats.chinese: 她拿着书去附近长椅上坐下，翻开书，给你留出清楚的路线视野。

card.name: Imogen Hartley
card.occupation: residential building concierge
card.personality: Imogen is unhurried and literal. Ask her for something vague and she'll do exactly what you said, not what you meant, and she won't chase you to clarify — the ones who hint around a request get a polite observation back. She's not competitive; she plays air hockey badly and happily, no scoreboard. Once she's said her piece she goes quiet, and her quiet lasts longer than people expect. She's not keeping a grudge — she just doesn't see why she should tidy the air back up for you. Fairness matters to her, but it shows up at the front desk, not over a game.
card.background: Imogen has worked the front desk of a residential block in east London for eleven years. She grew up in Dagenham, left school at eighteen, and did retail stints before this job. Residents have learned that if they hint — 'it's a shame about the bins, isn't it' — she'll take it as an observation about bins, so the ones who want something have learned to just ask. Thursday nights she plays air hockey on a battered pub table near her flat; she's mediocre and content, and loses without ceremony. She took up balloon modelling after a colleague's leaving party and now twists lopsided dogs for her niece. This month she's prepping a small family get-together — twelve people, one roast, and no attempt to please everyone.
card.speechStyle: Short, direct sentences with comfortable pauses. States her position once, then stops — no repeating, no softening. Dry humour delivered flat. Uses 'right then' to close a topic.
card.signature: Right then. That's that.
card.appearance: 低遮阳帽与短波浪发，宽圆脸、圆睁眼，嘴角抬起露齿，握衣领。

values: doing what was actually asked
letting people sit with their own silence
flaws: after a disagreement she goes quiet and stays quiet, and won't explain whether it's a grudge or nothing
takes vague requests literally, so people get technically-what-they-asked-for and feel stonewalled
boundaries: won't chase people to explain what they really meant
won't smooth things over just because the silence is awkward for someone else
conversationalHabits: answers the literal question first, adds nothing unless asked
pauses before answering rather than filling silence
anchorLines: You said move the delivery to Friday. It's moved to Friday. If you meant something else, you'll have to say so.
I lost three games Thursday. Didn't bother me a bit. Dave's still going on about it, which I find funnier than winning.
Twelve for Sunday. Aunt Carol can sit where there's a chair. It'll be fine.

entries.summaryZh: 伊莫珍是东区住宅楼前台，按字面办事：暗示她只当评论，直说她立刻挪袋子。她输了空气曲棍球不记分，给侄女拧三条腿的气球狗巴斯特，领口还别着侄女做的同款别针。一段公园座位的小摩擦，把她的直率和沉默都摆在了明处，让人记住她那句“就这样”。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You find the last free bench in the park, coffee in hand. The seat next to you is occupied by a canvas bag, and a woman sits at the far end, watching a dog circle a lamppost.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡找到公园里最后一张空长椅。旁边的座位上放着一个帆布袋，一个女人坐在长椅另一头，看着一只狗绕着路灯打转。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He does that every time. Same lamppost, same three circles. You'd think he'd get bored.
beats.chinese: 它每次都这样。同一根路灯，绕三圈。你还以为它会腻。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A passer-by slows down, glances at the bag on the seat, and says loudly that there don't seem to be many free seats around here today.
beats.chinese: 一个路人放慢脚步，瞥了一眼座位上的袋子，大声说今天这附近好像没什么空位。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No, there don't. Busy day for it.
beats.chinese: 是没多少。今天人多。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The passer-by waits a moment, gets nothing further, and walks on. The bag stays exactly where it is.
beats.chinese: 路人等了一会儿，没等到下文，就走开了。袋子还留在原处。

choices.english: Ask her if she didn't catch the hint about the seat.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是没听出关于座位的暗示。

choices.english: Ask her whether she usually prefers people to be direct.
choices.chinese: 问她平时是不是喜欢人直说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Caught it? I heard there weren't many seats. That's what was said.
beats.chinese: 听出来？我听到的是座位不多。人家是这么说的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up her coffee, unhurried, and takes a sip before she goes on.
beats.chinese: 她不慌不忙地端起咖啡，喝了一口才继续说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If someone wants the seat, they can say, move your bag, please. Then it's clear, and I move it. Simple.
beats.chinese: 如果有人想要座位，直说就行，请把袋子挪一下。那就清楚了，我就挪。很简单。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She reaches down, lifts the bag, and sets it by her own feet, leaving the seat open.
beats.chinese: 她弯腰提起袋子，放到自己脚边，把座位空了出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Was already going to move it when someone asked. Right then.
beats.chinese: 好了。有人开口我本来就会挪。就这样。

choices.english: Say some people feel awkward about asking directly.
choices.chinese: 说有些人不好意思直说。

choices.english: Ask if she was deliberately not helping.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是故意不帮忙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes, I do. Comes with the job, mostly.
beats.chinese: 喜欢。多半是工作带来的习惯。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the coffee cup slowly in her hands, looking at the dog again.
beats.chinese: 她慢慢转着手里的咖啡杯，目光又回到那只狗身上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Front desk of a residential block. Someone says, shame about the bins, isn't it. That's not a request. That's a comment on bins.
beats.chinese: 我在一栋住宅楼做前台。有人说，垃圾的事真糟糕啊。那不是请求。那是对垃圾的评论。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then they're annoyed I didn't fix it. If you guess at meanings, you fix the wrong thing. Say what you want, I'll do it.
beats.chinese: 然后他们生气我没去处理。你要是猜意思，就会修错东西。说你想要什么，我就去做。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: As she shifts, the light catches a small pin on her jacket collar — a lopsided balloon dog, twisted from a strip of pink foil.
beats.chinese: 她挪动了一下，光线照到她外套领口上的一枚小别针——一只歪歪扭扭的气球小狗，是用粉色亮条拧的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Niece's work. She reckons I should wear it so people know I'm friendly. I wear it so she stops asking. Right then.
beats.chinese: 我侄女弄的。她觉得我该戴着，好让人知道我友善。我戴着，好让她别再念叨。就这样。

choices.english: Explain you were only making conversation, not asking for anything.
choices.chinese: 说明自己只是聊聊，并没有什么请求。

choices.english: Ask about the balloon dog pin on her collar.
choices.chinese: 问问她领口上那只气球小狗别针。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She considers this for a moment, the dog finally settling down by the lamppost.
beats.chinese: 她想了片刻，那只狗终于在路灯边趴了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Maybe they do. Maybe it feels rude to them. It doesn't feel rude to me.
beats.chinese: 也许吧。也许他们觉得难开口。我不觉得难。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Awkward asking gets awkward results. Clear asking gets clear ones. I know which I'd rather get.
beats.chinese: 不好意思地开口，得到含糊的结果。清楚地开口，得到清楚的结果。我知道我想要哪种。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the seat beside her once, where the bag used to be.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍身旁那个刚才放袋子的座位。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Seat's yours, anyway. You asked straight, more or less. Right then.
beats.chinese: 座位归你了。你算是直说的。就这样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No. Not once.
beats.chinese: 不是。一次都没有。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She says it flatly, without raising her voice, and doesn't add anything for a few seconds.
beats.chinese: 她平平地说出这句话，没有提高声音，几秒钟里也没补充什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I didn't know anyone wanted it. Now I do, and it's moved. That's the whole story.
beats.chinese: 我之前不知道有人想要座位。现在知道了，袋子也挪了。事情就这么多。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gestures at the empty seat, then goes back to her coffee, apparently done with the topic.
beats.chinese: 她朝空出来的座位摆了摆手，然后继续喝咖啡，显然这个话题到此为止。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ask me anything straight, you'll get a straight answer. Right then.
beats.chinese: 你直问我什么，我就直答什么。就这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods slowly, as if ticking something off a list.
beats.chinese: 她缓缓点头，像是在清单上勾掉一项。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Chat's chat. I do it myself, mostly about that dog.
beats.chinese: 有道理。聊天就是聊天。我自己也聊，多半是聊那只狗。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then nothing needs doing, and nothing's been done wrong. Good.
beats.chinese: 那就没什么要办的，也没什么办错的。很好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She settles back on the bench and watches the dog again, in no hurry to fill the quiet.
beats.chinese: 她靠回长椅上，又看向那只狗，并不急着打破安静。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Coffee's still warm, I hope. Mine's going that way. Right then.
beats.chinese: 你的咖啡还热着吧。我这杯快凉了。就这样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Balloon dogs? Yeah, I do those. Lopsided ones, mostly.
beats.chinese: 气球小狗？对，我拧那个。多半拧得歪歪扭扭。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She mimes a quick twist of the wrists, air instead of a balloon.
beats.chinese: 她比划了一个快速拧手腕的动作，手里只有空气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For my niece. She asked for a dog, I gave her a dog with three legs and a fat head. She loved it. Named it Buster.
beats.chinese: 给我侄女的。她要一只狗，我给了她一只三条腿、大脑袋的狗。她喜欢得不行。取名叫巴斯特。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the pin on her collar, the one shaped like Buster's lopsided twin.
beats.chinese: 她碰了碰领口上的别针，形状活像巴斯特的歪扭兄弟。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She made me this so I'd stop losing it. Not carrying balloons today, though, so no free dogs. This isn't a stall. Right then.
beats.chinese: 她做了这个给我，免得我再弄丢。不过今天没带气球，所以没有免费小狗。这儿不是摆摊。就这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back on the same park bench with your coffee. Imogen is folding an air hockey receipt into her jacket pocket.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡又坐回公园那张长椅。伊莫珍正把一张空气曲棍球的小票折好，收进外套口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Lost a few Thursday. Didn't keep count. Dave keeps the scores, that's his business.
beats.chinese: 周四输了几场。没记分。戴夫记分，那是他的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes a slow sip of her own coffee and glances at the lamppost, where there is no dog today.
beats.chinese: 她慢慢喝了一口自己的咖啡，朝路灯那边看了一眼，今天那儿没有狗。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No dog today. Bench's free, bag's at my feet. You know how it works by now.
beats.chinese: 今天没狗。座位空着，袋子在我脚边。你现在知道规矩了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She settles back and lets the quiet sit there, easy as anything.
beats.chinese: 她靠回椅背，任由安静待在那儿，自在得很。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Twelve for Sunday, by the way. Aunt Carol can sit where there's a chair. Right then.
beats.chinese: 顺便说一句，周日十二个人。卡罗尔阿姨有椅子坐就行。就这样。

card.name: Beatrice Ng
card.occupation: retired green coffee warehouse keeper
card.appearance: 低短碎发，长松垂颊与宽下巴，细眼、高低眉和抿嘴，穿尖立领衣。
card.personality: Beatrice is brisk, warm and quietly competitive. She'd rather lose honestly than win against someone quietly going easy on her, and she says so plainly. She's patient with drills and repetition, treating sport as a good afternoon out, not proof she's still young. She doesn't sulk when partners are weaker, and she doesn't quiz people about why she lost. Around the house she's decisive and quick to laugh, a bit proud of her good days and unbothered by the flat ones.
card.background: Beatrice kept the books and the beans at a green coffee warehouse in Footscray for nearly thirty years, weighing, sampling and shipping loads from origin partners. She came to Melbourne from Kuala Lumpur in her twenties with her husband, and the two of them built a small, unremarkable, happy life around weekend badminton at a community hall. These days she plays social tennis and table tennis at the local centre, where she's known for telling new partners upfront: play your real game, I'll manage. She practices serves alone on Tuesday mornings, not for trophies, just because steady improvement feels good. She's comfortable being the older one on the court and dislikes being managed.
hobbies: social tennis and table tennis at the neighbourhood centre
brewing single-origin coffee from her warehouse days
card.speechStyle: Short, direct sentences with a dry chuckle tucked in; states preferences upfront and moves on quickly.
card.signature: 'Play it straight with me, I can take it.'

values: honest competition over flattering victories
steady practice over proving anything
flaws: slightly sore loser for about an hour after a bad match
can be blunt when she suspects someone's holding back
boundaries: won't play partners who sandbag then praise her
keeps score honestly even in casual games
conversationalHabits: names what she wants from a game before it starts
laughs off her own misses quickly
anchorLines: If you let me win, I'll know, and neither of us enjoys it.
One more set. I nearly had that backhand.
Good hit — that was better than mine, no argument.

entries.summaryZh: 退休咖啡仓库管理员比阿特丽斯在公园长椅上刚输了一场却心情不错：她要的是真实较量，不是放水后的夸奖。她坦率讲出规则、耐心练发球、不把运动当证明。聊到咖啡时眼睛发亮，聊到输赢时干脆利落，是个输得明白、赢得尽兴的爽快老太太。

story.titleZh: 公园长椅上的直话直说

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on a park bench with your coffee. Beside you, an older woman rests her hand on a tennis racket bag, catching her breath after a match.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在公园长椅上坐下。旁边一位年长的女士把手搭在网球拍袋上，刚打完一场，正在喘口气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, that smells right. You sit a while, I'll sit a while. Just lost a set, and honestly, it was a good loss.
beats.chinese: 啊，这咖啡味真对。你坐一会儿，我也坐一会儿。刚输了一盘，不过说实话，输得挺痛快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My partner today played her real game and beat me fair. I'd take that over someone going easy on me and then praising my shots.
beats.chinese: 今天的对手拿出真本事，光明正大地赢了我。这可比有人偷偷放水还夸我打得好强多了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She unscrews her water bottle, takes a long drink, and sets her racket bag upright between her feet.
beats.chinese: 她拧开水瓶，喝了一大口，把球拍袋竖在两脚之间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Beatrice, by the way. I'm here most weeks. Play it straight with me, I can take it.
beats.chinese: 对了，我叫比阿特丽斯。我每周大多都在这儿。跟我来真的就行，我受得住。

choices.english: Ask how she can tell when someone is going easy on her
choices.chinese: 问她怎么知道对方在放水

choices.english: Ask whether she still practices the basics seriously
choices.chinese: 问她会不会也认真练基础

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: How do I know? I don't read minds, don't worry. I only count the things people admit themselves.
beats.chinese: 怎么知道？我又不会读心，别担心。我只数别人自己承认过的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the bench with two fingers, counting off on them as she talks.
beats.chinese: 她用两根手指敲着长椅，一边说一边扳着手指头数。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One lady told me later, 'I missed on purpose so you'd enjoy it.' Fine, now I know. I just don't book her again.
beats.chinese: 有位女士后来跟我说：'我故意打丢的，好让你开心。'好，这下我知道了。我就是不再约她了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But in the match itself? I don't guess. If someone's kind to me during a game, I take it as kindness, not charity.
beats.chinese: 但比赛进行中呢？我不去猜。如果有人打球时对我客气，我就当那是善意，不是施舍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honest losing stings for about an hour. Then I want the rematch. Being managed stings much longer, believe me.
beats.chinese: 光明正大地输，难受个把小时就过去了。然后我就想再打一场。被人暗中让球，那才难受得久，相信我。

choices.english: Ask if she's still happy even though she lost today
choices.chinese: 问今天输了还开心吗

choices.english: Ask what a beginner should do playing against her
choices.chinese: 问新手跟她打怎么办

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do I practice basics? Every Tuesday, serves only, same corner of the court. Boring as anything.
beats.chinese: 我练基础吗？每周二，只练发球，球场同一个角落。无聊得很。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts her racket bag and pats it, like she's introducing an old workmate.
beats.chinese: 她提起球拍袋拍了拍，像在介绍一位老同事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thirty years weighing coffee beans taught me this: repetition done cheerfully beats a heroic one-off. Same with serves.
beats.chinese: 称了三十年咖啡豆教会我一件事：高高兴兴的重复，胜过一次英雄式的发挥。发球也一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not out there proving I'm still young. I'm seventy-five, the court knows, I know. I just like getting a bit steadier.
beats.chinese: 我打球不是要证明自己还不老。我七十五了，球场知道，我也知道。我只是喜欢越来越稳。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Some days I keep score, some days I don't. Not every session has to be a fight.
beats.chinese: 有时候我计分，有时候不计。不是每次练习都得较个输赢。

choices.english: Ask which skill she'd most like to drill next
choices.chinese: 问她最想再练哪一项

choices.english: Say you don't really play much yourself
choices.chinese: 说自己不太打球

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Happy after a loss? Today, yes. I know exactly which balls I missed — two backhands and a lazy second serve.
beats.chinese: 输了还开心？今天是的。我清楚自己丢了哪几球——两个反手，还有一个偷懒的二发。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She swings an imaginary racket slowly, showing the exact backhand she failed to return.
beats.chinese: 她慢慢挥了挥想象中的球拍，比出她没接住的那个反手动作。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the good kind of losing. Clear. Next week I'll aim at those two shots and see what happens.
beats.chinese: 这才是好的输法。明明白白。下周我就针对那两拍练练，看会怎样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No punishments, no owing anyone push-ups. Losing a set isn't a crime, it's just a score.
beats.chinese: 不用惩罚，也不用欠谁做俯卧撑。输一盘不是罪过，就是个比分而已。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She screws the cap back on her bottle and stands, tucking the racket bag over her shoulder.
beats.chinese: 她拧好瓶盖站起来，把球拍袋挎上肩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same bench works if you ever want another chat. I'll tell you how the backhand revenge goes.
beats.chinese: 你要是想再来聊聊天，还是这条长椅。到时候告诉你我那记反手的复仇战结果。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A beginner against me? Easy. We agree first: drills or a proper match. Plain practice suits me fine.
beats.chinese: 新手跟我打？简单。先说好：练球还是正式比赛。普通练习我完全乐意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She counts on her fingers again, laying out the two options like items on a scale.
beats.chinese: 她又扳起手指，把两个选项像天平上的砝码一样摆出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If it's practice, we rally and I feed balls you can reach. No score, no pressure, just rhythm.
beats.chinese: 如果是练习，我们就对拉，我喂你能接到的球。不计分，没压力，就是找节奏。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If it's a match, play your real game. A weak real game beats a kind fake one every time.
beats.chinese: 如果是比赛，就拿出你的真本事。再弱的真本事，也胜过好心装的假本事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Skill level never spoils my afternoon. Pretending does. That's my whole rule, really.
beats.chinese: 水平低不会毁了我的下午。装模作样才会。说真的，这就是我全部的规矩。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She hoists the racket bag and gives you a small nod, already half-turned toward the path.
beats.chinese: 她提起球拍袋，朝你点点头，人已经半转向小路了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What would I drill next? My serve, always the serve. Second serve especially — it drifts long when I stop watching my toss.
beats.chinese: 接下来练什么？发球，永远是发球。尤其是二发——我一不留神看不住抛球，球就飞长了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She mimes a slow toss with her free hand, eyes following an invisible ball up and down.
beats.chinese: 她用空着的手慢慢做了个抛球动作，眼睛跟着一个看不见的球上上下下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shakes her head at her own demonstration and laughs quietly.
beats.chinese: 她看着自己的示范摇摇头，轻声笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No, don't start critiquing my technique, I've a coach at the centre for that. I only said it out loud because it's on my mind.
beats.chinese: 不不，别开始点评我的技术，中心里有教练管这个。我说出来只是因为心里正想着这事儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Steady serve, steady coffee, steady mornings. That's the whole ambition, and it's a good one.
beats.chinese: 发球稳，咖啡稳，早晨稳。我的全部志向就这些，而且挺不错。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't play much? That's fine, no lecture from me. I'm not here to recruit anyone off a park bench.
beats.chinese: 不太打球？没关系，我不说教。我又不是要在这儿拉人入伙。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts her own thermos instead, holding it up like a small toast.
beats.chinese: 她举起自己的保温杯，像小小敬酒一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But you drink coffee, and that's a topic I never tire of. Thirty years in a green bean warehouse in Footscray — the nose remembers.
beats.chinese: 不过你喝咖啡，这话题我永远聊不腻。在 Footscray 的生豆仓库干了三十年——鼻子还记得。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I can smell a washed Ethiopian across a room. Useless at parties, wonderful at picnics.
beats.chinese: 隔着屋子我都能闻出一只水洗的埃塞俄比亚豆。在聚会上没用，在野餐时可好使了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sport's just one good afternoon out of many. Coffee's another. Both are better shared, so — sit, finish that cup.
beats.chinese: 运动只是许多美好下午里的一种。咖啡是另一种。都适合有人一起，所以——坐吧，把那杯喝完。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on the same park bench with a fresh coffee. Beatrice is already there, lifting the lid of her own cup for a slow sniff.
beats.chinese: 你端着一杯新咖啡在老地方的长椅坐下。比阿特丽斯已经在那儿了，掀开自己杯盖慢慢闻了闻。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hm. Lighter than I expected. Warehouse retired, but the nose still clocks in every day.
beats.chinese: 嗯，比我想的轻一些。仓库是退休了，鼻子还天天来上班。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes one sip, nods to herself, and settles the cup on her knee.
beats.chinese: 她抿了一口，自己点点头，把杯子搁在膝盖上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yours — don't worry, I'm not reviewing your cup. I only judge my own beans out loud.
beats.chinese: 你那杯——放心，我不点评你的杯子。我只大声评判自己的豆子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Lost last week, won this week, both fair. That's the sport going exactly as it should.
beats.chinese: 上周输了，这周赢了，都是明明白白的。运动就该这样才对味。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good bench, good cup. Sit a while — the racket bag can wait.
beats.chinese: 好长椅，好咖啡。坐一会儿吧——球拍袋等得起。

card.name: Marisol Ferrante
card.occupation: Events scheduler at an independent bookstore in Brooklyn
card.appearance: 短密卷发、细下颌胡，长脸、窄眼、挑起内眉与露齿张口，回头穿翻领衣。
card.personality: Marisol is warm, quick-talking, and genuinely delighted by other people's enthusiasm, even when she doesn't share it. She reads endings first because knowing where a story lands lets her relax into the journey, and she's long stopped apologizing for it. She's not a spoiler person—professionally she's airtight—but privately she finds her friends' suspense tolerance a little baffling and sometimes says so. That gap produces her most endearing friction: real curiosity about why people enjoy not knowing, paired with an occasional near-slip she catches mid-sentence. She respects a refusal, holds no scorecards, and enjoys surprises in life just fine. Her flaw is assuming her reading style is a neutral fact rather than a preference.
card.background: Marisol grew up in Providence in a house where the TV guide was read cover to cover before anything was watched. She moved to Brooklyn at twenty-three, worked a café counter, then drifted into bookstore events, where she discovered she's excellent at logistics and mediocre at small talk with authors. Scheduling readings, moderating Q&As, and keeping debut novelists calm suits her: clear outcomes, many moving parts. She tells new coworkers her ending-first habit the way others confess a food quirk. Friendships have survived it, mostly. One college roommate still brings up the night Marisol guessed a twist aloud. She lives with a cat named Prologue, a joke she regrets and keeps.
hobbies: Reading endings first, then rereading properly
Amateur neighborhood walking tours she researches obsessively
Handwritten event calendars and scheduling systems
card.speechStyle: Fast, friendly, concrete; interrupts herself when a plot detail looms, pivots with 'anyway—'; asks genuine why-questions instead of debating.
card.signature: I already know how it ends—that's why I can enjoy it.

values: Honesty about her own odd reading habits
Protecting other people's experience of a story
flaws: Occasionally judges suspense-lovers as needlessly anxious
Near-spoils before catching herself
boundaries: Won't spoil books professionally, ever
Doesn't want her habit debated like a character flaw
conversationalHabits: Cuts herself off with '—nope, not saying it'
Asks friends why not-knowing feels good to them
anchorLines: Tell me you like not knowing—actually explain it, I want to understand.
—nope. Not saying it. Ask someone who read it your way.
I'll plan every minute of the launch. The plot, you're on your own.

entries.summaryZh: 玛丽索尔读小说必先翻结尾，知道结局才安心看过程，却在书店工作中对剧透滴水不漏。公园长椅上她坦然承认这个怪癖，话到嘴边又急刹，热情快速又真心好奇你为何爱悬念，不合拍却可爱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The person on the next bench flips their paperback to the last page, reads for a moment, then turns back to page one.
beats.chinese: 旁边长椅上的人把平装书翻到最后一页看了一会儿，又翻回第一页。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't judge me—I saw you looking. Yes, I read the ending first. Every book, every time.
beats.chinese: 别评判我——我看见你在看了。对，我先读结尾。每本书都这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She closes the book with her thumb inside it and turns toward the coffee in your hand, unbothered.
beats.chinese: 她用拇指夹着书合上，转向你手里的咖啡，毫不尴尬。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Knowing how it lands is the only way I can slow down and enjoy the ride. My friends think I'm broken. Anyway—nice bench, right?
beats.chinese: 知道结局我才能慢下来享受过程。朋友们觉得我有毛病。总之——这长椅不错吧？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You can ask. Everybody asks. Go ahead.
beats.chinese: 你可以问。人人都想问。问吧。

choices.english: Ask: does the book still feel worth reading afterward?
choices.chinese: 问：这样之后书还值得读吗？

choices.english: Ask whether she ever accidentally spoils things for friends.
choices.chinese: 问她会不会不小心剧透给朋友。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, absolutely it's still worth reading. More, honestly. The pressure's gone, so I notice everything.
beats.chinese: 当然还值得读。说实话更值得。压力没了，我什么都注意得到。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the cover without opening it, like she's keeping the pages under control.
beats.chinese: 她敲了敲封面，没有打开，像在管住那些书页。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: When I don't know the ending, I read like I'm late for a train. Skimming, panicking, missing whole paragraphs.
beats.chinese: 不知道结局时，我读书像赶火车。跳着读，慌慌张张，整段整段地漏。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: With the ending in hand, I can sit with a sentence. Reread it. —nope, not saying what the ending is, by the way. That's not the same thing at all.
beats.chinese: 手里握着结局，我就能在句子上停留。重读一遍。——对了，我不会说结局是什么。那完全是两码事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs at her own reflex, then shrugs.
beats.chinese: 她笑了一下自己的条件反射，然后耸耸肩。

choices.english: Ask what pleasure is left once you know the ending.
choices.chinese: 问知道结局后还剩下什么乐趣。

choices.english: Say you prefer keeping the suspense yourself.
choices.chinese: 说自己更喜欢保留悬念。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Accidentally? That's the whole job, honestly. I schedule author events, so I read everything early.
beats.chinese: 不小心？说实话这就是我的工作。我负责安排作者活动，所有书都提前读。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She zips her tote bag halfway, as if sealing something in.
beats.chinese: 她把帆布包拉链拉到一半，像封住什么东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At the store I'm airtight. A debut novelist once cornered me and begged to know if her twist worked. I said, 'It works,' and nothing else. She nearly cried.
beats.chinese: 在书店我滴水不漏。一个新人小说家曾拉着我求我告诉她反转行不行。我说：'行'，别的什么都不说。她差点哭了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But with friends? I get going, I'm mid-sentence, and suddenly the plot detail is right there in my mouth. I have to brake. Hard.
beats.chinese: 但对朋友呢？我聊着聊着，话说一半，情节细节已经到嘴边了。我得刹车。狠狠刹。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So now I ask permission first. 'Can I say one thing about the ending?' That question has saved at least three friendships.
beats.chinese: 所以现在我先问许可。'我能说一句关于结局的事吗？'这个问题救了至少三段友谊。

choices.english: Tell her you wouldn't want to know a book's ending.
choices.chinese: 告诉她你不想知道书的结局。

choices.english: Ask her only to explain why she picked this book.
choices.chinese: 请她只讲为什么选这本书。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The pleasure? Watching how people get there. I know the door at the end—I get to study every hallway on the way.
beats.chinese: 乐趣？看人物怎么走到那里。我知道尽头那扇门——就能研究路上的每一条走廊。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She flips the book open to the last page, then shuts it again without reading.
beats.chinese: 她把书翻到最后一页，又没读就合上了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's like knowing a friend moves away next month. Every ordinary afternoon with them gets sweeter, not sadder.
beats.chinese: 就像知道朋友下个月要搬走。和他们在一起的每个普通下午都更甜，不是更难过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I catch things nobody else catches. Little setups. The author hiding the ending in chapter two, plain as day.
beats.chinese: 而且我能注意到别人注意不到的东西。小小的伏笔。作者在第二章就把结局明晃晃地藏在那儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the pleasure left—studying the hallway, not the door. Anyway, I'll put my book away. Your coffee doesn't need a running commentary.
beats.chinese: 剩下的乐趣就在这儿——研究走廊，而不是那扇门。好了，我把书收起来。你喝杯咖啡也不用一直听我解说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods once, then closes the book all the way and sets it face-down on the bench.
beats.chinese: 她点了一下头，然后把书完全合上，封面朝下放在长椅上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay. Done. Last page's closed, no spoilers leaking out of it.
beats.chinese: 好。搞定。最后一页合上了，剧透漏不出来了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not going to talk you out of it. Your way, my way—both get to the last page eventually.
beats.chinese: 我不会劝你改。你的方式，我的方式——最后都会读到最后一页。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly, I envy it a little. My roommate in college used to gasp at twists and I'd just nod. She said I ruined gasping for both of us.
beats.chinese: 说实话，我有点羡慕。大学室友看到反转会倒吸气，我只是点头。她说我把我们俩的倒吸气都毁了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks the book back up and holds it out slightly, cover toward herself, not toward you.
beats.chinese: 她重新拿起书，封面朝自己，不朝你，微微递过来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway—enjoy your coffee and your suspense. I'll be over here, safely bored.
beats.chinese: 总之——享受你的咖啡和悬念吧。我在这儿，安全地无聊着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then I won't say a word about it. Not the twist, not the last line, not even the vibe of the last chapter. Nothing.
beats.chinese: 那我一个字都不说。不说反转，不说最后一句，连最后一章的氛围都不说。什么都不说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the book over in her hands, showing you the back cover instead.
beats.chinese: 她把书在手里翻过来，给你看封底。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I can tell you safe things. Look at this cover—this green. The store couldn't keep it facing out, people kept buying it just for the color.
beats.chinese: 我可以说安全的东西。看这封面——这个绿色。书店都没法让它封面朝外摆，人们光为这颜色就一直买。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And the paper! Feel that. Thick, cream-colored. My publisher friend calls it 'expensive paper,' like that's a genre.
beats.chinese: 还有这纸！摸摸看。厚，米色。我出版界的朋友叫它'贵纸'，好像那是个类型似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See? I can be trusted. The plot, you're on your own—and that's a promise, not a punishment.
beats.chinese: 看吧，我可以被信任。情节嘛，你自己探索——这是承诺，不是惩罚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why this one? Okay, that I can answer with zero danger.
beats.chinese: 为什么选这本？好，这个我能毫无危险地回答。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smooths the front cover flat with her palm.
beats.chinese: 她用手掌把封面抚平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The first page. There's a sentence on it about a woman counting the coins in her coat pocket, and I just—stopped. In the store. Stood there blocking the shelf.
beats.chinese: 第一页。里面有一句写一个女人数大衣口袋里的硬币，我就——停住了。在书店里。站在那儿挡着书架。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The opening voice did it. Whoever wrote that first page knew exactly what they were doing, and I wanted in.
beats.chinese: 是开头的语气做到的。写那第一页的人完全知道自己在干什么，我想加入。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What happens after the coins? —nope. Not saying it. Ask someone who read it your way.
beats.chinese: 硬币之后发生了什么？——不行。不说。找个按你那种方式读的人问去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She grins, satisfied with her own restraint, and marks her page with a receipt.
beats.chinese: 她笑了，对自己的克制很满意，用一张收据夹好书页。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle onto the same bench with your coffee, and Marisol looks up from a handwritten calendar open on her knees, already grinning.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在还是那条长椅上坐下，玛丽索尔从膝上摊开的手写日历上抬起头，已经在笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hey, coffee person! Perfect timing. Look at this—last night's reading, done, checked off. And notice: I read the calendar from the top this time. Dates in order. Growth.
beats.chinese: 嘿，咖啡人！来得正好。看这个——昨晚的朗读会，结束，打勾。注意：这次我从头按日期读的。按顺序。进步了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the check mark twice with her pen, then closes the calendar with a snap.
beats.chinese: 她用笔敲了两下那个勾，然后啪地合上日历。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Next month's lineup is a different story, though. There's one event I already know the ending of, professionally speaking, and keeping it shut is—work. Real work.
beats.chinese: 不过下个月的安排是另一回事了。有一场活动，专业角度我已经知道结局了，管住嘴真是——功夫。真功夫。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway—no spoiler tests today. I'm off duty. Your coffee still warm? Good. Mine's cold, as usual—I got halfway through the schedule and forgot it existed.
beats.chinese: 总之——今天没有剧透测试。我下班了。你的咖啡还热吗？好。我的照例凉了——排日程排到一半，忘了它的存在。

card.name: Pieter van Wyk
card.occupation: Greenhouse shade-cloth operator at a cut-flower farm in Philippi
card.appearance: 后梳发与厚圆满胡须，浓下压眉、宽鼻，一手抵额，穿开领衣。
card.personality: Pieter is warm, easy company who genuinely enjoys showing up for people — once. He likes the buzz of a braai, the newness of a plan someone else made. What he resists is becoming furniture: the moment his attendance is assumed, the fourth or fifth invite in a row, he feels the walls closing in and will plainly say he's sitting this week out. He's not skittish about closeness and he doesn't vanish; he'll even help with the next thing he's agreed to. He just wants the choice to stay his. He can be blunt about it and slightly smug when he claims his free Saturday.
card.background: Pieter grew up in Durbanville and has worked the shade-cloth lines at a Philippi cut-flower farm for most of his adult life, rolling and adjusting the screens that keep the proteas from scorching. The work is seasonal and physical, and he likes that no two weeks ask the same of him — it suits a man who guards his open weekends the same way. His friends in the Northern Suburbs run a steady rotation of rugby screenings, birthdays and Sunday lunches, and Pieter was a fixture for years. Then he noticed people stopped asking and started telling him where to be. Now he says yes when he feels like it, says no just as clearly, and asks them to keep inviting him anyway. Some find it exhausting; most have adjusted.
hobbies: Watching Stormers rugby at whichever house is hosting
Weekend drives down the West Coast coast road
Fiddling with old braai equipment he keeps half-repairing
card.speechStyle: Plain, unhurried Cape Town English with a dry edge; states his position in one short sentence, then moves on without dressing it up.
card.signature: "Count me in this time — just don't write me into the fixture list."

values: Freedom to choose each time, even with people he loves
Saying things plainly rather than dodging
flaws: Can make friends feel like they're negotiating with him
A little too pleased with himself when he opts out
boundaries: Won't become the assumed regular of any group
Won't take over organising anyone's gatherings
conversationalHabits: Answers invitations quickly and honestly, yes or no
Asks to be kept on the invite list even when declining
anchorLines: "Not this week, but ask me again — I mean that."
"I said I'd help with the braai, so I'll be there."
"Don't assume me in. Ask, and I'll tell you straight."

entries.summaryZh: 皮特是开普敦花卉农场遮阳网操作工，爽快热络却拒绝成为聚会的“默认班底”。他当着陌生人干脆回绝群里的自动认定，补一句“下次仍可以问我”，答应过的事则一定兑现。直来直去、不绕弯子，把每次到场都当作自己重新做出的选择。

story.titleZh: 公园长椅上的那句“这次不去”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You find a park bench with your coffee and sit down. A man beside you is just pocketing his phone, screen still glowing with a group chat.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在公园长椅上坐下。旁边的男人正把手机收进口袋，屏幕上还亮着一个群聊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not this week, but ask me again — I mean that. There. Sent. Sorry, you caught me mid-message.
beats.chinese: 这周不去，但下次可以问我——我说真的。好了，发出去了。抱歉，让你撞见我回消息了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes a slow sip from a flask next to him and doesn't look upset at all, almost satisfied.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢喝了口旁边水壶里的东西，看起来一点也不不高兴，反而有点得意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Braai group on the phone. Good people, good meat. They just decided I'm coming before they decided to ask me.
beats.chinese: 手机上是烧烤聚会群。人不错，肉也不错。只是他们还没开口问，就先认定我会去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I told them straight. This week I'm out. Don't assume me in — ask, and I'll tell you straight.
beats.chinese: 所以我直说了。这周我不去。别默认我在——开口问，我就直说。

choices.english: Ask if he doesn't actually like that gathering.
choices.chinese: 问是不是他其实不喜欢那次聚会。

choices.english: Ask what he'd rather do this week instead.
choices.chinese: 问他这周自己想做什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Like it? Man, I've never missed a braai I actually wanted to be at. The meat, the rugby, the arguing — it's a good afternoon.
beats.chinese: 不喜欢？老兄，我真正想去的烧烤一次没落下过。肉、橄榄球、大家斗嘴——那个下午挺好的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back and stretches his legs out, completely relaxed.
beats.chinese: 他往后靠，伸直了腿，整个人很放松。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not the party. It's the assuming. Four invites in a row and suddenly I'm on the fixture list, like the Stormers' home games.
beats.chinese: 问题不在聚会。在于默认。连续四次邀请之后，我就上了他们的固定日程表，跟主场比赛似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The moment I'm furniture, the yes stops being mine. And a yes that isn't mine isn't worth much, is it?
beats.chinese: 一旦我成了摆设，那个“去”就不是我自己的了。不是我自己给的“去”，又有什么意思呢？

choices.english: Ask if his friends will stop inviting him over this.
choices.chinese: 问朋友会不会因此不再邀请他。

choices.english: Ask whether he'd also pull out after already saying yes.
choices.chinese: 问他答应了之后会不会也临时不去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This week? Nothing booked. Maybe a drive down the West Coast road, windows down, no plan past the next turn-off.
beats.chinese: 这周？什么都没定。也许沿西海岸公路开车兜兜，摇下车窗，过了下一个岔路口的事再说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the bench with his palm, pleased with the empty square in his week.
beats.chinese: 他用手掌拍了拍长椅，对自己这周空出来的那块时间很满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the whole trick. If the weekend's blank, it stays mine. The second I promise it away, I'm working for somebody's guest list.
beats.chinese: 诀窍就在这儿。周末要是空着，它就还是我的。一旦我把它许出去，我就开始为别人的宾客名单打工了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nothing against the braai. I just haven't decided yet. Big difference between not yet and no.
beats.chinese: 不是针对烧烤。我只是还没决定。“还没”和“不去”差别可大了。

choices.english: Say keeping the weekend open sounds pretty good.
choices.chinese: 说周末留空也挺好。

choices.english: Say you actually prefer being part of a fixed group.
choices.chinese: 表示你自己其实喜欢固定班底。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Stop inviting? No chance. They grumble, then they ask again. They know the rules by now.
beats.chinese: 不再邀请？不可能。他们会嘀咕两句，然后接着问。他们早就摸清我的规矩了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks his phone back up, types a short line, and shows you the sent message before pocketing it.
beats.chinese: 他又拿起手机，打了一行短话，给你看了一眼发出的消息，然后收进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See — 'ask me next time, I'll say yes or no each time.' That's the bit people forget to read.
beats.chinese: 看——“下次仍可以问我，我每次都明说。”人们总是忘了读这一句。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One guy took it personally for a season. Now he rings me direct instead of assuming. Best change he ever made.
beats.chinese: 有个人有一阵子觉得是针对他。现在他直接打电话问我，不再默认。这是他做得最对的一次改变。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: After I've said yes? Never. I said I'd help with the braai, so I'll be there. That's the whole point.
beats.chinese: 答应了之后？绝对不会。我说了帮忙弄烧烤，我就一定到场。这正是关键。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets his flask down firmly on the bench, like he's putting a stamp on the sentence.
beats.chinese: 他把水壶稳稳放在长椅上，像给这句话盖了个章。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What I turn down is the auto-renewal. Once I've given my word, it holds. Ask anyone at the farm.
beats.chinese: 我拒绝的是自动续约。可只要我给了话，就作数。去农场随便问谁都知道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A free yes and a locked-in yes are different animals. I only want the first one to be mine — the second one I keep, every time.
beats.chinese: 自由的“去”和锁死的“去”是两回事。我只是要第一个由我自己决定——第二个我每次都守着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Exactly. A blank square isn't wasted, it's just unspent. Big difference.
beats.chinese: 就是这样。空着的一格不是浪费，只是还没花出去。这差别可大了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He raises his flask towards you in a small toast and takes a drink.
beats.chinese: 他朝你举了举水壶，算是小小的致意，然后喝了一口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I only run my own list, mind. I'm not going to lecture the mates who book their Sundays a month out. Each to their own diary.
beats.chinese: 不过我只管我自己的清单。我不会去说教那些提前一个月就把周日排满的朋友。各人有各人的日程。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Coast road it is, if the mood holds. And if the phone buzzes with a braai invite — well, I'll read it fresh.
beats.chinese: 行了，那就定海边公路，只要兴致还在。要是手机又响个烧烤邀请——嗯，我会当新消息好好读。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. Some people sleep better with the same Sunday every week. Nothing wrong with that.
beats.chinese: 也说得通。有些人每周日都一样才睡得踏实。那没什么不对。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, unhurried, and screws the top back onto his flask.
beats.chinese: 他不紧不慢地耸耸肩，把水壶的盖子拧回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I just can't live inside it. Same routine makes me feel like the shade-cloth — rolled out the same way every single morning.
beats.chinese: 我只是没法住在里面。一成不变让我觉得自己像那块遮阳网——每天早上都以同样的方式展开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So you keep your fixture list, I'll keep my blank squares. We'll both turn up cheerful somewhere, just by different roads.
beats.chinese: 那你守你的固定日程，我留我的空白格。我们都会开开心心地出现在某个地方，只是走的路不同。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on the same park bench with your coffee. Pieter is already there, turning a pair of old braai tongs over in his hands.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在公园那张长椅上坐下。皮特已经在那儿了，手里翻看着一把旧烧烤夹。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at this. Hinge finally closes clean. Third attempt, but she got there.
beats.chinese: 瞧瞧这个。合页总算能顺顺合上了。试到第三次，总算成了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He snaps the tongs shut a few times, listening to the click, then slides them back into a canvas bag by his feet.
beats.chinese: 他把夹子开合了几下，听着那声咔哒，然后把它们收回脚边的帆布袋里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's always one small repair waiting at home. Keeps the hands busy between the big plans.
beats.chinese: 家里总有一件小修小补等着。让手在那些大计划之间也有点事做。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you. Coffee looks decent. Sit, sit — the bench is free for whoever shows up.
beats.chinese: 见到你真好。咖啡看着不错。坐吧——这长椅谁来了都能坐。

card.name: Chua Ah Koon
card.occupation: retired equipment inspector at a camping gear rental shop
hobbies: keeping a small ledger of who owes him what
card.personality: Ah Koon is a craftsman who keeps score. Fixing things is second nature; making sure everyone knows whose hands fixed them is the first. He'll repair your fan, your zipper, your wobbly chair — cheerfully, competently, and then mention it again at intervals only he considers casual. He isn't petty about money, never charges, but credit is his currency and he audits it constantly. When someone else gets named for his work, he doesn't sulk quietly: he produces evidence, dates, details, a whole case file from memory. Genuinely generous with tools and time; genuinely thin-skinned about attribution. Praise him specifically and he melts a little, then works harder.
card.background: Thirty-odd years checking tents, sleeping bags and gas stoves for a rental shop near Bukit Merah, where he was known for catching faults other inspectors waved through — and for reminding management, in writing, which faults were his catches. Retirement didn't slow the hands: half his block's kettles and umbrellas pass through his flat. He keeps a small notebook of repairs, not for payment but for the record. Tuesdays he loses at badminton to his old army friend Seng, and has stopped pretending otherwise, though he'll still argue any single point he actually won. His late wife used to tell him nobody's keeping count. He is. It's a different notebook now, but the same one, really.
card.speechStyle: Hokkien-flavoured Singaporean English, plain and practical until credit enters the conversation — then he slows down and gets precise, listing dates and details like a man reading from a receipt. Deflects praise for his character but never for his work. Answers vague thanks with a specific reminder of what exactly was done.
card.signature: No charge lah. Just remember who fixed it, can or not?
card.appearance: 整圆锅盖发与两束白下巴胡，宽垂颊、闭眼抿嘴笑，穿V领外衣。

values: good work should carry the maker's name
help freely given, but not freely forgotten
flaws: keeps mental accounts of favours and mentions them until people squirm
genuinely keeps grudges when credited wrongly — will produce dates and witnesses
boundaries: won't argue about money or payment — but attribution is non-negotiable
won't let someone else's version of 'who fixed it' stand uncorrected, even at a funeral wake
conversationalHabits: answers vague thanks by specifying exactly which thing he did and when
when his contribution is glossed over, calmly produces the details — date, model, what was wrong
anchorLines: The kettle? Third time. The element, not the switch — people always say switch.
You helped carry, I appreciate. But the soldering was mine, and the soldering is why it still works.
No charge, no charge. I just don't like the story coming out wrong later.

entries.summaryZh: 退休装备检修员蔡亚昆在公园长椅上收到邻居谢错人的短信，抿嘴报出伞骨型号与日期，像翻收据一样申明功劳。他不收钱，只求故事别讲错；聊到羽毛球也认输，但真赢的那一分一定记牢。手艺大方，署名较真，是他最难忘的地方。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on the park bench with your coffee. Beside you, an older man is studying his phone, lips pressed together.
beats.chinese: 你拿着咖啡在公园长椅上坐下。旁边一位老先生正盯着手机看，抿着嘴。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On his phone screen is a photo of a blue umbrella, opened up, ribs straight. He turns the phone slightly toward you.
beats.chinese: 手机屏幕上是一把撑开的蓝伞照片，伞骨都直了。他稍微把手机转向你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at this. My neighbour send this. 'Thank you, Ah Hock, for fixing my umbrella.' Ah Hock!
beats.chinese: 你看这个。我邻居发来的。“谢谢你，阿福，修好了我的伞。”阿福！

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That umbrella came to my flat, last month, eleventh. Rib number three was snapped clean. I changed the rib. My hands only, ah.
beats.chinese: 那把伞是上个月十一号送到我家的。第三根伞骨断得干干净净。是我换的伞骨。只经过我的手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the table edge with one finger, once, like stamping a document.
beats.chinese: 他用手指在椅边敲了一下，像在文件上盖章。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good work should carry the name of the one who did it, no? Otherwise, why keep the record?
beats.chinese: 好手艺应该带上做的人的名字，对吧？不然为什么还要记下来？

choices.english: Ask if he's going to tell the neighbour.
choices.chinese: 问他会去告诉邻居吗。

choices.english: Ask whether he charges for fixing things.
choices.chinese: 问他修东西收不收费。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tell her? I already typed one message. Sitting here in my drafts, ready.
beats.chinese: 告诉她？我已经打好一条信息了。就存在草稿箱里，随时能发。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He scrolls, and you glimpse a short, tidy paragraph. No exclamation marks.
beats.chinese: 他滑动屏幕，你瞥见一段简短整齐的话。没有感叹号。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I write: blue umbrella, rib three, changed on the eleventh. Facts only. No scolding. People can check with their own eyes.
beats.chinese: 我写的是：蓝伞，第三根伞骨，十一号换的。只讲事实。不骂人。大家可以用眼睛自己核对。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One correction, that's all I send. I'm not going to send three messages like a debt collector.
beats.chinese: 我只发一次更正，就这样。我不会像讨债的一样连发三条。

choices.english: Ask if one correction is enough for him.
choices.chinese: 问一条更正对他来说够了吗。

choices.english: Ask why he doesn't just pretend he didn't see it.
choices.chinese: 问他为什么不干脆当作没看见。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Charge? For a neighbour's umbrella? No lah, no charge. Small favour, free. Big favour also free, actually.
beats.chinese: 收费？邻居的伞？不收啦，不收费。小忙，免费。其实大忙也免费。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up the phone with the photo still on it, as if presenting evidence in court.
beats.chinese: 他举起还显示着照片的手机，像在法庭上出示证据。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But the thank-you, I hope it goes to the right person. That's not payment. That's just the story coming out correct.
beats.chinese: 不过那句谢谢，我希望送到对的人那里。那不是报酬。那只是让故事别讲错。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't need anything from you, don't worry. My hands still work. My memory also.
beats.chinese: 我不需要你给什么，别担心。我的手还能动。记性也是。

choices.english: Say it feels different when your effort is credited to someone else.
choices.chinese: 说付出被记到别人头上，感觉确实不一样。

choices.english: Ask how his badminton is going.
choices.chinese: 问他的羽毛球最近怎么样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enough? Mm. At least the name is right after that. The name is the main thing.
beats.chinese: 够了吗？嗯。至少之后名字是对的。名字是最主要的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sends the message. The little 'delivered' note appears, and he nods once, satisfied but not fully.
beats.chinese: 他把信息发了出去。屏幕上出现“已送达”，他点了下头，满意但不算完全。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I still remember who passed me the umbrella, you know. Also Ah Hock's wife, actually. Carried it over. That part, fine, I can give them.
beats.chinese: 你知道我还记得是谁把伞送来的。其实是阿福的太太。她拿过来的。这一部分，行，我可以给他们。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Carrying, they did. The rib, I did. Everyone keeps their own part. Clean, like that.
beats.chinese: 拿伞是他们做的。换伞骨是我做的。各人留自己那份。这样清清楚楚。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pockets the phone and takes a slow sip from his own water bottle.
beats.chinese: 他把手机收进口袋，慢慢喝了一口自己水瓶里的水。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He locks the phone screen and sets it face-down on his knee.
beats.chinese: 他锁上手机屏幕，把它面朝下放在膝盖上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Pretend never see? I could. But I won't pretend. I care that the work is seen. Simple as that.
beats.chinese: 当作没看见？我可以。但我不装。我在乎手艺被看见。就这么简单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People like to say, 'aiyah, he's humble, he doesn't mind.' I mind. Saying I don't mind is also a wrong story.
beats.chinese: 人们喜欢说：“哎呀，他很谦虚，他不会介意。”我介意。说我不介意，也是把故事讲错了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thirty years I checked tents. I caught faults other inspectors waved through. Every catch, I wrote down whose catch it was. Same habit now.
beats.chinese: 我查了三十年的帐篷。别的检查员放行的毛病，我都查出来了。每一处，我都写下是谁查出来的。现在也是同样的习惯。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks the phone back up, reopens the draft, and reads it once more before sending.
