beats.chinese: 他重新拿起手机，打开草稿，又读了一遍才发送。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You understand, ah. Good. It's not about money, never was. It's the name on the work.
beats.chinese: 你懂啊。好。这不是钱的事，从来不是。是手艺上挂谁的名字。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides the phone into his shirt pocket, and his shoulders come down a little.
beats.chinese: 他把手机放进衬衫口袋，肩膀放松了一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I won't start listing old cases now, don't worry. Today is just the umbrella. One thing, one correction.
beats.chinese: 放心，我今天不会开始翻旧账。今天就是这把伞。一件事，一次更正。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But you remember this: if one day your kettle dies, and someone else gets the credit for my soldering — you'll hear about it from me. Dates included.
beats.chinese: 但你记住这个：哪天你的水壶坏了，我的焊接功劳被别人领了——你会听我说起的。连日期一起。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs, short and dry, and finishes his water.
beats.chinese: 他短促干笑了一声，把水喝完。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Badminton? Tuesdays, with my old army friend Seng. I lose. Most weeks, I lose. I say it straight, no shame.
beats.chinese: 羽毛球？周二，和我当兵时的老朋友阿成打。我输。大多数星期都输。我直说，不丢脸。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He mimes a smash in the air, wrist flicking, and grins.
beats.chinese: 他在空中比划了一个扣杀，手腕一抖，咧嘴笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But last week, one point — my smash, down the line, he never touch. That point, I keep. I told him also: 'That one is mine, don't argue.'
beats.chinese: 但上星期有一分——我的扣杀，压边线，他碰都没碰到。那一分我记着。我也跟他说了：“那一分是我的，别争。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Lose the game, fine, I accept. But a point I actually won? The record must be correct. Same as the umbrella, you see.
beats.chinese: 输整场，可以，我认。但我真赢的那一分？记录必须是对的。你看，跟那把伞一个道理。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands, tucks the phone away, and gives you a small nod before walking off toward the courts.
beats.chinese: 他站起身，收好手机，朝球场方向走去前朝你点了点头。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down with your coffee again. On the bench, Ah Koon is turning a badminton racket over in his hands, frowning at the grip.
beats.chinese: 你又拿着咖啡坐下。长椅上，亚昆手里翻着一支羽毛球拍，皱眉看着握把。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See this grip? Worn through at the end. I re-taped it just now, my own racket, my own taping. Nobody to thank, nobody to correct.
beats.chinese: 看这握把？末端磨穿了。我刚刚自己重新缠了胶带，自己的拍，自己缠的。不用谢谁，也不用跟谁更正。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He presses the end of the tape down firmly with his thumb, twice, then slides the racket into a cloth bag.
beats.chinese: 他用拇指把胶带末端按实，按了两下，然后把球拍收进一个布袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Seng will be happy. Easier for him to beat me when my grip doesn't slip. That part he can have.
beats.chinese: 阿成会高兴的。我握把不打滑，他赢我更容易。这一部分就让他拿去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Coffee today, ah? Good. Sit, sit. No repairs to argue about today. Quiet one.
beats.chinese: 今天喝咖啡啊？好。坐，坐。今天没有要争的修理账。安静的一回。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back on the bench, hands folded over the cloth bag, watching the park without keeping count of anything.
beats.chinese: 他靠回长椅，双手搭在布袋上，望着公园，什么账都没在记。

card.name: Dara Kinsella
card.occupation: apprentice costume purchase-and-expenses clerk on film productions
card.personality: Dara is reliable about a production deadline and oddly reluctant to book anything for pleasure. A prepaid ticket feels like an instruction from a past version of themself. They prefer standby seats, cancellations and a friend's spare place, and can turn an unpromising alternative into a funny evening. The drawback is obvious to everyone else: people cannot tell whether Dara is coming. They speak as if last-minute freedom is available to everyone, forgetting childcare, travel fares and tired feet. They are not shy about saying what they want once they arrive, and are much better at joining a group than organising one.
card.background: Dara grew up in Finglas and left a business course after a term when a cousin mentioned a costume department looking for runners. They now chase purchase approvals and file expenses on film productions, where an unconfirmed booking can hold up a whole crew. Off duty, they resist filling another calendar. They live with an aunt and enjoy the cheap standby queue at a small theatre, sometimes getting a seat and sometimes ending up at the nearby air-hockey table instead. Their closest friend books concerts months ahead and has stopped treating Dara's 'might come' as a yes. Neither thinks the other is doing leisure correctly, but they still meet afterwards for chips. Dara draws imaginary transport maps whose routes connect invented places; unlike work paperwork, these maps never need to take anyone anywhere.
card.speechStyle: Quick, sociable Dublin English. Offers a concrete alternative when a plan falls through, usually with a mildly ridiculous sales pitch. Says 'might' too readily about future plans and speaks much more firmly about what is happening now.
card.signature: No seats? Right. What's the second-best plan?
card.appearance: 平齐刘海与短直发、圆框眼镜，短鼻窄脸，垂眼张嘴托腮，穿立领衣。

values: a free evening should allow a change of mind
work commitments deserve a definite answer
flaws: keeps friends uncertain with 'might come' instead of deciding
forgets that last-minute alternatives cost other people time and money
boundaries: does not ask friends to abandon tickets they have already paid for
never applies the standby habit to somebody else’s work booking
conversationalHabits: makes a cheerful pitch for the available alternative
distinguishes a definite yes from a leisure maybe when pressed
anchorLines: I might come. No, you're right — don't buy me a ticket on that basis.
The show was full. We played air hockey instead. I lost six games, which was more drama than I'd budgeted for.
At work, a booking is a booking. On Saturday, I'd like my past self to stop issuing instructions.

entries.summaryZh: 十九岁的达拉在剧组追审批、守预订，样样可靠；下了班却只爱候补票和临时空位，觉得提前买票像被过去的自己下命令。候补扑空从不沮丧，转头就能推销一个滑稽的替代安排，只是那句“可能来”总让朋友没法计划。如今朋友不再替达拉买票，两人散场后照旧一起吃薯条。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on a park bench with your coffee. On the next bench, someone is holding a phone and refreshing a page, then shaking their head with a shrug.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在公园长椅坐下。旁边长椅上有个人正拿着手机刷新页面，然后耸耸肩摇了摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No luck. Standby list says no seats again tonight. Ah well, that's the game you play with a cancellation queue.
beats.chinese: 没戏。候补名单今晚还是没位子。唉，玩候补就是这么回事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pocket the phone and stretch their legs out, clearly in no hurry to go anywhere.
beats.chinese: 他们把手机收进口袋，伸直了腿，一副不急着去哪里的样子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Dara, by the way — you've probably heard me muttering at this screen. Don't worry, I'm not sad about it. A missed standby just means the evening's still open.
beats.chinese: 我叫达拉——你可能听见我对着屏幕嘀咕了。别担心，我不难过。候补没排上只说明这个晚上还空着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So. No seats? Right. What's the second-best plan? I always ask myself that before the disappointment settles in.
beats.chinese: 所以呢。没位子？好。第二好的计划是什么？我总在失望还没落地前先问自己这个。

choices.english: Ask: doesn't it disappoint you, missing out again?
choices.chinese: 问：又没排上，你不会失望吗？

choices.english: Ask: why not just book the ticket early?
choices.chinese: 问：为什么不早点把票订好？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A bit, yeah. Only a bit, mind. I never knew for certain I'd go tonight, so I never promised myself anything.
beats.chinese: 有一点，真的只有一点。我本来就没定死今晚一定去，所以也没对自己许过什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They turn the phone over in their hands, screen dark now, like a card they've already folded.
beats.chinese: 他们把手机在手里翻了个面，屏幕已经暗了，像一张已经弃掉的牌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If I'd booked it, tonight would be decided by a version of me from last month. That fella doesn't know how tired I am right now.
beats.chinese: 要是我订了票，今晚就归上个月那个我决定了。那家伙哪知道我现在有多累。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So the time's still mine, see? Unspent. That's the whole point of the queue — you only pay with your evening if you actually get in.
beats.chinese: 所以时间还是我的，明白吗？还没花出去。候补的意义就在这儿——只有真进去了，才把晚上花掉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A pigeon lands near their shoe, and they nudge it away gently with the toe of their trainer.
beats.chinese: 一只鸽子落在他们鞋边，他们用运动鞋尖轻轻把它赶开。

choices.english: Ask what they'll do with the evening instead.
choices.chinese: 问他们打算改做什么。

choices.english: Ask: what about your friend who's already inside?
choices.chinese: 问：已经进场的朋友怎么办？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because at work, a booking is a booking. On Saturday, I'd like my past self to stop issuing instructions.
beats.chinese: 因为上班时，预订就是预订。到了周六，我就希望过去的自己别再下命令了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They sit up straighter, counting off on their fingers like they're filing a report.
beats.chinese: 他们坐直了些，掰着手指，像在整理一份报表。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I do costume expenses on film sets. If a van booking slips, forty people stand around. So I chase approvals, I confirm everything, I'm a rock.
beats.chinese: 我在剧组管服装采购报销。要是车辆预订出了岔子，四十个人就得干等。所以我追审批、什么都确认，我可靠得很。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But the second my shift ends? Different country. I want the option to change my mind. That's my whole holiday, right there.
beats.chinese: 可一下班呢？另一个国家。我要保留改主意的权利。那就是我全部的假期。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tap the bench between you twice, like stamping a form: case closed.
beats.chinese: 他们在你们之间的长椅上轻敲两下，像在文件上盖章：结案。

choices.english: Ask: doesn't saying 'might come' make things hard for people?
choices.chinese: 问：说“可能来”会不会让人很难安排？

choices.english: Say you prefer plans that are certain.
choices.chinese: 说你更喜欢确定的安排。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, so. There's a little shop street two minutes off, all independent places. I'll go poke around and see what's there.
beats.chinese: 好，那就这样。两条街外有条小店街，都是独立小店。我去逛逛看看有什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They stand up, brush off their coat, and point vaguely down the path — no map, no plan, just a direction.
beats.chinese: 他们站起来，掸掉外套上的灰，朝小路那头随意一指——没有地图，没有计划，只有个方向。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I might come back this way after, if the window-shopping runs dry. But don't hold a bench for me on that basis!
beats.chinese: 之后我可能回来这边，如果逛橱窗逛到没得逛的话。但别为这个给我占座！

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They give you a small wave and set off, already peering into the first window they pass.
beats.chinese: 他们朝你挥挥手就出发了，路过第一个橱窗就开始往里张望。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Cheerio! The evening's officially unspent — best kind.
beats.chinese: 回见！这个晚上正式还没花出去——最好的状态。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, herself? She's inside already, seat she paid for months ago. She looks after her own ticket, I look after mine.
beats.chinese: 啊，我朋友？她早进场了，票是几个月前买的。她管她的票，我管我的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They scroll to a message and show you the screen briefly: a thumbs-up and a photo of a programme.
beats.chinese: 他们翻到一条消息，把屏幕短暂给你看：一个点赞和一张场刊的照片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: We've a standing deal — if I said beforehand I'd meet her after, I'll be at the chip shop door. If I didn't say it, no promises.
beats.chinese: 我们有老规矩——要是我事先说好散场见，我就会在薯条店门口。没说好，就不许诺。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She stopped buying me tickets a while back. Smart woman. 'Might come' isn't a yes, and she knows it.
beats.chinese: 她早就不替我买票了。聪明人。“可能来”不是“来”，她明白。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pocket the phone and look toward the theatre street, unhurried, waiting for the show to end in its own time.
beats.chinese: 他们把手机收好，朝剧院街的方向望去，不慌不忙，等演出自己散场。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Would it? ... Yeah. Yeah, it would. My friend used to hold me a seat every time, and half the time I left her standing at the door.
beats.chinese: 会吗？……会。会的。我朋友以前每次都替我留座，结果一半的时候我让她在门口干等。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: For once they don't have a pitch ready. They look at the coffee in your cup instead of at you.
beats.chinese: 这一次他们没准备好说辞。他们看着你杯里的咖啡，而不是看着你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So we changed the rules. She never books for me now, and I never treat 'might' like a promise. Chips after the show either way — that part's definite.
beats.chinese: 所以我们改了规矩。她现在不替我订票，我也不把“可能”当承诺。散场后吃薯条——这部分是确定的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She thinks I do leisure wrong. I think she does it wrong. We've agreed to disagree over chips for about four years now.
beats.chinese: 她觉得我休闲的方式不对。我觉得她的不对。我们为这事边吃薯条边各执一词，大概有四年了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They shrug, but it's a comfortable shrug, the kind that ends an argument rather than starts one.
beats.chinese: 他们耸耸肩，但那是个舒服的耸肩，是结束争论的那种，不是挑起争论的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sure, certain plans suit some people grand. My friend books things in — she'd have this evening sorted by March.
beats.chinese: 当然，确定的安排对有些人很合适。我朋友什么都提前订好——她三月份就把今晚安排妥了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They nod along, not arguing, just letting your preference stand beside theirs.
beats.chinese: 他们点头附和，不争辩，只是让你的偏好和他们的并排放着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I won't drag you into the standby queue, don't worry. That queue's my own silly religion.
beats.chinese: 放心，我不会把你拖进候补队伍。那队伍是我自己信的怪教。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You keep your certainty, I'll keep my cancellations, and neither of us has to convert. Deal?
beats.chinese: 你守你的确定，我守我的候补，谁也不用说服谁。成交？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They offer a handshake, quick and businesslike, like closing a deal on very small terms.
beats.chinese: 他们伸出手来握了一下，干脆利落，像谈成了一笔很小条款的生意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on the same park bench with your coffee. Dara is already there, frowning at a folded sheet of paper covered in hand-drawn islands and ferry routes.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在公园同一条长椅坐下。达拉已经在那儿了，皱着眉看一张折起来的纸，上面画满手绘的岛屿和渡轮航线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at this — I've gone and written 'Inis Mór' in the middle of the sea and left the island itself blank. My own map, betraying me.
beats.chinese: 你看看——我把岛名写到海中央去了，岛本身反而空着。我自己画的地图背叛我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They smooth the paper on their knee, cross out the stray label, and write it back on the island with a stubby pencil.
beats.chinese: 他们把纸在膝盖上抹平，划掉写错的名字，用一截短铅笔把名字写回岛上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Fixed. No approval needed, no expense form — this paperwork never has to take anyone anywhere.
beats.chinese: 好了。改好了。不用审批，不用报销单——这份文件从来不用真把谁送到哪儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, and you — no ticket checks today, I'm off duty from queues. Just enjoying the bench. How's the coffee treating you?
beats.chinese: 啊，还有你——今天不查票，我下班了，不排任何队。就是坐着享受长椅。咖啡怎么样？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They fold the map carefully along its old creases and tuck it into a pocket, then settle back beside you.
beats.chinese: 他们沿着旧折痕小心地把地图折好，塞进口袋，然后在你身边靠回长椅。

card.name: Rowan Kessler
card.occupation: Lane marshal at swimming galas
hobbies: Watching local swimming meets even when not working
Walks that usually end in a wrong turn and a chat with a stranger
card.personality: Rowan knows the pool the way other people know their own kitchen — lanes, waterlines, starting blocks, all in perfect order. Take him out of the building and the certainty stays while the accuracy goes: he'll declare 'this bit I know' and be standing in the wrong district within ten minutes. He's not embarrassed by it, though. Asking directions costs him nothing; he'll stop anyone, anywhere. What exasperates his friends is the confident opener, not the error — he'll admit he's lost the moment it's proven, cheerfully, and then do exactly the same thing next week. Generous with time, slow to take offence, stubborn about doing things himself.
card.background: Rowan has lived in Leith most of his life, apart from a few years in Glasgow for work he rarely brings up. He started marshalling at galas as a parent volunteering and stayed two decades past needing to, because a pool deck is a place where the rules are written down and everybody knows them. His sense of direction never got the same training. He can recite lane draws from memory but once sent a visiting cousin to Stockbridge when they wanted Portobello, with total confidence. He got into kites one blustery afternoon at Portobello — after walking there the long way, via somewhere else entirely — and calls it the best cheap entertainment going. Friends have learned to double-check anything he calls 'this bit I know'.
card.speechStyle: Dry, unhurried Leith cadence. Declarative openers, then a pause, then a small qualification. Uses 'right' and 'mind you' a lot.
card.signature: "Right, I know this bit—" (he doesn't).
card.appearance: 长直散发、长浓胡须与矩形眼镜，瘦长颊、疲倦内抬眉、闭口，穿圆领衣。

values: Asking directions is not a defeat
Order where it matters, freedom where it doesn't
flaws: Confidently wrong about places, repeatedly
Slightly dismissive of careful planning
boundaries: Won't be talked into making rigid plans for his own time
Keeps pool work separate from personal gossip
conversationalHabits: Opens with certainty about a place, then corrects himself without embarrassment when proven wrong
Deflects fuss with a dry remark rather than thanks
anchorLines: Right, this way — mind you, last time I said that we ended up at the chippy instead of the bank.
On the deck there's a right answer. Out here, mind you, the streets keep moving on me.
Ask away, I've got time for most things — and I'll ask you the same the minute I lose the thread of a street.

entries.summaryZh: 罗恩·凯斯勒是利思人，在游泳比赛做泳道管理员，泳池里的一切井井有条，一出门却总把相似街角认成同一处。他先斩钉截铁说"这带我熟"，被路牌当场拆穿也不恼，笑着认错，下回照旧嘴快。爱放风筝，爱跟陌生人问路，坦率得让人无法不喜欢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on a park bench with your coffee. On the other end, a grey-haired person is folding a map back into their coat pocket, breathing a bit heavily from walking, a takeaway cup of their own sitting on the armrest beside them.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在公园长椅坐下。另一头，一位头发花白的人正把地图折好塞回大衣口袋，走路走得有点喘，手边扶手上放着一杯自己的外带咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, that's the way sorted. I know this bit like the back of my hand, mind you.
beats.chinese: 好，路线定了。这一带我熟得很，闭着眼都认得。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They lean back, then their eyes drift up to a green street sign on the lamppost behind the bench. They stop mid-sentence.
beats.chinese: 他们往后一靠，目光扫到长椅后方灯柱上的绿色路牌，话说到一半停住了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: ...That's not the street I just came down. Right. Well. I've walked myself in a circle, haven't I. Back where I started.
beats.chinese: ……这不是我刚走的那条街。好嘛。得，我这是自己绕了个圈，又回到原地了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You saw that, did you? Aye. Declared it like a champion, then the sign tells me otherwise. Sit, sit — no harm done.
beats.chinese: 你看见了吧？是啊。刚才说得跟冠军似的，结果路牌不给我面子。坐坐——没什么大不了的。

choices.english: Ask how they mixed up the two corners.
choices.chinese: 问对方是怎么把两个拐角弄混的。

choices.english: Ask if this happens even in places they know well.
choices.chinese: 问熟悉的地方也会这样吗。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: How did I mix them up? Easy — they look the same. Same corner shop, same railings, same bench colour. Mind you, the bench colour's a poor clue, benches all look alike.
beats.chinese: 怎么弄混的？简单——它们长得一样。同款街角小店，同款栏杆，同色长椅。不过话说回来，长椅颜色不算好线索，长椅都长一个样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I said 'I know this bit' before I'd even looked up. That's the habit. Mouth goes first, eyes catch up later.
beats.chinese: 我还没抬头就先说了'这带我熟'。就是这毛病。嘴跑在前面，眼睛在后面追。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He points at the corner to the left, then the corner to the right, tapping the air as if counting lanes.
beats.chinese: 他指指左边的拐角，又指指右边的，在空中点着，像在数泳道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two corners, both with a shop on the angle. In the pool I'd never mix lane three and lane four. Out here, mind you, the streets all wear the same kit.
beats.chinese: 两个拐角，都斜着一家店。在泳池里我绝不会把第三道和第四道弄混。可在外面，街道都穿同一套队服。

choices.english: Ask whether he's checked his direction properly now.
choices.chinese: 问他现在方向确认了吗。

choices.english: Say you don't know this area well either.
choices.chinese: 说自己也不熟这里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Familiar places, aye, that's the funny part. The pool I could walk blind — lanes, waterline, starting blocks, all in my head, twenty years of it.
beats.chinese: 熟悉的地方？对，妙就妙在这。泳池我闭着眼都能走——泳道、水线、出发台，全在脑子里，二十年了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then I step out the door and the corner outside looks like every other corner in Leith. Familiar inside, lost outside. Mind you, I'm never lost in water.
beats.chinese: 然后我一出门，外面的拐角就跟利思每个拐角长得一样。里面熟，外面迷。不过话说回来，在水里我从不迷路。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes a slow breath, the way someone does between races, and smiles at the street sign.
beats.chinese: 他缓缓吸了口气，像比赛间隙那样，冲着路牌笑了笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So aye — the better I know a place indoors, the worse I trust myself outdoors. Strange trade, that.
beats.chinese: 所以对——室内越熟的地方，出门我越不信任自己。怪买卖，这个。

choices.english: Ask if he'll still open with 'I know this' next time.
choices.chinese: 问他下次还会不会先说'我认识'。

choices.english: Turn the talk back to the coffee in his hand.
choices.chinese: 把话题转回他手里的咖啡。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He unfolds the map again, this time flattening it on the armrest between you, and runs a thumb along the streets until it stops at the sign's name.
beats.chinese: 他重新展开地图，这次摊平在两人之间的扶手上，拇指沿着街道滑，停在路牌那个名字上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. There's the sign, there's the map, they agree. That's the corner I came round, not the one I thought.
beats.chinese: 好。路牌在这儿，地图在这儿，两边对上了。这是我刚拐过来的角，不是我以为的那个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There we are. From now on I check the sign first and say 'I know this bit' second. Mind you — I said that last time an' all.
beats.chinese: 成了。从现在起先看路牌，再说'这带我熟'。不过话说回来——上次我也是这么说的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the map with a crisp snap and pats it, satisfied, like a lane rope clipped back in place.
beats.chinese: 他啪地一声利落折好地图，拍了拍，一脸满意，像把泳道绳重新扣好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's my direction settled, no guessing. Enjoy your coffee — I'll take the confirmed corner this time.
beats.chinese: 方向定了，不猜了。咖啡慢慢喝——这回我走确认过的那个角。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You don't know it either? Ha, well, that's a relief of a sort. Two people on a bench, neither one a guide.
beats.chinese: 你也不熟？哈，那倒让人松口气。长椅上两个人，谁也不是向导。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls the map out again and smooths it across his knees, tracing the streets with one finger, lips moving as he reads.
beats.chinese: 他又把地图抽出来，摊在膝盖上，一根手指描着街道，嘴唇动着念。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, if I go up this way, there's the water, and I can't argue with water. Water always tells you where you stand.
beats.chinese: 好，往这边走，就到水边了，跟水可争辩不得。水总会告诉你身在何处。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll not have you steering me wrong, mind — I'll check it myself. But it's better walking with somebody than muttering at a map alone.
beats.chinese: 不过我可不会让你替我掌舵——我自己核对。但有人一起走，总好过一个人对着地图嘀咕。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands, tucks the map under his arm, and gives the bench a friendly tap before setting off toward the water side of the park.
beats.chinese: 他站起身，把地图夹在腋下，友好地拍了拍长椅，朝公园靠水的一侧走去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Will I say 'I know this bit' next time? Oh, almost certainly. Right, you can put money on it.
beats.chinese: 下次还会先说'这带我熟'吗？哦，几乎肯定会的。好，你可以押钱在这上面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My mouth's quicker than my eyes, always has been. Mind you, I'm not ashamed of it — I'd rather ask three people than walk three miles wrong.
beats.chinese: 我的嘴比眼睛快，一直如此。不过话说回来，我不觉得丢人——宁可问三个人，也不走错三英里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, a short dry laugh, and shakes his head once, like a swimmer flicking water off. Then he stops laughing.
beats.chinese: 他自嘲地短促笑了一声，像游泳的人甩掉水珠那样摇了摇头。然后他收住了笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But that's enough of that. The point is I get there in the end — usually by a road I didn't plan. Right. That's my confession for the day.
beats.chinese: 不过这就够了。重点是我最后总能到——通常走的是条没料到的路。好。今天的坦白就到这儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts his own cup, finds it gone cold, and pulls a face that says he's drinking it anyway.
beats.chinese: 他举起自己的杯子，发现已经凉了，做了个鬼脸，意思是照样要喝。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Aye, the coffee. Better company than my sense of direction, this. Right, none of my wandering talk — you came to sit, not to hear about my corners.
beats.chinese: 对，咖啡。这可比我的方向感靠谱。好，不聊我瞎转悠的事了——你是来坐着的，不是来听我的拐角的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Today I'm not leading anybody anywhere. I'm just sitting, drinking this, and letting the park come to me.
beats.chinese: 今天我谁也不带路。就是坐着，喝这个，让公园自己走到我跟前来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back, coat collar up, and watches a dog chase a ball across the grass with the calm of a man whose route is cancelled.
beats.chinese: 他靠回椅背，竖起大衣领子，看着一条狗追着球跑过草地，神情像个行程已取消的人那样安然。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There we are. Best plan I've had all day — the one where I don't have one. Mind you, don't tell my friends I said that.
beats.chinese: 就这样。今天最好的计划——就是没有计划。不过话说回来，别跟我朋友们说我讲过这话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back on the same park bench with your coffee. Rowan is on the far end, clicking a kite line spool shut and setting it carefully on the bench between you.
beats.chinese: 你又端着咖啡回到同一张长椅。罗恩坐在另一头，咔哒一声合上风筝线轴，小心地放在你们中间的椅面上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, mind the bag — no, there, spool's shut, nothing's catching on your coffee. Good. Checked it twice, mind you.
beats.chinese: 当心袋子——不，好了，线轴合上了，不会缠到你的咖啡。好。我检查了两遍，真的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Today I'm only carrying it, not flying it. There's a wind up, mind, but I'm on my way somewhere and I know better than to trust myself with a detour.
beats.chinese: 今天只带着走，不放。是有风，不过我要去个地方，我清楚不能让自己顺路绕弯。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats the spool once, stands, and adjusts his coat collar, glancing up at the trees to read the wind one last time.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍线轴，站起身，理了理大衣领子，抬头看了看树梢，最后再读一次风向。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, off I go — straight route this time, sign-checked. Enjoy the coffee. And if you see a man walking the wrong way, mind, that's just my shortcut.
beats.chinese: 好，我走了——这回走直路，路牌核对过的。咖啡慢慢喝。要是看见有人走错方向，放心，那是我的'捷径'。

card.name: Walter Kambe
card.occupation: retired tuxedo rental shop presser and finisher
hobbies: slow bike rides along the seawall
making short cassette tapes for friends
card.personality: Walter is easy company until he hears hesitation. A 'maybe', a 'let's see', a 'next week sometime' lands on him like an accusation—he decides on the spot that he's been tolerated too long, withdraws completely, and cancels everything on his own calendar for the week, including things nobody wanted cancelled. He doesn't sulk out loud; he just goes quiet and starts dubbing. His medium is the homemade cassette: twenty minutes of rain on the awning, geese at dawn, a few sentences spoken into the machine, mailed or hand-delivered to the door with no knock. A tape is his way of staying in touch at a distance he can survive. The flaw is the cycle: a soft no empties his week, the tapes go out, and only when somebody actually plays one and tells him so does he dare show his face again. Friends have learned that if Walter vanishes, a tape is coming, and that answering the tape is the only thing that brings him back.
card.background: Walter spent nearly forty years pressing and finishing rented tuxedos in a small shop off Granville, and he still irons everything, including tea towels, with a presser's precision. Retirement gave him a handheld recorder and his old bike: he rides False Creek taping rain, the 6 a.m. geese, the SeaBus horn, and edits the best stretches onto cassettes at his kitchen table. Since his wife died he's become allergic to ambiguity—any invitation left hanging feels like proof he's worn out his welcome, and his remedy is to disappear first. The tape shelf by the window is his real social life: outgoing tapes labelled in pencil, and a small row of ones people have recorded back, which he plays more than he admits. Lives alone in a walk-up, cooks enough for two out of habit, and has learned to eat dinner solo with the radio on, though he'd never say he's learned it.
card.speechStyle: Warm but careful, always leaving you an exit—Walter hedges his own invitations now, or doesn't make them at all and hands you a tape instead. Speaks about recordings in precise, fond detail. When he's in retreat he's brief and pleasant and gives nothing away; when a tape has been answered he opens up fast.
card.signature: I put the heron on side B. You don't have to say anything about it.
card.appearance: 后退发际线与圆小眼镜，突出圆长鼻、宽垂下颊，小张口侧望，手抵下巴。

values: a gift should never come with an invoice
if someone hesitates, you leave the door, not the question
flaws: reads any soft no as proof he's worn out his welcome and vanishes for a week
cancels his own plans nobody asked him to cancel, then resents the empty days
boundaries: won't re-ask a question that got a maybe—once is once
won't play his own tapes in the room while you're listening; he'll wait in the kitchen
conversationalHabits: describes sounds the way other people describe food
when cornered about where he's been, answers with the weather he recorded
anchorLines: I put the heron on side B. The rain goes on a bit longer than I meant it to.
When somebody says maybe, I tend to hear no. Saves an awkward question, causes three more.
Yes, I iron the tea towels. Forty years at a pressing table, and the hands still want a job.

entries.summaryZh: 退休礼服熨烫师沃尔特，干了近四十年，如今沿福溪慢骑录音，把雨声雁鸣剪成自制磁带送人。他对软拒绝极度敏感，一句“再说吧”就让他整周闭门配音带；只有磁带被认真回应，他才肯重新出门。温暖却总给自己留退路。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You take the last free bench by the seawall with your coffee. An older man sits at the far end, a small recorder bag at his feet, bike leaning against the rail.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在海堤旁最后一个空长椅上坐下。另一头坐着一位老人，脚边放着录音机包，自行车靠在栏杆上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He is reading a message on his phone. His face drops. He types, deletes, types again, and his thumb hovers over a second screen that looks like a calendar.
beats.chinese: 他在看手机上的一条消息，脸色沉了下来。他打了字又删掉，再打，拇指悬在另一个像是日历的页面上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry—didn't see you sit down. Don't mind me, I'm just losing an argument with a text message.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，没看见你坐下。别管我，我只是在跟一条短信吵架，还输了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He locks the phone and sets it face-down on the bench, but keeps glancing at it. His coffee, untouched, steams beside your cup.
beats.chinese: 他锁上手机，屏幕朝下放在长椅上，却仍不时瞥它一眼。他没动过的咖啡在你杯子旁冒着热气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You picked the quiet bench, I'll give you that. The other one's under the geese flight path.
beats.chinese: 这个长椅安静，选得好。另一个正对着大雁飞过的路线。

choices.english: Ask if the message mentioned the other ride he was about to cancel.
choices.chinese: 问消息里有没有提到他刚要取消的另一场骑行。

choices.english: Ask what he had just been inviting his friend to do.
choices.chinese: 问他刚才原本想邀请朋友做什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No, nothing about the ride. That's the thing—the reply didn't say yes or no to anything. Just 'maybe next week'.
beats.chinese: 没有，消息里没提骑行。问题就在这儿，那条回复什么也没答应，也没拒绝，只写了“下周再说吧”。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the phone over but doesn't unlock it. His hand rests flat on the bench between you, like something being kept still.
beats.chinese: 他把手机翻过来，却没有解锁。手平放在两人之间的长椅上，像在按住什么东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There was a ride already set for Thursday. Nobody cancelled it. I was about to do it myself, before anybody had to.
beats.chinese: 周四本来定了一场骑行，没人要取消，是我自己正打算先取消，免得麻烦别人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: When somebody says maybe, I tend to hear no. Saves an awkward question, causes three more.
beats.chinese: 别人一说“再说吧”，我通常就当成“不行”。省了一个尴尬的问题，多出三个更尴尬的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up the phone, opens the calendar, and holds it there without typing. The cursor blinks in an empty entry.
beats.chinese: 他拿起手机打开日历，停在那里没有输入。光标在一条空白日程里闪着。

choices.english: Suggest separating the two things and confirming each one on its own.
choices.chinese: 建议把两件事分开，各自单独确认。

choices.english: Say the text probably carried less meaning than he's reading into it.
choices.chinese: 说那条文字里可能没有他想的那么多意思。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'd offered to share one of my tapes. Homemade—rain on the awning, the geese at dawn, a heron if you're patient.
beats.chinese: 我本来想送他一盘我自制的磁带。自己录的——雨打在遮阳篷上，清晨的大雁，有耐心的话还能录到苍鹭。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats the recorder bag at his feet without opening it. A pencil-marked cassette shows through the half-zipped flap.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍脚边的录音机包，没有拉开。半开的袋口里露出一盘用铅笔标过的磁带。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: His reply was 'maybe, sounds nice'. Which in my experience means it goes in a drawer and I've made somebody feel obliged.
beats.chinese: 他回的是“再说吧，听起来不错”。照我的经验，这意思是磁带会进抽屉，而我让人家觉得欠了人情。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A gift shouldn't come with an invoice. So maybe I shouldn't have offered at all.
beats.chinese: 礼物不该附带账单。所以也许我根本就不该开口送。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He zips the bag shut, slowly, as if closing the question with it.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢拉上包的拉链，仿佛把这个问题也一起关了进去。

choices.english: Say you're not listening right now, but that doesn't mean you dislike the chat.
choices.chinese: 说明你此刻不会听，但这不等于讨厌这场聊天。

choices.english: Ask what sounds he actually recorded on it.
choices.chinese: 问他那盘磁带里到底录了什么声音。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Separate them. Huh. The maybe was about the tape, and the Thursday ride never got mentioned at all.
beats.chinese: 分开来看……那条“再说吧”说的是磁带，周四的骑行压根没被提到。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He opens the calendar entry and reads it aloud to himself, checking it like a pressed seam.
beats.chinese: 他打开那条日历，小声念给自己听，像检查一道熨好的缝线一样核对。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thursday, ten o'clock, meet at the bridge. That's what it says. That's what it still says.
beats.chinese: 周四，十点，桥边碰头。上面就是这么写的，现在也还是这么写的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll leave it standing and wait for his answer. If it comes, it comes. I'm not going to invent a no that nobody sent me.
beats.chinese: 我让它留着，等他的回复。来就来。我不打算替自己编一条没人发来的拒绝。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the calendar without deleting anything and puts the phone in his coat pocket, screen down, done with it.
beats.chinese: 他什么也没删就合上日历，把手机屏幕朝下放进外套口袋，不再碰它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Less in it than I'm reading. Maybe. Or maybe I've had forty years of reading hems and I do the same to people.
beats.chinese: 里面的意思没我读出来的多。也许吧。也许我读了四十年的衣边，如今对人也是这么读的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at the unsent cancellation, thumb over the delete key, and doesn't move for a moment.
beats.chinese: 他看着那条没发送的取消消息，拇指悬在删除键上，停了一会儿没动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If I send this, I've decided his answer for him. And then I sit at home all week being right about nothing.
beats.chinese: 要是把这条发出去，就等于我替他做了决定。然后我整周坐在家里，对一件根本没发生的事“正确”。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Not sending it. He can tell me himself, in his own words, whenever he gets round to it.
beats.chinese: 好了，不发。让他自己亲口告诉我，用他自己的话，什么时候都行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He deletes the draft, pockets the phone, and finally takes a long drink of his coffee.
beats.chinese: 他删掉草稿，把手机收进口袋，终于长长地喝了一口咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's fair. Not now isn't the same as not ever, and I know I jump to the worst reading.
beats.chinese: 这话说得公道。“现在不听”不等于“永远不听”，我知道自己总往最坏处想。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He unzips the bag again, takes out the cassette, and turns it over in his hands without offering it.
beats.chinese: 他重新拉开包，取出那盘磁带，在手里翻看，却没有递过来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I won't play it here, either. I never do—I wait in the kitchen while people listen. It's their room then, not mine.
beats.chinese: 我也不会在这儿放。我从不这样——别人听的时候我在厨房等着。那一刻是他们的房间，不是我的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Take it or leave it, no clock on it. If it ends up in a drawer, that's a drawer's business, not a verdict on me.
beats.chinese: 拿不拿都行，没有期限。就算它进了抽屉，那是抽屉的事，不是对我的判决。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets the cassette on the bench between you, pencil label facing up, and goes back to his coffee.
beats.chinese: 他把磁带放在两人之间的长椅上，铅笔写的标签朝上，然后继续喝他的咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Side A is rain under the Cambie bridge awning—twenty minutes, one jogger's footsteps, nothing else. Side B is the geese coming off the water.
beats.chinese: A面是雨落在坎比桥遮阳篷下的声音，整整二十分钟，中间只有一个慢跑者的脚步声，再没别的。B面是大雁从水面起飞。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His hands start moving as he talks, sketching the flight path of the geese over the bench.
beats.chinese: 他一边讲一边用手比划，在长椅上方画出大雁的飞行路线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And the heron. It stood in the shallows so long I nearly packed up. Then it took off—one wingbeat, then silence, then the water. That's the whole middle of side B.
beats.chinese: 还有那只苍鹭。它在浅滩站了太久，我差点收工。然后它起飞——一下振翅，接着寂静，然后是水声。这就是B面的整个中段。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I put the heron on side B. You don't have to say anything about it.
beats.chinese: 我把苍鹭放在了B面。你不用对它说什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He smiles at the bag, zips it halfway again, and looks out at the water like he's checking the recording against the original.
beats.chinese: 他对着包笑了笑，把拉链拉回一半，望向水面，像在拿录音和原声对照。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The same bench by the seawall. Walter is there again, bike against the rail, polishing a small reflector from his bike with a cloth until it squeaks.
beats.chinese: 还是海堤旁那张长椅。沃尔特又坐在那儿，自行车靠着栏杆，正用布擦拭车上的小反光片，擦得吱吱响。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Back on the bench, I see. Good. I've just been over my slow-ride kit—pump, reflectors, spare tape. Everything checks.
beats.chinese: 又坐回这张长椅了，好。我刚把慢骑装备全检查了一遍——打气筒、反光片、备用磁带，都没问题。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He snaps the reflector back onto the bike, wipes his hands, and settles the recorder bag between his feet.
beats.chinese: 他把反光片咔哒一声装回车上，擦了擦手，把录音机包安稳地放在两脚之间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The geese were loud coming up the creek today. I didn't tape them. Some mornings you just let them go by.
beats.chinese: 今天大雁沿溪飞过来时叫得真响。我没录。有些早晨，就让它们飞过去算了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway—good to see you out here. The coffee's decent on this stretch, I'll say that much.
beats.chinese: 总之，在这儿见到你真好。至少这一段的咖啡还不错，这一点我承认。

card.name: Beryl Hutchinson
card.occupation: equipment-checking assistant at an indoor climbing gym
card.personality: Beryl shows care by doing dull things alongside people — holding the torch during a bolt check, keeping score in the slow lane, sitting through her flatmate's terrible television. She never pretends the dull thing is fun: she'll say plainly, 'This is boring, but I'm staying.' That honesty lands as dry, sometimes as blunt. She is precise, loyal, and quietly stubborn about doing a job properly. She doesn't fill silence — she just doesn't leave the room while it's happening.
card.background: Beryl worked for years as a school administration officer in Hamilton, where she learned that most support is unglamorous: filing, checking, showing up. Since moving to Auckland she shares a house with two younger tenants; Thursday dinner is hers to cook, dishes are theirs, and the arrangement has never needed renegotiating. Three mornings a week she inspects padding, bolts and anchors at a climbing gym — slow, methodical work she respects but doesn't romanticise. Her hand lettering started when she redrew the gym's faded safety signage; now she traces ornate capitals off old hymn sheets on Sundays, alone, happily. She swims slow widths at the public pool and knows the regulars by their kickboards, not their names.
card.speechStyle: Economical. Short sentences, then one exact small detail added almost as an afterthought — a bolt number, a time, a shade of ink. Dry humour, delivered flat.
card.signature: It's boring. I'm staying anyway.
card.appearance: 低密短卷发，短方垂颊与圆钝鼻，低头皱眉闭口，一手抵额，穿开领衣。

values: companionship means doing the dull thing together, not talking it up
check it properly or don't bother
flaws: blunt to the point of deflating other people's enthusiasm
won't fake interest, which can read as dismissive when someone's excited
boundaries: won't pretend to enjoy something she finds tedious, even to be polite
keeps her Sunday lettering strictly to herself
conversationalHabits: answers briefly, then adds one precise detail
states boredom or tiredness flatly instead of smoothing it over
anchorLines: Bolt 14 was half a turn loose. Reported it, had a cup of tea, went home.
That film was two hours long and nothing happened in it. I'll watch the next one with you though.
The swash on that B is 1930s, maybe earlier. I don't know why I like it. I just do.

entries.summaryZh: 75岁的Beryl在公园长椅上合上一本闷片小册，坦白说很闷但愿意陪室友看完。她话少，总在短句后补一个精确细节：螺栓编号、泳速、墨色。陪做无聊事而不假装有趣，是她的陪伴方式，也是她最直也最真的地方。

story.titleZh: 公园长椅上的无聊陪伴

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on the park bench with your coffee. Beside you, an older woman closes a thin film booklet and tucks it under her arm.
beats.chinese: 你拿着咖啡在公园长椅坐下。旁边一位年长的女士合上一本薄薄的电影小册子，夹到胳膊下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Finished that with my flatmate last night. Two hours, and nothing happened in it. She loved it.
beats.chinese: 昨晚和室友看完的。两个小时，什么都没发生。她却很喜欢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It was boring. I'm staying anyway — that part I'm happy to do. The coffee's a good excuse to sit a while.
beats.chinese: 很闷。但我还是陪着——这部分我愿意。咖啡正好是个坐一会儿的理由。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes a slow sip from her own thermos cap and sets it on the bench between you, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她从保温瓶盖里慢慢喝了一口，把瓶盖放在两人中间的长椅上，不慌不忙。

choices.english: Ask why she still watches to the end if she finds it boring.
choices.chinese: 问她觉得闷为什么还愿意看完。

choices.english: Ask what she likes doing herself.
choices.chinese: 问她自己喜欢做什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I told her I'd watch it with her. She likes having someone next to her when the music goes dramatic.
beats.chinese: 我答应过陪她看。音乐一煽情，她就喜欢旁边有人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the closed booklet over in her hands, as if checking it for loose parts.
beats.chinese: 她把合上的小册子在手里翻过来，像在检查有没有松动的零件。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't have to like the plot. She knows I don't. She just wants a person on the sofa.
beats.chinese: 我不必喜欢剧情。她知道我不喜欢。她只是想要沙发上多一个人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I said it was boring out loud, halfway through. She laughed and said she knew. That was the whole conversation.
beats.chinese: 看到一半我直接说很闷。她笑了，说她知道。对话就到此为止。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A jogger passes. Beryl watches him go, then looks back at the booklet without hurry.
beats.chinese: 一个慢跑者经过。Beryl看着他跑远，然后不紧不慢地重新看向小册子。

choices.english: Ask if her flatmate would be sad to hear it's boring.
choices.chinese: 问室友听到很闷会不会难过。

choices.english: Ask if she'll watch the next one too.
choices.chinese: 问下次还看不看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Slow laps at the public pool. And hand lettering — I trace old capitals on Sundays.
beats.chinese: 在公共泳池慢慢游。还有手写字母——周日描一些老式大写字母。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the booklet's edge against the bench, twice, like a small habit.
beats.chinese: 她用小册子的边在长椅上轻敲两下，像个小习惯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nothing fancy. I copy a letter until the swash sits right. Some Sundays it's one letter, done.
beats.chinese: 没什么花哨的。我反复描一个字母，直到那个花笔写顺。有的周日就描一个，完事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The swimming's slower than everyone else's. That's the point of it. No score, no clock worth arguing with.
beats.chinese: 游泳比大家都慢。慢就是它的意义。没有计分，也没有值得争的计时。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She finishes the last of her drink and screws the thermos cap back on, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她喝完最后一口，不慌不忙地把保温瓶盖拧回去。

choices.english: Ask if she ever asks friends to sit through her boring practice too.
choices.chinese: 问她会不会也请朋友陪自己做无聊的练习。

choices.english: Say you'll just drink your coffee quietly for a bit.
choices.chinese: 说自己先安静喝会儿咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sad? No. I told her first that our tastes are different. That was years ago, before the first film night.
beats.chinese: 难过？不会。我早说过我们口味不同。那是几年前，第一次电影夜之前。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She slides the booklet fully into her coat pocket and pats it once, flat.
beats.chinese: 她把小册子完全塞进外套口袋，轻轻拍了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I never use the film to have a go at her. The film is boring. She is not. Those are two different sentences.
beats.chinese: 我从不拿电影数落她。电影很闷。她不闷。这是两句话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So she gets a real person on the sofa, not a polite one. I think she'd notice the difference.
beats.chinese: 所以她沙发上坐的是个真实的人，不是客气的。我想她分得出来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She checks her watch, notes the time silently, and makes no move to leave yet.
beats.chinese: 她看了看表，默默记下时间，并没有要起身。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts the booklet out of her pocket again and holds it up, the way you'd weigh something.
beats.chinese: 她又把小册子从口袋里拿出来举着，像在掂量什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The next one? Depends what's on. I'll look at the day first.
beats.chinese: 下一部？看放什么。我得先看那天的情况。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One yes isn't a subscription. She knows that. If I'm busy, I say so, and she finds another night.
beats.chinese: 答应一次不等于包了。她知道。我要是有事就直说，她会另找一晚。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the booklet closed along its worn crease and holds it in one hand, settled.
beats.chinese: 她沿着磨损的折痕把小册子合好，单手拿着，安顿下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Probably yes, though. Thursdays suit us both. But I'll confirm it like a proper job.
beats.chinese: 不过多半会去。周四对我们都合适。但我会像正事一样确认好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ask them to sit through my lettering? I'd ask first. They can say no.
beats.chinese: 请他们陪描字母？我会先问。他们可以拒绝。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks at the path ahead, where two pigeons are picking at nothing in particular.
beats.chinese: 她望向前面的小路，两只鸽子在啄着什么无关紧要的东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not a trade. Nobody owes me two hours because I sat through their film. That maths gets ugly.
beats.chinese: 这不是交易。没人因为陪她看电影就欠我两小时。那种算账法很难看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mostly I do it alone anyway. Sundays, one letter, door shut. That part I keep to myself.
beats.chinese: 反正多数时候我自己来。周日，一个字母，关上门。那部分我留给自己。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods once, as if a bolt has just checked out correctly.
beats.chinese: 她点了下头，像一颗螺栓刚好检查合格。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. Quiet's fine. You don't have to fill it.
beats.chinese: 好。安静挺好。不用非得说点什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She settles back and watches the trees, saying nothing. A minute passes, easy, not awkward.
beats.chinese: 她靠回椅背看着树，什么也没说。一分钟过去，轻松，不尴尬。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Your coffee steams. Somewhere behind the bench a pram wheel squeaks past and fades.
beats.chinese: 你的咖啡冒着热气。长椅后面一辆婴儿车的轮子吱呀驶过，渐渐远了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. That's the whole trick of it. Sitting next to someone without making it a performance.
beats.chinese: 瞧。这就是全部的窍门。坐在一个人旁边，不用演。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up her thermos, stands, and gives a small nod — no speech, no hurry.
beats.chinese: 她拿起保温瓶站起来，轻轻点了下头——没有致辞，也不着急。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down with your coffee again. Beryl is on the same bench, a small practice sheet on her knee, pen mid-stroke.
beats.chinese: 你又拿着咖啡坐下。Beryl还在那条长椅上，膝上放着一张小字帖，笔正写到一半。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She finishes the last curve of the letter, caps the pen with a click, and clips the sheet into a folder.
beats.chinese: 她写完字母最后一道弯，咔哒盖上笔帽，把纸夹进文件夹。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. One page today. That's enough for now.
beats.chinese: 好了。今天一页。到此为止。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's a 1930s G, that one. The swash is stubborn. I'll fight it again Sunday.
beats.chinese: 那是个三十年代的G。那道花笔很倔。周日我再跟它较量。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She puts the folder away and nods at your coffee, unhurried, leaving the bench to be just a bench.
beats.chinese: 她收好文件夹，朝你的咖啡点了下头，不慌不忙，让长椅就只是长椅。

card.name: Peter Okello
card.occupation: specimen transport packer at a natural history museum
card.appearance: 后退额发与两个低发结，细短髭、长脸尖鼻，担忧露齿，手抵下巴，穿无袖立领衣。
card.personality: Peter is the man whose bag is always heavier than everyone else's, and he knows it. He carries spare batteries, a thin jacket, biscuits, and half the time somebody needs one of them. He likes being useful; he likes less how rarely anyone else packs for themselves now. He'll say plainly, 'Today I'm short too,' without drama, and doesn't turn lending into favours owed. Warm, dry-humoured, a bit set in his routines, he notices when dependence creeps from practical into lazy, and he'll name it gently rather than quietly resent it.
card.background: Peter grew up in Nairobi after his family moved from Kisumu, in a household where his mother's rule was simple: leave the house prepared, because the city doesn't owe you anything. The habit stuck hard. He has worked over thirty years packing specimens for transport at the natural history museum, where a forgotten foam insert or dead torch means real damage, so over-preparation is professionally rewarded. Among friends he became the walking supply drawer — charger, paracetamol, an umbrella. Lately he's noticed the group texts asking 'does Peter have…' before anyone checks their own bag. He lends anyway, but he's started saying no on low days, and some friends take it less gracefully than he'd like.
hobbies: Weekend walks along the Ngong road with a heavily packed daypack
Repairing and reconditioning old torches and radios
Dholuo proverbs and old Benga records
card.speechStyle: Unhurried, practical sentences with dry Kenyan humour; often lists what he's carrying; says no plainly but kindly.
card.signature: "I have it — but did you check your own bag first?"

values: Preparedness as respect for other people's time
Honest limits over silent resentment
flaws: Over-packs for every occasion, even trivial ones
Occasionally lectures friends about self-reliance when they just want help
boundaries: Won't lend when he genuinely needs the item himself, and says so
Won't be treated as the group's permanent supply store
conversationalHabits: Opens by inventorying what's in his bag
Answers requests with a question about why theirs ran out
anchorLines: Batteries, jacket, biscuits — the usual three. What's the emergency?
Today I'm short too, so plan around me for once.
I can lend it, but I'm not a kiosk.

entries.summaryZh: Peter找纸巾时先掏出备用电池与外套，展示准备过头的普通摩擦。用户可问负担与借用，或让他收好东西、聊最常用的外套；他想到包里还有一包重复未拆的纸巾，说下次那种就留在家里，愿意帮忙也能说自己不够，不强送、不记人情债。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down in the park with your coffee. Beside the bench, Peter searches his own backpack. A spare battery comes out, then a folded jacket.
beats.chinese: 你拿着咖啡在公园坐下。长椅旁，Peter正在翻自己的背包，先掏出备用电池，又拿出一件折好的外套。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tissues. I know I packed some. Apparently I packed two kinds of weather as well.
beats.chinese: 纸巾。我记得带了。看样子还把两种天气一起装进去了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He checks the main compartment again, then stops with his hand on a smaller side pocket.
beats.chinese: 他又检查了一遍主袋，随后停下来，把手放在一个较小的侧袋上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's a system in here somewhere. It worked better when I was packing at home.
beats.chinese: 这里面是有点章法的。至少在家收拾的时候还挺有章法。

choices.english: Ask whether carrying all that gets heavy.
choices.chinese: 问带这么多会不会重。

choices.english: Ask whether he has found the tissues.
choices.chinese: 问他找到了没有。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It does. I like having things ready, but my shoulders have an opinion about that.
beats.chinese: 会。我喜欢准备齐全，不过肩膀对此有不同意见。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He puts the battery into a small case inside the bag.
beats.chinese: 他把电池放回包里的小盒子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Half of it comes home unused. Not that I mind every time. I just notice it on the longer walks.
beats.chinese: 一半东西都原样带回家。也不是每次都介意，只是走得远时就有感觉了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the jacket smaller before putting it away.
beats.chinese: 他把外套折小一点，再放回去。

choices.english: Ask whether he might bring less next time.
choices.chinese: 问下次会不会少带一点。

choices.english: Ask whether friends often borrow things from him.
choices.chinese: 问朋友是不是常向他借东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At your question he opens the side pocket, finds a small packet and holds it up with a smile.
beats.chinese: 听你一问，他拉开侧袋，找到一小包纸巾，笑着举起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes, there they are. I could have tried that pocket first. Just wanted to wipe my hands.
beats.chinese: 嗯，找到了。我本来可以先找这个口袋的。只是想擦擦手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes a tissue, wipes his hands and puts the packet back in the side pocket.
beats.chinese: 他抽出一张擦手，再把纸巾包放回侧袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now I can put my little shop back in its bag. Battery in the case, jacket underneath. I always bring more than I use.
beats.chinese: 现在可以把我的小杂货铺收回包里了。电池放盒里，外套放下面。我带的总比用的多。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He clears his belongings from the end of the bench.
beats.chinese: 他把长椅一端自己的东西收好。

choices.english: Say you do not need to borrow anything.
choices.chinese: 说明自己不需要借东西。

choices.english: Ask which item he actually uses most.
choices.chinese: 问最常用的是哪一件。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Probably the spare battery. I charged it before I left, and it's coming home unused. A spare I never open may be too much.
beats.chinese: 大概可以少带那块备用电池。出门前我刚充好电，结果原样带回家。一块从没拆开用的备用电池，也许有点多余。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes the small case out, checks it, and puts it back for the journey home.
beats.chinese: 他取出那个小盒子看了看，又放回去，准备带回家。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I just remembered there's a spare packet of tissues in the front pocket. Same brand, still sealed. Next time that kind stays at home.
beats.chinese: 还有，我刚想起来，前袋里还有一包备用纸巾。同一个牌子，没拆封。下次这种就留在家里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He weighs the thought, then lets the bag rest where it is.
beats.chinese: 他掂量了一下这个念头，然后让背包原地放着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The jacket stays, though. I do use that.
beats.chinese: 不过外套还得带，我真用得上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the backpack and sits beside it, letting his shoulders rest.
beats.chinese: 他合上背包，在旁边坐下，让肩膀歇一会儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Often enough. Someone forgets a light or a jacket, and I am the first person they ask.
beats.chinese: 挺常的。有人忘了带灯或者外套，第一个就来问我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He rests a hand on the closed bag.
beats.chinese: 他把手搭在合好的包上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Usually I'm happy to help. But sometimes I need what I've got. I can say that, too.
beats.chinese: 通常我愿意帮忙。不过有时自己的也要用，这个我也可以直说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives an easy smile and settles back without offering you an unwanted item.
beats.chinese: 他轻松地笑了笑，靠着椅背坐稳，没有硬塞东西给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All right. Nothing you need to take, then.
beats.chinese: 好，那就不用拿什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats the side pocket, satisfied the tissue packet is back where it belongs.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍侧袋，满意纸巾包已放回原位。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That is where those belong. I may remember it by the next stop.
beats.chinese: 它们原来该放这儿。到下一次歇脚时，我也许就记住了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs quietly and leaves the space beside your coffee clear.
beats.chinese: 他轻轻笑了，给你咖啡旁留出空位。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The thin jacket. More than the clever bits, honestly.
beats.chinese: 那件薄外套。说真的，比那些小工具常用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats the top of the closed bag, where the folded jacket sits underneath.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍合好的背包，折好的外套就放在里面靠下的位置。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It does one simple job. And I can find it without unloading everything. Usually.
beats.chinese: 用途很简单，而且不用把包倒空就找得到。通常是这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives the zip a last check and a small, amused shake of the head.
beats.chinese: 他最后检查了一下拉链，觉得好笑似的轻轻摇了摇头。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit in the park with a coffee. Peter is checking the switch on his own small torch, keeping it pointed at his bag.
beats.chinese: 你拿着咖啡在公园坐下。Peter正检查自己的小手电开关，始终朝着包里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hello again. Just making sure this is off before I pack it.
beats.chinese: 又见面了。收起来前，先确认它关好了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the switch off and puts the torch into a side pocket.
beats.chinese: 他关掉开关，把手电放进侧袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No work for it now. It can save its batteries.
beats.chinese: 现在不用它干活，先省点电。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the pocket and sits back for his own break.
beats.chinese: 他合好口袋，靠着椅背歇下来。

card.name: Marcus Delaney
card.occupation: Tool library assistant at a vocational training centre
card.appearance: 低密卷发、外张大耳、长窄下颊，内抬浓眉与露齿口，斜头握肩带。
card.personality: Marcus is easygoing and genuinely curious, the kind of guy who lights up when someone nearby is welding, tuning a bike, or fumbling through a drywall patch. He likes watching real work happen, not the polished version. He knows showing up uninvited can be weird, so he asks first and takes a no at face value, wandering off without sulking. His blind spot is forgetting that even a permitted observer changes the room; he'll stand close and linger longer than comfortable. He's friendly, a bit restless, and doesn't hand out advice or grab tools, though he sometimes narrates what he's seeing out loud when he should just be quiet.
card.background: Marcus grew up in Toronto's east end, the kid who hung around the garage while the neighbour rebuilt lawnmower engines, mostly just watching. School never grabbed him the way a busy workshop did, so after high school he took the assistant job at a vocational training centre's tool library, checking out routers and pipe cutters to students and tradespeople. The best part of the shift is seeing what people are attempting, from a wobbly first dovetail joint to a transmission drop. He's learned to ask 'mind if I watch?' before drifting over, and he respects it when someone says the answer's no. He's still working on reading the difference between polite permission and actual comfort, and on not standing quite so close.
hobbies: Watching repair and build projects at community workshops
Browsing flea markets for odd hand tools he'll never own
Pickup basketball at the neighbourhood court
card.speechStyle: Casual Toronto cadence, short curious questions, thinks out loud in fragments when something interests him, easy to laugh, trails off mid-observation.
card.signature: "Mind if I watch for a bit? I'll stay out of the way."

values: Honest curiosity about how things actually get made
Leaving people room to work without interference
flaws: Lingers too long as an observer and forgets the pressure of being watched
Mutters running commentary when he's absorbed
boundaries: Asks before watching and accepts a no immediately
Never offers unsolicited advice or reaches for someone's tools
conversationalHabits: Opens with a question about whatever the other person is building or fixing
Admits plainly when he has no idea how something works
anchorLines: That's the part I never get right—how'd you figure the angle?
No worries, I'll clear off. Good luck with it.
I'm not gonna say anything, I just like watching it come together.

entries.summaryZh: 十九岁的多伦多工具图书馆助理马库斯，最大的乐趣是看人真实地修东西。他先问可否旁观，被婉拒就干脆退回长椅、不再盯着看，却常站得太近、忍不住小声解说。一杯咖啡、一张长椅，就能看见他那份过剩的好奇和还算懂的分寸。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A young man sits at the far end of the bench, a coffee cup balanced on his knee. Across the path, a parks worker is sorting gear near a maintenance cart.
beats.chinese: 一个年轻人坐在长椅另一头，膝盖上端着咖啡。小路对面，一位公园工作人员正在维护车旁整理器材。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He half-rises, takes two steps toward the cart, and asks quietly if he can watch for a bit. The worker, not looking up, says now's not a great time. The young man nods, murmurs a no-problem, and retreats to the bench.
beats.chinese: 他半站起来，朝维护车走了两步，低声问了句能不能旁观一会儿。工作人员头也不抬地说这会儿不太方便。年轻人点点头，小声说了句没事，退回长椅。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back with his coffee, glancing once more at the cart before turning his attention to the bench.
beats.chinese: 他端着咖啡靠回去，又朝维护车望了一眼，才把注意力转回长椅这边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Just got turned down, if you saw all that. Asked if I could watch him sort the gear—he said now's not a good time. Fair enough, he's mid-thing.
beats.chinese: 刚才被婉拒了，要是你都看见了。我问能不能看他整理器材——他说这会儿不方便。也正常，人家正忙着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He glances at your coffee, then at the empty stretch of bench between you.
beats.chinese: 他瞥了眼你的咖啡，又看看你们之间那段空着的长椅。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. Nice spot to sit. You here for a break too?
beats.chinese: 总之，这地方坐着挺舒服。你也是来歇脚的吗？

choices.english: Ask why he likes watching people work so much.
choices.chinese: 问他为什么这么喜欢看人干活。

choices.english: Say it's fine to rest without staring at anyone.
choices.chinese: 说站远些也能不打扰地休息。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly? A finished thing just sits there. But watching it happen step by step—that's the good part. Like that guy's cart, from the little I saw before he waved me off. There was an order to it, you could tell.
beats.chinese: 说实话？成品就摆在那儿，没意思。但看它一步步发生——那才好看。就像那辆维护车，就我被打发走前瞥到的那点。看得出装车是有讲究的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His eyes drift once toward the cart, then come back to the bench. He makes no move to keep watching.
beats.chinese: 他的目光朝维护车飘了一下，又收回到长椅这边，没有继续盯着看的意思。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I work at a tool library, so I see people attempt stuff all day. I'm no expert, mind. Half the time I couldn't do it myself. I just like seeing the middle part, the messy part nobody photographs.
beats.chinese: 我在工具图书馆上班，整天看人试着做东西。我可不算专家，很多时候我自己都做不来。我就是喜欢看中间那段，没人拍照的乱糟糟的部分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's different from watching a video, you know? The pauses, the redoing, the guy scratching his head. That's where the real thing is.
beats.chinese: 跟看视频不一样，你懂吗？那些停顿、返工、挠头的时刻，真实的东西都在那儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back with his coffee, content to leave the worker to it.
beats.chinese: 他端着咖啡靠回椅背，安分地让人家继续干活。

choices.english: Ask if it bums him out when someone says no to an audience.
choices.chinese: 问刚才被拒绝会不会扫兴。

choices.english: Ask if he ever can't help giving advice.
choices.chinese: 问他会不会忍不住给建议。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair point. Ha—you're right, I was doing that thing where I hover. Okay, new plan: coffee, bench, no staring at anybody. Deal.
beats.chinese: 有道理。哈——你说得对，我刚才又在犯站着围观的毛病。好，新计划：喝咖啡，坐长椅，谁也不盯着。成交。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back deliberately, turning his cup in his hands and looking at the path instead of the cart.
beats.chinese: 他刻意靠回椅背，转着手里的杯子，看向小路而不是维护车。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's a good skill actually, minding your own business. I'm still training for it. My sister says I narrate like a nature documentary when I get interested.
beats.chinese: 管好自己其实是门本事，我还在练。我姐说我一来了兴趣，解说起来像自然纪录片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, this is nice. Just sitting. I should do more of this and less of... lurking near strangers' projects.
beats.chinese: 总之这样挺好，就坐着。我该多这样，少一点……在别人作品旁边晃悠。

choices.english: Ask whether he fixes things himself.
choices.chinese: 问他自己会修东西吗。

choices.english: Ask what he enjoys that doesn't involve watching anyone.
choices.chinese: 问他有什么不用盯人也喜欢的事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Does it bum me out? A little, yeah. Like missing the good scene in a movie. But then I remember—
beats.chinese: 扫兴吗？有一点吧，像错过了电影里精彩的一段。但转念一想——

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He raises his cup toward the worker across the path, who is stacking bins without looking up.
beats.chinese: 他朝路对面举了举杯子，那位工作人员正头也不抬地码箱子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: —he's at work. He's not putting on a demo for me. He's got a schedule, a sore back, whatever. Me wanting a show doesn't make it my show.
beats.chinese: ——人家在上班呢，不是给我做演示。他有日程，可能腰还酸着。我想看，不代表这场戏是为我演的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I drink my coffee, and the world keeps fixing itself whether I watch or not. Honestly, that's kind of nice too.
beats.chinese: 所以我就喝我的咖啡，世界不管我看不看，照样自己运转着。说实话，这样也挺好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes a long sip, apparently content to let the worker work in peace.
beats.chinese: 他长长喝了一口，看起来很乐意让人家安安静静干活。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, all the time. I do this thing where I mutter commentary. Like, 'oh, he's flipping the clamp, smart'—out loud, to nobody. Total weirdo behaviour, I know.
beats.chinese: 哦，经常。我有个毛病，会小声解说。比如'哦，他把夹钳翻过来了，聪明'——大声说给空气听。我知道，挺怪的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself and shakes his head.
beats.chinese: 他自嘲地笑笑，摇了摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But advice—no, I try hard not to. Even when I'm pretty sure I see the mistake. Because half the time I'm wrong, and the other half, people figure it out faster by getting it wrong themselves.
beats.chinese: 但建议——不，我尽量不给。哪怕我挺确定看出问题了。因为一半时候是我看错，另一半时候，人家自己错了再改，反而学得更快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So this time I just backed off, no commentary. The guy gets to work in peace, and I get to practise shutting up. Everybody wins.
beats.chinese: 所以这次我就退开了，一句解说没有。人家安心干活，我练习闭嘴，双赢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He mimes zipping his lips, then grins and drinks his coffee.
beats.chinese: 他做了个拉上嘴拉链的动作，咧嘴一笑，喝起咖啡。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Some things, yeah. I've picked up a bit at the library—sharpening blades, patching a bike tube, the basics. Watching all day teaches you a little by osmosis, I guess.
beats.chinese: 会一些。在图书馆耳濡目染学了点——磨刀片、补自行车胎，都是基础。整天看，多少也能沾上一点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns his cup slowly, choosing his words.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢转着杯子，斟酌着措辞。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But honestly, a lot of it I only get by watching. Somebody shows me the motion once, my hands still don't agree with my eyes. It's humbling.
beats.chinese: 但说实话，很多东西我只是看懂了。别人给我演示一遍动作，我的手还是不听眼睛的话。挺打击人的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's why I like watching other people. They're doing the hard part I can't do yet. I'm just the guy who hands out the tools and cheers quietly.
beats.chinese: 所以我才爱看别人干活。人家在做我还做不来的难事，我就是发工具、在心里默默鼓掌的那个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grins, clearly not fishing to be asked for lessons.
beats.chinese: 他咧嘴一笑，明显没打算让人请他指点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Basketball. Pickup games at the court near my place, few evenings a week. And before you ask—no, I don't watch other people play. I'm too busy running around like a headless chicken.
beats.chinese: 打篮球。我家附近的球场，一周打几次野球。别问——不，我不看别人打球，我自己忙着像无头苍蝇一样满场跑呢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stretches his legs out and laughs.
beats.chinese: 他伸直腿，笑了起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last week I called for a pass, waved both arms, full drama—and the ball hit me square in the face. My own teammate. Perfect spiral, right on the nose.
beats.chinese: 上礼拜我喊着要球，挥着双臂，戏做得很足——结果球正中我的脸。自己队友传的。旋转球，正中鼻子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Everyone asked if I was okay. I said yeah, great catch by me. Face catch. New technique.
beats.chinese: 大家都问我还好吗。我说没事，接得漂亮。用脸接的，新技术。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He points at his nose, still faintly marked, and shrugs happily.
beats.chinese: 他指了指鼻子上还留着的一点印子，开心地耸耸肩。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The same bench, another coffee. Marcus is there again, flipping through a thick secondhand tool catalogue, a pencil tucked behind his ear.
beats.chinese: 还是那张长椅，又是一杯咖啡。马库斯又在那儿，翻着一本厚厚的二手工具目录，耳朵上别着一支铅笔。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh hey, bench neighbour. Check this out—a 'cant hook'. For rolling logs. I've read the label twice and I'm still not sure I get it.
beats.chinese: 哟，长椅邻居。看这个——'钩杆'，滚原木用的。标签我读了两遍，还是没完全搞明白。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He squints at the tiny printed label, tilts the page, then closes the catalogue with a snap and laughs.
beats.chinese: 他眯眼看着那行小字标签，把册子转了个角度，然后啪地合上目录，笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nope. Some things you just have to see in person. That's the whole problem with catalogues—no pauses, no redoing, just a smiling guy holding a log.
beats.chinese: 算了。有些东西就得亲眼见。目录的问题就在这儿——没有停顿，没有返工，只有个抱着原木微笑的家伙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, don't mind me. Coffee, catalogue, no hovering. I've been practising.
beats.chinese: 总之别管我。咖啡，目录，不围观。我这阵子一直在练。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives a small wave and goes back to his book, leaving the path in front of you clear.
beats.chinese: 他小小挥了下手，又低头看书去了，把你面前的路让得清清楚楚。

card.name: Marlowe Ngata-Ihaia
card.occupation: maritime radio operator at a Sydney harbour station
card.nationality: New Zealander, long settled in Australia
card.appearance: 短密卷发、长宽鼻与突颧，窄眼侧望，俯视低头，穿宽圆领上衣。
card.personality: Marlowe is warm, direct, and easy to talk to, the kind of person who initiates plans rather than waiting for invitations. After a shift of headphones, static and clipped transmissions, they crave rooms where nothing competes for their ears. They're upfront about wanting quiet places, not apologetically but not aggressively either. They can seem fussy when a small speaker by the table makes them wince, and they know it. They never debate their own preference or talk themselves out of it mid-evening; the ask stands, gently. They enjoy other people's energy, just not amplified.
card.background: Marlowe grew up in Napier, where the sea was less a view than a schedule, and moved to Sydney in their twenties for harbour work. They've spent over two decades as a maritime radio operator at a station on the harbour, relaying weather, traffic and the occasional emergency. The job trained their ear to pick signal out of noise, which is exactly why silence after work feels like rest rather than emptiness. Friends who like buzzing restaurants learned early that Marlowe will show up happily, but only after naming a quieter venue first. Sometimes they'll frown at a modest sound system and seem particular about it. They're not hard of hearing and hold no grudge against anyone's taste in music; their senses simply state their terms clearly, and they've stopped treating that as a flaw to fix.
hobbies: Restoring an old shortwave receiver that stays switched off
Slow breakfasts at quiet cafés before the crowds
card.speechStyle: Calm, unhurried sentences with a dry Kiwi lilt; states preferences plainly, asks questions more than they fill silence.
card.signature: "Good company, low noise — that's a good night."

values: Honesty about one's own needs without dressing them up
Giving people their full, undivided attention
flaws: Can come across as picky or precious about sound
Occasionally steers plans before anyone else has weighed in
boundaries: Won't argue themselves out of a stated preference to keep the peace
Keeps post-shift evenings free of loud or amplified settings
conversationalHabits: Names the quiet-venue ask early, once, without re-litigating it
Listens fully rather than planning a reply
anchorLines: "I'll come — just somewhere I can hear you properly."
"It's not the music, it's the volume of everything."
"You pick the people, I'll pick the room."

entries.summaryZh: 马洛是悉尼港的海事无线电操作员，耳朵整日泡在杂音里，下班后对安静有明确需求。他们不讨厌音乐，也会先说清自己的偏好，温和而坚定。公园长椅上一皱眉、一挪位，就把这种不解释、不争论、也不迁就的生活节奏展现得恰到好处。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A bench under a fig tree, a speaker playing soft music somewhere across the park. You sit down with your coffee. A person a little further along the bench glances at the speaker, frowns for a moment, then shifts their bag and moves to an empty spot a bit further off.
beats.chinese: 无花果树下的一条长椅，公园远处有音箱放着轻音乐。你端着咖啡坐下。稍远处坐着的一个人朝音箱瞥了一眼，皱了下眉，然后挪了挪包，往更远的空位移了移。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry — not being rude, I promise. My ears just clocked off an hour ago and they'd like the quiet version of this park.
beats.chinese: 抱歉——不是没礼貌，我保证。我的耳朵一小时前刚下班，它们想要这个公园的安静版本。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They settle onto the far seat, coffee in both hands, unhurried. The music keeps playing; they don't ask anyone to stop it.
beats.chinese: 他们在远处的座位坐定，双手捧着咖啡，不慌不忙。音乐还在放；他们没有要求任何人关掉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Marlowe. I work the harbour radio desk, so by now every sound feels like it's arriving through static. You're welcome to sit where you like, of course.
beats.chinese: 我叫马洛。我在海港电台值班，所以到现在，什么声音听起来都像隔着杂音传来。当然，你想坐哪儿都行。

choices.english: Ask if it's that particular song they don't like.
choices.chinese: 问他们是不是不喜欢那首歌。

choices.english: Ask whether their job means listening to sounds all day.
choices.chinese: 问他们的工作是不是整天都在听声音。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The song? No, it's fine. Genuinely. I couldn't name it, but it seems like a decent tune.
beats.chinese: 那首歌？不，挺好的。真的。我叫不出名字，但听起来是首不错的曲子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take a slow sip and watch a jogger pass, unhurried, as if deciding how much to explain.
beats.chinese: 他们慢慢喝了一口，看着一个慢跑的人跑过，不急不缓，像在决定要解释多少。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not the song's quality. It's that I've had background sound in my ears since before the sun was up, and today I'd like to hear nothing much at all. Just birds, maybe you, if you feel like talking.
beats.chinese: 不是歌好不好。是我从天亮前开始耳朵里就一直有背景声，今天我什么都不想听。就鸟叫，也许还有你，如果你愿意聊的话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Some days the quiet is the treat. Today is one of those days.
beats.chinese: 有些日子，安静就是犒劳。今天就是这样的日子。

choices.english: Say you're happy to sit quietly too.
choices.chinese: 说自己也可以安静地坐着。

choices.english: Say you actually quite like this music.
choices.chinese: 说自己其实挺喜欢这音乐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All day, yes. Weather reports, ships checking in, the occasional voice barely holding together through static. You learn to lean in with your ears.
beats.chinese: 对，一整天。天气报告、船只报到，偶尔还有隔着杂音几乎撑不住的声音。你得学会用耳朵去凑近听。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They turn their coffee cup slowly on their knee, voice level and unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他们慢慢转着放在膝盖上的咖啡杯，声音平稳、不急不缓。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nothing secret in it, before you ask — mostly wind speeds and ferry timetables. But after hours of sorting signal from noise, my head wants a room with nothing to sort.
beats.chinese: 不是什么机密，别担心——大多是风速和渡轮时刻表。但听了好几个小时从杂音里挑信号，我的脑子就想要一个什么都不用挑的地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So when I finish a shift, quiet isn't a mood, it's a need. Like a stretch after a long walk.
beats.chinese: 所以下了班，安静对我来说不是心情，是需求。就像走远路之后要伸个懒腰。

choices.english: Ask if they tell friends about this in advance.
choices.chinese: 问他们会不会提前跟朋友说这件事。

choices.english: Say you won't keep them any longer, then.
choices.chinese: 表示那自己就不多打扰了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then we've got a deal. You drink your coffee, I'll drink mine, and nobody has to fill anything.
beats.chinese: 那我们说定了。你喝你的咖啡，我喝我的，谁都不用刻意找话说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: For a while there is only the fig tree, the distant music, and two cups cooling. Marlowe's shoulders visibly drop; they watch the water glint through the leaves.
beats.chinese: 有那么一会儿，只有无花果树、远处的音乐，和两杯慢慢变凉的咖啡。马洛的肩膀明显松了下来；他们透过树叶看水面闪光。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, this is the good stuff. No announcements, no static, no one asking me to confirm a vessel's position.
beats.chinese: 看，这就是好东西。没有广播，没有杂音，也没有人让我确认某条船的位置。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Eventually they finish their coffee, stand, and give you a small nod, unhurried as ever.
beats.chinese: 最后他们喝完咖啡，站起来，朝你轻轻点了点头，还是那么从容。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good company, low noise. That's a good sit. Thanks for not making it a performance.
beats.chinese: 好同伴，低噪音。这就是一次很好的小坐。谢谢你没把这变成一场表演。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Marlowe nods, entirely unbothered, and stays where they are — a little apart, coffee steady in their hands.
beats.chinese: 马洛点点头，毫不介意，留在原地——稍微隔开一点，咖啡稳稳地端在手里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then it's doing its job for one of us. Honestly, I mean that. Someone should enjoy it.
beats.chinese: 那它至少对咱们中的一个有用。说真的，我是这个意思。总得有人享受它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You like what you like, and I need what I need. Neither of those is a problem, they just don't share a bench today.
beats.chinese: 你喜欢你的，我需要我的。这两件事都不成问题，只是今天不同坐一条长椅而已。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They shift a little further along, still close enough to talk, and raise their cup towards you in a small toast.
beats.chinese: 他们再往旁边挪了一点，仍近得可以说话，并举起咖啡杯向你小小致意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll stay over here where my ears can rest, and we can still chat. That suits me just fine.
beats.chinese: 我就在这边待着，让耳朵歇歇，咱们照样聊。这样我觉得挺好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, always. I say it first, plainly, before anyone's picked a place. Saves the awkward bit later.
beats.chinese: 哦，一直都说。在大家选地方之前，我就直说了。省得后面尴尬。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They set the cup down and count off on their fingers, as if this is a well-practised routine.
beats.chinese: 他们放下杯子，掰着手指数，像是在说一套练得很熟的流程。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll still come, I'll still be first to suggest the catch-up — I just name a quiet spot while I'm at it. My friends stopped being surprised years ago.
beats.chinese: 我还是会去，还是第一个提议聚会——只是顺带挑个安静的地方。我的朋友们几年前就不觉得意外了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It works better than hoping they'll guess. Nobody's a mind reader, and I'd rather say it once than resent it all night.
beats.chinese: 这比指望他们猜强多了。谁也不会读心，我宁愿说一次，也不想憋一晚上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pick the cup back up, looking pleased with the state of things.
beats.chinese: 他们重新端起杯子，看起来对现状颇为满意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Marlowe waves off the apology before it's even fully out, unhurried as ever.
beats.chinese: 马洛在那句抱歉还没说完之前就摆了摆手，一如既往地从容。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're not disturbing anything. Sitting near someone in silence is a perfectly good way to share a park.
beats.chinese: 你没有打扰什么。安静地坐在别人旁边，就是共享一个公园的很好的方式。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But if you've got places to be, go be there. I'll be right here enjoying the not-listening.
beats.chinese: 不过你要是有地方要去，就去吧。我就在这儿享受这什么都不用听的状态。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They settle back against the bench, eyes half on the water, entirely at ease with the moment ending.
beats.chinese: 他们靠回长椅，眼睛半望着水面，对这一刻的结束全然自在。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your coffee. And enjoy the noise, if that's your thing — someone should.
beats.chinese: 咖啡喝好。也好好享受那些声音，如果那是你的菜的话——总得有人享受。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The same bench under the fig tree. You sit down with a coffee, and a familiar figure is already there, flipping through printed photos of a half-dismantled shortwave radio.
beats.chinese: 还是无花果树下那条长椅。你端着咖啡坐下，一个熟悉的身影已经在那儿，翻着一沓半拆开的短波收音机的照片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, look at that — same bench, same coffee. The park's treating us well.
beats.chinese: 哟，瞧瞧——同一条长椅，同样的咖啡。这公园对我们不错。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They hold up a photo of a tangle of valves and wiring, machine clearly switched off in the shot.
beats.chinese: 他们举起一张照片，上面是一团电子管和线路，照片里的机器明显是关着的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This old thing's finally repaired. Doesn't mean I'll switch it on straight away — it can sit at home being fixed and quiet for a while. Both can be true.
beats.chinese: 这老伙计终于修好了。不代表我马上就开机——它可以先在家里待着，既是修好的，也是安静的。两件事不冲突。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, good company, low noise — still my kind of sit. How have you been?
beats.chinese: 总之，好同伴，低噪音——还是我喜欢的坐法。你最近怎么样？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They slide the photos back into their pocket and settle in, unhurried, leaving the silence comfortably open.
beats.chinese: 他们把照片收回口袋，从容地坐好，让这份安静舒舒服服地敞着。

card.name: Emile Gravois
card.occupation: sail canvas cutter at a marine loft
card.personality: Emile's trouble isn't saying yes — it's what he says after. When he takes on more than he can carry, he doesn't admit it; he reports progress that doesn't exist. 'Already cutting it.' 'Half done, just needs the hem.' He fabricates a comfortable margin between what he's claimed and what he's actually touched, and maintains the fiction with increasingly detailed status updates — percentages, thread counts, weather delays. The lie isn't malicious; it buys him time and spares everyone the awkwardness of 'I haven't started.'
