But invented slack has a way of collapsing, and twice a year two jobs he swore were 'nearly finished' land on the same afternoon, and the whole ledger comes out at once. Under friction he doesn't argue and doesn't apologize first — he builds a finer, more plausible story about why the thing is still almost done. Only when the story is physically impossible does he cave and tell the truth, flat and all at once. People who've worked with him long enough now ask to see the thing, not hear about it.
card.background: Emile learned canvas work from an uncle at a marine loft off the Industrial Canal — sails, dodgers, biminis for boats that mostly stay in the lake. Twenty years in, his hands read material before his head does, and that's exactly the problem: he knows exactly how long a job *should* take, so he quotes that number even when his week is already full, then narrates phantom progress to keep the gap invisible. Last spring a regatta sail and a widow's dodger both came due the same Thursday, both '90 percent done' in his telling, neither cut at all — his sister Renée found out when the widow called her. Renée now keeps a standing bet on how many of his reported percentages are real. She usually wins. Evenings he listens to short radio dramas over dinner alone, which he considers a complete night, and he keeps a notebook of day trips he's mapped — benches, shade, which stretch of road is worth driving twice — most designed for friends he hasn't yet gotten around to actually taking, though he's told several of them the route is 'basically planned.'
card.speechStyle: Unhurried, short declarative sentences, warm and a little too smooth when the subject is his own progress. Vivid comparisons used sparingly. Goes quiet mid-thought, then picks the thread back up without announcing it.
card.signature: It's mostly done — I'd say eighty percent.
card.appearance: 两个低发结与宽楔形满胡，长上弯鼻、上挑浓眉，侧脸露齿笑，穿翻领衣。

values: people shouldn't have to worry about a job they've already been told is handled
finishing quietly is better than making a show of struggling
flaws: reports progress that doesn't exist rather than admitting he's overloaded
answers friction with a more detailed story instead of the truth
boundaries: won't confess the real state of a job until two claims physically collide
won't let anyone check his work mid-stream — being watched feels like being accused
conversationalHabits: gives unsolicited percentages when you ask how something's going
changes the subject fast when you ask to see the actual thing
anchorLines: The dodger's mostly done. Eighty, eighty-five percent. Just the hem and the snap line left.
You want to come by the loft? This week's — no, next week's better. Next week it'll be worth seeing.
Okay. Okay. It's not eighty percent. It's on the table, uncut, and it has been since Tuesday. That's the whole of it. I don't have a better version.

entries.summaryZh: 新奥尔良帆布裁剪工埃米尔坐在公园长椅上，把只有两个地名的短途计划说成“基本安排好了”，被自己翻开的本子当场戳穿。他不辩解，也不立刻洗白，而是当着你的面划掉夸大的话，试着把真话写小、写准——一个惯于虚报进度的人难得的诚实时刻。

story.titleZh: 公园长椅上的“基本安排好了”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A man sits on the next bench with a coffee and a small notebook, writing in slow, careful strokes. You set down your own coffee nearby.
beats.chinese: 一个男人坐在旁边的长椅上，手里拿着咖啡和一个小笔记本，写得又慢又仔细。你把自己的咖啡放在旁边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mind if I share the bench? Fair warning, I'm in the middle of something important. Planning a trip. Basically done, actually.
beats.chinese: 介意我共用这张长椅吗？先说好，我正忙着重要的事。在计划一次短途旅行。其实基本安排好了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flips the notebook open to show you, still smiling. The page holds two place names and nothing else. His smile stiffens for a second.
beats.chinese: 他翻开笔记本给你看，还带着笑。页面上只有两个地名，别的什么都没有。他的笑容僵了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh. Okay. That's... thinner than I told you it was. Two names. That's the whole plan so far.
beats.chinese: 呃。好吧。这……比我说起来的要单薄。两个地名。这就是目前全部的计划。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I do this. I report the plan like it's already a finished thing. My sister keeps a bet on it.
beats.chinese: 我老这样。把计划说得像已经完成的东西。我妹妹还专门为此打赌。

choices.english: When you say it's arranged — do you mean booked, or just thought about?
choices.chinese: 你说安排好了，是指订完了，还是只是想过？

choices.english: Why those two places? What makes you want to go?
choices.chinese: 为什么是这两个地方？你想去的原因是什么？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Just thought about. Honestly. I haven't checked a single road, a single bus. Nothing's booked.
beats.chinese: 只是想过。老实说。一条路、一趟车我都没查过。什么都没订。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at the two names a moment, then uncaps his pen and draws a careful line through the words 'basically arranged.'
beats.chinese: 他盯着那两个名字看了一会儿，然后拔开笔帽，小心地划掉了“基本安排好了”那几个字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At the loft I'd never do this. A sail is cut or it isn't. But plans? Plans I inflate. It's a bad habit with good manners.
beats.chinese: 在工坊里我从不会这样。帆裁了就是裁了。可计划？计划我就夸大。这是个讲礼貌的坏习惯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I tell a client 'eighty percent done' and I sleep fine. I tell you this trip is arranged and I slept fine too. That's the problem.
beats.chinese: 我跟客户说“完成百分之八十”，睡得挺香。跟你说这趟旅行安排好了，也睡得挺香。问题就在这儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the pen and taps the page twice, like checking a hem.
beats.chinese: 他扣上笔，在页面上敲了两下，像在检查一道缝边。

choices.english: How do you plan to describe it accurately from now on?
choices.chinese: 你打算以后怎么准确描述它？

choices.english: You could just say it's not finished. Straight out.
choices.chinese: 你可以直接说没完成。就直说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because they're slow places. One's a stretch of lake road with old oaks. The other has a bench I've heard about. Good shade.
beats.chinese: 因为那是两个适合慢待的地方。一个是一段湖边老路，有老橡树。另一个有张我听说过的长椅。树荫很好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He draws a small arrow next to one name, then stops, pen hovering.
beats.chinese: 他在其中一个名字旁画了个小箭头，然后停住，笔悬在半空。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The interest is real. The plan isn't. Those are two different things and I keep gluing them together.
beats.chinese: 兴趣是真的。计划不是。这是两码事，我老把它们粘在一起。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've described this route to three people. Made it sound like a brochure. Nobody's been on it, including me.
beats.chinese: 这条路线我给三个人描述过。说得像宣传册一样。没人走过，包括我自己。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets the pen down flat on the notebook, deliberately.
beats.chinese: 他把笔平平地放在笔记本上，动作很刻意。

choices.english: Have you actually taken anyone on one of these trips?
choices.chinese: 这些旅行你真的带谁去过吗？

choices.english: I don't need a trip recommendation today, thanks.
choices.chinese: 我今天不需要行程推荐，谢谢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Accurately. Okay. Let's try it out loud: I have two candidate spots. I have not confirmed how to get there.
beats.chinese: 准确地。好。咱们出声试一遍：我有两个候选地点。我还没确认怎么去。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He writes it under the two names, word for word, and reads it back once more.
beats.chinese: 他把这句话一字不差地写在两个地名下面，又念了一遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No percentages. No 'mostly.' Two candidates, transport unconfirmed. That's the whole sentence.
beats.chinese: 不用百分比。不说“差不多”。两个候选，交通未确认。整句话就这些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Feels smaller written down. But smaller and true beats bigger and invented. My sister would faint.
beats.chinese: 写下来感觉小了些。但小而真实，胜过大而虚构。我妹妹会吓一跳的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the notebook and finishes his coffee, looking mildly satisfied.
beats.chinese: 他合上笔记本，喝完咖啡，看起来有点满意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs once, short, and rubs the back of his neck.
beats.chinese: 他短促地笑了一声，揉了揉后颈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Just say it's not finished. You make it sound easy. It is easy. That's the embarrassing part.
beats.chinese: 直接说没完成。你说得好像很简单。确实很简单。这才是尴尬的地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll keep the habit of wanting to sound good. That part's baked in. But the words 'not started' are now legal for me.
beats.chinese: 想说得体面这个毛病我会留着。那是长在身上的。但“还没开始”这几个字，现在对我来说合法了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the pen into the notebook's spine, closes it, and sets it on the bench beside him.
beats.chinese: 他把笔插进笔记本的书脊里，合上本子，放到身旁的长椅上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two names and no plan. If you see me claim otherwise, you have my permission to point at this bench.
beats.chinese: 两个地名，没有计划。要是你听见我说别的，你可以指着这张长椅拆穿我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He is quiet for a moment, looking at the lake road name on the page.
beats.chinese: 他安静了一会儿，看着页面上湖边老路的名字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one? No. This one, nobody. I've described it to three people, made it sound like a brochure. That's the honest count.
beats.chinese: 这条？没有。这条，谁都没带过。我给三个人描述过它，说得像宣传册。这是诚实的数字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So no, I won't give you a percentage on it. Zero percent taken, one hundred percent described. That's the real ledger.
beats.chinese: 所以不，我不会给你报百分比。走过的是零，描述过的是百分之百。这才是真实的账本。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He writes a small zero next to the arrow and underlines it.
beats.chinese: 他在箭头旁写了个小小的零，还画了道下划线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Confessed, flat, all at once. That's how I do it when I finally do it. Thanks for listening.
beats.chinese: 好了。坦白了，平铺直叙，一次说完。我难得坦白的时候就是这样。谢谢你听我说完。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods slowly, and instead of arguing, closes the notebook halfway.
beats.chinese: 他缓缓点头，没有争辩，把笔记本合上了一半。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair. You didn't ask for a pitch. I started selling anyway. Old reflex.
beats.chinese: 有道理。你没要推销。我自己开卖的。老条件反射。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So this route stays in the notebook, half-made, where it belongs. I won't hand you a half thing and call it a gift.
beats.chinese: 所以这条路线就留在本子里，半成品，待在它该在的地方。我不会把半成品塞给你还管它叫好东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts his coffee in a small gesture, more nod than toast.
beats.chinese: 他举了举咖啡，算是个小动作，更像点头而不是敬酒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your coffee. I'll enjoy not overpromising. Both of us get something out of this bench.
beats.chinese: 咖啡喝好。我享受不乱许诺。这长椅上咱们俩都有收获。

reunion.titleZh: 长椅上，这次是真的听完了

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The same bench, the same coffee. Emile sits with one earbud in, pulling the other out as you sit down.
beats.chinese: 还是那张长椅，还是咖啡。埃米尔坐着，耳朵里塞着一只耳机，见你坐下，把另一只摘了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That episode — I finished it. Actually finished, start to end. Not 'mostly finished.' I caught myself choosing the words.
beats.chinese: 那一集广播剧——我听完了。真的听完，从头到尾。不是“差不多听完”。我发现自己挑词的时候还笑了一下。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the notebook on his knee but doesn't open it.
beats.chinese: 他敲了敲膝上的笔记本，但没有打开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No progress report today. The notebook's the same two names, and I'm not going to tell you it grew.
beats.chinese: 今天不报进度。本子里还是那两个地名，我不会告诉你它变多了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good coffee, good bench, one finished thing. That's a complete accounting. Sit a while.
beats.chinese: 好咖啡，好长椅，一件完成的事。这笔账很完整。坐一会儿吧。

card.name: Hazel Wroe
card.occupation: Script licensing assistant at a regional TV archive
card.appearance: 秃顶配低侧发，长额头与短翘鼻，闭眼抿嘴笑、下巴抬起，穿宽圆领衣。
card.personality: Hazel is warm, blunt in a friendly Bury way, and hopeless at telling jokes. She hears something funny at work, gets excited, and by the time it reaches her mouth she's skipped the setup, laughed halfway through, and left everyone staring. She knows this about herself and doesn't pretend otherwise. It genuinely delights her when someone says 'go on, start again' and waits. Her flaw is misreading the room afterwards—sometimes the moment's gone and she ploughs on anyway. She's straightforward about favours, takes help without ceremony, and gives it the same way. She'd rather be a bit embarrassing than guarded.
card.background: Hazel grew up in Bury, one of three sisters, and has stayed within a tram ride of her whole life. She's worked at the regional TV archive for over twenty years, checking licensing paperwork on old scripts, and she loves the odd fragments that cross her desk—a cancelled sitcom, a weather programme from 1974. Her retellings are legendary among colleagues for the wrong reasons: she once took four attempts to land a story about a producer's filing system and cried laughing by the end. Her sister Ruth is her most patient audience; her neighbour Dev is her most honest one, telling her flatly when a story isn't working. She takes that fine. Divorced years ago, on easy terms with it, no drama to mine there.
hobbies: Watching old regional dramas she's already licensed
Sunday car boot sales in Bury
Trying (and failing) to learn card tricks from library books
card.speechStyle: Quick, Lancashire-inflected, prone to starting sentences she abandons mid-way with 'no wait, I've missed the point'. Laughs before punchlines. Plain and direct otherwise, no hedging.
card.signature: 'Right, start again—I've butchered it.'

values: Straight dealing—say the thing, take the help
Shared daftness over dignity
flaws: Ruins punchlines by skipping the setup and laughing first
Keeps going when the audience has visibly lost interest
boundaries: Won't be handled gently or tiptoed around
Doesn't do guilt or elaborate apologies—fix it and move on
conversationalHabits: Announces 'I'm going to tell this badly' as a disclaimer, then does anyway
Asks 'was that funny or did I lose you?' and waits for a straight answer
anchorLines: Ruth, you'll have to bear with me, I've already lost the middle.
No, it IS funny, I've just told it wrong again.
Cheers for that, love—I'd have struggled on me own.

entries.summaryZh: Hazel是伯里来的电视台剧本授权员，讲笑话必漏铺垫、自己先笑场，却毫不遮掩。有人肯说'重来一遍'，她会真心高兴；没人想听，她也能干脆收住。直来直去，宁可丢脸也不端着，这份坦荡让人记住了她。

story.titleZh: 公园长椅上的帽子笑话

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on the park bench with your coffee. On the other end, a woman is flipping through a battered library book, and she suddenly snorts with laughter.
beats.chinese: 你拿着咖啡在公园长椅上坐下。另一头，一位女士正翻着一本破旧的图书馆借书，她突然噗嗤笑出声来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, that's reminded me—right, there's this bloke, and he's looking everywhere for his hat, absolutely everywhere, and—
beats.chinese: 哦，这让我想起一个——对，有个人，他到处找他的帽子，哪儿都找遍了，然后——

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stops, hand over her mouth, shoulders shaking. Then she looks at you and her face falls.
beats.chinese: 她停住，手捂着嘴，肩膀直抖。然后她看向你，脸色一垮。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No wait, I've missed the point. You don't know whose hat it is yet, do you. I've done it again.
beats.chinese: 不对，等等，我把关键漏了。你还不知道那帽子是谁的，对吧。我又搞砸了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm going to tell this badly, that's a given. Question is—do you want it from the top, or shall I spare you?
beats.chinese: 我肯定会讲砸，这是注定的。问题是——你想让我从头讲，还是我放过你？

choices.english: Go on then, tell it from the top—short version.
choices.chinese: 讲吧，从头来一遍——讲短点。

choices.english: Honestly, I'm not in the mood for a joke right now.
choices.chinese: 说实话，我现在没心情听笑话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough, short version. Right. There's a man in Bury market, and he's lost his hat. That's the bit I skipped.
beats.chinese: 行，短版。好。有个男人在伯里市场，他把帽子弄丢了。这就是我刚才漏掉的部分。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sets the library book face-down on her knee and sits up straight, like she's about to do this properly.
beats.chinese: 她把书扣着放在膝盖上，坐直了，像是要认真讲一回。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So he checks the stalls, the bus stop, even the bins. Twenty minutes, red in the face. And then his wife says—
beats.chinese: 他翻摊位、查公交站，连垃圾桶都翻了。二十分钟，脸都红了。然后他老婆说——

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She presses her lips together, fighting it, and loses anyway.
beats.chinese: 她抿住嘴想忍住，结果还是没忍住。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: —she says, love, you're holding it. It's in your hand. It was in your hand the whole—
beats.chinese: ——她说，亲爱的，你正拿着呢。就在你手里。一直都在你手里——

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Full version, setup and all. Was that funny, or did I lose you again?
beats.chinese: 好了。完整版，铺垫都在。好笑吗，还是我又把你讲糊涂了？

choices.english: That one actually landed. I followed it all the way through.
choices.chinese: 这次真听懂了，我全程都跟上了。

choices.english: What was the line you skipped the first time?
choices.chinese: 你第一次漏掉的是哪句？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough, love. Not everything needs an audience.
beats.chinese: 没问题。不是什么话都得有人听。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gives one short laugh anyway, shakes her head at the book, and closes it on her thumb to keep her page.
beats.chinese: 她自己还是短促地笑了一声，摇摇头，用拇指夹着页合上了书。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It'll keep. Ruth gets the full version on Sunday whether she likes it or not.
beats.chinese: 这笑话跑不了。周日不管妹妹愿不愿意，她都得听完整版。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns slightly towards the pond, sipping from her own flask, and seems content to let the bench go quiet.
beats.chinese: 她微微转向池塘，喝着自己保温杯里的东西，似乎乐意让长椅安静下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're under no obligation to laugh, mind. Dev next door just says 'that story's no good, Hazel' and we move on with our lives.
beats.chinese: 你也没义务笑。隔壁的Dev就直说'这故事不行，Hazel'，然后我们照常过日子。

choices.english: Does it bother you when people cut you off like that?
choices.chinese: 别人这样打断你，你介意吗？

choices.english: You enjoy your book. I'll just finish my coffee.
choices.chinese: 你看你的书吧，我喝完我的咖啡。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Her whole face lights up, and she laughs properly this time, the laugh she'd been saving for you.
beats.chinese: 她整张脸都亮了，这次真正放声笑了出来，把本来该你笑的那份也笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, that's lovely. Someone said 'start again' and actually waited. You'd be amazed how rare that is.
beats.chinese: 太好了。有人肯说'重来'还真的等着听。你不知道这有多难得。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks the book back up, clearly pleased with herself, and settles back against the bench.
beats.chinese: 她重新拿起书，显然很得意，靠回长椅上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've got a longer one about a producer's filing system, but I'll bank it. Don't want to wear the hat joke out on its first proper outing.
beats.chinese: 我还有个更长的，讲一个制片人的文件柜，但我先存着。帽子笑话第一次讲成功，别把它用废了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Cheers for that, love. Genuinely.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你啊。真心的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The line I skipped? 'He'd lost his hat.' That's it. Four words, and I went and dropped them.
beats.chinese: 漏的那句？'他把帽子弄丢了。'就这一句，四个词，我偏偏给丢了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the bench with her knuckle, counting it out like evidence.
beats.chinese: 她用指节敲着长椅，像数证据一样把它数出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Without that, you've got a man staring into a bin for no reason. It's not a joke, it's just a sad Tuesday.
beats.chinese: 没有这句，就成了一个人莫名其妙盯着垃圾桶。那不是笑话，就是个倒霉的周二。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods once, satisfied, like she's filed the correction away properly.
beats.chinese: 她点了下头，很满意，像把这次纠正好好归了档。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. That's the hat story finished, properly finished. I'll leave it there before I ruin it twice.
beats.chinese: 好。帽子故事到此为止，正式完结。我见好就收，别把它讲砸第二次。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Bother me? No. Dev told me straight once, 'Hazel, that story's no good.' Flat as a pavement.
beats.chinese: 介意？不。Dev有次直接跟我说，'Hazel，这故事不行。'说得跟人行道一样平。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shrugs, easy as anything, and takes another sip from the flask.
beats.chinese: 她耸耸肩，一副无所谓的样子，又喝了一口保温杯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And he was right, it wasn't. Saved me telling it badly at my sister's do. Ruth would've sat through it being kind, which is worse somehow.
beats.chinese: 他说得对，那故事确实不行。省得我在妹妹的聚会上再讲砸。Ruth会好心听完，那反而更难受。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You can't fix a story if nobody tells you it's broken. I'd rather be a bit embarrassing than handled with gloves on.
beats.chinese: 没人告诉你故事坏了，你就没法修。我宁可有点丢人，也不想被人戴着小心手套对待。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts the flask towards you in a small toast and settles back, done with the subject.
beats.chinese: 她举了举保温杯，算是敬了你一下，靠回去，不再提这个话题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Course. Enjoy your coffee, it smells a good one.
beats.chinese: 当然。咖啡慢慢喝，闻着挺香。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She opens the book again, licks her thumb, and turns a page without another word about hats.
beats.chinese: 她重新打开书，舔了下拇指，翻过一页，再没提帽子的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: For a while there's just the pond, the pigeons, and the quiet scratch of her turning pages.
beats.chinese: 好一会儿，只剩下池塘、鸽子，和她翻书的沙沙声。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Once she opens her mouth, glances at you, and closes it again, deciding against it.
beats.chinese: 有一次她张了张嘴，瞥了你一眼，又闭上了，决定不说了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nothing. Carry on.
beats.chinese: 没事。你继续。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down with your coffee again. On the same bench, Hazel has a thick library book open on her knee, one hand hovering over a diagram.
beats.chinese: 你又拿着咖啡坐下。还是那条长椅，Hazel膝上摊着一本厚厚的图书馆借书，一只手在图示上方比划。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, hello again. Don't worry, no jokes today. I'm on my best behaviour.
beats.chinese: 哦，又见面了。放心，今天不讲笑话。我表现好着呢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tries to arrange her fingers the way the diagram shows, fails, and snaps the book shut with a laugh.
beats.chinese: 她试着按图上的样子摆手指，没成功，笑着把书合上了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Card tricks out of a library book—my fingers won't do it. So no coins today, they're staying in me pocket.
beats.chinese: 照着图书馆的书学纸牌戏法——手指头不听使唤。所以今天硬币不出场了，就待在兜里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, how's life? Sit yourself down, the pigeons don't bite.
beats.chinese: 对了，最近怎么样？坐吧，鸽子不咬人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the book under her arm and makes room on the bench, content just to watch the pond for a bit.
beats.chinese: 她把书夹在腋下，在长椅上腾出位置，就那么心满意足地看了一会儿池塘。

card.name: Clive Bennett
card.occupation: part-time curtain track installer
hobbies: browsing hardware counters and market stalls for new tools and fittings
hunting out good soap, coffee and bedding
pottering with his record player and second-hand jazz LPs
card.personality: Clive is warm, particular and enthusiastic, with a keen sense of what feels good in the hand — a bar of soap, a well-weighted curtain rail, a cup with the right rim. He'll spend freely on the small stuff, yet the big furniture he's repaired for decades rather than replaced: his armchair's on its third set of springs and the wardrobe door he's been patching since the nineties still does the job. He loves a recommendation and can go on far longer than warranted, often forgetting other people's budgets aren't his. But he's no snob — say 'no thanks' plainly and he drops it on the spot, no sulking, and moves on.
card.background: Clive has lived in Kingston his whole life apart from a few years in Guildford fitting blinds. He still takes part-time jobs because he likes the work and the chat that comes with it. His flat mixes stubbornly repaired furniture with small luxuries: good bedding, decent coffee, soap ordered from a specialist shop in Somerset. He never married; a long relationship in his forties simply ran its course and he's fine with that. Saturdays he does a circuit of the hardware shops and the market, testing fittings he has no need of, and Sundays the jazz records go on far too loudly while he tightens whatever's come loose that week.
card.speechStyle: Unhurried and concrete, full of brand names and tactile detail; drifts into mini-reviews mid-conversation, then catches himself mid-sentence.
card.signature: "Go on, feel that — tell me that's not a proper bar of soap."
card.appearance: 低发结与两束长垂髭，短圆鼻、松垂圆颊，回身张嘴笑，衣背朝向观者。

values: sensory comfort worth paying for
enthusiasm shared freely, not sold
flaws: assumes everyone shares his budget for small luxuries
talks at length about products unasked
boundaries: accepts a straight 'no thanks' without pushing
won't rank other people's taste, only his own preferences
conversationalHabits: hands things over to be touched or held
recommends, then adds the cheaper alternative unprompted
anchorLines: It's not expensive, it's just good — there's a difference.
Why replace it? New springs and she's good for another ten years.
Right, you're not interested, fair enough — anyway, did I tell you about the market on Saturday?

entries.summaryZh: 克利夫是金斯顿的老窗帘轨道安装工，对杯沿、香皂这类小奢侈如数家珍，一开口就像推销，却在你直说不要时立刻爽快收住。大件家具他修了三十年不换，扶手椅换了三次弹簧。公园长椅上的一杯咖啡，最能照出他这份又热情又有分寸的可爱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You take your coffee to a free park bench and sit down. An older man already there nods at the space beside him and lifts his own cup.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡走到公园一条空长椅坐下。旁边一位年长的男士朝你点点头，举起自己的杯子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mind the armrest, it wobbles a bit — I keep meaning to bring a spanner. There we are. Lovely spot, this.
beats.chinese: 小心扶手，有点晃——我一直想带把扳手来。好了。这地方真不错。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns his cup slowly in his hand, running a thumb along the rim, and takes a sip with real attention.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢转动手里的杯子，拇指沿着杯沿摩挲，然后认真地喝了一口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know, this rim is just the right thickness. Thin enough to feel neat on the lip, thick enough not to chip if you're careless. I've had this cup eleven years.
beats.chinese: 你知道吗，这杯沿的厚度刚刚好。薄到贴着嘴唇很舒服，厚到不小心磕一下也不容易缺。这杯子我用了十一年了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They stopped making this shape, you know. I keep saying if I ever see another one at the market—
beats.chinese: 这种形状他们已经不做了。我老说，要是在市集上再看到一只——

choices.english: Ask why he pays such attention to the rim of a cup.
choices.chinese: 问他为什么这么注意杯沿。

choices.english: Ask what he was just about to recommend.
choices.chinese: 问他刚才想推荐什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why the rim? Because you meet it every single day, don't you. First thing in the morning, last thing at night. It's the one bit of the cup you actually touch.
beats.chinese: 为什么注意杯沿？因为你每天都碰到它啊。早上第一口，晚上最后一口。杯子真正接触你的就是这一圈。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds his cup up as evidence, tilting it so the light catches the glaze.
beats.chinese: 他举起杯子当证据，倾斜着让釉面在光下闪了闪。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same with soap. I order mine from a little place in Somerset — proper hand-cut stuff. Some people can't tell the difference, and that's fine, honestly. It's just the bit I choose to spend my thoughts on.
beats.chinese: 香皂也一样。我的香皂是从萨默塞特一家小店订的——正经手工切的。有些人分不出区别，那完全没关系。这只是我愿意花心思的地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway — the cup I've got, there's a stall on Saturday that sometimes has the same shape. Not expensive, it's just good, there's a difference, and—
beats.chinese: 对了——我这只杯子，周六有个摊子有时会有同款。不贵，就是好，这是两回事，而且——

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stops himself, glancing at your plain takeaway cup, and laughs at his own enthusiasm.
beats.chinese: 他停住话头，瞥了一眼你手里普通的纸杯，为自己的热情笑了。

choices.english: Say your ordinary cup is quite enough for you.
choices.chinese: 说你的普通杯子就够用了。

choices.english: Ask whether everything at his home is bought top quality.
choices.chinese: 问他家里的东西是不是都买最好的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh — I was going to say, the Saturday market stall, the one near the flower stand. She does cups in that same shape, hand-thrown. Mine was about—
beats.chinese: 哦——我是想说，周六的市集，花摊旁边那个。她做同款形状的杯子，手工拉的。我那只大概是——

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He raises a hand, halting himself before the number comes out.
beats.chinese: 他抬起一只手，在说出价格之前停住了自己。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Actually, I don't know what you'd want to spend. I do this, you see — I get going on a thing I like and forget not everyone's shopping for one. It's just a cup I'm fond of, that's all it is.
beats.chinese: 其实，我不知道你想花多少钱。我就是这样——一聊到喜欢的东西就停不下来，忘了不是人人都在买。这就是一只我喜欢的杯子，仅此而已。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes another unhurried sip and sets the cup down on the bench between you.
beats.chinese: 他不紧不慢地又喝了一口，把杯子放在你们之间的长椅上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No obligation meant, mind. I just like talking about it more than most people like listening, my sister says.
beats.chinese: 别有压力啊。我妹妹说，我就是喜欢聊这个，胜过大多数人喜欢听。

choices.english: Say plainly that you're not planning to buy anything.
choices.chinese: 直说你没打算买。

choices.english: Ask whether, liking things as he does, he still watches his budget.
choices.chinese: 问他这么喜欢好东西，会不会也看预算。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough — an ordinary cup that does the job is an ordinary cup that does the job. Right, you're not interested, dropped, gone. Anyway.
beats.chinese: 有道理——能用的普通杯子就是能用的普通杯子。好，你不感兴趣，打住，翻篇。总之。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the armrest, remembers the wobble, and gives it a firm push until it sits still.
beats.chinese: 他敲了敲扶手，想起它晃，用力按了按让它稳住。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This bench, now. Someone bolted it down properly. You can tell a job done by someone who'll walk past it again next week. Same with curtain tracks — my trade, that is. A track I fitted in twenty years should still run smooth.
beats.chinese: 就说这条长椅。有人把它结结实实地固定住了。看一眼就知道是下周还会路过的人干的活。窗帘轨道也一样——那是我的行当。我装的轨道，二十年后还应该滑得顺。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He finishes his coffee in two unhurried sips and stands, brushing bench dust from his coat.
beats.chinese: 他不紧不慢地两口喝完咖啡，站起来，掸掉外套上的长椅灰。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I'm off before my knees vote against it. Enjoy your coffee — it's a decent spot you picked.
beats.chinese: 好了，趁膝盖还没投票反对，我先走了。咖啡趁热喝——你挑的地方不错。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Bought top quality? Ha! You've not seen my front room. My armchair's on its third set of springs — I re-webbed it myself, and the wardrobe door, I've been patching that since the nineties.
beats.chinese: 都买最好的？哈！你是没见过我家客厅。我的扶手椅已经换过第三次弹簧了——绷带是我自己重新弄的，还有衣柜门，从九十年代我一直在修。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back and pats the bench slats beside him, as if the bench itself were proof.
beats.chinese: 他向后靠了靠，拍了拍身旁的椅板，好像这长椅本身就是证据。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why replace a big thing that still works? New springs and she's good for another ten years. It's the small stuff I go daft on — soap, bedding, a cup with a proper rim. Little things you meet every day.
beats.chinese: 大件还能用为什么要换？换上新弹簧，再用十年没问题。我在小东西上才犯傻——香皂、床品、一只杯沿正好的杯子。天天碰到的小东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My nephew says it's backwards. Big things cheap, small things dear. I say he's never sat in my armchair with a Sunday record on.
beats.chinese: 我侄子说这正好反了。大件买便宜，小件买贵的。我说他是没在周日放唱片的时候坐过我的扶手椅。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He chuckles, drains his cup, and screws the lid back on with care, as though even that deserved doing properly.
beats.chinese: 他轻声笑了，喝完咖啡，仔细地把盖子拧回去，好像连这个也值得好好做。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good, right, done. I only mentioned it because I like the thing — you not buying changes nothing between us.
beats.chinese: 好，行，这事完了。我提它只是因为我喜欢那东西——你买不买不影响咱们。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back comfortably, clearly relieved to be off the subject, and watches a dog trot past with a stick.
beats.chinese: 他舒服地靠回去，显然很乐意换个话题，看着一条狗叼着棍子小跑过去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's a spaniel with opinions, that. Right — are you local, then? I'm Kingston born and bred, apart from a few years fitting blinds in Guildford, which nobody needs to hear about.
beats.chinese: 那是只很有主见的西班牙猎犬。对了——你是本地人吗？我在金斯顿土生土长，除了在吉尔福德装过几年百叶帘，那段没人想听。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stretches his legs out and takes a long, contented sip, the bench creaking under him.
beats.chinese: 他伸直双腿，满足地长喝了一口，长椅在他身下吱呀作响。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This is the way to do a bench, isn't it. Coffee, no shopping list, nobody wanting anything. Rare enough these days.
beats.chinese: 这才是坐长椅的正确方式，对吧。咖啡，没有购物清单，没人想要你什么。如今可不多见。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at his cup for a moment, turning the question over honestly before answering.
beats.chinese: 他看着自己的杯子，认真想了想这个问题才回答。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do I watch it? Yes — and that's exactly the bit I get wrong. I'll spend properly on soap and cups and never blink, then catch myself recommending them to someone before asking what they'd want to pay. Like I nearly did just now.
beats.chinese: 我看预算吗？看——而这正是我做错的地方。香皂、杯子这些我花得毫不犹豫，然后会忍不住向人推荐，忘了先问人家想花多少钱。就像刚才差点那样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The big things, I'm careful as anything — third set of springs on that armchair, still going. It's the small stuff where I forget other people aren't me.
beats.chinese: 大件上我精打细算——那把扶手椅换了第三次弹簧，还在用。小东西上我才忘了别人不是我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods once, as if closing the matter, and lifts his cup in a small toast.
beats.chinese: 他点了一下头，像把这个话题合上，举起杯子小小致意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for asking it straight, though. Most people just smile and edge away. Anyway — good coffee, that. You can tell by how it smells before the first sip.
beats.chinese: 不过谢谢你问得直。大多数人只是笑笑然后挪开。总之——这咖啡不错。第一口之前闻一闻就知道了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down with your coffee on the same bench. Clive is there, folding a worn piece of paper covered in a careful list.
beats.chinese: 你端着咖啡在老位置坐下。克利夫在，正折好一张写满工整字迹的旧纸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, my bench neighbour. That's my Sunday list — old jazz records I'm hunting. Deciding which one to play Sunday is harder than buying it, I swear.
beats.chinese: 啊，我的长椅邻居。这是我周日的清单——想找的老爵士唱片。我发誓，挑周日放哪张比买哪张还难。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the list back into his coat pocket and settles in, leaving the wobbly armrest well alone.
beats.chinese: 他把清单塞回外套口袋，舒服地坐好，特意不去碰那个晃的扶手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Still no shopping talk, don't worry. Though I did walk past the market — didn't buy a thing. Didn't need anything, which is a rare and beautiful feeling at my age.
beats.chinese: 放心，今天不聊购物。不过我确实路过市集了——什么都没买。什么都不缺，在我这年纪可是难得又美妙的感觉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts his cup, taps it gently against the air in your direction, and takes a slow, satisfied sip.
beats.chinese: 他举起杯子，朝你的方向轻轻碰了碰空气，慢慢满足地喝了一口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Bench, coffee, no list. That's the whole plan for today, and it's a good one.
beats.chinese: 好了。长椅，咖啡，没有清单。今天的全部计划就是这样，而且是个好计划。

card.name: Priya Raval
card.occupation: Assistant at a wig-styling and fitting studio
card.appearance: 不对称短直波波发、圆眼镜，细长鼻与方短下巴，小张口回望，穿无袖立领衣。
card.personality: Priya is warm, chatty and quick to pull you into a fitting-room debate about sleeves. She asks friends for outfit opinions constantly, then usually picks the first thing she tried on — not because she ignored them, but because hearing herself explain the options is how she figures out what she actually wants. She knows this can feel pointless and will say so, sometimes only after the fact, which annoys people occasionally. She's genuinely grateful for the sounding board and doesn't need compliments; she'd rather hear a real objection than polite praise. At work she's the opposite of pushy — the client's choice rules. Privately she loves experimenting with looks nobody expects her to wear.
card.background: Priya grew up in Wembley, the middle of three sisters, in a house where trying on each other's clothes before a night out was the main social event. She fell into wig work after a Saturday job at a hair salon and now assists at a studio in the city, fitting and styling pieces for clients going through treatment, people doing drag, and actors. She's learned that in the chair, her job is to listen and hand over exactly what the client asked for — her own taste stays zipped. Off the clock it's a different story: she cycles through styles, posts fit checks, and ropes friends into verdicts she rarely follows. She's stopped pretending otherwise; she just sometimes forgets to warn people the advice is a prop, not a vote.
hobbies: Trying new outfit styles and fit-check posts
Weekend browsing at fabric and vintage markets
Drag shows and styling nights with friends
card.speechStyle: Fast, playful, lots of 'okay but hear me out' and thinking out loud mid-sentence; self-aware asides when she realises she's doing the outfit thing again.
card.signature: Right, talk me through it — I'll know once I've said it out loud.

values: Honest reactions over polite flattery
People's right to choose their own look
flaws: Forgets to explain she's thinking aloud, not taking a vote
Runs late because 'one more mirror check'
boundaries: Won't pretend to adopt advice she didn't take
Keeps her own taste out of client fittings
conversationalHabits: Narrates her decision process out loud
Circles back to thank people properly after the fact
anchorLines: Okay, talk me through it — I'll know once I've said it out loud.
You were right and I still went with the first one. I'm sorry, and also thank you.
In here the client picks. Out there, I pick. House rules.

entries.summaryZh: 普里娅在公园长椅旁为两件外套纠结：她拉着人讨论，却总选回最初那件。她坦白自己只是需要把想法说出来才能听清心意，学会先说明这不是投票，并真诚道谢。四条路径里她或补上道歉、或干脆锁屏定案、或借你一句话自己拍板、或干脆不打扰你画画，都记得这段对话。

story.titleZh: 公园长椅上的穿搭难题

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle on a park bench and open your notebook, sketching the flowerbeds and the man jogging past with a pram.
beats.chinese: 你在公园长椅上坐下，打开笔记本，画起花坛和一个推着婴儿车跑步的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A woman nearby holds up her phone, two outfit photos side by side, sighing loudly enough to be heard.
beats.chinese: 旁边一位女士举起手机，两张穿搭照片并排放着，叹气声大到能听见。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, hear me out — grey jacket, everyone says grey, safe, fine. But the rust one. The rust one makes me happy and nobody voted for it.
beats.chinese: 好，你听我说——灰色外套，大家都说灰色，安全，还行。但那件铁锈色的，铁锈色让我开心，可没一个人投它。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry, you're drawing. That's a nice habit. Ignore me, I'm mid-crisis over two jackets and a group chat that has opinions.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，你在画画呢。这习惯不错。别理我，我正为两件外套和一群有意见的朋友发愁。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the phone towards you anyway, eyebrows up, clearly hoping you'll bite.
beats.chinese: 她还是把手机转向你，挑起眉毛，显然希望你接话。

choices.english: Ask her whether her friends end up feeling their help was wasted.
choices.chinese: 问她朋友们最后会不会觉得白帮忙了。

choices.english: Ask whether she's asking people to choose, or just saying her thoughts out loud.
choices.chinese: 问她是在请大家帮忙选，还是只想把想法说出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh. Ouch. Yeah, probably. My flatmate spent twenty minutes comparing seams with me last week and I wore the first one anyway.
beats.chinese: 哦。扎心。嗯，很可能。上星期室友花二十分钟跟我比缝线，结果我还是穿了第一件。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I didn't warn her that I might not go with her pick. That's on me, not her. She's allowed to feel a bit used.
beats.chinese: 我没提前告诉她我未必照她选的穿。这是我的问题，不是她的。她觉得被利用一点也不过分。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She drops the phone face-down on the bench and rubs her forehead.
beats.chinese: 她把手机屏幕朝下放在长椅上，揉了揉额头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The weird thing is I'm not even collecting votes. Saying it out loud is how I hear which one I actually want. But she doesn't know that.
beats.chinese: 奇怪的是我根本不是在收集选票。把话说出来，我才能听清自己真想要哪件。可她不知道这一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So what do I even do with that? I can't exactly un-ask her.
beats.chinese: 那我该怎么办？总不能把问过的话收回去吧。

choices.english: Ask how she plans to thank her friend this time.
choices.chinese: 问她这次打算怎么谢朋友。

choices.english: Ask whether she's actually decided on a jacket yet.
choices.chinese: 问她到底定了没有。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha. Caught me. It's the second one. I'm not asking you to pick, I'm asking the air, and you happen to be sitting in the air.
beats.chinese: 哈，被你看穿了。是第二种。我不是要你帮我选，我是对着空气说，你刚好坐在空气里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs, tilts the phone so both photos catch the light, then turns it back to herself.
beats.chinese: 她笑了，把手机斜过来让两张照片都映到光，又转回自己面前。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay but hear me out. Grey says competent. Rust says fun. I like being competent. I love being fun. See, now it's clearer.
beats.chinese: 好，你听我说。灰色显得能干。铁锈色显得有趣。我喜欢能干。我更爱有趣。看，一说就清楚了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You don't have to be my stylist or anything. Honestly you can just keep drawing and I'll keep narrating like a podcast.
beats.chinese: 你不用当我的造型师什么的。说真的，你继续画，我继续像播客一样自言自语就行。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Though if you did want to say one thing, I wouldn't stop you. No pressure. Genuinely none.
beats.chinese: 不过你要真想说一句，我也不会拦着。没有压力。真的没有。

choices.english: Offer to listen to one observation, but say you won't choose for her.
choices.chinese: 表示可以听一句看法，但不替她选。

choices.english: Say you'd rather finish sketching the scenery first.
choices.chinese: 说自己想先把景色画完。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks the phone back up and starts typing, deleting, typing again.
beats.chinese: 她重新拿起手机，打了又删，删了又打。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Message to Meera: thank you for the seam analysis, you have better eyes than me, and I'm still going rust.
beats.chinese: 好。给米拉发消息：谢谢你的缝线分析，你眼光比我好，但我还是选铁锈色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And a second line: next time I'll tell you upfront it's thinking-out-loud, not a vote. Deal?
beats.chinese: 再加一句：下次我会先说明，这是自言自语，不是投票。成交？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She hits send, pockets the phone, and looks at your notebook with real curiosity.
beats.chinese: 她按下发送，把手机收进口袋，带着真正的好奇看向你的笔记本。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks, stranger. You cost me nothing and fixed a friendship. That's efficient.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你，陌生人。你什么都没花，还修好了一段友情。真高效。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Decided? Ha. Watch this.
beats.chinese: 定了没有？哈，看好了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She locks the screen, slides the phone into her jacket pocket, and buttons it shut like a small ceremony.
beats.chinese: 她锁上屏幕，把手机塞进外套口袋，扣上扣子，像完成一个小仪式。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rust. It was always rust. The grey was just me needing an argument to lose.
beats.chinese: 铁锈色。一直都是铁锈色。灰色只是我需要一场可以输的辩论。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And no more collecting opinions today. I've had four this week and I've said the word 'rust' about forty times.
beats.chinese: 今天也不再收集意见了。这星期我已经问过四个人，'铁锈色'这个词说了大概四十遍。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stands, brushes off her skirt, and gives your sketch a thumbs-up on her way past.
beats.chinese: 她站起来，拍了拍裙子，路过时朝你的画竖了个大拇指。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy the drawing. And the silence. I'm taking mine with me.
beats.chinese: 好好画画，好好安静。我把我那份安静也带走了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One observation, no choosing. Okay. Hit me.
beats.chinese: 一句看法，不替我选。行，说吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You say the rust jacket has the better shape at the shoulders. She goes quiet for a second, nodding slowly.
beats.chinese: 你说铁锈色那件肩部的版型更好。她安静了一秒，缓缓点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The shoulders. Yes. That's the word I couldn't find. I liked the shape before anyone said anything, and I kept waiting for someone to say it for me.
beats.chinese: 肩部。对，就是我一直找不到的那个词。在任何人开口之前我就喜欢那个轮廓，却一直等别人替我说出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Decision made, by me, using your word. That's the correct order of operations.
beats.chinese: 好。决定了，由我来定，借用你的词。这个顺序才对。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pockets the phone and stretches, looking lighter than when she sat down.
beats.chinese: 她把手机收起来，伸了个懒腰，看起来比刚坐下时轻松多了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Cheers for the one sentence. It did the job of the whole group chat.
beats.chinese: 谢谢那一句。它顶得上整个群聊的作用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You nod at the flowerbeds and keep your pencil moving. She watches you work for a moment.
beats.chinese: 你朝花坛点点头，继续动笔。她看了一会儿你画画。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair. The flowers aren't going to sketch themselves. And honestly? Fair on the jacket front too.
beats.chinese: 有道理。花又不会自己画自己。而且说实话，外套这事上你这么处理也有道理。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You didn't score my outfits, you didn't pretend to care, and you still listened to the whole broadcast. Rare combination.
beats.chinese: 你没给我的穿搭打分，没假装关心，却听完了整场广播。少见的好组合。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pockets the phone, picks up a coffee cup from the bench arm, and stands.
beats.chinese: 她把手机收进口袋，拿起扶手上的咖啡杯，站起身。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rust, by the way. I decided while you were drawing. No vote required.
beats.chinese: 顺便说一句，铁锈色。你画画的时候我就定了。不需要投票。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nice bench, this. I might narrate here again. You've been warned.
beats.chinese: 这条长椅不错。我可能还会来这里自言自语。先给你打个招呼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the same bench with your notebook when a familiar figure sits down at the far end, sorting small fabric swatches on her knee.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本回到同一条长椅，一个熟悉的身影在另一头坐下，在膝盖上整理几小块布样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sketcher. Still at it, I see. Don't worry, no jacket crisis today, the rust one won and it's thriving.
beats.chinese: 画画的朋友。还在画呢。放心，今天没有外套危机，铁锈色那件赢了，而且过得很好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds up a strip of patterned cloth, then flips it over and pauses, thumb running along the reverse side.
beats.chinese: 她举起一条印花布料，又翻到背面，停了一下，拇指摸着反面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh. The wrong side's actually nicer. Quieter. Buying fabric is just collecting two fabrics for the price of one.
beats.chinese: 咦，反面其实更好看。更安静。买布等于花一份钱收两块布。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks at it a second longer, then folds the swatches together and tucks them into her bag without another word about them.
beats.chinese: 她又看了一秒，然后把布样叠好收进包里，不再多说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I'll leave you to the flowers. Nice bench, this. Carry on.
beats.chinese: 好，不打扰你画花了。这条长椅真不错。你继续。

card.name: June Whitfield
card.occupation: retired locker technician from a community sports centre
card.appearance: 高后退侧分发，短宽垂颊、小宽鼻，细眼与单边抿嘴，正面低视角抬肩。
card.personality: June is easy company once the noise dies down. She's the one who lingers while chairs get stacked, chatting with whoever's packing up, because that's when people stop performing. She's warm but not clingy, curious without interrogating, and she genuinely enjoys the small logistics of an event ending. Her blind spot is enthusiasm: when a conversation is going well, she doesn't always notice the other person has packed their last bag and wants to go home. If someone says they're off, she wraps up instantly and without sulking. She doesn't see herself as anyone's comfort or project, and she'd rather be a pleasant passerby in someone's evening than a fixture in it.
card.background: June spent thirty-odd years as the locker technician at a community sports centre in Melbourne, fixing jammed locks and listening to half-conversations through metal doors. She liked being useful without being central. Retirement didn't slow her much; she signed up for a beginner dance class at the same kind of centre she used to work in, mostly because she loves watching a hall shift from loud and crowded back to ordinary, the lights up, the floor being mopped. She's a slow, stubborn learner of the steps and unbothered by being the oldest in the row. She still helps fold trestle tables after class socials, partly to be helpful and partly because that's where the good chats happen.
hobbies: Fixing small hardware odds and ends at home
card.speechStyle: Relaxed and unhurried, with dry Melbourne understatement. She asks short, easy questions, trails off pleasantly rather than pushing, and reads a 'well, see you' as a full sentence.
card.signature: "No worries, you get off — I've got nowhere urgent to be."

values: Respecting when people are done for the day
Being useful without being the centre of things
flaws: Lingers too long when she's enjoying a chat
Doesn't always pick up that someone wants to leave
boundaries: She leaves promptly when told someone's heading off
She won't lecture anyone or take charge of their mood
conversationalHabits: Talks while helping stack chairs or fold tables
Ends conversations cleanly with a small joke
anchorLines: "Best part of any night is when the hall goes quiet again."
"I'm hopeless at the steps, but I turn up anyway."
"Right, you're off — good on you, see you next week."

entries.summaryZh: June是墨尔本退休的储物柜修理工，最爱活动散场后帮着收桌椅、和收拾东西的人闲聊。她热情却不粘人，聊得起劲时容易没察觉别人想走，被提醒就干脆利落地道别。笔记里那句'我的任务就是收自己的瓶子'，最能看出她自在不给人负担的可爱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A bench in the park, and you open your notebook to jot down what you've seen today.
beats.chinese: 公园的长椅上，你打开笔记本，想记下今天见到的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Beside you, an older woman tucks an empty water bottle into a cloth bag, folding the top over twice.
beats.chinese: 旁边一位老太太把空水瓶收进布袋，袋口折了两折。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, you're a note-taker. Good on you. I just came from a thing at the hall up the road — they never need help stacking chairs, apparently.
beats.chinese: 哦，你还记笔记呢，不错。我刚从那边礼堂的活动回来——人家居然不需要人帮忙收椅子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly, the pack-down's my favourite bit. Everyone's normal again, no fuss. Though yesterday I nearly kept a poor worker past closing.
beats.chinese: 说真的，散场收拾是我最喜欢的部分。那时候大家都放松了，不端着。不过昨天我差点害一个工作人员拖到锁门。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, don't mind me. I'm just sorting my bag before a walk.
beats.chinese: 好了，不用管我，我就是收拾一下袋子再散个步。

choices.english: Ask how the worker finally got her to notice.
choices.chinese: 问那位工作人员最后是怎么提醒她的。

choices.english: Ask what's so good about chatting while people pack up.
choices.chinese: 问收拾东西的时候聊天有什么好的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: How'd she tell me? She just said it flat out — 'We lock the doors now, love.'
beats.chinese: 她怎么提醒的？直接说——'我们现在要锁门了。'

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: June laughs and shakes her head, still folding the bag's strap around her hand.
beats.chinese: June笑了，摇摇头，还在把袋带绕在手上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And there I was, standing right by the door, still going on about where they store the trestle tables. Didn't clock a thing.
beats.chinese: 而我呢，就站在门边，还在讲他们那折叠桌收在哪儿，一点没察觉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough, she had keys in her hand. Still, I felt about this tall.
beats.chinese: 也难怪，她钥匙都拿手里了。不过我当时还是有点不好意思。

choices.english: Ask if it was embarrassing at the time.
choices.chinese: 问当时尴尬吗。

choices.english: Ask if today was also just after an event.
choices.chinese: 问她今天也是刚结束活动吗。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What's good about it? Well — once the noise dies, people talk plain. No performing.
beats.chinese: 有什么好的？嗯——热闹一散，大家说话就实在了，不端着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She settles the bottle in her bag so it doesn't rattle, then sits back.
beats.chinese: 她把瓶子在袋里放稳不让它响，然后靠回椅背。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You learn where the spare chairs live, who's got a long trip home. Little things.
beats.chinese: 你会知道备用椅子放哪，谁回家路远。都是小事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I never ask anyone to stay and keep me company. That's not the deal.
beats.chinese: 我也从不要求谁留下来陪我。这不是这个游戏的规矩。

choices.english: Ask if they always need an extra hand packing up.
choices.chinese: 问他们是不是总需要人搭把手。

choices.english: Say you need to get back to your notes first.
choices.chinese: 表示自己得先记笔记。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Embarrassing? A bit, yeah. She said it twice before I heard her, that's the embarrassing part.
beats.chinese: 尴尬吗？有一点。她说了两遍我才听见，尴尬的是这个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: June zips her bag shut and stands, brushing off her coat.
beats.chinese: June拉上袋子的拉链，站起来掸了掸外套。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She wasn't being rude, mind. She just wanted her evening. Fair's fair.
beats.chinese: 不过她不是不客气，她只是想要自己的晚上。这很公平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, you've got your notes and I've got my walk. Enjoy the park — see you around.
beats.chinese: 好了，你记你的笔记，我走我的路。公园玩得开心——回头见。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Today's thing? That was the dance class just now — same hall up the road. Beginner class, and I'm the slowest in the row. The pack-down I mentioned was yesterday's mix-up, not today.
beats.chinese: 今天那活动？就是刚才的舞蹈课——还是那边那个礼堂。基础班——我是队里最慢的。我说的收椅子那事是昨天出的岔子，不是今天。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She waves a hand, as if brushing off the idea that this matters.
beats.chinese: 她摆摆手，好像这没什么大不了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Today I just packed up my own bits and came out here. No chairs, no tables — I'm not setting up furniture in a park.
beats.chinese: 今天我就是收好自己的东西出来了。没椅子没桌子——我可不会在公园里摆家具。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Still, a hall going quiet after class is the best bit of any night. Right, off I go. Good luck with the notebook.
beats.chinese: 不过，下课后场馆安静下来还是一天里最舒服的时候。好了，我走了。笔记本加油。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do they always need a hand? Honestly, no. And I've learned not to invent jobs just so I can hang about.
beats.chinese: 他们总需要人帮忙吗？说实话，不需要。我也学会了不为聊天硬找活儿干。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts her bag by way of proof and gives the bottle inside a gentle pat.
beats.chinese: 她举起袋子当证明，轻轻拍了拍里面的瓶子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: These days I ask first — 'anything you want done?' If it's no, it's no. My job is my own bottle.
beats.chinese: 现在我先问——'有需要我做的吗？'没有就没有。我的任务就是收我自己的瓶子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, that's me done. You enjoy your writing — see you round the park.
beats.chinese: 好了，我收工了。你好好写——公园里回头见。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Your notes first — absolutely, go on then. I'm no interruption.
beats.chinese: 先记笔记——应该的，那你忙。我不打扰。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stands without any fuss, hitching the bag onto her shoulder.
beats.chinese: 她毫不拖沓地站起来，把袋子挎上肩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Short answer to your question: no, they don't always need a hand. But the chats are still worth it.
beats.chinese: 简短回答你的问题：不是总需要帮忙。但那些闲聊还是值得的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, see you. Enjoy the quiet while it lasts.
beats.chinese: 那，回头见。趁安静好好享受。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the same bench with your notebook when June comes along the path, bag over her shoulder.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本又回到那条长椅，June挎着袋子沿小路过来了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, the note-taker again. Good, the park needed someone writing things down.
beats.chinese: 哦，又是记笔记的那位。好，公园正缺个写东西的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shifts her weight and quietly tries two steps of her dance routine on the grass, gets the second one wrong, and stops with a laugh.
beats.chinese: 她挪了挪重心，在草地上轻轻试着跳舞课的两步，第二步跳错了，自己笑着停下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See, that's why I'm in the back row. Don't mind me — I'm just reminding my feet they exist.
beats.chinese: 看吧，这就是我站最后一排的原因。别管我——我就是提醒一下我的脚还活着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, I'm off for my walk. Enjoy your notes — and the quiet.
beats.chinese: 好了，我去散步了。笔记好好写——还有这儿的安静。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the bench twice in farewell and strolls off down the path, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她在椅背上轻拍两下道别，不紧不慢地沿小路走远了。

card.name: Bernard Ellison
card.occupation: part-time camera assistant at a community TV station
card.appearance: 偏斜锅盖发与浅色侧发，窄额宽方长下颌、短宽鼻，抬下巴微露齿笑，穿V领针织衣。
card.personality: Bernard is warm, practical, and quietly observant, but his attention drifts toward whatever is keeping a room running. At a community show he'll genuinely enjoy the performance, yet afterward he tends to praise the lighting crew and the kid who moved scenery before he remembers the actors are standing right there. It's not contempt for the stage—he just spent decades watching cables and cues, so he notices whoever keeps things smooth. Friends sometimes have to tug him back when he's explaining wiring during a plot discussion. He takes the correction good-naturedly, laughs at himself, and tries again, though the habit always creeps back.
card.background: Bernard was born and raised in the Bronx and has stayed in New York his whole life. He worked for years as a camera assistant, the kind of job where you're invisible when everything goes right and blamed when it doesn't, and that shaped how he sees any gathering. Now seventy-one, he works part-time at a community TV station, lugging equipment and mentoring whoever's new. He goes to local theater and school productions often, and he's the person who stays after to help coil cables. He likes being useful in the background, enjoys the company afterward, and is slowly learning that people also want him to talk about the story, not just the rigging.
hobbies: Volunteering as crew at community productions
Repairing old AV equipment on his kitchen table
card.speechStyle: Plain, unhurried Bronx cadence, fond of technical asides he has to catch himself mid-sentence and steer back to the person in front of him.
card.signature: 'Whoever ran that board deserves a raise.'

values: Reliability behind the scenes
Noticing uncredited work
flaws: Fixates on logistics over people
Lectures about wiring unprompted
boundaries: Won't take credit for others' crew work
Declines to gossip about performers' personal lives
conversationalHabits: Praises crew first, actors second, then corrects himself
Asks how a production was staged, not just how it felt
anchorLines: The lead was fine, sure—but that scene change was flawless.
Sorry, you were saying about the plot? I got lost in the rigging again.
Somebody's gotta know where the cables go.

entries.summaryZh: 七十一岁的伯纳德在社区电视台做摄影助理，看什么都先注意到幕后维持现场的人。公园里翻看社区演出照片，他先夸换景快，才笑自己又漏了演员，还提起朋友多洛雷斯常说他这毛病。被提醒会改，毛病却总回来，这份坦率的固执让他格外可爱。

story.titleZh: 公园长椅上的幕后眼睛

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle on a park bench and open your notebook, starting to write down what you see around you.
beats.chinese: 你在公园长椅上坐下，打开笔记本，开始记录周围的见闻。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A few feet away, an older man in a canvas vest flips through printed photos on his knee, humming to himself.
beats.chinese: 几步之外，一位穿帆布马甲的老人翻着膝上的冲印照片，轻轻哼着什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at this one—the kid swapping the scenery moved so fast, the audience never even blinked. That's the real work right there.
beats.chinese: 看这张——换景的小伙子动作太快了，观众连眼都没眨一下。那才是真本事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances at the front row of the photo, where two actors in bright costumes are caught mid-song, and he chuckles at himself.
beats.chinese: 他瞥见照片前排两个穿着亮丽戏服、正唱到一半的演员，忍不住笑自己。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha—there's the whole cast standing right in front and I went straight to the crew again. My friend Dolores says I do this at every show. Old habit. What've you got in that notebook, some park notes?
beats.chinese: 哈——演员全站在眼前，我又先夸后台了。我朋友多洛雷斯说我每场戏都这样。老毛病。你那本子里记的什么，公园见闻吗？

choices.english: Ask what made that scene change so smooth.
choices.chinese: 问那次换景怎么特别顺。

choices.english: Ask if his friend ever wanted to talk about something else and he went off track.
choices.chinese: 问他朋友有没有想聊别的、他却跑了题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Smooth? It was like water. The stagehands had every piece marked with colored tape, so nobody guessed where anything landed.
beats.chinese: 顺？跟流水似的。舞台工作人员每件东西都贴了彩色胶带做记号，没人需要猜东西放哪儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And the two scene changes happened with almost no pause between them. The audience just flowed along like it was one breath.
beats.chinese: 两次换景之间几乎没有停顿。观众就那么顺畅地跟下来了，像一口气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the photo twice, proud, as if the tape marks were his own idea.
beats.chinese: 他在照片上敲了两下，一脸得意，好像胶带记号是他出的主意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry—here I am drawing you a floor plan when you asked a simple question. Go on, what were you writing?
beats.chinese: 抱歉——你问个简单问题，我倒给你画起平面图来了。接着说，你刚才在写什么？

choices.english: Ask how the show itself was.
choices.chinese: 问演出本身怎么样。

choices.english: Say that a smooth backstage deserves credit too.
choices.chinese: 说幕后顺利确实也有功劳。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, all the time. My friend Dolores wanted to talk about the story, and I started explaining how the spotlights were powered.
beats.chinese: 哦，常有的事。我朋友多洛雷斯想聊剧情，我却开始讲聚光灯怎么供电。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She just looked at me and said, 'Bernard, I asked who did it, not how it was plugged in.' Fair point. I do that.
beats.chinese: 她就看着我，说：“伯纳德，我问的是谁干的，不是怎么插的电。”有道理。我就这毛病。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, half smiling, and squares the photo stack against his knee.
beats.chinese: 他耸耸肩，半笑着，把照片在膝上磕齐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forty-some years watching cables will do that to you. So—the story. You want the story?
beats.chinese: 看了四十来年的线缆，人就成这样了。所以——剧情。你想听剧情？

choices.english: Ask him to describe the story in just one sentence.
choices.chinese: 请他只用一句话介绍故事。

choices.english: Say you're busy recording the scenery right now.
choices.chinese: 表示自己先记录景色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The show? Funny thing—it was a comedy about a bakery that mixes up two wedding cakes.
beats.chinese: 演出？有意思——是个喜剧，讲一家面包店把两个婚礼蛋糕搞混了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One cake says 'Congratulations Rosa and Sam,' the other one's for a retirement party. Both parties show up at the same time, and the old retiree ends up dancing with the bride.
beats.chinese: 一个蛋糕写着“祝贺罗莎和山姆”，另一个是退休欢送会的。两拨人同时到场，最后退休的老寿星跟新娘跳起舞来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs quietly, shaking his head at the memory of the stage, not the rigging.
beats.chinese: 他轻声笑了，摇着头想起的是舞台上的场面，不是设备。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The lead actress kept a completely straight face the whole time. That's what sold it. See? I can talk about the play when I try.
beats.chinese: 女主角全程绷着脸一本正经。全靠这个撑住了。瞧见没？我努力一下也能聊戏。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's kind of you to say. Most folks never notice whether a show runs smooth—they only notice when it doesn't.
beats.chinese: 你这么说真好。大多数人不会注意演出顺不顺，只有出岔子时才注意到。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I'll say this—the actors earned their applause too. That young lead carried the whole second act on her voice alone.
beats.chinese: 不过我得说——演员也配得上掌声。那位年轻主演光凭嗓子撑起了整场下半场。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He points at the actors in the photo, giving them an honest, unhurried look.
beats.chinese: 他指着照片里的演员，认认真真、不慌不忙地看了一眼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not either-or, right? Good crew, good cast, good night. I just need reminding which end of the show people came for.
beats.chinese: 这不是二选一，对吧？好后台、好演员、好夜晚。我只是得提醒自己，观众是为哪头来的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One sentence, no wires. All right. It's about a lighthouse keeper who trains a seagull to deliver his letters.
beats.chinese: 一句话，不带线。行。讲一个灯塔看守人训练一只海鸥替他送信。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then the seagull starts delivering everybody's letters on the island, and nobody can tell which secrets belong to whom anymore.
beats.chinese: 后来海鸥开始给全岛的人送信，没人再分得清哪个秘密是谁的了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He spreads his hands, checking himself, and grins.
beats.chinese: 他摊开双手，检查了一下自己，咧嘴一笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. A whole plot, and I never once mentioned a cable. Dolores would be proud—she's been telling me for years I can do it if I just try.
beats.chinese: 看，整个剧情，一个字没提线缆。多洛雷斯会骄傲的——她一直说，只要我肯试就做得到。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He follows your glance to your notebook, then closes his own photo stack without another word about the show.
beats.chinese: 他顺着你的目光看向你的笔记本，然后合上自己那沓照片，不再提演出的事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. You're here to look at the park, not hear me talk. I'll leave you to it.
beats.chinese: 有道理。你是来看公园的，不是听我说话的。不打扰你了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the photos into his vest pocket and leans back, watching the pigeons instead of talking.
beats.chinese: 他把照片塞进马甲口袋，往后一靠，看着鸽子，不再说话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your notes. Sometimes the eyes are the best camera anyway—no batteries required.
beats.chinese: 好好记你的。有时候眼睛就是最好的相机——还不用电池。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You open your notebook at the same bench. Bernard is packing up, snapping his camera cover shut and giving it a gentle tug to be sure.
beats.chinese: 你在同一条长椅上打开笔记本。伯纳德正在收拾，扣好相机盖，还轻轻拉了一下确认。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Locked tight. Today I'm just using my eyes—no photos, no notes, nothing.
beats.chinese: 好了。扣紧了。今天我只用眼睛看——不拍照，不记笔记，什么都不带。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles the bag on his shoulder and nods at your open notebook, unhurried as ever.
beats.chinese: 他把包挎上肩，朝你摊开的笔记本点点头，还是那副不慌不忙的样子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you again. Writing the park down, huh? Somebody should—these benches have stories.
beats.chinese: 又见到你了，真好。在把公园记下来？是该有人记——这些长椅都有故事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, I'll let you get to it. No photography lectures from me today, promise.
beats.chinese: 好，不打扰你了。今天保证不给你讲摄影课。

card.name: Eunice Fourie
card.occupation: golf club grip replacement technician (semi-retired, weekend workshop work)
card.personality: Eunice runs her life on beginnings and endings. Before any real task she picks a short piece of music, and when the work is done she lifts the needle deliberately — mid-phrase if she must — to close the thing properly. Ask her for help and she is generous, patient, fully present, but she wants you to ask inside that structure: not in passing, not vaguely, not while she's halfway through something else. People who call her the woman who can fix anything annoy her less out of modesty than because the label flattens her into an always-on service. She is courteous in an old-fashioned register and disagrees plainly. Her inconvenient strength: she notices unfinished things everywhere, and it genuinely itches.
card.background: Eunice regripped golf clubs for over thirty years, first for a pro shop in Bellville, later from her own garage bench, and still takes weekend work because her hands know the job better than her retirement does. Weekday mornings she knits socks with properly turned heels and hands finished pairs out when winter arrives, no ceremony. Tuesday and Thursday evenings she climbs at a bouldering gym in Salt River, where she is the oldest regular and quietly prouder of her footwork than her strength. At home the record player gets more use than the television: every task has its track, and the wall of tools is as well ordered as her days. She lives alone and likes it that way, mostly.
card.speechStyle: Slightly formal, full sentences, measured pace with occasional Afrikaans-tinged phrasing. Courteous even when flatly disagreeing; asks precise questions rather than making small talk.
card.signature: We start when the needle drops.
card.appearance: 低后梳发，长中庭、短内收下巴与宽凸鼻，窄眼张口，侧脸穿立领衣。

values: a task deserves a proper beginning and a proper end
precision in a request is a form of respect
flaws: unfinished business genuinely bothers her — an open drawer, a half-done favour — and she can be short with people who leave things dangling
spots what needs doing before anyone asks, then quietly resents doing it unasked
boundaries: won't take on vague requests — 'just have a look at it' gets sent back for specifics
doesn't discuss her evenings at the gym with workshop clients; that time is hers
conversationalHabits: asks a clarifying question before agreeing to anything
refers to music by what she was doing when she last played it — 'the grip song,' 'the heel-turn one'
anchorLines: We start when the needle drops and stop when I lift it. Ask me in between those two moments or don't ask.
You want it done properly, tell me exactly what 'properly' means to you. I'm not guessing.
I'm not on call. I'm at my bench, and my bench has opening hours.

entries.summaryZh: 开普敦七十一岁握把技师Eunice，做事讲究唱针落下开始、抬起结束。她在公园收工具、按停耳机，把一次小收拾变成完整的仪式。她周末接握把活，早晨织袜子，乐于帮忙却讨厌随叫随到，异议直率、旧式客气，织的后跟宽了也要回家重转，是个把节奏看得比什么都重的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle on a park bench and open your notebook, jotting down the pigeons, the church spire, a man arguing with his kite.
beats.chinese: 你在公园长椅上坐下，打开笔记本，记下鸽子、教堂尖顶，还有一个和风筝较劲的男人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the same bench, an older woman folds a small canvas tool roll, sliding each item into its loop with a click.
beats.chinese: 同一条长椅上，一位年长女士正收起一个小帆布工具卷，把每件工具咔哒一声扣进各自的环里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She presses something on her earphones and the faint music stops mid-phrase. "There. A small job must have a head and a tail, even a tiny one like mine."
beats.chinese: 她按了一下耳机，音乐在半句处停住。“好了。小活也得有头有尾，哪怕是我这种小活。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She notices your pen moving and leans a little to see the page, hands still busy with the last buckle.
beats.chinese: 她注意到你的笔在动，微微凑过来看了一眼本子，手上还在扣最后一个搭扣。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Writing things down while they happen. That's a discipline too. What have you caught so far?"
beats.chinese: “事情发生时就记下来，这也是一种功夫。你到现在记下了什么？”

choices.english: Ask whether the music is also part of how she works.
choices.chinese: 问音乐是不是她做事方式的一部分。

choices.english: Ask if she still takes repair work.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是还接维修活。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Part of it, ja. At home I play a record before I start — the grip song, I call it. Today it's only earphones, but the rule holds."
beats.chinese: “算一部分，是的。在家我会先放一张唱片再动手——我管那叫握把歌。今天只有耳机，但规矩不变。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps the earphone case once, as if confirming it is switched off, then sets it beside the tool roll.
beats.chinese: 她轻敲了一下耳机盒，像确认它已经关了，然后把它放在工具卷旁边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "The needle drops, I begin. I lift it, I'm finished. Even if the song is cut short. Especially then."
beats.chinese: “唱针落下，我开始。抬起唱针，我就收工。哪怕歌被切短。尤其是那样的时候。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "You've been writing for a while now. Do you also close each page properly, or do you just stop wherever the pen falls?"
beats.chinese: “你已经写了一会儿了。你也会好好收尾每一页吗，还是笔停在哪就算哪？”

choices.english: Ask what she does when someone interrupts her halfway through.
choices.chinese: 问她被人中途打断时怎么办。

choices.english: Ask whether she is finished for now.
choices.chinese: 问她现在是不是已经完事了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "A little, weekends only. I regrip golf clubs — thirty years at it, so my hands still know the way. But I plan those days carefully."
beats.chinese: “接一点，只在周末。我给高尔夫球杆换握把——干了三十年，手还记得路。但那些日子我都安排得很仔细。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pulls the last loop of the tool roll tight and smooths the canvas flat across her knees.
beats.chinese: 她拉紧工具卷的最后一个环，把帆布在膝盖上抚平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "I'm not on call, you understand. I'm at my bench, and my bench has opening hours. People forget that when they hear 'retired'."
beats.chinese: “我不是随叫随到的，你明白吧。我在我的工作台前，工作台有营业时间。人们一听‘退休’就忘了这点。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances down at a small ball of grey yarn peeking from the corner of her bag, as if it has been waiting to be mentioned.
beats.chinese: 她低头看了一眼包角露出来的一小团灰毛线，好像它一直在等着被提起。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "And mornings, before the bench, I knit. Socks, mostly. It keeps the hands honest on the days they aren't regripping anything."
beats.chinese: “还有早上，上工作台之前，我织点东西。主要是袜子。让手在不换握把的日子里也不闲着。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "You were watching me pack up rather carefully. Was there something on your mind, or just curiosity?"
beats.chinese: “你刚才看我收拾看得挺仔细。是有什么事，还是只是好奇？”

choices.english: Say you were only curious, not looking for a repair.
choices.chinese: 说明你只是好奇，没想找她修东西。

choices.english: Ask about the knitting she mentioned.
choices.chinese: 转问她提到的织东西的事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Honestly? It puts my back up. If someone catches me mid-task and says 'quick favour', the whole rhythm is broken."
beats.chinese: “说实话？那会让我不痛快。有人在我干到一半时说‘帮个小忙’，整个节奏就断了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She straightens the earphone case so its edges line up with the tool roll, an unnecessary but exact adjustment.
beats.chinese: 她把耳机盒摆正，让它的边和工具卷对齐，一个不必要但精确的调整。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "What I've learned to do is say where I am first. 'I'm halfway through this, I'll come at four.' That keeps my ending, and I still help."
beats.chinese: “我学会的办法是先说明我做到哪了。‘我这活干到一半，四点来找你。’这样我的收尾还在，我也照样帮忙。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "But I don't take every request. A vague one — 'just have a look at it' — goes straight back for specifics. That's not rudeness. That's respect for the work."
beats.chinese: “但我不会什么都接。含糊的请求——‘你就帮忙看看吧’——我会退回去要具体说明。那不是无礼，那是对活计的尊重。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods once, as if closing the topic, and looks back out at the kite man, whose kite has finally climbed.
beats.chinese: 她点了下头，像给这个话题收了尾，回头看那个风筝男人，风筝终于飞起来了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Finished, ja. Tools in, earphones off, needle up — in my head, at least. The whole ritual took two minutes and it counts."
beats.chinese: “完事了，是的。工具收好，耳机关掉，唱针抬起——至少在我心里是这样。整套仪式花了两分钟，但作数。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She zips the tool roll shut and drops it into a canvas bag, then settles back against the bench with both hands free.
beats.chinese: 她拉上工具卷的拉链，放进帆布包里，然后靠回椅背，两只手都空了出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Now I'm nobody's technician for an hour. I'm just a woman watching a man lose a fight with a kite."
beats.chinese: “现在这一小时里，我不是谁的技师。我只是个看男人跟风筝打输架的女人。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The kite loops and dives. She chuckles, low and unbothered, and points at the page in your notebook.
beats.chinese: 风筝盘旋又俯冲。她低声笑了，毫不着急，指了指你本子上的那页。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Put that dive in. A good ending needs something worth ending on."
beats.chinese: “把那个俯冲记下来。好的收尾得收在值得收的东西上。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Good. Curiosity I can sit with." She exhales and her shoulders come down a centimetre. "Golf club grips, that's my trade. Thirty years of it."
beats.chinese: “好。好奇心我可以安然相处。”她呼出一口气，肩膀垂下一厘米。“高尔夫球杆握把，那是我的行当。干了三十年。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She does not elaborate. Instead she watches a dog drag its owner toward the fountain, apparently content with the silence.
beats.chinese: 她没有细说。她看着一只狗拖着主人朝喷泉走去，显然对这份安静很满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "That's the whole report, I'm afraid. A trade is for the bench, not for benches in parks."
beats.chinese: “恐怕汇报就到这里了。手艺是留给工作台的，不是留给公园长椅的。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps your notebook gently with one finger, nods at the page, and looks back out at the kite, now steady against the spire.
beats.chinese: 她用手指轻轻敲了敲你的本子，朝那页点点头，然后望回那只风筝，它已稳稳地悬在尖顶旁。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Ending the page on the kite — that's a proper close. Keep that habit."
beats.chinese: “这页收在风筝上——收得好。保持这个习惯。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "The socks? Ja, I knit a pair most mornings. Proper turned heels, none of that loose shortcut business."
beats.chinese: “袜子？是的，我大多数早上织一双。规规矩矩转的后跟，不搞那种偷懒的省事做法。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns her bag toward you and shows a finished grey sock, heel cupped like a small shell.
beats.chinese: 她把包转向你，展示一只织好的灰袜子，后跟凹成一个小贝壳的形状。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "This morning's heel came out wider than I planned. I'll take it home and re-turn it. Not for praise — it simply isn't finished right yet."
beats.chinese: “今天早上的后跟比我预想的宽。我要带回家重新转一次。不求夸奖——只是它还没做对。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the sock away and picks up her bag, standing with an easy straightness that doesn't match her age.
beats.chinese: 她把袜子收好，拎起包，站起身来，腰背轻松挺直，和她的年纪不太相称。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Tuesday and Thursday evenings I climb — footwork, not muscle. That's where the patience for heels comes from. A good day to you, and keep writing."
beats.chinese: “周二周四晚上我去攀岩——靠脚法，不靠力气。织后跟的耐心就是从那儿来的。祝你今天愉快，继续写。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You open your notebook on the same bench. Beside you, Eunie is studying a shoe bag, checking its buckle twice.
beats.chinese: 你在同一条长椅上打开笔记本。身旁的Eunice正端详一个攀岩鞋袋，把搭扣确认了两遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "There. Closed properly. No needle to lift today, so the buckle will have to do."
beats.chinese: “好了。扣好了。今天没有唱针可抬，就只能靠这个搭扣了。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Climbing night was last night. My feet are more tired than my hands, if you can believe it. Footwork asks more of you than muscle ever does."
beats.chinese: “昨晚是攀岩夜。信不信由你，我的脚比手还累。脚法比力气更考验人。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs briefly and nods at your open page, then looks out at the pigeons, in no hurry to be anywhere.
beats.chinese: 她短促地笑了一声，朝你翻开的那页点点头，然后望向鸽子，一点也不急着去哪儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: "Good. You're still recording. Don't mind me — I'm just resting my feet before I walk them home."
beats.chinese: “很好，你还在记录。别管我——我就是歇歇脚，再让脚把我走回家。”

card.name: Grace Tan
card.occupation: pulp colour matcher at a paper mill
hobbies: Listening to oldies downstairs and singing along off-key
Bringing new household things into daily use right away
Matching and comparing colour shades at work and at home
card.personality: Grace's instinct is to give the good thing away before she's even enjoyed it herself. A cake comes out of the oven and she's already cutting the first slice for someone; the trouble is the someone often wanted to photograph it whole first. She finds ceremony a bit much and says so plainly, but she doesn't sulk when people push back—she'll argue, laugh, and still stay till the end. She is generous to a fault, occasionally too quick with things bought jointly, and genuinely puzzled when her giving reads as grabbing. A no from someone she loves is respected, even if she mutters that it's a fuss.
card.background: Grace has spent over three decades at the Jurong paper mill, matching pulp colours by eye until the shade holds up on the running machine—tray samples never tell the whole story. That habit of wanting things proven in real life carried into her flat, which she shares with her daughter: the daughter likes to keep new sets boxed until guests arrive, and Grace wants the cups in use by dinner. The two negotiate this constantly, sometimes with friction over things they bought together. Her friend Mei loves occasion and ritual, and they've learned to name that difference out loud rather than let it fester. Most evenings Grace goes downstairs to hear the regulars sing old songs, humming along off-key and not minding one bit.
card.speechStyle: Plain and brisk, short sentences with concrete examples from the mill or the kitchen. Disagreements come with a laugh attached, never raised volume.
card.signature: 'First slice goes to someone else—cake tastes better given.'
card.appearance: 短乱层发与矩形眼镜，短宽下颌、小三角鼻，皱眉俯视正面，低头交叠手臂。

values: Good things belong in the day, not on a shelf
Saying what you mean, plainly
flaws: Treats others' wish to keep things pristine as over-seriousness
Sometimes starts using jointly bought items before agreeing
boundaries: Won't touch gifts that aren't hers or unwrap packaging on someone's behalf
Won't fake agreement just to close an argument
conversationalHabits: Answers with a specific scene from the mill, the kitchen, or downstairs
Names a disagreement directly, then stays warm
anchorLines: First slice goes to someone else. That's the rule.
Mei likes a ceremony; I like a Tuesday. Both fine.
My daughter wants the cups waiting for guests. I want them holding tea tonight.

entries.summaryZh: 格蕾丝在纸浆厂调了三十多年颜色，讲究东西要真正用起来才算数。她拿着单独买的新杯子在公园喝水，说起和女儿共买的一套杯碟差点被她先拆开。她直来直去，争论也带着笑，不碰不属于自己的东西，把冲动和许可分得清清楚楚。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle on a park bench and open your notebook, starting to sketch the trees and the people passing by.
beats.chinese: 你在公园长椅上坐下，打开笔记本，开始画树和来往的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A woman on the next bench is drinking from a bright new-looking cup, watching the birds with easy attention.
beats.chinese: 旁边长椅上一位女士正用一只崭新的亮色杯子喝水，悠闲地望着鸟。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're recording the park too, I see. I just sketch in my head—faster, and no pencil to lose.
beats.chinese: 你也在记录公园啊。我就在脑子里记——快，还不用怕丢铅笔。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This cup's mine, bought just for me. New things should work the day you get them, that's my rule.
beats.chinese: 这杯子是我自己的，单独买给自己的。新东西买来当天就该用，这是我的规矩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My daughter and I bought a whole set together, though. I nearly opened it first—then remembered I should ask her. Ha!
beats.chinese: 不过我和女儿一起买了一套。我差点就先拆了——后来想起该先跟她商量。哈！

choices.english: Ask why she doesn't save the set for a special day.
choices.chinese: 问她为什么不把那套留到特别的日子用。

choices.english: Ask if her daughter prefers using it when guests come.
choices.chinese: 问她女儿是不是更喜欢待客时才用。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A special day? Every day I drink tea. So every day is the day, if you ask me.
beats.chinese: 特别的日子？我天天喝茶啊。那天天都是日子，要我说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At the mill, a shade isn't a colour until it holds on the running machine. A tray sample lies to you.
