beats.chinese: 在厂里，一个颜色要在大机器上站得住才算数。小样会骗人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same with cups. In the cupboard they're just shapes. Holding tea, they're cups.
beats.chinese: 杯子也一样。放在柜子里就只是个形状。装了茶，才是杯子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts her cup, takes a slow sip, and nods at the pond like she's proving a point.
beats.chinese: 她举起杯子慢慢喝了一口，朝池塘点点头，像在证明什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But that set isn't only mine. So I only talk about this one. Hers to decide too.
beats.chinese: 但那套不只是我的。所以我只说我这只。她也有份决定。

choices.english: Ask what happened with the jointly bought set in the end.
choices.chinese: 问那套共买的东西后来怎么办了。

choices.english: Ask how the new cup feels to use.
choices.chinese: 问新杯子用起来感觉怎么样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She does, yes. She likes the table looking nice when people visit. Nothing wrong with that.
beats.chinese: 是啊，她喜欢。她喜欢客人来时桌子漂亮。这没什么不对。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: We just want different things from the same cups. She wants them ready. I want them working.
beats.chinese: 同一套杯子，我们想要的不一样。她想让它们等着，我想让它们干活。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs and taps the cup in her hand with one finger.
beats.chinese: 她笑着用手指敲了敲手里的杯子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My trouble is my hands move faster than my mouth. I nearly unwrapped the set before I thought.
beats.chinese: 我的毛病是手比嘴快。差点没想就拆了那套。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mei, my friend, is the same about cake—she wants a photo before the first slice. We argue, we laugh, we finish the cake.
beats.chinese: 我朋友梅对蛋糕也这样——第一刀之前要先拍照。我们争，我们笑，最后蛋糕还是吃完了。

choices.english: Suggest picking one cup each to use first, as something to negotiate.
choices.chinese: 提议一人先选一只用，当作可以商量的事。

choices.english: Say you'll keep recording the scenery and leave her to her tea.
choices.chinese: 说你继续记风景，让她安心喝茶。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's still boxed. I didn't open it. Wanting to isn't permission, I know that much.
beats.chinese: 还盒着呢。我没拆。想拆不等于可以拆，这点我懂。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sets her own cup down carefully on the bench between you.
beats.chinese: 她把自己的杯子小心地放在两人中间的长椅上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: We'll talk tonight, she and I. Maybe she says wait. Maybe she says one cup now. Either way, we agree first.
beats.chinese: 今晚我们俩会谈谈。也许她说再等等，也许她说先用一只。不管怎样，先商量好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At the mill I learned—you don't rush the shade. You check it twice. Same rule at home.
beats.chinese: 在厂里我就学会了——颜色急不得。要查两遍。家里也一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your drawing. The park holds still better than my kettle does.
beats.chinese: 好好画吧。公园可比我的水壶稳当多了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good handle. Sits right in the hand—see, I grip it here, no squeezing.
beats.chinese: 把手很好。握着正合适——你看，我握这儿，不用使劲。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes a long drink, then holds the cup up so the light moves across the glaze.
beats.chinese: 她喝了一大口，然后举起杯子，让光在釉面上流动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nice colour too. I'd call it warm grey, not plain grey. Thirty-one years of staring at pulp, I notice.
beats.chinese: 颜色也不错。这叫暖灰，不是纯灰。盯着纸浆看了三十一年，我看得出。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. It's drunk from, it's used. Now it's a real cup, not a display.
beats.chinese: 好了。喝过了，用过了。现在它是真杯子了，不是摆设。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You try yours if you ever get one. I won't hand you mine—hands off things that aren't mine, and mine aren't yours either. Ha!
beats.chinese: 你以后有了自己试。我不硬塞给你——不是我的东西我不碰，我的也不归你。哈！

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One cup each first... now that's a thought. I could put that to her tonight.
beats.chinese: 一人先用一只……这倒是个想法。今晚我可以跟她提提。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the idea over visibly, tapping the bench, then smiling.
beats.chinese: 她明显地琢磨起这个主意，敲了敲长椅，然后笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'd take the green one. She'd pick the blue. She always picks blue.
beats.chinese: 我拿绿的那只。她会挑蓝的。她总是挑蓝色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But it's a maybe, mind. She gets a real say. I've jumped ahead of her before and it started a proper argument.
beats.chinese: 但这只是个可能。她得真正同意才行。我以前抢在她前头，好好吵过一场。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If she laughs at it, good. If she says no, the set waits and I drink from this one. Both fine.
beats.chinese: 她要是觉得好笑，那很好。她要是说不，那套就等着，我用这只。都行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She raises her cup slightly, like a small toast, and settles back to watch the pond.
beats.chinese: 她微微举了举杯子，像小小的致意，然后靠回去看池塘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. Draw the heron if it comes back—it stood there looking proud of itself for ages.
beats.chinese: 好。那只鹭要是回来你就画它——它在那儿站了好久，一副得意的样子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She finishes her tea in easy silence, no fuss, no offering of snacks from her bag.
beats.chinese: 她安安静静地把茶喝完，不折腾，也没从包里掏零食硬塞给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I used to bring cake everywhere for people. Learned some folks just want quiet and their own page. Fair enough.
beats.chinese: 我以前走到哪儿都给人带蛋糕。后来明白有人就想要安静和自己的一页纸。有道理。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nice to watch someone else keeping notes for once. You've a steady hand.
beats.chinese: 难得看别人做记录。你手挺稳的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You open your notebook at the same bench. Grace is nearby with her cup, half-listening to a melody drifting from somewhere across the park.
beats.chinese: 你在同一条长椅上打开笔记本。格蕾丝就在附近拿着她的杯子，半听着公园那头飘来的旋律。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, I know that one. Can't sing it straight to save my life, but I know it.
beats.chinese: 哦，那首歌我认得。让我唱准是不可能的，但我认得。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps two soft beats on her cup, hums half a line off-key, then stops herself with a laugh.
beats.chinese: 她用杯子轻轻打了两拍，跑了调地哼了半句，然后笑着停住了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There, that's my lot. The regulars downstairs do it better, and I sing along anyway. Nobody minds.
beats.chinese: 好了，我就会这么多。楼下那些老常客唱得更好，我照样跟着唱。没人介意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Back to your notes? Good. That heron came back yesterday—stood there like it owned the pond.
beats.chinese: 继续记你的？好。那只鹭昨天又来了——站在那儿像池塘是它的一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tea's good today. Cup's earning its keep, as it should.
beats.chinese: 今天的茶不错。这杯子没白买，本来就该这样。

card.name: Saoirse Byrne
card.occupation: part-time runner and selector for small independent magazines
hobbies: Hunting obscure periodicals in second-hand bookshops
Dropping in at the print works to watch the morning run
card.personality: Saoirse cares whether a thing actually lands in someone's hands — a magazine, a bit of news, an invitation. She'd rather walk it over than click share, and she'll say so without apology. She's warm but concrete: ask her something vague and she'll steer you back to the specific shop, street, or issue. She knows her way is slower and admits it freely, sometimes before you notice. She doesn't keep score with friends and states her wishes plainly, which reads as refreshing to some and blunt to others.
card.background: Born in Rathmines, Saoirse spent years in print shops and newsagents before taking on her current work: choosing which small publications suit which corners of Dublin and carrying them round herself. She knows which café will shelve a poetry zine and which shopkeeper wants cash up front. Friends keep recommending group chats and online archives; she listens, thanks them, and keeps her delivery bag by the door. She enjoys the counter chat and the moment someone flips through something she picked with them in mind. Once an event notice reached her too late to use, and she'll still bring it up. She lives near Rathmines, keeps the flat tidy, and prefers arrangements made face to face.
card.speechStyle: Measured Dublin speech, plain sentences; names the concrete thing first — the shop, the street, the magazine — then makes her point.
card.signature: "Sure, I'll bring it round myself."
card.appearance: 全白外翻齐肩发，长窄垂颊、长鼻与小下巴，低头露齿，穿翻领外套。

values: Things reaching the people who actually need them
Face-to-face reliability
flaws: Stubbornly slow methods even when faster ones exist
Impatient with vagueness
boundaries: Won't be talked into managing other people's relationships for them
Prefers plans made directly, not relayed through third parties
conversationalHabits: Opens with something concrete she saw or carried that day
Admits her own slowness before anyone else can point it out
anchorLines: I could've sent the link, but you'd never have read it.
That one's for the man in the shop on Camden Street — he asked after it.
I'm slow, I know. But it got there.

entries.summaryZh: Saoirse是都柏林替独立小刊物跑腿选刊的人，最看重消息真正送到人手里。公园歇脚时薄刊歪出，她坦然承认自己方式慢，却坚持亲手交付。和她聊装订、摆法或走过的空趟，都能听见具体街道与店铺的名字，朴实又固执。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit on a park bench with your notebook open, sketching the flowerbeds. An older woman settles at the far end with a canvas delivery bag, and a thin magazine leans sideways out of the upright spines inside.
beats.chinese: 你坐在公园长椅上，打开笔记本描画花坛。一位年长女士在另一端坐下，身边放着帆布送刊包，包里一本薄刊从直立的书脊间歪了出来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She steadies the leaning magazine with one finger, then laughs quietly to herself.
beats.chinese: 她用一根手指扶稳那本歪出的杂志，自己轻声笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the trouble with thin ones — every one of these is lighter than I am, and still they won't sit straight. Mind if we talk a minute? You're not in a rush, I can see that.
beats.chinese: 薄刊就是这样——每一本都比我还轻，可就是站不直。方便聊两句吗？我看你不赶时间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Saoirse. I carry these round the city myself — three little magazines today, all bound differently, as it happens.
beats.chinese: 我叫Saoirse。这些是我自己跑腿送遍全城的——今天带了三本小杂志，碰巧装订方式各不相同。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She keeps one hand resting on the bag strap, as if the bag might wander off without her.
beats.chinese: 她一只手搭在包带上，好像包没了她就会自己走掉似的。

choices.english: Ask her why she delivers these magazines in person.
choices.chinese: 问她为什么选择亲自送这些刊物。

choices.english: Suggest the leaning magazine might sit steadier turned the other way.
choices.chinese: 提醒她歪出的那本换个方向也许更稳。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why in person? Because when I hand it over, I hear the answer. The woman in the café on Wexford Street — she'll tell me straight if a poetry zine isn't moving. A link in a message tells you nothing.
beats.chinese: 为什么亲自送？因为当面交出去，我能听见答复。韦克斯福德街那家咖啡馆的女士——如果诗集小刊不受欢迎，她会直说。消息里的链接什么也告诉不了你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shifts the bag onto her lap and looks down at it, weighing it without lifting.
beats.chinese: 她把包挪到膝上，低头看着，没提起来却像在掂量。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's heavier today than I reckoned, I'll admit that. I always think three magazines is nothing, and then Rathmines to here is a long way with them on your shoulder.
beats.chinese: 今天比我预想的沉，我承认。我总觉得三本不算什么，可从拉思米尼斯走到这儿，肩上一直背着就远了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My friends laugh at me for it. Sure, I could send photos of every page in a second. I tell them — I'm slow, I know. But it got there.
beats.chinese: 朋友们为此笑我。是啊，我一秒就能把每页拍照发过去。我跟他们说——我知道我慢。可它送到了。

choices.english: Ask if you could just look at one public sample copy.
choices.chinese: 问她能否只留一本公开样本拿出来看看。

choices.english: Ask if she's ever walked all the way somewhere and not managed to deliver.
choices.chinese: 问她有没有一次走到了却没送成的经历。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks at the leaning magazine, then at you, and takes the suggestion seriously.
beats.chinese: 她看看那本歪出的杂志，又看看你，认真考虑起这个建议。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Turned the other way, is it? Let me try it flat in the bag first.
beats.chinese: 换个方向是吧？我先试试在包里平放。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lays the thin magazine flat across the others, then stops — it's pressing down on the strap buckle inside.
beats.chinese: 她把那本薄刊平放在其他几本上面，然后停手——它压住了包里的提带扣。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There now. Flat, it sits on the strap. Upright, it leans out. Two ways of doing it and neither one perfect. That's the whole of my career, that is.
beats.chinese: 瞧。平放，压着提带。竖放，又歪出来。两种摆法都不完美。我的整个工作就是这样。

choices.english: Suggest sandwiching the thinnest one between the two stiffer magazines.
choices.chinese: 建议把最薄的夹到两本较硬的中间。

choices.english: Suggest leaving it as it is and just tightening the bag strap first.
choices.chinese: 建议维持原样，只先拉紧包带。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A look? Of course. It's a sample — that's what samples are for. Here, this one's the thinnest.
beats.chinese: 看看？当然可以。这是样本，样本就是给人看的。来，这本最薄。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She draws out the slimmest magazine and lays it open on her palm, showing the folded spine.
beats.chinese: 她抽出最薄的一本，摊开托在掌心，给你看折页的书脊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Folded, not stitched. That's why it's light. A woman in Galway folds every page by hand, and I carry them for her because nobody else would walk them round.
beats.chinese: 折页的，不是缝线的。所以轻。戈尔韦有位女士每页都手工折叠，我替她送，因为没别人愿意跑这个腿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns it once so you can see the fold clearly, then closes it and slides it back into the bag.
beats.chinese: 她转了一下让你看清折痕，然后合上，放回包里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No need to buy anything or read it cover to cover. You've seen how it's made — that's the whole visit. Now, that's a better minute than any link I could've sent you.
beats.chinese: 不用买，也不用从头读到尾。你看过它是怎么做的——这就够了。这可比我能发给你的任何链接都强。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Once? There was a bookshop on Capel Street. Walked the whole way with two copies under my arm, and when I got there the shelves were changed. No magazines any more, just candles and cards.
beats.chinese: 有没有一次？卡佩尔街有家书店。我夹着两本走了全程，到了那儿货架改了。杂志一本不收，只摆蜡烛和贺卡。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She says it evenly, without any bitterness, the way you'd report the weather.
beats.chinese: 她说得很平静，没有怨气，就像在报天气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I didn't argue with the man. He was honest about it — the trade's changed. So I carried them home again, and my legs ached that night, I don't mind telling you.
beats.chinese: 我没跟店主争。他挺实在——行情变了。所以我又把它们背回家，那晚腿酸得很，我不瞒你说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I got a clear answer, and that's worth the walk. If I'd only messaged, I'd still be wondering. Now I know: not Capel Street. Next week I try the shop near the canal instead.
beats.chinese: 可我得到了明确答复，这就值这一趟。要是只发消息，我现在还在猜呢。现在我清楚了：卡佩尔街不行。下周我去运河边那家店试试。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lifts the two stiffer magazines, slips the thin one between them, and settles the stack upright.
beats.chinese: 她拿起两本较硬的杂志，把最薄的夹在中间，让整摞竖直放好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well now. Would you look at that. Straight as a soldier.
beats.chinese: 哎，你瞧。站得笔直，像个士兵。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the top of the bag twice, satisfied, and gives the strap a small tug.
beats.chinese: 她在包顶上拍了两下，很满意，又轻轻拉了拉提带。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's a handy thing you've shown me. I'd have carried on leaning it out and cursing it every street for another year. Thank you for that.
beats.chinese: 你这一手对我很有用。不然我还得让它歪着，再咒它一年。谢谢你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll remember it too — the thin one in the middle. That's the sort of thing you only learn by carrying the bag, and now you've learned it without the shoulder ache.
beats.chinese: 我也会记住——最薄的放中间。这种事本来只有背着包才学得到，现在你不酸肩膀也学会了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods slowly, pulls the strap tight, and the leaning magazine stops moving.
beats.chinese: 她缓缓点头，拉紧包带，那本歪出的杂志不再动了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. It's not tidy, but it's not going anywhere. You're right — why make a project of it?
beats.chinese: 好了。不算整齐，但跑不掉了。你说得对——何必把它变成一项工程呢？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leaves the stack exactly as it is and leans back against the bench.
beats.chinese: 她让那摞杂志保持原样，靠回椅背上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's my trouble, if I'm honest. I'll fiddle with a thing long past the point of usefulness. A strap does the job, and here I am arranging magazines like they're going to a fair.
beats.chinese: 说实话，这就是我的毛病。一件东西我总摆弄到没用的地步。拉紧带子就够了，我倒好，像要去参展似的摆弄杂志。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good advice, and I didn't have to walk a step for it. That's a novelty.
beats.chinese: 好建议，而且我一步都没走就得到了。真是新鲜事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the same bench with your notebook. Saoirse sets her delivery bag down, takes out a water bottle, and turns the cap hard without result.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本又回到那张长椅。Saoirse放下送刊包，掏出水瓶，使劲拧盖子却拧不动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, would you look at that. I tightened it myself before I left the house — overdid it, clearly.
beats.chinese: 哎，你瞧这。出门前是我自己拧紧的——显然拧过头了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sets the bag steady against the bench leg, wraps both hands round the bottle, and works at the cap slowly, bit by bit.
beats.chinese: 她把包稳稳靠在椅腿边，双手握住瓶子，一点一点慢慢拧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There it goes. I shouldn't put that much force into a bottle before nine, that's the lesson. My hands aren't what they were, and the bottle doesn't care.
beats.chinese: 开了。出门前不该对个瓶子使那么大劲，教训就在这儿。我的手不如从前了，瓶子可不管这些。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes a long drink, screws the cap back on loosely this time, and settles onto the bench beside her bag.
beats.chinese: 她痛快喝了一大口，这次松松地拧回盖子，挨着包在长椅上坐下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you again. Sit a while — the flowers are the same as ever, and that suits me fine.
beats.chinese: 又见到你了，真好。坐一会儿吧——花还是老样子，这正合我意。

card.name: Callum Wren
card.occupation: apprentice window dresser at a community charity shop
card.appearance: 短前发与低侧马尾，圆颊短鼻，低眉垂眼小张口，头大幅侧倾低垂，穿立领衣。
card.personality: Callum is easy company, quick with a dry Leith joke and genuinely good at making second-hand things look appealing on a shop floor. He's not precious about it, though. At home he'll happily wreck a corner he spent an hour styling because the kettle lead needs to reach. He finds it funny rather than frustrating, and he's learned to say plainly that his room is for living in, not for looking at. He can feel a bit self-conscious when friends want photos, but he doesn't apologise for the mess or promise to tidy up next time. He respects other people's aesthetics even when he won't copy them, and he expects the same in return.
card.background: Callum grew up in Leith, a few streets from the water, and started volunteering at the charity shop on Leith Walk at sixteen because a mate's mum ran it. He turned out to have a knack for displays — colour-blocking jumpers, arranging chipped teapots so they look intentional — and at eighteen he got taken on as an apprentice window dresser. He likes the work because it has a clear frame: the window is for looking at, the stockroom is for working in. That distinction runs through everything he does. His flat in a shared tenement is comfortable and functional, corners constantly re-stacked around whatever he actually uses. He's still figuring out what he wants beyond this, and he's fine admitting that.
hobbies: Charity shop hunting for odd ceramics
Sketching display ideas on till receipts
card.speechStyle: Relaxed Scottish cadence, short sentences, wry asides, often narrating his own contradictions without drama.
card.signature: It's a window, noo, no a life.

values: Practicality over presentation
Honesty about what a space is for
flaws: Lets things slide into genuine clutter
Dodges conversations about longer-term plans
boundaries: Won't keep his room photo-ready for anyone
Won't let work display standards follow him home
conversationalHabits: Laughs at his own contradictions before anyone else can
Deflects big future questions with a joke, then circles back
anchorLines: Aye, it looked great yesterday. Then I needed a spoon.
The window's art. My room's just where my socks live.
Take your photo, but don't expect me tae feel bad after.

entries.summaryZh: 卡拉姆是利斯的橱窗陈列学徒，能把二手旧物摆得赏心悦目，自己的房间却怎么方便怎么来。他先笑自己的矛盾，也不为乱道歉：橱窗给路人看，卧室给自己住。公园里他讲钥匙、运动袋和一只缺口小碗，务实幽默，边界清楚，对未来还有点含糊，但毫不在意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle on a park bench, flip open your notebook, and start writing down what you can see: dogs, pigeons, a man arguing with a pram.
beats.chinese: 你在公园长椅上坐下，翻开笔记本，开始记录眼前所见：狗、鸽子、一个跟婴儿车较劲的男人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A young man on the same bench glances over, then holds up his phone, which shows a photo of a messy bedroom corner.
beats.chinese: 同一条长椅上的年轻人瞥了一眼，然后举起手机，屏幕上是一张卧室角落乱堆东西的照片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry, noo, that's no a great advert for me. That's my room. Everythin' I need, right where my hand falls.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，这照片可不太给我长脸。那是我房间。我需要的东西，全在手一伸就够到的地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I do windows for a charity shop in Leith. Apparently I'm good at it. My room never got the memo.
beats.chinese: 我在利斯一家慈善商店做橱窗。听说我做得还挺好。我房间从来没收到通知。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, not waiting for you to, and nods at your notebook.
beats.chinese: 他先笑了自己，不等你笑，然后朝你的笔记本点点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You writin' about the park? Fair enough. Mind, if you put my corner in there, spell Leith right.
beats.chinese: 你在写公园见闻？行吧。不过你要是把我的角落写进去，记得把利斯拼对。

choices.english: Ask him: doesn't it bother you that it looks bad?
choices.chinese: 问他：这样不好看，你不在意吗？

choices.english: Ask him: how do you manage to make the shop windows look good, then?
choices.chinese: 问他：那你怎么能把店里橱窗摆得那么好看？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Does it bother me? Maybe a wee bit, when my pal takes a photo and I'm like, oh no, that's what it looks like.
beats.chinese: 在不在意？也许有一点点，朋友拍照的时候我会想，哦不，原来它长这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He scrolls to another photo — a styled shelf, jumpers colour-blocked, teapots lined up just so.
beats.chinese: 他滑到另一张照片——一个摆好的架子，毛衣按颜色排开，茶壶摆得恰到好处。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the shop. Looks great. Then I go hame and need a spoon, and the spoon wins every time.
beats.chinese: 那是店里。很好看。然后我回家需要个勺子，勺子每次都赢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I could make my room look like that. I'd just have to dig for everythin' I own, every single day. No thanks.
beats.chinese: 我可以把房间摆成那样。只是每天找自己的东西都得挖半天。不了，谢谢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, entirely unbothered, and pockets the phone.
beats.chinese: 他耸耸肩，毫不在意，把手机收进口袋。

choices.english: Ask which things he reaches for most often.
choices.chinese: 问他哪些东西最常伸手拿。

choices.english: Tell him you'd still rather keep things tidy yourself.
choices.chinese: 告诉他你自己还是更喜欢整齐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: How do I manage it? Easy. The window's for folk walkin' past. My bedroom's for me. Different jobs, different rules.
beats.chinese: 怎么做到的？简单。橱窗是给路过的人看的。卧室是给我自己住的。用途不同，规矩不同。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gestures at the park like it's a display he's judging.
beats.chinese: 他朝公园比划了一下，像在评估一个陈列。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See that bin? Ugly as anything, but it's doin' its job. My room's the bin. Works fine, nobody's meant tae admire it.
beats.chinese: 看见那个垃圾桶了吗？丑得要命，但它在干活。我的房间就是那个垃圾桶。挺好用，本来也没打算让人欣赏。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At work I move a teapot two inches for ten minutes. At home, if it's within arm's reach, it's exactly where it should be.
beats.chinese: 在店里我会为一只茶壶挪两英寸花十分钟。在家里，只要一伸手够得着，它就在它该在的地方。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grins, clearly having given this speech before, probably to himself.
beats.chinese: 他咧嘴一笑，这套话显然说过，大概是对自己说的。

choices.english: Ask if he ever tidies up just for a photo.
choices.chinese: 问他会不会为了拍照临时整理一下。

choices.english: Ask if there's any corner of his room that's both nice-looking and handy.
choices.chinese: 问他房间里有没有既好看又方便的角落。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What do I reach for most? Keys, every day. They live in the left pocket of whatever bag I used last. No system, but it's a system.
beats.chinese: 最常拿什么？钥匙，天天要。它们住在最近那个包的左口袋里。没体系，但也算个体系。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He counts on his fingers, getting into it now.
beats.chinese: 他掰着手指数，越说越起劲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Football bag by the door, 'cause Tuesday's five-a-side waits for nobody. Charger within a metre of the bed. That's the top three.
beats.chinese: 运动袋在门口，因为周二的五人足球不等人。充电器在床边一米以内。前三名就这些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's no chaos, mind. It's a map of what I actually do. You could read my week off that floor.
beats.chinese: 那可不是乱。那是我实际生活的地图。看那地板就能读出我这一周。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks pleased with the phrase, like he might use it in a window caption.
beats.chinese: 他对这个说法很满意，像是要写进橱窗标语里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods along, not offended in the slightest.
beats.chinese: 他点点头，一点也不觉得被冒犯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then keep it tidy, by all means. Genuinely. Some folk relax when a room looks right. That's no me, but it's no wrong either.
beats.chinese: 那你就保持整齐，完全没问题。真的。有些人房间看着顺眼才放松。那不是我，但也不是错。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My flatmate's like that. Her shelf's a museum. I've knocked it once, never again, I still get the look.
beats.chinese: 我室友就那样。她的架子像博物馆。我碰倒过一次，再也不敢了，到现在还挨白眼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He mimes the look — flat, unblinking — and you can tell he's had practice receiving it.
beats.chinese: 他模仿那个眼神——平静、不眨眼——看得出他挨过不少次。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So we'll no convert each other, but I'll no tell you tae live in a tip either. Deal's a deal.
beats.chinese: 所以我们谁也别想改造谁，但我也不会劝你住在垃圾堆里。一言为定。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For a photo? Aye, alright, I'll admit it. If my pal's visitin' and wants a snap, I'll shift the pile off the chair.
beats.chinese: 为了拍照？行吧，我承认。朋友来做客想拍照的话，我会把椅子上的那堆东西挪开。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up a hand, pre-empting the follow-up.
beats.chinese: 他举起一只手，先堵住你的追问。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But — big but — the pile goes back on after. I'm no livin' in a showhome. The chair has a job.
beats.chinese: 但是——很大的但是——拍完那堆东西就回来。我可不是住在样板间里。那把椅子有它的工作。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's like fluffin' a cushion before a viewing. One photo, everyone's happy, then real life resumes.
beats.chinese: 就像看房前把靠垫拍松。一张照片，大家都高兴，然后真实生活继续。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself before you can, right on schedule.
beats.chinese: 他抢在你之前笑了自己，一如既往。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Both at once? Actually, aye, there's one. A wee bowl on the shelf by the door. Keys go in it. It's no magic, it's just a bowl.
beats.chinese: 两者兼得？还真有一个。门边架子上的一个小碗。钥匙放里面。不是什么魔法，就是个碗。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He draws the shelf in the air, oddly precise for someone so relaxed.
beats.chinese: 他在空中比划那个架子，对一个这么随性的人来说出奇地精确。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Found it in a donation bag, chipped at the rim. In the window it'd be 'character'. At home it's just where keys live.
beats.chinese: 从捐赠袋里翻出来的，碗边有个缺口。在橱窗里这叫'韵味'。在家里它就是钥匙的家。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the whole trick, if there is one. One nice thing, doin' one useful job. The rest of the room's on its own.
beats.chinese: 要说有什么诀窍，就这个。一件好看的东西，干一件实用的活。房间其余部分自求多福。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, satisfied, like he's just finished a small display.
beats.chinese: 他满意地耸耸肩，像刚完成一个小陈列。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the same bench, flipping open your notebook to record the park's morning — dogs, pigeons, the usual — when Callum arrives, folding a till receipt covered in small display sketches.
beats.chinese: 你回到同一条长椅，翻开笔记本，开始记录公园的早晨——狗、鸽子，老一套——这时卡拉姆来了，正折着一张画满陈列草图的收银小票。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Alright? Aye, this — I sketch window ideas on receipts. Turns oot this one was for a loaf of bread. My paper comes free from breakfast.
beats.chinese: 好啊？对，这个——我在收据上画橱窗草图。结果这张原来买的是面包。我的画纸都从早餐来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the receipt neatly into a pocket, which is somehow the tidiest thing you've seen him do.
beats.chinese: 他把收据整齐地折好放进口袋，这大概是你见过他做的最整齐的一件事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Room's still a tip, before you ask. The bowl's still holdin' the keys though. One hundred percent success rate.
beats.chinese: 不用问，房间还是乱。不过那个碗还在装钥匙。百分之百的成功率。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I'm off tae shift some teapots. Enjoy the pigeons — write them kindly, mind.
beats.chinese: 好了，我去搬茶壶了。好好看鸽子——写的时候嘴下留情啊。

card.name: Evald Krisjanis
card.occupation: retired kitchen exhaust system cleaner
card.appearance: 全白短碎发，方角宽下颌与长直尖鼻，重眉窄眼、紧闭口，纯侧脸穿无袖立领衣。
card.personality: Evald is a practical, unhurried man who judges everything by how it sits in his hand rather than what it says about him. He peels labels off jars, snips tags off new shirts, and genuinely forgets brand names because they never mattered to him. He is warm but not sentimental, generous without keeping score, and mildly exasperated when friends try to help him shop and get lost in his vague descriptions. He enjoys company, laughs easily, and will respect a refusal without sulking. He is not a crusader against advertising; he just dislikes his home looking like a billboard. His stubbornness shows in small ways: he would rather use a worn-out thing than hunt down its model number.
card.background: Evald came to Vancouver from Tartu in his thirties and spent decades cleaning kitchen exhaust systems for restaurants, a job of grease, ladders and strong arms that he describes as honest and mostly invisible work. Retirement suits him. His apartment is comfortable and deliberately anonymous: good knives with no logos, a kettle chosen by weight and balance, furniture bought second-hand and scrubbed back to plain wood. Friends tease him when he asks them to find a replacement for something he can only describe as 'the dark one that pours well'. He waves off thanks and debts alike, believing favours are for using, not recording. He cooks simple Estonian food, walks the seawall, and keeps his tools oiled and label-free.
hobbies: Restoring and using unbranded hand tools
card.speechStyle: Slow, plain sentences with dry humour; concrete and tactile descriptions, vague on names and models, often comparing things to how they feel or work.
card.signature: 'Don't tell me the brand, just tell me it works.'

values: Usefulness over appearances
Favours given freely, not tallied
flaws: Cannot name or find model numbers when replacements are needed
Stubborn about worn-out possessions
boundaries: Won't accept owing anyone a recorded favour
Won't keep branded clutter visible in his home
conversationalHabits: Describes objects by feel and function instead of name
Waves off thanks quickly, changing the subject
anchorLines: It pours well and it's dark-coloured. That's all I know.
Take it, use it, pass it on. No debts here.
Tags off, thank you. My house isn't a shop window.

entries.summaryZh: 七十五岁的爱沙尼亚退休排烟清洁工埃瓦尔德，家里不留一件带标志的物件，却因此在公园里为一把顺手的小刀报不出型号。他谈手感不谈牌子，帮人不要欠条，宁可慢慢量尺寸也不肯将就。一次打开笔记本的偶遇，让他的固执和体面都露了出来。

story.titleZh: 公园长椅上的无鞘之刀

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You find a bench in the park, open your notebook, and start writing down what you see around you.
beats.chinese: 你在公园找到一条长椅，打开笔记本，开始记下周围的见闻。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: An older man on the next bench holds a small knife, turning it over and sliding it into a worn leather sheath that no longer closes properly.
beats.chinese: 旁边长椅上一位年长者拿着一把小刀，翻来覆去，把它插进一个已经合不拢的旧皮鞘里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The blade won't stay in. See? It slides out on its own. The sheath is worn through, so I need the same kind again.
beats.chinese: 刀刃收不住。看？它自己会滑出来。鞘磨穿了，所以我得买个同款的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But there's a problem. I tore the tag off the day I bought it. Twenty years ago, maybe more. So now I don't know the model.
beats.chinese: 可有个麻烦。买的那天我就把吊牌剪了。二十年前，也许更早。所以现在我说不出型号。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're writing things down, I see. Maybe a fresh pair of eyes can help me think. What would you do?
beats.chinese: 我看见你在记东西。也许一双新的眼睛能帮我想想。你会怎么办？

choices.english: Why do you tear the tags off so quickly?
choices.chinese: 你为什么那么快就把吊牌剪掉？

choices.english: What exactly feels right about the knife you're holding?
choices.chinese: 你手里这件到底哪里顺手？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because a tag is a little voice in my kitchen, shouting a name at me all day. I don't like it.
beats.chinese: 因为吊牌就像厨房里的一个小声音，整天朝我喊一个名字。我不喜欢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the knife slowly in his palm, as if weighing it against the question.
beats.chinese: 他在掌心里慢慢转着刀，像在掂量这个问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My home is small and quiet. No logos on the kettle, none on the chairs. It's just a private taste, nothing more. I'm not preaching at anyone.
beats.chinese: 我家小而安静。水壶上没有标志，椅子上也没有。这只是我个人的偏好，没别的。我不是在向谁宣讲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But you see where it leaves me. The one thing I liked enough to keep, and I erased its name myself.
beats.chinese: 但你也看到这让我落到什么地步。唯一一件我喜欢到留下来的东西，名字还是我自己抹掉的。

choices.english: So how do you find the model now?
choices.chinese: 那现在你怎么找型号？

choices.english: Maybe keeping the box would have made this easier.
choices.chinese: 也许留着盒子会方便些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The handle. It sits in my hand like it was poured there. My thumb finds the groove without looking.
beats.chinese: 是刀柄。它握在手里就像浇铸上去的一样。我不用看，拇指自己就找到那个凹槽。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds the knife closed, handle up, and lets you feel the weight of it without drawing the blade.
beats.chinese: 他握着合上的刀，柄朝上，让你感受它的分量，并不拔刃。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Light at the front, heavy at the back. Balanced. That's all I can tell you. I wouldn't tell you to buy one, though. A knife has to suit your own hand, not mine.
beats.chinese: 前轻后重。平衡。我能说的就这些。不过我不会劝你买。刀得合你自己的手，不是我的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides the knife halfway into the broken sheath and it slips back out again.
beats.chinese: 他把刀半插进破鞘里，刀又滑了出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You see my trouble. I can describe the feeling perfectly and the model not at all.
beats.chinese: 你看到我的难处了吧。手感我能说得完美，型号却一个字也说不出。

choices.english: Do you truly not care about the brand at all?
choices.chinese: 你真的完全不在意品牌吗？

choices.english: I'll just write my notes first, you carry on.
choices.chinese: 我先写我的笔记，你继续。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now? I'll go home and dig through my purchase records. I keep the receipts in a tin, in the back of a cupboard.
beats.chinese: 现在？我回家翻购买记录。收据都收在一个铁盒里，在柜子最里面。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the knife and sets it flat on his knee, pressing the broken sheath around it.
beats.chinese: 他合上刀，平放在膝盖上，把破鞘往刀上按了按。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't you start guessing from the look of it. A sheath that's a hair too loose lets the blade cut the stitching. I'd rather wait and be sure.
beats.chinese: 你可别凭外观替我猜。鞘松一丝丝，刃就会割断缝线。我宁愿等，等个准的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So that's my plan. Tin, receipts, and a slow read. Thank you for listening to an old man think out loud.
beats.chinese: 计划就是这样。铁盒、收据，慢慢读。谢谢你听一个老头把想法说出声。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He is quiet for a moment, turning the empty sheath inside out.
beats.chinese: 他安静了一会儿，把空鞘翻了个面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The box. Yes. The box has the number printed on it, doesn't it. I burned mine with the garden leaves, I think.
beats.chinese: 盒子。对。盒子上印着编号，对吧。我的那个，好像跟花园的落叶一起烧了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You have a point. Next time I'll take a photo of the model sticker before I peel it off. A photo in a drawer hurts nobody.
beats.chinese: 你说得有理。下次剪掉之前，我先拍张型号的照片。抽屉里一张照片，不碍谁的眼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I can live with that. A picture isn't a sticker on my wall. It's just a memory with a number in it.
beats.chinese: 这个我能接受。照片不是贴在我墙上的标牌。只是一段带编号的记忆。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. You fixed me without touching my house. That's the right kind of help.
beats.chinese: 就这样。你帮了我，还没动我家里一件东西。这才是对的帮忙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Careful now. I don't hate brands. I hate my rooms shouting them.
beats.chinese: 慢着说。我不恨品牌。我恨的是我的屋子替它们喊。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the knife handle lightly against his palm, thinking.
beats.chinese: 他用手掌轻轻敲着刀柄，想着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If this one has a name stamped somewhere, fine. It worked for twenty years. That's what I care about.
beats.chinese: 如果这刀哪里印着名字，也行。它用了二十年。我在意的是这个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And if you like a brand, you like it. Your kitchen, your walls. Mine just happen to be plain. Use what suits you, that's all.
beats.chinese: 你要是喜欢某个牌子，那就喜欢。你的厨房，你的墙。我的只是碰巧素净。用合你手的东西，仅此而已。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now, about this sheath. I'll take the knife home and measure it properly with a ruler. That's a start.
beats.chinese: 好了，说回这个鞘。我把刀带回家，用尺子好好量一量。这是个开头。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods at your open notebook and gathers his things without hurry.
beats.chinese: 他朝你摊开的笔记本点点头，不慌不忙地收拾自己的东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. Keep your notes. A person writing is a person thinking, and I won't interrupt that.
beats.chinese: 好。记你的笔记。写字的人就是在思考的人，我不打断这个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He wraps the knife in a cloth and tucks the broken sheath into his coat pocket.
beats.chinese: 他用布把刀包起来，把破鞘塞进外套口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll measure the blade at home with a ruler. Slow work, but it works. Enjoy your writing.
beats.chinese: 我回家用尺子量量刀刃。慢功夫，但管用。祝你写得开心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands, straightens his coat, and walks off along the path at an even pace.
beats.chinese: 他站起身，理了理外套，沿着小径不紧不慢地走远了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle on the same bench with your notebook again. The older man is already there, opening a plain lunch box.
beats.chinese: 你又带着笔记本坐上同一条长椅。那位长者已经在那儿了，正打开一个素净的午餐盒。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Inside are ordinary boiled potatoes and a bit of dark bread. He presses the lid down until it clicks shut, then opens it again.
beats.chinese: 里面是普通的煮土豆和一点黑面包。他把盒盖按到咔哒一声扣紧，然后又打开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tight lid. Good. That's the only number that matters today. If it doesn't leak, it works.
beats.chinese: 盖子扣得紧。好。今天要紧的编号就这一个。不漏，就是好用。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He laughs at his own joke and offers you nothing but a nod at your open notebook.
beats.chinese: 他为自己的玩笑笑出声，只朝你摊开的笔记本点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Writing again? Good. Don't miss the ducks, they're arguing by the water. I'd note that if I were you.
beats.chinese: 又在写？好。别漏了那几只鸭子，它们在水边吵架呢。换我就把这条记下来。

card.name: Wren Tualagi-Fahey
card.occupation: part-time after-sales technician for smart door locks
card.appearance: 秃顶与短马蹄侧发，长尖鼻、瘦颊与小口，圆睁单眼，侧脸穿围裙。
card.personality: Wren is a warm, brisk seventy-one-year-old who knows every dog and cat on the block by name and most of their quirks. He'll happily crouch down for a scratch and a chat with the owner, then stand up and go home to a quiet flat he genuinely enjoys. He's sociable without being needy, practical, a bit blunt when people project loneliness onto him. He likes short, uncomplicated contact — with animals, with neighbours, with most things. He can be impatient with sentimentality and with anyone treating his preferences as a puzzle to fix.
card.background: Wren grew up in West Auckland in a big, noisy family, and after decades of full houses — flatmates, kids, a partner, various animals that came with all of them — he lives alone now and finds it restful rather than empty. He works part-time fixing smart door locks, which suits him: turn up, sort the problem, chat briefly, leave. The neighbourhood dogs know him because he stops, every time, and their owners know him as the man who asks the right questions about a limp or a fussy appetite. When someone suggests he take one home for company, he gets short: he likes the visits, not the vet bills, the 5 a.m. walks, the whole weight of it. He's firm that this isn't sadness. It's just what he wants, and he's had enough decades to know the difference.
hobbies: Fixing and tinkering with small mechanisms
Short evening walks around the block
card.speechStyle: Short, dry, warm underneath; asks practical questions, cuts through fuss, laughs in single syllables.
card.signature: 'Nah, I'm right — but he's a good boy, eh.'

values: Honest affection without obligation
Respecting other people's animals and rules
flaws: Impatient when people psychoanalyse him
Can shut a conversation down too abruptly
boundaries: Won't take a pet home, full stop
Won't play with an animal without the owner's okay
conversationalHabits: Opens with the animal, not the person
Deflects concern with dry humour
anchorLines: Nah, I'm right — but he's a good boy, eh.
I like the visits. That's the whole arrangement.
Don't make it sad. It's not sad, it's Tuesday.

entries.summaryZh: 七十一岁的温伦是奥克兰西区的智能门锁售后技师，独居却自在。他熟悉街坊每只猫狗，先问主人、摸两分钟就收手，坚决不养——喜欢短暂相处不等于想承担全天照料。有人劝他'带一只回家'时，他会干脆说明自己喜欢的是拜访不是饲养，语气轻松但不接对方塞来的担子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You open your notebook on a park bench. Nearby, an older person raises a hand to a passer-by with a scruffy brown dog.
beats.chinese: 你在公园长椅上打开笔记本。附近一位长者朝牵着棕色杂毛狗的路人抬了抬手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hello, Tom. Is Biscuit in the mood for a scratch today?
beats.chinese: 你好，汤姆。饼干今天愿意让人挠挠吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The owner nods and pauses. Wren crouches, lets the dog approach and gently scratches behind its ears. When Tom moves on, Wren drops his hand straight away.
beats.chinese: 主人点头停下。温伦蹲下来，等狗靠近后，轻轻挠了挠它耳后。汤姆继续走时，温伦立刻收回手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two minutes of Biscuit. Lovely. People see me doing that and think I must want a dog. I don't, actually.
beats.chinese: 和饼干待两分钟，真不错。人家看我这样，就以为我一定想养只狗。其实我不想。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Wren sits at the other end of the bench, leaving your notebook plenty of room. The dog and its owner continue down the path.
beats.chinese: 温伦在长椅另一端坐下，给你的笔记本留出足够的地方。狗和主人继续沿小路往前走。

choices.english: Ask why he doesn't want a dog of his own.
choices.chinese: 问为什么不自己养一只狗。

choices.english: Ask whether he knows that dog.
choices.chinese: 问是不是认识那只狗。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because looking after one is every day. The walks, the company, the vet. I enjoy saying hello. That isn't the same offer.
beats.chinese: 因为照顾它是每天的事。遛狗、陪伴、看兽医。我喜欢打个招呼。这跟愿意养它不是一回事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His answer comes out a little sharper than before. He rubs a loose thread on his coat cuff, then looks back at you.
beats.chinese: 这句回答比刚才硬了一点。他捻了捻袖口的一根线头，又看向你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nothing against people who do it. Tom loves the whole business. I like going home to my quiet flat and leaving things exactly where I put them.
beats.chinese: 我没觉得养狗的人有什么不好。汤姆就喜欢这一整套。我喜欢回到自己安静的公寓，东西都还待在我放下的位置。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances along the path. Biscuit stops to investigate a tuft of grass, and Tom waits.
beats.chinese: 他朝小路上看去。饼干停下来研究一丛草，汤姆在旁边等着。

choices.english: Say enjoying dogs and keeping one are different things.
choices.chinese: 表示喜欢狗和养狗是两回事。

choices.english: Ask whether anyone tries to persuade him to adopt.
choices.chinese: 问有没有人劝他领养。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Biscuit, yes. I see those two around here. Tom used to stop while I was on my way to a lock repair, and Biscuit inspected the tool bag.
beats.chinese: 认识饼干。经常在这儿看到他们俩。以前我出门修锁时，汤姆会停下来聊两句，饼干就检查我的工具包。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats the coat pocket where a small brass puzzle box makes a faint click.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍外套口袋，里面一个黄铜小机关盒轻轻响了一声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Still ask each time. Sometimes Tom's in a hurry, sometimes the dog's not interested. Being familiar doesn't reserve me a turn.
beats.chinese: 不过每次还是会问。有时汤姆赶时间，有时狗没兴趣。认识不代表就给我留着摸它的份儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The pair are farther down the path now. Wren stays seated rather than calling them back.
beats.chinese: 一人一狗已经沿小路走远。温伦仍坐着，没有把他喊回来。

choices.english: Ask whether he misses the dog when it leaves.
choices.chinese: 问狗走了会不会舍不得。

choices.english: Say you would rather not touch a dog yourself.
choices.chinese: 说自己不想摸狗。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At that distinction, his shoulders loosen. He nods once, looking pleased not to have another case to argue.
beats.chinese: 听到这个区别，他肩膀放松下来，点了点头，很高兴不用再争辩一场。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Exactly. I like watching the cricket, too. Nobody hands me a bat and says the team is my responsibility now.
beats.chinese: 就是。我也喜欢看板球，可没人因此塞给我一根球棒，说现在这支队归我负责。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Tom and Biscuit disappear around the hedge. Wren follows them with his eyes, then settles back.
beats.chinese: 汤姆和饼干消失在树篱后。温伦目送他们，随后靠回椅背。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That was a good little visit. I'm quite happy for it to have been little.
beats.chinese: 刚才那一小会儿挺好。就只有一小会儿，我也很满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now and then. Someone offered to introduce me to a rescue dog last month. A very nice offer, but I said no before they arranged anything.
beats.chinese: 偶尔。上个月有人想带我认识一只待领养的狗。好意是好意，但我在他们安排之前就说不了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flattens the loose cuff thread with a thumbnail and gives a small shrug.
beats.chinese: 他用指甲把袖口线头压平，轻轻耸了耸肩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I said I enjoyed their dog's company and wasn't looking for my own. They looked disappointed. I can live with that; I couldn't promise a dog a different life.
beats.chinese: 我说我喜欢跟他们的狗待着，可没在找自己的狗。他们有点失望。这我能接受，但我不能给一只狗许下另一种生活。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His voice eases again. He watches a cyclist pass, giving the subject a moment to settle.
beats.chinese: 他语气又松下来，看着一辆自行车经过，让话题慢慢落定。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They're still talking to me, by the way. We managed that much.
beats.chinese: 对了，他们现在还跟我说话呢。至少这点我们处理好了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not sad, no. I enjoyed the hello. I don't need to stretch it until one of us gets fed up.
beats.chinese: 不难过。刚才打招呼我已经挺高兴。不必非延长到谁先不耐烦。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes the brass box from his pocket, checks that its little sliding panel is closed and puts it away again.
beats.chinese: 他从口袋里掏出黄铜盒，确认小滑板关好了，又收回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Besides, I've got a walk to finish. Biscuit isn't the only one who needs to get round the park.
beats.chinese: 而且我自己的散步还没走完呢。又不是只有饼干需要绕公园走一圈。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Wren rises, checks the bench for anything left behind and gives you a brief wave before setting off along the path.
beats.chinese: 温伦站起来，检查长椅上有没有落下东西，朝你简短挥了挥手，沿小路走了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. I'll remember that if we see him again. You don't owe Biscuit a greeting either.
beats.chinese: 那很正常。下次碰到它我会记着的。你也不欠饼干一个招呼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He doesn't call the dog back or suggest that you might change your mind. His hand rests on his own coat pocket.
beats.chinese: 他没有把狗叫回来，也没暗示你可能会改变主意，手安稳地放在自己的外套口袋上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People do love turning a preference into a project. I spend enough time getting stubborn locks to cooperate. People can make their own arrangements.
beats.chinese: 人们真爱把别人的喜好当成一项改造工程。我对付不听话的门锁就花够时间了。人还是自己安排自己吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A leaf lands near the notebook. Wren shifts his shoe out of the way, leaving it where you can see it.
beats.chinese: 一片叶子落在笔记本附近。温伦把鞋挪开，让它留在你看得见的地方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You've got your notes; I've got my walk. That works nicely.
beats.chinese: 你有你的笔记，我有我的散步。这样挺好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back on the same bench. You open your notebook and start writing down what you see, and Wren is beside you, turning a small worn brass box over in his hands, clicking its latch open and shut.
beats.chinese: 你回到同一条长椅，打开笔记本开始记录周围的见闻。温伦就坐在旁边，手里转着一个磨旧的黄铜小盒，咔哒咔哒地开合搭扣。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Latch was sticking. Fixed it on the spot — no house call needed today, which suits me fine.
beats.chinese: 搭扣卡住了。当场就修好了——今天不用上门，正合我意。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He snaps the box shut, drops it into his coat pocket, and gives you a short nod instead of a handshake.
beats.chinese: 他把盒子咔哒扣好，收进外套口袋，朝你短短点了下头，没有握手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No call-outs booked today. I brought this little box along anyway. Apparently even my day off needs a latch.
beats.chinese: 今天没约上门的活儿，我还是把这小盒子带出来了。看来连我的休息日都得有个搭扣。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I'll get a walk in before I find something else to take apart. Enjoy your notes.
beats.chinese: 好了，趁我还没找到别的东西要拆，先去散个步。慢慢记笔记吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets off around the path at an easy pace, pocket clicking faintly with every step.
beats.chinese: 他迈着轻松的步子沿小路走去，口袋里的盒子随着脚步轻轻作响。

card.name: Baraka Onyango
card.occupation: retired projection equipment technician, formerly maintaining 35mm projectors for old Nairobi cinemas
hobbies: layered paper dioramas of old cinema facades
card.personality: Baraka runs a room the way they once ran a booth: watching, always, for the flicker that says somebody's lost the thread. They don't perform so much as monitor — mid-story they'll read faces like a reel, and if attention drops they don't push harder, they switch. A new story, better matched to whoever's at the table. They are genuinely, ungrudgingly delighted when someone else lands a good tale first, and will clear the deck for it. What they can't tolerate is a listener who pretends to follow; they'd rather lose you honestly than keep you politely. Their blind spot: so busy tracking the room they forget to say what they actually want from it.
card.background: Baraka spent nearly four decades keeping 35mm projectors alive in Nairobi's single-screen cinemas, the last one closing years after the rest had gone digital. The booth taught them to watch the audience, not the screen — the screen tells you nothing. Mornings now belong to a thermos of tea and a sketchbook outside whatever building interests them: the old Kileleshwa post office, a half-demolished arcade. Evenings go to layered paper versions of those facades, cut and glued at the kitchen table. They live alone, see their sister on Sundays — she claims Baraka listens to her properly now, which she counts as a late-life improvement — and their knees have opinions about stairs.
card.speechStyle: Warm, unhurried, with named characters and exact dates they'll correct plainly — 'no, that was '84' — without apology. Pauses deliberately to check faces, and will stop a story cold and swap it if the room drifts. When someone else talks, they actually listen, then hand the floor back.
card.signature: Hold on — wrong reel for you. Let me start a different one.
card.appearance: 后梳高额发与细后辫，宽垂颊和窄下巴，浓眉窄眼斜压嘴，俯视正面握肩带。

values: a story told properly is a form of respect
watch the listener, not the tale
flaws: monitors people so closely it can feel like being audited
won't say when they actually want company — just arranges reasons for people to be there
boundaries: won't keep talking to a listener who's clearly gone — they'd rather stop mid-sentence
won't fake a laugh at a flat anecdote; they'll nod and move on, and the moving-on is the tell
conversationalHabits: pauses mid-story to read the room, like checking a reel for jitter
swaps stories to fit the listener instead of repeating a favourite
anchorLines: You've gone somewhere else — fair enough. Different story for a different crowd. This one's shorter.
No, that's not right, it was '84. I was there. The manager wasn't, which is why he got it wrong.
Your aunt's market story is better than my post office one. Tell it again, I wasn't finished enjoying it the first time.

entries.summaryZh: 巴拉卡·奥尼扬戈，七十五岁，退休放映机保养员，如今在公园画建筑速写。他们讲故事时盯着听者的脸，像查票一样，发现人走神就干脆停住或换一盘。旧影院掉字母的小事、纸雕门脸和一张折起的照片，让这次偶遇有旧内罗毕的温度，也有一点不肯直说想要陪伴的倔强。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You find a bench in the park, open your notebook, and start writing down what you see. On the next bench sits an older person with a thermos and a small sketchbook, drawing a building across the path.
beats.chinese: 你在公园找到一条长椅，打开笔记本，开始记录眼前的见闻。旁边长椅上坐着一位老人，带着保温壶和一本小速写本，正画着小路对面的建筑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The person glances over at your notebook, then at their own sketch, then back at you. They set their pencil down on the bench.
beats.chinese: 那人瞥了一眼你的笔记本，又看看自己的速写，再回头看你。他们把铅笔放在长椅上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're writing, not drawing. I noticed that right away. Most people sketch the trees. Nobody writes them down.
beats.chinese: 你是在写字，不是画画。我一眼就看出来了。大多数人画树，没人把树写下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I was about to tell you about the old cinema facade on Koinange Street — but hold on. You've gone somewhere else. Fair enough.
beats.chinese: 我本来正想给你讲基尼安吉街那家老影院的门脸——不过等一下。你走神了。没关系。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Like checking if your ticket is still in your hand, that look. So — want to hear one short story, or should I let you keep writing?
beats.chinese: 我那样盯着看，就像在确认你的票还在不在手里。所以——想听一个短故事，还是让我继续让你写你的？

choices.english: Sure, one short one.
choices.chinese: 好啊，听一个短的。

choices.english: Let me finish my notes first.
choices.chinese: 让我先把笔记写完。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. Short one, I promise. In '88, the Regal Cinema had a sign above the door. REGAL. Five letters, brass, older than me.
beats.chinese: 好。短故事，我保证。一九八八年，雷加尔影院门上有一块招牌。REGAL。五个铜字母，比我还老。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They hold up one hand, fingers spread, counting letters one by one.
beats.chinese: 他们举起一只手，张开手指，一个一个数字母。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One day the G falls off. Just the G. The shop girl under it reads it as REGAL without the G — 'REAL'. She sends letters to REAL CINEMA for a whole month.
beats.chinese: 有一天G掉了。就掉了G。下面的店员把它读成没有G的REGAL——'REAL'。她整整一个月把信寄给'REAL影院'。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pause and look at your face carefully, the way someone checks a gauge.
beats.chinese: 他们停下来，仔细看你的表情，像在查看仪表。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There I go again, checking your face like a ticket inspector. Tell me — is this one fine to finish, or should I stop here?
beats.chinese: 我又来了，像查票一样看你的脸。告诉我——这个讲完就好，还是我就在这儿停下？

choices.english: Finish it, it's good.
choices.chinese: 讲完吧，挺好的。

choices.english: Why do you like saving old facades?
choices.chinese: 你为什么喜欢保存旧门脸？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You keep writing. The person picks up their pencil again but doesn't draw. After a moment they speak, quieter than before.
beats.chinese: 你继续写。那人重新拿起铅笔，却没有画。过了一会儿，他们开口，声音比刚才轻。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You chose your notes. Good. I'll stop watching your face then — I was doing it again, like checking tickets at the door. Old habit from the projection booth.
beats.chinese: 你选了写笔记。好。那我就不看你的脸色了——我又犯老毛病了，像在门口查票。放映间的老习惯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forty years in a booth teaches you to watch the audience, not the screen. The screen tells you nothing. But you didn't ask for that lecture.
beats.chinese: 在放映间待四十年，教会你看观众，不看银幕。银幕什么也不会告诉你。但你没要求听这番话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They turn their sketchbook toward themselves and begin a slow line along a rooftop.
beats.chinese: 他们把速写本转向自己，沿着一条屋脊慢慢画线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So. You're the writer here. Shall I tell you what I'm doing in this park, or shall we just nod and let each other work?
beats.chinese: 那么。这里写字的人是你。要我说说我在这公园里做什么，还是我们就点个头，各干各的？

choices.english: Tell me what you're doing here.
choices.chinese: 说说你在这里做什么吧。

choices.english: A friendly nod, and back to my notes.
choices.chinese: 友好地点点头，回到我的笔记。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Finished, then. The manager finally walks over, looks up, and says — 'We are the Regal. The G is on the ground.'
beats.chinese: 那就讲完。经理最后走过去，抬头一看，说——'我们是雷加尔。G在地上呢。'

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They laugh once, a short warm sound, and screw the cap back onto their thermos.
beats.chinese: 他们短促温暖地笑了一声，把保温壶的盖子拧回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nobody was hurt, nobody was fooled for long. It's just a small true thing, and small true things keep a street alive.
beats.chinese: 没人受伤，也没人被骗多久。这只是件小事，真实的小事能让一条街活着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They look at your notebook, then deliberately turn back to their own sketch, giving you the quiet.
beats.chinese: 他们看了看你的笔记本，然后刻意转回自己的速写，把安静留给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I stop there. One story, done, no second reel. Write well.
beats.chinese: 我就在这儿停。一个故事，讲完，不放第二盘。好好写。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why save old facades? Simple. A shape holds a memory better than a page does. I remember my whole street by its doorways.
beats.chinese: 为什么保存旧门脸？很简单。形状比纸页更能留住记忆。我靠一扇扇门记住整条街。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They take a small folded photo from their coat pocket, open it, and tilt it toward you.
beats.chinese: 他们从外套口袋里拿出一张折起的小照片，打开，朝你倾斜过来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The Tower Cinema, 1984 — no, that's not right, it was '86. I was there. The manager wasn't, which is why his book got it wrong.
beats.chinese: 塔影院，一九八四年——不对，是八六年。我在场。经理不在，所以他的书记错了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They study the photo a moment longer, then fold it closed and put it away.
beats.chinese: 他们又端详了一会儿照片，然后折好收起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's enough of that. Your notes are waiting, and I've got a roofline to finish. Good luck with the writing.
beats.chinese: 这就够了。你的笔记在等着，我还有条屋脊要画完。祝你写作顺利。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They open their sketchbook wider so you can see: a building's outline, half-finished, in careful pencil.
beats.chinese: 他们把速写本开得更大让你看：一栋建筑的轮廓，用铅笔细心画了一半。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I look at building shapes. At home I cut them out of paper, layer by layer — old cinema fronts, little paper dioramas. This one wants to become a doorway tonight.
beats.chinese: 我看建筑的形状。回家后我用纸把它们剪出来，一层一层——老影院门脸，小小的纸雕。今天这个晚上要变成一扇门。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tap the pencil lightly against the page, not asking for help, just showing the line they're unsure about.
beats.chinese: 他们用铅笔在纸上轻轻敲了敲，不是求帮忙，只是指出没把握的那条线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't need a hand with it. I just like cutting paper with a view in my eyes. That's the whole plan for today.
beats.chinese: 我不需要人帮忙。我只是喜欢看着眼前的景色剪纸。今天全部的计划就是这个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You write your park, I'll cut my park. Between us we'll have the whole place twice.
beats.chinese: 你写你的公园，我剪我的公园。咱们俩加起来，这地方就有两份了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You nod and return to your notebook. The person nods back once and picks up their pencil.
beats.chinese: 你点点头，回到笔记本。那人回点了一下头，拿起铅笔。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good luck with the writing. May your pen move faster than my pencil.
beats.chinese: 祝你写作顺利。愿你的笔比我的铅笔跑得快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pour the last of their tea, cap the thermos, and settle into their sketch without another glance at you.
beats.chinese: 他们倒出最后一点茶，盖上保温壶，专心画起来，不再看你一眼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: For a while the only sounds are your pen and their pencil, two small rhythms on one bench.
beats.chinese: 好一阵子，只有你的笔和他们的铅笔发出声音，一条长椅上两个小小的节奏。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. The roofline holds. Enjoy your notes — the park's a good subject today.
beats.chinese: 好了。屋脊立住了。好好写笔记——今天这公园是个好题材。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the same bench with your notebook. Baraka is there, steadying a small paper box on their knees and checking the lid is shut.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本回到同一条长椅。巴拉卡也在，把一个小纸盒在膝上摆稳，确认盖子盖好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The old sign stays in the bag today. It doesn't screen, it just rides along. Some things like to travel.
beats.chinese: 旧招牌今天坐包里，不放映。它只是跟着出门。有些东西就是喜欢旅行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They close the lid once more with two fingers, then look at your notebook, not your face this time.
beats.chinese: 他们用两根手指又按了按盖子，然后看你的笔记本，这次没看你的脸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Still writing, I see. Good. The park hasn't run out of things to say yet.
beats.chinese: 还在写呢，我看。很好。这公园还没把话说完。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tea's still warm if you ever want a cup. No obligation — the thermos just holds more than I drink.
beats.chinese: 茶还温着，想喝就来一杯。不强求——保温壶装的比我喝的多。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They settle back with their sketchbook, leaving the bench easy to share.
beats.chinese: 他们靠回长椅，翻开速写本，把长椅留得让人容易坐下。

card.name: Sasha Okafor-Ryan
card.occupation: document scanner at a community legal centre
card.appearance: 乱层长前发遮单眼，长尖鼻与前突圆下巴，侧脸宽露齿笑，手抵下巴，穿围裙。
card.personality: Sasha is easy to be around and quietly restless. She keeps appointments precisely, but hates walking the same route twice and will build in extra minutes just to turn down a different street. Friends call it pointless; she can't really argue, only say she wants to see something different. She's warm but not a talker, happier doing something side by side than hashing things out. At work she's methodical to the point of tedium and likes that her scanning has to be exact. Her friction shows when people mistake her route-changing for flakiness — she's never late, she just refuses the obvious path, and she doesn't always manage to explain why that matters to her.
card.background: Sasha grew up in Hamilton, where she learned the city by walking it after school, always picking the street she hadn't tried. She moved to Toronto at twenty-three and has worked at a community legal centre for nine years, scanning case files — repetitive, accuracy-critical work she's genuinely good at. She lives alone in a small apartment near a streetcar line she rides out of sequence on purpose. Her friends have learned that if she says she'll be somewhere, she's early, sometimes suspiciously so, because she budgeted time for a detour. What she hasn't managed to explain, even to people she loves, is that variety in the route is how she pays attention to her own life; the destination can stay exactly the same.
hobbies: Walking unfamiliar streets between familiar points
Shortwave radio listening at fixed evening times
Browsing secondhand maps and transit diagrams
card.speechStyle: Plain and unhurried, with small concrete details; shrugs off her own habits lightly and doesn't over-justify them.
card.signature: "Same place, different way there."

values: Reliability to other people
Variety in her own path
flaws: Can't articulate why routine bores her
Occasionally dismisses friends' preferences as 'the obvious way'
boundaries: Won't sacrifice punctuality for wandering
Won't be talked out of a detour just because it's inefficient
conversationalHabits: Mentions small street-level details nobody else noticed
Deflects personal questions with a concrete observation
anchorLines: I left early on purpose — I wanted to try the other street.
I'm never late. I'm just never on the route you expect.
You go your way, I'll meet you there.

entries.summaryZh: 萨沙在公园里摊开地图，核对一条绕路也能准时的走法。她的工作要求重复精确，换路线却是她私下的小小任性——但从不让别人等。四条分支分别落在她的守时底线、门廊颜色的小发现、对熟路者的坦然，和固定钟点的短波收听上。

story.titleZh: 同一条路，不一样的走法

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You find a quiet bench in the park, open your notebook, and start writing down what you see around you.
beats.chinese: 你在公园里找到一张安静的长椅，打开笔记本，开始记下周围的见闻。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the next bench, someone sits with a folded paper map spread across their knees, tracing a line with one finger.
beats.chinese: 旁边长椅上坐着一个人，腿上摊着一张折起来的纸地图，用手指描着一条线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry — didn't mean to crowd you. I'm just checking something. There's a second way to my friend's place, and I want to be sure it still gets me there on time.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，不是想挤你。我只是在核对一件事。去朋友那儿还有第二条路，我想确认走它也还来得及。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances at your open notebook, then back at her map, clearly curious but not prying.
beats.chinese: 她看了一眼你打开的笔记本，又低头看地图，明显好奇但没有多问。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I left early on purpose — I wanted to try the other street. Looks like the spare time is finally getting used.
beats.chinese: 我是特意提前出门的——想试试另一条街。看来留出来的那点时间终于用上了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're writing things down too, I see. Everyone in this park is collecting something today.
beats.chinese: 我看见你也在往本子上记东西。今天这公园里人人都在收集点什么。

choices.english: Ask why she doesn't just take her usual route
choices.chinese: 问她为什么不走熟路

choices.english: Ask whether her work also involves constant change
choices.chinese: 问她工作是不是也喜欢不停变化

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same place, different way there. The destination doesn't move. I just want to see something else on the way.
beats.chinese: 同一个地方，不一样的走法。目的地没变。我只是想在路上看点不同的东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps a side street on the map, one block over from the main road.
beats.chinese: 她点了点地图上一条旁街，离大路只隔一个街区。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My friends think it's pointless. I can't really argue with them. I just like turning down a street I haven't tried.
beats.chinese: 朋友们觉得这没必要。我也说不过他们。我就是喜欢拐进一条没走过的街。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The trick is leaving early. I build in extra minutes for the detour, so nobody waits for me. Ever.
beats.chinese: 诀窍是早点出门。我给绕路留了富余时间，所以没人会等我。从来没有。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds one corner of the map down and checks the time, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她折起地图一角，看了看时间，不慌不忙。

choices.english: Ask if she still detours when time is tight
choices.chinese: 问时间不够的时候她还会绕吗

choices.english: Ask what different thing she's seen today
choices.chinese: 问她今天见到了什么不一样的东西

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny you ask. My work is the opposite. I scan case files at a legal centre — same motion, page after page, and it has to be exact.
beats.chinese: 你这么问挺有意思。我的工作正好相反。我在一家法律中心扫描案卷——同样的动作，一页接一页，还得一点不能错。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds her hands up, miming a slow, careful page turn.
beats.chinese: 她举起双手，慢慢比划了一个小心翻页的动作。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nine years of it. I'm good at it, and I like that it has to be right. That part of me doesn't need change.
beats.chinese: 干了九年了。我做得不错，而且我喜欢它必须准确这一点。我这一面不需要变化。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The route thing is private. It's not that I can't sit still. It's just the one place I let myself wander.
beats.chinese: 换路线是私人的事。不是我坐不住。那只是我唯一允许自己乱走的地方。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smooths the map flat on her knees and looks out at the path ahead of you both.
beats.chinese: 她把地图在膝盖上抚平，望向你们前面的小路。

choices.english: Say you prefer familiar routes yourself
choices.chinese: 说自己更喜欢熟悉的路线

choices.english: Ask if her evenings have variety too
choices.chinese: 问她晚上的活动也会找不同吗

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You find a quiet bench in the park, open your notebook, and start writing down what you see around you.
beats.chinese: 你在公园里找到一张安静的长椅，打开笔记本，开始记下周围的见闻。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No. If the clock is tight, I take the straight road. Full stop.
beats.chinese: 不会。时间紧的话，我就走直路。就这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She says it plainly, like a rule she has never once broken.
beats.chinese: 她说得很干脆，像一条从没破过的规矩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The wandering is mine. The waiting is other people's. I don't mix those two up.
beats.chinese: 乱逛是我自己的事。等人是别人的事。这两样我不会搞混。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the map along its old creases and stands, brushing bench dust from her coat.
beats.chinese: 她沿着旧折痕把地图叠好，站起身，掸掉外套上的长椅灰。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right — I'm off the early way, so I'll still be early. You keep writing; I've got a friend waiting.
beats.chinese: 好了——我走那条早的路，所以我还是会早到。你继续记吧，我朋友还等着呢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A porch, actually. On the side street I came down. Somebody painted it a deep green, almost black, with white steps.
beats.chinese: 其实是一个门廊。在我来的那条旁街上。有人把它漆成了深绿色，近乎黑色，台阶是白的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She points vaguely down the path, as if the colour is still in her eyes.
beats.chinese: 她朝小路那边大致指了指，好像那颜色还留在她眼里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nobody paints a porch that colour by accident. Somebody made a choice there. That's the kind of thing I'd never see on the main road.
beats.chinese: 没人会不小心把门廊漆成那种颜色。那是有人做的决定。走大路就看不到这种东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up the map and tucks it under her arm, satisfied with today's findings.
beats.chinese: 她拿起地图夹在腋下，对今天的收获挺满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's my one new thing for the day. Cheap entertainment. Anyway — I should get moving while I'm still early.
beats.chinese: 这就是我今天的一样新东西。便宜的娱乐。好了——趁还早，我该动身了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's fair. Honestly, the familiar route is faster and you know every crack in the sidewalk.
beats.chinese: 有道理。说实话，熟路更快，而且人行道每条裂缝你都认识。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shrugs, not offended in the slightest.
beats.chinese: 她耸耸肩，一点也不觉得被冒犯。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not out here converting people. You go your way, I'll go mine. Both of us still get where we're going.
beats.chinese: 我又不是出来劝人入伙的。你走你的，我走我的。我们俩照样都能到地方。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She rolls the map loosely and taps it against her palm, twice.
beats.chinese: 她松松地卷起地图，在掌心轻轻敲了两下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Somebody has to know the normal way, anyway. Otherwise how would my detours count as different?
beats.chinese: 反正总得有人认识正常的路。不然我的绕路又怎么算得上不一样呢？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You find a quiet bench in the park, open your notebook, and start writing down what you see around you.
beats.chinese: 你在公园里找到一张安静的长椅，打开笔记本，开始记下周围的见闻。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Opposite, actually. Most nights I listen to shortwave radio at a fixed time. Same chair, same dial, same hour.
beats.chinese: 其实正相反。大多数晚上我在固定时间听短波收音机。同一把椅子，同一个旋钮，同一个钟点。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She draws a small circle in the air, like turning a dial.
beats.chinese: 她在空中画了个小圈，像在转动旋钮。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Voices from stations halfway around the world, coming in through static. Some nights it's clear, some nights it's all crackle. That's my variety.
beats.chinese: 世界另一头电台的声音，穿过杂音传过来。有的晚上清楚，有的晚上全是噼啪声。这就是我的变化。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She checks the time once more, then begins folding the map with practiced, even creases.
beats.chinese: 她又看了一次时间，然后开始用熟练均匀的折痕叠地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well. Same place, different way there. Enjoy your notes — I should get going.
beats.chinese: 好了。同一个地方，不一样的走法。祝你记笔记愉快——我该走了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the same bench. You open your notebook and pick up where you left off, writing down the park around you.
beats.chinese: 你回到同一张长椅，打开笔记本，接着上次的地方，继续记下公园里的见闻。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the next bench, Sasha is sorting through a small stack of paper slips, each one marked with a frequency.
beats.chinese: 旁边长椅上，萨沙正在整理一小叠纸条，每张都标着一个频率。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Checking I haven't dropped one — these are my evening stations. If a slip goes missing, my fixed hour turns into a guessing game.
beats.chinese: 在确认没落下哪张——这些是我晚上的电台。丢一张，我固定的钟点就变成猜谜了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She counts the slips once more, taps the little stack square, and tucks it into her coat pocket.
beats.chinese: 她再数了一遍纸条，把那小叠敲齐，收进外套口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All there. And I see the notebook made it back too — the park's records are in good hands.
beats.chinese: 都在。你的本子也回来了——公园的记录有人管了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, I'm off the usual way this time, so no stories from the road. But I'll be early anyway. Enjoy your writing — I'm off.
beats.chinese: 好了，这次我走老路，所以路上没故事可讲。不过我照样会早到。祝你写得开心——我先走一步。

card.name: Fay Kettering
card.occupation: part-time ornamental fish breeder, mostly guppies and bettas
hobbies: clearing out the corner behind the cabinet
card.personality: Fay loves a room full of talk — overlapping opinions, someone arguing about the wrong thing, a good tangent. What kills it for her is the moment a discussion turns into a ranking: best fish, best player, vote for your favourite. She goes quiet, finds a reason to be elsewhere, and won't explain why unless pressed. She'll happily argue a point for an hour but refuses to be placed on a list. Dry, precise with words, generous with attention to whatever you actually care about, and noticeably harder to reach once someone starts keeping score.
card.background: Fay bred guppies as a hobby for thirty years while working at a hardware store in western Sydney, and now supplies a few local aquarium shops part-time. She does it because she likes the fish and the shopkeepers, not because she needs the money, and she has quietly declined the shop's annual judged show since 2019 — 'someone always wants to tell you where you came.' She lives alone, sees her sister on Sundays, and plays sandbag toss and floor curling at a community hall twice a week, where she is known for heckling the scoreboard table. She recently moved a heavy cabinet and found a corner untouched since the nineties; she's clearing it slowly, mostly because every box turns up something worth sitting down and reading.
card.speechStyle: Short, dry sentences with precise ordinary words. Pauses before a punchline. Names specifics — tank temperatures, kilos of sand, which box she opened — rather than generalities. Goes flat and brief when the talk turns to rankings.
card.signature: Count it if you like. I'll be out the back.
card.appearance: 贴头冠辫、宽高颧与短下巴，闭眼张嘴大笑，斜头穿立领衣。

values: a good argument is company; a scoreboard is a queue
things are worth doing for the doing, not the placing
flaws: withdraws abruptly when a conversation turns competitive, which people read as sulking
won't explain herself in the moment, so small slights fester longer than they should
boundaries: won't take part in votes, polls or best-of lists, even friendly ones
doesn't take fish-keeping advice from people who've never kept fish
conversationalHabits: redirects heated discussions with a specific question rather than an opinion
when someone asks her to rank something, answers with a fact instead
anchorLines: Everyone's got a theory about bettas. That's the fun part. The list-making's the boring part.
Third place, second place — I couldn't tell you. The fry tank's at twenty-six and that's the number I keep.
Moved the cabinet last week and found a corner I haven't looked at since the nineties. Been reading old receipts like they're letters.

entries.summaryZh: 重逢：菲给你看新一批鱼苗的照片，只许看不评奖。

story.titleZh: 公园笔记与不排名的人

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit on a park bench and open your notebook, starting to jot down what you see — joggers, a magpie, a man losing a hat.
beats.chinese: 你坐在公园长椅上打开笔记本，开始记下眼前的见闻——跑步的人、一只喜鹊、一个帽子被吹跑的男士。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hah. Write down the magpie twice. It's been following that bloke for three laps now. I've counted.
beats.chinese: 哈。把那只喜鹊记两遍。它跟着那家伙绕了三圈了。我数过。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: An older woman is on the next bench, phone to her ear, half a sandwich in her other hand. Her voice carries — fish shows, a torn fin, someone's 'battle damage'.
beats.chinese: 旁边长椅上坐着一位年长女士，正打电话，另一只手拿着半个三明治。她的声音飘过来——鱼展、撕裂的鱼鳍、还有谁的'战斗伤'。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: ...No, Deb, love, I'm not lining them up for you. Don't start ranking everyone, that's how it goes — ...Sorry, something's come up. Talk later.
beats.chinese: ……不行，黛布，我不是要替你把它们排成一排。别又给所有人排名，每次都这样——……抱歉，我等会儿还有事。回头聊。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She hangs up with visible relief and slides the phone into her coat pocket, then notices your notebook and nods at it.
beats.chinese: 她如释重负地挂断，把手机塞进外套口袋，然后注意到你的笔记本，朝它点点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forty minutes we argued about that fin. Best one I've heard all month — right up until she wanted a winner. Go on with your notes, love.
beats.chinese: 那片鱼鳍我们争了四十分钟。我这个月听过最精彩的——直到她想选个冠军为止。你继续记你的。

choices.english: Listen for a moment, then ask why she stops enjoying it when people start ranking
choices.chinese: 听了一会儿，然后问她为什么一到排名就没劲了

choices.english: Ask what activities she usually plays around here
choices.chinese: 问她平时都玩些什么活动

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes the phone back out of her pocket and sets it face-down on the bench between you.
beats.chinese: 她把手机从口袋里重新拿出来，屏幕朝下放在你们之间的长椅上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You caught that, did you. ...The talking's the good bit. Everyone's got a theory about bettas. That's the fun part.
beats.chinese: 你听到了啊。……聊天才有意思。每个人对斗鱼都有一套理论。那才好玩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The list-making's the boring part. The moment Deb says 'so who was best', I'm suddenly very busy. As you just heard.
beats.chinese: 排名那部分就无聊了。黛布一说'那到底谁最好'，我就突然很忙。你刚才也听到了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns her sandwich over, as if checking it for an exit.
beats.chinese: 她把三明治翻了个面，好像在检查它有没有出口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not sneering at people who judge. Someone's got to hand out the ribbons. It's just not a chair I sit in.
beats.chinese: 我不是瞧不起当评委的人。总得有人发绶带。只是那把椅子我不坐。

choices.english: Ask whether she'd ever tell her friend directly that she avoids rankings
choices.chinese: 问她会不会直接告诉朋友自己回避排名

choices.english: Say she can simply skip that part and keep enjoying the arguments
choices.chinese: 说她完全可以跳过那部分，继续享受争论就好

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the pocket where the phone went, like confirming a door is shut.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍手机放进去的那个口袋，像在确认一扇门已经关好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What do I play? Sandbag tossing Tuesdays, floor curling Thursdays. Community hall out west. Both, properly.
beats.chinese: 我玩什么？周二扔沙包，周四旱地冰壶。西区的社区活动馆。两项都正经玩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Floor curling's the one with the stones you slide. I like it because you can argue about every single shot and nobody stops you.
beats.chinese: 旱地冰壶就是推那种石饼的。我喜欢它是因为每一投都能争个没完，没人拦你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She finishes the sandwich and dusts her hands on her knee.
beats.chinese: 她吃完三明治，在膝盖上拍了拍手上的碎屑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Between the two, mind, I'm meant to be clearing out the corner behind the cabinet at home. Moved the thing last week and it's been slow going ever since.
beats.chinese: 不过这中间，我本来还该清一清家里柜子后面那个角落。上周把柜子挪开了，之后进度就一直很慢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The scoreboard table's another matter. I heckle it. Politely. Mostly.
beats.chinese: 记分台就是另一回事了。我会调侃它。礼貌地。大部分时候。

choices.english: Ask what she actually does when she's near the scoreboard table
choices.chinese: 问她在记分台附近到底会做什么

choices.english: Change tack and ask about the corner of her house she's been clearing out
choices.chinese: 换个话题，问她家里正在清理的那个角落

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks the phone back up but doesn't dial, just holds it.
beats.chinese: 她重新拿起手机，但没有拨号，只是握着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tell Deb straight? I hung up on her not ten minutes ago over exactly that. So, no. Not yet.
beats.chinese: 直接跟黛布说？十分钟前我才因为这事挂了她电话。所以，还没有。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks at the magpie, which has given up on the jogger and is eyeing her sandwich wrapper.
beats.chinese: 她看看那只喜鹊——它已经放弃那位跑步者，正盯着她的三明治包装纸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Let me fix what I said earlier, because it came out vague. I'm out of the judged show since 2019. Not the show. Just the judging.
beats.chinese: 好。我更正一下刚才的话，说得太含糊了。从2019年起我退出的是评比赛。不是展览本身。只是评审那块。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll still supply the fish, still turn up, still argue about someone's torn fin for forty minutes. I just won't be on anyone's list.
beats.chinese: 我还是会供鱼，还是会去，还是会为别人的鱼鳍撕伤争上四十分钟。我只是不进任何人的名单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Skip that part. Hm. You make it sound simple.
beats.chinese: 跳过那部分就行。嗯。你说得倒轻巧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the phone over and over in her hand, then stops.
beats.chinese: 她把手机在手里翻来覆去，然后停住了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It is simple, isn't it. I keep waiting for a moment to explain myself properly, and meanwhile I'm hanging up on people.
beats.chinese: 确实挺简单的，不是吗。我一直在等一个好好解释的时机，结果却一直在挂别人电话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The fish don't care where they came. Tank's at twenty-six degrees, fry are feeding, that's the whole report.
beats.chinese: 鱼根本不在乎自己排第几。缸温二十六度，鱼苗在吃食，汇报完毕。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She puts the phone away, screen dark, and leans back on the bench.
beats.chinese: 她把手机收起来，屏幕已经暗了，靠回长椅上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Deb can rank her heart out. I'll bring the arguments. No declarations today.
beats.chinese: 行。让黛布排她的名去吧。我负责出论点。今天不发什么胜负宣言。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs, short and dry, like a cough she decided to keep.
beats.chinese: 她笑了，短促而干巴巴，像一声决定留下的咳嗽。

beats.speaker: npc
