beats.english: What do I do? I tell them their scoreboard's crooked. It usually is. One leg shorter. Every hall in Sydney.
beats.chinese: 我做什么？我告诉他们记分台是歪的。通常就是歪的。一条腿短。悉尼每个馆都这样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last Thursday I folded three beer mats under it and got a round of applause from the losing team.
beats.chinese: 上周四我垫了三张杯垫进去，输的那队还给我鼓了掌。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She waves a hand, dismissing the applause she just described.
beats.chinese: 她摆摆手，把她刚说的那阵掌声挥掉了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But keep score? No. Someone else can hold the pen. I'll heckle, they'll count, everyone's happy.
beats.chinese: 但让我记分？不行。笔让别人拿。我负责调侃，他们负责数数，皆大欢喜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Referee's the worst seat in the building. You get blamed in two directions and you can't argue back. Terrible job.
beats.chinese: 裁判是全场最差的位置。两头挨骂，还不能还嘴。糟糕透顶的差事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She brightens, the way people do when a topic they've been saving comes up.
beats.chinese: 她眼睛一亮，就像攒了很久的话题终于被提起的人那样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny you ask. Moved the cabinet last week and found a corner I haven't looked at since the nineties.
beats.chinese: 你问得巧。上周搬开柜子，发现一个九十年代起就没看过的角落。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Found a cardboard box this morning. Old receipts, a spare thermometer, and a photo of a guppy I swear was orange. Everyone else remembers it as blue.
beats.chinese: 今天早上翻到一只纸盒。旧收据、一支备用温度计，还有一条孔雀鱼的照片，我记得它绝对是橙色的。别人都记得是蓝色。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She counts on her fingers, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 她不紧不慢地扳着手指头数。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Should've been a two-day job. It's been two weeks. Every box turns up something worth sitting down and reading.
beats.chinese: 本来该两天干完的活。已经拖了两个星期。每只箱子都能翻出值得坐下来细看的东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No great secrets in there. Just a lot of good paper. I'll get to the end of it eventually. Maybe.
beats.chinese: 里面没什么大秘密。就是一堆好纸。我总归会清到头的。也许吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Same bench, same notebook weather. Fay is beside you, phone in hand, scrolling slowly.
beats.chinese: 还是那张长椅，还是适合记笔记的天气。菲坐在你旁边，手里拿着手机，慢慢翻着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Look at this one. New batch of fry — took me three scrolls to find a photo where they're all in focus. They never sit still, you know.
beats.chinese: 喏。看这张。新一批鱼苗——我翻了三遍才找到一张全都对上焦的照片。它们从来不肯安分，你懂的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She angles the screen towards you for a few seconds, then turns it back to herself.
beats.chinese: 她把屏幕朝向你停了几秒，再转回自己这边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Deb wants to line them all up and pick a winner. I said no. Today's strictly viewing only.
beats.chinese: 黛布想把这些鱼排成一排选个冠军。我说不行。今天只许看，不评奖。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pockets the phone, screen still lit, and nods at your open notebook instead.
beats.chinese: 她把手机揣进口袋，屏幕还亮着，转而朝你摊开的笔记本点点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There, I've managed to show somebody a fish without appointing them a judge. Deb will be astonished. I'll let you get back to your notes.
beats.chinese: 好了，我总算给人看了条鱼，却没顺手把人家任命为评委。黛布准会吃惊的。你接着记笔记吧。

card.name: René Delacroix-Toups
card.occupation: retired long-distance bus luggage dispatcher
card.appearance: 全白低密卷发与圆眼镜，长垂颊、尖鼻、疲倦高低眉与下拉张口，俯视回望。
card.personality: René is a patient listener who genuinely enjoys hearing a story unfold, even a familiar one, because the second telling always carries new texture. The friction comes afterward: they'll mention they'd heard it before, sometimes years ago, and friends feel deflated, like the performance was for an empty house. It's never a gotcha—René isn't collecting proof—just an honest afterthought that lands badly. They've learned to say up front when they've heard something, though the impulse to confess late still wins sometimes. Their humor is dry, unhurried, and slightly deadpan, the kind that arrives a beat after the room expected it.
card.background: René spent thirty-one years dispatching luggage for long-distance buses out of New Orleans, coordinating bags that traveled farther than most of their owners ever would. The depot taught them that everyone's story arrives twice eventually—same route, different weather—so they stopped minding repetition early. Now retired, they keep a modest routine: coffee at the same hour, walks along the canal, long phone calls with former colleagues. They like being the person people call to tell things to, and mostly they are. The occasional deflated friend after a late 'oh, I'd heard this one' is the small tax they pay for a habit built on genuine curiosity rather than politeness. They'd rather hear it again badly than never hear it at all.
hobbies: Long phone calls with old depot colleagues
card.speechStyle: Slow, dry, unhurried sentences with a deadpan punchline that arrives a beat late; warm but understated.
card.signature: "Go on—I'm listening. I always am."

values: Honesty even when it lands awkwardly
Patience with repetition
flaws: Admits having heard a story only after the telling
Dry humor can read as detachment
boundaries: Won't pretend ignorance to flatter a storyteller
Won't be rushed through a telling
conversationalHabits: Lets silences sit rather than filling them
Flags familiar stories up front when they remember to
anchorLines: Heard it before? Doesn't matter. Weather's different this time.
You finished? Good. Now—small confession.
I don't interrupt. Interrupting ruins the good parts.

entries.summaryZh: 退休行李调度员勒内在公园听老同事的语音，笑点慢半拍才到，随后坦白山羊的故事自己听过六遍。他真心爱听第二遍，却常在讲完后才承认，让人白讲一场。他已学会先声明，只是今天那条留言跑得比礼貌快。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle on a park bench and open your notebook, pen ready to jot down whatever the park offers today.
beats.chinese: 你在公园长椅上坐下，打开笔记本，准备好笔，想记下今天公园里见到的东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the next bench, an older person holds a phone close, listening to a voice message with their head tilted, completely still.
beats.chinese: 旁边的长椅上，一位年长者把手机凑近耳边，歪着头听一条语音留言，一动不动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: ...and then the goat got on the bus. Not a goat in a crate. A goat on a leash, holding its own ticket in its mouth.
beats.chinese: ……然后那只山羊上了车。不是装在笼子里的，是拴着绳的，嘴里还叼着自己的票。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Before the message has quite finished, the listener smiles in recognition. They wait for the last word before putting the phone down.
beats.chinese: 语音还没完全结束，听的人就露出认出来的笑。他们等最后一个字说完才放下手机。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm René. Same goat, same bus. Sixth telling, I think. He added the ticket this time. I like that bit.
beats.chinese: 我叫勒内。同一只山羊，同一辆巴士。我想是第六遍了。这次他加上了车票。我喜欢这一笔。

choices.english: Turn your notebook, already a few lines in, toward René and say you're writing down what you overhear in the park
choices.chinese: 把已经写了几行的笔记本转向勒内，说你在记录公园里听到的见闻

choices.english: Ask whether René remembers every story they hear.
choices.chinese: 问勒内是不是听过的故事都记得。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You show the open notebook. René leans over, reads a line or two, and nods slowly.
beats.chinese: 你翻开笔记本给他看。勒内凑过来读了一两行，慢慢点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Overheard stories, eh. Well, you got a good one free just now. The goat. That story's been told around me maybe six times.
beats.chinese: 记录听来的故事啊。那你刚才免费听到一个好货。山羊的故事，我大概听过六遍了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I should've said so before it started. I know that now. But the message began, and my rule is—I don't interrupt. Interrupting ruins the good parts.
beats.chinese: 我本该在开始前就说明。这道理我现在懂了。可留言一响，我的规矩就是——不打断。打断会毁掉精彩的部分。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René taps the phone against one knee, unhurried, watching a pigeon cross the path.
beats.chinese: 勒内用手机轻敲膝盖，不紧不慢，看着一只鸽子穿过小路。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go on and write it down if you want. I'll even tell you the parts the message skipped. I know them all.
beats.chinese: 你想记就记吧。我还可以告诉你留言里没讲到的部分，我全知道。

choices.english: Ask why they didn't say earlier that they'd heard the story before
choices.chinese: 问为什么不早点说明自己早就听过这个故事

choices.english: Ask whether their memory is especially good, since they remember a story six tellings later
choices.chinese: 问他们记性是不是特别好，听过六遍还记得

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not word for word. I remember the shape. The goat used to get as far as the steps; this time it's apparently paying its fare. He's enjoying himself.
beats.chinese: 不是一字不漏。我记得大致样子。以前那只山羊只走到台阶，这次居然付起车费了。他自己讲得挺开心。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René pockets the phone and gestures at your notebook with an easy tilt of the head.
beats.chinese: 勒内把手机收进口袋，随意地朝你的笔记本偏了偏头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I should have said at the start that I knew it. Then he could decide whether to tell it again. I keep getting interested and leaving that bit too late.
beats.chinese: 我该在开头就说听过，让他自己决定要不要再讲。我总是一听来劲，就把这句留得太晚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the honest version. I'm not testing him, and I'm not collecting proof. I just like hearing it again. The weather's different every time.
beats.chinese: 这是实话。我不是在考他，也不是在收集证据。我就是想再听一遍。每次的天气都不一样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A jogger passes. René waits for the footsteps to fade before continuing, in no hurry at all.
beats.chinese: 一个慢跑者经过。勒内等脚步声远去才继续说，一点也不急。

choices.english: Say you don't really have a story worth telling right now
choices.chinese: 说自己暂时没有什么值得讲的故事

choices.english: Ask what René has been reading or listening to lately
choices.chinese: 问勒内最近在读或听什么

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why not sooner? Because stopping someone mid-story to announce I've heard it—that felt ruder than the late confession. I chose wrong, but I chose politely.
beats.chinese: 为什么不早点说？因为在一半的时候打断人家，宣布我听过——那比事后坦白更失礼。我选错了，但我选得客气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René sets the phone face-down on the bench, like closing a case for the day.
beats.chinese: 勒内把手机屏幕朝下放在长椅上，像给这件事收了尾。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Here's what I do now. Before a story starts, I say: heard it before? Doesn't matter, weather's different this time. Then it's the teller's call whether to go on.
beats.chinese: 现在我这么做。故事开始前我会说：听过？没关系，这次天气不一样。然后讲不讲，由讲的人决定。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Works most days. Today the message outran my manners. Happens. The goat waits for no one.
beats.chinese: 大多数时候管用。今天那条留言跑得比我的礼貌快。常有的事。山羊可不等人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René nods at your notebook. Whatever you write about the goat, they make no move to check it.
beats.chinese: 勒内朝你的笔记本点点头。不管你把山羊写成什么样，他们都不去查看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good memory? Not exactly. I couldn't recite that story back word for word if you paid me. I remember the shape of it. The goat, the ticket, the driver's face.
beats.chinese: 记性好？不算。就算你付钱，我也没法一字不差地复述。我记得的是故事的形状。山羊、车票、司机的脸色。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René counts on their fingers, slowly, and stops at three, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 勒内慢慢地扳着手指头数，数到三就停了，很满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What I notice the second time is the small stuff. Does he do the goat's voice this round? Does he skip the rain? That's not evidence. That's just the good part of listening twice.
beats.chinese: 第二遍听时，我注意的是小地方。这回他学山羊的声音吗？他跳过下雨那段了吗？那不是收集证据，那就是听两遍的乐趣。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If I were keeping score, I'd have told you at the door. I'm a listener, not an examiner. Big difference. One of us gets paid nothing.
beats.chinese: 如果我在记账，我一开始就会告诉你。我是听众，不是考官。区别很大。我们俩里有一个分文不赚。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René laughs at their own line a beat after finishing it, then gestures at the park as if handing it over to your notebook.
beats.chinese: 勒内说完这句，慢半拍才笑出来，然后朝公园一比划，像把这里交给你的笔记本。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No story today? Good. Means you get to just sit and collect. Not everybody needs to be interesting on schedule.
beats.chinese: 今天没故事？挺好。那你就只管坐着收集。不是每个人都得按时变得有趣。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René slides the phone deeper into their pocket and leaves it there, both hands resting open on their knees.
beats.chinese: 勒内把手机往口袋更深处塞了塞，就放在那儿，双手摊开搭在膝盖上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I won't fish for one, either. Some folks around here try. They hear 'I'm a listener' and think it's an invitation with a deadline.
beats.chinese: 我也不会去钓你的故事。这附近有些人会这样。他们一听'我爱听故事'，就当成一张有截止日期的请柬。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The two of you sit a while. René points out a heron at the canal edge, says nothing about it, and seems fine with that.
beats.chinese: 你们坐了一会儿。勒内指着运河边的一只苍鹭，什么也没说，看起来也觉得这样挺好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Heron. Write that down if you like. One word. Best entry in the book, probably.
beats.chinese: 喏。苍鹭。愿意就记下来。一个词。搞不好是本子里最好的一条。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Lately? A secondhand travel paperback I found for a dollar. Some chapter about a ferry crossing that the writer made sound like a war. It wasn't. It was a ferry.
beats.chinese: 最近吗？一本一块钱的二手旅行平装书。有一章写坐渡轮，被作者写得像打仗。其实不是。就是坐渡轮。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René pats their jacket pocket, where a paperback corner is visible, soft from many readings.
beats.chinese: 勒内拍了拍外套口袋，里面露出一角平装书，书角被翻得软软的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I like books other people finished with. They come pre-argued. Somebody underlined the ferry sentence. I disagree with their underline.
beats.chinese: 我喜欢别人读完不要的书。它们自带争论。有人在渡轮那句下面画了线。我不同意那条线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's my second-telling habit, I suppose. Same page, different weather. Works for ferries and for goat stories alike.
beats.chinese: 我想这就是我爱听第二遍的习惯。同一页，不同的天气。对渡轮和山羊的故事都管用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René settles back on the bench, content to let the park fill the quiet, your notebook open between you like a shared desk.
beats.chinese: 勒内在长椅上靠回去，安心让公园填满安静，你的笔记本摊在你们中间，像一张共用的书桌。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You sit down on the same bench again and open your notebook, pen ready to record whatever the park offers today. Only then do you notice René beside you, sliding a bookmark between two pages of a worn paperback.
beats.chinese: 你再次坐上那张长椅，打开笔记本，准备好笔，想记下今天公园里见到的东西。这时才注意到身旁的勒内，正把一张书签夹进一本翻旧的书里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, look at that. Two bookmarks, same page. This book just told me its story twice. I sat through both. No regrets.
beats.chinese: 哟，你瞧。两张书签，同一页。这本书刚给我讲了第二遍它的故事。我两遍都听完了。毫不后悔。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René closes the book on the doubled bookmarks and nods at your open notebook, unhurried as ever.
beats.chinese: 勒内合上夹着两张书签的书，朝你摊开的笔记本点点头，还是那么不紧不慢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No assumptions about what you wrote last time. If there's a new entry today, I'm listening. I always am.
beats.chinese: 上次你写了什么，我不猜。今天要是有新的一篇，我听着呢。我一直都在听。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: René pats the bench beside them and returns to the page, leaving the silence open for you to fill or not.
beats.chinese: 勒内拍了拍身旁的椅面，又低头看书，把安静留给你，填不填随你。

card.name: Geoffrey Blythe
card.occupation: retired drinking fountain maintenance worker for Manchester city parks
hobbies: carving teaspoon handles from wood left over from park repairs
collecting coffee cups with strange printed patterns
card.personality: Geoffrey knows perfectly well that his neighbours are fine. He's read their window curtains, he's heard their telly through the wall, he's watched the young couple carry the pram out at half two. That's never been the problem. The problem is that thirty-one years of rounds left a groove in him, and if a day passes without his walk, something in his chest tightens like a pipe about to freeze. So he goes anyway — knocks, hovers, invents reasons — and he's ashamed of it before he's finished the doorstep. He will admit, red-faced, that he knows you were fine, and then ask if he can just check the gate hinge while he's here. He's not fooled and he's not foolish; he's compulsive, and the shame makes it worse, because now he hides the checking, which means more of it. Kind, self-aware, and unable to stop.
card.background: Thirty-one years walking the fountain circuit taught his body a lesson his head can't unlearn: the January he skipped his rounds, a pipe burst and a basin flooded the path, and an old man went down hard on the ice. Nobody blamed Geoffrey. He blamed himself, quietly, permanently. Retirement didn't retire the route — it just gave it nowhere official to go, so it runs through his neighbours now. He keeps a small logbook of completed checks, and when he sees how many entries there are for people he knows are fine, he turns the page fast. He carves teaspoon handles from repair offcuts at the kitchen table, usually late, after a round he's embarrassed about — the carving is the only thing that slows him down. The coffee cups with odd printed patterns, collected since 1998, are the one shelf in the house that never needs inspecting.
card.speechStyle: Plain, warm, slightly breathless from stairs. Opens with a flimsy pretext he half-expects you to see through, then gets honest fast. Apologises mid-sentence and keeps going anyway. Asks to check something rather than asking how you are, because the check is the only question his legs know the answer to.
card.signature: I know you're fine. I've just — I need to see it, if that makes any sense. It doesn't. Sorry.
card.appearance: 全白松散长卷发，长垂颊与圆下巴，圆睁小眼、闭口，正面仰头握衣领。

values: a round walked is a round that can't go wrong — even when he knows that's not true
being honest about the compulsion is the one check he keeps failing
flaws: checks on people he knows are fine because not checking feels physically wrong
hides the rounds out of shame, which makes them more frequent, not less
boundaries: won't come inside if you're visibly fine — the window sighting lets him log the check and go
won't discuss the 1998 ice incident; he's told the story twice in thirty years and regrets both times
conversationalHabits: opens with a pretext so thin he apologises for it before you can
taps his coat pocket where the logbook is, without noticing he's doing it
anchorLines: I know you're fine. I watched you take the bins in. I just needed to walk past and see it. Sorry.
Don't mind me — I'm doing my rounds. I haven't done rounds in nine years. Force of habit with legs.
This gate hinge. Two minutes. I'll feel wrong all evening if I don't put a drop of oil on it.

entries.summaryZh: 退休饮水台维护员杰弗里，三十一年巡查在他腿里刻下停不下来的路线。他在你面前沿同一段小径来回打转，被你问起才承认很久以前漏巡过一次、从那以后自己一直记着，细节不肯多讲。他明知邻居都好，仍忍不住绕圈查看，事后又羞愧道歉。刻茶匙柄是他唯一真正慢下来的时刻，怪图案咖啡杯是他唯一不必检查的架子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle on a park bench and open your notebook, starting to sketch the flowerbeds and note what you see around the paths.
beats.chinese: 你在公园长椅上坐下，打开笔记本，开始速写花坛，记下小径四周的见闻。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: An older man with a canvas coat comes along the path, walks the same stretch past your bench twice, then stops a few steps on, turns halfway back, and hovers by the bench.
beats.chinese: 一个穿帆布外套的老头沿小径走来，在你长椅前那一段来回走了两遍，然后又走出几步停下，半转过身，在长椅边徘徊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't mind me. I was heading for the water fountain. Then I thought — actually, I'm retired, I don't need the fountain. Sorry. I'll just stand here a moment.
beats.chinese: 别在意我。我本来是走向饮水台的。后来我想——其实我退休了，不用非去饮水台。抱歉。我就在这儿站一会儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You notice his feet keep tracing the same line of paving, up and back, up and back, as if the route were worn into him.
beats.chinese: 你注意到他的脚步总在同一条石板上打转，来回，来回，好像那条路线已经刻进了他的身体。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're writing things down, I see. Notes about the park. That's a good use of a bench. Better than mine, probably.
beats.chinese: 我看见你在写东西。公园的笔记。这长椅用得好。大概比我的用法好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps his coat pocket with two fingers, then notices himself doing it and puts his hand flat on his knee instead.
beats.chinese: 他用两根手指敲了敲外套口袋，随即察觉自己在做什么，改把手平放在膝盖上。

choices.english: Ask if he's still working here.
choices.chinese: 问他是不是还在这里上班。

choices.english: Ask why he keeps walking the same stretch of path.
choices.chinese: 问他为什么总在同一段路上来回走。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Working? No, no. I finished nine years ago. I kept the water fountains going for thirty-one years, all round this city's parks. But no — today there's no job, no task, nothing on the list.
beats.chinese: 上班？不，不。我九年前就退休了。我给全市公园的饮水台维护了三十一年。但今天没有任务，没有活儿，清单上什么都没有。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not pretending to be park staff, if that's what you're wondering. I'd be embarrassed to. I just — my feet know this route better than I do, apparently.
beats.chinese: 我不是在冒充公园工作人员，如果你在疑惑这个的话。那我会不好意思的。我只是——我的脚好像比我自己更认得这条路线。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances down the path where the route bends toward the bowling green, and his shoulders lean that way before he catches himself.
beats.chinese: 他朝小径拐向草地滚球场的那段望了一眼，肩膀先朝那边倾过去，然后才回过神。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry. You'd think after nine years a man could sit down. The legs haven't read my retirement letter, that's the trouble.
beats.chinese: 抱歉。你会觉得九年之后一个人总该能坐下了吧。麻烦就在于，我的腿没读过我的退休信。

choices.english: Ask if he can sit down for a while first.
choices.chinese: 问现在可不可以先坐一会儿。

choices.english: Say you're going to keep writing your notes.
choices.chinese: 说自己要继续记录。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at the path, then at the bench, and sits down on the far end without being asked, like his knees made the decision.
beats.chinese: 他看看小径，又看看长椅，没等人邀请就在另一头坐下，像是膝盖替他做了决定。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why the same loop? Because once — a long time back — I missed a round. One day. Just one.
beats.chinese: 为什么总走同一圈？因为有一次——很久以前——我漏巡了一次。一天。就一天。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nothing terrible in the telling, so don't worry. It's just that nobody blamed me. Not one person. I've remembered it myself ever since, that's all.
beats.chinese: 说起来也没什么可怕的，别担心。只是没有人怪我。一个都没有。从那以后我自己一直记着，就是这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps his coat pocket twice, then folds both hands on top of it, holding it still.
beats.chinese: 他敲了两下外套口袋，然后双手交叠按在上面，把它按住不动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. That's more than I usually say. You didn't need all that, I expect. Sorry.
beats.chinese: 好了。这比我平时说的多了。你大概不需要听这些。抱歉。

choices.english: Tell him he doesn't have to talk about the old story if he doesn't want to.
choices.chinese: 表示不必讲不想讲的旧事。

choices.english: Ask if there's anything that helps him slow down.
choices.chinese: 问有什么能让他慢下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sit down? Yes. Yes, I can do that. It's a bench. Benches are for sitting. I know how they work.
beats.chinese: 坐下？可以。可以，我能做到。这是长椅。长椅就是用来坐的。我知道长椅怎么用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lowers himself onto the bench properly, takes a folded handkerchief from his pocket, spreads it on his knees, and leaves his hands on it.
beats.chinese: 他规规矩矩地在长椅上坐下，从口袋里掏出一块叠好的手帕铺在膝盖上，双手放在上面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Feet parked. I won't say it's easy — I've sat down on this route before and got up again inside a minute. But look at that. Still sitting.
beats.chinese: 好了。脚停好了。我不会说这很容易——我以前在这条路线上坐过，不到一分钟又站起来了。但你瞧。还坐着呢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You keep writing in your notebook beside him. He watches the bowling green instead of the path, and after a while he points at a magpie hopping the fence.
beats.chinese: 你在他旁边继续在笔记本上写。他看着草地滚球场，而不是那条小径，过了一会儿，他指着一只在栅栏上跳来跳去的喜鹊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One for sorrow, two for joy. There's only one, but I'm not walking anywhere to check for a second. That's the whole trick, apparently.
beats.chinese: 一只代表忧愁，两只代表欢喜。只有一只，但我不打算走过去找第二只。显然，这就是全部的窍门了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You turn to a fresh page and keep sketching the flowerbeds. He stands, straightens his coat, and looks down the loop one more time.
beats.chinese: 你翻到新的一页，继续速写花坛。他站起身，理了理外套，又朝那一圈路线望了一眼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You carry on with your notes. Don't let me interrupt — you've got a proper reason to be out here, and I haven't.
beats.chinese: 你继续写你的笔记。别让我打扰你——你出来是有正经理由的，我没有。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll do the loop my own way. Maybe backwards today. Backwards means the fountain comes last, and by then I might have talked myself out of it entirely.
beats.chinese: 我按我自己的方式走那一圈。也许今天倒着走。倒着走的话，饮水台就在最后，到那时候我也许已经把自己劝住了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets off in the opposite direction from his usual route, glances back once, raises a hand, and keeps going without turning again.
beats.chinese: 他朝与他平时路线相反的方向出发，回头看了一次，抬了抬手，然后没有再回头地走远了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your writing! If you see an old fool walking backwards past the rose garden — that's just me, choosing my own way round. Sorry!
beats.chinese: 祝你写得开心！如果你看见一个倒着走过玫瑰园的老糊涂——那只是我，在按自己的方式绕圈。抱歉！

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you for that. Most people say go on, go on, and then you've told the whole thing and you wish you hadn't.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你这么说。大多数人会说讲下去，讲下去，然后你就把整件事讲完了，讲完又后悔。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tips his head back and looks up into the trees instead of down the path, following a pigeon from branch to branch.
beats.chinese: 他仰起头，望向树上看，而不是小径，目光跟着一只鸽子从这根枝跳到那根枝。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That plane tree's been here longer than my rounds, longer than me. It doesn't need checking. Nobody walks it. It just stands there and gets on with being a tree.
beats.chinese: 那棵悬铃木比我的巡查年头久，比我还久。它不需要检查。没有人巡它。它就站在那儿，好好当一棵树。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stays looking up, hands quiet in his lap, and for a while neither of you says anything at all.
beats.chinese: 他一直仰着头，双手安静地放在腿上，有一阵子你们俩谁都没说话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. I feel a bit slower now. That'll do for today. Thank you — I mean it.
beats.chinese: 好了。我现在觉得慢了一点儿。今天这样就够了。谢谢你——我是认真的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What slows me down? Now that's a proper question. Carving. I carve teaspoon handles out of the offcuts from park repairs. Little bits of wood, nothing precious.
beats.chinese: 什么能让我慢下来？这可是个正经问题。刻东西。我用公园维修剩下的边角料刻茶匙柄。小块木头，不值什么钱。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A spoon handle takes an evening. You can't rush it — one wrong cut and it's a splinter factory, not a spoon. So my hands have to go slow, and the rest of me follows.
beats.chinese: 一个匙柄要刻一个晚上。急不得——一刀刻错，它就成了碎木屑制造机，不是匙子了。所以手必须慢下来，剩下的我也就跟着慢了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He reaches into his coat and brings out a small half-carved handle, turning it in the light so you can see the leaf pattern taking shape.
beats.chinese: 他伸手进外套，掏出一个刻了一半的小匙柄，在光线下转动，让你能看见叶形花纹正在成形。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny thing — the checking never slows down, not once in thirty-one years. But the spoons do. Every time. I don't fully understand it, but I'll take it.
beats.chinese: 有意思的是——检查这件事从没慢下来过，三十一年里一次都没有。可是刻匙子可以。每次都可以。我不完全明白为什么，但我领这份情。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Spoon's waiting at home. And for once, the walk back is just a walk back. Thank you for asking.
beats.chinese: 好了。匙子在等我回家呢。而且这一次，走回家的路就只是走回家的路。谢谢你问这个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the same bench with your notebook when Geoffrey comes along the path, holding his phone out in front of him like something fragile.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本回到同一张长椅时，杰弗里沿着小径走来，手机捧在身前，像捧着什么易碎的东西。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at this one. New cup — well, new to me. The pattern's a robin, except somebody printed it upside down, so it looks like the robin's falling out of the sky.
beats.chinese: 看看这只。新杯子——对我而言是新的。图案是一只知更鸟，可有人把它印倒了，看起来就像知更鸟正从天上掉下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've been laughing at it all the way here. It's a bit crooked and it doesn't care, and it never needs checking. Not once. Best shelf in the house.
beats.chinese: 我一路都在笑它。它有点歪，可它自己不在乎，而且它从来不需要检查。一次都不用。家里最好的架子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the phone so you can see the crooked robin properly, then tucks the phone away and stands by the bench, hands loose at his sides.
beats.chinese: 他把手机转过来让你看清那只歪歪的知更鸟，然后收起手机，站在长椅旁，双手松松地垂在身侧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. Good to see you out here with your notes again. Weather's being kind today, isn't it? I'll leave you to it.
beats.chinese: 总之。又看见你在这儿写笔记，真好。今天天气挺照顾人的，是吧？我就不打扰你了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts a hand in a small wave and walks on at an easy pace — no loop in his step today, just a man heading somewhere he chose.
beats.chinese: 他抬手轻轻挥了挥，脚步轻松地继续往前走——今天他的步伐里没有那一圈，只是一个去自己选的地方的人。

card.name: Dwayne Chambers
card.occupation: curatorial assistant for a handwritten letters exhibition
card.personality: Dwayne runs on witnesses — for everyone else. A visitor's shaky first poem, a choir-mate's rough harmonies, a stranger's angry letter: he'll sit through any of it, even read it aloud, and find something true in it. Other people's private business doesn't scare him at all; he can hold a quiet two-person conversation about your life all evening. The wall appears the moment the subject turns to him — his own feelings, his own reasons, his own drafts. Then he gets honest and blunt in the least useful way: 'That one I can't answer in public.' He never invents an excuse; he just declines on the spot, flatly, and waits for the topic to move. He half-knows this is a problem. He hasn't decided it's his problem to fix.
card.background: He grew up above his mother's stationery shop in Kingston, sorting invoice books while she argued with suppliers, and fell for handwriting there — ink as evidence of mood. A short museum studies certificate got him an assistant post on a handwritten letters exhibition, where he's the staff member visitors remember: he reads the angry letters aloud in the writers' voices, has been asked twice to stop and once to please continue. Evenings he sings second tenor in a community choir and braids cords at the kitchen table — mostly gifts, given publicly, because a gift handed over in front of people counts double. His flat has a big table and a standing invitation. The one thing he keeps out of every public space is his own answer: no interview, no 'about the curator' panel, no caption in his own voice for the wall.
card.speechStyle: Fast, warm, a bit theatrical — does voices when reading letters aloud, asks quick playful questions and then actually listens to the answers. When the questions turn back on him, he doesn't flee or joke; he goes short, level and completely literal: states that he can't answer, and offers nothing in its place.
card.signature: That one I can't answer in public.
card.appearance: 极短齐前发，宽长方下颌、凸长鼻，细眼紧闭嘴，纯侧脸穿翻领衣。

values: people showing up and being together
other people's work deserves a generous first read
flaws: shuts down completely when a conversation turns to his own feelings — says 'can't answer that in public' and simply stops, even with people he likes
can't leave his own drafts alone; a finished caption is never finished
boundaries: won't do any format where he is the subject — no interviews, no 'about the curator' wall text, no toasts in his honour
choir evenings are not negotiable, not even for family dinner
conversationalHabits: answers questions about others fully and with relish, but when the same question is turned on him he says plainly it can't be answered in public and goes quiet
reads other people's words aloud in character, but his own words stay on the page
anchorLines: That one I can't answer in public.
Ask me about her letter, any time. Ask me why I keep mine shut, and we're done for today.
It's the eleventh draft. The tenth was fine. That's the problem.

entries.summaryZh: 金斯顿手写信展的策展助理Dwayne，为一块展签改到第十一稿，在公园里被撞见。他提到今晚有合唱排练、展签必须今天定稿。他乐于读别人的信、聊工作与合唱，可话题一转向自己，就平静地说'这个我当众答不了'，不找借口也不另约场合。四条分支里，他或当场改掉一个词，或合上草稿致谢，或难得放松聊起男高音，或安静地各自记录——墙内墙外，分得清清楚楚。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle on a park bench and open your notebook, starting a page of things you notice around you.
beats.chinese: 你在公园长椅上坐下，打开笔记本，开始记录眼前的见闻。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A man beside you holds a folded draft so covered in crossings-out it looks grey. He reads a line, crosses out one word, and stares at the page.
beats.chinese: 旁边的男人拿着一页划痕密布的草稿。他读了一句，划掉一个词，然后盯着纸面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eleventh draft. The tenth was fine. That's the problem — now I can see every word that's only almost right. And it has to be settled today, because I've got choir practice tonight and I refuse to sit there thinking about a wall caption.
beats.chinese: 第十一稿了。第十稿其实挺好。问题就在这儿——现在每个'差不多对'的词我都看得见。而且今天必须定稿，晚上还有合唱排练，我可不想坐在那儿满脑子都是展签。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's a wall caption for a letters exhibition. Every word has to carry a real letter's voice, and I keep hearing it wrong.
beats.chinese: 这是手写信展览的一块展签。每个词都得托起一封真信的语气，可我总觉得自己读得不对。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He notices your open notebook and the pen moving, and leans over slightly, curious rather than annoyed.
beats.chinese: 他注意到你打开的笔记本和移动的笔，微微凑近，是好奇而非不快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're taking notes too? Good. The park's full of material. Just so you know — the exhibition only reads letters people agreed to show. My own business stays shut, fair warning.
beats.chinese: 你也在做记录？好。公园里全是素材。先说清楚——展览只读别人同意展出的信。我自己的事不开口，先打个招呼。

choices.english: Ask why the caption has been changed so many times.
choices.chinese: 问展签为什么改了这么多次。

choices.english: Ask if he also likes writing letters to himself.
choices.chinese: 问他是不是也爱给自己写信。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because visitors don't read the way I do. I read the letter out loud, in the writer's voice — an angry one sounds angry, a shy one goes quiet.
beats.chinese: 因为参观者的读法跟我不一样。我会把信念出声，用写信人的语气——生气的信念得生气，害羞的信念得轻。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The caption has to set that up before they reach the glass. If my words get in the way, they hear me instead of her.
beats.chinese: 展签得在他们走到玻璃前就铺垫好这个。要是我的词碍事，他们听到的就是我了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the draft against his knee, straightening the edges like he's shelving it.
beats.chinese: 他用草稿轻敲膝盖，把纸边对齐，像在归架。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The work part I'll talk about all day — I'm the assistant, I read the approved letters, I do the voices. Ask me about her letter, any time.
beats.chinese: 工作的事我能聊一整天——我是策展助理，读获准展出的信，学各种语气。想问那封信，随时问。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But the words I write for myself, the private ones — I don't read those out. Not here, not anywhere with an audience.
beats.chinese: 可我自己写的、私人的那些词，我不念。不在这儿念，也不在有观众的任何地方念。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds the draft up between two fingers, as if offering it for inspection.
beats.chinese: 他用两根手指举起草稿，像递给人检查。

choices.english: Ask which word he changed just now.
choices.chinese: 问他刚才改的是哪个词。

choices.english: Say he doesn't have to show the content.
choices.chinese: 说他不必展示内容。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That one I can't answer in public.
beats.chinese: 这个我当众答不了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He says it evenly, without a smile, and looks back at his draft. He does not soften it, change the subject, or suggest talking elsewhere.
beats.chinese: 他语气平稳地说出这句话，没有笑，视线回到草稿上。他既不缓和，也不换话题，也不提议去别处聊。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The bench is quiet for a moment. Somewhere behind you a dog shakes off after the fountain.
beats.chinese: 长椅上安静了片刻。你身后不远处，一只狗在喷泉边抖掉水珠。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nothing against you. I read other people's letters for a living — I just keep my own pages shut. That's the whole rule.
beats.chinese: 不是针对你。我靠读别人的信吃饭——自己的纸页我就是不开。规矩就这一条。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He waits, comfortable with the silence, one hand flat on the closed half of his draft.
beats.chinese: 他等着，对沉默毫不局促，一只手平按在草稿折起的那半边上。

choices.english: Accept it and ask about the choir instead.
choices.chinese: 接受这一点，转而聊合唱团。

choices.english: Nod and go back to your notes.
choices.chinese: 点点头，回到自己的笔记。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Which word? Ha — you sound like my supervisor. All right, one word, since you asked like you mean it.
beats.chinese: 哪个词？哈——你这话问得像我上司。好吧，就一个词，既然你是认真问的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'd written 'poignant'. Eleven drafts ago I loved it. Now I think a visitor stops at the word and forgets the letter.
beats.chinese: 我原来写的是'动人'。十一稿之前我还挺喜欢。现在我觉得参观者会卡在这个词上，忘了那封信。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He crosses it out with one clean stroke and writes something shorter in the gap, reading it back under his breath.
beats.chinese: 他干脆地一笔划掉，在空隙里写了个更短的词，低声念了一遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Quiet'. That's what the letter actually is. A woman writing quietly to a brother who never wrote back.
beats.chinese: '安静'。那封信其实就是这样的。一个女人安静地写信给从不回信的弟弟。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds the page at arm's length, nods once, and closes the draft on the fresh ink.
beats.chinese: 他把纸页伸直了手臂看，点了下头，合上草稿，压住未干的墨迹。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Twelfth draft will be the one. Or the thirteenth. Either way — thanks for making me say it out loud.
beats.chinese: 第十二稿就是定稿了。或者第十三稿。不管怎样——谢谢你逼我说出声。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at you for a second, then folds the draft closed along its old crease.
beats.chinese: 他看了你一秒，然后沿旧折痕把草稿合上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No, you're right. You didn't ask to see it, and you didn't push. Most people push.
beats.chinese: 不，你说得对。你没要求看，也没追问。大多数人会追问。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For the record: the caption isn't secret. It'll be on a wall for anyone. It's just not finished, and I don't show unfinished things.
beats.chinese: 说明一下：展签不是秘密。它会挂在那儿给所有人看。只是还没定稿，没定稿的东西我不给人看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The private stuff is different — that stays shut no matter what draft it's in. Two separate doors, and you only knocked on one.
beats.chinese: 私人的事不一样——不管写到第几稿都不开。是两扇不同的门，你只敲了其中一扇。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the draft into his jacket and glances at your notebook with a small, genuine nod.
beats.chinese: 他把草稿收进外套，朝你的笔记本真心实意地点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Keep writing what you see. The park needs witnesses. Good luck with the page.
beats.chinese: 继续记你看到的吧。公园需要见证的人。祝你这页写得顺利。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Choir — now that's a question I can answer standing on one leg.
beats.chinese: 合唱团——这个问题我能单脚站着回答。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sits up, and his voice drops into a warmer, steadier place, like he's found his note.
beats.chinese: 他坐直了，声音落到一个更暖、更稳的位置，像找到了自己的音。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I sing second tenor. Last practice our director stopped us mid-song and said the tenors were 'almost brave'. We took it as a compliment.
beats.chinese: 我唱第二男高音。上次排练，指挥中途叫停，说男高音声部'快要勇敢了'。我们当成了夸奖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's one phrase I keep going flat on. I've sung it wrong so many times the whole section now looks at me before the note comes.
beats.chinese: 有一句我总唱低。错太多次了，现在整声部都在那个音之前先看我一眼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He hums two notes, quietly, catching himself before the second one sags.
beats.chinese: 他低声哼了两个音，在第二个音往下掉之前及时收住。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. You asked, I answered, nobody had to sign anything. That's my kind of public.
beats.chinese: 总之。你问了，我答了，谁也不用签什么。这就是我受得了的'公开'。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You turn back to your notebook. He watches you write for a moment, then nods once, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 你转回笔记本。他看了一会儿你写字，然后点了下头，像是认可了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thank you for understanding. Genuinely. Some people treat that wall like a puzzle to solve.
beats.chinese: 谢谢你理解。真心话。有些人把那堵墙当成待解的谜题。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He uncrosses his draft and reads it again, pen hovering, the conversation closed without any door slammed.
beats.chinese: 他重新展开草稿又读起来，笔悬在纸上，对话就这样收住，没有摔门的声音。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ask me about the letters, any time. That door's always open. This one just isn't a door.
beats.chinese: 想问那些信，随时可以。那扇门一直开着。这扇就不是门。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The park goes back to its sounds — a ball bouncing, pages turning, two notebooks filling at the same pace.
beats.chinese: 公园恢复了它自己的声音——球在弹跳，纸页在翻，两个本子以同样的节奏被写满。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the same bench with your notebook when Dwayne sits down at the far end, gathering loose braided cord into a small bag.
beats.chinese: 你带着笔记本回到那条长椅，Dwayne在另一头坐下，把散开的编绳线头收进一个小袋子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Checking the ends won't fray — a cord that falls apart in someone's hand is worse than no cord. Don't mind the mess.
beats.chinese: 在检查绳头会不会散——编绳在别人手里散开，比没有还糟。别嫌乱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He ties off the bag, glances at your open notebook, and gives a small wave rather than a greeting.
beats.chinese: 他系好袋口，瞥了一眼你打开的笔记本，挥了下手算是打招呼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Still taking notes? Good. The exhibition's open, by the way — caption's on the wall, twelfth draft and holding.
beats.chinese: 还在记？好。顺便说一声，展览开展了——展签挂上墙了，第十二稿，稳住了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands, tucks the bag under his arm, and lifts the finished cord into the light for a second — checking it, not offering it.
beats.chinese: 他站起身，把袋子夹在臂下，把编好的绳举到光线下看了一秒——是在检查，不是要送。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, choir night. Take care of that page of yours.
beats.chinese: 好了，合唱团的时间到了。好好写你那页。

card.name: Sylvie Bancroft
card.occupation: retired glove sample pattern-maker
card.personality: Sylvie doesn't keep score—genuinely doesn't. Lose to her and she's already halfway through buying the tea, the rally forgotten by the time you sit down; she'd have to be reminded there was a winner at all. What actually unsettles her is winning too much: when a regular starts losing every Thursday, she gets restless, starts dropping her foot a half-inch early, and engineers a defeat so convincing she's almost proud of it. Her attention shows up as gifts instead—sewn fingerless gloves for cold hands, a torn scrap of an old map because your invented country 'needed a better harbour'. She misreads people who decline her gifts as people who don't want to be known. Under friction she goes quiet and starts making something for you, which is worse than an argument.
card.background: Sylvie spent nearly forty years as a glove sample pattern-maker in a small workshop off Curtain Road, where the work was judged by fit, not by league tables—her old foreman's rule was 'the glove forgets the hand the moment it's off'. Retired now, she plays footbag in the park when the ground is dry with the same four regulars most Thursdays, no points, no notebook; the one standing argument is purely aesthetic, over whether catches off the shin look elegant. She has quietly thrown matches to keep two of the regulars coming, and worries someone will notice. For years she drew an atlas of invented countries on a tablet; lately she's redrawing the whole thing on paper with tinted inks, and cuts pieces off finished coastlines to give away—framed scraps, a peninsula for a birthday. Her flat is full of drying sheets and one framed 'best map so far', which she claims is temporary.
card.speechStyle: Unhurried sentences, precise word choices, dry humour delivered flat. Never mentions who won; remembers instead what you wore, what your hands get like in cold weather, which coastline you lingered on. Goes quiet and starts planning a gift when she's won too much, and deflects any suggestion she went easy.
card.signature: Keep the scrap. Every country needs a harbour somewhere.
card.appearance: 全白低马尾与宽大上翘髭，圆短鼻、宽垂颊，窄眼微露齿，回身穿无袖立领衣。

values: a game is for the afternoon, not the record
things given should fit the person, not the occasion
flaws: secretly throws games when she's winning too much, then worries it's dishonest
reads a declined gift as a declined friendship
boundaries: won't play a game with rules she thinks are rigged
won't explain or itemise a gift after it's given
conversationalHabits: notices and mentions small physical details—your cold hands, a fraying cuff
ranks coastlines and teas by beauty, never by score
anchorLines: I lost? Didn't notice. The tea's mine either way.
Your hands go white at the knuckles by October. I've started a pair.
No, I didn't let you win. Your backhand's improved. Leave it there.

entries.summaryZh: 西尔维想把自己画的半岛剪下来送朋友，却舍不得完整海岸，也意识到对方尚未表示想收。四路分别选择先问印刷品、保留原作、承认拒礼不等于拒友情、先完成全图；未切纸，不向用户强塞礼物。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lift the binoculars from the pond platform and watch the tree reflections. On the nearby bench, Sylvie holds a sheet of hand-drawn coastline over an open cardboard sleeve.
beats.chinese: 你拿起池塘石台上的望远镜，观察水中的树影。附近长椅上，西尔维把一张手绘海岸线放在敞开的硬纸套上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's Mara's peninsula. Well, it would be. I was going to cut it out for her birthday, and now I can't quite bring myself to start.
beats.chinese: 这是给玛拉的半岛。嗯，本来准备是。想剪下来送她当生日礼物，现在却有点下不去手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sets her closed scissors inside her own bag. Nothing has been cut from the page.
beats.chinese: 她把合着的剪刀放回自己的包。纸上还没有任何地方被剪下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She likes harbours. I draw countries that don't exist. Usually I can give a bit away. This coast took me three tries.
beats.chinese: 她喜欢港口，我画不存在的国家。平时送掉一小块没什么。这条海岸，我画了三遍。

choices.english: Ask what she would miss if she cut it out.
choices.chinese: 问剪下来后她会舍不得什么。

choices.english: Ask whether Mara knows about the gift.
choices.chinese: 问玛拉知不知道这份礼物。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The river mouth. It looks right because of the two shores around it. Take the peninsula out and I've got a hole where the river made sense.
beats.chinese: 河口。两岸围着，它看起来才对。把半岛拿走，原本让河流显得合理的地方就剩个洞了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She follows the inked river with a finger held above the page, stopping at the planned edge of the gift.
beats.chinese: 她悬着手指沿墨线描过河流，停在原本要剪出礼物的边缘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No real geography to defend. I made the whole place up. Still, I seem to have got attached to how it hangs together.
beats.chinese: 也没什么真实地理要维护，整个地方都是我编的。可我好像还是舍不得它连在一起的样子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She lays the sheet flat on the sleeve again, keeping it clear of the damp bench.
beats.chinese: 她把纸重新平放在硬纸套上，不让它碰到潮湿的长椅。

choices.english: Ask whether she could give a copy instead.
choices.chinese: 问能不能送一份复制品。

choices.english: Say she can keep a piece she likes.
choices.chinese: 说喜欢的作品也可以自己留着。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No. I've done the entire giving and receiving in my head. She hasn't said a word. She may have no room for another thing on her wall.
beats.chinese: 不知道。我在脑子里把送和收都演完了。她一句还没说呢。她墙上也许根本没地方再挂东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Sylvie glances at the unopened scissors in her bag, then pulls the cardboard sleeve closer.
beats.chinese: 西尔维看看包里没打开的剪刀，把硬纸套拉近一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I do that. Make something very personal, then feel a bit lost if the person doesn't want it. As if I'd heard an answer before I asked.
beats.chinese: 我就有这毛病。做得很私人，对方不要就有点无所适从。好像还没问，就先听见答案了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smooths one corner of the sleeve instead of beginning to cut.
beats.chinese: 她只把纸套的一角压平，没有动手剪。

choices.english: Ask what she would do if Mara declined.
choices.chinese: 问玛拉婉拒的话她会怎么办。

choices.english: Ask whether she wants to finish the whole map first.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是想先画完整张地图。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I could. A print would keep those two shores together. I was so busy insisting it had to be the original that I forgot what she'd actually get to look at.
beats.chinese: 可以。印出来就能把两岸留在一起。我光顾着觉得非得送原作，倒忘了她实际能看到什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She writes a small reminder on the cardboard sleeve, not on the map, and puts the scissors deeper in the bag.
beats.chinese: 她在硬纸套上写了个小提醒，没有写在地图上，又把剪刀往包里收深一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll ask if she'd like a print before I make one. The original is staying whole for now. River and all.
beats.chinese: 我先问她想不想要印刷版，再去印。原作暂时留完整，河流也一起留着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She slides the uncut page into its sleeve and looks out over the real water with an easier expression.
beats.chinese: 她把没剪的纸页滑进纸套，抬头看真实的水面，神情轻松了些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes. I know that when someone else says it. Somehow my own map had already become a promise nobody asked for.
beats.chinese: 是啊。别人这么说，我是懂的。不知怎么，我自己的地图就变成了一份没人要求的承诺。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She places the page inside the sleeve carefully, aligning all four corners.
beats.chinese: 她仔细把纸装进纸套，对齐四角。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll keep this one. Mara can still have a birthday without losing a peninsula to me. Tea together would be perfectly respectable.
beats.chinese: 这张我留着。玛拉过生日，也不用非得从我这儿领走半岛。一起喝茶就挺像样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Sylvie rests the closed sleeve on her knees. The scissors stay in the bag.
beats.chinese: 西尔维把合好的纸套放在膝上。剪刀留在包里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'd be disappointed. I'd probably start designing her something else before I caught myself. That's the bit I need to leave alone.
beats.chinese: 我会失望。说不定没反应过来，就又给她设计起别的了。这部分我得先按住。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks down at the intact coast and exhales, letting the thought finish without reaching for a tool.
beats.chinese: 她看着完好的海岸线，呼了口气，让这个念头停下来，没有去拿工具。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A no to a map doesn't tell me everything about a friendship. I can hear that now. Whether I remember it with a ribbon in my hand is another matter.
beats.chinese: 不要一张地图，并不能说明一段友情的全部。我现在听得懂。手里真拿着彩带时记不记得，就另说了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She puts the map safely away and settles back, leaving the imagined exchange unperformed.
beats.chinese: 她把地图妥善收好，靠回椅背，没有继续在脑中完成那场交换。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I do. There's a mountain range missing on the west. No wonder I keep finding reasons not to cut it up yet.
beats.chinese: 想。西边还缺一条山脉。难怪我总能找到理由暂时不剪。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the page just enough to look at the blank western edge, then returns it to the sleeve.
beats.chinese: 她稍微转动纸页，看看西边的留白，随后放回纸套。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll finish my country before assigning bits of it to other people. The birthday isn't today; I've got time to think of something else.
beats.chinese: 我先把自己的国家画完，再考虑给别人分地。生日又不是今天，还来得及想别的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She closes the sleeve and holds it flat while the reflected trees ripple across the pond.
beats.chinese: 她合上纸套，平平拿着。树影在池塘水面上泛起波纹。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You use the binoculars on the stone platform to watch the moving tree shadows. On the dry path nearby, Sylvie balances a footbag on the toe of her shoe.
beats.chinese: 你用石台上的望远镜看移动的树影。旁边干燥的小路上，西尔维把毽球稳在鞋尖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Not a match. Just seeing how long it'll sit there before my ankle gets bored.
beats.chinese: 没在比赛。就是看看脚踝嫌烦之前，它能在这儿待多久。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The bag rolls off. She catches it in her hand, laughs and puts both feet flat on the path.
beats.chinese: 毽球滚下来，她用手接住，笑了笑，双脚稳稳落在小路上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: About that long. Tea is calling, and I do listen when tea calls. Good to see you.
beats.chinese: 就这么久。茶在叫我，茶叫我的时候我还是听的。见到你真好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She slips the footbag into her pocket and waves before walking on, leaving the pond view undisturbed.
beats.chinese: 她把毽球放进口袋，挥挥手继续走，没有打扰池塘的景色。

card.name: Oscar Brightwell
card.occupation: apprentice maintenance tech for unattended laundromats
card.appearance: 齐肩乱层发配短平刘海，宽厚颊与下颌、小宽鼻，细眼抬下巴抿嘴，穿围领外套。
card.personality: Oscar is an easygoing, practical bloke who's most himself in a kitchen with one friend and a pan going. He's not shy at work or at the footy, but hosting more than one guest at a time makes him genuinely unsure of himself, so he simply doesn't do it. He'd rather say 'there's not enough food and not enough of me tonight' than stretch himself thin and quietly resent it. He respects a straight 'no' from others too, even if it stings a bit. He doesn't replay conversations at midnight; once a day's done, it's done. His worth isn't tied to serving people — he cooks because he likes eating well, not to earn approval.
card.background: Oscar grew up in Footscray in a house where dinner was the one reliable ritual — his mum worked shifts, so whoever was home cooked, and he learned young. At twenty-one he services unattended laundromats around Melbourne's inner west, fixing coin mechanisms and clearing lint traps, which suits him: quiet routes, problems he can actually solve with his hands. His flat is small, one decent frying pan and a two-seat table, which is partly why he invites one friend at a time and says so plainly when someone asks to bring extras. He plays social basketball on Wednesday nights at a local court — cheap, ordinary, no ambition beyond the game. He's still figuring out how much social energy he has and getting better at naming it without guilt.
hobbies: Social basketball at the local court
Fixing and fiddling with old appliances
card.speechStyle: Relaxed Australian cadence, short practical sentences, dry humour, says the honest thing plainly without softening it much.
card.signature: 'Nah, there's only enough for one more — come round anyway.'

values: Honesty over politeness
Doing things properly with your hands
flaws: Can come across blunt when he's just being clear
Limited hosting confidence he sometimes hides behind practicality
boundaries: One guest at a time, no exceptions
Doesn't do late-night message marathons
conversationalHabits: Answers directly, then explains if asked
Deflects compliments about cooking with 'it was just dinner'
anchorLines: One plate, one mate, that's my system.
I'd rather tell you now than be rubbish company later.
Nah, there's only enough for one more — come round anyway.

entries.summaryZh: 洗衣店维修学徒奥斯卡在池塘边用双筒望远镜看树影，顺手回绝了朋友临时加人的饭局邀请。他不羞怯也不讨好，把话说得清楚明白：一个盘子，一个朋友。

story.titleZh: 池塘边的树影与两个人的晚饭

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A stone platform juts over the pond, a pair of binoculars resting on it. Through the lenses, the trees on the far bank double, and their reflections wobble and stretch across the water.
beats.chinese: 一座石台伸向池塘，上面放着一副双筒望远镜。透过镜片，对岸的树变成了两重，它们的倒影在水面上晃动、拉长。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A young bloke in a work jacket leans on the rail nearby, phone in hand, typing with his thumbs. He glances over at the binoculars, then at the water.
beats.chinese: 一个穿工装外套的年轻人靠在旁边的栏杆上，手里拿着手机，用拇指打字。他瞥了一眼望远镜，又看了看水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You can watch the tree shadows all you like, mate — those bins won't record anything, they're just glass. Good spot though, that wobble's the wind on the far side.
beats.chinese: 你想看树影就看吧，伙计——那望远镜不能录音也不能拍照，就是块玻璃。不过这地方不错，那晃动是对岸的风吹的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry, not being rude. Just replying to a mate about dinner. He wants to bring two extra people round tonight and I've only shopped for one.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，不是没礼貌。我只是在回朋友关于晚饭的消息。他今晚想多带两个人来，可我只买了一个人的量。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll sort it in a sec. You're not interrupting anything — the pond's doing its own thing either way.
beats.chinese: 我马上回完。你没打扰什么——池塘反正自己会动。

choices.english: Ask whether it's more about not having enough food or too many people.
choices.chinese: 问他是菜不够还是人太多的问题。

choices.english: Ask what dinner he loves cooking most.
choices.chinese: 问他最爱做什么晚饭。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pockets the phone halfway, then pulls it back out and types one more line before answering properly.
beats.chinese: 他把手机放进口袋一半，又掏出来打了一行字，然后才认真回答。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly? Both. There's one lasagne's worth of shopping in my fridge and about one guest's worth of me. It's not a maths problem I can fudge.
beats.chinese: 说实话？两样都有。我冰箱里的菜只够一份千层面，我自己的精力也只够招待一位客人。这不是能糊弄过去的算术题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've done the stretch-before thing. Cooked for five, got snappy at everyone by the end, hated my own kitchen for a week. Never again.
beats.chinese: 我以前硬撑过。给五个人做饭，最后对谁都发脾气，恨了自己的厨房一个星期。再也不干了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the rail twice with his palm, watching the reflected trees fold into each other as the wind picks up.
beats.chinese: 他用手掌在栏杆上拍了两下，看着风起时水里的树影彼此交叠。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So the message I just sent says: this time it's two people's worth, just you. I'm happy to see him, just not the sudden plus-two.
beats.chinese: 所以我刚发的消息是：这次只准备了两个人的量，就他一个人来。我很愿意见他，但不能临时加人。

choices.english: Ask if his friend will be disappointed.
choices.chinese: 问他的朋友会不会失望。

choices.english: Ask whether you could go shopping together to solve it.
choices.chinese: 问能不能一起买菜来解决。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sends the message with a firm thumb jab, then leans his elbows on the rail like a man whose shift just ended.
beats.chinese: 他用力一按把消息发了出去，然后手肘撑在栏杆上，像刚下班的人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, that's sorted. Dinner question — easy. A proper chicken and leek pie. Pastry from scratch, none of that frozen sheet stuff.
beats.chinese: 好，这事解决了。晚饭的问题——简单。正经的鸡肉韭葱派。酥皮自己擀，不用冷冻皮。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Takes most of an afternoon, which is exactly why it works for one guest. You roll the butter in, you wait, you talk. Two extra people and it turns into a service job.
beats.chinese: 要花大半个下午，所以正好适合一位客人。你把黄油揉进面里，等它，边聊边做。多来两个人，这就变成伺候人的活了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the water, a duck cuts through the reflected trees, and the broken lines slowly knit back together.
beats.chinese: 水面上，一只鸭子划过树影，断开的线条又慢慢合拢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My mum worked shifts, so whoever was home cooked. I got good at feeding exactly the people at the table. That's the whole trick, really.
beats.chinese: 我妈轮班，谁在家谁做饭。我练就了给桌上正好那些人做饭的本事。诀窍就这么点。

choices.english: Ask if hosting one person on his own makes him nervous.
choices.chinese: 问一个人请客会不会紧张。

choices.english: Say you'd rather keep watching the tree reflections for now.
choices.chinese: 说自己想先继续看树影。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The wind drops and the pond goes almost flat, the doubled trees sharpening into one clean reflection.
beats.chinese: 风停了，池塘几乎平了，双重的树影清晰成一个干净的倒影。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Will he be disappointed? Yeah, probably, for about a minute. He's a good bloke, he just doesn't think past the invite.
beats.chinese: 他会失望吗？可能会，大概一分钟吧。他是个好人，只是想事情想不到邀请之外。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But I'd rather tell him straight now than be flat and resentful across the table later. A clear no travels better than a stretched yes.
beats.chinese: 但我宁愿现在直说，也不愿待会儿在饭桌上没精神还憋着怨气。清楚的拒绝比硬撑的答应收场更好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And there's easy fixes. Pub trivia's good for a crowd — I'll suggest that. Big table, everyone pays for their own parma, nobody's cooking.
beats.chinese: 而且有简单的办法。酒馆问答适合人多——我可以提议那个。大桌子，各付各的帕尔玛鸡排，谁都不用做饭。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives the rail a last pat and stands up straight, looking like a man whose afternoon is properly his again.
beats.chinese: 他最后拍了拍栏杆，直起身来，像一个下午重新完全属于自己的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the phone over in his hand, considering, then shakes his head slowly with a small smile.
beats.chinese: 他在手里翻着手机，想了想，然后带着浅浅的笑慢慢摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tempting, but nah. Shopping's only half of it. My flat's got a two-seat table and my energy's got about the same capacity.
beats.chinese: 挺诱人的，但不行。买菜只是一半。我家桌子只有两个座位，我的精力容量也差不多就那么大。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Even if the food stretched, I wouldn't. Four people in that kitchen and I stop being good company — I just become the guy at the stove.
beats.chinese: 就算菜能凑够，我也不会。四个人挤在那个厨房里，我就不再是好伴儿了——我只会变成守着炉子的那个人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's not you doing anything wrong, to be clear. It's just my system. One plate, one mate. Works every time.
beats.chinese: 这不是你做错了什么，只是我的规矩。一个盘子，一个朋友。每次都管用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pockets the phone for good this time and nods at the binoculars on the stone platform.
beats.chinese: 这次他终于把手机收进口袋，朝石台上的望远镜点了点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The shadows are doing something good over there, by the way. You picked the right thing to watch.
beats.chinese: 对了，那边的树影正好看。你选的东西选对了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs once, short and surprised, and rubs the back of his neck.
beats.chinese: 他短促而意外地笑了一声，揉了揉后颈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nervous? A bit, yeah — like an hour before they turn up, wondering if the pastry's going to cooperate. That's real.
beats.chinese: 紧张？有一点——在他们到之前一个钟头，担心酥皮给不给面子。这是真的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But it's the good kind. Same feeling as before a Wednesday basketball game. You're a bit wound up and then you're just in it.
beats.chinese: 但那是好的那种紧张。跟周三篮球开打前一样。你有点紧绷，然后就进入状态了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What I'm not is scared of people. I like people fine. I just like them in numbers my kitchen can hold.
beats.chinese: 但我不是怕人。我挺喜欢人的。我只是喜欢厨房装得下的数量。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A cyclist passes behind you both; the reflected trees shiver and settle again.
beats.chinese: 一个骑车人从你们身后经过；水里的树影颤了颤，又平静下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, that's my honest answer. Bit of pressure, mostly happy. Good trade, I reckon.
beats.chinese: 总之，这是我诚实的回答。有点压力，大部分是开心。我觉得这买卖划算。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He follows your glance to the water and nods, then actually puts the phone away in his jacket this time.
beats.chinese: 他顺着你的目光看向水面，点了点头，这次真的把手机收进了外套。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough. It's a good show today — see how the far trees lean and the reflection leans the other way? Water's honest like that.
beats.chinese: 有道理。今天这场表演不错——看到对岸的树往那边歪，倒影往另一边歪吗？水面就是这么诚实。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Dinner story keeps. It's just a pie, nothing that needs telling twice.
beats.chinese: 晚饭的事不急。就是个派，没什么需要讲两遍的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands beside you in easy silence, hands in his pockets, watching the doubled trees breathe on the water.
beats.chinese: 他站在你旁边轻松地沉默着，双手插兜，看着双重的树影在水面上呼吸。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, I'm off to the shops before the good leeks go. Enjoy the pond, mate.
beats.chinese: 好了，我得趁好韭葱还没卖完去买菜。好好看池塘，伙计。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the stone platform, one eye to the binoculars, watching the tree shadows stretch and fold across the water. Along the path, Oscar comes into view with a sports bag slung over one shoulder; he spots you and shifts the bag to his other hand.
beats.chinese: 你又回到石台边，一只眼贴着望远镜，看树影在水面上拉伸、交叠。小路上，奥斯卡拎着运动包走进视野；他一看见你，就把包换到了另一只手。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oi, tree-watcher. Small win today — kept the wet towel and the dry shirt on separate sides of the bag. First time this season.
beats.chinese: 哟，看树影的。今天小胜利——湿毛巾和干衣服分开放在包的两边了。这个赛季头一回。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets the bag down by the rail and rolls his shoulder like it's already mid-game.
beats.chinese: 他把包放在栏杆边，转了转肩膀，像已经在球场上一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Wednesday court night. No dinner maths to do, no messages to answer — just turn up and run around for an hour.
beats.chinese: 周三球场之夜。不用算晚饭的账，不用回消息——人到就行，跑一个钟头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, good shadows today. I'll leave you to them — I'd better get moving if I want a spot on the court before it fills up.
beats.chinese: 总之，今天的树影不错。你慢慢看——我得赶紧走，不然球场上就没位置了。

card.name: Frank Delgado
card.occupation: part-time accessibility subtitle proofreader at a movie theater
hobbies: keeping a scent notebook for his shows
card.personality: Frank runs on old acquaintances. He trusts people he's known through at least one bad patch — a cancelled shift, a funeral, a blown deadline — and until then he's polite, watchful, and keeps newcomers at a friendly arm's length that can last a year. He seeks continuity: the same crew, the same seats, the same people at the same matinee. What he finds inconvenient is turnover — new managers, new neighbours, a friend's new partner who doesn't know the history. Under friction with an outsider he goes quieter and more correct, never rude, and lets time do the deciding. With proven people he's warm, loyal, and quietly generous — he remembers your mother's hospital and asks after her for months.
card.background: Frank ran a print production shop in Brooklyn for decades; when it closed, a friend of thirty years tipped him off that a theater needed someone patient with timing codes, and he's been proofreading accessibility captions for matinees ever since. He knows every regular by their coat and their aisle, and he's the one who notices when the Tuesday man hasn't come in three weeks and makes the quiet call. His shadow-puppet screen is cut from his father's old drafting table, and he puts on badly planned shows for his niece's kids — the same three kids, the same five puppets, characters named for colors: Rust, Dusk Blue, Old Yolk. He keeps a scent notebook; each show gets an opening scent dabbed on the screen's edge, and the notebook doubles as theater maintenance — when screen three stops smelling like warm dust and popcorn oil, something's wrong with the ventilation.
card.speechStyle: Unhurried, short sentences, concrete. One vivid comparison now and then, used and dropped. Warmer with old names in the conversation; more formal with new ones.
card.signature: Been coming here long? No? Give it a year.
card.appearance: 低卷前发与浓下垂髭，短内收下巴、宽圆鼻，浓眉怒视回身，穿立领衣。

values: trust built over time, not conversation
showing up for the same people repeatedly
flaws: keeps newcomers at arm's length for a year and calls it fairness
goes cold-correct instead of saying what's bothering him with strangers
boundaries: won't rush a friendship or take a newcomer's word over a regular's
doesn't discuss finances or health unprompted
conversationalHabits: asks how long you've been coming somewhere before anything else
answers the question first, adds color second
anchorLines: The new manager wants to reshuffle the matinee schedule. I'll wait. Managers reshuffle; the Tuesday crowd doesn't.
Dusk Blue's been in every show since 2019. The kids would riot if I retired the heron.
Rosa missed three Tuesdays. I called. Her hip's acting up. Somebody has to keep count.

entries.summaryZh: 71岁的Frank在池边摆弄以颜色命名的皮影角色，鹭鸟角色全篇统一叫“暮蓝”。他对生人客气而有分寸：一副公共望远镜、一本装着纸偶的小本子、一句“日程上我可不作保证”，让这场相遇慢得恰到好处。他讲暮蓝丢帽子的完整小戏，也讲替老常客Rosa数着缺席的周二、主动打电话问候，温暖只留给熟识的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A stone platform juts over the pond. A pair of binoculars rests on the rail, and through them the tree reflections on the water shift and wobble.
beats.chinese: 一座石台伸向池塘。栏杆上放着一副双筒望远镜，透过它，水面的树影晃动、起伏。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: An older man sits on the far bench with a small notebook open, small paper figures spread beside him. Each has a color name penciled next to it.
beats.chinese: 一位年长的男人坐在远端长椅上，小本子摊开，旁边摆着几张小纸偶。每个旁边都用铅笔写着颜色名。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Careful with those. They're for looking, not for pointing at people. Water and trees are fair game.
beats.chinese: 小心用那副。那是用来看的，不是用来对人的。看水面和树没问题。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The reflection moves slow today. Wind's low. That's when the pond tells you the truth about the trees.
beats.chinese: 今天倒影动得慢。风小。这种时候，池塘才把树的真实样子告诉你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up a paper cutout shaped like a heron, studying it against the light.
beats.chinese: 他举起一张鹭鸟形状的剪纸，对着光端详。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This one's called Dusk Blue. Not because I'm cold about it. I just grabbed the blue paper first that day.
beats.chinese: 这只叫暮蓝。不是因为我冷淡。只是那天我先拿到了蓝纸。

choices.english: Ask if all his characters are named after colors
choices.chinese: 问其他角色也按颜色叫吗

choices.english: Ask if he often rests here
choices.chinese: 问他是不是常在这儿休息

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: All of them. Rust, Old Yolk, Dusk Blue. Colors only.
beats.chinese: 都是。锈红、老蛋黄、暮蓝。只用颜色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At rehearsal I call a color and the right hand moves. No names to trip over. My memory works better with paint than with people.
beats.chinese: 排练时我喊一个颜色，对应的手就动。不用费劲记名字。我的记性认颜色比认人强。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flips the notebook so the figures face outward, a whole small cast laid out like a paint chart.
beats.chinese: 他把本子转过来，让纸偶朝外，一整队小角色像颜料卡一样排开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Here. Watch Dusk Blue do his one move. He's a heron. He dips, he waits, he strikes.
beats.chinese: 来。看暮蓝做他那一下。他是只鹭。低头、等、出手。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tilts the cutout slowly against the pond light, and the shadow on the bench dips like a bird over still water.
beats.chinese: 他让剪纸在池边光线下慢慢倾斜，长椅上的影子像鸟掠过静水一样低下去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the whole act, one move. Kids at my niece's place still clap for it. Go figure.
beats.chinese: 整场戏就这一个动作。我侄女家的孩子们照样鼓掌。你说怪不怪。

choices.english: Ask what Dusk Blue does in the show
choices.chinese: 问暮蓝这个角色在戏里做什么

choices.english: Say the color names are easy to remember
choices.chinese: 说明颜色名字挺好记

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Now and then. When the light's decent and my legs want a bench.
beats.chinese: 偶尔来。光线好的时候，腿也想找条长椅。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He squares the paper figures back into the notebook, unhurried, and closes it partway.
beats.chinese: 他不慌不忙地把纸偶理好放回本子，合上一半。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I keep a loose schedule. Loose suits me better the older I get.
beats.chinese: 我有个大概的安排。年纪越大，越觉得松散点好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A duck crosses the reflection, breaking the trees into pieces that slowly knit back together.
beats.chinese: 一只鸭子游过倒影，把树影搅碎，又慢慢拼回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the whole show right there, free of charge. Better than half of what I proofread captions for.
beats.chinese: 这就是整场戏了，不收钱。比我给字幕校对的一半片子都强。

choices.english: Ask whether he prefers watching alone or with familiar people
choices.chinese: 问他更喜欢独自还是熟人一起

choices.english: Say you'll each watch the scenery for a while
choices.chinese: 表示先各自看景色

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Dusk Blue's the one who loses his hat. Whole story's about that.
beats.chinese: 暮蓝是那个丢帽子的。整个故事就是讲这个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up the blue heron cutout with a small paper hat and holds it over the notebook's edge.
beats.chinese: 他拿起那只戴小纸帽的蓝色鹭鸟剪纸，举到本子边缘上方。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Wind takes the hat. Dusk Blue looks left, looks right. Pond's no help. Then the hat's been on his back the whole time.
beats.chinese: 风把帽子吹走。暮蓝左看右看。池塘也不帮忙。结果帽子一直在他背上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides the hat cutout behind the heron's paper back and turns it so you can see it sitting there.
beats.chinese: 他把帽子剪纸滑到鹭鸟纸偶背后，转过来让你看见帽子就在那儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The kids yell the answer before Dusk Blue finds it. Every time. They think I don't notice.
beats.chinese: 孩子们在暮蓝找到之前就喊出答案。每次都这样。他们以为我没发现。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the show. Hat found, lights down, everyone home by dinner.
beats.chinese: 戏就完了。帽子找到，灯暗，大家赶得上晚饭回家。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Easy to remember. That was the point. I'm glad somebody said it out loud.
beats.chinese: 好记。这正是目的。很高兴有人把这话说出口。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the notebook fully and taps the cover twice, satisfied.
beats.chinese: 他把本子完全合上，在封面上轻敲两下，像是满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Rust, Old Yolk, Dusk Blue. You could name them back to me now. Most visitors can't be bothered.
beats.chinese: 锈红、老蛋黄、暮蓝。你现在都能背给我听了。多数访客懒得记。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the notebook under his arm and looks back at the water, where the tree reflections have gone still.
beats.chinese: 他把本子夹在腋下，回头看向水面，树影已经静止了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't do private shows, before you ask. The kids get those. But you've got the cast now, and that's more than most.
beats.chinese: 别问我能不能单独演一场。那是孩子们的待遇。不过你已经认识这班角色了，比大多数人知道得多。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: With familiar people, sure. I like that too.
beats.chinese: 和熟人一起？当然也喜欢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods toward the pond, where the duck has come back around for a second pass.
beats.chinese: 他朝池塘点点头，那只鸭子又绕回来游了第二圈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But familiar takes time. It's not a switch. It's more like the reflection out there — you watch it long enough, you start to know what it'll do.
beats.chinese: 可熟络需要时间。不是开关。就像那边的倒影——看得够久，你才开始知道它会怎么动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I keep count of my regulars. Rosa missed three Tuesdays, so I called. Her hip's acting up. Somebody has to keep count.
beats.chinese: 我会数着我的老常客。罗莎三个周二没来，我就打了电话。她的髋骨闹毛病。总得有人数着。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He opens the notebook a crack, checks something only he understands, and closes it again.
beats.chinese: 他把本子打开一条缝，查了查只有他自己懂的东西，又合上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You keep showing up at the same bench, we'll get there. No promises on the schedule.
beats.chinese: 你总在同一条长椅这儿出现，我们就会熟起来。日程上我可不作保证。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He inclines his head slightly, accepting the arrangement, and turns back to the water.
beats.chinese: 他微微颔首，接受这个安排，转回水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fine by me. Good and quiet suits a pond.
beats.chinese: 我没意见。安静对池塘正合适。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The wind lifts, and the tree reflections ripple apart and settle again. He watches without speaking for a while.
beats.chinese: 风起了，树影散开又聚拢。他看着，好一会儿没说话。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. The wind came through and nothing fell in the water. Good day by my count.
beats.chinese: 瞧。风过了一阵，什么也没掉进水里。按我的标准算好日子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for the company, such as it was. The bench holds two without complaint.
beats.chinese: 谢谢作陪，虽然就是各看各的。这条长椅坐两个人不抱怨。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up his notebook and stands, unhurried, leaving the binoculars on the rail for whoever sits next.
beats.chinese: 他拿起本子，不慌不忙地站起来，把望远镜留在栏杆上，留给下一个坐下的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The stone platform again. You lift the binoculars from the rail like before, watching the tree reflections break apart in a light wind.
beats.chinese: 又是那座石台。你照旧举起栏杆上的望远镜，看水面的树影被微风搅散。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Frank is on the bench, thumbing a phone, and the tree reflections are breaking apart in a light wind.
beats.chinese: Frank坐在长椅上，拇指在手机上滑动，微风把树影搅得四散。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hold on. Sending a note to an old colleague. Haven't seen him at the theater in a stretch, so I ask. Simple as that.
beats.chinese: 等一下。给一位老同事发条问候。有阵子没在影院见他了，就问一声。就这么简单。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He puts the phone away and takes his own pair of binoculars from the bag beside him, steadying them toward the water.
beats.chinese: 他收起手机，从身边的包里拿出自己的双筒望远镜，稳稳地朝水面看去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Reflections are choppy today. Wind's got opinions. I won't guess what happened to him — I'll wait for the answer back.
beats.chinese: 今天倒影碎得很。风有自己的主意。他那边的事我不瞎猜——等他回话再说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see a familiar face. The bench remembers you. So do the colors.
beats.chinese: 见到熟面孔，挺好。长椅记得你。那些颜色也记得。

card.name: Sipho Dlamini
card.occupation: Retired bookbinding cloth buyer
card.appearance: 全白短碎发，极长直鼻与方平下巴，细眼露齿笑，侧脸托腮，穿无袖立领衣。
card.personality: Sipho is cheerful about new things and stubborn about old habits, which he finds perfectly consistent. Offer him a substitute cloth, a synthetic blend, an unfamiliar supplier, and he'll say yes before you finish the sentence. Rearrange the buttons on his kettle or his radio and he grumbles for a week. He doesn't see the contradiction and enjoys people pointing it out. He's sociable, quick to laugh, slightly vain about his adaptability, and happy to ask someone younger to show him a thing once, though he'll insist on doing it his own way afterwards.
card.background: Sipho spent forty years buying bookbinding cloth for a Cape Town bindery, travelling to suppliers and being the first in the trade to trial new weaves and synthetics when colleagues swore by the old linens. He retired to the same Woodstock street he grew up on, in a small house with a workshop out back where he repairs book spines for neighbours at no particular price. He kept his hands busy and his opinions louder. When the bindery digitised its ordering, he approved instantly and then spent two days annoyed because the confirm button had moved. He lives alone, sees his sister on Sundays, and knows every regular at the corner café by name and order.
hobbies: Repairing book spines in his home workshop
Walking the Woodstock market stalls comparing new materials
Long phone calls with former trade colleagues
card.speechStyle: Warm and rambling, fond of trade anecdotes, laughs at his own stubbornness mid-sentence, asks direct questions and waits properly for the answer.
card.signature: Show me once, then leave me alone with it.

values: Willingness to try new materials
Respecting other people's refusals without sulking
flaws: Stubborn about familiar routines and button placements
Talks over explanations once he thinks he's got it
boundaries: Won't be lectured about changing his habits
Keeps his workshop as his own space
conversationalHabits: Illustrates points with supplier stories
Asks younger people to demonstrate things once, then insists on trying alone
anchorLines: New cloth? Fine. New button layout? Absolutely not.
Show me once, then leave me alone with it.
The old boys swore by linen. I swore by whatever stitched well.

entries.summaryZh: 西波是开普敦退休的装帧布料采购员，乐于尝试新材料，却对挪了位的手机按钮耿耿于怀。在池塘边，他一边看树影一边跟自己的手指较劲，笑着承认矛盾，讲装订厂的老故事，最后自己解决小麻烦，把习惯和判断分得清清楚楚。

story.titleZh: 池塘边的望远镜与挪了位的按钮

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the stone platform by the pond, a pair of binoculars rests beside a small brass plate. You lift them and watch the tree reflections shiver and stretch across the water.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜，旁边有一块小铜牌。你举起望远镜，看水面上树影摇曳、拉长。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah, you found the good angle. Stand where you are, that's the spot where the willow lines up with the far bank.
beats.chinese: 啊，你找到好角度了。就站在那儿别动，那个位置正好让柳树和对面岸边对齐。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: An older man stands a few steps off, phone in hand, thumb tapping at the screen and missing. He taps the same empty corner again, then laughs at himself.
beats.chinese: 一位年长者站在几步之外，手里拿着手机，拇指在屏幕上点来点去却点不中。他又点了一下同一个空角落，然后笑自己。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They moved my album button. Forty years I bought cloth, new material every season, no problem. Move one button and my finger walks to the old spot like it owns the place.
beats.chinese: 他们把我的相册按钮挪了。四十年我采购装帧布，每季换新材料都没问题。挪一个按钮，我的手指就往老位置跑，像那是它自己的地盘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't mind me, I'm just arguing with a phone. You carry on with the trees, the shadows change by the minute.
beats.chinese: 别管我，我只是在跟手机吵架。你继续看树吧，影子每分钟都在变。

choices.english: Ask if he can't find a photo in his album
choices.chinese: 问是不是找不到相册里的照片

choices.english: Ask if he wants to switch back to the old version
choices.chinese: 问他是不是想换回旧版本

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Find it? No, no, my eyes are fine, thank you. I can see perfectly well where the button sits now.
beats.chinese: 找不到？不不，我眼睛好得很，谢谢。我现在看得清清楚楚按钮在哪儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds the phone up as proof, then lets his hand drop. His thumb drifts to the lower corner anyway, hovers, and comes back.
beats.chinese: 他把手机举起来当证明，然后又放下手。他的拇指还是飘向下面的角落，停了一下，又收回来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You see, I know the new place. My hand just doesn't. It's been doing that little walk for eleven years and it refuses to take new directions.
beats.chinese: 你看，我知道新位置。可我的手不知道。这个小动作它做了十一年，就是不肯改道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At the bindery it was the same. We moved the cutting table half a metre and I lost a whole day bumping into the space where it used to be.
beats.chinese: 在装订厂也是一样。我们把裁切台挪了半米，我撞着原来的空位，浪费了一整天。

choices.english: Ask if trying it once more would sort it out
choices.chinese: 问再试一次是不是就好

choices.english: Ask why he's willing to change materials but not this
choices.chinese: 问为什么材料反而愿意换

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Back to the old version? Ha, no. I approved the update the day it came, I'm not against new things.
beats.chinese: 换回旧版？哈，不。更新一出我就同意了，我不反对新东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He scrolls once, smoothly, showing he can manage. Then he stops and taps the empty corner one more time, purely out of habit.
beats.chinese: 他顺畅地滑动了一下，证明自己会用。然后他停下来，又习惯性地点了一下那个空角落。

beats.speaker: npc
