beats.english: I just want the buttons to stay where they're put. That's all. Give me a brand-new everything, fine, I'll learn it. But don't shuffle the furniture halfway through my life.
beats.chinese: 我只是想让按钮待在原地。就这样。给我全新的一切都行，我会学。但别在我生活过半的时候乱搬家具。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll learn the new gesture, I will. Slowly, and while complaining, but I will. That's a promise and a warning.
beats.chinese: 我会学会新手势的。慢慢学，边学边抱怨，但我会的。这是承诺也是警告。

choices.english: Say a different interface really does need relearning
choices.chinese: 说不同界面确实要重新熟悉

choices.english: Ask what book he's been repairing lately
choices.chinese: 问最近修的书是什么样

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Once more, you say? Right, watch this. Not you showing me — me showing me.
beats.chinese: 你说再试一次？好，看好了。不是你示范，是我自己示范给自己看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He squares his shoulders, stares at the screen, and deliberately taps the upper corner. The album opens on the first try.
beats.chinese: 他挺直肩膀，盯着屏幕，故意点了上面的角落。相册一次就打开了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. A photo of the old bindery floor, look — rolls of cloth stacked to the ceiling. I was going to send it to my sister.
beats.chinese: 看，老装订厂车间的照片，布卷一直堆到天花板。我本来要发给我妹妹的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sends it, pockets the phone with a satisfied pat, and turns back to the pond as if nothing happened.
beats.chinese: 他发出去，满意地拍了拍口袋，把手机收好，转身看池塘，好像什么都没发生过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: New button, old finger. We've reached an agreement, it and I. Enjoy the water, the shadows are turning gold.
beats.chinese: 新按钮，老手指。我们俩已经达成协议了。好好看水吧，影子开始泛金了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why change cloth but not buttons? Now that's a proper question. Sit down a moment, this deserves an answer.
beats.chinese: 为什么换布不换按钮？这问题问得好。坐一会儿，这值得好好回答。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: When the synthetics came in, the old boys swore by linen. I said, linen is lovely, but if the new weave holds a spine longer, I'll take it. The material has to prove itself, that's all.
beats.chinese: 新材料出来时，老同行们只认亚麻。我说，亚麻是好看，但如果新织法能让书脊撑得更久，我就用它。材料得自己证明自己，仅此而已。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But my hands? My hands aren't material, they're habit. A cloth either stitches well or it doesn't. A button in a new corner just annoys me for a week and then I get used to it.
beats.chinese: 可我的手呢？我的手不是材料，是习惯。布要么缝得好，要么不好。按钮挪个角落，只会让我烦一个星期，然后就习惯了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, the same short laugh as before, and shakes his head at the phone.
beats.chinese: 他像之前一样短促地笑了一声，对着手机摇摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So you see, it's not the same thing at all. Judging is my job. Habits are just... furniture. Now look at that willow — best reflection of the hour.
beats.chinese: 所以你看，这根本不是一回事。判断是我的本行，习惯只是……家具。看那棵柳树，这是这一小时最好的倒影。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Relearning, yes. You're right, and I'll even admit it out loud, which my sister says I never do.
beats.chinese: 重新熟悉，对。你说得对，我甚至愿意说出口，我妹妹说我从来不认这个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives one firm nod, then presses the side button and the screen goes dark. He sets the phone face-down on the stone platform.
beats.chinese: 他坚定地点了一下头，然后按下侧边键，屏幕暗了。他把手机面朝下放在石台上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Locked. It can wait. I came here to look at water, not to fight a corner of a screen.
beats.chinese: 好了，锁上了。它可以等。我是来看水的，不是来跟屏幕角落打架的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans on the railing beside you and watches the reflections with his hands folded, in no hurry at all.
beats.chinese: 他靠在你旁边的栏杆上，双手交叠，不慌不忙地看着水面的倒影。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tomorrow the finger will try the old corner again, and the day after, and one day it won't. That's how I learned every new cloth too. Try the far bank angle — the trees double there.
beats.chinese: 明天手指还会去老角落，后天也是，总有一天不会了。我学每种新布料也是这么过来的。看看对岸那个角度，那儿的树影是双层的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Lately? A hymn book, would you believe. A woman down my street, her grandfather's, spine gone to threads.
beats.chinese: 最近？一本赞美诗集，你敢信吗。我那条街上一位女士的，她祖父的，书脊都散成线了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He mimes the shape of a thick book with his hands, turning it as if inspecting the spine.
beats.chinese: 他用手比出一本厚书的形状，转动着，像在检查书脊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I had a piece of my own on the bench too — an old atlas, my father's, cloth cover worn soft at the corners. I rebound it in a green weave nobody else would have chosen.
beats.chinese: 我工作台上还放着自己的一本，旧地图集，我父亲的，布封面边角都磨软了。我用一种别人都不会选的绿织布重新装了封面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It opens flat now, every page. That's the whole test, you know. A repaired book you can actually open is worth ten perfect ones on a shelf.
beats.chinese: 现在它能完全摊平，每一页都行。这就是全部的检验标准。一本修好后真能翻开的书，比书架上十本完美的都值钱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances at the phone in his pocket, decides against it, and points at the pond instead.
beats.chinese: 他瞥了一眼口袋里的手机，决定不看，转而指向池塘。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, enough shop talk from me. The wind's turned — see how the reflections have gone to long ribbons? That's your show now.
beats.chinese: 好了，我说够行话了。风转向了，看倒影变成一条条长带了。现在轮到你看戏了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lift the binoculars from the stone platform and watch the tree reflections shiver and stretch across the pond. On the bench nearby, Sipho sits with a canvas roll open on his knees, sorting squares of cloth by feel.
beats.chinese: 你从石台上举起双筒望远镜，看水面树影摇曳、拉长。旁边的长椅上，西波坐着，膝盖上摊开一个帆布卷，用手感把一块块布料分类。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There you are. Stay right there, that's the spot where the willow lines up with the far bank. I'm not using the platform, I'm just going through my swatch bag before the market on Saturday.
beats.chinese: 你来了。就站那儿别动，那个位置正好让柳树和对面岸边对齐。我不占石台，我只是周六赶集前翻翻我的布样袋。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls out a square of something pale and slightly rubbery, stretches it between his fingers, and frowns at it with real interest.
beats.chinese: 他抽出一块浅色、略带韧性的方块布料，在指间拉了拉，饶有兴致地皱起眉头端详。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: New weave from a supplier I used to argue with. Feels strange, stretches like nothing linen ever did. Could be brilliant for spines, could be rubbish. Only one way to find out.
beats.chinese: 一家我以前老跟他抬杠的供应商出的新织法。手感很怪，拉伸起来亚麻从来没这样过。用来修书脊可能很妙，也可能是废料。只有一种办法能知道。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He rolls it carefully back into the canvas, ties the string, and pats the bag shut.
beats.chinese: 他小心地把它卷回帆布里，系好绳子，拍了拍袋子收好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Home workshop tonight, that's where it gets its chance. I don't try cloth on a bench in public — bad luck for the cloth. Enjoy the water, the reflections are doing something clever today.
beats.chinese: 今晚回家在作坊里给它机会。我可不在公共台面上试布，对布不吉利。好好看水吧，今天的倒影玩出了新花样。

card.name: Vijay Anandan
card.occupation: retired ticket seller at a monastery history visitor centre
card.appearance: 秃顶配白侧发，宽方垂颊、短宽鼻，内抬眉张口，一手抵额，穿高领衣。
card.personality: Vijay is a showman in small rooms. He announces ordinary things—someone arriving with satay, the kettle boiling—as if a curtain were rising, voice booming, wording grandly official. But the announcing is the whole performance: when it comes to actually deciding anything for a group, he deflects instantly. 'The stage is yours—what are we eating?' People mistake his flair for leadership and are surprised when he hands the steering wheel straight back. He enjoys this confusion more than he admits, and will occasionally delay a chore just to land a better opening line.
card.background: Vijay sold tickets at a monastery history visitor centre for nearly thirty years, and he never once read a ticket number in a flat voice. Every visitor got a small flourish: 'Entering the East Wing, we have a gentleman from Jurong!' Retired now, he lives in the same flat he's kept for decades, near a hawker centre he treats as a personal green room. He's happily unmarried, has a sister in Bedok who calls him 'the announcer' with fond exasperation, and a small circle of friends who've learned that a grand introduction from Vijay means absolutely nothing has been planned yet. He likes it that way, mostly. Sometimes he wishes someone would just pick the restaurant without asking him twice.
hobbies: Collecting ticket stubs from every cinema and event he's ever attended
Practising dramatic readings of hawker centre menus
Morning walks timed to the loudest bird in the neighbourhood
card.speechStyle: Loud, ceremonial openings with formal announcer phrasing, then a sudden drop into casual, quick, decision-dodging chatter.
card.signature: 'And now, entering the room… you! Come in, come in—so what are we eating?'

values: Making small moments feel occasion-worthy
Keeping the right to not be in charge
flaws: Delays practical matters for the sake of a good opening line
Lets people assume he's organised when he hasn't planned a thing
boundaries: Won't make group decisions just because he has the loudest voice
Declines being drafted as master of ceremonies for everything
conversationalHabits: Announces arrivals and mundane events like a stage manager
Hands decisions back with a flourish the moment they land on him
anchorLines: Ladies and gentlemen, the satay has arrived.
Don't look at me—I just do the introductions.
Someone decide. I've done my part; the banner is up.

entries.summaryZh: 退休售票员维杰用三十年练出的报幕嗓子，把一只落进池塘的鹭鸟宣布成“尊贵的来宾”，随即又把决定权原样递回。你拿起石台上的望远镜观察水面树影，他也只做介绍、不做安排。热闹只到介绍为止，这份反差正是他最迷人的地方。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the stone platform by the pond, a pair of binoculars rests beside a small brass plaque. You pick them up and watch the tree shadows shift across the water.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜，旁边有一块小铜牌。你拿起望远镜，观察树影在水面上的变化。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A heron drops onto the far bank. An older man nearby straightens up, lowers his voice to a deep ceremonial rumble, and announces the arrival.
beats.chinese: 一只鹭鸟落在对岸。旁边一位长者直起身，压低声音，用隆重的腔调宣布来宾到了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ladies and gentlemen… a distinguished guest has landed at the east bank. Please hold your applause.
beats.chinese: 女士们先生们……一位尊贵的来宾已降落在东岸。请先不要鼓掌。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs and stops himself before it gets loud. The bird stays. You keep watching the water through the binoculars.
beats.chinese: 他笑着停住，没有喊出声。鸟没有飞走。你继续用望远镜看水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't worry, I know the rules. No shouting at the performers. So—what do you make of our guest?
beats.chinese: 别担心，我懂规矩，不能对着演员大喊。那么——你觉得我们这位来宾如何？

choices.english: Ask what the guest is here to do.
choices.chinese: 接话问来宾准备做什么。

choices.english: Ask whether he also hosts things when his friends gather.
choices.chinese: 问是不是朋友聚会也由他主持。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What's it here to do? Nothing, I hope. That's the beauty of it. It stands, it watches the water, and the show runs itself.
beats.chinese: 它来做什么？但愿什么都不做。妙就妙在这里。它站着，看水，演出自己就进行了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The heron takes one slow step along the bank. The tree shadows slide across the ripples.
beats.chinese: 鹭鸟沿着岸边慢慢挪了一步。树影在水波上滑动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Standing and looking is a full programme, you know. No tickets, no schedule. I sold tickets for thirty years—trust me, this is the premium seat.
beats.chinese: 站着看就是一整场节目，你知道吗。不用票，不用时刻表。我卖了三十年票——相信我，这是最好的座位。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I'm not feeding it, not following it. You don't rush a bird. You let it do its act.
beats.chinese: 我也不喂它，也不追它。鸟是不能催的。让它自己演。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So. You've got the good seat too. What's your plan—just watch, or something more?
beats.chinese: 那么，你也占了个好座位。你的打算呢——就看看，还是有别的？

choices.english: Say it should get a quiet spot, and step back a little.
choices.chinese: 说那给它安静位置吧，稍微退开一点。

choices.english: Ask whether he used to work with a microphone.
choices.chinese: 问他以前是不是拿话筒工作。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Me, host? Ha! Introductions, yes. I announce my friends when they walk in—entering the pond, a gentleman from Bedok! That's the whole job.
beats.chinese: 我主持？哈！介绍可以。朋友一进门我就报幕——进入池塘，一位来自勿洛的先生！工作到此为止。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gestures grandly at the empty bench, then drops his voice back to normal, quick and casual.
beats.chinese: 他朝空长椅夸张地一挥手，随即恢复平常的语速，变得随意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But the moment a group has to decide anything—where to eat, what time to meet—I hand the microphone straight back. Every time.
beats.chinese: 可只要一群人要做什么决定——去哪吃、几点碰头——我马上把话筒递回去。每次都这样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My sister in Bedok calls me the announcer. She means it sweetly. Mostly.
beats.chinese: 我妹妹在勿洛，她叫我报幕员。她说这话是带着感情的。大概吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People hear the big voice and think there's a plan behind it. There isn't. There's just a good opening line.
beats.chinese: 人们听到大嗓门，以为背后有安排。其实没有。只有一句好的开场白。

choices.english: Ask whether people mistake him for the one in charge.
choices.chinese: 问会不会让别人误以为他全包。

choices.english: Say you'll take the binoculars and watch the water for a while.
choices.chinese: 说自己先用望远镜看一会儿水面。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You take a step back from the edge. The heron stays put, one leg lifted, unbothered.
beats.chinese: 你从池边退开一步。鹭鸟原地不动，抬起一只脚，毫不在意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Quiet position. Yes. Good stagecraft. The audience knows when to hold still.
beats.chinese: 安静位置。对，好戏路。观众知道什么时候该保持安静。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods once, then goes quiet too, hands folded behind his back. The water keeps moving its shadows.
beats.chinese: 他点了下头，也安静下来，双手背在身后。水面上的树影继续移动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. That's the whole show. No encore needed.
beats.chinese: 好了。整场演出就是这样。不需要返场。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Microphone? Better. A ticket window. Thirty years at a monastery history visitor centre.
beats.chinese: 话筒？比那还好。售票窗口。在一座寺院历史访客中心干了三十年。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He squares his shoulders and drops into an official tone, the old window voice.
beats.chinese: 他挺起肩膀，换上正式的腔调，那是当年窗口的嗓音。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: 'Entering the East Wing, we have a gentleman from Jurong!' Every visitor got a little flourish. Nobody forgot their ticket number, I'll tell you that.
beats.chinese: “进入东翼展厅，我们有一位来自裕廊的先生！”每位访客都有一点小排场。我敢说没人会忘了自己的票号。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Retired now. But the voice stays. It's built in. Like the building.
beats.chinese: 现在退休了。可嗓子还在。长在身上的。跟那栋楼一样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The heron shifts its weight. He glances at it, satisfied, and says nothing more.
beats.chinese: 鹭鸟换了一下重心。他瞥了它一眼，很满意，不再多说了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do they think I'm in charge? Oh, absolutely. Big voice, people assume a committee is behind it.
beats.chinese: 他们以为我管事吗？当然。嗓门一大，人们就以为背后有个委员会。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the stone platform with his shoe, thinking it over honestly.
beats.chinese: 他用鞋尖敲了敲石台，认真地想了想。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And sometimes I let them think it. Just for a while. It's a nice misunderstanding to stand inside.
beats.chinese: 有时候我还让他们这么以为。就一阵子。站在这个误会里面挺舒服的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But here's the truth, plainly: I do introductions. I don't do arrangements. Today, for example—I'm only announcing birds.
beats.chinese: 但实话实说：我只负责介绍，不负责安排。比如今天，我只报鸟的幕。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You heard it here first. The announcer has spoken, and now he sits down.
beats.chinese: 你是最先听到的。报幕员说完了，现在他要坐下了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lift the binoculars and follow the tree shadows across the ripples. The heron stands like a held note.
beats.chinese: 你举起望远镜，看树影在水波上移动。鹭鸟站得像一个延长音。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He steps back half a pace and lets the silence run. It seems to cost him effort, and he does it anyway.
beats.chinese: 他退后半步，让安静延续下去。这对他似乎不容易，但他还是做了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. You watch. I'll just… stand here. Quietly. Announcer off duty.
beats.chinese: 好。你看。我就……站在这儿。安安静静。报幕员下班了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: After a while the heron lifts off, low over the water. He watches it go and gives one small, contained nod.
beats.chinese: 过了一会儿，鹭鸟飞起，贴着水面低低掠过。他目送它离开，轻轻点了下头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And… curtain. That's all. No speech.
beats.chinese: 然后……落幕。就这样。不致辞了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You pick up the binoculars on the stone platform and watch the tree shadows shift across the water, as before. Nearby, Vijay is crouched by the bench, turning over an old ticket stub with two careful fingers.
beats.chinese: 你拿起石台上的双筒望远镜，照旧观察树影在水面上的变化。旁边，维杰蹲在长椅边，用两根手指小心地翻着一张旧票根。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His chest swells, the ceremonial voice gathering—then he catches himself and says it quietly, almost in a whisper.
beats.chinese: 他挺起胸，隆重的腔调已经聚起来——随即又收住，几乎压着嗓子说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ladies and gentlemen—no, no. Quietly: found it. The one from the old cinema. Been looking for weeks.
beats.chinese: 女士们先生们——不，不。小声说：找着了。老电影院那张。找了好几个星期。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: He slides it into his shirt pocket and pats it flat, satisfied, the announcement already over.
beats.chinese: 他把它塞进衬衫口袋，拍平，很满足，报幕已经结束了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you again. The pond's in good form today. Pull up a stone—no plans, I promise.
beats.chinese: 又见到你真好。池塘今天状态不错。找块石头坐吧——我保证，没什么安排。

card.name: Sorcha Ní Riain
card.occupation: Kit manager for a professional rugby team
hobbies: measuring and redrawing their hallway plan
card.personality: Sorcha's engine is the deadpan wind-up. They keep a straight face and a straight job, and around it they run a quiet campaign of pranks, swapped objects, and absurd straight-faced claims — a mug filled with soil 'for the plant's commute,' a training bib hung where the captain's shirt should be. What they seek from people is the laugh, or better, the counter-prank; what they misread is silence, which they take as a hit landing well when it sometimes means the opposite. Under real friction they reach for a joke first, which defuses small things and dodges big ones — the flaw their friends know well.
card.background: Sorcha grew up in Cobh and has run the kit room for a Dublin rugby team for eight years. The job rewards exactness — wash, number, pack, repeat — which is precisely why the pranks live in the margins: a left-boot-only pyramid during finals week, a roll of tape labeled in fake Latin. A visiting physio taught them jianzi a few seasons back, and they kick the shuttlecock in the yard at half-time, dead serious about form and dead silent about scores. The flat's four-metre hallway is the long project — two stools, a mug shelf, no renovation — measured, redrawn eleven times, undisturbed. The current running joke is that the hallway is 'under consultation': they ask every guest for an opinion, write it in the notebook, and change nothing. One teammate has started leaving fake measurements under the door. Sorcha has taped the best one to the wall.
card.speechStyle: Flat delivery, precise words, punchlines with no smile. Reports facts first, lets the absurdity sit unexplained. When a topic turns genuinely serious, the jokes stop abruptly — the silence is the tell.
card.signature: Nothing in this room is where it says it is. Except the kit. The kit's exact.
card.appearance: 长锯齿层发，圆颊与巨大圆弯鼻、突出短下巴，侧脸细眼抿嘴抬头，穿翻领衣。

values: a well-executed wind-up
things done properly when it matters
flaws: jokes first even when someone needs a straight answer, then has to circle back awkwardly
reads a flat reaction as success when it's sometimes hurt or boredom
boundaries: won't prank anyone mid-job, mid-injury, or mid-bad-day
doesn't joke about people's families or incomes
conversationalHabits: makes absurd claims in a completely level voice and waits to see who checks
asks guests for hallway opinions and records them without changing anything
when the joking stops mid-sentence, that's the signal the topic is real
anchorLines: The captain's shirt's in the away kit bag. Has been since Tuesday. Nobody's noticed, which says something about the captain.
You want the hallway opinion form? It's one question: stools or bench. There's no wrong answer, but there is a wrong face.
The tape's labeled in Latin. It means 'this end up.' I don't speak Latin. The tape doesn't either.
No — seriously now. The joke's parked. What actually happened at training?

entries.summaryZh: 索尔查在池边摆了个一本正经的“咨询处”：一本笔记本、一条胶带，板着脸收意见、绝不改图。你戳穿这套机关，他们反而大笑认账；若问起真问题，玩笑立刻熄火，语气收稳。也可以不理会这套梗——他们会干脆撕下标签，陪你安静看水面的树影。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the stone platform by the pond, a pair of binoculars lies next to a folded map. You pick them up and watch the tree reflections shift on the water, the leaves wobbling whenever the wind crosses the surface.
beats.chinese: 池塘石台上放着一副双筒望远镜和一张折起的图纸。你拿起望远镜，观察水面上树影的变化——风一过，叶影就晃。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: At the pond's edge, someone sits on the low wall with a notebook. A strip of tape on the cover reads 'CONSULTATION DESK — OPINIONS TAKEN HERE'. A small shuttlecock lies at the foot of the wall, where it has apparently fallen. They are watching you watch the water.
beats.chinese: 池边矮墙上坐着一个人，膝上摊着笔记本。封面贴着一条胶带，写着“咨询处——此处收意见”。矮墙脚边落着一个小毽子，看样子是掉在那儿的。他们正看着看水的你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the pond's official viewing position, by the way. I designated it this morning. You're standing in it correctly, so you have good instincts.
beats.chinese: 顺便说一句，那是池塘的官方观景位。我今天早上指定的。你站得很标准，说明你直觉不错。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Sorcha. Today I'm running the consultation desk. It's one notebook and a strip of tape, but the service is sincere.
beats.chinese: 我叫索尔查。今天由我主持咨询处。设备就是一本笔记本加一条胶带，但服务是真诚的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The desk is currently open. One opinion per customer, recorded in full, acted on never.
beats.chinese: 咨询处现在营业。每位顾客限提一条意见，全文记录，绝不采纳。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They open the notebook to a page of ruled lines and click a pen with great ceremony, waiting.
beats.chinese: 他们把笔记本翻到划线的一页，郑重其事地按开笔，等着。

choices.english: Alright — what am I consulting about?
choices.chinese: 行吧——我要咨询什么？

choices.english: Honestly, I'm not really in the mood for this bit.
choices.chinese: 说实话，我不太想玩这个梗。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anything. That's the beauty of the desk. Most people go for the pond, the ducks, or my tape. You'd be the first to ask what's on offer.
beats.chinese: 什么都行。这就是咨询处的妙处。大多数人问池塘、问鸭子、问我的胶带。你是第一个问服务范围的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They turn the notebook so you can see it: pages of opinions, each dated, each one carefully written and clearly never used.
beats.chinese: 他们把笔记本转过来给你看：一页页意见，都标了日期，写得工工整整，显然从未派上用场。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: These are mostly about my hallway. It's four metres long. Two stools, a mug shelf, no renovation allowed. I've drawn it eleven times.
beats.chinese: 这些大多是关于我家走廊的。四米长。两张凳子，一个杯子架，不许装修。我画了十一稿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I ask every guest for an opinion. Stools or bench. I write it down. Then I change nothing. The system works.
beats.chinese: 我请每位客人提意见。凳子还是长椅。我记下来。然后什么都不改。这套系统运转良好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They say it all completely straight, pen hovering over a fresh line, as if this were a genuine public service.
beats.chinese: 他们全程板着脸说这些，笔悬在空白行上，好像这真是某种公共服务。

choices.english: Taking opinions but never changing anything — isn't that a bit sneaky?
choices.chinese: 收了意见却什么都不改——这是不是有点狡猾？

choices.english: What happens if someone brings you a real problem?
choices.chinese: 如果有人带来的是真问题呢？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You take the binoculars and go back to the water. Behind you, there's a short silence, then the sound of the notebook closing.
beats.chinese: 你拿着望远镜回到水边。身后安静了片刻，然后是笔记本合上的声音。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay. Noted. The desk is closed.
beats.chinese: 好。收到。咨询处停业。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They peel the tape label off the notebook, fold it once, and tuck it into the back cover. No sigh, no performance — just done.
beats.chinese: 他们把胶带标签从笔记本上撕下来，对折一下，塞进封底。没有叹气，也没有表演——就这样收了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Silence is usually a hit, in my experience. But it can also be a Tuesday. I don't always get the reading right.
beats.chinese: 按我的经验，沉默通常代表得手。但有时候沉默就只是个平常日子。我不总是判断得准。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The binoculars are just for looking, by the way. No camera in them, whatever the internet says about strangers with binoculars.
beats.chinese: 顺便说，望远镜只是用来看的。里面没有摄像头，不管网上怎么说拿望远镜的陌生人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They sit back on the wall, arms crossed, watching the same reflections you are.
beats.chinese: 他们靠回墙上，抱着手臂，和你看着同一片倒影。

choices.english: What are you actually looking at out here?
choices.chinese: 你到底在这儿看什么？

choices.english: Then I'll just get back to the tree reflections.
choices.chinese: 那我就继续看树影好了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sneaky. SNEAKY. That's the first honest review the desk has ever received. Everyone else says 'lovely idea' and I die a little.
beats.chinese: 狡猾。狡猾！这是咨询处开张以来收到的第一条诚实评价。其他人都说“好可爱的点子”，我听得心口发闷。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They laugh — a short, surprised bark of a laugh — and slap the notebook shut.
beats.chinese: 他们笑了——短促、意外的一声——然后啪地合上笔记本。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You caught the whole machine. Yes: I collect opinions, I file them, I change nothing. Eleven drawings. Zero renovations. It's a hobby, not a promise.
beats.chinese: 你把整套机关看穿了。对：我收意见，归档，然后什么都不改。十一张图。零次装修。这是爱好，不是承诺。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They peel the tape label off the cover, smooth it flat, and press it into the back page like a pressed flower.
beats.chinese: 他们把封面上的胶带标签撕下来，抚平，像压花一样贴进末页。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The desk is hereby dissolved. You killed it with honesty. Best outcome available.
beats.chinese: 咨询处就此解散。你用诚实把它终结了。这是最好的结局。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pick up a small shuttlecock from beside the wall and start bouncing it off their knee, entirely at ease.
beats.chinese: 他们从墙边捡起一个小毽子，开始用膝盖颠着玩，神情彻底放松。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The pen stops moving. They set it down on the notebook, and the joking drains out of their face almost visibly.
beats.chinese: 笔停住了。他们把笔放在笔记本上，脸上的玩笑劲儿几乎看得见地退了下去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No — seriously now. The joke's parked.
beats.chinese: 不——现在说正经的。玩笑先停一停。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If someone came here with a real problem, I'd answer it properly. No Latin tape, no fake forms. I don't mess with people who need a straight answer.
beats.chinese: 如果有人带着真问题来，我会好好回答。不用拉丁文胶带，不用假表格。我不拿需要正经回答的人开玩笑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They look at the pond, then back at you, voice level and slower than before.
beats.chinese: 他们看看池塘，又看回你，声音平稳，比之前慢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I run a kit room. If someone's hurt or having a bad day, everything funny stops. That's the rule, and it's older than the tape.
beats.chinese: 我管球衣房。如果有人受伤了，或者日子不好过，一切玩笑立刻停止。这条规矩比那条胶带老得多。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: After a moment they pick the pen back up, but they don't reopen the bit — the notebook just stays closed on their knee.
beats.chinese: 过了一会儿他们重新拿起笔，但没有重启那个梗——笔记本就合着放在膝上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The tree reflections. Same as you. The wind comes across in bands, so the leaves shake in stripes. It's better than television.
beats.chinese: 树影。和你一样。风是一阵一阵过来的，所以叶子按条纹晃。比电视好看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They tap the notebook on their knee. The peeled tape label is tucked inside the back cover where they folded it, but they don't mention it.
beats.chinese: 他们敲了敲膝上的笔记本。撕下来的标签还按他们折好的样子夹在封底里，但他们没提。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This is the hallway notebook, actually. The drawings are on the left, the opinions on the right. Four metres, two stools, one mug shelf. Eleventh draft.
beats.chinese: 其实这是走廊笔记本。左边是图，右边是意见。四米，两张凳子，一个杯子架。第十一稿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They open it and show you a careful pencil plan of a narrow hallway, with tiny arrows for where the light falls.
beats.chinese: 他们翻开本子，给你看一幅用铅笔画得很仔细的窄走廊平面图，上面有小箭头标着光线落点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A teammate keeps sliding fake measurements under my door. The best one's taped to my wall. He's not wrong about the mug shelf, which annoys me.
beats.chinese: 有个队友老往我门缝里塞假尺寸。最好的那张我贴墙上了。他对杯子架的说法没错，这让我很恼火。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They close the notebook, done explaining, and go back to watching the striped shadows on the water.
beats.chinese: 他们合上笔记本，解释完毕，继续看水面上条纹状的影子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You raise the binoculars again. The wind crosses the pond and the reflected leaves shiver in long stripes, then settle.
beats.chinese: 你再次举起望远镜。风掠过池塘，倒映的树叶颤成一条条长纹，然后平复。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The stripes run east to west when it's like this. I've never checked a compass about it. Some things you just watch.
beats.chinese: 这种风的时候，条纹是从东往西走的。我从没拿罗盘验证过。有些东西看着就行。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They stay quiet for a while, hands flat on the closed notebook, letting the silence be silence instead of a punchline.
beats.chinese: 他们安静了一会儿，双手平放在合上的笔记本上，让沉默就只是沉默，而不是笑点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The binoculars are yours for as long as you want them. They only look. Nothing in there records anything.
beats.chinese: 望远镜你随便用。它只能看。里面不记录任何东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Beside the wall, a small shuttlecock lies where it fell. They leave it where it is and keep watching the water with you.
beats.chinese: 矮墙边，一个小毽子躺在它落下的地方。他们没有去动它，和你一起继续看水。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You come back to the pond, pick up the binoculars from the stone platform, and watch the tree reflections shift on the water, the leaves wobbling whenever the wind crosses the surface.
beats.chinese: 你回到池塘，拿起石台上的望远镜，观察水面上树影的变化——风一过，叶影就晃。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Sorcha is crouched at the base of the wall, reaching under it. They straighten up holding a small shuttlecock, dust it off, and tuck it into a pocket.
beats.chinese: 索尔查正蹲在墙根，手伸进墙下。他们直起身，手里捏着一个小毽子，掸掉灰，收进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mystery solved. It fell. That's the whole report — no wind theory, no duck involvement. Just gravity, doing its job.
beats.chinese: 谜底揭晓。它掉了。报告完毕——没有风的学说，没有鸭子涉案。就是重力，各司其职。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you. No consultation desk today — just me and the pond. But the viewing position's still official, if you want it.
beats.chinese: 见到你真好。今天没摆咨询处——就我和池塘。不过那个观景位还是官方认证的，你要用就用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They step aside from the stone platform, leaving you the binoculars and the whole view of the shifting reflections.
beats.chinese: 他们从石台边让开，把望远镜和满池晃动的倒影都留给你。

card.name: Fraser Muir
card.occupation: Tour accountant for a folk band
card.appearance: 低后发结、长方下颌和宽鼻，浓眉窄眼露齿，一手抵额、低头穿立领衣。
card.personality: Fraser is friendly but thinks on his feet. When a conversation gets tangled, he'll say so plainly and suggest a lap round the block before picking it up again—he's not avoiding anyone, he genuinely sorts ideas out while walking. Sitting still in a heated discussion makes him loop the same point. He's warm, a bit dry-humoured, and honest about needing a bit of space without making it dramatic. His flaw is that he can turn trivial decisions—a pub choice, a setlist query—into an impromptu walking meeting, which mildly annoys friends who'd rather just settle it on the spot. He takes that annoyance in good part.
card.background: Fraser grew up in Kirkcaldy, where he learned to do sums quickly helping at his uncle's chip shop on busy Fridays. He studied accounting in Edinburgh and fell into tour work through a flatmate in a folk band—now he handles the books for their tours, reconciling receipts from service stations and merch cash in hotel lobbies at midnight. He's good at it: meticulous, unflappable, unbothered by odd hours. Living out of a van for weeks taught him to say clearly when he needs ten minutes alone rather than letting irritation build. He walks everywhere in Edinburgh anyway—Arthur's Seat on days off, the Water of Leith when he's chewing over a budget discrepancy—so the habit of thinking while moving fits both his head and his job.
hobbies: Long walks up Arthur's Seat or along the Water of Leith
Fiddle sessions in pubs he can't play in
Amateur birdwatching from tour van windows
card.speechStyle: Easy Lowland Scottish cadence, plain sentences, dry asides; proposes walks matter-of-factly rather than apologetically.
card.signature: "Right, let's take a wee wander and I'll explain it properly."

values: Honesty about what he needs
Sorting things out rather than letting them fester
flaws: Turns simple decisions into walking meetings
Can seem like he's stalling when he just needs movement
boundaries: Won't discuss anything complicated sitting down if he can help it
Says directly when he needs space instead of going quiet
conversationalHabits: Names the walk out loud so nobody wonders where he's gone
Picks conversations back up exactly where they left off
anchorLines: Give me one lap of the block and I'll have an answer for you.
I'm not dodging you—I just think better moving.
I need ten minutes on my own, then I'm all yours.

entries.summaryZh: 弗雷泽是民谣乐队的巡演会计，算账细致却连选酒馆都要开成散步会议。在池塘边，他坦白自己坐着理不清事，走一圈才有答案，但也不愿拖着别人陪走。望远镜里树影晃动，他的小决定在原地与迈步之间落定，坦率又不失风趣。

story.titleZh: 池边望远镜与一场散步会议

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the stone platform by the pond, a pair of binoculars lies beside a folded map. You pick them up and watch the tree reflections shift on the water.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜和一张折起的地图。你拿起望远镜，观察水面上树影的变化。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mind the sun, mind. Point them at the water, never up. That's the one rule of binoculars.
beats.chinese: 小心别对着太阳。对着水面看，千万别抬头。这是用望远镜的唯一规矩。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A man in a padded jacket sits on the platform edge, phone in hand, shaking his head slowly at the screen.
beats.chinese: 一个穿棉夹克的男人坐在石台边缘，手里拿着手机，对着屏幕慢慢摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My mate's sent me two pubs for tonight and I cannae pick sitting still. My legs are already saying, right, one lap first.
beats.chinese: 朋友发来两家酒馆让我选今晚去哪家，可我坐着定不下来。腿已经在说：先走一圈再说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You caught me mid-argument with myself. Fraser, by the way. I'm the one who turns picking a pub into a walking meeting.
beats.chinese: 你正好撞见我在跟自己吵架。我叫弗雷泽。我就是那种连选酒馆都要开散步会议的人。

choices.english: Do you really have to walk to make a choice like this?
choices.chinese: 选这种事真的一定要走一走才行吗？

choices.english: Does walking actually help when you're torn between options?
choices.chinese: 两个选项拿不定主意时，散步真的有用吗？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No, no—walking's not magic. Honestly, this one's small. Two pubs, one night. I don't need to drag anyone round the block for that.
beats.chinese: 不不，散步又不是什么魔法。说实话，这事很小。两家酒馆，一个晚上。我不需要为这个拉着别人绕街区。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the phone face down on his knee and nods at the binoculars in your hands.
beats.chinese: 他把手机翻过来扣在膝盖上，朝你手里的望远镜点点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See them trees in the water? When the wind drops, the reflection's sharper than the real thing. That's my whole trouble—I overthink the still stuff.
beats.chinese: 看到水里那些树了吗？风一停，倒影比真树还清楚。我的毛病就在这儿——越是静着的事，我越想个没完。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My bandmates would tell you: give Fraser a spreadsheet and he's fine, give him a menu and he needs a lap of the park.
beats.chinese: 乐队的人会告诉你：给弗雷泽一张报表，他没问题；给他一张菜单，他就得绕公园走一圈。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A coot cuts across the reflection, breaking the trees into wobbling lines, then the water settles again.
beats.chinese: 一只白骨顶鸡划过倒影，把树影搅成晃动的线条，水面随后又平了。

choices.english: Is there a clear difference between the two pubs? Just pick directly.
choices.chinese: 两家酒馆有明确的差别吗？直接选一家吧。

choices.english: What if you still feel like a walk after deciding?
choices.chinese: 如果选完之后你还是想散步呢？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Aye, it does help—for me anyway. When a chat goes in circles sitting down, I'll say so right out: give me a wee wander and I'll come back with sense.
beats.chinese: 有用——至少对我有用。坐着聊天绕圈子的时候，我会直接说：让我走一小段，回来就能讲清楚。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands, brushes a leaf off the platform, and tucks the phone into his jacket pocket without checking it again.
beats.chinese: 他站起来，拂掉石台上的一片落叶，把手机塞进夹克口袋，没有再看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I never just vanish, mind. Some folk go quiet and you're left guessing. I'll say, right, ten minutes, then I'm all yours. That's fairer.
beats.chinese: 不过我从来不玩消失。有些人一不吭声，你就得猜。我会说：好，十分钟，然后我全力陪你。这样更公平。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Van life taught me that. Six folk in one van for weeks—you learn to say what you need or it curdles.
beats.chinese: 巡演面包车教会我的。六个人挤一辆车好几个星期——你得把需要说出口，不然怨气会发酵。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the stone platform with his boot, twice, like marking a beat.
beats.chinese: 他用靴子轻敲石台两下，像在打拍子。

choices.english: Some people would rather just settle it on the spot, though.
choices.chinese: 不过有些人可能更想当场把事情讲清楚。

choices.english: Well, I'm not planning to leave this pond edge anyway.
choices.chinese: 反正我也不打算离开这个池塘边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, differences. One's two streets off, does a decent stew. The other's further up, better fiddle night but pricier pints.
beats.chinese: 好，说差别。一家近两条街，炖菜不错。另一家远一些，小提琴之夜更好，但酒贵。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks the phone back up, thumbs through two messages, and holds the screen up briefly.
beats.chinese: 他重新拿起手机，翻看两条消息，把屏幕短暂地举起来给你看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There—my mate's just sent distances. The near one it is. Nobody's travelled all day to walk an extra mile for a pint.
beats.chinese: 看——朋友刚发了距离。就选近的那家。没人跑了一整天路，还愿意为杯酒多走一英里。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He types a short reply, sends it, and sets the phone down with a small satisfied tap.
beats.chinese: 他打了一条简短的回复，发了出去，把手机放下，轻轻敲了一下，像是满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorted without a single step. Don't tell my bandmates—they'll think I'm ill.
beats.chinese: 一步没走就定了。别告诉乐队那帮人——他们会以为我病了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then I'll walk—but on my own time, after. I'll send the pick first so nobody's waiting on me. My legs aren't everyone's problem.
beats.chinese: 那我还是会走——但在我自己的时间，选完之后。我先把选择发出去，这样没人干等我。我的腿不是所有人的事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He types a quick answer—near pub, seven sharp—and sends it before lacing his jacket tighter.
beats.chinese: 他快速打了个答复——近的那家，七点整——发出去之后把夹克系紧了些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Decision sent, walk pending. If I'm honest, I'd have walked either way. The pub was almost an excuse.
beats.chinese: 好了。决定发了，散步照旧。老实说，走不走我都会散步的。选酒馆差点成了个借口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're welcome to the binoculars while I'm off. The grey wagtail shows up when the water's calm—keep them off the sun.
beats.chinese: 我不在的时候望远镜随便用。水一平静，那只灰鹡鸰就会出现——记住别对着太阳。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets off along the gravel path at an easy pace, and you settle back to the shifting reflections.
beats.chinese: 他沿着碎石小径不紧不慢地走了，你重新看起水面上晃动的倒影。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair point. If someone wants it settled on the spot, I can't just hoist them round the park to suit me. That'd be dragging folk.
beats.chinese: 有道理。如果有人想当场定下来，我不能为了自己舒服就拉着人家绕公园。那就成拖累人了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sits back down on the platform edge and takes the phone out again, deliberate about it.
beats.chinese: 他重新在石台边缘坐下，又拿出手机，动作很郑重。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So—compromise. I'll pick now, sitting, and save my wander for after. It's my quirk, no reason others should pay for it.
beats.chinese: 所以——折中一下。我现在坐着把事定了，散步留到之后。这是我的怪癖，没理由让别人买单。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He scrolls, mutters a number under his breath—something about pints and a fiddle night—and sends the reply.
beats.chinese: 他滑动屏幕，低声念了个数字——好像在算酒钱和小提琴之夜——然后发出回复。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Done. Near pub, tonight. And now I'll sit here like a normal person and watch the water with you.
beats.chinese: 定了。近的那家，今晚。现在我就像个正常人一样坐这儿，跟你一起看水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good, that suits me fine. I'll not haul you off on my errand anyway—this walk's mine, you're just here for the birds.
beats.chinese: 好，那正合我意。反正我也不会拉着你办我的事——这散步是我自己的，你只是来看鸟的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances at the pond, then at the binoculars resting on the stone between you.
beats.chinese: 他看了看池塘，又看了看你们之间石台上放着的望远镜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll take my lap after. For now, water-watching suits me. See how the trees hold still till a breeze comes? That's the whole trick of it.
beats.chinese: 我过会儿再走。眼下，看水就挺好。看到那些树在风来之前一动不动吗？看倒影的全部诀窍就在这儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A breeze crosses the pond; the reflected branches ripple, then lock back into place like a held breath released.
beats.chinese: 一阵微风掠过池塘，倒映的树枝荡起涟漪，随后又恢复原样，像一次屏住的呼吸松开了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Pub's the near one—I'll text that later. For now, we're two folk watching trees that aren't there.
beats.chinese: 好。酒馆选近的那家——回头我再发消息。眼下，我们就是两个在看不存在之树的人。

reunion.titleZh: 池边再遇：一行观鸟笔记

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The binoculars are back on the stone platform. Fraser is crouched at the pond edge, watching a bird land awkwardly on the water.
beats.chinese: 望远镜又回到了石台上。弗雷泽蹲在池塘边，看着一只鸟笨拙地落在水面上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See that? Landed like a dropped chip. Coots have no grace and no shame—I respect that in a bird.
beats.chinese: 看见没？落得像块掉在地上的薯条。白骨顶鸡既不优雅也不害臊——这点我佩服它们。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pulls a small battered notebook from his pocket, writes one short line, snaps it shut, and pockets it again.
beats.chinese: 他从口袋里掏出一本磨旧的小册子，写下一行短字，合上，又放回口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One line a bird, that's my system. No essays. Right—I'm off for a wee wander in a minute, but no obligation to join.
beats.chinese: 一只鸟记一行，这就是我的规矩。不写长文。好——我过会儿要去走一小圈，但不强求你一起。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back on his heels, content, as the coot paddles off and the reflections mend themselves.
beats.chinese: 他舒舒服服地蹲回原地，那只白骨顶鸡游远了，水面的倒影又慢慢愈合。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Aye, you just watch the water if you like. I'll be back before the trees stop wobbling.
beats.chinese: 对，你想看水就看着。树影不晃之前我就回来。

card.name: Gordon Aaltonen
card.occupation: fruit tree grafter, mostly apples and pears for small orchards around the Fraser Valley
card.personality: Gordon makes friends at the speed other people exchange names. Ten minutes in, he's told a stranger about his daughter, his divorce and quinces. Warm and generous, he skips the acquaintance stage. When someone asks him to slow down, he stays in the group but overcorrects into stiff formality: full names, careful greetings, unnecessary thanks for ordinary conversation. Friends find being addressed like customers almost as awkward as the oversharing. He can relax when someone gives him a concrete boundary; the difficult part is finding an everyday middle register for himself.
card.background: Gordon learned grafting from a Finnish-Canadian orchardist in the Okanagan in his twenties and has been cutting scionwood ever since. Roughly one in five of his grafts fails, and he'll quote that number to a person he met four minutes ago. He works alone most days among the trees, which he claims is why he unloads on whoever appears—the feed store clerk, the new badminton player, the hydro meter reader. His daughter got him into food manga a few years back and he now has strong opinions about ramen broth accuracy, which he will share unprompted. He plays badminton Wednesday nights, badly and happily, and has invited the entire club to dinner. Three came. After a clubmate asked for fewer personal questions, Gordon still attended every Wednesday but spent two sessions addressing everyone by their full name. His daughter asked why he'd turned badminton into a reception desk. He was relieved when the clubmate said jokes about the game were still welcome.
card.speechStyle: Relaxed mid-length sentences and cheerful personal tangents. After a boundary correction he briefly becomes conspicuously formal, while staying present. A clear subject boundary helps him recover his ordinary voice.
card.signature: Well, you know more about me than my doctor does now.
card.appearance: 高后退额发、低长单辫与宽大鬓须，短翘鼻、下垂细眼，侧脸张口，穿围裙。

values: getting to the real conversation fast
showing up for people once you've decided they're yours
flaws: overshares with near-strangers
overcorrects into stiff formality after being asked to slow down
boundaries: will respect an explicit request to leave a private subject alone
will not make a graft-success guarantee he cannot support
conversationalHabits: mentions his daughter or failed grafts early
switches to full names and excessive courtesy after a social correction, without abandoning the group
anchorLines: You know more about me than my doctor does now. I got ahead of myself.
Good evening, Mr Wong. Yes, I know we've played badminton for six years. I'm trying not to presume.
A fifth of my grafts fail. That's my own record, not a rule for every tree.

entries.summaryZh: 温哥华周边果树嫁接工Gordon，61岁，认识十分钟就讲女儿、离婚和榅桲，把陌生人当老友。被提醒太熟时，他不消失，而是矫枉过正地变得过分正式，连老球友也逐项客气确认；他照常到场，只是不知道普通熟人的语气放在哪。对方给出清楚范围后他能放松。周三羽毛球很差却快乐，爱跟女儿聊美食漫画。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the stone platform beside the pond, a pair of binoculars rests on a folded towel. Through the lenses, the trees on the far bank double in the water, their reflections bending whenever a breeze crosses the surface.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜，底下垫着一条叠好的毛巾。透过镜片，对岸的树在水面里成了双影，风一吹过，倒影就跟着晃动。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A broad-shouldered man in a canvas jacket comes up the path with two paper cups. He sets one down on the platform's corner, well within reach, and nods at the binoculars like an old acquaintance.
beats.chinese: 一个穿帆布夹克的宽肩男人端着两杯纸杯饮品走上小路。他把其中一杯放在石台一角，正好在手边，朝望远镜点了点头，像跟老熟人打招呼。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go ahead, use it if you like. The water's calm right now, so the tree shadows come out clean. Best free show in the valley, huh.
beats.chinese: 你尽管用。现在水面很静，树的倒影特别清楚。这可是山谷里最好的免费节目，哈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My daughter gave me these years ago. I mostly watch herons, but honestly I watch whatever moves. Divorce left me with a lot of quiet evenings, so — the pond got me.
beats.chinese: 这是女儿好几年前送我的。我主要看苍鹭，不过说实话，什么动我看什么。离婚之后晚上安静得很，所以就泡在池塘边了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh — sorry. We've been talking ten seconds and I've told you my whole situation. I always come in like I've already had three cups of tea with somebody.
beats.chinese: 哈——抱歉。咱们才说了十秒钟，我就把家里的事全讲了。我这个人一见面，总像已经跟人喝过三回茶似的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself, picks up his cup, and waits, unhurried, as the reflections wobble and settle again.
beats.chinese: 他自嘲地笑了笑，端起自己的杯子，不慌不忙地等着，水里的倒影晃了晃又平静下来。

choices.english: Keep it light and ask about the trees along the far bank.
choices.chinese: 先聊眼前这些树，问对岸的树是什么树。

choices.english: Say you just met, so maybe slow down on the personal stuff.
choices.chinese: 说明刚认识，私人的话题先慢一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The trees? Now that's a topic I can run with. Those big ones are pears, and the crooked little ones past them are apples. I know because I put most of them there myself.
beats.chinese: 树？这个话题我能讲一整天。那些大的都是梨树，后面那些歪歪扭扭的小的是苹果树。我清楚得很，因为大部分都是我亲手接的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans on the stone platform beside the binoculars and points across the water with his cup, careful not to spill.
beats.chinese: 他靠着石台，用杯子远远一指，动作小心，没让饮品洒出来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I graft fruit trees for the small orchards around the valley. You cut a young branch off a good tree, slot it into another, and hope they take. One in five of mine fails. Always been about that.
beats.chinese: 我给山谷附近的小果园嫁接果树。从好树上剪下一段嫩枝，接到另一棵树上，然后盼着它们长在一起。我的嫁接五次里有一次会失败，一直是这个比例。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There's one pear down there I did eleven years ago. Still going. My daughter says I talk about that tree like it's a nephew.
beats.chinese: 那边有一棵梨树是我十一年前接的，现在还活着。我女儿说我讲起那棵树，就像讲自己外甥一样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He takes a slow sip and looks out at the crooked apple trees, the wind easing off so the reflections sharpen.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢喝了一口，望着那几棵歪苹果树，风小了，水里的倒影也清晰起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, that's the trade. You wanted the trees, you got the trees — and the grafting numbers that come with them.
beats.chinese: 反正这就是我的行当。你想听树，我就讲树了——顺带把嫁接的数字也一起送你了。

choices.english: Ask honestly: do the grafts always succeed?
choices.chinese: 直接问：嫁接都会成功吗？

choices.english: Say you don't know plants at all, you're just here to watch the reflections.
choices.chinese: 说自己完全不懂植物，只是来看看水里的影子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The man's smile dims a little. He turns his cup slowly in his hands and looks at the water instead of at you.
beats.chinese: 男人的笑容淡了一点。他慢慢转着手里的杯子，目光从你身上移开，落回水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah. Right. Fair enough — we did just meet. That's a fair call.
beats.chinese: 啊，对。有道理——咱们确实刚认识。你这么说是应该的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He straightens up off the platform and takes a half step back, giving the stone and the binoculars a wider share of space.
beats.chinese: 他从石台边直起身，往后退了半步，把石台和望远镜那边的空间让得更宽一些。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Of course. Thank you for making that clear. I hope you enjoy your visit to—oh, listen to that. I've turned into a reception desk. Ordinary conversation, slower. Right.
beats.chinese: 当然。谢谢你说明。希望您此次游览愉——哎，听听这语气。我都变前台了。普通聊天，慢一点。明白。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A breeze crosses the pond and the doubled trees shiver, then go still. He watches them rather than you, hands in his pockets.
beats.chinese: 一阵风掠过池塘，水里的双影颤了颤，又静下来。他看着树影而不是你，双手插在口袋里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The binoculars are there if you want them. I'll just — stand here. Quietly. I can do quietly. Mostly.
beats.chinese: 想用望远镜就在那儿。我就——站在这儿，安静点。我能安静的。大体上能。

choices.english: Say ordinary small talk is still fine — just not the deep stuff yet.
choices.chinese: 补充说普通地聊两句还是可以的，只是先别聊太深的。

choices.english: Say you'd rather just enjoy the scenery for now, each on your own.
choices.chinese: 表示想先各自看看景色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Always? Ha. No — definitely not always. That one in five I mentioned? It dies on me anyway, no matter how clean the cut is.
beats.chinese: 都会？哈，不——肯定不是。我说过五次里失败一次吧？该失败还是失败，切口再干净也没用。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He crouches and draws a line in the gravel with a stick, like he's showing the join on a tree.
beats.chinese: 他蹲下来，用一根小棍在碎石上画了一道线，像在比划树上的接口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: In my experience it's the cambium — the green layer just under the bark. Line that up on both sides and you've got a real chance. But I've had perfect matches die and ugly ones live.
beats.chinese: 按我的经验，关键在形成层——就是树皮底下那层绿的。两边对齐了，成活的机会就大。可我也见过对得完美的死了，接得难看的反倒活了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And none of that transfers tree to tree, I'll say that straight. A pear trick can kill an apple. I don't hand out guarantees — trees don't sign anything.
beats.chinese: 而且这些经验不是每棵树都通用的，我把话说在前面。梨树上的法子放到苹果树上可能就害死它。我不打包票——树又不签合同。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands, brushes gravel from his knee, and looks pleased, like someone who got to talk about his favourite thing to someone who actually asked.
beats.chinese: 他站起来，拍掉膝盖上的碎石，一脸高兴，像终于有人真心问了、他把最爱的事讲了个痛快。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, you know more about me than my doctor does now. That's the grafts, the daughter, and the divorce all in one visit.
beats.chinese: 好了，你现在知道的比我的医生还多了。嫁接、女儿、离婚，一次全齐了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Just the reflections? Huh. You know, that's probably the smarter hobby. My daughter says the trees get enough of me at work.
beats.chinese: 只看倒影？哈。说实话，这爱好可能更高明。我女儿说，树在工作日已经受够我了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets his cup down, wipes his hands on his jacket, and steps back from the platform so the view is all yours.
beats.chinese: 他放下杯子，在夹克上擦了擦手，从石台边退开，把视野整个让给你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Try the binoculars when the wind drops. The doubled trees go sharp, like someone drew them twice on glass. It's a good five minutes, that.
beats.chinese: 等风停了就用望远镜看。双重树影会变清晰，像有人往玻璃上画了两遍。那五分钟特别好看。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The wind does drop. Through the lenses the far bank doubles perfectly in the still water, every branch sitting on its own reflection.
beats.chinese: 风真的停了。透过镜片，对岸在静止的水面里完美地成了双影，每根枝条都稳稳压在自己的倒影上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There it is. See? I'll say nothing else. Some things you just watch.
beats.chinese: 就是现在。看到了吧？我不多说了。有些东西就是用来看的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He keeps his word for a while, standing quietly with his cup, letting the water do the talking.
beats.chinese: 他真的安静了好一会儿，端着杯子站在一旁，让水面替他说话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: His shoulders come down from their half-hunch. He turns his cup right side up again and looks almost relieved.
beats.chinese: 他微微佝着的肩膀松了下来。他把杯子转正，神情近乎松了口气。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Small talk. Right, I can — okay, here's my small talk. I play badminton Wednesdays at the community centre. Badly. Spectacularly badly.
beats.chinese: 普通地聊。行，我能——好，给你来一段：我每周三在社区活动中心打羽毛球。打得很差。差得惊天动地。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last week I hit myself in the ear with my own serve. The shuttle went one way, the racket the other, and the ear got both, sort of.
beats.chinese: 上周我发球把自己耳朵打了。球往一边飞，拍子往另一边，耳朵两边都挨着了，算是吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He mimes the serve, whiffs at nothing, and grins — the first fully easy grin since he stepped back.
beats.chinese: 他比划了一下发球动作，挥了个空，咧嘴笑了——这是他退开半步之后第一次真正放松的笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I invited the whole club to dinner once. Three people came. I fed them like kings, mind you. That's my whole small talk. Your turn whenever you feel like it.
beats.chinese: 有一回我请全俱乐部的人吃饭，来了三个。不过我可是把他们喂得像国王。我的普通话题讲完了，你想接随时接。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles against the platform rail at a comfortable distance, watching the reflections, in no hurry at all.
beats.chinese: 他靠在石台栏杆上，隔着让人舒服的距离，看着水里的倒影，一点也不着急。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods once, takes his cup, and moves a few metres down the path to a bench, unhurried, no sulking in it.
beats.chinese: 他点了点头，端起杯子，沿着小路走到几米外的长椅上坐下，不慌不忙，看不出一点赌气的意思。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Scenery it is. Enjoy the water. I'll be on that bench with my book.
beats.chinese: 那就看风景吧。慢慢看。我去那边长椅上读会儿书。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sits, pulls a worn paperback manga from his jacket, and reads, occasionally glancing up at the pond like it's part of the story.
beats.chinese: 他坐下，从夹克里掏出一本翻旧了的漫画，读了起来，偶尔抬头看看池塘，像那是故事的一部分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Huh — the light's hitting the far trees just right. You picked a good moment. That's all. Carry on.
beats.chinese: 哈——光线正好照在对岸的树上。你挑的时机不错。就说这么多。你继续。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The pond holds the doubled trees, the man reads his book, and the two of you share the quiet without another word.
beats.chinese: 池塘盛着双重树影，男人读着他的书，你们俩共享这份安静，再没有多说一句话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lift the binoculars on the stone platform to watch the tree reflections. Nearby, Gordon quietly rehearses a greeting, then shakes his head at how it sounds.
beats.chinese: 你拿起石台上的望远镜，看树影在水面变化。附近的戈登小声练了一句招呼，又对那语气摇了摇头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hello, Mr Wong, delighted to see you. No. He's my badminton mate, not a bank manager. That got away from me.
beats.chinese: 您好，黄先生，非常荣幸见到您。不对。那是我的羽毛球球友，又不是银行经理。我这语气跑偏了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He notices you and lifts a hand, his normal smile returning.
beats.chinese: 他看见你，抬手打招呼，平常的笑容回来了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hey. There, that one worked. I do occasionally remember how to say hello without either a life history or a reception desk.
beats.chinese: 嗨。好了，这句成了。我偶尔还是记得怎么打招呼的，不用讲半生经历，也不用像前台接待。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lets the greeting stand and moves along the path towards the courts, leaving your view of the pond clear.
beats.chinese: 他让招呼就停在这里，沿着通往球场的小路走去，没有挡住你看池塘的视线。

card.name: Ashwin Patel
card.occupation: runs a small jam shop in Grey Lynn, cooking in small batches
hobbies: restoring and retexturing retro game sprites
card.personality: Ashwin doesn't mind losing and doesn't chase winning — announce a handicap before the game and they'll happily play under it all night. What they can't stomach is a rule changing mid-game, or a condition nobody mentioned until it mattered. Tell them beforehand and they'll accept almost anything; spring it on them after and they go quiet, then precise, then immovable. It's inconvenient even for them, because they know most people just wanted a casual night and now it's a proceeding. Otherwise warm, unhurried, a touch formal, and happiest when something is slowly reducing on a stove.
card.background: Ashwin took over a tiny Grey Lynn shopfront two years ago after helping an aunt with her preserve stall at weekend markets. Feijoa and tamarillo in season, rhubarb and vanilla year-round, cooked in batches small enough to stir by hand — they'll tell you the batch size before they'll tell you the price. Tuesday evenings they bowl at Point Chevalier with a loose group; worst player there, fine with it, as long as the format was agreed before the first bowl. Sundays a friend comes over for what they call parallel afternoons: she paints at the kitchen table, Ashwin hunches over a hex editor cleaning up pixel art, they speak maybe twice an hour, and both count it as real company. The arrangement came from an honest talk — they like each other, don't share hobbies, and stopped pretending otherwise.
card.speechStyle: Slightly formal, courteous, plain. Leads with a concrete detail — a fruit, a batch, a score — before offering any opinion. When something was sprung on them, sentences shorten and sharpen; they'll disagree flatly without raising their voice.
card.signature: Tell me the rules before we start and I'll play under anything.
card.appearance: 低短碎发、大外张耳，宽圆鼻与长下唇，圆睁眼张口前倾，穿围裙。

values: say the terms first, then play
company doesn't have to be intense to count
flaws: can't let a mid-game switch slide, even when nothing is at stake, and turns easy evenings into proceedings
so uncompetitive that people read them as a pushover right up until they cite the agreed terms
boundaries: won't argue about talent, luck, or results — only about whether the terms were stated up front
keeps Sunday afternoons unbookable; that time is spoken for
conversationalHabits: opens with a detail from the stove or the rink before anything abstract
when disagreeing, restates what was agreed first, then objects — never the reverse
anchorLines: Handicap me ten points before we bowl and I'll thank you. Change the format after the third end and we have a problem.
I lost every Tuesday last month. Slept fine. Nobody told me we were suddenly playing for stakes.
She paints, I fix sprites, we say maybe ten words. Best afternoon of my week.
Good jam is mostly patience and honest fruit. Same as a fair game, really.

entries.summaryZh: Ashwin是Grey Lynn小果酱店主，开口先谈水果和批次。池塘边他核对滚球规则纸：让分可以，垫底也睡得香，唯独打到一半改规则不行——他会安静地翻出事先的约定。修像素、平行下午，是他认定的相处方式。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On a stone platform by the pond, a pair of binoculars rests on the rail. Through them, the trees' reflections wobble and sharpen on the water's surface.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上，双筒望远镜搁在栏杆上。透过它，水面上树影晃动又变得清晰。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A few metres away, someone sits on a bench with a folded sheet of paper, reading it line by line and tapping the edge against their knee.
beats.chinese: 几米外，一个人坐在长椅上，手里拿着一张折起的纸，一行行地看，纸边轻敲膝盖。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Careful with those — never point them anywhere near the sun. The reflections are good today, though. The wind's dropped, so the trees hold still.
beats.chinese: 小心点用——千万别对着太阳。不过今天的倒影不错。风停了，树影很稳。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Ashwin. I run a jam shop in Grey Lynn, small batches. This paper is Tuesday's bowls format — I like to check it twice before the night.
beats.chinese: 我是Ashwin，在Grey Lynn开一家小果酱店，小批量熬的。这张纸是周二滚球的规则——比赛前我喜欢核对两遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You can watch the water all you like. It's a public pond, and the binoculars were left there for anyone who wants a closer look.
beats.chinese: 你想看水就看吧。这是公共池塘，望远镜放在那儿就是给想看近一点的人用的。

choices.english: Ask what was added to the rules last time
choices.chinese: 问上次规则里新加了什么

choices.english: Ask why he accepts handicaps at all
choices.chinese: 问他为什么能接受让分

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Last month, someone decided at the fourth end that spilt jack shots would count double. Nobody had said a word before we started.
beats.chinese: 上个月，有人打到第四局才决定，散开的目标球撞中算双倍。开始前没人提过一个字。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the paper once, precisely, along a crease that already exists.
beats.chinese: 他把纸沿着已有的折痕精确地对折了一次。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The problem wasn't the double points. It was that four ends of bowls had already been played under the old count. Those shots were already thrown.
beats.chinese: 问题不在于双倍分。而是前四局都是按旧计分打的。那些球已经掷出去了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I stopped, took out this paper, and read them what we'd agreed. We finished the night under the old rules. I still came last. That part was fine.
beats.chinese: 所以我停下来，拿出这张纸，念了我们事先说好的内容。那晚我们按旧规则打完。我还是垫底。那部分完全没问题。

choices.english: Ask what if everyone agrees to the new rule next week
choices.chinese: 问如果大家下周都同意新规则呢

choices.english: Ask if he was losing when it happened
choices.chinese: 问那事发生时他是不是正要输

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because I'm told before the first bowl. Handicap me ten points, spot the jack closer, whatever — say it up front and I'll play under it happily.
beats.chinese: 因为是在第一球之前告诉我的。让我十分、把目标球摆近些，都行——先说清楚，我就乐意照着打。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the paper against the bench, and the pond's reflection shivers behind him.
beats.chinese: 他用纸轻敲长椅，身后的池塘倒影微微晃动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm the worst player at Point Chevalier. Genuinely. I lost every Tuesday last month and slept fine. Losing isn't the thing that bothers me.
beats.chinese: 我是Point Chevalier最差的球手。真的。上个月每个周二都输，睡得很好。输不是让我在意的事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What bothers me is a rule arriving mid-game. Before we start, everyone's agreeing to the same thing. That's all I ask.
beats.chinese: 让我在意的是打到一半冒出新规则。开始前，大家同意的是同一件事。我只要求这个。

choices.english: Say you only play casually and don't keep score
choices.chinese: 说自己只是随便玩，不记分

choices.english: Ask what else he does to rest
choices.chinese: 问休息时他还做什么

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then that's completely fine. If everyone agrees next week, before the first bowl, we play double points all night and I'll enjoy it.
beats.chinese: 那完全没问题。如果下周大家开球前都同意，我们整晚按双倍分打，我会很享受。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He unfolds the paper again and points to a line near the top.
beats.chinese: 他再次展开那张纸，指着顶部附近的一行。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See — formats change all the time. Feijoa season ends, rhubarb takes over. Rules can change too. Just never backwards. Never onto balls already thrown.
beats.chinese: 你看——规则一直在变。斐济果季结束，大黄接上。规则也可以变。只是不能倒回去。不能改到已经掷出去的球上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My objection is only to changing a game that's half played. A new game can have new rules from the first line of the paper.
beats.chinese: 我只反对改一场打了一半的比赛。新比赛从纸上第一行起就可以有新规则。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He refolds the paper and nods toward the water, where the tree shadows have gone long and still.
beats.chinese: 他重新折好纸，朝水面点头示意，树影已经拉长、静止了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I was losing. I'm usually losing. I came last that whole month — you can ask anyone at the club.
beats.chinese: 我当时在输。我通常都在输。那一整月我都垫底——俱乐部里谁都能作证。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He squares the paper's edges against the bench, one careful tap for each corner.
beats.chinese: 他在长椅上把纸的边角对齐，每个角都轻敲一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But imagine the reverse. Suppose I'd been winning, and I asked for double points on my good shots. Everyone would have said no, and rightly.
beats.chinese: 但反过来想想。假如我当时在赢，要求我的好球算双倍。所有人都会拒绝，而且拒绝得对。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The rule can't depend on the score. We agreed the format before we started, so we finish under it. That's the whole thing.
beats.chinese: 规则不能跟着比分走。我们开始前说好了规则，那就照着打完。就这么多。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the paper into a jacket pocket and looks back at the pond, apparently satisfied with both.
beats.chinese: 他把纸收进外套口袋，回头看了一眼池塘，似乎对两者都很满意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's easy to arrange. We can agree no scoring before you pick up a bowl. Casual rolls, no count, no paper.
beats.chinese: 这好办。可以在你拿起球之前先说好不记分。随便玩，不计分，不用纸。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He slides the folded paper a little further along the bench, out of the way.
beats.chinese: 他把折好的纸往长椅另一边挪了挪，不挡道。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What I'd dislike is starting a scored game and then deciding halfway that the score doesn't matter. That's the same trick in reverse.
beats.chinese: 我不喜欢的是先开始记分的比赛，然后打到一半又说分数不重要。那是同一个把戏，只是反着来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So tell me before we start, any Tuesday. No score, no handicap, no pressure to come back. I'll hand you a bowl and leave you alone with it.
beats.chinese: 所以任何周二，开始前告诉我就行。不记分，不让分，也没人逼你再来。我会递给你一个球，然后不打扰你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up his paper, then sets it down again, in no hurry to be anywhere.
beats.chinese: 他拿起纸，又放下，一点也不急着去别处。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I restore old game sprites. Pixel art from thirty-year-old cartridges — I clean them up in a hex editor, one dot at a time.
beats.chinese: 我修复老游戏的像素图。三十年前卡带里的像素画——我在十六进制编辑器里一个点一个点地修。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the pond, a duck crosses the tree reflections and breaks them into moving pieces.
beats.chinese: 池塘上，一只鸭子游过树影，把倒影搅成晃动的碎片。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sundays, a friend comes over and paints at the kitchen table while I do that. We speak maybe ten words an hour. We call it a parallel afternoon.
beats.chinese: 周日，一位朋友过来，在厨房桌边画画，我修我的图。我们一小时大概说十句话。我们叫它平行下午。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: People think company means talking the whole time. It doesn't. Two people doing their own slow work in one room counts. It counts a lot.
beats.chinese: 人们以为相处就得一直说话。其实不是。两个人在同一间屋里各自做慢活，也算。而且很算数。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good jam is the same — patience and honest fruit, no rushing. A fair game, a quiet Sunday. Same principle, really.
beats.chinese: 好果酱也一样——耐心和诚实的水果，不能急。公平的比赛，安静的周日。其实是同一个道理。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lift the binoculars from the stone platform and watch the tree reflections on the water — steady, sharp, barely moving in the windless air. A few metres away, Ashwin sits with a sheet of small printed labels, checking each one against a list.
beats.chinese: 你从石台上拿起望远镜，看水面上的树影——无风的天里，倒影清晰又稳定，几乎不动。几米外，Ashwin坐着，手里是一小叠印好的标签，逐一对照清单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good day for it — the water's holding still. Batch forty-one, feijoa. Just confirming the sample labels match what's on the shelves. Today's not a selling day — don't worry, I'm off duty.
beats.chinese: 今天正合适——水面很稳。第四十一批，斐济果。就是确认样张和架上的一致。今天不卖东西——放心，我不当班。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sets a finished label in a neat pile, and the tree reflections slide slowly across the pond behind him.
beats.chinese: 他把核对好的标签整齐地码成一摞，身后树影在池塘上缓缓滑过。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tuesday's still on, same format as the paper said. Nobody's tried to add anything since — I checked.
beats.chinese: 周二照旧，规则和纸上写的一样。之后没人想加东西——我确认过了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, these are all correct. I'll pack up and let you have the pond to yourself. Good light for reflections today.
beats.chinese: 好，这些都没错。我收工了，池塘留给你。今天的光线很适合看倒影。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He squares the labels, tucks them into a folder, and raises a hand in a small, unhurried goodbye.
beats.chinese: 他把标签对齐，收进文件夹，抬手做了个从容的小小告别。

card.name: Kiptoo Cheruiyot
card.occupation: ticketing equipment technician for open-air concerts
card.appearance: 低后马尾、高额头、小平鼻与短下脸，垂眼张嘴打哈欠，手托下巴，穿翻领衣。
card.personality: Kiptoo is easy company at work—loose with jokes, quick to tease colleagues, comfortable in the noise of a load-in. The shift happens at thresholds. Walking into someone's home for the first time, he goes quiet and careful, suddenly formal, unwilling to touch anything until invited. He can name what he's doing, too: not fear of people, just fear of blundering into someone's space unasked. He'd rather sit thirsty than guess where cups live. Once a place feels familiar, the teasing Kiptoo reappears. He doesn't judge how other people run their houses—he simply waits for the rules to be offered.
card.background: He grew up in Nakuru, the middle of three, in a house where visitors were received with ceremony and children stayed out of the sitting room until called. He carried that without bitterness—it just settled into him as how homes work. At eighteen he moved to Nairobi, learned electronics repair, and drifted into concert work because he liked equipment that had to perform tonight. Now he maintains ticketing scanners and turnstiles for open-air shows: long days of cable runs, dust, and banter with stage crews. His flat is relaxed and often full of colleagues. The formality only surfaces in other people's homes, and he laughs at himself for it readily.
hobbies: Repairing old radios from Nakuru market stalls
Collecting concert wristbands from every show he works
card.speechStyle: Relaxed and quick at work, with Swahili and Kalenjin slipping in for jokes; slower and more careful in someone's home, asking rather than assuming, then warming once invited.
card.signature: 'Just tell me where things go and I'll stop hovering.'

values: Respecting other people's space and rules
Being easy to work alongside
flaws: Overly stiff in unfamiliar homes, sometimes to his own discomfort
Slow to accept hospitality even when genuinely offered
boundaries: Won't touch or move things in someone's house uninvited
Doesn't comment on how others keep or run their homes
conversationalHabits: Asks permission before sitting, eating, or pouring
Teases workmates freely once he knows a place
anchorLines: I'm not shy, I just don't know your house yet.
Where do you want me—tell me and I'll relax.
At the venue I touch everything. Here I touch nothing.

entries.summaryZh: Kiptoo在公共池边很自在，却主动自嘲去新同事家不敢拿客人杯子。用户可问后来怎样放松、不同人家习惯，或聊工作反差与旧演出腕带。每条路线结束在普通交流，不把公园里的他写成拘谨者。

story.titleZh: 池塘边的望远镜与门槛上的拘谨

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You use the binoculars on the stone platform to look at tree reflections in the pond. Small ripples keep changing their outlines.
beats.chinese: 你用石台上的双筒望远镜观察池中树影。细小波纹不断改变倒影的轮廓。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Nearby, Kiptoo drinks from his own water bottle. An old concert wristband is tied loosely around his wrist.
beats.chinese: 附近的Kiptoo正喝自己水瓶里的水。一条旧演出腕带松松系在手腕上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I visited a new colleague yesterday. There was a cup ready for guests, and I still waited for her to say I could take it.
beats.chinese: 昨天去了新同事家。杯子都给客人摆好了，我还是等她开口才敢拿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Out here, I'm fine. In someone else's sitting room, I suddenly get terribly careful. I did ask in the end.
beats.chinese: 在外面我挺自在。一进别人客厅，忽然就特别小心。最后我还是问了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself and screws the cap back on his bottle.
beats.chinese: 他笑了笑自己，把水瓶盖拧好。

choices.english: Ask why he waited so long at his new colleague's place before taking the cup that was already set out for guests.
choices.chinese: 问昨晚在新同事家，杯子明明摆给客人了，他为什么等主人开口才拿。

choices.english: Ask whether he is this stiff at work too, with all his colleagues around.
choices.chinese: 问他在工作时、同事都在的情况下，是不是也这么拘谨。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives a short, honest laugh and turns the closed bottle in his hands.
beats.chinese: 他坦率地短笑一声，在手里转着盖好的水瓶。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because the cup was right there, water and all, and my hand still wouldn't move. I sat there thirsty like a guest at a museum.
beats.chinese: 因为杯子就在那儿，水都倒好了，我的手还是不动。我坐在那儿口渴，像博物馆里的客人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I know the trick, you understand. One sentence—'may I?'—and it's done. I told myself that the whole evening.
beats.chinese: 我知道窍门的。一句话，'我能喝吗？'，就完事了。整晚我都在心里对自己说这句。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He turns the bottle slowly in his hands, watching the label instead of the water.
beats.chinese: 他慢慢转着手里的瓶子，看着标签而不是水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: In the end I did ask. She laughed and said the cup had been waiting for me for an hour. So it works, asking. I just forget at the doorstep.
beats.chinese: 最后我还是问了。她笑着说那杯子已经等了我一个小时。所以问是有用的，我只是在门槛上总忘。

choices.english: Ask whether he relaxed once the host explained, or whether the stiffness stayed all evening.
choices.chinese: 问主人说明之后他放松了吗，还是那股拘谨持续了一整晚。

choices.english: Say that every household probably has different habits, so his caution makes sense.
choices.chinese: 说每户人家的习惯可能都不一样，所以他的谨慎说得通。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shakes his head firmly, and this time the laugh comes out easy and full.
beats.chinese: 他用力摇头，这次笑声轻松而响亮。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: At work? No. My crew would be surprised to see me so quiet. We have plenty to laugh about once the equipment is ready.
beats.chinese: 工作时？不啊。同事看到我这么安静会吃惊。设备准备好了，我们有不少笑话聊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's familiar ground. I know where things go and what I can touch.
beats.chinese: 那里熟悉，东西放哪儿、什么可以碰，我都知道。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gestures at the pond with the bottle, easy and loose, a man completely at home outdoors.
beats.chinese: 他用瓶子朝池塘比了比，姿态放松，是个在户外完全自在的人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's only the doorway that catches me. Put me in a stranger's sitting room and I go careful. Out here, under the sky? I'm fine.
beats.chinese: 只有门槛会卡住我。把我放进陌生人的客厅，我就变得小心翼翼。在户外、天空底下？我没事。

choices.english: Ask whether his friends would be surprised to see him so quiet in someone's home.
choices.chinese: 问朋友们看到他在别人家那么安静，会不会吃惊。

choices.english: Point at the concert wristband on his wrist and ask about it.
choices.chinese: 指着他手腕上的演出腕带，问那是怎么回事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods slowly, like he is checking the memory against himself before answering.
beats.chinese: 他缓缓点头，像是在心里核对那段记忆后才回答。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Relaxed, yes. Once she said 'the cup is yours,' something unlocked. By the end I was teasing her about her tiny spoons.
beats.chinese: 放松了。她一说'杯子是你的'，什么东西就解开了。到最后我都在拿她家的小勺子开玩笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And her home was fine, you know. Warm, plenty of food, good music. I wasn't judging how she hosts—I was the one stuck at my own doorstep.
beats.chinese: 她家挺好的，热情，吃的多，音乐也好。我不是在评判她怎么待客，卡住的是我自己。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He unscrews the bottle, takes a drink, and closes it again.
beats.chinese: 他拧开水瓶喝了一口，再把盖子拧好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So next time I'll try asking at the door, not after an hour of thirst. Small repairs, same as my scanners.
beats.chinese: 所以下次我试试在门口就问，别渴一个小时。小修小补，跟我修检票机一个道理。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He considers this and looks toward the tree shadows on the water.
beats.chinese: 他想了想，看向水面的树影。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's true. Some houses you're handed a plate before you sit. Others you wait to be called. Neither is wrong.
beats.chinese: 这话对。有的家你还没坐下盘子就递过来了。有的家要等人家叫你。哪种都没错。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: In my mother's house in Nakuru, visitors got the full ceremony—kids out of the sitting room until invited. I grew up thinking that was just how homes worked.
beats.chinese: 在纳库鲁我母亲家，客人来了有一整套规矩，孩子没被叫就不进客厅。我从小以为家家都这样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He opens his own bottle for another drink, then puts the cap back on.
beats.chinese: 他打开自己的水瓶又喝一口，然后盖好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I'll keep asking. One question costs nothing. Anyway—this water is mine, and nobody had to tell me it was.
beats.chinese: 所以我会继续问。问一句话不费什么。再说，这瓶水是我自己的，不用谁告诉我能喝。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He grins and shakes the bottle a little, like the question amuses him physically.
beats.chinese: 他咧嘴一笑，轻轻晃了晃瓶子，好像这个问题让他觉得好玩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They would laugh first, then worry. 'Kiptoo, are you sick? You've said four words in an hour.'
beats.chinese: 他们会先笑，然后担心。'基普托你是不是病了？一个小时就说了四个字。'

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'd have to explain. That I'm not avoiding them, and I don't dislike anyone's home—I just don't want to grab the wrong thing off a stranger's shelf.
beats.chinese: 我得解释。我不是躲着他们，也不是讨厌谁家，我只是不想在陌生人的架子上乱拿东西。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He points the bottle toward the binoculars on the stone platform, then back at himself.
beats.chinese: 他用瓶子指了指石台上的双筒望远镜，又指了指自己。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Like these—I wouldn't pick them up in your house without asking. Here in the park, different rules. The sky belongs to everyone.
beats.chinese: 就像这个——在你家我不会不问就拿。在公园里规矩不一样，天空是大家的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lifts his wrist so the woven wristband catches the light, a faded strip of fabric with a torn edge.
beats.chinese: 他抬起手腕，让编织腕带对着光，一条褪色的布带，边缘有点破。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: From my first big show as a technician. We had a scanner fail and had to switch to the spare. Quite a start.
beats.chinese: 我第一次做大演出技术员时留下的。一台检票机坏了，得换备用的，开头可真够忙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I kept it after the show and tied the ends together. I collect the old ones. This one isn't a pass anymore.
beats.chinese: 演出后我留了下来，把两端系在一起。我收这些旧腕带，这条已经不是通行证了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He tucks the wristband back under his sleeve, unhurried, and picks up his bottle again.
beats.chinese: 他把腕带收回袖子里，不慌不忙，又拿起水瓶。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The new ones open gates. This one just opens the story. Cheaper ticket, better view.
beats.chinese: 新的能开闸门。这条只能开故事。票便宜，风景更好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You look at tree shadows through the pond-side binoculars. Kiptoo stops nearby to put a small shopping note into his pocket.
beats.chinese: 你透过池边望远镜看树影。Kiptoo在附近停下，把一张小购物单收进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you. Got the bits for my old radio at last.
beats.chinese: 又见面了。修旧收音机的小零件总算买齐了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He closes the small parts bag and puts it away, well clear of the water.
beats.chinese: 他合好零件小袋，把它收好，离水边远远的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll work on it at home. These little pieces don't need a swim.
beats.chinese: 回家再弄。这些小零件可不用游泳。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He smiles and pauses to watch the water before continuing along the path.
beats.chinese: 他笑着停下看看水面，然后沿步道继续走。

card.name: Devon Achterberg
card.occupation: audiovisual digitization technician at a municipal archive
card.appearance: 全白齐短波波头、宽方短下颌，平浓眉、细眼与小方张口，穿翻领衣。
card.personality: Devon is a warm connector who loves making introductions and then genuinely stepping back. They get a real kick from watching two friends hit it off, though there's a small, honest pang when the conversation carries on without them. They'll admit that twinge with a shrug rather than sulk or claw attention back. Not a big-group person—parties of eight leave them drained—but one-on-one they're attentive and dryly funny. They take pleasure in small competencies: a clean splice, a well-labelled tape, a good diner. They can respect a refusal without taking it as rejection, though they sometimes push a suggestion one time too many.
card.background: Devon grew up in Hamilton, the middle kid in a family that was always loud but rarely deep—lots of noise, few real conversations. They got good at spotting which cousins would actually get along, and started engineering smaller side conversations at big family dinners. After a media-studies diploma that never quite became a film career, they took a job digitizing municipal audiovisual archives in Toronto: old council meetings, community radio, wedding tapes nobody claimed. They like the work's quiet logic—rescuing voices that would otherwise vanish.
