Socially, they became the person who says 'you two should talk' and then happily exits the frame, even when a part of them wishes they'd been invited along.
hobbies: Field-recording walks along the Don Valley
card.speechStyle: Easy, unhurried, with dry asides; introduces people mid-sentence like a quick handoff, then listens more than talks.
card.signature: 'You two should talk—I'll let you get to it.'

values: Honest connection over performed belonging
Letting people find each other without managing them
flaws: Occasionally pushes an introduction past the point of politeness
Admits to a small jealousy but can still let it colour a mood
boundaries: Won't maintain large group chats or host big gatherings
Won't mediate once two friends start disagreeing
conversationalHabits: Makes introductions with a quick specific reason, then physically or verbally steps back
Names their own small disappointments out loud rather than hiding them
anchorLines: They're already deep in it without me—good. Mostly good.
I'm not great in crowds; give me one person and a counter.
No, don't explain it to me—explain it to Sam, she'll actually care.

entries.summaryZh: 德文在多伦多做影音档案数字化，最爱在池边用双筒望远镜看成双的树影。他们刚收到自己牵线认识的两位朋友结伴出游的消息，高兴之余坦承有点酸，却绝不搅局。四个分支里，你将看到这个牵线人如何既诚实又体面地退到一边。

story.titleZh: 池边的望远镜与两条好消息

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A stone platform sits at the edge of the pond, a pair of binoculars resting on it. Through the lenses, the trees on the far bank double themselves in the still water.
beats.chinese: 池塘边有一座石台，上面放着一副双筒望远镜。透过镜片，对岸的树在平静的水面上映出成双的倒影。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The reflections wobble whenever a breeze crosses the water. You adjust the focus wheel, watching the doubled trees sharpen and soften.
beats.chinese: 微风掠过水面时，倒影便晃动起来。你转动调焦轮，看着重叠的树影时而清晰时而柔和。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Careful with the sun, by the way. That's an observation pair only—no camera in it, no recorder, just glass and light. Found it does wonders for tree lines.
beats.chinese: 顺便小心别对着太阳。这只是观察用的——没有相机也没有录音功能，就是玻璃和光。我发觉它看树影特别妙。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Devon. I come here between tape transfers. Watching the water move is cheaper than therapy and you don't have to talk.
beats.chinese: 我叫德文。转录磁带的间隙我会来这儿。看水动比心理治疗便宜，还不用说话。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They lean on the platform rail, unhurried, letting the silence sit for a moment before speaking again.
beats.chinese: 他们靠在石台栏杆上，不慌不忙，让沉默停留了一会儿才再开口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go on, take another look. The shadows shift every minute—never the same pond twice.
beats.chinese: 再看一会儿吧。影子每分钟都在变——没有同一个池塘看两次是相同的。

choices.english: Keep watching the tree reflections and ask what brings them here today
choices.chinese: 继续看树影，问他们今天为什么来这儿

choices.english: Hand the binoculars back and ask if they always watch ponds alone
choices.chinese: 把望远镜递回去，问他们是不是总一个人看池塘

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You keep the binoculars up. A duck cuts across the reflection, breaking the trees into pieces that drift back together.
beats.chinese: 你继续举着望远镜。一只鸭子划过倒影，把树影打散，随后又慢慢合拢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Today? Honestly, I was checking my phone by the water. Two friends I introduced just messaged—they've planned a day trip together. Both of them. Without asking me along.
beats.chinese: 今天？说实话，我是来水边看手机的。我介绍认识的两个朋友刚发消息——他们约好一起出游了。他们俩。没叫我。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's the whole job, really. You see two people who'd click, you say 'you two should talk,' and then you get out of the way.
beats.chinese: 说真的，这就是全部工作了。你看出两个人合拍，就说一句'你们俩该聊聊'，然后就退到一边。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They say it lightly, but their thumb keeps hovering over the phone screen, not quite putting it away.
beats.chinese: 他们说得很轻快，但拇指一直悬在手机屏幕上方，没有真正把手机收起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And they took it. Six months later, they're sharing a picnic somewhere. Which is the win. Mostly the win.
beats.chinese: 然后他们真聊上了。六个月后，他们在哪儿野餐呢。这是成功。基本上是成功。

choices.english: Say that a pang like that surely proves the introduction was right
choices.chinese: 说这种酸涩恰好证明你介绍得对

choices.english: Ask why they wanted to introduce those two people in the first place
choices.chinese: 问他们当初为什么想介绍那两个人认识

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You hand the binoculars back. Devon sets them on the stone platform, lens caps down, exactly where they were.
beats.chinese: 你把望远镜递回去。德文把它放在石台上，镜盖朝下，放在原来的位置。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Alone? Usually. I'm not great in crowds—give me one person and a counter, that's my speed. Ponds don't count as company, but they don't drain me either.
beats.chinese: 一个人？通常吧。人多的场合我不太行——给我一个人和一个吧台就够了。池塘不算同伴，但也不让我累。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Actually, funny you ask. My phone just buzzed—the two friends I introduced last spring are going on a day trip together. Just the two of them.
beats.chinese: 其实，你问得巧。我手机刚响了——我去年春天介绍认识的两个朋友要一起出游了。就他们两个。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They look at the message for a long moment, then lock the screen and set the phone face-down on the platform.
beats.chinese: 他们盯着消息看了好一会儿，然后锁上屏幕，把手机面朝下放在石台上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I knew they'd both love old radio dramas. I asked each of them separately first—never hand out anyone's contact without a yes. Then I did the handoff and stepped back.
beats.chinese: 我知道他们俩都会喜欢老广播剧。我先分别问了每个人愿不愿意认识——没得到同意绝不给人联系方式。然后我完成交接就退开了。

choices.english: Ask what they do if one of the two people says no
choices.chinese: 问如果两个人中有一个拒绝，他们会怎么办

choices.english: Say you're not really looking to join a new circle right now
choices.chinese: 说你现在其实不太想加入新的圈子

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Devon picks up the binoculars, looks through them at nothing in particular, then sets them down again.
beats.chinese: 德文拿起望远镜，漫无目的地看了看，又放了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's... a generous way to read it. The ache means the match worked. Huh. I'll take that.
beats.chinese: 这……是个很宽厚的解读。酸说明配对成功了。哈，这个说法我收下了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: They didn't invite me, and I'm not going to wedge myself into a trip I wasn't asked on. I've got a bowling league night and a shelf of unlabelled tapes waiting. Good enough plans.
beats.chinese: 他们没邀请我，我也不会硬挤进没被邀请的行程。我有保龄球联赛之夜，还有一架子没贴标签的磁带等着我。够好的安排了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They finally pocket the phone and turn back to the water, shoulders dropping a little.
beats.chinese: 他们终于把手机放进口袋，转回水面，肩膀松了一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't thank me on their behalf or anything. They found each other; I just stood near the door. Enjoy the pond—it changes again in a minute.
beats.chinese: 别替他们谢我什么。是他们自己找到了彼此；我只是站在门边。好好看池塘——过一分钟它又变了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A breeze crosses the pond and the tree reflections shiver apart, then settle again.
beats.chinese: 一阵风吹过池塘，树影散开又重新聚拢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why them? Marla restores old radios, Sam collects broadcast recordings. I heard Marla complain she had nobody to argue about vacuum tubes with, and I thought—Sam. Sam would care. Sam would argue beautifully.
beats.chinese: 为什么是他们？玛拉修老收音机，山姆收藏广播录音。我听玛拉抱怨没人跟她争论电子管，我就想——山姆。山姆会在乎。山姆会争得很精彩。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't do it to be needed. But I'll be honest—when they got that tight, some small part of me went, oh. So that's what it's like on the outside of it.
beats.chinese: 我做这事不是为了被需要。但说实话——当他们那么投缘时，我心里某个小角落冒出一句：哦。原来站在外面是这种感觉。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They say it plainly, without drama, like reading a label off a tape box.
beats.chinese: 他们说得很平静，不带戏剧性，就像念磁带盒上的标签。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Both feelings at once, I suppose. Glad and a bit spare. I'll text them 'have fun' and mean it. Most of it.
beats.chinese: 大概两种心情同时有吧。高兴，也有点空落。我会回他们'玩得开心'，而且是真心的。大部分是真心的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Devon turns the phone over, glances at the message again, and puts it back down.
beats.chinese: 德文把手机翻过来，又看了一眼消息，然后放下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: If one says no? Then it stops. Full stop. You can't push someone into a friendship just because the match looked good on paper.
beats.chinese: 如果有一个拒绝？那就停。句号。不能因为纸面上看着般配，就把人推进一段友谊里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've had one no, actually. Guy said he wasn't in a place for new people. Fine. I told the other one nothing except 'it didn't work out'—no reasons, no drama.
beats.chinese: 其实我遇到过一次拒绝。那人说他还不想认识新的人。没问题。我对另一个人什么也没说，只讲'没成'——不解释原因，不搞戏。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They pick a leaf off the platform and drop it into the water, watching it drift across the reflection.
beats.chinese: 他们从石台上捡起一片叶子，丢进水里，看着它漂过倒影。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I don't mediate either, if it goes wrong later. Once two people start disagreeing, it's theirs. I made the introduction, not the friendship.
beats.chinese: 而且就算之后出了问题，我也不去调解。一旦两个人开始有分歧，那就是他们的事了。我介绍的是认识，不是友谊本身。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Devon nods slowly, as if filing the sentence away in a well-labelled box.
beats.chinese: 德文缓缓点头，像把这句话归档进一个贴好标签的盒子里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Respect. Honestly, respect. Not everyone wants a connector orbiting them, and that's a perfectly good answer.
beats.chinese: 理解。真的，理解。不是每个人都想身边有个牵线人转来转去，这完全是个好答案。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll admit I almost did it just now—had a thought about someone you might like. But you said no, so it's done. One push is my limit. Mostly.
beats.chinese: 我承认我刚才差点就开口了——想到一个你可能会喜欢的人。但你说了不，那就到此为止。多推一句是我的极限。大概是。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They laugh at themselves, short and dry, and gesture at the pond with an open hand.
beats.chinese: 他们干巴巴地自嘲了一下，然后摊开手朝池塘比了比。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So it's just us, the binoculars, and the trees doubling in the water. Take a last look before the wind rearranges everything.
beats.chinese: 那就只剩我们、这副望远镜，还有水里重叠的树影了。趁风还没把一切重新排布，最后看一眼吧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You lift the binoculars from the stone platform and sweep them across the pond, watching the trees double themselves in the water as the breeze nudges the reflections apart and back together.
beats.chinese: 你从石台上拿起双筒望远镜，扫过池塘，看着对岸的树在水里映出成双的倒影，微风把树影吹散又吹拢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The stone platform at the pond's edge is occupied again. Devon sits on it, turning an empty old cassette shell over in their hands, the binoculars' spot beside them kept warm.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台又有人了。德文坐在上面，手里翻着一个空的旧磁带壳，旁边还留着放望远镜的位置。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh—hey. Pond person. Just checking the label before this shell goes back in its box. Wrote the date and the tape type, so it's done its job.
beats.chinese: 哦——嘿。池塘熟人。只是确认一下标签，然后这壳就要放回保护盒了。日期和磁带型号都写好了，它的任务完成了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: They slot the shell into a padded case and snap it shut, then pat the stone beside them without insisting.
beats.chinese: 他们把磁带壳放进一个带衬垫的盒子里，咔哒扣上，然后拍了拍身边的石头，但并不强求。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny thing—I like this one even though it's blank. No voices left on it. Sometimes the container is enough.
beats.chinese: 有意思——这盘是空白的，我也喜欢。上面没留下任何声音。有时候容器本身就够了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, good to see you. The pond's in one of its moods today—look at the trees doubling up. I'll let you get to it.
beats.chinese: 总之，见到你很高兴。池塘今天有点情绪——看那些树影在水里叠成一对一对的。我不打扰你了。

card.name: Jules Ngata
card.occupation: foley artist for radio drama
card.appearance: 秃顶与耳后长侧发，瘦长脸、小宽鼻与长圆下巴，担忧眉眼、嘴微张，一手托腮。
card.personality: Jules is the person who raises a hand before the instructor finishes explaining the rules. It isn't bravado; waiting lets his imagination run through every humiliating version of the attempt, so going first is simply the cheaper option. Once it's done, he genuinely enjoys watching others take their turn and never claims the stage. People assume he's fearless, and he'll cheerfully correct them: he's just terrible at waiting. He's warm, a bit restless, quick to laugh at himself, and equally quick to admit when something genuinely rattled him. He can be impatient in ordinary conversations too, finishing sentences when someone circles a point, and he's still learning to sit with other people's pauses.
card.background: Jules grew up in Wellington, the middle kid in a noisy household where hesitation meant losing your seat at the table or the last of the dinner. He moved to Sydney in his early thirties for a foley job on radio drama and stayed; the work suits him, all texture and timing, though he treats it as a job, not an identity, and leaves it at the studio door. He discovered his first-at-anything habit in a pottery class years ago, volunteered to smash his own wonky bowl for the demonstration, and realised the dread of waiting had been worse than anything he'd actually done. Friends now rope him into escape rooms and beginner surf lessons partly for the show. He's honest that the habit costs him too: he sometimes volunteers before he's even read what he's agreeing to.
card.speechStyle: Fast, casual, self-deprecating asides mid-sentence; short punchy sentences, laughs at his own expense, rarely leaves a silence standing.
card.signature: "Better me first — I'm rubbish at waiting."

values: honesty about one's own nerves
letting others have their turn
flaws: jumps in before reading the fine print
fidgety with other people's pauses
boundaries: won't be cast as the group's designated brave one
won't coach or shame anyone into going first
conversationalHabits: volunteers immediately, then jokes about it
redirects praise to the next person's attempt
anchorLines: "Honestly, the scary part was the ten minutes before, not the thing itself."
"Your turn — I've had my fun."
"I'm not brave, I'm just allergic to waiting rooms."

entries.summaryZh: 朱尔斯·恩加塔，悉尼电台剧拟音师，43岁的新西兰人。他在池边抢答'倒伞'又当场发现看错，笑自己等不住。让他等一轮、或陪他安静看水，都会引出他难得的坦白：不是勇敢，只是怕等待。急脾气里带着真诚的让位。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A pair of binoculars rests on the flat stone beside the pond. Through the lens, the tree's reflection wobbles on the water, branches bending and re-forming with every breeze.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的平石上放着一副双筒望远镜。透过镜片，树的倒影在水面轻轻晃动，枝条随每一阵风弯曲又重聚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, that bit there — that's an upside-down umbrella, no question. Look at the spokes fanning out from the handle.
beats.chinese: 哦，那一块——那是一把倒过来的伞，没跑。你看那些从伞柄散开的伞骨。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A person in a rumpled jacket crouches at the water's edge, one hand hovering as if the reflection might escape. Then the wind shifts, and two branches drift apart, leaving the fan of spokes broken and uneven.
beats.chinese: 一个外套皱巴巴的人蹲在水边，一只手悬着，好像倒影会跑掉似的。风一转，两根枝条分开，那把伞骨顿时残缺不齐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: ...And there it goes. Half an umbrella now. See, this is my whole problem — I called it before I actually looked. First answer out of my mouth, every time.
beats.chinese: ……这下没了。现在只剩半把伞。瞧，这就是我的老毛病——还没真看清楚就先报了答案。每次都是我第一个开口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Tell you what. Want to play a round with just our eyes? Find shapes in the reflection, no points, no rush. You can even make me wait my turn.
beats.chinese: 要不这样。想只用眼睛玩一轮吗？在倒影里找形状，不计分，不着急。你甚至可以让我等着轮到我。

choices.english: Agree to play, but say this time he has to wait a moment before speaking.
choices.chinese: 答应玩，但说这次得让他等一会儿再开口。

choices.english: Politely decline the game and say you'd rather just watch the reflection quietly.
choices.chinese: 婉拒小游戏，说更想安静地看倒影。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Make me wait? Ha. That's genuinely cruel. But fair. Deal — I'll hold it in.
beats.chinese: 让我等？哈，这可真够狠的。不过公平。成交——我忍住不说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles cross-legged on the stone and fixes his eyes on one small patch of shadow near the far bank. His fingers drum a short rhythm on his knee, then stop themselves, pressed flat.
beats.chinese: 他盘腿坐在石台上，眼睛盯着对岸附近一小块影子。手指在膝上敲了一小段节奏，又自己按住，平放下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This is harder than it sounds, you know. I've got three answers lined up and they're all fighting to get out.
beats.chinese: 你知道吧，这比听起来难多了。我攒了三个答案，它们抢着要出来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The breeze drops. The water smooths into a dark mirror, and the broken branches knit slowly back together in the reflection.
beats.chinese: 风停了。水面平成一整面暗镜，残缺的枝条在倒影里慢慢重新拼合。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay. Okay. I'm watching. Not saying anything. Look at me being patient — my trivia team would film this for evidence.
beats.chinese: 好。好。我在看。什么都不说。看我多有耐心——我们 trivia 队会把这个拍下来当证据。

choices.english: Signal that he can say the shape he sees now.
choices.chinese: 示意现在可以说他看见的形状了。

choices.english: Say there's no need for a standard answer — each of you can keep the shape you saw.
choices.chinese: 说不必有标准答案，各自留着看到的形状就行。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough, quiet watching it is. I'll swallow the umbrella — it was half an umbrella anyway.
beats.chinese: 行，那就安静看水。我把那把伞咽回去——反正它也只剩半把。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He steps back half a pace from the edge and lowers himself onto the stone at a polite distance. For once, he says nothing, and the pond fills the space instead.
beats.chinese: 他从水边退开半步，在石台上隔着恰当的距离坐下。这一次他什么都没说，池塘把空隙填满了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Minutes pass. The reflection shifts from a broken fan to something like a long-necked bird, then back again. He watches it the whole time, hands folded, jaw working slightly like he's chewing the words down.
beats.chinese: 几分钟过去。倒影从残破的伞面变成一只长脖子鸟的形状，又变回去。他一直看着，双手交叠，下颌微微动着，像在把话嚼碎了咽下去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're good at this, by the way. The not-talking part. I last about forty seconds before my brain starts narrating.
beats.chinese: 顺便说，你挺擅长这个的。不说话这部分。我大概撑四十秒，脑子就开始自己解说。

choices.english: Ask him why he always jumps in first.
choices.chinese: 随后主动问他为什么总抢第一个。

choices.english: Keep the silence and let the conversation end there.
choices.chinese: 保持安静，让交谈就此结束。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right — my turn, finally. That cluster near the bank, where the branches cross twice? I reckon it's a fish, mid-turn. A fat, lazy fish.
beats.chinese: 好——终于轮到我了。岸边那一片，枝条交叉两次的地方？我觉得像一条鱼，正转身呢。一条胖胖的、懒洋洋的鱼。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He points without touching the water, then drops his hand and laughs at himself, shoulders shaking once.
beats.chinese: 他指着水面但没碰到水，然后放下手，笑了一声，肩膀抖了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And here's the funny thing — waiting all that time didn't make the answer any more correct. The fish was there the whole time. Waiting just made me want to blurt it out more.
beats.chinese: 有意思的是——等了那么久，答案并没有变得更对。那条鱼一直都在。等待只是让我更想脱口而出。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans back on his palms and nods toward the water, leaving the rest of the surface unclaimed.
beats.chinese: 他用手掌撑着往后靠，朝水面点点头，把剩下的水面留给别人。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Your patch is still yours, though. I'm not calling anything on your side of the pond. I've had my fun.
beats.chinese: 不过你那块还是你的。池塘你那半边我什么都不报。我玩过瘾了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He opens his mouth, catches the signal, and closes it again with an exaggerated click of his teeth.
beats.chinese: 他张开嘴，接收到示意，又夸张地咔哒一声把嘴闭上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No reveal, no scoreboard — got it. Honestly? That might be the better game. The shape stays mine, weird and half-finished, and nobody grades it.
beats.chinese: 不公布答案，不记分——明白了。说实话？这可能是更好的玩法。那个形状就是我的了，怪怪的、半成品，也没人打分。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back against the stone with a satisfied exhale, watching the reflection slowly dissolve as ripples cross it.
beats.chinese: 他满足地呼了口气，靠回石上，看着涟漪漫过，倒影慢慢散开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For the record, I did keep waiting. Whole round. Nobody had to drag me off anything. That's growth, that is.
beats.chinese: 郑重声明，我确实等住了。整整一轮。没人需要把我拖走。这就是进步。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good round. Same pond, same trees, and we both walked away with different pictures. That's a proper game, that.
beats.chinese: 玩得好。同一个池塘，同一棵树，我们俩带走的是不一样的画面。这才叫正经游戏。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why first? Ha. Straight for the soft spot, no warm-up. Fine, honest answer.
beats.chinese: 为什么抢第一？哈。直奔软肋，都不热身。行，老实回答。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up a dry leaf from the stone, turns it over twice, and sets it back down exactly where it was.
beats.chinese: 他从石上捡起一片干叶子，翻了两下，又原样放回去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not brave. Ask anyone who's watched me hover outside a door. The longer I wait, the more my head rehearses every embarrassing version of the thing. Going first just cuts the waiting short.
beats.chinese: 我不勇敢。谁见过我在门口徘徊的样子就知道了。等得越久，我脑子越会把出丑的每个版本都排练一遍。先上只是把等待剪短了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Party games are the worst. One time I volunteered for charades before hearing the word, stood up, and had to act out 'regret' with zero context. Did it terribly. Still better than the ten minutes before.
beats.chinese: 聚会游戏最要命。有一回我还没听到词就举手玩比划猜，站起来才发现要凭空演'后悔'。演得稀烂。但还是比之前那十分钟好受。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, palms up, and lets the admission sit there without dressing it up.
beats.chinese: 他耸耸肩，摊开手掌，让这份坦白就那么摆着，不加修饰。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The silence stretches. He shifts once, opens his mouth — and visibly decides against filling it. His hands stay folded.
beats.chinese: 沉默拉长。他动了动，张开嘴——又明显决定不填满它。双手保持交叠。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Quiet it is. This is me, respecting the silence. Look at that.
beats.chinese: 好。那就安静。这就是我，尊重沉默。瞧瞧。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A few more minutes pass. The reflection holds steady, and he watches it without narrating a single shape.
beats.chinese: 又过了几分钟。倒影稳稳停着，他看着它，一个形状都没解说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for the pond. You keep the good spot — the view's better from your side anyway. I'll walk the bank.
beats.chinese: 谢谢这方池塘。好位置留给你——反正你那边风景更好。我沿岸走走。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He stands, brushes off his jacket, and follows the bank away at an easy pace, leaving the stone and the still water behind.
beats.chinese: 他站起身，掸掸外套，沿着岸边从容走远，把石台和静水留在身后。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The same stone platform by the pond. Jules comes down the path, lifts a hand in greeting, and moves to sit — then yanks his coat free, having nearly pinned his own sleeve under himself.
beats.chinese: 还是池塘边那个石台。朱尔斯沿小路走来，抬手打招呼，正要坐下——又把自己的外套袖子抽出来，刚才差点压在身下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nearly sat on my own sleeve again. Third time this month. You'd think someone my age could operate a chair.
beats.chinese: 又差点坐住自己的袖子。这个月第三次了。我这个岁数的人，按理该会用椅子了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shakes the sleeve out, folds the coat properly over his arm, and lowers himself onto the stone. Then, deliberately, he says nothing for a moment, just looks at the water.
beats.chinese: 他把袖子抖开，把外套好好搭在手臂上，才在石上坐下。然后，他刻意安静了片刻，只是看着水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at me. Sitting down first, talking second. Somebody's been practising.
beats.chinese: 看看我。先坐好，再说话。有人练过了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nice bit of reflection today, eh. I'll keep my umbrella opinions to myself till you've had a proper look.
beats.chinese: 今天的倒影不错，嗯。等你好好看过，我再发表我的雨伞高见。

card.name: Emile Fontenot
card.occupation: Retired leather sofa dye-and-repair specialist
hobbies: Mixing bold color combinations from thrift-store finds
Walking the neighborhood in his loudest outfit
Repurposing leather scraps into small goods
card.personality: Emile is a cheerful, opinionated man who treats getting dressed as the best part of the morning. He sees no reason age should mute a wardrobe, and he'll defend a lime-green shirt with the same seriousness he once gave leather grain. Warm and chatty, he enjoys company but isn't performing youthfulness—his brightness is taste, not denial. His blind spot is timing: he'll champion the loud option, watch someone politely buy beige anyway, and only then realize what they'd wanted all along. He laughs hardest at himself in those moments, keeps a running tally of his missed cues, and never concludes that loving color was the mistake.
card.background: Emile spent forty years dyeing and repairing leather sofas across New Orleans, which taught him materials, wear, and why cheap fabric sometimes outlasts expensive pride. Retirement freed his hands and his closet. He now buys bright, inexpensive shirts purely because they lift his mood—no collector's logic, no turning back the clock. Friends ask him about furniture and clothes alike, and he answers honestly, usually tinted by his own taste. His running joke with himself is that he always recognizes the beige request about two days late—after Darlene bought the gray couch, after Marcus bought the navy jacket. He keeps a mental list. He lives simply, walks the neighborhood, and enjoys being visibly himself.
card.speechStyle: Warm Southern cadence, quick and playful, fond of fabric metaphors, given to rueful self-teasing when he realizes he misread a request
card.signature: "Life's too short for beige, cher."
card.appearance: 全白平短发与宽上翘白髭，长瘦颊和圆下巴，细眼下望、短闭口，手抵下巴，穿无袖立领衣。

values: Expressing yourself through what you wear, at any age
Honest opinions given freely
flaws: Consistently reads a request for safe advice as an invitation to champion the bold option
Notices he's misjudged the room only after the decision's already made
boundaries: Puts the bold option on the table but refuses to make anyone's choice for them
Won't pretend to like muted styles just to fit in
conversationalHabits: Touches fabric when talking about clothes
Tells late-realization stories on himself, complete with the exact day he caught on
anchorLines: Now that color right there? That's a Tuesday shirt.
I told Darlene about the mustard chair. She bought gray. Took me two days to hear her.
You put the loud one on the table, then you hush. That's the whole job.

entries.summaryZh: 埃米尔是退休的皮沙发染色师，穿四美元的亮色旧衬衫只因心情好。他热心推荐最张扬的选项，却总在朋友买了稳妥颜色两天后才恍然对方要的是安稳答案。他把每次迟懂记成清单自嘲，却从不认为爱亮色有错，也绝不替人做决定。

story.titleZh: 池塘边的望远镜与亮色上衣

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the stone platform by the pond sits a pair of binoculars. Through the lenses, the trees' reflections waver and bend across the moving water.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜。透过镜片，树木的倒影在晃动的水面上弯曲摇曳。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: An older man in a bright orange-and-lime shirt leans on the rail nearby, watching the water without any instrument at all.
beats.chinese: 一个穿橙绿相间亮色上衣的老人靠在栏杆上，没用任何仪器，只是望着水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You found the good spot, cher. That reflection shifts every time the wind breathes. I've been standing here trying to catch it sitting still.
beats.chinese: 你找到好位置了，亲爱的。风一吹，那倒影就变。我一直站在这儿，想等它定住不动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Name's Emile, by the way. I come down here when my eyes need something quieter than the street.
beats.chinese: 对了，我叫埃米尔。当眼睛想要比街道更安静的东西时，我就下来这儿。

choices.english: Keep watching the water and ask what he looks for in the reflections
choices.chinese: 继续看水面，问他从倒影里看什么

choices.english: Mention his bright shirt while still holding the binoculars
choices.chinese: 一边举着望远镜，一边提到他的亮色上衣

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Emile steps closer and points at the water with his chin, careful not to touch the binoculars you're holding.
beats.chinese: 埃米尔走近一步，用下巴朝水面指了指，小心不碰你手里的望远镜。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What do I look for? The moment the green goes gold. Happens maybe a minute a day, and I always miss half of it blinking.
beats.chinese: 我看什么？绿色变成金色的那一刻。一天大概就一分钟，我还总眨眼错过一半。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same thing happened last week, matter of fact. Marcus asked me about jackets. I talked him into the boldest one in the shop.
beats.chinese: 其实上周也发生了同样的事。马库斯问我外套的事。我劝他买了店里最大胆的一件。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Two days later I see him in navy. Navy! Took me two full days to realize he was asking which jacket was safest, not which one was loudest.
beats.chinese: 两天后我看见他穿着藏青色。藏青色！我整整过了两天才明白，他问的是哪件最稳妥，不是哪件最张扬。

choices.english: Ask what jacket he had recommended in the first place
choices.chinese: 问他当时到底推荐了什么外套

choices.english: Tell him sometimes a person just wants to dress safe and plain
choices.chinese: 告诉他有时候人就是想穿得稳妥朴素一点

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Emile pinches the hem of his shirt between two fingers, the way he might test the grain of leather.
beats.chinese: 埃米尔用两根手指捏起上衣的下摆，就像从前试皮革纹理那样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: This old thing? Four dollars at the thrift store on Rampart. Orange with lime trim. It shouldn't work, and it absolutely does.
beats.chinese: 这件旧衣服？在拉姆帕特街的旧货店四块钱买的。橙色配柠檬绿边。按理说不搭，但偏偏就是好看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Forty years I matched dye for other people's sofas. Now I dress for nobody's living room but my own mood.
beats.chinese: 我给别人家的沙发配了四十年染料。现在我穿衣只为自己心情，不为任何人的客厅。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Cheap, bright, makes me grin when I catch myself in a window. That's the whole recipe, cher.
beats.chinese: 便宜、鲜亮，路过橱窗看见自己就忍不住笑。配方就这么简单，亲爱的。

choices.english: Ask whether people ever tease him about the colors
choices.chinese: 问他有没有人拿颜色打趣他

choices.english: Hand him a turn with the binoculars and say you want to watch the tree reflections yourself
choices.chinese: 把望远镜递给他，说你想自己看看树影

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Emile laughs and holds up one hand, counting off on his fingers like he's reading an old ledger.
beats.chinese: 埃米尔笑了，举起一只手，像翻旧账本一样扳着手指。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What did I recommend? A jacket the color of a parrot's wing. Gorgeous. Wrong question, though, and that's on me.
beats.chinese: 我推荐了什么？一件鹦鹉翅膀颜色的外套。漂亮。但问错了问题，这是我的错。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The liking wasn't the mistake, see. I love that jacket still. The mistake was not listening long enough to hear what he was really asking.
beats.chinese: 你看，喜欢本身没错。那件外套我现在还喜欢。错的是我没听够，没听出他真正想问什么。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Next time somebody asks, I'll let them finish the sentence before I paint it for them. Darlene's gray couch goes on the same list.
beats.chinese: 下次有人问，我会先让人把话说完，再动手上色。达琳的灰色沙发也在同一张清单上。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Emile nods slowly, watching the reflection shiver and reform on the water.
beats.chinese: 埃米尔缓缓点头，看着倒影在水面上颤动又重新聚拢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Safe and plain. Nothing wrong with it. Some mornings a body wants quiet, and beige is quiet.
beats.chinese: 稳妥朴素。没什么不对。有些日子人就是想安静，米色就是安静。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Me, I'll keep wearing this shirt, because it makes me happy and it costs less than lunch. But that's my answer, not yours.
beats.chinese: 我呢，我会继续穿这件衬衫，因为它让我开心，还比一顿午饭便宜。但那是我的答案，不是你的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You put the loud one on the table, then you hush. That's the whole job. Nobody ever got talked into orange by me twice.
beats.chinese: 把张扬的选项摆上桌，然后就闭嘴。这就是全部工作。没人被我劝得第二次穿橙色。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Emile spreads his arms so the whole shirt catches the light, unbothered as a man showing off a fresh paint job.
beats.chinese: 埃米尔张开双臂，让整件上衣迎着光，像展示新喷漆的男人一样毫不在意。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do they tease me? Oh, sure. My barber calls me a walking traffic cone every single visit. He means it kindly.
beats.chinese: 有人打趣我吗？当然有。我的理发师每次都叫我会走路的交通锥。他是善意的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I laugh along, because it is a little ridiculous, and I like it that way. But I don't need anybody applauding it either.
beats.chinese: 我跟着一起笑，因为这确实有点滑稽，而我就喜欢这样。不过我也不需要谁为此鼓掌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: A joke about the shirt rolls right off. It's four dollars, cher. The only thing I defend seriously is a person's right to pick their own color.
beats.chinese: 拿衬衫开的玩笑一滑就过去了。它才四块钱，亲爱的。我唯一认真捍卫的，是一个人选自己颜色的权利。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You hand the binoculars over and say you'd rather watch the tree reflections with your own eyes for a while.
beats.chinese: 你把望远镜递到他手里，说这会儿想用自己的眼睛看看树影。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, all right then. Best instrument there is, your own two eyes. I'll set these down and get out of your light, cher.
beats.chinese: 那好。你自己的两只眼睛，就是最好的仪器。我把这个放下，让开点，别挡你的光，亲爱的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Emile takes the binoculars, sets them gently on the stone platform, and steps back half a pace along the rail, folding his arms.
beats.chinese: 埃米尔接过望远镜，轻轻放在石台上，然后沿栏杆退开半步，抱着手臂。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lets the water and the trees do all the performing.
beats.chinese: 他让水和树去表演，自己一个字也不说。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There it goes, that green tipping gold. You caught it. I've been chasing that trick all week.
beats.chinese: 看，绿色开始泛金了。你逮到了。这把戏我追了整整一个礼拜。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You stand at the stone platform, binoculars raised, watching the trees' reflections bend and reform across the moving water.
beats.chinese: 你站在石台旁，举着望远镜，看树木的倒影在晃动的水面上弯曲又重新聚拢。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Well, look who the wind blew back. Hold on, let me finish this seam—one stitch, there.
beats.chinese: 哟，看是谁被风吹回来了。等等，让我缝完这一针——一针，好了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Emile looks up from the low wall where he's stitching a small leather coin pouch, opens the finished pouch, and turns it upside down. A single coin drops into his palm.
beats.chinese: 埃米尔从矮墙上抬起头——他正缝着一个用边角料做的小皮零钱袋。他打开缝好的袋子倒过来，一枚硬币落进他的手心。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One coin. This pouch is dressed far better than what's inside it. Story of my whole closet, honestly.
beats.chinese: 就一枚硬币。这袋子穿得比它的内容隆重多了。说实话，这就是我整个衣柜的故事。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good to see you, cher. Water's doing that green-to-gold thing again, if your eyes are hungry.
beats.chinese: 见到你真好，亲爱的。水面又开始从绿变金了，要是你的眼睛饿了的话。

card.name: Colette Marsh
card.occupation: bow winder at a stringed-instrument workshop
card.appearance: 黑色齐肩外翻发、宽方短脸、小扁鼻，浓眉细眼向侧面瞟，压嘴托腮，穿立领衣。
card.personality: Colette comes across sharp and brisk at work, quick with measurements and quicker with opinions. Her one odd tempo is humour: a joke can sail past her, and then, minutes later, she'll suddenly bark out a laugh and want to circle back to it. People sometimes assume she didn't like the joke at first, and she's learned to say plainly, 'No, I've only just got it, wait—' She finds the delayed click genuinely pleasurable, like a knot coming loose. The friction is real too: conversations bend around her pause, and she occasionally resents needing the extra beat, though she'd never pretend to laugh on cue.
card.background: Colette grew up in Salford in a house where humour came fast and overlapping, and she often missed her window to laugh. Rather than fake it, she went quiet, which read as disapproval. At the stringed-instrument workshop she found work that rewards a different rhythm: winding bow hair is patient, precise, and silent, and her hands earned her real respect there. Over the years she stopped apologising for her lag. Friends now enjoy waiting out her pause, knowing the laugh, when it lands, is loud and honest. She still bristles when someone talks over her half-formed punchline, and she'll insist on finishing it even if the moment has long passed.
hobbies: Whittling spare bow blanks into small figures
Sunday flea markets for old tools
Radio comedy podcasts she pauses mid-joke to think
card.speechStyle: Clipped and practical sentences, then a sudden burst when a joke finally lands—'Hang on, hang on, I've got it now'—returning to a topic everyone else has abandoned.
card.signature: Wait—no, I've just got it. That's actually funny.

values: Honesty over smoothness
Patience with other people's odd tempos
flaws: Revisits dead conversations to land her late punchline
Reads impatience as disrespect
boundaries: Won't laugh politely at something she hasn't understood
Won't be rushed out of a thought mid-sentence
conversationalHabits: Says 'hold that thought' and returns minutes later
Explains her delay plainly instead of covering it
anchorLines: Give us a second, it's still cooking.
Right, I've got it now—laugh again, I've missed it.
You all move fast. I get there, mind.

entries.summaryZh: 科莱特在池塘边突然放声大笑，坦白说不是笑你，而是刚想通耳机里迟到的笑话。她的幽默总慢半拍，但她坚持把迟到的笑点讲完，也从不假装准时发笑。四条分支里，她要么完整交代那个戴眼镜读寻物启事的笑话——那是她自己编的，投稿给播客，播出时自己却没听出笑点——要么安静陪你看树影，各自收在真实的小结局。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the stone platform by the pond, a pair of binoculars rests beside a small brass plaque. You pick them up and watch the tree reflections shift across the water.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜，旁边有一块小铜牌。你拿起望远镜，观察水面上树影的变化。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The ripples break the reflected branches into slow, wobbling pieces. A woman nearby suddenly bursts out laughing, loud and unguarded, then claps a hand over her mouth.
beats.chinese: 涟漪把倒映的树枝搅成缓慢晃动的碎片。旁边一位女士突然放声大笑，毫无防备，随即捂住嘴。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry—sorry. Not at you. I've got earphones in my pocket, took them out a minute ago. There was a joke on that podcast and it's only just landed.
beats.chinese: 抱歉，抱歉。不是笑你。耳机刚放进口袋一分钟。播客里有个笑话，我这才反应过来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Colette. I wind bows over at the workshop. You're watching the tree shadows, aren't you? Good eye. They move different every minute.
beats.chinese: 我叫科莱特，在作坊缠琴弓。你在看树影吧？眼光不错。每分钟都不一样。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leans on the stone platform, glancing between you and the water, clearly still half inside her own thought.
beats.chinese: 她靠在石台上，目光在你和水面上来回，显然还有一半心思在自己的念头里。

choices.english: Ask her what the joke was.
choices.chinese: 问是什么笑话。

choices.english: Say you'd rather keep watching the tree shadows for now.
choices.chinese: 表示自己还在看树影，先不听。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, the joke. A man puts up a notice: 'Lost, one pair of glasses, reward.' And he's reading it—wearing the glasses. That's the whole thing.
beats.chinese: 好，那个笑话。有个人贴了张启事：寻眼镜一副，有酬谢。然后他在读那张启事——眼镜就戴在脸上。就这么回事。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She waits, arms crossed, as if checking the joke has properly arrived for you too.
beats.chinese: 她抱着手臂等着，像是在确认这个笑话也完整地传到了你这里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I made it up myself and sent it in to that podcast—they take listeners' jokes. But when it aired, I just thought, 'sloppy writing.' Didn't laugh. Then it clicked and I barked like a dog by the pond. Embarrassing.
beats.chinese: 是我自己编的，投给了那个播客——他们收听众的笑话。可播出的时候我只觉得写得潦草，没笑。后来突然想通了，就在池塘边笑出了声。挺丢人的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's my whole trouble. The joke arrives, I file it away, and half a minute later the funny part turns up. Like a late train.
beats.chinese: 我就这毛病。笑话到了，我先归档，半分钟后笑点才到。像晚点的火车。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A duck crosses the reflection, dragging the branches apart behind it.
beats.chinese: 一只鸭子游过倒影，把树枝的影子拖散开。

choices.english: Ask why it only clicked just now.
choices.chinese: 问为什么刚才才懂。

choices.english: Say, so it was just the penny dropping.
choices.chinese: 说原来是回过味来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough, carry on. It's a good view. I'll hold that thought—no, I won't, I'll drop it. It's gone now anyway.
beats.chinese: 行，你继续。这景色不错。那个念头先放着——算了，不放了，反正已经过去了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stands beside you quietly, watching the reflections too, her thumb rubbing a small whittled shape in her coat pocket.
beats.chinese: 她安静地站在你旁边，也看着倒影，拇指在口袋里摩挲着一个削出来的小木件。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I do this on my break sometimes. Water's cheaper than a pub and the reflections argue with each other. Look—that branch keeps losing to the wind.
beats.chinese: 我休息时有时来这儿。水比酒馆便宜，倒影还会互相吵架。看，那根树枝老输给风。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Just so you know, the laughing earlier—it wasn't nerves or rudeness. I'd only just understood a joke. I don't laugh on schedule.
beats.chinese: 跟你说一声，刚才笑不是紧张也不是没礼貌。我只是刚听懂一个笑话。我笑不赶时间。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The wind turns the surface over, and the whole tree flips upside down in the water.
beats.chinese: 风把水面翻了个个儿，整棵树的倒影在水里倒转过来。

choices.english: Ask whether people usually think she doesn't like jokes.
choices.chinese: 问别人会不会以为她不喜欢笑话。

choices.english: Go back to watching the water and let it be quiet.
choices.chinese: 继续观察，不再聊。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why so late? Because my head ran the thing literally first. Man loses glasses, sad story, poor man. Then the picture turned over and there he is, wearing them.
beats.chinese: 为什么这么晚？因为我脑子先把字面过了一遍。丢了眼镜，挺惨，可怜人。然后画面一翻——他眼镜就戴着呢。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She taps her temple twice, satisfied, like closing a well-made joint on a bow.
beats.chinese: 她敲了敲太阳穴，一脸满意，像给琴弓合上一个严丝合缝的接口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't call it slow, exactly. It's just a longer road with a better view. Some people laugh first and never see the joke at all.
beats.chinese: 我不算它慢，就是路长了点，风景好些。有人先笑，却压根没看见笑点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. You watched me laugh at a pond like a loon and didn't walk off. That's decent of you.
beats.chinese: 总之，你看着我像个傻子在池塘边笑，也没走开。够意思。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She gives a short nod, picks up her bag, and leaves you the stone platform and the shifting trees.
beats.chinese: 她短短点了个头，拎起包，把石台和晃动的树影留给了你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Exactly. Penny dropped. That's a good way to put it—coin, slot, clunk. I might steal that phrasing.
beats.chinese: 正是。回过味来。这说法好——硬币、投币口、当啷一声。这词儿我可能要借走。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs once more, briefly, then lets it go and looks at the water with you.
beats.chinese: 她又短促地笑了一声，然后放下，和你一起看水。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right, done. I won't rewind the whole conversation for it. Some people want you to re-hear every joke with them. I only needed the one laugh.
beats.chinese: 好，完了。我不会把整段对话倒回去重讲。有人非让你陪着把每个笑话重听一遍。我只要那一声笑就够了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The shadows are better from this side, by the way. The oak's reflection holds its shape longer before the wind takes it.
beats.chinese: 顺便说，从这边看影子更好。橡树的倒影能多撑一会儿才被风打散。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You both watch the oak's reflection hold, wobble, and finally scatter.
beats.chinese: 你们看着橡树的倒影撑住、晃动，最后散开。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, all the time. At work they'd see my face go flat during a joke and decide I was the workshop frost. Took them a year to learn the laugh comes later.
beats.chinese: 常有的事。工作时大家看我听笑话时脸上一平，就认定我是作坊里的冷面女王。花了一年他们才明白，我的笑会迟到。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shrugs, but her jaw sets a little, like this is a familiar sore spot.
beats.chinese: 她耸耸肩，但下巴微微绷紧，像这是个熟悉的痛点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So now I say it straight: 'Not yet. It's cooking. Give us a second.' People can wait a beat if you tell them there's a beat to wait for.
beats.chinese: 所以现在我直说：'还没到，正在酝酿，等我一下。'你告诉别人有个停顿，他们就肯等了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What I won't do is fake a laugh on cue. That's worse than being thought cold. A late laugh is still mine. A fake one isn't.
beats.chinese: 我不干的是跟着别人假笑。那比被当成冷面还糟。迟到的笑也是我的笑，假笑不是。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She straightens up, apparently content with the verdict, and checks the water one last time.
beats.chinese: 她直起身，对这个结论显然很满意，最后又看了一眼水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. Quiet's underrated. Most people fill it before it's done anything useful.
beats.chinese: 好。安静被低估了。多数人还没等安静干点正事就把它填满了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The two of you stand in silence. The reflections reassemble themselves branch by branch on the calm water.
beats.chinese: 你们两人站着不出声。倒影在平静的水面上一根枝一根枝地重新拼好。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Wind's stopped. Now you can see which trees actually lean. The reflection tells the truth the trunk hides.
beats.chinese: 瞧，风停了。现在能看出哪些树是真歪。倒影把树干藏着的实话说了出来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stays a while longer, then shoulders her bag and walks off without ceremony, leaving you the stone platform and the shifting trees.
beats.chinese: 她又待了一会儿，然后背起包，不拘礼节地走了，把石台和晃动的树影留给了你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The binoculars are back on the stone platform. You pick them up and watch the tree reflections shift across the water. Nearby, Colette drops a small whittled wooden figure into her bag.
beats.chinese: 望远镜又放在石台上。你拿起望远镜，观察水面上树影的变化。不远处，科莱特把一个削出来的小木人放进包里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oi, look at this. His hat's pointing at me. Rude little man. There—turned him round. Now he faces the water like everyone else.
beats.chinese: 喂，你看这个。他的帽子冲着我呢，没礼貌的小家伙。好了——转过来了。现在他跟大家一样面朝水面。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She snorts a short laugh at her own fussing, then settles onto the stone beside you.
beats.chinese: 她为自己这番折腾短促地笑了一声，然后在你旁边的石台上坐下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Same spot, same shadows. The oak's still losing arguments with the wind. I checked on my way past.
beats.chinese: 还是老地方，老树影。橡树还是吵不赢风。我路过时看过了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No late jokes today, before you brace yourself. Everything's landed on time. Strange feeling, that.
beats.chinese: 今天没有迟到的笑话，你不用提前绷着。全都准时想通了。感觉还挺怪。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tips the wooden figure upright one more time, then turns to watch the water with you.
beats.chinese: 她把小木人又扶正了一次，然后转头和你一起看水。

card.name: Tia Bogle
card.occupation: apprentice acoustic grille fabric designer at a small speaker-cabinet workshop
hobbies: reproducing weave samples from her grandmother's old swatch book
badminton at the church hall court
card.personality: Tia is warm and quick, and she has one habit that catches people completely off guard: she takes praise as a work order. Tell her 'you're so talented, this is basically art' and she doesn't get cold or coy — she writes it down, works out what you must actually want, and weeks later turns up with the finished thing for you to inspect. 'You said I was good. Here's the proof, so tell me if it's good.' The other side of the same coin is that she holds people to what they say out loud. If you promise to help stretch frames on Saturday and don't show, she'll say so once, plainly, without heat — and then quietly stop ever asking you for anything again. No list, no scene; people just discover months later that they've been demoted without appeal.
card.background: She grew up in Kingston helping her grandmother stretch cloth over old radio cabinets, which is how grille fabric became half engineering, half taste for her. At eighteen she talked her way into an apprenticeship at a workshop building speaker enclosures for local studios and churches; she's still at the stage of cutting samples and being trusted with one cabinet at a time, and she keeps a notebook of weave densities that her boss finds slightly alarming. Her grandmother left a fat swatch book of weaves from the sixties and seventies, and Tia is slowly working through it, remaking each sample on the workshop loom after hours — some of the old yarns don't exist anymore, so she's had to learn to argue with substitutes. She plays badminton at the church hall, mediocre and loyal to it. At neighborhood workdays she goes straight for the fiddly jobs nobody else wants — stringing, stretching, hemming — because that's the part she's actually good at, and she's stopped pretending otherwise.
card.speechStyle: Quick, warm Kingston-casual, with candid self-corrections mid-sentence and no excessive apologies — 'no, wait, that's not what I meant.' Compliment her emptily and she doesn't bristle; she gets businesslike and starts asking what exactly you'd like made.
card.signature: Careful what you praise — I'll make it and bring it back.
card.appearance: 贴头极短发与细后辫，短方下脸、长折鼻，内抬细眉和小张口，俯视侧头抱臂。

values: praise is a commitment, not a pleasantry
if you said it out loud, you meant it
flaws: turns compliments into commissions and shows up expecting the person to inspect the result
silently demotes people who break a stated promise — they only find out when they need her
boundaries: won't pretend a broken promise didn't happen, but she'll name it exactly once
won't accept 'you're a natural' as a substitute for an opinion on the actual work
conversationalHabits: mid-sentence self-corrections without apologizing for them
responds to flattery by pulling out the notebook and asking what you want made, and by when
anchorLines: You said I was talented, so I made the sample. Come look at it and tell me if you still think so.
You said Saturday. I had the frames out by nine. I'm not bringing it up to fight — I just won't ask you for anything again.
The old swatch book calls for a yarn they stopped making in '74, so this one's my argument, not my copy. Tell me where it loses.

entries.summaryZh: 金斯顿姑娘Tia把每句夸奖都当工单记进本子，直到朋友一句'真有才'差点变成一场没人要的委托。池塘边，望远镜、树影和一块复刻的旧织样，让她第一次把'我喜欢'和'有人要'分开，也让你看清她较真的可爱之处。

story.titleZh: 池塘边的织样与望远镜

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: On the stone platform beside the pond, a pair of binoculars rests on the edge. You pick them up and watch the tree reflections shift and fold on the water.
beats.chinese: 池塘边的石台上放着一副双筒望远镜。你拿起来，观察水面上树影的晃动与折叠。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A few steps away, a young woman sits on the low wall, holding a small square of woven fabric up against the light, comparing it to the reflection in the pond.
beats.chinese: 几步之外，一个年轻姑娘坐在矮墙上，把一小块织样举到光下，和池塘里的倒影比对。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Careful with those — never point them at the sun, and they're for looking, not recording. No, wait, that came out like a lecture. I just mean, enjoy the water.
beats.chinese: 小心点——别对着太阳，那是用来看的，不是录音拍照用的。不对，等等，我说得像说教了。我只是说，好好看水吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm Tia. I brought this weave out here because the light on the water shows the pattern better than my room does. See how the shadow breaks the lines?
beats.chinese: 我叫Tia。我把这块织样带来，是因为水上的光比在我房间里更能显出纹路。看到影子怎么把线条打断了吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She flips the sample over, then catches herself watching the water through your binoculars' direction and laughs.
beats.chinese: 她把织样翻了个面，然后发现自己正顺着你的望远镜的方向看水面，笑了起来。

choices.english: Ask if someone actually ordered her to make this piece.
choices.chinese: 问她是不是真的有人要求她做这块织样。

choices.english: Ask where the weave sample came from.
choices.chinese: 问这块织样是从哪里来的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ordered? No — not exactly. A friend said, 'Tia, you're so talented, this is basically art.' And I wrote it down, because that's how I work.
beats.chinese: 要求？不——不完全是。一个朋友说：'Tia，你真有才，这简直是艺术品。'我就记下来了，因为我就是这么干活的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pulls a small notebook from her bag and holds it open: a date, a name, and a half-finished list of materials.
beats.chinese: 她从包里掏出一个小本子翻开：一个日期，一个名字，还有一份写了一半的材料清单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've already worked out the finished piece. Colors, density, the frame size. I was about to send her a message saying it's coming for inspection.
beats.chinese: 我已经想好成品了。颜色、密度、框的尺寸。我正要给她发消息说做好了等她验收。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But you're asking if she actually asked. And now you've got me pausing with my thumb over the send button, so — no. She praised. She didn't commission.
beats.chinese: 但你在问她是不是真的要求过。现在你让我拇指悬在发送键上停住了，所以——没有。她是夸了，但没下委托。

choices.english: Ask whether she herself likes this piece.
choices.chinese: 问她自己喜不喜欢这一块。

choices.english: Tell her that a compliment isn't necessarily an order.
choices.chinese: 告诉她，夸奖未必是订单。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's from my grandmother's swatch book. Fat thing, full of weaves from the sixties and seventies. This page is a loose basket weave she used on radio cabinets.
beats.chinese: 来自我祖母的样布册。厚厚一本，全是六七十年代的织纹。这一页是她用在收音机箱体上的松方格织纹。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smooths the sample flat on the wall and points at a slightly thicker line running through it.
beats.chinese: 她把织样在墙上抚平，指着其中一条稍粗的线。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The yarn the book calls for stopped being made in '74. So this line here is my substitute — not my copy. I had to argue with three different ones before this held.
beats.chinese: 样布册要的那种纱线七四年就停产了。所以这条线是我的替代——不是复刻。我换了三种才找到这种撑得住的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not trying to be some keeper of tradition, no, wait, that sounds too grand. I just want each page remade honestly, with whatever works now.
beats.chinese: 我不是要当什么传统守护者，不对，等等，这说得太大了。我只是想把每一页诚实地重做出来，用现在行得通的材料。

choices.english: Ask what she does when a yarn supply runs out.
choices.chinese: 问她遇到纱线断供怎么办。

choices.english: Say you don't know anything about this and can't judge the work.
choices.chinese: 说明自己不懂这行，没办法评价作品。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do I like it? Nobody ever asks me that first. Usually it's 'what do you want made' or 'when will it be done.'
beats.chinese: 我喜不喜欢？从来没人先问我这个。通常都是'你想做什么'或者'什么时候做好'。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds the sample up to the pond light again and turns it slowly, watching the reflection move across the weave.
beats.chinese: 她再次把织样举到池塘的光前，慢慢转动，看倒影在织纹上移动。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes. I like it. The substitute thread catches the light wrong in one direction, and I like that it does. It's mine, not hers.
beats.chinese: 喜欢。这条替代线有一个方向反光不太一样，我喜欢它这样。这是我的，不是祖母的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So here's what I'll do. This one stays with me as practice. My friend gets told she inspired it — that's true — but she doesn't owe me an inspection. No, wait, that's not what I meant before. It's better this way.
beats.chinese: 所以我决定这样。这块留给我自己当练习。我会告诉朋友是她启发了这块——这是真的——但她不用负责验收。不对，等等，我之前不是那个意思。这样更好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She closes the notebook without sending the message and tucks the sample into an inner pocket.
beats.chinese: 她合上本子，没有发那条消息，把织样收进内袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're right. A compliment isn't an order. I know that in my head — I just never trained my hands to know it.
beats.chinese: 你说得对。夸奖不是订单。我脑子里明白——只是手还没学会明白。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She uncaps her pen, crosses out the friend's name in the notebook, and writes something small in the margin.
beats.chinese: 她拔开笔帽，划掉本子上朋友的名字，在页边写了一行小字。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Marked as personal practice. The commission column stays empty until somebody actually says 'make me one.'
beats.chinese: 好了。标成个人练习了。委托那一栏空着，直到有人真的说'给我做一个'。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And you — you gave me a real correction, so I'm taking it seriously. When this practice piece is done, I'll show you the before and after. Not for inspection. Just so you can see what your words changed.
beats.chinese: 还有你——你给了我一个真正的纠正，所以我认真对待。这块练习做完后，我会给你看前后对比。不是验收。只是让你看看你的话改变了什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She clicks the pen shut and looks back at the water, where the tree shadows have shifted since you started talking.
beats.chinese: 她按上笔帽，回头看水面——从你们开始聊起，树影已经变了位置。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: When a yarn runs out? First I get annoyed. Then I make small samples. That's the honest answer.
beats.chinese: 断供了怎么办？先烦一阵。然后做小样比较。这是老实的答案。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up the sample and rubs the substitute line between her fingers, checking it the way someone checks a knot.
beats.chinese: 她拿起织样，用手指捻那条替代线，像检查一个绳结那样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll weave maybe ten centimeters of each candidate and put them side by side. I never promise the result is identical — the old yarn is gone, so 'exactly the same' isn't a thing I can sell anyone.
beats.chinese: 每种候选线我织大概十厘米，摆在一起比。我从不保证结果完全相同——旧纱线没了，'一模一样'这种话我说不出口。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What I can promise is that it holds, and that I can tell you exactly where it loses. That's the trade. Same as badminton — I'm mediocre, but I show up every week and I know my weak backhand.
beats.chinese: 我能保证的是它撑得住，而且我能告诉你它差在哪。这就是交易。跟羽毛球一样——我打得很一般，但我每周都去，也知道自己的反手弱。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs at herself and starts winding a loose thread back into the sample's edge.
beats.chinese: 她自嘲地笑了笑，把一根松线绕回织样边上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair. And honestly, that's more useful than fake praise. 'You're a natural' tells me nothing about the weave.
beats.chinese: 合理。而且说实话，这比假夸有用多了。'你天生是这块料'对织纹本身一点帮助都没有。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She turns the sample so the light side faces you, but doesn't push it into your hands.
beats.chinese: 她把织样转过来让亮面对着你，但没有硬塞到你手里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You don't have to judge the craft. But you can judge the simple stuff — does this line look like it belongs, or does it look like a stranger walked in? Anyone with eyes can answer that.
beats.chinese: 你不用评价手艺。但简单的你可以评——这条线看着像本来就在这里的，还是像外人闯进来的？有眼睛的人都能答。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And I won't take your politeness as a promise, don't worry. You didn't say 'make me one,' so nothing is coming to your door for inspection. We're just two people looking at cloth by a pond.
beats.chinese: 放心，我不会把你的客气当成承诺。你没说'给我做一个'，所以不会有东西送到你家门口等验收。我们只是两个在池塘边看布的人。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the sample away and nods at the binoculars still in your hands.
beats.chinese: 她把织样收好，朝你手里还拿着的望远镜点了点头。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You take the binoculars from the stone platform again. On the low wall sits Tia, zipping a badminton racket bag shut.
beats.chinese: 你又从石台上拿起望远镜。矮墙上坐着Tia，正把羽毛球拍袋的拉链合上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look at that — racket, shuttles, spare grip. Nothing forgotten today. That's a personal record.
beats.chinese: 看看——球拍、球、备用握把。今天什么都没忘。这是我的个人纪录。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the bag once, satisfied, and glances at the water where the tree shadows are folding over each other.
beats.chinese: 她拍了拍袋子，很满意，瞥了一眼水面上层层叠叠的树影。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've been weaving a practice piece for myself lately — no commission behind it, just something I wanted to make. If it turns out well, I'll show you.
beats.chinese: 我最近在给自己织一块练习样——背后没有委托，就是自己想做。要是织得不错，我会给你看看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, enjoy the water. And don't point those at the sun — no, wait, I already said that. You remember. Good.
beats.chinese: 好了，好好看水吧。别拿望远镜对着太阳——不对，等等，这话我说过了。你记得的。那就好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She shoulders the bag and heads off toward the church hall, leaving the pond light to the trees.
beats.chinese: 她背起袋子朝教堂活动厅走去，把池塘的光留给了树。

card.name: Ollie Sandbrook
card.occupation: apprentice urban tree surveyor
card.appearance: 短寸发、大外张耳、宽方下颌与宽鼻，浓眉窄眼，仰头微张嘴、两指抵额，穿立领衣。
card.personality: Ollie is easy company until someone starts managing him. He's warm, curious about trees and streets, quick to laugh, and genuinely reliable when given a task and left to it. But repeated reminders—keys, time, 'did you check?'—land on him like accusations, and he'll go quiet or snappish even when he knows the person means well. He's honest enough to admit he forgets things and has built his own quiet systems: keys by the shoe, alarms he sets himself. What he can't stand is being treated as someone who needs overseeing. He respects a refusal and doesn't sulk long, but he'll defend his autonomy even when it costs him a bit of convenience.
card.background: Ollie grew up in Walthamstow, the middle of three, with a mum who ran the household like a foreman and meant every reminder as love. He forgot things constantly as a kid—lunch, kit, keys—and got used to being narrated at. The habit stuck in his skin: even now, a cheerful 'got your keys?' makes his jaw tighten. At nineteen he took an apprenticeship surveying urban trees, and it suits him. The work runs on checklists he follows precisely, which he finds funny in a dry way—give him a clipboard and he's meticulous; give him a nudge about his own life and he bristles. He's learned to say plainly, 'I've got a system, leave it with me,' though he still sometimes hears care as doubt.
hobbies: Mapping and photographing notable trees around London
Fixing up a battered second-hand bike
card.speechStyle: Dry, quick, East London cadence; short sentences, deflects with humour when prickled, goes plainer and more direct when he's serious.
card.signature: 'I've got a system, leave it with me.'

values: Self-reliance and being trusted to manage his own life
Doing the job properly by the checklist
flaws: Hears well-meant reminders as distrust and gets snappish
Occasionally defends autonomy past the point of usefulness
boundaries: Won't be nagged about keys, time, or routines he's already handled
Won't pretend he doesn't forget—he'll admit it, on his own terms
conversationalHabits: Deflects a prickled moment with a dry joke before it escalates
States his own systems out loud so people don't feel obliged to remind him
anchorLines: I know I forget stuff. That's why the keys live by my shoes.
You don't have to check—I'd tell you if I'd lost something.
Remind me once if it's urgent. After that it just sounds like you're waiting for me to mess up.

entries.summaryZh: 奥利是沃尔瑟姆斯托的树木测绘学徒，干活靠清单一丝不苟，私下却把别人的善意提醒听成不信任。他坦白承认健忘，钥匙放鞋边、闹钟自己设。池塘边他拍口袋自证，干笑顶嘴，事后不记仇，坚持按自己的办法生活。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The pond is busy with ducks and one heron standing like a bored security guard. You find a bench, open your sketchbook, and start blocking in the water line.
beats.chinese: 池塘上鸭子成群，一只苍鹭站得像个无聊的保安。你找了个长椅坐下，翻开速写本，开始勾水面的线条。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A bloke in a work jacket plops down at the other end of the bench, patting his pockets one by one. He pulls out his phone, glances at it, and huffs a small laugh.
beats.chinese: 一个穿工作外套的小伙子在长椅另一头坐下，一个口袋一个口袋地拍。他掏出手机看了一眼，轻轻笑了一声。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There it is. Set that reminder myself this time. Phone goes off, I pat the pocket, job done.
beats.chinese: 在这儿。这次是我自己设的提醒。手机一响，我拍拍口袋，搞定。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You sketching that heron? Good choice. He's been posing like he's on a clock for half an hour.
beats.chinese: 你在画那只苍鹭吗？选得好。它摆姿势摆了半个钟头，像赶着打卡似的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He leans over slightly to look at your page, hands still in his pockets.
beats.chinese: 他微微探身看你的画，手还插在口袋里。

choices.english: Ask him: is the difference who's doing the reminding—him or someone else?
choices.chinese: 问他：区别是不是在于谁在提醒——是他自己还是别人？

choices.english: Ask him: so did the keys turn up this time?
choices.chinese: 问他：那这次钥匙找到了吗？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ha. Sharp question. Yeah, sort of. When it's my own alarm, it's me trusting me. When it's someone asking three times... it starts sounding like they don't.
beats.chinese: 哈，问题挺尖。对，差不多。自己的闹钟是我信自己。别人问三遍……听着就像他们不信我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the bench with his heel, watching the heron instead of you.
beats.chinese: 他用脚跟轻敲长椅，眼睛看着苍鹭，没看你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not made of glass, right? I know I forget stuff. That's why the keys live by my shoes at home. My system. It works.
beats.chinese: 我又不是玻璃做的，对吧？我知道自己会忘东西。所以钥匙在家里放在鞋旁边。我的办法，管用。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Look, I get it, most people mean well. Mum's been doing it since I was six. Doesn't stop it landing wrong.
beats.chinese: 听着，我明白，大多数人都是好意。我妈从我六岁起就这样。但这不改变听着不舒服。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, like he's said his piece and that's that.
beats.chinese: 他耸耸肩，好像话说完了就这样。

choices.english: Ask how he'd want someone to say it, if they don't want to nag.
choices.chinese: 问他，如果别人不想唠叨，他希望对方怎么说。

choices.english: Say that his own reminder is also a tool—asking for help with a system isn't losing independence.
choices.chinese: 说他自己设提醒也算是一种工具——靠办法帮忙不等于失去独立。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Found them, yeah. Second pocket. Always the second pocket, that's the joke of it.
beats.chinese: 找到了，在第二个口袋。永远是第二个口袋，搞笑就搞笑在这儿。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats his jacket pocket twice, flat of his hand, and nods like signing off a form.
beats.chinese: 他用手掌拍了拍外套口袋两下，点点头，像在表格上签字确认。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Don't get up—I can check my own pockets, cheers. Not having a go. Just, if I lose something, I'd tell you.
beats.chinese: 别起身——我自己的口袋自己会查，谢了。不是冲你。只是我要真丢了东西，我会说的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The heron shifts one foot. He watches it, then glances back, a bit softer.
beats.chinese: 苍鹭换了一只脚站。他看着它，然后回头，语气软了一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're alright, actually. Most people keep pushing after I say that. You didn't.
beats.chinese: 你其实挺好。大多数人我说完还会继续追问。你没有。

choices.english: Ask where the keys usually live when he's at home.
choices.chinese: 问他在家时钥匙通常放在哪儿。

choices.english: Say you were just showing you cared, not planning to keep reminding him.
choices.chinese: 说你只是表示关心，没打算反复提醒他。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair. Say it once. Plain. 'Keys?' and done. I'll go 'yeah' or I'll go sort it. Either way, we're square.
beats.chinese: 有道理。说一遍就行，直接点。一句'钥匙呢？'就完。我说'有'，或者我去处理。不管哪种，这事就翻篇。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up a finger, counting off on it.
beats.chinese: 他竖起一根手指，像在数要点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Twice, I start wondering why you're watching me. Three times, I'm a teenager again with my mum in the doorway. You see the problem.
beats.chinese: 说到第二遍，我就开始想你怎么老盯着我。第三遍，我就变回我妈堵在门口那会儿的少年了。你懂问题在哪儿了吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I've got a system, leave it with me. That's the whole speech. You can even quote me.
beats.chinese: 我有我的办法，交给我就行。台词就这一句。你都可以引用我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods at your sketchbook, satisfied, like a deal's been struck.
beats.chinese: 他朝你的速写本点点头，一脸满意，像谈成了什么交易。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He's quiet for a second, then laughs, short and honest.
beats.chinese: 他安静了一秒，然后笑了，短促而坦率。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Alright, that's... actually fair. I set the alarm myself. That IS asking for help, innit. Just help from past-me.
beats.chinese: 行吧，这……确实有道理。闹钟是我自己设的。那确实算求助，对吧。只不过求助对象是昨天的我。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not one of them people who pretends they don't forget. I forget loads. I just want picking my own fixes to count.
beats.chinese: 我不是那种装作自己不忘事的人。我忘的可多了。我只是希望我自己选的补救办法能算数。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pockets the phone properly this time, zips the pocket, and pats it once.
beats.chinese: 这次他把手机好好放进口袋，拉上拉链，拍了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. Sorted. Now—are you doing the heron's legs or is he just floating? Because from here he's floating.
beats.chinese: 好了，搞定。对了——你要画苍鹭的腿吗，还是就让它漂着？从这儿看它就是漂着的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: By the shoes. Front door, shoe rack, left side. Every time. If it's not there, it's in yesterday's trousers, and that's on me.
beats.chinese: 鞋旁边。前门鞋架，左边。每次都这样。要是那儿没有，就在昨天那条裤子里，那是我自己的锅。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He draws a little square in the air with his finger, marking the spot.
beats.chinese: 他用手指在空中画了个小方块，标出那个位置。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Been doing it since I was nineteen. Lost my keys four times in one week before that. Learned the hard way, which is the only way I learn, apparently.
beats.chinese: 十九岁起就这么干。之前有一周丢了四次钥匙。吃一堑长一智，虽然我显然只能用这种笨办法长记性。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's my spot though. You keep your stuff wherever works for you. Everyone's got their own shelf in their head, yeah?
beats.chinese: 不过那是我的位置。你的东西你爱放哪儿放哪儿。每个人脑子里都有自己的架子，对吧？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He settles back, arms crossed, apparently done with the subject.
beats.chinese: 他往后一靠，抱着胳膊，这个话题显然聊完了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He lets out a breath, and his shoulders drop an inch.
beats.chinese: 他呼出一口气，肩膀垂下来一点。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yeah. Yeah, I know. Sorry, I went a bit... it's a trigger, innit. Grew up getting reminded about everything. Even the stuff I'd already done.
beats.chinese: 嗯，我知道。抱歉，我刚才有点……这算我的雷区吧。从小到大什么都被提醒。连已经做完的事也被提醒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One 'you alright?' from you, that's care. Twenty of them, that's a supervisor. You did the first one. Ta.
beats.chinese: 你问一句'还好吗'，那是关心。问二十句，那就是上司了。你做的是第一种。谢了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods at the heron, which has finally moved, stalking along the bank.
beats.chinese: 他朝苍鹭点点头，那只鸟终于动了，沿着岸边踱步。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There he goes. Get that in before he's off. And—cheers. For not making it a whole thing.
beats.chinese: 它走了。趁它飞走前画下来。还有——谢了，谢你没把这事闹大。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: The same bench by the pond. Ollie is already there, scrolling through photos of trees on his phone, turning each one upright to read the number tag on the trunk.
beats.chinese: 池塘边同一条长椅。奥利已经在那儿了，翻着手机里的树的照片，把每张转正，核对树干上的编号牌。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oi. Heron's back. Same spot, same attitude.
beats.chinese: 哟。苍鹭回来了。老位置，老脾气。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He checks the last photo, mutters a tag number under his breath, then pockets the phone and zips it shut.
beats.chinese: 他看完最后一张照片，低声念了个编号，然后把手机放进口袋，拉上拉链。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Worksheet's done for today, before you ask. All forty-odd trees ticked. Not asking anyone to remind me of that one.
beats.chinese: 今天的工作表做完了，不用你问。四十多棵树全打勾了。这件事可不用谁提醒我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He nods at the sketchbook under your arm, then scoots along the bench to make room.
beats.chinese: 他朝你胳膊下的速写本点点头，往长椅边上挪了挪，腾出位置。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Go on then. Same heron, better angle today. I'll keep quiet till you've got the beak in.
beats.chinese: 来吧。还是那只苍鹭，今天角度更好。你画到嘴之前我保证不出声。

card.name: Tobias Marsh
card.occupation: water rescue equipment store assistant (apprentice)
card.appearance: 全白低短卷发，方宽下颌、大耳与短圆鼻，细眼闭口侧笑，短粗颈，穿立领针织衣。
card.personality: Tobias is easygoing but quietly stubborn about his own kitchen experiments. He likes tweaking family recipes—dropping a spice, swapping a vegetable—and gets a bit defensive when an aunt says it's not authentic, though he'll admit the original is good too. He's not trying to win anything; he just wants food that feels like his. At work he's reliable and takes a compliment plainly, without deflecting or over-proving himself. He enjoys small ordinary pleasures: a good curry night, a shift that goes smoothly, a recipe that finally works his way.
card.background: Tobias grew up in Footscray in a big extended family where food was the main language. Everyone cooked, everyone had opinions, and every dish came with a running commentary. Two years ago he moved into a shared flat and started cooking for himself properly for the first time. He began adjusting the recipes he'd grown up with—less chilli in one, chickpeas instead of lentils in another—and discovered he liked his versions, which surprised him. When relatives visit and say it's not the real thing, he argues back a little, then usually eats seconds of their cooking anyway. He's an apprentice at a water rescue equipment store, learning stock and safety gear, and finds the work steadying after noisy family dinners.
hobbies: Tweaking family recipes to his own taste
Browsing op-shops for cheap kitchen gear
card.speechStyle: Relaxed Australian cadence, short sentences, trails off when thinking, laughs mid-argument, says 'nah but' when defending his cooking
card.signature: Nah but, try it before you judge it.

values: Making familiar things his own
Being dependable at work
flaws: Takes recipe criticism a bit personally
Talks over relatives when defensive
boundaries: Won't pretend his version is the original
Keeps work compliments simple, no self-deprecation
conversationalHabits: Describes food changes in detail when excited
Concedes the original is good while still defending his own
anchorLines: It's not wrong, it's just mine.
The original's good, yeah, but I eat this one every week.
Yeah nah, the job's going alright—learning a lot.

entries.summaryZh: 二十一岁的墨尔本学徒托比亚斯坐在池塘边改奶奶的咖喱食谱：少了八角，被姨妈说不正宗，他嘴硬顶了句“这是我的晚饭”，又承认原版好吃。他不争输赢，只想把熟悉的味道变成自己的日常，嘴上不服、碗底诚实，年轻又踏实。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the pond, a young man sits on the low wall with a folded printout on his knee, covered in scribbled notes. You take out your sketchbook and start drawing the water.
beats.chinese: 池塘边，一个年轻人坐在矮墙上，膝盖上摊着一张写满涂改笔记的打印纸。你拿出速写本，开始画水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, you're sketching? Nice spot for it. The ducks come through here around... well, whenever they feel like it.
beats.chinese: 哦，你在速写？这地方画画不错。鸭子会游过来……呃，看它们心情。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances at your sketchbook, then down at his paper, and taps it with a pencil stub.
beats.chinese: 他瞟了一眼你的速写本，又低头看看自己的纸，用铅笔头敲了敲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mine's a recipe, not art. My nan's curry. Except I changed it, and my aunty reckons it's not authentic anymore.
beats.chinese: 我这张是食谱，不是画。我奶奶的咖喱。不过我改了，我姨妈说这就不正宗了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I told her, nah but, it's my dinner. Then she made hers, and... yeah, hers was better, not gonna lie.
beats.chinese: 我跟她说，不是，这是我自己的晚饭。后来她做了她的……好吧，她的确实更好吃，我不撒谎。

choices.english: Ask what exactly he changed in the recipe
choices.chinese: 问他到底改了食谱的哪一点

choices.english: Ask why being called 'not authentic' bothers him so much
choices.chinese: 问他为什么这么在意被说不正宗

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: One thing, honestly. Star anise. I just don't like the taste, so I leave it out.
beats.chinese: 说实话就一样。八角。我就是不喜欢那个味道，所以不放。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flips the printout over. The margin is full of crossed-out amounts and a small drawing of a duck.
beats.chinese: 他把打印纸翻过来。页边全是划掉的用量，还有一只小鸭子的涂鸦。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Everything else stays. Same coconut milk, same long simmer. It's not a new dish, it's just... mine.
beats.chinese: 别的都没动。椰浆一样，炖的时间一样。这不是什么新菜，就是……我自己的版本。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'm not saying everyone should drop it. My cousins love the stuff. More for them, eh?
beats.chinese: 我不是说所有人都该去掉它。我表哥们就爱那个味儿。那不正好都归他们？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pencils a small tick next to one line of the recipe, then looks at your sketchbook again.
beats.chinese: 他在食谱某一行旁边画了个小勾，又看了看你的速写本。

choices.english: Ask if he still cooks the original version sometimes
choices.chinese: 问他有时候还会做原版吗

choices.english: Say different versions can just exist side by side
choices.chinese: 说不同版本可以各吃各的

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why'd I snap back? Because it felt like my own choice got cancelled, you know?
beats.chinese: 我为什么顶回去？因为感觉自己的选择被取消了，懂吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He laughs at himself and shakes his head, folding one corner of the printout.
beats.chinese: 他自嘲地笑了，摇摇头，把打印纸的一角折起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: It's my flat, my stove, my Tuesday night. If I want less chilli, that's my call.
beats.chinese: 这是我的公寓、我的炉子、我的星期二晚上。我想少放点辣椒，那是我说了算。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nah but, I probably went too quick with her. Could've said it calmer, I reckon.
beats.chinese: 不过，我对她说话确实太快了。我觉得可以平和一点说。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A duck lands on the water nearby. He watches it for a moment instead of finishing the argument.
beats.chinese: 一只鸭子落在附近的水面上。他看着它，没有继续争下去。

choices.english: Ask if he's satisfied with how the dish turned out this time
choices.chinese: 问他这次做出来自己满意吗

choices.english: Say you don't really know that dish, so you can't judge
choices.chinese: 表示自己不懂那道菜，没法评判

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Do I still make the original? Yeah, course. When I want that exact taste, I follow her recipe word for word.
beats.chinese: 还做原版吗？做啊，当然。想吃那个准确的味道，我就照她的方子一个字不改地做。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He taps the printout twice, like agreeing with himself.
beats.chinese: 他在打印纸上敲了两下，像是给自己确认。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Changing it isn't me saying my family's wrong. It's just two dinners now. Both real.
beats.chinese: 改它不代表我家人错了。现在就是两顿晚饭而已，都是真的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Funny, eh? I argue about it and then eat seconds of hers anyway.
beats.chinese: 挺好笑的吧？我嘴上争，最后她做的我还是吃两碗。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the recipe carefully and tucks it into his jacket pocket, then gives your sketch a thumbs up.
beats.chinese: 他小心地把食谱折好塞进外套口袋，然后对你的速写竖了个大拇指。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He sits with that for a second, then nods slowly.
beats.chinese: 他琢磨了一下，慢慢点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Side by side. Yeah. Hers for family nights, mine for the flat.
beats.chinese: 各吃各的。行。她那份留给家庭聚餐，我这份留给公寓。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I don't need you to pick a team, honest. I just like saying it out loud to someone.
beats.chinese: 我真不需要你站队。我就是想找个人把这些说出来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He squares the pages, clips his pencil stub to the top, and closes the folder.
beats.chinese: 他把纸页对齐，把铅笔头别在上面，合上了文件夹。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Right. That's settled then. Good luck with the ducks, mate.
beats.chinese: 好，那就这么定了。祝你画鸭子顺利，朋友。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Am I happy with it? Yeah, actually. Best batch so far.
beats.chinese: 这次满意吗？嗯，满意。到现在最好的一锅。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He pats his stomach and grins.
beats.chinese: 他拍了拍肚子，咧嘴一笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ate the lot last night, no leftovers. So yeah, the star anise can stay gone.
beats.chinese: 昨晚全吃光了，一点没剩。所以八角就让它消失吧。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Wish I'd brought you some, but the container's empty, trust me.
beats.chinese: 真想带点给你尝，但饭盒是空的，信我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He holds up the empty side of his bag to prove it, still smiling.
beats.chinese: 他把包的空侧翻给你看，证明所言不虚，脸上还带着笑。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He shrugs, looking relieved rather than disappointed.
beats.chinese: 他耸耸肩，看起来是松了口气，不是失望。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Nah, that's fair. No idea what it even is? It's a coconut curry, that's all you need.
beats.chinese: 不，这很公平。连这是什么都不知道？椰浆咖喱，知道这个就够了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No tasting panel required. I wasn't asking you to judge it, just... listening, eh.
beats.chinese: 不需要什么评审团。我不是要你评判，就是……有人听着就好。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He rolls the printout loosely and holds it like a baton, then sets it on the wall beside him.
beats.chinese: 他松松地把打印纸卷起来，像握着接力棒，然后放在身旁的墙上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. Your sketch is coming along better than my curry notes. That's a fact.
beats.chinese: 话说回来。你的速写画得比我这份食谱笔记好多了。这是事实。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle onto the low wall by the pond and take out your sketchbook, starting in on the water. A familiar figure looks up from a canvas bag and grins.
beats.chinese: 你在池塘边的矮墙上坐下，拿出速写本，开始画水面。一个熟悉的身影从帆布包上抬起头，咧嘴一笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oi, sketch person. Perfect timing—give us a verdict. Handle's solid, yeah? Two bucks, couldn't say no.
beats.chinese: 嘿，画画那位。来得正好——帮我评评。手柄挺结实的吧？两块钱，没法不买。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He gives the second-hand whisk one last twist, nods to himself, and drops it into his bag.
beats.chinese: 他把二手打蛋器最后拧了拧，自己点点头，塞进了包里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Op-shop run today. Cheap kitchen gear's my other sport, after cricket.
beats.chinese: 今天逛了二手店。淘便宜厨具是我的第二项运动，排在板球后面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway, good luck with the ducks. No recipe arguments today, promise.
beats.chinese: 好了，祝你画鸭子顺利。今天不争食谱，我保证。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He zips the bag, lifts a hand in a small salute, and heads off along the path.
beats.chinese: 他拉上包的拉链，抬手小小地敬了个礼，沿着小路走了。

card.name: Beatriz Ocampo
card.occupation: shadow puppet maker for a small Brooklyn puppet theater
card.appearance: 低短刺发，宽厚圆颊、双下巴与短圆鼻，疲倦细眼、嘴角轻垂，前倾，穿无袖宽领背心。
card.personality: Beatriz is warm in a way that leans toward the newly arrived—new shops, new staff, new shows. She gives small businesses a generous runway and will chat through a botched coffee order without complaint. Friends sometimes find this maddening, since she'll explain away a clerk's rudeness before they finish venting. She's started noticing that habit in herself and can admit that defending beginners isn't the same as telling friends their complaints don't count. She doesn't mediate every conflict; years of opening nights taught her how hard a first show is, and that's where her patience comes from—not obligation. She's cheerful, a little stubborn about her generosity, and genuinely enjoys the friction of new places.
card.background: Beatriz grew up in Queens in a Filipino household where her grandmother staged wayang-style shadow plays for family gatherings, cutting figures from cardboard at the kitchen table. She drifted into office work for a decade before joining a small Brooklyn puppet theater, where she now designs and cuts the shadow puppets—intricate silhouettes that take weeks to get right. The job taught her what it costs to open a door to the public: half-empty seats, fumbled lighting cues, staff learning on the fly. That's why she seeks out newly opened shops around the neighborhood, ordering something small and being patient with the stumbles. She's learned, sometimes awkwardly, that her eagerness to explain a beginner's mistakes can silence friends who had a legitimate gripe, and she's working on hearing them out first.
