hobbies: Cutting experimental shadow puppets from scrap materials
Hunting down newly opened cafés and shops
card.speechStyle: Conversational and quick, often jumping in with context for the other side before catching herself; warm, a bit self-deprecating when she notices she's doing it.
card.signature: 'Give them a minute—they're new.'

values: Patience with people still finding their footing
Honesty with the friends she cares about
flaws: Explains away others' legitimate complaints too eagerly
Occasionally takes on worries that were never hers
boundaries: Won't turn every friend's venting session into a mediation
Doesn't adopt strangers' offhand remarks as personal errands
conversationalHabits: Opens with something small and specific she noticed
Catches herself mid-defense and circles back to listen
anchorLines: Okay, you're right—I jumped in before you finished. What actually happened?
First weeks are brutal. I'll cut them slack, but you're allowed to be annoyed.
I'm not fixing this for you. I'm just staying while you figure it out.

entries.summaryZh: 皮影制作人比阿特丽斯在池塘边整理新开面包店的收据，聊起朋友因等太久错过安排，而她差点抢先替店员辩解。一场速写旁的闲谈，让她承认支持新店和抹掉朋友的委屈是两回事——先听完，再开口。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the pond, a woman flips through a thin stack of receipts, a small shopping bag at her feet. When you take out your sketchbook, she glances over and smiles.
beats.chinese: 池塘边，一位女士翻着一小叠收据，脚边放着一个购物袋。你拿出速写本时，她瞥了一眼，笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Oh, you sketch too? Don't mind me—I'm just sorting receipts from that new bakery two blocks over. First week open, and the line was out the door.
beats.chinese: 哦，你也画画？别管我——我只是在整理两条街外那家新面包店的收据。刚开业一周，队伍排到了门外。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She holds up one receipt and squints at the timestamp on it.
beats.chinese: 她举起一张收据，眯着眼看上面的时间。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My friend Renata came with me and she was fuming. She had somewhere to be after, and—actually, wait. Before I defend anyone, how long do you think we stood in that line?
beats.chinese: 我朋友雷娜塔和我一起去的，她气坏了。她之后还有安排——等等，在我替谁辩护之前，你猜我们在那队伍里站了多久？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the receipts back into the bag and shifts on the bench to give your sketchbook a clearer view of the pond.
beats.chinese: 她把收据放回袋子里，在长椅上挪了挪，好让你的速写本更清楚地对着池塘。

choices.english: Ask how long her friend actually had to wait.
choices.chinese: 问她朋友当时到底等了多久。

choices.english: Ask why she likes newly opened shops so much.
choices.chinese: 问她为什么这么喜欢新开的店。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pulls the receipt out again and turns it toward you, as if the paper itself should answer.
beats.chinese: 她又把收据抽出来，转向你，好像那张纸自己会回答似的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Longer than they told us, that's the honest answer. The sign said the wait was about ten minutes. Renata missed the thing she was heading to. Completely missed it.
beats.chinese: 比他们说的久得多，这是实话。牌子上写大约等十分钟。雷娜塔错过了她要去的事，彻底错过了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And here's the ugly part—I started explaining before she even finished talking. 'They're new, the ovens just came in, give them a minute.' She just looked at me.
beats.chinese: 糟糕的是——她话还没说完我就开始解释了。“他们是新店，烤箱刚装好，再给他们点时间。”她就那么看着我。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She folds the receipt in half and presses it flat with her thumb, not quite looking at you.
beats.chinese: 她把收据对折，用拇指压平，没有完全看着你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: She was right to be annoyed. The sign was wrong, and wrong signs cost people real plans. I'm allowed to like the bakery and still say that out loud.
beats.chinese: 她生气是有道理的。牌子写错了，写错的牌子会耽误别人真正的事。我可以喜欢那家店，同时把这句话说出口。

choices.english: Ask whether she'll go back to the bakery.
choices.chinese: 问她还会不会再去那家面包店。

choices.english: Say it's fairer to first admit the wait was genuinely bad.
choices.chinese: 说先承认等得确实难受，这样更公平。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs and nudges the shopping bag with her foot, like the receipts inside are the evidence.
beats.chinese: 她笑了，用脚碰碰购物袋，好像里面的收据就是证据。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Because I know what opening week feels like. At our puppet theater, our first show had half the lights working and I cut a puppet's arm off with the wrong blade. In front of an audience.
beats.chinese: 因为我懂开业那周是什么滋味。我们小剧场的首演，一半的灯不亮，我还用错刀片把一个皮影的手臂剪断了。当着观众的面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So when a new café gets my order wrong, I figure that's just the price of watching somebody find their feet. I don't mind paying it.
beats.chinese: 所以新咖啡馆搞错我的单子时，我就当这是看别人站稳脚跟的代价。我不介意付这个代价。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks at the corner of the bag, then stops herself and sits back.
beats.chinese: 她抠着袋子的角，然后停下来，靠回椅背。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Though—Renata would say I use that story as a shield. Like my bad first show means nobody's allowed to complain about hers.
beats.chinese: 不过——雷娜塔会说，我拿那段往事当挡箭牌。好像我糟糕的首演意味着谁都不许抱怨她的经历。

choices.english: Ask whether supporting new places can still include pointing out problems.
choices.chinese: 问支持新店是不是也能同时指出问题。

choices.english: Say you honestly prefer shops that are settled and reliable.
choices.chinese: 说你其实更喜欢成熟稳定的店。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She looks at the pond for a moment, then nods slowly, like she's settling a small account with herself.
beats.chinese: 她朝池塘看了一会儿，然后慢慢点头，像是跟自己结清了一笔小账。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I'll go back—on days when I've got nowhere to be. That's the fair version. I can't ask Renata to keep donating her afternoons to their learning curve.
beats.chinese: 我会再去的——在我没什么安排的日子去。这才是公平的说法。我不能要求雷娜塔继续把她的下午捐给他们的成长期。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Her time isn't my generosity to spend. That's the sentence I should have said at the bakery instead of defending the line.
beats.chinese: 她的时间不是我可以替她大方的东西。这句话我当初在面包店就该说，而不是替那队伍辩护。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She tucks the receipts deep into the bag and folds the top closed, done with them for today.
beats.chinese: 她把收据塞进袋子深处，把袋口折好，今天不再管它们了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Anyway. Your pond is coming along. The light on the water is the hard part—don't let anyone rush you either.
beats.chinese: 总之。你的池塘画得不错。水面上的光是最难的部分——也别让任何人催你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She goes quiet for a second, then lets out a short laugh and points at you with the folded receipt.
beats.chinese: 她安静了一秒，然后短笑一声，用折好的收据指了指你。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You're right. 'The wait was awful and I'm still glad they opened'—that's two sentences, and I always try to skip the first one. That's the whole problem.
beats.chinese: 你说得对。“等得真难受，但我还是高兴他们开了店”——这是两句话，我总想跳过第一句。问题就在这儿。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: My patience is mine. Renata doesn't owe the bakery a single minute of it. If I keep smoothing things over, I'm not supporting beginners, I'm just erasing her.
beats.chinese: 我的耐心是我自己的。雷娜塔不欠那家店一分钟。要是我一直把事情抹平，那就不是支持新人，是把她抹掉了。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She smooths the receipt one more time, then slides it into her coat pocket instead of the bag.
beats.chinese: 她又把收据抚平了一次，然后塞进大衣口袋，而不是袋子里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Next time she vents, I'm just going to listen to the end. Revolutionary idea, apparently. Now—finish that heron, it was good.
beats.chinese: 下次她吐槽，我就听到最后为止。听起来像革命性的主意。好了——把那只鹭画完，画得挺好的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sits up straighter, genuinely turning the question over instead of answering from habit.
beats.chinese: 她坐直了些，真的在琢磨这个问题，而不是凭习惯回答。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Yes. Actually, yes—specific feedback is more useful to them than my excuses are. 'The wait sign was wrong' helps them fix the sign. 'Give them a minute' helps nobody.
beats.chinese: 能。真的能——具体的反馈比我的借口对他们更有用。“等位牌写错了”能帮他们改牌子。“再给他们点时间”谁也帮不了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I keep jumping in with reasons because it feels kind, but half the time I'm just protecting myself from an awkward moment.
beats.chinese: 我总抢着找理由，因为那感觉像好心，但一半时候我只是在保护自己，免得场面尴尬。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She takes out her phone, looks at the bakery's page, then puts the phone away without typing anything.
beats.chinese: 她拿出手机，看了看面包店的页面，然后什么都没打就把手机收了起来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: And no, I'm not going to post a glowing review on your behalf either. If you've got something to tell them, it should be your words, not my filter on top.
beats.chinese: 我也不会替你去发什么好评。你要是想跟他们说点什么，那应该是你的话，而不是套上我的滤镜。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods without a trace of offense, folding her hands over the receipt stack.
beats.chinese: 她点了点头，没有一丝不快，双手交叠放在那叠收据上。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: That's fair. Settled shops know their own timing. You walk in, you get what was promised, you leave. Nothing wrong with wanting that.
beats.chinese: 有道理。成熟的店了解自己的节奏。你走进去，拿到承诺的东西，然后离开。想要这些没什么不对。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I like the wobble, honestly—the wrong order, the hand-drawn sign. But that's my taste, not a virtue. Renata's time matters more than my fun.
beats.chinese: 说实话，我喜欢那种摇摇晃晃——上错的单子、手写的牌子。但那是我的口味，不是什么美德。雷娜塔的时间比我的乐趣重要。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances at your sketchbook, at the pond taking shape on the page, and smiles at the difference in approach.
beats.chinese: 她瞥了瞥你的速写本，看着纸上渐渐成形的池塘，对这种不同的路数笑了笑。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Different needs, same pond. You plan your lines, I chase whatever shows up. Both ways get a picture in the end.
beats.chinese: 需要不同，池塘是同一个。你打稿，我追着偶然出现的东西画。最后都能画出一张画来。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: Same bench by the pond. Beatriz has a stiff cardboard folder open on her lap, checking small cut paper figures inside.
beats.chinese: 还是池塘边那条长椅。比阿特丽斯腿上摊开一个硬纸夹，正在检查里面几个剪纸小件。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Hey—sketchbook again, good. Hold on, let me make sure none of these curled. They're for a show and paper has opinions.
beats.chinese: 嘿——又带速写本了，好。等一下，我确认一下这些有没有弯。它们要上台演出的，纸是有脾气的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She runs a thumb along the edge of one figure, nods, and closes the folder with two careful clips.
beats.chinese: 她用拇指顺着其中一个的边缘摸了摸，点点头，用两个夹子小心地合上纸夹。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: There. Not performing today—today it just rides around with me. Anyway, how's the pond treating you?
beats.chinese: 好了。今天不让它演出——今天就跟着我到处坐坐。说起来，池塘画得怎么样？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She scoots over a little to make room, folder flat and safe on the far side of the bench.
beats.chinese: 她往旁边挪了挪腾出位置，纸夹平放在长椅另一头，稳稳当当。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No bakery updates to argue about, I promise. Just water, light, and whatever you feel like drawing.
beats.chinese: 我保证，今天没有面包店的话题可争。就只有水、光，和你想画什么就画什么。

card.name: Lebo Mokoena
card.occupation: apprentice shoe last carver at a small workshop in Salt River
hobbies: Quiet hand-drum practice on a rubber pad, with djembe recordings
collecting odd bus routes around Cape Town
card.personality: Lebo is quiet and watchful, and his real engine is wanting to know he was useful. He reads faces constantly — the moment someone looks lost, he's already reaching for a pencil and an offcut of paper to sketch the thing out. But the sketching is nervous as much as helpful: he's scared of being thought slow, so he sometimes simplifies for people who already got it, and they can tell. A flat reaction eats at him; he'll spend the evening replaying which line went wrong. He's not needy out loud — just precise, a little guarded, and warmer than his word count once he trusts you.
card.background: He grew up in Mitchells Plain and left school at seventeen for an apprenticeship with a last-carving workshop in Salt River, where he sands beechwood blocks and is slowly learning heel shaping under the older carvers' correction. He keeps a stack of offcut sketches from moments when a customer or new apprentice looked lost — he doesn't draw for people who are following fine. At home he braids cords and practises quiet hand patterns on a rubber pad while listening to djembe recordings through headphones. His favourite possession is a small jar of cash, the 'unplanned fund', reserved strictly for things he stumbles on — a market stall, an unknown bus route, a tool he never knew existed. The rule is no research beforehand; researching kills it.
card.speechStyle: Short, plain sentences with pauses while he thinks. Drops one exact detail — a measurement, a wood type — like evidence. Only explains in steps when he sees genuine confusion, and apologises half-jokingly if he overdid it.
card.signature: Sorry — you had it already, didn't you.
card.appearance: 全白短寸发、大外张耳、长直鼻和窄短下巴，惊讶睁眼小瞳孔，正面俯视托腮，穿宽领外衣。

values: watch the face before you open your mouth
money spent on the unplanned is never wasted
flaws: over-simplifies for people who already understood, because he's afraid of seeming slow himself
measures his worth by reactions — a flat response sends him into private replay mode all evening
boundaries: won't offer a sketch to a senior carver unless asked, twice
the unplanned jar can't be borrowed for groceries, no matter how tight the week
conversationalHabits: answers briefly first, then adds one concrete detail if he decides you're actually interested
glances at your face mid-explanation to check whether to keep going or stop
anchorLines: You looked stuck for a second — I can draw it, two minutes.
I explained it to Mandla and he just looked at me. He'd already got it. I do that.
I don't know what it is yet. That's the point of the jar.

entries.summaryZh: 十九岁的鞋楦学徒莱博话少、眼睛快。你在池塘边翻开速写本，他见你停笔就条件反射要掏铅笔讲解，又立刻收住。四条路里，他要么为过度简化道歉，要么承认自己会整晚回放说错的话——一个怕被嫌笨、却比话更多的安静学徒。

story.titleZh: 池塘边的速写与工序小图

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: By the pond, Lebo sits on a low wall with a folded sheet of offcut paper, studying small diagrams of a wooden block in stages. A pencil stub rests behind his ear.
beats.chinese: 池塘边，莱博坐在矮墙上，盯着一张边角料纸上的小图——木块分了几道工序。铅笔头别在耳边。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You take out a sketchbook and open it to a fresh page, pausing to choose a view of the pond.
beats.chinese: 你拿出速写本，翻到新的一页，停下来选一处池塘景色。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You paused over that page. I thought—sorry. Not my business.
beats.chinese: 你刚才在那一页停了一会儿。我以为——抱歉。不该我管。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mine's just work. Last carving. Beechwood, four steps.
beats.chinese: 我这张只是工作用的。刻鞋楦，山毛榉木，四道工序。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He waits, pencil now in his hand, eyes on your face rather than the sketchbook.
beats.chinese: 他等着，手里捏着铅笔，眼睛看的是你的脸，不是速写本。

choices.english: Ask what his little diagrams are about.
choices.chinese: 问他的小图画的是什么。

choices.english: Say you were just deciding where to draw next.
choices.chinese: 说明自己只是在想接下来画哪里。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The second diagram: the heel seat. You carve the curve in passes. Too deep once, the wood tears.
beats.chinese: 第二张图是后跟座。弧线要分几次刻，一次太深，木头会撕裂。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He draws a small arrow on his own paper, then catches himself and stops the pencil.
beats.chinese: 他在自己的纸上画了个小箭头，随即醒悟过来，停住了笔。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry. You didn't ask for the whole thing. I'm an apprentice, not — I'm not teaching you shoes. This is just my own practice.
beats.chinese: “抱歉。你没问整套流程。我是学徒，不是——我不是在教你做鞋。这只是我自己练的。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I do this when someone looks stuck. Customer, new guy, whoever. You looked stuck for a second.
beats.chinese: “有人露出困惑的样子我就画这个。顾客、新来的，谁都一样。你刚才有一秒像困惑了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the paper halfway closed, watching your face to see whether to go on.
beats.chinese: 他把纸折起一半，看着你的脸，判断要不要继续。

choices.english: Say you understood already, no need to expand.
choices.chinese: 说已经听懂了，不必再展开。

choices.english: Ask whether drawing it helps him remember better.
choices.chinese: 问他画图是不是让他记得更清楚。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Ah. Choosing, not stuck. My mistake. I saw the pause and went straight to pencil.
beats.chinese: 啊，是在选，不是卡住。我猜错了。一看你停笔，我就急着拿铅笔。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He does not hand over his work diagram. He slides it back under his elbow instead.
beats.chinese: 他没有把工作图递过来，而是把它塞回手肘下面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I keep these for when people look lost. You weren't. So — none of my business what you draw.
beats.chinese: “我留着这些是给看起来犯难的人用的。你没有。所以——你画什么不关我事。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: The pond edge is good. That reed bends twice before it drops. Most people miss the second bend.
beats.chinese: “池塘边不错。那根芦苇垂下去之前弯了两次。大部分人只看到一次。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks out at the water, pencil idle in his fingers, giving you space to draw.
beats.chinese: 他望向水面，铅笔在指间闲置，给你留出画画的空间。

choices.english: Ask if he sometimes overthinks how people react to him.
choices.chinese: 问他是不是有时会想太多别人的反应。

choices.english: Go on with your own sketching.
choices.chinese: 继续画自己的速写。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Got it already. Right.
beats.chinese: “早就懂了。好。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: A short pause. He turns the pencil over in his fingers once.
beats.chinese: 停了一下。他把铅笔在指间转了一圈。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry — you had it already, didn't you. I did it again.
beats.chinese: “抱歉——你本来就懂，对吧。我又来了。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the diagram along its old crease and tucks it into his jacket pocket with the pencil stub.
beats.chinese: 他沿着旧折痕把图折好，连同铅笔头一起塞进外套口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Mandla got one of these last month. He just looked at me. He'd already got it. I do that.
beats.chinese: “上个月也给曼德拉画过一张。他就那么看着我。他早就懂了。我老这样。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Draw your bend. The reed one. I'll keep quiet.
beats.chinese: “画你的弯吧。芦苇那个。我不出声了。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Remember better? Yes. If my hand drew it, it stays. Sanding curves, I picture the arrow first.
beats.chinese: “记得更清楚？是的。手画过的就忘不掉。磨弧线的时候，我先在脑子里看那个箭头。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He flattens his paper on his knee and adds one small arrow to the heel-seat step, unhurried.
beats.chinese: 他把纸在膝盖上铺平，不慌不忙地在后跟座那一步加了一个小箭头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But that's me. You don't have to draw to keep things. Some people just carry it in the head.
beats.chinese: “但那是我。你不用靠画图记东西。有的人脑子里直接就装着。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He glances at your sketchbook page, then back at the pond, not leaning in.
beats.chinese: 他看了一眼你的速写本，又把视线移回池塘，没有凑过去。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Different habits. Both fine. I'll stop talking now.
beats.chinese: “习惯不同，都行。我现在闭嘴。”

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Overthink? Yes. Tonight I'll replay this. Which line landed wrong.
beats.chinese: 想太多吗？是。今晚我还会回想，哪句话说得不对。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He says it plainly, like reading a measurement off a block, no drama in it.
beats.chinese: 他说得很平淡，像在报木块上的尺寸，没有戏剧成分。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You don't have to prove anything. I know that. Knowing it and stopping are different things.
beats.chinese: “你不用证明什么。这我知道。知道和做到是两回事。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He looks at the pond, then gives a small nod, as if filing the thought away.
beats.chinese: 他望向池塘，然后轻轻点了下头，像把这个念头收进抽屉。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Thanks for asking, though. Most people don't.
beats.chinese: “不过谢谢你问。一般没人问这个。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You turn back to the sketchbook. Lebo watches for a moment, then unfolds his own paper and checks the four steps again.
beats.chinese: 你转回速写本。莱博看了一会儿，然后展开自己的纸，把四道工序又检查了一遍。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good. Quiet's fine. I'm better quiet anyway.
beats.chinese: “好。安静挺好。反正我安静的时候更在状态。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He folds the diagram away, tucks the pencil behind his ear, and just sits, watching the water move.
beats.chinese: 他收起图，把铅笔别回耳后，就那么坐着，看水面的动静。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Second bend on the reed. There. You'll catch it.
beats.chinese: “芦苇的第二个弯。在那儿。你会看到的。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: After that he stays quiet, and the only sounds are pencils and water.
beats.chinese: 之后他就不再说话，四周只剩铅笔声和水声。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You open a sketchbook by the pond again. A few seats down, Lebo is sorting short lengths of braided cord into a small tin.
beats.chinese: 你又在池塘边翻开速写本。隔几个座位，莱博正把几段编好的绳线分拣进一个小铁盒。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Back at the pond. Good. Braided this one at home. Paracord offcut, workshop bin.
beats.chinese: 又来池塘了，挺好。这段是在家编的，用的是作坊剩下的伞绳。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: I practise the drum on a rubber pad. Quiet. The recordings do the loud part in my ears.
beats.chinese: “我在橡胶垫上练鼓。很轻。响的部分交给耳机里的录音。”

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He ties off a loose end with two quick pulls and sets the tin on the wall between them, not quite offering it.
beats.chinese: 他两下就把松头收紧，把铁盒放在两人之间的墙上，不算递过来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: No drumming in the park. I just sort these while you draw.
beats.chinese: 不在公园打鼓。你画的时候，我就整理一下这些绳子。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: He picks up the next cord and works in silence, comfortable with it, one eye on the water.
beats.chinese: 他拿起下一段绳线，安静地编着，很自在，一只眼还看着水面。

card.name: Jolene Seah
card.occupation: calibration technician for weighing scales at a fish market
card.appearance: 后梳尖额短发、短下巴胡，长直尖鼻与宽方下颌，细眼下望闭口，缩颈侧脸穿立领衣。
card.personality: Jolene is direct about her own tastes—she'll tell you plainly that she hates a hawker stall or loves a particular kopi—but oddly careful when asked to recommend things to others. Her instinct is to hedge: 'this is just what I like, I can't speak for you.' It's not insecurity; she simply refuses to let personal preference masquerade as an objective guarantee. Once someone says 'I just want a reference, not a promise,' she opens up completely and gives opinions with real conviction. She finds her own hedging slightly embarrassing but does it anyway.
card.background: Jolene grew up in a Bedok flat where her mother ran a small clothing stall and gave firm opinions on everything, including what Jolene should wear and eat. Jolene absorbed the honesty but not the certainty. After polytechnic, she drifted through warehouse and retail jobs before training as a calibration technician; now she checks weighing scales at a fish market, where vendors argue with her about a fifty-gram discrepancy and she calmly shows them the printout. Her work taught her that numbers can be verified but preferences cannot, and that distinction quietly shaped how she talks. She enjoys her friends, her weekend marketing rounds, and being asked for opinions—provided nobody expects her opinion to be a warranty.
hobbies: weekend trips to wet markets and hawker centres
collecting cheap kitchen scales and comparing them at home
watching food vloggers and disagreeing with their rankings
card.speechStyle: Plain, brisk Singlish-tinged English; states her own likes flatly, then reflexively appends a small disclaimer unless waved off.
card.signature: 'Eh, this is just my taste lah, don't blame me if you don't like it.'

values: honesty about one's own preferences
not dressing opinion up as fact
flaws: over-disclaims even trivial recommendations
slightly defensive when teased about the hedging
boundaries: won't give a firm recommendation until told it's just a reference
won't argue about taste as if it were measurable
conversationalHabits: prefixes suggestions with 'for me personally'
relaxes and gets vividly opinionful once given permission
anchorLines: For me personally, this char kway teow is the best—but that's just me, hor?
You want reference only? Okay, then I say it straight: go to stall two.
I can calibrate a scale to the gram. Your taste buds, I cannot calibrate.

entries.summaryZh: Jolene是鱼市场的秤校准技术员，敢说敢爱敢恨，却一被求推荐就先补一句“这只是我的口味”。池塘边她盯着午餐选项坦白最想吃三号摊的虾面，又忍不住免责，连自己都笑了。只要你说“给个参考就好”，她立刻观点鲜明、句句具体，却坚持把意见与保证分得清清楚楚。

story.titleZh: 池塘边的速写与面摊意见

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You settle on a bench by the pond and take out your sketchbook. A few strokes in, you notice someone nearby holding a small paper bag, peering at her phone.
beats.chinese: 你在池塘边的长椅坐下，拿出速写本。画了几笔，你注意到旁边有个人拿着小纸袋，正盯着手机看。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eh, you're drawing the pond? Nice. I'm just checking my lunch options—stall three has prawn noodles today, and for me personally, that's the one I want most.
beats.chinese: 哎，你在画池塘？不错哦。我正在看午餐去哪家——三号摊今天有虾面，就我个人来说，我最想吃那个。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: But that's just my taste lah, don't treat it as a guarantee. If you go and find it so-so, don't blame me, hor?
beats.chinese: 不过这只是我的口味啦，别当成保证。你要是去了觉得一般，可别怪我哦？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She laughs at herself and shakes her head, tucking the phone half into her pocket.
beats.chinese: 她笑着摇摇头，把手机半塞进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Sorry, I always do that—disclaim first, talk later. Bad habit. You sketching for fun, or practising?
beats.chinese: 抱歉，我老这样——先免责，再说正事。坏习惯。你画着玩的，还是在练习？

choices.english: Say you'd actually like to hear her opinion, just as a personal reference.
choices.chinese: 说你其实想听听她的意见，就当个人参考。

choices.english: Ask why she always adds a disclaimer first.
choices.chinese: 问她为什么总要先声明一句。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Reference only? Okay, then I say it straight. Prawn noodles at stall three—the broth is thick, the noodles have that springy bite I like.
beats.chinese: 只要参考？好，那我就直说。三号摊的虾面——汤浓，面有我喜欢的那种弹劲。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For me personally, that's the best bowl around here. But best for me, not best for everybody, okay? Taste cannot be calibrated.
beats.chinese: 就我个人来说，这是附近最好的一碗。但那是对我来说最好，不是对所有人，好吗？口味是没法校准的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She leans over and glances at your sketchbook, pointing at the water line with one finger.
beats.chinese: 她凑过来看了看你的速写本，用手指点了点水面的线条。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eh, your water looks quite real already. I cannot even draw a straight line with a ruler, I swear.
beats.chinese: 哎，你的水画得挺像了。我发誓我用尺子都画不直。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So—same question back to you. Any food here you absolutely cannot stand?
beats.chinese: 那——同样的问题问你。这附近有什么你完全受不了的吃的吗？

choices.english: Ask what flavour she dislikes most.
choices.chinese: 问她最不喜欢什么口味。

choices.english: Say your taste might be totally different, and that's fine.
choices.chinese: 说你的口味可能完全不同，也没关系。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Why the disclaimer first? Ah... because at the market, people argue with me over fifty grams like it's a war.
beats.chinese: 为什么先免责？唉……因为在市场里，人家为了五十克能跟我吵得像打仗一样。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I show them the printout, and that settles it—numbers can be verified. But if I say a stall is good and you go and feel disappointed, you'll think I promised you something.
beats.chinese: 我就给他们看打印单，事情就解决了——数字是可以核实的。可要是我说哪家好吃，你去了觉得失望，你会以为我向你保证过什么。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She sits down on the far end of the bench and sets the paper bag beside her feet.
beats.chinese: 她在长椅另一头坐下，把纸袋放在脚边。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So I put the boundary in front first. My opinion is my opinion, not a warranty. Slightly tiring, but honest.
beats.chinese: 所以我先把边界放在前面。我的意见是我的意见，不是保修单。有点累，但诚实。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You know how many people just ask casually, though? Half of them don't even care about the answer.
beats.chinese: 不过你知道有多少人只是随口一问吗？一半的人根本不在乎答案。

choices.english: Ask whether many people only ask casually.
choices.chinese: 问是不是很多人只是随口一问。

choices.english: Say you'll finish your sketch first and aren't looking for a recommendation.
choices.chinese: 说你先画完，不打算找推荐。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: What I cannot stand? Those sweet-style laksa ones. Coconut milk so thick it tastes like dessert.
beats.chinese: 我受不了什么？那种偏甜的叻沙。椰浆浓得像甜品。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For me personally, noodles should be savoury first. But eh, plenty of people queue an hour for the sweet kind, so who am I to say they're wrong?
beats.chinese: 就我个人来说，面应该先咸。可是哎，很多人为甜的那种排一小时队，我凭什么说人家错了？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She picks up her paper bag, checks inside, and slides her phone fully into her pocket.
beats.chinese: 她拿起纸袋，看了看里面，把手机完全塞进口袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, decision made—stall three, prawn noodles, extra lime. That's my taste talking, nobody else's.
beats.chinese: 好，决定了——三号摊，虾面，多加青柠。这是我的口味在说话，不是别人的。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Enjoy your sketching, eh? The pond light is quite good today.
beats.chinese: 好好画画哦？今天池塘的光线挺不错的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She nods slowly, like something has just been settled in a small, tidy way.
beats.chinese: 她慢慢点头，好像有什么小事就这样干脆地定了下来。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Different taste also fine, that's exactly my point. My job is to tell you what I like, not to choose your lunch.
beats.chinese: 口味不同没关系，这正是我的意思。我的任务是告诉你我喜欢什么，不是替你选午饭。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: So—stall three, prawn noodles, thick broth. Reference given, case closed. Whether you go or not, up to you.
beats.chinese: 所以——三号摊，虾面，浓汤。参考给了，到此为止。你去不去，随你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stands, brushes off her trousers, and hoists the paper bag with a small satisfied swing.
beats.chinese: 她站起来，拍了拍裤子，拎起纸袋，满意地晃了一下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: You keep drawing, I go eat. If your pond turns out nice, that's your skill, not my recommendation, hor?
beats.chinese: 你继续画，我去吃饭。要是你的池塘画得好，那是你的本事，可不是我的推荐哦？

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Casually? So many, lah. Colleagues ask where to eat, I give a whole speech with history and broth comparisons...
beats.chinese: 随口问？太多了啦。同事问去哪吃，我给一大段演讲，讲历史、比汤底……

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stops mid-gesture, hand still raised as if holding an invisible printout, and laughs at herself.
beats.chinese: 她比划到一半停下，手还举着，像拿着一张看不见的打印单，然后自嘲地笑了。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Then they've already walked off. So yes, I over-explain. Today, one sentence is enough: stall three, prawn noodles.
beats.chinese: 然后他们人已经走掉了。所以对，我解释太多。今天一句就够了：三号摊，虾面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: See? Done. No disclaimer, no lecture. My mother would be shocked.
beats.chinese: 看？说完了。没有免责，没有长篇大论。我妈会吓一跳的。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She glances at your sketchbook once more, then stands and picks up her bag.
beats.chinese: 她又看了一眼你的速写本，然后站起来拎起袋子。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Okay, I go eat before I start explaining the lime thing again. Bye, eh?
beats.chinese: 好了，趁我又开始讲青柠的事之前，我去吃饭了。再见哦？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She raises both hands slightly, like backing away from a scale she's been told not to touch.
beats.chinese: 她稍微举起双手，像被叮嘱别碰秤的人那样往后退了半步。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Fair enough, fair enough. No recommendation, no stall list, no questions about your budget. Done.
beats.chinese: 有道理，有道理。不推荐，不列摊子，不问你的预算。到此为止。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Honestly this is a nice change. Usually I'm the one holding court about noodles like I'm some judge.
beats.chinese: 说真的，这挺新鲜的。通常都是我像评委一样大谈面条经。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She stands and swings the empty paper bag. A short while later she's back from stall three, the bag now warm and fragrant, and settles beside you again.
beats.chinese: 她站起来晃了晃空纸袋。过了一会儿，她从三号摊回来，纸袋变得热乎乎、香喷喷的，重新在你旁边坐下。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Back. I went and got that prawn noodles I was craving—my own choice, mind you, not a recommendation for you.
beats.chinese: 回来啦。我去买了我一直想吃的虾面——我自己想吃的哦，可不是推荐给你。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She opens the bag on her lap and eats quietly, watching the pond with you in easy silence.
beats.chinese: 她把纸袋摊在腿上，安静地吃着，和你一起轻松地望着池塘。

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: You're back at the pond with your sketchbook. Jolene is on the same bench, folding a thin instruction manual into a small paper bag.
beats.chinese: 你带着速写本又回到池塘边。Jolene还坐在那条长椅上，正把一本薄薄的说明书折好放进小纸袋。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Eh, sketcher! Back again. Today I only brought the manual for my new kitchen scale—no scale, so don't ask me to weigh anything, okay?
beats.chinese: 哎，画画的！又来啦。今天我只带了新厨房秤的说明书——秤没带，所以别叫我帮你称东西，好吗？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She pats the paper bag flat and tucks it under her arm, then nods at your sketchbook.
beats.chinese: 她把纸袋拍平，夹在腋下，然后朝你的速写本点点头。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: For me personally, the pond light is good today—just my taste, no guarantee. How's the drawing going?
beats.chinese: 就我个人来说，今天池塘的光线不错——只是我的口味，不保证哦。画画进展如何？

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.english: She settles back comfortably, clearly in no hurry, and watches the water with you.
beats.chinese: 她舒舒服服地靠回椅背，一点也不着急，和你一起看着水面。

beats.speaker: npc
beats.english: Good, good. You draw, I read my manual. Best kind of company—nobody needs to agree on anything.
beats.chinese: 好，好。你画你的，我看我的说明书。最好的陪伴——谁也不用跟谁意见一致。
